(4) Rule (a)'s path check reads the whole docs set, deployed content included, and another project's path is written with a placeholder (`<clone>/…`, `<project>/…`), never an ignore marker (plan D12, D26, D27).

**Consequences:** `internal/check` is a new package importing the standard library, `internal/trail` and `internal/brain` (for `ReadTrail` only); it opens no SQLite database and imports no driver itself (the driver reaches it only through `internal/brain`), so R4's list of the driver's users does not grow. `cmd/fyr` builds the vocabulary from its own verb table and `recordFlags`, so a doc naming a verb of a newer binary is a finding. A refactor that changes no behaviour still marks its spec stale; the remedy is a re-read and `fyr record edit <ID> --status current`, never a change to the rule. Deployed content's other-project paths are reworded to placeholders (plan Phase 3). Rejected: going through the brain store (writes `brain.db`, refuses unmigrated projects), a per-spec `Code:` field, comparing `updated` with commit times (never converges), an ignore marker, `--json`, auto-fix.

title: `fyr eval` — the Antigravity run kit as a verb, and the second thing that leaves the machine
body:
## ADR-065: `fyr eval` — the Antigravity run kit as a verb, and the second thing that leaves the machine     (2026-10-26) — Accepted

**Context:** Roadmap item 4 asks for the Antigravity run kit (`.agents/kit/agy-rel/run.sh` and `kit-preamble.sh`) moved into `fyr`, runnable on any project, its results stored as records and compared over time; R0 says fyr grows to evaluate projects. The kit runs only in this checkout, against one fixture and a hard-coded row list, stores nothing, and its safety checks are bash with Linux-only tools. Each run sends a sandboxed clone's prompts, and the files its agent reads, to the model of the CLI: until now R8 named the nightly dreamer's redacted prompt as the one thing that leaves the machine, and the kit's runs were outside the harness. Plan: `PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-plan-fyr-eval-the-antigravity-run-kit-as-a-verb`, cold read `REVIEW-2026-10-26-0708-review-cold-read-of-the-fyr-eval-plan-2026-10-26`, approved by the operator 2026-10-26 (D31), the R8 and Non-goals texts with it (D4, D4b).

**Decision:** (1) A new verb, `fyr eval [--fixture DIR] <row>...` and `fyr eval --list`, in a new package `internal/eval` wired from `cmd/fyr/eval.go`. It runs each named row in its own sandbox under `<home>/.config/fyr/eval/<stamp>/<row>/` (a clone of the fixture and a throwaway HOME with the harness installed as `fyr install` would give a place, plan D16), with every check the kit's preamble made: refused roots, outside every checkout, the real config unchanged, no new credentials against a baseline, no processes left, and the agent invoked. Only the operator starts it; no gate and no timer runs it (R3). (2) The suite is one `guide` record per project, `GUIDE-eval`, holding a seven-column table (plan D2); a new record kind or files under `.agents/evals/` were rejected. (3) eval reads `GUIDE-eval` from the project's `.agents/trail.jsonl`, not from the brain store, and refuses when its body or `updated` differs from HEAD's copy, read with the new `brain.ParseTrail` (plan D3, D28): a run always names the commit its scenarios came from, and a testing record an earlier run wrote does not block the next. (4) Results are one `testing` record per invocation in the evaluated project's scope, and each sandbox ingested into the metrics store with label `eval=<row>` and the final verdict as outcome, only after the verdict (plan D6, D22); comparison over time is `fyr metrics show --label eval=<row>` and `fyr record list --kind testing`, with no compare verb (plan D7). (5) R8 now names two things that leave the machine, both to the model of the CLI the machine already uses: the dreamer's redacted prompt and `fyr eval`'s runs, which send a sandboxed clone's prompts and the files its agent reads unredacted, as any session of that CLI does (plan D4). The Non-goal on vendor settings now says the one vendor file `fyr` writes is a sandbox's `settings.json`, never the operator's (plan D4b).

**Consequences:** R0 needs no edit: its "nothing in fyr acts on the CLI between its turns" concerns the operator's session, and eval drives a separate CLI process in a sandbox HOME. R3 needs no edit: its exception governs what runs on a timer, and eval runs only when typed. ADR-056 and ADR-056a forbid permission keys in what the harness installs; a sandbox's grants are the operator's permission mode for that sandbox, written by eval from the suite the operator committed. `internal/eval` imports no SQLite driver (plan D10): its agent check is a bytes search, and its stores are reached through `brain` and `metrics` from `cmd/fyr`, so R4's list of the driver's users does not grow. A suite's `setup` and `check` are bash that runs as the operator, so running `fyr eval` trusts the project as much as running its tests does (plan D30). The README map gains an `eval` node with a dashed olive line to the model provider, which, like the dreamer's, never turns solid (AGENTS.md rule 4). On macOS the leftover-process check does not run and says so (plan O1). The kit stays until the plan's Phase 3 moves its consumers and deletes it. Rejected: redacting what eval sends (the point is an agent working on the fixture as any session does), running rows in parallel, a `--history` verb, in-process install (it skips the rebuild a checkout place gets).

title: Code modularity is the harness's third always-on rule
body:
## ADR-066: Code modularity is the harness's third always-on rule     (2026-10-26) — Accepted
**Context:** On 2026-10-26 the operator asked, in their own turn: "This needs to be added to the harness right away as a global rule or context and we need to run this ASAP on this project right now", followed by the rule's text. The text sets file and function size limits, a pre-edit split check, paradigm-aware splitting, no dumping-ground files, an acyclic import graph, and an audit-then-approve protocol for files over 600 LOC. `context/AGENTS.md` (the hand-written part) stood at 14,814 bytes against its 15,000 target. The Antigravity rules block stood at 18,491 of 22,000.
**Decision:** `rules/code-modularity.md` holds the operator's text verbatim, under a title and the `trigger: always_on` frontmatter of the other two rules (`critical-thinking.md`, ADR-050; `session-sizing.md`, ADR-058). It deploys verbatim to `~/.gemini/config/rules/` like them. It is a file drop with no code change (AGENTS.md § Rules for working here).
**Consequences:**
- The rules block is 20,945 of 22,000 bytes (`TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock`). That leaves 1,055 bytes for every future rule and context line together.
- The cyclomatic-complexity limit (10) has no tool here. The Go code is stdlib-only and there is no CI, so the limit holds only by reading, like the rest of the context.
- The rule exempts machine-generated files but does not name vendored ones. AGENTS.md's rule that vendored skills and the catalog are never edited still governs them.
- Files already over the ceilings get the rule's item-5 audit table before anything moves. The audit of this checkout ran on 2026-10-26, in the session that added the rule.
- Work in flight on files over 600 LOC waits for that audit's approval, since item 2 requires extracting the touched cluster first. The open case is the `fyr eval` plan's Done-section fixes in `internal/eval/run.go`.
- The rule reaches a machine only through `fyr install` or `fyr update` there. No behavioural Antigravity run of it exists yet, so it is a release-gate item (AGENTS.md § Release).
**Amended (2026-10-26, same day):** the operator approved the audit's item 12 ("go all approved as plan"), so item 1's exemption now also names vendored third-party files. The audit's items 2–8 are `PLAN-2026-10-26-modularity`, one phase per file. Item 1, `internal/eval/run.go`, was split at 52259a5 before the `fyr eval` Done-section fixes landed. Item 11 stays a reading-only limit.

title: A child process that reads untrusted input gets an allow-listed environment
body:
## ADR-067: A child process that reads untrusted input gets an allow-listed environment     (2026-10-28) — Accepted
**Context:** `fyr dream` runs `agy` over text it did not write: project trails, memory, feedback and Antigravity transcripts, any of which may carry a planted instruction (prompt injection). Until now the child got fyr's whole environment with only `HOME` replaced (`withHome(os.Environ(), …)`). The ledger's dream sandbox showed the cost at ade98e8 (`PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` § The dream sandbox, finding 2; audit finding SD25): every `agy` call received 50 variables, the canary values of `GEMINI_API_KEY` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` among them. The child runs with no tools granted, so the credentials are only one injection or one `agy` bug away from use. The operator approved the allow-list's contents on 2026-10-27 (audit-choices row 4, D8), and asked for the dream to be verified in a sandbox before it is built on (D46).
**Decision:**
- A child process that reads input fyr did not write gets its environment from an allow-list, never from `os.Environ()` minus a deny-list. A deny-list fails open for every credential variable nobody named; an allow-list fails closed, and its failure is visible (the child cannot log in or reach the network).
- One helper filters such a list out of fyr's own environment: `trail.AllowEnv(env []string, names ...string) []string` keeps the entries whose name is listed, a name ending in `*` being a prefix, in the input's order (choices D6, D20). `internal/trail` already has no SQLite and is imported by every package that runs a child into a project.
- The dreamer's `agy` gets `AllowEnv(os.Environ(), PATH, LANG, the thirteen locale category names (LC_ALL, LC_CTYPE, LC_COLLATE, LC_MESSAGES, LC_MONETARY, LC_NUMERIC, LC_TIME, LC_ADDRESS, LC_IDENTIFICATION, LC_MEASUREMENT, LC_NAME, LC_PAPER, LC_TELEPHONE), TERM, TMPDIR, TZ, the proxy variables in both cases, SSL_CERT_FILE, SSL_CERT_DIR)`, then `HOME` set to its private login copy (choices D8, § Interfaces "Child environments"). The locale names replace D8's `LC_*`, because Debian's sshd accepts any `LC_` variable a client sends, so the prefix carries arbitrary values (ledger D10, from the Phase 1 security review).
- A name joins the dreamer's list only after a run shows `agy` needs it, and only by the operator (`USER`, `LOGNAME`, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` are the named candidates, D8).
**Consequences:**
- No variable outside the list reaches the model's process, so a credential exported in the operator's shell (an API key, a cloud secret) stays out. A listed variable passes as it is: a proxy URL in `https_proxy` that embeds a user name and password still reaches `agy`. The private `HOME` keeps `agy` from loading the operator's own config and settings; it does not stop a read by absolute path, which only the run's no-tools setting refuses.
- `agy` on Linux was verified with this list by one real run in the ledger's sandbox (run R1). macOS cannot be verified from the Linux box: its login reads the Keychain, which may need `USER` or `LOGNAME`. The macOS `fyr dream --all` run is a release obligation, and the release is NO-SHIP until it passes; if it fails, a fix or a revert lands first (choices D27, ledger A2).
- When the list drops something `agy` needs, the dream fails with its existing `not logged in` or `invalid output` hint in `dream.log`, and widening the list is the operator's call.
- `trail.Command`'s git keeps its SD24 deny-list (`repoVars`): its allow-list half was struck because the deny-list already drops every locating variable (choices D40). git reads repository config, not prose, so it is not a child of this decision; a later change that makes git or any other child read untrusted text brings it under this ADR.
- `fyr eval`'s `agy` already gets an allow-list that predates this ADR: a constructed one, where eval names every variable, copying `PATH` (its sandbox `bin` first), `TERM`, `LANG`, `USER` and `LOGNAME` from its own environment and setting the rest (`(*row).agyEnv` in `internal/eval/row_env.go`, `SPEC-fyr-eval` § One row, step 10). It meets this decision as built and stays as it is; it is not rebuilt on `AllowEnv`.

title: A project reaches the cross-project consumers only by the operator's registration
body:
## ADR-068: A project reaches the cross-project consumers only by the operator's registration     (2026-10-28) — Accepted
**Context:** Until now a checkout registered itself in the global search index whenever `fyr search` or `fyr index` ran in it and it held a `.agents/docs/` directory, and a checkout whose trail is records reached the brain store's scopes whenever any `fyr record` or `fyr search` call ran in it. Every cross-project consumer reads those two lists: `fyr dream --all` (whose redacted prompt leaves the machine, R3, R8), `fyr search --global`, `fyr record import --global` and the metrics trail join. A clone of someone else's harness-scaffolded repository therefore became a dream target and a `--global` source the first time a command ran in it, without the operator ever saying so. The ledger's dream sandbox showed it at ade98e8 (`PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` § The dream sandbox, finding 1; audit finding SD19): one `fyr search` in a foreign clone, a search that itself failed, made it a brain scope; `fyr dream --all` then sent its bug record, a canary string and a planted instruction included, to `agy`. The operator approved opt-in registration and its R3 wording on 2026-10-27 (audit-choices row 1, O1, D32).
**Decision:**
- A checkout is registered only by the operator's act: `fyr index --register`, run in it. It writes the marker, the regular file `fyr-registered` (mode 0600, one line `registered <YYYY-MM-DD>`) in the checkout's git common directory, then indexes as a plain `fyr index` does (choices D2, D19).
- The marker sits inside `.git/` (the common directory, so every linked worktree of one repository shares it), because git never copies `.git/` files: a clone, a fork or an unpacked archive is never registered, whatever it carries in its tree. Only the marker's existence is read, and only a regular file counts: `trail.Registered` reads a symlink, a directory or any stat error as not registered, and `trail.Register` refuses to write through a symlink or over a non-regular file.
- The marker is checked at every cross-project consumer, not only where a checkout joins the global search index (choices D3, D15): the dream's `--all` targets, `reconcileGlobal`, the `--global` record hits, `brain.ImportGlobal` and `brain.ForMetrics`. `ListProjects` and `brain.Scopes` stay raw lists of what the index and the store hold. `fyr dream --project <dir>` needs no marker: naming the directory is the same explicit act (choices D16).
- The file index registers a checkout only when it carries the marker; the `.agents/docs` condition goes (ledger Phase 2). The consumers' filters land in ledger Phase 3.
- Today's registrations are not carried over (choices D4): every one came from the automatic registration this ADR removes. The operator re-registers their own projects, listed by `fyr dream --dry-run --all`'s `skip not registered` lines (choices D17).
- There is no `--unregister`: deleting the marker file is the opt-out (choices D5). `init-project` does not register what it scaffolds (choices D18).
**Consequences:**
- REQUIREMENTS.md R3's exception narrows to the projects the operator registered, in choices D32's words. R0's one store still holds every project's records: only the cross-project consumers narrow, and a project's own `fyr search` and `fyr record` are unchanged.
- After the upgrade nothing is registered: the first `fyr dream --all` skips every former target and `fyr search --global` answers only from `~/.config/fyr` until the operator runs `fyr index --register` in each project they want back (Phase 3's handoff tells them).
- The marker is local state the trail does not hold: a fresh clone of the operator's own repository, or a new machine, must be registered again. It is lost with a re-clone and survives `git gc`, a branch switch and a worktree prune.
- Registration is consent, not a trust check of the content: a registered project's records still pass through the redactor and reach the dream's prompt as text.

title: Addendum to ADR-068: the marker is sealed to its checkout and its home; the file index keeps .agents/docs; Phases 2 and 3 ship together
body:
## ADR-068a: Addendum to ADR-068 — the marker is sealed to its checkout and its home, the file index keeps its `.agents/docs` condition, and Phases 2 and 3 ship together     (2026-10-28) — Accepted
**Context:** ADR-068's fourth decision bullet says "the file index registers a checkout only when it carries the marker; the `.agents/docs` condition goes (ledger Phase 2)". Building Phase 2 showed that the global search index's reconcile (`dropReason`, `internal/search/global.go`) drops every registration without `.agents/docs`, because a plain `docs/` is never served in its place (security review rounds 2-3). Phase 2's review (`reviewer`, 2026-10-28) found the ADR stating the opposite of the code, the spec and `TestRegistersOnlyHarnessProjects`, and found that REQUIREMENTS.md R3, as edited with ADR-068, is not yet true of the dreamer: until ledger Phase 3, `fyr dream --all` still takes every file-index row and every brain scope. The Phase 2 security review (2026-10-28) reproduced two ways a third party's tree read as registered without the operator's act, both of them with an existence-only marker: (1) a tree whose `.git` file names a registered repository's git dir (`gitdir: <a>/.git`) resolves to that repository's marker; (2) any tree that carries `.git/` itself — an archive of a working directory, `cp -a`, rsync, or a tarball built to carry the marker, whose name README publishes — brings the marker with it, so ADR-068's "an unpacked archive is never registered" was false. One `fyr search` in either then put the tree's own `.agents/docs` into `--global`. An ADR is never rewritten, so this addendum corrects it.
**Decision:**
- The marker is sealed. Its body is `registered <YYYY-MM-DD>` and `seal <hex>`, the HMAC-SHA256 (Go's `crypto/hmac`) of the checkout's main top level under a random key kept in the fyr state directory, `~/.config/fyr/registration.key` (0600, `crypto/rand.Text()`, created by the first `fyr index --register`, hard-linked into place so two first registrations agree on one key, and never followed through a link). `trail.Registered(stateDir, root)` counts the marker only when its seal matches this checkout's main root under that home's key, so a redirect tree, a copy at another path, a moved checkout, a planted marker and another home all read as unregistered; the consumers pass the state directory beside the root. Only existence was read before (audit-choices D2's "only its existence is read" is superseded).
- The file index registers a checkout when it carries the marker AND has `.agents/docs`, the one trail the global search index reads (ledger D11). A registered checkout without it, such as a project whose trail is records, is not added only to be dropped by the next `--global`; it reaches the cross-project consumers through its brain scope once Phase 3 filters them.
- Ledger Phases 2 and 3 ship as one: no tag is cut between them (none is cut before the ledger's Done in any case, ledger § Session order). ADR-068's consequences ("after the upgrade nothing is registered") describe the release that carries both.
**Consequences:**
- ADR-068 stands, with its fourth bullet read as above.
- At the Phase 2 commit, R3's "over the projects the operator registered" is a requirement the dreamer meets only after Phase 3; `--global` also still serves rows registered before ADR-068 until Phase 3's reconcile checks the marker (`SPEC-fyr-search` says so). Phase 3's Kickoff names the restatements to bring in line then (`README.md`'s dream row, the dream lines of `cmd/fyr/main.go`'s usage, the `dream` flag help in `cmd/fyr/ctx_verbs.go`, `SPEC-fyr-dream`'s target list, `internal/search/dream.go`'s doc comments).
- A moved checkout, a restored backup at another path and a new machine must run `fyr index --register` again; so must a home whose `registration.key` was deleted (deleting it unregisters every checkout of that home at once). The key is a local secret of the same kind as the stores beside it; it never leaves the machine and `uninstall` leaves it with them.
- `fyr index --register` run inside a redirect tree writes the shared git dir's one marker sealed for that tree, so the repository the tree borrows from reads as unregistered until it is registered again: it fails closed, and it takes the operator's own act (security review finding 4, accepted).

title: The dream cap drops news newest first, and the watermark stops before what it dropped
body:
## ADR-069: The dream cap drops news newest first, and the watermark stops before what it dropped     (2026-10-28) — Accepted, amends ADR-055a
**Context:** `fyr dream` caps each project's prompt at 256 KB. ADR-055a fixed the metrics summary as the first input dropped over the cap; the dream plan's D21 then dropped transcripts oldest first, then trail files oldest first, then feedback, then skills, with memory always whole. After a successful run the project's watermark moved to the run's start, so an input dropped to fit the cap was older than the next run's watermark and was never sent. The ledger's dream sandbox showed it at ade98e8 (`PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` § The dream sandbox, finding 3; audit finding SD28): of nine ~40 KB change records, the first run sent six, named the three oldest as left out, and the second run logged `unchanged` and made no call. The operator approved the mechanism on 2026-10-27 (`PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-choices` § Interfaces "The dream cap", O2 answered by D33; D24).
**Decision:**
- The dated kinds — transcripts, trail and feedback — are dropped together, newest first, after the metrics summary and before the skills. What a capped run sends is the oldest news, so everything older than what it dropped has been sent. Two inputs of the same time drop transcript first, then trail, then feedback.
- `Collected.Through` is the instant just before the oldest dated input dropped this way, or zero when none was. A successful run stores it as the project's watermark when it is non-zero and before the run's start, else the run's start, as before. The next run reads the dropped inputs again, because they are newer than the watermark.
- A dated input too big to be sent beside memory and the skills under the cap is dropped first, named `(too big for the <n> KB cap beside memory and skills)`, and does not hold the watermark (D33): the budget is the cap less the prompt's head, memory and the skills, not the cap alone, or memory and skills that nearly fill the cap would drop every dated input every night and the watermark would never move. A drop holds the watermark only while an input strictly older than it is kept. One of the oldest time left — the last dated input when the left-out line beside it leaves no room, or part of a group of one time (a batch of records from one commit) bigger than the room — is dropped for good and named `(dropped to fit the <n> KB cap; not sent again)`: a time watermark cannot split a group of one time, so holding it there would re-read the same group and drop the same part every night (the Phase 4 code review). So a run always advances.
- The metrics summary and the skills are undated and never hold the watermark. Memory is never dropped; a project whose memory alone passes the cap still fails.
**Consequences:**
- Nothing dated that fits is lost: a backlog larger than the cap is sent over consecutive runs, oldest first. Only an input too big to fit beside memory and the skills is lost, named in the prompt, the proposal body and the dry run, as before this ADR.
- Inside one capped run, a new trail record now gives way to an older transcript: the kinds' order (transcripts before trail before feedback) holds only between inputs of the same time. Dropping each kind in turn, as D21 did, would let a kept new input sit above a dropped old one, so the watermark could not advance past that old one while the kinds above it always filled the cap: a run that never moves on.
- Lost besides a too-big input: the part of a group of one time that does not fit beside memory, the skills and the left-out line, named as not sent again. A cursor finer than a time (a time and a label) would lose nothing, at the cost of a new `dream-state.json` shape; not built.
- An input of the same time as the oldest held-back one may be sent twice, once kept and once with its group the next run; a re-sent input may give a duplicate global `proposal`, which `/retro` drops by hand (D33). Two inputs of one time and kind drop the later label first, so a rerun drops the same ones.
- A watermark is now any instant, not only a run's start; `dream-state.json` stores it at nanosecond precision, as it stores every time.

title: Experience reaches the harness checkout only through /retro --harness; retro and distill from another project queue a global proposal
body:
## ADR-070: Experience reaches the harness checkout only through `/retro --harness`; `retro` and `distill` run from another project queue a global `proposal`     (2026-10-28) — Accepted, amends ADR-062

**Context:** AGENTS.md rule 1 (and ADR-062) says experience does not come back to the harness by any path but one: a harness-target proposal reaches this checkout only through `/retro --harness`, run by the operator on that machine. Two skills still wrote the checkout from another project (audit finding WS40): `skills/retro/SKILL.md` Step 6 let a retro run elsewhere locate the checkout and apply a harness proposal there "when the user asks in the same turn to apply now", and `skills/distill/SKILL.md`'s `--global` wrote `<harness-repo>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, installed it and committed in the harness repo, or ran `fyr adopt` on a project-local draft. The operator approved striking both (`PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-choices` row 6 and D39, carried as `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` items 14 and 15, D8). The same audit found the `dreamer` dispatch written out in full in both skills (WS-S5), so a change to it had two places to drift.

**Decision:**
- A `retro` run from any project but the harness checkout gives every harness-scope proposal the status `queued`, always; the same-turn "apply now" branch is struck. The harness checkout's own `/retro` and `/retro --harness` are the only runs that apply a harness proposal.
- `distill --global` from another project stores the drafted skill, in full, as one global `proposal` record (`fyr record add proposal --global --project <root>`), status `queued`, and writes nothing under the harness checkout: no `skills/<name>/`, no `fyr install`, no `fyr adopt`, no commit there. Run in the harness checkout itself, `--global` writes `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` there under that repo's own rules, as a retro there applies a harness proposal. `/retro --harness` applies a queued distill proposal as a new `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
- The `dreamer` dispatch is written out once, in `retro` Step 1 source 8; `distill` Step 1 points at it and names its one difference (`Promoted: none`).

**Consequences:**
- A harness skill or rule drafted in a project waits for the operator's `/retro --harness` in the checkout, where the harness's own Definition of Done (install, eval, review, change record, release) runs on it; nothing lands in the checkout from a session whose checks and trail belong to another repository.
- Experience still stays on the machine that logged it (rule 1): the proposal is a global record in that machine's `~/.config/fyr/brain.db`, never exported. A checkout on another machine sees it only when the operator runs `/retro --harness` on this one.
- Not changed: `fyr adopt` itself (the operator's verb for a skill installed by another tool, run in the checkout), and `skills/discover-skills/SKILL.md:113`, which suggests where a new global skill belongs without writing it.
- No test pins the new branch: the `retro` and `distill` eval rows run project-scope paths only. The skill text is pinned by `git grep` in the ledger's Phase 5 box.

title: The map's experience node names the brain store; the old logs are what import --global migrates, not what stays
body:
## ADR-071: The map's experience node names the brain store; the old logs are what `import --global` migrates, not what stays (2026-10-28) — Accepted, amends ADR-062's map **Context:** AGENTS.md rule 3 makes the README map the contract for what reaches a machine and what stays on one. Its experience node still read `~/.config/fyr/ feedback.jsonl, retros.jsonl, proposals/, state.json, search.db, metrics.db — stays on this machine`, and `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § What stays on the machine named the same three logs as a place's experience (audit finding C37, `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` item 32). Since ADR-063 the experience is in the brain store, `~/.config/fyr/brain.db`: every project's trail records and the global `feedback`, `retro` and `proposal` records, which the `feedback-log` skill, `/retro` and `fyr dream` write. The map never named `brain.db`. The three logs are the shape from before the store: `fyr record import --global` reads them into it and lists them for the operator to remove; `fyr dream` and `fyr metrics` still read a `feedback.jsonl` where one is left. The dreamer's harness-target proposals are global `proposal` records, not files under `proposals/dream/harness/`; only its draft skills are files, under `proposals/dream/drafts/`, which a record names (`DEPLOY-local` keeps that path, because it is true). **Decision:** - The node becomes `~/.config/fyr/
brain.db, metrics.db, search.db, state.json
stays on this machine`. No line on the map moves: `sessions -- "logs" --> configDir`, the dreamer's `proposal records, metrics.db` and eval's `testing record, metrics.db` already point at it, and they now point at the store their labels name. - `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § What stays on the machine names the same four files, says the old logs are migrated by `import --global` and left in place for the operator to remove, and names a harness-target proposal as a global `proposal` record that `/retro` or the dreamer queued. - One commit holds this ADR, the map and the spec (rule 3); rule 6's one home for the delivery claim is unchanged, because which place gets what from a tag does not move. **Consequences:** - The map now says where the experience actually is, so a reader looking for a place's corrections or proposals is sent to `fyr record list --global`, not to files that may never exist on a place installed after v3.0.0. - Not a new path: a project's own records are also exported to its committed `.agents/trail.jsonl`, which travels with that project's repository when the operator pushes it. That is the project's git, not a harness path, and the map draws no line for it, as before. - Not changed: `TestHarnessMap` checks verbs and the report path, not node labels, so the node's text rests on this ADR and on the item's `git grep` (no `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl` or `proposals/` in README.md). - The interactive page of the map is a view (rule 5) and is updated from it by the operator (ledger item 38).

title: What ADR-062 reversed in ADR-003 and ADR-006
body:
## ADR-072: What ADR-062 reversed in ADR-003 and ADR-006     (2026-10-28) — Accepted, amends ADR-003 and ADR-006

**Context:** ADR-003 and ADR-006 still read `accepted` and state facts that ADR-062 (fyr: the Antigravity CLI only, renamed) reversed, and neither carries a pointer to it (audit finding C44; `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` item 33). An ADR is never rewritten and a status cannot say "in part" (`PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-choices` D10, after the audit fix's D23), so the correction is this record. ADR-003 and ADR-006 are left as written.

**Decision:** read ADR-003 and ADR-006 through this list. What ADR-062 reversed:
- **ADR-003, derived agents.** `agents/` is no longer in Claude Code format, and nothing is translated at install: an agent is authored natively as `agents/<name>/agent.md` in Antigravity's format and installed as written (ADR-062 decision 1; project AGENTS.md § Layout). `derive.go`, `toolMap` and `modelMap` are gone; the one place a vendor constraint lives is `knownTools` in `internal/harness/inventory.go`, where an unknown tool still fails the install, because Antigravity hangs a subagent that names one. The verb is `fyr install`, not `styrman install`.
- **ADR-006, the name.** The binary is `fyr`, not `sh-agent`; its state directory is `~/.config/fyr` (`fyr install` migrates `~/.config/sh-agent`); its environment variables are `FYR_*` (`FYR_REPO`, not `SH_AGENT_REPO`); its marker is `.fyr-noindex`, with `.sh-agent-noindex` still honoured (`trail.NoIndexMarkers`) (ADR-062 decision 3).

What still stands:
- ADR-003: `context/`, `agents/` and `skills/` (with `commands/` and `rules/`) are the only sources; `fyr install` assembles the context (AGENTS.md, dev-setup.md and the generated inventory); nothing generated is committed.
- ADR-006: GCP defaults are asked for before the first GCP action and never assumed.

Also out of date in ADR-006, and not ADR-062's reversal (this record does not trace which decision changed them): the defaults are now recorded in the project's `DEPLOY-gcp` record, not its `AGENTS.md` (`context/dev-setup.md`); and the repository holds shell scripts again (`skills/handoff/scripts/check-trailers.sh`, the `google-catalog` refresh script, the vendored catalog's own).

**Consequences:** A reader of ADR-003 or ADR-006 who finds this record by `fyr search --refs ADR-003` (or `ADR-006`) gets the current facts; the two records' bodies and statuses are unchanged. ADR-002's name, superseded by ADR-006, is superseded again by ADR-062's.

title: The visible dream
body:
## ADR-073: The visible dream     (2026-10-28) — Accepted, amends ADR-047a and ADR-067

**Context:** The operator wants to see the dream. Their words (`PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` D32 3, 2026-10-28): "If antigravity is open and there are idle/stale projects. Dream is allowed to run by it self as a agy conversation that would be visible to the user." Today `fyr dream --all` runs nightly at 03:00, when no one is at the machine, and runs `agy` in a private HOME that fyr deletes, so nothing it did is listed anywhere the operator looks. That conflicts with R0 ("nothing in `fyr` acts on the CLI between its turns") and with R3's one exception (the nightly timer, a CLI with no tools), and it moves a line on the map (AGENTS.md rule 3). Phase 8a of the ledger researched what agy 1.4.9 allows (ledger D35: its help, changelog and web docs, and one sandbox dream): agy has no no-tools flag and no per-run permission file, a conversation is listed by `/resume` from the home it was written in, and print mode reports the effective permission state through `/permissions` and `/config` without starting a turn. The operator approved the seven-row proposal, "Approve recommendations (Recommended)" (ledger D36), and the plan that builds it, `PLAN-2026-10-28-1510-plan-the-visible-dream-2026-10-28`, after its cold read ("Approve all (Recommended)", that plan's D17).

**Decision:**
- **R0 and R3 change** to the texts quoted in the plan's D1 (ledger D36 1 and 3), and R8's "the nightly dreamer's redacted prompt" loses "nightly" (approved by the operator, "Approve drop 'nightly' (Recommended)", 2026-10-28; the plan's D19). The one conversation `fyr` starts is the visible dream, a conversation of its own that no session is sent into; R3's exception becomes an hourly user timer that acts only while an Antigravity CLI process of the operator's runs, and runs the CLI headless in plan mode with no tools.
- **Where the CLI runs** (ledger D36 2; plan D3, D6, D11, D12): in the operator's own Antigravity home — `--home`, by default `$HOME`, never `$HOME` when they differ — from the empty `~/.config/fyr/dream-work`, when that home grants no tool without review, so each project's dream stays as a conversation `/resume` lists. "Grants no tool without review" is what `agy -p "/permissions"` and `agy -p "/config"` (`--output-format json`) report, asked before each project's call, failing closed: a report fyr cannot read, an allow rule from any source, a review mode that auto-approves, a grant outside the workspace, a non-empty working directory or a missing login sends that project to a private home as today. Never `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. Settings files are not parsed by hand.
- **When it runs** (ledger D36 4; plan D2, D9, D10): the timer fires hourly; `--all` first checks for an interactive `agy` session of the operator's uid (Linux `/proc`, macOS `ps`; a `-p` run or a subcommand such as `remote-control` does not count) and, without one, prints one line, creates nothing and exits 0; a check that errors exits 2 and creates nothing. Each project is attempted at most once per 24 hours under `--all`, success or failure (`dream-state.json` `attempts`). `--project` never checks and ignores the cooldown.
- **What the conversation looks like** (ledger D36 5; plan D14): no pinned title; the prompt's first line reads `dreaming: <project>`.
- **The dream reads no dream** (plan D5, D15): a conversation whose workspace is `dream-work` (as written or through its symlinks) is no project's: not ingested into the metrics store, not read by any project's dream or its in-use check.
- **The map** (ledger D36 6; plan D16): the dreamer node reads "hourly user timer, while agy runs"; a new olive line `dreamer` → `sessions`, "one conversation per project, in /resume", is drawn DASHED until the build works end to end (the plan's V1 and ledger A2), then solid, per AGENTS.md rule 4; the dashed line to the model provider is unchanged.
- **Amends** ADR-047a (the schedule, and where the CLI runs) and ADR-067 (in the visible branch the child's `HOME` is `--home`, not a private login copy; the allow-list itself is unchanged). Neither record is edited.

**Consequences:**
- In the visible branch the no-tools guarantee rests on agy's own report of the home's settings, not on isolation; the window between the report and the call is a Known limit (`SPEC-fyr-dream`).
- The redacted prompt and the model's answer persist in the operator's Antigravity store, where until now they were deleted with the private HOME; what leaves the machine is unchanged (R8).
- The operator's MCP servers, plugins and hooks load in a visible dream as in any session they start (plan D8, accepted by the operator as a Known limit); the model still has no tool it may use without review.
- The dream spends the operator's quota while they work: at most one attempt per registered project per day, the same ceiling as the nightly run. The oracle adds two print-mode calls per project, which start no turn.
- An installed nightly unit is not rewritten by `install`, `update` or `--install-timer`; the operator runs `fyr dream --remove-timer`, then `fyr dream --install-timer`, and `fyr status` names a unit of the older schedule (plan D4, D13).
- The macOS process check is verified only by the operator's Mac run (ledger A2). Until the plan's Phase 5 the binary still runs nightly and privately; the specs say so in one sentence each, and no tag is cut while the plan is open (plan D16).

title: The root documents are PRD, SDD, TDD and TODO; REQUIREMENTS.md becomes PRD.md and ROADMAP.md goes
body:
## ADR-074: The root documents are PRD, SDD, TDD and TODO; REQUIREMENTS.md becomes PRD.md and ROADMAP.md goes     (2026-10-29) — Accepted
**Context:** A project's root held `REQUIREMENTS.md` (requirements only, dense), `ROADMAP.md` (Now and Next) and a `TODO.md` that had to be empty at every checkpoint, while the design lived only in spec and ADR records that a human does not browse. The operator asked, 2026-10-29, for a small set of clear, connected root documents (PLAN-2026-10-29-root-docs-and-fyr-serve D1) and approved this edit's exact text on 2026-10-29 ("go all approved").
**Decision:** The root holds `PRD.md` (what and why: problem, users, goals, non-goals, requirements, known limits), `SDD.md` (how the parts fit: components M#, flows, decisions linking ADRs), `TDD.md` (how each part is built: one section T# per component, pointing at its SPEC record), `TODO.md` (Now, Next, Backlog), `README.md` (for humans) and `AGENTS.md` (for agents). IDs flow forward: R# → M# → T# → tasks. `REQUIREMENTS.md` is renamed `PRD.md` with its requirement text unchanged; `ROADMAP.md` is removed and its Now and Next live in `TODO.md`. SDD and TDD summarise and link the spec and ADR records, which keep the detail. `TODO.md` gets a Backlog, reversing "empty at every checkpoint" and "ideas live only in handoffs". The PRD keeps the requirement item shape, so `fyr check` reads `PRD.md` and falls back to `REQUIREMENTS.md`. Every project gets the templates through init-project; an existing project migrates on its user's yes.
**Consequences:** The PRD stays immutable and needs no routine edits: goal baselines are dated, and the trace from requirement to test lives in SDD and TDD. The context's resume order, DoD step 4, hard rule and layout name the new files; the skill and agent files that name either old file (17 name `ROADMAP.md`, 18 `REQUIREMENTS.md`, counted 2026-10-29), the init-project templates, `fyr check`, the trail import, two `GUIDE-eval` rows and the recall fixtures change with it. History records that name `REQUIREMENTS.md` or `ROADMAP.md` are not rewritten. A `TODO.md` that mirrors the plan's boxes can drift from them; the plan record wins. A project not yet migrated keeps working: `fyr check` reads its `REQUIREMENTS.md`.

title: fyr serve is a foreground process on loopback, behind a per-run token
body:
## ADR-075: `fyr serve` is a foreground process on loopback, behind a per-run token     (2026-10-29) — Accepted
**Context:** The operator asked, 2026-10-29, for `fyr serve`: a local page that shows the context, metrics, evals, logs and memory, browses the records, and later does basic maintenance (PLAN-2026-10-29-root-docs-and-fyr-serve D2). It approved six decisions with it, S-D1 to S-D6 (D13–D15, D18–D20), and named the two maintenance actions in row 7 (D39). A local HTTP server meets three requirements head-on: R3 (no daemon; the one process `fyr` runs on its own is the dream timer), R7 (memory stays on the machine) and R8 (no service; exactly two things leave the machine). It also crosses a trust boundary the binary never had: any local process, and any web page open in the operator's browser, can send requests to `127.0.0.1` (CSRF, DNS rebinding).
**Decision:** `fyr serve` runs in the foreground, started and stopped by the operator's hand, with no timer, autostart, unit or background flag (S-D2). It binds `127.0.0.1:<port>` only (`--port`, default 3000; a busy port is refused, never moved), with no flag that widens it, and checks the `Host` header against `127.0.0.1:<port>` alone (S-D3), and refuses a request a browser marks `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` or `same-site`, since a browser scopes cookies by host and not by port, so a page on another local port is same-site. Each run draws two 32-byte tokens from `crypto/rand`: the session token, which travels once in the printed URL and then as a `SameSite=Strict`, `HttpOnly` cookie named by the port, and a CSRF token carried in every form; every request needs the session token, every POST needs the cookie, the CSRF token in its body and a same-origin `Origin` when one is sent, and the pages carry no script under a `default-src 'none'` CSP. Pages read first (S-D4, row 8); the only writes are the operator-named actions `fyr index` and `fyr metrics ingest` (D39, row 9), each the verb's own function passed in from `cmd/fyr`, one at a time. Stdlib only: `net/http`, `html/template`, `go:embed` (S-D1, R4). The surface is `SPEC-fyr-serve`.
**Consequences:** R3 holds: nothing runs that the operator did not start in a terminal, and no `dream` action exists, so no conversation starts from the page (D21). R7 and R8 hold: loopback is not a channel, nothing leaves the machine, and `fyr serve` moves no harness between machines, so it is not drawn on the README map (D17); AGENTS.md rule 1's "no service" is about delivery. The token is the only thing standing between a local process and the brain store's records over HTTP; a process running as the operator can already read `brain.db` directly, so the token guards against other users' processes and browser-borne requests, not against the operator's own account. Read pages still write what the CLI's reads write (a changed `trail.jsonl` loaded, the project's search index reconciled, a registered checkout entered in the global index, an older metrics store migrated forward), all under `~/.config/fyr` or the project's `.agents/scratch/`. A Ctrl-C reaches a running index action's `git` children, so that action may end failed; the index is a cache. Each new action is a new decision of the operator's and a `security` review (D15).
**Rejected:** a background or autostarted server (R3); binding `0.0.0.0` or offering a `--host` flag (R7, R8); accepting `localhost` (a browser may resolve it to `::1`, and the printed URL never uses it); relying on `SameSite` alone (it does not separate ports); a token in the URL on every request (it lands in history and `Referer`); one token for both session and CSRF (the session token would then sit in every page's source); a JavaScript front end or a router module (R4); a `dream` or `dream --dry-run` action (D21, D39).

title: Addendum to ADR-075: the session cookie lives under a per-run path prefix, and /check runs one at a time
body:
## ADR-075a: Addendum to ADR-075 — the session cookie lives under a per-run path prefix, and `/check` runs one at a time (2026-10-29) — Accepted **Context:** ADR-075 puts the session token `T` in a cookie, and its Consequences say the token "guards against other users' processes and browser-borne requests". The security review of row 8 (2026-10-29, `security`, medium, confidence high) found that the cookie as specified (`Path=/`) defeated that claim. A browser scopes cookies by host, not by port, so it sends `fyr_serve_=T` with every request to any port of `127.0.0.1`. Any listener there that the operator's browser visits during a run reads `T` from its `Cookie` header: another user's process, an untrusted dev server, a tool's callback listener. With a plain client it can then send `Host: 127.0.0.1:` and no `Sec-Fetch-Site`, and read every page, the global records and the memory included. The spec's cross-port defences (`Sec-Fetch-Site`, CSRF, `Origin`) guard requests sent to `fyr serve`, not the token's own disclosure. The same review found that every `/check` runs a full `fyr check`, 3–4 minutes of CPU on this checkout, with no limit on how many run at once, and that shutdown waits for every one. An ADR is never rewritten, so this addendum corrects ADR-075. **Decision:** - Each run draws a third 32-byte `crypto/rand` value, `P`. Every page lives under `/s/

/`, and the printed URL is `http://127.0.0.1:/s/

/?token=`. The cookie is `Path=/s/

`, so the browser sends `T` only for paths under that prefix, which a server on another port never learns: the pages send no `Referer` and serve no CORS, and CORP is `same-origin`. A path outside the prefix is the plain `404`, after the token check, so the request order of `SPEC-fyr-serve` is unchanged. Every link and form a page renders carries the prefix. Handler log lines name the path under the prefix, so `P` never reaches a log. - `/check` runs one at a time. While one runs, another is `409` with `fyr check is already running; reload when it finishes`, and the other pages serve. - Rejected: - Stating the leak as a residual and keeping `Path=/`, because the token would no longer do what ADR-075 says it does. - Binding another loopback address such as `127.0.0.2`, which macOS does not configure by default. - The `__Host-` cookie prefix, which needs `Secure` and so HTTPS. - A token on every URL, which lands in the browser's history (ADR-075's rejection stands). - By: the operator, 2026-10-29 (row 8's session, two-item table: "Path prefix (Recommended)", "One at a time (Recommended)"); plan D48, D49. **Consequences:** - ADR-075 stands, with the cookie read as scoped to `/s/

` and the token's claim restored for the cookie: a foreign listener on another port receives nothing from the browser. - The printed URL is about 46 characters longer. A bookmark of a page dies with its run, as the cookie already did. - A page on another local port can still send requests to the prefix only if it knows `P`, and it learns `P` only from the operator. So the accepted residual of `SPEC-fyr-serve` (the idempotent writes of read pages, with the cookie, from a browser that sends no `Sec-Fetch-Site`) now also needs `P`. - `/check` costs one `fyr check` at a time. A slow check is still slow (a property of `fyr check`, measured 3m22s with the pre-row-8 binary). - Row 9's action routes live under the prefix too, and `security` reviews them there.

title: Addendum to ADR-075: the token-and-cookie session is the named exception to never hand-roll auth or sessions
body:
## ADR-075b: `fyr serve`'s token-and-cookie session is the named exception to "never hand-roll auth or sessions" (2026-10-31) — Accepted **Context:** The v5.0.0 gate's security review (`REVIEW-…-security-review-v4-1-0-5b716dd`, finding 1: high, confidence medium, a policy finding) found that `fyr serve` composes its own session. A per-run 32-byte `crypto/rand` token is exchanged once through `?token=` for a cookie scoped to `/s/

` (ADR-075a). Every request compares that cookie. A separate CSRF token rides in every POST body, beside the Origin and `Sec-Fetch-Site` checks (`internal/serve/guard.go`, `actions.go`, `serve.go`). The global context's hard rule says never hand-roll auth or sessions, however well it is done. ADR-075 and ADR-075a decided this design with the operator, but neither named it as an exception to that rule. The review found no exploitable flaw: exact Host match, duplicate-cookie refusal, no token in a POST query, `no-store` and `no-referrer`, CSP `default-src 'none'`. **Decision:** The flow stays, as the one named exception to the rule, limited to `internal/serve` (`guard.go`, `actions.go`, `serve.go`). The reasons: - R4 allows the standard library and `modernc.org/sqlite` only, so there is no session or CSRF library to use. - The parts that are cryptography are the standard library as designed (`crypto/rand`, `crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`). - The server binds `127.0.0.1` only, runs in the foreground by the operator's hand, and its token dies with the run (ADR-075). No other code in this repository composes auth or sessions without an ADR of its own. **Rejected:** - `net/http.CrossOriginProtection` for the CSRF half. It needs `go.mod`'s `go` line raised from 1.24 to 1.25, a new build floor at every place, and the token-to-cookie session would still be composed here, so the exception would remain. - A vetted session library: a dependency R4 forbids. **Consequences:** - A review that meets this flow may report it, and its answer is this ADR: the risk is accepted, not fixed. - A change to the token, cookie or CSRF handling in those three files gets a `security` review, as the rule's spirit asks. **By:** the operator, 2026-10-31, in their own turn of the v5.0.0 release session. They were asked: "Do you accept it as a named exception (ADR-075b)?" They answered: "Accept the exception (Recommended)". An earlier "I trust your judgement fix all" was not taken as that acceptance; the round-2 security review asked for the operator's own words.

title: fyr work runs a Kickoff as a sandboxed worker: the third thing that leaves the machine, and a second path for a Kickoff
body:
## ADR-076: `fyr work` runs a Kickoff as a sandboxed worker: the third thing that leaves the machine, and a second path for a Kickoff     (2026-10-29) — Accepted, amends ADR-058a
**Context:** The operator asked, 2026-10-29, for workers: their interactive `agy` session becomes the lead, and each session-sized task runs as an unattended `agy -p` session in its own sandbox, on its own copy of the repository, with only the files its task names (`PLAN-2026-10-29-workers`, § The operator's brief). Two decided things stand in the way. R8 names exactly two things that leave the machine, the dreamer's redacted prompt and `fyr eval`'s runs. ADR-058a made the paste the whole path for a Kickoff: no verb reads a handoff. The sandbox exists already: ADR-065's eval sandbox, moved into `internal/sandbox` with eval's behaviour unchanged (plan Phase 1). The operator approved the R8, Non-goals and Known-limits sentences with the plan's Step 1 (D27), the README map's new node and olive line (D9), and the clone with no remote, fetched back by path (D14, D22).
**Decision:** `fyr work <kickoff-file>` runs one Kickoff as a worker. The lead's session composes the Kickoff from the plan and the handoff skill's template, writes it to a file whose `Files:` line names the scope, and runs the verb; no verb reads a handoff, so ADR-058a's D3 stands, and the paste gains a second path beside it, not in its place. The verb refuses a dirty tree, then clones the checkout's `HEAD` into `<home>/.config/fyr/work/<stamp>/<name>/` with ADR-065's sandbox: a throwaway HOME with the harness installed, the wide grant in the clone, the operator's token linked for the session and removed after, the allow-listed environment, the kill, and eval's safety checks, with check c leaving out what the operator's own sessions, the metrics ingest and the dream write at the top of the state directory (plan D45, D64, D70). The clone's `origin` is removed before agy starts, and the worker commits as the checkout's git identity on `work/<name>`. After the session the verb fetches that branch into the lead's checkout by path, checks the branch's every commit against `Files:`, copies the clone's `.agents/scratch/agents/` drafts, and prints a result contract of at most 39 lines per worker, read from the branch's committed `trail.jsonl` (ADR-063). It never pushes, merges or opens a sandbox's brain store, and it writes no store, so its default `--home` is the real one. A worker is the third thing that leaves the machine: it sends the clone's prompts and the files its agent reads, unredacted, to the model of the CLI the machine already uses, as an eval run does. It runs only inside a verb the operator's own session typed, in the foreground (R3).
**Consequences:** R8 names three things that leave the machine, and the Non-goals' one vendor file is the `settings.json` of a sandbox HOME, eval's or work's. The README map gains a `fyr work` node with a dashed olive line to the model provider, dashed for the reason eval's is (AGENTS.md rule 4): it is not a harness path, and it never turns solid. A development run of `fyr work` takes a home outside every checkout (`~/sandbox/fyr-work/`), the third named exception in AGENTS.md § Rules. On macOS the leftover-process check does not run, as for eval, and a Known-limits line says so. The worker's reach is eval's accepted threat model (`GUIDE-testing` § 4): it runs with `command(*)` under the operator's uid, and the guards, not isolation, keep a run honest; `--runner docker` narrows it later (plan Phase 7). Several Kickoffs at once, `--max-workers` and `--kill` come in the plan's Phase 4; the lead's loop is the `work` skill (Phases 5a and 5b).
**Rejected:** a worktree per worker (its `.git` file points into the lead's repository and shares the index lock); a push from the clone (its `origin` is the lead's checkout, so a push would land in the lead's tree); in-session subagents as workers (one working tree, one permission mode); a verb that reads the handoff (ADR-058a); a second sandbox implementation, a queue, a background runner or a `--detach` (R3, ADR-065); redacting the worker's prompt (it is the text the worker's model already holds, going to the same provider).

title: A lead session is one plan's planning and dispatch loop
body:
## ADR-077: A lead session is one plan's planning and dispatch loop     (2026-10-30) — Accepted, amends ADR-058 (1) and (4)
**Context:** ADR-058 made a session one Task or one plan phase, ending at its checkpoint with a handoff whose Kickoff starts the next session (1), and made the feature skill's checkpoint sentence end the session, so the planning session ends after its cold read (4). `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers` turns the operator's interactive session into a lead: once the cold read is closed, the planner decides whether the plan runs as workers (D48), and on a yes the same conversation loads the `work` skill and dispatches each phase to a sandboxed `fyr work` worker (ADR-076), which is itself one plan phase ending at its own handoff. The operator asked that the exception be written, not implied, and land in one commit with the feature skill, so the rule and the skill never disagree (D49, D57). The lead never implements, so its context holds the plan, the Kickoffs and the verb's result contracts, never a transcript.
**Decision:** (1) is amended: a session is one Task or one plan phase, or, when the feature skill runs a plan as workers, its planning and dispatch loop (`rules/session-sizing.md`, one clause and four words of its description, 118 bytes of the 22,000-byte Antigravity block; no limit raised, `context/` untouched, PRD G1 unchanged, D86). (4) is amended: the feature skill's "the planning session ends here" holds unless the workers decision says yes; then the session is the lead and ends at the lead's handoff, which lists every blocked phase, unmerged branch and closed-set item. The cold read asks a fifth question (parallelism: which phases could run at once without sharing a file, and is an `after:` missing), and in a session that may lead, a BLOCKING question only the user can settle becomes an `Open:` row, asked only when the workers decision is no (D56, D76). The feature skill's gate rule gains that, in a lead session, the `work` skill's judgement rule answers a worker's question in the user's place, except an item of its closed set; it never waives the scope confirmation (D55). A lead defers a Checkpoint's real-home install to its closing handoff's Next Steps, for the final tree (D58; `AGENTS.md` § Rules, `DEPLOY-local` § Operator steps). The worker's Kickoff is fixed text in the handoff skill, and in worker mode the handoff skips `TODO.md`, the push and the metrics ingest (D51, D54, D59). ADR-058 (2), (3) as amended by ADR-058a, and (5) stand.
**Consequences:** a lead's context is measured against the 300,000-token target of ADR-058 (5), planning included, in the plan's Phase 6 E2E, and `/retro` decides from that number whether the loop needs a wave limit (D74); until then the lead has no context-based stop, since the model cannot see its own fill. The yes branch of the workers decision and the lead's loop first run in Phase 6: the `feature` and `handoff` eval rows, run unchanged, stop before them (D90). `.gitattributes` gains `.agents/trail.jsonl merge=union`, so two workers' trail lines squash-merge without a conflict and a record edited on two branches surfaces as `duplicate ID` at the lead's next `fyr record list` (D84).

title: PRD R6 names the standing real-home install on dave
body:
## ADR-078: PRD R6 names the standing real-home install on dave     (2026-10-30) — Accepted

**Context:** PRD R6 said deploying to the operator's real `$HOME` is the operator's action. Since 2026-10-29 the operator's standing permission (`DEPLOY-local` § Operator steps, the project `AGENTS.md` § Rules for working here) has a session's checkpoint on dave end with `fyr install` into the real home, from a clean, pushed tree. The requirement and the practice disagreed. Root-docs D42 drafted the amendment as `PLAN-2026-10-29-root-docs-and-fyr-serve` § Drafts C, and it waited for the operator's approval of its exact text, as the AGENTS.md hard rule on requirements edits requires.

**Decision:** R6's second sentence becomes the § Drafts C text, unchanged: "Deploying to the operator's real `$HOME` is the operator's action, except on a machine whose `DEPLOY-local` record § Operator steps records the operator's standing permission to keep it current: there a session's checkpoint ends with `fyr install` from a clean, pushed checkout into the real home." Its first sentence (every test and development run uses `--home` with a scratch directory) is unchanged. — by: the operator, 2026-10-30 ("go approved 1-2", item 2).

**Consequences:** the requirement and `DEPLOY-local` now agree, and the exception is per machine, granted only through that record. A lead still defers its install to its closing handoff (ADR-077). Not settled by this ADR: the handoff skill's fixed Kickoff text says "Never: … a real-home install", so on dave a session started from a Kickoff still defers the install to the operator (as `HANDOFF-2026-10-30-1021-…` did). Changing that line is a separate change to the handoff skill, not yet proposed or approved.

title: fyr work --runner docker checks the macOS worker's container, though not its processes
body:
## ADR-079: `fyr work --runner docker` checks the macOS worker's container, though not its processes     (2026-10-30) — Accepted, amends ADR-076's macOS known limit

**Context:** ADR-076 recorded that on macOS the leftover-process check does not run for `fyr work`, as for `fyr eval`, because the check reads /proc. PRD.md's Known limits says so in one line (PRD.md:109). `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers` Phase 7 adds `--runner docker` (D102–D110). There the session runs in a container, which on the Mac lives in Colima's VM (D111), and check e gains a container half: the worker's labelled containers are listed through docker, which reaches the VM. A container left running, created, or still listed after `rm -f`, or any docker error, fails the worker `processes left`, failing closed (D109). The host process scan still cannot run without /proc. The operator approved the proposed edit of the Known-limits line on 2026-10-30 ("go all approved with your recommendations").
**Decision:** PRD.md's Known-limits line becomes: on macOS the host runner has no leftover-process check; with `--runner docker` the check lists the worker's container by its labels and fails the worker on one left running, while the host process scan still does not run. ADR-076 stands otherwise.
**Consequences:** a Mac worker in docker mode cannot leave a running container unseen. It can still leave a host process unseen only as the host runner can, and in docker mode nothing of the session runs on the host but the docker client, whose process group the box kills. The line is true once 7d's Mac smoke runs; until then the container half is verified on dave only (`TEST-2026-10-30-1405-testing-workers-phase-7c-the-container-smoke-on`), and the PRD line says what the code does, not what was run on the Mac.

title: A worker's model comes from its plan phase, checked against agy models before anything is made
body:
## ADR-080: a worker's model comes from its plan phase, checked against `agy models` before anything is made     (2026-10-30) — Accepted, amends D26 of `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers` and `SPEC-fyr-work` § The verb

**Context:** ADR-076 is the `fyr work` verb's ADR; it holds no `--model` and is not amended here (D121). The verb's `--model M` (D26) passes one model to every worker of a run, and D26 left `--effort` unbuilt. The `work` skill runs one `fyr work` per wave, so every worker of a wave shares a model, and a phase whose work wants a cheaper or a stronger model cannot have one. agy's model IDs carry their effort (`agy models` on dave, agy 1.4.11: `claude-opus-5-5-low|medium|high`, `gemini-3.8-flash-low|medium|high`, …), so a model per worker is an effort per worker (D114). An ID agy does not know fails each worker only after its sandbox, clone and install are made. The operator asked for a model per worker (D103, "Go all approved") and approved Phase 8's eleven items (D113, "Approved with your recommendations").
**Decision:**
1. A plan phase may carry one `model: <ID>` line beside its `files:` line; the lead copies its value into that phase's worker-mode Kickoff as one `Model: <ID>` line (D126). The verb parses it as it parses `Files:`: at most one line at column 0, its trimmed value matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`, else refusal 3, offline. `--model` is held to the same pattern (refusal 11, D115).
2. A worker runs on its Kickoff's `Model:`, else `--model`, else agy's default; the Kickoff text still reaches agy verbatim.
3. Refusal 21, the last one: when the run names a model (a `Model:` line or `--model`), the host's `agy models` is run once, in `/`, with the verb's environment, a one-minute deadline that kills its process group, and stdout and stderr capped at 64 KiB; every named ID must be one it lists. A failed call, an empty list or an unlisted ID refuses the run with nothing made (fail closed, D103 item 3). A run naming no model makes no call.
4. The result line gains `  model <ID>`, or `  model default`, after `<s>s`, on every result line and both runners (D103 item 4, D113 item 5).
5. No `--effort` flag: this supersedes D26's "`--effort` is not built" in substance (D114); D26's `--model` and `--kill` clauses stand, `--model` now being the default for a worker without a `Model:` line.
6. `agy models` is not a fourth thing that leaves the machine: an authenticated list request to the provider of the CLI the machine already uses, given no prompt and no project file, run in `/` with `PWD=/` (D116). That the request carries no project content is by design, not observed (D122; the Phase 8a security review). R8, the README map and `SPEC-fyr-delivery` are unchanged.
**Consequences:** a phase's model is a line in the plan, auditable and read by `/retro` from the result line; an unknown ID costs one refusal instead of a wave of failed sandboxes. A run that names a model needs the network and a login at its start, and in docker mode the host's `agy` on PATH too, whose list may differ from the container's linux agy (accepted, named in `SPEC-fyr-work`). `agy models` writes agy's own log, cache and summaries files under `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/`, outside check c's watched paths (D122). The skills that write and copy the line (feature, handoff, work) change in Phase 8b; until then only a hand-written Kickoff carries `Model:`. A model agy lists but cannot run (a quota, an outage) still fails that worker's session with agy's own error.

title: PRD's open question on R → M → T traces is struck as answered
body:
## ADR-081: PRD's open question on R → M → T traces is struck as answered     (2026-10-30) — Accepted

**Context:** `PRD.md` § Open questions asked whether `fyr check` verifies the R → M → T traces between PRD, SDD and TDD (`PLAN-2026-10-29-root-docs-and-fyr-serve` row 7). The operator answered yes (D40), and row 10 built it as `fyr check` rule (d) (D54, `dab94f6`, `SPEC-fyr-check` § Rule (d)). The question stayed open in `PRD.md` because `PRD.md` changes only with the operator's approval (the AGENTS.md hard rule on requirements edits); row 10's review named it (`REVIEW-2026-10-30-1714-review-root-docs-row-10-fyr-check-rule-d-r-m-t-t`), and the exact strike was drafted in `HANDOFF-2026-10-30-1725-handoff-2026-10-30-root-docs-row-10-done-fyr-che` § Open.

**Decision:** the line is struck as drafted, the template's "struck when answered": "- ~~Whether `fyr check` verifies the R → M → T traces between PRD, SDD and TDD (asked in PLAN-2026-10-29-root-docs-and-fyr-serve row 7).~~ Answered 2026-10-29: yes (D40); built in row 10 (D54)." No other line of `PRD.md` changes. — by: the operator, 2026-10-30 (D55 (1), "Approved with your recommendations").

**Consequences:** `PRD.md` has no open question left. Not settled by this ADR: rule (d)'s R → M half still reads nothing here, because this repository's `PRD.md` keeps its `### R<n>` sections, not the template's Must/Should items, and `fyr check` prints `note: PRD.md has no Must or Should items: requirements not traced`. D55 (2) moves `PRD.md` to the template's shape as a separate requirements change, its exact edit drafted for the operator's approval first, with its own ADR.

title: A development build at a zip place reports, refuses update with the way back, and never makes a checkout place a zip place
body:
## ADR-082: A development build at a zip place reports, refuses update with the way back, and never makes a checkout place a zip place     (2026-10-31) — Accepted

**Context:** On borken a development build (`b9cae29346b2`) ran `fyr update --from-zip`, which installed the zip's harness and kept the running binary, as ADR-038 designs. The manifest then recorded `zip:sha256:…` in place of the checkout's path. From then on `status` and `update` could not run at all: both are verbs that resolve the harness source first, and a development build resolves only a tree, never one a zip place records. The not-found error ADR-038's last consequence describes told the operator to "run `fyr update --from-zip <file>` again", which keeps the same build and the same place. The place was stranded (BUG-203, `PLAN.md` item 37).

**Decision:** (D5 and `PLAN.md` § Item 37 § Cells, approved by the operator on 2026-10-31.)
- At a zip place, when the source does not resolve, a development build's `status` reports from the manifest alone: a `source none` line, the install, the binary, and the zip drift check as a release binary prints it. Exit 0, or 1 on a missing manifest file.
- Its `update` (with `--check` or `--dry-run` too) is refused with exit 1. The message names the two ways the place moves: a newer release zip run with that release's binary, and `fyr install --repo <checkout>`.
- Its `update --from-zip` installs as before and adds one line: the binary did not move, and `fyr install --repo <checkout>` moves it.
- A development build's `update --from-zip` at a place whose manifest records a tree is refused before anything is written, naming `fyr update` and `fyr install --repo <path>`; an unreadable manifest refuses too. The check runs after the migration of `~/.config/sh-agent`, so a real run reads the manifest it would install over; a dry run, which moves nothing and so cannot read it, refuses while that directory waits. A development build never turns a checkout place into a zip place. The path the refusal suggests pasting is single-quoted.
- Every message a development build prints at a zip place (the not-found error's zip note, `status`'s source line, `diff`'s not-compared line) names `fyr install --repo <checkout>` as the way back, never `--from-zip` again. A release binary's messages are unchanged: repeating `--from-zip` is how its zip place moves.
- A release binary's cells are unchanged, including its refusal of `install --repo` (ADR-034, D15): the way back from a zip place is a development build of a checkout.

**Amends:** ADR-038's last consequence ("a development build with no checkout names the zip install in its not-found error"). The zip still never replaces the binary, and ADR-038 otherwise stands.

**Rejected:** building the binary from the zip's Go source. It would be a new delivery path (project `AGENTS.md` § How the harness works, rule 3) and would need Go on every zip place.

**Consequences:** `TestPlaceMatrix` (`cmd/fyr/place_matrix_test.go`) pins every binary × place × command cell. `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model, the README map's zip-place label, `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` and `fyr help update` say so in the same commit. A place already stranded the way borken was leaves by the way back: build fyr in the checkout and run that build's `install --repo <checkout>`.

title: fyr work --runner docker limits each container and puts each run on its own network; the lead's HEAD reflog guards the fetch
body:
## ADR-083: `fyr work --runner docker` limits each container and puts each run on its own network; the lead's HEAD reflog guards the fetch     (2026-10-31) — Accepted, amends ADR-079 and closes D109's open question

**Context:** `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers` D109 left two questions of docker mode to the operator: a container had no memory, swap or CPU limit (`--pids-limit 4096` only), and every worker ran on docker's default bridge, where one run's containers, and other runs', could reach each other. ADR-079 recorded docker mode's macOS check; `SPEC-fyr-work` § Docker mode and § Open questions carried the two gaps. Separately, BUG-198: a work lead committed to its checkout during a run and reset back, so HEAD was the base again and the tree clean, and step 6's lead check (D35) passed. And P2's second security review (finding 3) found that `leadGit` turned off replace refs and grafts but not the commit-graph, which can also rewire a commit's parents. The operator approved `PLAN.md` items 12 and 13 on 2026-10-31 ("Lets go with your recommendations"); item 42 joined P4 under the plan's rule 2 (found during the run, fixed in a named phase).

**Decision:**
- **Limits.** Each worker's container runs with `--memory 8g --memory-swap 8g --cpus 2 --pids-limit 1024` (item 13): 8 GiB and no swap beyond it, two CPUs, 1024 processes, sized for one worker's `go test -race ./...`. A daemon that cannot apply one of them, which dockerd would drop with a warning only, is refused (refusal 24, `docker info`'s `MemoryLimit`, `SwapLimit`, `PidsLimit` and `CPUCfsQuota`; the P4 security review, finding 1).
- **The run's network.** After the refusals and before the stamp line, a docker-mode run makes `fyr-work-<stamp>`, a bridge labelled `fyr.work=<stamp>` with `com.docker.network.bridge.enable_icc=false`, and every container of the run joins it. The label sweep that already removed a run's containers (at the run's end, and by `--kill <stamp>` once the run's pid file is stale) removes the network after them; `--kill <stamp>` of a stamp with no pid file removes its networks only, never a container, since labels span the daemon and the stamp may be another home's live run. When the network cannot be made the run is refused, exit 2, nothing made: a worker never falls back to the default bridge, and `dockerArgs` refuses any network that is not a run's own.
- **The lead's reflog.** The newest reflog entry of the lead's HEAD and of the branch it points to is recorded with the base; a checkout that keeps either reflog empty is refused (refusal 23). Step 6 fails a worker `lead checkout changed` when either entry is no longer the newest, naming how many entries the run added and the first of them (BUG-198). The branch's reflog catches a move made from another worktree of the checkout, which HEAD's misses (the P4 security review, finding 3).
- **The commit-graph.** `leadGit` adds `-c core.commitGraph=false` (item 42), beside `--no-replace-objects`, `GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null` and no hooks.

**Amends:** ADR-079's docker mode, which this extends; D109's open question is answered. ADR-076 and ADR-079 otherwise stand.

**Rejected:** a network with no route out (`--internal`): agy must reach its model provider. Refusing traffic to the host's own services: it needs firewall rules outside docker's flags, and the host runner already reaches them. A limit on the whole run rather than on each container: `--max-workers` already bounds the run. A skill rule in place of the reflog guard: BUG-198 happened with the skill's rule present.

**Consequences:** one worker cannot take the machine's memory, CPUs or process table, nor reach another worker's container. The second rests on dockerd's iptables rules: on dave a two-container check showed `enable_icc=false` blocking and `true` passing, and a connection from one run's network to another's timing out; a daemon run with `"iptables": false` would make the networks without enforcing either, which is not checked. The bridge still reaches the host's services and the network, as before, and four workers at the default `--max-workers` can ask for 32 GiB together. A lead commit undone during a run fails every worker of that run, as an undone commit already did when the checkout stayed moved. Pinned by `TestDockerArgs`, `TestDockerArgsRefuses`, `TestRunDockerPass`, `TestRunDockerRefusals`, `TestKillStaleSweeps`, `TestSweepContinues`, `TestRunNetworkLeftIsNamed`, `TestRunPidFileFailSweepsNetwork`, `TestRunLeadReflogMoved`, `TestRunLeadNoReflog`, `TestReflogMoved`, `TestReflogBranchMovedFromWorktree` and `TestLeadGitHistoryOptions`; `SPEC-fyr-work`, `TDD.md` § T17 and § T18 and `GUIDE-testing` § 3k say so in the same commit.

title: PRD.md moves to the template's Must/Should shape, so fyr check rules (c) and (d) run on this repository
body:
## ADR-084: `PRD.md` moves to the template's Must/Should shape, so `fyr check` rules (c) and (d) run on this repository     (2026-10-31) — Accepted

**Context:** `fyr check` rule (c) checks each Must and Should item's `enforced by:` field, and rule (d) traces each item to an `SDD.md` component (`SPEC-fyr-check`). Both parse the PRD template's item shape, `- **R<n>** — <sentence>` under `## Must` or `## Should`, with a `<!-- provenance: …; enforced by: … -->` comment. This repository's `PRD.md` kept a `## Requirements` index table and eleven `### R<n> — <title>` sections with no `enforced by:` field (`PLAN-2026-10-29-root-docs-and-fyr-serve` D6), so every `fyr check` printed two notes, `PRD.md has no enforced-by field: not checked` and `PRD.md has no Must or Should items: requirements not traced`, and neither rule read a requirement here. The operator chose to reshape `PRD.md` rather than teach rule (d) the old shape (that plan's D55 (2)). The exact edit was drafted against `db38c01` (`.agents/scratch/prd-reshape/PROPOSAL.md` and `PRD.diff`) and approved as drafted, its decisions 1–5 included (`PLAN.md` item 10, 2026-10-31: "Lets go with your recommendations").

**Decision:**
- `## Requirements`, its index table and its `### R<n>` headings become `## Must — non-negotiable`, one item per requirement: `- **R<n>** — <its old title>.`, its provenance comment, then its old text, indented and unchanged word for word. No requirement wording is new (decision 1).
- Every requirement is a Must. `## Should` and `## Could` say None, as the template has them (decision 2).
- R0 keeps its number, so no ADR, AGENTS.md line or SDD row that cites R0–R10 changes (decision 3).
- Each provenance date is the day the item's title first appears in git (`git log -S`). For R1, R9 and R10 that is the day an ADR-062-era rename wrote the title, so the requirement may be older. The comment under `## Must` says how the dates were found (decision 4).
- Each `enforced by:` names test functions, tracked paths or records. They are the `TDD.md` trace's tests for the components `SDD.md`'s trace maps to that R, plus a few found by name. R0 is a purpose, so its sites show only that the verbs it names exist. R10's sites are unit tests of the macOS paths and the 2026-09-04 Mac smoke record (decision 5).
- `Last updated` is the commit's date. `SPEC-fyr-check` no longer cites this repository as the example of a PRD in another shape.
