**Rejected:** new one-sentence item summaries (new requirement text to approve word by word, which could drift from the text below it); renumbering from R1 as the template does (breaks every citation of R0); `not yet enforced: …` for the weak items (a `fyr check` finding, against `PLAN.md` D6's 0 findings at every Checkpoint); one stable site per item such as `TDD.md` (it always resolves, so rule (c) would prove almost nothing); a rule (d) parser for the `### R<n>` shape (D55 (2)).

**Consequences:** `fyr check` reads all eleven items here: rule (c) resolves each `enforced by:` site and rule (d) traces each R to `SDD.md`. Both PRD notes are gone, and the check reports 0 findings at this commit. From now on a rename or removal of a test an `enforced by:` names is a `fyr check` finding on `PRD.md`. Fixing it is a `PRD.md` edit, which needs the operator's approval (`PLAN.md` D6). That is the cost of the check meaning something. Shown in a full clone with the draft (`PROPOSAL.md` § Must-fail): with `TestTimerMacOS` replaced by `TestNoSuchThing` and SDD's `| R7 |` row deleted, the check reported one requirements finding and one traces finding, exit 1. The R10 Mac run (`PLAN-2026-10-29-workers` D112) was struck by `PLAN.md` D1 as covered by `PRD.md` Known limits, so R10 rests on its unit tests and the 2026-09-04 smoke.

title: The eval suite gains four optional columns, version, kind, cluster and expect
body:
## ADR-085: The eval suite gains four optional columns, `version`, `kind`, `cluster` and `expect`     (2026-10-31) — Accepted, supersedes D2 of `PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-plan-fyr-eval-the-antigravity-run-kit-as-a-verb`

**Context:** D2 of the eval plan fixed `GUIDE-eval` as one seven-column table (`| id | setup | prompt | prompt2 | check | agent | grants |`). The eval-metrics plan (`PLAN-2026-10-31-0300-plan-eval-metrics-the-standard-set-collected-fro`, § Interfaces § `GUIDE-eval`: four optional columns, D7, D9, D10, D14) needs four facts per row that the seven columns cannot carry: which revision of a row a trial ran (so a changed row's history restarts), what kind of row it is (so regression and adversarial rows are reported as their own rates), the family a clustered interval groups by, and the tools or verbs a trial is expected to use. The `trials` table already holds `row_version`, `kind`, `cluster` and `expect` (migration 4), written as NULL until now. The operator approved the plan's Phase 5a as `PLAN.md` P8 (item 5, "Lets go with your recommendations", 2026-10-31).

**Decision:**
- **Two headers.** The suite table's header is either the seven columns or the seven followed by `| version | kind | cluster | expect |`. Exactly one table in the record has one of the two; a row has as many cells as its table's header. A seven-column suite parses as before.
- **`version`:** empty (1) or an integer from 1 to 999999999 written in plain digits, no sign and no leading zero. The row's author bumps it on any change to `setup`, `prompt`, `prompt2` or `check`.
- **`kind`:** empty (`capability`) or one of `capability`, `regression`, `adversarial`, `indicator`.
- **`cluster`:** empty (the row's id) or one word under `SPEC-fyr-metrics`' identifier rule.
- **`expect`:** empty or a comma-separated list of tool names or normalised verbs: each entry one or more words separated by single spaces, each word under the identifier rule, no entry empty or repeated, and the list, stored as its entries joined by `,`, at most 120 bytes (the trial's text bound). It is compared as strings against the stored sequence at read time, never executed.
- Every refusal names the GUIDE-eval line, as the seven columns' refusals do (exit 2 from `fyr eval`).
- **The store.** `recordEval` writes each trial's row version, kind and cluster with the defaults applied, and `expect` as the joined list or NULL when empty. A trial stored before this ADR has NULL in all four; a reader takes NULL as version 1, kind `capability` and cluster the row id. `fyr metrics evals`, which already keyed its lines on the version, reads a NULL version, and a session no trial claims, as 1, so a row's history does not split when the default starts being written; the per-kind rates and the `expect` match are the eval-metrics plan's Phase 5b (`PLAN.md` P9).
- **`fyr eval --list`** prints `v<version>` and the kind after the grants column.
- **The id** is at most 64 bytes, since it is the default `cluster` and so falls under the identifier rule's bound.

**Supersedes:** D2 of the eval plan (the seven-column table). ADR-065 otherwise stands; the suite's trust (D30: it is the project's and runs as its tests do) is unchanged, and no new cell runs as code.

**Rejected:** a label per version (`eval=<row>@<v>`), which would change every consumer of `--label` (the eval-metrics plan D9); free text in `expect` (prose would reach the store, `SPEC-fyr-metrics` § Invariants); rows of a long table with only seven cells, which would make a missing cell indistinguishable from a forgotten one; storing NULL for an empty cell, which would let a later change of a default reinterpret history.

**Consequences:** a row's history in `fyr metrics evals` restarts at a new version, and once P9 lands the adversarial and regression rows become their own rates. The view's `v` column prints `1` where it printed `-`. An id over 64 bytes is refused (none in this repository's suite comes near). The suite parser takes four more cells from a committed record, at the trust it already has. The identifier rule is copied into `internal/eval`, which links no SQLite driver (D10 of the eval plan) and so cannot import `internal/metrics`. Pinned by `TestSuiteGrammar`, `TestSuiteGrammarLong`, `TestSuiteRefusals`, `TestEvalVerbList`, `TestEvalVerbListLong`, `TestEvalTrialSuiteFields` and `TestEvalRowsVersionDefault`; `SPEC-fyr-eval` § The suite, `SPEC-fyr-metrics` § Per-row view, `GUIDE-eval` § Columns and `fyr help eval` say so in the same commit.

title: A project with .agents/trail.jsonl registers for --global, and search reads no docs root
body:
## ADR-086: A project with `.agents/trail.jsonl` registers for `--global`, and search reads no docs root     (2026-10-31) — Accepted, amends ADR-068

**Context:** ADR-068 dropped `.agents/docs` as a condition of joining the global search index in its plan, but the code and ledger D11 kept it: `.agents/docs` was the one trail the global index read, so a registered checkout without it would be dropped by the next `--global`. Every migrated project has no `.agents/docs`. It therefore has no row in the `projects` table, so `fyr record import --global`, which reads `search.ListProjects`, does not reach it (the dream reaches it through `brain.Scopes`, so its targets do not change). The operator set the rule (`PLAN.md` D4: "clean up old files in the docs folder because we are using fyr instead"; D9: "trail.jsonl + split"). Search also still read a docs root in the project index: `.agents/docs`, else a plain `docs/`, so a migrated project's own `docs/` was read as a trail, and an unticked box in `docs/plans/x.md` answered `--open`.

**Decision:**
- **The rule.** A checkout registers for `--global` when it carries this home's marker and `.agents/trail.jsonl` is a regular file in a real `.agents` directory. A directory or a symlink at the file's name, or a symlink or file at `.agents`, is no trail. The row is always the main root's, whichever linked worktree ran, because the dream keys its target and watermark on the row. `index --register` on a checkout with no trail writes the marker and prints a note that nothing reads it yet. `dropReason` applies the same test (`no longer has .agents/trail.jsonl`), and an error reading it keeps the registration, as every check there does. A drop removes the row only: the marker still governs the checkout's records in the brain store, so a `--global` can print a record hit beside `note: dropped` until the marker goes.
- **The global index holds `~/.config/fyr` only.** A registered checkout's records answer `--global` from the brain store (ADR-063), and `.agents/trail.jsonl` was never a file hit, so no checkout file is read into it. `gitView`'s prefix, the per-checkout reconcile, the `name~2` file labels and the partial-clone skip of `--global` go with it. A row in `projects` is now only the list of checkouts the cross-project consumers read.
- **Search reads no docs root.** The project index keeps every file as `code` or `doc`, whatever directory it is in. Files make no records: `records` (the table), `parseRecords`, `recordAt`, the first line of `--refs <ID>` and the file half of `--open` go, so `--open` prints only the brain store's `records:` lines and `--refs` prints them and then `referenced by N:`. `--kind` keeps every value; a file now answers only `code`, `doc`, and the `~config` kinds, and the others are answered by records alone. `fyr index` drops its `records` count.
- **The schema moves to 2**, which rebuilds both indexes on first open (they are caches). The global rebuild empties `projects`, and each registered checkout returns on its next `fyr search` or `fyr index` in it.

**Consequences:**
- A registered, migrated project reaches `record import --global` for the first time. `fyr dream --all` already took it from `brain.Scopes` at its main root, and the row is at that root too, so the dream's target and watermark do not move (P10a's security review, finding 1, which a row at a worktree would have broken).
- An unmigrated project is searched as plain text. Its records answer nothing until `fyr record import`, the one path left (D4); `unmigrated()` already refuses the record verbs, and a marker on it no longer joins the global index.
- `--global` no longer depends on a checkout's git state beyond `dropReason`, so its cost no longer grows with the size of each registered trail, and a word in a checkout's file is no longer a `--global` hit. A file left under `.agents/docs` no longer answers `--global`; it stays in the project index.
- `search.KindOf` and `trail.DocsRoot` stay for `internal/metrics`, which classifies a session's file targets. The dream's reader and the `docs_root` column go in P10b.

**Alternatives rejected:** keeping a docs root for an unmigrated project only (D4 leaves one path, and a second answer for the same file by project state is what this removes); indexing `trail.jsonl` as a file (every record would print twice, brain plan Phase 2); leaving the `records` table empty (dead schema and code).

title: A dream reads records only, and the global index holds no file
body:
## ADR-087: A dream reads records only, and the global index holds no file     (2026-10-31) — Accepted, amends ADR-086

**Context:** D4 leaves the file-era trail one path, `fyr record import`. ADR-086 took search's docs roots and left the dream's: its file collector read `.agents/docs`, `.agents/memory` and `feedback.jsonl`, and the global index still read `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl` and `proposals/*.md`, as did `fyr status`'s retro line. Nothing writes those stores now: `feedback-log`, `/retro` and the dream write records. Item 34 cannot delete them while a reader remains.

**Decision:**
- **A dream reads records only.** A project's input is its memory and trail records and the global feedback records about it, then the skills, the metrics summary and the transcripts. A checkout with no `.agents/trail.jsonl` is skipped as `no .agents/trail.jsonl: fyr record import`, whatever files it holds. `feedback.jsonl` is never read.
- **The global index holds no file.** `--global` reconciles the `projects` table and answers from the brain store. A file hit needs a checkout's own index, and `--global` reads none, so `~config:<path>` hits, `configView` and the `~config` kinds go. `--kind feedback`, `retro` and `proposal` are answered by records. `index --global` prints zero files.
- **`fyr status`'s retro line reads the global `retro` records alone.**
- **The dead readers go with them:** `trail.Dates`, `memory.Store` and its trust checks (`fyr record import` has its own), `harness.LastRetro`, and the `docs_root` column, so the schema moves to 3.
- **The old store's hook pin moves.** `TestStoreRunsNoProjectHook` is named by `PRD.md` R3 and kept by D6: its body now exercises the import's read, the store's one reader.
- **The writers stay.** `proposals/dream/drafts/` is where the dream writes draft skills, and nothing reads it but the operator. `harness` still moves the whole old state directory at the rename crossing. `fyr record import --global` still reads the three old stores.

**Consequences:**
- A machine that has not run `fyr record import --global` keeps its old stores unread until it does: they stop answering `--global`, the dream and the retro line, and nothing is lost, because the import reads them whenever it runs. `fyr status` says `retro none yet` there until then.
- A project that is registered but unmigrated gets no dream, and its log line names the import.
- The schema change empties `projects` again, for the reason ADR-086 gives: each registered checkout returns on its next `fyr search` or `fyr index`. `ListProjects` selects only `root` and `name`, so it reads a schema-2 file too.
- A dream's watermark is unchanged by the migration of a project, as before. A project that imports after a long gap sends its first 14 days by record `updated`.

**Alternatives rejected:** a note on `--global` naming old stores found on disk (a reader by another name, D4); dropping the `search.db` global index for a plain list (a larger change than item 33, and `ListProjects` and the marker checks work as they are); removing `TestStoreRunsNoProjectHook` (D6 puts that to the operator, and the import's read still needs the pin).

title: PRD provenance dates: R0 corrected, R8's earlier wording named
body:
# ADR — PRD provenance dates: R0 corrected, R8's earlier wording named

Status: accepted. Date: 2026-10-31. By: the operator, 2026-10-31 (item 47, "Make the edit").

## Context

`PRD.md`'s comment says an item's provenance date is the day its title first appears in git (`git log -S`). P5's review reproduced 9 of 11. R0 is stored as 2026-10-23, and every search gives 2026-10-24 (`ebfc1cb`). R8 is stored as 2026-09-17, the day its earlier wording "One delivery channel, and it is `sh-agent`" entered the requirements (`9222762`); its full title gives 2026-10-24.

## Decision

R0's date becomes 2026-10-24. R8 keeps 2026-09-17, because the requirement dates from then, and the comment names that exception: "its title, or its earlier wording (R8: `9222762`)".

## Consequences

No requirement changes: only a date and the comment that defines it. `451381b`, three minutes before `9222762`, also holds the wording, but in a plan draft, not in the requirements.

title: The dream runs with no tool granted, not with no tools
body:
# ADR-089 — The dream runs with no tool granted, not with no tools (2026-10-31) — Accepted, amends R3

**Context.** R3, `SPEC-fyr-dream` step 4, `internal/dream` and the README map said the dream ran with no tools, and that any tool call was refused. The v5.5.0 gate read `internal/dream/testdata/agy-1.4.12/tool.jsonl`: under the dream's argv, `request-review` and no allow rule, `agy` 1.4.12 runs `write_file` for `implementation_plan.md` in its own `brain/<conversation>/` directory, with no `denied_actions`. `answer` drops the turn after the write. The private branch deletes that HOME; the visible branch leaves the file in the operator's Antigravity home. A probe on 2026-10-31 asked the model to write two paths outside `brain/`: it wrote its plan and asked for approval, and neither path was written. That was the model's choice, so confinement to `brain/` is not shown.

**Decision.** The operator's word in the release session, 2026-10-31: "Amend R3, ship (Recommended)". R3 reads "with no tool granted (plan mode still writes its own plan file in the CLI's `brain/` directory, and such a turn gives no answer)". The restatements say the same, and `SPEC-fyr-dream` § Known limits names what is not shown.

**Consequences.** No code path changes but one prompt sentence, which no longer claims a refusal. Nothing stops a plan-mode write outside `brain/` if the CLI allows one. Rejected: holding the release for a no-write design, since Antigravity has no no-tools flag.

title: Addendum to ADR-089: R3's writes clause names what is unproved
body:
# ADR-089a — Addendum to ADR-089: R3's writes clause names what is unproved (2026-11-01) — Accepted, amends R3

**Context.** ADR-089 left R3 saying the dream "writes only under `~/.config/fyr/`", while agy's plan file lands in its own `brain/` directory and confinement to it is not shown. `REVIEW-2026-11-01-0134-preflight-v5-5-0` left that as a medium finding, and the newest handoff's Next Steps item 2 put it to the operator. A first wording with `fyr` as the subject was rejected before approval: `install`, `record` and later `auto` write elsewhere, so the claim stays about a dream run.

**Decision.** The operator's word, 2026-11-01: "Go all approved" (the auto plan's D19 item 1). R3's clause now reads: "A dream run's own writes stay under `~/.config/fyr/`, its proposals as global `proposal` records. The CLI writes its conversation and that plan file in its own store: in the operator's Antigravity home on the visible branch, where they stay, and in the private home otherwise, which goes when the run ends. That a plan-mode write cannot land elsewhere is not shown (ADR-089). The dream's own code never edits a project, a skill, a rule or the context,". R3's citation gains ADR-089 and ADR-089a. `SPEC-fyr-dream` § State and files quotes the new words.

**Consequences.** No code changes and no behaviour changes. The requirement no longer claims more than is shown. Whether agy refuses a plan-mode write outside `brain/` stays unchecked (`SPEC-fyr-dream` § Known limits).

title: `fyr auto`, a second timer exception
body:
# ADR-090 — `fyr auto`, a second timer exception (2026-11-01) — Accepted, amends ADR-047a and ADR-073

**Context.** The operator asked on 2026-10-31 for an auto-mode: "fyr auto-mode on/off", running audit and eval on idle projects, the agent fixing problems and asking only when it thinks a step risky, and "Fyr Will improve it self". R3 allows one timer, the dream, which only proposes and "never edits a project". R8 lists what leaves the machine, and R9 has only the operator committing to the harness. Approach B of `PLAN-2026-10-31-1632-research-fyr-auto-mode-idle-time-self-improvemen` keeps them true by amending them, not by working round them. Three read-only readers checked the first drafted sentences on 2026-11-01. They found claims that landed before their behaviour, guarantees that were only tripwires, and conflicts with R4, R6, R7 and R10.

**Decision.** Approved by the operator: rows 1–9 of the research record, "go all approved", "with your recommendations", "Approach B as you are recommending" (2026-10-31, the plan's D1); host workers from the timer, "approved go" (D17); the requirement sentences word for word and eight items with them, "Go all approved" (2026-11-01, D18, D19).
- `fyr auto` is a second, separately switched timer exception to R3, built by `PLAN-2026-10-31-1636-plan-fyr-auto-mode-idle-time-self-improvement-of`. The dream's trigger, idle rule and writes do not change.
- The approved texts of R0, R3, R4, R7, R8, R9, R10 and Non-goals are quoted in that plan's § PRD.md edits. This is the record of their approval. Each lands in the commit that builds it, with tests that then exist (D3). None is in `PRD.md` by this ADR.
- At level `project`, `fyr`'s own Go step applies a change; the model never does. Level `harness` is kept on eval evidence. Nothing pushes.
- `fyr auto` never installs into a real home (D19), so R6 stands unedited.
- Learning tasks get their store content through the dream's redactor (D19). The route is designed in Phase 5.
- R8's list is what is designed, not what is confined: a worker's agent has `command(*)` and the network with either runner.

**Consequences.** This is one binary path that runs model work from a timer as the operator's uid when docker's preflight fails, which is always on dave, where a development build runs. Check c and `auto.json`'s watch are tripwires, not containment. The README map, `AGENTS.md` rule 1 and `SDD.md:152` change in Phase 3 (`AGENTS.md` rule 3), and `TestHarnessMap` then names `auto`. Rejected: approaches A, C and D (the plan § Decisions); landing all sentences now, which would fail `fyr check` rule (c) and claim unbuilt behaviour; an R6 exception for auto's install.

title: `status` reported the installed binary as stale right after `install`
body:
# BUG-001: `status` reported the installed binary as stale right after `install`

## Prevention
A path that install writes but status cannot compare must be excluded from drift explicitly, and the exclusion needs a test. Before adding a new managed path, decide how status compares it.

title: `sh-agent adopt <path> --home DIR` failed with a usage error
body:
# BUG-002: `sh-agent adopt <path> --home DIR` failed with a usage error

## Prevention
When a command takes positionals, test it with flags after the positional; the stdlib parser does not interleave.

title: two scratch rules in the deployed context contradicted each other
body:
# BUG-003: two scratch rules in the deployed context contradicted each other

## Prevention
When a rule changes, run `sh-agent render | grep -n <keyword>` before deploying and read every hit; the deployed file is the concatenation, not one source file.

title: Antigravity silently dropped the `bug` and `feature` skills
body:
# BUG-004: Antigravity silently dropped the `bug` and `feature` skills

## Prevention
The lenient parser is not the reference; the vendors' strict parsers are. After any frontmatter change, install into the sandbox home, run each CLI once, and grep its log for parse errors — `sh-agent status` says the files match, not that the vendor read them.

title: `verifier` ran in a fresh worktree and could not see uncommitted work
body:
# BUG-005: `verifier` ran in a fresh worktree and could not see uncommitted work

## Prevention
A Claude-only agent key is not free: `isolation: worktree` is only right for an agent that must work on a committed base, never for one that judges uncommitted work. Any change to an agent's frontmatter is followed by one dispatch in the sandbox on an uncommitted change.

title: `sh-agent install` kept the operator's real `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` stuck on the 2026-09-03 build
body:
# BUG-006: `sh-agent install` kept the operator's real `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` stuck on the 2026-09-03 build

## Prevention
A self-updating tool that copies "itself" runs its OLD code on the very tick meant to install the change — the same shape as styrman-crew's BUG-035 and the review-standards §2 "installers count as callers" paragraph. Any installer that copies its own running binary must instead build from source, and `status` must compare the running build's stamp against the repo. After any change to `cmd/` or `internal/`, run `sh-agent status` from the real home and read the `binary` line before calling the install done.

title: repo docs told tests to use /tmp while the deployed hard rule forbids it
body:
# BUG-007: repo docs told tests to use /tmp while the deployed hard rule forbids it

## Prevention
Widen BUG-003's rule: when a global rule changes, `git grep -n '<old
wording>'` across the WHOLE repo, not only `context/` — the repo's own
`AGENTS.md`/`README.md` count as context because the global context is
deployed from here.

title: five retro commits changed context/agents/skills with no trail
body:
# BUG-008: five retro commits changed context/agents/skills with no trail

## Prevention
A change to another repo made from inside a project session is a task IN
THAT REPO — its own AGENTS.md rules (here: sandbox start of each CLI, changes
entry) and the Definition of Done apply there before the push; the retro
skill must say so explicitly.

title: `TestRunInstallStatusUninstall` asserted uninstall removes `~/.claude` itself
body:
# BUG-009: `TestRunInstallStatusUninstall` asserted uninstall removes `~/.claude` itself

## Prevention
Before asserting that something is removed, read the code's documented stop/keep list first (here `pruneEmptyDirs`'s comment) and assert on what it actually says it removes, not on an assumption. A test that fails on its first run for a reason other than the change under test is itself a recorded failure, per the global context's "every failure gets a number" rule.

title: Python batch-edit script silently left later files unedited after an assert failed on an earlier one
body:
# BUG-010: Python batch-edit script silently left later files unedited after an assert failed on an earlier one

## Prevention
Before writing any file, check every `old` string against every target file in a first pass (or process one file
per script invocation) so a stale assumption fails before anything is written. Have the script print a
"written: <file>" line per file so success/failure is legible from output, not inferred. After any batch edit,
run `git status --short` and `git diff --stat` against the list of files the edit was supposed to touch, before
trusting the change is complete.

title: commit message described 60 files, commit contained one
body:
# BUG-011: commit message described 60 files, commit contained one

## Prevention
Staging is a verification step like a test run: run `git add` bare, read its
exit status and `git diff --cached --stat`, then commit in a separate call —
never `git add … ; git commit` or `… && git commit`. A path list saved
earlier is stale after any delete or rename in the same session; regenerate
it from `git status --porcelain` immediately before staging, don't reuse it.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "A verification command is never piped into a filter inside a `&&` chain" bullet ("Staging is a verification step too: … never `add … ; commit`")

title: explorer claims a written brief that does not exist on disk
body:
# BUG-012: explorer claims a written brief that does not exist on disk

## Prevention
A user's "change nothing" scopes source, never the trail — `context/AGENTS.md`
now says so explicitly; an agent names an artifact only after its write
succeeded (never report a file you did not write); a dispatcher that needs an
artifact checks the path exists (already the pattern in `/review`).

title: main agent cited a headless run's output tail as evidence without reading its own exit-status file first
body:
# BUG-013: main agent cited a headless run's output tail as evidence without reading its own exit-status file first

## Prevention
Every headless run cited as evidence is read from its exit status first (`<name> exit N`),
then its artifacts; a non-zero or missing status line is a FAIL of the evidence, whatever
the output tail says. A run that fans out to several subagents gets a budget beyond the
tool's ten-minute limit by running detached (`setsid nohup … &`) with its own status file.

title: verifier installed its scratch home under /tmp instead of .agents/scratch/
body:
# BUG-014: verifier installed its scratch home under /tmp instead of .agents/scratch/

## Prevention
An agent definition must restate the global rules that govern its own side effects
(where it writes, what it never touches) — a global rule alone does not reach a
subagent reliably. Before writing or editing an `agents/*.md` file, check it names
its own scratch/output location explicitly rather than relying on the global context
being read.

title: install rebuilds from source even in a read-only, git-less copy of the tree
body:
# BUG-015: install rebuilds from source even in a read-only, git-less copy of the tree

## Prevention
A behavior that depends on the environment the binary runs in (toolchain on
PATH, writable tree, git present) must be designed against every deployment
shape the trail names — `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md § Downstream mirrors`
lists both consumers and their call sites. A change to `install` is not done
until that section has been re-read and those call sites traced, not just
the sandbox scratch-home path this repo tests against itself.

title: TestDryRunNeverBuilds asserted a checkout-only message from a test that never built a checkout
body:
# BUG-016: TestDryRunNeverBuilds asserted a checkout-only message from a test that never built a checkout

## Prevention
A test that asserts a shape-dependent path (checkout vs. plain copy) builds
that shape itself in a temp dir; `../..` in a test is the shape of wherever
the tree happens to sit, which a downstream mirror changes. Same family as
BUG-015's "designed against every deployment shape the trail names" —
`.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md § Downstream mirrors` — but this is a test
fixture, not the production code path, so recheck test fixtures too, not
just `install`/`status`, whenever a change touches `IsCheckout`.

title: Workflow resumeFromRunId re-ran finished proposer agents live instead of replaying them from cache
body:
# BUG-017: Workflow resumeFromRunId re-ran finished proposer agents live instead of replaying them from cache

## Prevention
Before resuming a Workflow run whose earlier stage used concurrent/pipelined agent() calls, assume `resumeFromRunId` cannot guarantee a stable prefix — completion-order-dependent stages break the replay even with unchanged prompts. To reuse finished agents after a failure, write their outputs to scratch files (`.agents/scratch/`) and start a new run that reads them by path instead of resuming. On any long-running workflow, pin `model` on every agent explicitly, since the session model can change mid-run and pinning only the failed calls does not protect calls not yet started. Always access hyphenated object keys with bracket notation, never dot notation.

title: the bug skill's missing-repro gate no longer holds against an "autonomous" instruction
body:
# BUG-018: the bug skill's missing-repro gate no longer holds against an "autonomous" instruction

## Prevention
A change that trims or moves instructions lists each removed rule with its new home (file:line) or with why it was dropped, and a reviewer checks that list against the diff — do not rely on a line-count target ("under 70 lines") as the sole acceptance criterion for a trim.

title: skill texts and references instruct against the global hard rules
body:
# BUG-019: skill texts and references instruct against the global hard rules

## Prevention
A change to a global hard rule greps `skills/*/SKILL.md` **and**
`skills/*/references/` for guidance that contradicts it. Graduated:
`TestNoTmpInHarnessProse` — its prevention rule is now a test, not prose.

Graduated to: `TestNoTmpInHarnessProse` (walks every non-vendored skill's `references/`, `commands/`, `rules/`) and the corrected reference files

title: cloud-run-deploy skill's own triggers bypass the /preflight gate
body:
# BUG-020: cloud-run-deploy skill's own triggers bypass the /preflight gate

## Prevention
A skill whose triggers overlap a gated command names that gate as the entry
point rather than restating the trigger words itself. Graduated:
`skills/cloud-run-deploy/SKILL.md` description.

Graduated to: `skills/cloud-run-deploy/SKILL.md` description (defers to `/preflight`)

title: distill's feedback.jsonl entry omits the `project` field, breaking retro's cross-project filter
body:
# BUG-021: distill's feedback.jsonl entry omits the `project` field, breaking retro's cross-project filter

## Prevention
Every writer of `~/.config/sh-agent/feedback.jsonl` uses the `feedback`
skill's entry shape rather than a locally drafted example. Graduated:
`skills/distill/SKILL.md`.

Graduated to: `skills/distill/SKILL.md` (defers to `skills/feedback/SKILL.md` entry shape)

title: golang-ecosystem reference tells agents to register private code with third-party indexers
body:
# BUG-022: golang-ecosystem reference tells agents to register private code with third-party indexers

## Prevention
Imported skill text is checked for steps that send code or data to an
external service before it is vendored or kept; a step that "registers" or
"publishes" project content to a third party is scoped to public/OSS work
only. Graduated: `skills/golang/references/golang-ecosystem.md`.

Graduated to: `skills/VENDORED.md` (opening paragraph: imported skill text checked for register/publish/telemetry steps)

title: preflight's security trigger list omits crypto, so a crypto-only release skips security review
body:
# BUG-023: preflight's security trigger list omits crypto, so a crypto-only release skips security review

## Prevention
A trigger-list change greps every restatement of it (here, `context/AGENTS.md`, `agents/security.md`, and `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` all needed the same edit); a restated list should instead point at the canonical source.
Graduated: this rule has lived in `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md` § 3's
last bullet ("a rule, ban, threshold or trigger the diff changes has every
other restatement of it in the repository changed too...") since the
2026-09-16 commit applying Proposal 5 of `retros/2026-09-16-retro.md`.

Graduated to: `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md` § 3 (every other restatement of a changed rule is changed with it)

title: `explorer` and `init-deploy` rows failed the matrix although the run did what the row asks
body:
# BUG-024: `explorer` and `init-deploy` rows failed the matrix although the run did what the row asks

## Prevention
A kit built from a Markdown table unescapes `\|` in code spans before running it as shell. Before
trusting a check's FAIL, run the check once against a state where it must pass — a must-fail control
alone cannot catch a check that fails on everything.

title: init-project's "keep content, add `@AGENTS.md`" edit left CLAUDE.md not a one-line import
body:
# BUG-025: init-project's "keep content, add `@AGENTS.md`" edit left CLAUDE.md not a one-line import

## Prevention
A plan's cold-reader check and rehearsal compare every edit against `REQUIREMENTS.md`; an edit that
changes a requirement's invariant stops at the operator before it lands.

title: Step 4 docs-freshness routing patched twice, each patch introducing new defects
body:
# BUG-026: Step 4 docs-freshness routing patched twice, each patch introducing new defects

## Prevention
When one mechanism draws findings in two consecutive rounds — a cold read or a review — stop patching
and settle its purpose with the operator before a third change.

title: plan's describing-text check missed restatements in other words
body:
# BUG-027: plan's describing-text check missed restatements in other words

## Prevention
A rule change greps the rule's subject nouns — "deferred work", "Antigravity", "graduat", "`documentation`
when" — not only its old wording.

title: docs-lens finding applied without checking a recorded decision that already set the threshold
body:
# BUG-028: docs-lens finding applied without checking a recorded decision that already set the threshold

## Prevention
Before applying a review finding, grep `DECISIONS.md` and the active plan's decision rows for the rule
it changes. A recorded decision makes the finding a rebuttal, not a fix.

title: five checks and guards in scratch scripts matched the wrong state
body:
# BUG-029: five checks and guards in scratch scripts matched the wrong state

## Prevention
Before a check or guard gates anything, run it once where it must pass and once where it must fail.
Read a failing control's exit status for its reason: 126, 127 and 2 (not executable, not found,
usage) are not a failing check. A pattern that searches process lists or files must not be able to
match its own invocation or a quotation of its target.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "Silence from your own instrumentation" bullet

title: Phase 6.4 comparison's first launch died at its base install
body:
# BUG-030: Phase 6.4 comparison's first launch died at its base install

## Prevention
Run a detached script's setup steps once in the foreground before launching it, or give it a dry-run
mode. A script that installs a second tree into a home passes `--repo` on every install and status
call for that tree.

title: a print-mode run ends its turn while a dispatched agent is still running
body:
# BUG-031: a print-mode run ends its turn while a dispatched agent is still running

## Prevention
A headless run waits for every agent it dispatched to return before it ends
its turn, and says so in its output when one has not. Graduated:
`context/AGENTS.md`, next to "Unattended runs on Claude Code set a `/goal`
naming the check that must pass."

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` (a headless run waits for its dispatched agents)

title: a changed status message shipped without a covering test, behind a coverage claim that named one test for two strings
body:
# BUG-032: a changed status message shipped without a covering test, behind a coverage claim that named one test for two strings

## Prevention
When one change edits the same message or rule in more than one file, each edited file gets its own assertion, and the coverage claim names the covering test per file plus what is left uncovered — the global hard rule "Claims of test COVERAGE are the sharpest case: name what is not covered." A reviewer checks a per-file coverage map, not one failable test standing for the whole diff.

title: agent-name shadowing defeats the independent review rows
body:
# BUG-033: agent-name shadowing defeats the independent review rows

## Prevention
Before dispatching `reviewer`, `security`, `verifier`, or `explorer` for an independent judgement, list `.claude/agents/` and `.agents/agents/` (and the diff's changed paths there) for a name clash with a harness review agent; a clash stops the dispatch and is blocking in `/preflight` Step 5, not just Step 2.

title: the release gate's blocking list fails open on an incomplete security row
body:
# BUG-034: the release gate's blocking list fails open on an incomplete security row

## Prevention
Before trusting a preflight VERDICT: SHIP, check that every dispatch Step 2 required actually produced a complete artifact — a report a dispatcher decided not to write is not distinguishable, at the gate, from one that found nothing.

title: installer and status advise moving a hand-written CLAUDE.md into rules/, which ships everywhere
body:
# BUG-035: installer and status advise moving a hand-written CLAUDE.md into rules/, which ships everywhere

## Prevention
Guidance text that tells a user to move content into a harness-managed, deployed-everywhere path (`rules/`, `context/`, `skills/`) states what must never go there (credentials, personal/host-specific notes) in the same sentence, not as a separate caveat a reader can miss.

title: the symlink refusal is incomplete
body:
# BUG-036: the symlink refusal is incomplete

## Prevention
A security fix scoped to "the reader that was flagged" is incomplete by default; when a review finds one unsafe reader of a file class (here: symlinks under harness-managed directories), grep every other reader of that same class in the same change, not just the one cited.

title: `sh-agent adopt --force` can delete the harness checkout
body:
# BUG-037: `sh-agent adopt --force` can delete the harness checkout

## Prevention
A command that composes a deletion path from user-typed input validates the resolved path is inside its intended subtree and distinct from any ancestor of the deletion root before calling `RemoveAll` — `.` and `..` are not edge cases to special-case after the fact, they are the default inputs `EvalSymlinks` passes through unchanged.

title: a read-only agent ran a destructive git command against the tracked working tree
body:
# BUG-038: a read-only agent ran a destructive git command against the tracked working tree

## Prevention
An agent that does not own the working tree never runs a git command that changes
it — `checkout --`, `restore`, `stash`, `clean`, `reset`, `apply` — even to reproduce
a prior state. To compare against another revision it copies what it needs into
`.agents/scratch/` and reverts the copy, or reads old content with
`git show <rev>:<path>`. Reading commands (`status`, `diff`, `log`, `show`, `grep`)
stay allowed. This belongs in each read-only agent definition (`verifier`,
`reviewer`, `security`, `explorer`) and is a candidate for `context/AGENTS.md` where
it describes what a subagent may do.

title: Claude Code headless commits carried a Co-Authored-By trailer despite the no-attribution rule
body:
# BUG-039: Claude Code headless commits carried a Co-Authored-By trailer despite the no-attribution rule

## Prevention
A rule that overrides a CLI's built-in behaviour must name the CLI's own setting for it and the command
that reports the setting missing — prose alone does not hold against a vendor-injected reminder. Before
writing a "never do X" rule about agent-emitted output, check whether X is actually a tool/vendor default
rather than a choice the agent is making.

title: init-project's deploy/local.md template shipped invented facts for a project that didn't exist yet
body:
# BUG-040: init-project's deploy/local.md template shipped invented facts for a project that didn't exist yet

## Prevention
A template ships no value that could be mistaken for a fact: an example is either a `<placeholder>`
or wrapped in a comment, and the filling instruction states explicitly what happens to a placeholder
the answers don't cover (delete it, don't invent a value).

Graduated to: `skills/init-project/SKILL.md` Step 4 and `skills/init-project/assets/agents-tree/docs/deploy/local.md`

title: security agent graded stdlib crypto/rand UUID generation as hand-rolled cryptography
body:
# BUG-041: security agent graded stdlib crypto/rand UUID generation as hand-rolled cryptography

## Prevention
A ban must name the thing banned precisely enough that its stdlib counterpart is not caught by it.
When two harness agents contradict each other on the same mechanism in the same round, the rule is the
defect, not the code — fix the rule before trusting either report.

title: feature skill's cold-read cap, scope rule and decision rows all had gaps the simulation exposed
body:
# BUG-042: feature skill's cold-read cap, scope rule and decision rows all had gaps the simulation exposed

## Prevention
A gate must count something a print-mode (headless) run cannot argue its way around — reports, not
subjective "convergence". A design ambiguity is resolved by one recorded, named choice, never left open
for the agent to build every candidate under "simplest reading". A decision row that a later fix
reverses is updated in the same change that reverses it, not left standing as stale description.

title: verifier skipped the first-use guide and let a cached Go test result hide an e2e regression
body:
# BUG-043: verifier skipped the first-use guide and let a cached Go test result hide an e2e regression

## Prevention
An agent's "first time" duty is keyed to whether a specific file exists, never to a judgement call about whether another file "describes" the same thing. A verifier's counted test run is never a cached one — always force `-count=1` on the counts command, in this repo and in any project's own verification guide.

Graduated to: `agents/verifier.md` § What to run (`-count=1` always) and § Records (guide sentence)

title: security agent's crafted-input probes landed as untracked files in the repo root
body:
# BUG-044: security agent's crafted-input probes landed as untracked files in the repo root

## Prevention
Before writing ad hoc probe inputs, a review or verification agent puts
them under `.agents/scratch/<slug>/` with names it chooses itself, never
derived from the input content and never in the working directory — this
is already the agent's own stated rule (`agents/security.md:77`,
mirrored in `agents/verifier.md`), so the gap here is that it was not
followed, not that it was missing.
Second rule, new: after any dispatch that ran probes or crafted-input
tests, the main agent runs `git status --short --untracked-files=all` and
treats an untracked path outside `.agents/docs/` as a stop sign — the same
posture the hard rules already require for an unexplained `D` on tree
changes.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "Ask git what actually changed before committing" bullet (sentence beginning "After any dispatch that can write")

title: failed probe-repo init fell through to the real checkout
body:
# BUG-045: failed probe-repo init fell through to the real checkout

## Prevention
Both halves written in the same commit as this record:
`context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "Ask git what actually changed" bullet
now also runs `git log --oneline @{u}..HEAD` and `git tag` after any
dispatch that can write, treating a commit or tag the dispatch did not
name as a stop sign; `agents/security.md` now says a probe repository is
created with `git init <dir>` whose exit status is read, and every later
command names that directory (`git -C <dir>`).

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules ("Ask git what actually changed" bullet, `git log`/`git tag` check) and `agents/security.md` (probe repo bound with `git init <dir>` / `git -C <dir>`)

title: `sh-agent update` reinstalled an uncommitted, dirty checkout
body:
# BUG-046: `sh-agent update` reinstalled an uncommitted, dirty checkout

## Prevention
`update` refuses a dirty checkout on every path, not just "behind
upstream" — graduated into `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`, `ADR-027`, and
`REQUIREMENTS.md` R4. Before relying on `sh-agent update` on a checkout used
for active development, confirm the dirty check itself is pinned (see
BUG-049): a guard that trusts git's configurable default can still pass a
dirty-looking-clean tree.

Graduated to: `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` `update()` (refuses a dirty checkout on every path); ADR-027; `REQUIREMENTS.md` R4

title: signed-tag release check compared a placeholder to itself
body:
# BUG-047: signed-tag release check compared a placeholder to itself

## Prevention
A check's expected value never comes from the same hand-substituted
input as the thing it checks — bind it to something produced elsewhere
(HEAD, a prior gate report), never a placeholder threaded through both
sides. A must-fail case is validated only in a state the real flow can
actually produce, or it validates nothing.

Graduated to: `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases (tag sits on HEAD; checks bind to HEAD and the gate report's `Range reviewed:` head)

title: the documented gate `gofmt -l .` fails on junk left in `.agents/scratch`
body:
# BUG-048: the documented gate `gofmt -l .` fails on junk left in `.agents/scratch`

## Prevention
A verification command that walks the whole tree is scoped to the source
directories on any project that keeps generated files under
`.agents/scratch/`; `agents/verifier.md` § What to run now names this caveat
for its Go auto-detect so the rule reaches every project, not just this one.

Graduated to: `agents/verifier.md` § What to run, plus `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/sh-agent/guide.md` (`gofmt -l cmd internal`)

title: the BUG-046 dirty-checkout guard trusted git's configurable default
body:
# BUG-049: the BUG-046 dirty-checkout guard trusted git's configurable default

## Prevention
A guard never trusts a git command's default when a config key can change
it — pass the flag that pins the behaviour, and test with that key set
against you.

Graduated to: `internal/harness/repo.go` (`--untracked-files=all`) and `TestInspectCountsUntrackedFiles`

title: the install walk copied secret-shaped files into every vendor directory
body:
# BUG-050: the install walk copied secret-shaped files into every vendor directory

## Prevention
The same secret shapes that stop a commit (`context/AGENTS.md` § Hard
rules, "Ask git what actually changed" bullet) stop a deploy too: any step
that copies project files outward applies that list, not just the commit
step.

Graduated to: `internal/harness/plan.go` (`secretShaped`) and `TestPlanRefusesSecretShapedFiles`

title: `git init --bare` failed with "GIT_WORK_TREE not allowed without GIT_DIR" inside an isolated test
body:
# BUG-051: `git init --bare` failed with "GIT_WORK_TREE not allowed without GIT_DIR" inside an isolated test

## Prevention
Before isolating git (or any tool with "empty means set" semantics) from the
environment in a test, unset variables with `os.Unsetenv` after
`t.Setenv(k, "")`, not `t.Setenv(k, "")` alone; a blank string is not an unset
variable.

title: rejected-push case of `TestSendReport` returned nil error, no rejection
body:
# BUG-052: rejected-push case of `TestSendReport` returned nil error, no rejection

## Prevention
A test asserting a git conflict (rejected push, merge conflict, divergent
history) must make the competing commits differ in content, not just in
timing or checkout path; a fixed clock combined with otherwise-identical
inputs produces byte-identical, same-hash commits, which git treats as
already-applied rather than conflicting.

title: `sh-agent report`'s redaction needles missed most real credential shapes, and `--dry-run` could not reveal the miss
body:
# BUG-053: `sh-agent report`'s redaction needles missed most real credential shapes, and `--dry-run` could not reveal the miss

## Prevention
Before shipping a redaction or secret-detection feature, build adversarial fixtures of the realistic shapes it must catch (case variants, env-var prefixes, common vendor formats) — not only the shapes named in the design doc — and run them as must-fail tests against the shipped matcher. A safeguard the docs recommend to catch a failure mode must itself be tested against that failure mode (does `--dry-run` show a miss, not just a hit) before the docs claim it.

title: a secret in a JSON key was written verbatim into `report.json` as the redaction's recorded path
body:
# BUG-054: a secret in a JSON key was written verbatim into `report.json` as the redaction's recorded path

## Prevention
A test that verifies redaction correctness must assert on content (the marshalled/sent bytes contain no secret), not just record count — `len(recs) == 1` proves a record was made, not that it is safe. When a field is meant to carry metadata only (a path, a location), assert directly that it never carries the value it points at.

title: `sh-agent report` pushed to whatever remote its checkout resolved to, with no check that it was the feedback repository
body:
# BUG-055: `sh-agent report` pushed to whatever remote its checkout resolved to, with no check that it was the feedback repository

## Prevention
A tool that commits and pushes to a repository resolved from a flag, default, or the environment must verify the resolved remote matches the expected target before writing anything — not just that a `.git` exists. Refuse (do not silently follow) redirect-shaped environment variables (`GIT_DIR` and siblings) in any tool that shells out to git.

title: `sh-agent report`'s redaction had four structural gaps where a needle was present but content was still sent and the run reported success
body:
# BUG-056: `sh-agent report`'s redaction had four structural gaps where a needle was present but content was still sent and the run reported success

## Prevention
A text-processing redaction pipeline needs fixtures for malformed/adversarial structure, not just malformed *content*: duplicate keys, multi-marker lines, altered delimiters, and a structure that satisfies one parser (JSON) while defeating another (block scanning) in the same pipeline. When two matching strategies (JSON walk, line/block scan) can each individually "succeed" on the same input, test what happens when one finds nothing but the raw text still contains the needle — it must fall through, not be treated as clean.

title: a file-editing tool converted a JSON escape into its literal character, so a test named for that escape never exercised it
body:
# BUG-057: a file-editing tool converted a JSON escape into its literal character, so a test named for that escape never exercised it

## Prevention
After writing any fixture or text containing an escape sequence (`\u`, `\n` inside a string literal meant to stay literal, etc.) via an editing tool, check the actual bytes (`grep -n` / `od -c`) before trusting the file. A test's name is not evidence that it exercises the path it names — run a mutant that removes the path under test and confirm the test fails.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "Ask git what actually changed" bullet

title: a review Outcome marked a finding "fixed by deleting the mechanism" while one of the finding's two triggers still leaked
body:
# BUG-058: a review Outcome marked a finding "fixed by deleting the mechanism" while one of the finding's two triggers still leaked

## Prevention
When a review Outcome marks a finding fixed, check every trigger the finding names — not only the headline reproduction — against a must-fail test before recording "fixed". "Fixed by deleting the mechanism" is only true if the deletion removes every path the finding described.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Definition of Done, step 2

title: replacing a matcher and a decoder each introduced a regression the old implementation had handled
body:
# BUG-059: replacing a matcher and a decoder each introduced a regression the old implementation had handled

## Prevention
When replacing a decoder or a matcher, run the old implementation's already-accepted inputs (edge-case numbers, quoting styles, encodings it previously handled) as must-pass cases against the new one before deleting the old code — a swap is a regression risk even when it targets a real, named defect.

title: code comments and docs claimed a push "cannot be redirected" without naming the redirect mechanisms actually checked
body:
# BUG-060: code comments and docs claimed a push "cannot be redirected" without naming the redirect mechanisms actually checked

## Prevention
A claim that a destination "cannot be redirected" or "never goes to X" names the specific redirect mechanisms it was checked against, not an unscoped guarantee — the next round otherwise finds the mechanism nobody tried. When a review finding lands a second consecutive round on the same mechanism (here: the push target, three rounds running), stop patching and take it to the operator for what it must guarantee, per the project's own review-convergence rule.

title: changelog agent's ADR-031 draft asserted facts not in its dispatch or the diff
body:
# BUG-061: changelog agent's ADR-031 draft asserted facts not in its dispatch or the diff

## Prevention
An ADR or changes entry states only what its dispatch and the diff say — every factual claim traceable to one of the two, no fill-in from memory of older ADRs or other repos. The main agent reads an agent-written ADR against the diff itself before committing it, not only via the reviewer. A claim about another project's use of the harness never enters a decision record (R8); this is the second time R8's no-consumer-naming rule was violated by a subagent (see BUG-015 for the installer-side case) and reinforces graduating a "no consumer names in this repo" check into the `changelog` agent definition or a `.agents/rules/` file, plus a citation rule (name sections, never line numbers, since lines drift).

Graduated to: `feature § Decisions (the main agent writes ADRs; changelog refuses them) and context § Definition of Done step 4`

title: Claude Code's verifier resolved `<app>` to the repo directory name, Antigravity to `cmd/<app>`
body:
# BUG-062: Claude Code's verifier resolved `<app>` to the repo directory name, Antigravity to `cmd/<app>`

## Prevention
An ordered resolution rule names the check for its first branch, not only the outcome, so an agent cannot silently fall through; the artifact records which branch fired, making a wrong resolution visible without a repro.

Addendum (2026-09-17): the b093fd6 fix was not reliable — repro-8 (`.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-17-bug-063-adr-032-repro.md`, 1 of 5 runs with it) never ran `ls -d cmd/*/` and named the guide `demo` again. The operator then chose to delete the `<app>` level for testing guides (ADR-032): one guide per project at `testing/guide.md`, so nothing needs resolving. Status stays fixed, now by removing the mechanism rather than patching the rule; the fix commit carries ADR-032 and the `agents/verifier.md`/`agents/documentation.md` update. When a prose rule is followed in most but not all runs, prefer deleting the decision it asks the agent to make over rewording it — three defects on `<app>` resolution (G20, BUG-062, the b093fd6 miss).

title: verifier's log said `Scope: complete` while a required testing guide was never written
body:
# BUG-063: verifier's log said `Scope: complete` while a required testing guide was never written

## Prevention
A duty an agent must perform is a numbered step it runs, not a paragraph beside the steps; "complete" is defined by the artifacts it owes, not only the commands it ran.

title: verifier's guide duty still not reliably performed on Claude Code after BUG-063's fix
body:
# BUG-064: verifier's guide duty still not reliably performed on Claude Code after BUG-063's fix

## Prevention
A duty a subagent must not skip goes in the dispatch text the main agent writes, not only in the subagent's own definition: rules inside `agents/verifier.md` itself were followed intermittently on Claude Code, while the same instruction placed in the dispatch prompt held in every run today.

title: `/feedback` loaded the harness skill instead of Claude Code's built-in
body:
# BUG-065: `/feedback` loaded the harness skill instead of Claude Code's built-in

## Prevention
A skill, agent, or command in this harness never takes the name of a built-in
slash command of either target CLI; check the CLI's built-in command list
before adding or renaming one. This is the same class of clash one level up
from `AGENTS.md` (project) § Rules for working here, which already forbids a
project skill reusing a harness name — that rule should be read as covering
vendor built-ins too, or a matching check added alongside it.

title: `go:embed all:` compiles untracked or gitignored files into the release binary
body:
# BUG-066: `go:embed all:` compiles untracked or gitignored files into the release binary

## Prevention
A test that a generated or embedded artifact matches a source must assert BOTH directions — extra content is as much a defect as missing content. An artifact built from the working tree, not from git, must be pinned to what git tracks, not just checked for completeness.

Graduated to: `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md` § 2 (generated-counterpart checklist item); one-line version in `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules

title: `knownCheckout` resolved an `embedded:vX.Y.Z` manifest value as a filesystem path
body:
# BUG-067: `knownCheckout` resolved an `embedded:vX.Y.Z` manifest value as a filesystem path

## Prevention
When one field gains a value of a new kind, grep every reader of that field in the same change — guarding only the reader that prompted the change is half a fix. Same shape as BUG-036.

title: a must-fail mutation anchored on non-unique text hit the wrong site and its restore didn't undo the damage
body:
# BUG-068: a must-fail mutation anchored on non-unique text hit the wrong site and its restore didn't undo the damage

## Prevention
A must-fail mutation asserts its target is unique before writing (count occurrences, fail if not exactly one). Undo it by restoring the saved copy of the file, never by a reverse text replacement. After restoring, read `git diff` to confirm nothing else changed.

Graduated to: `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md` § 2 (mutation checklist item), cited from `skills/bug/SKILL.md` Step 3 and `skills/feature/SKILL.md` Step 4

title: `RemoveKeptClone`'s unpushed-commit guard fails open, deleting the operator's only copy
body:
# BUG-069: `RemoveKeptClone`'s unpushed-commit guard fails open, deleting the operator's only copy

## Prevention
A guard standing in front of a destructive action is written so that an
ERROR from the check keeps the data — `if err != nil` leaves, never falls
through to the delete — and its test suite includes the case where the check
itself cannot run, not only the cases where it runs and answers.

Graduated to: one-line form in `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules; `err == nil && somethingToLose` example in `skills/golang/SKILL.md` § Error Handling

title: `sh-agent update --check` deleted files despite its read-only contract
body:
# BUG-070: `sh-agent update --check` deleted files despite its read-only contract

## Prevention
When adding a side effect to a command that has a read-only or dry-run mode,
find that mode's early returns first and place the effect below them — and
the test for the effect asserts the read-only mode does NOT perform it, not
only that the normal mode does.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "When a command has a read-only mode" bullet

title: two Phase 3 tests set up conditions that did not hold, so they passed or failed for the wrong reason
body:
# BUG-071: two Phase 3 tests set up conditions that did not hold, so they passed or failed for the wrong reason

## Prevention
Before trusting a test that sets up an unusual condition, prove the
condition actually holds — run the command by hand in a scratch fixture and
read its output — because a premise that silently does not hold produces a
test that passes or fails for the wrong reason. This is BUG-024's rule
("validate a check against a must-pass state, not only a must-fail one"),
applied to test setup rather than to the assertion; it did not generalize on
its own and needed re-recording here for the setup case specifically.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "A test that sets up an unusual condition proves the condition HOLDS" clause

title: verifier dispatched against a tree the main agent kept editing
body:
# BUG-072: verifier dispatched against a tree the main agent kept editing

## Prevention
While a `verifier` dispatch is in flight, do not edit any file in its scope — keep
the tree frozen until the artifact lands; note anything found meanwhile and apply
it after. When a fix cannot wait, stop the run (TaskStop) rather than let it verify
a moving tree, then dispatch again after committing.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Definition of Done, step 1, "While that dispatch is IN FLIGHT the tree stays frozen" sentence

title: new retro record overwrote an existing same-day retro instead of taking the next free suffix
body:
# BUG-073: new retro record overwrote an existing same-day retro instead of taking the next free suffix

## Prevention
Before writing any DATED trail artifact whose name may already be taken (retro, handoff, changes entry, testing log, review), `ls` the target directory in the same turn as the write and pick the next free suffix from what is there, never from what this session remembers writing — an in-context directory listing goes stale the moment another session commits. When a write meant to create a file instead shows as MODIFIED in `git status`, that is read before staging, per BUG-011.

title: RemoveKeptClone reported "unpushed commits" for commits already on the remote
body:
# BUG-074: RemoveKeptClone reported "unpushed commits" for commits already on the remote

## Prevention
A message that reports a count names what the count was measured against whenever that basis can be stale or indirect, and never restates it as a stronger conclusion than the measurement supports — "N commits no remote-tracking ref holds" is what `--not --remotes` establishes; "N unpushed commits" is not. When the difference affects a decision the reader will make (here: delete a directory or not), the message also gives the command that settles it.

title: documented `go install` line for v1.1.0 fails without an SSH rewrite the reader was never told to add
body:
# BUG-075: documented `go install` line for v1.1.0 fails without an SSH rewrite the reader was never told to add

## Prevention
A command a doc tells the reader to RUN is executed as written, from the state the reader will be in, before the release that documents it — never approximated with different flags or read against the code instead. When it cannot be run before the release because it needs the tag the release itself creates, the release's Done row runs it immediately after and the doc is corrected in that same task; a docs review that can only read such a command says so under `## Not examined` rather than passing it.

title: `ResolveSource`'s not-found error hid the real precondition (no harness built in)
body:
# BUG-076: `ResolveSource`'s not-found error hid the real precondition (no harness built in)

## Prevention
When a fallback or guard refuses because a precondition failed, the error names the precondition that failed, not only the alternatives the reader might try. "X not found: try A, B or C" is right only when X's absence is the whole story; when the code knows something more specific — this build cannot do it at all, this file is the wrong kind, this mode forbids it — say that first, since the reader's next action depends on which it is.

title: release binary silently installed a stale plain-copy tree instead of its embedded harness
body:
# BUG-077: release binary silently installed a stale plain-copy tree instead of its embedded harness

## Prevention
When a program can obtain the same input from several sources, decide the order per KIND of
build, not once for all of them — an artifact that ships its own copy of an input must never
silently prefer a copy it found on the machine, and a source that cannot be updated (a plain
copy) is never preferred over one that can. State which source won whenever more than one was
possible and the choice changes what the tool then deploys.

title: verified v1.2.1 release binary installed to /usr/local/bin, but an earlier PATH entry kept running a stale (devel) build
body:
# BUG-078: verified v1.2.1 release binary installed to /usr/local/bin, but an earlier PATH entry kept running a stale (devel) build

## Prevention
Candidate rule (not yet written into any file — proposing, not applying): after installing or replacing the `sh-agent` binary, run `which -a sh-agent` and compare every match against the binary just installed; a "verified install" claim is only true once `sh-agent version` (run through the shell, unqualified — not by absolute path) reports the expected version. Separately: a downloaded release artifact is run (`version`) and checksum-verified before being moved into a system path, and the download step uses `--clobber` so a stale file at the download path can't be silently reused.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "A claim that something works states HOW it was verified" bullet

title: `sh-agent update` reported success but left the running binary stale (bash hash cache)
body:
# BUG-079: `sh-agent update` reported success but left the running binary stale (bash hash cache)

## Prevention
Before shipping a fix, `update`/`install` should compare the running binary's path (`os.Executable()`, resolved) via `os.SameFile` against the file it just wrote; when they differ, the output should say the running binary was not replaced and is stale, and name the remedy (`hash -r` in bash, `rehash` in zsh). Docs (README / `remote.md`) should add `type sh-agent` (or `hash -r` before `which -a`) to the post-install/update verification steps, since `which -a` cannot see a shell's hash cache. Now also in `testing/guide.md` § 5's post-update check (a doc, not yet a formal graduation target — see Related for the recommendation).

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "A claim that something works states HOW it was verified" bullet; § Definition of Done, step 2

title: relative `--home` resolved against the repo directory on a real install, against cwd on `--dry-run`
body:
# BUG-080: relative `--home` resolved against the repo directory on a real install, against cwd on `--dry-run`

## Prevention
A path handed to a child process started with a different working directory (`cmd.Dir`) is made absolute before the handoff — the child cannot know the parent's cwd. This is also an instance of the `context/AGENTS.md` read-only-mode rule: `--dry-run` must resolve paths exactly as the real run does, or it is not a dry run of the real run.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "When a command has a read-only mode" bullet

title: three fixes each passed their own test and the next review round found the same mechanism still broken
body:
# BUG-081: three fixes each passed their own test and the next review round found the same mechanism still broken

## Prevention
`context/AGENTS.md` § Definition of Done, step 2 already states: a fix's test builds the arrangement the finding measured — the pre-existing loose directory, the branch that installs nothing, the symlinked path — not a fresh fixture where the fix cannot lose. This rule was added as part of the session that produced this bug and covers it going forward.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Definition of Done, step 2 ("that test builds the ARRANGEMENT the finding measured" clause)

title: four must-fail mutations printed "fails as it must" when `go test` had failed at the build, so no test ever ran
body:
# BUG-082: four must-fail mutations printed "fails as it must" when `go test` had failed at the build, so no test ever ran

## Prevention
`context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, the mutation clause already states: a must-fail mutation "counts as a verdict only when the mutated code COMPILED and a named test failed — a build failure … is printed as such and is no evidence". This rule was added as part of the session that produced this bug and covers it going forward.

Graduated to: `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md` § 2 (mutation checklist item, names BUG-082)

title: rewritten "write the artifact EARLY" rule in verifier.md followed in only 1 of 3 runs
body:
# BUG-083: rewritten "write the artifact EARLY" rule in verifier.md followed in only 1 of 3 runs

## Prevention
A change to an agent definition is verified by runs whose dispatch does NOT repeat the changed rule, and the count is reported as n of N, never "works". The sentence that must hold every run goes in the dispatch text (BUG-064) — the definition alone is not reliable enforcement on Claude Code.
`Diagnosis missed:` n/a.

Graduated to: `guide.md § 4 § Behavioural runs (n of N, never "works")`

title: retro-applied edits left a vocabulary enumerated in one place stale in another
body:
# BUG-084: retro-applied edits left a vocabulary enumerated in one place stale in another

## Prevention
When a value joins a vocabulary (a signal, a status, a category), grep the file and its consumers for every enumeration of that vocabulary — schema lines, templates, tables — and change them in the same edit. A rule that names an ordinal step ("the first command") is read against the agent's own step order before it is written.

Graduated to: `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, "A behaviour change includes the text that DESCRIBES it" bullet ("Two shapes hide best: a value joining a VOCABULARY …")

title: Antigravity loads only the first 24,000 bytes of the deployed global context
body:
# BUG-085: Antigravity loads only the first 24,000 bytes of the deployed global context

## Prevention
A deployed file that a vendor caps is pinned by a test that renders it from the real repo against the observed cap with a margin. Every smoke check asks one question answerable ONLY from the file's last section — never a question (like a skill count) the CLI can answer from its own internal listing, because that gives a false pass on a truncated file.

title: installer piped into `head` was killed by SIGPIPE, leaving files with no manifest
body:
# BUG-086: installer piped into `head` was killed by SIGPIPE, leaving files with no manifest

## Prevention
Never pipe a command that has side effects (install, update, report, a git write) into a filter that can exit before consuming its output (`head`, `grep -q`, `grep -m1`, `sed q`); run it bare, redirect its output to a file under `.agents/scratch/` if it must be shortened, and read that file. Recommend widening the existing `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules sentence "A verification command is never piped into a filter inside a `&&` chain that leads to a commit…" with one clause covering a side-effecting command piped into an early-exiting filter, rather than a new bullet — the rendered context is size-pinned at 22,000 bytes (ADR-035, `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock`).

Graduated to: `review-standards § 8 (code-shape rules; the reviewer's criterion, and golang/typescript/bash point at it)`

title: a behavioural-run fixture did not hold the condition its dispatch claimed, twice
body:
# BUG-087: a behavioural-run fixture did not hold the condition its dispatch claimed, twice

## Prevention
Before a behavioural run, prove the fixture's claimed state with the same command the agent will use (e.g. `git log -1 --format=%B | grep -c <line>` → 1), and choose the repository kind in which the changed rule can actually fire — a rule about the global context runs in a clone of the harness, not of a project.

Graduated to: `GUIDE-testing` § 4 § Behavioural runs + `fyr eval` (a `GUIDE-eval` row's setup asserts its fixture and a failed setup fails the row; the sandbox's `settings.json` is written for each row, `internal/eval/run.go` step 8) (the run kit's preamble until plan `PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-plan-fyr-eval-the-antigravity-run-kit-as-a-verb` Phase 3 deleted it)

title: cross-project survey findings landed in this repo's trail and issue lists
body:
# BUG-088: cross-project survey findings landed in this repo's trail and issue lists

## Prevention
A finding about another project is not recorded in this project's trail,
handoff Next Steps, or issue lists; a cross-project survey records only the
answer to the question it was run for. Before listing an issue, check which
repository it lives in.

Graduated to: `skills/research/SKILL.md` § Step 1: Discovery

title: changelog agent's date rule named a command it has no Bash to run
body:
# BUG-089: changelog agent's date rule named a command it has no Bash to run

## Prevention
An instruction in an agent or skill that names a command is checked against that agent's `tools:` list before it ships; an agent without Bash receives the command's output in its dispatch text instead of an instruction to run it.

title: changelog-agent behavioural fixture did not hold the state its dispatch claimed
body:
# BUG-090: changelog-agent behavioural fixture did not hold the state its dispatch claimed

## Prevention
A behavioural-run fixture is built to hold every fact its dispatch states, and the run script asserts each such fact (a grep for the line, a git log for the commit) before the CLI starts; a fixture fact with no assertion is not trusted.

Graduated to: `GUIDE-testing` § 4 § Behavioural runs + `fyr eval` (a `GUIDE-eval` row's setup asserts its fixture and a failed setup fails the row; the sandbox's `settings.json` is written for each row, `internal/eval/run.go` step 8) (the run kit's preamble until plan `PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-plan-fyr-eval-the-antigravity-run-kit-as-a-verb` Phase 3 deleted it)

title: first E2E 1 attempt invalid — headless agy auto-denied, control run couldn't isolate context
body:
# BUG-091: first E2E 1 attempt invalid — headless agy auto-denied, control run couldn't isolate context

## Prevention
A sandbox home for headless agy runs gets the real home's
`~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` (no credential in it) copied in beside the copied token; a run
that uses tools is checked for the "auto-denied" stderr line before its output is read. A control for a
context change runs in a project that does not contain the harness source, never in a clone of
styrman-harness.

Graduated to: `GUIDE-testing` § 4 § Behavioural runs + `fyr eval` (a `GUIDE-eval` row's setup asserts its fixture and a failed setup fails the row; the sandbox's `settings.json` is written for each row and an `auto-denied` line fails it, `internal/eval/run.go` steps 8 and 12) (the run kit's preamble until plan `PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-plan-fyr-eval-the-antigravity-run-kit-as-a-verb` Phase 3 deleted it)

title: behavioural probe's truncated fixture left `claude -p` running inside the harness checkout, one run wrote a fake change entry
body:
# BUG-092: behavioural probe's truncated fixture left `claude -p` running inside the harness checkout, one run wrote a fake change entry

## Prevention
A probe script never extracts shell code from another file with a line-range pattern (a `}` inside a heredoc ends the range early); shared fixture code lives in its own file and is sourced whole. Every `cd` into a fixture directory is `cd <dir> || exit 1`, preceded by the fixture assertion that the graduated `AGENTS.md` § Testing rule ("a behavioural or sandbox run proves its setup before its output counts") already requires.

title: a refused `--from-zip` still created `~/.config/sh-agent`
body:
# BUG-093: a refused `--from-zip` still created `~/.config/sh-agent`

## Prevention
A command that can refuse its input creates nothing before the refusal
point; its test for the refused case asserts the whole target is
unchanged (an empty home stays empty), not only that the obvious
temporary artifact is absent.

title: A red test run pushed a real report to the feedback repository
body:
# BUG-094: A red test run pushed a real report to the feedback repository

## Prevention
A test for a command with an outward-facing side effect (report, download, push, deploy) cuts that reach first — empty `PATH`, no reachable credentials — before the command can run, and above all when the test is written ahead of the refusal or guard it checks: the red run executes the real thing. `--home` pointing at scratch does not isolate credentials that live elsewhere (`~/.ssh`, `gh` auth).

title: retro-applied rule text contradicted its own neighbors twice; verify log counted refused calls as executed
body:
# BUG-095: retro-applied rule text contradicted its own neighbors twice; verify log counted refused calls as executed

## Prevention
Before inserting a rule from a retro proposal, grep the target file for the mechanism's key words and
read every hit, not just the insertion point. A rule that changes a gate updates every sentence in that
file that lists the gate, in the same edit. A behavioural or verify log's call count reads each tool
result's error/refusal flag and states executed and refused as separate numbers, never one combined
count.

title: `skills/retro/SKILL.md` cited `dream`'s step numbers wrong, twice
body:
# BUG-096: `skills/retro/SKILL.md` cited `dream`'s step numbers wrong, twice

## Prevention
Before writing a sentence that cites another file's numbered steps or sections, run `grep -n "^## Step"` (or the equivalent heading pattern) on the target file and keep it on screen while writing the citation; name what the step does, not only its number. This is a specific case of `review-standards` § 3 ("every other restatement of a changed rule is changed with it") — extend it, or the project `AGENTS.md`, to cover cross-file numeric citations specifically, since three records now share this shape (BUG-027, BUG-032, BUG-096 all involve stale/wrong restatements caught only by grepping the subject, not the old wording).

title: verifier grep needle didn't match the sentence it was checking
body:
# BUG-097: verifier grep needle didn't match the sentence it was checking

## Prevention
