title: two first opens of a new SQLite index or metrics store at once fail busy at once, past the 10 s busy timeout (TestConcurrentReconcile flake)
body:
owner: main

## Symptom
`TestConcurrentReconcile` (internal/search/open_test.go) failed intermittently: one of its two helper processes failed after 0.01 s with `search: index busy (another fyr is indexing); retry, or use grep`, well inside the 10 s busy timeout. Rates: about 1 in 9 serial runs of the package and 1 in 4 under parallel load (funclen Phase 4, 2026-10-27); 1 in 100 runs of the test alone under CPU load. Two real `fyr search` or `fyr index` runs started together on a checkout with no index yet would fail the same way.

## Repro
`go test -c ./internal/search/`, then run the binary with `-test.run '^TestConcurrentReconcile$' -test.count 100`, three copies at once beside twelve busy loops: 2 failures in 900 runs (`.agents/scratch/bug-busy/`). Deterministic: a connection holds `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on a new file that is not yet in WAL mode, and `openStore` on that path fails within 0.3 ms. That is `TestFirstOpenWaitsForALock` in internal/search/open_test.go, and the same test in internal/metrics/store_test.go for `metrics.Open`.

## Root cause
The first open of a new database switches it to WAL (`_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)` in `search.DSN`). SQLite does that switch by opening a read transaction and upgrading it to a write. When another connection holds a lock at that moment, SQLite answers the upgrade `SQLITE_BUSY` at once and never calls the busy handler, because waiting while holding a read lock could deadlock. So `busy_timeout(10000)` does not apply. `openStore` (internal/search/store.go) mapped that error straight to `errBusy`. The metrics store's `Open` returned it as `database is locked`. Instrumented runs showed the extended code was plain 5 (SQLITE_BUSY, not 517 BUSY_SNAPSHOT), from the first statement on a fresh connection, inside `openStore`'s first `tryOpen`. The brain store had the same exposure and was written with a retry loop for it (internal/brain/store.go:85-101, plan brain Phase 1), but the loop and its reason were never carried to the two older stores.

## Fix
- `internal/search/store.go`: `tryOpenWaiting` retries `tryOpen` while it fails busy, for up to the busy timeout, every 50 ms. `openStore` uses it at both of its opens.
- `internal/search/store.go`: `IsBusy` exports `isBusy` for the metrics store.
- `internal/metrics/store.go`: `Open` retries a new `open` (one attempt) the same way, for `openWait` (10 s).

The two SQLite stores outside `internal/brain` are the whole class: `git grep journal_mode` names only `search.DSN`, and the three stores open through it.

## Prevention
A SQLite store that opens through `search.DSN` (WAL) retries its whole open while it fails busy, for as long as the busy timeout. `busy_timeout` does not cover the first open's switch to WAL. A new store copies that loop, as brain, search and metrics now do, and gets a test that holds a write lock on a fresh, non-WAL file across its open.

## Diagnosis
The goldfish explorer ranked "pragma order in the DSN" first, as did my own hypothesis. The driver's source falsified it: modernc.org/sqlite runs `busy_timeout` first whatever the order. Its second candidate, BUSY_SNAPSHOT in `ensureSchema`, was falsified by the extended code, 5. The cause found, the WAL switch's lock upgrade, was in neither list.
Diagnosis missed: the WAL switch's lock upgrade at connection setup. The brief's "Investigate the codebase" read only this module. A line asking to check how the driver and SQLite apply the busy timeout to the failing statement would have led there, as would "look for the same failure handled elsewhere in the repo" (internal/brain/store.go:85-101 names it).

title: trail.Dirty is fooled by a tracked name opening with a double quote: hash-object --stdin-paths unquotes it and hashes another path (false clean, a read outside the checkout)
body:
owner: main

## Symptom
`trail.Dirty` (internal/trail/dirty.go) answered "clean" for a tree where `git status --porcelain` shows ` M "\"x\""`: a committed file whose name opens with `"` had been modified. It could also hash a file beside the repository, outside the checkout that the code's comments say `os.Root` confines it to. Its two callers rely on the answer: `fyr record import` refuses a tree with uncommitted changes (internal/brain/import.go:126), and `fyr eval` labels its install source `(dirty)` (cmd/fyr/eval.go:293). The same `hashesDiffer` serves `trail.Dates` (internal/trail/trail.go:118), which dates a project's trail files for the dream: a quoted name under the docs root could keep a modified record on its commit date. Found by the v3.1.0 release gate's security review, part B (`REVIEW-2026-10-27-1556-security-review-v3-1-0-gate-part-b-metrics-redac`), medium, high confidence. `trail.Dirty` came in with the 2026-10-27 audit fix (SD38, ce4f977) and was never in a release.

## Repro
A repository with `a` and `"a"` committed, both holding the same bytes. Modify `"a"`. `Dirty(root)` returns `false, nil`. That is `TestDirtyCannotAnswerQuotedName` in internal/trail/dirty_test.go. The security agent's probes are under `.agents/scratch/sec-B-probe/` (`repo`: false clean; `repo2`: a tracked file named `"../outside.txt"`, which git unquotes to `../outside.txt` and reads outside the checkout).

## Root cause
`hashesDiffer` feeds tracked names, one per line, to `git hash-object --no-filters --stdin-paths`. git reads a stdin line that opens with `"` as a C-quoted string and unquotes it, so `"a"` is hashed as `a`, and a name `"../outside.txt"` as `../outside.txt`, outside the tree. The guard refused only `\n` and `\r`. The same class was found and closed in `internal/search` by an earlier security review: `git_view.go:193-196` hashes a file's own bytes and never calls `--stdin-paths`. The rule was not carried to `trail.Dirty` when it was written.

## Fix
`internal/trail/dirty.go`, `hashesDiffer`: a path that opens with `"` is refused with `errUnhashable`, as a newline or CR already was, so `Dirty` says it cannot answer instead of guessing. Every caller already handles the error safely: `record import` refuses with "checking for uncommitted changes: …", `eval` labels the source `(dirty: unknown, …)`, and `trail.Dates` treats every record as modified, keeping its mtime. `errUnhashable`'s text names the new case.

Class check: `git grep -e '--stdin' -e 'stdin-paths' -e 'cmd.Stdin = '` over the non-test Go code finds two other git calls fed on stdin. `internal/check/docs.go:262` runs `check-ignore -z --stdin`, NUL-separated, which does no unquoting. `internal/search/git_view.go` hashes in Go. `hashesDiffer`, shared by `trail.Dirty` and `trail.Dates`, was the only site.

## Prevention
Never pass a path to git on a line-oriented stdin (`--stdin-paths`, `--stdin` without `-z`): git C-unquotes a line that opens with `"` and strips a trailing CR, so the name git acts on can differ from the one meant. Use `-z` where the command has it; otherwise hash or read the file in Go through `os.Root` (as `internal/search/git_view.go` does), or refuse such a name and say the answer is unknown.

## Diagnosis
The location was given by the security agent's reproduced probe, so Step 2's explorer dispatch was skipped as mechanically obvious. My hypothesis matched the probe: `--stdin-paths` unquoting.

title: fyr install's directory-in-the-way refusal names no alternative, and the real run fails with a bare rename error
body:
owner: main

## Symptom
`fyr install --dry-run` into a home where a directory sits at a managed file's path refused with `writing …: a directory is in the way; the install cannot replace it`, naming the cause but no alternative. The real `fyr install` into the same home failed with a bare `writing …: rename …/.fyr-NNN …: file exists`. GUIDE-testing § 3c passes a refused cell only when its message names both the cause and the alternative. Found by the v3.1.0 gate's § 3c matrix run (`TEST-2026-10-27-1619-verification-v3-1-0-gate-3c-matrix-v3-0-0-31de61`), FAIL. The dry-run refusal came in with the 2026-10-27 audit fix (IN41, 5f2b941) and was never in a release. The real run's bare rename error is older: a v3.0.0 build gives the same.

## Repro
`mkdir -p <home>/.gemini/config/rules/AGENTS.md`, then `fyr install --dry-run --home <home>` and `fyr install --home <home>` (the matrix's cell). In a test: `TestDryRunRefusesADirectoryAtAFilePath` (internal/harness/dryrun_dir_test.go), which now also requires the cause, "move or remove it" and "fyr install" in both runs' errors.

## Root cause
`dirInTheWay` (internal/harness/apply_guard.go) was written as the dry run's copy of the real write's failure (IN41). Its message carried only the cause, and the real run never called it: it reached `WriteAtomic`, whose rename error names neither the cause in words nor a way out.

## Fix
- `internal/harness/apply_guard.go`: the message ends `: move or remove it, then run fyr install again`.
- `internal/harness/apply_steps.go`, `installRun.write`: both runs call `dirInTheWay` before writing. The real run returns through `saveOnError`, as a failed write already did, so the files written before it stay in the manifest.

## Prevention
A refusal names the cause and the alternative, and a dry run's guard is the real run's guard: one function that both runs call before acting, never a dry-run copy of an error the real run meets later (review-standards § 8). The matrix (GUIDE-testing § 3c) checks the message's two halves.

## Diagnosis
The location was named by the matrix cell and the guard's own comment, so Step 2's explorer dispatch was skipped. Not fixed here: the real install still writes the files before the one in the way (nine in the matrix's home) before it stops. `saveOnError` records them, so `status` and a later install see them, and the behaviour is unchanged since v3.0.0.

title: the release gate's verifier opened the operator's live Antigravity conversation_summaries.db instead of a copy (copies-only rule, GUIDE-testing § 3g)
body:
owner: main

## Symptom
During the `/preflight v3.1.0` gate, the first `verifier` run (`TEST-2026-10-27-1619-verification-v3-1-0-gate-v1-v3-0-0-31de61a-fail`, § 3g and the audit-fix E2E 2 setup) opened the operator's LIVE `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversation_summaries.db` with Python's `sqlite3`. Its log says: "(I also read the live conversation_summaries.db once with python sqlite3, read-only, before building the E2E fixture: a read of the real home, no write.)" GUIDE-testing § 3g allows real data from copies only, and the dispatch said so in capitals ("a real-data check from COPIES only"). `sqlite3.connect` opens read-write, so "read-only" is the agent's claim, not a mode it set. Found by the gate's security read of its own records (`REVIEW-2026-10-27-1809-security-review-v3-1-0-gate-trail-records-31de61`, low, medium confidence).

## What was checked afterwards
The database's mtime is still 2026-10-26 21:53:22, and there is no `-wal`, `-shm` or `-journal` beside it, so the file itself was not written. The directory `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli` has an mtime of 2026-10-27 16:11:35, within the verifier's run, so an entry was added, removed or renamed then. The cause is not determined: Antigravity rewriting its token by rename is one candidate. The token's own mtime is 17:21, from the eval run's refresh through its link.

## Root cause
The verifier's definition (agents/verifier/agent.md) has no rule against opening the operator's real Antigravity or fyr data. The copies-only rule lives in GUIDE-testing § 3g and the dispatch, and the agent read the live file to learn the table's schema before it built a fixture.

## Fix
None in this change. The record is written so the rule is known. The graduation below changes an agent definition, which owes `GUIDE-eval` rows and a review, so it is left to `PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-cleanup`.

## Prevention
An agent never opens a file under the operator's real `~/.gemini/` or `~/.config/fyr/` in place, read-only or not. It copies the file into `.agents/scratch/` first (`cp -p`), reads the copy, and deletes the copy by name. A schema is learned from a copy, or from the code that reads it. Graduation target: a sentence in `agents/verifier/agent.md` (and `security`, which also probes), with an `inject`/`lane` row in `GUIDE-eval`.

## Graduated
2026-10-28, ledger Phase 6 (item 17): the prevention rule is the "Copies only (BUG-190)" bullet under § Records in `agents/verifier/agent.md` and `agents/security/agent.md`, with two carve-outs the rule above did not state: the installed harness text under `~/.gemini/config/` (both agents read `init-project/references/trail.md` there) and the `fyr` verbs each definition names (which open `~/.config/fyr/brain.db` as its own reader). Behavioural runs on that text: `TEST-2026-10-28-1127-eval-2-of-2-pass-at-bfb4329` (`agent-verifier`, `agents-security`). The proving `GUIDE-eval` row stays deferred (ledger item 18).

title: the v3.1.0 gate added GUIDE-eval's smoke row without TestSuiteHarness's want entry and committed it without go test (BUG-183 again)
body:
owner: main

## Symptom
At 8bfd2bc on `main` (committed, not pushed), `go test ./internal/eval` fails: `TestSuiteHarness`: `suite_test.go:171: 61 rows, want 60`. The v3.1.0 gate added the `smoke` row to `GUIDE-eval` and committed it without running `go test`. The main agent caught it before the verifier's test step reached the package: the verifier was stopped, and its partial run is in `.agents/scratch/v310-v1c/`.

## Repro
At 8bfd2bc: `go test -count=1 -run TestSuiteHarness ./internal/eval`.

## Root cause
The same as BUG-183. The row's check was validated by hand, in must-pass and must-fail states, against a kept eval sandbox and a fake store. A record edit felt like data, so `go test` did not run before the commit. `TestSuiteHarness` pins every row by id, agent and grant. BUG-183's prevention rule is a sentence in that bug record and nowhere a session reads before editing `GUIDE-eval`, so it did not fire.

## Fix
`internal/eval/suite_test.go`: `want` holds `"smoke": {"", false}`, and `TestSuiteHarness` passes. Without the entry it fails with "61 rows, want 60" (checked with `git stash`). Landed before 8bfd2bc was pushed.

## Prevention
The rule is BUG-183's: a `GUIDE-eval` row is added together with its `want` entry, and the commit runs `go test ./internal/eval` first. It has now recurred, so it graduates into a mechanism, filed as a PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-cleanup Follow-up. Candidates: `fyr record edit GUIDE-eval` (or any edit of a record a Go test reads) prints the test to run, or the note in GUIDE-eval § Columns names `TestSuiteHarness`. This record's status becomes `graduated` when one lands.

## Graduated
2026-10-28, ledger Phase 6 (item 20, D5): `AGENTS.md` § Testing now says a `GUIDE-eval` edit is a test change: `TestSuiteHarness` (`internal/eval/suite_test.go`) pins every row by id, agent and grant, so a row added or changed changes its `want` entry in the same commit, and `go test ./internal/eval` runs before that commit. `TestSuiteHarness` is the mechanism; the AGENTS.md line makes running it the rule a session reads before editing the suite.

title: the ledger Phase 7a checkpoint commit was pushed with a Claude-Session trailer (BUG-177 again, on a checkpoint push)
body:
# BUG-192: the ledger Phase 7a checkpoint commit was pushed with a `Claude-Session:` trailer (BUG-177 again, on a checkpoint push)

## Symptom
97cf077 ("Ledger Phase 7a: Slack handling removed from the redactor (D32 1)") is on `origin/main` with a `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_…` line. The context's § Git forbids it: "no session links … and not the trailer a CLI's own reminder asks for". The commit before it, 296cc0d, carries none. Published history is never rewritten, so the trailer stays.

## Repro
`git log -1 --format=%B 97cf077`.

## Root cause
The main agent wrote the message from the CLI's attribution reminder instead of from § Git, as BUG-177 did. BUG-177's mechanism, `skills/handoff/scripts/check-trailers.sh`, runs only before the handoff skill's push (Step 6) and preflight's (Step 6.4). A plan phase's checkpoint commits and pushes at step 10 before the handoff is written, and that push runs no check. The script reads `@{u}..HEAD`, so once the handoff runs, an already-pushed commit is never seen.

## Fix
None possible for 97cf077 without a force-push, which the context forbids. The handoff commit of this session was checked with `check-trailers.sh` before its push.

## Prevention
Every push runs `check-trailers.sh` first, not only the handoff and preflight pushes. Two candidates: § Git in `context/AGENTS.md` names the script ("before any push, run the handoff skill's `check-trailers.sh`"), or the checkpoint step of the feature skill and the plan template names it before its push. Either one is a harness change for the operator to approve. The first landed in ledger Phase 9 (§ Graduated).

## Graduated
2026-10-28, ledger Phase 9 (D33 2): `context/AGENTS.md` § Git now says "Before any push, run the handoff skill's `check-trailers.sh`.", after the trailer rule, so every push a session makes, a plan phase's checkpoint push included, runs the script first, not only the handoff's and preflight's. `skills/handoff/scripts/check-trailers.sh` is the mechanism; the context line makes running it the rule every session reads. Inside both size pins (`TestRenderedContextUnderTarget`: 14,876 of 15,000 bytes).

title: fyr check failed at the ledger's closing head with five findings the Done called pre-existing
body:
# BUG-193: `fyr check` failed at the ledger's closing head with five findings the Done called pre-existing

## Symptom
At 93da61e, `go run ./cmd/fyr check --home .agents/scratch/home-trail` exited 1: `check: 5 findings (docs 5, specs 0, requirements 0)`, each `` path `.agents/docs`: .agents/docs does not exist `` on `SPEC-fyr-search:26`, `:37` and `GUIDE-fyr-matrix:50` (twice), `:51`. `GUIDE-testing` § 3h says "Before a completion claim, `fyr check` here exits 0". The ledger Done's handoff (`HANDOFF-2026-10-28-1942-…`) said: "Five `.agents/docs` path hits remain; they are true by design and predate this range". They do not predate it. None of the five lines is in v3.1.0's `.agents/trail.jsonl`; the range v3.1.0..93da61e added each of them (the `index --register` bullet and the registration sentence in `SPEC-fyr-search`, and the `index --register` and `search --global zip` rows in `GUIDE-fyr-matrix`). The v4.0.0 gate's docs-lens review found it (`reviewer-2026-10-28-2003`, its first finding).

## Repro
`git show 93da61e:.agents/trail.jsonl` into a scratch file. Then `fyr check` at 93da61e, then grep the five lines' text in `git show v3.1.0:.agents/trail.jsonl`: 0 hits.

## Root cause
The Done labelled the hits "pre-existing" without comparing them with the base's records. The Done's verifier dispatch (`TEST-2026-10-28-1940-…`) did not name § 3h, and § 3h was owed: the range changed `cmd/fyr/ctx_verbs.go`, the check's vocabulary. So no log showed `fyr check` at the head.

## Fix
In the v4.0.0 gate, before its verifier ran, each path was reworded as another checkout's: `<project>/.agents/docs`, or `<clone>/.agents/docs` (`SPEC-fyr-check` § Rule (a)). `fyr check` then printed `check: 0 findings`.

## Prevention
A `fyr check` hit is called pre-existing only when the base's text shows the same line (`git show <base>:.agents/trail.jsonl`, or the file at `<base>`). Otherwise it is the range's, and it is fixed before the completion claim. A verifier dispatch over a range that touches § 3h's paths names § 3h.

## Graduated
2026-10-28, into `GUIDE-testing` § 3h, its bullet "A hit is pre-existing only when the base shows it": both halves of the rule above, the base comparison and the verifier dispatch naming § 3h.

title: fyr check showed 0 findings on the tree before 5baf159 and 2 at the committed head
body:
# BUG-194: `fyr check` showed 0 findings on the tree before 5baf159 and 2 at the committed head

## Symptom
At 905a18a, `fyr check --home .agents/scratch/home-trail` exited 1: `check: 2 findings (docs 0, specs 2, requirements 0)`. The two findings were `SPEC-fyr-check  spec-stale  1 commit to … cmd/fyr … since 03ce1d470059` and `SPEC-fyr-eval  spec-stale  1 commit to cmd/fyr/eval.go internal/eval cmd/fyr since 03ce1d470059`. The previous session's handoff (`HANDOFF-2026-10-28-2154-…`) and its log (`TEST-2026-10-28-2152-…`) both said `fyr check: 0 findings`. The kickoff's Done needs 0. This session's resume found the gap before it changed anything.

## Repro
`git checkout 905a18a`, then `go run ./cmd/fyr check --home .agents/scratch/home-trail`: 2 findings. At 4b416e8, with 5baf159's `cmd/fyr/eval_home.go` edit left uncommitted in the tree: 0 findings. That second run is the state `TEST-2026-10-28-2152-…` logged ("HEAD 4b416e8; ` M cmd/fyr/eval_home.go`").

## Root cause
Rule (b) counts commits: `git rev-list --count <spec commit>..HEAD` over the spec's code (`SPEC-fyr-check` § Rule (b)). An uncommitted edit to that code is not a commit yet, so the check before the commit could not see it. 5baf159 then committed a comment-only change under `cmd/fyr`, which is code to both specs. That commit made both specs stale. Nobody ran `fyr check` again after the commit, and the handoff restated the pre-commit result.

## Fix
2026-10-28: both diffs re-read. 5baf159 changes only `evalHomeRefused`'s doc comment, and neither spec describes that comment. Both specs were then re-stamped with an identical body (`fyr record edit <ID> --body`), which moved only their `updated` field. The run after the commit is recorded under § Verified.

## Prevention
A range that changes code under a current spec's code paths runs `fyr check` once more after its commit and before the handoff claims 0. A spec-stale hit at that point is cleared in the same Task: re-read the spec against the diff, then re-stamp it or fix it. A `fyr check` result from an uncommitted tree is never cited as the result at the head.

## Verified
2026-10-28, at c016f1a (clean tree, after the commit): `fyr check --home .agents/scratch/home-trail` printed `check: 0 findings (docs 0, specs 0, requirements 0)` and exited 0. Its one note was `REQUIREMENTS.md has no enforced-by field: not checked`.

## Graduated
2026-10-29: the prevention rule is now `GUIDE-testing` § 3h, bullet "Run it again after the commit (BUG-194)".

title: 4b0f9a4 was pushed with a Claude-Session trailer (BUG-177/192 again, from a Claude Code session whose context predates BUG-192's graduation)
body:
# BUG-195: 4b0f9a4 was pushed with a `Claude-Session:` trailer (BUG-177 and BUG-192 again, from a Claude Code session whose context predates BUG-192's graduation)

## Symptom
4b0f9a4 ("GUIDE-skill-matrix: the four .agents/memory rows retired …") is on `origin/main` with a `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_…` line. The context's § Git forbids it: "no session links … and not the trailer a CLI's own reminder asks for". Published history is never rewritten, so the trailer stays.

## Repro
`git log -1 --format=%B 4b0f9a4`.

## Root cause
The session ran in Claude Code, which read `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` (mtime 2026-10-27 10:56). That copy predates ledger Phase 9 (2026-10-28), which graduated BUG-192 by adding "Before any push, run the handoff skill's `check-trailers.sh`." to `context/AGENTS.md:49`. `grep -c check-trailers ~/.claude/AGENTS.md` prints 0. `fyr install` deploys to the Antigravity CLI, not to `~/.claude`, so nothing refreshed that copy. The main agent followed the CLI's attribution reminder, and no check ran before the push.

## Fix
None possible for 4b0f9a4 without a force-push, which the context forbids. This session's handoff commit carries no trailer, and `check-trailers.sh` was run before its push.

## Prevention
A session's context must be the current `context/AGENTS.md`, whichever CLI reads it. The operator either refreshes `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` from the current render, or stops running harness sessions from Claude Code. Either is outside this repository, so it is an operator step (handoff Next Steps). Until then, a Claude Code session runs `skills/handoff/scripts/check-trailers.sh` before every push.

title: internal/serve TestRefusals/wrong token fails about once in 64 runs (its wrong token equals the real one when that starts with x)
body:
# BUG-196: `internal/serve` `TestRefusals/wrong token` fails about once in 64 runs

## Symptom
The Phase 4 verifier's full run (`TEST` record of workers Phase 4, 2026-10-29) failed one test outside the change: `internal/serve` `TestRefusals`, subtest "wrong token", got 303 where it wanted 403. It passed alone and in 30 of 30 repeats.

## Repro
Run `go test -count=200 -run 'TestRefusals' ./internal/serve`; a few runs fail. Deterministic form: any token whose first character is `x`.

## Root cause
`internal/serve/guard_test.go:80` builds the wrong token as `"x"+r.Token()[1:]`. The token is 32 bytes from `crypto/rand` in base64url (`internal/serve/serve.go:100`), so its first character is `x` one time in 64. Then the "wrong" token is the real one, the guard accepts it, and the redirect (303) is right. The product is correct; the test's negative case is not always negative.

## Fix
`internal/serve/guard_test.go`: the new helper `wrongToken` (`:142`) changes the first character to `a`, or to `b` when it is already `a`, so the wrong token always differs from the real one. `TestRefusals` (`:51`) asserts the two differ before it sends the request. `TestWrongTokenIsWrong` (`:125`) forces the real token to start with `x`, `a` and `b` and wants 403 for each. With the helper still written as `"x"+tok[1:]`, it failed on `x` before the fix. The class is one site: `git grep` over `*_test.go` found no other wrong value derived from a right one (the `"x"` literal at `:87` cannot equal a 43-character token). Fixed 2026-10-30 in the commit that carries this record. Reviewed in `REVIEW-2026-10-30-0530-review-bug-196-the-wrong-token-in-internal-serve`, verified in `TEST-2026-10-30-0537-verification-bug-196-the-wrong-token-in-internal`. No explorer diagnosis was run: the location was mechanically obvious from the record.

## Prevention
A negative test that derives its wrong value from the right one asserts they differ before it uses it.

title: The merge=union line duplicates trail records when two parallel workers' records sort around one existing line
body:
# The `merge=union` line duplicates trail records when two workers' records sort around one existing line

## Symptom
Phase 6 of `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers`, the E2E on dave (2026-10-30): wave 1 ran `p1` (greet) and `p2` (count) at once, both PASS. The lead squash-merged `p1`; the squash of `p2` then failed `fyr record list` with `trail.jsonl line 5: duplicate ID GUIDE-2026-10-29-2010-the-fixture (first at line 2)`. The lead undid it (`git reset --hard HEAD`) and re-ran the phase as `-r2`, which merged. The golden path's "both branches are squash-merged" was a no on the first attempt.

## Repro
From the fixture's branches (`~/sandbox/fyr-work/fixture`): base `3e3273e`, ours `5fd70c3` (p1 merged), theirs `work/plan-greet-count-cli-wiring-and-count-p2`. `git merge-file --union ours base theirs` on `.agents/trail.jsonl` gives 8 lines with `GUIDE-2026-10-29-2010-the-fixture` twice (`.agents/scratch/phase6/dup/` in the harness checkout holds the four files, not committed).

## Root cause
`fyr record` rewrites the whole export sorted by ID (`internal/brain/export.go:294`). Both workers added a `CHANGE-…` record (sorts before `GUIDE-…`) and a `HANDOFF-…` record (sorts after it), so each side's diff is one hunk spanning the unchanged `GUIDE` line. Union keeps both sides of an overlapping hunk whole, so the unchanged line comes out twice, and the read refuses a duplicate ID (`internal/brain/export.go:228`). Any two parallel workers whose new records sort on both sides of a common existing line collide; with every worker adding a CHANGE and a HANDOFF record, any record of a kind between them (DEPLOY, FEEDBACK, GUIDE) triggers it. ADR-077 and D73 chose `merge=union` (in `c3cc1a8`, the `work` skill's loop step 1, and this repo's `.gitattributes`) on the assumption that union of two appends is clean; a sorted full rewrite is not an append.

## Fix
Chosen by the operator, 2026-10-30 (`PLAN-2026-10-29-workers` D99): candidate (a). The rejected candidates: the lead merges a worker's records through `fyr record` instead of git; the export keeps the existing order and appends new IDs.

Built 2026-10-30, at both readers of the file (the class: every `trail.jsonl` parse that refuses a second line of one ID):
- `internal/brain/export.go` `readRecords` (the load, `ReadTrail`, `ParseTrail`): a second line of an ID whose bytes, line ending trimmed, hash the same as the first is skipped; one that differs is refused as before (`line N: duplicate ID X (first at line M)`). The load stores the deduplicated rows, so the next export, written from the store, has the line once.
- `internal/work/records.go` `parseTrail` (the lead's read of a base and a worker branch): the same rule by `bytes.Equal`, so a base that holds an unexported union squash does not fail `no handoff`.

Tests: `internal/brain/union_test.go` `TestUnionMergeOfSortedExports` (the repro through the real generator: two branches from one GUIDE line, each `fyr record add`s a change and a handoff, `.gitattributes` `merge=union`, `git merge --squash`; the merged file holds the GUIDE line twice, `List` gives 5 records, the next `Add` exports it once) and `TestDuplicateLines` (a CRLF first copy and a last copy with no final newline included); `internal/work/records_test.go` `TestParseTrail`'s byte-identical case (a CRLF first copy included) and `TestTrailAtFailsClosed` (a commit whose trail holds its line twice, read through `git cat-file`). Each fails without its fix (mutation runs, files restored and compared). Three cases that fed a byte-identical pair to pin the refusal now feed a pair that differs (`TestLoadRefusals`, brain `TestParseTrail`, work `TestParseTrail`).

Not covered: the dropped copy stays in the file until the next `fyr record` write; a read alone (`list`, `get`, `check`) does not rewrite it. In the lead's loop the squash commit (the `work` skill's step 7.4) keeps it, and step 8's `fyr record edit <PLAN-ID>` drops it before step 10's push (review finding 1, rebutted with this sentence, not a skill change). Two branches that edit the same record still give two different lines and are still refused, as D17 and the plan's Edge cases expect.

## Prevention
A merge strategy chosen for a generated file is tested against that file's real generator on two divergent branches, never against hand-written appends.

title: The work lead committed to its checkout during a fyr work run, then reset to a named commit outside its approvals
body:
# The lead committed to its checkout while a `fyr work` run was going, then undid it with a reset outside its approvals

## Symptom
Phase 6 of `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers`, the E2E on dave (2026-10-30), lead session `b9bd8eda` (agy 1.4.11). The fixture's reflog: `fyr work` for `p3` started at 09:36:51 (stamp `2026-10-30-093651-680063`); at 09:37:48 the lead committed `0379041` "record D5 for p3", before the worker had asked anything (its gate-question handoff is `6cf90db`, 09:39:13); at 09:38:16 it ran `git reset` to `b5eef37`; after the run it recommitted D5 as `f7bb2ba` (09:40:08) and dispatched `-r2`. The run was not failed, because HEAD was back at its base before the verb's lead-checkout check.

## Repro
`git -C ~/sandbox/fyr-work/fixture reflog --date=format:%T`; the step outputs under `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/b9bd8eda-2883-48e8-bc99-533efa3b6458/.system_generated/steps/` (step 151 holds the p3 run).

## Root cause
The `work` skill's step 6 says no commit, no edit to a tracked file and no `fyr` write while a run is going, and its standing approvals allow `git reset --hard HEAD` only after a failed squash on a clean tree. The lead anticipated the cli worker's flag question, wrote the answer during the run, then noticed and reverted. The skill's text was present; nothing in the loop stops a write mid-run (the lead waits through agy timers, so it gets turns while the run goes).

## Fix
2026-10-31, `PLAN.md` P4 item 12 (the operator chose the verb's guard, 2026-10-31; ADR-083). `fyr work` records the newest reflog entry of the lead's HEAD and of the branch it points to with the base (`internal/work/reflog.go`, refusal 23 refuses a checkout that keeps either empty), and step 6 fails every worker `lead checkout changed` when either entry is no longer the newest (the branch's catches the same moves made from another worktree), naming how many entries the run added and the first of them, so a commit undone by a reset during the run is caught though HEAD is back at the base. `TestRunLeadReflogMoved` replays this bug (a commit, then `git reset --hard HEAD~1`, from inside the session) and failed before the fix; `TestRunLeadNoReflog` pins refusal 23. The `work` skill's step 6 is unchanged: its claim that a commit fails every worker is now true of an undone one too.

## Prevention
The verb's reflog guard (above). Before it: a lead that waits for a run through timers rather than one blocking call re-reads step 6 on every wake: between runs only.

## Rerun evidence (2026-10-30, D99, D100)
Phase 6 box 2's rerun on dave, lead agy `c9a06951`, the same `work` skill text: no recurrence. The fixture's reflog from 11:11 to 11:46 holds no reset. A 30-second watcher of HEAD, the newest reflog entry and tracked changes shows none of them moving inside the four `fyr work` runs, and the lead's flag answer D9 was committed at 11:33:49, after p3's run ended at 11:32:36 (`TEST-2026-10-30-1147-e2e-workers-phase-6-box-2-rerun-the-lead-loop-on`). One occurrence in two runs. A commit or reset between two polls would still be in the reflog, which has none; an uncommitted edit undone within 30 seconds would not be seen. The fix is still the operator's question.

title: A background test run reported as passed from the notification's exit code, which was the trailing echo's
body:
# A background test run reported as passed from the notification's exit code, which was the trailing `echo`'s

## Symptom
Workers Phase 7b-2, 2026-10-30, on dave. The full test command ran in the background as `( gofmt … && go vet ./... && go test -race … ./... ) > log 2>&1; echo "exit=$?" >> log`. The completion notice said exit code 0, and the main thread told the operator "The full test command passed for 7b-2 (exit 0, own call)". The log's last line was `exit=1`: `TestFunctionLength` in the root package had failed (`internal/work/work.go:Run is 52 lines, over 50`). The reviewer found the failure; nothing was committed with it.

## Repro
`(false) > x.log 2>&1; echo "exit=$?" >> x.log`, run in the background: the command's status is the `echo`'s (0), while `x.log` ends `exit=1`.

## Root cause
The background command's status is its last command's, the `echo`. The main thread read that status, not the `exit=` line it had written to the log for this purpose. The same reading was used for 7a and 7b-1, and their logs, checked afterwards, end `exit=0`: those claims held by luck, not by check.

## Fix
Every later claim reads the log's `exit=` line (`tail -1 <log>`) before reporting. The 7b-2 failure is fixed: the sweep moved out of `Run` into `Options.sweepRun`.

## Prevention
A test run's verdict comes from the line it wrote for that purpose, read before the claim, never from the status of a wrapper that ends with `echo`. Better: no trailing `echo`, so the background status is the test's own.

title: fyr work's scope check let a worker's symlink or gitlink through to the lead's squash
body:
# `fyr work`'s scope check let a worker's symlink or gitlink through to the lead's squash

## Symptom
The v5.0.0 gate's security review (finding 3: medium, confidence medium) read `internal/work/fetch.go`'s scope check. It checks the paths a worker's branch changed against the Kickoff's `Files:` line, and never their modes. A worker could commit a symlink (mode 120000) or a gitlink (160000) at a path its `Files:` line covers, and the worker passed. The `work` skill's lead squash-merges a PASS and pushes it. A symlink in the lead's tree pointing at `~/.ssh/` or `~/.config/gcloud/` would then let later builds, tools and agents read or write outside the checkout through an ordinary-looking path. It reached commits from workers Phase 2 (`internal/work`) through `5b716dd`. No run is known to have hit it.

## Repro
`internal/work/run_test.go` `TestRunLinks`: the rig's fake worker commits `src/link` as a symlink to `/etc/passwd`, as one to `a.txt`, or as a gitlink, under a Kickoff whose `Files:` is `src/a.txt, src/link`. Before the fix, each case passed.

## Root cause
`changedPaths` runs `git diff-tree --name-only`, which drops the mode. A scope check written as "which paths" never asked "what kind of entry".

## Fix
`internal/work/fetch.go`: `links` runs `git diff-tree -r -z --no-renames base ref` in raw form. `scope` fails the worker `changed outside its Files`, with the note `a symlink or submodule on the branch, whatever its Files: <paths>`, when the tip holds a 120000 or 160000 entry the base did not hold as the same. It also fails when that read errors. A Kickoff cannot allow a link: the fix is a refusal, not an option. Round 2 of the security review found that a `.gitmodules` entry with `ignore = all` in the lead hid a gitlink from both `diff-tree` calls (reproduced with git 2.47.3). Both now pass `--ignore-submodules=none`, and `TestRunLinks/gitlink-ignored` is red without it.

Test: `TestRunLinks` (a regular file at the same path is the control). It is red with the check removed (`return` before `links`) and with the gitlink mode dropped from the match (the `gitlink` case), with the file restored afterwards.

## Prevention
A check of what a worker may change checks the kind of entry (its mode) as well as its path.

title: Two kill tests reached the machine's real docker daemon
body:
# Two kill tests reached the machine's real docker daemon

## Symptom
The v5.0.0 gate's security reviews of the test files (part B finding 1: medium, confidence high; part A finding 1: low) found two tests that ran the real docker CLI against the operator's daemon on any machine with `docker` on PATH. `internal/work/slots_test.go` `TestKillRefusals` (the stale case) and `cmd/fyr/verb_work_test.go` `TestWorkVerbKill` (the second `--kill`) both reach `Kill`'s sweep of a stale run (`internal/work/slots.go:289`). That sweep runs `docker context inspect`, `docker ps -a --filter label=fyr.work=<stamp>` and `docker rm -f` on any match. The label holds the test process's pid, so removing a real container was unlikely. But a unit test asked the real daemon, and its assertion passed whether docker was asked or not. It reached commits from workers Phase 7b-2 through `5b716dd`, and every full test run on dave since.

## Repro
Each test with the rig as it was: a fake docker absent from PATH, so `exec.LookPath("docker")` found `/usr/bin/docker`. The control written for the fix shows it: with the fake removed from PATH, the new assertion reports `the stale sweep did not reach the fake docker: ""`.

## Root cause
The two rigs put a fake `agy` and a fake `fyr` on PATH, but not a fake for the third CLI the code under test may call. Docker mode came after the rigs were written, and the kill path reaches docker even on a host run.

## Fix
- `internal/work/slots_test.go` `TestKillRefusals` takes `dockerRig`'s recording fake docker, and asserts that the stale sweep reached it.
- `cmd/fyr/verb_work_test.go` `newWorkRig` puts a recording fake docker first on PATH, with `DOCKER_HOST` and `DOCKER_CONTEXT` cleared. `TestWorkVerbKill` asserts the stale sweep reached it.

Both assertions are red with the fake off PATH, files restored afterwards.

## Prevention
A test rig puts a recording fake first on PATH for every external CLI the code under test may call, including through a path the test does not aim at, and asserts that the fake was the one asked.

title: The docs promised that a fyr work worker's data reaches only the model
body:
# The docs promised that a `fyr work` worker's data reaches only the model

## Symptom
The v5.0.0 gate's security review (finding 4: medium, confidence high) found the isolation claim overstated in three places:
- `README.md:76`: "whose clone has no remote, so nothing it holds goes anywhere but to that model".
- `SDD.md:152`: "whose clone has no remote".
- `cmd/fyr/help_text.go:44` and `cmd/fyr/main.go:21`: "sandboxed agy workers".

`SPEC-fyr-work` § Purpose and `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § What stays on the machine said the same. A worker's agent runs with `command(*)` (`internal/work/worker.go:16`) and the network. On `--runner host` it is the operator's uid, outside the clone too, so removing the git remote stops `git push` and nothing else. The design accepts this (D20, D45, `GUIDE-testing` § 4). The docs stated a guarantee the code does not give. It reached the README and the help page from workers Phase 3 through `5b716dd`.

## Repro
Read `internal/work/worker.go:16`'s grants beside `README.md:76` at `5b716dd`.

## Root cause
"The clone has no remote" was written about what git can reach, and read on as a statement about what the agent can reach.

## Fix
- README:76 and SDD:152 say that fyr sends nothing else, that the agent has `command(*)` and the network, and that `--runner docker` keeps it off the operator's files, not off the network.
- The help line and `main.go`'s doc comment say "isolated only with --runner docker".
- `SPEC-fyr-work` and `SPEC-fyr-delivery` say the same.

Docs only. No test pins the old wording (`TestHarnessMap` and the help tests pass on the new).

## Prevention
A sentence about what a sandboxed agent cannot do names the mechanism that stops it, and is checked against the grants the code gives that agent.

title: A development build at a zip place could neither report nor update it (borken's deadlock)
body:
# A development build at a zip place could neither report nor update it (borken's deadlock)

owner: main

## Symptom
On borken (2026-10-31, quoted by the operator), `fyr version` printed `b9cae29346b2`, a development build. `fyr update --from-zip ~/Downloads/fyr-v5.0.0.zip` exited 0 ("installing its harness and the running binary b9cae29346b2 … nothing in the zip replaces the binary"), and the version did not move. From then on `fyr status` and `fyr update` both exited 1: "this home was installed from a zip … harness repo not found and this build is b9cae29346b2, a development build". The place was deadlocked: the one verb that still worked, `update --from-zip`, was the one that could not move the binary.

## Repro
A development build: `fyr install --repo <checkout> --home H`, then `fyr update --from-zip <a release zip> --home H`, then `fyr status --home H` and `fyr update --home H`, run outside the checkout. Pinned by `TestPlaceMatrix` (`cmd/fyr/place_matrix_test.go`): before the fix, 8 cells failed (the development build at a zip place, and its `--from-zip` at a checkout and a binary-only place), and every release cell passed on the old code.

## Root cause
Three gaps met.
- `status` and `update` are `source: true` verbs: `run` resolves the harness before either can reach its own zip branch (`zipDrift`).
- A development build resolves only a tree. A zip install records `zip:sha256:…` in place of the checkout's path, so outside a checkout nothing resolves (`harness.ResolveSource`, `sourceCandidates`).
- `update --from-zip` by a development build at a checkout place was allowed, and it turned the place into a zip place. The not-found error's zip note then advised "run `fyr update --from-zip <file>` again", which keeps the same build and the same place.

ADR-038's last consequence described that error as the design. No test crossed the binary kinds with the place kinds: every zip test ran a release binary.

## Fix
ADR-082. The fix:
- `cmd/fyr/zip_place.go`:
  - `zipPlaceWithoutSource` (line 16) is called from `resolveSource` (`cmd/fyr/run_dispatch.go`) when the source does not resolve. At a zip place, `status` reports from the manifest (`statusWithoutSource`, line 38). `update` is refused with exit 1, naming a newer release zip run with its release binary, and `fyr install --repo <checkout>`.
  - `refuseDevelZipOverPath` (line 53) refuses a development build's `--from-zip` at a place installed from a tree, before anything is written. An unreadable manifest refuses too.
  - `develZipNote` (line 70) adds "the binary did not move" with the way back.
  - `zipAdvice` (line 80) gives a development build `install --repo` in `status`'s and `diff`'s zip notes, in place of `--from-zip` again.
- `internal/harness/repo.go:104`: the not-found error's zip note names `fyr install --repo <checkout>`.

The class, by `git grep` of "from-zip <file> again": the sites were `sourceCandidates`' note, `status.go`'s zip note and `runDiff`'s not-compared line. All three are fixed. A release binary keeps "--from-zip again", which is how its zip place moves.

Tests:
- `TestPlaceMatrix` (23 cells);
- `TestZipPlaceNamedPathKeepsItsError`;
- `TestZipPlaceWayBack`;
- `TestZipPlaceDevelStatusMissing`;
- `TestZipPlaceAdviceByBuild`;
- `TestDevelZipRefusesUnreadableManifest`, which is red with the manifest-error branch mutated to `return nil`.

`TestResolveSourceSkipsZipManifest` pinned the old advice and now pins the way back.

P3's reviews added:
- The refusal runs after the state directory's migration. A dry run refuses while `~/.config/sh-agent` waits (`TestDevelZipRefusesUnmigratedHome`).
- The suggested path is quoted for pasting (`harness.ShellArg`; `TestDevelZipRefusalQuotesThePath`, `TestShellArgRoundTrips`, `TestShellArgEscapes`).

Same phase, item 40: `harness.Behind`'s fetch error now names the remote URL (`git ls-remote --get-url`, its userinfo, query and fragment dropped, and not shown when it does not parse, by `remoteForDisplay`; `TestRemoteForDisplay`, `TestBehindFetchErrorHidesCredentials`, `TestBehindFetchErrorHidesInsteadOfToken`) and the hint for SSH on port 22 (`internal/harness/repo.go:245`, `TestBehindFetchErrorNamesTheRemote`).

## Prevention
A behaviour of a place is tested on every binary kind (release, development) at every place kind (checkout, binary-only, zip): a cell added to one kind is added to `TestPlaceMatrix` for all. An error or note that tells the operator how to move a place names a step that changes the place for THIS build, never one that repeats the state that produced the error.

title: The security agent's git probe rewrote this checkout's .git/HEAD to an unborn branch
body:
# The `security` agent's git probe rewrote this checkout's `.git/HEAD`

## Symptom
`PLAN.md` P4, round 2 of the security review (2026-10-31): at 12:43:26 this checkout's `.git/HEAD` became `ref: refs/heads/-x`, an unborn branch. `git status` then listed every tracked file as added, and `git log` failed with "your current branch '-x' does not have any commits yet". `main` (`6f3109c`) and the index (last written 12:24:47) were untouched. Its report (`REVIEW-2026-10-31-1246-security-review-plan-md-p4-round-2-over-the-fixe`, § Checked) says the probe ran in a "scratch repo, removed": it was testing whether `git symbolic-ref -q HEAD` can print a ref that reaches `git reflog show` as a flag, with HEAD set to `refs/heads/-x`.

## Repro
Run `git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/-x` from a directory under this checkout that has no `.git` of its own (for example a scratch repo whose `.git` was already removed, or one never `git init`ed): git walks up to the checkout's `.git` and rewrites its HEAD.

## Root cause
The agent's dispatch said "change nothing" and "read-only commands", but a probe repository under `.agents/scratch/` (inside this checkout) resolves to the checkout's `.git` whenever its own is missing. Nothing stops git's upward discovery. The agent definition does not say where a git probe may run.

## Fix
Found by the main thread before any commit: `find .git -newermt` listed `.git/HEAD` as the only changed file, and `git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main` restored it. The records stored in the window are in the trail.

## Prevention
A subagent's git probe runs only in a repository it `git init`s under a fresh `mktemp -d` outside every checkout, every command naming it with `git -C <that dir>`, under `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` set to its parent. A dispatch that allows commands repeats this. After every dispatch that can run commands, the main thread checks `cat .git/HEAD` along with `git status`. To graduate into `agents/security/agent.md` and `agents/reviewer/agent.md` (`PLAN.md` item 46).

title: A commit went past the function limit after a late review fix
body:
## BUG-205: A commit went past the function limit after a late review fix

**Symptom:** `TestFunctionLength` failed on `5889b4b`: `scope.prepareProject` was 53 lines against the limit of 50. The verifier caught it; the commit was never pushed.

**Repro:** round 2's fix added the marker and row logic inside `prepareProject`, then `go test ./internal/search ./cmd/fyr` passed and the tree was committed. The root package's pin was not run after that fix.

**Root cause:** the last edit before the commit was checked with the changed packages only, and `funclen_test.go` lives in the root package.

**Fix:** `registerConsented` moved out (`1b14564`).

**Prevention rule:** after the last edit before a commit, run the root package too (`go test . ./<changed packages>`): its pins read every package.

title: internal/sandbox's tests did not build on macOS, and two date tests failed near local midnight
body:
# internal/sandbox's tests did not build on macOS, and two date tests failed near local midnight

## Symptom

The v5.5.0 gate's verifier, run at 00:13 CET: `GOOS=darwin go vet ./internal/sandbox` failed with `failclosed_test.go:15: undefined: procDir`; `TestStatusRetroLine` and `TestRunZone` failed.

## Root cause

`failclosed_test.go` (98f090f) names `procDir`, which only `procs_linux.go` defines, and had no build tag. `TestStatusRetroLine` formats its dates in local time, while status prints UTC. `TestRunZone`'s no-name case takes `time.Local`, which Go fixes at first use under whatever `TZ` held, while its fake agy's `date` reads `/etc/localtime`; `go test -race ./internal/work` reproduced it at 00:25 CET: an earlier test in the package fixes `time.Local` at UTC. A run of the zone tests alone does not. Only tests were wrong.

## Fix

The build tag, `.UTC()` in the test, and `machineLocal` in `zone_test.go`.

## Prevention rule

A test that compares a date names its zone, and a verifier run across local midnight is a test of that. A test file naming a symbol from a `_linux.go` file carries the same build tag: `GOOS=darwin go vet` catches it, so it runs in every checkpoint that touches `internal/sandbox` or `internal/work`, as GUIDE-testing § 3k already says.

Deferred to `TODO.md` Backlog (an agent definition change in `agents/verifier/agent.md` and `agents/reviewer/agent.md` needs its own behavioural run).

title: uneditedScaffoldCount in internal/auto created empty SDD.md, TDD.md and TODO.md files in a project that lacked them
body:
# `uneditedScaffoldCount` in `internal/auto` created empty `SDD.md`, `TDD.md` and `TODO.md` files in a project that lacked them

## Symptom

In Phase 6's `TestEvalRerunExecAndBetweenRowsG9`, the second `auto.Run` on a fixture repository without `SDD.md`, `TDD.md` or `TODO.md` stopped at `G8 clean: the tree is dirty`, with untracked 0-byte `SDD.md`, `TDD.md` and `TODO.md` files left in the checkout by the first `Run`.

## Root cause

In Phase 5 (`f4c24fc`), `uneditedScaffoldCount` and `readFileMentionsRoot` in `internal/auto/tasks.go` called `internal/auto`'s `openRegular(path, os.O_RDONLY)`. Unlike `sandbox.OpenRegular(path, os.O_RDONLY)`, `internal/auto`'s `openRegular` helper (written for `auto.log` and `auto.lock` in `internal/auto/files.go:202`) unconditionally ORs `os.O_CREATE` into its flags. Every `pickProjectTask` rotation that reached `scaffold-drift` therefore created empty `SDD.md`, `TDD.md` and `TODO.md` files in any checkout where they did not exist. Phase 5's `scaffold-drift` test pre-created all three files in its fixture, so the side effect was not observed there.

## Fix

Switched `readFileMentionsRoot` and `uneditedScaffoldCount` in `internal/auto/tasks.go` to `sandbox.OpenRegular(path, os.O_RDONLY)`, which does not pass `os.O_CREATE`, and verified in `TestEvalRerunExecAndBetweenRowsG9` that `git status --porcelain` on the checkout stays empty across `auto.Run` passes.

## Prevention rule

Read-only opens in `internal/auto` must call `sandbox.OpenRegular(path, os.O_RDONLY)` or `readBounded(path, limit)`, never `internal/auto`'s `openRegular` (which is for creating `auto.log` and `auto.lock` under `~/.config/fyr/auto/`). Any test of `auto.Run` on a checkout fixture must assert `git status --porcelain` is empty after the run.

# Rebuild: single-source harness with the `styrman` installer     (date: 2026-09-03)

## Summary

Rebuilt the harness after the hook-driven design was reverted (09fc5cc, 20a5abd). The harness is now context + skills + subagents only, installed by a small Go binary. Twelve design questions were put to the operator first; the answers are recorded in `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-03-rebuild.md`.

- **Layout:** `shared/`, `claude/`, `antigravity/` collapsed into `context/`, `agents/`, `skills/`. No generated copies committed. `.agents/skills -> ../skills` so `npx skills add` from the repo root lands in `skills/`.
- **Context:** `context/AGENTS.md` rewritten without the binary, dispatch rows, scope digests, or hooks. Definition of Done is prose: tests, changelog, reviewer on 50+ lines / 5+ files, security on sensitive paths, docs on behavior change, commit and push. `context/dev-setup.md` holds the environment, stack, and GCP defaults (two placeholders to confirm).
- **Agents:** all six rewritten. `verifier` now runs the project's tests itself. Frontmatter is `owner:` + `date:`; descriptions are single-line and quoted.
- **Skills:** `audit`, `preflight`, `init-project`, `retro` rewritten; `handoff`, `distill`, `feedback`, `find-skills`, `VENDORED.md` edited to drop the binary. `init-project` now ships its templates in `assets/` and creates the `.claude/` symlinks and `CLAUDE.md` import. The other 19 skills are unchanged.
- **Binary:** `cmd/styrman` + `internal/harness` (stdlib only): install/sync, status, diff, update (`git fetch`, `pull --ff-only`, rebuild, reinstall), uninstall (manifest-only), list, render, adopt. Self-installs to `~/.local/bin/styrman`. Foreign `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is never overwritten.
- **Repo docs:** README, AGENTS.md, REQUIREMENTS.md (R1–R6), TODO, ROADMAP, ADR-001..005, this entry, and the rebuild checklist.

task

# Harness practices Phase 4: agents and records (G07, G16 verifier half, G17, G18, G23, G24)     (2026-09-15)

## Summary

Phase 4 of `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-15-harness-practices-g01-g26.md`: edits I-16a–d, I-17a–f and I-18a–n, applied verbatim from the plan's old/new blocks, and ADR-021. The verifier runs every command on its own, records test counts against the previous log, marks inherited failures and lists added suppressions. The agents that can be cut off count a cut tool result as not reached, and the reviewer, security and verifier templates carry a Not examined section. A bug record can carry a `Diagnosis missed:` line that the retro reads. A bug's index row moves to a Graduated table when its prevention rule graduates.

## Type

task

## Files changed

- `agents/verifier.md` — I-16a–d and I-17b. What to run gains four rules. Every command on its own: a chain is split into its commands, each run in the directory the chain would run it in, and `gofmt -l` fails by printing. Test counts: each Go test command runs once with `-v`, its output saved under `.agents/scratch/verify-<slug>/`, and the log writes a `counts:` line and a `vs previous:` line against the newest earlier log with counts; a fall in pass or a rise in skip is a FAIL unless the diff or the environment explains it. Inherited failures: a failing test the change set did not touch is marked `pre-existing?` and Status stays FAIL. Suppressions added: every added suppression, skip or `.only` is listed as file:line, and an added `.only(` or a suppression with no reason is a FAIL. The log template's Go line records exit status, counts and vs previous, and the template gains `## Not examined`. A cut tool result counts as not reached.
- `agents/reviewer.md` — I-17a and I-17e: a cut tool result (a preview, a saved-output path, a line limit) counts as not reached until the rest is read; the report template gains `## Not examined` for files, criteria and commits, or `nothing`.
- `agents/security.md` — I-17c and I-17f: the same sentence; the findings template gains `## Not examined` for paths, surfaces and tools, or `nothing`.
- `agents/explorer.md` — I-17d: the same sentence.
- `agents/bugs.md` — I-18a–g: it keeps both tables of `INDEX.md`, and a new id is the highest in either table plus one; a record carries a `Diagnosis missed:` line when the dispatch names one; when a dispatch says a prevention rule graduated in this repository, the bug's row moves to a `## Graduated` table (`| ID | Area | Graduated to |`) and the record file stays untouched, while a rule promoted from a project to the harness leaves the project's row in place; the prevention recommendation says whether the rule is actionable and generalizable, as information and never a filter; moving a row edits the index, not a record.
- `skills/bug/SKILL.md` — I-18h: when Step 2 ran and the reviewer, the verifier or the fix surfaced a cause the diagnosis did not rank, the `bugs` dispatch carries a `Diagnosis missed:` line naming the line of the Step 2 brief that would have found it.
- `skills/retro/SKILL.md` — I-18i–k: the retro reads `Diagnosis missed:` lines in bug records dated on or after the newest retro record; a bug-derived proposal that targets an `AGENTS.md` says whether its rule is actionable and generalizable; when an applied rule is a bug's prevention rule, `bugs` moves that bug's row to the Graduated table in the same task.
- `context/AGENTS.md` — I-18l: a recurring rule can also graduate into a skill or an agent definition, and the commit that writes it has `bugs` move the matching index rows to the Graduated table. The rendered context stays at 93 lines.
- `.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md` and `skills/init-project/assets/agents-tree/docs/bugs/INDEX.md` — I-18m and I-18n: the header says a row lives in the main table, or in the Graduated table once its prevention rule lives in an `AGENTS.md`, a rule, a skill, an agent definition or a test.
- `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` — ADR-021, "Bug index rows move to a Graduated table when their rule graduates" (task 4.4).
- `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-15-harness-practices-g01-g26.md` — boxes 4.1–4.5 and the Phase 4 checkpoint ticked with evidence; task 4.3's label corrected from I-18a–l to I-18a–n, since I-18m and I-18n are the index edits its check already covered.

# `sh-agent install` writes Claude Code's attribution setting when absent     (date: 2026-09-16)

## Summary
Implements ADR-025 to resolve BUG-039: `sh-agent install` (and its alias `sync`, for vendor `all` or `claude` only) now writes `"attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""}` to `~/.claude/settings.json` when the `attribution` key is absent, creating the file if missing. A present key of any value is left alone and the advisory note stays. File edits use textual insertion re-parsed before writing so the operator's other keys and formatting remain byte-identical. `--dry-run` reports and writes nothing. No state of the file fails install; the setting is advisory (R4). `uninstall` leaves the key (the trailer must stay off with or without the harness). Supersedes ADR-010's "never touch vendor settings" clause on this one point only; the permission-write refusal it stated still stands.

## Type
feature

## Files changed
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` — `attributionSet` (file creation, textual insertion, Lstat guard, size/format checks, Sync before rename), `readSettings` (shared helper for `attributionSet` and `attributionOff`), `abandonTemp` (temp-file cleanup with error reporting), `attributionOff` refactored to use `readSettings`, install/sync case wired to call `attributionSet` before `attributionHint`
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` — `TestAttributionSet` (14 subtests: missing file, other keys with formatting/mode preservation, CRLF, empty object, off/custom value, malformed, non-object JSON, null, >1 MiB bound, symlink guard, dry-run, vendor-agy no-op), `TestAttributionNote` cases `no settings file` and `other settings only` updated for new order (install leg expects `settings:` line and no note; status leg has no note because key now present); new case `status alone on a home without the key` keeps the note
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` — R4 sentence approved 2026-09-16: "`install` also sets one key in the operator's `~/.claude/settings.json`, `attribution` (commit and PR trailers off), only when the key is absent; it never changes or removes another key, and `uninstall` leaves it."; § Non-goals exception approved 2026-09-16: narrowed "Editing `settings.json` or any vendor setting" to name the exception and ADR-025
- `context/AGENTS.md` § Git — "`sh-agent install` sets it when absent; `status` says when a different value is set"
- `README.md` — § Install: attribution sentence and line reworded to "the installer touches no vendor setting except the attribution key (ADR-025)"; `status` row updated for the absent-file note-firing condition
- `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md` — § Verify and § First session after install (line 37 reworded to "the installer touches no vendor setting except the attribution key (ADR-025)")
- `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` — § First install
- `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` — ADR-025 (full decision: context, decision, consequences naming R4/Non-goals changes and the operator's approval); ADR-010's heading marked "Superseded in part by ADR-025"

## Agents dispatched
reviewer ×5 (three cold-read rounds with round-3 findings: one doc-line residue left as Open rows; code lens APPROVE WITH NITS: three findings fixed — null handling, error-path cleanup, symlink/size guards; docs lens REQUEST CHANGES: two findings fixed — status note-firing condition restatement, README antecedent noun), security ×1 (five low-severity findings: TOCTOU symlink/FIFO race fixed with `O_EXCL`, missing `Sync` fixed, non-object JSON output fixed, CRLF line-ending handling confirmed, uninstall promise updated; four earlier defects closed: dangling/live symlinks rejected, >1 MiB guard added, bare `null` caught, `abandonTemp` helper added), verifier ×3 (third and final pass: three runs, last on final tree after security fixes; `go test -race -v -count=1 ./...` PASS: counts pass 79, fail 0, skip 1; install/status/reinstall e2e PASS; coverage: `TestAttributionSet` branch-by-branch vs `attributionSet` live; gaps: `abandonTemp` error paths and `readSettings` open failure untested), documentation ×1 (README, deploy/local.md, deploy/remote.md), changelog ×2 (ADR-025 and this entry), bugs ×1 (BUG-044: security agent's crafted-input probes left seven untracked files in repo root; removed; prevention rule added to Definition of Done step 1).

## Verification
Unit: `go test -race -v -count=1 ./...` PASS (pass 79, fail 0, skip 1). Integration: `go run ./cmd/sh-agent install --home .agents/scratch/verify-attribution-write-3` created settings file with key and printed `settings: …/.claude/settings.json created with "attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""} — Claude Code's commit and PR trailers are off`; `status` printed no note (key now present, rendered 93 lines). E2E: second install to same home idempotent (0 written, no settings line). Both CLIs: `sh-agent list` returned expected counts (Skills 27, Subagents 7). Logs: `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-16-verify-attribution-write.md` (third pass after security fixes; two prior passes overwritten; full matrix of crafted inputs exercised in `.agents/scratch/secrev/`).

## Docs
README.md (Install section, status row), .agents/docs/deploy/local.md (Verify and First session after install), .agents/docs/deploy/remote.md (First install), context/AGENTS.md (§ Git sentence). REQUIREMENTS.md changed — R4 and § Non-goals — both approved by operator 2026-09-16.

# Release binary — Phase 2 of the release-binary plan: the embedded source     (2026-09-17)

## Summary

The harness's own files now live inside the binary, and every reader reaches them through one abstraction. `embed.go` (package `styrman`, module root) embeds `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/` and `rules/` with `//go:embed all:…`, so the 15 `.gitkeep` files come along. `Source{FS, Dir, Version}` replaces the `repo string` every reader took: `Dir` is a checkout or plain copy (`FS` is `os.DirFS(Dir)`), and an empty `Dir` with a `Version` is the files built into a release binary. title: `sh-agent report` keeps nothing — Phase 3 of the release-binary plan (2026-09-17)
