# `sh-agent report` keeps nothing — Phase 3 of the release-binary plan     (2026-09-17)

## Summary

`sh-agent report` no longer keeps a clone of the private feedback repository on every machine, which is what let each place read every other place's reports ("But why can I see dave reports?"). Without `--feedback-repo`, a run now clones `~/.config/sh-agent/report-<pid>` with `--filter=blob:none --no-checkout --depth 1`, limits it with `git sparse-checkout set --no-cone reports/<host>/`, writes its run directory, commits, pushes to the feedback URL, and removes that directory on every path out — a failed push, a refusal and an early return included. No other machine's report content is fetched to the disk; this machine's own earlier runs do come along, which is what lets the `-2` suffix pick a free directory name. A server that does not support the filter makes git warn and send everything: slower, still correct. Because a throwaway clone has nowhere to keep a rejected commit, a non-fast-forward push is retried once from a fresh clone; a second rejection says `push rejected twice; re-run sh-agent report — nothing is kept locally` and leaves nothing behind. `--feedback-repo DIR` is unchanged in every respect: that checkout is the operator's, so it is written into and never removed, a stray file in it is named and left alone, and a rejected push leaves the commit there with today's `pull --rebase` message. `sh-agent update` removes the clone earlier versions kept at `~/.config/sh-agent/feedback`, but only when it is that clone, clean, and not ahead of its upstream; anything else is left in place with the reason named.

## Type

task

## Files changed

- `internal/harness/report.go` — `ResolveFeedback` reduced to the `--feedback-repo` resolver; new `throwawayDir`, `cloneThrowaway`, `sweepInterruptedClones`, `alive`, `RemoveKeptClone`, `writeAndPush`, `scrubCredentials`, `errPushRejected` and the `testHooks` pair; `SendReport` split into the dry-run, named-checkout and throwaway paths, the last a two-attempt loop with removal deferred inside each attempt; `commitAndPush` returns the rejection sentinel so each caller words it
- `internal/harness/report_test.go` — `TestSendReport` rewritten for the default path (reads what was sent from the origin, `assertKeepsNothing` after each run); new `TestSendReportNamedCheckout`, `TestSendReportThrowawayClone`, `TestSendReportRetriesRejectedPush`, `TestRemoveKeptClone` (nine subtests), `TestSendReportSweepsInterruptedClones`, `TestCloneFailureDoesNotPrintCredentials`; `TestResolveFeedbackFailures` rewritten for the new signature plus the unreachable-URL case; helpers `seedFeedback`, `localBlobHolds`, `configDir`
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` — `update` calls `harness.RemoveKeptClone` below every `--check` return, reported and never fatal; usage text and the command comment describe the throwaway clone
- `internal/harness/repo.go` — `gitOut` split so `gitOutC` can run one call with `LC_ALL=C`: the push whose rejection message the retry has to recognise
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` — `TestUpdateKeptCloneCleanupOnlyWhenUpdating`
- `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md` — § Report back rewritten: a new "Nothing is kept here" bullet, both rejection paths, and what `update` does with an old kept clone
- `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-17-release-binary.md` — Phase 3's three task boxes ticked with evidence; the partial-clone assumption marked settled; D25

## Agents dispatched

- `verifier` — PASS, `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-17-release-binary-phase-3.md` (87 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip at 83f3cf6)
- `security` — 2 medium, 6 low, `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-17-security-73f2c36-83f3cf6.md`; five fixed with tests, three rebutted in its `## Outcome`. The two mediums were real defects in this phase's own code: `RemoveKeptClone`'s unpushed-commit guard failed OPEN when the count could not be taken (a branch with no upstream), and the cleanup call sat above `update --check`'s returns, so the read-only mode deleted the clone. Both now have a test that fails without the fix, and the function additionally refuses a symlink at that path, treats a stash and ignored files as work, and resolves a relative `--home`. Also fixed: an interrupted run's `report-<pid>` is swept by the next run (a deferred removal cannot cover a signal), git's clone error no longer repeats a URL a rewrite can fill with a token, and the one push whose message the retry must recognise runs with `LC_ALL=C`.

## Verification

`gofmt`, `go vet` and `go test -race -count=1 ./...` clean at each commit. The git mechanics were settled before any code was written (`.agents/scratch/p3-probe/probe.sh`), which caught two things that would have made the isolation check vacuous: a `file://` remote ignores `--filter` unless it sets `uploadpack.allowFilter`, and `git cat-file` on a promised object lazily FETCHES it, so a naive check answers yes about a blob the clone never held. The tests therefore seed `uploadpack.allowFilter` and read with `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`. `TestSendReportThrowawayClone` inspects the clone through `testHooks.beforeRemove`: the other host's directory is never checked out and its canary is in no local blob, the run lands on the remote, and afterwards there is no kept checkout and no `report-*`. Must-fail: every new and rewritten test failed to BUILD against the old `ResolveFeedback`, so the guards were mutated one at a time instead (`.agents/scratch/p3-mustfail/mutate.py`, which asserts each target text is unique and restores from a saved copy, per BUG-068) — removal not deferred, `--filter` dropped, `sparse-checkout` dropped, the retry removed, and the dirty check dropped each failed exactly the test that covers it, and the file was restored. One real run against GitHub, authorised by the operator (D25) and logged in `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-17-release-binary-phase-3-real-report.md`, settled the last assumption: the blob-less shallow clone over SSH succeeded, the push landed as `09586ff`, and nothing was left in `~/.config/sh-agent/`. The security review then found two real defects in this phase's own code (see § Agents dispatched); each was reproduced, fixed, and covered by a test seen failing without the fix, and the suite ended at 90 top-level tests and 73 subtests, none failing or skipped. Not exercised: what the real clone contained (it is removed by design, so only the tests can show that), the retry against the real remote, `RemoveKeptClone` against this box's own kept clone (which is `sh-agent update`'s job in the operator's home), and a pid collision between two runs in separate pid namespaces (rebutted in the review's `## Outcome`).

## Docs

`.agents/docs/deploy/local.md` § Report back is current with this change. `README.md` § How it works (the map's report line), `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § The four places and `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` still describe a kept clone; they land with R8, R9 and the map in Phase 5's single commit to `main` (D11, R9).

## Requirements

R9's "Report back" bullet changes to the text the operator approved in the plan's Interfaces, applied in Phase 5. R4 holds: stdlib only, git and ssh shelled out as before, no dependency added. Nothing here reaches a machine until that commit lands and a place updates.

title: `update` from a signed release — Phase 4 of the release-binary plan (2026-09-17)
body:
# `update` from a signed release — Phase 4 of the release-binary plan     (2026-09-17)

## Summary

`sh-agent update` on a place with no harness checkout now moves that place forward from a GitHub release instead of refusing. `gh release view` gives the newest tag; the tag must parse as `vX.Y.Z` and be numerically newer than the running binary, or nothing is downloaded and the reason is printed. `gh release download` fetches this platform's `sh-agent-<goos>-<goarch>`, `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig` into a random `~/.config/sh-agent/release-*` directory that is removed on every path out. Verification is two checks and a third fact: `ssh-keygen -Y verify` checks the signature over `SHA256SUMS` against an allowed-signers line compiled into the binary, in the namespace `sh-agent-release`; the downloaded binary's SHA-256 must equal its line in that file; and the file must name the release it belongs to, `# styrman-harness vX.Y.Z`, matching the tag — so the version is part of what was signed (D26). Only then is `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` replaced through a temp file and a rename, and the NEW binary runs its own install, which deploys the harness built into it. `--check` stops after the tag comparison: `up to date (vX.Y.Z)`, or `newer release vA.B.C available` and exit 2. A development build is never overwritten from a release; it is told to download one by hand.

## Type

feature

## Files changed

- `internal/harness/release.go` (new) — `ReleaseRepo`, `ReleaseNamespace`, `releaseSigner`, `sumsVersionMarker`, `ErrNewerRelease`, `AssetName`, `LatestRelease`, `UpdateFromRelease`, `downloadRelease`, `verifyRelease`, `checksumFor`, `compareRelease`, `releaseParts`, `sshKeygen`, `sshKeygenSystemPaths`, `readCapped`, `maxAssetBytes`, `maxSumsBytes`
- `internal/harness/release_test.go` (new) — a fake `gh` and real `ssh-keygen` signatures from a test key, on a PATH holding nothing else: the good path, both up-to-date modes, `--check`, twelve refusals, the downgrade and bad-tag cases, `TestChecksumFor`, `TestCompareRelease`, `TestSSHKeygenPrefersASystemPath`, `TestReleaseSignerMatchesTheDeployGuide`
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` — `update` with an embedded source routes to `UpdateFromRelease`, mapping `ErrNewerRelease` to exit 2; `installPassArgs` extracted and shared with the checkout path; usage text and the command comment describe both kinds of update
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` — `TestReleaseBinaryUpdateCheckExitsTwo`; `TestReleaseBinaryWithoutCheckout`'s update leg rewritten for the release flow with PATH emptied
- `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-17-release-binary.md` — Phase 4's two boxes ticked with evidence; D26, D27, D28; D22 marked superseded; Phase 5's release-procedure box now also requires the `SHA256SUMS` version marker and a rehearsal

## Agents dispatched

- `verifier` — PASS at 4d45155, `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-17-release-binary-phase-4.md` (96 pass, 0 fail, 0 skip). That run predates the security fixes below; the counts at 40bf2db are 99 top-level tests and 85 subtests, none failing or skipped, with `gofmt`, `go vet`, `go test -race` and `govulncheck` clean, re-run by the main agent.
- `security` — 1 medium, 6 low, `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-17-security-dab2565-4d45155.md`; six fixed, two rebutted in its `## Outcome`. The medium was real and load-bearing: `tag == version` was an equality test and the signed bytes did not name the version, so a genuinely signed OLDER release would install, and one release's signed checksums verified under another release's tag. It found the signature chain otherwise sound — signer, namespace, identity and asset name compiled in or from `runtime`, nothing in a release able to redirect them, nothing outside the download directory written before both checks pass.

## Verification

Measured before any code: `ssh-keygen -Y verify` exits 0 on a good signature and 255 for a wrong key, a wrong namespace and altered content (OpenSSH 10.0p2). Twelve refusals are covered, each asserting the installed binary is byte-identical afterwards, no install ran, and no download directory is left: `gh` missing, `gh` unable to reach the repository, no verifier anywhere, no asset for this platform, a signature from another key, `SHA256SUMS` altered after signing, a checksum mismatch, a release shipping its own allowed-signers line under the compiled-in identity, signed checksums naming another version, signed checksums naming no version, no `.sig`, no `SHA256SUMS`. Must-fail by mutation (`.agents/scratch/p4-mustfail/mutate.py`, which asserts each target is unique, restores from a saved copy and reports a stale mutation as a failure, per BUG-068): all twelve mutations fail the tests that cover them — signature unchecked, checksum uncompared, verification skipped, no verifier required, verifier taken from PATH first, `gh` unchecked, namespace unpinned, signer taken from the release, downgrade allowed, tag unvalidated, the signed version marker unchecked, and a development build overwritten. Two mistakes of the session's own making, both caught by running rather than assuming: a test reached the REAL `gh` and the real repository because `/usr/bin` was on its PATH for `ssh-keygen` (PATH is now a single controlled directory, with `ssh-keygen` linked in), and a generated Go literal had its `\n` escapes turned into newlines, breaking the build (BUG-057's hazard; repaired and then verified by grepping for the escape itself). Not exercised: no real release exists yet, so every download is against the fake `gh`; the three-platform cross-compilation and the real `gh release create` are Phase 5; `darwin/arm64` behaviour is untested on this Linux box.

## Docs

`cmd/sh-agent/main.go`'s usage text and package comment describe both kinds of `update`. `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md` § Update still describes only the checkout kind, and `README.md`, the map, `AGENTS.md` rules 1 and 2, `REQUIREMENTS.md` R8/R9 and `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` still describe the unpacked bundle; all of them land in Phase 5's single commit to `main` (D11, R9). Phase 5 must also write the `SHA256SUMS` version marker into `/preflight` Step 6 and `remote.md` § Releases — until it does, no release this code will accept can be cut (D26), which is stated in that box.

## Requirements

R4 holds: stdlib only, `gh` and `ssh-keygen` shelled out, no dependency added. R8 and R9 gain the release-binary way in, in Phase 5's commit, with the operator's approved text. The signer line is the same operator key `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases gives `git verify-tag`, pinned by a test so the two copies cannot drift.

title: BUG-078 — a verified release binary shadowed by an earlier PATH entry (2026-09-18)
body:
# BUG-078 — a verified release binary shadowed by an earlier PATH entry     (2026-09-18)

## Summary

On devbox the operator downloaded v1.2.1, verified its signature and checksum, saw `./sh-agent-linux-amd64 version` print `v1.2.1`, moved it to `/usr/local/bin` — and `sh-agent` kept running a stale `(devel)` build from `/opt/devbox/bin`, which installed an old tree and reported `drift none`. Two PATH entries sat ahead of the new binary and nothing said so. This change makes `install` and `status` say so, and makes both install guides verify the *file* before it moves and the *shell's resolution* after. Unreleased: it reaches binary-only places at the next release.

## Type

bugfix

## What changed

- **`internal/harness/pathguard.go`** (new): `PathShadows(pathEnv, binPath) (shadows []string, onPath bool)` walks PATH as a shell does. `onPath` is true when the walk reaches an executable that `os.SameFile`s the installed file — through its own directory, a symlinked directory, a symlink or a hard link; there is no lexical directory comparison anywhere. `shadows` are the executables of that name found before it, in order, without repeats; an empty PATH entry prints as `./sh-agent`. `executableAt` is what it calls a binary (`os.Stat`, not a directory, execute bit set).
- **`cmd/sh-agent/main.go`**: `install` prints `warning: <path> comes before <installed> on PATH, so `sh-agent` runs that one` when PATH reaches the installed file but only after an earlier entry; when PATH does not reach it and something else answers, the old "not on PATH" note names it instead (`… so `sh-agent` runs <path> instead; put <bin dir> ahead of it`). `status` gains a `shadowed   <path> comes first on PATH, so `sh-agent` runs that, not the binary above` line under the same condition. `install --dry-run` prints no PATH claim: it wrote no binary. One `PathShadows` call feeds each; there is no second definition of "on PATH".
- **README § Install without cloning**: the `gh` route is one `&&` chain — download into `mktemp -d` with `--clobber`, the real signer line written to `allowed_signers`, `ssh-keygen -Y verify`, `sha256sum -c`, `./<asset> version` on the file, then the one `mv` and the scratch dir removed — so a failed check stops the move and no checksum or signer file lands in a PATH directory. The `go install` route says what it trusts (SSH to GitHub and git's hashes; no checksum database, no release signature) and the browser route is the same chain over the files in `~/Downloads`; each route is its own fence, so a paste runs one route. Then: `sh-agent version` *unqualified* first, with the sentence that it tells stale from fresh and never genuine from forged.
- **`.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § First install**: the same procedure as one chained block for a release-binary machine; § Verify asks for the unqualified `version` and no `shadowed` line. **`local.md` § Verify** says the same for a checkout place.
- **`.agents/docs/bugs/BUG-078-…`** and `INDEX.md`: `fixed`, with what the code half does *not* catch stated plainly (below).

## What it does not do

On devbox as it happened, the wrong binary ran the install and wrote itself to `~/.local/bin`, first on PATH — from its own point of view nothing was shadowed, so no in-binary check could have fired. The doc half catches that ordering: `sh-agent version` unqualified and `which -a`. The code half catches the other ordering, where `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/…` or a Homebrew dir precedes `~/.local/bin`, which is common on a Mac.

## Tests

`TestPathShadows` (14 cases over real temp files: installed dir first, earlier entry, order and later entries, symlink, hard link, symlinked directory before and after a shadow, repeated entry, empty directory, non-executable, missing installed dir, `//`, `/.`, empty entry via `t.Chdir`, missing installed file), `TestExecutableAt`, `TestInstallAndStatusNameAPathShadow` (warning, `shadowed`, both quiet after a symlink to the installed binary), `TestOffPathInstallNamesWhatAnswersAndDoesNotWarnTwice` (the off-PATH note names what answers; no double warning; `--dry-run` makes no PATH claim). Ten must-fail mutations in `.agents/scratch/bug078-mustfail/mutate.py`, each failing as a test failure — three first attempts did not compile (an unused variable each) and were redone, since a build failure proves nothing.

## Definition of Done

Four review rounds, because two landed on one mechanism and the context rule then sends the mechanism to the operator:

- Round 1 (`52574a0`): `verifier` PASS (`testing/2026-09-18-verify-bug078-path-shadow.md`); `reviewer` REQUEST CHANGES — high: `binOnPath` (string compare) and `PathShadows` (`Clean`) disagreed on `.local/bin//`, hiding a real shadow; medium: a hard link reported as a shadow; low: an unbacked "for an hour" in README. `security` 1 medium (README's signer line a placeholder, the file left in a PATH dir) + 6 low. `/review --docs` APPROVE, 2 low (`local.md` narrowed; no changes entry). All fixed except two lows rebutted (`reviews/…-4cdc0b5-52574a0*.md` § Outcome).
- Round 2 (`8ce58a0`): `verifier` PASS; `reviewer` REQUEST CHANGES — the same mechanism again, lexical `onPath` vs `SameFile` on a symlinked directory. `security`: two mediums, both docs (`remote.md`'s block a sketch with `$D` unassigned; README unchained at the verify), plus the rebuttal reasons corrected. **Stopped here and asked the operator what the gate was for**; their choice: "on PATH" is the identity walk reaching the file, nothing lexical.
- Round 3 (`b029ea1`): `verifier` PASS, the alias repro run by hand; `reviewer` APPROVE; `security` all low. The three-round cap; the operator granted one bounded extra round for the cheap fixes.
- Round 4 (`28e4747`): `verifier` PASS (215 tests/subtests, unchanged; a fresh-home `--dry-run` printed no PATH line); `security` four lows, no high — it validated the dry-run gate in both states itself. One low was a docs-only edit made in the closing commit (the browser fence became the same `&&` chain as the `gh` route); the others corrected two `left` reasons and confirmed the hung-mount reason (`reviews/2026-09-18-security-4cdc0b5-28e4747.md` § Outcome).

# install names every file it changes     (2026-09-18)

## Summary

`sh-agent install` (and the install `update` runs) prints one line per file it adds, updates, corrects the mode of, or removes, on every run — not only under `--dry-run`, which used to be the only run that listed anything. Unchanged files stay a count. The operator asked for it ("more info … It should be clear what is installed new or things like that. Go with 1", 2026-09-18). Phase 1 of `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-18-sh-agent-works-everywhere.md`. Unreleased.

## Type

feature (output), phase checkpoint

## What changed

- **`internal/harness/apply.go` `Install`**: `add     ~/<rel>` when no previous file existed; `update  ~/<rel>` when the bytes differed; `update  ~/<rel> (previous file unreadable: <err>)` when the previous file could not be read — written over as before, the line says why (D6); `mode    ~/<rel> (0666 -> 0644)` when only the permission differed — the probe runs on a dry run too, only the `chmod` is gated (D7, D8), and the file stays in the `unchanged` count; `remove  ~/<rel> (no longer in the source)` on the real run as on the dry run (it was dry-run only). The line for a written file prints after the write succeeds, so a write that fails — a directory at the path, which the rename cannot replace (`EISDIR`) — leaves no line claiming a change (Phase 1 review). The summary line's shape is unchanged; `written` = add + update.
- **README § Daily commands** (`install` row) and **`specs/sh-agent/delivery.md`** say so.

## Tests

`TestInstallNamesEveryChange`: first install lists every managed file as `add` and nothing else; an identical install lists nothing; a changed source file lists exactly its deployed copies as `update`; a removed source file lists `remove … (no longer in the source)`; a mode-only drift lists one `mode` line and is counted unchanged; a `0000` previous file (D9) lists `update … (previous file unreadable: …)` and is written; `--dry-run` lists the same `update` and `mode` lines and leaves bytes and modes as they were; a directory at a destination fails the install with no line for it. Eight must-fail mutations in `.agents/scratch/phase1-mustfail/mutate.py`, each failing as a test failure. Live: 260 `add` lines then none; a touched skill in a scratch clone → its two vendor copies as `update`; a chmodded file under `--dry-run` → one `mode` line, mode untouched.

## Definition of Done

`verifier` PASS (`testing/2026-09-18-verify-sh-agent-works-everywhere-phase-1.md`, 227/0/0, all four checkpoint legs live — the agent hit its turn limit once with an empty log and finished on a continuation; and `…-phase-1-2.md` over the final range); `reviewer` APPROVE WITH NITS (`reviews/2026-09-18-review-b393525-028a43b.md`, one low fixed — the line now prints after the write); `/review --docs` APPROVE (`…-docs.md`); the docs clause done in the same change. title: The sh-agent audit: every verb on every kind of place (2026-09-18)
body:
# The sh-agent audit: every verb on every kind of place     (2026-09-18)

## Summary

Phase 2 of `plans/2026-09-18-sh-agent-works-everywhere.md` — the operator's Definition of Done for this session: "work until the delivery mechanism sh-agent is flawless". Five review lenses read `cmd/sh-agent` and `internal/harness` whole, an explorer mapped every verb × place-kind cell, and everything they found was fixed with a test that failed first or rebutted in writing; three review rounds of the fixes followed, two of them stopped at the operator's door because a fix had introduced the next round's defect. Phase 3, the matrix on this box, ran on the result: 53 cells, none silent. Unreleased.

## Type

fix (audit); phase checkpoint

## What changed

Behaviour a user of `sh-agent` sees:

- **Release tags are canonical.** `v1.02.2`, `v01.2.2`, `v1.2.02` and a component that does not fit an int are not release tags: `IsReleaseVersion` refuses them, so `update` never downloads such a tag, and a tag that is not newer than the running binary is refused with "the newest release X is not newer than this binary Y; nothing installed".
- **Refusals name the alternative.** `update` on a plain copy: "not its own git checkout; a plain copy cannot be updated with git — `install` still deploys it as it is; to move forward, use a checkout (`git clone …`) or a release binary (README § Install without cloning)". `adopt` on a release binary names the checkout to clone; on a plain copy its "next:" line says to copy the skill into a checkout and commit there, not "commit and push" a tree with no repository.
- **The BUG-079 note** prints only for the user's real home (never under `--home` elsewhere), identity by `os.SameFile` so a symlinked `$HOME` counts, and offers `ln -sfn` only when the file's directory is the caller's — otherwise "it is not yours to relink — remove it, with the rights that own its directory, or leave it and run the installed one by its path".
- **`~/.config/sh-agent` is private.** Created 0700; an existing looser one is tightened by `install` before it writes anything, with `mode    ~/.config/sh-agent (0755 -> 0700)`; a dry run names it and touches nothing; a symlinked directory and one the caller does not own are left alone; a failed `chmod` is a note. `diff` and `report` create it private and never change an existing one.
- **A relative `--home` beside `--repo`** lands under the invoking directory on a real install as on a dry run (BUG-080).
- **`adopt`** strips group/other write bits like `install` does. **`diff`** renders under `~/.config/sh-agent/`, never `/tmp`, and removes its temp file on every path. **`install`/`status`** report an oversized `settings.json` with one note. A description with a control character renders as valid YAML for Antigravity; a table cell never cuts a multi-byte character.
- **Docs**: the `keep` line, the `knownCheckout` refusal (README's "works from anywhere" qualified), `report: --repo is not used here`, and every changed message quoted where it is described.

Not changed, by decision: the ~220-line `settings.json` editor stays in `main.go` (a Follow-up); `LoadState` does not sanitise `Repo` (reason narrowed in the record); loose modes inside the runtime dir; ownership as the proxy for relinkability.

## Tests

`internal/harness/audit_test.go` (11 tests, one per finding) and `owned_unix_test.go`; eight tests in `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` (plain-copy `update`/`adopt`/`status` through the CLI, `adopt` on a release binary, `sync`, `diff` with drift, the relative `--home`, the oversized settings). Nineteen must-fail mutations in `.agents/scratch/phase2-mustfail/mutate.py`, each failing as a test failure; the ones that could not compile or could not be reached were redone or dropped and say so in the reports. Suite 250, `govulncheck` clean, `GOOS=windows` and `darwin/arm64` builds clean.

## Definition of Done

- **Audit** (`reviews/2026-09-18-review-harness-merged.md`, 19 findings, `## Outcome`): code lens APPROVE WITH NITS; security (opus) 1 medium + 7 low; simplify 1 medium + 3 low; docs 2 medium + 1 low; tests PASS with 2 gaps. Explorer recon `plans/2026-09-18-recon-sh-agent-audit.md`: no silent cell, four coverage gaps.
- **Round 1** (`3209cf3`): verifier PASS (244); reviewer (opus) APPROVE WITH NITS, 3 low; security 1 medium (the 0700 was a no-op after `SaveState`'s 0755) + 2 low; docs lens APPROVE.
- **Round 2** (`e7fec88`): verifier PASS (248, cross-builds); reviewer APPROVE WITH NITS — two mediums on the new `ConfigDir` (symlink followed; `EPERM` fails the run); security 1 medium — the same mechanism, worse (an install aborted after every write, no manifest). **The operator's call** (option 1): tighten as a `mode` line at the top of `install`, never fail.
- **Round 3** (`42840fb`): verifier PASS (250; four live legs quoted, the `mode` line before the first `add`); reviewer APPROVE, one low/low (README's overpromise); security four lows, no high, the medium closed structurally. After the cap, in the checkpoint commit: the two skips print a `note:` (the symlink one pinned by a test), README's clause corrected; Phase 4's gate reviews those lines.
- `documentation` ×3 (audit docs findings; the Phase 2 messages; the runtime-dir mode line); `bugs` for BUG-080.

## Where it stops

Unreleased; Phase 4 of the plan is the release. The Follow-ups are in the plan.

# `sh-agent update --from-zip`: a third way in, the zip place     (date: 2026-09-28)

## Summary
A machine that can hold neither the operator's SSH key nor `gh` can now take the harness from a repository zip downloaded by hand. `sh-agent update --from-zip <file>`:
- reads the zip once, hashes it, and checks every entry before writing anything;
- unpacks only the five harness trees under `~/.config/sh-agent/zip-*`;
- installs them with the running binary, and deletes the unpacked copy.

Nothing is fetched, and the output flags the zip as `UNVERIFIED`. The manifest records `zip:sha256:<hex>`, and `status` and `diff` say that a zip install is not compared.

ADR-038 supersedes ADR-034 in part. `AGENTS.md` rule 1, `delivery.md` § The model, the README map (drawn dashed, because a zip is fetched by hand) and the deploy guides all say three ways.

**Also in this change:**
- `update --dry-run` is now read-only on both paths; it used to act.
- `diff` has a zip branch.
- Leftover `zip-*` directories are swept after a successful run.
- `secretShaped` and `.gitignore` cover `*oauth-token*`.

# Release v1.9.0     (date: 2026-09-28)

## Summary
v1.9.0 is gated SHIP over `v1.8.0..b5d4cb3` (`reviews/2026-09-28-preflight-v1.9.0.md`).

## Type
release

## Release notes
## New features
- **Signed release zip.** Each release now publishes `styrman-harness-vX.Y.Z.zip`, a `git archive` of the tag, under the signed `SHA256SUMS`.
  - `sh-agent update --from-zip <file>` verifies the zip when `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig` sit beside it, and prints `VERIFIED against the signed SHA256SUMS of release vX.Y.Z`.
  - It refuses the zip on any failed check, and nothing is written.
  - A zip with neither file beside it (a `main` zip) still installs, marked `UNVERIFIED` (ADR-039).
## Improvements and optimisation
- **The zip verdict is kept.** An install from a zip records in its manifest whether the zip was verified, and `sh-agent status` shows `(verified vX.Y.Z)` or `(unverified)`.
- **Refusals name the right file.** When the zip is not the one the release published, for example GitHub's automatic "Source code" archive, the refusal names the zip that release does publish.
## Fixes
- **The report sweep no longer builds a glob from the home path**, so a home containing glob characters cannot reach another home's clones.
- **Tests can no longer run the real `sh-agent report`:** they cut `PATH` first, so none can push to the feedback repository (BUG-094). The report a test pushed during v1.8.0 has been removed.
- **The pid in the sweep test is now deterministic**, so the test can no longer fail by chance.
## Other updates
- **`find-skills` is vendored verbatim again.** Its routing (a found skill goes into the harness checkout's `skills/`, then `sh-agent install`) now lives in the global context, including `npx skills add … -y`.
- **R9 wording:** "nothing in the zip replaces the binary".
- **The skill matrix drops `curl`.**
- **The README map** draws the release zip and the Releases → zip place path (by hand, verified).
## Install
- **Download:** see README § Install without cloning. Existing binary-only places: `sh-agent update`.
- **Zip place:** download `styrman-harness-v1.9.0.zip`, `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig` from this release into one folder, then run `sh-agent update --from-zip styrman-harness-v1.9.0.zip`. The output must say `VERIFIED`.

## Agents dispatched
- **Gate:** `reviewer` (opus: code, docs), `security`, `verifier` ×2.
- **Gate fixes:** `reviewer`.

# v1.13.0 gate fixes   (2026-09-30-0505)

The release gate for v1.13.0 (its report, `reviews/2026-09-30-preflight-v1.13.0.md`, is written in the release commit) ran over v1.12.1..c872598. Its reviews found four low findings; three are fixed here before the tag, one is a documented limit by the operator's choice. - **Symlink test strengthened** (code review finding 1): the link's target is an empty file and must stay 0 bytes.
- **Comment corrected** (code review finding 2): `prepareFiles` says what its `O_EXCL` create does and does not cover.
- **Copied index, documented** (security finding 2): the spec's failure modes say an index is only as trusted as the folder it sits in and name `sh-agent index --rebuild` after copying a project in.
- **Docs lens** findings on the two closed bug records: rebutted in the report's Outcome (a record's body is history; its status is the living value).

# Release signer rotated; the release key signs through the SSH agent (ADR-052)

## Summary

`a0a54b4`. The previous release key's private half was pasted into a chat session (exposed; no known misuse), and it doubled as dave's GitHub login key. New signer `SHA256:BwBzPnfX…` compiled into `internal/harness/release.go` and printed in `deploy/remote.md` § Releases and README § Install without cloning (with the v2.4.0 bridge note). The procedure no longer reads `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`: it checks the key is in the SSH agent (`ssh-add -L`), signs the tag with `user.signingkey='key::<public key>'` and `SHA256SUMS` with `ssh-keygen -Y sign -f <public key file>`. Project `AGENTS.md` § Release says the same. v2.4.0 is the bridge: tag by the new key, `SHA256SUMS.sig` by the retired one, so v2.3.2 places accept it.

## Review fixes (41af344, 48ae45c, 18b9018)

The code, docs and security reviews of a0a54b4 found the procedure ran the bridge with the wrong key. `41af344`: a v2.4.0-only bridge block in `remote.md` § Releases (two signatures over one `SHA256SUMS`: `SHA256SUMS.current.sig` by the current key, `SHA256SUMS.sig` by the retired key; step 3b with a v2.3.2 binary built from its tag and with the v2.4.0 binary both ways), the zip-place and binary-only edges in `delivery.md` § The model, ADR-052a, README's v2.4.0 path on `SHA256SUMS.current.sig`, release-key agent hygiene, and `TestEveryDocumentedReleaseKeyIsKnown`. `48ae45c`: `git -C <toplevel> archive` (a bare archive from the scratch subdirectory packs nothing), explicit retired-key load and delete, `remote.md:103` points at the current key, the test confines the retired key to the bridge block and reads every key type. `18b9018`: fingerprint check of the retired key file before load or delete, an agent-must-answer check, a tab before a key. Credential copies in scratch sandbox homes deleted by name (BUG-160, open for the kit fix).

## Verification

`TestReleaseSignerMatchesTheDeployGuide` passes, and fails with the old line restored in `release.go` (mutation run). Agent signing checked with a throwaway key on OpenSSH 10.0p2 / git 2.47.3: `ssh-keygen -Y sign -f <pub>` through the agent, then `-Y verify`, and the `ssh-add -L` check, all exit 0. Verifier PASS at 18b9018 (`testing/2026-10-05-1425-verify-v2.4.0-gate-r4.md`); main-agent rows and every mutation run in `testing/2026-10-05-verify-v2.4.0-gate-rows-r2.md`. ## Not covered

The new key's private file at `~/.ssh/styrman-release_ed25519` has no passphrase yet (the operator sets it). The operator deleted the `dave` GitHub key (161370382) at ~13:27Z; the same key was re-added at 13:29:05Z (165439402), by nothing on this box; the operator is removing it and what re-adds it on dave.

## Summary
The release gate's reviewer and security agents reviewed v2.6.2..13c5bde. Nothing blocked; every finding was low. The operator chose what went in. Round 1 fixes:
- **BUG-171:** a bad `--vendor` is a usage error, exit 2, for every verb before the verb does anything. Before, `update` fetched and pulled the checkout first and exited 1, `--dry-run` never checked the value, `status` exited 1, and `uninstall` and `report` took any word.

- **The command-line credential rule, three more shapes (operator's choice):**
  - an escaped `\n`, `\r` or `\t` written out before the flag;
  - a quote around the user and the password;
  - six clients' password flags: mongosh/mongo and sqlcmd `-p`/`-P`, an LDAP tool's `-w`, OpenSSL's `pass:`, keytool's `-storepass`/`-keypass` and lftp's `-u user,password`.

Round 2 verified all six fixes and reached the review cap. The operator chose "Fix small ones, no round 3":
- OpenSSL's `pass:` is caught inside quotes too.
- Five harmless over-redactions are pinned.
- README and the local deploy guide now say `update --vendor all` widens a single-vendor install.

Amber is now the loop on this machine: `~/.config/sh-agent/` and `/retro --harness`. The project `AGENTS.md` rule 1 is now "Three ways in, no way back". `delivery.md` § The loop back became § What stays on the machine.

## Type
task (plan phase)

## Files changed
from git diff --numstat (+830 −534 in the working tree; the two deleted files on top)
- `internal/harness/report.go` (−1,102), `internal/harness/report_test.go` (−1,584): deleted

- Tests: `TestHarnessMap` requires install, update and dream, and refuses `report` both as a verb and on the map, along with the feedback repository; `TestMainExitStatus` gains `report is gone` (exit 1, `unknown command "report"`); `TestReorder`'s value-flag rows use `dream --project` instead of `report --feedback-repo`; deleted: `TestUpdateKeptCloneCleanupOnlyWhenUpdating`, `TestReportWithoutCheckout`, `TestReleaseBinaryUpdateShedsKeptClone`, `TestReportOnReleaseBinaryIgnoresRepoFlags`, `TestThrowawayParentIsPrivate`, `TestSweepInterruptedClonesGlobCharsInHome`, `TestResolveSourceLenient`, the report rows of `TestUsageErrorsExit2` and `TestFromZipRefusedOnOtherCommands`, the record half of `TestEmbeddedInstallStateAndRecord` (now `TestEmbeddedInstallState`)

- The redaction tests kept every case that exercises `Redact`, `RedactJSONL` or the line redactor. The shape, over-redaction and benign near-miss lists are byte-identical to the old ones (checked with diff). The cases that exercised `redactDocument` were dropped. That function redacted `state.json` for report alone, so it would have been dead code (review-standards). Two state.json cases went from `TestReportRedactStructuralGaps`, one from `TestReportRedactCleanIsByteIdentical`, and the first two of `TestReportRedactDocument`. Its third case, a needle in a JSON key, is now `TestRedactKeyHit`.

That guard is the only hit of the plan's `git grep -n 'styrman-harness-feedback' -- ':!.agents/docs' ':!skills/google-catalog/catalog'`.

none. The plan's Phase 5 holds the Definition of Done over the whole feature: the `verifier` log, `reviewer --code --docs` and `security`. This phase's diff was read by the main agent only.

- Tests first: `go test ./internal/redact` without `redact.go` failed (`undefined: redactLines`, `marker`, `redactedValue`), then passed with it. `TestHarnessMap` and `TestMainExitStatus/report_is_gone` failed before the code went (`the binary still has a report verb`, exit 0) and passed after.

Every file above. The ADR is ADR-062, which covered this removal from Phase 0. The map, the code and the docs land in this one commit (project `AGENTS.md` rule 3).

# fyr Phase 2: Claude Code leaves the binary     (date: 2026-10-24)

## Summary
`sh-agent` installs into the Antigravity CLI only (ADR-062, plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` Phase 2, D7, D14, D17). `Plan` and `Install` lost their vendor argument. Nothing is planned or written under `~/.claude`, and the `CLAUDE.md` stub is gone. `--vendor` is gone from every verb, so passing it is a usage error, exit 2. `~/.claude/settings.json` is never read or written: `settings.go` is deleted, so the attribution and auto-compact keys an older install wrote stay as the operator's. An install over an older manifest sheds that manifest's `~/.claude` files through the existing resync, unchanged. A symlink, or a path under a linked directory, stays, and `~/.claude` itself stays in `pruneEmptyDirs`' stop map. `memory show` prints the index only. `dream` always runs `agy`, reads skills from `~/.gemini/config/skills` and reads transcripts from Antigravity's conversations only. `metrics ingest` reads Antigravity only. `show`, `report` and the dream summary have one `agy` column. A second column, `claude (historical)`, appears only when the window holds rows an older ingest stored (D7). Nothing deletes those rows, and `export` writes them as before.

## Type
task (plan phase)

## Files changed
from `git diff --numstat` (+1,172 −1,784 in the working tree, deleted files included)
- Deleted: `internal/harness/settings.go`, `internal/harness/settings_test.go`, `cmd/sh-agent/settings_test.go`, `internal/metrics/claude.go`, `internal/metrics/claude_test.go`
- `internal/harness/plan.go`: one target. `VendorAll`, `VendorClaude`, `NormalizeVendor`, `KeepForeign`, `IsOurs` and `ClaudeRoot` are gone. `VendorAntigravity` stays, so the manifest still records it.
- `internal/harness/apply.go`: `Install(src, home, files, dryRun, out)`. The foreign-file branches are gone. The stop map names `~/.claude` as a literal, with the reason beside it.
- `internal/harness/{render,state,adopt,inventory,frontmatter}.go`: the stub constant goes. The manifest's `Vendor` is written `antigravity`, and an old value is read and ignored. `adopt` no longer looks in `~/.claude/skills`. Comments changed.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`: the `--vendor` flag, `resolveVendor`, `ctx.vendor`, the settings calls, the foreign-`CLAUDE.md` note and the `claude` status line are gone. `installPassArgs` forwards `--home` alone. Usage text changed.
- `internal/memory/memory.go`: `Show(dir)`. The native-memory hint and `nativeOn` are gone.
- `internal/dream/{dream,collect,run,metrics,timer}.go`: `command()` is agy-only, and the private HOME and the stream-json stdin are unconditional. `answer(stdout)`. The Claude transcript reader is gone. The summary counts sessions over every column.
- `internal/metrics`: `writer.go` is new and holds the writer helpers `agy.go` shares, moved verbatim from `claude.go`. `ingest.go` reads agy only. `show.go` has `Columns` and the `historical` column, with lazily made count maps. `numbers.go` and `report.go` follow the columns; the report's series and tables are built per summary, and Antigravity keeps colour slot 2. `store.go` and `agy.go` comments changed.
- `internal/search/dream.go`: one comment.
- Tests, new: `TestPlanAntigravityOnly`, `TestResyncShedsOldClaudeFiles`, `TestInstallLeavesClaudeCodeAlone`, `TestUpdateRefusesTheVendorFlagFirst` (BUG-171's rule, kept for the flag that no longer exists), `TestInstallPassArgsForwardsTheHomeOnly`, the six `--vendor agy` rows of `TestUsageErrorsExit2`, `TestShowHistoricalColumn`, `TestShowAgyOnly`, `TestReportAgyOnly`, `TestAgyIdentifiersAreNameShaped`, `TestIngestPrintsNoControlOrFormatCharacters`.
- Tests, moved onto Antigravity fixtures: `TestSourceLabelAndOutcome`, `TestOutcomeStampedAfterTheRun`, `TestMetricsVerb` (with a decoy `HOME`, for R6), every dream run test (`fakeAgy`), and the dream collect tests (`agyConversations`, whose schema both readers accept).
- Tests, historical: `historical_test.go`'s `historicalRows` inserts what an old ingest stored, for the show, report and numbers tests.
- Tests, deleted: the Claude transcript, settings, stub, foreign-`CLAUDE.md`, vendor-selection and native-memory-hint tests.
- Docs (the `documentation` agent): `README.md`, `specs/sh-agent/{metrics,memory-loop,dream}.md`, `deploy/{local,remote}.md`, `testing/guide.md`. `memory-loop.md` § Known differences is retired. Main agent: `AGENTS.md` lines 7, 39 and 44, and one `memory-loop.md` phrase.
- Plan: Phase 2's two work boxes are ticked. The checkpoint stays open (below).

## Deviations from the plan's box
- **The checkpoint's grep is met in part.** `git grep -il claude -- 'cmd' 'internal' '*.go'` lists 17 files. Expected among them: the stop-map entry (`apply.go`, with the resync comment of `Install`), the historical column (`main.go:65` and `internal/metrics/{ingest,report,show,store}.go` with their tests) and the stop-map tests. Not expected:
  - the Claude Code agent format: `derive.go`, `inventory.go` lines 23, 225 and 234, and `harness_test.go` lines 43, 155, 2351–2371 and 2439. Phase 3a deletes it (D3, D17).
  - the listing-budget comments: `catalog_test.go:671` and `size_test.go:90`. The 19,500-byte budget rests on Claude Code's listing; Antigravity's is about 44,000.
  - `internal/search/testdata/recall.tsv` rows 19 and 39 (D20).
  The box stays open until Phase 3a lands or the operator amends it.
- The "tests first" red was a build failure of the old tests against the new API in six packages, not a test-by-test red. Each removed symbol appears in `.agents/scratch/fyr/go-test-phase2-red.txt`.
- `State.Vendor` is still written, as `antigravity`, rather than dropped. `skills/init-project` and `skills/dream` grep for it until Phase 3b removes the check.
- `metrics.DefaultContextTarget` keeps 300,000. Its other half, the auto-compact window, went with `settings.go`, and so did `TestAutoCompactWindowIsTheContextTarget`.
- The `testing/guide.md` three-sandbox kit (§ 4, Claude Code runs) is left for Phase 3b. `memory-loop.md`'s `/init-project` rows are the skill's, also Phase 3b.

## Agents dispatched
- `documentation`: the README, specs, deploy and testing-guide edits. Its diff was read against the code by the main agent. One claim it kept ("Antigravity prompts … for paths outside the workspace") was already in the old text.
- The plan's Phase 5 holds the Definition of Done over the whole feature: the `verifier` log, `reviewer --code --docs` and `security`. This phase's code diff was read by the main agent only.

## Verification
- Full suite: `gofmt -l cmd internal` empty, `go vet ./...` ok, `go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30m ./...` exit 0, all 9 packages ok (`.agents/scratch/fyr/go-test-phase2.txt`). It ran on go1.24.4 (`~/.local/bin/go` still dangles). `govulncheck` reports the same 15 standard-library advisories as Phase 1, all fixed in later Go (`.agents/scratch/fyr/govulncheck-p2.txt`).
- Fresh scratch home (`.agents/scratch/fyr/home-p2`): `go run ./cmd/sh-agent install --home …` exit 0, 896 files, and no `.claude` directory. The installed binary's `status` exits 0 with `drift none — 895 files match the repo`, and the `binary` line has no warning. The `installed` line no longer prints a vendor.
- Crossing, local half (`.agents/scratch/fyr/home-p2-old`):
  - The `HEAD` build (from `git archive a60f83a`) installed 897 files under `.claude`, 896 of them in its manifest, and created `settings.json`.
  - This tree's install then exited 0 with `896 removed`, each reported as `remove  ~/.claude/… (no longer in the source)`.
  - `~/.claude` and `settings.json` stayed, untouched. The new manifest has vendor `antigravity` and no `.claude` entry, and `status` reports `drift none`.
- The usage rows prove that `--vendor agy` exits 2 with `flag provided but not defined: -vendor` on install, status, uninstall, dream, memory show, metrics ingest and update (checkout, dry run, zip). No checkout moved.

## Docs
Every file above. The map's node labels changed text only: no line or node was added, removed or rerouted (rule 3), and `TestHarnessMap` passes. The ADR is ADR-062.

# fyr Phase 3a: agents native, the lint, the context and rules     (date: 2026-10-24)

## Summary
Agents are authored as `agents/<name>/agent.md` in Antigravity's format and installed as written; `derive.go` is gone (ADR-062, plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` Phase 3a, D3, D17, F6). Each of the eight files is `DeriveAgy`'s output at the phase's base commit `a2e6a5a`, generated into `.agents/scratch/fyr/derived/` before the derivation was deleted and compared with `cmp`. The lint keeps both allow-lists: `agentKeys` is now the derived keys (`name`, `description`, `subagent`, `mainAgent`, `model`, `tools`), so an old-format key such as `maxTurns` or `effort` is refused; `knownTools` is the six names the old `toolMap` produced; a harness agent sets `subagent: true` and `mainAgent: false`; a flat `agents/<name>.md`, an agent directory with no `agent.md`, and a symlinked `agent.md` are refused with the file named. The inventory prints an agent's `model` key as written, and nothing when it is absent. The global context and the two rules name one CLI: the `/goal` and `claude -p` clause, the `.claude/*` links, the `CLAUDE.md` stub and both `TaskStop` mentions are gone, and "a budget below the agent's `maxTurns`" is now "a tool-call budget" (D17). `# Compact instructions` is kept as prose. BUG-173: the committed `agy-rel` kit still passed `--vendor agy`, a usage error since Phase 2, and is fixed.

## Type
task (plan phase)

## Files changed
From `git diff HEAD -M --numstat` over the working tree:
- Agents: `agents/<name>.md` → `agents/<name>/agent.md` for all eight, each the derived file byte for byte. Git sees them as renames (−3/+4 lines each: the format keys).
- Deleted: `internal/harness/derive.go`; `yamlQuote` in `frontmatter.go` (its only caller was `DeriveAgy`).
- `internal/harness/inventory.go`: `LoadAgents` reads `agents/<name>/agent.md` through `readRegular` (a symlinked `agent.md` is refused). New: `agentKeys`, `knownTools`, the subagent and mainAgent check, and the refusals of a flat file and a missing `agent.md`. `RenderInventory` and `RenderInventoryCompact` print the model as written.
- `internal/harness/plan.go`: an agent is copied from `a.Raw`.
- Tests: `agents_test.go` is new. `harness_test.go`, `pathguard_test.go`, `source_test.go` and `zip_test.go` moved to native fixtures. `TestDeriveAgy`, `TestDeriveAgyRealReviewer` and `TestYamlQuoteEscapesControlCharacters` are deleted.
- `context/AGENTS.md`: lines 3, 15, 31, 35, 39 and 64.
- Docs: `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` (§ Antigravity derivation becomes § Agents), `specs/sh-agent/memory-loop.md`, `testing/guide.md`.
- Fixture: `internal/search/testdata/recall.tsv` gold paths.
- Kit: `testing/agy-rel/run.sh` (BUG-173).
- Trail: BUG-173, BUG-174 and the INDEX rows; `testing/2026-10-24-verify-fyr-agents.md`; the plan's ticks.

## Deviations from the plan's box
- **Byte-equality is a one-time `cmp`, not a standing test.** The derived files live in gitignored scratch, so a test that read them would fail on every other checkout. `TestCheckoutAgentsAreNative` and the lint pin the shape that stays: the keys, `subagent`/`mainAgent`, the known tools, and the reviewer's skill path.
- **No standing check of an agent body's skill path.** The derivation rewrote `~/.claude/skills/` in bodies. Nothing is rewritten now, and a lint for that string would name the old CLI in the code. The reviewer's Antigravity path is pinned by `TestCheckoutAgentsAreNative`, and every other agent names no skill path.
- **Lint wording.** The lint and its tests name "the format before ADR-062", never the old CLI, so Phase 2's checkpoint grep lists only its expected hits plus D24's exemptions. That box is ticked.
- **Two agent bodies still name the old CLI** (`dreamer`: `~/.claude/AGENTS.md`; `verifier`: "Claude Code's maximum"). They are kept byte-equal by D17, and Phase 3b edits them.
- **`recall.tsv` was edited before Phase 4a.** `TestRecallQuestionsAreWellFormed` stats every gold path, and the moved agents and the deleted `derive.go` broke it. Row 39 waits for Phase 4a.
- **The behavioural log's status is FAIL.** Every row is stated as n of N, and the cause is BUG-174, which predates this phase (base-tree control 0/2). Its fix is the operator's call.

## Agents dispatched

# fyr Phase 4a: the rename in the tree, mechanical     (date: 2026-10-25)

## Summary
The tree is `fyr` (plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` Phase 4a, D12, D15, D22):
- module `github.com/kesokaj/fyr`, root package `fyr`, the binary at `cmd/fyr`;
- every path into the state directory reads `harness.StateDir` (`.config/fyr`);
- search honours `.fyr-noindex` and still honours the old `.sh-agent-noindex`;
- `fyr` reads `FYR_*` only, and names each set `SH_AGENT_*` variable once on stderr.

The living text says `fyr`. A scratch-home install from this tree is `fyr`: `~/.local/bin/fyr`, `~/.config/fyr/state.json`, `drift none` (§ 3 and § 3a). No migration exists yet. That is Phase 4b's, along with the release names, the dream unit names and `deploy/remote.md`.

## Type
task (plan phase)

## Files changed
From `git show --stat c565b27` (117 files, +1147 −918; Go: 70 files, +758 −531):
- **Moves (`git mv`):**
  - `cmd/sh-agent/` → `cmd/fyr/`;
  - `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/` → `specs/fyr/`;
  - `testing/sh-agent-matrix.md` → `testing/fyr-matrix.md`;
  - `skills/google-catalog/catalog/.sh-agent-noindex` → `.fyr-noindex`.
- **Go:**
  - `go.mod` and every import path.
  - `package styrman` → `fyr` (`embed.go` and the root tests), and `source.go`'s alias.
  - `internal/harness/state.go`: new `const StateDir`. Every `filepath.Join(…, ".config", "sh-agent", …)` in code and tests now reads it; `metrics` imports `harness` for it.
  - `internal/search/reconcile.go`: `noIndexMarker = ".fyr-noindex"`, `oldNoIndexMarker = ".sh-agent-noindex"`, `isNoIndexMarker`. The header says `left out by a noindex marker:`.
  - `cmd/fyr/main.go`: `oldEnvNotices`, called from `main` outside the rebuilt child. `SH_AGENT_REPO` → `FYR_REPO` and `SH_AGENT_CHILD` → `FYR_CHILD`; the test-only variables were renamed too.
  - `internal/metrics/{verb,show}.go`: a `fyr` verb table (no `report`). The `sh-agent` table is kept, and `isSQLiteVerb` counts both names: earlier transcripts and stored rows carry `sh-agent search` (D7, D20).
  - `internal/harness/render.go`: the context marker line. `internal/redact`: `[redacted by fyr]`.
  - Every message, comment and doc comment naming the binary.
- **Content:** `context/AGENTS.md` (5 mentions); the 5 agent bodies that named the binary; the skills (`sh-agent` → `fyr`, `~/.config/sh-agent` → `~/.config/fyr`); `google-catalog/catalog/MANIFEST.md`'s hand-written Notes line; `refresh-catalog.sh` (the marker it writes).
- **Docs:**
  - `README.md` (title, quick start, verbs table, map labels, layout);
  - `AGENTS.md` (title, rules, setup commands, layout, key files);
  - `deploy/local.md`;
  - `specs/fyr/*.md` (search.md describes both markers; delivery.md says the tags through v2.7.0 ship `sh-agent`);
  - `testing/{guide.md,skill-matrix.md,kit-preamble.sh,agy-rel/run.sh}` (the wrapper is `fyr`, the grant is `command(fyr)`);
  - `fyr-matrix.md` (title, one note, one command cell);
  - `.gitignore` (`/fyr`).
- **Fixture:** `internal/search/testdata/recall.tsv` (gold paths under `cmd/fyr/`).

## Left for Phase 4b, and kept as history
The Phase 4a grep (`git grep -n 'sh-agent'` over the living files) lists these, each kept on purpose:
- **The old marker** and its test: `reconcile.go`, `search_test.go` (`TestOldNoIndexMarkerStillCounts`), `specs/fyr/search.md` (D12).
- **The env notice:** `main.go`, `usage_test.go`, `harness_test.go`, in upper case (`SH_AGENT_`), so the lower-case grep does not list them (D15).
- **`deploy/remote.md`:** rewritten in 4b.
- **The release names, 4b's `release.go` box:**
  - `release.go`'s asset name, `ReleaseRepo` and sums marker, and `release_test.go`;
  - README's § Install without cloning and § Install from a zip, which describe the published v2.7.0 assets. They were restored to their text at `5da24a5` after the scripted pass, so that no step mixes an old asset with the new installed name.
- **The dream unit names, 4b's timer box:** `sh-agent-dream` and `com.styrman.sh-agent-dream` in `timer.go`, `timer_test.go`, `memory_test.go`, `deploy/local.md:69` and `specs/fyr/dream.md:49`. Their text and the binary path in the unit are `fyr`.
- **History:**
  - `internal/metrics/{verb,show}.go` and `verb_test.go`: the old verb name (D20's historical-metrics exemption);
  - `fyr-matrix.md`'s dated records, which quote what the binary printed then, as its new note says;
  - the plan names `sh-agent-works-everywhere` and `recon-sh-agent-audit`: trail file names, in `apply.go:83`, `harness_test.go:1600` and the matrix.
- **The repository name `styrman-harness`:** clone URLs, `ReleaseRepo`, the README map's repository node, `errPlainCopy` and `adopt`'s message. The repository is renamed in Phase 6, and the release identity in 4b.

## Deviations from the plan's box
Recorded as plan D28 (by: implementer, open to the operator's veto).
- **Release names and timer unit names stay** (above). The box's grep expectation did not list them, but 4b's own boxes test and change them (`release.go`, "the timer rename"). Renaming them here would have done 4b's tests-first work without its tests.
- **The catalog's marker file was renamed** with `git mv`, and `refresh-catalog.sh` writes `.fyr-noindex`. The project `AGENTS.md` says the catalog changes only through its refresh script. The marker is the harness's own file, not an entry: `CHECKSUMS` does not cover it, and the script now writes what the tree holds. The MANIFEST's Notes line ("a new skill goes through `fyr adopt`") is hand-written text that the script keeps byte for byte.
- **The search header no longer names a marker file:** `left out by a noindex marker:`. With two names, either fixed name would be false for some directory.
- **`SH_AGENT_*` notices skip empty values.** An exported empty variable changes nothing.
- **The `fyr-matrix.md` records are not rewritten** (D8's reasoning applied to a living file's dated rows). A note says why.

## Agents dispatched
None. The main agent read its own diff. As in Phases 2, 3a and 3b, Phase 5 holds the `verifier`, `reviewer --code --docs` and `security` dispatches over the whole feature.

## Verification
`testing/2026-10-25-verify-fyr-rename.md` (PASS):
- red, then green, as the box asks;
- `gofmt` empty, `go vet` ok, `go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30m ./...` exit 0, all 9 packages;
- size pins 18,112 / 14,623 / 19,165;
- § 3 and § 3a scratch installs are `fyr`;
- govulncheck: 15 standard-library advisories of go1.24.4, the same on the base.

No Antigravity behavioural run; Phase 5 owes it.

## Process note
The rename commit was first written with a `Claude-Session:` trailer, against the global git rule (author from the local config only, no session links). It was amended before the push. The pushed `c565b27` carries none.

# fyr Phase 4b: migration, timers, release, the crossing guide     (date: 2026-10-25)

## Summary
A home on v2.7.0 now crosses to `fyr` with one `fyr install` (plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` Phase 4b, D13, D14, D29, D30):
- **The state directory moves first.** Every verb that writes under it renames `~/.config/sh-agent` to `~/.config/fyr` before anything opens it, and says `migrated ~/.config/sh-agent → ~/.config/fyr`.
  - Both present: neither is touched, and one line says fyr reads the new one (F3).
  - A symlinked old dir: the writing verb is refused (D30).
  - Read-only verbs and modes never migrate. They name the old dir once on stderr and read nothing from it.
- **The resync removes the old files.** It reads the old manifest from the moved dir and removes the `~/.claude` files and `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` by today's rule. A symlinked entry stays (F2).
- **The dream timer is renamed** `fyr-dream` / `com.fyr.dream`. `install` replaces this home's unit under the old name, installing the new unit first and removing the old one after.
- **The release names are fyr's.** Asset `fyr-<os>-<arch>`, `ReleaseRepo = "github.com/kesokaj/fyr"`, and one sums marker, `# fyr vX.Y.Z`. The old `# styrman-harness` marker is refused.
- **`deploy/remote.md` has § Crossing to fyr**, and its release step names `fyr-*`, `fyr-vX.Y.Z.zip` and the one marker.
- **The kit preamble watches both real state dirs** until every place has crossed.
- **BUG-176 and BUG-177 are recorded**, and BUG-176's line is fixed.

## Type
task (plan phase)

## Files changed
- **Go, new:**
  - `internal/harness/migrate.go`: `OldStateDir`, `MigrateStateDir`, `StateDirNotice`.
  - `internal/harness/migrate_test.go`: the four cases, plus the notice.
  - `cmd/fyr/migrate_test.go`: 11 writing and 16 read-only invocations, plus the symlink refusal stopping `install` before any write.
  - `cmd/fyr/crossing_test.go`: `TestCrossingFromV270`, which builds v2.7.0 from `git archive v2.7.0` and installs it with a dream unit, then runs one `fyr install` (D14). It skips without the tag, `go`, `git` or `tar`, and under `-short`.
- **Go, changed:**
  - `cmd/fyr/main.go`: `writesState` and `migrateStateDir` run before the source is resolved and on the `--from-zip` branch, after its refusals. `installFiles` calls `dream.ReplaceOldTimer` after the install. `stderr` is a test seam.
  - `internal/dream/timer.go`:
    - the new names, with `oldUnitName`/`oldPlistName`;
    - `namesFor` behind `UnitFor` and `oldUnitFor`;
    - `timerUnit` (`unitOn`, `present`, `remove`), shared by `RemoveTimer` and the new `ReplaceOldTimer`;
    - `LegacyTimerFiles` and its notice now name the old bare names.
  - `internal/harness/release.go`: the asset name, `ReleaseRepo` and the marker.
  - `statedir_test.go`: exempts the `OldStateDir` constant's line.
- **Tests renamed or extended:**
  - `timer_test.go` (new names; `TestReplaceOldTimer`, seven cases);
  - `release_test.go` (`fyr-*`, `# fyr`, the old-marker refusal, `TestReleaseNames`);
  - `zip_test.go`, `cmd/fyr/zip_test.go` (release zips `fyr-vX.Y.Z.zip`);
  - `catalog_test.go` (the guard cases for `~/.config/sh-agent`).
- **Content:**
  - `skills/bug/SKILL.md:55` (BUG-176);
  - `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:31` ("an installed command that changes its name" is a MAJOR).
- **Docs:**
  - `deploy/remote.md` (§ Crossing to fyr; every living command, asset, marker and `--repo`; the timer example `fyr-update.service`; v3.0.0 as a MAJOR);
  - `specs/fyr/delivery.md` § The model (the crossing claim, two sentences);
  - `README.md` § Install without cloning and § Install from a zip;
  - `deploy/local.md:69`, `specs/fyr/dream.md:49` (the timer names and the replacement);
  - `testing/kit-preamble.sh`, `testing/guide.md` § 4 (the guard).
- **Trail:**
  - `bugs/BUG-176-*.md`, `bugs/BUG-177-*.md` and their `INDEX.md` rows;
  - the plan (D30, Phase 4b ticked);
  - `testing/2026-10-25-verify-fyr-crossing-local.md`.

## Agents dispatched
- **`documentation`**: `remote.md`, `delivery.md`, README and the two timer docs.
  - The main agent read its diff and changed two things in `remote.md` § Crossing to fyr. The opening restated part of the delivery claim, so it now points at it in one sentence (project `AGENTS.md` rule 6).
  - The checkout place's `go run ./cmd/fyr install` gained `--repo "$PWD"`. Without it, the dev box's home, last installed by the v2.7.0 release binary, is refused by `knownCheckout`.
- **No review dispatches**, as in Phases 2 to 4a: Phase 5 holds `verifier`, `reviewer --code --docs` and `security` over the whole feature. The main agent read its own diff.

## Verification
`testing/2026-10-25-verify-fyr-crossing-local.md`: PASS. In short:
- **Red first.** The new tests failed to compile, and with the migration test set aside, seven release and zip tests failed on behaviour.
- **Mutations.** Dropping `dream` from the writing verbs fails `TestStateDirMigrationByVerb`. Skipping `ReplaceOldTimer` fails `TestCrossingFromV270`. The preamble at HEAD fails the three new guard cases.
- **Full suite** under `-race`: exit 0.
- **The checkpoint crossing.** A scratch home was installed by a release-built v2.7.0 with a dream unit, behind a recording fake `systemctl`, then migrated by one `go run ./cmd/fyr install`. Result: 897 old files removed, the timer replaced, `fyr status` clean with `drift none`.
- **The release-step dry run** (`remote.md` steps 1 to 3, version v9.9.9, scratch) lists the three `fyr-*` binaries, `fyr-v9.9.9.zip` and `SHA256SUMS` with one marker line. The zip check printed CHECKED.
- **The real home.** `~/.config/sh-agent` and its units were untouched, and no `~/.config/fyr` was created.

## Deviations from the plan's boxes
Recorded as plan D30 (by: implementer, open to the operator's veto):
- **A symlinked `~/.config/sh-agent` refuses a writing verb.** Interfaces named only the plain-directory case.
- **The read-only notice goes to stderr**, and `migrated …` goes to stdout.
- **The timer replacement uses the installing shell's PATH.** A refused new unit keeps the old one and fails the install.
- **`LegacyTimerFiles` looks for the old bare names only.**
- **The bug-skill line says "names a tool-call budget"**, not the box's "a tool-call budget the dispatch names", which would repeat its subject.
- **The global preflight skill names the rule, not the tag.** `v3.0.0` is named in `deploy/remote.md` § Releases. Step 6's bridge check had no `sh-agent` wording to drop.

## Not built, named for Phase 5
- **`uninstall` and `dream --remove-timer` leave an old-named unit.** Before a crossing install it is named nowhere.
- **F4:** `status` does not name a leftover `sh-agent` on PATH. § Crossing to fyr checks it with `ls`.
- **No Antigravity behavioural run** of the changed skills (`bug`, `preflight`). Phase 5 and preflight's rule owe it.

## Summary
Plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` Phase 5 (D29 item 5, D31). The tree is `fyr`, it targets the Antigravity CLI only, and the only path off the machine is the dreamer's redacted prompt. It is gated for release, pending Phase 6.

  - Every finding is fixed, rebutted or left in the report's `## Outcome`.
- **The dream timer's rename respects a timer the operator turned off.** `install` replaces an old-named unit only when the service manager says it is on. When it answers `disabled`/`masked` (systemd) or `Could not find service` (launchd), only the old files go and no fyr timer is turned on. A manager that cannot be asked counts as on.
- **One repository name.** The clone URL is `git@github.com:kesokaj/fyr.git` in README, both deploy guides, `adopt`'s message and `errPlainCopy`. The map's repository node is relabelled `fyr`, and `TestOneRepositoryName` pins it.

  - Antigravity tool names in three agent bodies.
  - The crossing guide says no content is compared before the old `~/.claude` files go.
- **Antigravity.** 17 rows and one re-run, 18 of 18 PASS: the canary, the eight agents, and the content rows (`handoff`, `project-context`, `init-bare`, `review`, `preflight`, `feedback`, `project-memory`, `bug`). E2E 1, 3 and 4: yes.

## Type
task (plan phase)

# Metrics Phase 1: one reference per trail item     (date: 2026-10-25)

## Summary
Phase 1 of `PLAN-2026-10-25-1754-plan-metrics-fed-at-every-checkpoint-joined-to-r`. A `handoff`, `verifier` or `review` event's `ref` is now the trail item's record ID. For a file, that is the ID `fyr record import` gives it: `brain.ImportedID(kind, stem)`, the kind's prefix, a dash, `slugOf(stem)`; the import's classify now calls the same function. Every ingest first rewrites, inside the join's transaction, the file-name refs an older ingest stored (`*.md`) to that ID form, and deletes a row whose ID form the session already holds. A ref already in ID form is left alone, even one ending in `.md`. No schema change (D10). Phase 2 (the join reads records) builds on this.

## Type
task

## Files changed
from git diff --numstat
- internal/brain/import.go — `ImportedID`, used by classify
- internal/brain/import_test.go — `TestImportedID`: five stems (space, `+`, upper case, trailing `.`), each against both the literal ID and the ID a dry-run import gives the file
- internal/metrics/events.go — `fileRef`, `rewriteFileRefs`; the file join writes ID-form refs; metrics now imports `internal/brain`
- internal/metrics/events_test.go — `TestJoinEvents` wants ID-form refs; `TestJoinFilesRefs`, `TestRefRewrite` new
- .agents/trail.jsonl — SPEC-fyr-metrics: the `events` payload table and a "One reference per trail item" invariant with its two known limits

## Agents dispatched
none. The plan puts reviewer, security and verifier at Done, over the whole feature. I read this phase's diff myself.

## Verification
- Unit: `go test -race -run TestImportedID ./internal/brain/`, `go test -race -run 'TestJoinEvents|TestRefRewrite|TestJoinFilesRefs' ./internal/metrics/` pass. Mutations each caught, then restored: `ImportedID` without the slug (TestImportedID), no rewrite call (TestRefRewrite), basename refs (TestJoinFilesRefs, TestRefRewrite), no duplicate delete (TestRefRewrite).
- Full suite: `gofmt -l cmd internal && go vet ./... && go test -race -timeout 30m ./...` exit 0, every package ok (2026-10-25). govulncheck not re-run: no module was added (metrics now imports internal/brain, already in the module graph).
- E2E criterion 2 on copies (`.agents/scratch/e2e2-home`, this box's `metrics.db` and `brain.db`, read through a read-only query tool in scratch whose slug rule is a separate copy): before, 276 trail events with a `.md` ref and 0 items held twice. After one ingest by the new binary (exit 0, 6 events added): 0 `.md` refs, 0 held twice, trail events 276 → 278 (none lost). A second ingest: 0 events added, same counts. Must-fail check: on another copy with one ID-form duplicate injected, the check reported 1; after one ingest it reported 0. So the duplicate delete also ran on real data.

## Deviations
- Reading my own diff, I found that a ref already in ID form and ending in `.md` (`HANDOFF-notes.md`, from a file `notes.md.md`) would be rewritten again on the next ingest (`HANDOFF-handoff-notes`), which broke idempotence. I wrote the failing case into `TestRefRewrite`, then made the fix (skip ID-form refs; `GLOB` instead of the case-insensitive `LIKE`) before the commit. Accepted limit, in the spec: an old file whose name is itself ID-shaped (`HANDOFF-x.md`) keeps its file-name ref.
- The plan's interface comment on `ImportedID` mentions a `-N` collision suffix. The import itself refuses two files that slug alike (classify); the `-N` is what `slugOf` leaves room for. The doc comment says it is not reproduced, as the plan does.

## Requirements
R4 (no schema change; the store's rows rewritten in place, none rebuilt), R6 (every test and run on a scratch home).

## Summary
Phase 2 of `PLAN-2026-10-25-1754-plan-metrics-fed-at-every-checkpoint-joined-to-r`. A migrated project's handoff, verifier, review and bug events now come from its records, not its files (D4). A record is placed by the minute stamped in its ID, read in the machine's zone, never by `updated` (D3, D15). A verifier event needs both the verifier's title and a `## Status:` heading (D12). A bug event needs a commit its body cites. Corrections now come from the global `feedback` records and `feedback.jsonl` for every root, whether migrated, unmigrated or gone (D11). They are keyed by `ts` in UTC, so one entry held by both sources counts once. Correction refs an older ingest stored with an offset are rewritten in place (D20). If a migrated root's records can't be read, that is a note: `records not read: <root>: <reason>`, ingest exit 0, and the root's stored events stay.

task

- E2E on copies (`.agents/scratch/e2e-p2-home`: this box's `metrics.db`, `brain.db`, `feedback.jsonl`, `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli`). See Deviations for the session windows. # Metrics feature Done: review, security, verification     (date: 2026-10-25)

## Summary
The Done section of `PLAN-2026-10-25-1754-plan-metrics-fed-at-every-checkpoint-joined-to-r` (roadmap item 2). It covers the whole feature, 811442c..33c652a: Phase 1 (68870aa), Phase 2 (000233f), Phase 3 (a225df7) and Phase 4 (33c652a), with their handoff commits. A reviewer (code and docs lenses) and a security review each read that range, one fix landed, and the verifier ran after it. The fix: the metrics store now opens every transaction `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. The join's transaction begins with reads (the two ref rewrites from Phases 1 and 2). As a deferred transaction, a concurrent ingest's commit would make its first write fail at once with SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT, without waiting out the busy timeout. Ingests at every handoff and `/retro` make that concurrency routine. The plan is closed and leaves ROADMAP Now.

## Type
task

## Files changed
from git diff --numstat (this change only; the feature's own files are in the four phase change records)

## Agents dispatched
- `reviewer` (`--code --docs`, range 811442c..33c652a): `REVIEW-2026-10-25-2008-review-811442c-33c652a-code-docs-2026-10-25`. APPROVE WITH NITS, two low findings. - `security` (same range): `REVIEW-2026-10-25-2008-security-review-811442c-33c652a-2026-10-25`. FINDINGS, three low, nothing medium or higher. ## Verification
- `TestTxTakesWriteLockAtBegin` FAILED before the fix ("a second connection wrote while the store's transaction was open") and passes after it. `go test -race ./internal/metrics/ ./internal/dream/` exit 0 after the fix.
- Verifier: PASS. `gofmt -l cmd internal` printed nothing; `go vet ./...` exit 0; `go test -race -count=1 -v -timeout 30m ./...` exit 0 (798 pass, 0 fail, 6 skip, all 10 packages ok, go1.24.4); the ten named tests of the feature ran and passed; `govulncheck` exit 3 with 15 reachable advisories, all standard library on go1.24.4 (environment), none in a third-party module; scratch-home `fyr install` and `fyr status`: `binary` line without a warning, drift none; every changed Go function in the range has a covering test.

Every code finding is fixed with a test that fails without the fix (must-fail runs by reverting each fix, 2026-10-25); one half-finding rebutted, one left to the operator.
- **`trail.Log` passes `--no-textconv`** (`internal/trail/trail.go`): `fyr check`'s `git log -G` over `.agents/trail.jsonl` no longer starts a textconv driver the checkout's own `.gitattributes` picks (security finding 1, medium). Every `Log` caller gets it. `--no-ext-diff`, added in round 1, was removed after round 2: `git log` runs an external diff only with `--ext-diff` (checked on git 2.47.3). Tests: `TestLogRunsNoTextconv`, `TestSpecRuleRunsNoTextconv`.
- **Rule (b)** (`internal/check/specs.go`): the `-G` pattern quotes the ID and the stamp with `regexp.QuoteMeta`, because `-G` compiles an extended regex, so a `+02:00` stamp is literal (`breQuote` removed; both reviews). A failed `git log` or `git rev-list` for a spec is now a `note: <ID>: git … failed: spec not checked`, not a silent pass. Tests: `TestSpecRuleOffsetStamp`, `TestSpecRuleGitFailureIsANote`.
- **Rule (a) paths** (`internal/check/docs.go`): `splitLine` strips every trailing `/`, so a Go before 1.25.12 cannot follow a symlink out of the `os.Root` (GO-2026-4970). Test: `TestDocsRuleTrailingSlashAfterASymlink`, which fails without the fix on go1.24.4.
- **Reads** (`internal/check/check.go`, `open_unix.go`, `open_other.go`): `readFile` Lstats, then opens through `openRegular`, which opens non-blocking and checks the opened handle. `lineCount` reads through it, so a FIFO swapped in cannot hang the run. Test: `TestReadsRefuseAFIFO`.
- **Scanner** (`internal/check/scan.go`): `spans` indexes a line's backtick runs once, so the scan is linear. Its output matched the old scanner on 200,000 random lines. Test: `TestSpansLinearOnUnclosedRuns`: 0.07 s, against 5.8 s for the old scanner.
