# fyr eval Phase 1: internal/eval (suite, sandbox, safety checks, runner) and GUIDE-eval     (date: 2026-10-26-0740)

## Summary

Phase 1 of `PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-plan-fyr-eval-the-antigravity-run-kit-as-a-verb` (roadmap item 4).

The operator approved the plan, the R8 text (D4), the Non-goals text (D4b) and O1–O3 at their defaults: "go all approved". That approval is recorded as D31, with the approval box ticked and ROADMAP Now updated.

The new package `internal/eval` ports `.agents/kit/agy-rel/run.sh` and `.agents/kit/kit-preamble.sh` to Go. `cmd` does not use it yet; the verb comes in Phase 2. It has:
- `ParseSuite`, `SelectRows` and `Expand`, for the seven-column `GUIDE-eval` table and its four placeholders;
- the safety checks a–f: refused roots, outside every checkout, the real-config fingerprint, credentials against a baseline, leftover processes through `/proc` (with a named gap elsewhere), and the agent-invoked bytes search;
- `Preflight`, and `Run` with steps 0–16 against any `agy` on PATH.

The harness's own suite is the new `guide` record `GUIDE-eval`, with 29 rows. It holds run.sh's 16 case-list rows and `project-memory`, plus the 13 matrix rows run.sh read from `GUIDE-skill-matrix`, ported with D21, D23, D25 and D27.

## Type
feature

## Files changed
From `git status` and `git diff --numstat`; all of `internal/eval/` is new.
- internal/eval/suite.go — `Row`, `ParseSuite` (the table grammar, the note rule D23, the refusals), `SelectRows`, `Expand` (D21)
- internal/eval/guard.go — check a `checkRoots` with `resolve` and `nearestExisting`; check b `outsideCheckout` and `withoutGit`; check c `fingerprint` (over `harness.StateDir` and `harness.OldStateDir`) and `changedPaths`
- internal/eval/creds.go — check d: `scanCreds` and `newCreds`, the preamble's name, path and content shapes counted per kind, the ELF and Mach-O skip, AWS's example key set aside (D17)
- internal/eval/procs_linux.go, procs_other.go — check e: `leftoverProcs` (cwd, exe, exact `HOME=`; SIGTERM; eval and its ancestors skipped); off Linux, the named gap (O1); `ProcsChecked`
- internal/eval/invoked.go — check f: `"TypeName":"<agent>"` in `conversations/*.db` (D11, D24)
- internal/eval/run.go — `Options`, `Result`, the reason strings, `SandboxRoot`, `Preflight`, `Run`, and steps 1–16 per row (`prepare`, `session`, `agy`, `afterSession`, `unlink`, `exitChecks`); agy's environment is the D27 allowlist
- internal/eval/*_test.go — the tests listed under Verification; `testmain_test.go` drops `GIT_*` as the other packages do
- ROADMAP.md — Now: approved, then Phase 1 done, Phase 2 next
- .agents/trail.jsonl — the plan (Status; the approval box and Phase 1's boxes ticked with evidence; D31–D33; O1–O3 marked answered); the new `GUIDE-eval`; this record

## Agents dispatched
None. The plan puts `reviewer` (`--code --docs`), `security` (exec, suite parsing, credentials, the token link; D30) and `verifier` in its Done section, over the whole feature range. For this phase I read the diff myself. That read found two defects before the commit, and both are fixed: a `Mkdir` error other than "exists" was reported as `sandbox exists`, and `{{STAMP}}` was taken at the session's start instead of the row's.

## Verification
- A1, on the operator's two kept homes (read only): the bytes search and `strings | grep -c` agree. `lane-reviewer-p1` gives 9 and 9 for `reviewer` and 0 and 0 for the others; `project-memory-5` gives 0 and 0 for all three (`.agents/scratch/eval/a1.txt`).
- A5: `grep -ac 'BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY'` on the scratch home's `brain.db` counts 4. The plan's command, without `-a`, prints nothing and exits 1 on a binary file (D32). The preamble's `-aoE` patterns find 3 key headers and 15 copies of AWS's example key.
- Unit and integration tests, under `go test -race ./internal/eval/`:
  - the parser: `TestSuiteGrammar`, `TestSuiteRefusals` (14), `TestSuiteSelectRows`;
  - the guards: `TestGuardRefusedRoots` (the port of `catalog_test.go:2140-2170`), `TestGuardOutsideCheckout`, `TestGuardPreflight`, `TestGuardFingerprint` (7 changes, `eval/` ignored, a linked config directory);
  - credentials: `TestCredsLeftovers` (20 cases, the port of `:1719-1748`), `TestCredsNotCredentials`, `TestCredsBaseline`;
  - processes: `TestProcsLeftovers` (the port of `:2107-2127`);
  - the agent check: `TestInvoked`;
  - the runner, against a fake `agy` and a fake Self in `t.TempDir()` homes: `TestRunPass`, `TestRunVerdicts` (9), `TestRunWide`, `TestRunPrompt2`, `TestRunSetup`, `TestRunEarlyFailures` (4), `TestRunExitChecks`, `TestRunTimeout`, `TestRunInterrupted`, `TestRunRefusals` (7);
  - `TestRunRealFyrBaseline`, with a build of this checkout installed from this checkout: A5's string is in the sandbox's store (asserted), the row PASSes, and a written token FAILs it;
  - the suite and the package: `TestSuiteHarness`, `TestPrintableMatchesSearch`, `TestNoSQLiteDriver`.
  - The cross-build `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 go vet` and `go test -c` both pass.
- Must-fail state. Each check's body was replaced by a pass-through, run against `-run 'Guard|Creds|Procs|Invoked|Run'`, then restored (`.agents/scratch/eval/mutation.txt`):

  | check | tests that failed |
  |---|---|
  | a refused roots | `TestGuardRefusedRoots` |
  | b outside checkout | `TestGuardOutsideCheckout`, `TestGuardPreflight`, and every `TestRun*` (pre-flight's checkout test shares the function) |
  | c real config | `TestGuardFingerprint`, `TestRunExitChecks` |
  | d credentials | `TestCredsLeftovers`, `TestCredsNotCredentials`, `TestCredsBaseline`, `TestRunVerdicts`, `TestRunRealFyrBaseline` |
  | e processes | `TestProcsLeftovers`, `TestRunExitChecks` |
  | f agent invoked | `TestInvoked`, `TestRunVerdicts` |

- The `GUIDE-eval` port was compared mechanically in scratch. Every prompt, prompt2 and check equals run.sh's own strings: 33 fields, extracted by bash from the case arms, with `date` read as `{{STAMP}}` and `$M` as `{{CLONE}}/.agents/memory`. Each also equals the kit's own matrix extraction of `GUIDE-skill-matrix`: 26 fields. The setups were translated by hand and checked by reading and by `bash -n`, not by running; Phase 2's E2E runs them.
- `fyr check`: 0 findings.
- Checkpoint: `gofmt -l cmd internal && go vet ./... && go test -race -timeout 30m ./...` exited 0 at 2026-10-26-0740 (`gofmt -l` empty, 12 packages ok; `.agents/scratch/eval/checkpoint.log`). The first run, at 2026-10-26-0734, failed one test outside the package. `TestStateDirHasOneHome` (`statedir_test.go`) found the state directory spelled as a literal (`".config", "fyr"` and the old name) in `run.go` and three test files. Those paths, and `guard.go`'s fingerprint, now go through `harness.StateDir` and `harness.OldStateDir`, and the mutation table above was re-run after that change with the same result.
- Not covered:
  - any real `agy` run (Phase 2, E2E 1–3);
  - running the ported setups against the demo fixture: it is outside this repository, and the standing approval covers only reading `~/sandbox/agy-rel/homes`;
  - check e on macOS (O1: the named gap; only its build is checked);
  - a guard-a refusal through `Run` (unit-tested only: a sandbox root under `.config/fyr/eval` cannot be a parent of the real home, and guard b refuses a home inside the source tree first);
  - `govulncheck` (no new dependency).

## Deviations
- D32: implementation details settled inside the plan's interfaces. They are `Preflight` exported, `--no-hardlinks`, four extra suite refusals, problems that always fail the scan, no skip of descendants, SIGTERM then SIGKILL on interrupt, the per-step log files, `{{STAMP}}` at the row's start, a copy of `printable` pinned to search's, and `grep -a` in A5.
- D33: two known limits for the spec. A false FAIL is possible on the harness-as-fixture through SQLite page copies, and an operator session writing the real config fails a row, as with the kit.
- The kit's bash-only test cases are dropped, as D15 says: a function shadowing grep, find or od; a grep that cannot read for `-o`; `bash -x`. The kit's bash tests stay until Phase 3.

## Requirements
- R0: eval drives a separate sandboxed CLI, not yet wired to any verb.
- R3: no gate and no timer.
- R4: `internal/eval` links no SQLite driver, pinned by `TestNoSQLiteDriver`.
- R6: every test uses `t.TempDir()` homes, a fake `agy` and a scratch token.
- R7: sandboxes go under `<home>/.config/fyr/eval`.
- R10: the macOS build is checked, with check e's gap named (O1).
- R8 and Non-goals are unchanged until Phase 2's commit.

# Release v3.0.0 (2026-10-26-2218)

## Type
release

## Summary
v3.0.0, the first release named `fyr`, for the Antigravity CLI only. It is MAJOR because the installed command changes name. Gate: `REVIEW-2026-10-26-preflight-v3-0-0`, SHIP over v2.7.0..1acfc6c. The tag sits on this release commit, whose parent is 1acfc6c.

## Agents dispatched
- reviewer on opus, twice: the ten uncovered commits, then round 2 over e53a7cb.
- security, twice: the same two scopes.
- verifier, four times: d341d8f FAIL (fyr check), then d15d0a2 PASS, then at 1acfc6c both § 1/§ 3/§ 3a PASS and § 2/§ 3b–3h PASS.
- `fyr eval`: 35 rows on Antigravity, 34 + 1 PASS. The main agent ran this box's crossing and the real-home smoke.

## Gate fixes in the range
e53a7cb, 74ecdda, c92219f, d15d0a2 and 1acfc6c (the gate report lists each).

## Release notes
**fyr v3.0.0: the harness is renamed `fyr` and serves the Antigravity CLI only.** This is a MAJOR release because the installed command changes name. A place on v2.7.0 or earlier does not move forward by its own `update`: cross it by hand once, following `DEPLOY-remote` § Crossing to fyr (summary under Install below).

## New features
- fyr check, Phase 1: the verb and rule (a). `fyr check` is a read-only drift check of a checkout's docs against the binary and the tree (BUG-179).
- fyr check, Phase 2: rule (b) checks the specs, and rule (c) the requirements.
- fyr eval, Phase 1: `internal/eval`, with the suite, the sandbox, safety checks a–f, the runner, and `GUIDE-eval`.
- fyr eval, Phase 2: the verb, plus ADR-065, R8 and the map. Behavioural rows run against the real Antigravity CLI, each in its own sandbox, and every run leaves a `testing` record and labelled metrics.
- Brain Phases 3 to 5: the harness speaks records, and the dream reads and writes them. `fyr record` and the brain store at `~/.config/fyr/brain.db` hold every project's trail as records, exported to `.agents/trail.jsonl` (BUG-178).
- Brain Phase 1 checkpoint and Phase 2: the import (`fyr record import`) and the memory alias.
- Session-sized work, Phase 1: the session-sizing rule and the handoff Kickoff.
- The peak-context metric: sessions over the context target.

## Improvements and optimisation
- fyr Phase 1: the report path leaves, and the redactor moves to `internal/redact`.
- fyr Phase 2: Claude Code leaves the binary.
- fyr Phase 3a: agents are authored natively in Antigravity's `agent.md`; the lint, the context and the rules follow (BUG-173).
- fyr Phase 4a: the rename in the tree (module, `cmd/fyr`, `~/.config/fyr`, `.fyr-noindex`, `FYR_*`).
- fyr Phase 4b: the state-dir migration, the dream timer renamed `fyr-dream`, and the release assets named `fyr-*`.
- fyr Phase 5b: the old `~/.claude` files stay where they are at the crossing, and leave fyr's manifest.
- Metrics Phases 1 to 4: one reference per trail item, the join reads records, first reads see record verbs, and metrics are fed at every checkpoint.
- fyr check Phase 3: the consumers and the guides use it, and this repository is clean under it.
- fyr eval Phase 3: the consumers point at `fyr eval`, and the run kit is deleted.
- Modularity Phases 1 to 7e: the large source and test files are split by whole-declaration moves, under the code-modularity rule (ADR-066).
- The v3.0.0 gate's fixes: the memory import skips a file the store refuses; a future-dated record is no dream news; eval's credential scan counts a directory link that leads out of the sandbox; a relative worktree `gitdir` resolves.

## Fixes
- BUG-175 fixed: project-memory's date line uses no command substitution.
- fyr Phase 3b: the skills, kits and content name one CLI (BUG-174).
- Audit fix closed: `memory.Root` refuses an unregistered linked worktree, along with the audit's other fixes.

## Other updates
- Rules: `code-modularity.md`, the third always-on rule (ADR-066), and `session-sizing.md`.
- The `sh-agent kickoff` verb was removed (ADR-058a). The `report` verb and the `styrman-harness-feedback` path are gone (ADR-062).
- Requirements were rewritten for one CLI (ADR-062), and the repository was renamed `kesokaj/fyr`.
- Specs and guides are records: `SPEC-fyr-*`, `GUIDE-*`, `DEPLOY-*`.

## Install
- **New place:** see README § Install without cloning (`ASSET=fyr-<os>-<arch>`, `V=v3.0.0`, marker `# fyr v3.0.0`, `--repo github.com/kesokaj/fyr`).
- **A place on v2.7.0 or earlier:** follow `DEPLOY-remote` § Crossing to fyr, v3.0.0 only.
  1. First disable any unit or profile line of your own that names `sh-agent`, such as `sh-agent-update.timer`.
  2. Do not run `sh-agent uninstall`.
  3. Then, by kind of place:
     - **Release binary:** download `fyr-<os>-<arch>`, check it against `SHA256SUMS`, move it to `~/.local/bin/fyr`, then `hash -r && fyr install`.
     - **Checkout:** `git remote set-url origin git@github.com:kesokaj/fyr.git && git pull --ff-only && go run ./cmd/fyr install --repo "$PWD"`.
     - **Zip place:** download the `fyr-<os>-<arch>` binary by hand, then `./fyr update --from-zip fyr-v3.0.0.zip`.
  4. `fyr install` moves `~/.config/sh-agent` to `~/.config/fyr`, removes `~/.local/bin/sh-agent`, and replaces the dream timer.
- **Existing fyr places, after this release:** `fyr update`.

# Sandbox app-building evals, and the handoff's carried follow-ups (2026-10-27-0043)

The operator asked for sandbox runs of simple app-building projects, with a report of their results and decisions, and approved every follow-up carried by HANDOFF-2026-10-26-2308 ("go all approved", twice). Commits f12f499..b94ed44. The follow-ups were made on a worktree branch, `followups`, and merged at 39ea863, so the eval run in progress kept installing an unchanged tree.

## What changed

- **Evals (GUIDE-eval).** Three `build-*` rows build an app from an empty repository (`~/sandbox/fyr-eval/blank`): a Go CLI, a Go JSON API, and a Go plus TanStack Start full-stack app. They run with wide grants, and their checks build, test and call what the agent wrote. A fourth new row, `rule-code-modularity`, is the release gate's run of `rules/code-modularity.md`. Every check was run before use against a reference build (exit 0) and an empty, broken or mutant one (exit 1).
- **BUG-181, fixed (3db3c77).** `agyTime` (`internal/search/dream.go`) now treats a time before 1970 as no time, which covers both of its callers. Metrics migration 3 (`internal/metrics/store.go`) repairs the rows already stored. SPEC-fyr-metrics § Data and SPEC-fyr-dream state the rule.
- **BUG-179, obsolete (e21a6dc).** Every place has crossed, and on a crossed box `MigrateStateDir` moves nothing.
- **`fyr check` (e0069cb, 7774710).** A bare Go file name in a current spec's `## Verification` section must be the base name of a tracked file, and a heading inside a fence does not bound the section (`internal/check/verification.go`). On the tree at 60e34c7~1 the new rule finds the `tools_test.go` drift; the installed binary found nothing there. SPEC-fyr-check documents the rule.
- **`TestAgyToolVocabulary` (ad023e3)** pins all ten Antigravity tool mappings, the eight untested ones included.
- **GUIDE-testing § 3d (d3db2ae).** The warm-search target is split in two: the file index alone under 100 ms, measured at 35-39 ms; records and files under 250 ms, measured at 90-177 ms. The 100 ms target predates the brain-store half (ADR-063).
- **Comments.** The three kit-port comments in `internal/eval` now cite the run kit's test names instead of line ranges (64128b3).
- **ROADMAP Next.** Splitting the functions over 50 lines is scheduled as a milestone (28e0fcb).
- **BUG-183, fixed (28f3cb4).** f12f499 and e139789 added GUIDE-eval rows without running `go test`, and `TestSuiteHarness`'s pinned row count failed. Neither commit had been pushed.

## Eval results

- TEST-2026-10-26-2357 (at f12f499, blank fixture): 2 of 3 PASS. `build-cli` and `build-api` passed. `build-fullstack` passed its own check (go test, tsc, `npm run build`, a live `/api/hello`), but the eval's credential scan matched an AKIA-shaped string in `node_modules/prettier/plugins/flow.js`, a false positive left to the operator.

## Verification

TEST-2026-10-27-0043-verification-followups-merge-at-b94ed44-pass-202: PASS. gofmt clean, `go vet` clean, `go test -race` across 12 packages (973 passed, 0 failed, 6 env-gated skips), the six named tests, `fyr check` 0 findings. govulncheck reported GO-2026-5024 only, which is known.

## Review

- REVIEW-2026-10-26-2339 (BUG-181 fix): APPROVE WITH NITS. One finding was rebutted with the BUG-181 prevention scoped; one was left (a negative `steps.ts` needs a corrupt database).

- No file was over 400 lines before the phase. `dream.go` was 391, and its two splits would have pushed it past 400. So the protobuf step decoder (`maxDepth`, `proseLeaves`, `walk` and its helpers, `textField`, `prose`) moved whole to the new `dream_proto.go` (124 lines) (D7). `dream.go` is now 300.

Characterization tests (D13) were committed first, in 5294170, before any split:

- `reconcile_arms_test.go`:
  - `applyLocked`'s failing blob, chunk and files writes (insert, delete, state update), made by schema triggers, not seams (D12);
  - an unopenable project directory;
  - an inserter that cannot prepare: a records table with only `oid`, so `gc` still runs;

  - an unreadable tracked file and an unreadable untracked file (mode 000; skipped as root);

- `global_arms_test.go`:
  - `reconcileGlobal`'s `--rebuild` over a non-empty directory;
  - the projects table dropped, or a row with a NULL docs root;
  - a gone registration whose drop a trigger refuses;
  - a registered checkout with a corrupt `.git/index`;
  - a registered checkout whose rows a trigger refuses;
  - `prepare`'s `index --rebuild` of the checkout's own index, and over a non-empty directory;
  - a partial clone on an old git (the existing `lazyFetchSafe` variable);
  - a global index that cannot be opened at registration.
- `refs_arms_test.go`:
  - `refs`' docs-relative directory match;
  - the records table dropped;
  - a record, a file state and a reference that do not scan (NULLs);
  - a LIKE pattern over SQLite's 50,000-byte limit, both in the same-name hint and in the references query;
  - `find`'s snippet read of a chunk whose body is NULL.
- `dream_arms_test.go`:
  - `AgyConversationText`'s list that is not a regular file, has no table, or has a NULL id, each checked to leave no state directory behind;
  - `walk`'s short varint, short 64-bit and short 32-bit fields, and a whole 32-bit field before prose.

After review, tests were added in the checkpoint commit, each killed by its mutation (3 of 3):

- `TestWalkFixedAndVarintFields` gains "64-bit then prose".
- `TestApplyLockedWriteErrors` gains the last-seen update and the touched mark.

## Evidence

- **Mutations before the split:** 37, at least one per targeted block, applied to the code at 5294170. All 37 were killed, one of them only after its test was tightened. The mutant that skipped the inserter's error first survived: `gc` then failed on the same dropped table with the same message. The test now keeps `oid` in the table so that only the inserter can fail, and the mutant is killed. The list, the runner and its output are in `.agents/scratch/funclen-p4/` (`mutations.txt`, `run-mutations.sh`, `mutations-before.txt`). The runner restores each file from a backup copy, and `git diff` was empty after the run.
- **Mutations after the split:** the same 37, adapted to the moved code (`mutations-after.txt` and `mutations-after2.txt`, five of them rewritten by hand where the text had moved), all killed. Two adapted mutants first survived: `return msg, true` in `skipScalar` is equivalent, because `walk` parses the same bytes again and refuses them. The real counterpart, `return nil, true`, which makes `walk` accept the message, is killed.
- **`walk`, old against new:** a temporary differential test (not committed) ran the 5294170 `walk` and the new one on 300,000 inputs, random bytes and generated wire messages. title: Change — BUG-187: first open of a new SQLite store waits (2026-10-27)
body:
owner: main

# Change — BUG-187: the first open of a new SQLite store waits (2026-10-27)

## What changed
- `internal/search/store.go`: `tryOpenWaiting` retries `tryOpen` while it fails busy, for up to the busy timeout, every 50 ms. `openStore` uses it for both of its opens. `IsBusy` exports `isBusy` for the metrics store.
- `internal/metrics/store.go`: `Open` retries `open` (one attempt, the former body) the same way, for `openWait` (10 s).
- Tests: `TestFirstOpenWaitsForALock` in `internal/search/open_test.go` and `internal/metrics/store_test.go`. Each holds `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on a new, non-WAL file, releases it after 300 ms, and requires the open to succeed. Before the fix, both failed within 0.3 ms.

Root cause, repro and prevention rule: BUG-187. In short: SQLite's switch of a new file to WAL upgrades a read transaction and skips the busy handler, so `busy_timeout` never applied to the first open. The brain store already retried; search and metrics now do too.

## Evidence
- The original flake: `TestConcurrentReconcile`, 3 rounds × 3 parallel × 100 runs under 12 busy loops. Fixed build: 900 of 900 PASS. Unfixed: 2 failures in 900 (and 1 run in 9 for the plain package run, Phase 4).
- The verifier at 075cbbe: `TESTING` record of 2026-10-27, PASS. `gofmt` empty, `go vet` 0, `go test -race -timeout 30m ./...` all 13 packages ok (1151 pass, 6 skips none new), the two new tests, and `TestConcurrentReconcile` 20 of 20.

## Agents
- `explorer` (goldfish diagnosis): ranked the DSN's pragma order first, as the main thread did. The driver's source falsified it. Its second candidate (BUSY_SNAPSHOT) was falsified by the extended code. The cause was in neither list (BUG-187 § Diagnosis).
- `reviewer`: `REVIEW-2026-10-27-1408-review-index-busy-on-first-open-bug-fix-2026-10`, APPROVE WITH NITS. Two lows rebutted (the about-20 s worst case matches brain's and the spec's "past 10 s"; the duplicate predicate predates the fix).
- `verifier`: PASS at 075cbbe.

## Not covered
- macOS.
- The about-20 s worst case is not tested.

## What changed

- **BUG-188** (security review part B, medium): `internal/trail/dirty.go` `hashesDiffer` refuses a tracked name opening with `"`, which `git hash-object --stdin-paths` C-unquotes into another path. Before the fix a modified `"a"` read clean beside an unchanged `a`, and a name `"../outside.txt"` was hashed outside the checkout. `Dirty` now says it cannot answer: `record import` refuses, and `eval` labels its source `(dirty: unknown, …)`. Test: `TestDirtyCannotAnswerQuotedName` (internal/trail/dirty_test.go). The class has one site: `check-ignore -z --stdin` is NUL-separated, and `internal/search` hashes in Go.

# Release v3.1.0 (2026-10-27-2117)

## Type
release

## Summary
v3.1.0, a MINOR: new behaviour (the build evals, `fyr check`'s tracked-file rule, the function-length guard) and fixes, nothing an existing place must react to. Gate: `REVIEW-2026-10-27-2117-preflight-v3-1-0-2026-10-27-resumed-final-ship-o`, SHIP over v3.0.0..835a990, after two NO-SHIP reports (`REVIEW-2026-10-27-1809-…`, `REVIEW-2026-10-27-2055-…`). The tag sits on this release commit, whose parent is 835a990. v3.0.0 was a bridge; the operator confirmed in their own turn that every place has crossed it.

## Agents dispatched
- reviewer: over the four uncovered code commits with the docs lens, round 2 over the gate fixes, BUG-189's fix, and two rounds over the gate delta (98ed6b3..48ee381); every report APPROVE or APPROVE WITH NITS.
- security: parts A–D over the code, the trail records in parts through 3cd0b48, two rounds over the gate fixes, and a last read over the records after 3cd0b48 (this run).
- verifier: v1 (FAIL, then FAIL on timing only), § 3c (FAIL BUG-189, then PASS), § 3d timings PASS, the final run at 3cd0b48 PASS.
- `fyr eval` on Antigravity: 15 of 15 changed skill and agent rows after one timeout re-run, the sandbox smoke 3 of 3.
- The main agent: the § 3e corpus measurement (K = 0) and the real-home smoke on dave, 3 of 3 (`TEST-2026-10-27-2113-…`).

## Gate fixes in the range
31de61a (BUG-188, security part C), d8c2129 (BUG-189), 75453d1 (specs re-read), 8bfd2bc (§ 3d bound, on the operator's delegation), ff4c959 (BUG-191), 48ee381 and 0594905 (the smoke row's check), 4fe0bb6 (SPEC-fyr-eval re-stamp).

## Release notes
### New features
- Sandbox app-building evals and the carried follow-ups: three `build-*` rows (a Go CLI, a Go JSON API, a Go plus TanStack Start app) built from an empty repository, the `rule-code-modularity` row, and `fyr check`'s rule that a Go file a current spec's Verification section names must be a tracked file.
- Funclen Phase 1, the length guard: `TestFunctionLength` fails on any non-test function over 50 lines; its allowlist has been empty since the funclen plan closed.

### Improvements and optimisation
- Audit fix Phase 1, trust boundaries in the binary: the dirty-tree check uses git plumbing only and never runs a repository's own clean filter; conversation files are opened non-blocking and no-follow, and a non-regular file is refused.
- Audit fix Phase 2, dream: `--install-timer`/`--remove-timer` with `--all` or `--project` is a usage error, labels are redacted like the texts, the run's clock reaches every input, and an input left out says it was dropped to fit the 256 KB cap.
- Audit fix Phase 3, brain, search, memory, metrics, redact: a query no longer writes to the project database; the metrics report renders before it creates its file; heredoc handling covers `<<-`; the redactor's needles are pinned shape by shape.
- Audit fix Phase 4, cmd/fyr, harness, eval, check: an install dry run refuses a directory at a planned file path; `adopt` compares resolved paths; the state file is read plain only; `record import --dry-run` leaves the old state directory alone; eval fingerprints the real config before a row's setup; `fyr check` notes skipped files and resolves an `enforced by:` path only when it is tracked.
- Audit fix Phase 5, the re-audit fixes and the close: docs, records and agent definitions brought in line with the code.
- Funclen Phases 2–10 and Done: every function over 50 lines split, in internal/brain, internal/metrics, internal/search, internal/harness, cmd/fyr, internal/dream, internal/eval and internal/check, plus the catalog refresh test. No behaviour change.

### Fixes
- First open of a new SQLite index or metrics store waits instead of failing busy (BUG-187).
- agy 1.4.7's file tools are counted in metrics, and eval's credential scan no longer reads an installed node_modules (BUG-184, BUG-185).
- An Antigravity conversation whose summary time is zero is no longer stored with a negative end time (BUG-181).
- A tracked name opening with a double quote can no longer fool the dirty-tree and dates checks (BUG-188).
- `fyr install`'s refusal for a directory in the way names the way out, and the real run meets the same guard instead of a bare rename error (BUG-189).
- A GUIDE-eval row lands together with its test entry (BUG-183, BUG-191).

### Other updates
- The v3.0.0 crossing finished at every place, and the old feedback repository was deleted.
- From the v3.1.0 gate's verification: GUIDE-testing § 3d's warm records-and-files search bound is now 400 ms, and GUIDE-eval has a `smoke` row, the sandbox form of the real-home context check.

### Install
Download: see README § Install without cloning. Existing places, checkout or binary-only: `fyr update`. A place on v2.7.0 or earlier: `DEPLOY-remote` § Crossing to fyr (v3.0.0) first.

After updating, on each machine: `hash -r` (or `rehash` in zsh), `fyr version` (expect v3.1.0), `fyr status` (no drift, no `shadowed` line), then the three smoke checks of `TEST-2026-09-03-verify-real-home` on Antigravity. On a Mac, also run `fyr dream --all` once and check `~/.config/fyr/dream.log` for "not logged in" (BUG-166): v3.1.0 was gated without a macOS dream run.

## Not checked
A real `fyr dream --all` on macOS, lifted by the operator for this release; every Mac place runs it after updating, as the notes say.

## Records in the release commit
This record, the gate report, `REVIEW-2026-10-27-2116-security-review-v3-1-0-gate-records-3cd0b48-work`, `TEST-2026-10-27-2113-verify-v3-1-0-gate-the-real-home-smoke-on-dave-a`, and `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § Where things stand naming v3.1.0.

# Change — ledger Phase 2: the registration marker and `fyr index --register`   (2026-10-28)

Plan: `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` Phase 2 (item 3; audit finding SD19, part 1). ADR-068 (committed first, 0f026b0, with the R3 edit in audit-choices D32's words and ROADMAP), ADR-068a (the addendum). Ledger D11, D12.

## What changed

- `internal/trail/register.go` (new):
  - `Registered(stateDir, root)` reads the marker `<git common dir>/fyr-registered` and counts it only when its `seal` line is the HMAC-SHA256 of the checkout's main top level under `<stateDir>/registration.key`.
  - `Register(stateDir, root, now)` writes `registered <date>` and `seal <hex>` through a temporary file and a rename. It refuses a symlink or non-regular file at the name, and a relative state dir.
- `internal/trail/register_key.go` (new): the per-home key, `crypto/rand.Text()`, 0600, in a 0700 state dir, hard-linked into place so concurrent first registrations agree on one key.
- `internal/trail/open_{unix,other}.go` (new): `openRegular`, which opens with no-follow and non-blocking flags and accepts only a regular file.
- `internal/trail/trail.go`: `Roots` is now a wrapper over the unexported `roots`, which also returns the git common dir, with the same worktree checks.
- `cmd/fyr/verb_index_register.go` (new):
  - `index --register`: the marker first, then the plain index, then `registered <root>`.
  - Exit 2 with `--global` or outside a checkout.
  - Exit 1, naming the path, on a refused or unwritable marker. A failed index after the marker says the checkout is registered.
- `cmd/fyr/ctx_verbs.go`: the `--register` flag on `index`. `verb_search_memory.go`: dispatches it. `main.go`: the usage line and doc comment, and the `--global` line now says registered checkouts.
- `internal/search/scope_prepare.go`: `register` runs when the checkout has `.agents/docs` AND `trail.Registered` under the home's state dir (ledger D11: one without `.agents/docs` would be dropped by `dropReason` on the next `--global`). Its comments are reworded.
- Tests:
  - New: `internal/trail/register_test.go` (11 tests) and `cmd/fyr/index_register_test.go` (5).
  - `TestRegistersOnlyHarnessProjects` gains the committed-`.agents/docs`, clone and no-churn cases.
  - Twelve search tests register their fixtures through `markRegistered`.
  - `TestGlobalDirIsPrivate` now creates the state dir by `--global`, because a registration's key would create it first.
- Docs: `README.md`'s search row; `SPEC-fyr-search` (the command, the `index --register` bullet, the registration paragraph, the covers cell, four failure rows); `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` (a new `index --register` row, exercised on a scratch clone, and a note on the 2026-10-25 `search --global` cell).
- Records: ADR-068 and ADR-068a; the ledger's Phase 2 boxes, D11, D12, and the Phase 3 Kickoff (it now reads ADR-068a and D11-D12); two review records.

## Verification

- Must-fail mutations:
  - Every trail test against its branch: odd marker accepted, marker read outside the common dir, every checkout registered, the guard off, the date format, the seal ignoring the root, the seal unchecked, links followed, the state dir mode, the relative guard off.
  - Six of the verb: the global refusal, the non-checkout refusal, no marker written, an unexplained index failure, no `registered` line, the clock ignored.
  - The search gate with the old condition restored, and with the docs half dropped.
  - Two equivalent mutants (the linked-key guard, and Link→Rename without a race). `TestRegisterFirstKeyRace` catches Link→Rename 1 run in 3.
- The security agent's probe re-run on the fixed build: `--global` serves only the registered repository's file; the redirect tree's canary and the copy's file get 0 hits.
- `fyr index --register` on a scratch clone of this checkout with a scratch home: the counts, `registered …`, a 0600 marker. `--global` exits 2. A `git archive` copy exits 2.
- `gofmt -l cmd internal`: nothing. `go vet ./...`: exit 0. `go test -race -timeout 30m ./...`: exit 0, 12 packages ok, on the final tree.
- Scratch-home install: `binary 0f026b029fb2+dirty`, no warning, drift none.

## Agents dispatched

- `reviewer` (code and docs lenses, diff only), two rounds:
  - Round 1: request changes (1 high, 1 medium, 4 low).
  - Round 2: approve with nits (3 low).
  - Every finding is fixed except the R3 gap, rebutted as a process gate in ADR-068a, and `os.Link` on filesystems without hard links, accepted because it fails closed.
- `security`, two rounds:
  - Round 1: three mediums. The redirect-tree and copy bypasses are fixed by the seal; R3 ahead of the code is rebutted (ADR-068a). One low is accepted.
  - Round 2: no medium or high. The relative state dir is fixed. A checkout place picking up Phase 2 from `main` before Phase 3 is accepted (nothing the dream sends changes).
- Review records: `REVIEW-2026-10-28-0645-review-ledger-phase-2-the-registration-marker-an` and `REVIEW-2026-10-28-0645-security-review-ledger-phase-2-the-registration`.

## Not verified

- No consumer filters on the marker yet except the global file index. The dream's `--all` targets, the `--global` record hits, `ImportGlobal` and the metrics join are Phase 3. Until then R3's "over the projects the operator registered" is not true of the dreamer (ADR-068a).
- Not run: a Windows build's `openRegular` (it compiles; not run), a real `--separate-git-dir` or submodule layout (only reasoned about), and a filesystem without hard links.

# Change — ledger Phase 3: the consumers and the metrics join take registered roots only   (2026-10-28)

Plan: `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` Phase 3 (item 4; SD19 part 2, SD49). Design: audit-choices § Interfaces "The consumers" and "The metrics join", D15-D17; ADR-068, ADR-068a; ledger D11-D15.

## What changed

Every cross-project consumer now checks `trail.Registered(<home>/.config/fyr, root)`. A checkout the operator never registered with `fyr index --register` under this home is reached by none of them. That covers a third-party clone, a copy, a moved checkout, and a row from before ADR-068.

- **`fyr dream --all`** (`internal/dream/targets.go`, new). `targets` was moved out of `dream.go`; `registeredOnly` splits out after the worktree dedup. Each unregistered root is logged once per run, before the projects, as `<root> skip not registered (fyr index --register)`; the dry run prints `[dry-run] <root>: skip (not registered (fyr index --register))`. A root that is gone, or is not a checkout, says that instead (`absent`, split out of `skipReason`; D14). Skipped roots are not counted in `- run <n> projects`. `--project` needs no marker (choices D16).
- **`--global` file hits** (`internal/search/global.go`). `reconcileRegistered` drops a row whose checkout has no valid marker, with `note: dropped <root> (not registered: fyr index --register)`. The rebuild note now reads "each registered one returns on its next search".
- **`--global` record hits** (`internal/brain/search_scope.go`, new). `searchScopes` and `openScopes` serve search, `--refs` and `--open`: the global scope, the project's own scope (D13) and every other registered scope. `scopeFilter` now takes the scope list.
- **`record import --global`** (`internal/brain/import_global.go`). An unregistered project's memory store is a problem, `<root>: not registered (fyr index --register); its memory store is not imported`, and the store is left in place.
- **The metrics join** (`internal/brain/dream.go` `ForMetrics`). An unregistered root reads as not migrated, so its `trail.jsonl` never becomes a brain scope. Its feedback is still read and its sessions still land. An `fyr eval` sandbox is such a root (D15).
- **Text.** These now name registered projects:
  - the `search`, `--global`, `index --register`, `dream` and `import --global` usage lines (`cmd/fyr/main.go`);
  - the `dream --all` and `index --register` flag help;
  - the package and function doc comments in `internal/dream`, `internal/brain`, `internal/search/dream.go` and `internal/memory`;
  - README's search and dream rows;
  - the records `SPEC-fyr-dream`, `SPEC-fyr-search`, `SPEC-fyr-record` and `SPEC-fyr-metrics`.
- **The plan.** Four Phase 3 boxes ticked, plus D13, D14 and D15.

## Tests

- New tests:
  - `TestAllSkipsUnregistered` and the rewritten `TestTargets` (`internal/dream`);
  - `TestGlobalDropsUnregisteredRow` (`internal/search`);
  - `TestGlobalRecordHitsOnlyRegistered` and `TestForMetricsUnregisteredReadsNoTrail` (`internal/brain`);
  - `TestIngestJoinsRegisteredTrailOnly` (`internal/metrics`);
  - an unregistered case in `TestImportGlobalReadsEveryProjectsMemory`.
- Fixtures that `--all`, `--global` or the join read are now registered (`markRegistered`).
- Ten mutations, one per check (the filter in each consumer, the gone precedence, the dry-run line, the log line, the own scope), each fail their test.
- Sandbox S2 holds, and with the Phase 2 binary it fails as expected (the plan's evidence).
- On the final tree: `gofmt -l cmd internal` printed nothing, `go vet ./...` exited 0, and `go test -race -timeout 30m ./...` exited 0. The scratch install has no warning.

## Agents dispatched

- `reviewer`, code and docs lenses: `REVIEW-2026-10-28-0713-review-ledger-phase-3-the-consumers-and-the-metr`. Verdict: approve with nits. One finding fixed, one rebutted, two deferred to the operator.
- `security`: `REVIEW-2026-10-28-0713-security-review-ledger-phase-3-the-consumers-and`. Lows only. One rebutted; three went to the operator (D15).

## Not covered

- No macOS run.
- No real `agy` run. S2 uses the fake agy.
- An erroring `Registered` check inside `reconcileRegistered` is untested. It fails closed, and the row is a cache entry.

title: Change — ledger Phase 4: the dream cap drops news newest first, and the watermark stops before what it dropped
body:
# Change — ledger Phase 4: the dream cap drops news newest first, and the watermark stops before what it dropped   (2026-10-28)

Plan: `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` Phase 4 (item 5; SD28, SD60a). Design: audit-choices § Interfaces "The dream cap", D24, D33; ADR-069 (amends ADR-055a); ledger D17.

## What changed

Before, an input the 256 KB cap dropped was never sent: the watermark moved to the run's start, past it (sandbox finding 3). Now a capped run sends the oldest news and stops the watermark just before the oldest input it held back, so the next run sends the rest.

- **`fit`** moved to `internal/dream/collect_fit.go` (new), behind a `fitter`. The order is now:
  - the metrics summary;
  - the dated kinds (transcripts, trail, feedback) together, newest first. For a tie: transcript, then trail, then feedback; within one kind, the later label first;
  - the skills.
- **`datedVictim`** chooses which input to drop and how:
  - a dated input larger than the room the cap leaves after the head, memory and skills goes first, named `(too big for the <n> KB cap beside memory and skills)` (D33);
  - otherwise the newest goes. It holds the watermark back only while an input strictly older than it is kept;
  - an input of the oldest time left is named `(dropped to fit the <n> KB cap; not sent again)`, because a time watermark cannot split a group of one time (review finding 1);
  - every held-back drop keeps `(dropped to fit the <n> KB cap)`.
- **`Collected.Through`** (`dream.go`) is the instant just before the oldest held-back input. `run.go` stores `watermark(c, t0)`: `Through` when it is non-zero and before the run's start, else the run's start.
- **SD60a.** `TestFitRendersOnce` no longer copies `fit`'s wording. It runs the real `fit` with `fitter.over` swapped for a render after every drop. The wording is pinned as literal strings in the new tests.
- **Text.** `collect.go`'s kind comment, `fit`'s doc comment and the fixture comment. `SPEC-fyr-dream` covers it in steps 3 (Cap) and 6 (Advance), a new failure row and § Verification. ADR-069 is new; ADR-055a is unchanged.
- **The plan.** Phase 4's boxes are ticked, plus D17.

## Tests

- New in `internal/dream/collect_fit_test.go`:
  - `TestFitDropsDatedNewestFirst`, `…TooBigDoesNotHoldWatermark`, `…TooBigNewestFirst`, `…LastDatedDoesNotHoldWatermark`, `…UndatedDoNotHoldWatermark` and `…UntimedDatedHoldsNothing`;
  - `…TieGroupNeverStalls`, `…TieAboveOlderNeverStalls` and `…DistinctTimesLoseNothing`. These run `fit` once per run through `sendRuns`, which fails any run whose watermark does not move;
  - `TestWatermark`;
  - `TestTwoRunsSendEveryCappedInput`: two real runs with a fake agy over nine ~40 KB trail files send all nine.
- Rewritten: `TestCollectCapDropsNewestNewsFirst` (formerly `…TranscriptThenTrail`) and `TestFitRendersOnce`.
- Fourteen mutations, and each failed a test. A fourteenth was equivalent and is not counted.
- Sandbox S3 on the final binary:
  - F3 run twice: the first call carried MARK-5 to 10 (246,084 bytes), the second MARK-2 to 4. All nine were sent.
  - The HEAD binary (3d5b83b) sent MARK-2 to 7, then logged `unchanged`.

## Verification

- `gofmt -l cmd internal` printed nothing.
- `go vet ./...` exited 0.
- `go test -race -timeout 30m ./...` exited 0 (12 packages ok) on the final tree.
- The scratch-home install shows `binary 3d5b83b1001d+dirty`, with no warning and no drift.

## Agents dispatched

- `reviewer` (code and docs lenses), two rounds. Round 1: request changes. Finding 1, a stall on ties, was fixed with tests that fail without the fix. Findings 2 and 3, the wording, were fixed. Round 2: approve with nits; the nit was `datedVictim`'s complexity, fixed through `newerOf`, and the mutation that exposed gained `TestFitTooBigNewestFirst`. The record is `REVIEW-2026-10-28-0753-review-ledger-phase-4-the-dream-cap-drops-news-n`.

# Change — ledger Phase 4b: fyr help, written for a person (2026-10-28)

Plan: `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger`, Phase 4b (item 81; D19–D26). Base: 74de149.

## What changed

- **New `cmd/fyr/help_text.go`** holds the help text as data:
  - the short page (three groups, one line per verb, no `sync`);
  - each verb's synopsis and description of at most ten lines;
  - the fact audit's three `verb page` sentences: U7d on update's page, A12b on adopt's, M25b on metrics'.
- **New `cmd/fyr/help.go`** builds and routes the pages:
  - `verbHelp` builds a page. Its `Flags:` list comes from the verb's own FlagSet, with each `<ARG>` taken by `flag.UnquoteUsage` from the backquoted name in the usage string.
  - `usageErr` is the one usage-error helper.
  - `runHelp` serves `fyr help [<verb>]` and `fyr -h|-help|--help [<verb>]`.
- **`run_dispatch.go`:**
  - `fyr` with no verb prints the short page; `help`, `-h`, `-help` and `--help` go to `runHelp`.
  - An unknown verb prints its reason and `run 'fyr help' for the commands`. It no longer prints the whole usage.
  - `parse` answers `-h` with the verb page. A flag error or a stray argument goes through `usageErr`.
- **`ctx_verbs.go`:**
  - `newCtx` silences the FlagSet's own usage, so `Usage of <verb>:` is never printed.
  - Every flag's usage string now carries a backquoted name. The redundant `<verb>:` prefixes are dropped, and `--status` names the kind's list.
- **Usage-error sites now call `usageErr`.** Each prints the reason, then the verb's synopsis, then `run 'fyr help <verb>' for its flags`, and exits 2:
  - `record.go`: three sites. An unknown subverb now gets `fyr record: unknown subcommand "<x>"`, the operator's reading (D24).
  - `verb_install.go` (adopt), `eval.go`, `verb_search_memory.go` (memory) and `verb_metrics.go` (bare verb and unknown subverb).
- **Deleted:**
  - the `usage` const in `main.go`; its doc comment is rewritten to mirror the short page;
  - `recordUsage`;
  - the literal usage lines at the sites above.
- **Restatements:**
  - `internal/search/search.go` says `; see fyr help search` in four messages, and `parse.go:249`'s comment matches.
  - README:56 describes the short page and the verb pages.
  - `SPEC-fyr-search`'s failure-mode row now quotes `; see fyr help search`. The operator approved that edit (D25).
- **Tests:**
  - New `cmd/fyr/help_test.go`: (a) to (g), `TestUsageErrSites` (12 rows), the unknown verb, the three left-out sites, and the `--kind` list pin.
  - Rewritten: `auditfix_test.go`, `check_test.go`, `usage_test.go`, `search_test.go` (`TestUsageMatchesDocComment`), `harnessmap_test.go` and `record_test.go` (`TestHelpListsRecord`).

No verb's behaviour, flag or exit status changed. Only the help output and the usage-error output did.

## Verification

- **Red first.** The compile failure came first, then the routing and usage-error tests with `help.go` unwired. Both outputs are under `.agents/scratch/ledger/p4b/`.

# Change — ledger Phase 5: retro and distill queue proposals, never write the harness checkout (2026-10-28)

Plan: `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger`, Phase 5 (items 14, 15; D27). Base: 9738ac7. ADR: ADR-070.

## What changed

- **`skills/retro/SKILL.md`:**
  - Step 6, harness scope: from another project the status is `queued`, always. The same-turn "apply now" branch is struck: it located the checkout and applied, installed, committed and pushed there.
  - In the harness checkout itself an approved harness proposal is still applied in the run, now naming that repo's own rules (`fyr install`, its Testing section, a `change` record, commit, push) before its status is set.
  - Project scope: "apply now as a task" became "apply it in this run as a task" (wording only).
  - Step 1, `--harness`: a `/distill --global` proposal (titled `Distill — skill <name>`) is applied as a new `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, its text read as data and checked against the files first.
- **`skills/distill/SKILL.md`:**
  - Step 1: the dreamer dispatch is no longer written out; it points at `retro` Step 1 source 8, with `Promoted: none.`, and is dispatched even with no memory, as before (WS-S5).
  - Step 3's Global row, Step 4's question and Step 5's Global skill: from another project `--global` writes the full SKILL.md to `.agents/scratch/distill-<name>.md` and stores it as one global `proposal` (`fyr record add proposal --global --project <root>`), queued for `/retro --harness`. No `skills/<name>/`, no `fyr install`, no `fyr adopt`, no commit in the checkout. In the checkout itself it writes `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` under that repo's rules.
  - "After installation" is skipped for a queued skill. Step 6's Skill line and the index JSON's `status` gain `queued (<PROPOSAL-ID>)`.
- **Records:** ADR-070 (stored before the skill edits); `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` Phase 5 ticked, D27 added; `REVIEW-2026-10-28-1018-…`; `TEST-2026-10-28-1018-eval-2-of-2-pass-at-9738ac7`.

body:
# Change — visible dream Phase 2: the session check, the cooldown, the hourly timer and the status line

Plan: `PLAN-2026-10-28-1510-plan-the-visible-dream-2026-10-28`, Phase 2 (D2, D4, D9, D10, D13, D18; new D21, D22). Review: `REVIEW-2026-10-28-1623-review-visible-dream-phase-2-session-check-coold`. Agents dispatched: one `reviewer` (code and docs lenses, given the diff only). No verifier: the Kickoff's closed set names the full command, which the author ran bare twice (see Verification).

## What changed

- **The session check** (`internal/dream/agy_process.go`, new). `agySession(goos, uid)` looks for an interactive `agy` process of the operator's uid.
  - Linux reads `/proc/<pid>/status`, taking the real uid from the first field of `Uid:`, and `cmdline`. When `cmdline` does not name `agy`, it reads the `exe` link with ` (deleted)` stripped.
  - macOS runs `ps -ww -U <uid> -o args=`.
  - A process does not count when it carries `-p`, `--print` or `--prompt` (one or two dashes, `=value` allowed), or when its first non-flag argument is an `agy` subcommand. The list is `agy --help`'s on 1.4.9 (D21).
  - The check is wired into `Options.Session`. When it is nil, `Run` uses the real check.
  - `realRun` asks it for `--all` before `harness.ConfigDir`. With no session it prints `fyr dream: no agy session of this user; nothing to do`, creates nothing and exits 0. A check that errors exits 2.
  - `--project` never asks.
  - The dry run prints `[dry-run] agy session: yes|no (a real --all run would stop here)` first. It exits 2 on an error, as the real run does.
- **The cooldown** (`state.go`, `dream.go`, `run.go`, `run_dry.go`). `dream-state.json` gains `attempts` (root → start time), stored before each CLI call.
  - `--all` skips a project tried in the last 24 h and logs `<root> skip attempted <time>`; the dry run says the same.
  - `--project` ignores the cooldown.
  - An older state file without the key reads as empty.
- **The timer** (`timer.go`): `OnCalendar=hourly`; the launchd plist has `Minute` 0 and no `Hour`; both `Description=` lines say hourly. These texts now say hourly while an `agy` session runs:
  - `verb_dream.go`'s three messages;
  - the flag help in `ctx_verbs.go`;
  - `help_text.go` (the verb list and the `dream` page);
  - the `main.go` doc comment.
- **The status line** (`timer_stale.go`, new; `StatusLine`). A unit on disk whose text is not this fyr's render, for the home and the unit's own frozen `PATH` (systemd `%%` and plist XML unescaped), reads `timer installed, older schedule: fyr dream --remove-timer, then fyr dream --install-timer`. Under a home that is not the real one, both commands carry `--home '<home>'` (D22).
- **Splits for `TestFunctionLength`**: `noSession` and `prepareAgy` (from `realRun`), `drySession` and `drySkip` (from `dryRun`).
- **Comments**: every line about the dream's schedule in `cmd` and `internal` now says hourly, or names the timer or the run instead (none left that say "nightly", "03:00" or "every night").
- **Docs** (the restatement rule, D22):
  - README: the `fyr status` row names the older-schedule commands; lines 3, 50 and 117 drop "nightly until then" and keep only that the dream still runs privately until Phase 5.
  - AGENTS.md rule 1 says hourly.
  - `SPEC-fyr-dream`: the being-built sentence names what is built; the session check names `ps -ww` and `--prompt`; the dry-run line carries its `[dry-run]` prefix; the status line names `--home`.
  - `SPEC-fyr-delivery`: the being-built sentence.
  - ROADMAP Now.
- **Tests** — new:
  - `TestAgySessionLinux` (12 cases), `TestAgySessionErrors`, `TestAgySessionMac`;
  - `TestRunAllNeedsASession`, with a positive control;
  - `TestRunProjectNeverAsks`, `TestDryRunSessionLine`;
  - `TestCooldown`, `TestStateWithoutAttempts`;
  - `TestTimerStale`, `TestStatusLineOlderSchedule`;
  - render pins for `OnCalendar=hourly` and the plist's lone `Minute`.

  Updated:
  - `TestMain` gives the package a fake session;
  - `TestStatusLine` now writes a real render;
  - `TestRunWritesProposalsDraftsAndState` and `TestTwoRunsSendEveryCappedInput` make their second run a day later;
  - `dream_arms_test.go` expects the new install message.

## Verification

- `gofmt -l cmd internal` empty; `go vet ./... && go test -race -timeout 30m ./...` exit 0, 12 packages ok (`.agents/scratch/vd2/full2.log`). The first full run failed with exit 1 on four stale tests and `TestFunctionLength` (`full.log`); all are fixed.
- Must-fail: `.agents/scratch/vd2/mutate.py` makes 12 mutations, and each FAILs its tests, before and after the function split. The mutations:
  - the uid check, the `-p` check, the subcommand check and the ` (deleted)` strip;
  - the check moved after `ConfigDir`;
  - the cooldown off, `--project` not exempt, the attempt not stored;
  - the stale check off, the `PATH` not unescaped, the `--home` flag off;
  - the dry-run line off.
- Live on this box: `fyr dream --all --home <fresh scratch>` printed the no-session line, exit 0, and the home stayed empty. `fyr dream --all --dry-run --home .agents/scratch/home-dream` printed `[dry-run] agy session: no (a real --all run would stop here)`, exit 0. No `agy` session was running.
- Scratch-home install: `fyr status --home .agents/scratch/home-trail` shows `binary b7a763a485a9+dirty` with no warning.

## Not covered

- An interactive session detected live (`yes`) — Phase 5's V0.
- The macOS `ps` path beyond a replaced `psArgs` — ledger A2.
- Whether `agy remote-control start` leaves a child whose argv is not a subcommand.
- The four skills that still say "nightly" (`dream` description, `project-memory`, `retro`, `handoff`) — Phase 5's docs box.

Neither report names a workspace or project root, and from a dream-work under a git checkout agy loads the `.agents/` skills of every directory up to it.
- `internal/dream/agy_visible.go` (new): `visibleHome(argv0, home, work, env)` — the login under `home` (`loginIn`); dream-work empty and no `.git`, nor `.agents` other than the home's own, above it as written or resolved (D25); the oracle run from dream-work under `HOME=home` with `childEnv`'s allow-list, 30 s each; `toolPermission` `request-review` or `strict`, `agentMode` empty or `plan`, no allow rule in any scope or in the settings, no access outside the workspace, no trusted workspace at or above dream-work; each report exactly one SUCCESS object of the shape seen. Anything else is `false` with the first reason. Not yet called: Phase 4b wires it in.
- `internal/dream/agy_home.go`: `loginIn(goos, home)`, `findLogin`'s rule under any home; `findLogin` calls it with `$HOME`.
- `internal/dream/agy_exec.go`: `runGroup`, `callWithin`'s process group, signal relay and kills taken out unchanged so the oracle shares them (review finding 1).

# Change — visible dream Phase 4b: the branch wired in, and the first line (D12, D14, D26)

Plan: `PLAN-2026-10-28-1510-plan-the-visible-dream-2026-10-28`, Phase 4b. Agents dispatched: `reviewer` and `security`, over Phases 2–4b's diff (`b7a763a..` plus this phase's tree): `REVIEW-2026-10-28-1741-review-visible-dream-phases-2-4b-session-check-c` (APPROVE WITH NITS, 4 low) and `REVIEW-2026-10-28-1741-security-review-visible-dream-phases-2-4b-oracle` (2 medium, 4 low). Each finding is fixed, deferred or rebutted in its Outcome. One round each: the second round would cover only fixes, and the mutation runs below cover those.

## What changed

- `internal/dream/run_branch.go` (new):
  - `branchFor` asks `visibleHome` before every project's call and logs `<root> agy home visible` or `<root> agy home private (<why>)`. The visible branch runs with `childEnv(…, --home)`. The private branch builds `agyHome` on the run's first private project and reuses it for the rest; a failure to build it fails that project, not the run.
  - `removePrivate` is the run's deferred cleanup.
  - `dryBranch` is the dry run's per-project line: visible; private with "a copy of the login, with no grants"; private with ", would fail: <reason>"; or "not asked: no dream-work yet". The dry run makes nothing.
  - `logReason` redacts the oracle's reason, folds it to one line and strips control characters (security finding 5).
- `internal/dream/run.go`:
  - `prepareAgy` only checks the CLI and makes dream-work. The run's `env` field is gone; `project` gets a branch and `ask` takes it.
  - `sweepIdle`: a run that stops for want of a session sweeps a killed run's copies. It acts only in an existing `~/.config/fyr` and only under `dream.lock` (security finding 3).
- `internal/dream/agy_home.go`:
  - `checkAgy()` checks PATH only. The login now belongs to the branch (D12).
  - `agyAuthHint` takes the branch's home and names it.
- `internal/dream/agy_visible.go`:
  - A third oracle report, `/hooks`. `hooksAny` takes only `{"hooks":[]}` (D26 1, the operator's choice).
  - `readConfig` pins `/config` both ways to `configKeys`, the 36 keys agy 1.4.9 reported; `permissions` to `allow`/`deny`/`ask`; and `artifactReviewPolicy` to `asks-for-review` (D26 2, security finding 1).
  - `sortedKeys` is shared with `permissionsGrant`.
- `internal/dream/prompt.go`: `head` opens `dreaming: <name>`, then a blank line, so the tool warning is the second paragraph (D14).
- `internal/dream/run_dry.go`: PATH check only; the CLI line points at the branch line. `dream.go` and `agy_exec.go` comments name the branch.
- Tests:
  - new `run_branch_test.go`: `TestRunBranchPerProject`, `TestRunBranchPrivateFailsOneProject`, `TestDryRunBranchLine`, `TestLogReason`.
  - new `prompt_test.go`: `TestPromptFirstLine`.
  - `run_session_test.go`: `TestNoSessionSweepsKilledRun`.
  - `agy_visible_test.go`: `configReport`; 9 new shape rows (config keys, permissions key, artifact policy, four hooks rows); the hooks fixture.
  - `run_agy_test.go`: `TestRunAgyWithoutLoginFailsTheProject` replaces the exit-2 test; the auth hint names the home; stdin opens `dreaming:`.
  - `dryrun_test.go`: no login and a relative HOME are now a project's `would fail`.
  - `testdata/oracle/hooks.json`: the sandbox's one `/hooks` report, holding no account data.
- Records and docs:
  - `SPEC-fyr-dream`: being-built sentence; step 4 (three reports, the pinned shape, hooks, the dry-run lines, the hint); Failure modes; Known limits (D8 narrowed; a resumed dream).
  - `SPEC-fyr-delivery` and README rows 50 and 117: say what is built and what Phase 5 still runs. Row 50 also names the full visible condition (review finding 3).
  - README legend: dashed until the end-to-end run passes (review finding 4).
  - `DEPLOY-local`: the login is used in place in the visible branch.
  - ROADMAP Now; the plan: two boxes ticked, D26, the Risks line.

## Verification

- `test -z "$(gofmt -l cmd internal)" && go vet ./... && go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30m ./...`: exit 0 on the final tree, 12 packages ok. The run before the review fixes also exited 0.
- Must-fail mutations, every one FAILs a test:
  - 9 over the lifecycle (`.agents/scratch/vd4b/mutate.py`): the per-project ask once per run, the private home not reused, not removed, the visible env, the branch log, a build failure that fails the run, the dry run's oracle, the dry run's login check, the first line.
  - 11 over the review fixes (`mutate2.py`): the hooks call, count and shape; unknown, missing and permissions keys; the artifact policy; the idle sweep and its lock; the control-character strip; the redaction.
  - Two mutations first failed only by not compiling; both were rewritten to compile and then FAILed a test.
- Scratch-home install, repeated on the final tree: `fyr install --home .agents/scratch/home-trail` exit 0; `fyr status` shows `binary f6071290c209+dirty`, no warning.
- Live dry runs with the scratch binary under `.agents/scratch/home-dream`:

  - `--project .`: `agy home not asked: no dream-work yet…`, then, after making dream-work, `agy home private (no Antigravity login in ~)`. That wording led to `logReason`'s paths-as-written rule.

## Not covered

# Change — visible dream Phase 5: end to end in the sandbox, the docs, and Done

## End to end, against the real agy 1.4.9 (V0–V3)

- Records:

New Known limits: a `--home` below a `.agents`, custom agents (D29), the login used in place, and log growth. The resumed-dream limit is widened to `@conversation:` and search. § Verification gains the end-to-end runs.

## Decisions

- D28: the operator chose the sandbox at `/var/tmp/fyr-visible`, and an interactive `agy` started by the session for V0.
- D29: the closing reviews.
  - Security finding 1 (custom agents) is answered by a probe with a control. agy denied a subagent's command under `request-review`, with and without plan mode, although the subagent had `commandExecutionPolicy: eager`; it ran under `always-proceed`.

title: Release v4.0.0 — opt-in registration, the visible hourly dream, fyr help pages, eval --home required (2026-10-28-2121)
body:
# Release v4.0.0 (2026-10-28)

## Type
release

## Summary
v4.0.0 is a MAJOR. An existing place must act on three things:
- registration: `fyr index --register` (ADR-068), without which a project is no longer dreamt over or searched globally;
- the timer: a timer an older fyr installed keeps its nightly schedule and must be reinstalled;
- `fyr eval`: it now requires `--home`.

Gate: `Preflight — v4.0.0` (this release commit's review record), SHIP over v3.1.0..49c0b00. The tag sits on this release commit, whose parent is the gated head 49c0b00 and whose diff from it is `.agents/trail.jsonl` only.

## Agents dispatched
- **reviewer:** the docs lens over v3.1.0..93da61e (REQUEST CHANGES on docs; the three mediums fixed in 49c0b00). Code coverage is cited from the range's earlier COMPLETE reviews.
- **security:** the uncovered code commits (one low), the range's trail records in three parts (lows and info only), and the gate's own records with the release notes (lows, all fixed or left as the gate report says).
- **verifier:** part 1 (FAIL on § 3d under eval load, everything else PASS), part 1 re-run (§ 3d PASS on a quiet box, govulncheck IDs), and part 2 (§ 3c changed-verb rows, § 3e, § 3g: PASS).
- **`fyr eval` on Antigravity:**
  - batch 1 at 93da61e: 8 of 9, with the `agents-security` failure caused by the main agent's concurrent real-home install;
  - `agents-security` and `preflight` at 49c0b00: 2 of 2;
  - batch 3 at 49c0b00: `TEST-2026-10-28-2121-eval-9-of-9-pass-at-49c0b00`, 9 of 9 PASS (`smoke`, `scaffold`, `agents-security`, `agent-verifier`, `distill`, `dream`, `handoff`, `project-memory`, `retro`).
- **The main agent:** the real-home smoke on dave, 3 of 3 at 93da61e and 3 of 3 at 49c0b00; BUG-193 and its fix (49c0b00).

## Gate fixes in the range
49c0b00, records only. It rewords five `.agents/docs` paths so `fyr check` reports 0 findings (BUG-193), fixes `DEPLOY-local`'s registration line, and fixes `SPEC-fyr-delivery`'s eval sandbox path. The release commit also:
- elides the broker path in `…-gate-trail-3`;
- updates `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § Where things stand to name v4.0.0.

## Release notes
### New features
- **Opt-in registration:** `fyr index --register` (ledger Phases 2 and 3, ADR-068, ADR-068a). It writes a sealed marker into the checkout's git directory. Only a registered checkout is read across projects: `fyr dream --all`, `fyr search --global`, `record import --global` and the metrics join each take registered projects only. A clone, a copy or a moved checkout never carries the registration. Deleting the marker opts out.
- **The visible dream** (visible-dream Phases 1–5, ADR-073):
  - The dream timer now runs hourly, and it runs only while an interactive `agy` session of yours is running.
  - Each project is tried at most once a day.
  - When your Antigravity home's settings grant no tool without review, the dream runs there, and its conversation stays in your `/resume` list. Otherwise it runs in a private home, as before.
  - The dream's own conversations are no project's: search, metrics and the next dream skip them.
  - `fyr status` names a timer installed by an older fyr.
- **`fyr help`, written for a person** (ledger Phases 4a and 4b): a short page, a page per verb (`fyr help <verb>` or `fyr <verb> --help`), and usage errors that print the verb's synopsis.

### Improvements and optimisation
- **Ledger Phase 1:** the dreamer's `agy` gets only an allow-listed environment (ADR-067): `PATH`, the locale names, `TERM`, `TMPDIR`, `TZ`, the proxy variables and the CA variables. A credential in any other environment variable no longer reaches it. A credential inside a proxy URL still does. The systemd unit gets `TimeoutStartSec=2h`.
- **Ledger Phase 4:** when news does not fit the dream's input cap, the newest is dropped first, and the watermark stops before what was dropped, so a later dream sends it instead of losing it (ADR-069).
- **Ledger Phase 5:** `/retro` and `/distill` queue harness proposals as global `proposal` records and never write the harness checkout (ADR-070). `/retro --harness` applies them.
- **Ledger Phase 6:** the `verifier` and `security` agents read live stores from copies only, and an edit to `GUIDE-eval` runs `TestSuiteHarness`.
- **Phase 7 of audit-choices, and ledger Phase 7:**
  - New redactor needles: Docker access tokens, HCP Terraform tokens, and shapes from each vendor's docs.
  - `fyr record add`, `edit` and `import` warn on stderr when a title or body holds text the redactor would change. The text is still stored, and the exit status is unchanged.
  - Eval's credential table is pinned to the redactor.
- **Ledger Phase 8:** small code and test gaps closed.
  - The dream sends a conversation only when it is the project's own: every workspace must resolve to the project's root. A left-out conversation is listed by ID, never by path.
  - `fyr eval` registers each sandbox clone under its eval home before ingesting it.
  - A verb that never reads `--repo` now warns that it ignores it.
  - The dirty-tree check refuses a root that is not the checkout's top level.
  - The areas pin `TestAreasRunPatternsExist` was added.
- **Ledger Phase 9:**
  - `fyr eval` refuses to run without `--home`, and refuses the real home (D37).
  - Before any push, the context names the trailer check (BUG-192).
  - The README map names `brain.db` as where experience lives.

### Fixes
- `fyr check` is back to 0 findings on this checkout. Five lines in two records named another checkout's `.agents/docs` as this one's path (BUG-193).

### Other updates
- **Slack token handling was removed from the redactor** (ledger Phase 7a, the operator's decision D32 (1)). Slack tokens and webhook URLs are no longer redacted from what the dreamer sends. Keep them out of the trail, the memory and the `agy` sessions (transcripts) of a registered project. A line where a password, secret, token or api-key assignment, or an authorization header, holds the token is still redacted.
- **The trail:** the ledger plan (one list of every unfinished item, now closed), the visible-dream plan (closed), ADR-067 through ADR-073, and the specs, guides and README brought in line.

### Install
Download: see README § Install without cloning. Existing places, checkout or binary-only: `fyr update`. A zip place: download the v4.0.0 zip and binary, then `fyr update --from-zip <file>` (`SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model). A place on v2.7.0 or earlier: `DEPLOY-remote` § Crossing to fyr (v3.0.0) first.

v4.0.0 is a MAJOR. An existing place must act on three things:
1. **Register each project you want dreamt over and searched globally:** run `fyr index --register` inside it. Until then `fyr dream --all` skips it ("skip not registered"), and `fyr search --global` does not read it.
2. **Replace the old timer:** `fyr dream --remove-timer`, then `fyr dream --install-timer`. A timer an older fyr installed keeps its nightly 03:00 schedule. Since the dream now needs a running `agy` session, it would almost never fire. `fyr status` says so.
3. **`fyr eval` needs `--home <dir>`,** never the real home.

After updating, on each machine:
- `hash -r` (or `rehash` in zsh).
- `fyr version`: expect v4.0.0 at a binary-only place, or the tagged commit at a checkout.
- `fyr status`: no drift, no `shadowed` line.
- The three smoke checks of `TEST-2026-09-03-verify-real-home` on Antigravity.

**On a Mac,** also run `fyr dream --all --dry-run` twice: once with an interactive `agy` open, expecting `[dry-run] agy session: yes`, and once without, expecting `[dry-run] agy session: no …`. The session check uses `ps` on macOS, and v4.0.0 was gated without a run on a real Mac. If `ps` fails, the check fails closed and no dream runs.

After the first hourly dream with an `agy` session open, look at `/resume` (Ctrl+F) once for the dream's conversation.

## Not checked
These were lifted by the operator in this release session (the gate report quotes the turns):
- a real `fyr dream --all --dry-run` on macOS;
- the sandbox S1–S3 and visible-dream E2E runs at the gated head, on a byte-identical binary.

## Records in the release commit
This record, the gate report, the records security read, the batch-3 eval record, the smoke at 49c0b00, the elided trail-3 review, and `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § Where things stand naming v4.0.0. The gate's earlier records ride along too: the docs and security reviews, the verifier logs, the eval records and the first smoke.

body:
# Change — 2026-10-29 — root-docs row 8 (S2): `fyr serve` read-only pages Plan: `PLAN-2026-10-29-root-docs-and-fyr-serve`, row 8. Spec: `SPEC-fyr-serve`, agreed by the operator at the start of the session (D45). Decisions: ADR-075, ADR-075a (new), D45–D49. ## What changed - **New verb `fyr serve [--port N]`**, in `cmd/fyr/verb_serve.go`. It is registered in `init()`, like `check`. - `serveOptions` builds the options. Its printer closures map a verb's ordinary exit status (nothing installed, findings, a refusal) to a 200 page. - `serveRun`, `serveExit` and `serveNotify` are the test seams. - The first SIGINT or SIGTERM cancels the run; a second exits 1. - `--port` outside 1–65535 is a usage error, exit 2. - `writesState` is true for it. Its help page and the short page carry it, and `main.go`'s usage comment too. `ctx` has a `port` field. - **New package `internal/serve`**: - `serve.go`: `Options`, `Run`, `NewRun`, `Serve`. Each run draws three `crypto/rand` values: T, C and the path prefix P. It listens only on `127.0.0.1:`, sets the timeouts, and prints two start lines through `search.Printable`. - `guard.go`: the five security headers on every response, then in order the `Host` check, the `Sec-Fetch-Site` check, and the token exchange (a 303 with a slash-collapsed `url.URL`, cookie `Path=/s/

`, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict). Then every cookie of the name is compared in constant time. - `routes.go`: everything outside the prefix is the plain 404; under it, 404 for an unknown path and 405 for a wrong method. Handler errors are logged with the path under the prefix. - `view.go` with `assets/layout.html` and `assets/style.css` (embedded): `html/template`, a nav bar, no script. - `pages.go`: `/`, `/context`, `/check` (one at a time, 409 otherwise), `/memory`, `/metrics` (`Lstat` first, never creating the store), `/metrics/report` (the report document whole), `/evals`, `/dream`. - `records.go`: `/records` with its `kind`, `open` and `scope` filters, `/records/{id}`, and `/search` (record hits linked, then file hits). - `dreamlog.go` with `open_unix.go` and `open_other.go`: the tail of `dream.log`, opened `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK` and checked with `Fstat`. It keeps the last 200 lines of the last 256 KiB, each line made printable with its tabs kept. - **Docs:** - `README.md` verb table; `TDD.md` § T5 row, the `--repo` list, T16 and its trace row; `SDD.md` M16 and § Security. - `AGENTS.md`: the layout, `serve` in the `--home` list, and § 3a–3i. - Records: `SPEC-fyr-serve` (agreed, D46's readings, the prefix, the 409, the verification rows), `ADR-075a`, `GUIDE-testing` § 3i, `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` § `serve`. - `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § Where things stand names `serve` as on `main`, in no tag yet. `TestDeliverySpecCurrent` failed until it did. - **Trail:** plan D45–D49 and row 8's three boxes ticked; `TODO.md` Now is row 9, and a Backlog item records `fyr check`'s slowness. ## Verification - **Tests first.** 25 mutants on the first build, 12 on the prefix fix and 4 on round 2's tests; each was caught. - **The verb.** `cmd/fyr/verb_work.go` adds `fyr work [--timeout D] [--model M] [--keep] <kickoff-file>`, which runs exactly one file. Its refusals exit 2 before anything is made: the usage errors and a `--timeout` of 0 or less, then not a checkout, the install source as eval resolves it, and then `internal/work`'s own refusals. Exit 1 is a FAIL, exit 0 a PASS. SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGQUIT end the run's context, so the worker fails `killed` with its token link removed and the contract still prints. `writesState` gains `work`, so a pre-rename state directory is migrated first. The verb also gets a help page, a line on the short page and a line in `main.go`'s doc list.

body:
# Change — workers Phase 4: several Kickoffs, `--max-workers`, `--kill`   (2026-10-29)

Plan: `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers` Phase 4. Its three `who: AI` task boxes are ticked, with D92.

## What changed

- **Several files.** `internal/work/work.go`: `Run(ctx, o, files...)` returns the results in file order. `dispatch` starts each file as a slot frees and prints each block whole, in file order, once it and every file before it have ended (D19). Once the context ends, no waiting file starts; each fails `killed`, never started, with no sandbox. Steps 6–8 (the lead check, the fetch, the scope check and the drafts) run for one worker at a time. `worker.go` gains `unstarted` and `result`.
- **The limit and the pid file** (`internal/work/slots.go`, new):
  - `Options.MaxWorkers` defaults to 4 and may be 1 to 8 (D30).
  - `<home>/.config/fyr/work/<stamp>/pid` holds one line, `<pid> <running>`. It is locked under `pid.new` and then renamed, held under an exclusive flock for the whole run, and removed at the end (D33).
  - A slot is taken under `slots.lock`, never waited for, and given back without it.
  - The other runs are read with `os.ReadDir`. A stale file counts nothing. A file that cannot be read, or whose lock test errors, counts as the whole limit and is named in the refusal.
  - `Kill(home, stamp)`: the stamp's pid must have at most seven digits, the file must be live and its pid must be the stamp's, and the pid must be at most 1<<22. Then it sends SIGTERM.
- **The refusals** (`internal/work/preflight.go`) cover several files:
  - a name given twice;
  - two files sharing scope, naming both files and both entries (D17);
  - the machine at its limit, naming the stamps; it is counted after the sandbox root's check.
- **The verb** (`cmd/fyr/verb_work.go`): `--max-workers N` (0 or less refused) and `--kill <stamp>`, which takes no file and migrates no state. Exit 1 when any worker fails. The help page, the short page and `main.go`'s list are updated.
- **Docs**:
  - README's verb row, `TDD.md` T5, T18 and the M18 test list, and `SDD.md` M18;
  - the records `SPEC-fyr-work` (Status still `draft`), `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` § `work`, `GUIDE-testing` § 3k, and `SPEC-fyr-delivery`'s built line;
  - `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers` (D92, the boxes, the Status line).

## Tests

- New tests in `internal/work`: `several_test.go` and `slots_test.go`, with a stand-in run that is the test binary re-run and never the go test process (D33). The fake agy has a `together` barrier, which proves either overlap or its absence without timing races.
- New tests in `cmd/fyr`: `TestWorkVerbSeveral`, `TestWorkVerbKill`, new rows in `TestWorkVerbRefusals`, and a `work --kill` row in `TestStateDirMigrationByVerb`.
- 27 mutations of the pinned branches, all red.
- The full test command exited 0 in my own call, after every fix.
- The risk check (task 1) ran on dave with real agy: two concurrent workers on one linked token, both PASS (D92).

## Agents dispatched

- `documentation`: the record drafts and the repo docs. I corrected them after the review fixes.
- `reviewer`, code and docs, two rounds: `REVIEW-2026-10-29-2207-review-workers-phase-4-several-kickoffs-max-work`. APPROVE WITH NITS both times; every finding fixed, or accepted with its reason.
- `security`, two rounds: `REVIEW-2026-10-29-2207-security-review-workers-phase-4-the-pid-file-the`. Fixed: pid truncation (medium), the fail-open counts, the blocking locks and the order of the limit before the root check. Accepted: `--kill` cannot prove the pid is a `fyr` process, and a worker can rewrite its run's pid file (`SPEC-fyr-work` § Open questions).
- `verifier`: `TEST-2026-10-29-2207-verification-workers-phase-4-several-kickoffs-ma`. FAIL only on BUG-196, a committed `internal/serve` test that fails one time in 64, outside this change. Phase 4: 388 unit tests pass, and the new tests passed three rounds repeated.

## Not covered

- The Mac (the plan's `who: user` box).
- A real Antigravity run of two workers in one invocation; the risk check ran two invocations at once.

  - otherwise no name, read as `time.Local`.
  
  `runZone` is refusal 22. It refuses an invalid `TZ` on either runner, and `--runner docker` when there is no name. It is made in `prepared.session` after `--timeout`, before the base and any docker call. `localtimeLink` and `loadLocation` are the test seams (D146).

# Change — the v5.0.0 gate's fixes: worker links refused, test rigs kept off the real daemon and git config, the worker isolation claim corrected, ADR-075b   (2026-10-31)

## Type
bugfix

## Summary
The release gate over v4.1.0..5b716dd (reviewer, security and two security reads of the test files, then round 2 of each over the fixes) found three defects that reached commits, and a policy finding. All are answered here. The range is 28 files, +193 −15, plus records.

## What changed
- **`internal/work/fetch.go`** (BUG-200): `links` reads `git diff-tree -r -z --no-renames --ignore-submodules=none <base> <ref>`. `scope` fails the worker `changed outside its Files` when the branch's tip holds a symlink (120000) or gitlink (160000) that the base did not hold as the same, whatever `Files:` says, or when that read fails. `changedPaths` also passes `--ignore-submodules=none`, so a `.gitmodules` `ignore = all` hides nothing (round 2). Test: `TestRunLinks`, five cases, with two new fake-agy knobs in `internal/work/rig_test.go`.
- **Test rigs** (BUG-201, and the test-file reads' lows):
  - `TestKillRefusals` and `cmd/fyr`'s `newWorkRig` and `TestWorkVerbKill` put a recording fake docker first on PATH and assert that the stale sweep reached it.

- **Docs** (BUG-202):

- **`TODO.md` Backlog**: the agy token's account check, and worker handoffs as instruction-shaped text in the trail.
