# Deploy — GCP

**Not applicable.** The harness is a file copier into home directories, plus a local search index; it has no image, service, or project. The guide exists so the convention every project follows (`docs/deploy/{local,remote,gcp}.md`) holds here too, and so an agent looking for a GCP path finds this answer instead of inventing one.

Projects that do deploy to GCP fill the template that `/init-project` ships (`skills/init-project/assets/records/DEPLOY-gcp.md`): recorded defaults, image, procedure via the `cloud-run-deploy` skill, secrets, verify, rollback.

title: Deploy — local (this machine)
body:
# Deploy — local (this machine)

"Deploying" the harness means installing the context, skills, and agents into a home directory. Development never touches the real `$HOME` (`PRD.md` R6); deploying to it is the operator's action.

## Prerequisites

Go 1.24+ and git. `~/.local/bin` on `PATH`. The Antigravity CLI (`agy`) installed; it is the only target. The installer writes only under `~/.gemini/config/` and `~/.local/bin` and edits no vendor setting (PRD.md § Non-goals, ADR-062); `--vendor` is a usage error.

## Build and install

```bash
cd ~/workspace/fyr   # the checkout; a place cloned before the rename keeps its directory name
gofmt -l cmd internal && go vet ./... && go test -race -timeout 30m ./...   # before deploying anything; gofmt takes the source dirs, not `.` (it walks .agents/scratch, BUG-048); -timeout 30m for a one-CPU box (cmd/fyr ~13 min under -race)
go run ./cmd/fyr install                             # builds the binary from this checkout, writes ~/.gemini/config, installs the build to ~/.local/bin/fyr
fyr status                                           # must end with "drift none"
```

The worker image for `fyr work --runner docker` (optional; Docker, or Colima on the Mac): the build line is `SPEC-fyr-work` § The worker image. Rebuild it after every `fyr install` that changes the binary, because the verb will refuse an image stamped with another version (Phase 7b-2).

## Update

```bash
fyr update                 # fetch; refuse a dirty checkout; if behind: pull --ff-only; rebuild and reinstall
fyr update --check         # only reports; exit 2 when behind
```

The normal way a checkout moves forward, run whenever the operator decides the harness has changed; `remote.md` § The resync loop covers the timer and the dirty-checkout refusal.

## Update a release-binary install

A place installed from a release binary (README § Install without cloning) has no checkout and nothing to build from, so `update` moves it to the newest RELEASE instead (which place gets what from a tag: `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model):

```bash
fyr update --check         # only reports; exit 2 when a newer release exists
fyr update                 # download the newest release, verify it, replace ~/.local/bin/fyr, reinstall
```

What it does, in order: asks `gh` for the newest release's tag; refuses anything that is not a `vX.Y.Z` tag, and anything not numerically newer than the installed version — nothing but this check stops a downgrade to an older, genuine release; downloads this platform's binary with `SHA256SUMS` into a temporary directory under `~/.config/fyr/`, removed on every path out; checks that `SHA256SUMS` names this release and that the binary matches its line in it (integrity only; no key signs a release, ADR-053); and only then replaces `~/.local/bin/fyr` through a rename and runs the new binary's `install`. Any failure leaves the installed binary untouched and names the check that failed. It needs `gh` on `PATH`; a development build is never overwritten from a release.

## From a plain copy (no `.git`)

A copy of the repository with no `.git` — for a major remodel, or a machine that cannot authenticate to GitHub. It needs Go, and the Go module proxy or a filled module cache for the one dependency, `modernc.org/sqlite` (ADR-045):

```bash
cd <unpacked directory>
go run ./cmd/fyr install             # installs the running binary as is; never rebuilds (BUG-015)
fyr status                           # first line names a plain copy with no commit; must end with "drift none"
```

`fyr update` refuses a plain copy, by design, with a message naming `install` still deploying it as it is and the alternatives. To move it forward, unpack a newer copy and run `install` from it again; to roll back, install the earlier one. This path is not one of the ways in — `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model names the three (a checkout, a release binary, a zip place — `README.md` § Install from a zip (no SSH, no gh)) and this plain copy as their fallback; it stays because the code path does and because it is the fallback when none of the three can reach GitHub.

## What stays on this machine

Nothing is sent from this machine but the dreamer's redacted prompt (below), `fyr eval`'s runs (started by you or, when `fyr auto` is turned on at level `harness`, by its hourly run), and the `fyr work` workers you start or that `fyr auto` starts when you turn it on, plus a `missing-skill` worker's search of `skills.sh` with the pinned CLI (`SPEC-fyr-delivery` § What stays on the machine). The `report` verb is gone (ADR-062): the brain store `brain.db` (the global feedback, proposal and retro records), the search index and the metrics store stay in `~/.config/fyr/`, and a harness-target proposal reaches the harness checkout only through `/retro --harness`, run there by you, or, when `fyr auto` is turned on at level `harness`, as an eval-gated commit to a skill or agent in that checkout, never pushed (ADR-090). An older version left two things no verb removes any more: a kept clone at `~/.config/fyr/feedback` (versions before the throwaway clone) and a `~/.config/fyr/report-<pid>` directory after an interrupted run. Each is a clone of the feedback repository; read what it holds, then delete it by hand.

## The background dreamer (optional, once per machine)

```bash
fyr dream --install-timer        # systemd user timer (Linux) or launchd agent (macOS): fyr dream --all hourly, while an agy session of yours runs
fyr status                       # its line: dream      last run <date>: <n> projects, <m> proposals; timer installed
fyr dream --all --dry-run        # what each registered project would send (an unregistered one: skip not registered), and the CLI command; writes nothing
fyr dream --remove-timer         # stop and remove it (uninstall does too)
```

- The unit runs `~/.local/bin/fyr`, with the absolute entries of the PATH of the shell that ran `--install-timer`, so it finds `agy` there; one reachable only through a relative PATH entry is not found when the timer fires. Run it from the shell you work in. A rerun from a shell with another PATH renders other text: the installed unit is kept and named, so run `--remove-timer` first.
- The unit is `fyr-dream.timer` (Linux) or `com.fyr.dream` (macOS) for the real home and carries a short hash suffix for any other `--home`. It runs `dream --all --home <that home>`, so a scratch install or removal leaves the real timer alone and a scratch timer never dreams over the real home (the service manager is shared by every home of the user; BUG-144). The real home is the account's home in the account database, never `HOME`. A unit under the names from before v3.0.0 is no longer read, replaced, removed or named by any verb: every place crossed (ledger A1, D40; Phase 10).
- The dream job always runs `agy` (plan mode, the prompt on stdin); with no `agy` on PATH it fails before the first project.
- Antigravity needs the operator's login: on Linux `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/antigravity-oauth-token`, which agy uses in place in the visible branch (under `--home`) and which the private branch (`SPEC-fyr-dream` step 4) copies into a private HOME under `~/.config/fyr/dream-agy-home-*`; on macOS agy keeps it in the Keychain, so the run links `~/Library/Keychains` into that HOME instead (and copies the token file too when one exists), so the dream job's agy shares the operator's real Keychain login: a refresh it makes reaches the interactive agy too. The HOME is removed after the run; a locked Keychain (no user logged in to the Mac) makes agy ask for a browser login, which it gives up on after its own 60-second wait, so each project fails in about a minute with `agy is not logged in inside the dream job's private HOME` (BUG-166).
- A project is dreamt over only once `fyr index --register` has run in it (the operator's consent, ADR-068); which registered projects a run takes is `SPEC-fyr-dream`'s.
- On Linux a user timer fires only while your user manager runs (a login, or `loginctl enable-linger`). dave has `Linger=yes` (`loginctl show-user $USER -p Linger`, 2026-11-01), so the dream's timer, and `fyr auto`'s when turned on (`observe` on dave from 2026-11-01), fire while the operator is logged out. `Persistent=true` runs a missed hour at the next login. A timer an older fyr installed keeps its nightly 03:00 schedule, and with the session check it dreams only when an `agy` session of yours runs at 03:00, which is almost never; `fyr status` says so: run `fyr dream --remove-timer`, then `fyr dream --install-timer`.
- Every real run first runs `fyr metrics ingest`. It reads the shape of Antigravity sessions into `~/.config/fyr/metrics.db` (never sent anywhere; `uninstall` keeps it) and logs its summary line to `dream.log`. Each project's prompt then carries a numbers-only summary of its metrics. The store is the only copy once Antigravity deletes a transcript, so back it up now and then with `fyr metrics export <file>`. Look at it with `fyr metrics show` or `fyr metrics report` (spec `SPEC-fyr-metrics`).
- Output: global `proposal` records in `brain.db`, `Dream, project — …` per project and `Dream, harness — …` for harness targets, which wait for `/retro --harness`; draft skills under `~/.config/fyr/proposals/dream/drafts/`. A failed project's output goes to `dream-failed/`, and the log is `dream.log`. Nothing is applied until `/retro` does it.

## Auto-mode (optional, once per machine)

```bash
fyr auto on --level observe      # writes ~/.config/fyr/auto.json (0600) and installs fyr-auto.timer (Linux) or com.fyr.auto (macOS)
fyr auto status                  # level and thresholds, last run and gate verdicts, today's model runs (n of 4), open asks
fyr auto run --dry-run           # prints each gate's verdict per registered project and the task class it would choose; writes nothing
fyr auto off                     # writes enabled: false with no lock and removes the timer (uninstall removes the timer too)
```

- Runs `fyr auto run` hourly from `~/.local/bin/fyr` with the absolute `PATH` entries of the shell that ran `fyr auto on` (`Nice=19`, `IOSchedulingClass=idle`, `RandomizedDelaySec=10m`, `ConditionACPower=true`, `TimeoutStartSec=3h` on Linux; `ProcessType=Background`, `LowPriorityIO`, `Nice=15` on macOS; spec `SPEC-fyr-auto`, ADR-090).
- Trust ramp on dave (`PLAN-2026-10-31-1636-plan-fyr-auto-mode-idle-time-self-improvement-of` Phase 8): turned on at `--level observe` on 2026-11-01 (`project_idle` 6h, `user_idle` 15m; free health checks and global `review` report records only, no model calls and no project writes). Raising the level (`project`, then `harness`) requires the operator's word after reading the report records.

## Configure

Nothing to configure. The global flags are `--repo` and `--home`; `--vendor` is gone and any use of it is a usage error on every verb, exit 2 (`flag provided but not defined: -vendor`). The manifest still records `"vendor": "antigravity"`; an older value is read and ignored. `--repo DIR` overrides where the checkout is; `$FYR_REPO` does the same persistently (an `SH_AGENT_*` variable is ignored, with a notice on stderr). Without either, install and update discover the checkout by walking up from the working directory, then fall back to the path recorded at the last install; when that discovery finds a checkout OTHER than the one already on record — an unpacked copy, a second clone sitting in a harness-shaped directory — the build is refused rather than run and deployed: `"checkout %s is not the installed one (%s); pass --repo %s to build and install from it"`, or, on a release-binary install, `"this home was installed from the release binary %s, not from a checkout; pass --repo %s to build and install from it"`. `--home DIR` installs elsewhere and is what every development run uses (a scratch home under `.agents/scratch/`, never `/tmp`). From its own git checkout, `install` rebuilds the binary with `go build` first; the running binary is installed as is when `go` is missing (with a warning) or when the tree is a plain copy with no `.git` — an unpacked bundle (BUG-015).

## Verify

- `fyr status` shows the current commit, a `binary` line carrying the same revision (a warning there means the installed binary is older than the checkout or unstamped: run `fyr update`), and no drift, with no `shadowed` line — a checkout place can be shadowed the same way a release-binary place was (BUG-078). `fyr version` run unqualified must match what was just installed; if it does not, `hash -r` (bash) or `rehash` (zsh) first — the shell caches where it last found `fyr`, and `update` replaces only `~/.local/bin/fyr` (BUG-079; `update` says so when it ran from another copy, but only against the real home, never `--home` elsewhere — remedy is `ln -sfn` to the installed binary when that copy is yours, or, when it is not, removing it with the rights that own it or running the installed one by its path) — and if still wrong, an earlier `fyr` on `PATH` is running instead of the installed one (`type fyr` shows which). `status` shows one `agy  ~/.gemini/config …` line, no `(vendor: …)` text and no settings note.
- `fyr render | head -3` prints the assembled context.
- Start Antigravity once and check it read the files: `/skills` and `/agents` list the harness entries, and `grep 'Failed to parse' ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/log/cli-*.log` is empty (BUG-004).

## First session after install

Antigravity prompts once per session for paths outside the workspace, such as the first read or write under `~/.config/fyr/` (the brain store `brain.db`, which holds the global `feedback`, `proposal` and `retro` records, and the metrics store `metrics.db`); approve it. The installer touches no vendor setting file (ADR-062). A project's memory is not a file in the project: `fyr memory add` writes it as `memory` records in the brain store, `~/.config/fyr/brain.db`, keyed by the main worktree's root (`SPEC-fyr-memory-loop`).

## agy models and quota (before every agy dispatch)

The operator's rule (`rules/agy-dispatch.md`): before scheduling `fyr work`, choose each worker's model by tier and pass it with `--model`. Before that and before every `fyr eval` run, read the quota, then state the tier, the model and the quota left in one line per dispatch. A model out means a similar model in the same tier, named with why. A tier out means stop and ask; never a weaker tier.

- **Quota:** `agy -p "/usage"` (the same as `/quota`), run outside every checkout; `--output-format json` gives `command.data.groups[].buckets[]` with `remaining_fraction` and `reset_time`. It starts no agent turn, spends no quota and leaves no conversation (agy changelog; on 2026-10-31 it gave 0 turns, 0 tokens).
- **Models:** `agy models` lists them, and `agy -p "/model"` prints the default.
- **Pools:** quota is per pool, not per model. Each pool has a weekly limit and a 5-hour limit, charged by token cost, so when a pool is out every tier in it is out.

Tiers on dave, agy 1.4.12, 2026-10-31:

| Tier | Models | Pool |
|---|---|---|
| [pro] | `gemini-4-argon-low`, `-medium`, `-high` | Gemini Models |
| [flash] | `gemini-3.8-flash-low`, `-medium`, `-high` | Gemini Models |
| [opus] | `claude-opus-5-5-low`, `-medium`, `-high` | Claude and GPT models |
| [sonnet] | `claude-sonnet-5-5-low`, `-medium`, `-high` | Claude and GPT models |
| [gpt-oss] | `gpt-oss-120b-medium` | Claude and GPT models |

- **The tiers' source:** `/usage` names the Gemini pool's families "Gemini Flash, Gemini Pro". Argon is [pro] by elimination, an inference.
- **No [plan] tier:** "plan" in the rule is the scheduling step.
- **`fyr eval`'s model:** it has no `--model`, so it runs the account default, `gemini-4-argon-medium` ([pro]). The real `settings.json` sets no model, and the eval home's sessions recorded `gemini-4-argon`.
- **Refresh:** re-run `agy models` when agy is updated, and update this table.

## Operator steps

Standing by-hand procedures on this box, never pending items (those live in the newest handoff):

- After a push from another machine: `fyr update`, then `fyr status` shows a stamped `binary` line and no drift.
- Keep dave current (standing permission, the operator, 2026-10-29): on dave, every session's checkpoint ends, after its commit and push and on a clean tree only, with `fyr install` from this checkout into the real home. Then `fyr status` must show a `binary` line without a warning and `drift none`, and the handoff quotes both lines. A dirty tree, a failing suite or an unpushed commit means no install, and the handoff says why. A lead (`work` skill) defers it to its closing handoff's Next Steps, for the final tree (ADR-077). The smoke checks below remain the operator's.
- After the upgrade to opt-in registration (ADR-068): `fyr dream --dry-run --all` lists every indexed project it now skips as `not registered`; run `fyr index --register` in each project you want the dream, `search --global`, `record import --global` and the metrics join to read again. A copy, a moved checkout or another `--home` registers again.
- After any change to `context/`, `agents/`, or `skills/` reaches this home: the three smoke checks of `TEST-2026-09-03-verify-real-home` on Antigravity, from a fresh clone of the demo service.
- When `govulncheck ./...` names a toolchain-fixed advisory: get a newer Go, never raise the `go` directive or add a `toolchain` line in `go.mod` (ADR-029 — a pin makes the module unbuildable on a host that cannot fetch a toolchain). Try the system package manager first; when it has nothing newer, as Debian trixie did on 2026-09-16 (`golang-1.24-go 1.24.4-1` and no later package), install a user-level SDK instead, which needs no root:

```bash
go install golang.org/dl/go1.27.3@latest     # the wrapper lands in ~/.go/bin
~/.go/bin/go1.27.3 download                  # the SDK lands in ~/sdk/go1.27.3
ln -sfn "$HOME/sdk/go1.27.3/bin/go" "$HOME/.local/bin/go"   # ~/.local/bin is ahead of /usr/local/bin on PATH here
go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest         # rebuild it, or it cannot parse the newer sources
go version && "$(go env GOPATH)/bin/govulncheck" ./...   # the full path: GOPATH/bin is not on every shell's PATH
```

  Undo by repointing that one symlink at an older SDK under `~/sdk`, or by deleting it: `/usr/bin/go` (go1.24.4) stays where it was; `/usr/local/go`, a root-owned go1.27.1 on 2026-10-09, was gone by 2026-10-26. On 2026-10-09 this box moved to go1.27.2 this way, for GO-2026-6604, -6600 and -6599; on 2026-10-26 to go1.27.3, for GO-2026-6809, after `~/sdk/go1.27.1` had gone missing under the symlink. After the switch, run the full gate and `fyr install`, so the deployed binary is built by the new toolchain — `go version -m ~/.local/bin/fyr` names it.

  The known findings, so a NEW one stands out (moved from the project `AGENTS.md` § Setup commands, 2026-10-29): on go1.27.3, no finding the code reaches (2026-10-26; go1.27.2 reported GO-2026-6809, crypto/x509, not reached). Known in required modules: GO-2026-5024 (golang.org/x/sys via the SQLite driver, not reachable; ADR-045a) and, on a Go before 1.25.12, GO-2026-4970 (os.Root.Open, reached from internal/search, guarded by an Lstat first, and from internal/check, which strips every trailing slash before os.Root sees a name). On a Go older than go1.24.6 or go1.25.8, two standard-library advisories (`os`, `os/exec`): the fix is upgrading the machine's Go, never pinning it.

## Roll back

`fyr uninstall` removes exactly the files the manifest lists, plus the dream timer and `fyr auto`'s timer when installed (leaving `fyr auto`'s config and state), even with no manifest left. To return to an earlier harness commit: `git checkout <commit> && go run ./cmd/fyr install`.

## Sandbox instead of the real home

`TEST-2026-09-03-verify-sandbox` records how a throwaway `HOME` with the CLI logged in is used to test a change end to end before it reaches the real home.

title: Deploy — other machines
body:
# Deploy — other machines

The harness reaches a machine one way: `fyr` (R8, R9, ADR-030, ADR-033); what each kind of place fetches is `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model, on the operator's own credentials; there is no push-based deploy, no CI, no hooks, no service.

## First install on a machine

```bash
git clone git@github.com:kesokaj/fyr.git ~/workspace/fyr
cd ~/workspace/fyr
go run ./cmd/fyr install
fyr status
```

`install` writes only under `~/.gemini/config` and `~/.local/bin` and edits no vendor setting (PRD.md § Non-goals, ADR-062). Check `fyr status` ends with "drift none". A machine that already has `sh-agent` (v2.7.0 or earlier) does not start here: § Crossing to fyr.

On a machine that installs from a RELEASE BINARY instead, the download is verified before it is moved and the install is verified after it — two different checks, and skipping the second is what BUG-078 cost:

```bash
# One chained command: a failed check stops the move. V is the version you expect, from OUTSIDE
# the download (you cut it, or read it on a machine you already trust); ASSET is fyr-linux-amd64,
# fyr-darwin-arm64 or fyr-linux-arm64. macOS: shasum -a 256 -c -
V=vX.Y.Z && ASSET=fyr-linux-amd64 \
&& D=$(mktemp -d) && cd "$D" \
&& gh release download "$V" --repo github.com/kesokaj/fyr --clobber \
     --pattern "$ASSET" --pattern 'SHA256SUMS' --dir "$D" \
&& grep -qxF "# fyr $V" SHA256SUMS \
&& grep -v '^#' SHA256SUMS | sha256sum -c - --ignore-missing \
&& chmod +x "$ASSET" \
&& test "$("./$ASSET" version)" = "fyr $V" \
&& mv "$ASSET" ~/.local/bin/fyr && cd ~ && rm -r "$D"
# The `grep` and the `test` tie the checksum file and the binary to the version YOU named — what
# `fyr update` does with the tag it asked GitHub for (update also refuses a tag that is not
# newer than what it has, which no first install can mirror). The checksums are not signed
# (ADR-053): they prove the download is whole and is the file the release lists; who made the
# release rests on your GitHub credential and HTTPS. The checksum file leaves with "$D". A system
# path instead of ~/.local/bin is a `sudo mv` on that one line and changes nothing else.

hash -r                               # bash (zsh: rehash): the shell caches where it last found fyr
fyr version                           # unqualified: what the SHELL resolves, after the move
type fyr                              # when the version is wrong: the path the shell actually runs, cached or not
which -a fyr                          # every candidate, in PATH order
```

`fyr version` unqualified is the one that matters, and `hash -r` comes first because a shell caches where it last found `fyr`: `update` replaces `~/.local/bin/fyr` and nothing else, so a shell that once resolved the name to a copy elsewhere keeps running that copy whatever PATH says — devbox stayed on v1.2.1 this way after a successful update to v1.2.2 (BUG-079); `update` now says when it ran from such a copy — but only when the update ran against the real home (never a `--home` elsewhere), and only when the copy it ran from was actually written; the remedy is `ln -sfn` to the installed binary when that copy is yours, or, when it belongs to someone else, removing it with the rights that own it, or leaving it and running the installed one by its path. A binary moved into a system path is not installed if an earlier `PATH` entry holds another `fyr`: that one runs, installs whatever source it resolves, and reports `drift none` about it. It tells stale from fresh, never genuine from forged — it is the suspect binary's own output; what you can check is the checksum on the file, before the move, and it proves integrity only (ADR-053). `install` and `status` name such a binary now (a `warning:` line and a `shadowed` line), and a symlink from the earlier entry to the installed binary settles it — it runs the same file, so it is not a shadow. `--clobber` matters for the same class of reason: without it a leftover file from an earlier attempt makes the download refuse, and the stale file is what gets moved.

The binary is the one file fyr writes through a link. When `~/.local/bin` is a symlink to a directory, `fyr update` on a release-binary place replaces `fyr` in the directory the link points to, while `fyr install` never writes a linked destination or one under a linked directory and prints `keep    ~/<path> (a symlink; fyr never writes through a link)` for it, the binary included. This is accepted, not a defect (audit finding IN39, `PLAN-2026-10-27-audit-choices`): a linked `~/.local/bin` is the operator's own layout, and the binary is the exception to the link rule.

## The four places

The operator installs the harness in four places: the work Mac, the home Mac, and two Linux hosts where they work on other projects; at each the harness serves the Antigravity CLI. Every one is reached on the operator's own SSH key and `gh` login — there are no deploy keys and no per-machine credentials, because the operator authenticates as themselves everywhere and a key would restrict nothing (ADR-030 D1). A place gets the harness one of three ways, named in `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model:

- **A checkout the operator owns** — the normal path. First install as above; after that, `fyr update` whenever the operator decides the harness has changed. A timer (§ The resync loop) is a convenience a machine may add, not the mechanism.
- **A release binary** — one downloaded `fyr` with `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/` and `rules/` built into it, for a place that only USES the harness and should not have a checkout of it sitting beside its projects. `fyr install` installs what the binary carries and copies the binary itself; `fyr status` shows `source embedded vX.Y.Z`; `fyr update` downloads the newest release, checks it against its `SHA256SUMS` and replaces `~/.local/bin/fyr` (which place gets what from a tag: `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model). `fyr adopt` needs a checkout and says so. See `README.md` § Install without cloning and `DEPLOY-local` § Update a release-binary install.
- **A zip place** — a repository zip downloaded by hand, unpacked and installed with the running binary by `fyr update --from-zip <file>`, which then deletes the unpacked copy; nothing is fetched and nothing in the zip replaces the binary, so the operator moves it forward by repeating the download and `--from-zip`. See `README.md` § Install from a zip (no SSH, no gh).

A plain copy with no `.git` — an unpacked bundle — still installs, and `update` refuses it, naming `install` still deploying it as it is and the alternatives above (`DEPLOY-local` § From a plain copy); it is not one of the ways in, it is the fallback when none of the three can reach GitHub, and it differs from a zip place in what is kept — a plain copy is a tree someone unpacked and left on disk, while a zip place keeps no tree at all.

Nothing else carries the harness: no copy vendored inside a project, no per-project copy, no service. A project that wants the harness installs it with `fyr` into a home. That home receives installed FILES — `fyr install` writes the context, skills, agents, commands and rules and creates no repository. That alone does not stop a change flowing back: changing the harness takes a credential that can push to this repository, not a checkout, and anything that reaches the operator's SSH key or `gh` login can clone and push. A home seeded for agents is therefore read-only only when it reaches no such credential — no forwarded ssh-agent, no `gh` token, no readable key. This repository names no consumer project and depends on none (R8).

Nothing flows back: a place's brain store (every project's trail records and memory, and the global `feedback`, `retro` and `proposal` records), search index and metrics store stay under `~/.config/fyr/` on that place, and a project's memory is `memory` records in that brain store, never a directory in the project (`SPEC-fyr-memory-loop`); the three things that leave a place, all to the model of the CLI it already uses (except a `missing-skill` worker's search of `skills.sh` with the pinned CLI), are the dreamer's redacted prompt, `fyr eval`'s runs (started by the operator or, when `fyr auto` is turned on at level `harness`, by its hourly run), and `fyr work` workers started by the operator or, when `fyr auto` is turned on, by its hourly run (ADR-062, ADR-065, ADR-076, ADR-090; `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § What stays on the machine, `DEPLOY-local` § What stays on this machine).

## Crossing to fyr

What v3.0.0 delivers, and why a place on v2.7.0 or earlier crosses by hand, is `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model; this is the procedure, by kind of place. The state-dir migration and the resync below are `fyr install`'s, and run on that first install. The dream timer's replacement under its fyr name was `fyr install`'s too, until every place had crossed (ledger A1, D40); it was removed in ledger Phase 10, and an old-named unit left anywhere is the operator's to remove by hand.

**Before the crossing, at every place.** Disable or rewrite any unit or profile line of the operator's own that names `sh-agent` (on the dev box the hourly `sh-agent-update.timer`: `systemctl --user disable --now sh-agent-update.timer`; it fails today anyway, because the v2.7.0 release binary refuses `--repo`), and rename any exported `SH_AGENT_*` variable to its `FYR_*` name (a set `SH_AGENT_*` variable is not read; the verb prints one stderr notice naming the `FYR_*` name). Do NOT run `sh-agent uninstall` first: it deletes the state the migration carries. Since ledger Phase 10 `fyr install` no longer replaces the old dream timer, so stop and remove it by hand too: `systemctl --user disable --now 'sh-agent-dream*.timer'`, delete `~/.config/systemd/user/sh-agent-dream*.{service,timer}`, then `systemctl --user daemon-reload` (macOS: `launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u) <plist>` for each `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.styrman.sh-agent-dream*.plist`, then delete it); `fyr dream --install-timer` installs the fyr one.

**A release-binary place.** Run the First install block above with the fyr names (`ASSET=fyr-<os>-<arch>`, `V=v3.0.0`, `# fyr v3.0.0`, `--repo github.com/kesokaj/fyr`): it checks the marker and the checksum and moves the binary to `~/.local/bin/fyr`. Then `hash -r` and `fyr install`.

**A checkout place.** Stop any own timer that runs `sh-agent update` first. Then:

```bash
git remote set-url origin git@github.com:kesokaj/fyr.git
git pull --ff-only
go run ./cmd/fyr install --repo "$PWD"
```

`--repo` because a home last installed by a release binary (the dev box runs the v2.7.0 one) refuses a checkout that is only found from the working directory (`knownCheckout`).

**A zip place.** Download the `fyr-<os>-<arch>` asset by hand, as a release-binary place does, verify it the same way and `chmod +x`. Then `./fyr update --from-zip <fyr-v3.0.0.zip>`. A plain-copy install copies the running `./fyr` to `~/.local/bin/fyr`; the zip replaces no binary.

**What `fyr install` does at the crossing.**

- The state dir moves first, before anything opens it, in every verb that writes under it (`install`, `sync`, `update` without `--check` or `--dry-run`, `uninstall`, `adopt`, `index`, `search`, `memory add`, `metrics ingest`, `dream` without `--dry-run`). With `~/.config/fyr` absent and `~/.config/sh-agent` a plain directory, one `os.Rename` moves it and the verb prints `migrated ~/.config/sh-agent → ~/.config/fyr`. With both present neither is touched: one line says `fyr` reads `~/.config/fyr` and leaves `~/.config/sh-agent` for the operator to merge or remove. With `~/.config/sh-agent` a symlink (and `~/.config/fyr` absent) the verb is refused: move what it points to to `~/.config/fyr` (or point a `~/.config/fyr` link at it) and run again.
- Read-only verbs and modes never migrate (`status`, `diff`, `list`, `render`, `version`, `memory show`, `metrics show|report|evals|export`, every `--dry-run`, `update --check`): with the old dir present they print one stderr line, `run fyr install to migrate ~/.config/sh-agent`, and read nothing from it.
- The resync reads the old manifest from the moved dir. Claude Code's files from that install (`~/.claude/AGENTS.md`, the `CLAUDE.md` stub, `~/.claude/{agents,skills,commands,rules}/*`) stay exactly as they are: they leave fyr's manifest, install says so in one line (`keep    ~/.claude: <n> files an install before fyr wrote for Claude Code; fyr never removes them, and they leave its manifest`), and no later `fyr install` or `fyr uninstall` touches them (plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` D32: a Claude Code still used on a machine keeps its files, frozen at v2.7.0's text). Every other file the old manifest lists and the new plan does not — `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` — is removed. A symlink, or a path under a linked directory, stays (the operator's). A removal error stops the install: remove the file by hand and run `fyr install` again. `~/.claude/settings.json` stays too; the two keys v2.7.0 wrote there (`attribution`, `autoCompactWindow`) are the operator's to keep or remove.
- `fyr status` names every `sh-agent` PATH finds with a `leftover` line (F4).

**After the crossing, at every place:**

```bash
hash -r
fyr version                                   # fyr v3.0.0 or newer
fyr status                                    # no warning, ends "drift none"
ls ~/.config/sh-agent ~/.local/bin/sh-agent   # both: No such file or directory
systemctl --user list-timers | grep -cw sh-agent   # 0 (macOS: launchctl list | grep -cw sh-agent)
```

**Accepted risks after the crossing.**

- A Claude Code session at a crossed place still runs the v2.7.0 harness under `~/.claude`, which fyr keeps frozen (above), and that harness's `feedback-log` writes under `~/.config/sh-agent`, bringing the old directory back (it did on the dev box on 2026-10-26, `TEST-2026-10-26-2233-verify-the-crossing-to-fyr-at-the-work-mac-the-h`). With both directories present no verb moves anything: each prints the both-directories notice and fyr reads only `~/.config/fyr`. Merge or remove the old directory by hand, and stop using Claude Code there, or remove its v2.7.0 files, to end it.
- The crossings of the work Mac, the home Mac and the second Linux host rest on the operator's word ("Crossed, all clean", the same testing record): no `fyr status` line or binary version from those places is recorded. Only the dev box's crossing was checked by commands (`TEST-2026-10-26-2217-verify-the-crossing-to-fyr-on-the-dev-box-and-th`).

## The resync loop

```bash
# machine A: change, verify, install, commit, push
fyr install && git add <the file> && git commit -m "context: tweak" && git push
# machine B
fyr update            # fetch; refuse a dirty checkout; if behind: pull --ff-only; rebuild and reinstall
fyr update --check    # only reports; exit 2 when behind, 0 when current; on a dirty checkout it prints the real run's refusal and exits 1 (so does --dry-run)
```

`fyr update` finds the checkout from `$FYR_REPO`, then the working directory or any of its parents, then the path recorded at the last install, so it works from anywhere. It refuses a non-fast-forward pull; resolve that by hand in the checkout.

**`update` refuses a checkout with uncommitted changes, whether or not it is behind.** It deploys the WORKING TREE, not the commit it just fetched, so on a machine where the harness is also being edited it would put half-finished work into the live context — which is what an hourly timer did here on 2026-09-16 (BUG-046). Commit or stash, or run `fyr install` to deploy a dirty tree deliberately. That makes `update` safe to run from a timer:

```ini
# ~/.config/systemd/user/fyr-update.service  — with the matching hourly .timer
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=%h/.local/bin/fyr update --repo %h/workspace/fyr
Environment=PATH=%h/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
```

The dev box's old `sh-agent-update` unit is disabled at its crossing (§ Crossing to fyr), not carried over.

On a box where nobody edits the checkout the timer simply keeps it current; on a box where somebody does, it now declines instead of deploying their draft.

The timer follows `main` by fast-forward: its trust root is whoever can push to this repository, exactly as a hand-typed `fyr update` is. That is the operator, on their own machines, and the accepted position (ADR-030). A box where that is not acceptable runs `fyr update --check` on the timer and updates by hand (on a dirty checkout that run exits 1 with the refusal, not 2). What a tag delivers, and to which place: `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model.

## Releases — tags, as release markers

A release is an annotated `vX.Y.Z` tag on `main`, and the binaries published with it, with their `SHA256SUMS`. No key signs anything (ADR-053, superseding ADR-026's signing, ADR-033's signed checksums and ADR-052). What a tag delivers, and to which kind of place, is `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model (ADR-033, superseding ADR-030 D2; the history of the channel is there too). v3.0.0 is a MAJOR because the installed command changes name; its notes carry § Crossing to fyr. A release is cut by `/preflight vX.Y.Z` from the operator's own turn, from this checkout (never a plain copy), on any machine where the operator is logged in to GitHub (`gh auth status`). Nothing else is tagged: no lightweight tag, no `-rc` suffix, no other prefix. Only a canonical `vX.Y.Z` (no leading zeros, e.g. never `v1.02.2`) counts as a release tag anywhere in this repository's tooling, so never cut one with a leading zero — every place refuses it. The tag is the only version tracking; there is no version file.

Procedure — what `/preflight` runs at its Step 6 here (the skill's Step 6.3 follows a project's Release section), each command its own call, its exit status read before the next; `<gated head>` is the head SHA of the gate report's `Range reviewed:` line, the one external input — the tag itself takes no target, so no placeholder can sit on both sides of a check:
```bash
gh auth status                                                                                          # exit 0: this machine can push and publish
# gate passed and the release commit made (preflight Step 6.3): HEAD is that commit; <gated head> is the head SHA of the gate report's `Range reviewed:` line
go test -count=1 -run TestDeliverySpecCurrent ./cmd/fyr                                                # exit 0: the release's `change` record (ID …-release-vX-Y-Z) and `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § Where things stand both name vX.Y.Z (BUG-167)
test -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all)"                                              # exit 0: clean tree — the bare form inherits status.showUntrackedFiles (BUG-049)
# BEFORE the tag, never after the push: `go:embed` reads the WORKING TREE, so a stray file under the
# five embedded directories is compiled into every released binary. The clean-tree test above cannot
# see an IGNORED file, and a tag is unrecallable once pushed (D23, BUG-066; security review 2026-09-17)
test -z "$(git status --porcelain --ignored --untracked-files=all -- context skills agents commands rules)"   # exit 0: nothing untracked or ignored there
go test -count=1 -run TestEmbedHoldsOnlyTrackedFiles ./...                                             # exit 0: the embedded set is exactly what git tracks
test "$(git rev-parse HEAD^)" = "$(git rev-parse <gated head>)"                                        # exit 0: the release commit sits on the gated head
git diff --quiet <gated head> HEAD -- ':(top)' ':(top,exclude).agents/trail.jsonl'                      # exit 0: records only — ':(top)' because a bare '.' is relative to the cwd and misses a change in a sibling directory (measured)
git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "fyr vX.Y.Z"                                                                     # no target argument: tags HEAD
# check the tag before any push — every line carries its verdict in its exit status:
test "$(git rev-parse vX.Y.Z^{commit})" = "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"                                      # exit 0: the tag is on the release commit
git merge-base --is-ancestor vX.Y.Z^{commit} main                                                       # exit 0: on main
test "$(git cat-file -t vX.Y.Z)" = tag                                                                  # exit 0: annotated ("commit" means lightweight)
git push origin main
git push origin vX.Y.Z                                                                                  # plain pushes, never --force
```

Then the release's binaries (`SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model; R9, ADR-033). Built here, from the tagged tree, never by a service:
```bash
# 0. the contamination guard AGAIN, here: it ran before the tag so a bad tree is
#    never tagged, and it runs again here because `go:embed` reads the working
#    tree at BUILD time — which is after the tag and the pushes, so a .DS_Store
#    or an editor swap file appearing under skills/ in between would otherwise be
#    embedded unguarded (D23, BUG-066; code review 2026-09-17 round 2). Both
#    commands are read-only, so running them twice costs nothing.
test -z "$(git status --porcelain --ignored --untracked-files=all -- context skills agents commands rules)"   # exit 0: nothing untracked or ignored there
go test -count=1 -run TestEmbedHoldsOnlyTrackedFiles ./...                 # exit 0: embedded set == git's
# 1. the three platforms, from the tag's own tree, reproducible flags
for target in linux/amd64 darwin/arm64 linux/arm64; do
  GOOS="${target%/*}" GOARCH="${target#*/}" CGO_ENABLED=0 GOTOOLCHAIN=local \
    go build -trimpath -ldflags "-X main.version=vX.Y.Z" \
    -o ".agents/scratch/release-vX.Y.Z/fyr-${target%/*}-${target#*/}" ./cmd/fyr
done
# 1b. the zip of the tagged tree, for a zip place (ADR-039): `update --from-zip` checks it
#    against this release's SHA256SUMS when that sits beside it
git archive --format=zip --prefix=fyr-vX.Y.Z/ -o .agents/scratch/release-vX.Y.Z/fyr-vX.Y.Z.zip vX.Y.Z
# 2. the checksums, with the VERSION as the first line — `fyr update` refuses a
#    release whose SHA256SUMS names another version or none (D26 of the
#    release-binary plan), and `sha256sum -c` ignores a '#' line
cd .agents/scratch/release-vX.Y.Z
printf '# fyr %s\n' vX.Y.Z > SHA256SUMS
sha256sum fyr-linux-amd64 fyr-darwin-arm64 fyr-linux-arm64 fyr-vX.Y.Z.zip >> SHA256SUMS
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS                                                    # exit 0: the file describes these files
# 3. BEFORE anything is published: this host's own built binary checks the release zip
#    against SHA256SUMS, as a zip place will (ADR-039)
mkdir -p ../zipcheck && "./fyr-$(go env GOOS)-$(go env GOARCH)" update --from-zip fyr-vX.Y.Z.zip --home ../zipcheck --dry-run > ../zipcheck.out   # into a file, never a pipe (BUG-086)
grep -q "CHECKED against the SHA256SUMS of release vX.Y.Z" ../zipcheck.out   # exit 0
# 4. the release, with notes read by the operator before the upload — created with the
#    notes ALONE, then one upload per asset: a create carrying every asset rolls the whole
#    release back when a single upload fails, which is what GitHub did twice for v1.1.0
#    (`HTTP 500: Error creating asset temp dir`), while one call per file then worked first
#    time each. Retry an individual upload before calling it a failure.
gh release create vX.Y.Z --repo github.com/kesokaj/fyr --verify-tag --title "fyr vX.Y.Z" \
  --notes-file ../release-notes-vX.Y.Z.md
for a in SHA256SUMS fyr-linux-amd64 fyr-darwin-arm64 fyr-linux-arm64 fyr-vX.Y.Z.zip; do
  gh release upload vX.Y.Z --repo github.com/kesokaj/fyr "$a" --clobber || echo "retry $a by hand"
done
gh release view vX.Y.Z --repo github.com/kesokaj/fyr --json assets --jq '.assets[].name'   # all five
cd -
```

The release notes are built as § Release notes below says. Before this repository is ever made public, read the trail for what it names (this box's login-shell credential broker, `/etc/profile.d/zz-styrman-credentials.sh`, is described in `BUG-160` § Addendum and the 2026-10-07 security reviews under `reviews/`): the trail, `.agents/trail.jsonl`, carries hostnames (`spgo-mac.roam.internal`, `devbox`), machine paths (`/opt/devbox/deploy/harness`), links to the operator's private web artifacts (the "Harness Delivery Map" page, in the 2026-10-09 handoff and changes entry), and a report record's contents, all of which are fine inside a private repository and are internal identifiers outside one. There is no secret in them — that is checked every release — but publication is a separate decision from releasing, and this is the paragraph that says so (security review 2026-09-18).

Publishing a release changes NOTHING about the repository's visibility: `fyr` stays private, the release page is readable only by accounts that can already read the repository, and every asset download needs that credential — which is what README § Install without cloning depends on. `gh repo view github.com/kesokaj/fyr --json visibility` after the upload is the check; only a deliberate change in the repository's settings makes anything public.

Upload the assets one call at a time, not all of them on `gh release create`: a single create-with-assets call ROLLS THE WHOLE RELEASE BACK when one upload fails, which is what GitHub's upload endpoint did twice for v1.1.0 (`HTTP 500: Error creating asset temp dir`, both attempts leaving no release and the tag intact). Create the release with `--notes-file` alone, then `gh release upload vX.Y.Z --repo github.com/kesokaj/fyr <asset> --clobber` per file, retrying an individual upload before calling it a failure.

Since the Google skills catalog (plan `2026-10-01-google-skills-catalog`) each binary embeds it, about 6 MB more (linux/amd64: 19.9 MB), and the zip of the tree is about 7 MB with some 2,575 entries, inside the 5,000 entries `update --from-zip` accepts; the uploads take correspondingly longer, nothing else in the procedure changes.

After the upload: `gh release view vX.Y.Z --repo github.com/kesokaj/fyr --json assets --jq '.assets[].name'` lists the five assets, and nothing further is pushed anywhere — a binary-only place picks the release up the next time the operator runs `fyr update` there.

### Release notes

Every release carries notes, built from the `change` records dated after the previous tag's commit and read by the operator before the upload (D19). Write `.agents/scratch/release-notes-vX.Y.Z.md` with one line per entry under the groups that have any:

```markdown
## New features
- <entry title> — <one line, from the entry's Summary>
## Improvements and optimisation
## Fixes
- <entry title> (BUG-NNN)
## Other updates
## Install
Download: see README § Install without cloning. Existing binary-only places: `fyr update`; a place on v2.7.0 or earlier: `DEPLOY-remote` § Crossing to fyr (v3.0.0 only).
```

An entry's `## Type` decides its group: `feature` → New features; `task` or `refactor` that changes behaviour → Improvements and optimisation; `bugfix` → Fixes, with its BUG id; rules, skills, docs and context → Other updates. An empty group is left out. The same text goes into the release's own `changes/` entry.
A tag that fails any check: `git tag -d vX.Y.Z`, fix, re-gate. A pushed tag is never moved or deleted; a bad release gets the next PATCH. `git` is never run under `sudo`. The tag checks above (`test` assertions, tag-on-HEAD, parent-is-gated-head, records-only diff, ancestor, annotated) were rehearsed 2026-09-16 in `.agents/scratch/tagcheck/`: passing on a records-only release commit tagged at HEAD, failing on a tag made on the earlier commit, on a release commit carrying a source change, on a dirty tree, and on a lightweight tag. Tags were SSH-signed until v2.3.2; from v2.4.0 they are not (ADR-053).

Version: MINOR for anything an installed place gains (a new or changed skill, agent, command, rule, context rule or installer behaviour), PATCH for a fix to released behaviour only, MAJOR for what an existing deployment must react to (a moved install path, a renamed installed command, a dropped vendor, a `state.json` or manifest shape change, a new required flag) — the context's Git rule. First tag `v1.0.0`, base ref for its gate 4aa19be. The gate's verification row: the `AGENTS.md` Setup commands, `go run ./cmd/fyr install --home .agents/scratch/home` with `status` reporting no drift, and `fyr list` — 34 skills and 8 agents at v2.0.0; a release that changes them says so in its changelog entry. There is no deploy step after the push: each place moves forward with `fyr update` when the operator runs it (`SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model). The handoff after a release names the live tag.

## Verify

Same as `DEPLOY-local` § Verify: `fyr version` unqualified matching what was installed, `fyr status` with no drift and no `shadowed` line, then one start of the CLI. On the Mac, additionally confirm the Antigravity paths — passed 2026-09-04 (`TEST-2026-09-04-verify-mac-real-home`); re-run after a change that touches Antigravity-specific behavior and record the result there.

## Operator steps

Standing by-hand procedures, never pending items (those live in the newest handoff):

- On the Mac after a push from the Linux box: `fyr update`, `fyr status`, then the three smoke checks on Antigravity (`TEST-2026-09-03-verify-real-home`; the Mac procedure is `2026-09-04-verify-mac-real-home.md`).
- After any change to `context/`, `skills/`, or `agents/` is pushed: `fyr update` at each of the four places, when the operator decides to. Nothing else needs refreshing.
- At a place that has been in use, before its harness-target proposals can matter here: run `/retro --harness` in a harness checkout on that place, which reads its own queue under `~/.config/fyr/` (nothing carries a queue between places, ADR-062).
- After a place updates across v4.0.0 (a MAJOR: what an existing deployment must react to, by the Version line of § Releases): its steps are `DEPLOY-local` § The background dreamer (the timer an older fyr installed: `fyr dream --remove-timer`, then `--install-timer`) and § Operator steps (the opt-in registration: `fyr index --register` in each project), and `fyr eval` now takes `--home` (README, the `fyr eval --home DIR` row); the v4.0.0 release notes § Install list the same.
- On a new machine, `gh auth status` must pass before that machine cuts a release; no key is needed (ADR-053).
- Go upgrades on the Mac: `brew upgrade go`. On the Linux box the distribution had nothing newer, so it runs a user-level SDK on PATH ahead of `/usr/bin/go` — the procedure is in `DEPLOY-local` § Operator steps, and it needs no root.

## Roll back

`git checkout <last good commit> && go run ./cmd/fyr install` on the affected machine; `fyr update` will refuse to move until the branch is fast-forwardable again, so push a fix or reset the branch first. A plain copy rolls back by installing the earlier copy. A release-binary place rolls back by downloading the previous release's binary by hand and running `fyr install` — `update` never goes backwards, on purpose (README § Install without cloning).

## Access

Remote boxes are reached only on the operator's explicit request with details they supply. Nothing in this repo assumes a host.

title: GUIDE-eval — the harness's behavioural suite (one row per Antigravity scenario)
body:
# GUIDE-eval — the harness's behavioural suite

The scenarios the harness's Antigravity runs take, one row per scenario, in the format of plan `PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-plan-fyr-eval-the-antigravity-run-kit-as-a-verb` (§ Interfaces, The suite). Each row runs in its own sandbox: a fresh clone of the fixture, a throwaway HOME with this harness installed and the operator's Antigravity login linked in, and the safety checks `fyr eval` makes around the run (refused roots, outside every checkout, the real config unchanged, no new credential in the sandbox home, no process left, the named agent invoked).

Run rows with `fyr eval <id>...` from this checkout (`--fixture DIR` for another fixture, a `--home` outside every checkout); `fyr eval --list` prints them (spec `SPEC-fyr-eval`). A run reads this record's committed copy and refuses while it has uncommitted changes, so every run names the commit its rows came from. These rows are the port of the Antigravity run kit's, which Phase 3 of the plan deleted; the kit's history is in the trail, not here.

## Columns

- **id**: the row's name, one path element; it names the sandbox directory and the metrics label `eval=<id>`.
- **setup**: bash, run in the clone before the CLI starts, as the operator, with `SB` (the sandbox home), `CLONE` (the clone), `FIXDIR` (the fixture), `OUT` and `OUT2` (the two stdout files), `FYR` (the running binary: `$SB/bin/fyr` does not exist until the install, step 6) and the fixture git identity (`fixture`, `f@localhost`). Empty for none; a failed setup fails the row before any CLI runs.
- **prompt**, **prompt2**: literal text handed to `agy -p` after the line naming the project root; prompt2, when present, is a second session on the same home after a clean first exit. Four placeholders are filled by the runner, never by a shell: `{{CLONE}}`, `{{SB}}`, `{{FIXDIR}}`, `{{STAMP}}` (the row's start, `%F-%H%M`).
- **check**: bash, run in the clone with the setup's variables and `HOME` set to the sandbox home; exit 0 is PASS. Only the leading backticked span of a cell is the check: a note after it never reaches bash.
- **agent**: empty, or the agent whose invocation the conversation store must show; the artifact alone would pass if the main agent wrote it itself.
- **grants**: `named` (eval's named command list) or `wide: <reason>` (`command(*)` in the throwaway clone, with the reason printed).

The table carries four optional columns after `grants`, `| version | kind | cluster | expect |` (ADR-085; the rules are `SPEC-fyr-eval` § The suite). Every row has eleven cells, and an empty one takes its default.

- **version**: an integer from 1, bumped on any change to the row's setup, prompts or check, so its history restarts.
- **kind**: `capability` (the default), `regression` (expected to pass every time), `adversarial` (a planted instruction or a lane) or `indicator` (reported, left out of the suite's rate). Today's `adversarial` rows are `agents-security`, `agent-reviewer`, `inject-*`, `lane-*` and `auto-*`; the `regression` rows are `smoke` and `catalog-*`. `fyr metrics evals` prints each kind's rate on a suite line.
- **cluster**: one identifier word, a family name for rows that share a setup or a fixture; the default is the row's id. It is stored and no view reads it.
- **expect**: comma-separated tool names or normalised verbs the trial is expected to use, in the store's vocabulary (`Read`, not `view_file`; `fyr record` is found in `fyr record add --title`), never gating; `fyr metrics evals` and the testing record print the any-order `m of n`.

## Fixture and known limits

- The fixture is the demo service, migrated once to records (`~/sandbox/fyr-eval/fixture`, plan D29); the harness itself is a fixture only for rows that say so.
- The trail is records, so a check that looks for an agent's artifact names a new record: `"$SB/bin/fyr" record list --kind <k> | grep -vxFf "$SB/records-before.txt"`, the store's listing taken before the setup ran (plan O2). An agent drafts under `.agents/scratch/agents/` and the main thread stores the draft, so an agent row's prompt says that storing it is approved.
- A setup runs before the harness is installed and has no `fyr`. One that seeds records appends to `.agents/trail.jsonl` and commits, and the store loads the changed export as it would after a pull. Memories are never exported, so `agent-dreamer`'s setup writes a script that its prompt runs first, through the sandbox's `fyr` (plan D35).
- The fixture's `DEPLOY-local` already names `PORT` and its default, so the documentation rows ask for a `PORT=9090` example, which the check can tell from the fixture's text (D35).
- The rows from `api-auth` on were ported from `GUIDE-skill-matrix` on 2026-10-26 for the v3.0.0 gate's per-skill runs: their checks are the matrix's, with a file the matrix looked for under the old docs tree read as the record that replaced it, `distill` seeding the feedback log as `retro` does, and `dream` adding its one memory through the sandbox's `fyr` in the prompt; `catalog-route` is six rows, one task each, passing when the conversation store shows a read under the expected `google-catalog/catalog/<entry>`.
- Ported from the kit with the plan's changes: shell-expanded stamps and kit variables became placeholders and `$CLONE` / `$SB` (D21); a check cell keeps only its leading span (D23); the `resume` row is struck (D25); the matrix rows come from `GUIDE-skill-matrix` without its `extra` column (D27).
- `rule-agy-dispatch` is the release gate's run of `rules/agy-dispatch.md`: the prompt names a coming `fyr eval` and neither the quota nor the command that reads it, so the check needs `Limit Remaining`, which only `agy -p "/usage"`'s output puts in the conversation store (the rule's text does not hold it), then `argon` and a percentage in the reply, and a clean clone. It does not prove the percentage is the one read.
- `frontend-ui-modern-overrides` is the run D23 of `PLAN.md` owed: whether the skill's `## Harness overrides` beats its 27 contrary lines, read on the `npx shadcn` pin alone: a command line naming `@latest` fails, and a sentence quoting the override does not. It does not cover the publishing or companion-skill overrides.

- The `build-*` rows build an app from nothing and take the blank fixture, `--fixture ~/sandbox/fyr-eval/blank`: a repository holding one commit of a README (`git init -q blank && cd blank && printf '# blank\n\nAn empty project for the build-* rows.\n' > README.md && git add README.md && git commit -qm "blank: README"`). They run `wide`, since a build runs its own toolchain, server and curl, and their checks build, test and call what the agent wrote on ports 18181 and 18182; an untracked `.agents/` is allowed, because the blank project is unscaffolded and has no `.gitignore` until the agent writes one.
- `smoke` is the sandbox form of `GUIDE-testing` § 5's context check, added in the v3.1.0 gate (2026-10-27) when the operator asked for sandbox verification in place of the real-home run: the canary word, the installed skill count read from the rendered context's `Skills (N)` line, every rule file installed under the sandbox's `rules/` present as a `<RULE[...]>` block in the conversation store and, but for `AGENTS.md`, named in the answer, and no `<truncated` line. # fyr — every verb on every kind of place

The verb × place-kind matrix, first built for `PLAN-2026-09-18-sh-agent-works-everywhere` and re-run under `fyr` on 2026-10-25 (audit IN19, plan `2026-10-25-harness-audit-fix.md` D14). A cell is `exercised` (ran, output logged), `refused` (a message naming the cause and the alternative), `n/a` (the verb has no meaning there), `test` (covered by the named Go test, not run by hand here) or `not run` (with the reason). Nothing is blank. The 2026-09-18 cells, recorded under the old binary name, and the real-machine records of that day are in this file's git history (`git show 3797da5:GUIDE-fyr-matrix`).

## How the cells were run (this box, 2026-10-25, tree 3797da5)

Last re-run: 2026-10-27 on tree 75453d1, the v3.1.0 gate's § 3c (`TEST-2026-10-27-1720-verification-v3-1-0-gate-3c-matrix-re-run-v3-0-0`): PASS, 185 cells, none regressed against its previous run. The outputs below are still the 2026-10-25 run's; that record lists the cells whose text changed by then (the directory-in-the-way refusals, `check`'s findings, the newer records), and the cells this table dates later say so.

- **Scripts.** `.agents/scratch/p5/matrix.sh`, `matrix2.sh` and `matrix3.sh`, with logs `run.log`, `run2.log` and `run3.log` beside them (gitignored).
- **Go.** `/usr/bin/go` go1.24.4 (plan D16).
- **The binary's code.** The matrix ran on tree `3797da5`. The Phase 5 commit changes no code the binary carries (one test comment only).
- **Place kinds.** Three kinds, built from a `git clone` of this checkout:
  - **checkout**: the clone itself, driven by a development build (`go build ./cmd/fyr`) with `--repo`.
  - **plain copy**: `git archive HEAD | tar -x`, with no `.git`, driven by the same development build with `--repo`.
  - **release binary**: `go build -trimpath -ldflags "-X main.version=v9.9.9"` of the clone, with no `--repo`.
- **Homes.** Each kind gets a fresh `--home` under `.agents/scratch/p5/matrix/homes/`.
- **PATH.** It holds only links to the tools the verbs call. There is no `gh`, so nothing reaches the network.
- **Environment.** `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` is set to the matrix directory, so the plain copy never finds this checkout's `.git`. No `FYR_*`, `SH_AGENT_*` or `GIT_*` variable is set.
- **`version`.** It was run without `--home`. Its stderr names this box's real `~/.config/sh-agent`, which has not crossed yet. The line says it reads nothing from it.

## Matrix

body:
# Skill matrix — one mock scenario per skill and agent, on Antigravity

The reproducible spec behind `TEST-2026-09-03-verify-sandbox-skills`. The rows below are MANUAL: scripts are not committed (ADR-010), and a run is built by hand in `.agents/scratch/skilltest/` from this file. The rows a release runs unchanged are not here: `project-memory`, `feature`, `bug`, `review`, `review-docs-check`, `requirements-check`, `preflight`, `handoff`, `metrics-feed`, `retro`, `operate`, `documentation`, `discover-skills` and `gcloud-auth`, the rows ported on 2026-10-26 (`api-auth`, `bash`, `cloud-run`, `data`, `distill`, `docker`, `dream`, `explain-project`, `feedback`, `frontend-ui-economist`, `frontend-ui-modern`, `gke`, `golang`, `harness-audit-elsewhere`, `research`, `review-standards`, `spec`, `terraform`, `testing-strategy`, `typescript`, `catalog-no-leak`, `catalog-route-1` to `-6`, `catalog-precedence`), with the `scaffold`, dispatch, agent, inject and lane rows, are in `GUIDE-eval` and run with `fyr eval` (`SPEC-fyr-eval`; `GUIDE-testing` § 4). Prompts for `/grill-me` and `skill-repair` were dropped with those skills; `/grilling` is covered by the `grilling` row typed as `/grilling`.

## Procedure

1. Sandbox home `<home>` logged in to Antigravity; `fyr install --home <home>`, and `HOME=<home>` for every seed below, so no seed writes the real store; demo service checkouts (a three-file Go HTTP service with `/healthz` and `/hello`, scaffolded by `/init-project`, plus the `/version` task). Seeds: three identical tooling corrections stored as global `feedback` records (the `distill-from-log` row's command); for the `bug` row, commit `sed -i 's/name = strings.TrimSpace(name)/name = strings.TrimLeft(name, " ")/' internal/greet/greet.go`.
2. Per row: fresh `git clone` of the demo into `/home/<user>/sandbox/runs/agy-<id>`, base as in the table, then
   - `HOME=<home> agy -p "The project root is the current directory, <dir>; ignore any other checkout. <prompt>" --mode accept-edits --print-timeout 20m`, with `<home>/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` written for the run (`GUIDE-testing` § 4 § Behavioural runs): `"permissions": {"allow": ["command(git)", "command(go)", "command(gofmt)", "command(cat)", "command(ls)", "command(date)", "command(mkdir)", "command(pwd)", "command(grep)", "command(find)", "command(wc)", "command(head)", "command(tail)", "command(printf)", "command(echo)", "command(cp)", "command(ln)", "command(test)", "command(diff)", "command(fyr)", "command(chmod)", "command(readlink)", "command(bash)", "command(python3)", "command(sleep)", "read_file(*)", "write_file(*)"]}` — the grant store knows four actions (`command`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `mcp`; an unknown one is logged as `ignoring invalid allow entry` in `cli.log` and skipped), and `command(<name>)` matches one command name: a `for` loop, a heredoc or a command outside the list (`node`, `docker`, `gcloud`) is denied, and the headless denial names neither the tool nor the command (BUG-141). A row whose skill text itself holds a shell construct, or reaches for a tool the sandbox lacks, runs with `command(*)` in its clone and the log says so (`edit_file(*)` and `list_dir(*)` are invalid entries in agy 1.2.8; its log names them) and `"trustedWorkspaces"` naming only the run's clone; no `toolPermission` key, checked before the batch with `grep -c toolPermission <home>/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` printing `0`; the file and the copied token are deleted by name after the batch (`fyr eval` links the token instead and deletes the link and file after each row). A `command(<name>)` grant allows every argument of that command. A run counts only when its stderr has no "auto-denied" line and the newest `<home>/.gemini/antigravity-cli/log/cli-*.log` has no "invalid allow entry" line; a scenario denied a command it needs gets that one command added here, by name, in the same change. No `gcloud`, `docker`, `terraform` or `npx` is granted: a cloud command is denied, which is the mock. The grants are NOT a security boundary: the sandbox home runs as the operator's own OS user, and `go`, `git`, `bash` and `python3` can each run anything and reach the real home. They are the batch's, not a row's: the fewest the batch as a whole needs. Nothing is protected during a batch; afterwards the copied Antigravity `antigravity-oauth-token` is deleted by name. A row's `--add-dir <path>` extra is passed to `agy` as written (the init rows read the skill templates through it; the headless run also needs a `read_file(<home>/.gemini/config/skills/init-project)` allow-rule).
3. Run the check in the clone with `OUT=<stdout file>`, `SB=<home>` and `HOME=<home>`, so its `fyr` reads the sandbox's store, and with `rec() { fyr record list --kind "$1" | grep -i "$2" | head -1 | cut -d' ' -f1; }` defined: `rec <kind> <words>` prints the newest matching record's ID, empty when none matches. Exit 0 is PASS. A check cell writes each `|` as `\|`, the table's escape, so a driver built from this file unescapes it before running the check. Then read the CLI's transcript (`<home>/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/*.db`, `steps.step_payload`) for skills loaded and agents dispatched, and audit every executed command for `gcloud|terraform|docker (build|run|push)|kubectl|git push|npx skills add`.
4. Drive with `xargs -P 3` under a monitor that outlives a ten-minute tool timeout. Never edit the driver while runs are in flight.

title: Verification guide — fyr
body:
# Verification guide — fyr

The standing procedure for this repo. Written under the rule in `agents/verifier/agent.md`
("What to run"): the first run under a new project writes this guide; later runs cite
it and record outcomes only. Update this file in the same run that changes the steps.

## 1. Go checks (every change, including one that touches only `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/` or `rules/`: the root package's embed tests compare those trees with the binary's embedded copy, so a new file or mode there fails here, BUG-137)

```bash
gofmt -l cmd internal     # must print nothing; NOT `gofmt -l .` — it walks .agents/scratch,
                          # where a stray Go file fails a gate that has nothing to do with it (BUG-048)
go vet ./...
go test -race -timeout 30m ./...   # -timeout 30m: on a one-CPU box (nproc = 1) cmd/fyr takes ~13 min under -race,
                                   # past Go's 10-minute default per-package timeout (a larger machine: ~62 s)
```

The suite does not depend on the caller's environment: every test package whose tests run git drops `GIT_*` variables in a `TestMain` (git exports them inside a hook, and they would aim a fixture's git at another repository) and then sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, so the operator's git config (a `core.hooksPath`, a signing key) never reaches a fixture commit (the v5.0.0 gate's security review), pinned by the root package's `TestGitTestPackagesDropGitVariables` for every package whose test files name the git binary (a literal `"git"`; one that reaches git only through another package's helper, such as `trail.Command`, is not seen by the pin). A check for that, when a test helper that runs git changes: `GIT_DIR=/nonexistent go test ./...`.

`go test ./...` also runs `TestFunctionLength` (`funclen_test.go`): it fails on a non-test function over 50 lines (`rules/code-modularity.md` item 1) in any `.go` file git lists, tracked or untracked but not ignored, unless its allowlist `longFuncs` names it (empty since `PLAN-2026-10-27-funclen`), and on a stale allowlist row.

## 2. Harness self-check (every change to `context/`, `agents/`, or `skills/`)

```bash
go run ./cmd/fyr list           # sanity: every skill and agent parses; its section headers print the counts
go run ./cmd/fyr render | wc -l        # rendered context/AGENTS.md must stay under 100 lines
go test ./internal/harness/... -run 'TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock|TestRenderedContextUnderTarget' -v   # a change to context/*.md
  # or rules/*.md must pass this: it renders the real checkout plus every rules/*.md and pins the
```
