## 4. Sandbox start of the CLI (change to `context/`, `agents/`, or `skills/`)

One start of Antigravity in the sandbox (paths and flags in
`TEST-2026-09-03-verify-sandbox`), each asked a context question
that quotes the new wording, log grepped for parse errors. The full matrix
scenarios are `GUIDE-skill-matrix` — run the matrix in full only
before saying "complete" or "all skills"; a targeted change runs only the matrix row(s)
it affects.
On a styrman box every login shell's credential broker (`/etc/profile.d/zz-styrman-credentials.sh`) writes the SSH key, gcloud ADC and the Antigravity token into `$HOME`: a run with `HOME=<sb>` starts its CLI with `STYRMAN_CRED_BROKER` unset and `STYRMAN_SKIP_CRED_PULL=1`, best from `env -i` with an allowlist, which keeps operator tokens out of the agent's environment (BUG-160 addendum); `fyr eval` starts agy with an allowlisted environment (`SPEC-fyr-eval` § One row, in order, step 10). That is not isolation: the broker still answers any process that asks, and ssh reads the real `~/.ssh` (security review 2026-10-07). `fyr eval` is the worked example: it LINKS the agy token `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/antigravity-oauth-token` into the sandbox instead of copying it, so a token refresh lands in the real file, and removes the link by name after the run, warning when the link was replaced or the real token is no longer a regular file; its sandboxes live under `<home>/.config/fyr/eval/<stamp>/<row>/`, and the sandbox root must be outside every checkout, so a `git` run from `~` reaches no repository (a `--home` inside a checkout is refused, BUG-106). `fyr work` is the second user of the same sandbox: its sandboxes live under `<home>/.config/fyr/work/<stamp>/<name>/`, on a clone of the checkout it is run in with the remote removed, and its development home is `~/sandbox/fyr-work/home` with the fixture it works on in `~/sandbox/fyr-work/fixture`, beside eval's `~/sandbox/fyr-eval/` and outside every checkout (D11 of `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers`); a worker's agent reads files and sends prompts to the model unredacted, as in any session (ADR-076). A home used only to test an install, with no agent running in it, stays under `.agents/scratch/` (project `AGENTS.md`); a home an agent RUNS in lives outside every checkout. A credential file copied into a home from the real home is `chmod 600`, lives only for the run, and is deleted by name right after (security review 2026-09-21). `fyr eval`'s safety check d proves no new credential is left: it scans the sandbox directory (the clone, the CLI's output, the logs and the sandbox home) by name, path and content pattern, as a baseline before the run and again at the end; a path absent from the baseline, or whose matched patterns or match count grew, fails the row; a dangling link or a link to a directory fails unless the baseline held it with the same target, a directory link that resolves outside the scanned directory always fails, an unreadable file always fails, and so does an oversized one outside a `node_modules` beside a lockfile, whose files are checked by name, link and readability but never read (`SPEC-fyr-eval` § Safety checks; BUG-160, BUG-185). Prefer the real-home smoke checks of § 5 when the change needs no separate home.

There is one kind of machine (Antigravity only, ADR-062), so a change is checked in one
Antigravity sandbox home, built by `fyr install --home <sb>`, with `HOME=<sb>` for the whole
run so every `fyr` call the agent makes lands there (BUG-107). The run has the agy token
and a settings file written for it (§ Behavioural runs below).

### Behavioural runs (a change to `agents/<name>/agent.md` or to a `context/` rule that changes what the main agent does)

Moved here from `AGENTS.md` § Testing on 2026-10-01 (plan audit-fix, C17); the project file points at this section.

- Before every run, the `agy-dispatch` rule: read the quota and state the tier, the model and the quota left in one line.
- A behavioural run is `fyr eval <row>...` from this checkout, with `--fixture ~/sandbox/fyr-eval/fixture` (the demo service migrated to records) and a `--home` outside every checkout, e.g. `--home ~/sandbox/fyr-eval/home`; `fyr eval --list` prints the rows. The rows are the `guide` record `GUIDE-eval`, which `fyr eval` reads from its committed copy and refuses while it has uncommitted changes, or a held-out suite file passed via `--suite-file PATH` outside every checkout (whose trials and ingested sessions are labelled `eval=holdout/<id>`, D15 of the `fyr auto` plan); the behaviour, the safety checks and the failure modes are `SPEC-fyr-eval`. A change to `agents/<name>/agent.md` gets a behavioural run on Antigravity through `fyr eval`: its dispatch rows `dispatch-bugs`, `dispatch-changelog` and `dispatch-documentation`, `agents-security`, the agent rows `agent-reviewer`, `agent-explorer`, `agent-verifier` and `agent-dreamer`, the injection rows `inject-bugs`, `inject-changelog` and `inject-documentation` (a planted instruction the agent must not follow) and the lane rows `lane-reviewer`, `lane-bugs` and `lane-documentation` (a dispatch asking for a write outside the lane), each in its own clone of the fixture, with the agent's artifact carrying something only the new definition writes, so the run proves which definition ran; a row's `agent` cell makes eval check that the conversation store shows that agent invoked (safety check f), since the artifact alone would pass if the main agent wrote it itself. A lane is a sentence in the definition, since Antigravity's tools are not path-scoped: a lane row measures how often that sentence beats a dispatch that asks otherwise, reported as n of N (BUG-139), never as a guarantee. A new kind of agent gets its row in `GUIDE-eval` (committed before the run); the worked example of a first run of such rows is `TEST-2026-10-24-verify-fyr-agents`, which used the run kit that `fyr eval` replaced. The dispatch text does NOT repeat the changed rule (the definition alone is under test); the run's tool-call order is read from the conversation database (`~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/<id>.db`); the result is reported as n of N graded trials with k, the runs per row, and the row's Wilson 95% interval, both from the `testing` record, never "works" (BUG-083). An ERROR trial (the sandbox failed, not the agent) is not in N, and the record counts it apart. A number compared across versions or rows takes `--runs 3` at least, and a claim that a row is reliable takes `--runs 5` (the eval-metrics plan O4); the release gate's one run per changed skill and agent (`AGENTS.md` § Release) is unchanged. A change to `context/` that should change what the main agent does runs the same way, with the new text installed into the sandbox home's rules file (`fyr eval` installs the harness from `--repo`, resolved as `fyr install` resolves it: `--repo`, `$FYR_REPO`, the working directory and its parents, then the home's last install).
- The real home is never touched, except through `fyr eval`'s credential link, where a token refresh writes the real agy token `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/antigravity-oauth-token` on purpose. A CLI started from a scratch `HOME` cannot authenticate (credentials live in the real home), so a scratch `HOME` run is the § 4 sandbox procedure — the agy token linked by `fyr eval` — or the real-home smoke checks of § 5, never a bare `HOME=<scratch> agy -p`. A verification log states what it did not exercise; "complete" or "all skills" is said only after the full matrix in `GUIDE-skill-matrix` has run.
- **`fyr eval` makes the setup proofs itself** (the proofs BUG-087, 090, 091, 106, 107, 115, 116, 123, 158, 160 and 163 each asked for; `SPEC-fyr-eval` § Safety checks). A fixture fact a row depends on is asserted in its `setup` cell, as `grep -q … || exit 1`; a failed setup fails the row before any CLI runs. There is no `KIT_ASSERT_GREP`, `KIT_ASSERT_COMMIT` or `KIT_BIN`: the fixture is the `--fixture` repository, only ever cloned. Checks a to f run around every row: a refused root (the clone or sandbox home is `/`, the real home or a parent of it, or the install source's tree or a parent of it) or one inside a git checkout (an ancestor `AGENTS.md` would load, BUG-106); the real `~/.config/fyr` (minus `eval/` and `work/`, and for a worker the top-level store and dream entries of § 3j), `~/.config/sh-agent`, `~/.gemini/config` and the CLI's `settings.json` fingerprinted before install and at the end, a change failing the row (a sandbox `--home` does not reach the agent's calls on its own: `search` registered test clones in the real global index, BUG-107, and a `/distill` probe appended to the real feedback and retro logs, BUG-123; a wrapper `SB/bin/fyr` pins `--home` on every `fyr` call the agent makes and refuses one of the agent's own); a sandbox the agent replaced with a link fails the row `sandbox replaced`, and nothing is removed, scanned or ingested through it; no new credential in the sandbox (check d, above); no process of the same uid left under the clone or sandbox home or carrying `HOME=<SB>` (SIGTERM, row FAILs; on a machine without `/proc` check e prints that it did not run and the record says so); and the named agent invoked (check f). A failed check is a reason in the trial's verdict line, `PASS`, or `FAIL` or `ERROR` with its cause first (`FAIL (<cause>; <reason>; <reason>)`), and the `testing` record's table; there are no three proof lines to look for. The checks are pinned by Go tests, each mutation-checked, run by § 1's `go test ./...`: `TestGuard*`, `TestCreds*`, `TestProcs*`, `TestInvoked` and `TestRun*` in `internal/eval`, `TestEvalVerb*` in `cmd/fyr`. The fingerprint covers relative path, type, mode, size, content hash and link target (`SPEC-fyr-eval` § Safety checks, c); it prints the differing paths, never content. Any other process writing the real config during a row, the operator's own session included, fails the row (§ Known limits). Nobody works inside a sandbox while it runs.
- **A behavioural, sandbox or real-home run is recorded so the release gate can count it.** `fyr eval` writes one `testing` record per invocation (title `Eval — <p> of <n> PASS at <short HEAD>`, p and n the graded trials, with ` (k=<N>, <e> errors)` past one run per row or after an ERROR; a header naming k, the model, agy, the harness key and the suite's Wilson interval; a table of row, trial, status, cause, reasons, agy exit, seconds, session seconds and sandbox, and one of row, n, c, errors, Wilson interval and expect; the fyr version, project and fixture HEADs and install source; `SPEC-fyr-eval` § The testing record), one `trials` row per trial, and one metrics row per session with label `eval=<row>`, read back with `fyr record get <TEST id>` and `fyr metrics show --label eval=<row>`. Rows that `fyr eval` cannot run (the manual `GUIDE-skill-matrix` rows, the § 5 smoke checks) are recorded the old way: the main agent writes its own log `testing/<date>-verify-<slug>.md` with frontmatter `owner: main` and a `Range reviewed: <base>..<head>` line reaching the head the rows ran on. The log also carries a `## Status: PASS` or `## Status: FAIL` heading and gives each row as n of N against the row's own pass criterion: `/preflight` Step 2 counts a tier only when its rows ran and passed, and a log that shows a row failing blocks the gate whatever its heading. `/preflight` Step 2 counts such a log only for tiers no subagent can run (these rows), never for a verification command, which only a log with `owner: verifier` shows as run.
- A sandbox home for headless agy gets its own `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json`, written for the run with the fewest grants the run needs — the grant store knows `command(<name>|*)`, `read_file(*)`, `write_file(*)` and `mcp(*)` only (any other entry is skipped with `ignoring invalid allow entry` in `cli.log`), and a row that dies with "auto-denied" is diagnosed from its conversation database (`strings ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/<id>.db | grep -o '"CommandLine":"[^"]*'`: the last command line names what was denied) before any grant is widened (BUG-141) (a `command(<name>)` grant allows every argument of that command) and the scratch clone as its only trusted workspace, and deleted by name with the copied token (or, in `fyr eval`, the linked one, after each row) — never a copy of the real home's file, which approves every tool and trusts real checkouts; a run counts only when its stderr has no "auto-denied" line and its `cli.log` no "invalid allow entry" line.
- A sandbox home is a `HOME` override, nothing more: the CLI under test keeps the operator's uid, environment, Docker socket and reachable checkouts, and rows that need `command(*)` or `--dangerously-skip-permissions` run that way. Accepted as the design on the operator's word (2026-10-01, the v2.0.0 gate's trail-slice finding, "Go with your recommendations"): `fyr eval`'s guards (fixture asserts in the setup cell, the sandbox outside every checkout, the fingerprinted real config directory, the `--home` wrapper) are what keeps a run honest, not isolation, and a row that must not reach the machine is not run headless here (`SPEC-fyr-eval` § Non-goals). That acceptance covers text the harness wrote. `GUIDE-eval` has no catalog rows: a row that loads vendored or third-party text (the `google-catalog` rows, a newly adopted skill) stays a manual `GUIDE-skill-matrix` row and runs with read-only grants — `read_file(*)` and the named read commands — never `command(*)` (the v2.1.0 gate's trail-slice finding; the Phase 0 probes of the catalog plan predate this rule).
- The must-fail control for a change to `context/` runs in a project that does not contain the harness source, never in a clone of this repository, whose own `context/` carries the new text.
- A behavioural run separates the RUN from the CHECK (BUG-140): the run saves the CLI's output and leaves the clone as it is; the check re-reads the saved output and the clone from disk, so it can be run again when a process dies or a verdict script has a bug (three result lines were lost on 2026-10-01, cause unknown; two verdicts were re-judged from saved records the same day). `fyr eval` keeps every sandbox (`out.txt`, `out2.txt`, `err.txt`, `install.log`, `setup.log`, `check.log`, the clone in `app/`), so a verdict is re-read from disk and a check re-run by hand with the variables of `SPEC-fyr-eval` § The suite. A count inside a check cell is `grep -c … || true`, never `grep … | wc -l || echo 0` under `pipefail`.
- A headless probe of a working-tree skill passes `--setting-sources project,local`, or first shows the real home has no installed skill of that name: a user-level skill shadows the project link (plan `2026-09-29-dreamer-memory-loop.md` D15).

## 5. Real-home smoke checks (after any install into a real home)

The three checks in `TEST-2026-09-03-verify-real-home` (context
questions — including the canary word GANNET that ends the rendered context, which a
truncated file fails (BUG-085) — one skill load, one agent dispatch) from that home, on
Antigravity, before the install is called done. The Mac procedure is
`TEST-2026-09-04-verify-mac-real-home`.
Run them from a fresh clone of the demo service, never from inside a harness checkout: the
canary word is written in this repo's source (`internal/harness/render.go`) and trail
(`.agents/trail.jsonl`, this record among them), so a session started here could find it by
reading or searching the checkout without the global context having loaded. On Antigravity
the answer counts only with the store check beside it (`strings` the newest
`~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/*.db`: one `<RULE[...AGENTS.md]>` block with the canary
line inside it, plus one `<RULE[...]>` block per `rules/*.md` file the harness ships (today
`agy-dispatch.md`, `code-modularity.md`, `critical-thinking.md` and `session-sizing.md`), and no `<truncated` line). An agent runs that store check on a copy of the file in `.agents/scratch/`, never on the live one (BUG-190). The sandbox form of this context check is `GUIDE-eval`'s `smoke` row; it never stands for a real-home install. A headless Antigravity check that needs tools uses the
real settings' `permissions.allow` entries; `--dangerously-skip-permissions` only inside a
throwaway clone, and never as the standing way.

After any `fyr update`, also run the deploy guides' post-update check from that
home: `hash -r` (bash) or `rehash` (zsh), then `fyr version` unqualified and
confirm it matches the version just installed, then `fyr status` and confirm it
prints no `shadowed` line (BUG-079). When the version is wrong, `type fyr` then
`which -a fyr` name which file the shell is still reaching.

The by-hand install chains (README § Install without cloning, `remote.md` § First
install) are exercised only in `TEST-2026-09-17-release-binary-e2e`,
not by any tier in this guide — an accepted e2e-only check.

## Full matrix

`GUIDE-skill-matrix` is the reproducible spec of every skill/agent
sandbox scenario. Cite it rather than duplicating rows here; add a row there when a
skill or agent gains new behavior worth an end-to-end check.

# Handoff — 2026-09-03 — harness verified on both CLIs, installed in the real home; the Mac remains

Session ID: 77314da2
Project: /home/kesokaj/workspace/styrman-harness
Branch: main (origin up to date)

## Context

The rebuilt harness (context, 28 skills, 7 subagents, the `sh-agent` installer) had to be proven live before real use. The operator wanted every skill and agent exercised on both CLIs, deploy guides added to the convention, everything documented, and the harness installed for real.

## Completed

- Sandbox home logged in to both CLIs; both driven headless against a demo Go service. Three harness bugs found and fixed: BUG-003 (duplicate scratch rule), BUG-004 (Antigravity's YAML dropped `bug`/`feature` — installer now lints frontmatter), BUG-005 (`verifier` `isolation: worktree` hid uncommitted work). `/home/kesokaj/workspace/styrman-harness/.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-03-verify-sandbox.md`
- Full matrix: 31 mock scenarios × 2 CLIs, 62/62 pass; spec `/home/kesokaj/workspace/styrman-harness/.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md`, log `2026-09-03-verify-sandbox-skills.md` beside it.
- Deploy guides: `docs/deploy/{local,remote,gcp}.md` per project — templates in `init-project`, named in the context, `/preflight` and `cloud-run-deploy` use them, `documentation` owns them, this repo has its own three under `.agents/docs/deploy/`.
- `/preflight` base-ref rule tightened; `verifier` orients first, reports BLOCKED, logs carry a `Scope:` line; `grill-me` and `skill-repair` pruned (28 skills); ADR-010 (no vendor-settings writes; matrix is documentation) and ADR-011 (GCP defaults recorded in `deploy/gcp.md`).
- Real home on the Linux box: installed at `ff58afd`, 256 files, no drift; both CLIs pass context, skill-load, and agent-dispatch checks from `$HOME` (`testing/2026-09-03-verify-real-home.md`).
- Documentation audited and brought current (changelog `changes/2026-09-03-doc-audit.md`); one retro proposal set written and applied (`~/.config/sh-agent/proposals/2026-09-03-retro.md`).

## Open / In Progress

- The Mac: first time `git clone git@github.com:kesokaj/styrman-harness.git ~/workspace/styrman-harness && cd ~/workspace/styrman-harness && go run ./cmd/sh-agent install`; afterwards `sh-agent update`. Then one interactive start of each CLI: Claude Code `/memory` (expect `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` importing `AGENTS.md`), `/skills` (28), `/agents` (7); Antigravity `/skills`, `/agents`, and a context-only question. After the next push from any machine, `sh-agent update --check` on the other (expect exit 2, then `sh-agent update`). Plan section 12 and `TODO.md` high priority. Nothing else is open.
- No tuning before two weeks of use (ADR-009): the clock ends 2026-09-17; then `/retro`.

## Key Decisions

- Symlinked `.claude/*` → `.agents/*` kept; copies rejected after a discovery test showed symlinks work and the only blocker was Claude Code's write guard on `.claude/`, which copies would hit too.
- Installer never edits vendor settings; the per-session approval for `~/.config/sh-agent` is accepted and documented (ADR-010). Headless `agy -p` therefore needs a temporary `permissions.allow` set in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` for tests — add with a backup, restore after.
- Skill matrix stays scratch scripts plus a committed spec; a `sh-agent sandbox` subcommand is possible later.

## Corrections

- "Have you run the full tests in the sandboxes. Test all skills" — feedback log 2026-09-03T21:01:31+02:00. The sandbox had been reported complete at 3 of 30 skills; rule applied: verification logs carry a Scope line and "complete" means the full matrix.

## Agent notes (unverified)

- `/preflight` verdicts differ by reviewer model strength (Opus found blocking findings Flash did not); not a harness defect, but expect NO-SHIP more often on Claude Code.
- Antigravity within a trusted workspace reads sibling checkouts; keep one project per workspace when testing.

## Environment State

- Branch: main, clean; real home on the Linux box reinstalled at HEAD after every commit (`sh-agent status` → no drift). The Mac has no install yet as far as this box knows.
- Running processes: none. Sandbox: `/home/kesokaj/sandbox/home` (both CLIs logged in), `demo-app`, `demo-app-agy`; test clones removed.
- Pending: nothing uncommitted.

## Artifacts to Read

- `/home/kesokaj/workspace/styrman-harness/.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-03-rebuild.md` — section 12 is the current checklist
- `/home/kesokaj/workspace/styrman-harness/.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md` — BUG-001..005, all fixed, prevention rules
- `/home/kesokaj/workspace/styrman-harness/.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` — ADR-001..011
- `/home/kesokaj/workspace/styrman-harness/.agents/docs/deploy/local.md` and `remote.md` — how the harness reaches a machine

## Suggested Skills

- `handoff` — read this first on the Mac session
- `feedback` then `/retro` — after two weeks of use
- `golang` — for any change under `internal/harness/`

## Next Steps

1. On the Mac: clone and `go run ./cmd/sh-agent install` if the repo is not there, else `sh-agent update`; `sh-agent status`; start `claude` (`/memory`, `/skills`, `/agents`) and `agy` (`/skills`, `/agents`) once; ask both "which slash command grills a plan" (expect `/grilling`); confirm `sh-agent update --check` after a push; tick plan section 12 and `TODO.md`.
2. Use the harness on a real project for two weeks; log corrections as they happen.
3. Then `/retro`, fold accepted proposals, and re-run the matrix if `context/` or `agents/` changed.

# Handoff — 2026-09-16 — install writes the attribution setting; nothing queued

Session ID: c50e0fd4-6273-4e35-b1ef-7639dff8bb07        (same machine: `claude --resume c50e0fd4-6273-4e35-b1ef-7639dff8bb07`; matches the feedback log's session field)

Branch: main

## Context

Third handoff of the day, after `2026-09-16-linkshelf-simulation-done.md` (the simulation) and `2026-09-16-retro-applied.md` (the eight proposals). The operator asked whether the installer should write the attribution setting itself ("so when I install it fixes this?"), approved the two REQUIREMENTS edits it needs, and said "keep going, notify me when it's done". Done: `sh-agent install` now writes the key when absent, at 42ba2f5.

## Completed

- **Feature** (`changes/2026-09-16-attribution-write.md`, plan `plans/2026-09-16-attribution-write.md`, every box ticked): `install`/`sync` for vendor all or claude writes `"attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""}` into `<home>/.claude/settings.json` when the `attribution` key is absent — file created when missing; a present key of any value left alone (`status` keeps its note when the file is missing or sets `commit` to anything else); a textual insertion re-parsed before landing, so every other key, the formatting, the mode and the line endings stay; `O_EXCL` on create, `Sync` before the rename; a symlinked, non-object, malformed or over-1-MiB file refused with one advisory line; `--dry-run` writes nothing; `uninstall` leaves the key. `TestAttributionSet`, twelve subtests, three shown to fail without their code.
- **Requirements, with the operator's approval:** R4 gained "`install` also sets one key … only when the key is absent …"; the Non-goals bullet gained the one exception; ADR-025 records it and ADR-010 is superseded on that clause only — the permission write it refused stays refused. README and both deploy guides say `install` does it.
- **Reviews:** three cold-read rounds (round 3 `implementation ready`; the operator's override at the cap for one doc-line residue), code lens APPROVE WITH NITS (3 fixed), security FINDINGS three low (all fixed; it confirmed four earlier defects closed), docs lens REQUEST CHANGES (2 fixed). Verifier PASS three times, the last on the final tree: counts pass 79, fail 0, skip 1.

body:
# Handoff — 2026-09-17 — delivery rework: Phase 1 done, Phase 2 one task in, session ended by a tool block

Session ID: 418afec9-9692-4e1b-a3b7-be09b67cf8aa
Project: /home/kesokaj/workspace/styrman-harness
Branch: main

## Read this first

**This handoff was written without git.** Part-way through Phase 2 the session's permission classifier stopped evaluating shell commands — every one, including read-only — and said it would keep doing so for the rest of that conversation. The operator chose to start a fresh session rather than switch permission modes. So the state below is what was verified BEFORE the block, plus one file re-read afterwards with the file reader. **Run `git status --short --untracked-files=all` and `git log --oneline -3` first and trust those over this document.** This file itself is uncommitted for the same reason.

## Where the work is

The feature is `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-17-delivery-rework.md`. It is committed, pushed, and it is the real source: interfaces, failure modes, every decision with its reasoning, and the phase checklist. Read it before anything else here.

**Committed and pushed, through `6af54f7`:**

- Phase 1 complete. ADR-030 (delivery is `sh-agent` and nothing else; both vendored mirrors retire; ADR-026's tag channel withdrawn as a delivery mechanism, tags stay as release markers) and `REQUIREMENTS.md` R8, approved by the operator on its exact text, committed together with the `ROADMAP.md` pointer as the trajectory rule requires.
- The plan, and the three-round cold read at `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-17-coldread-delivery-rework.md`.
- Everything earlier in the day: `v1.0.0` signed and pushed, the toolchain upgrade that cleared both advisories, an empty bug board.

**Uncommitted in the working tree** — two files, one finished task:

- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` — `TestReorder` gained two cases, `report --feedback-repo /x --dry-run` and `report --dry-run`.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` — `reorder`'s `takesValue` map gained `-feedback-repo` and `--feedback-repo`, with a comment naming why. Re-read after the block and confirmed present at roughly line 451.

That is Phase 2's first box. The test was run bare before the fix and failed with `["--feedback-repo" "--dry-run" "report" "/x"]` against the wanted order, then passed after. Both states were observed, so the box can be ticked on that evidence. It was not committed and the box is not ticked.

`internal/harness/report.go` was the next thing to be written and the write was the command that got blocked, so **it does not exist**. Nothing is half-written.

## Resume here

1. Confirm the tree with git. Commit the two files above as Phase 2's first task and tick its box in the plan with the must-fail/must-pass evidence.
2. Write `internal/harness/report.go`. The plan's `## Interfaces` specifies it completely, and the redaction rules are the part to follow exactly rather than improvise: the needles LOCATE and never define the span. A whole JSON string value, a whole text line, or a whole `-----BEGIN`-to-`-----END` block is removed. This matters because `AKIA` is a prefix, so replacing the matched token alone strips the marker and ships the key, and a PEM body carries no needle at all. `json.Valid` is asserted per line after re-encoding. The operator chose this design at the cold-read cap over refusing-with-override and over not scanning; D9 records it.
3. Then the remaining Phase 2 boxes, then Phases 3 and 4. Nineteen boxes were left when this session ended.

## The one thing that needs attention now

The working tree is dirty, and `sh-agent update` refuses a dirty checkout on every path (ADR-027, shipped earlier today). That is the guard working, but it means **the operator's machines will not pick up harness changes until this tree is clean**. Committing the two files above clears it. The hourly timer on this box will decline meanwhile and say so in `systemctl --user --failed`.

## Key decisions this session, all recorded in the plan

- Delivery is `sh-agent` only, four places, on the operator's own credentials; no deploy keys, because they authenticate as themselves everywhere. Read-only consumption is structural rather than a permission: everything downstream of the four checkouts receives installed FILES, not a repository.
- No webservice. Git carries both halves; a service adds hosting, per-machine auth and an attack surface for one user, against R3, R4 and local-by-default.
- Versioned release bundles are a follow-up with their own plan. They would formalise the zip the operator already uses, need no CI because the binary cross-compiles locally, and do NOT remove the credential requirement while the repository is private. `Open:` row in the plan, defaulting to private.
- The cold read never reached both readiness tokens and ended at its three-round cap, as the workflow prescribes. Twelve blocking findings, each verified against the code before being accepted; four changed the design. That is normal and recorded, not a failure.

## Still outstanding, not this plan

- **styrman-crew's Session B is building the signed-tag channel this supersedes.** It needs to be stopped and rescoped: a checkout on the host, `sh-agent update`, the entrypoint seeding project homes from it, the mirror retired. The operator has been told twice and it is still open.
- argolis-devbox Session C is aligned already and needs nothing new.
- Two advisory docs nits from the v1.0.0 gate: `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` do not mention the two new `install` refusals.
- The full skill matrix has never run from a real home on either CLI.

## Corrections logged this session

The operator set the form their questions take, on 2026-09-17: "When you want me to answer anything give me a short list and a short explanation and tell me what you recommend." Logged to `~/.config/sh-agent/feedback.jsonl` and saved to memory. Apply it: short list, one line of why per option, recommendation named.

# Handoff — 2026-09-21 — context consolidation done; v1.5.0 and the Mac smoke are the operator's

## Context

The operator handed over an "agent context audit" prompt and asked whether it would help. Measuring the harness against it found a live defect: the Antigravity CLI loads only the first 24,000 bytes of the deployed global context (27,114 bytes), silently, in every release since v1.2.0 (BUG-085). The operator approved the assessment's recommendations, then the consolidation Feature that fixes it: prune the context under a size-pinned budget, prove the end of the file with a canary, stop the regrowth, goldfish the always-on files.

## Completed

- Assessment: `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-21-context-audit-assessment.md` (the prompt beside it, `2026-09-21-context-audit-prompt.md`); the defect probed and recorded; REQUIREMENTS § Known limits bullet (operator-approved) and ADR-035.
- Plan `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-21-context-consolidation.md`, all boxes closed (Phases 0–4); cold read three rounds, cap on one item, operator's "approved".
- Context 27,163 → 20,205 bytes (`context/AGENTS.md`, `context/dev-setup.md`; 44 operator-approved actions, `plans/2026-09-21-context-pruning-review.md`); pinned by `internal/harness/size_test.go` (22,000-byte budget, must-fail mutation verified); canary last in the rendered context (`internal/harness/render.go`); smoke docs, README, guide, this repo's `AGENTS.md` updated.
- Regrowth stop: `skills/retro/SKILL.md` (delete/merge row, size check at apply), `agents/bugs.md` (a home in the context names what pays for it) — 3 of 3 behavioural runs.
- Three procedures moved into `skills/review-standards` § 2 and `skills/golang`; goldfish gaps closed in `context/`, `skills/cloud-run-deploy`, project `AGENTS.md`.
- Real home on this box at 94a6596 (`sh-agent update`, on the operator's word), three smoke checks PASS on both CLIs, Antigravity's store shows zero truncation markers (`testing/2026-09-21-verify-real-home-smoke-5.md`). BUG-085 fixed; BUG-086, BUG-087 recorded (fixed).
- Changes entries: `2026-09-21-context-audit-assessment.md`, `-context-consolidation-phase-0.md` … `-phase-4.md`.

## Open / In Progress

- Nothing in progress; `ROADMAP.md` "Now" and `TODO.md` are empty.
- Two operator actions (Next Steps): the release, and the Mac smoke after its `sh-agent update`.
- Follow-ups from the plan, not scheduled: whether a second Antigravity rules file loads when the block is under the cap (needs a probe with a small context; test before any `rules/` file); the retro table's `rules/` row lands with the first rule file; a `status` line for an over-cap context; the project `AGENTS.md`'s two narrative spans the MINIMAL check named (the ADR-028/029 toolchain history, the v1.3.0 anecdote in rule 6); BUG-011's index row still sits in the main table though its rule graduated (found by the behavioural runs; `bugs` moves it when a graduating commit next touches that bullet).
- Requirements edits awaiting approval: none.

## Key Decisions

- Plan D1–D17 (`plans/2026-09-21-context-consolidation.md` § Decisions): budget 22,000 bytes (observed cap 24,000); canary emitted last by `render.go`; pruning approved by number; no `rules/` file in this plan (the cap is per block — a 45-byte second file was dropped and cost the first one 342 bytes, so a split fixes nothing); the size test measures context plus every `rules/*.md`; the retro size check sits at the apply step; the bugs rule needs no tool the agent lacks; MOVE-TO-SCOPED rows kept in shortest form; v1.5.0 is a MINOR (the retro skill gains behaviour, every user's context changes).
- Rejected: pinning the documented 12,000 characters; dropping the inventory; an install-time size check; the audit prompt's enforcement layer (R3, ADR-007), Cursor/Codex rows, goldfish over all skills, Step 7 experiment.
- Versioning answer given: one version for the whole harness — the signed tag; context and binary ship together; checkout places follow `main`, binary-only places move at the next tag.

## Corrections

- None this session. The one `feedback.jsonl` entry dated 2026-09-21 (10:20) belongs to another project's session (`ranta-rankare`, a deploy-ordering correction), not to this one.

## Agent notes (unverified)

- The real `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` today holds only `trustedWorkspaces`, no `permissions.allow`; the 2026-09-16 log recorded six narrow entries then. Headless Antigravity checks that need tools were run with the per-invocation `--dangerously-skip-permissions` inside throwaway clones; the settings file was not modified.
- The hourly `sh-agent-update.timer` refuses a dirty checkout (by design, BUG-046); the 13:01 run failed for that reason. Leave the tree clean when a timer run should move the real home.
- Parallel shell calls share one working directory: a `cd` in one call was overtaken by another, so two smoke checks ran in the wrong clone once (recorded in `testing/2026-09-21-verify-sandbox-pruned-context.md`). Wrap each CLI run in its own subshell.
- The Antigravity cap number comes from `<truncated N bytes>` markers in its conversation store, twice at exactly 24,000; the vendor page says 12,000 characters. A later CLI may change it; the size test pins 22,000.

## Environment State

- Branch: `main`, clean; 470162b pushed. Real home on this box: 94a6596, drift none (the next timer run will move it to this handoff's commit, docs only).
- Running processes: none. Sandbox home `.agents/scratch/sandbox-home` remains (gitignored) without credentials; scratch clones under `.agents/scratch/sandbox-runs/` and `.agents/scratch/realhome-smoke/smoke5-*`.

## Next Steps

The devbox the same.

- `feature`, `dream` and `requirements` name the context's approval line; the testing guide's Antigravity store check expects one rule block per shipped rule file.

| # | Decision | Answer |

| 3 | Antigravity surface | agy CLI only, global root `~/.gemini/config/` |
| 4 | Inventory | Generated list of skills and agents appended to the deployed context |
| 5 | Skills | Keep all 28, rewritten without harness-binary references |
| 6 | Subagents | Keep all six, rewritten |
| 7 | Commits | Agent commits and pushes after each task, current branch |
| 8 | Done means | Changelog + tests + reviewer on 50+ lines / 5+ files + security on sensitive paths |
| 9 | Project tree | `.agents/` real, `.claude/{skills,agents}` symlinks, `CLAUDE.md` = `@AGENTS.md` |
| 10 | Uninstall | Manifest-only: removes exactly what it installed |
| 11 | Artifact frontmatter | `owner:` + `date:` |
| 12 | GCP defaults | Superseded the same day: no stored defaults; local by default, ask when GCP is requested |
| + | Standards | agents.md for context files, Agent Skills `SKILL.md` for skills |
