The content scan REFUSED on a match, and this repository's own `skills/terraform/references/security-compliance.md:290-291` documents `password="secret123"` and `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE` — a proposal quoting that rule would have bricked the feedback loop permanently with no override. It now redacts the matched token, reports file, line and pattern, and continues. The Phase-3 grep was unsatisfiable on the bare word `mirror` and on `styrman-crew`, both of which are true prose in files the plan must not touch, one of them vendored; it now greps the strings that actually go stale — by: cold read round 2, `reviews/2026-09-17-coldread-delivery-rework.md` § Round 2
D9 — 2026-09-17 — Round 3, the cap, returned `design needs revision` with three ambiguities and three items the reader would resolve the same way. The operator was asked the one that changes what gets built and chose JSON-aware redaction over refusing with an override or not scanning at all. The needles are now stated to LOCATE and never to define the span: a whole JSON string value, or a whole text line, or a whole BEGIN/END block. That closes the two leaks round 3 found — a prefix needle shipping the rest of the key, and a PEM body with no needle in it — because no span is ever partial. The same-way items were applied without asking: the Phase-2 expect rewritten to redact-and-continue, `json.Valid` asserted per line, the three prose paths the grep cannot see, and the empty-repository first push — by: the operator's choice at the cap, 2026-09-17, and cold read round 3. Revised by D13: the per-value JSON walk is gone
D10 — 2026-09-17 — `deploy/remote.md`'s versioning rule and signing recipe survive the Phase-3 retirement; only the prose describing a tag as the way a consumer receives the harness goes. Round 3 called this ambiguous and it was — D2 keeps tags as markers, which settles it — by: implementer, resolving cold read round 3 item 3
D11 — 2026-09-17 — The Definition-of-Done security review (`reviews/2026-09-17-security-6af54f7-015cf2d.md`) found three medium defects, each probed: the seven case-sensitive needles let 14 of 15 ordinary credential shapes through and the docs' "read `--dry-run` first" could not show a miss; a needle in a JSON key was written into `report.json` as the redaction path; and nothing checked that the checkout was the feedback repository, so `--feedback-repo` naming another project, or `GIT_DIR` in the environment, pushed there. Fixed, within D9's structural design rather than against it: keyword needles match case-insensitively and vendor prefixes widen (never shorter than a vendor's own prefix — a bare `sk-` hits every "task-"), deliberately over-redacting; a key hit records no path; a key block is found before the JSON walk and a JSON line the walk leaves carrying a needle is replaced whole; `report` refuses a checkout that is not its own top level with origin exactly the feedback URL, refuses redirecting `GIT_*` variables, refuses a linked `reports` path, and always pushes to `origin`. The docs now say the dry run shows only what was caught. The work-Mac policy question (finding 7) went to the operator, D12 — by: security review, fixes by implementer, 2026-09-17
D12 — 2026-09-17 — Every place runs `sh-agent report` the same way, the work Mac included; `report` does not distinguish where a report comes from. Resolves security finding 7 — by: the operator, asked with options, "You should not care from the report comes from. It is only me that has access to this."
D13 — 2026-09-17 — The second security review (`reviews/2026-09-17-security-015cf2d-012b4ca.md`, eight low findings, each probed) landed two findings on the two mechanisms D11 had already patched, so patching stopped and the operator was asked what each mechanism is for, with a numbered table and a recommendation per item; they took every recommendation as written. (1) Redaction: the per-value JSON walk kept leaking at structural edges (a key split across array values, a secret-named key beside another hit) after round 1 fixed four others. It existed only to keep a redacted line's non-secret fields, so it is struck: a line carrying a needle, in its raw text or its JSON-decoded text, goes whole, as a `{"redacted": …}` object in a JSONL file so each line still parses; `state.json` goes whole on any needle; a key block goes whole as before. `report.json` loses the key path. This reverses the JSON-aware half of D9, the operator's own earlier choice. (2) Push target: `git push origin` follows a remote's `pushurl` and every `url` it lists, none of which the origin check read; `report` now pushes to the feedback URL itself (`push -u <url> HEAD:main`), and the origin check stays to keep the COMMIT out of another project's repository. (3) `GIT_CONFIG_*` injection: struck — nothing sets it by accident, and (2) makes origin's pushurl moot (corrected by D14: not every redirect — the environment can still carry a URL rewrite, which D14 trusts as the operator's own configuration). (4) The refusal no longer prints the checkout's origin, which can carry a token. (5) Two shapes widen: `scheme://:pass@` (an empty user) and `Authorization: <any scheme>`; no chase for completeness. (6) An unterminated `-----BEGIN` in a JSONL file drops every later record: deferred — it fails safe, and `unterminated: true` in `report.json` says when it happens. (7) The testing guide's filter now runs the git-side tests. (8) The docs say to read what was added under `~/.config/sh-agent/` since the last report, before every report — by: the operator, 2026-09-17, "take the recommendations as written"
D14 — 2026-09-17 — The third security review (`reviews/2026-09-17-security-012b4ca-worktree.md`, eight low findings, each probed) landed on the push target and the redaction needles again, their third round, so the operator was asked what each must GUARANTEE, with a numbered table and a recommendation per item, and took every recommendation as written. The guarantees: redaction is a safety net, not a guarantee — the guarantee is the operator reading what was added under `~/.config/sh-agent/` before each report — so it catches the listed shapes on the line they appear and the docs state what it cannot see; and the push trusts the operator's own git configuration — `report` refuses the accidents (a wrong checkout, `GIT_DIR`, origin's pushurl) while a URL rewrite (`insteadOf`, `pushInsteadOf`) or a remote named after the feedback URL is the operator's own setting that redirects every push on that machine, so the claims say that instead of "nothing can redirect it". Per item: (1) push claims narrowed in code comments and docs, no code; (2a) a secret on the line after its needle (YAML `|`, heredoc, `\` continuation, pretty-printed JSON) stated as a limit; (2b) fixed — on a header's own line a block closes only at a footer naming the header's label, the "second trigger" round 2's Outcome wrongly marked fixed; (3) fixed — the `authorization` needle allows a quote before the colon, a gap D13 introduced; (4) fixed — the decoded check reads every value on a line with numbers kept as written, closing the `1e400` regression D13 introduced and two records on one line; a BOM, NaN and a shadowed duplicate stated as limits; (5) struck — a needle in `state.json`'s `vendor` or `installedAt` reaching `report.json` needs a hand-edited manifest; (6) fixed — a must-fail test for `redactDocument`'s decoded branch; (7) fixed — the dry-run list prints `lines` and `unterminated`; (8) struck — unlisted shapes are sent, as the docs already say. Must-fail: one mutant per fix, each failing its own test (`.agents/scratch/r3-mutants/`) — by: the operator, 2026-09-17, "take the recommendations as written"
Open: should the harness repository become public, which is what would let a machine bootstrap with no credential at all? — default: it stays private, and the credential requirement stands with the unzipped bundle as the fallback
Rejected: a webservice for delivery and feedback — hosting, per-machine auth and an attack surface for one user, against R3, R4 and local-by-default
Rejected: per-machine deploy keys — the operator authenticates as themselves everywhere, so they add key management and restrict nothing
Rejected: a branch in this repository for feedback — it would need write access to the harness, which is the thing being prevented

title: Recon — release binary with embedded assets (2026-09-17)
body:
# Recon — release binary with embedded assets (2026-09-17)

## Question
Survey the codebase to support a plan for: (a) releasing per-platform sh-agent
binaries with context/skills/agents/commands/rules embedded via `go:embed`,
usable via `go install .../cmd/sh-agent@latest`; (b) install source order
`--repo` > checkout-found-as-today > embedded; (c) `update` on a binary-only
place downloading the latest release via `gh release download`, verifying the
signed tag, replacing the binary, reinstalling; (d) `report` switching from a
kept clone to a throwaway partial clone per run; (e) README "install without
cloning" section, R9 and map changes.

## Summary
Every file-reading function in `internal/harness` (`Plan`, `LoadInventory`,
`LoadSkills`, `LoadAgents`, `LoadDocs`, `RenderContext`, `checkManagedTree`,
`readRegular`) takes a `repo string` and calls `os.ReadFile`/`os.ReadDir`/
`filepath.Glob`/`filepath.WalkDir`/`os.Lstat`/`filepath.EvalSymlinks` directly
— none takes an `fs.FS`, so all would need a parallel `fs.FS`-based path (or a
refactor to `io/fs` funcs) to also read from an embedded filesystem. `FindRepo`
already has exactly the "checkout found as today" behavior requested for (b);
adding embedded-as-fallback is a third source appended after it. `Reinstall`
in repo.go is the only thing that changes the deployed binary today and it
insists on `go build` from source (BUG-006) — a release binary changes this
substantially: R4's "single Go binary, stdlib only" and R8/R9's "one delivery
channel: checkout+update, or unpacked bundle+install" would need explicit
amendment (ADR + operator approval) since GitHub Releases would become a THIRD
channel not named in R8/R9. `report.go`'s tests (`TestSendReport`,
`TestSendReportRefusesRedirectsAndLinks`, `TestSendReportPushesOnlyToFeedbackURL`)
pin a `runDir`/kept-clone model (`~/.config/sh-agent/feedback`) that assumes a
persistent local clone across runs — switching to a throwaway partial clone
per run is a structural rewrite of `ResolveFeedback`, not an incremental patch.

## Relevant files
- `internal/harness/repo.go` — `FindRepo` (source order: explicit/env → cwd+parents → last-install state), `IsRepo`, `IsCheckout`, `Inspect`, `Behind`, `Pull`, `Reinstall` (git-build-only), `gitOut`.
- `internal/harness/plan.go` — `Plan()` builds `[]File` from `LoadInventory`+`RenderContext`; walks `skills/<name>` with `filepath.WalkDir`, refuses symlinks/secret-shaped files; `Reinstall`'s bin is added as `File{Rel: BinPath, ...}` when `selfExe != nil`.
- `internal/harness/inventory.go` — `LoadInventory`, `LoadSkills`, `LoadAgents`, `LoadDocs`, `checkManagedTree`, `readRegular`: all path-based, all refuse symlinks in the managed tree (BUG-036).
- `internal/harness/render.go` — `RenderContext`: reads `context/AGENTS.md` + `context/*.md` via `os.ReadFile`/`filepath.Glob`.
- `internal/harness/derive.go` — Antigravity agent translation; has `toolMap` (unmapped tool fails install per AGENTS.md rule). Small (56 lines), path-independent of repo reads (works on already-loaded `Agent` struct).
- `internal/harness/adopt.go` — `sh-agent adopt` (promotes a project customization into the repo); needs closer read (not yet fully read — see Not examined).
- `internal/harness/state.go` — `LoadState`/state persisted to `home` (`~/.config/sh-agent` in real use), records `st.Repo` used by `FindRepo`'s third candidate.
- `internal/harness/report.go` (632 lines) — feedback-repo report/send logic: `ResolveFeedback`, `verifyFeedback`, `runDir`, `commitAndPush`, `SendReport`. Not yet fully read — see Not examined; this is the piece (d) most directly rewrites.
- `internal/harness/report_test.go` (570 lines) — pins current kept-clone behavior; named tests confirmed to exist: grep found `TestSendReport`, `TestSendReportRefusesRedirectsAndLinks`, `TestSendReportPushesOnlyToFeedbackURL` referenced in report.go comments/tests (exact bodies not yet read).
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (781 lines) — CLI entry; `install` chooses rebuild-vs-plain-copy around line 107-154; `status` reporting around 233-273; `update` calls `Reinstall` at line 411. Not yet fully read line-by-line — see Not examined.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` (1014 lines) — install/status/update tests against checkout and plain-copy fixtures; not yet read in detail.
- `internal/harness/harness_test.go` (1499 lines) — includes `TestHarnessMap` per the dispatch; not yet located/read.
- `go.mod` — `module github.com/kesokaj/styrman-harness`, `go 1.24.4`, no `toolchain` directive (deliberate, ADR-029, per AGENTS.md).
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` — R4 (single binary, stdlib only, `update` = git pull + reinstall), R8 (one delivery channel: checkout+update or bundle+install, no other channel), R9 (four procedures fixed; any change to them needs ADR + operator approval, one commit with code+docs+map).
- `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases — not yet read, needed for (5).
- `skills/preflight` — not yet read, needed for (5) Step 6.
- `README.md` — not yet read, needed for the "Install without cloning" section and "the map" (R9's "README.md § How it works").

## Flows (partial)
- Install source order today, per `FindRepo` (repo.go:20-48): explicit `--repo` or `$SH_AGENT_REPO` (hard error if given but not a repo) → walk cwd and parents for `IsRepo` → `LoadState(home).Repo` (last install's recorded repo) → error. This already implements exactly the "explicit, then checkout found as today" half of requirement (b); embedded-fallback would be appended as a further candidate, but note `FindRepo` currently *errors* if nothing is found — the embedded path presumably becomes the state when FindRepo fails, which is a real branch to add in `main.go`, not just repo.go.
- `Plan()` (plan.go:68) calls `LoadInventory(repo)` then `RenderContext(repo, inv)`, both path-based against `repo string`; then walks `inv.Skills[i].Dir` via `filepath.WalkDir` for skill file contents, and reads `inv.Agents[i].Raw`/`inv.Commands[i].Raw`/`inv.Rules[i].Raw` which were already loaded into memory by `LoadAgents`/`LoadDocs` (path-based `os.ReadFile`).
- Install rebuild-vs-copy decision lives in `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` around lines 107-154: after `FindRepo`, checks `harness.IsCheckout(repo)` (`own`); if true and `go` is on PATH, calls `harness.Reinstall` (rebuilds from source, BUG-006's fix: an installed copy re-installing itself must never silently reuse its own already-built bytes); if plain copy (`!own`, i.e. `.git` absent — an unpacked bundle, BUG-015), installs the *running* binary as-is with a "plain copy... installed as is" message.

## Conventions
- Every repo-reading function refuses symlinks explicitly and cites the originating bug/review in a comment (BUG-036, security reviews dated in comments) — new fs.FS-based readers must preserve this refusal, and `fs.FS` (e.g. from `embed.FS`) does not expose `Lstat`/symlink info the same way, so the symlink-refusal logic cannot transfer mechanically.
- Every risky decision (rebuild vs. copy, dirty-tree refusal, secret-shaped refusal) has an inline comment naming the bug number or review date that justified it — a strong convention for any new decision code (embedded-fallback logic, release-binary trust boundary) to follow.
- `go.mod` deliberately carries no `toolchain` directive (ADR-029) — release automation must not reintroduce one.

## Risks (preliminary)
- **R8/R9 conflict**: R9 says the harness has exactly two install paths (checkout+update, bundle+install) and enumerates "Four procedures... and no others"; a GitHub Releases binary distributed via `go install .../cmd/sh-agent@latest` and `gh release download` is arguably a THIRD delivery channel and a fifth procedure-shaped thing. REQUIREMENTS.md is immutable without explicit operator approval + ADR (already reflected in R9's own text: "together, only with the operator's explicit approval, an ADR, and one commit"). This recon cannot determine whether that approval already covers today's dispatch — the dispatch text describes the change as already "confirmed by the operator," but REQUIREMENTS.md itself is unmodified as of this recon (R8/R9 text above still describes only two channels) — a plan must not proceed to code before REQUIREMENTS.md + an ADR are updated in the same commit as required by R9's own final sentence.
- **fs.FS refactor is pervasive, not local**: `LoadInventory`, `LoadSkills`, `LoadAgents`, `LoadDocs`, `RenderContext`, `checkManagedTree`, `readRegular`, `Plan`'s skill walk all need a filesystem abstraction; `embed.FS` is read-only and has no symlinks (so symlink-refusal code becomes dead code on that path, but must stay for the checkout/bundle path) — likely means introducing an interface or dual code paths, not a one-line signature change.
- `Reinstall` (repo.go) is the sole mutator of the deployed binary and currently requires `go build` from a git checkout; a release binary needs a wholly different `update` path when there is no checkout (no `go`, no source) — this is exactly gap (c) in the dispatch, confirmed structurally: today's `update` (main.go ~line 411 calls `Reinstall`) has no non-git branch at all for replacing the binary.
- `report.go`/`report_test.go` pin a kept-clone model; rewriting to throwaway partial clones will break `TestSendReport`, `TestResolveFeedbackFailures`, `TestSendReportRefusesRedirectsAndLinks`, `TestSendReportPushesOnlyToFeedbackURL` unless carefully re-targeted — these tests were not read in full; exact assertions unknown (see Not examined).

## Open questions
- Has REQUIREMENTS.md's R8/R9 actually been amended/approved already, or does the dispatch's "confirmed by the operator" cover only the recon scope, not a REQUIREMENTS.md edit? The file on disk right now still describes two channels only.
- What `.gitignore`/embed directive scheme is intended for `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/`, `rules/` so `//go:embed` at the module root does not also embed `.agents/scratch/` or `VENDORED.md` third-party content inadvertently?
- Are there dotfiles/underscore-prefixed files under skills/ or agents/ that `embed` would silently skip without `all:`? Not yet checked (see Not examined).

## Not examined (ran out of budget / did not reach)
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` full read (only grepped line numbers, not full bodies) — need lines ~1-780 read in full for install/status/update/report command wiring, flag parsing, and exact rebuild/copy branch code.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` (1014 lines) — not read at all.
- `internal/harness/harness_test.go` (1499 lines) including `TestHarnessMap` — not read at all.
- `internal/harness/report.go` (632 lines) and `report_test.go` (570 lines) — only referenced via grep/comments in repo.go's neighborhood; `ResolveFeedback`, `verifyFeedback`, `runDir`, `commitAndPush`, `SendReport` bodies not read.
- `internal/harness/adopt.go`, `apply.go`, `derive.go` (full body), `frontmatter.go`, `state.go` — not read in detail.
- `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases — not read.
- `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 6 — not read.
- `README.md` § How it works / map — not read.
- Listing actual files under `skills/` and `agents/` for dotfile/underscore-prefixed names (embed all: question) — not done.
- go.mod Go version cross-check against `go:embed` requirements (embed needs go1.16+; 1.24.4 is fine, not a concern, but not verified against any go.work or multi-module layout).

## Additional findings (second pass)

- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:136-138` — decision code confirmed:
  `own := harness.IsCheckout(repo)`, `rebuild := shouldRebuild(goErr == nil, os.Getenv(harness.ChildEnv) == "1", own)`.
  `shouldRebuild(goOnPath, child, ownCheckout bool) bool { return goOnPath && !child && ownCheckout }` (main.go ~450).
  `knownCheckout` (main.go ~420) refuses building from a harness-shaped directory that is not the one actually installed (no `--repo`/`$SH_AGENT_REPO`, and it doesn't match `state.Repo`) — a real guard a release-binary "third source" must respect or explicitly bypass.
  `binaryOlder(rev, commit string)` (main.go) compares the running binary's VCS stamp to the repo's HEAD for `status`'s staleness warning — a release binary built via `go install` carries `debug.ReadBuildInfo` module version info, not a short git commit hash, so this comparison logic will need to change too.
- `internal/harness/report.go` `ResolveFeedback` (line 377) is confirmed to look for an existing dir at `home/.config/sh-agent/feedback`; if absent it `git clone`s the feedback URL there and KEEPS it (no removal). This is the exact mechanism (d) replaces. `runDir` (line 550) computes `reports/<host>/<date>-<HHMMSS>[-N]` inside that persistent checkout. `commitAndPush` (line 599) stages/commits/pushes named paths only, to `url` explicitly (not `origin`), `HEAD:main`. None of these three currently do a partial/sparse/shallow clone — full `git clone` only. Switching to `--filter=blob:none --no-checkout --depth 1` + sparse-checkout is a rewrite of `ResolveFeedback`'s clone branch and adds an sparse-checkout/cleanup step SendReport must call at the end (not present today) and `update` must also gain: dispatch (d) says "`update` removes an old kept clone" — no code today references cleaning up `~/.config/sh-agent/feedback` from `update` at all; grepped `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` and found no such call. This is a new behavior, not a modification of an existing one.
- `internal/harness/report_test.go` confirmed test names matching dispatch: `TestSendReport` (:333), `TestResolveFeedbackFailures` (:434), `TestSendReportRefusesRedirectsAndLinks` (:489), `TestSendReportPushesOnlyToFeedbackURL` (:526), plus `TestSendReportDryRunShowsDroppedRecords` (:559) not named in the dispatch but adjacent and likely also affected. Bodies not read in full (budget) but their names alone confirm they exercise the persistent-clone/kept-checkout model that (d) removes.
- **`TestHarnessMap` does NOT exist** anywhere in the repo (grepped `internal/harness/harness_test.go` function list exhaustively — 45 test functions, none named `TestHarnessMap`). The dispatch's item (6) asks to report on it; it is either not yet written, misnamed in the dispatch, or the closest analog is `TestInstallStatusResyncUninstall` / `TestVendorSelection` / `TestNestedCopyIsNotACheckout`, none of which is a "map" test. Flag this back to the dispatcher.
- `skills/init-project/assets/agents-tree/**/.gitkeep` — 13 dotfiles found under `skills/`, all named `.gitkeep`, used by `init-project` to ship an empty directory skeleton for a new project's `.agents/` tree. Plain `//go:embed skills` SKIPS files/dirs starting with `.` or `_` (Go embed rule) — these `.gitkeep` files would silently vanish from an embedded build unless the embed directive uses `all:` (e.g. `//go:embed all:skills`). No other dotfiles or underscore-prefixed files found under `skills/` or `agents/` in this search (searched with `find ... -name ".*" -o -name "_*"`, only .gitkeep matched, all under init-project's assets tree, agents/ had none).
- Go toolchain present on this box: `go1.27.1` (ahead of what go.mod declares, `go 1.24.4`, no toolchain directive — consistent with AGENTS.md's note on ADR-029).
- `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases (lines 58-88): today's release procedure is signed-tag-only, explicitly "a MARKER naming a version, not a way the harness reaches a machine" (line 60) and "There is no deploy step after the push" (line 88) — this is the exact sentence ADR-030 D2 states and that a release-binary-attachment step would contradict or need to amend. `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 6 "SHIP" (lines 79-88 read) has 6 sub-steps (changelog, version bump, one release commit with gate artifacts, tag, push, "Deploy via the project's deploy guide"); nothing today builds or attaches platform binaries — step 6.5's "Deploy via deploy guide" is GCP/remote-box oriented (cloud-run-deploy skill, ssh box, or local-only), not "attach a binary to a GitHub Release." Attaching binaries to a release would need a NEW sub-step here, and reconciling with remote.md's "nothing pushes to a machine / no deploy step after tag push" framing is a real tension to resolve with the operator.
- `README.md` "How it works" (lines 5-56) contains the mermaid diagram (`checkoutLane`, `checkoutPlace`, `bundle`) that is "the map" referenced in dispatch (e) and R9. Confirmed two lanes exist today: checkout+update, and unpacked-bundle+install-only ("update refuses it — unpack a newer copy to move forward", line 99). A third lane (release binary via `go install`/`gh release download`) is a genuine addition to this diagram, not a relabeling.

## Risks (additional)

- `binaryOlder`'s git-short-hash comparison and `status`'s staleness detection assume every deployed binary carries a git VCS stamp; a `go install @latest`-built binary's `debug.ReadBuildInfo().Main.Version` is a module pseudo-version/tag, not a short commit hash matching `Inspect(repo).Commit` — `status` output and the staleness warning need new logic for this case, not just a new source branch.
- No existing code path removes `~/.config/sh-agent/feedback`; "update removes an old kept clone" (d) is wholly new logic to add to `update`'s flow in `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`, gated on detecting "binary-only place" (which itself needs a new way to detect "this place has no checkout, only a binary install" — today `FindRepo` either finds a repo or hard-errors; there's no persisted "binary-only" state distinct from "bundle, no .git" already handled by `own=false`).
- `go:embed all:` vs plain `embed` distinction matters concretely for `skills/init-project/assets/agents-tree/**/.gitkeep` — must use `all:` prefix or add the .gitkeep files back another way (they exist purely to make git track otherwise-empty directories; embed's directory model doesn't have "empty directories" as a concept anyway, so their omission may be harmless in practice — worth confirming with init-project's actual usage of that tree before assuming it's a problem).

## Open questions (additional)
- Has the operator actually approved amending R8/R9 already (dispatch says "confirmed by the operator") — recon cannot verify this from the repo since REQUIREMENTS.md and ADR list show no such change yet. A plan must not write code before REQUIREMENTS.md + a new ADR land in one commit, per R9's own final sentence.
- Where dispatch's `TestHarnessMap` should live / whether it's a test to be newly written for map-diagram-consistency (e.g., asserting README's diagram lists exactly the lanes `sh-agent` implements) — does not exist today.

title: Plan — release binary with the harness built in; `report` keeps nothing (2026-09-17)
body:
# Plan — release binary with the harness built in; `report` keeps nothing   (2026-09-17)

## Why

The operator wants a place to get the harness by downloading one `sh-agent` binary from a GitHub release — "Just downloading the binary makes a lot of sense. Because it will only work If I logged in to github or have the ssh key" — instead of cloning the whole repository, whose `.agents/docs` trail then sits beside their projects and can confuse a session opened there. They also found that `sh-agent report` keeps a full clone of `styrman-harness-feedback` on every place, so each machine holds every other machine's reports ("But why can I see dave reports?"). Scope confirmed in chat on 2026-09-17 with "go all, throwaway clone for 12". Recon: `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-17-recon-release-binary.md`.

## Scope

In (the operator's numbered list):
1. The release binary replaces the unpacked bundle as R9's second way in; a checkout stays the first. R9 edit on exact text, ADR.
2. `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/`, `rules/` embedded with Go `embed` from a package at the module root.
3. `install` source order: `--repo`, a checkout found as today, then the embedded files.
4. `update` on a binary-only place: newest release via `gh release download`, verified, binary replaced, reinstalled. (Verification is by signed checksums, D5 — the scope line said "the SSH-signed tag".)
5. Platforms linux/amd64, darwin/arm64, linux/arm64, cross-compiled locally in `/preflight`, attached to the release.
6. A binary-only place changes only when a release is cut.
7. The first download documented.
8. macOS quarantine documented, for a browser download only.
10. The unpacked bundle leaves the docs and the map; its code path stays.

## Interfaces

**R9 — proposed exact replacement of the Install, Update, Report back and Release bullets (operator approval required, Phase 1):**

- **Install:** a place either clones `styrman-harness` with the operator's own credential and runs `sh-agent install`, or downloads a release's `sh-agent` binary with that credential — `gh release download`, `go install` over SSH, or the Releases page — and runs `sh-agent install`, which installs the harness built into the binary. Either way installed files go into the vendor directories and no repository is created.
- **Update:** the operator edits, verifies, commits and pushes `main` in their checkout. A checkout place runs `sh-agent update` when the operator decides — fetch, refuse a dirty checkout, fast-forward, rebuild, reinstall. A binary-only place runs `sh-agent update`, which downloads the newest release, verifies its signed checksums, replaces the binary and reinstalls; it changes only when a release is cut. Nothing is pushed to a machine.
- **Report back:** each place runs `sh-agent report`, which sends a redacted copy of `~/.config/sh-agent/` and a metrics record to `styrman-harness-feedback` through a throwaway clone that holds only that place's folder and is deleted after the push; the harness is improved from the reports in the operator's checkout, and that change returns through Update.
- **Release:** `/preflight vX.Y.Z`, from the operator's own turn, gates the tree, pushes an SSH-signed tag on `main`, and publishes that tag's binaries with checksums signed by the same key. Checkout places follow `main`; binary-only places update to the newest release.

**R8 — proposed exact replacement of its first sentence (operator approval required, Phase 1):** "The harness reaches a machine one way: a checkout the operator owns, or a release's `sh-agent` binary with the harness built in, each installed with `sh-agent install` and kept current with `sh-agent update`." The rest of R8 is unchanged.

**Source.** `type Source struct { FS fs.FS; Dir string; Version string }` (`Version` set for the embedded files only, D20). `Dir` is the checkout or plain-copy path (`FS` is `os.DirFS(Dir)`), or `""` for the embedded files (`FS` is `styrman.Files`). Every reader takes a `Source`; symlink refusal (BUG-036) stays a `os.Lstat` on `filepath.Join(Dir, name)` when `Dir != ""` — `embed` cannot hold a link, so the embedded source needs none. `state.json` records `"repo": "<dir>"` or `"repo": "embedded:<version>"`.

**Source selection** (`install`, `status`, `diff`, `list`, `render`, `update`, `report`): an explicit `--repo` or `$SH_AGENT_REPO` is used or it is an error, exactly as today — never a fall-through (D15). Otherwise the working directory or a parent, then the recorded repo when it is still a harness tree, then the embedded files — but the embedded files only in a release binary, one whose version is a `vX.Y.Z` tag (release ldflags or `go install …@vX.Y.Z`); a development build with no tree found keeps today's `harness repo not found …` error (D14). `adopt` requires a checkout and says so.

**`ResolveSource` replaces `FindRepo`** (`internal/harness/repo.go:20`): `func ResolveSource(explicit, home, version string) (Source, error)` — `explicit` is `--repo` (else `$SH_AGENT_REPO`, read inside as today); `version` is the running binary's version; the embedded fallback applies only when `version` matches `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+$`. Every git helper — `IsCheckout`, `Inspect`, `Behind`, `Pull`, `Reinstall` — is called only with `src.Dir != ""`; with an embedded source none is called (D17).

**Per command with an embedded source (`src.Dir == ""`)** (D17):

| Command | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `install`, `sync` | install from `styrman.Files`; copy the running binary (D13) |
| `status` | first line `source     embedded vX.Y.Z (release binary; update downloads the newest release)` in place of the `repo` line; `binary` line shows the version; drift compared against the embedded files |
| `diff`, `list`, `render` | read the embedded files |
| `update` | the release flow (Interfaces § `update` on a binary-only place); with `--check`, only step 1: `up to date (vX.Y.Z)` exit 0, or `newer release vA.B.C available` exit 2 |
| `adopt` | `adopt needs a harness checkout; this install is a release binary`, exit 1 |
| `uninstall`, `version` | unchanged — neither reads the source |
| `report` | `BuildRecord` takes the `Source`; `harness_commit` is `null` and a new `harness_version` field carries `vX.Y.Z`; `drift`, `skills`, `agents` computed from the embedded files |

With a checkout or plain-copy source every command behaves exactly as today.

**Binary handling on install** (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go` today decides rebuild vs copy with `IsCheckout(repo)`): with the embedded source the running binary is copied to `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` and never rebuilt, and `IsCheckout` is never called with an empty path; a checkout or plain copy keeps today's rule (BUG-006, BUG-015) (D13).

**Version.** Release builds: `-trimpath -ldflags "-X main.version=vX.Y.Z"`, `CGO_ENABLED=0`. A `go install …@vX.Y.Z` binary: `debug.ReadBuildInfo().Main.Version`. Otherwise today's VCS stamp. `sh-agent version` prints it; `status` prints `source embedded vX.Y.Z` for an embedded install. `status` reads the INSTALLED file's version from its module version when that is a `vX.Y.Z` tag, because `-trimpath` keeps `-ldflags` out of the build info (D21).

**Release assets** (per tag): `sh-agent-linux-amd64`, `sh-agent-darwin-arm64`, `sh-agent-linux-arm64`, `SHA256SUMS` (`sha256sum` format), `SHA256SUMS.sig` = `ssh-keygen -Y sign -f <operator key> -n sh-agent-release SHA256SUMS`.

**`update` on a binary-only place** (no checkout found by the source order): requires `gh` on PATH, else `update: this install has no checkout; install gh and run gh auth login, or download a newer release by hand (README § Install without cloning)`, exit 1.
1. `gh release view --repo kesokaj/styrman-harness --json tagName` → latest tag; equal to this binary's version → `up to date (vX.Y.Z)`, exit 0.
2. `gh release download <tag> --pattern sh-agent-<GOOS>-<GOARCH> --pattern SHA256SUMS --pattern SHA256SUMS.sig --dir <tmp under ~/.config/sh-agent/>`.
3. `ssh-keygen -Y verify -f <allowed-signers file written from the signer line compiled into the binary> -I <signer identity> -n sh-agent-release -s SHA256SUMS.sig < SHA256SUMS`; then the binary's SHA-256 against its `SHA256SUMS` line (`crypto/sha256`). Any failure: nothing replaced, message names the check, exit 1.
4. Replace `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` by rename from the verified file (same filesystem), then run the new binary's `install`; the temp directory is removed on every path.

**Report throwaway clone.** `--feedback-repo DIR` keeps today's behaviour exactly (a persistent, verified checkout the operator names). Without it:
1. `git clone --quiet --filter=blob:none --no-checkout --depth 1 <FeedbackURL> ~/.config/sh-agent/report-<pid>`; an empty repository (no commits) is cloned plainly.
2. `verifyFeedback` on it; `git sparse-checkout set --no-cone reports/<host>/`; `git checkout`.
3. Write the run directory, stage, commit and push exactly as today (`push -u <FeedbackURL> HEAD:main`).
4. `os.RemoveAll` of the clone on every exit path (deferred). A rejected push: remove, re-clone, re-apply the same run once; a second rejection → `push rejected twice; re-run sh-agent report — nothing is kept locally`, exit 1.
`--dry-run` clones nothing, as today.

**Release notes** (D19): `/preflight` Step 6 writes `.agents/scratch/release-notes-vX.Y.Z.md` from the `changes/` entries dated after the previous tag's commit, one line per entry under `## New features` (Type feature), `## Improvements and optimisation` (Type task or refactor that changes behaviour), `## Fixes` (Type bugfix, with its BUG id), `## Other updates` (rules, skills, docs, context), plus `## Install` pointing at README § Install without cloning; an empty group is omitted. The operator reads it before the upload; `gh release create vX.Y.Z --notes-file <it>` attaches it. The same text goes into the release's `changes/` entry.

**Old kept clone cleanup** (`update`, both kinds of place): `~/.config/sh-agent/feedback` is removed when it is a git checkout whose origin is `FeedbackURL`, with a clean `git status --porcelain` and no commits ahead of its upstream; the output says `removed the kept feedback clone ~/.config/sh-agent/feedback (report no longer keeps one)`. Otherwise it is left and named with the reason.

## Failure modes

| When | What the operator sees |
|---|---|
| `install` with no tree found | a release binary installs its embedded files; a development build prints today's `harness repo not found …` (D14) |
| `--repo` or `$SH_AGENT_REPO` naming something that is not a harness tree | today's error, no fall-through to the embedded files (D15) |
| `update`, binary-only, no `gh` | the gh message above, exit 1, nothing changed |
| `update`, `gh` not logged in or no repo access | `update: gh release view failed: <gh's first line>`, exit 1 |
| No release asset for this platform | `update: release vX.Y.Z has no sh-agent-<os>-<arch>`, exit 1 |
| Signature or checksum mismatch | `update: SHA256SUMS signature does not verify` / `checksum mismatch for sh-agent-<os>-<arch>`, exit 1, binary untouched |
| `ssh-keygen` missing | `update: ssh-keygen not found; cannot verify the release`, exit 1 |
| `report`, partial clone unsupported by the server | No fallback branch exists, and none is needed: git itself warns `filtering not recognized by server, ignoring` and sends every blob, so the clone succeeds and the run is correct, only slower. The warning goes to git's stderr, which `gitOut` discards, so the output does NOT name it — corrected here 2026-09-17 after the release code review found this row promising a fallback the code never had. Measured on a `file://` remote without `uploadpack.allowFilter`. |
| `report`, push rejected twice | message above, exit 1, no directory left |
| A kept feedback clone with local work | left in place, named with `has uncommitted changes` or `has N unpushed commits` |

Its "260 managed vs 259 match" note is by design — `status` plans without the binary, which is excluded from drift checks (BUG-001). `security` 1 medium and 6 low, `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-17-security-dab2565-4d45155.md`: six fixed with tests seen failing first (no downgrade, tag validated before argv, the version bound inside the signed checksums, verifier preferred from a system path, random download directory, stricter checksum parsing, capped reads, gh's stderr in the message), two rebutted in that report's `## Outcome`; twelve mutations all fail the tests that cover them. Evidence: `cd0bbcb` on `main`, one commit of 54 files (5187 insertions, 413 deletions) squashing the branch's 22 commits, carrying the code, both deploy guides, the README and its map, `AGENTS.md` rules 1 and 2, `REQUIREMENTS.md` R8 and R9, ADR-033a, the plan, the reviews, the testing logs and BUG-066…072; `gofmt`, `go vet` and `go test -race -count=1 ./...` clean on the staged merge before the commit; pushed. - [x] E2E: `/preflight v1.1.0` from the operator's turn; on the work Mac the golden path and edge in Verification — verify: e2e, who: both — expect: as written; log `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-17-release-binary-e2e.md`. DONE on the work Mac 2026-09-18 on v1.2.0, by the operator (`.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-17-release-binary-e2e.md` § Added 2026-09-18 — the work Mac): the README `gh` one-liner, `install --vendor antigravity` (130 files, 2 written), `status` showing `source embedded v1.2.0` and drift none, `report` sending `c4b13a8` with `harness_version: v1.2.0` and leaving no `report-*` behind, `update --check`, `adopt` refusing, and `agy` starting cleanly on the installed skills. `go install …@v1.1.0` settled on Linux. DONE on devbox (Debian, linux/amd64) and again on the work Mac 2026-09-18 on v1.2.1, by the operator (same log, § Added 2026-09-18 — v1.2.1 on two machines the operator ran himself): the signed download verified before the move, `install --vendor=all` writing 260 files with `source embedded v1.2.1` and drift none, the installed context proven current by `grep -c 'A guard in front of a destructive' ~/.claude/AGENTS.md` → 1 and by `claude -p` quoting that rule, `report` from a release binary on both machines leaving no `feedback/` and no `report-*`, and `update` on the Mac shedding the kept clone it had held since 2026-09-17 — the last piece of "report keeps nothing on the machine". BUG-078 came out of the devbox run: a verified v1.2.1 binary at `/usr/local/bin` was shadowed by two earlier `PATH` entries, so a `(devel)` build installed a stale tree while reporting drift none. Three legs remain and are moved to § Follow-ups, because each needs hardware or a session this plan should not wait for

## Follow-ups

Deferred from the e2e box on 2026-09-18, each needing a machine or a session this plan should not hold open. Owner: the operator to run, the next session to log.

- The swapped-signature edge case on **darwin**: a tampered `SHA256SUMS.sig` must make `update` refuse and leave the binary untouched. Proven on Linux against the real releases; never run on the Mac.
- **The Claude Code side of the work Mac**: still installed `--vendor antigravity` only, so `~/.claude` there holds nothing from any release. devbox now covers the Claude side on Linux (`--vendor all`). One `sh-agent install --vendor all` on the Mac plus one `claude -p` closes it.
- **`sh-agent update` on devbox**: that machine reached v1.2.1 by download and `install`, never by updating from an earlier release. The cross-release update is proven on Linux (a scratch place, v1.1.0 → v1.2.0) and on the Mac (v1.2.0 → v1.2.1), so this is confirmation, not a gap.
- Struck 2026-09-30 on the operator's word ("Go with your recommendations"): the `linux/arm64` leg (built and published every release, never executed; no such box exists) and the BUG-078 line, which is stale: its rule graduated into `context/AGENTS.md` § Hard rules, and `sh-agent status` prints a `shadowed` line when an earlier `PATH` entry wins (BUG-079).

## Risks

Assumptions:
- GitHub serves `--filter=blob:none` partial clones over SSH and accepts a push from a `--depth 1` clone — SETTLED 2026-09-17 by one real `sh-agent report` from this box, authorised by the operator (D25): the blob-less `--no-checkout --depth 1` clone over SSH succeeded, `sparse-checkout` limited it to `reports/dave/`, and the push landed as `09586ff` (`reports/dave/2026-09-17-200615`, five files). The clone was removed and `~/.config/sh-agent/` holds no `report-*`. The push stalled on the network for about four minutes before completing — slow, not refused. Log: `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-17-release-binary-phase-3-real-report.md`. Note: a local bare repository ignores `--filter` unless it sets `uploadpack.allowFilter`, so the local tiers seed that.
- `go install github.com/kesokaj/styrman-harness/cmd/sh-agent@latest` resolves the newest semver tag: `v1.0.0` has no embed, so `@latest` gives a binary that cannot install until `v1.1.0` exists — SETTLED 2026-09-18 with `go install …@v1.1.0` in a scratch `GOPATH`: exit 0, the binary reports `v1.1.0` from build info (the D6/D21 branch nothing else reached), and installing from it gave 260 files with `source embedded v1.1.0`, drift none. It needs git told to fetch the private module over SSH, which the README did not say — BUG-075, fixed the same day. Log: `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-17-release-binary-e2e.md` § Added 2026-09-18.
- `ssh-keygen -Y verify` exists on macOS and Debian (OpenSSH ≥ 8.1) — checked with `ssh-keygen -Y 2>&1 | head -1` on this box and the work Mac, first task of Phase 4.

## Decisions

D1 — 2026-09-17 — The release binary replaces the unpacked bundle as the second way in; R9's four bullets change to the exact text in Interfaces, subject to approval — by: the operator, "go all" on scope items 1 and 10
D2 — 2026-09-17 — Embedding from a root package `styrman` with `all:` so the 15 `.gitkeep` files are included — by: implementer, from recon risk 3 (`embed` skips dotfiles without `all:`)
D3 — 2026-09-17 — Readers take a `Source{FS, Dir}`; link refusal stays an `os.Lstat` on the disk path when `Dir` is set — by: implementer, from recon: every reader takes a path today and BUG-036 must not regress
D4 — 2026-09-17 — Source order `--repo`, env, working directory, recorded path, embedded — by: the operator, scope item 3, with the recorded path kept from today
D5 — 2026-09-17 — `update` verifies `SHA256SUMS.sig` (`ssh-keygen -Y verify`, namespace `sh-agent-release`) and each binary's checksum, not the git tag: a tag's signature covers the commit, never a release asset — needs the operator's approval since scope item 4 said "the SSH-signed tag" — by: implementer, flagged for the operator
D6 — 2026-09-17 — Version from `-ldflags -X main.version` for releases, `debug.ReadBuildInfo` for `go install`, the VCS stamp otherwise — by: implementer
D7 — 2026-09-17 — Binary-only `update` shells out to `gh` and `ssh-keygen`; no Go dependency added (R4) — by: the operator, scope item 4, and R4
D8 — 2026-09-17 — `report` without `--feedback-repo` uses a throwaway partial clone under `~/.config/sh-agent/report-<pid>`; a rejected push is retried once from a fresh clone — by: the operator, "throwaway clone for 12"; the retry by implementer, since a throwaway clone cannot keep a rejected commit
D9 — 2026-09-17 — `update` removes a kept `~/.config/sh-agent/feedback` only when clean, origin-verified and not ahead — by: the operator, scope item 12. Amended 2026-09-17 after BUG-069: "not ahead" is counted over ALL local refs against ALL remote-tracking refs, never `@{upstream}..HEAD`, whose failure on a branch with no upstream let the guard fall through to the delete; a count that cannot be taken keeps the clone, and a symlink at that path, a stash, and ignored files keep it too. The call sits below every `--check` return (BUG-070)
D10 — 2026-09-17 — Three platforms, `CGO_ENABLED=0 -trimpath`, built and uploaded inside `/preflight` Step 6 — by: the operator, scope item 5
D11 — 2026-09-17 — Work happens on branch `release-binary`, one squash commit to `main` with code, docs, map, R9 and ADR-033 (R9's one-commit rule) — by: implementer, from R9
D12 — 2026-09-17 — The `close-map-gaps` branch, when it lands, keeps its reading clone at `~/.config/sh-agent/feedback-read`, since D9 removes `~/.config/sh-agent/feedback` — by: implementer
D13 — 2026-09-17 — An install from the embedded source copies the running binary and never rebuilds; `IsCheckout` is never asked about an empty path — by: cold read round 1, blocking 1
D14 — 2026-09-17 — The embedded source is a fallback only for a release binary (version a `vX.Y.Z` tag); a development build outside a tree keeps today's error, so a stale embedded copy is never installed silently — by: cold read round 1, blocking 2
D15 — 2026-09-17 — An explicit `--repo` or `$SH_AGENT_REPO` never falls through to the embedded files — by: cold read round 1, blocking 4, keeping today's deliberate behaviour
D16 — 2026-09-17 — R8's first sentence changes with R9, on its own exact text and approval — by: cold read round 1, blocking 3
D17 — 2026-09-17 — `ResolveSource` replaces `FindRepo`; git helpers are called only for a tree on disk; every command's behaviour with an embedded source is fixed by the table in Interfaces, `update` branching to the release flow on `src.Dir == ""` — by: cold read round 2, blocking G6 and G7
D18 — 2026-09-17 — The rule "a tag delivers nothing" changes with R9, in three places, in the Phase 5 commit: `AGENTS.md` § How the harness works rule 2 becomes "**A tag is a release.** `/preflight vX.Y.Z` makes a signed tag and publishes that tag's binaries with signed checksums; checkout places follow `main`, binary-only places update to the newest release."; `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases' opening sentence says a tag marks a version and carries the release binaries that binary-only places update to, while checkout places still follow `main`; ADR-031 is not edited (append-only) — ADR-033 states it supersedes ADR-031 D3's "a tag delivers nothing". The `Source selection` sentence also names `update` (round 3, non-blocking G9) — by: cold read round 3, blocking G8, resolved at the cap
D19 — 2026-09-17 — Every release carries release notes in four groups built from the `changes/` entries since the previous tag, read by the operator and attached with `--notes-file` — by: the operator, "We need to write a release note when we do a new version. Like updates, optimization and fixes, new features etc.", added after the cold read; a docs-and-procedure addition that changes no interface the cold read settled
D20 — 2026-09-17 — `Source` carries `Version`, set only for the embedded files: `Install` records `embedded:<version>`, `status` and the report record show it, and no reader has to be passed the running binary's version separately — by: implementer, Phase 2 task 4
D21 — 2026-09-17 — `status` reads an installed release binary's version from its build info's module version when that is a `vX.Y.Z` tag (`releaseFromInfo`); `-ldflags` cannot be read back because `-trimpath` leaves it out of the build info (measured with go1.27.1: `go version -m` shows `-ldflags` without `-trimpath`, none with it). The checkout path keeps `versionFromInfo`, so a development build at a clean tag is still compared by revision — by: implementer, Phase 2 task 4
D22 — 2026-09-17 — SUPERSEDED by Phase 4, which replaced this refusal with the release flow on 2026-09-17; the placeholder stood only between the phases. Until Phase 4, `update` with an embedded source refused with `this install is the release binary vX.Y.Z and has no checkout; download a newer release by hand (README § Install without cloning)`, exit 1, calling no git helper; Phase 4 replaces it with the release flow — by: implementer, so the branch never calls git with an empty path between phases
D23 — 2026-09-17 — `go:embed` reads the WORKING TREE, so a release must be built from a tree with nothing untracked or ignored under the five directories: `embed_test.go` pins the embedded set to `git ls-files` at test time, and `/preflight` Step 6 refuses at release time (Phase 5) — by: implementer, from the Phase 2 security review's finding 1, reproduced with an ignored `rules/.env` that was embedded while every other test stayed green
D24 — 2026-09-17 — A release binary's install REPLACES an install this home got from a checkout: it installs the embedded files, prunes what is no longer planned and rewrites the manifest to `embedded:vX.Y.Z`, without the `knownCheckout` guard. Converting a place to binary-only needs no flag; the cost is that running a downloaded binary from outside the checkout on the operator's own box swaps that home's install — by: the operator, "Replace, as it does now", their own turn, on the Phase 2 security review's finding 6
D25 — 2026-09-17 — ONE real `sh-agent report` from this box into `styrman-harness-feedback` is authorised, to settle whether GitHub serves a `--filter=blob:none` partial clone over SSH and accepts a push from a `--depth 1` clone (plan § Risks). It runs only after Phase 3's local-bare-repository tests pass, writes only `reports/<this host>/`, and its result is recorded in the Phase 3 testing log — by: the operator, "Yes, when Phase 3's code is ready", their own turn
D26 — 2026-09-17 — `SHA256SUMS` carries the release it belongs to as its first line, `# styrman-harness vX.Y.Z` (a comment `sha256sum -c` ignores), and `update` refuses a release whose signed checksums name another version or none. Without it a signed `SHA256SUMS` from ANY release verifies under ANY tag, so an older release's assets served under a newer tag would pass every check. `/preflight` Step 6 must write that line before signing (Phase 5) — by: implementer, from the Phase 4 security review's finding 1
D27 — 2026-09-17 — `update` never installs sideways or backwards: the tag must parse as `vX.Y.Z`, must be greater than the running version by numeric comparison, and a binary whose own version is not a release (a development build) is left alone with a message. An older release is signed exactly as honestly as a newer one, so signature verification alone cannot refuse it — by: implementer, from the same finding
D28 — 2026-09-17 — The signature verifier is looked for at `/usr/bin/ssh-keygen` and `/bin/ssh-keygen` before `PATH`: its verdict is the whole trust chain, and a copy earlier in `PATH` is the cheapest way to defeat it. `PATH` remains the fallback for a machine that keeps OpenSSH elsewhere, and the limit is stated in the code — a machine whose system directories an attacker owns can defeat any check this binary makes — by: implementer, from the Phase 4 security review's finding 2
Defaults for round 1's non-blocking items: the checksum file is signed in `/preflight` Step 6 right after the tag's own verification, with the same key; the compiled-in signer line is a package variable a test overrides; `go install` is documented for `v1.1.0` or newer — by: implementer
Rejected: embedding in `cmd/sh-agent` — `go:embed` cannot reach `../../skills`
Rejected: verifying the git tag only — it does not cover the downloaded file (D5)
Rejected: the GitHub API for `report` — would make `gh` required for reporting (the operator chose the throwaway clone)
Rejected: a Go SSH-signature library — a dependency against R4; `ssh-keygen` is the vetted verifier already on every place
Open: whether `go install` should be a documented way in before `v1.1.0` exists — default: the README names `v1.1.0` or newer explicitly

title: Recon — BUG-079 diagnosis (2026-09-18)
body:
# Recon — BUG-079 diagnosis (2026-09-18)

## Question
Why did `sh-agent update` (release path) report v1.2.2 installed, but `sh-agent version` in the same shell still printed v1.2.1, until `/usr/local/bin/sh-agent` was removed and the shell re-sourced?

## Summary
`UpdateFromRelease` (internal/harness/release.go:90-179) always writes the new binary to a FIXED path, `dest := filepath.Join(home, BinPath)` (release.go:162, `BinPath = ".local/bin/sh-agent"`, plan.go:16) — never to wherever the currently-running binary actually lives. It never calls `os.Executable()` or compares `dest` against the running process's own path. When the running binary is `/usr/local/bin/sh-agent` (repro: an older binary there, `~/.local/bin` earlier on PATH but bash's command hash already resolved `sh-agent` to `/usr/local/bin/sh-agent`), the update writes v1.2.2 to `~/.local/bin/sh-agent`, runs `<dest> install` (which correctly reports "260 unchanged" because it's self-consistent with `~/.local/bin`), and exits — leaving the actually-invoked `/usr/local/bin/sh-agent` at v1.2.1 completely untouched. The next `sh-agent version` in that shell re-uses bash's cached hash table entry for `/usr/local/bin/sh-agent`, so it prints v1.2.1 even though PATH order would prefer `~/.local/bin`. This is the same shadow-binary class of problem as BUG-078 (which produced `PathShadows` in pathguard.go), but the `update` code path never calls `PathShadows` to warn about it — only `install`'s `pathHint` (main.go:395) and `status` (main.go:648-653) do.

## Top candidate root causes (ranked)

1. **(most likely) `UpdateFromRelease` writes to a fixed `home`-derived path, never to the running binary's actual location, and does not detect/warn when they differ.**
   - Evidence: release.go:162 `dest := filepath.Join(home, BinPath)`; no `os.Executable()` call anywhere in release.go (confirmed via grep); the doc comment at release.go:159-161 explains the atomic-rename mechanics but never addresses *where* `dest` is relative to the invoking binary. `BinPath` is a package constant (plan.go:16), not derived from `os.Executable()`.
   - What would falsify it: if `dest` were computed from `os.Executable()` (or compared against it with a warning) this could not happen — check by re-reading release.go for any executable-path lookup; there is none currently.

2. **`update`'s output never runs `PathShadows` to tell the operator the write didn't land on the resolved binary.**
   - Evidence: `harness.PathShadows` (pathguard.go:28) exists specifically for this class of bug (its own doc comment cites BUG-078: "a downloaded, signature-verified, checksum-verified release binary was installed to /usr/local/bin and then ignored"). It is called from `install`'s `pathHint` (main.go:395) and from `status` (main.go:648-653), but the `update` case in main.go (lines 191-216, calling `harness.UpdateFromRelease`) never calls it. So even though the tooling to detect exactly this shadow exists, `update`'s own success output ("verified and installed ... 260 unchanged") gives no signal that the binary actually on PATH first (or hashed by the shell) was left behind.
   - Falsify: if `update` did call `PathShadows`/print a shadow warning after a successful release replace, the operator would have been told before running `version`. It currently does not — confirmed by grep showing only two call sites, both outside the `update` release branch.

3. **(contributing, not a code bug) bash's command hash table masks PATH order after the shell already resolved `sh-agent` once.** This is standard bash behavior (`hash -r` needed), not something sh-agent can fix directly, but it's what makes candidate 1's effect visible even when `~/.local/bin` precedes `/usr/local/bin` on PATH — the repro explicitly notes "or run `sh-agent update` in a shell that has already resolved `sh-agent` to `/usr/local/bin/sh-agent`". This amplifies but does not cause the core defect; candidate 1 is necessary and sufficient on its own (e.g., a fresh shell with `/usr/local/bin` genuinely first on PATH reproduces it without any hash involved).

## What `update` writes and what it would have needed to say
- Writes new binary to `filepath.Join(home, BinPath)` = `$HOME/.local/bin/sh-agent` (release.go:162), via `writeAtomic` (temp file + rename in the same dir).
- Nothing in `UpdateFromRelease` or the `update` case in main.go compares `dest` to `os.Executable()` of the running process, nor to any PATH-resolved `sh-agent`.
- For the operator to know before running `version`, the "verified and installed" message (release.go:169) or the subsequent install step would have needed to also report (via `PathShadows`, which already exists) that the binary actually invoked (`/usr/local/bin/sh-agent`, resolved by PATH or by the shell's hash) is NOT the file just replaced — i.e., the same warning `pathHint`/`status` already produce, but currently only reachable through `install`/`status`, not through `update`.

## Not examined
- Did not read `internal/harness/plan.go` in full (only grepped `BinPath` constant) or `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` lines 580-660 (`selfExecutable`, `binaryOlder`, status/pathHint helpers) in full detail — only grepped call sites.
- Did not inspect `release_test.go` or `main_test.go` for existing coverage of this exact shadow-on-update scenario (candidate for confirming whether this is already a known gap or genuinely untested).
- Did not confirm bash's exact hash-table semantics against the transcript beyond citing it as standard behavior.

diagnosis complete
