D14 — 2026-09-21 — The retro size check lives in Step 6 (apply), the only step at which the addition exists on disk, not in Step 2, which already has five items and runs before any draft — supersedes the Step 2 wording of D11's round — by: cold read round 2, gap 1
Rejected: splitting into `rules/` files — the cap is per block (BUG-085 probe). Pinning 12,000 chars — `context/AGENTS.md` alone is 23,194 chars. Dropping the inventory — asserted by tests and read by the smoke check. A size check at install time — a binary-only place cannot act on it.

D17 — 2026-09-21 — Phase 4 changed no source (docs, records, the mutation), so its checkpoint evidence is the main agent's bare `go test -race -count=1 ./...` run and the smoke log, not a `verifier` log — by: implementer

D15 — 2026-09-21 — The G3 task for `context/dev-setup.md` is "deploy a new Go service to Cloud Run for the first time"; the cold-reader check closed at its cap on this one item — by: "approved" (option 1, 2026-09-21)

body:
# Pruning review — `context/AGENTS.md` and `context/dev-setup.md`   (2026-09-21)

Phase 1 of `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-21-context-consolidation.md`, the audit prompt's Step 4 applied. Every non-empty line of the two files is a row (62 rows, 26,246 bytes; the rendered context is 27,163 bytes with the 134-byte marker, blank lines, the 708-byte inventory and the 49-byte canary). Three independent classifiers (Workflow `wf_ebd17196-757`: a strict pruner, a fresh-session sufficiency reader, an evidence-first reader) each classified all 62 rows with grep evidence; the table holds the majority class and action, the vote split where they differed, and the sufficiency reader's replacement text where it agreed with the majority (the most conservative of the three), else the evidence reader's. Bytes after are measured on the exact replacement text, newline included.

## Totals

- Rows per class (majority): KEEP 40, DUPLICATE 10, DERIVABLE 8, MOVE-TO-SKILL 3, MOVE-TO-SCOPED 1. MOVE-TO-ENFORCEMENT: none (R3). STALE: none — every path, verb, flag and bug record cited was checked by at least one reader. CONFLICT: none.
- Actions: shorten 34, keep 18, delete 7, move 3.
- Bytes in rows: 26246 → 19096. Projected rendered context: 20013 bytes (budget 22,000; cap 24,000). Projected if only KEEP rows remained unchanged and every other row were deleted: 19834 bytes.
- Discrete instructions (the prompt's A3): 214 before → 188 after by the evidence reader's count (the strict reader counted 230 → 192, the sufficiency reader 227 → 208; the readers split clauses differently, the direction agrees). title: Plan — Projects use `AGENTS.md` alone: no project `CLAUDE.md` stub (2026-09-21)
body:
# Plan — Projects use `AGENTS.md` alone: no project `CLAUDE.md` stub   (2026-09-21)

## Why

The operator, 2026-09-21: "I saw that claude can use AGENTS.md from version 2.1.277. That would be greats so we use the full AGENTS.md for everything. Go and verify that and If it is true fix it and cut a new minor", then "Your recommendation. Approved." Verified today on this box (Claude Code 2.1.278): a probe project with only `AGENTS.md` (no `CLAUDE.md` in or above it) was read natively on the second session ("The probe word is HERON-4412, from …/AGENTS.md"); the first session after the upgrade read nothing, as the memory page documents. The user level is different: with the `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` stub removed from a sandbox home, the global context did not load (UNKNOWN); the docs and the 2.1.277 changelog entry cover project `AGENTS.md` only. So the project stub goes and the global stub stays.

## Scope

In: `/init-project` no longer writes a project `CLAUDE.md`; its asset is removed; its description, Step 2 loop and bullet say so and name when a stub is still needed by hand (Claude Code before 2.1.277; Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry or a telemetry-disabled session, which fetch no feature flags; the first session after an upgrade reads nothing either way). An update run leaves an existing stub alone (D1). This repo's own `CLAUDE.md` is deleted (D2). `context/AGENTS.md` § Project layout says a project root is `AGENTS.md` alone. ADR-036 supersedes the project half of ADR-005. Release v1.6.0, MINOR (init-project behaviour changes for every user).

Out: the global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` stub written by `sh-agent install` (`plan.go:89`, `render.go:17`), verified required; removing stubs from existing projects; Antigravity (reads `AGENTS.md` natively already, ADR-005).

Follow-ups noted, not built: none.

## Surfaces touched

- `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:3` (description names "CLAUDE.md import"), `:22` (update rule mentions the `CLAUDE.md` fold), `:42-44` (the template loop lists `CLAUDE.md`), `:48` (the `CLAUDE.md` bullet); `skills/init-project/assets/CLAUDE.md` (deleted).
- `CLAUDE.md` at this repo's root (deleted); `AGENTS.md` § Layout / Key files if they name it (grep).
- `context/AGENTS.md:65` — "Root: `AGENTS.md` (`CLAUDE.md` is the line `@AGENTS.md`; no `GEMINI.md`)".
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` R2 — the sentence "(`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and a project's `CLAUDE.md` are one-line imports)" is the claim this plan reverses; replaced by the operator-approved text in Interfaces (D4), in the same commit as ADR-036 (the immutability rule; BUG-025 was this exact violation).
- `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md:22` — the `init-deploy` row's prompt says "including the .claude symlinks, CLAUDE.md, .gitignore lines"; `CLAUDE.md` is dropped from it and its check gains `! test -e CLAUDE.md`.
- `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-21-verify-agents-md-native.md` (new) — the probes of today that back § Why, written before the code lands.
- `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` — ADR-036. README: no project-stub statement (grepped: none). `TestHarnessMap`, `plan.go`: untouched (the global stub is not in scope).

## Interfaces

- `skills/init-project/SKILL.md`: description drops "CLAUDE.md import"; the Step 3 template loop becomes `for f in AGENTS.md REQUIREMENTS.md TODO.md ROADMAP.md`; the `CLAUDE.md` bullet becomes: "`CLAUDE.md` — not written: Claude Code 2.1.277+ reads `AGENTS.md` natively when no `CLAUDE.md` sits in or above the project. An existing `CLAUDE.md` is left exactly as it is (an update never removes it; one that holds content other than `@AGENTS.md` is offered the fold as before). Write the one-line stub `@AGENTS.md` by hand only where native reading is unavailable: Claude Code before 2.1.277, Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry or a telemetry-disabled session; note that the first session after a Claude Code upgrade reads no `AGENTS.md` at all." The update sentence at `:22` keeps the fold exception.
- `context/AGENTS.md` Project layout line: "Root: `AGENTS.md` alone (no `CLAUDE.md`, no `GEMINI.md`; a `CLAUDE.md` stub `@AGENTS.md` only where Claude Code cannot read `AGENTS.md`: before 2.1.277, Bedrock, telemetry off), …" — about 100 bytes longer than today's parenthetical; the size test stays green (20,205 of 22,000 today).
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` R2, verbatim (approved 2026-09-21): "The context follows the agents.md standard and is named `AGENTS.md` at every level. A project has no `CLAUDE.md`: Claude Code 2.1.277+ reads `AGENTS.md` natively, and a one-line `@AGENTS.md` stub is written by hand only where it cannot (before 2.1.277, Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, or telemetry disabled). `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` stays a one-line import: Claude reads a user-level `AGENTS.md` only as an ancestor file, and a project with its own `CLAUDE.md`, or one outside the home directory, would then lose the global context. Skills follow the Agent Skills `SKILL.md` standard so that anything from skills.sh or any other source drops into `skills/` unchanged."
- ADR-036: supersedes ADR-005's sentence "a project's `CLAUDE.md` [is] the single line `@AGENTS.md`"; keeps the user-level stub with the verification that it is required; names the conditions above.

## Failure modes

- A project on an older Claude, Bedrock, or telemetry-off reads no instructions: the init-project bullet and ADR name the by-hand stub; nothing in the harness detects it (no hooks, R3).
- A place pulls this repo with a Claude older than 2.1.277: this repo's instructions stop loading there. The devbox is the only other Claude place; the handoff asks the operator to check `claude --version` before pulling.

## Verification

Tiers: unit (`gofmt -l cmd internal && go vet ./... && go test -race ./...`, the size test); integration (scratch install + status; a sandbox start of Claude Code with a question quoting the new Project layout line); behavioural, one run: `/init-project` headless in a fresh scratch repo (`.agents/scratch/init-probe`, `--add-dir <home>/.claude/skills/init-project`, answers in the prompt as the matrix's `init-deploy` row) and `ls CLAUDE.md` afterwards must fail; e2e: from this checkout with its `CLAUDE.md` deleted, `claude -p` with no tools answers a question only this repo's `AGENTS.md` can (the first heading "AGENTS.md — styrman-harness" and the canary GANNET from the global context) — run twice if the first is a first-session-after-upgrade case.

E2E criteria: (1) golden: in this checkout without `CLAUDE.md`, Claude Code names this repo's AGENTS.md first heading; (2) edge: `/init-project` in a fresh repo leaves no `CLAUDE.md`.

## Phases

- [x] Cold-reader check — design ready and implementation ready (`reviews/2026-09-21-coldread-project-agents-md-native-r1.md`, `-r2.md`, `-r3.md`: round 3 both tokens, 2026-09-21)

### Phase 1 — The change
- [x] `skills/init-project/SKILL.md` edits (Interfaces) and `git rm skills/init-project/assets/CLAUDE.md` (2026-09-21: grep shows the description, the update sentence and the new bullet) — verify: `grep -n "CLAUDE.md" skills/init-project/SKILL.md` shows only the new bullet and the update-fold sentence, AI — expect: two hits — docs: `skills/init-project/SKILL.md`
- [x] `git rm CLAUDE.md` at the repo root (2026-09-21; no stale claim in `AGENTS.md`/README); grep `AGENTS.md`/README for a claim that this repo has one — verify: `git ls-files CLAUDE.md` empty, AI — expect: empty; no stale claim
- [x] `context/AGENTS.md` Project layout line (Interfaces) (2026-09-21: size test PASS, 20,328 of 22,000) — verify: size test bare, AI — expect: PASS against the 22,000-byte budget (today 20,205; the new line is a few bytes longer or shorter)
- [x] Testing log `testing/2026-09-21-verify-agents-md-native.md` (written 2026-09-21): the four probes (project scope with/without stub; user scope in a home outside `/home`: no stub → both files load; project `CLAUDE.md` → global context dropped; stub → loads) — verify: file exists, AI — expect: written first
- [x] `REQUIREMENTS.md` R2 replaced by the main agent with the operator-approved Interfaces text (the file's "agents never edit" rule bars subagents and unapproved edits; the operator approved this exact text, D4) and ADR-036 by `changelog` (its lane: `DECISIONS.md` only), read against the diff, one commit — verify: `git diff --stat`, AI — expect: R2 one paragraph replaced; DECISIONS.md appended only — docs: `REQUIREMENTS.md`
- [x] `skill-matrix.md` `init-deploy` row (2026-09-21): drop `CLAUDE.md` from the prompt, add `! test -e CLAUDE.md` to the check — verify: `grep -c CLAUDE.md` on that row, AI — expect: 1 (the check only)
- [x] Integration and behavioural runs (Verification) — verify: AI — expect: scratch install drift none; Claude Code quotes the new line; the init probe has no `CLAUDE.md`; this checkout answers from its `AGENTS.md` (2026-09-21: sandbox home reinstalled, drift none, 257 files; both CLIs quoted the new Root line and GANNET, Antigravity store 0 truncation markers, 0 parse errors; headless `/init-project` in `.agents/scratch/init-probe`: scaffold written, `CLAUDE.md` absent — that run did not make the init commit the matrix row expects, one run, out of this plan's scope; e2e golden: this checkout answered `# AGENTS.md — styrman-harness` from its `AGENTS.md` twice)
- [x] Review row: diff under 50 lines read by the main agent; `/review --docs` over the range (an init-project behaviour changed) — expect: findings fixed or rebutted (2026-09-21: `reviews/2026-09-21-review-v1.5.0-HEAD-docs.md` APPROVE WITH NITS, one punctuation nit fixed)
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: `go test -race ./...` exit 0 — evidence: `verifier` log `testing/2026-09-21-project-agents-md-native.md` PASS (251 tests, size 20,328, install drift none, asset gone, global stub kept, root CLAUDE.md absent), 2026-09-21; the punctuation fix after it re-checked bare by the main agent

### Phase 2 — Release
- [x] `/preflight v1.6.0` — who: user's word "cut a new minor" (2026-09-21) — expect: SHIP, signed tag, five assets (gate `reviews/2026-09-21-preflight-v1.6.0.md` SHIP; the tag and assets follow this release commit, 2026-09-21)

## Risks

Assumptions: the devbox's Claude Code is 2.1.277 or newer — checked by the operator (`claude --version`) before pulling this repo there; named in the handoff. The feature-flag fetch works on this box (it did: the second probe read the file).

## Decisions

D1 — 2026-09-21 — An update run never removes an existing project `CLAUDE.md`; the pre-existing offer to fold a `CLAUDE.md` that holds other content into `AGENTS.md` (on the user's yes, leaving the one-line stub) stays as it is — by: "Your recommendation. Approved."
D2 — 2026-09-21 — This repo's own `CLAUDE.md` is removed; the devbox checks its Claude version first — by: "Your recommendation. Approved."
D3 — 2026-09-21 — The global `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` stub stays — by: "Approve your recommendations" (2026-09-21), after the measured probes of D5
D4 — 2026-09-21 — REQUIREMENTS R2 edit, exact text in Interfaces — by: "Approve your recommendations" (2026-09-21); ADR-036 and the edit land in one commit
D5 — 2026-09-21 — Measured in a probe home outside `/home` (Claude Code 2.1.278): with no stub, `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` and the project's `AGENTS.md` both load (as ancestor `.claude/AGENTS.md` plus project file); a project with its own `CLAUDE.md` switches Claude to CLAUDE.md-only mode and the global context is dropped; with the stub it loads in every case. A probe home under `/home/kesokaj` is invalid: the real `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` counts as an ancestor `.claude/CLAUDE.md` there — by: implementer, measured (BUG-087's rule: the arrangement)
Rejected: an `--claude-stub` flag on `/init-project` (a by-hand one-liner is enough; a flag is code); removing stubs on update (breaks older or flag-less Claude sessions silently).

title: Recon — sh-agent update --from-zip (2026-09-28)
body:
# Recon — sh-agent update --from-zip   (2026-09-28)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Question
Add `sh-agent update --from-zip <file>`: unpack a GitHub-downloaded zip into a temp dir,
refuse zip-slip entries, install with the RUNNING binary (no rebuild, no replace), delete
the temp dir; must work from a release binary, which `ResolveSource` today refuses (ADR-034).
Map status drift, Install/Plan manifest recording, update's flag handling, README map +
TestHarnessMap, every living-doc "two ways in" statement, embedded-tree sizes, report's use
of `State.Repo`.

## Summary
The scope statement is in direct tension with a documented, ADR-backed design decision:
`.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` § How a machine gets the harness says "Two ways,
and no third," and AGENTS.md rule 1 says "no third [way]" implicitly via "Two ways in, one
way back, nothing else." A zip unpack today is explicitly the demoted **third case** — "a
plain copy… it is no longer one of the ways in… it is the fallback." Making `update --from-zip`
work *from a release binary* turns that fallback into a second way a release-binary place can
move forward (alongside the signed-checksum download), which is exactly the kind of path
change AGENTS.md rule 3 requires going to the operator first, with an ADR, landing with the
map/doc changes in one commit — before writing any code. Mechanically the feature is buildable:
`cmd/sh-agent/main.go`'s `update` case (main.go:198-230) already branches on `repo == ""` for
the release-binary path calling `harness.UpdateFromRelease` — a `--from-zip` branch would sit
beside it, build a `harness.Source{Dir: <tempdir>, FS: os.DirFS(tempdir)}` (see `source.go:18`),
call `harness.Install`/`harness.Plan` directly (never `harness.Reinstall`, which always spawns
`go build`), and `os.RemoveAll` the temp dir afterward. The unresolved design problems are: (a)
the ADR/doc conflict above, (b) what `State.Repo` should record once the temp dir is gone
(status's `EmbeddedPrefix` branch at main.go:383 and `knownCheckout` at main.go:573 both assume
`st.Repo` is either a real path or an `embedded:` release string — a stale temp path breaks
both), and (c) zip-slip / top-folder handling (GitHub's zip has one top folder,
`styrman-harness-<branch>/`, that must be stripped before `IsRepo`/`Plan` see the tree).

## Relevant files
- `internal/harness/repo.go:22-48` — `ResolveSource`; release-binary branch (34-48) refuses
  any `--repo`/`$SH_AGENT_REPO` unconditionally and returns `EmbeddedSource(version)`. This is
  the function the scope names as "superseded… for the one file the operator names" — but
  `--from-zip` most naturally bypasses `ResolveSource` entirely (own resolution in `main.go`,
  producing a `DirSource` pointed at the unpacked temp dir) rather than adding a branch inside
  it, matching how `report()` (main.go:304-319) already builds its own `Source` instead of
  going through `ResolveSource` when it needs release-binary-specific behaviour.
- `internal/harness/repo.go:196-236` — `Reinstall`: rebuilds via `go build ./cmd/sh-agent` then
  runs that build's `install --repo <repo>`. Scope explicitly forbids this for `--from-zip`
  ("never rebuilding, never replacing the binary… installs that tree with the RUNNING binary").
  `update`'s existing checkout path (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go:474-524`, see `update()`) calls
  `harness.Reinstall` at line 517 — `--from-zip` must NOT reuse this function; it needs its own
  small path that calls `harness.Install`/`harness.Plan` in-process, the same shape `install`
  uses for a release binary (main.go:137-146, `installFiles`) or a plain copy (main.go:175-182).
- `internal/harness/source.go:18,36-54` — `Source` struct, `EmbeddedSource`, `EmbeddedPrefix =
  "embedded:"`, `IsReleaseVersion`. A `DirSource` helper (used by `absSource` in repo.go:90-96)
  is the existing constructor for a Dir-backed Source; `--from-zip` would use the same shape.
- `internal/harness/apply.go:19-148` (`Install`) — for a Dir source (`src.Dir != ""`, line
  119-123) it records `repo = src.Dir` (the literal temp path) and `commit = Inspect(repo).Commit`
  in `State{Repo: repo, Commit: commit, ...}` (line 134). `Inspect` (repo.go:135-148) checks
  `IsCheckout` first (`.git` present) — the unpacked zip tree has no `.git`, so `Inspect` returns
  an EMPTY `RepoInfo{}` silently (no error), giving `commit == ""` and a manifest that records
  `Repo: <temp-dir-path>` with an empty commit — a path that will not exist once the temp dir is
  removed. This is the finding behind item 1 of the dispatch: no `checkManagedTree`/link-refusal
  call happens automatically inside `Install` — that runs earlier, inside `RenderContext` and
  `LoadInventory` (`render.go:31`, `inventory.go:90,128`), which `Plan` calls (plan.go:76-83,
  98-99) BEFORE `Install` ever sees the files, so it does run, just not from `Install` itself.
- `internal/harness/plan.go:53-199` (`Plan`) — reads exactly `context/*.md` (via
  `RenderContext`), `skills/<name>/**`, `agents/<name>.md`, `commands/<name>.md` +
  `workflows/<name>.md` (comment says both map the same as commands; only `inv.Commands` is
  actually walked — `workflows/` is not a separate directory read, contrary to the doc comment
  at plan.go:61), and `rules/<name>.md` — five source directories total, matching the scope's
  list (context, skills, agents, commands, rules). No separate `workflows/` dir exists in the
  repo today (confirmed: `find commands rules -type f` → 2 files total, `commands/` is empty).
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:198-230` (`update` case) — the exact insertion point. `repo == ""` (a
  release binary) already branches to `harness.UpdateFromRelease` (line 218); a
  `--from-zip` flag would need to be checked even earlier (before or alongside this branch),
  since scope requires it to work "from a RELEASE binary" specifically, and today the checkout
  branch (`repo != ""`, line 227-230) calls `update()` → `harness.Reinstall`, which is also
  wrong for `--from-zip`. A `*zipFlag != ""` check likely wants to short-circuit both branches.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:346-472` (`status`) — `repo := src.Dir` (347); when `repo == ""`
  (release binary, line 350-352) prints `source embedded vX.Y.Z`, no git state. For a DEV BUILD
  today, `repo` is always a real, resolvable checkout path (ResolveSource never returns a
  vanished Dir for a dev build in the current code) — so nothing today exercises "status after
  install from a now-deleted temp dir." Adding `--from-zip` for a dev build is out of scope
  (scope says the feature targets release binaries) but if `ResolveSource`/`status` share the
  Dir-source code path afterward, `Inspect(repo)` at line 354 would run `git -C <deleted-dir>
  rev-parse …`, which fails quietly into `RepoInfo{}` (IsCheckout returns false via `os.Lstat`
  error) — `status` would print `repo <deleted-path> (plain copy, not its own git checkout;
  update is refused)` (line 364), which is misleading (there is no such repo at all) and
  `update` would then be permanently refused for that home (matches `errPlainCopy`,
  repo.go:118-119) even though the operator wants to run `--from-zip` again. This is the
  strongest argument for a distinct `ZipPrefix` (`"zip:sha256:<hex>"` or similar) recorded in
  `State.Repo` instead of the literal temp path, paralleling `EmbeddedPrefix` exactly.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:383` — `from := "commit " + st.Commit; if release, ok :=
  strings.CutPrefix(st.Repo, harness.EmbeddedPrefix); ok { from = "release " + release }`. A
  `ZipPrefix` would need a third branch here: `else if zipInfo, ok :=
  strings.CutPrefix(st.Repo, harness.ZipPrefix); ok { from = "zip " + zipInfo }` (or similar),
  printed instead of `commit ` + an empty/stale string.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:553-580` (`knownCheckout`) — already has the pattern to copy: it
  special-cases `EmbeddedPrefix` (line 573) to avoid calling `samePath` against a release
  string. `knownCheckout` is called from the `install`/`update`-checkout branches
  (main.go:147, 227) — NOT from the release-binary `update` branch (line 198-226) — so if
  `--from-zip` reuses the release-binary branch's shape, `knownCheckout` likely does not need
  to change; if a `ZipPrefix`-recorded home is later re-resolved through `ResolveSource`'s
  dev-build walk (repo.go:75, which already special-cases `EmbeddedPrefix` to avoid treating it
  as a candidate path), that same `strings.HasPrefix(st.Repo, EmbeddedPrefix)` guard
  (repo.go:75) would ALSO need a `ZipPrefix` exclusion, or a stale zip manifest entry gets
  treated as a literal (deleted) candidate directory.
- `internal/harness/report.go:311-319` (`report()`'s own Source construction, mirrors
  main.go:304-319) and `report.go:345-358` — `report` does NOT read `st.Repo` from the loaded
  state at all (confirmed by grep: only `report.go:332` calls `LoadState`, and that result's
  `.Repo`/`.Commit` fields are never referenced — only `.Vendor`, `.Files`, `.InstalledAt`).
  Instead `report` re-resolves its OWN `src` independently (release binary → `EmbeddedSource`,
  else → fresh `ResolveSource` call) and uses `Inspect(src.Dir)` on that fresh source
  (report.go:354-358) to get `harness_commit`. **This means a stale `State.Repo` after a zip
  install does NOT directly break `report`'s output fields** — but if a future `report` call's
  own `ResolveSource` (for a dev build only; release binaries skip it, report.go:312-313) walks
  up from the working directory or falls back to `st.Repo` as a candidate path (repo.go:75-77),
  a `ZipPrefix`-tagged `st.Repo` must be excluded the same way `EmbeddedPrefix` already is,
  or `report` tries to `Inspect`/`LoadInventory` a directory that no longer exists.
- `README.md:182` and `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` § How a machine gets the
  harness — "Two ways, and no third" / "A plain copy… it is no longer one of the ways in… it
  is the fallback for a machine that can reach neither of the two, not a way in." Both need an
  ADR-driven rewrite if `--from-zip` becomes a real path for a release-binary place, not merely
  a code change.
- `README.md:9-45` (mermaid map, § How it works) and `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go:1341-1373`
  (`TestHarnessMap`) — the test only checks that every `sh-agent <verb>` mentioned in the map
  exists in `usage` (main.go:35) and that `install`, `update`, `report` are all present
  (main_test.go:1362-1372); it does NOT parse flags, so `--from-zip` needs no new map NODE
  unless the feature adds a genuinely new LANE (e.g. "operator's own machine, GitHub web UI
  download" → temp dir → installer, bypassing both `harnessRepo` and `releases` nodes in the
  map, README.md:18-30). Per AGENTS.md rule 3, if this is a new path on the map, it is a design
  question requiring an ADR and a map edit in the same commit as the code.
- AGENTS.md rule 1 ("Two ways in, one way back, nothing else") and rule 6 ("The delivery claim
  has one home… stated once, in `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` § The model") — rule
  6 means the actual prose fix, if approved, is ONE edit to delivery.md § The model / § How a
  machine gets the harness; README.md:182, `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:56-61`, and
  `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md:45-55` all currently just point at / restate that same claim in
  one sentence each and would need the pointer sentence updated, not full rewrites (per rule 6's
  "point at it in one sentence and never restate it").

## Flows
- Existing release-binary `update`: `main.go` `update` case, `repo == ""` branch (198-226) →
  `harness.UpdateFromRelease(home, version, checkOnly, installArgs, out)` (`release.go:90`) →
  downloads+verifies signed release asset → replaces `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` → runs that new
  binary's `install`. This is the pattern `--from-zip` diverges from: no download, no binary
  replacement, no rebuild — just unzip → `Install`/`Plan` with the CURRENT running binary as
  `selfExe` (Plan's `selfExe []byte` param, plan.go:68,188-189) so `~/.local/bin/sh-agent`
  keeps being deployed as it is today (`installFiles`, main.go:277, not read in full this pass —
  worth a quick look before implementing, it is the shared helper both `install` branches use).
- Proposed `--from-zip` flow (not yet in code): validate flag/file → `os.MkdirTemp` under
  `ConfigDir(home)` or repo-analogous scratch (per project convention, never `/tmp` —
  `render.go`'s `diffOne` and `release.go` both already avoid `/tmp` for exactly this reason,
  apply.go:222-229) → unzip with a path-traversal guard (`filepath.Clean`/`strings.HasPrefix`
  check per entry — GitHub zips have one top-level folder to strip, e.g.
  `styrman-harness-main/context/...`) → `harness.IsRepo(tempdir)` sanity check (repo.go:99-105)
  → build `Source{Dir: tempdir, FS: os.DirFS(tempdir), Version: <running version>}` → call
  `harness.Plan` + `harness.Install` in-process exactly as `installFiles` does (main.go:277,
  not fully read) → `os.RemoveAll(tempdir)` → print a status line distinguishing this from both
  existing update paths.

## Conventions
- Every refusal in `repo.go` names WHERE a bad path/value came from (the `--repo`/
  `$SH_AGENT_REPO` error at repo.go:44) and is actionable; a `--from-zip` error (bad zip,
  traversal attempt, not-a-repo-shaped unpack) should match this voice.
- Scratch/temp files never go to `/tmp`; existing code uses `ConfigDir(home)`-relative temp
  dirs (apply.go:222-229 `Diff`, and `release.go`'s download directory at repo.go-adjacent
  `release.go:132-138` pattern) — `--from-zip`'s unpack dir should follow the same rule.
  `Reinstall` (repo.go:205) uses `.agents/scratch/sh-agent-build-<pid>` INSIDE the source repo
  itself — not applicable here since there is no source repo to nest inside for a release
  binary; the `ConfigDir(home)` pattern is the right model.
- `EmbeddedPrefix` (source.go:44) is the existing precedent for "manifest records something
  other than a live directory path" — a `ZipPrefix` constant alongside it is the natural shape
  the dispatch's own suggested `zip:sha256:<hex>` value fits (hashing the zip's bytes, not the
  temp dir, since the temp dir is deleted).
- Every state-machine-ish `if strings.HasPrefix(st.Repo, EmbeddedPrefix)` site found (repo.go:75,
  main.go:383, main.go:573) needs the equivalent `ZipPrefix` branch — three call sites, not one.

## Risks
1. **Design/doc conflict (highest risk).** delivery.md and AGENTS.md rule 1 currently say
   "two ways in… no third," with the unpacked-zip case explicitly demoted to "fallback… not a
   way in." Scope's own framing ("this path supersedes that [ADR-034] for the one file the
   operator names") suggests awareness of tension with ADR-034 specifically, but does not
   address the delivery-model "no third way" claim. Per AGENTS.md rule 3 this needs the
   operator's sign-off and an ADR BEFORE code, landed in one commit with docs + map (rule 3,
   rule 6). This is a recon finding to raise, not something to silently code around.
2. **Reinstall vs Install split.** It would be easy to accidentally route `--from-zip` through
   the existing checkout `update()` function (main.go:474) which unconditionally calls
   `harness.Reinstall` (rebuild) — scope explicitly forbids this. The new code must call
   `harness.Install`/`harness.Plan` directly, mirroring `installFiles` (main.go:277, not read
   this pass — read it before implementing).
3. **Manifest staleness.** Recording the literal temp dir path in `State.Repo` (as `Install`
   does today for any Dir source, apply.go:117-123) leaves `status`/`update`/`knownCheckout`
   pointing at a directory that no longer exists after cleanup — three call sites listed above
   need a `ZipPrefix` (or similar) to handle this, matching the `EmbeddedPrefix` precedent.
4. **Zip-slip.** No existing code in this repo unzips anything (grep found no `archive/zip`
   usage) — this is new territory; the entry-refusal logic (scope: "refuses any entry that
   would leave it") has no existing pattern to copy from within this codebase.
5. **`workflows/` doc-comment mismatch** (plan.go:61) is a pre-existing minor inaccuracy, not
   caused by this feature, but worth noting if editing plan.go nearby.

## Not examined
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` `installFiles` function body (main.go:277) — named but not read in
  full; read before implementing, since `--from-zip` should likely reuse it directly.
- `internal/harness/release.go` beyond lines 80-139 (download, checksum/signature verification,
  binary replacement) — not needed for `--from-zip` (no download/replace) but worth a skim for
  the temp-directory-cleanup idiom it already uses.
- `internal/harness/source.go` full file (only lines 18-54 read) — `DirSource`,
  `FS`/`os.DirFS` wiring, `src.path()` helper referenced in plan.go/inventory.go.
- `internal/harness/inventory.go` `checkManagedTree` full body (only referenced by line number,
  not read) — confirm exactly what it refuses (symlinks only, per plan.go:108's comment, or more).
- Existing tests: `internal/harness/*_test.go`, `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` other than
  `TestHarnessMap` — no test-naming conventions or existing `--check`/`--dry-run` test patterns
  surveyed; needed before writing the plan's test list.
- `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-17-delivery-rework.md` (referenced by delivery.md as the PLANNED
  doc) — not read; may already discuss or foreclose a zip-install path.
- `skills/init-project`, `skills/find-skills` install-path mentions (dispatch item 5) — not
  grepped; likely low-risk (probably just point at README § Install without cloning) but
  unconfirmed.
- `context/` directory's own statements of the delivery model (dispatch item 5) — not grepped.
- Full `installPassArgs`/flag-parsing interaction for a new `--from-zip DIR` flag: whether it
  needs its own entry in `reorder()`'s `takesValue` map (main.go:622-627) — almost certainly
  yes (a flag taking a value) but not yet drafted/confirmed against `flag.FlagSet` registration
  style used for `--feedback-repo` etc. (main.go:84-90).

## Sizes (dispatch item 6)
`du -sb`: `context` 19,658 bytes; `skills` 852,476 bytes; `agents` 47,801 bytes; `commands` 0
bytes (empty dir); `rules` 0 bytes at top level but contains 2 files (`find` reports 2 files
under `rules/`, likely one level down or `du` miscounting an empty-looking top — worth
re-verifying with `find rules -type f -exec du -b {} +` before setting an unpack byte limit).
Total tracked files across all five dirs: 132. A zip of the whole repo (GitHub's "Download ZIP")
will be larger than these five dirs alone since it includes `.agents/`, `cmd/`, `internal/`,
`.git`-adjacent metadata is excluded by GitHub zips but everything else in the repo is included —
an unpack size/file-count limit should be set generously above ~1MB / 200 files, or scoped to
validate only that the five expected top-level dirs exist post-unpack rather than capping total
zip size tightly.

title: Research — OKF (Open Knowledge Format) against the harness (2026-09-28)
body:
# Research — OKF (Open Knowledge Format) against the harness   (2026-09-28)

## Question

The operator asked: "Have we implemented OKF in styrman-harness, should we do it?" This record answers both questions and ends with what approving it would do.

## Answer in brief

1. **Not implemented.** There is no trace of OKF anywhere in the repo, its history, the machine state or the six projects on this box, and no directory is a conformant bundle.
2. **Recommendation: A, not now and not never.**
   - Nothing reads OKF: no coding-agent CLI does, and no project here produces or consumes it.
   - The spec has one committer and has changed without a version bump.
   - Every way of adopting it costs more than it returns.
   - Only one realistic trigger would reopen the question: a project that actually has to import, publish or maintain an OKF bundle.
3. **Approved by the operator on 2026-09-28.** They answered §6's question: "no BigQuery work on other machines". So A stands.

## Method

- **Eight agents** in one workflow run on 2026-09-28, all on Opus 5.5:
  - four independent read-only readers: spec, ecosystem, harness map, consumer projects;
  - one drafter;
  - three adversarial verification lenses: external facts, harness claims and compliance, and a devil's advocate arguing for adoption.
- **Verification:** all three lenses returned "holds with corrections", and none changed the recommendation. Their corrections are applied throughout and listed in § Corrections from verification.
- **Spec source:** a clone of `GoogleCloudPlatform/open-knowledge-format` at `ad30107` (2026-08-21). `SPEC.md:n` below means that clone.
- **Other sources:**
  - the v0.1 text from `knowledge-catalog` at `d44368c15e`;
  - the three Google Cloud blog posts (2026-06-12, 2026-07-25, 2026-08-27);
  - live vendor changelogs;
  - eight community skill repositories;
  - this repo at `914dc90`.
- **Notes, clones and saved changelogs** are in `.agents/scratch/research/okf/` (gitignored): `spec.md`, `ecosystem.md`, `harness.md`, `consumers.md`, `draft.md`, `factcheck-external.md`, `check-harness.md`, `counter.md`.
- **Re-checked by the main agent** against the clone, the saved changelogs and the repo:
  - the conformance and trust wording (`SPEC.md:3,57-63,403-410,736-764`);
  - zero OKF hits in the Claude Code (2.1.283), agy (1.2.12), Gemini CLI and Codex changelogs;
  - the contents of the fabricioctelles skill;
  - ADR-005, ADR-006, ADR-007;
  - `embed.go:9`;
  - `deploy/remote.md:56`;
  - the frontmatter keys our own skills use.

## 1. Have we implemented it?

**No.** OKF appears nowhere in:
- this repo;
- its full history (`git log --all -S OKF`, `--grep okf`);
- `~/.config/sh-agent`;
- the six projects under `~/workspace`.

The only hit for `git grep -i okf` is `@hookform` in `skills/frontend/references/component-patterns.md:204`.

**Nothing is conformant either.** OKF requires every non-reserved `.md` file to carry YAML frontmatter with a non-empty `type` (`SPEC.md:736-744`). Of the 743 tracked `.md` files, 661 have frontmatter and none has `type:`. In `.agents/docs` (628 files):
- 525 carry only `owner:` and `date:`;
- 87 bug records add `id`, `status` and `area`;
- 9 retros add `session`;
- 3 deploy guides add `target`;
- 4 have no frontmatter.

## 2. What OKF is: the facts that decide this

- **The format.** A bundle is a directory of markdown files.
  - **What conformance requires:** every non-reserved `.md` file has parseable YAML frontmatter with a non-empty `type`, from an open, unregistered vocabulary. `index.md` and `log.md` are optional; when present, they follow §8 and §9 (`SPEC.md:736-744`).
  - **What consumers MUST NOT reject:** unknown keys, unknown types, missing optional fields, broken links, or a missing `index.md` (`SPEC.md:755-762`).
- **Versions.**
  - **v0.1** shipped on 2026-06-12 inside Google's `knowledge-catalog` samples.
  - **v0.2** shipped on 2026-07-24/25, with two breaking renames under a minor bump: `timestamp` became `generated.at`, and the body `# Citations` list became `sources`. It also added optional fields: `sources`, `usage_window`, `generated`, `verified`, `status: draft|stable|deprecated` and `stale_after`. Finally, it added an `Attested Computation` type, whose attester code runs on the consumer's side (`SPEC.md:287-433,584-608,803-811`).
  - The spec moved to its own repo on 2026-08-11.
  - **Changed in place:** on 2026-08-21, PR #6 turned every timestamp-valued key (`stale_after`, `sources[].last_modified`, `usage_window`) into a datetime with a UTC offset, and did not bump the version. "0.2" now names two texts. Issue #24 about this is open.
- **What it is for.** Knowledge about data catalogs.
  - All four sample bundles are analytics datasets.
  - The reference agent is a *producer*, built on Python, ADK, BigQuery and Gemini.
  - Google ships no consumer agent, no MCP server, no validator and no JSON Schema. Issue #8, which asks for a schema, is open with no replies.
  - On 2026-08-27 Google's third blog post showed ingestion into Knowledge Catalog. It came after the last spec commit, so product work continues. Whether that ingestion is preview or GA is not stated.
- **Governance.**
  - One Google engineer made all 6 commits on the current main.
  - There are no tags and no releases.
  - No maintainer has replied on any OKF thread in either repo: about 361 human comments across 119 threads. Maintainers are active elsewhere in `knowledge-catalog`.
- **Security.**
  - There is no security section.
  - The trust fields are unsigned and self-asserted, and the trust tiers derived from them are "advisory signals, not access control" (`SPEC.md:410`).
  - Attester sandboxing is deferred (`SPEC.md:788`).
- **Coding agents.** None of these reads OKF natively as of 2026-09-28, each checked through its changelog: Claude Code (2.1.283), agy (1.2.12), Gemini CLI (all 641 releases, plus a code search), Codex (500 releases) and Cursor (2026-08-19 to 2026-09-23).
  - This is unlikely to change, because OKF deliberately prescribes no runtime (`SPEC.md:57-63`). An agent reads a bundle with Read and grep, which both CLIs already do.
- **Relation to AGENTS.md.** The spec never mentions AGENTS.md, Agent Skills or MCP.
  - Google's v0.1 blog calls "the AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md family of convention files" one bespoke example of the pattern that OKF formalises.
  - The largest producer by stars among those found, LangChain OpenWiki (16.8k), still writes `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` so that agents find its bundle (its README lines 310 and 361-374). Writing `CLAUDE.md` into a project conflicts with R2.
  - *Inference:* OKF works in practice as a knowledge layer beside AGENTS.md, not a replacement for it.

## 3. The approaches

- **A. Watch.** Commit this record as the answer and change nothing else. §5 names the triggers that would reopen the question.
- **B. Vendor a community skill.**
  - **Best candidate:** `fabricioctelles/skills` → `okf-open-knowledge-format` (Apache-2.0).
    - 694-line SKILL.md with a description of about 750 characters.
    - 104 KB in all, including copies of both spec versions.
    - Ships `scripts/validate.sh` (8.5 KB of bash that greps frontmatter rather than parsing it) and offers to install the third-party `okflint`.
    - Repo HEAD is `4fcc2bf` (2026-09-27); the skill directory last changed at `875f499` (2026-09-09).
  - **Rejected candidates:**
    - `scaccogatto`: a Stop hook, a `uv run` MCP server, and a backfill skill that reads `~/.claude` transcripts.
    - `inkeep`: needs its own MCP server, even though it is the most-installed OKF skill (about 6.9k installs).
    - `rakibtg`: targets v0.1 and says to use it proactively in all coding work.
    - `siculo` and `catancs`: break the Agent Skills name rules.
    - `hamakyo`: maintains an `okf/` bundle beside the trail after every durable change, which would be a second trail.
    - `xSAVIKx`: `go build`s 13 binaries into `$HOME`.
- **C. A harness-owned authoring skill.**
  - Prose only, about 120 lines, pinned to `SPEC.md@ad30107`, with no script.
  - Carries the one safety rule the spec lacks: never run attester code that arrives inside a bundle without the operator's approval.
  - Must take a side on the spec's open contradictions: the spec recommends `/` links while Google's own reference agent forbids them, the relative-path base is unclear, and so is frontmatter on `log.md`.
- **D. Make the harness's own trail conformant, and have `/init-project` scaffold it.**
  - New trail files get `type:`.
  - The bug `status: fixed|open|wontfix` key is renamed, because it collides with OKF's lifecycle `status`.
  - `bugs/INDEX.md` gets `type:`, or a new name: on macOS's case-insensitive disk it collides with the reserved `index.md`.
  - One context sentence changes.
  - This touches at least 21 files: 1 context file, 7 agents, 7 skills, `init-project/SKILL.md`, 3 deploy templates, and the `DECISIONS.md` and `INDEX.md` templates. It amends rebuild decision #11 (owner and date), since both keys stay.
- **E. `sh-agent` validates OKF.** Either:
  - a YAML dependency, which breaks R4;
  - a hand-written parser for the YAML subset OKF uses (several hundred lines, unmeasured) in "a file copier with a manifest" (`AGENTS.md:57`);
  - or a check that only `type` is present, about 30 lines reusing `internal/harness/frontmatter.go`, which does not prove conformance.
- **F. A project pilot.**
  - The closest shape is `unifi-home-network`, "a written record of what the network actually looks like" (its `AGENTS.md:5-7`). A device and WLAN inventory with `verified` and `stale_after` would express in fields what its `AGENTS.md:49` says in prose.
  - Its real gap is different: its config snapshot is stranded in a handoff, and plain trail files fix that without OKF.
- **G. Reject it as a non-goal.**
  - Add a REQUIREMENTS line and an ADR. This would be the first non-goal added that way: ADR-007 only annotated the hooks line, which already existed.

## 4. Comparison

| Approach | Pros | Cons | Complexity | Cost | Maturity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. Watch | Costs nothing. Nothing to re-pin while the spec moves. A grep for "OKF" finds this record. | No hands-on experience. The harness ships no watcher (ADR-001: the installer is the only executable), so a trigger is noticed only when someone looks. | None | 0 context bytes; 3-4 trail files | n/a |
| B. Vendor skill | Quickest route. No Go. Drops in under R2. | **Breaks the zero-scripts rule** (ADR-006, ADR-007): `validate.sh` would ship, and `embed.go:9` would build it into every release binary. Offers a third-party linter. The broad trigger fits our own trail and would fire on routine trail work; it cannot be trimmed in place (a trimmed fork is C). One maintainer. Nobody here would use it. | Low | +29 B of context. A ~750-character description in every session on both CLIs. 104 KB to vet for payloads (arXiv:2606.19191, PhantomSkill). A re-vendor on every spec change. | Low |
| C. Harness skill | Our text. Short. Carries the missing safety rule. Precedent exists for generic skills no project uses yet (`gke-basics`, `terraform`, `json-api-style`). | No known user (YAGNI). OKF is not in the declared stack. Must take sides on contradictions no maintainer has resolved. Needs a re-pin whenever "0.2" changes in place. | Medium | +14 B of context. Description tokens in every session. Reviewer and a sandbox check on both CLIs. | Low |
| D. Conformant trail | Typed documents. Approvals could be recorded as `verified: {by: human:<id>}`. | **`type:` adds nothing**: every trail file is already typed by its directory, and every reader selects by path. Append-only records never gain `type`, so every trail stays mixed and non-conformant. Needs the `status` rename and has the `INDEX.md` collision. `stale_after` would not have caught this harness's actual stale-text bugs (BUG-027, BUG-042, BUG-084), which are restatements, not age. | High | At least 21 files, an ADR, and a MINOR release that changes every project's trail | Low |
| E. Validator | A mechanical check. | R4 (a dependency) or several hundred lines of parser. Nothing to check without D. No schema or corpus to test against. May only run by hand (R3). | High (Medium for type only) | A new command, tests, a security review, a pinned spec SHA | Low |
| F. Project pilot | The right home under global-vs-project. No harness bytes. | Nothing reads it there either. The actual gap closes without OKF. | Low | Work in that project only | Low |
| G. Reject | Closes the question. | Claims more than the evidence supports: "nothing reads it" and "immature" can both change. A REQUIREMENTS edit to add, and another to undo. | Low | 1 REQUIREMENTS line and an ADR | n/a |

Fit with this project's own rules ("ok" fits, "strains" fits awkwardly, "conflict" breaks it, "–" does not apply):

| Rule | A | B | C | D | E | F | G |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R2: standards, skills drop in unchanged | ok | ok | ok | ok for the trail (see T5 for skills) | ok | – | ok |
| R3: no hooks, gates or CI | ok | ok | ok | ok | strains: by hand only | – | ok |
| R4: stdlib only | ok | ok for the binary | ok | ok | conflict or strains | – | ok |
| R5 / file drop, no code | ok | ok | ok | ok | new code: a design question | – | ok |
| Zero scripts (ADR-006, ADR-007) | ok | **conflict** | ok | ok | ok | – | ok |
| Vendored verbatim (`AGENTS.md:56`) | – | binding: no trimming in place | – | – | – | – | – |
| Append-only records | – | – | – | conflict: old records stay untyped | – | – | – |
| ADR-035 budget (20,329 of 22,000 B, re-measured) | 0 | +29 B | +14 B | tens of bytes | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Global vs project (`context/AGENTS.md:37,41`) | ok | ok | strains: no known user | ok in form, no project asks | strains | ok | ok |

R1, R6 to R9 and the other non-goals are unaffected by every approach.

On precedent: the operator asked for agents.md, and the reason recorded in ADR-005 is just that ("The operator asked for the agents.md standard"). R2 adopts SKILL.md for ecosystem drop-in. No ADR states "adopt a standard when something outside the harness reads it", so that criterion is this report's inference, not a rule. That is why it is not a column above.

## 5. Recommendation

**A: not now, but not never.** Commit this record and change nothing else.

- **No reader and no producer here.** No CLI reads OKF, and nothing the operator runs emits a bundle that should drop in. A conformant trail would be read exactly as today's markdown is, because readers select by directory, not by `type`.
- **No need on this box.** None of the six projects uses BigQuery, Knowledge Catalog, Looker or dbt. The two needs shaped like OKF are both met without it:
  - `unifi-home-network`'s stranded snapshot;
  - `ranta-rankare`'s BUG-005, about where constants come from and when they were checked.
- **The spec cannot be pinned with confidence.** It has one committer, no maintainer triage, no tags, "0.2" naming two texts, and Google's own tooling contradicting the spec on links.
- **Every other option costs more than it returns.**
  - B breaks the zero-scripts rule.
  - C is honest work for no user.
  - D's `type:` adds nothing the directories do not already say, and leaves every existing trail non-conformant forever.
  - E needs D and a parser.
  - F closes a gap that plain files already close.
- **Not G:** both objections are observable and can change. Waiting costs nothing, so no REQUIREMENTS line is needed.

**Triggers that reopen it.** T2 is the realistic one. T1 is unlikely to ever fire, because OKF asks no CLI to do anything beyond what Read and grep already do. So A works like G unless a real need turns up in a session. That is acceptable because waiting costs nothing, and grepping for "OKF" finds this record.

| # | Trigger | How it is noticed | Smallest first step |
|---|---|---|---|
| T2 | A project must import, publish or maintain an OKF bundle: BigQuery or Knowledge Catalog work, a bundle handed over, an Outline export | Scoping that work with `/feature` | **F in that project:** a prose project skill under a non-harness name, pinned to a spec SHA. No harness change. If OpenWiki is the producer, it writes `CLAUDE.md`, which R2 forbids, so bring that to the operator as a harness question. |
| T3 | A second project needs the same | A second project skill like T2's exists | **C** through `/retro --harness`. The project copies are removed or renamed in the same change, because a project skill never reuses a harness name. |
| T1 | Claude Code or agy documents native OKF reading | Grep their changelogs for `open knowledge format\|\bokf\b` (0 hits on 2026-09-28) | A probe project holding a three-concept bundle, asked with `claude -p` / `agy -p` in the real home or from a sandbox home per `testing/guide.md` §4, as `testing/2026-09-21-verify-agents-md-native.md` did. Then reconsider D, limited to what the CLI actually reads. |
| T4 | The spec stabilises: a tag or release, an answer on #24, or a Google validator or JSON Schema (#8) | Reading the spec repo | Not a trigger on its own; a precondition for D and E. Re-read SPEC.md at the tag, and only then cost out E. |
| T5 | `type: Skill` lands in the canonical SPEC.md (proposed only in `knowledge-catalog` #312, an issue against the frozen copy), or agentskills.io adopts `type` | Reading the spec repo or agentskills.io | Check that both CLIs load a SKILL.md with a top-level `type:` key. The agentskills `skills-ref` validator rejects unknown keys, but 8 of our skills already carry `argument-hint`, so CLI loading is the real bar, not `skills-ref`. |

## 6. The one question that could change this

The consumer survey covered the six projects on this Linux box. The harness is also installed on the work Mac (Antigravity only) and on two other Linux hosts where the operator works on other projects (`deploy/remote.md:56`), and none of those was surveyed. If work there touches BigQuery, Knowledge Catalog or OKF bundles today, T2 has already fired. The answer then becomes F on that machine's project, and C once a second project needs it. If it does not, A stands as written.

**Answered 2026-09-28.** The operator, in their own turn: "Approve A, no BigQuery work on other machines". A stands. This is the operator's statement; those machines were not surveyed.

## 7. What you would be approving

1. **This record:** `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-28-research-okf.md`.
2. **The change entry:** `.agents/docs/changes/2026-09-28-research-okf.md`, naming all eight agents dispatched (four readers, a drafter, three verification lenses) and the main agent's spot checks.
3. **The Definition of Done for a docs-only change over ten lines:**
   - `verifier` runs the project's checks on the unchanged source tree (step 1) and writes its log.
   - No `reviewer`, because there is no source diff (`agents/reviewer.md:3`).
   - No `documentation` dispatch, because no behaviour changed.
4. **Closing the trail:** a handoff that says nothing is queued, then commit and push.

**Cost:** four or five markdown files, docs only. Nothing changes in `context/`, the skills, the agents, the templates, the Go code, `REQUIREMENTS.md` or `DECISIONS.md`. It uses 0 bytes of the context budget and needs no release.

**Found along the way in this repo, not part of this approval** (details in `.agents/scratch/research/okf/check-harness.md`). The consumer survey also turned up problems inside other projects. They were removed from this table on the operator's correction: this repo's trail tracks only this repo, and the survey was only there to establish whether any project uses OKF.

| # | Problem | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `owner:` means different things: our deploy guides say `main`, the `/init-project` deploy templates say `documentation`, and `testing/guide.md` says `verifier` | defer: decide whether `owner:` names the writer or the lane |
| 2 | `plans/2026-09-21-context-audit-prompt.md` has no frontmatter (`context/AGENTS.md:65`). `handoffs/2026-09-04-argolis-devbox-instructions.md` also lacks it, but handoffs are immutable. | **fixed** in this record's commit, as the operator asked on 2026-09-28; the handoff is left alone |

## Corrections from verification

The three lenses corrected the draft before this record was written.

- **Harness lens:**
  - B conflicts with the zero-scripts rule, which the draft had missed.
  - ADR-005's reason is "the operator asked". An "outside consumer" rule was never stated.
  - The two-project promotion is a retro trigger, not a gate against C.
  - T1's probe method must use the real home or a sandbox home, never `--home`, which is an `sh-agent` flag.
  - Handoffs are immutable, so found-along-the-way #2 shrank to one file, and #1 became a question.
  - The change entry must name all eight agents, and the verifier's step applies.
  - D touches at least 21 files, not 18.
  - D amends rebuild decision #11 rather than reversing it.
- **Facts lens:**
  - A third Google blog post exists (2026-08-27).
  - PR #6 changed the timestamp-valued keys only.
  - "Advisory" describes the trust tiers, not the fields.
  - The maintainer silence covers OKF threads only (about 361 human comments, not 405).
  - The OpenWiki citation was on the wrong lines.
  - `usage_window` was missing from the v0.2 list.
  - #312 is an issue against the frozen copy.
  - The Gemini CLI check was widened to all 641 releases.
- **Devil's-advocate lens:**
  - The survey was limited to this box (§6).
  - T1 is unlikely to fire by design, so T2 is the realistic trigger.
  - T2 as drafted could never fire for unifi-home-network, so F there is declined on its merits.
  - OpenWiki conflicts with R2.
  - D's `type:` duplicates the directory.
  - `stale_after` would not catch this harness's stale-text bugs.
  - B's trigger would fire on our own trail work.
- **Main agent:** the draft had called skills-ref's rejection of a top-level `type` a conflict. That is weak, because 8 of our skills already carry `argument-hint`, which skills-ref also rejects.

## Not verified

- **Absence findings:** no maintainer replies and no spec commits since 2026-08-21. These come from API reads on 2026-09-28 and could change any day.
- **Cursor:** checked only through its changelog for 2026-08-19 to 2026-09-23.
- **Knowledge Catalog:** whether its OKF ingestion is preview or GA is not stated anywhere read.
- **Third-party validators** (`okflint`, `okf-graph`, `W4G1/okf`, `jfomhover/okf-validator`): known only by name.
- **Size of a hand-written YAML-subset validator:** an estimate, not a measurement.
- **Case of the reserved filenames:** the spec does not say whether matching is case-sensitive. The `INDEX.md` collision comes from APFS being case-insensitive by default.
- **Other install places:** the projects on the work Mac and the other two Linux hosts were not surveyed. The operator answered for them instead (§6).
- **Measured benefit:** no eval compared an agent with and without a bundle. "No measurable benefit" rests on there being no reader and no use case.
- **Popularity counts:** star and install figures are as the GitHub and skills.sh APIs reported them, and some look inflated.

title: Plan — a signed release zip that `--from-zip` verifies (2026-09-28)
body:
# Plan — a signed release zip that `--from-zip` verifies   (2026-09-28)

## Why

The v1.8.0 gate's open medium: an unsigned zip becomes the agents' instructions, and `UNVERIFIED` only discloses that (`reviews/2026-09-28-preflight-v1.8.0.md` row 1). The handoff put the fix to the operator as Next Steps 1b: "/preflight could publish a `git archive` zip under the signed SHA256SUMS, and --from-zip would verify it … changes R9's Release procedure, so it needs your approval". The operator answered, 2026-09-28: "All approved. Cut new version if needed. All needs to be fixed."

## Scope

- **In:**
  - Each release publishes `styrman-harness-vX.Y.Z.zip`, a `git archive` of the tag with the top folder `styrman-harness-vX.Y.Z/`, listed in the signed `SHA256SUMS`.
  - `update --from-zip` verifies a zip when `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig` sit in the same directory as the zip. Otherwise it installs the zip marked `UNVERIFIED`, as today.
  - REQUIREMENTS R9 (the Release bullet and the zip place), ADR-039, the release procedure (`deploy/remote.md` § Releases), README, and `delivery.md`.
- **Out:**
  - a new flag;
  - verifying a `main` zip, which has no signature to check;
  - a manifest change.
- **Follow-ups, not built:** a zip handed over WITHOUT its sums still installs, marked UNVERIFIED, as R9 allows. This change narrows the v1.8.0 medium rather than closing it. Requiring an explicit `--unverified` would be a REQUIREMENTS R9 change and is put to the operator (ADR-039 Open; security reviews r1–r2).

## Surfaces touched

- `internal/harness/release.go`: `verifyRelease` (lines 219-294) splits into `verifySignedSums(keygen, sumsDir, signersDir) (sums []byte, tag string, err error)` and the per-asset check. `verifyRelease` keeps its behaviour and error texts; the existing `TestUpdateFromRelease*` tests pin them.
- `internal/harness/zip.go`: `UnpackZip` gains a check that runs after hashing and before anything is written.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (`updateFromZip`); tests in `internal/harness/zip_test.go` and `cmd/sh-agent/zip_test.go`.
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` R9; `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` ADR-039; `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases (the build, checksum and upload lines, and "all five" becoming six); `README.md` § Install from a zip; `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` § The model.

## Interfaces

- **`func UnpackZip(zipPath, parent string, check func(sum string) error) (dir, sum string, err error)`.** `check` may be nil. It runs once, right after the sha256 of the one read buffer is known, before `zip.NewReader`, and its error is returned unchanged, with nothing written.
- **`func VerifyZipSums(zipPath, sum string) (tag string, err error)`**, with `ErrZipUnsigned` beside it, in `internal/harness/release.go` next to `verifySignedSums` and `checksumFor`.
  - It looks for `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig` in `filepath.Dir(zipPath)`.
  - Neither present: it returns `"", ErrZipUnsigned`, a new sentinel.
  - Only one present: an error naming the missing one.
  - Both present:
    1. It writes the compiled-in signer to a temp directory, `os.MkdirTemp("", "sh-agent-verify-*")`, removed in a `defer`.
    2. `verifySignedSums` checks the signature and reads the `# styrman-harness vX.Y.Z` marker.
    3. `checksumFor(sums, filepath.Base(zipPath))` must equal `sum`.

    Any failure is an error, and the zip is refused.
  - It returns the marker's tag.
- **`updateFromZip`** passes a `check` closure that calls `VerifyZipSums` and handles `ErrZipUnsigned` ITSELF (D3):
  - `ErrZipUnsigned`: the closure records "unverified" and returns nil, so `UnpackZip` goes on to unpack, and the output says `UNVERIFIED` as today;
  - success: the closure records the tag and returns nil, and the first line reads `zip <file> (sha256 <hex>, VERIFIED against the signed SHA256SUMS of release vX.Y.Z)`, and the rest is unchanged;
  - any other error: the closure returns it, `UnpackZip` returns it unchanged with nothing written, and the command exits non-zero.
- **The release asset:** `git archive --format=zip --prefix=styrman-harness-vX.Y.Z/ -o <release dir>/styrman-harness-vX.Y.Z.zip vX.Y.Z`, added to the `sha256sum` line and the upload loop in `deploy/remote.md` § Releases.
- **REQUIREMENTS R9.**
  - The Release bullet: "…and publishes that tag's binaries with checksums signed by the same key." becomes "…and publishes that tag's binaries and a zip of its tree (`git archive`), with checksums signed by the same key."
  - The zip place sub-bullet gains: "When the release's `SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig` sit beside the zip, the zip is verified against them and refused if either check fails; a zip without them is installed marked `UNVERIFIED`."
  - The approval note records "All approved", 2026-09-28, and ADR-039.

## Failure modes

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| The `.sig` is missing, or only one of the two files is there | Refused, naming the missing file |
| The signature is bad, or a different key signed it | Refused: "SHA256SUMS signature does not verify (…)" |
| The zip is renamed (a browser's `(1)` suffix), so `SHA256SUMS` has no line for it | Refused: "no line names <file>", with a hint to use the release's file name |
| The checksum differs | Refused: "checksum mismatch" |
| `ssh-keygen` is missing | Refused: "ssh-keygen not found; cannot verify" |

In every case the verification runs before any write, so the home is untouched.

## Verification

- **Unit tests** (`internal/harness`, with `newRelease`'s key and a zip built by `writeZip`):
  - verified;
  - `.sig` missing;
  - a foreign key;
  - checksum mismatch;
  - renamed zip;
  - no sums (`ErrZipUnsigned`);
  - `check`'s error stops the unpack before any write.
- **The existing `TestUpdateFromRelease*`** tests stay green unchanged.
- **CLI:** `cmd/sh-agent`, isolated with an empty `PATH` except `ssh-keygen`, linked into a temp bin the way the release tests do. A verified zip prints `VERIFIED` and installs; a tampered checksum refuses and leaves the home empty.
- **E2E criterion:** a release-versioned build verifies a `git archive` zip of `HEAD`, signed with a scratch key in the release layout, and prints `VERIFIED`. Flipping one byte of the zip refuses it with nothing written. The real v1.9.0 zip is verified the same way after the release, with the real key (operator smoke).

## Phases

- [x] Cold-reader check — r1 needed revision (fixed as D3); r2 was implementation ready with zero BLOCKING questions, and its non-blocking points are D4–D7 (`reviews/2026-09-28-coldread-signed-zip-r{1,2}.md`)
### Phase 1 — Verification and CLI
- [x] Refactor `verifyRelease` → `verifySignedSums` — verify: `go test -race -run 'TestUpdateFromRelease|TestVerifier' ./internal/harness`, AI — expect: pass unchanged
- [x] `UnpackZip` check hook and `VerifyZipSums` — verify: `go test -race -run 'TestVerifyZipSums|TestUnpackZipCheck' ./internal/harness`, AI — expect: the unit cases above, each seen red first
- [x] `updateFromZip` wiring and output — verify: `go test -race -run 'TestUpdateFromZipVerified|TestUpdateFromZipTampered' ./cmd/sh-agent`, AI — expect: `VERIFIED` printed; a tampered zip refused with an empty home
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: full suite green — evidence: `testing/2026-09-28-verify-signed-zip.md` PASS, 2026-09-28
### Phase 2 — Requirements, ADR, release procedure, docs, E2E, one commit
- [x] R9 text, ADR-039, `deploy/remote.md` § Releases, README, `delivery.md` — docs: those files — verify: `/review --docs` — expect: no stale "unsigned only" statement
- [x] E2E criterion — verify: the scratch-key run, AI
- [x] `reviewer` and `security` over the diff; `verifier` — expect: findings fixed or rebutted
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: one commit, pushed — evidence: the signed-zip commit on `main` (`git log --grep 'signed release zip'`), 2026-09-28

## Risks

Assumptions: none open. `git archive` keeps the tracked symlink `.agents/skills`, which sits outside the five trees, so `checkZipTrees` never opens it (`internal/harness/zip.go`); a symlink inside the five trees is refused. Both are covered by the zip plan's tests.

## Decisions

- D1 — 2026-09-28 — The check hook sits inside `UnpackZip`, so the sum is taken from the same buffer that is unpacked (security review r1, low 3) and verification precedes every write — by: implementer.
- D2 — 2026-09-28 — The sums are found beside the zip, with no flag. The operator downloads three files from the Releases page into one folder — by: implementer.
- D3 — 2026-09-28 — `UnpackZip`'s hook stays one rule (any error refuses, nothing written). The unsigned case is not an error at that level: `updateFromZip`'s closure turns `ErrZipUnsigned` into "unverified" and returns nil. One read, one buffer — by: cold read round 1 (`reviews/2026-09-28-coldread-signed-zip-r1.md`, finding 1).
- D4 — 2026-09-28 — The closure reports back through variables it captures in `updateFromZip` (`verifiedTag string`) — by: implementer, cold read r2.
- D5 — 2026-09-28 — `verifySignedSums` returns the marker's tag, and `verifyRelease` compares it with the tag it expects, keeping its existing error text — by: implementer, cold read r2.
- D6 — 2026-09-28 — No separate check of the file name against the tag: `checksumFor(sums, base(zip))` already requires that exact name in the signed file, so a renamed or foreign zip is refused — by: implementer, cold read r1–r2.
- D7 — 2026-09-28 — `SHA256SUMS` and its `.sig` found beside a zip that does not match them refuse it, rather than degrading to UNVERIFIED. Signed sums in the zip's folder say it is meant to be a release zip, so a mismatch is the case to stop at. The error names the release the sums belong to, and never suggests removing them (security review r1, finding 2: that hint was a one-step bypass) — by: implementer, cold read r2; amended after security r1.
- Rejected:
  - a `--sums` flag, one more thing to type wrong;
  - refusing every unsigned zip, which would break the approved `main` zip path (R9).

title: Plan — time-sortable handoff and change-entry names (2026-09-28)
body:
# Plan — time-sortable handoff and change-entry names   (2026-09-28)

## Why

The Resume Protocol (`context/AGENTS.md:9`) reads the newest handoff and the three newest change entries. It finds "newest" by file name, and names are `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md`.

When one day has several files, they sort by slug, not by time:
- This repo has 8 days with several handoffs, up to 15 on 2026-09-17.
- On 2026-09-28, `2026-09-28-research-okf.md` sorts last but is the oldest of three (commits 13:25, 13:29, 13:35).
- In a fresh clone every mtime is the clone time, so `ls -t` cannot settle the tie either.

**Measured.** In the 2026-09-28 cold-start probe (`.agents/scratch/agy-probe/`, 20 runs), agy spent about 8 of 17 calls on resume run 1 working out which handoff was newest. It opened the wrong one first and recovered through `git log`.

**The operator's request, 2026-09-28:**
- "go ahead with the naming change";
- "add this to the context so we continiue doing this in all following projects";
- "if ./init-project is run on a active project it should warn for this";
- then "go all" on scope items 1–8.

The scope items, as put to the operator in chat and approved with "go all":
1. Only `handoffs/` and `changes/` get timed names.
2. Local time (`date +%F-%H%M`).
3. Existing files are never renamed.
4. One rule sentence: a date-only name is older than every timed name of its day.
5. `/init-project` update mode warns about date-only names and never renames.
6. The rule goes in `context/AGENTS.md` § Project layout, the handoff skill, `agents/changelog.md`, and every text that shows the old pattern.
7. Full verification: size test, scratch install, sandbox start on both CLIs, behavioural runs, reviewer, `/review --docs`, change entry, handoff.
8. No release in this plan; `/preflight v1.7.0` is asked about after Done.

## Scope

- **In:**
  - handoff and change-entry files are named `YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-<slug>.md`, from local time (`date +%F-%H%M`);
  - one rule sentence in the global context, including how names without a time order against timed ones;
  - the handoff skill's save step and artifact table;
  - the `changelog` agent's naming;
  - a warning from `/init-project` in update mode when date-only names exist.
- **Out:**
  - renaming existing files, which are immutable or append-only and linked from other records;
  - `plans/`, `reviews/`, `testing/` and `retros/` names, which are found by path or by the active plan;
  - a release: after Done the operator is asked about `/preflight v1.7.0` (scope item 8).
- **Follow-ups noted, not built:**
  - timed names for `reviews/` and `testing/`, if the probe data ever shows a same-day ambiguity cost there.

## Surfaces touched

- `context/AGENTS.md:65` (§ Project layout): one sentence. Rendered context today is 20,329 of 22,000 B; the sentence is about 190 B.
- `skills/handoff/SKILL.md`:
  - `:43`, the artifact table row `changes/YYYY-MM-DD-*.md`;
  - `:145`, `# Save as: $DOCS_ROOT/handoffs/$(date +%F)-<topic>.md`;
  - `:62`, the Step 3.1 date line stays `date +%F`, because it covers frontmatter and headings.
- `agents/changelog.md`:
  - `:3`, the description, which tells dispatchers to pass "today's date from date +%F" (the agent has no Bash, `:4`, so it cannot run `date` itself);
  - `:22-24`, the date rules;
  - `:30`, the lane tree comment;
  - `:39`, the entry heading;
  - `:89`, Records.
- `skills/init-project/SKILL.md`:
  - `:22`, the update-mode paragraph;
  - `:106`, the Step 7 summary.
- `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:86`: "Dispatch the `changelog` agent with today's date for the release entry".
- No Go code and no template file. The `handoffs/` and `changes/` template directories are empty.
- Describing text found by `git grep -nE '(changes|handoffs)/[^ \`]*(date|YYYY|<)'` over `context agents skills commands rules README.md AGENTS.md`: exactly the four hits above (`agents/changelog.md:39,89`, `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:43,145`). The re-run of that grep after Phase 1 must show only timed forms.

## Interfaces

- **File name:** `<docs-root>/handoffs/<stamp>-<slug>.md` and `<docs-root>/changes/<stamp>-<slug>.md`.
  - `<stamp>` is the output of `date +%F-%H%M` (local time), run by the writer when it writes the file.
  - The frontmatter `date:` stays `date +%F`.
- **Context sentence**, appended to the paragraph at `context/AGENTS.md:65` after "…append-only;":

  > `handoffs/` and `changes/` files are named `$(date +%F-%H%M)-<slug>.md`, so name order is time order; a name without the time is older than every timed name of its day.

- **Handoff skill:**
  - `:145` becomes `# Save as: $DOCS_ROOT/handoffs/$(date +%F-%H%M)-<topic>.md`;
  - the table row at `:43` becomes `.agents/docs/changes/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-*.md (older entries: YYYY-MM-DD-*.md)`.
- **Changelog agent** (no Bash; D3): the dispatcher passes the stamp, and the agent uses it.
  - `:3`: "passing today's date from date +%F in the prompt" becomes "passing the stamp from `date +%F-%H%M` in the prompt";
  - `:22`'s rule 1 becomes: "Use the stamp given in the dispatch prompt (`YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM`): its first ten characters are the date, and the whole stamp starts the file name. A dispatch that gives only a date gets a date-only file name, flagged in your reply.";
  - rule 2 ("If absent, run `date +%F` yourself", which a Bash-less agent cannot do) is deleted, and rule 3 (derive from a sibling artifact, else `DATE-UNKNOWN`) becomes rule 2 (D4);
  - `:30` becomes `# YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-short-description.md — …`;
  - `:39` becomes `changes/YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-<desc>.md`;
  - `:89` becomes `<docs-root>/changes/<stamp>-<slug>.md`.
- **Preflight** `:86`: "with today's date" becomes "with the stamp from `date +%F-%H%M`".
- **`/init-project` update mode**, a sentence added to `:22`:

  > In an update, count the files in `<docs-root>/handoffs/` and `<docs-root>/changes/` whose names start with a date not followed by a four-digit time. A directory that does not exist counts zero; for one that exists, run `ls <dir>`, and when that command fails, Step 7's summary says "<dir> could not be listed; date-only names not counted". Otherwise count its output with `grep -E '^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-' | grep -vcE '^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{4}-'`. When the total is above zero, Step 7's summary carries this warning, and nothing is renamed:
  >
  > "N handoff/change files have date-only names. New files are named YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-<slug>.md; the old names stay, and a date-only name counts as older than every timed name of its day."

  Step 7 at `:106` gains "and the date-only-names warning when Step 1 counted any".

## Failure modes

- **An agent writes a date-only name anyway.** Same-day ties come back for that file only. The context rule and both writers state the format, and the behavioural runs measure adherence (n of N).
- **Machines in different timezones.** Timed names from two machines interleave by local clock. The operator accepted local time (scope #2); a later D-row can switch to UTC.
- **A slug that begins with four digits** (for example `2026-09-28-2024-report`) reads as timed. Accepted: the warning is advisory and renames nothing.
- **The switch-over day** (today here, and the first day in any project): an old-style name sorts after that day's timed names in both byte order and the operator's locale. An agent that ignores the rule sentence picks the date-only file as newest, exactly today's behaviour and no worse.
- **`/init-project` cannot list a directory.** A missing directory holds no date-only names and counts zero. An existing one whose `ls` fails is named in the summary as not counted. Neither fails the run.

## Verification

- **Tiers:**
  - the Go suite, including `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock`;
  - a scratch-home install with no drift;
  - a sandbox start of each CLI (guide § 4);
  - behavioural runs (`AGENTS.md` § Testing) of the changed agent, the changed skills and the context rule, each reported n of N;
  - an e2e cold resume on agy.
- **E2E criteria:**
  1. In a fresh clone of this repo after the feature lands, a cold agy session asked for status and next step names the newest handoff (this feature's own timed handoff) as its source, even though today's three date-only handoffs sort after it by name. Run 2 times.
  2. `/init-project` run on a scratch clone of this repo reports the date-only-names warning with a count above zero and renames nothing (`git status` shows no rename). Run on a scratch project whose `changes/` holds only timed names, it reports no warning.

## Phases

- [x] Cold-reader check — design ready and implementation ready (`reviews/2026-09-28-coldread-time-sortable-names-r1.md`, `-r2.md`, `-r3.md`: r3 design ready, implementation ready)

### Phase 1 — Rule text

- [x] Context sentence at `context/AGENTS.md:65` — verify: `go test ./internal/harness -run TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock -v`, AI — expect: PASS, with the printed size ≤ 22,000 B.
- [x] Handoff skill `:43,:145` — verify: `grep -n 'date +%F-%H%M' skills/handoff/SKILL.md`, AI — expect: the save line.
- [x] Changelog agent `:3,:22-24,:30,:39,:89` — verify: `grep -nE 'HHMM|%H%M|<stamp>' agents/changelog.md`, AI — expect: five lines; `tools:` unchanged.
- [x] Preflight `:86` — verify: `grep -n 'date +%F-%H%M' skills/preflight/SKILL.md`, AI — expect: the dispatch line.
- [x] `/init-project` `:22`, `:106` — verify: `grep -n 'date-only' skills/init-project/SKILL.md`, AI — expect: both lines.
- [x] Describing-text sweep — verify: the Surfaces grep, AI — expect: no date-only pattern left for `handoffs/` or `changes/`. Positive control: the same grep at HEAD prints the four known hits.
- [x] Checkpoint — expect:
  - gofmt, vet and `go test -race ./...` green;
  - `sh-agent install --home .agents/scratch/tsn` then `status`: drift none;
  - `sh-agent list` parses.

  Evidence: `verifier` log `testing/2026-09-28-verify-time-sortable-names-phase-1.md` PASS: race suite ok, context 20,498 of 22,000 B, scratch install drift none, sweep clean with the positive control firing at HEAD; 2026-09-28.

### Phase 2 — Behavioural runs

- [x] **Changelog agent**, 3 runs, plus a 3-run must-fail control.
  - Setup: `claude -p --agents <json from agents/changelog.md>` in a scratch clone of a small repo, prompt on stdin. `--allowedTools` names exactly the agent's own tools (Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, plus Agent for the dispatch), with no Bash, the same as production.
  - The dispatch says what the new description tells a dispatcher to say, "Stamp: <output of `date +%F-%H%M`>", and names no file-name format.
  - Control: the same dispatch with the definition from HEAD (`git show HEAD:agents/changelog.md`).
  - Verify: `ls changes/` in each clone. AI.
  - Expect: a name matching `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{4}-` in n of 3 for the new definition, and the control's names recorded (a control that also writes timed names means the dispatch alone carries the behaviour, which is reported, not hidden). The tool-call order is read from the subagent transcript.
- [x] **Handoff skill**, 3 runs. The new `SKILL.md` is copied into the scratch clone at `.claude/skills/handoff-probe/SKILL.md`, and the copy's frontmatter line `name: handoff` is changed to `name: handoff-probe`. Nothing else changes, so the probe cannot collide with the installed `handoff`. It is invoked as `/handoff-probe`, from the real home. Verify: `ls <docs-root>/handoffs/`, AI. Expect: a timed name in n of 3.
- [x] **Context rule**, 3 runs: `claude -p --append-system-prompt "$(cat <rendered new context>)"`, asked to "write a handoff note for this session into the trail" in a scratch clone, naming no format. Expect: a timed name in n of 3.
- [x] **Sandbox start of each CLI** (guide § 4).
  - Setup: a sandbox home under `.agents/scratch/`, `sh-agent install --home` into it, credential files copied with `chmod 600` and deleted by name after.
  - Each CLI is asked "how are handoff files named, and which is newest when a date-only and a timed name share a day?"
  - Expect: the timed form and "the timed one" on both CLIs; `cli-*.log` has no parse-error line.
- [x] **E2E 2 (`/init-project` warning).** Sandbox home as above, on a scratch clone of this repo (must fire) and on a scratch project with only timed names (must stay silent). Expect: the warning with a count, then none; `git status` shows no rename.
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: every run above at or above 2 of 3 (the init-project and sandbox runs: 1 of 1 each); failures are recorded, not hidden. Evidence: `testing/2026-09-28-verify-time-sortable-names-phase-2.md`: changelog, handoff and context each 3 of 3 with every control 0 of 3; sandbox 1 of 1 on both CLIs; E2E 2 fired (160) and stayed silent; 2026-09-28.

### Phase 3 — Done

- [x] `reviewer` (diff only), then `/review --docs` over the range — expect: findings fixed or rebutted in the report's `## Outcome`. — done: code APPROVE WITH NITS (1 finding), docs REQUEST CHANGES (2 findings); all fixed (D5), Outcome sections written; `testing/2026-09-28-verify-time-sortable-names-fixes.md` PASS.
