- [x] Commit and push the feature, with this feature's change entry and handoff written under timed names. — `9a17e0a`: `changes/2026-09-28-1450-…`, `handoffs/2026-09-28-1450-…`.
- [x] **E2E 1 (agy cold resume)**, 2 runs, on a fresh clone of the pushed HEAD, from the Phase 2 sandbox home with the new harness installed (D2). Question: "State the status and the single next step." Verify: the answer's cited handoff, AI. Expect: this feature's timed handoff named as the source in n of 2; an honest failure otherwise. — done: 2 of 2 on this repo, plus 2 of 2 on a clean demo; the old-context control was also 2 of 2 (via `git log`, 9 calls against 7), so the control did not fail (`testing/2026-09-28-verify-time-sortable-names-e2e1.md`, BUG-091 for the first, invalid attempt).
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: tree clean and pushed; handoff written. Evidence: the closing commit's `git status` and `git log @{u}..HEAD` both empty, 2026-09-28.

## Risks

Assumptions:
- Claude Code accepts a `--agents` JSON built from `agents/changelog.md`. Checked by the first Phase 2 run.
- Copied credentials authenticate a sandbox-home CLI, as guide § 4 says. Checked by the sandbox task's first command.

## Decisions

- D1 — 2026-09-28 — Timed names for `handoffs/` and `changes/` only; local time; no renames; `/init-project` warns and never renames; no release in this plan — by: the operator, "go all" on scope items 1–8.
- D2 — 2026-09-28 — E2E 1 can only see the new context sentence once the context is installed where agy reads it. The real home runs v1.6.0 and R6 forbids installing into it from development. So E2E 1 runs from the Phase 2 sandbox home, with the new harness installed, on a fresh clone of the pushed HEAD, not from the real home — by: implementer.
- D3 — 2026-09-28 — The changelog agent keeps its tools; its dispatcher passes the stamp from `date +%F-%H%M` (the description, preflight's dispatch line), and the agent names the file from it. Adding Bash to a records agent widens what it can do in order to read a clock — by: cold read round 1 (`reviews/2026-09-28-coldread-time-sortable-names-r1.md`, finding 1).
- D4 — 2026-09-28 — The changelog agent's rule 2 ("run `date +%F` yourself") is deleted in the same edit, because the agent has no Bash; rule 3 takes its place — by: cold read round 3 (`reviews/2026-09-28-coldread-time-sortable-names-r3.md`); a bug record follows at Done.
- D5 — 2026-09-28 — Supersedes the Surfaces note that `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:62` stays as it was: it now also names `date +%F-%H%M` for the file name. `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:40`'s changelog dispatch passes the stamp like `:86` — by: docs-lens review (`reviews/2026-09-28-review-time-sortable-names-docs.md`, findings 1 and 2).
- Open: whether E2E 1 should also be repeated on the real home after the operator next runs `sh-agent update` — default: listed in the handoff's Next Steps as an operator smoke check, not run here.
- Rejected:
  - an `INDEX.md` per trail folder: measured at 240 locate calls against 472 writes (`.agents/scratch/trail-search/`, 2026-09-28);
  - `_` as the separator so that timed names sort after date-only ones: the locale collation `ls` uses ignores punctuation, so it would not hold;
  - renaming today's date-only files: they are immutable records, and other records link them by name;
  - adding Bash to the changelog agent: see D3.

title: Plan — `sh-agent update --from-zip <file>` (2026-09-28)
body:
# Plan — `sh-agent update --from-zip <file>`   (2026-09-28)

## Why

A machine that can neither hold the operator's SSH key nor run `gh`, such as a corporate workstation, cannot reach the harness today. A checkout needs git over SSH, and `sh-agent update` on a release binary downloads through `gh` (R8, R9). The operator can download the repository zip by hand in a browser.

The operator's words, 2026-09-28:
- "add the --from-zip option so i can run manually";
- then "approve as written, go all but number 6".

That approval covers the REQUIREMENTS text quoted under Interfaces, scope items 1–5 and 7, and, for item 7, the recommended matrix option 1. Item 6 is out: the pasted proposal's report stripping, `trigger: always_on` frontmatter, Cloudtop overlay and skill filtering.

Recon: `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-28-recon-from-zip.md`.

## Scope

- **In:**
  - `sh-agent update --from-zip <file>` from any binary, release or development build (D7 says what other commands do afterwards). It unpacks the zip into a temporary directory under `~/.config/sh-agent/`, refuses any entry that would leave it, installs that tree with the running binary (no rebuild, no binary replacement), and deletes the directory.
  - The manifest marks the install as coming from a zip, and `status`, `knownCheckout` and `ResolveSource` handle that marker.
  - The REQUIREMENTS R8/R9 text as approved; ADR-038; the README map and the delivery docs; `AGENTS.md` rule 1.
  - Then item 7: the matrix lists, and the v1.8.0 release.
- **Out:**
  - fetching anything;
  - verifying the zip's signature, since a zip is unsigned and trust rests on the operator's own download;
  - replacing the binary from a zip;
  - item 6 of the pasted proposal;
  - a manifest schema change.
- **Follow-ups noted, not built:**
  - **A signed zip:** `/preflight` would publish a `git archive` zip under the release's signed `SHA256SUMS`, and `--from-zip` would verify it through the existing `ssh-keygen` path, refusing or clearly flagging an unverified zip. It changes R9's Release procedure, so it needs the operator's approval. Until then the command prints `UNVERIFIED` (security reviews r1 and r2, medium, open by decision).
  - `skills/find-skills/SKILL.md:97` names `styrman-harness` in a vendored skill: an old in-place edit, found during the item-4/5 sweep.

## Surfaces touched

- `internal/harness/zip.go` (new): `UnpackZip`. `internal/harness/zip_test.go` (new).
- `internal/harness/source.go`:
  - `ZipPrefix`;
  - a `Source.Origin` field the manifest records instead of `Dir`, when set.
- `internal/harness/apply.go:117-123`: the manifest's `Repo`/`Commit` for a zip source.
- `internal/harness/repo.go:75`: the `ResolveSource` candidate walk skips a `ZipPrefix` manifest value, as it skips `EmbeddedPrefix`.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`:
  - the flag (`:84-90`);
  - the `reorder` value table (`:617`);
  - the usage string;
  - the `update` case (`:198-230`), with a `--from-zip` branch placed before `ResolveSource` (`:123`);
  - `status` (`:346-472`, the `from` line `:382-385` and the drift block `:444-471`);
  - `knownCheckout` (`:573`).
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go`: the CLI tests.
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` R8 and R9 (approved text); `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` ADR-038.
- `README.md`: § How it works (the map) and the install and update sections. `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` § How a machine gets the harness and § The model. `.agents/docs/deploy/{local,remote}.md` where they state the number of ways. `AGENTS.md` rule 1 ("Two ways in").
- `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md` (item 7).

## Interfaces

- **The command.** `sh-agent update --from-zip <file> [--home <dir>] [--vendor <v>] [--dry-run]`. `--from-zip` takes a value and joins `reorder`'s value table.
  - `--from-zip` with `--check` or with `--repo` is refused before anything is read: "--from-zip installs the named zip; --check/--repo do not apply to it".
  - `$SH_AGENT_REPO` is ignored on this path. The operator named the file, so D15 holds.
- **Order of work.**
  1. `sha256` of the file.
  2. `cfg, err := harness.ConfigDir(home)` (it returns an error too), then `harness.UnpackZip(file, cfg)`, which returns the tree's directory.
  3. `IsRepo(dir)`; failing it is an error naming the zip.
  4. `src := harness.Source{FS: os.DirFS(dir), Dir: dir, Origin: harness.ZipPrefix + "sha256:" + hex}`.
  5. `installFiles(src, home, vendor, dryRun, out)`, the same helper `install` uses: the running binary via `selfExecutable`, never `Reinstall`.
  6. `os.RemoveAll` of the unpack directory in a `defer`, on every path, errors and dry run included.
- **Output.**
  - First line: `zip <file> (sha256 <hex>): installing its harness with the running binary <version>; the binary itself is not replaced`, or the same with a `[dry-run]` prefix.
- **`harness.UnpackZip(zipPath, parent string) (dir string, err error)`**
  - It creates `os.MkdirTemp(parent, "zip-*")`.
  - It reads the archive with `archive/zip`.
  - Checks run at two scopes (D6).
    - **Archive-wide, on every entry:** the name must be relative, contain no `..` element and no backslash, and be `filepath.IsLocal` after cleaning. The archive may hold at most 5,000 entries. A breach refuses the whole zip, with nothing installed and the temp directory removed.
    - **Only on entries under the five extracted trees:** a symlink or any non-regular, non-directory mode refuses the whole zip. So does more than 16 MiB uncompressed for one file, or more than 128 MiB in total across the extracted files, counted from bytes actually written through an `io.LimitReader`, never from the header.
    - An entry outside the five trees is never opened and never written, whatever its mode. That includes this repository's own tracked symlink `.agents/skills`, which GitHub's zip keeps as a symlink entry.
  - **Layout.**
    - When every entry sits under one top-level folder and that folder holds `context/AGENTS.md`, the folder is stripped. That is GitHub's "Download ZIP" (`styrman-harness-main/…`) and its API zipball (`<owner>-<repo>-<sha>/…`).
    - Otherwise, when `context/AGENTS.md` is at the root, the root is used.
    - Otherwise the error is "not a harness zip: no context/AGENTS.md at its root or under one top folder".
  - **Extracted:** only entries under `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/` and `rules/`, the five trees the binary embeds. Every other entry is still name-checked, but never written.
  - File mode `0o644`, directories `0o755`.
- **`State.Repo` for a zip install:** `zip:sha256:<hex>`. `State.Commit` is `""`. `ZipPrefix = "zip:"`.
  - In `Install` (`apply.go:117-123`, which today branches on `src.Dir != ""` only), `src.Origin != ""` is checked FIRST and wins: `repo, commit = src.Origin, ""`. Then comes the existing `Dir` branch (path plus commit), and then the embedded branch. A zip source sets both `Dir` (the temp directory) and `Origin`; the temp path must never reach the manifest.
  - `ResolveSource` (`repo.go:75`) skips it as a candidate.
  - When `ResolveSource` finds no tree and the manifest's `Repo` has `ZipPrefix`, the not-found error (`repo.go:87`) gains, first: "this home was installed from a zip (sha256 <first 12 hex>); a development build needs a checkout or --repo — or run `sh-agent update --from-zip <file>` again". The rest of the message is unchanged (D7).
  - `knownCheckout` (`main.go:573`) treats it like `EmbeddedPrefix`: "this home was installed from a zip (sha256 <hex>), not from a checkout; pass --repo <dir> to build and install from it".
- **`status` for a manifest whose `Repo` has `ZipPrefix`.** `status` moves `harness.LoadState(home)` (today at `main.go:370`) to the top of the function, before the `source`/`repo` line (`:349-368`), so that line can append the zip note. The `installed nothing` early return keeps its place and message after the source line.
  - `installed  <time> from zip sha256:<first 12 hex> (…)`.
  - The drift block is replaced by a presence check over the manifest's files: `drift      not compared — installed from a zip that is not kept; <n> of <m> manifest files present`, then `  missing  ~/<rel>` for each absent one. The exit status is 1 when any is missing, 0 otherwise.
  - The `source` line for a release binary adds: `; this home was installed from a zip — run update --from-zip <file> again to change it`.
- **REQUIREMENTS, exactly as approved.**
  - R8's first sentence is replaced by: "The harness reaches a machine one of three ways: a checkout the operator owns; a release's `sh-agent` binary with the harness built in; or a zip of the repository that the operator downloads with their own credential and passes to `sh-agent update --from-zip <file>`. Each is kept current with `sh-agent update`: the checkout and the binary as today, and a zip place by the operator repeating the download and `--from-zip`."
  - R9's Install/Update procedure gains, as an indented sub-bullet under **Update** (D9), not as a fifth top-level procedure: "**Zip place:** the operator downloads the repository zip by hand and runs `sh-agent update --from-zip <file>`. It unpacks the zip into a temporary directory, refuses any entry that would leave it, installs that tree with the running binary, and deletes the directory. Nothing is fetched, no repository is created, and the binary itself is not replaced."
  - Both keep their approval notes: "(Approved by the operator 2026-09-28, on the exact text above: "approve as written"; ADR-038.)".
- **ADR-038.** A third way in, the zip place.
  - It supersedes ADR-034 for this one path only: a release binary installs a tree on disk solely when the operator names a zip with `--from-zip`, never a recorded or discovered path.
  - It amends the "two ways, no third" claim in `delivery.md`.

## Failure modes

- **Not a zip, or corrupt.** Error: "<file>: not a readable zip: <err>". Nothing is installed, the temp directory is removed, and the exit status is non-zero.
- **An unsafe entry** (slip, symlink, over a limit). The error names the entry and the rule it broke. Nothing is installed and the temp directory is removed.
- **Not a harness zip.** The error says so, and names the expected layout.
- **The zip carries a harness that needs a newer binary.** The install proceeds with the running binary; the first output line says the binary is not replaced. When the zip's `skills/` or `agents/` use something this binary cannot map (for example an unmapped tool in `derive.go`), the existing plan error stops the install before any write. That is the existing guard, unchanged.
- **The temp directory cannot be created** (unwritable `~/.config/sh-agent`). Error, and nothing installed.
- **`status` after a zip install** reports presence, not content. Content drift against the zip cannot be computed; the output says so rather than pretending.
- **A zip-installed home, then a development build with no checkout nearby and no `--repo`.** `status`, `diff`, `list`, `render` and `install` fail as they do today for a development build with no tree, and the error names the zip install (D7). A release binary never hits this: its source is its embedded files.
- **Dry run.** It unpacks and plans, prints what would change, and removes the temp directory. It writes no installed file, no manifest and no binary.

## Verification

- **Tiers:**
  - unit (`zip_test.go`: zip fixtures built in the test with `archive/zip`'s writer);
  - CLI (`main_test.go`);
  - an e2e with a real GitHub zip, using a release-versioned build;
  - security review (input parsing, a new way in);
  - `/review --docs`;
  - `TestHarnessMap`, which pins verbs; `--from-zip` is a flag, but the map gains a line.
- **E2E criteria:**
  1. **Golden path.** A binary built with a canonical release version runs `update --from-zip <GitHub zipball of main> --home <scratch>`. It installs, `status --home <scratch>` names the zip and reports every manifest file present, and the installed `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` equals the zip's rendered context.
  2. **Edge case.** A zip with an entry `x/../../escape` is refused, nothing is written under `<scratch>`, and no `zip-*` directory is left under `<scratch>/.config/sh-agent/`.
  3. **Dry run.** It leaves `<scratch>` byte-identical to before (manifest absent or unchanged), with no `zip-*` directory left.

## Phases

- [x] Cold-reader check — rounds 1–3 (`reviews/2026-09-28-coldread-update-from-zip-r{1,2,3}.md`); round 3 ended at the cap with one narrow residue (R9's structure), put to the operator, whose answer was "Go with your recommendations" (2026-09-28): D9

### Phase 1 — Zip source (internal/harness)

- [x] `UnpackZip` with the layout rules, limits and refusals — verify: `go test -race -run 'TestUnpackZip' ./internal/harness`, AI — expect: tests for GitHub top-folder strip, root layout, `..` slip, absolute name, backslash name, symlink entry INSIDE `skills/` (refused), symlink entry OUTSIDE the five trees such as `.agents/skills` (accepted, not written), over-count, over-size (written bytes), not-a-harness, and "entries outside the five trees not written" all pass. Each is written first and seen failing against a zero-value `UnpackZip`.
- [x] `ZipPrefix`, `Source.Origin`, the manifest record (`apply.go`), and the `ResolveSource` skip — verify: `go test -race ./internal/harness`, AI — expect: a test that an `Origin` source records `zip:sha256:…` with an empty commit, and that `ResolveSource` never returns a `zip:` manifest value as a candidate.
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: `go test -race ./...` green, gofmt and vet clean — evidence: `verifier` log `testing/2026-09-28-verify-update-from-zip-phase-1.md` PASS (139/266 pass; the must-fail mutation compiled and failed `one_file_too_large`; coverage 80–100% on the new functions, with uncovered error branches named), 2026-09-28. **No commit at this checkpoint:** the path change lands in ONE commit with its docs and map (`AGENTS.md` rule 3; D2).

### Phase 2 — CLI, status, knownCheckout

- [x] `--from-zip` flag, the `reorder` table and usage; the `update` branch before `ResolveSource`; the `--check`/`--repo` refusals; dry run — verify: `go test -race -run 'TestUpdateFromZip' ./cmd/sh-agent`, AI — expect: golden path into a scratch home; refusals; dry run writes nothing and leaves no `zip-*` directory (asserted absent, not only "normal mode present"); a release-versioned run installs from the zip, not the embedded files. — docs: `README.md` § update
- [x] `status` zip lines and presence check; `knownCheckout` zip branch — verify: `go test -race -run 'TestStatusAfterZip|TestKnownCheckoutZip' ./cmd/sh-agent`, AI — expect: the `from zip` line, "not compared" with the present count, missing files listed with exit 1, and the `knownCheckout` refusal text.
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: the full suite green — evidence: `verifier` log `testing/2026-09-28-verify-update-from-zip-phase-2.md` PASS (mutations (a) dry-run and (b) status both compiled and failed their named tests; restored identical), 2026-09-28. No commit (D2).

### Phase 3 — Requirements, ADR, docs, map, e2e, one commit

- [x] `REQUIREMENTS.md` R8/R9 exactly as approved; ADR-038 — verify: `git diff REQUIREMENTS.md`, AI — expect: only the two approved passages and their approval notes.
- [x] `AGENTS.md` rule 1 ("Two ways in" → three); `documentation` updates `README.md` (map and install/update), `delivery.md` § The model and § How a machine gets the harness, and `deploy/{local,remote}.md` pointers — verify: `/review --docs` over the phase diff, and `go test -run TestHarnessMap ./...`, both — expect: no restatement of the old count left. `git grep -niP '\btwo ways\b|\bno third\b|only way the harness|\bways in\b|one of the ways'` (`\b` because a bare `ways in` matches "always include") over the living docs (`README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `.agents/docs/{specs,deploy}/`, `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md`) prints only lines that state the new three-way model, plus `skills/golang/references/golang-samber.md:431` ("two ways to compose operations", unrelated). Positive control: the same grep at the pre-feature HEAD prints `README.md:182` and `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:61` among its hits. The map shows the zip line. — docs: `README.md`, `delivery.md`
- [x] E2E 1–3 — verify: a release-versioned build (`-ldflags "-X main.version=v0.0.1"`) in `.agents/scratch/`; the zip from `gh api repos/kesokaj/styrman-harness/zipball/main`; hand-built slip and dry-run cases; AI — expect: the three criteria above. Proven before trusting: the zip has one top folder, and the slip fixture holds the `..` entry (`unzip -l`).
- [x] `security` over the feature diff; `reviewer` over the diff — expect: findings fixed or rebutted in `## Outcome`.
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: ONE commit carrying the code, tests, REQUIREMENTS, ADR-038, docs and map; pushed — evidence: `verifier` log `testing/2026-09-28-verify-update-from-zip-phase-3.md` PASS; the feature commit follows this tick; 2026-09-28.

### Phase 4 — Matrix (item 7) and release

- [x] `testing/skill-matrix.md`: restore the lists the scenarios need (`bash`, `python3`, `curl` for Claude; the matching named agy commands), keep `edit_file(*)` and `list_dir(*)` out, and state that the allowlist lets scenarios run and is not a security boundary, because the sandbox runs as the operator's OS user; the protection is the throwaway home, with the copied token deleted by name after each batch — verify: read against the v1.8.0 gate code review's findings 1–3 (`reviews/2026-09-28-review-v1.7.0-381e86d-code.md`), AI — expect: each finding closed or rebutted.
- [x] `/preflight v1.8.0` over `v1.7.0..HEAD` — expect: VERDICT SHIP; tag, binaries, notes.
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: the release published; handoff written — evidence: the gate report path and release URL, <date>.

## Risks

Assumptions:
- GitHub's API zipball and the web "Download ZIP" both have exactly one top folder. Checked by `unzip -l` on the fetched zipball, the first task of the Phase 3 e2e.
- `archive/zip` exposes a symlink entry through `FileInfo().Mode()&fs.ModeSymlink`. Checked by the symlink unit test's fixture, whose `Mode()` is asserted before the refusal is tested.

## Decisions

- D1 — 2026-09-28 — Unpack under `ConfigDir(home)` (`~/.config/sh-agent/zip-*`), never `/tmp`. This follows the code's convention (`apply.go` `Diff`, `release.go` downloads), and a scratch `--home` keeps tests inside the scratch tree — by: implementer.
- D2 — 2026-09-28 — Phases 1–3 commit once, at the end of Phase 3. `AGENTS.md` rule 3 puts a path change in ONE commit with the code, docs and map, so the feature skill's per-phase commit is waived for these phases. The plan file and verify logs hold the state between them — by: implementer, per `AGENTS.md` rule 3.
- D3 — 2026-09-28 — No manifest schema change. The marker is a `State.Repo` value (`zip:sha256:<hex>`, the `EmbeddedPrefix` precedent), and `status` reports presence instead of content for zip installs. A new manifest field is what the repo's versioning rule calls MAJOR — by: implementer.
- D4 — 2026-09-28 — Extract only the five embedded trees. Name-check every entry, write only those. The zip also carries `.agents/`, `cmd/` and `internal/`, which the install never reads — by: implementer.
- D6 — 2026-09-28 — The symlink, mode and size checks apply only to entries under the five extracted trees; name safety and the entry count apply archive-wide. Otherwise the repo's own GitHub zip, whose `.agents/skills` is a tracked symlink, would be refused — by: cold read round 1 (`reviews/2026-09-28-coldread-update-from-zip-r1.md`, finding 1).
- D7 — 2026-09-28 — `--from-zip` works from any binary. Afterwards, a development build with no checkout and no `--repo` has no source for the other commands; they fail with the existing not-found error, which then names the zip install first. It is not given a way to read the manifest as a source, because nothing of the zip is kept. The zip place's intended binary is a release binary (R8), whose source is its embedded files — by: cold read round 2 (`reviews/2026-09-28-coldread-update-from-zip-r2.md`, finding 1).
- D8 — 2026-09-28 — The existing plain-copy path (an unpacked tree installed by a binary built from it; `update` refuses it) stays exactly as it is, the fallback `delivery.md` already describes. `--from-zip` is the zip place's way in and forward. The docs name both and say which is which: a zip place keeps no tree, while a plain copy is a tree someone unpacked and keeps — by: cold read rounds 1–2, finding 3.
- D9 — 2026-09-28 — The zip text sits inside R9's existing Update procedure, as a nested sub-bullet with the exact wording approved. It is a new kind of place, not a new procedure, so R9's "Four procedures" title and ADR-031 stay true. ADR-038 says so — by: the operator, "Go with your recommendations", on cold read round 3's residue (`reviews/2026-09-28-coldread-update-from-zip-r3.md`).
- D10 — 2026-09-28 — A dry run unpacks under `~/.config/sh-agent/` only when that directory already exists, and otherwise under the system temp directory. `ConfigDir` creates the directory, which a dry run must not do — by: implementer, Phase 1.
- D11 — 2026-09-28 — Supersedes the Interfaces lines on the output, `UnpackZip`'s signature, and "`--from-zip` with `--check` or `--repo` is refused", as well as D10's place of directory creation. It follows the review round (`reviews/2026-09-28-review-update-from-zip-{code,docs}.md`, `reviews/2026-09-28-security-update-from-zip.md`):
  - `UnpackZip(zipPath, parent) (dir, sum string, err error)` reads the file once (at most 256 MiB), hashes and parses that one buffer, and validates everything before writing: names (at most 1,024 bytes, fewer than 32 levels), count, kinds, duplicates, and sizes counted by decompressing. Only then does it create the parent chain, and on any error it removes everything it created.
  - `--from-zip` is detected with `fs.Visit` and refused before ANY command runs, when used with a command other than `update`, with an empty value, or with `--check`/`--repo`.
  - The first output line says `UNVERIFIED`, and that the running binary is installed but nothing in the zip replaces it.
  - `diff` does not compare a zip install.
  - A real run sweeps `zip-*` directories older than an hour.
  - `update --dry-run`, on the checkout and release paths, is its `--check`: it reports and changes nothing.

  — by: code review REQUEST CHANGES findings 1–3 and lows; security lows 2 and 3; docs lens 1–3.
- D12 — 2026-09-28 — The approved R9 sentence "the binary itself is not replaced" is imprecise: the running binary is installed as in every install; what holds is that nothing in the zip replaces it. REQUIREMENTS is not edited without the operator's approval, so the docs and output say the precise thing, and the sentence is put to the operator in the release report — by: implementer, from security review low 3.
- D13 — 2026-09-28 — Supersedes D11's "creates the parent chain … removes everything it created" inside `UnpackZip`, following round 2 (`reviews/2026-09-28-review-update-from-zip-code-r2.md`, `reviews/2026-09-28-security-update-from-zip-r2.md`):
  - `UnpackZip` no longer creates any directory beyond its own `zip-*`. `updateFromZip` creates `~/.config/sh-agent` with `MkdirAllTracked` and removes what it created on ANY failure, the install's own refusals included (BUG-093, third layer).
  - The sweep matches `zip-` names from `os.ReadDir` and never globs; a glob built from `--home 'h[1]'` reached another home.
  - The archive cap is 64 MiB.
  - Every zip CLI test runs with an empty `PATH` and a scratch working directory (BUG-094).

  — by: code review r2 findings 1–3; security r2 lows 2–3.
- D5 — 2026-09-28 — Item 7 takes matrix option 1 (the recommendation), read from "go all but number 6" on a row whose recommendation named the matrix choice — by: implementer, stated to the operator in chat.
- Rejected:
  - reading the zip in place as an `fs.FS` with no unpack: the approved REQUIREMENTS text says it unpacks into a temporary directory;
  - routing through `update()`/`Reinstall`: that rebuilds, and the scope forbids it;
  - per-file hashes in the manifest: a schema change (D3).

title: Recon — audit-search-consumers (2026-09-29)
body:
# Recon — audit-search-consumers (2026-09-29)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Question
Audit every consumer in styrman-harness for whether the planned local SQLite index (per-project FTS5 + trail metadata graph; global feedback/retro index) would help, and how much: context/AGENTS.md procedures, non-vendored skills, agents/*.md, commands/, rules/, sh-agent verbs, testing/skill-matrix.md.

## Summary
The highest-value consumers are all "restatement/paraphrase grep" and "structured trail query" steps: `review-standards` skill's restatement check, `dream`'s graduation grep, `dreamer`'s rule-evidence grep, the global hard rule on reversed claims, and the resume/handoff awk-parsing of unticked plan boxes and INDEX.md rows — these replace fragile exact-grep or hand-rolled parsing with ranked/paraphrase-tolerant search or a direct structured answer. The clearest **non-consumers** are the verifier's own diff-scoped greps (suppressions, coverage), preflight's secret scan, and any `/review --docs` grep run "at the scope's head" of a historical range — all freshness-critical or need an exact literal match on a specific git revision the index (built from tracked files, presumably at HEAD) would not represent. `commands/` and `rules/` are both empty — nothing to audit there. Instruction placement: `context/AGENTS.md` has ~48 bytes of headroom under its pinned 22,000-byte budget, so a durable pointer to the index belongs in individual skill/agent files, not the global context; I directly observed (as this dispatch's own subagent) that Claude Code injects the full `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`→`AGENTS.md` chain into a subagent's context, so a line already in `context/AGENTS.md` would reach Claude Code subagents for free — but with only ~48 bytes free that channel is effectively unusable, and Antigravity's equivalent inheritance for subagents is not stated anywhere in this repo (open question).

## Relevant files
- `context/AGENTS.md` — global procedures; Resume line 9 (unticked plan boxes, INDEX.md), Hard rules line 55 (restatement grep), line 51 (git-diff-based checks)
- `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md:48` — restatement-of-a-rule grep across context/, skills/, agents/, README.md
- `skills/review/SKILL.md:51` — `--docs` lens: `git grep` old wording "as the scope's head" across living docs
- `skills/dream/SKILL.md:32,41,48` — reads MEMORY.md + trail + context/skills/agents; graduation check is "one grep over key words, each hit read in full"
- `skills/retro/SKILL.md:36,43,68-69` — reads feedback.jsonl/retros.jsonl, exact-match controlled-vocabulary greps
- `skills/bug/SKILL.md:33` — reads `<docs-root>/bugs/INDEX.md` first
- `skills/feature/SKILL.md:19` — checks REQUIREMENTS.md/ROADMAP.md/bugs/INDEX.md
- `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:154` — Resume Protocol incl. an `awk` one-liner over every `plans/*.md` to find unticked boxes outside fenced blocks
- `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:24` — counts date-only handoff/change filenames via `ls`+`grep` (filename pattern, not content)
- `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:40` — secret scan on staged diff (must stay exact/live)
- `agents/bugs.md` — "if three records share a prevention rule, say so" (cross-record similarity, currently manual)
- `agents/dreamer.md:29,36` — reads every INDEX.md row + opens records; `git grep` key words over context/AGENTS.md/rules/skills before every rule row (restatement check, same shape as review-standards)
- `agents/reviewer.md`, `agents/verifier.md`, `agents/explorer.md`, `agents/changelog.md`, `agents/documentation.md`, `agents/security.md` — read in full; verifier is the clearest non-consumer (diff-scoped, freshness-critical)
- `internal/harness/report.go` — collects/pushes `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl`, `proposals/`; a write path, not a search consumer itself, but is the source the global index would ingest
- `internal/harness/derive.go` — no mention of context injection for Antigravity subagents; comment "markdown agents inherit the global skills anyway" is the only hint
- `REQUIREMENTS.md:49-51` — "Known limits": deployed context pinned under 22,000 bytes; `rules/` files share Antigravity's 24,000-byte block with it
- `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md` — behavioural-test procedure; no search-index consumer, but any new skill/agent behavior needs a matrix row + sandbox run before it can be claimed to work (project convention, not this audit's finding but relevant to landing the feature)
- `commands/`, `rules/` — both empty (`ls` returned nothing) — no consumers here

## Flows
- Restatement-check pattern (repeated 3×, independently, in `review-standards`, `dream`, `dreamer`): grep key words/subject nouns across a fixed small set of living files (`context/`, `skills/*/SKILL.md`, `agents/`, `README.md`, or the project's own `AGENTS.md`/rules) → read each hit in full → judge. This is exactly the "restatements of a claim" query the dispatch names.
- Resume/handoff pattern: read several named files in a fixed order (`AGENTS.md`→`TODO.md`→newest handoff→`ROADMAP.md`→active plan's unticked boxes→3 newest changes→`bugs/INDEX.md`) then run a hand-written `awk` script over `plans/*.md` to find unticked boxes ROADMAP does not already name. This `awk` is the kind of thing "unticked plan boxes" as a structured query directly replaces.
- Bug/ADR trail pattern (`dreamer`, `bug`, `feature`): read `INDEX.md` (all rows, newest last) then open matching records individually. A "every record that names file X" or "open bugs" graph query collapses the read-INDEX-then-open-records loop into one structured answer, though the records still need opening for their prose (root cause, prevention text).
- Verifier/preflight pattern: grep the **diff** (not the repo) for suppressions, secrets, added `.skip(`/`.only(`. This is scoped to uncommitted/staged changes on the live tree — an index over tracked files at some snapshot cannot see this and must never be substituted.

## Conventions
- Every subagent writes its artifact early and updates it (shared template across `explorer`, `verifier`, `reviewer`, `bugs`, `dreamer`) — any index-query instruction added to an agent file should sit in that agent's own numbered procedure, not as a late aside, to survive a cut-off run.
- Skills state "Docs root: `.agents/docs/` if it exists, else `docs/`" repeatedly — any index path/query wrapper needs to resolve the same way (index lives under `.agents/scratch/search.db`, independent of docs-root, but its queries target `<docs-root>`).
- The project explicitly documents a size budget as a *test-pinned* constraint (`REQUIREMENTS.md` "Known limits", `internal/harness/size_test.go`'s `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock`) — any edit to `context/AGENTS.md` must be checked against that test, and per the dispatch's own note there is only ~48 bytes of slack, i.e. effectively none.

## Risks
- The `--docs` review lens and `dreamer`/`dream`'s restatement greps explicitly search "as the scope's head" or "before every rule row" — if the index is built once (or on-demand only from the current working tree) and a review scope is a past range `<a>..<b>`, using the index instead of `git grep` at `<b>` would silently search the wrong revision. Any instruction to prefer the index for these must carve out non-HEAD ranges.
- `retro`'s two exact-match greps (`rule_ref`, `target`) are deliberately literal matches against a controlled vocabulary — a ranked/fuzzy FTS hit could return a near-miss (different `rule_ref`) that reads as a false "this recurred elsewhere" positive; these should stay `grep -E` unless the index also supports exact-match mode.
- `verifier`'s own coverage/suppression checks and `preflight`'s secret scan are described in `AGENTS.md`'s Hard rules as never-piped, freshness-critical, live-tree operations — using a cached index here directly risks the "silence from your own instrumentation is not evidence" failure mode this project already guards against elsewhere.
- Whether Antigravity subagents receive `context/AGENTS.md` content at all is undetermined from this repo's code or docs (see Open questions) — an instruction placed only in `context/AGENTS.md` may not reach an Antigravity-dispatched agent, which argues for placing the instruction directly in each `agents/*.md` / `skills/*/SKILL.md` regardless of the context-injection answer.

## Open questions
- Does Antigravity inject the deployed global rules block (`~/.gemini/config/rules/AGENTS.md`) into a dispatched subagent's context, the way Claude Code demonstrably does (I received the full CLAUDE.md→AGENTS.md chain as this dispatch's own subagent)? Not stated anywhere in `internal/harness/derive.go`, `agents/*.md`, or `REQUIREMENTS.md`. `testing/skill-matrix.md`'s `ctx-deploy` row tests that the *main* agent can quote the context; no row tests a dispatched subagent's visibility into it on either CLI.
- Whether the planned index would be rebuilt automatically before each query (freshness) or on a stale cache — not specified in the dispatch; this determines whether the "verifier/preflight must not use it" risk above is absolute or just "must rebuild first."
- Prior research (`.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-29-research-sqlite-index.md`) already concluded CONDITIONAL/build-nothing based on measured grep latency (git grep 11ms on this repo) — this audit does not re-litigate that verdict, only maps consumers assuming the index is built.

## Not examined
- `internal/harness/plan.go` beyond the context-deployment grep (full install-plan logic not read)
- `skills/cloud-run-deploy`, `skills/docker`, `skills/gcloud-setup`, `skills/golang`, `skills/json-api-style`, `skills/mermaid-syntax`, `skills/python`, `skills/typescript` SKILL.md bodies were not read in full (grepped only for grep/read/scan keywords, none matched — low prior they are consumers, but not confirmed by full read)
- `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-29-recon-project-index.md` and `2026-09-29-research-memory-and-prompt-audit.md` (sibling docs, not opened — may contain overlapping findings)
- Frequency/volume of past subagent trail-file reads (dispatch said "optional, only if cheap") — not measured

title: Plan — `dream`: consolidate Claude Code's auto memory (2026-09-29)
body:
# Plan — `dream`: consolidate Claude Code's auto memory   (2026-09-29)

## Why

The operator asked (2026-09-29) whether memory or "dreaming" plugins exist for Claude Code and Antigravity, and then for this draft. Claude Code writes auto memory on its own (`~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/`, one file per fact, `MEMORY.md` as the index) and nothing ever tidies it. Anthropic's "Dreaming" (a between-session consolidation pass: merge duplicates, drop stale entries, absolute dates, a reviewable diff) is a research preview on the Managed Agents API only, not in Claude Code. Community plugins (claude-mem, Mem0, dream-skill and others) add a second store with its own drift, and the agy ones need hooks, which this harness forbids.

The harness already has the learning loop (`feedback-log` → `/retro` → `/distill`) but auto memory sits beside it, unread by it. The cost is visible today: this project's memory `asking-format.md` records a rule that its own text says is "now in the harness context (`context/AGENTS.md` Operator line)". A memory that graduated into a rule is loaded every session for nothing, and a memory that never graduates is a correction the retro never sees.

## Scope

- **In:**
  - A harness skill `dream` (`skills/dream/SKILL.md`, typed as `/dream`, `--dry-run`): reads the project's auto-memory store, gives every memory one verdict, rewrites the index, and hands `promote` verdicts to the retro. It never writes a rule, a skill or context itself.
  - `/retro` runs the skill's orientation as one more evidence source (Step 1) and applies its edits with the rest (Step 6).
  - One sentence in `context/AGENTS.md` § Learning loop; a row in `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md`.
- **Out:**
  - A memory store for Antigravity. agy keeps none; the skill reads Claude Code's store whichever CLI runs it (the path is per project under `~/.claude`), and says so when there is none.
  - A timer or session counter (Anthropic's 24 h / 5 sessions). No hooks, no timers (project rule 1); the retro's own cadence is the trigger.
  - Any third-party memory plugin, MCP server or database.
  - Memories of other projects. A `user`-type memory that belongs in every project graduates through the retro's promotion check, as today.
- **Follow-ups noted, not built:** if Claude Code ships its leaked `autoDream` as a built-in `/dream`, this skill is deleted in the release that adopts it (D2).

## Surfaces touched

- `skills/dream/SKILL.md` — new; a file drop, no Go change (project rule: adding a skill is never a code change).
- `skills/retro/SKILL.md` — Step 1 gains source 7 "Memory evidence"; the Step 4 record template gains `## Memory`; Step 6 applies the verdicts with the proposals.
- `context/AGENTS.md` § Learning loop — one sentence. Headroom on 2026-09-29: 21,539 of 22,000 bytes (`TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock`), so the sentence is under 120 bytes or it pays with a deletion.
- The `## Installed` section is generated by `sh-agent install` (`internal/harness/inventory.go:346`); the skill count updates itself.
- `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md` — one row.
- `README.md` — nothing: `/dream` crosses no line on the map (it is machine-local, like `feedback-log`), so project rule 3 does not fire. `/review --docs` confirms.

## Interfaces

### The store

`<store>` = `autoMemoryDirectory` from the effective Claude Code settings when set, else `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/` where `<slug>` is the repository's absolute path with every `/` turned into `-` (worktrees and subdirectories share one store). Source, read 2026-09-29 from `https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md` § Storage location, against Claude Code 2.1.284 on this box: "Each project gets its own memory directory at `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/`"; "To store auto memory in a different location, set `autoMemoryDirectory` in your `settings.json`. It is read from any settings scope: user, project, local, policy, or `--settings`"; "The value must be an absolute path or start with `~/`"; and § How it works: "The first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation"; topic files are read on demand. `claude --help` on this box lists `--settings` (2.1.284). The slug is verified by `ls`, never assumed: a missing or empty store ends the run with one line, `no auto memory for <repo> (<store>)`. The skill finds the effective `autoMemoryDirectory` by reading, in order, `.claude/settings.local.json`, `.claude/settings.json` and `~/.claude/settings.json` (the first that sets it wins), and a `--settings` file only when the operator names it in the same turn; when none sets it, the slug path applies.

### One verdict per memory

Every `*.md` under `<store>` except `MEMORY.md` gets exactly one verdict, with a one-line why citing `file:line` where the rule says so. The `type` values the verdicts read are Claude Code's own: "Claude records the kind as a `type` field in the memory file's frontmatter" — `user`, `feedback`, `project`, `reference` (memory docs § Auto memory, read 2026-09-29):

| Verdict | Test | Edit |
|---|---|---|
| `keep` | Still true; recorded nowhere the session already loads. | none |
| `graduated` | Its rule now lives in `context/AGENTS.md`, the project `AGENTS.md`, `.agents/rules/`, a skill, or a bug record's prevention rule — found by one `grep` over the memory's key words, hit read in full. | delete the file and its index line |
| `stale` | A `project` memory whose work the newest handoff or a `changes/` entry shows done; a `reference` whose target is gone. | delete |
| `broken` | Names a file, function, flag or command that no longer exists (`ls`, `grep`); or carries a relative date. | rewrite to the current name and an absolute date, or delete when nothing current matches |
| `merge` | Two files on one fact. | one file; the newer `modified:` wins a contradiction; `[[links]]` repointed |
| `promote` | Not a fifth file verdict but a flag set on a memory that survives as `keep` or as the result of a `merge`: its type is `feedback` or `user`, no rule records it, and its fact reached the store from two sessions — either the files it was merged from carry different `originSessionId` values (each file carries exactly one; a file without the field counts as one session), or an entry in `~/.config/sh-agent/feedback.jsonl` from a session other than the memory's `originSessionId` names the same rule (same `rule_ref`, or the memory's key words in the entry's text). | none here; the memory stays, and it becomes a retro finding with `rule_ref null` |

Doubt resolves to `keep`: a memory is deleted only when the check that says so ran and returned (the global guard rule: a check that errors keeps the data).

### The index

`MEMORY.md` is rewritten from the files after the edits: one line per file, every line naming a file that exists (both directions, the global artifact rule), under 200 lines and 25 KB, which is all Claude Code loads at start.

### The gate and the record

- `--dry-run` stops after the table.
- Otherwise the table is put to the operator in the asking format — `#`, memory, verdict, one-line why — and applied per number or "go all". The store is not under git, so the table is the undo point, and the record quotes every deleted memory in full.
- Standalone: `<docs-root>/retros/<date>-dream.md` (frontmatter `owner:`, `date:`; counts per verdict; the table; the deleted text), plus one line in `~/.config/sh-agent/retros.jsonl` with `"kind":"dream"`; when that directory is denied, the same fallback as `/retro` Step 5.
- From `/retro`: no separate record; the retro record gets `## Memory` with the same content, and each `promote` is a row under `## Findings`.

### `/retro` changes

- Step 1, new source: "7. **Memory evidence** — the `dream` skill's orientation and verdict table (its `--dry-run`); each `promote` verdict is a finding with `rule_ref null`." Order: memory evidence is read after the feedback log, before drafting.
- Step 4 template: `## Memory` after `## Feedback log entries`.
- Step 6: the verdict edits are applied with the approved proposals, in the same table.

### `context/AGENTS.md` § Learning loop, the sentence

After "run `/distill` on the third repeat of a procedure.": `/dream` tidies Claude Code's auto memory for the project, and `/retro` reads it first. (about 95 bytes).

## Failure modes

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| No store, or an empty one | one line, exit 0; nothing written |
| Run on Antigravity | same path: it reads Claude Code's store for the project when one exists, otherwise the one line above |
| A graduation grep hits but the hit is a different rule | `keep`, with the why saying what the hit was |
| `~/.config/sh-agent/` denied | the record stands; the exact `cat >>` command is printed, as in `/retro` |
| `MEMORY.md` names a file that is gone, or a file has no line | the index rewrite fixes both; the table lists them as `index` rows |
| Headless run (`claude -p`) | verdicts computed and recorded, nothing deleted; every verdict stays `proposed` |

## Verification

Tiers: unit (the Go suite, for the context edit) / install / behavioural / real-home smoke / docs review.

- **Unit:** `gofmt -l cmd internal && go vet ./... && go test -race ./...` bare; `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` green after the § Learning loop edit.
- **Install:** `go run ./cmd/sh-agent install --home .agents/scratch/dream-home`, then `status` with no drift and `list` naming `dream`. The CLI-start tier of `AGENTS.md` § Testing ("one start of each CLI in the sandbox") is substituted (D10): the sandbox home that procedure names does not exist on this box (`ls /home/kesokaj/sandbox/home` fails; `testing/2026-09-29-prompts-lens-behavioural.md` § Not exercised). Claude Code's start is the behavioural runs below, whose transcript shows the skill loaded; Antigravity's start is the real-home smoke in Phase 2 (`who: user`, after `sh-agent update`), and until then the installer's frontmatter lint (BUG-004) is the only agy parse check, named as such in the Phase 1 log.
- **Behavioural, n of N:** a scratch clone of a small repository that does not contain the harness source (`.agents/scratch/dream-probe/`), with the working-tree skill reachable as a project skill (`.claude/skills/dream` → `skills/dream`) and `--settings <clone>/.agents/scratch/dream-settings.json` holding `{"autoMemoryDirectory":"<absolute path of clone>/.agents/scratch/mem"}` (absolute, as the docs require) pointing the store at a seeded fixture of five memory files: one whose rule sits verbatim in the clone's `AGENTS.md` (expect `graduated`), one naming a file the clone lacks (`broken`), a pair on one fact with two different `originSessionId` values (expect `merge`, and the merged memory flagged `promote`), one clean (`keep`). The run script asserts each seed fact (`grep`, `ls`, and `grep -c originSessionId` showing two distinct values across the pair) before the CLI starts, and the run's stdout must name the store it read (the skill prints `<store>` on its first line), which is the check that `--settings` took effect. `claude -p "/dream --dry-run"` with the prompt on stdin, `--allowedTools` naming the skill's tools; the verdict table is read from the output, the tool-call order from the run's transcript under `~/.claude/projects/`. Expect: the four seeded verdicts and the `promote` flag in n of N runs, and nothing deleted (dry run). Control, same clone without the project skill: no verdict table in n of N.
- **Must-fail for the guard:** a sixth seed whose graduation grep cannot run (the `AGENTS.md` unreadable) expects `keep`.
- **Real-home smoke:** after `sh-agent install` into the real home, the three checks in `testing/2026-09-03-verify-real-home.md` on each CLI, plus `/dream --dry-run` in this repository, which is expected to name `asking-format.md` as `graduated` (its own text names the context line).
- **Docs:** `/review --docs` over the range; the living docs here include `context/`, `skills/dream/` and `skills/retro/`.

E2E criteria: (1) in this repository, `/dream` lists `asking-format.md` as `graduated` with the `context/AGENTS.md` line cited, and after "go" the file and its index line are gone and `MEMORY.md` has one line per remaining file; (2) `/retro --dry-run` in the probe clone shows the merged, `promote`-flagged memory as a finding with `rule_ref null`.

## Phases

- [x] Cold-reader check — three rounds: `reviews/2026-09-29-review-dream-skill-coldread-r1.md` (design needs revision, two blocking, answered by D7–D9), `-r2.md` (design ready, one blocking, answered by D10–D11), `-r3.md` (design needs revision on one new item, the cap); at the cap the operator chose "Proceed, add the rows (Recommended)" on 2026-09-29, the residue recorded as D12 and the two Phase 2 rows below
### Phase 1 — the skill
- [x] `skills/dream/SKILL.md` per Interfaces — verify: install tier, AI — expect: `sh-agent install` into the scratch home succeeds (its lint passes the frontmatter), `status` drift none, `sh-agent list` prints `dream` with its description — done 2026-09-29: install into `.agents/scratch/dream-home` 263 files, `status` "28 skills, drift none", `list` row `dream`, the file under both vendors' skill directories
- [x] Behavioural run, seeded fixture, N=3, plus a control of N=3 without the project skill — done 2026-09-29, `testing/2026-09-29-dream-phase-1-behavioural.md`: round 2 runs 4–6 3 of 3 on the store line, every seeded verdict, the `promote` flag, the guard `keep`, the load marker, nothing written; controls c4–c6 0 of 3 on the skill's vocabulary (round 1's two setup defects, a seed restating a global rule and a contaminated control, recorded there and in D13) — verify: behavioural tier, AI — expect: the store line names the fixture, the four seeded verdicts and the `promote` flag in 3 of 3; the control shows no verdict table in 3 of 3; the guard seed `keep` in 3 of 3; each run's transcript proves the skill loaded — in a `claude -p` run the slash command is expanded into the first user message (`<command-name>/dream</command-name>` followed by the skill body), so that marker is the evidence, not a `Skill` tool call (D13)
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: the skill installed in a scratch home and proven on the fixture — evidence: `testing/2026-09-29-verify-dream-skill-phase-1.md` (verifier PASS: Go suite 171 pass, `list` row `dream`, install 264 files, status 28 skills drift none, SKILL.md under both vendors, frontmatter quoted) and `testing/2026-09-29-dream-phase-1-behavioural.md` (PASS, 3 of 3 and 0 of 3), 2026-09-29
### Phase 2 — the loop
- [x] `skills/retro/SKILL.md` Steps 1, 4, 6 per Interfaces — done 2026-09-29: three `/retro --dry-run` probes in the fixture with the working-tree retro and dream skills linked (`testing/2026-09-29-dream-phase-1-behavioural.md` § Phase 2), 3 of 3 with a `## Memory` section carrying the store line and the verdicts, the merged pair as a finding with `rule_ref null`, nothing written — verify: `retro` matrix row unchanged plus a `/retro --dry-run` in the probe clone, AI — expect: the `promote` seed as a finding
- [x] `context/AGENTS.md` § Learning loop sentence — verify: `go test ./internal/harness -run TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock -count=1` bare, AI — expect: PASS under 22,000 — done 2026-09-29: PASS, 21,636 bytes
- [x] `skill-matrix.md` row `dream` (done 2026-09-29: the row's check command run against the Phase 1 clones 4–6, PASS in each) — seeded like the `review-prompts` row: the base column names the five memory files of Verification under the clone's `.agents/scratch/mem` and the `--settings` file that points `autoMemoryDirectory` at it (absolute path), the extra column carries `--settings <that file>`, the prompt is `/dream --dry-run`, the check greps the four verdicts and the `promote` flag — verify: read, AI — expect: the row's check command passes on the Phase 1 fixture clones
- [-] Real-home install and smoke — verify: real-home tier, both — expect: three checks PASS on each CLI; `/dream --dry-run` here names `asking-format.md` — moved to the 2026-09-29 closing handoff's Next Steps (the real home is the operator's; `asking-format.md` is already gone after the apply run below, so the smoke's dry run should find the store consistent) (2026-09-29)
- [x] Apply run on this checkout's real store (E2E criterion 1) — done 2026-09-29 by hand from the working-tree skill (not yet installed in the real home): the table named `asking-format.md` graduated citing `~/.claude/AGENTS.md:6` and `fallback-paths-stay-simple.md` graduated citing `:17`; the operator said "Go all (Recommended)"; both files and their index lines are gone, `MEMORY.md` has one line per remaining file and no line without a file, `retros/2026-09-29-dream.md` quotes both in full, one `kind: dream` line in `~/.config/sh-agent/retros.jsonl` — verify: e2e, who: both
- [x] `/review --docs` over the range — done 2026-09-29: `reviews/2026-09-29-review-dream-docs.md`, APPROVE WITH NITS, four enumerations of what `retros/` holds fixed (REQUIREMENTS with the operator's approval and ADR-042, README by `documentation`, the handoff and feedback-log skills, plus the context sentence the documentation agent's grep found), all in the report's Outcome — verify: docs tier, AI — expect: no finding, or each fixed or rebutted in the report's Outcome
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: Definition of Done closed, `changes/` entry, commit, push — evidence: `testing/2026-09-29-verify-dream-skill-phase-2.md` (PASS), `-r2.md` (FAIL on a dispatch needle, BUG record), `-r3.md` (PASS: suite, size test 21,643 bytes, install 264 files drift none, every restatement once on both vendors, GANNET); `reviews/2026-09-29-review-dream-code.md` APPROVE WITH NITS (two citations fixed); `changes/2026-09-29-1348-dream-skill-phase-2.md`; 2026-09-29

## Risks

Assumptions:
- Claude Code loads a project skill from `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` in a `claude -p` run — checked by the control run above, first task of Phase 1.
- `autoMemoryDirectory` given through `--settings` redirects the store for a `claude -p` run (documented, § Storage location, read 2026-09-29) — checked by the run's first stdout line naming the fixture store, first task of Phase 1; the fixture path is absolute because the docs accept only an absolute path or `~/`.
- Antigravity CLI keeps no memory store (checked 2026-09-29 on agy 1.2.13: no docs page, no help entry, no settings key; the binary links the editor's Knowledge Base code and `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/knowledge/` exists with only a lock file, never written). Re-check `ls ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/knowledge/` after each agy update; a populated store is a new Decisions row, not a change to this plan.
- `originSessionId` is present in every auto-memory file's frontmatter (it is in this project's four) — checked by `grep -L originSessionId <store>/*.md`; a file without it counts as one session.

## Decisions

- D1 (2026-09-29): dream never writes a rule; `promote` hands the memory to the retro. Why: one place decides where a rule lives (retro Step 2), and a second writer would drift from it.
- D2 (2026-09-29): named `dream` after Anthropic's term; if Claude Code ships a built-in `/dream` that does this, the skill is deleted rather than renamed. Why: a built-in that does the same job makes the skill redundant, not conflicting.
- D3 (2026-09-29): doubt resolves to `keep`. Why: the store is not under git; the global guard rule for destructive actions.
- D4 (2026-09-29): trigger is `/retro` and the operator's hand, no timer and no session counter — by: "Go all on the dream plan" (operator, 2026-09-29), on O1. Rejected: a `sh-agent status` line counting sessions since the last dream — a Go change for a file-drop feature, and project rule 1 keeps timers out of the mechanism.
- D5 (2026-09-29): a standalone run records to `<docs-root>/retros/<date>-dream.md`, plus one `retros.jsonl` line — by: the same words, on O2. Rejected: nothing on disk beyond `retros.jsonl` — REQUIREMENTS line 31 puts the learning loop's records in `retros/`.
- D7 (2026-09-29): the store's default path, the `autoMemoryDirectory` override (any settings scope including `--settings`, absolute or `~/` only) and the 200-line / 25 KB index load are cited from `code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md` § Storage location and § How it works, read 2026-09-29, and `claude --help` of 2.1.284 on this box — by: cold read round 1, gap 1 (`reviews/2026-09-29-review-dream-skill-coldread-r1.md`).
- D8 (2026-09-29): `promote` is a flag on a memory that survives as `keep` or as a merge result, evidenced by the merged files' differing `originSessionId` values or by a `feedback.jsonl` entry from another session naming the same rule — by: cold read round 1, gap 2. Rejected: "a memory with two `originSessionId`s" — the file format holds exactly one per file (every file on this box), so that fixture cannot exist.
- D9 (2026-09-29): the `skill-matrix.md` row seeds the store through a `--settings` file naming an absolute `autoMemoryDirectory`, the way the `review-prompts` row carries `--add-dir` in its extra column — by: cold read round 1, question 3 (non-blocking).
- D10 (2026-09-29): the sandbox CLI-start tier is substituted for this plan — Claude Code's start is the behavioural run (the transcript proves the skill loaded), Antigravity's is the operator's real-home smoke in Phase 2, and the installer's lint stands in for an agy parse check until then, named in the Phase 1 log — by: cold read round 2, blocking question 1 (`reviews/2026-09-29-review-dream-skill-coldread-r2.md`); the same substitution the `--prompts` lens task made on 2026-09-29. Rejected: rebuilding the sandbox home — it needs both CLIs logged in to a second home, an operator step outside this plan's scope.
- D11 (2026-09-29): the control run count is 3, stated in the Phase 1 task — by: cold read round 2, non-blocking question 2.
- D12 (2026-09-29): at the cold-read cap, the apply path (delete, merge, index rewrite) gets its own Phase 2 task, interactive on this checkout's real store with the operator's go, since every scripted run is `--dry-run` and headless runs never delete; the `type` vocabulary is cited from the docs; `/review --docs` has a Phase 2 box — by: "Proceed, add the rows (Recommended)" (operator, 2026-09-29, at the cap after `reviews/2026-09-29-review-dream-skill-coldread-r3.md`). Rejected: cutting the apply-path E2E — a delete path with no run behind it; and a fourth round — the cap is the cap.
- D13 (2026-09-29): in a headless run the load evidence is the command expansion in the first user message, not a `Skill` tool call — by: implementer, from the round-1 probe transcripts (`Skill` tool uses 0 of 3 while every run followed the procedure). Also from round 1: a control must not carry `--add-dir` on the harness skill directory nor a deleted-but-tracked skill link, or the model reads the skill anyway (3 of 3 contaminated controls); and a seed pair must state a fact no loaded rule holds — the first pair restated the global context's asking rule and was correctly marked `graduated` citing `~/.claude/AGENTS.md:6`.
- D6 (2026-09-29): this project's store only — by: the same words, on O3. Rejected: one pass over every store under `~/.claude/projects/` — it reads other projects' state from here (the 2026-09-28 retro's finding 2).

title: Plan — one memory store for both CLIs, and the `dreamer` agent (2026-09-29)
body:
# Plan — one memory store for both CLIs, and the `dreamer` agent   (2026-09-29)

## Why

The operator, 2026-09-29: "Cant we build dreaming and memory as a subagents that triggers when something in the project/conversation highlights to generate a skill/rule or procedure? … I want them to work the same for claude and agy." Research `plans/2026-09-29-research-memory-subagents.md` compared four shapes; the operator chose B ("Option B", 2026-09-29): one `dreamer` subagent for the consolidation judgement, capture kept in-thread, and a vendor-neutral store by pointing Claude Code's `autoMemoryDirectory` at a harness-owned directory. Spec: `specs/sh-agent/memory-loop.md`.

## Scope

- **In:**
  - The store at `~/.config/sh-agent/memory/<slug>/`, set up by `/init-project` (new and update paths): the `autoMemoryDirectory` key in `.claude/settings.local.json`, the `.gitignore` line, the directory, and the move of an existing default store.
  - The Resume Protocol clause for Antigravity (`context/AGENTS.md`), the Antigravity capture rule in `feedback-log`, and `/dream`'s split-store check.
  - `agents/dreamer.md` per the spec; `/retro` Step 1 source 8 and `/distill` Step 1 dispatching it; two `skill-matrix.md` rows.
- **Out:**
  - Sending memory through `sh-agent report` (D1); any Go change; any hook or timer; a `memory` capture subagent (research, D-row there); auto-applying anything the `dreamer` proposes.
  - Moving stores of projects other than the one `/init-project` runs in.
- **Follow-ups noted, not built:** a `sh-agent status` line naming the project's store (a Go change, out of a file drop); a `--since` argument on the dreamer dispatch beyond the newest-record date.

## Surfaces touched

- `skills/init-project/SKILL.md` — a new Step 5b between the symlinks (Step 5, lines 79–92) and README/.gitignore (Step 6, lines 94–104); Step 6's `.gitignore` list gains one line; Step 7's summary names the store.
- `context/AGENTS.md` § Resume, then checkpoint (line 9): one clause; headroom 357 bytes (`TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock`, 21,643 of 22,000 on 2026-09-29).
- `skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md` § Behavior Rules (line 80): one rule for Antigravity.
- `skills/dream/SKILL.md` Step 1: the split-store check.
- `agents/dreamer.md` — new; `internal/harness/derive.go`'s `toolMap` already maps every tool it names (Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write), so no Go change.
- `skills/retro/SKILL.md` Step 1 (after source 7) and Step 4 (the record cites the artifact); `skills/distill/SKILL.md` Step 1 (dispatch first).
- `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md` — rows `init-memory` and `dreamer`.
- `README.md` — nothing: no line on the map moves (`sh-agent report` ships the same files; the store is machine-local like `feedback.jsonl`), so project rule 3 does not fire; `/review --docs` confirms. `specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` — nothing.

## Interfaces

> D17 (2026-09-29) moved the store to `<repository root>/.agents/memory/`, gitignored: read every `~/.config/sh-agent/memory/<slug>/` below as that path, the settings value as its absolute form, and the `.gitignore` list as also carrying `.agents/memory/`. The spec and the skills carry the final text; this section keeps the shape the cold read checked.

- **Store path:** `~/.config/sh-agent/memory/<slug>/`, `<slug>` = the absolute repository root with every character other than a letter, a digit or a hyphen replaced by a hyphen (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel | sed 's#[^A-Za-z0-9-]#-#g'`) — Claude Code's `<project>` name under `~/.claude/projects/`, read off this box: `/home/kesokaj/workspace/styrman-harness` → `-home-kesokaj-workspace-styrman-harness`, and `…/styrman-harness/.agents/scratch/dream-probe/runs/1/clone` → `…-styrman-harness--agents-scratch-dream-probe-runs-1-clone` (the `.` became `-`, the hyphens stayed); D9. Layout as the spec says.
- **`/init-project` Step 5b — the memory store** (new and update paths, after the symlinks):
  1. `slug=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel | tr / -)`; `store=~/.config/sh-agent/memory/$slug`; `mkdir -p "$store"`.
  2. `.claude/settings.local.json`: absent → write `{"autoMemoryDirectory": "~/.config/sh-agent/memory/<slug>"}`; present without the key → copy the file to `.agents/scratch/settings.local.json.before`; when its content is an empty object (`{}` with any whitespace), overwrite it with the one-key object; otherwise add the key with the Edit tool as one new line after the opening `{` (`"autoMemoryDirectory": "~/.config/sh-agent/memory/<slug>",`), touching no other line — never `jq` or a re-serialisation, which reformat the file — then `python3 -c 'import json,sys; json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))' .claude/settings.local.json`; a failed parse restores the copy and reports the intended content for the user, with no second attempt; say what was added; present with the key → keep it, report its value, and use that value as `store` for step 3.
  3. Migration: `old=~/.claude/projects/$slug/memory`; when `old` holds files and `store` holds none, `mv "$old"/* "$store"/` and report each file; when both hold files, move nothing and report both paths (the operator merges); when `old` holds no memory files (absent, or present and empty — one branch: `ls "$old"/*.md` finds nothing), print `no memory files at <old>` and, as a hint, every `~/.claude/projects/*/memory` directory whose name ends with the repository's last path component; nothing is moved.
  4. Step 6's `.gitignore` list gains `.claude/settings.local.json`.
  5. Step 7's summary names the store path and what moved.
  Headless refusal of writes under `.claude/` (the existing Step 5 note) applies: report the file's exact content for the user to create.
- **Resume clause** (`context/AGENTS.md` § Resume, appended to the reading order): `→ on Antigravity, MEMORY.md in the project's memory store (~/.config/sh-agent/memory/<slug>/) when it exists; Claude Code loads it itself.` (about 140 bytes).
- **`feedback-log` rule** (§ Behavior Rules): on Antigravity, an entry that is a correction or a stated preference is also written as one memory file in the store — Claude Code's shape (frontmatter `name`, `description`, `metadata.type` `feedback` or `user`, `originSessionId`, `modified` from `date -u +%FT%TZ`), body with `**Why:**` and `**How to apply:**` — plus its `MEMORY.md` line; when the store does not exist, nothing (the project has not run `/init-project` since the store existed). On Claude Code nothing changes: its auto memory writes the file itself.
- **`/dream` Step 1 addition:** after resolving `<store>` from settings, also `ls ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`; when both hold memory files, print both paths with their counts, say "split store — merge before running", and stop with nothing written.
- **`agents/dreamer.md`:** frontmatter `name: dreamer`, one-line double-quoted `description` (what it returns, when to dispatch, never edits), `tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write`, `model: sonnet`, `effort: medium`, `maxTurns: 40`. Body per the spec: write early; what it reads; the candidate tests; the artifact template; Records (only its artifact and drafts under `.agents/scratch/dreamer/`); Output (at most ten lines). Dispatch contract: `Store: <path>. Docs root: <docs-root>. Since: <date|all>. Promoted: <memory files, or none>.` plus "Write your artifact with the Write tool; report only means no source edits." and a tool-call budget.
- **`/retro` Step 1 source 8:** "**Dreamer candidates** — after source 7, dispatch `dreamer` with `Store:`, `Docs root:`, `Since:` and `Promoted: <the memory files source 7 flagged promote, or none>`, a 30-call budget and the artifact sentence. The dreamer does not re-derive `promote`: its rule candidates are the promoted memories (with a target file and the rule text), bug rows whose prevention rule is written nowhere, and trail rows; source 7's `promote` findings are replaced by the dreamer's rows for the same memory files, one row per memory, so no memory appears twice; skill and procedure candidates are noted for `/distill`." Step 4's record cites the artifact path under `## Findings`. (D8)
- **`/distill` Step 1:** first dispatch `dreamer` the same way (`Promoted: none` when `/dream` did not run); its skill and procedure candidates are the first entries of the candidate list, with their evidence; the session transcript scan follows as today and adds only patterns the artifact does not already name (same name or same steps), so a pattern appears once. (D8)
- **Matrix rows:** `init-memory` (base: demo HEAD scaffolded by an older harness, plus a seeded default store `~/.claude/projects/<slug of the clone>/memory/` with two files and an index; prompt: `/init-project` update path; check: `.claude/settings.local.json` holds the key with the clone's slug, the store holds the two files and the index, the old directory is empty, `.gitignore` has the line); `dreamer` (base: demo HEAD plus a seeded store — two `feedback` memories on one fact from two sessions, one `project` memory — and a trail with two `bugs/INDEX.md` rows for one recurring defect whose prevention rule is written nowhere and a release procedure of five steps recorded twice (a handoff and a `changes/` entry); dispatch text as the contract with `Promoted: <the two feedback files>` (what `/retro` passes after `/dream`); check: the artifact exists with `Status: COMPLETE`, a rule candidate naming both promoted files with a target file and rule text, a rule candidate naming the bug rows, a skill or procedure candidate naming the release steps, "Left alone" naming the project memory, and `git status --short` shows only the artifact and `.agents/scratch/`); `init-memory-absent` (the `init-memory` base without the seeded default store, and a committed `.claude/settings.local.json` holding `{}`; check: the output contains `no memory files at`, the settings file is exactly the one-key object, `.claude/settings.local.json` holds the key, the store directory exists and is empty).

## Failure modes

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| `/init-project` cannot write under `.claude/` (headless guard) | the settings file's exact content is reported for the user; the store is still created and the migration still runs |
| The setting is ignored (untrusted workspace) | Claude writes to the default store; `/dream` reports a split store and stops; the `dreamer` reads the settings store and lists the other as not examined |
| `~/.config/sh-agent/` denied to an Antigravity session | the resume clause reads nothing and says so; `feedback-log` logs the entry to chat as it does for the log itself |
| Old and new stores both hold files at migration | nothing moved, both paths reported |
| No memory files at the computed default path (absent or empty: a slug mismatch, or a project Claude Code never wrote memory for) | `no memory files at <old>` plus the hint list; nothing moved; the store is still created and the setting written |
| `.claude/settings.local.json` is `{}` | overwritten with the one-key object |
| The settings edit fails its parse check | the pre-edit copy restored, the intended content reported, no second attempt |
| `dreamer` cut at its turn limit | partial artifact, `IN PROGRESS`, named as such by the caller |
| `dreamer` finds nothing | an artifact with an empty Candidates table and a full "Left alone" |

## Verification

Tiers: unit (the Go suite; the size test for the context clause) / install (scratch home, drift none, `dreamer` under both vendors' agent directories, `sh-agent list` naming it) / behavioural on Claude Code / real-home smoke and an Antigravity run (`who: user`, D-row below) / docs review.

- **Behavioural, Phase 1:** a scratch clone of a small repository scaffolded by an older harness (the matrix's `init-update` base), a seeded default store under the real home's `~/.claude/projects/<slug of the clone>/memory/` (per-project, harmless, removed after); `claude -p` running `/init-project` with the update-path answers, 3 runs; expect the `init-memory` row's check in 3 of 3; then the `init-memory-absent` variant, 2 runs, expecting its check in 2 of 2. Then in one of those clones, a `claude -p` "remember that the demo deploys on Fridays" with `.claude/settings.local.json` in place; expect a new memory file in the new store and none in the default (the positive control for the setting being honoured; if Claude Code refuses the project setting headless as untrusted, the run says so and the split-store path is what gets exercised instead — either result is recorded). `/dream --dry-run` on a fixture with files in both stores: expect the split-store stop line, nothing written, 3 of 3.
- **Behavioural, Phase 2:** `claude -p --agents <json built from agents/dreamer.md>`, the dispatch contract on stdin, the seeded store and trail of the `dreamer` matrix row, 3 runs; expect the row's check in 3 of 3, the artifact carrying the definition's own section headings (only the new definition writes them), executed and refused calls counted separately. Then `/retro --dry-run` with the working-tree retro skill linked, 2 runs: expect the artifact dispatched and its rule candidates as findings with `rule_ref null`.
- **Docs:** `/review --docs` over the range; the living docs include the spec, `init-project`, `feedback-log`, `retro`, `distill`, `dream`, `context/`.

E2E criteria: (1) in this checkout, the `/init-project` update path writes `.claude/settings.local.json`, moves the two real memories into `~/.config/sh-agent/memory/-home-kesokaj-workspace-styrman-harness/`, and `/dream --dry-run` prints that store line with two files; (2) `/retro --dry-run` here dispatches the `dreamer`, whose artifact names BUG-096's prevention rule as a rule candidate (it is written nowhere loaded) and the read-neighbours memory as its evidence.

## Phases

- [x] Cold-reader check — three rounds: `reviews/2026-09-29-review-dreamer-memory-loop-coldread-r1.md` (one blocking, D8–D10), `-r2.md` (two blocking, D11–D12), `-r3.md` (one blocking, one coverage gap, the cap); residue resolved as D13–D14 under the operator's words "Go all on the cold-read gaps and keep building" (2026-09-29)
### Phase 1 — the store
- [x] `skills/init-project/SKILL.md` Step 5b, Step 6 line, Step 7 summary — done 2026-09-29, `testing/2026-09-29-memory-loop-phase-1-behavioural.md`: store, migration, `.gitignore` 3 of 3; message 2 of 2; the settings write refused by Claude Code's headless `.claude/` guard in every run with the exact content reported each time (the write itself is Phase 2's interactive E2E) — verify: behavioural tier (`init-memory` 3 runs, `init-memory-absent` 2 runs), AI — expect: 3 of 3 and 2 of 2 — docs: `skills/init-project/SKILL.md` (it is `/init-project`'s documentation) and `specs/sh-agent/memory-loop.md`
- [x] `context/AGENTS.md` resume clause — done 2026-09-29: PASS, 21,787 bytes — verify: `go test ./internal/harness -run TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock -count=1` bare, AI — expect: PASS under 22,000
- [x] `skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md` Antigravity capture rule — done 2026-09-29: rule 7 names every field of the spec's layout — verify: read against the store layout in the spec, AI — expect: the rule names every frontmatter field the spec lists
- [x] `skills/dream/SKILL.md` split-store check — done 2026-09-29: s10–s12 3 of 3 stop lines, no table, nothing written (after D15's shadowing was found and D16 moved the counts onto the first line; nine earlier runs void) — verify: behavioural tier, AI — expect: the stop line in 3 of 3, nothing written
- [x] The setting honoured headless — done 2026-09-29: m1, m2, the memory file in the new store and nothing in the default, 2 of 2 — verify: the "remember" run above, AI — expect: the memory file in the new store, or the refusal recorded
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: the store set up by `/init-project` and proven on the fixture; the resume clause installed under both vendors — evidence: `testing/2026-09-29-verify-dreamer-memory-loop-phase-1.md` (PASS: suite, size test 21,787 bytes, install 264 files drift none, Step 5b and the dream first line under both vendors, GANNET) and `testing/2026-09-29-memory-loop-phase-1-behavioural.md` (PASS), 2026-09-29
### Phase 2 — the dreamer
- [x] `agents/dreamer.md` per Interfaces — done 2026-09-29: install into `.agents/scratch/mloop-home` 265 files, `status` "8 agents, drift none", `list` row `dreamer`, `.claude/agents/dreamer.md` and `.gemini/config/agents/dreamer/agent.md` with five tools mapped — verify: install tier, AI — expect: `sh-agent install` succeeds (every tool mapped), `status` drift none, the agent under both vendors' agent directories, `sh-agent list` naming it
- [x] Behavioural runs, N=3 — done 2026-09-29, `testing/2026-09-29-memory-loop-phase-2-behavioural.md`: six runs over two definitions; artifact, promoted pair, bug candidate, left-alone row 6 of 6; the skill candidate 4 of 6 (reported as the soft column, not reworded a third time) — verify: behavioural tier, AI — expect: the `dreamer` row's check in 3 of 3
- [x] `skills/retro/SKILL.md` source 8 and record citation; `skills/distill/SKILL.md` Step 1 — done 2026-09-29: t3–t4 2 of 2 dispatch the dreamer and cite its artifact after the dry-run clause (t1–t2 skipped it, reading "nothing written" as covering the artifact); distill's dispatch not probed — verify: two `/retro --dry-run` probes, AI — expect: the artifact dispatched and its rule candidates as findings — docs: the two skill files are their own documentation; the spec's Consumers line
- [x] `skill-matrix.md` rows `init-memory`, `init-memory-absent` and `dreamer` — done 2026-09-29: the rows' conditions checked by the kit scripts on the fixture clones (the check commands carry `<slug>` placeholders and were not run verbatim); the `dreamer` row's skill column would have failed d3 and d4 — verify: the checks run on the fixture clones, AI — expect: PASS

- [-] Real-home install and smoke, plus the first Antigravity run of the resume clause and `/dream` — moved to the 2026-09-29 closing handoff's Next Steps (the real home is the operator's; they updated it to 4426e58 mid-session) (2026-09-29)
- [x] `/review --docs` over the range — done 2026-09-29: `reviews/2026-09-29-review-memory-loop-docs.md`, APPROVE WITH NITS, three findings: the REQUIREMENTS clause (approved, ADR-043), the `dreamer` in three loop enumerations (fixed), the map label (rebutted after D17); the `documentation` agent brought README and the deploy guides to the final store location — verify: docs tier, AI — expect: no finding, or each fixed or rebutted
