- [x] Checkpoint — expect: Definition of Done closed, `changes/` entry, commit, push — evidence: `testing/2026-09-29-verify-dreamer-memory-loop-phase-2.md` (PASS), `-phase-2-r2.md` (PASS, the tree moved under it by the main agent's approved edits), `-final.md` (PASS over a frozen tree: suite, size test 21,855 bytes, govulncheck clean, install 266 files drift none, the old path gone from every installed file, GANNET), `-r4.md` (PASS after the round-3 security edits, 21,887 bytes); `testing/2026-09-29-memory-loop-phase-2-behavioural.md`; reviews: code APPROVE, docs APPROVE WITH NITS (all fixed or rebutted), security three rounds (every finding fixed or `left: operator`, Outcomes on each); `changes/2026-09-29-1517-memory-loop-phase-2.md`; 2026-09-29

## Risks

Assumptions:
- Claude Code honours `autoMemoryDirectory` from `.claude/settings.local.json` in a headless run of a scratch clone (trust) — checked by the "remember" run, Phase 1; the split-store path covers the refusal.
- Claude Code creates the store directory when absent — not relied on: `/init-project` runs `mkdir -p`.
- The Antigravity CLI can read `~/.config/sh-agent/memory/` from a project session — the same directory `feedback-log` already writes to on agy (one approval per session per the README § harness state); checked in the operator's smoke, Phase 2.
- `~/.config/sh-agent/` is 0700 and owned by the operator (the installer tightens it) — the store inherits that; checked by `stat -c %a` in the Phase 1 log.

## Decisions

- D1 (2026-09-29): memory stays out of `sh-agent report` — by: implementer, from `internal/harness/report.go:263-288` (an allowlist: `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl`, `proposals/`). Why: memory holds facts about the operator; the `dreamer` artifact in `retros/` is what carries learning into the project, and the report already ships `retros.jsonl`. The research record's sentence "memory rides the feedback loop for free" was wrong and is corrected there. Rejected: extending the allowlist — a Go change and a redaction question for a personal store.
- D2 (2026-09-29): the store's per-project name is Claude Code's slug, so one rule names both the default and the harness store — by: implementer. Rejected: a hash or a project id — nothing on agy would map it back.
- D3 (2026-09-29): capture stays in-thread; on Antigravity the `feedback-log` skill writes the memory file — by: the research record's recommendation B, chosen by the operator. Rejected: a `memory` subagent — blind to the conversation.
- D4 (2026-09-29): the `dreamer` writes no `retros.jsonl` line; the retro or distill record that consumed it cites it — by: implementer. Rejected: a fourth record kind — nothing reads it.
- D5 (2026-09-29): `.claude/settings.local.json`, gitignored, carries the key — by: implementer. Why: the path is per machine (`~/`), and the docs read `autoMemoryDirectory` from the local scope. Rejected: `.claude/settings.json` (committed, and the harness's own `.claude/*` are symlinks to `.agents/` where a settings file would be shared).
- D6 (2026-09-29): the trust rule is handled by detection, not prevention — `/dream` stops on a split store — by: implementer, from the memory docs § Storage location ("honors it under the same workspace trust rule as hooks").
- D7 (2026-09-29): the sandbox CLI-start tier is substituted as in the dream plan's D10 — Claude Code's start is the behavioural run, Antigravity's is the operator's smoke — by: implementer.
- D8 (2026-09-29): one judgement, not two — the `dreamer` consumes `/dream`'s verdict table (the `Promoted:` line of its dispatch) and never re-derives `promote`; `/retro` replaces source 7's `promote` findings with the dreamer's rows for the same memory files; `/distill` takes the dreamer's skill and procedure candidates first and adds from the transcript only what the artifact does not name — by: cold read round 1, blocking gap 1 (`reviews/2026-09-29-review-dreamer-memory-loop-coldread-r1.md`), resolved on the operator's "Go all on the cold-read gaps and keep building" (2026-09-29). Rejected: dropping `/dream`'s `promote` flag — `/dream` runs standalone too, where no dreamer is dispatched.
- D9 (2026-09-29): the slug rule is "every character other than a letter, a digit or a hyphen becomes a hyphen", read off this box's `~/.claude/projects/` names (a `.` became `-`, hyphens stayed); `/init-project`'s migration prints "no default store at <old>" when the directory is absent, so a mismatch is visible, and lists any `~/.claude/projects/*/memory` directory whose name ends with the repository's last path component as a hint — by: cold read round 1, gap 2.
- D10 (2026-09-29): the settings edit is one inserted line with the Edit tool plus a parse check; "byte for byte" was unachievable with `jq` — by: cold read round 1, gap 3.
- D11 (2026-09-29): the dreamer's rule-candidate sources are the `Promoted:` files (given), recurring bug rows with no written rule, and a memory a trail row restates — never the two-memory test, which is `/dream`'s; the matrix row passes the seeded pair on the `Promoted:` line as `/retro` would — by: cold read round 2, G4 (`reviews/2026-09-29-review-dreamer-memory-loop-coldread-r2.md`), on the operator's "Go all on the cold-read gaps" (2026-09-29). The spec's Candidate tests line now says so.
- D12 (2026-09-29): an absent default store at migration prints `no default store at <old>` with the hint list, an empty one prints `default store empty at <old>`; both in Interfaces, the Failure modes and the `init-memory-absent` runs — by: cold read round 2, G5, on the same words.
- D13 (2026-09-29): an existing `.claude/settings.local.json` that is an empty object is overwritten with the one-key object; any other file gets the inserted line; a failed parse check restores the pre-edit copy and reports, never a second attempt — by: cold read round 3, finding 1 (`reviews/2026-09-29-review-dreamer-memory-loop-coldread-r3.md`), resolved at the cap under "Go all on the cold-read gaps and keep building" (2026-09-29).
- D14 (2026-09-29): absent and empty default stores are one branch and one message, `no memory files at <old>`, tested by `init-memory-absent` — supersedes D12's two messages — by: cold read round 3, finding 2, same words.
- D15 (2026-09-29): a headless probe of a working-tree skill passes `--setting-sources project,local`, because a user-level installed skill of the same name shadows the project link — found when the real home was installed from 4426e58 at 14:03 (the operator's action) and nine `/dream` split-store probes then measured the installed copy, not the edit (their outputs kept the old first line); the `/init-project` probes were valid because their prompt named Step 5b and the runs read the linked file (14 mentions in a transcript, none in the installed copy) — by: implementer. Rejected: uninstalling the skill from the real home for the probe — the real home is the operator's.
- D16 (2026-09-29): `/dream`'s split-store detection is a required field on its first line (`store: <store> (<n> memory files; default path <default>: <m>)`), not a conditional step, after the shadowed probes skipped the conditional step (all nine were shadowed, so that count proves nothing; the reruns under D15 decided: 3 of 3) — by: implementer. Rejected so far: striking the check — the trust rule makes a silent split likely enough to keep one line of output for it.
- D17 (2026-09-29): the store is `<repository root>/.agents/memory/`, gitignored, one per checkout, the absolute path in the per-machine `.claude/settings.local.json` — by: "Option 2" (operator, 2026-09-29), answering "Why cant we keep these inside the project?"; supersedes D2's and D5's harness-directory path (D5's file choice stands). Rejected: a committed `.agents/memory/` — personal and unreviewed content in history, merge conflicts between machines; and keeping `~/.config/sh-agent/memory/<slug>/` — the operator wants project state in the project. Consequences: every restatement of the path moved in this commit (spec, `/init-project`, `/dream`, `dreamer`, `feedback-log`, the context's resume clause, the matrix rows, README and the deploy guides), the accepted roots for `/dream` and the `dreamer` are the repository's `.agents/memory` and `~/.claude/projects/`, this checkout's store moved again, and the probes whose fixtures sat outside those roots reran.
- Open: none.

title: Recon — project/global SQLite index feature (2026-09-29)
body:
# Recon — project/global SQLite index feature   (2026-09-29)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Question
Recon for adding `sh-agent index` / `sh-agent search` (pure-Go modernc.org/sqlite + FTS5), a
per-project index (`.agents/scratch/index.db`) and a global index (`~/.config/sh-agent/index.db`),
plus exposure via `context/AGENTS.md` (22,000-byte budget) and a skill.

## Summary
The biggest blocker is not mechanical: R4 in REQUIREMENTS.md ("`sh-agent` is a single Go binary
with no dependencies") and the project AGENTS.md ("Stdlib only in the Go code. The binary is a
file copier with a manifest; it does not need a dependency") both make `modernc.org/sqlite` a
REQUIREMENTS.md change requiring the operator's explicit approval + an ADR before any code lands —
this is not a "just add the import" task. Mechanically the rest is straightforward: verb dispatch
is a flat switch in `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` `run()` sharing one `flag.FlagSet`; `TestHarnessMap`
(cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go:1350) only requires that verbs the mermaid map in README.md names exist
in `usage`, and that install/update/report appear in the map — adding `index`/`search` verbs does
NOT by itself force a README-map edit unless the map's prose is changed to mention them (they are
not one of the four R9 procedures). `~/.config/sh-agent/` already holds state.json/feedback.jsonl/
retros.jsonl/proposals/ with no project registry; `report.go`'s `Collect()` is a closed allowlist
of exactly those names, so a new `~/.config/sh-agent/index.db` is automatically NOT sent by
`sh-agent report` — good, but worth an explicit skip-list entry/comment for defense in depth.
CGO/cross-compile is not a blocker: the release build already sets `CGO_ENABLED=0` for
linux/amd64, darwin/arm64, linux/arm64 (deploy/remote.md:141), which is exactly why modernc.org's
pure-Go driver (not mattn/go-sqlite3) is the right choice if a dependency is approved — but go.mod
currently has no `go.sum` at all (zero deps), and `TestFilesMatchTree`/`TestEmbedHoldsOnlyTrackedFiles`
(embed_test.go) plus the release contamination guard only check that embedded context/skills/etc
files match git-tracked ones — they do not police go.mod, so no test currently blocks adding a
dependency, but doing so is still an R4 violation on its face. The context-size budget is tight:
`context/AGENTS.md` + `context/dev-setup.md` are already 21,031 bytes combined against a hard
22,000-byte ceiling pinned by `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock`
(internal/harness/size_test.go:19, comment: "never raised by an implementer... a rule that does
not fit is paid for by a deletion or a merge, or lives in a skill") — under 1,000 bytes of margin,
so "a few lines" for index/search usage will need real pruning elsewhere in context/AGENTS.md, and
note context/AGENTS.md IS the literal global context (same text shown to every session via
`~/.claude/AGENTS.md` → this repo), so any edit there is global-blast-radius, not scoped to this
feature's own project.

## Relevant files
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:1-20` doc comment and `:38-53` `usage` const — BOTH enumerate every verb
  and must be edited together for `index`/`search`; not test-enforced against each other (only the
  README mermaid map is pinned to `usage`, not the doc comment).
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` `run()` (~86 onward) — one shared `flag.FlagSet` parses `--repo`, `--home`,
  `--vendor`, `--dry-run`, `--check`, `--force`, `--feedback-repo`, `--from-zip` for every command
  before the verb switch; then `switch cmd { case "version": ...; case "uninstall": ...;
  case "report": ...}` handles verbs needing no `harness.ResolveSource`, followed by
  `src, err := harness.ResolveSource(...)` and a second `switch cmd { case "install","sync": ... }`
  for verbs that need a resolved harness tree. A `--query`/`--limit` flag for `search` would sit in
  this same global FlagSet (visible to every verb) unless a per-command sub-parsing pattern is
  added — none exists today; every flag is global. Positional args after the verb (e.g. the search
  query string) aren't handled anywhere yet — `reorder(rest)` (main.go, referenced at parse time)
  reorders flags ahead of positionals (BUG-002's fix), so a bare positional query arg is plausible
  but unprecedented in this codebase; would need new code, not just a new case.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go:1345-1377` `TestHarnessMap` — reads README.md `## How it works` §,
  extracts the mermaid block, regexes `sh-agent ([a-z]+)`, requires each named verb to appear in
  `usage` as `"\n  "+verb+" "`, and requires install/update/report to appear in the map. New verbs
  do not force a map edit unless the map's own prose grows to mention them.
- `internal/harness/state.go:71-137` — `ConfigDir(home)` = `~/.config/sh-agent` (created 0700 by
  `TightenConfigDir`, called from `apply.go:30` at install time). Comment at 71-75 currently
  enumerates what lives there ("the feedback log, the retro proposals and, briefly, a clone of the
  private feedback repo") — needs updating for a new `index.db`. Comment at 132-137 already uses
  the phrase "cross-project index ~/.config/sh-agent/retros.jsonl" for a DIFFERENT thing (a
  retros.jsonl-derived concept referenced by `harnessProposalInputs` or similar, feeding
  `/retro --harness`) — a literal `index.db` should not overload this existing term; reconcile
  naming with the operator before writing code/docs.
- `internal/harness/report.go:220-295` `Collected`/`Collection`/`Collect(home)` — closed allowlist:
  `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl` (both via `redactLines(...,true)`/jsonl mode), `state.json` (via
  `redactDocument`), and `proposals/*.md` (via text redaction). A new `index.db` at
  `~/.config/sh-agent/` is NOT in this list and thus never collected/sent by `sh-agent report` —
  matches the scope's "must not be sent" requirement by construction. No code change needed to
  exclude it, but recommend adding a comment/explicit skip entry (`c.Skipped = append(...,
  "index.db (binary index, never sent)")`) for auditability, matching the pattern already used for
  absent/non-regular files.
- `go.mod` — `module github.com/kesokaj/styrman-harness`, `go 1.24.4`, no `require` block, **no
  go.sum file exists** (zero dependencies today). Per project AGENTS.md, no `toolchain` directive
  (ADR-029, `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md:101` — "a pin makes the module unbuildable on a host that
  cannot fetch a toolchain... never raise the `go` directive or add a `toolchain` line").
- `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:139-144` — release cross-compile: `for target in linux/amd64
  darwin/arm64 linux/arm64; do GOOS=... GOARCH=... CGO_ENABLED=0 GOTOOLCHAIN=local go build
  -trimpath ...`. CGO is already off for every release target, which is consistent with (and
  arguably requires) a pure-Go SQLite driver like modernc.org/sqlite if one is approved — a cgo
  driver (mattn/go-sqlite3) would break this build outright.
- `embed_test.go` (repo root, package `styrman`) — `TestFilesMatchTree` and (grep hit only, not
  read in full) `TestEmbedHoldsOnlyTrackedFiles` police that `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`,
  `commands/`, `rules/` on disk exactly match what's embedded — irrelevant to go.mod dependencies,
  no test polices "no dependencies" mechanically; that constraint is REQUIREMENTS.md-only.
- `internal/harness/size_test.go:9-49` — `antigravityRulesBlockBytes = 24000` (Antigravity's real
  cutoff, BUG-085), `renderedContextBudgetBytes = 22000` (this repo's self-imposed ceiling, ADR-035,
  8% margin, "never raised by an implementer"). `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` sums
  `RenderContext(...)` output + every `rules/<name>.md` raw byte length and fails over budget.
- `context/AGENTS.md` (18,448 bytes) + `context/dev-setup.md` (2,583 bytes) = 21,031 bytes measured
  by `wc -c` (a rough proxy for the rendered/summed total the test checks; not identical since
  `RenderContext` may add wrapper bytes and rules/*.md also count) — margin to 22,000 is under
  ~1,000 bytes on this proxy, likely tighter once rules/*.md are included. "A few lines" of
  index/search guidance will require pruning elsewhere.

## Longest paragraphs in context/AGENTS.md (candidates to shrink if room is needed)
- Line 33 (~1,500 chars): "Skill = knowledge the main thread loads while working. Subagent =
  judgement independent of the author..." — dense, multi-topic (skill vs subagent, per-dispatch
  budget repetition rule, TaskStop handling).
- Line 51 (~1,450 chars): the git hygiene hard rule (heredoc/numstat, escape-character check,
  `rm -r` guard, post-delete/dispatch stop-sign checks) — four distinct sub-rules crammed into one
  bullet.
- Line 55 (~1,350 chars): "A behaviour change includes the text that DESCRIBES it..." — the
  description/coverage/vocabulary/claim-reversal rule, itself already dense.
- Line 57 (~1,050 chars): the "Silence from your own instrumentation is not evidence" mutation/
  monitor-validation rule, cross-references `review-standards` § 2 (partially already delegated to
  a skill — a template for delegating more).
- Line 5 (~750 chars): the operator-preferences paragraph (SHORT LIST / ONE NUMBERED TABLE rules) —
  stable, unlikely to be a pruning target since it governs interaction style broadly.
Not read in detail against actual redundancy — a real pruning pass needs the operator's read, not
just length ranking; flagging candidates only, per scope item 5's ask.

## Flows
- Verb dispatch: `os.Args[1:]` → `run(args, out)` → `cmd, rest := args[0], args[1:]` → shared
  `flag.FlagSet` parses `reorder(rest)` → `--from-zip` special-cased early (return before the main
  switch) → switch on `cmd` for verbs not needing a resolved source (`version`, `uninstall`,
  `report`) → `harness.ResolveSource(*repoFlag, home, buildVersion())` → second switch for
  `install`/`sync`, and (not fully traced past line ~180) presumably further cases for `status`,
  `diff`, `update`, `list`, `render`, `adopt`. New `index`/`search` verbs would each need a case in
  one of these two switches (likely the first, since building/querying an index needs no vendor
  resolution) plus a handler function mirroring existing ones (e.g. `report()` at main.go, `report`
  case).
- Report/redaction flow: `sh-agent report` → `Collect(home)` (report.go:235) reads a fixed name
  list under `~/.config/sh-agent/`, redacts each, builds a `Collection` → (not traced further)
  presumably pushed via a throwaway git clone per REQUIREMENTS R8/R9. A global `index.db` sits
  beside these files but outside the allowlist, so it is structurally excluded without code changes
  — confirm this is deliberate and durable (e.g. a comment or explicit test) rather than incidental.

## Conventions
- Every verb's usage line, doc comment, and (if it appears in the README mermaid map) the map
  itself are kept in sync by convention/test, not fully cross-tested; `TestHarnessMap` only checks
  map→usage, not usage→doc-comment or doc-comment→map.
- New `~/.config/sh-agent/` content gets documented in `ConfigDir`'s doc comment (state.go:71-75)
  and, if it should never be reported, an explicit `Skipped` entry pattern is already used in
  `Collect()` for absent/non-regular files — mirror that for a deliberately-excluded `index.db`.
- Trail record formats (from bugs/INDEX.md, a BUG file, and DECISIONS.md headings observed):
  - `bugs/INDEX.md` table: `| ID | Date | Area | Status | Symptom | Prevention |` with rows like
    `| BUG-105 | 2026-09-29 | skills/preflight (release gate verdict) | open | <symptom> |
    <prevention> |`; a second "Graduated" table exists elsewhere in the same file (not fully read)
    for prevention rules that made it into AGENTS.md/a rule/skill/agent/test.
  - BUG file frontmatter: `owner: bugs`, `date: 2026-09-29`, `id: BUG-105`, `status: open`,
    `area: skills/preflight (release gate verdict)`; body sections `## Symptom`, `## Repro`,
    `## Root cause`, `## Fix`.
  - `DECISIONS.md` ADR heading pattern: `## ADR-NNN: <title>     (<date>) — <Status>`, statuses
    seen: `Accepted`, `Superseded by ADR-041`, `Accepted; its one-file refusal superseded by
    ADR-041`, `Accepted; superseded in part by ADR-044 (...)`, `Accepted, amends ADR-042`.
  - `handoffs/` and `changes/` filenames: `$(date +%F-%H%M)-<slug>.md` per project AGENTS.md.
  - Trail artifacts consistently start with YAML frontmatter `owner:` + `date:`.

## Risks / constraints (REQUIREMENTS.md, read in full for R1–R9 + Known limits + Non-goals)
- **R4 (blocking):** "`sh-agent` is a single Go binary with no dependencies." Project AGENTS.md:
  "Stdlib only in the Go code. The binary is a file copier with a manifest; it does not need a
  dependency." Adding `modernc.org/sqlite` directly contradicts both. Per the global rule,
  REQUIREMENTS.md is "immutable without the operator's explicit approval": propose the exact edit →
  approval → ADR → update REQUIREMENTS.md and ROADMAP.md in one commit, BEFORE implementation.
  This is the single largest open item — flag to the operator as a SHORT LIST choice (amend R4 vs.
  find a stdlib-only approach vs. defer) rather than routing around it.
- **R7:** "The harness's own state (manifest, feedback log, the harness proposal queue, the
  cross-project index) lives in `~/.config/sh-agent/` and nowhere else." A global `index.db` there
  is consistent with R7's location rule in spirit, but R7 already uses the term "the cross-project
  index" for something else (apparently the retros.jsonl-derived concept referenced in state.go)
  — naming needs reconciling with the operator, not necessarily blocking.
- **R8:** "no vendored mirror inside a consumer project, no per-project copy, no service." The
  per-project `.agents/scratch/index.db` is scratch — gitignored, ephemeral, explicitly rebuildable
  from git per the feature scope ("reconciled against `git ls-files -s` + `git status` before every
  query") — this reads as consistent with R8 (it is not a copy of harness state, it is a derived
  cache of the project's own trail), but confirm with the operator since R8 is specifically about
  the harness's OWN delivery channel, and this feature is adjacent but not identical territory.
- **Project AGENTS.md rule 6** ("Changing a path is a design question... lands in ONE commit with
  the code, the docs and the map"): this rule is about the delivery map (install/update/report/
  release paths), not about adding a verb; `index`/`search` do not appear to be "a line on the map"
  under R9's four procedures, so the map likely does not need editing for the verbs themselves —
  only if the feature's rollout is later folded into report/update (unlikely, out of scope here).
- **Known limits / renderedContextBudgetBytes:** the 22,000-byte ceiling is explicitly "never
  raised by an implementer" (size_test.go:17-18 comment) — a hard constraint, not a target to
  negotiate; any context/AGENTS.md addition is paid for by deletion/merge/moving text to a skill.
- **Blast radius of editing context/AGENTS.md:** this file (verified identical in content to the
  `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` shown for THIS session) is the single global context deployed to every
  project via `sh-agent install`; editing it to mention index/search changes behavior for every
  project using the harness, not just this feature's target repo. Treat any edit there as a
  "Feature" under the project's own gates (design question), and prefer putting most detail in a
  skill (`skills/<name>/SKILL.md`) with only a short trigger line in context/AGENTS.md — this
  matches the existing pattern (`review-standards` is already referenced this way from a dense
  hard rule at line 57).

## Not examined
- Full `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` switch statement past ~line 180 (status/diff/update/list/render/adopt
  cases) — only install/sync case partially read; a new-verb author should read the rest before
  writing a case, but the pattern (case → dedicated handler function, e.g. `report()`) is clear
  enough from what was read.
- `internal/harness/repo.go`, `pathguard.go`, `inventory.go` — likely relevant to how a project's
  tracked files / `.agents/docs/` tree would be walked for the per-project index, not read.
- `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-03-verify-sandbox.md` and `skill-matrix.md` in full — only
  `2026-09-16-linkshelf-simulation.md`'s header/setup/checklist tables were read. That file does
  show a usable pattern for the scope's "later" sandboxed token-measurement runs: detached lanes
  per CLI with a status file, `audit.py` (transcripts) for post-hoc analysis, and `--allowedTools`
  lists that already include `sqlite3` in at least one prior sandbox run — a precedent worth
  reusing rather than re-deriving.
- Exact regex/parsing details for BUG frontmatter fields beyond what one file showed, and the
  bugs/INDEX.md "Graduated" table's exact columns (not scrolled to).
- `internal/harness/derive.go` (Claude→Antigravity agent translation) and `internal/harness/plan.go`
  (what installs where) — relevant if a skill for index/search needs agent-visible tool grants
  (`toolMap` in derive.go, per project AGENTS.md "Rules for working here") — not read this pass.
- Whether any existing test asserts go.mod has zero `require` entries (none found via search, but
  search was pattern-based, not exhaustive).

## Open questions
- Does the operator want a REQUIREMENTS.md R4 amendment (ADR) approved BEFORE any implementation,
  or should recon instead explore a stdlib-only alternative (e.g. shelling out to a system
  `sqlite3` binary, which is itself a dependency of a different kind and likely no better under R4;
  or a much simpler non-SQLite grep/JSON index) as a competing option to present?
- Where would `--query`/`--limit`-type flags for `search` live given the single shared FlagSet
  parsed once for every verb — a new per-verb sub-FlagSet pattern, or positional args via
  `reorder()`? No precedent exists in this codebase today.
- How should the global `index.db`'s existence be reconciled with R7's existing term "the
  cross-project index" (currently = retros.jsonl-derived), to avoid two different things sharing
  one name in the trail and in context/AGENTS.md.

title: Research — memory for Antigravity, and `prompt-audit` for both CLIs (2026-09-29)
body:
# Research — memory for Antigravity, and `prompt-audit` for both CLIs   (2026-09-29)

## Questions

The operator asked, 2026-09-29: (1) "Do some broader research on internet and github if you find anything for antigravity" — memory, knowledge and "dreaming" features or plugins for the Antigravity editor and the `agy` CLI; (2) "do a check if there are a ./claude-api prompt-audit that we can implement for agy and claude in this harness." Light mode: research, compare, recommend. Follow-on to `plans/2026-09-29-dream-skill.md`.

## Answer in brief

1. **Antigravity has no memory feature the harness can use, and nothing to adopt.** The editor generates Knowledge Items (auto-extracted at conversation end, viewable in the Agent Manager, stored under `~/.gemini/antigravity/knowledge/`), but the feature has no docs page (the one Google staff linked now 404s), two forum threads report it never firing, and the CLI does not expose it: no docs, no help entry, no settings key, and on this box `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/knowledge/` holds only a lock file. Every community memory project for agy runs on hooks, a daemon, or a cloud service, which the harness rules out; the two hook-free ones re-do what the trail already does. Recommendation: nothing; the dream plan stays Claude Code only, and the trail is agy's memory.
2. **`prompt-audit` exists and can run on both CLIs.** It is a subcommand of Anthropic's `claude-api` skill: one 47 KB reference file, Apache-2.0, that audits prompts and agent configuration files (`AGENTS.md`, rules, skills, commands, subagents) for dated patterns and stale or contradicting instructions, and produces a report plus a proposed diff, never applying. On Claude Code it is bundled and runs today as `/claude-api prompt-audit`; agy has no copy. Recommendation: vendor the reference into a harness skill `prompt-audit` (option 2 below) so both CLIs run the same audit over `context/`, `agents/`, `skills/`, `commands/` and `rules/`, with the bug index as provenance.

## Part 1 — Antigravity memory

### What exists (verified 2026-09-29)

| Surface | Finding | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Editor (Antigravity 2.0) Knowledge Items | Auto-extracted from conversations; no setup; viewable in the Agent Manager; on disk as `~/.gemini/antigravity/knowledge/<item>/` with `metadata.json` and `artifacts/` | launch blog 2025-11-18; Google staff on the forum 2026-03-03; two export tools that read the directory |
| Editor KIs, reliability | Two forum threads (Dec 2025 to May 2026) report KIs never generated; escalated as a possible bug, no resolution posted | discuss.ai.google.dev threads 111234, 126774 |
| Editor KIs, docs | No docs page; `antigravity.google/docs/knowledge` is a 404; the docs nav has no Knowledge or Memory entry | fetched 2026-09-29 |
| CLI (`agy` 1.2.13) | No memory feature: docs overview and changelog say nothing; `agy --help` has no memory verb; `settings.json` has no memory key. The binary links the editor's Knowledge Base code (`KnowledgeBaseItem`, `GetUserMemories`, `GetCascadeMemories`, `knowledge_base_enabled`); `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/knowledge/` exists with only `knowledge.lock` (created 2026-09-17, never written); `cli.log` never mentions knowledge | this box, `strings $(which agy)`, `agy changelog` |
| CLI, its own summaries | `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversation_summaries.db` exists; one community project (`agy-dreamer`) reads it as its consolidation input | this box; github.com/j-steve/agy-dreamer |
| CLI plugin system | `agy plugin install <path>` (local path; the help also says `plugin@marketplace`), `import` from gemini or claude, `link <mp> <target>`; a plugin is `plugin.json` plus `skills/`, `agents/`, `rules/`, `mcp_config.json`, `hooks.json`. The marketplace is in-app (editor v2.18.1, 2026-09-28); no CLI marketplace verb documented; no memory plugin named in it | antigravity.google/docs/plugins; `agy plugin help` |
| Google announcements 2026 | I/O 2026 introduced the CLI; changelog through editor v2.18.1 and agy 1.2.13 has hooks (v2.11.0, agent-declared hooks v2.17.0) and the marketplace, and zero entries on knowledge, memory, learning or consolidation. No "dreaming" exists or is announced | changelog, I/O post |

### Community projects (GitHub, web-only survey; stars as shown on 2026-09-29)

| Project | Mechanism | Needs | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| thedotmack/claude-mem (94.9k★) | `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json` (5 events) + MCP + `GEMINI.md` injection | hooks + local Node worker daemon | agy hooks target 1.2.1; several open schema-breakage issues; editor support closed "not planned" |
| Mem0 plugin v0.3.1 | PreInvocation / PostToolUse / Stop hooks + MCP `search_memories` + 6 skills | hooks, cloud API key, Python 3.10+ | no consolidation |
| mahirocoko/agy-memory-layer (2★, v1.23.0 2026-09-27) | plugin with PreInvocation / PreToolUse hooks; skills `/dream`, `/remember`, `/palace`; git-backed `~/.gemini/memory/` | hooks | `/dream` is regex by default, LLM reflection only by hand; human-gated |
| atlaso-labs/antigravity (0★) | SessionStart / PreInvocation / Stop hooks + MCP + skill + rules | hooks, Atlaso cloud | — |
| Digital-Process-Tools/claude-remember (186★) | hooks; Haiku-compressed session → daily → weekly summaries | hooks | no SessionEnd analogue on agy |
| HydStAn/agy-memory-engine (34★) | MCP + hooks → SQLite FTS5 | hooks + worker every 5 min | — |
| j-steve/agy-dreamer (0★) | cron 03:00 reads `conversation_summaries.db`, writes `~/.gemini/config/dreaming/` | cron daemon | closest to "dreaming"; three commits |
| nowledge-co, blackmoon87/antigravity-mem | hooks + MCP + daemon | server or daemon | — |
| thevisionhub/agent-sleep (1★) | MCP tool `agent_sleep_consolidate` | MCP server only | hook-free |
| feodus/antigravity-memory-bank (9★, 2025-12) | rules + markdown files autoloaded in planning mode | nothing | hook-free; the trail (`handoffs/`, `bugs/`, `retros/`) already is this |

### Comparison

| Approach | Pros | Cons | Complexity | Cost | Maturity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. Nothing; the trail is agy's memory; re-check the CLI store after updates | no new store, no hooks, no daemon; matches project rule 1 | agy carries nothing across sessions beyond what a session reads from the trail | none | none | the trail: in use since 2026-09-03 |
| B. A hook-based plugin (claude-mem, Mem0, agy-memory-layer, claude-remember) | real capture across sessions | hooks and a daemon or cloud key; a second store beside the trail and Claude's auto memory; agy hook schema still breaking | medium | daemon or API key per machine | claude-mem mature on Claude Code, fragile on agy |
| C. A hook-free consolidation (agent-sleep MCP, or a harness skill reading `conversation_summaries.db`) | no hooks | reads an undocumented sqlite the CLI owns; an MCP server to run; nothing writes back into a store agy loads | medium | low | one to three commits each |
| D. Wait for the CLI's own Knowledge Base | first-party, code already linked in | undocumented, no switch, editor version unreliable | none now | none | not shipped |

### Recommendation: A

Nothing to adopt. Every real option needs hooks (project rule 1 and the global no-hooks rule) or a daemon; the hook-free ones duplicate the trail. The dream plan's Out section stands: the skill reads Claude Code's store only. Two lines to keep: re-check `ls ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/knowledge/` after each agy update (already in the dream plan's Risks), and note that `conversation_summaries.db` is the input a future CLI-side consolidation would read, if the operator ever wants one.

## Part 2 — `prompt-audit`

### What it is

- A subcommand of Anthropic's `claude-api` skill (github.com/anthropics/skills, `skills/claude-api/`, Apache-2.0 per its `LICENSE.txt`). The bare invocation `/claude-api prompt-audit` reads `shared/prompt-audit.md` and executes it. On Claude Code the skill is bundled with the CLI (session-scoped extraction; this session's copy is at Claude Code 2.1.283). agy has no copy: it is not a plugin and not in any agy marketplace.
- The reference is one file: 47,233 bytes bundled, 48,983 bytes upstream at commit `8a1541c` (2026-09-29; the upstream adds Claude Sonnet 5.5 rows). It cites `shared/model-migration.md` twelve times and `shared/prompt-caching.md` once, all for API request code (which model 400s on which parameter). For a configuration repository those rows are `not applicable`; the file says so itself ("a configuration repository mostly Groups 1 and 2").
- What it does, in order: establish scope and target model without asking; inventory every file that reaches the model (`AGENTS.md`, rules, skills and their references, commands, subagent definitions); `git blame` for provenance ("which failure, on which model, did this prevent"); classify every line ("could the model already know this?"); scan four groups: dated prompt text (pressure language, scaffolds, over-specification, fossils, prohibition clusters), brittle configuration files (volatile paths and flags, contradicting files, history narratives, recency-trap rules), tool descriptions, request config; then a report (`file:line`, evidence, pattern, why obsolete, confidence, action) and a proposed diff, one finding per hunk, never applied unless the request said so. A keep list protects context, exact scripts for fragile operations, prohibitions against demonstrated failures, and working redundancy.

### Fit with this harness

- **The shape matches.** The harness is a configuration repository: `context/AGENTS.md` (21,539 of 22,000 bytes, ADR-035), seven agents, 27 skills, commands and rules. Group 2 ("brittle skill and configuration files": volatile paths, contradicting files, one session's stumble as a permanent rule) is the harness's known failure mode: BUG-095 and the 2026-09-28 retro were four review rounds over rules that contradicted their neighbours.
- **Provenance is on disk.** The audit's central question per prohibitive line is which failure it prevents. Here every such line is meant to trace to a `bugs/INDEX.md` row or an ADR; keep-list item 5 then protects it, and a line with no row is the finding. A quick signal count: `never` appears 29 times in `context/AGENTS.md` and 23 in `agents/verifier.md`; caps-lock boosters (MUST, NEVER, ALWAYS, CRITICAL, IMPORTANT) zero times in any of them.
- **Two target models, not one.** The reference reasons about Claude's documented behaviour. The files it would audit here are read by Claude Code and by Gemini on agy. A finding grounded only in Claude's behaviour ("current models are proactive by default") is `flag`, not `remove`, until it holds for both; a stale-fact or conflict finding (Group 2) is model-independent and stays actionable. This is the one adaptation the harness wording must add.
- **What it cannot do here:** Group 4 (request config, API fossils) has no surface in this repository; the twelve `model-migration.md` cross-references are unreachable in a vendored copy and matter only for that group.

### Comparison

| Approach | Pros | Cons | Complexity | Cost | Maturity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Claude Code only: run `/claude-api prompt-audit` as bundled, record the report in `reviews/` | zero harness change; always the current Anthropic text | not on agy; the bundled copy moves with the Claude Code version, so two machines audit against two texts; the two-model caveat lives nowhere | none | none | shipped |
| 2. Vendor the reference as a harness skill `prompt-audit` (thin `SKILL.md`, `references/prompt-audit.md` verbatim at a pin, `LICENSE.txt`, row in `VENDORED.md`) | same audit on both CLIs; pinned text, updated on purpose; the harness `SKILL.md` adds scope, provenance and the two-model rule; report goes to `<docs-root>/reviews/<date>-prompt-audit.md` | a 47 KB reference to re-vendor at each pin; a fork by the vendoring rule (the harness `SKILL.md` is the fork, the reference stays verbatim) | one sitting: file drop, `VENDORED.md` row, skill-matrix row, one behavioural run per CLI | none | upstream: active, Apache-2.0 |
| 3. A `/review --prompts` lens dispatching `reviewer` with the reference | reuses the review record and the report-only contract | `reviewer` runs on sonnet with a fixed report template the audit does not fit; the audit is judgment-heavy over the harness's own rules and wants the main model; adds a lens to a 66-line skill | medium | none | — |
| 4. Install the `claude-api` plugin on agy (`agy plugin import claude`, or a marketplace link) | whole skill, not one file | 1.8 MB, 79 files, most of it SDK code guides the harness never needs; `agy plugin install` takes a local path only per the docs; plugin import is untested here and the harness rules say a skill is deployed by `sh-agent install`, not by a vendor's plugin system | medium | none | untested |

### Recommendation: 2 — decided: option 3 (operator, 2026-09-29)

The operator chose option 3, a `/review --prompts` lens; built the same day (`changes/2026-09-29-1251-review-prompts-lens.md`). The reference is vendored under `skills/review-standards/references/prompt-audit/`, not a new skill.

Vendor `prompt-audit.md` verbatim (pin `8a1541c`, Apache-2.0, `LICENSE.txt` beside it) under `skills/prompt-audit/references/`, with a harness `SKILL.md` that says: scope is `context/`, `agents/`, every skill under `skills/` not in `VENDORED.md`, `commands/` and `rules/`, or the paths the user names; provenance comes from `bugs/INDEX.md`, `DECISIONS.md` and `git blame`, and a prohibition with a row is keep-list item 5; the target is both vendors, so a Claude-only rationale is `flag`; Group 4 is `not applicable` here; the report is written to `<docs-root>/reviews/<date>-prompt-audit.md` and nothing is applied. Run it by hand, and from `/retro` when a model release lands (the reference's own re-audit trigger). It is the only option that gives agy the audit at all, and the harness already has the vendoring path for it (`VENDORED.md`, the `anti-ui-slop` precedent for a bundled licence).

What approving it would do: a Task under the Definition of Done (one sitting, no design question left): the skill directory, the `VENDORED.md` row, a `skill-matrix.md` row, `sh-agent install` into a scratch home, one behavioural run per CLI on a fixture with a seeded contradiction and a seeded dead path (expect both found, nothing applied), `/review --docs` over the range, then a first real run over `context/` with the report in `reviews/`, put to the operator hunk by hunk.

## Not proposed

- Running `/claude-api prompt-audit` over this repository now: the operator asked whether it can be implemented, not for the audit; its findings over `context/AGENTS.md` would be a review round in their own right and belong to the approved task.
- Any change to the dream plan's design: Part 1 confirms its Out section.

title: Research — memory and dreaming as subagents, the same on Claude Code and Antigravity (2026-09-29)
body:
# Research — memory and dreaming as subagents, the same on Claude Code and Antigravity   (2026-09-29)

## Question

The operator, 2026-09-29, while the dream skill was in its cold-reader check: "Cant we build dreaming and memory as a subagents that triggers when something in the project/conversation highlights to generate a skill/rule or procedure? Think about this later when you are done. I want them to work the same for claude and agy." Light mode: what the harness already has, what a subagent design would add, three ways to build it, one recommendation.

## Answer in brief

1. **The loop exists; its capture side is in-thread and its store is Claude-only.** Capture: `feedback-log` (a correction → one line in `~/.config/sh-agent/feedback.jsonl`) and Claude Code's auto memory (Claude writes files under `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`, Claude-only). Consolidation: `/dream` (auto memory → verdicts → promotions), `/distill` (third repeat → a skill draft), `/retro` (corrections and trail → proposals). Everything but the auto memory store already runs the same on both CLIs, because skills deploy verbatim and agents are derived for agy.
2. **A trigger "when something highlights" is the main agent noticing.** The harness forbids hooks and timers, and neither CLI fires a subagent on its own. Every trigger the harness has today is a rule in the context that the main agent applies (`feedback-log` on a correction, `/distill` on the third repeat, `/retro` on two corrections). A subagent design keeps that: the main agent dispatches when a rule fires; the subagent brings independent judgement and its own artifact, never the conversation (context § Work).
3. **Recommendation: one new subagent, `dreamer`, plus a vendor-neutral store; keep capture in-thread.** The consolidation judgement (is this a rule, a skill, a procedure, or nothing?) is the part that benefits from an author-independent reader, and it is heavy enough to earn a dispatch. Capture is a one-line append at the moment of the correction; a dispatch per correction would cost more than it adds and the subagent could not see the exchange anyway. Vendor parity comes from where the store lives, not from who writes it: point Claude Code's auto memory at a harness-owned per-project directory (`autoMemoryDirectory` in `.claude/settings.local.json`, written by `/init-project`), so Claude writes natively and agy reads the same files under the Resume Protocol and the `dreamer` reads them on both.

## What each CLI offers (verified 2026-09-29)

| | Claude Code 2.1.284 | Antigravity CLI 1.2.13 |
|---|---|---|
| Native memory | auto memory: `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`, `MEMORY.md` index loaded at start (200 lines / 25 KB), topic files on demand; `autoMemoryDirectory` from any settings scope (`code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md` § Storage location) | none (`plans/2026-09-29-research-memory-and-prompt-audit.md` Part 1) |
| Subagents | `agents/*.md`, tools mapped by `internal/harness/derive.go` | the same definitions, derived at install (`agent.md`, `subagent: true`) |
| Subagent memory | a subagent may keep its own auto memory (`memory` field, docs § How it works) — Claude-only | none |
| Event triggers | hooks (forbidden here) | hooks (forbidden here) |
| What a subagent sees | its dispatch text and the files it reads; never the conversation | the same |

## Three ways to build it

| Approach | Pros | Cons | Complexity | Cost | Maturity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. Status quo plus `/dream` (skills in-thread; store stays Claude's) | nothing new; every skill already runs on both CLIs | agy has no store to consolidate; the consolidation judgement is the author's own | none | none | shipped today |
| B. `dreamer` subagent + harness-owned store via `autoMemoryDirectory` (recommended) | independent judgement on what becomes a rule, skill or procedure; one store both CLIs read, Claude writes natively; no hooks; a file drop (agent) plus one `/init-project` edit | the store's location is a per-project setting `/init-project` must write (`.claude/settings.local.json`, gitignored, honoured only in a trusted workspace); agy sessions write to the store only through the agent, since agy has no native writer | one sitting plus behavioural runs on both CLIs | none | agents on both vendors: proven by every harness agent |
| C. `memory` and `dreamer` subagents, store in the project trail (`.agents/docs/memory/`, committed) | cross-machine, reviewable in git | memory about the operator (`user` type) lands in every project's history; a capture dispatch per correction is slow and blind to the exchange; duplicates `feedback.jsonl` and the handoffs | medium | none | — |
| D. Subagents that write rules and skills directly | "generate a skill/rule" literally | no gate: a rule an agent changes on its own is the weaker home (global Hard rules on `REQUIREMENTS.md`); bypasses `/retro`'s promotion check and the cold read | low | none | rejected |

## Recommendation: B — decided: B (operator, "Option B", 2026-09-29); plan `plans/2026-09-29-dreamer-memory-loop.md`, spec `specs/sh-agent/memory-loop.md`; the store's location was then moved inside the project (`.agents/memory/`, gitignored) on the operator's "Option 2" the same day (plan D17), so the `~/.config/sh-agent/memory/<slug>/` path below is superseded

- **Store.** `~/.config/sh-agent/memory/<project slug>/`, the auto memory layout as is (`MEMORY.md` plus one file per fact, the frontmatter Claude writes). `/init-project` writes `{"autoMemoryDirectory": "~/.config/sh-agent/memory/<slug>"}` into `.claude/settings.local.json` (gitignored) so Claude Code reads and writes there natively; the context's Resume Protocol gains one clause so an agy session reads `MEMORY.md` from that directory at start; `sh-agent report` does not ship it: `internal/harness/report.go` sends an allowlist (`feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl`, `proposals/`), and memory stays out by design — the `dreamer` artifact in `retros/` is what carries learning into the project (corrected 2026-09-29 while planning; the first draft said the report would ship it). This keeps `/dream` unchanged (it resolves `autoMemoryDirectory` first).
- **`dreamer` agent** (`agents/dreamer.md`, tools Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write; sonnet). Input: the store path and the trail. Output: one artifact under `<docs-root>/retros/<date>-dreamer.md` listing what it would make — a rule (target file and the exact text), a skill (a draft `SKILL.md` under `.agents/scratch/`), or a procedure (a `references/` page) — each with the memories and trail rows that justify it, and what it left alone. It applies nothing; `/retro` and `/distill` consume its artifact as evidence (retro Step 1 source 8; distill's candidate list). Dispatched by `/retro` and `/dream`, and by the main agent when the distill trigger fires (third repeat) — a rule in the context's Learning loop, which the size budget (21,636 of 22,000 bytes) can take only if a sentence pays for it.
- **Capture stays in-thread.** `feedback-log` and Claude's own auto-memory writes are the capture; on agy the main agent writes the same memory file shape into the store when a rule fires (one Write, the frontmatter Claude uses), which is the only vendor gap left and closes it without a dispatch.
- **Not built:** a `memory` subagent (blind to the conversation, one dispatch per correction), timers or counters, any hook.

What approving it would do: a Feature under the feature skill — plan, cold-reader check, then phases: (1) `agents/dreamer.md` with behavioural runs on both CLIs (the agy sandbox procedure or the real-home smoke, per `AGENTS.md` § Testing), (2) the store move (`/init-project`, the resume clause, `/dream` unchanged), (3) `/retro` and `/distill` reading the artifact, (4) docs and the map are untouched (no delivery path changes; rule 3 does not fire).

## Not proposed

- Replacing `/dream` with the agent: the skill's verdict logic is what the agent would run; keep the skill as the in-thread path and let the agent load it.
- Auto-applying anything: every output stays a proposal until `/retro` or the operator says go.

title: Research — an embedded SQLite index (FTS5 + sqlite-vec) for the agent (2026-09-29)
body:
# Research — an embedded SQLite index (FTS5 + sqlite-vec) for the agent   (2026-09-29)

## Question

The operator asked, 2026-09-29, through `/research` (full mode): should the harness give the agent a local index inside a Git-tracked project, an embedded SQLite file using FTS5 for lexical search and sqlite-vec for dense vectors? Constraints: no daemon or server, a small storage footprint, and no binary index churn in Git. Wanted: a verdict (ADOPT, REJECT or CONDITIONAL); the boundary against Git and how branch switches, rebases and merges invalidate it; retrieval quality against LanceDB and against ripgrep, git grep and ctags; binary distribution and cross-compilation; failure modes; a decision matrix; and an exact adoption rule.

## Answer in brief

**Verdict: CONDITIONAL. SQLite is the right engine if the harness ever needs an index, but the harness does not need one today, so build nothing.**

- **The engine question is settled in SQLite's favour.** A pure-Go driver (`modernc.org/sqlite` v1.60.1) ships FTS5 and bundles sqlite-vec v0.1.9. Both were verified on this box: no cgo, a clean cross-compile to darwin/arm64, a single file, no daemon. LanceDB needs cgo over a Rust library through a thin Go SDK, and it grows a new version on every write.
- **The index question fails on this project's own numbers.** A full-tree `git grep` takes about 11 ms here. A query-time reconcile against Git (4 ms) plus an FTS5 query (under 1 ms) saves about 6 ms per search. It costs a dependency that R4 forbids, a new `sh-agent` verb, a cache that goes stale without hooks (R3 forbids them), and 3 to 23 MB of disk per checkout.
- **Dense vectors add a second, larger cost.** An embedding model must run somewhere. In-process means a model file of tens to hundreds of MB, and cgo for the fast runtimes. Otherwise it needs a daemon (Ollama) or a network API. Anthropic reports that Claude Code dropped its early local vector database for agentic grep. Published 2026 benchmarks find a small gain from fusing embeddings with lexical search, and no single retriever that wins.
- **The adoption rule is in § 4.** Adopt FTS5 when a measured search latency or recall failure exists and the operator approves the R4 edit. Add sqlite-vec only when a fixed query set on the project shows that fusion beats FTS5 plus grep by a stated margin.

## Measured on this repository (2026-09-29, Linux amd64, 16 cores, warm cache, go1.27.1)

Corpus: 1,033 tracked files, 7.9 MB of text. 859 of the files sit under `.agents/`, the trail.

| Measurement | Result |
|---|---|
| `git grep -n 'BUG-0'`, whole tree | 11 ms |
| `grep -rl` over every tracked file | 21 ms |
| `rg --hidden` / `git grep`, literal (web agent's run) | 13–14 ms / 10–12 ms |
| `git ls-files -s` (index blob IDs, 1,033 entries) | 1.6 ms |
| `git status --porcelain=v2` | 4 ms |
| FTS5 build, porter and trigram tables, Python sqlite 3.46.1 | 0.98 s |
| FTS5 BM25 query (three phrase and term queries) | 0.1–0.4 ms |
| FTS5 index, porter, content stored | 12.3 MB |
| FTS5 index, porter, contentless (`content=''`) | 3.4 MB |
| FTS5 index, trigram, content stored | 31.8 MB |
| FTS5 index, trigram, contentless | 22.9 MB |
| Go binary, stdlib only (baseline) | 2.3 MB |
| + `modernc.org/sqlite` (FTS5 trigram works) | 9.9 MB, 25 modules in the graph |
| + `modernc.org/sqlite/vec` (`vec_version()` = v0.1.9) | 10.7 MB |
| Cross-compile of both, `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0` | succeeds |
| sqlite-vec, 20,000 random 384-dim vectors, insert | 0.41 s |
| sqlite-vec, brute-force KNN k=10 over those vectors | 8–9 ms |
| sqlite-vec file after that insert | 32 MB database + 32 MB WAL, not yet checkpointed |
| `asg017/sqlite-vec-go-bindings/ncruces` v0.1.6, its README example | panics at startup ("i32.atomic.store invalid as feature threads is disabled"); fails to compile against current `ncruces/go-sqlite3` v0.35.6 |

The probe files were deleted after the run. The chunk count for real embeddings of this corpus was not measured. At 1 to 1.5 KB per chunk it would be roughly 5,000 to 8,000 vectors, which is under the 20,000 measured above.

## 1. Architectural role and Git hygiene

**The boundary.** Git (HEAD plus the working tree) is the only source of truth. The database is a derived, disposable cache: it is never committed, never read by a human, never the only copy of anything, and deleting it loses nothing but rebuild time. That rules out the "persistent storage" role for it. Anything worth keeping (a decision, a bug, a summary) belongs in a Markdown file in the trail, where Git versions it and review sees it. A cache that holds facts not in Git is a second memory store, which the 2026-09-29 memory research already rejected.

**Where it lives.** Under `.agents/scratch/index/`, which is already gitignored in every project `/init-project` scaffolds, so nothing new reaches `.gitignore`. It is not in `.git/`, which Git owns, and not in `~/.config/sh-agent/`, which R7 reserves for harness state. `git clean -fdx` deletes it, which is correct for a cache. A worktree gets its own index, because a worktree is a different working tree.

**Consistency across checkout, rebase and merge.** Key every indexed chunk by the Git blob ID of its file's content, never by path or mtime.

- The file table maps path to blob ID for the current view: the index blob IDs from `git ls-files -s` (1.6 ms here), plus a `git hash-object` of each path that `git status` reports dirty (4 ms here).
- Chunks and vectors are stored once per blob ID. A branch switch, rebase or merge changes the path-to-blob map. It re-chunks only blobs the database has never seen; switching back to a branch already visited costs nothing.
- Rebases rewrite commits but mostly keep blobs, so they are nearly free. A merge creates new blobs only for files it changed.
- Blobs no path references any more are garbage-collected on a size threshold, not on every switch.

**Invalidation is done at query time, never by a watcher.** There is no daemon (the constraint) and no hook (R3), so nothing learns about a checkout when it happens. Every query first runs the reconcile above, about 6 ms here, and indexes the difference before it answers. An index that answers without reconciling returns results from another branch. That is the one failure the design must make impossible, not merely unlikely.

**Why not mtime.** `git checkout` sets mtime to the checkout time, a same-second edit can keep the recorded mtime (Git's own "racy git" problem), and a copy with `cp -p` or a restore from an archive keeps old mtimes on new content. Blob IDs have none of these problems.

## 2. Retrieval capability against overhead

### What each option retrieves

| Query shape | grep / git grep / rg | ctags / repo map | FTS5 BM25 | FTS5 + sqlite-vec | LanceDB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Exact identifier, error string, BUG number | exact, fastest | symbols only | exact (trigram) or token | same as FTS5 | BM25 via Lance FTS |
| Regex (`func [A-Z]\w+Test`) | yes | no | no | no | no |
| Ranked "most relevant files for these words" | no ranking; the agent reads hit counts | ranks by reference graph | BM25 | BM25 fused with vector score | BM25 + vector |
| Paraphrase with no shared words ("where do we refuse unsafe archives" for the zip guard) | agent must guess synonyms | no | no, unless stems match | yes, the one real gain | yes |
| Definition and callers of a symbol | approximate | yes (ctags defs; Aider-style map adds refs) | no | no | no |

### Against LanceDB (a file-based columnar vector format)

- **Distribution.** The official Go SDK is v0.1.2 (2025-09-30), 61 stars. It is cgo over a prebuilt Rust static library you download separately. A cross-compile to darwin/arm64 from Linux needs that library for each target plus a C cross toolchain. The harness today ships a stdlib binary built with `go build`.
- **Growth.** Every write creates a new table version. Old versions stay until `optimize()` prunes them, after seven days by default. An index updated on every query-time reconcile writes often, so it grows until something compacts it.
- **What it wins.** Columnar storage and ANN indexes pay off from millions of vectors, and on multimodal data. Neither applies to a code and Markdown corpus of thousands of chunks.
- **Conclusion.** No property of this corpus needs LanceDB, and its distribution cost is the highest of the three.

### Against plain CLI tools (ripgrep, git grep, ctags)

- **Latency.** 11 to 21 ms for the whole tree here. The Linux kernel, about 70,000 files, searches in about 0.35 s (burntsushi.net/ripgrep, 2016). Grep latency stops mattering to an agent whose turn takes seconds only at kernel scale and above.
- **Freshness.** Grep reads the working tree, so it is never stale and has no invalidation logic. This is the property Boris Cherny names for Claude Code: "security, privacy, staleness, and reliability" (x.com/bcherny/status/2017824286489383315, 2026-02-01).
- **Availability.** `git grep` ships with Git. Both CLIs already expose a grep tool to the agent. `rg` is not installed on this box, but Claude Code bundles its own.
- **ctags.** It adds symbol definitions. For the Go code here, `go doc` and `gopls` already cover that, and the Go source is 31 files, 18 of them non-test.
- **What grep lacks** is ranking and paraphrase. The agent compensates by reformulating and reading, which costs tokens and turns, not latency.

### Binary distribution and process overhead

| Route | cgo | Cross-compile to darwin/arm64 from Linux | Binary delta | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `modernc.org/sqlite` + `/vec` | no | plain `go build` (verified) | +8.4 MB | FTS5 built in; sqlite-vec v0.1.9 bundled since 2026-03-15; verified working |
| `mattn/go-sqlite3` + sqlite-vec cgo bindings | yes | needs a C cross toolchain and a macOS SDK (osxcross or zig) | not measured | FTS5 only with a build tag |
| `ncruces/go-sqlite3` | no | plain `go build` | not measured | FTS5 opt-in per connection; own `ext/vec1` (IVF, "testing is insufficient"); the sqlite-vec binding for it is broken (measured) |
| LanceDB Go SDK | yes, over Rust | per-target prebuilt library + C toolchain | not measured | v0.1.2, thin |

Process overhead: SQLite runs inside the calling process, so there is nothing to start or keep alive. An embedding model is different. In-process options are a pure-Go MiniLM at about 4.5 ms per embedding (github.com/clems4ever/all-minilm-l6-v2-go), `hugot` on a pure-Go backend or on ONNX Runtime through cgo, or llama.cpp loaded as a shared library through purego. Each adds a model file: bge-small-en-v1.5 is 33M parameters, and jina-embeddings-v2-base-code is 161M. The alternatives are Ollama, which is a daemon, or a hosted API, which sends source off the machine.

## 3. Failure modes and bottlenecks

- **Concurrent access.** The harness runs parallel subagents and, on one machine, several sessions per checkout. WAL mode allows many readers and one writer across processes on one host. Every reconcile write must use `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` with a `busy_timeout`. A read transaction that later tries to write after another process committed fails with `SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT`, not a wait. WAL does not work on a network filesystem (sqlite.org/wal.html), so a checkout on NFS or a synced folder must fall back to grep. A reader inside a long read transaction also sees a snapshot older than the working tree another session just edited.
- **The verifier freeze.** The Definition of Done freezes the tree while the `verifier` runs. An index that writes at query time does not touch the tracked tree, so the freeze holds. An index stored inside the tree but outside `.agents/scratch/` would dirty `git status` and break the `sh-agent update` dirty-tree refusal.
- **Chunk invalidation on rapid edits.** The file is the unit: an edit re-chunks its file. For FTS5 that is sub-millisecond. For vectors it is the chunk count times the embed time, for example 50 chunks times 4.5 ms, about 0.23 s per file, paid on the next query after each edit. An agent that edits a file between every search pays it every time. AST-aware chunking adds a parser: the maintained tree-sitter Go bindings use cgo, and `go/ast` covers Go only. Chunking by heading and by blank line covers Markdown, which is 859 of 1,033 files here.
- **Embedding drift.** Vectors from two models, two model versions or two chunkers are not comparable, and mixing them degrades results silently rather than failing. The database needs a meta row (model ID, dimensions, chunker version) that forces a full drop and rebuild on any mismatch. A model upgrade becomes a full re-embed of every blob in the cache, not only of HEAD.
- **File growth.** FTS5 accumulates segments and tombstones under incremental updates until `optimize` runs. vec0 deletes do not shrink the file without `VACUUM`. The WAL grows until checkpointed: the probe left a 32 MB WAL beside a 32 MB database. Blob-keyed caching keeps every branch ever visited unless garbage-collected. The simplest bound: rebuild from scratch past a size threshold, since a full FTS5 build of this tree takes about one second.
- **Stale answers.** An index is wrong silently. Grep that finds nothing is honest about the tree it read. An index that skipped the reconcile, or that crashed half-way through one, answers from the past with the same confidence. This is the harness's own rule on silent instrumentation: "silence from your own instrumentation is not evidence".
- **Two stores of the same fact.** The trail already has curated indexes: `bugs/INDEX.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, and date-ordered file names. A search index over the trail competes with them for "where do I look first".

## 4. Recommendation and decision matrix

### Decision matrix

Scores run 1 to 5, higher is better, scored for this harness at this scale.

| Option | Latency | Portability | Git cleanliness | Search quality (lexical + semantic) | Maintenance overhead (5 = least) | Fits R3/R4 today |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. Agent-driven `git grep` / `rg` (today) | 4 (11–21 ms, never stale) | 5 (ships with Git and both CLIs) | 5 (no artifact) | 3 (exact and regex strong; no ranking, no paraphrase) | 5 | yes |
| B. A + ctags or a Go symbol map | 4 | 4 (universal-ctags not installed here) | 4 (a tags file to ignore) | 3.5 (adds definitions) | 4 | yes |
| C. SQLite FTS5 via `modernc.org/sqlite`, reconcile at query time | 5 (under 1 ms query + 6 ms reconcile) | 5 (pure Go, verified cross-compile) | 5 (gitignored scratch) | 3.5 (BM25 ranking; trigram for substrings) | 3 (invalidation code, growth, locks) | no: a dependency (R4); a new verb |
| D. C + sqlite-vec + an in-process model | 3 (embed on each changed file; 9 ms KNN at 20k) | 3 (pure Go possible; model file per machine; fast runtimes need cgo) | 5 | 4 (paraphrase recall; fusion gain small in published work) | 2 (model pin, drift, re-embed, growth) | no: dependencies, model distribution |
| E. LanceDB | 3 | 2 (cgo + per-target Rust library) | 4 (versions accumulate until pruned) | 4 | 2 | no |

### The adoption rule

Use **option A** (grep driven by the agent) while every one of these holds. All hold today.

1. A warm whole-tree `git grep` for a literal returns in under 500 ms. It is 11 ms here.
2. No named retrieval failure is on record: no BUG record whose root cause is "the agent did not find the file".
3. The corpus is text a model can grep for, not binary or generated material.

Use **option C** (SQLite FTS5 only) when all of these hold.

1. A trigger is measured, not assumed: condition 1 or 2 above fails, and the failure is recorded as a BUG with its measurement.
2. The operator approves an R4 edit that allows exactly one dependency, `modernc.org/sqlite`, with an ADR. cgo drivers stay out, because they break the plain `go build` cross-compile the release depends on.
3. The index is a derived cache under `.agents/scratch/`, keyed by blob ID, reconciled against `git ls-files -s` and `git status` before every query, with no watcher and no hook, and rebuilt from scratch in under 10 s.
4. The index is local only: WAL mode, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, `busy_timeout`, and a fallback to grep when the database is locked past the timeout, corrupt, or on a network filesystem.
5. Grep stays available and remains the tool for exact strings and regex. The index answers ranked and fuzzy queries only.

Add **sqlite-vec** to C (option D) only when all of these also hold.

1. A fixed query set of at least 30 of this project's own questions, including paraphrases with no shared vocabulary, shows BM25 fused with vectors beating BM25 plus agent grep by at least 10 points of recall@10. The query set is committed, and the result is recorded under `testing/`.
2. The embedding model runs in-process with no cgo, no daemon and no network, and it is pinned by name and hash. Otherwise the operator explicitly accepts which of the three the harness takes on.
3. The vector count stays under about 100,000. The sqlite-vec author puts brute-force latency at about 75 ms there (alexgarcia.xyz, 2024-08-01). Above that, wait for ANN indexes to ship stable (DiskANN and IVF are in v0.1.10-alpha only).
4. A meta row pins the model and chunker, and any mismatch forces a full rebuild.

Use **LanceDB** only when vectors reach the millions or the corpus is multimodal, and the harness has accepted cgo. Neither is on this project's horizon.

### Comparison (the research skill's table)

| Approach | Pros | Cons | Complexity | Cost | Maturity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. Agent grep (keep) | never stale; zero code; 11 ms here; what Claude Code and Codex CLI chose | no ranking, no paraphrase; more agent turns on vague questions | none | none | shipped in both CLIs |
| B. + symbol map | definitions and references | Go already has `go doc`/`gopls`; 31 Go files here | low | none | mature |
| C. SQLite FTS5 cache | sub-ms ranked search; pure Go; single file | a dependency against R4; invalidation code; saves ~6 ms here | medium | +7.6 MB binary; 3–23 MB per checkout | FTS5 mature; driver active (v1.60.1, 2026-09-29) |
| D. C + sqlite-vec | paraphrase recall | model distribution, drift, re-embed; sqlite-vec pre-1.0 after a 16-month gap between stable releases | high | model file + vectors per checkout | sqlite-vec v0.1.9 (2026-03-31), maintained again since 2026-03 |
| E. LanceDB | ANN at scale, multimodal | cgo over Rust; thin Go SDK; version growth | high | Rust library per target | Go SDK v0.1.2 |

### Recommendation: A, keep agent-driven grep; no index is built

C is the engine to reach for if the rule's triggers ever fire, and nothing else on the list comes close under R3 and R4. At today's scale, 11 ms searches and no recorded retrieval failure, an index would add a dependency, a cache that can lie, and a new verb, to save milliseconds the agent does not notice.

**Full mode stops here.** The research skill's Step 4 writes an integration spec and hands into the `feature` skill for the recommended option. The recommended option builds nothing, so no spec and no plan were written. If the operator chooses C or D instead, that is a Feature with three design questions for the operator first:

1. The R4 edit, as exact text for approval.
2. How the agent calls the index: a new `sh-agent search` verb, or an MCP server. An MCP server needs a vendor settings entry, which the non-goals forbid.
3. Whether the index covers the tracked tree only or also the trail.

## Sources

Web facts come from a research subagent's report, checked 2026-09-29. Dates are the sources' own. Two benchmark papers were located by search and not read in full: Agent Retrieval Bench (huggingface.co/papers/2607.24882, July 2026) and CORE-Bench (arxiv.org/abs/2606.11864).

- sqlite-vec releases, the v0.1.7 "back after a long hiatus" notes and issue #226: github.com/asg017/sqlite-vec
- sqlite-vec brute-force benchmarks: alexgarcia.xyz/blog/2024/sqlite-vec-stable-release (2024-08-01; figures as summarised, charts not read)
- `modernc.org/sqlite/vec`: pkg.go.dev/modernc.org/sqlite/vec (verified by build and run here)
- `ncruces/go-sqlite3` and `ext/vec1`: github.com/ncruces/go-sqlite3, sqlite.org/vec1/doc/trunk/doc/vec1.md
- FTS5 (BM25, trigram, external content, index sizes): sqlite.org/fts5.html
- WAL and network filesystems: sqlite.org/wal.html, sqlite.org/useovernet.html; busy handling: sqlite.org/rescode.html, sqlite.org/lang_transaction.html
- LanceDB Go SDK and versioning: github.com/lancedb/lancedb-go, docs.lancedb.com/tables/versioning
- Claude Code on RAG against agentic search: x.com/bcherny/status/2017824286489383315 (2026-02-01)
- Cursor's server-side index and Merkle sync: cursor.com/blog/secure-codebase-indexing (2026-01-27)
- Continue's deprecated `@Codebase`: docs.continue.dev/reference/deprecated-codebase
- Sourcegraph Cody dropping embeddings: sourcegraph.com/blog/how-cody-understands-your-codebase (2024-02-15)
- Augment on grep and SWE-bench: jxnl.co/writing/2025/09/11/why-grep-beat-embeddings-in-our-swe-bench-agent-lessons-from-augment
- Aider repo map: aider.chat/docs/repomap.html
- Pure-Go MiniLM throughput: github.com/clems4ever/all-minilm-l6-v2-go

## Not proposed

- Any change to `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `sh-agent`, a skill or the context. The recommendation is to build nothing.
- A skill that teaches the agent better grep habits. It was not asked for. The CLIs' own search tools and the trail's indexes already cover it.

title: Plan — `sh-agent search`: a project and a global SQLite index for the agent (2026-09-29)
body:
# Plan — `sh-agent search`: a project and a global SQLite index for the agent   (2026-09-29)

## Why

The operator, 2026-09-29, after the research record `plans/2026-09-29-research-sqlite-index.md`: "I have no problems to add this if it gives the agent a better understanding and more memory what it is doing. That is the whole point. Drift, searching through multiple files." Then, on the eight-row recommendation table (full versions in the conversation's scratch file, restated as D-rows below): "Go with your recommendations, start the phases", "make sure to add to the context how to use the database. Because having a database feels like a powerhouse in larger projects", "When everything is done I want you to run sandboxed projects that test the efficiency when building sample apps", and "audit the full project which services that will benefit of using the sqlite" (brief: `plans/2026-09-29-audit-search-consumers.md`).

Measured motivation (this project's transcripts, 2026-09-29): subagents spent 59% of their tool-output volume on file reads, 41% of that on trail files, and 583 of 827 reads loaded a whole file. Grep cannot rank, cannot find a claim restated in other words (BUG-027, BUG-097), and cannot answer "which records name this file" or "is this ADR superseded".

## Scope

In:
- A per-project index `.agents/scratch/search.db` over every tracked, modified and untracked-not-ignored text file of the git checkout, with a metadata graph of the trail (record IDs, status, date, cross-references, paths named).
- A global index `~/.config/sh-agent/search.db` over `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl`, `proposals/*.md` and the trail (docs root only) of every project that has run `sh-agent search` or `sh-agent index`.
- Two verbs: `sh-agent search` and `sh-agent index`. Both reconcile against git before answering. No service, no watcher, no hook.
- Instructions: a context entry (the operator's explicit ask) paid for by cuts elsewhere; one line in each agent and skill D13 names.
- A recall test (committed question set, a Go test behind an env var) that measures the index against a grep baseline and gates vectors.
- Sandboxed efficiency runs building sample apps, with and without the index, on both CLIs.
- The R4 edit, its ADR, the project `AGENTS.md` "stdlib only" restatement, docs.

Out:
- Vectors and an embedding model, unless the Phase 4 gate passes. If it passes, the model's delivery is a new path on the map and goes to the operator first (project rule 3); this plan then ends at the gate result.
- A service, watcher, daemon, MCP server or hook (R3, R8, project rule 1).
- A release. `/preflight` from the operator's own turn cuts it.
- Moving any record out of Markdown or JSONL. The databases are caches.

Follow-ups noted, not built: making the main agent use `sh-agent search` in real work (0 of 28 sessions; subagents with it as a fixed step did) — a design question for the operator (a step in the resume procedure, a skill, or leave it to subagents), found in: Phase 5 metrics.

## Surfaces touched

Recon brief: `plans/2026-09-29-recon-project-index.md`. Consumer audit: `plans/2026-09-29-audit-search-consumers.md`.

- `go.mod`, new `go.sum` — the one dependency.
- `internal/search/` — new package: open, reconcile, chunk, records, refs, query, global registry. Kept out of `internal/harness` so the installer's package does not import the driver.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` — doc comment (lines 1-15), `usage` (lines 38-58), the first verb switch (before `harness.ResolveSource`, line ~138: searching needs no harness tree, and a release-binary or zip place has none), new flags in the shared FlagSet and in `reorder`'s `takesValue` (line ~710).
- `internal/harness/state.go:71-75` — `ConfigDir` comment names `search.db`.
- `internal/harness/report.go:235-295` — `Collect` names `search.db` as skipped, never sent.
- `context/AGENTS.md` — the search entry and the cuts that pay for it; `size_test.go` budget unchanged.
- `agents/*.md`, `skills/*/SKILL.md` — one line each in the consumers D13 names.
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` R4, `AGENTS.md` (project) "Stdlib only" bullet and Setup/Layout, `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` (ADR), `README.md` verb list, `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md` (first build fetches modules), `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/` (a `search.md` spec), `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md` (rows for the changed agents and skills).

## Interfaces

### Commands

```
sh-agent search [--limit N] [--kind K] [--global] <words...>
sh-agent search --refs <BUG-NNN|ADR-NNN|path> [--kind K] [--global]
sh-agent search --open [--kind K] [--global]
sh-agent index [--global] [--rebuild]
```

- `<words...>` are joined with spaces and passed to FTS5 as a query of quoted terms ANDed (each word double-quoted, so `-`, `:` and `.` in `BUG-049` or `release.go` never reach FTS5 syntax). No hits for the AND query → retry once as OR and say so in the header line.
- `--limit` default 10; a value below 1 or above 50 is refused. At most 2 hits per file.
- `--kind` one of `bug adr plan change handoff review testing retro spec deploy trail code doc feedback proposal`. `feedback` and `proposal` exist only in the global index (Storage); `retro` covers both a trail `retros/` file and the global `retros.jsonl`. `trail` is every file under the docs root. It filters the hits of all three modes (`<words>`, `--refs`, `--open`) by the kind of the path each hit is printed at. For `--refs`, the ID's own record line is printed whatever the kind.
- `--refs X`: X matching `^(BUG|ADR)-\d{3}[a-z]?$` is an ID; anything else is a path, relative to the checkout root (a trailing `/` means a directory and matches every ref under it).
- `--open`: list records whose status is open — bugs with `status: open`, plans with an unticked box — one line each, `<path>:<line>  <kind> <id> <status> <date> <title>`, newest first, no limit. `--open` and `--refs` exclude each other and `<words>`.
- `--global`: query the global index instead. Every mode's output prefixes each path with the project's name, `<name>:<path>:<line>`; the files of `~/.config/sh-agent/` print as `~config:<file>:<line>`. `--refs X` with `--global` matches X in every project.
- `--rebuild` deletes this index's database files (the three names below, at this path only) and builds from scratch. `--global --rebuild` also drops the project registry, which lives in that file; each project re-registers on its next `search` or `index`, and the command prints how many registrations were dropped.
- `--limit`, `--kind`, `--refs` take values and join `takesValue` in `reorder`. `--global`, `--rebuild` are booleans. All five sit in the shared FlagSet, as every flag does today; the other verbs ignore them.
- Exit status: 0 with hits or with none (a "no hits" line is a result); 1 on any refusal or error.

Output of `search` (plain text, one hit per two lines; the snippet is one line, at most 200 characters, matched terms wrapped in `»«`):

```
search: 7 hits for "zip verify" (index current: 1,033 files, reconciled 4 changed in 38 ms)
.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md:355  adr ADR-039 Accepted; its one-file refusal superseded by ADR-041  2026-09-28
    … Release zips are signed, and `--from-zip` »verifies« them …
internal/harness/zip.go:88  code
    … // »verify« the »zip« against SHA256SUMS …
```

Output of `search --refs`:

```
ADR-040  .agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md:383  Superseded by ADR-041  2026-09-28  An unsigned zip needs `--unverified`
referenced by 6:
.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md:404  adr ADR-041 Accepted  2026-09-28
    … supersedes ADR-040 …
REQUIREMENTS.md:37  doc
    … (refused unless `--unverified`; ADR-040) …
```
For a path, the first line is `<path>  tracked|modified|untracked|absent` and then the references; for a directory (trailing `/`), it is `<dir>/  directory`.

Output of `index`: one line per count — `files`, `chunks`, `records`, `refs`, `changed` (this reconcile), `bytes` (database + WAL), `ms`.

### Storage

Per project: `<root>/.agents/scratch/search.db` (+ `-wal`, `-shm`). Global: `~/.config/sh-agent/search.db` (+ `-wal`, `-shm`), honouring `--home`. Driver `modernc.org/sqlite`, opened as `sql.Open("sqlite", "file:<path>?_pragma=journal_mode(WAL)&_pragma=busy_timeout(10000)&_pragma=foreign_keys(0)")`.

```sql
CREATE TABLE meta(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT);            -- schema=1, docs_root
CREATE TABLE projects(root TEXT PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, last_seen INTEGER); -- global only; per project: one row, itself
```
