```sql
CREATE TABLE files(project TEXT, path TEXT, oid TEXT, state TEXT, PRIMARY KEY(project, path)); -- state: tracked|modified|untracked
CREATE TABLE blobs(oid TEXT PRIMARY KEY, last_seen INTEGER);
CREATE TABLE chunks(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, oid TEXT, line INTEGER, heading TEXT, body TEXT);
CREATE INDEX chunks_oid ON chunks(oid);
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE chunks_fts USING fts5(heading, body, content='chunks', content_rowid='id', tokenize='porter unicode61');
CREATE TRIGGER chunks_ai AFTER INSERT ON chunks BEGIN
  INSERT INTO chunks_fts(rowid, heading, body) VALUES (new.id, new.heading, new.body);
END;
CREATE TRIGGER chunks_ad AFTER DELETE ON chunks BEGIN
  INSERT INTO chunks_fts(chunks_fts, rowid, heading, body) VALUES ('delete', old.id, old.heading, old.body);
END;
CREATE TABLE records(oid TEXT, id TEXT, line INTEGER, title TEXT, status TEXT, date TEXT);
CREATE INDEX records_id ON records(id);
CREATE TABLE refs(oid TEXT, line INTEGER, target TEXT);
CREATE INDEX refs_target ON refs(target);
```

Everything derived from content is keyed by the git blob ID (`oid`), so a blob seen on any branch is chunked once. `files` is the current view. A chunk row is never updated, only inserted and deleted; the two triggers are the only writers of `chunks_fts`, so the full-text index follows `chunks` on insert and on GC delete.

**Every query reads through `files`.** `search` joins `chunks_fts` → `chunks` (on `rowid = id`) → `files` (on `oid`, with `files.project` = the queried project; for `--global`, every registered project and `~config`). `--refs` joins `refs` → `files` on `oid`, and `--open` joins `records` → `files` on `oid`, the same way. A chunk, ref or record whose oid is in no current `files` row is never printed, which is what keeps another branch's content out of the answer. An oid current at two paths yields a hit at each path; the per-file cap applies per path. The printed path is always `files.path`.

Kind is derived from `files.path` at query time. Under the docs root, from its first directory: `bugs` → `bug`, `architecture` → `adr`, `plans` → `plan`, `changes` → `change`, `handoffs` → `handoff`, `reviews` → `review`, `testing` → `testing`, `retros` → `retro`, `specs` → `spec`, `deploy` → `deploy`, any other → `trail`. Outside it: `code` for extensions `go ts tsx js jsx mjs py sh rs java kt swift rb c h cc cpp cs sql tf`, else `doc`. `--kind trail` matches every kind under the docs root. The global index stores `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl` and `proposals/*.md` under project `~config` with their SHA-256 as `oid`, kind `feedback`, `retro`, `proposal`.

### Reconcile (before every query and every `index`)

1. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the working directory → root. Failure → refuse (Failure modes).
2. `git ls-files -s -z` → path, mode, oid for tracked entries. Mode `120000` (symlink) and `160000` (submodule) are skipped.
3. `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all` → modified and untracked paths (BUG-049: untracked files count). Their oids come from one `git hash-object --stdin-paths` call. Deleted paths leave the view.
4. A path whose content is binary (a NUL byte in its first 8 KiB) or larger than 1 MiB is skipped and not in `files`.
5. In one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction: replace `files` for this project with the new view; for every oid not in `blobs`, read the file and insert chunks, records and refs; set `last_seen` on every oid in the view; delete blobs (and their chunks, records, refs) not in any project's view whose `last_seen` is older than 14 days. After a transaction that changed anything: `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`.

### Chunking

- Markdown (`.md`): a chunk starts at each ATX heading; a chunk longer than 40 lines is split every 40 lines; `heading` is the nearest heading text.
- Everything else: windows of 40 lines, `heading` empty.
- `line` is the chunk's first line, 1-based. A hit's reported line is the first line in the chunk containing a matched term (found by a case-insensitive scan of the chunk for the query words), else the chunk's first line.

### Records (trail files only; docs root = `.agents/docs` if it exists, else `docs`)

Records and refs are parsed once per oid, when the oid is first indexed, using the first path at which the oid appears in that reconcile (`git ls-files` order, then `git status` order); the parser is chosen by that path. They are reported at every current path of the oid (D14).

- **Bug:** `<docs>/bugs/BUG-NNN*.md` → id from frontmatter `id:` else the file name's `BUG-NNN`; status from frontmatter `status:`; date from `date:`; title from the first `# ` heading.
- **ADR:** every line of `<docs>/architecture/DECISIONS.md` matching `^## (ADR-\d{3}[a-z]?): (.+?)\s+\((\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\) — (.+)$` → id, title, date, status (the whole text after the dash, e.g. `Accepted; superseded in part by ADR-044 (…)`).
- **Plan:** `<docs>/plans/*.md` → id is the docs-relative path; status `open: N unticked` when it has N lines matching `^- \[ \]` outside fenced blocks, else `closed`; `line` is the first such line. Fences follow the handoff skill's scan (`skills/handoff/SKILL.md:154`): a run of three or more backticks opens a block, a line of only a run of the same length closes it.
- **Other trail files:** id is the docs-relative path, date from frontmatter `date:`, status empty.

### Refs (every indexed file)

- IDs: `\b(BUG|ADR)-\d{3}[a-z]?\b`, target the ID.
- Paths: tokens matching `[A-Za-z0-9_.@-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_.@-]+)+/?` or `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.(go|md|ts|tsx|js|json|yaml|yml|sh|py|toml|mod|sum|sql|tf)`, with a trailing `:NN` or `:NN-NN` and trailing `.,;:)` removed and a leading `./` or `a/`, `b/` (diff prefixes) removed. Stored as written. A record's references to its own ID are kept.
- At query time `--refs X` matches targets equal to X, or equal to X without the docs-root prefix (the trail writes `plans/x.md` for `.agents/docs/plans/x.md`). A directory X (trailing `/`) matches targets with that prefix. No basename matching.

### Global registry

Every `search` and `index` run inside a git checkout, with or without `--global`, reconciles that checkout's own index and upserts `(root, base name, now)` into the global `projects` table first, so a project's first run being `--global` still includes itself. Run outside a git checkout, `--global` skips that step and does not refuse; plain `search` and `index` refuse there as Failure modes says. `--global` then reconciles `~config` from `~/.config/sh-agent/`, then each registered project: a root that no longer exists or is no longer a git checkout loses its registration and its rows (a note line says so); for the others, steps 2-5 limited to paths under the docs root. Two registered roots with the same base name are shown as `name`, `name~2` in registration order.

## Failure modes

| Case | What the user sees | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| Not inside a git checkout, or `git` missing | `search: not inside a git checkout; use grep` | 1 |
| `.agents/scratch/search.db` not gitignored (`git check-ignore -q` fails) | `search: .agents/scratch/search.db is not gitignored; add ".agents/scratch/*" to .gitignore (/init-project does)`; no file created | 1 |
| `.agents` or `.agents/scratch` is a symlink | `search: .agents/scratch is a symlink; refusing to write through it` | 1 |
| Another process holds the write lock past 10 s | `search: index busy (another sh-agent is indexing); retry, or use grep`; no stale answer is printed | 1 |
| Database unreadable (`SQLITE_CORRUPT`, `SQLITE_NOTADB`) or `meta.schema` ≠ 1 | `note: index at <path> was unreadable (or an older schema); rebuilt` and the answer | 0 |
| A file vanishes between `git status` and the read | the file is dropped from this reconcile; the next one picks up its state | 0 |
| `--refs` names an ID with no record | `<ID>  no record` then any references | 0 |
| `--limit` below 1 or above 50; `--kind` not in the list; `--refs` or `--open` with words, or with each other; `search` with no words and neither flag | `search: <what is wrong>; see sh-agent help` naming the valid values | 1 |
| The global index is rebuilt or found unreadable | the registry is gone with it; `note: N project registrations dropped; each returns on its next search` | 0 |
| Global: a registered root is gone | `note: dropped <root> (no longer a git checkout)` | 0 |
| The checkout is on a network filesystem | SQLite's own error, prefixed `search:`; documented as unsupported in the spec | 1 |
| `sh-agent report` | `search.db` is never collected; the dry run lists it under skipped | — |
| `sh-agent uninstall` | leaves `~/.config/sh-agent/search.db` (not in the manifest, R4); the spec says to delete it by hand | — |
| Checkout build with no module cache and no network (install's rebuild, BUG-006) | Go's own "cannot find module" error; `deploy/local.md` says the first build of a version needs the module proxy | 1 |

## Verification

Tiers: unit (Go tests with `-race`, temp git repositories), integration (the binary against this checkout and a scratch clone), behavioural (headless CLI runs per the project `AGENTS.md` § Testing), e2e (the sandboxed sample-app runs, Phase 5).

E2E criteria:
- In a checkout, after `git switch` to a branch that lacks a word, `sh-agent search <word>` returns no hit from the other branch; after switching back it returns the hit.
- An uncommitted edit and an untracked new file are found by the next search with no other command run.
- `sh-agent search --refs ADR-040` in this repository shows ADR-040's status as superseded by ADR-041 and lists ADR-041 among the references.
- `sh-agent search --global <a phrase from another project's bug record>` run in this repository returns that record.
- A fresh headless session on each CLI, asked where a past decision was made, runs `sh-agent search` before reading trail files (n of N reported).
- The rendered context stays under 22,000 bytes and ends with GANNET.

- [x] Checkpoint — expect: recall log committed, D-row written — evidence: `testing/2026-09-29-search-recall.md`, D30, 2026-09-29

### Phase 5 — Sandboxed efficiency runs (after Phases 1-4 are committed)
- [x] Kit in `.agents/scratch/eff-kit/` (not committed, ADR-010): per-arm sandbox homes, baseline arm installed from the v1.12.1 release binary, index arm from this checkout; run-specific agy `settings.json`; the run script asserts each fixture fact before the CLI starts — verify: AI, a dry run of the kit — expect: both homes install with no drift; `sh-agent search` absent from the baseline home's context and present in the index arm's — done 2026-09-29: both sandbox homes drift none; the baseline binary refuses `search`; `sh-agent` wrappers pin `--home` (BUG-107); projects under `~/sandbox/search/eff/work/` (BUG-106)
- [x] Two sample apps, three sessions each in one project: session 1 builds the app through `/feature` (gates waived by name in the prompt, as in the 2026-09-16 simulation), session 2 (fresh) adds a feature, session 3 (fresh) fixes a seeded bug through `/bug`. App A: linkshelf (the 2026-09-16 brief, verbatim). App B: a Go CLI `tasklog` (add, list, done, JSON file store, tests). Claude Code: 2 runs per arm per app. Antigravity: 1 run per arm per app — verify: both — expect: every run ends with tests passing and a handoff, or the failure is recorded — done 2026-09-29: Claude Code 8 of 8 lanes delivered in both arms; Antigravity app lanes not comparable (print mode ended before subagents returned; one lane void after three grant rounds) — D37
- [x] Larger-project task: in a scratch clone of this repository at v1.12.1, a fresh session per arm answers five trail questions and fixes one seeded doc drift; Claude Code 2 runs per arm, Antigravity 1 — verify: both — expect: answers scored against gold — done 2026-09-29: Claude Code 4 of 4 and Antigravity 2 of 2 answered 5 of 5 and fixed the seeded drift
- [x] Metrics from transcripts per session: input tokens (fresh, cache read, cache write), output tokens, tool calls by kind, read volume, `sh-agent search` calls, subagent tokens, wall time, success; Antigravity reports what its logs hold and names what they do not — verify: AI — expect: `testing/<date>-search-efficiency.md` with medians and ranges per arm, n of N, and what was not measured — done 2026-09-29: `testing/2026-09-29-search-efficiency.md` — no measurable efficiency difference on Claude Code (median lane cost 17.78 against 18.78 USD, ranges overlap, same quality); the main agent ran `sh-agent search` 0 times in 28 sessions, subagents 33 (D36)
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: the efficiency log committed — evidence: `testing/2026-09-29-search-efficiency.md`, 2026-09-29

### Done
- [x] Definition of Done: verifier over the whole range, reviewer (diff only), security, documentation, `/review --docs`, changes entries, bug records, plan closed, `ROADMAP.md`/`TODO.md` emptied, commit, push, handoff — done 2026-09-29: `testing/2026-09-29-verify-search-index-final.md` and `-final-2.md` PASS (HEAD 4c9a327, 359 subtests and tests pass); reviewer APPROVE ×2, security three rounds with Outcome, docs lens with Outcome; the docs were written by the main agent (no `documentation` dispatch) and reviewed by the docs lens; BUG-106 and BUG-107 recorded and graduated; changes entries for each phase; handoff `handoffs/2026-09-29-2102-search-index-done.md`

## Risks

Assumptions:
- `modernc.org/sqlite` v1.60.1 builds and runs FTS5 on linux/amd64 and cross-compiles for darwin/arm64 and linux/arm64 with `CGO_ENABLED=0` — checked 2026-09-29 for linux/amd64 (run) and darwin/arm64 (build); linux/arm64 checked by the Phase 1 build task.
- Claude Code subagents receive the global context — observed by the audit's own dispatch on 2026-09-29 (`plans/2026-09-29-audit-search-consumers.md`); Antigravity subagents unverified, which is why D13 puts a line in each consumer's own file; Phase 3's agy runs report it.
- `git check-ignore` reports `.agents/scratch/search.db` ignored in every project scaffolded by `/init-project` — checked by recon (`skills/init-project/SKILL.md:110-122`); Phase 1's guard test covers a project where it is not.
- The Linux box's `claude` and `agy` can run headless in a sandbox home with a copied token — checked by the 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-16 procedures; re-checked by Phase 5's kit dry run.
- Phase 5 cost: about 30 headless sessions of up to two hours each. Stated to the operator with the R4 question.

## Decisions

D1 — 2026-09-29 — `REQUIREMENTS.md` R4 changes to the text below — by: the operator, 2026-09-29, in their own turn, choosing "Approve as written (Recommended)" on this exact text, with the no-vendoring trade-off (D9) and the Phase 5 cost stated in the question.

> ## R4 — One binary, one dependency, easy on and off
>
> `sh-agent` is a single Go binary. Its one dependency is `modernc.org/sqlite`, a pure-Go SQLite driver used only by the search index, pinned in `go.mod` and `go.sum` and not vendored; any other dependency, and any driver that needs cgo, is a requirements change. The search indexes (`.agents/scratch/search.db` in a project, `~/.config/sh-agent/search.db`) are caches derived from files git or `~/.config/sh-agent/` already holds: never committed, never sent by `report`, rebuilt when deleted. `install` is idempotent … *(the rest of R4 unchanged)*

D2 — 2026-09-29 — The databases are derived indexes; Markdown and JSONL stay the source of truth — by: the operator, "Go with your recommendations" (row 1).
D3 — 2026-09-29 — No service: reconcile against git at query time — by: the operator (row 2).
D4 — 2026-09-29 — Per-project file under `.agents/scratch/`; named `search.db`, not `index.db`, because R7 already calls `retros.jsonl` "the cross-project index" — by: the operator (row 3); name by implementer from recon.
D5 — 2026-09-29 — A global index at `~/.config/sh-agent/search.db` over feedback, retros, proposals and registered projects' trails — by: the operator (row 4).
D6 — 2026-09-29 — Phase 1 is full-text search plus the metadata graph; vectors only through the Phase 4 gate — by: the operator (row 5).
D7 — 2026-09-29 — Instructions go in the context, paid for by cuts, plus one line per HIGH-ranked agent or skill; no new skill — supersedes recommendation row 6's "a new skill" — by: the operator, "make sure to add to the context how to use the database".
D8 — 2026-09-29 — The embedding model's delivery is deferred to the Phase 4 gate — by: the operator (row 7).
D9 — 2026-09-29 — Not vendored: `go mod vendor` measured 137 MB (modernc `libc` 71 MB, `sqlite` 57 MB), which would enter every clone and every release zip; a checkout's first build of a version needs the module proxy — by: implementer, measured 2026-09-29; stated to the operator with D1.
D10 — 2026-09-29 — The verbs sit in the first switch, before `ResolveSource`, so a release-binary or zip place with no harness tree can search — by: implementer, from recon.
D11 — 2026-09-29 — Phase 5 adds a larger-project task (a clone of this repository) beside the two sample apps, because the operator's reason is "a powerhouse in larger projects" and a new sample app has almost no trail — by: implementer, from the operator's words.
D12 — 2026-09-29 — Snippet text, not whole files: `search` prints at most 200 characters per hit and at most 50 hits, so a search costs a few hundred tokens — by: implementer, from the token baseline.
D14 — 2026-09-29 — An oid current at several paths is parsed once, by the first path seen; its records and refs are reported at every current path — by: cold read round 1 (`reviews/2026-09-29-coldread-search-index-r1.md`, readiness question 4, its default).
D15 — 2026-09-29 — `chunks_fts` is kept in sync by two triggers on `chunks` (insert, delete); chunks are never updated — by: cold read round 1, blocking question 1.
D16 — 2026-09-29 — Every query joins through `files` for the queried project(s); nothing keyed only by oid is printed without that join — by: cold read round 1, blocking question 2.
D17 — 2026-09-29 — The directory-to-kind table and the driver's DSN are written into Interfaces; the Phase 3 context edit measures the budget first — by: cold read round 1, readiness questions 3, 5 and 6.
D18 — 2026-09-29 — Round 2 fixes: `feedback` and `proposal` join the `--kind` list; a `--global` run inside a checkout registers and reconciles that checkout first; argument errors and the registry's loss on a global rebuild are Failure modes rows; the vector probe names its library and fusion — by: cold read round 2 (`reviews/2026-09-29-coldread-search-index-r2.md`) and implementer's own read before round 3.
D19 — 2026-09-29 — Round 3 residue: R7 already calls `retros.jsonl` "the cross-project index", so every doc, comment and message calls the new file "the global search index" and never "cross-project index"; R7 is not edited. `--refs <dir>/` prints `<dir>/  directory` first. D13's dream citation is line 41 — by: the operator, "Proceed with my fixes (Recommended)", on the cap question.
D20 — 2026-09-29 — Phase 0 adds only a measurement test that skips unless `SH_AGENT_RECALL=1`, so its verifier run is the Phase 1 dispatch, whose range starts before Phase 0. Reference and open questions are scored over the complete list, not the top ten, because those modes return exhaustive lists — by: implementer.
D21 — 2026-09-29 — `modernc.org/sqlite` is pinned at v1.46.1 (2026-02-18), the newest release whose `go.mod` says `go 1.24.0`: `go get` of v1.60.1 raised this module's `go` directive to 1.26.0, which ADR-029 and the project `AGENTS.md` forbid, and a Go 1.24 machine building with `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` could no longer build — by: implementer, measured.
D22 — 2026-09-29 — The Phase 1 tests were written after the code, against the feature skill's test-first rule. Compensation: every key test was checked by the mutation protocol (review-standards § 2): eleven mutations, each compiled; ten failed their named tests; M6 (skipping a rename's original path removed) passed, an equivalent mutation, because the unskipped original path is parsed as a nonexistent path and dropped. The rename test itself pins the path order: with the skip in place it passes only when `git status -z` lists the new path first. Recorded in the Phase 1 change entry — by: implementer.
D23 — 2026-09-29 — `--refs` groups references per file and record, not per file, so ADR-041's "supersedes ADR-040" is its own entry and not folded into ADR-040's heading; groups are ordered newest record date first, then path; a group naming the target more than once shows `×N`. The schema adds `blobs.skipped` (a skipped binary or large file is not re-read on every reconcile) and `projects.docs_root` (the global search index classifies each project's paths) — by: implementer, from `TestRefs` and the design.
D24 — 2026-09-29 — Word search materializes the FTS5 match first (`WITH m AS MATERIALIZED`) and makes snippets only for printed hits: joined directly, SQLite drove the loop from `files` and evaluated the match per row, 0.6–2.5 s per query on this repository; now 23–67 ms — by: implementer, measured.
D25 — 2026-09-29 — `govulncheck` reports GO-2026-5024 in `golang.org/x/sys` v0.37.0 (pulled in by the driver), not reachable from this code. Its fix, v0.44.0, needs `go 1.25.0`, which D21 rules out, so it stays until the module's `go` directive moves; the Done review names it — by: implementer, from the Phase 1 verifier log.
D26 — 2026-09-29 — `documentation`, `bugs` and `changelog` have no shell: the main agent runs `sh-agent search --refs <changed paths>` and puts the output in their dispatch, and each of the three files says to use it; their tool lists do not change — by: the operator, "Main agent runs it (Recommended)".
D27 — 2026-09-29 — Word search ranks chunks holding every word first, then fills the remaining slots with chunks holding any word, and the header says how many had every word; supersedes the Interfaces bullet "No hits for the AND query → retry once as OR". The recall test's first index run scored 0.077 on ordinary questions because an AND of many words matched two chunks and stopped — by: implementer, from the recall test.
D28 — 2026-09-29 — `--refs <bare file name>` that matches no path prints `hint: did you mean --refs <path>` for up to five tracked paths ending in that name; still no basename matching. Found in the behavioural runs: two reviewer runs passed `store.go` and got nothing — by: implementer.
D29 — 2026-09-29 — Behavioural runs go outside every checkout (`~/sandbox/search/`, BUG-106), and the lines that round 1 showed weak are ordered steps: `explorer` "your first command, before any Grep, Glob or Read"; `reviewer` a first pre-flight step with the full path; `dreamer` "run `sh-agent search` too (the Grep tool replaces neither)"; the context entry "Run it before Grep" (its "in a git checkout" dropped to pay for it) — by: implementer, from round 1 (0 of 3 for `explorer`, `dreamer` and the context; 1 of 3 for `reviewer`).
D30 — 2026-09-29 — Vector gate not passed: fusing MiniLM vectors into the index adds 6.4 points of mean recall@10 overall and 3.0 on drift against the index alone, under the 10-point bar; the plan's literal baseline, the RRF of index and grep, scores below the index alone, and a gate a weaker baseline passes measures the baseline. The delivery condition fails too: the "pure Go" MiniLM library loads ONNX Runtime as a shared library. Vectors are closed; the operator can reopen them — by: implementer, from `testing/2026-09-29-search-recall.md`.
D31 — 2026-09-29 — The context entry, final: "**Search first:** `sh-agent search <words>` ranks files and trail records; `--refs <BUG-NNN|ADR-NNN|path>` lists every record naming it (run it before touching an area); `--open` lists open bugs and plans; `--global` spans projects. Run it before Grep; grep stays for exact strings, regex, past revisions." — by: implementer, measured at 21,988 bytes.
D32 — 2026-09-29 — Security round 1 (`reviews/2026-09-29-security-search-index.md`): the DSN is built with `net/url`; only a checkout with `.agents/docs` registers in the global search index (supersedes the Interfaces § Global registry line "Every `search` and `index` run inside a git checkout … upserts"); modified and untracked files are hashed from their own bytes (no `git hash-object`); printed text carries no control characters; directories the index creates are 0700; secret-shaped names are never indexed (the installer's list, exported as `harness.SecretShaped`) — by: security review, each fix with a test that failed first.
D33 — 2026-09-29 — Docs review (`reviews/2026-09-29-review-8ee5d70-HEAD-docs.md`): ADR-045's version and module count corrected by addendum ADR-045a; `go mod tidy` makes the driver a direct requirement (the `go` directive stays 1.24.4); the project `AGENTS.md` names the known `x/sys` advisory — by: docs review.
D34 — 2026-09-29 — Security round 2: registration stays automatic for a checkout with `.agents/docs`; the residual (a crafted clone that commits `.agents/docs` and that the operator runs `search` in joins `--global` and `/retro` evidence until `index --global --rebuild`) is accepted — by: the operator, "Keep automatic (Recommended)". The global search index reads only `.agents/docs` and drops a registration that lost it; hint and note lines are printable; hashed bytes are the indexed bytes; the secret list ignores case and adds `.git-credentials` and `credentials` (the installer's list and `.gitignore` too) — by: security review round 2.
D35 — 2026-09-29 — Security round 3, the cap: the round-2 read-once change is reverted (it held every modified and untracked file in memory); a file edited and restored while `search` waits for the write lock can stay indexed with the edit until `index --rebuild`, a documented limit; a registration is dropped only on positive evidence, and a check that errors keeps it with a "skipped" note; the README and spec list the secret patterns as they are — by: the operator, "Revert and document (Recommended)".
D36 — 2026-09-29 — Phase 5 finding: on Claude Code the context entry did not make the main agent search in real work (0 of 28 sessions, the larger-project trail questions included); `security` and `reviewer`, which have it as a fixed step, made all 33 calls. Efficiency on sample apps: no measurable difference (median lane cost 5% lower, ranges overlap, n = 2 per app per arm). Recorded as a follow-up for the operator, not changed in this plan — by: implementer, from `testing/2026-09-29-search-efficiency.md`.
D37 — 2026-09-29 — The Antigravity app lanes are reported, not compared: `agy -p` returned before dispatched subagents did in the search arm's lanes, so they did less work, and the baseline tasklog lane stayed void after three rounds of grants (each added by name per the project `AGENTS.md`); the larger-project pair is the one Antigravity comparison — by: implementer.
D13 — 2026-09-29 — Consumers that get their own line, from the audit (`plans/2026-09-29-audit-search-consumers.md`): `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md:48` and `agents/dreamer.md:36` (restatements: `search <key words>` beside the literal grep), `skills/dream/SKILL.md:41` (graduation check), `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:154` (`search --open --kind plan` first, the awk scan when search refuses), `agents/dreamer.md:29`, `skills/bug/SKILL.md:33`, `skills/feature/SKILL.md:19` (`search --refs <path>` and `--open --kind bug` instead of reading all of `bugs/INDEX.md`), `skills/retro/SKILL.md` (`search --global` for "happened in another project"). The context's restatement rule (`context/AGENTS.md:55`) is covered by the new entry. Added on the operator's question "why not all places that generate lots of md files?" — the audit ranked steps that already grep, and the writers have none because they write without looking: `agents/documentation.md` (`search <changed command or flag>` for every doc that describes it, before editing), `agents/bugs.md` (`search <symptom words> --kind bug` and `--refs <path>` before assigning a new number, to find a duplicate or an existing prevention rule), `agents/changelog.md` (`--refs <path>` for the bug and ADR IDs a change entry should cite; `search` for the ADR a new decision supersedes), `agents/explorer.md` (`search` and `--refs` as its first recon step), `agents/reviewer.md` and `agents/security.md` (`--refs <path> --kind bug` for the files in the diff: past failures, never the author's intent), `skills/research/SKILL.md` Step 1 (`search <topic> --kind plan` for earlier research). Not to use it, and their lines unchanged: `agents/verifier.md` (live-tree, diff-scoped checks), `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:40` (secret scan), the retro skill's exact `rule_ref` greps, and any grep at a past revision (`/review --docs` at the scope's head) — by: implementer, from the audit.
Rejected: vendoring (D9); a watcher or service (D3); a trigram tokenizer (23 MB here against 3.4-12 MB for porter; exact substrings stay with grep); basename matching in `--refs` (`main.go` would match every command); a `--json` output (no consumer named); a separate skill (D7); storing records in the database as the source (D2).

title: Plan — `sh-agent search`: release readiness (2026-09-29)
body:
# Plan — `sh-agent search`: release readiness   (2026-09-29)

## Why

The operator, 2026-09-29, after the search index plan (`plans/2026-09-29-search-index.md`) closed: "I want everything to be done before we cut a new version. Nothing waiting, nothing in todo roadmap or waiting." The open items are that handoff's Next Steps (`handoffs/2026-09-29-2102-search-index-done.md`): the main agent does not use `sh-agent search` in real work (0 of 28 sessions, D36 of the search plan), the Antigravity runs the release gate needs are incomplete, and the benefit on a project with a large trail was never measured over several sessions.

## Scope

In:
- A clean A/B of the whole harness per arm on Claude Code: `--setting-sources project,local` (measured 2026-09-29: user-level skills and context not loaded, project skills loaded), each arm's installed `.claude/{skills,agents,commands}` copied into the run's project, its rendered context appended once. This removes the first comparison's two caveats (v1.12.1 skills in both arms; the context loaded twice).
- Main-agent adoption: measured with the new skills in place; if the main agent still does not search, one change to the context or a skill (D2), measured again.
- A multi-session test on a large trail: three sessions of ordinary work in a clone of this repository at v1.12.1, per arm.
- Every Antigravity run `AGENTS.md` § Release requires: one completed run of each changed skill and agent.
- Reviews and verification of anything this plan changes; docs; the real-home smoke after the operator's install on this box.
- Trail closed: `TODO.md` and `ROADMAP.md` empty, the handoff with nothing queued, so `/preflight v1.13.0` is the only next step.

Out: the release itself (`/preflight` from the operator's turn); the known limits D25 (`x/sys` advisory, needs Go 1.25) and D35 (the edit-during-lock race), both documented decisions; installs on the other machines (after the release).

Follow-ups noted, not built: none.

## Surfaces touched

- `.agents/scratch/eff-kit/` (kit, gitignored, ADR-010), new files beside the Phase 5 kit, which stays as it is: `clean-session.sh` (one clean-arm session), `lane-clean.sh <arm> <app|trail> <n>` (a fresh project, then sessions s1–s3; results in `results-clean/<arm>-<app|trail>-<n>-s<k>.{json,err}`, projects in `~/sandbox/search/eff/cwork/`), `metrics-clean.py` (per lane type, session and arm; the main agent's and the subagents' `sh-agent search` calls in separate columns; prints the D3 count), `score-trail.py` (s1 drift fixed, s2 answers out of 5, s3 `go test ./cmd/sh-agent -run '^TestUsageMatchesDocComment$' -v` shows the test ran and passed, pushed), prompts `LT1`–`LT3` in `prompts.sh`. Each arm's Claude Code install: `~/sandbox/search/eff/chome-<arm>/` (`sh-agent install --vendor claude` of v1.12.1 and of this tree).
- `context/AGENTS.md` or one skill, only if D2 changes wording.
- `.agents/docs/testing/` logs; `testing/skill-matrix.md` if a scenario changes.

## Interfaces

Clean-arm Claude session: `cd <project>; PATH=<arm wrapper dir>:$PATH claude -p --setting-sources project,local --append-system-prompt "$(cat ctx-<arm>.md)" --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools <the Phase 5 list> < prompt`, where `<project>/.claude/` holds a copy of `<arm home>/.claude/{skills,agents,commands}` from `sh-agent install --vendor claude --home <arm home>` of that arm's tree, excluded from git by `<project>/.git/info/exclude`. No `--agents`, no `--add-dir`.

Large-trail lane (per arm, one clone of this repository at v1.12.1 with its `.agents/docs` trail, the drift seed of the search plan's Phase 5, and a bare origin): s1 "resume from the trail, then fix the seeded drift: `sh-agent update --check` exits 2 when behind — make every living file agree, as a Task under the Definition of Done"; s2 "resume from the trail, then answer the five trail questions of the search plan's Phase 5 in ANSWERS.md with file:line, commit"; s3 "resume from the trail, then, as a Task under the Definition of Done, add a Go test `TestUsageMatchesDocComment` to `cmd/sh-agent` that fails when a verb in the usage text is missing from `main.go`'s doc comment, or the other way round"; the exact prompts are `LT1`–`LT3`. Each prompt carries its own "Do not ask me anything" and its push instruction; s2 is a question session that commits and pushes.

## Failure modes

- A run auto-denied on Antigravity: the command is added by name and the run repeated (project `AGENTS.md` § Testing).
- `agy -p` returns before a dispatched subagent: the run is repeated up to three times; still void after three, the gate is told in the log, and the operator decides (Open row).

## Verification

E2E criteria:
- The main agent of the search arm runs `sh-agent search` in at least 4 of 6 large-trail sessions (Phase 1, or Phase 2 after the change), or the operator has accepted the measured number in their own turn.
- The clean A/B's per-session table exists for Claude Code with both arms delivering; the main agent's `sh-agent search` count is reported for each arm.
- Every changed skill and agent has one completed Antigravity run on disk (artifact or answer) with no auto-denied line.
- After the operator's install on this box, the three real-home smoke checks pass on both CLIs, and `sh-agent search --refs ADR-040` answers from the installed binary.
- `TODO.md` and `ROADMAP.md` hold headers only; the newest handoff's Next Steps name only `/preflight v1.13.0`.

## Phases

- [x] Cold-reader check — round 1 `reviews/2026-09-29-coldread-search-release-readiness-r1.md` (one blocking gap, D3), round 2 `-r2.md` (two, D4), round 3 `-r3.md` (one narrow blocking item, one non-blocking) — cap reached; the operator, 2026-09-29: "Proceed with my fix (Recommended)", resolved as D5

### Phase 1 — Clean A/B on Claude Code, with the new skills
- [x] Kit: the files named in Surfaces touched; a dry run of one `trail` project per arm (setup only, no session) shows its `.claude/skills` holds that arm's skills (the search arm's `feature` skill contains `sh-agent search --refs`, the baseline's does not) and the drift seed in place — verify: AI — expect: `grep -c` 2 and 0, the seed line found — done 2026-09-29: `grep -c` 2 and 0, the seed line found, `.claude/` excluded, tree clean, in both arms' dry-run projects
- [x] Sample apps, both arms, 2 runs each, 3 sessions (`lane-clean.sh <arm> linkshelf|tasklog <n>`) — verify: AI, `outcomes.py` pointed at `cwork/`, `metrics-clean.py` — expect: the app rows of the table, main-agent and subagent searches in separate columns — done 2026-09-29: 24 of 24 sessions delivered, all eight lanes pass vet and tests with the feature built; median lane cost 18.02 (base) against 18.17 USD (search); the main agent searched in 9 of 12 search-arm sessions
- [x] Large-trail lane, both arms, 2 runs each (`lane-clean.sh <arm> trail <n>`) — verify: AI, `score-trail.py`, `metrics-clean.py` — expect: per session the trail rows of the table and the three scores — done 2026-09-29: 12 of 12 sessions delivered; every lane: drift fixed, 5 of 5 answers, the new test passes
- [x] Adoption decision (D3): count the large-trail sessions of the search arm in which the MAIN agent (not a subagent) ran `sh-agent search` — verify: AI, the D3 line `metrics-clean.py` prints (main-agent calls only, from the main transcript; subagent transcripts are counted in their own column) — expect: a D-row stating `n of 6` and `adopted` (n ≥ 4) or `not adopted` (n ≤ 3); `not adopted` opens Phase 2, `adopted` marks Phase 2's boxes `[-]` with that D-row as the reason — done 2026-09-29: 3 of 6, `not adopted` (D9); Phase 2 runs
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: `testing/<date>-search-adoption.md` committed — evidence: `testing/2026-09-29-search-adoption.md`, 2026-09-29

### Phase 2 — Main-agent adoption (runs when D3 says `not adopted`)
- [x] D2 decided with the operator: the change and its exact text — who: both — done 2026-09-29: pre-decided, D2
- [x] The change, `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` PASS if context — verify: unit — expect: PASS — done 2026-09-29: PASS at 21,996 of 22,000 bytes, GANNET last; the handoff skill's restatement of the order updated (D9)

- [x] Checkpoint — expect: log and change committed; `/review --docs` over the change — evidence: `testing/2026-09-29-search-adoption.md`; commit f41e5c0; `reviews/2026-09-29-review-abbaddc-1634787-docs.md` APPROVE, no findings, 2026-09-29

### Phase 2b — Optimizations (the operator: "run optimizations")
- [x] Measure, then keep only what measures better — verify: AI, `index --rebuild` three times each, and an equivalence run of `parseRefs` over every tracked file — expect: faster build, smaller index, identical references — done 2026-09-29: build 2.2 s → 1.7 s and index 24.1 MB → 21.7 MB on this repository; the prefiltered `parseRefs` returned the same 40,842 references on 1,077 files; kept: insert statements prepared once per reconcile, `parseRefs` skipping lines that cannot match, the `refs(oid)` index dropped (it served only garbage collection); rejected: merging the FTS index after a build (the file grew to 25.8 MB from free pages); `TestRefsPrefilterIsEquivalent` added, mutations O1–O3 each fail it; the extension list is one source for the regex and the prefilter (D8)

### Phase 4 — Real home and close
- [x] `sh-agent update` on this box (D7, on the operator's word), then `hash -r` — verify: AI, `sh-agent status` — expect: binary line without a warning, drift none — first run 2026-09-29 21:32 at 2716d08: 33 written, `binary 2716d0858bc1` without a warning, GANNET last, `sh-agent search --refs ADR-040` answered; repeated after the last change of this plan — third run 22:27 at 8e1b7f5 after the security fix: 1 written, `binary 8e1b7f5aee85` without a warning, both existing indexes tightened to 0600

- [x] Definition of Done: verifier, reviews for what changed, changes entries, plan closed, `TODO.md`/`ROADMAP.md` empty, handoff naming only `/preflight v1.13.0` — done 2026-09-29: `testing/2026-09-29-verify-search-release-readiness.md` PASS over aae16af..1634787 (362 pass, 2 skips with reasons); code review APPROVE; security findings fixed with Outcome (D10); docs lens APPROVE; `changes/2026-09-29-2326-search-release-readiness.md`; BUG-106 and BUG-107 graduated earlier; the release follows in the same session (D6), so the handoff is written after it and names nothing queued

## Risks

Assumptions: `--setting-sources project,local` excludes the real home's skills and context and loads project skills — checked 2026-09-29 by a probe (a project skill listed, no harness skill, no GANNET). Headless Claude Code reads `.claude/` in the project (only writes are refused) — checked by the same probe.

## Decisions

D1 — 2026-09-29 — The clean A/B replaces the first comparison's setup for everything in this plan; the first comparison stays as recorded — by: implementer, from the probe.
D4 — 2026-09-29 — The kit is new files beside the Phase 5 kit (named in Surfaces touched), because the Phase 5 `metrics.py` sums main and subagent searches and runs the larger task as one session; the matrix task adds a Zip place column, since the table has no row shape for a place — by: cold read round 2 (`reviews/2026-09-29-coldread-search-release-readiness-r2.md`).

D6 — 2026-09-29 — The release is v1.13.0, a MINOR: new verbs, nothing an existing install must react to — by: the operator, "v1.13.0 (Recommended)", and "Cut new version update docs. This is dod". Scope's Out line on the release is superseded: `/preflight v1.13.0` runs at the end of this plan.

D10 — 2026-09-29 — Reviews of this plan's source changes (aae16af..f41e5c0): code APPROVE (`reviews/2026-09-29-review-aae16af-f41e5c0-code.md`); security two findings, both fixed with tests that failed first (`reviews/2026-09-29-security-aae16af-f41e5c0.md` § Outcome): the index files are refused unless regular files, and are mode 0600 — by: security review.
D9 — 2026-09-29 — Adoption: with the first wording and the new skills the main agent ran `sh-agent search` in 3 of 6 large-trail sessions (`not adopted`). Per D2, `→ `sh-agent search --open` (what is open)` joins the context's resume reading order after `bugs/INDEX.md`, paid for by cutting "`--open` lists open bugs and plans; " from the Search first entry (net +8 bytes, 21,996 of 22,000); `skills/handoff/SKILL.md`'s restatement of the order gains the step. Measured again in a separate arm: 6 of 6 large-trail sessions, same quality; the trail-question session read 12k characters against the baseline's 27k and cost 0.58 against 0.66 USD; the whole lane cost about 15% more than the baseline in both search arms, mostly in s1, where the search arms' agents checked the new bug number against the other branch and renumbered it — by: measured by implementer; change per the operator's D2.
D8 — 2026-09-29 — Optimizations kept only where measured (Phase 2b); warm search was already 25–40 ms and is unchanged; the schema version stays 1 because no release carries the old index — a development cache keeps its extra index until `index --rebuild` — by: the operator, "run optimizations"; measured by implementer.
D7 — 2026-09-29 — The operator asked for the local harness to be updated ("Don't forget to update local harness"): `sh-agent update` runs on this box from this session, once the tree is clean — by: the operator.

title: Plan — audit fix: everything the 2026-09-30 audits found, fixed, improved and extended (2026-09-30)
body:
# Plan — audit fix: everything the 2026-09-30 audits found, fixed, improved and extended   (2026-09-30)

## Why

The operator (2026-09-30, own turn): "I want to fix all things you find, big and small. … Go with your recommendations on the ones you added a recommendation. On the others do research. … The bottom line I want everything fixed, improved, optimized, add new features from your audit report. … do your research first before execute. … split this up in phases and tasks and everything needs to be verified … You can update the local harness everything you need it. Also run sandboxed tests, all allowed. … a separate TODO file in this project that has the HIGHEST priority … when everything is done, re-run the audit."

The evidence is `plans/2026-09-30-recon-audit-fix.md` (IDs C, WS, TS, AG, IN, SD, TR, G). Research briefs: `plans/2026-09-30-research-audit-fix-{frontend,terraform-gcp,golang,cloudrun-operate,formats}.md`.

## Scope

In: every finding in the recon brief, by ID; the workflow gaps G1–G13 as new skills, templates and one context paragraph; the installer simplifications IN-S; a real-home install and the sandbox tiers; a re-audit at the end, published the same way as the two before.

Out: cutting a version (`/preflight`) — the operator cuts it; installing the dream timer on the real home (who: user); `/retro` (user-invoked only; the graduations here go through mechanisms and the bugs agent); the AWS terraform content (deleted, not ported); anything in a consumer project.

Follow-ups noted, not built: a per-project "size tier" beyond the one paragraph (G11); i18n skill; Node/npm hygiene beyond the docker build stage and a frontend paragraph.

## Surfaces touched

`context/AGENTS.md`, `context/dev-setup.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md` (approval-gated), `README.md` (map legend), `AGENTS.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `PRIORITY_TODO.md`; `agents/*.md` (8); `internal/harness/{derive,inventory,report,apply,release,zip,pathguard,frontmatter}.go` + tests, `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` + tests; `internal/search/{search,dream}.go`, `internal/dream/{collect,run,prompt}.go` + tests; `skills/*` (all 29; python and anti-ui-slop struck; new: requirements, spec, operate-gcp, data-gcp, api-auth-gcp, testing-strategy, explain-project); `skills/VENDORED.md`; `skills/init-project/assets/**`; `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/*.md`; `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md` + a committed kit preamble; five stopped review artifacts (appended void marker); `.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md` (via bugs agent); a new handoff.

## Interfaces

**Context budget (C1).** Hard verify: rendered context ≤ 15,000 bytes, pinned by a second test `TestRenderedContextUnderTarget` that FAILS above 15,000 (the 22,000 Antigravity pin stays; guide § 2 and AGENTS.md Setup commands name both pins — docs clause). 14,500 is the goal; a shortfall between 14,500 and 15,000 is reported in the checkpoint, not a failure. Arithmetic (cold read rounds 1–2): the first list saves ≈ 4,600; the second ≈ 2,950; line 11's compaction sentence (moved to `skills/handoff` § Usage) ≈ 200; add-backs ≈ +500 (G11 paragraph, seven skill names minus two, the resume-line clause): net ≈ 14,650. The formats brief's evidence: adherence tracks the number of distinct instructions and their presence, not bytes, so the cut removes whole rules from the always-loaded file and lands each in the skill or agent that acts on it. What moves where:
- line 52 → one short "before commit" bullet (numstat binary check, `rm -r` by name, ` D` stop sign) ≈ 300 chars; the escape/heredoc lesson → `skills/bash` § "Escapes survive tools"; the post-dispatch `git status/log/tag` check → the Skill/Subagent paragraph (one clause).
- line 56 → first sentence + "the two shapes are review-standards § 7"; shapes' text → review-standards § 7.
- line 57 → first two sentences; `hash -r`/`rehash`/`type` → `skills/bash` § "An installed command is verified by the shell".
- line 58 → first clause + pointer; the rest is already review-standards § 2.
- lines 59–62 → one bullet: "Code-shape rules a review checks and an author follows — guard on error, dry-run resolves every path, embedded artifact pinned both ways, verification never in a `&&` chain to a commit — are review-standards § 8"; full text → review-standards § 8 (new) and the four Go-flavoured ones also into `skills/golang/SKILL.md` § Coding Standards (review-standards' new sections are § 7 and § 8, after its existing six).
- line 34 → "A dispatch to reviewer, security or verifier names a tool-call budget below the agent's maxTurns and repeats the artifact duty; an agent stopped with work running is stopped (`TaskStop`) once its artifact is on disk." The verifier-specific sentence → `agents/verifier.md` (it is already there) and `skills/review` Step 3.
- line 16 → thresholds, "fixed or rebutted in `## Outcome`", `/review --docs` clause; rounds protocol, "shorter beats defended", operator-choice rule → `skills/review/SKILL.md` Step 4 (already the record's home).
- line 66 → drop the date-only-name clause; "where Claude Code cannot read `AGENTS.md` (R2 lists them)"; define `docs/` shorthand in the preamble (line 3) and use `<docs-root>` nowhere else in the file.
- line 30 → keep `/goal` (documented: `code.claude.com/docs/en/goal`); it is listed as a Claude-only known difference (C15).
- line 46 → keep; the secret-shaped list becomes "a secret-shaped path (the installer's list: `.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.tfvars`, `*.tfstate`, credential and token files)".
- line 18 (C2) → "`TODO.md` is empty at every checkpoint; `ROADMAP.md` holds only Now while a plan is open, and Now names that plan".
- Second list (whole rules that leave the always-loaded file, each landing where it is acted on): line 46 → the "Ship/deploy/release/cut" paragraph and the version-number rule move to `skills/preflight` § Usage (≈ −600); line 32 → the enumeration of what counts as a failure moves to `skills/bug` Step 0 and the graduation sentence to `agents/bugs.md`; the context keeps "Every failure gets a number: dispatch `bugs`; a rule that recurs graduates" (≈ −400); line 42 → the retro/distill/dream cadence detail moves to `skills/retro` § When to Suggest; the context keeps the two triggers and the queue path (≈ −450); line 38 → the name-clash and vendor-load caveats move to `skills/init-project` Step 4 (≈ −250); line 15 → the tree-freeze sentence moves to `agents/verifier.md` (it is there) and `skills/feature` Step 4 (≈ −250); line 54 → the runtime-data clause moves to `skills/golang` § Rules (≈ −250); line 17 → the list of owned files moves to `agents/documentation.md` (its lane); the context keeps "documentation owns the how-it-works docs; a new command, flag, endpoint or deploy step is not done until the file that describes it says so" (≈ −200); line 29 → the `--refs`/`--global` detail moves to a pointer at `specs/sh-agent/search.md`; keep "Search first: `sh-agent search <words>`; `--refs` before touching an area; grep for exact strings" (≈ −150); line 30 → keep `/goal` and the print-mode rule, drop the "name it rather than ending quietly" sentence into `skills/handoff` (≈ −150); line 9 → drop the parenthetical about the project-memory skill (≈ −100); line 21 (C14) → delete the docs-only clause (≈ −150). Author-side copies for non-Go work: review-standards § 8 is the one home of the code-shape rules; `golang`, `typescript` and `bash` SKILL.md each carry one line "before claiming done, apply review-standards § 8" (cold read round 1).
- line 9 (C6, C16) → order: `AGENTS.md` → newest handoff → `ROADMAP.md` Now → the active plan → three newest changes → bugs INDEX → `TODO.md` → `sh-agent search --open` → `sh-agent memory show`; "a verb that refuses because the project is not scaffolded is reported, then `/init-project` offered".
- new paragraph (G11) under Work: "A project without `.agents/docs/` runs Trivial and Task only: no verifier log, no changes entry, no handoff; commit and push close the task; offer `/init-project` once per session."
- line 13/21/25 (C14): keep the Trivial bullet, delete line 21's clause. Line 46 (C13): drop "bypass hooks".
- `dev-setup.md:8` (C7): "When the operator says to run a root step AND the project's `docs/deploy/local.md` § Operator steps records the standing permission, run it".

**Agents.** `changelog.md`: "Agents dispatched" and "Files changed" come from the dispatch text (`git log --stat <range>` output and the path list); ADR authoring removed; keeps `changes/` only. ADR template and "what is structural" → `skills/feature/SKILL.md` § Decisions (+ one paragraph) and `assets/agents-tree/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` keeps the template. `documentation.md`: ROADMAP and godoc struck from the lane. `reviewer.md` pre-flight step 2: "read `~/.claude/skills/review-standards/SKILL.md` and its `references/<language>.md` for each language in the diff" (derive rewrites the path). `verifier.md`: § What to run becomes numbered steps 1–9 (orient → guide → each command with its count line → compare with previous → coverage → suppressions → containers → kill children → finish the log); incidents removed; timeout sentence: "10 minutes on Claude Code; on Antigravity read the tool's own error". `bugs.md`: "Read the diff and the failing output the dispatch hands you (a scratch path or the hunks)"; "write the record before the index row". `explorer.md` and the context: recon briefs keep `plans/<date>-recon-<slug>.md`; resume line says "`recon-*` and `research-*` files are briefs, not plans". Early-write block: one shared core (the reviewer's block minus its trigger sentence, ≈ 10 lines: cut-off is normal, an unwritten artifact is a failed dispatch, update as you go, past two thirds stop reading and finish, always fill Not examined) copied verbatim into reviewer, security, verifier, explorer and dreamer, followed in each by ONE per-agent trigger line that stays: reviewer and security "after the first file of the range is read"; verifier "after the FIRST verification command, and update it after EVERY command" (its existing rule, kept); explorer "after the first directory listing"; dreamer "once you have one candidate or a third of the budget is spent". bugs gets the one-line order rule "write the record before the index row". Explorer's heading `## Write the brief EARLY` is renamed to `## Write the artifact EARLY` so the five headings match. Verify: the core extracted from the five files diffs empty pairwise AND `grep -c 'after EVERY command' agents/verifier.md` is 1. AG9 sentence in review Step 3 and preflight Step 2: "On Antigravity, `reviewer` inherits the session model and `security` is pinned to `pro` by its derived definition." Verifier step marker: the numbered § What to run says "each line under `## Commands` starts with its step number (`3.`)", which is the artifact evidence the behavioural run reads. Changelog evidence: the entry's `## Files changed` opens with "from the dispatch's `git log --stat`".
`derive.go`: the primary mechanism on both CLIs is the explicit path in the agent body (`~/.claude/skills/review-standards/SKILL.md`, which derive already rewrites to the agy path); Antigravity's documented `skills: ["skills/<name>"]` key is emitted in addition ONLY after the agy run below shows no hang and the file read in the transcript, else it is not emitted and the comment says why; `effort` and `maxTurns` stay dropped with a corrected comment (no Antigravity equivalent is documented; the dispatcher names the budget per the context, so no Budget prose line). A per-key emit/omit test. Docs: `specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` § Antigravity derivation (new paragraph) and AGENTS.md § Rules. `inventory.go`: `LoadAgents` refuses a description that is not one line or contains "dispatch prompt" / "harness binary" (test `TestAgentDescriptionRules`); `Lint` refuses any skill or agent description over 1,024 characters, the Agent Skills spec limit, measured after joining a multi-line (`|`) description's continuation lines with single spaces — one threshold, no note (cold read round 1). Measured 2026-09-30: the longest is cloud-run-deploy at 963, no vendored skill is over the limit, so nothing is refused today; a vendored skill that ever exceeds it is forked under another name per AGENTS.md § Rules, never edited in place — docs: AGENTS.md § Rules (the frontmatter refusals list).

**Skills (workflow).** review Step 3/5: the docs brief, prompts brief and fix loop as numbered lists; Step 5 adds "the dispatch to documentation carries `sh-agent search --refs <path>` output per changed path"; `--prompts` brief resolves the skill dir the way init-project Step 2 does; Step 4 gains the rounds and operator-choice rules moved from the context; new lens `--resume`, NOT part of `--all` (an explorer recon of the trail is not a review of a range; `--all` keeps its definition "every review lens"): dispatch `explorer` with the handoff skill's six cold-reader questions as the brief → `plans/<date>-recon-project-resume.md` (slug `project-resume`; the handoff skill's cold-reader check names `/review --resume` as its third way to run). preflight: Step 1 names documentation and bugs (or states deferral to Step 4), reviewer/security rows require `## Status: COMPLETE`; Step 4 carries refs output; item 6 says "follow the guide's procedure; for gcp.md that is …". handoff: quotes out of the template into Writing Rules; cold-reader check as six numbered questions with the awk in a fenced block; "the stamp is `date +%F-%H%M` at write time". init-project Step 5b as numbered sub-steps 1–6; the JSON write keeps `python3` (documented in one line as a prerequisite), with a `printf` fallback used only when the root path contains neither `"` nor `\` (D13). distill: `--from-log` implemented as a paragraph under Step 1 (read `feedback.jsonl` rows with `signal: gap` for this project) and `--global` in the argument-hint; Step 6.3 replaced by a one-line prohibition (a distill never appends to the log); reuse today's dreamer artifact when it exists. dream: row 70 deleted. feedback-log: rule 1 says "silent about the log; the memory refusal is said in one line". feature: budget clause at :78 and :90; "re-dispatched cold reader overwrites its artifact"; "What is structural" paragraph + ADR template. bug: budget clause at :53. review-standards: "loaded by the reviewer agent and by /preflight's own read of a small diff". research: `specs/<app>/<topic>.md` with sections by topic; the self-lookup is `sh-agent search <topic> --kind spec` (one kind per call; `search.go:84-92`), a second call `--kind plan` only when the first is empty. grilling (WS21, vendored verbatim, never edited in place): the VENDORED row's Local changes column gets "none; its 'dispatch a sub-agent' names no agent: on both CLIs that is `explorer`", and the review skill's `--prompts` keep-list item 5 gains "an unnamed sub-agent in a vendored skill (grilling): `explorer`" — D27. Scar tissue (WS8): parentheticals removed; the rule stays.

**Skills (technical).** Decisions per research brief, recorded as D-rows before Phase 6 (D20–D26). Fixed now: terraform rewritten clean-room in place under its directory name, no licence owed, VENDORED row removed (TS1, D8a); golang references rewritten to ≤ 3 stdlib-sourced files, samber file deleted, dead pointers gone, a `TestSkillLinksResolve` test walks every `skills/<name>/**/*.md` whose skill is NOT listed in either VENDORED.md table (vendored skills are never edited) and fails on any markdown link `](<relative path>)` or backticked `references/<file>` / `assets/<file>` path that does not exist under that skill; prose pointers ("See <Title>") are out of scope and the rewrite removes them (TS2, TS3); anti-ui-slop and python struck (TS4, TS13, TS23; D28); frontend references rewritten for Tailwind 4 + TanStack Start, tokens, a token focus ring, native forms (TS5, TS14, TS15, TS25); cloud-run-deploy gains a canary block, a flags table, token verify (TS16); docker base pin by go.mod, one `.dockerignore` list (TS17, TS26); gcloud-setup cask + Linux + CLI answers (TS18); json-api-style on AIP with camelCase tags and the golang examples aligned (TS19); bash fixes (TS20); gke override paragraph + asset paths (TS12, TS27); mermaid provenance row (TS28); typescript gets `references/{tsconfig,testing}.md` (TS29, D20).

**New skills (Phase 7).** `requirements` (elicit → tiered REQUIREMENTS.md: library / CLI / service; agents never edit the file, the skill drafts the operator's edit), `spec` (`docs/specs/<app>/<topic>.md` from `assets/agents-tree/docs/specs/TEMPLATE.md`), `operate-gcp` (runbook, logs, metrics and alerts, rollback outside a release, incident note → bug record, dependency cadence: `govulncheck`, `npm audit` monthly and before a release), `data-gcp` (Cloud SQL Postgres, pgx + connector, migrations as a Cloud Run job, local proxy, index/constraint checklist), `api-auth-gcp` (IAP, ID tokens, Identity Platform; vetted libraries only), `testing-strategy` (tiers, fixtures, e2e choice, coverage claims; ships `assets/guide-template.md` that init-project copies to `docs/testing/guide.md`), `explain-project` (a human-facing walkthrough: architecture in one page, how to run, where things are; written to `docs/onboarding.md`, which joins the documentation agent's lane so it is maintained after the skill creates it — docs: `agents/documentation.md` § Your lane). Each ≤ 200 lines SKILL.md, description with a Do-NOT routing line, a skill-matrix row.

**Installer (Phase 8).** `internal/harness/settings.go` holds the attribution code (S1); `main.go` verbs as a `map[string]func(*ctx) error` table with per-verb FlagSets (S2, IN5); `State.Origin()` and `Source.OriginString()` (IN6); `ResolveSourceLenient` for report (IN7); IN8 struck (D33); `pathHint`/`attributionHint` return nothing (IN9); signers file and dry-run unpack under the home or beside the zip (IN10); `Inspect` once (IN14); one `readCapped` (S7); one PATH walker (S6); `Lint` as a `Parse` option (S8) keeping `Lint(front string) error` as a thin wrapper so `TestLintDescriptionLimit` from Phase 4 stays green unchanged; incident-narrative comments cut to rationale (S5). Verbs unchanged (README map untouched).

## Failure modes

- A context edit that pushes the render over 22,000 fails `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock`; over 15,000 fails `TestRenderedContextUnderTarget`.
- A skill or agent that no longer parses fails `sh-agent install --home .agents/scratch/x` with the file named.
- A behavioural run that proves nothing (auto-denied, no skill loaded) is reported as such, never as n/N; the kit preamble asserts the fixture before the CLI starts.
- A struck skill leaves no dangling reference: `TestSkillLinksResolve` and `grep -rn python\|anti-ui-slop` over context, skills, docs.
- A REQUIREMENTS edit is made only after the operator approves its exact text (D29a); until then the phase ships without it and the task stays unticked.
- The real-home install fails the smoke checks → `sh-agent install` from the last good commit, reported.

## Verification

Tiers (guide §): 1 Go checks (every phase touching Go); 2 harness self-check (every phase touching context, agents, skills); 3 scratch-home install and drift; 3b report (Phase 1 redaction, Phase 8); 3c verb matrix (Phase 8); 3d search (Phase 1); 3e memory/dream (Phase 1); 4 sandbox CLI start (Phases 3–7); 5 real-home smoke (Phase 9); behavioural runs `claude -p --agents` n of N (Phase 4) and `--append-system-prompt` (Phase 3's size-tier paragraph); skill-matrix rows for every changed and new skill (Phase 9).
E2E criteria (yes/no): (a) the sandbox home of guide § 4 (logged-in copies, deleted by name after) installs the tree with no drift and both CLIs start and answer the canary; (b) in a scratch clone outside every checkout, driven from that sandbox home, `/init-project` then `/spec` then `/feature` produce a spec, a plan and a cold-read artifact; (c) `sh-agent dream --project` with the fake CLIs of guide § 3e on PATH, on a fixture database containing a tool call whose arguments sit in a string-only sub-message, leaks no argument into the recorded prompt; (d) the re-audit lists no high finding from the recon brief as open.
