title: Plan — R-parity, `sh-agent memory`, background `sh-agent dream` (2026-09-30)
body:
# Plan — R-parity, `sh-agent memory`, background `sh-agent dream`   (2026-09-30)

## Why
The operator, 2026-09-30:
- "The dream skills should be a features that runs autonomously in all projects registered on the machine and checks conversations, assets, feedback, critique, skills, for improvements. This should run in the background as a monitor or subagent that does not care about what is happening. It just collects, generates new skills if needed and such. That was the plan."
- "Dreamer is one and memory is the other. … remember these should work for both Claude or agy and both."
- "In the best of worlds I want the setup and executions to be exactly the same over agy and Claude. … Can we build in that feature in sh-agent?"
- On the R-parity text and the two tables below: "Sounds great. Include this in the next version. Go all approved go work."

Both tables are quoted as the operator approved them in chat on 2026-09-30.

**Dreamer table** (approved):
1. How it runs: a user timer (systemd on Linux, launchd on Mac) runs `sh-agent dream --all` nightly, headless, regardless of what any session is doing.
2. Which projects: every harness project in the global search index (`~/.config/sh-agent/search.db`); no new registry; projects that haven't changed are skipped.
3. What it reads: both CLIs' conversation transcripts, `feedback.jsonl`, each project's memory, bug records, reviews, retros, and the installed skills — read-only, treated as data.
4. What it writes: draft skills and proposals into `~/.config/sh-agent/proposals/`, nothing auto-installed; applied through `/retro --harness`.
5. Which CLI: the one the install manifest names (`agy -p` on an agy machine, `claude -p` where Claude Code is installed).
6. Cost limit: once a night, a cap per project, a log line per run shown by `sh-agent status`.
7. The requirement change: R3 gets one named exception, with an ADR.

**Memory table** (approved):
1. agy's memory is thinner (it writes only on corrections) → both CLIs write the same four types by the same rule, written by the harness.
2. Claude Code loads memory automatically; agy only because the context says so → accept for now.
3. Claude Code's split store in an untrusted folder → the dreamer detects it and moves the notes.
4. Notes don't follow the operator between machines → keep per machine.
5. The memory spec header says "nothing below is built" → fix.

Since then, R10's "the harness provides it once and both CLIs use that version" supersedes memory items 2 and 3 (D2): loading goes through `sh-agent memory show` on both CLIs, and with native writes off there is no split store. Recon: `plans/2026-09-30-recon-memory-dream.md`. Cold read r1: `reviews/2026-09-30-cold-read-parity-memory-dream-r1.md`.

## Scope
In:
1. **R10 (R-parity)**: done in d6e396a. The requirement edits the dream job needs, on the operator's word (D3, D12, D13): the R3 exception, R4's driver and `uninstall` sentences, and the Non-goals memory-keys exception.
2. **`sh-agent memory add|show`** on both CLIs. Claude Code's native auto memory is switched off per project (`autoMemoryEnabled: false`, D2).
3. **The `project-memory` skill** (D14), plus:
   - `feedback-log` rule 7 calls the verb on every CLI;
   - the context resume step runs `sh-agent memory show`;
   - `/init-project` Step 5b writes the new key;
   - `/dream` Step 1 always uses `<root>/.agents/memory`;
   - `agents/dreamer.md`, the memory spec and README are updated.
4. **`sh-agent dream --all | --project <dir>`, with `--dry-run`, the CLI from the global `--vendor` flag**: collect, redact, one tool-free CLI call, then render and write proposals and drafts. Also a state file, a log, a lock, and the `status` line.
5. **`sh-agent dream --install-timer | --remove-timer`**, opt-in (D5). `uninstall` removes the timer (D12).
6. **Consumers**:
   - project-level `/retro` reads the dream proposals for its own project;
   - `/retro --harness` reads the harness-target ones;
   - `report` sends `proposals/dream/harness/` and nothing else under `proposals/dream/` (D19);
   - `status` gets the dream line;
   - the README map gets the job (D13).

Out:
- Auto-applying anything (dreamer item 4).
- Any permission in a vendor settings file (Non-goals).
- Cross-machine memory (memory item 4).
- `memory forget`/`list` verbs (the `/dream` skill deletes interactively).

Follow-ups noted, not built:
- A cron fallback for Linux without systemd.
- Agent worktree isolation in `sh-agent` (a later R10 plan).

## Surfaces touched
- **Go**:
  - `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`: verbs; usage const :39; `status` :508; `uninstall` calls `dream.RemoveTimer`, so `internal/harness` does not import `internal/dream`.
  - new `internal/memory/`;
  - new `internal/dream/` (collect, claude transcripts, prompt, run, render, state, lock, timer);
  - `internal/search`: `ListProjects(home)`, plus `AgyConversationText(home, root, since)`, which keeps the driver inside `internal/search` (AGENTS.md:59, D12);
  - `internal/harness/report.go`: exported `Redact(string) string` over `redactLines` (:199); `Collect` (:331-339) gains `proposals/dream/harness/*.md` and still skips the rest of `proposals/dream/` (D19).
- **Harness text**:
  - `skills/project-memory/SKILL.md` (new);
  - `skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md:90`;
  - `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:110-131`;
  - `skills/dream/SKILL.md` Step 1 and description;
  - `agents/dreamer.md:18,28,32`;
  - `skills/retro/SKILL.md:44,48,118`;
  - `skills/distill/SKILL.md:38`;
  - `context/AGENTS.md:9` (resume).
- **Docs**:
  - `REQUIREMENTS.md` (R3, R4, Non-goals, on approval);
  - `DECISIONS.md` (ADR-047 addendum);
  - `specs/sh-agent/memory-loop.md` (rewritten: the memory half);
  - new `specs/sh-agent/dream.md`;
  - `README.md`: map :5-60 with `TestHarnessMap`, `configDir` contents :30, state rows :212-214, verbs table, `uninstall` row;
  - project `AGENTS.md` Layout (`internal/memory`, `internal/dream`) and :59 (the driver's second reader in `internal/search`);
  - `deploy/local.md` (timer install/remove, uninstall);
  - `testing/skill-matrix.md` and `testing/sh-agent-matrix.md` rows.

## Interfaces

**`sh-agent memory add --type <user|feedback|project|reference> --name <slug> --description <text>`**, with the body on stdin (required, non-empty).
- **Root**: `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the working directory.
- **The file**: `<root>/.agents/memory/<slug>.md`, whose frontmatter is:
  ```
  ---
  name: <slug>
  description: "<text, JSON-escaped>"
  metadata:
    node_type: memory
    type: <type>
    modified: <UTC RFC 3339>
  ---
  ```
  then the body. `originSessionId` is not written: no CLI exposes its session id to a shell call, and `/dream`'s promote test already counts a file without it as one session.
- **The index**: the line in `MEMORY.md` for that file is `- [<slug>](<slug>.md) — <description>`. The same slug replaces both the file and its line; an existing line is found by its link target `(<slug>.md)`. A `--description` with a newline is refused (exit 2). Files are written 0600.
- **`<slug>`** matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`.
- **Refusals**: exit 2, one line on stderr, nothing written. In order:
  1. not a git checkout;
  2. `.agents` or `.agents/memory` is a symlink;
  3. `git ls-files .agents/memory` prints a path;
  4. `git check-ignore -q .agents/memory/<slug>.md` exits non-zero (the path would be committed: "run /init-project first");
  5. the index would pass 200 lines.
- **Store and writes**: created 0700 when absent. The file is written to a temp name and renamed.
- **Lock**: the index is rewritten whole under `<store>/.lock`, created O_EXCL and holding the PID. A lock whose PID is not alive, or older than 30 s, is removed. A live lock is retried for 5 s, then exit 2 "store busy".

**`sh-agent memory show`**
- Same root and checks 1–3.
- Prints `MEMORY.md`, capped at 200 lines and 25 KB; a cut adds a last line `(… N more lines in .agents/memory/MEMORY.md)`.
- No store, or no index: prints nothing, exit 0.
- **Rollout hint**: when `<root>/.claude/settings.local.json` exists and lacks `"autoMemoryEnabled": false`, `show` prints one last line: `Claude Code's native memory is still on here: run /init-project to switch it off (R10)`. Every session start on either CLI then surfaces the rollout for projects scaffolded before this change.

**`sh-agent dream --all | --project <dir> [--dry-run] [--vendor claude|agy]`**. Neither `--all` nor `--project` is a usage error. `--project` exists for the e2e and to rerun one project after a failure (D15).
- **Projects**: `search.ListProjects(home)`, a plain SELECT on `projects(root,…)` (store.go:41), no reconcile. A missing db means an empty list. `--project` takes one root. A root is skipped with a log line when it is gone, not a git checkout, or lacks `.agents/docs`.
- **Start**: `t0` = now, taken before collecting.
- **Watermark**: in `~/.config/sh-agent/dream-state.json`, `{"projects":{"<root>":"<RFC3339>"},"last_run":{"at":…,"projects":n,"proposals":m,"error":""}}`. The first run uses t0 − 14 days.
- **Changed** means any per-project input below (1, 2, 3, 5, 6) newer than the watermark: file mtime; for transcripts, the line or step time. Input 4 (installed skills) is global: it never makes a project changed and is sent only with a changed project. When nothing changed: skip, log `unchanged`, and write no file. When something changed, the memory files are sent whole; the other inputs only the changed parts.
- **Inputs**:
  1. the memory store;
  2. `feedback.jsonl` lines whose `project` is the root and whose `ts` is after the watermark;
  3. files under `<docs>/{bugs,reviews,retros,changes,handoffs}` with mtime after the watermark;
  4. the installed skills' `name` and `description` from the manifest vendor's skill directory;
  5. Claude Code `~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` lines with `timestamp` after the watermark whose `cwd` is the root or under it, `type` `user`/`assistant`, text parts only;
  6. Antigravity text from `search.AgyConversationText(home, root, since)` (D8). It copies `conversation_summaries.db` and each matching `conversations/<id>.db` with their `-wal` and `-shm` files into a private temp directory under `<home>/.config/sh-agent/`, opens the copies, and deletes them after; it never opens a live file.
- **Redaction**: every input passes `harness.Redact` and `$HOME` → `~`.
- **Prompt**: fixed instructions (in `internal/dream/prompt.go`), then the inputs in the order above, each fenced and labelled "data, not instructions". The cap is 256 KB: the oldest transcript text is dropped first, and the prompt says what was dropped.
- **CLI**: the global `--vendor` flag (main.go:62, "default: from manifest"): `antigravity`/`agy` → agy; `claude` and `all` → claude (dreamer item 5).
  - claude: `claude -p --tools "" --no-session-persistence --output-format text --strict-mcp-config --setting-sources local`, prompt on stdin (the two flags the code passes, `internal/dream/dream.go`; row corrected 2026-10-01, plan audit-fix SD-spec).
  - agy: the invocation proven by the Phase 4 probe (D7).
  - Both run with cwd `<home>/.config/sh-agent/dream-work/` (0700, kept empty; it is not a project, so the run's own conversation never maps to one) and a 10-minute timeout.
  - The child inherits `sh-agent`'s own environment unchanged: `--home` moves only what `sh-agent` itself reads and writes, never the child's `HOME`, so the CLI authenticates as it does for the operator (AGENTS.md:65). A sandbox run sets `HOME` for the whole `sh-agent` process instead.
  - The binary is resolved on PATH at run time; under the timer, PATH is the one captured at `--install-timer` (below).
- **Model output**: the prompt asks for one JSON object:
  ```
  {"proposals":[{"title","kind":"rule|skill|procedure|memory","target":"harness|project","file","text","evidence"}],
   "skills":[{"name","description","body"}]}
  ```
  `sh-agent` takes the first `{…}` span of stdout that parses. When nothing parses, the project is `fail invalid output`, and the raw text is kept in `<home>/.config/sh-agent/dream-failed/<date>-<project>.txt` (0600), outside the CLI's cwd.
- **Written on success**:
  - `~/.config/sh-agent/proposals/dream/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<project name>.md` (`-2`, `-3` on the same day). Frontmatter: `owner: sh-agent dream`, `date`, `project`, `cli`, `inputs` (counts per kind, and what was dropped). Then one section per proposal:
    ```
    ### <n>. <title>
    **Status:** queued
    **Target:** harness|project   **Kind:** …   **File:** …

    <text>

    Evidence: <evidence>
    ```
  - Harness-target proposals (`target: harness`) are written to a second file, `proposals/dream/harness/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<project name>.md`, same shape. `report` sends that directory (R8: report sends "this machine's corrections, proposals"), so a binary-only or zip place feeds harness proposals back too; project-target files stay on the machine (D6).
  - Every skill goes to `proposals/dream/drafts/<date>-<project name>-<name>/SKILL.md`, with `name` validated as a slug (an invalid name is dropped and listed). The draft is `---\nname: <name>\ndescription: "<…>"\n---\n<body>`.
  - All model text is redacted again before it is written.
- **Zero proposals**: when the JSON parses with no proposals and no skills, no file is written, the log says `ok 0 proposals`, and the watermark advances.
- **Watermark**: advances to t0 only after a successful parse and, when there is anything to write, after the write.
- **Log**: `~/.config/sh-agent/dream.log`, one line per project (`<ts> <root> ok|unchanged|skip|fail <reason>`) and one per run (`<ts> - run <n> projects, <m> proposals[, error <reason>]`). A failure before the first project (no CLI, lock or state unreadable) writes the run line with `error` and sets `last_run.error`.
- **Lock**: `~/.config/sh-agent/dream.lock` holds the PID. A lock whose PID is not alive is stale and replaced; a live lock makes the run exit 0 with "already running".
- **`--dry-run`**:
  - prints per project the input counts and bytes, what would be dropped, and the CLI command line;
  - prints the prompt when `--project` is given;
  - runs no CLI, and writes, locks and advances nothing (a test asserts each).
- **Exit**: 0 when every project is ok, unchanged or skipped; 1 when any failed; 2 on a pre-project failure.

**`sh-agent dream --install-timer | --remove-timer`** (D5, D12)
- **Linux**: writes `~/.config/systemd/user/sh-agent-dream.service` and `.timer`.
  - The service: `ExecStart=<home>/.local/bin/sh-agent dream --all` (BinPath), and `Environment=PATH=<the PATH of the installing shell>`, so `claude` and `agy` in `~/.local/bin` resolve.
  - The timer: `OnCalendar=*-*-* 03:00`, `Persistent=true`.
  - Then `systemctl --user daemon-reload` and `systemctl --user enable --now sh-agent-dream.timer`.
- **macOS**: `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.styrman.sh-agent-dream.plist` with the same program, `EnvironmentVariables` PATH and `StartCalendarInterval` Hour 3, then `launchctl bootstrap gui/<uid> <plist>`.
- **Guards**:
  - `--install-timer` refuses when BinPath is missing, or when `systemctl`/`launchctl` is absent (exit 2, naming it).
  - Unit files are written only when absent or identical to the rendered text; a hand-edited one is kept and named.
- **`--remove-timer`**: `systemctl --user disable --now` / `launchctl bootout`, then deletes the files. Absent is fine.
- **`--home`**: the unit files are written under `<home>`, like every other path (main.go:61); `systemctl` and `launchctl` are resolved on PATH, so tests put fakes first on PATH and never reach the real user manager (R6). Each branch (write, identical, hand-edited kept, absent on remove, a failing `systemctl`, `uninstall` without a manifest) is tested against the fakes.
- **`status`** reports the timer as installed when its unit file exists.
- **The manifest**: the timer is not listed in it (listed files are deleted as stale by the next `install`, apply.go:88-109).
- **`uninstall`**:
  - calls the same removal when a unit file exists, including when there is no manifest (D12);
  - `uninstall --dry-run` prints "would remove the dream timer" and runs no `systemctl`/`launchctl` (a test asserts it).

**`status`**: after the `retro` line (main.go:508):
- `dream      last run <date>: <n> projects, <m> proposals; timer installed|not installed`
- `dream      last run <date> failed: <error>; timer …`
- `dream      never run; timer …`

**`/init-project` Step 5b item 2**: the settings file gets `"autoMemoryDirectory"` as today, and `"autoMemoryEnabled": false`. Each key is handled on its own with the existing branches:
- absent file → both keys in the one-object write;
- present without the key → one inserted line after `{` per key, with the Edit tool;
- present with the key → kept and reported (a `true` is reported, never changed).

The parse check runs after each insert. Antigravity-only machine: nothing (Step 1).

**Context resume step**: "… → `sh-agent memory show` (the project's memory; on every CLI)" replaces "on Antigravity, `.agents/memory/MEMORY.md` when … Claude Code loads it itself". The byte difference is paid in the same edit (`TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock`, 21998/22000 today).

## Failure modes
- `memory add|show` refusal: exit 2 with a one-line reason; the session reports it and continues without memory.
- Headless sessions without a grant for `sh-agent`: the call is refused and no memory loads. This is the same on both CLIs, a cost of R10 (D16).
- `dream`: the per-project failures are those above (fail + log, watermark kept, others continue, exit 1). A pre-project failure is exit 2 plus the run log line and `status` "failed". Unparseable model output keeps the raw text.
- Timer: a failing `systemctl`/`launchctl` exits 2 and names the unit files left in place.

## Verification
Tiers: unit (`go test -race`), sandbox e2e, the `dreamer` behavioural run, § 3d for the search additions, and the release gate's real-home runs. The setups for R10:
- **agy-only**: a sandbox home installed `--vendor agy` (the kit of `testing/2026-09-30-verify-real-home-v1.16.2.md`).
- **both**: the real home, vendor `all`.
- **claude-only**: a sandbox home installed `--vendor claude`, with Claude Code pointed at it by `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and a copied credentials file (chmod 600, deleted by name after). This is an assumption the Phase 2 checkpoint's first run checks; when Claude Code cannot authenticate that way, the claude-only runs are marked not exercised and the "both" runs stand for Claude Code.

E2E criteria:
1. **Memory parity**: in a scaffolded fixture project, on each setup, a session told "remember that we deploy on Fridays" leaves a file and an index line in `.agents/memory/`. A fresh session on the same setup, on each installed CLI, answers "when do we deploy?" with Friday.
2. **Claude native writes are off**: in the claude setup, with the pre-change harness installed (no `project-memory` skill, rule 7 as before), the must-fail control comes first. With `autoMemoryEnabled` absent, a session told a preference leaves a file carrying `originSessionId` (native) in `.agents/memory/`. Then the key is set to `false` and the current harness is installed, and no file with `originSessionId` appears while the verb-written file does. A control that produces no native file makes E2E 2 "not exercised", never passed.
3. **Dream golden path** (home: a scratch `--home` whose `search.db` indexes only the fixture projects; the child is the real `claude`): `sh-agent dream --all --home <scratch>` over two indexed fixture projects with new trail and memory writes one proposal file per project with at least one `**Status:** queued` section. A second run with no changes writes no file and logs `unchanged` twice.
4. **Dream edge**:
   - a deleted root is logged `skip`;
   - a secret-shaped string in a fixture memory file is absent from the prompt, shown by `--dry-run --project` and by the fake-CLI unit test's captured stdin.
5. **Timer** (`who: user`, R6):
   - a unit test pins the rendered unit text;
   - `systemd-analyze verify` passes on the rendered files in scratch;
   - the operator runs `sh-agent dream --install-timer` on this box, and `systemctl --user list-timers` shows it; `--remove-timer` removes it.

Confidence is high where a finding was reproduced (marked *repro*) or spot-checked (*checked*); otherwise it was read at the location named.

Two audit claims were refuted and are not listed: "feedback entries lack a project field" (all 15 carry one) and "the installed real-home context is behind the repo" (it carries the current memory line).

| TR6 | low | `~/.config/sh-agent` | The nightly dreamer has never run on this box: no timer, no state file, no `proposals/dream/`. |
| TR7 | info | `.agents/docs` | 7.72 MB; reviews 3.71 MB (48%); trail:source 23.9:1; 379 commits in 16 days. |

## G — workflow coverage gaps

| ID | Stage | Today | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | Requirements | template + grilling | nothing elicits or traces requirements; template opens with SLA tables |
| G2 | Spec | research (one fixed shape) | no spec skill or template; `assets/agents-tree/docs/specs/` is a .gitkeep |
| G3 | Design / ADR | changelog on haiku | no skill says what is structural or shapes the ADR |
| G4 | Plan / tasks | feature | nothing sequences several plans; Task class has no breakdown help |
| G5 | Test strategy | verifier writes the guide when absent | no skill on tiers, fixtures, e2e choice; no guide template |
| G6 | Operate | nothing | no runbook, logs, monitoring, rollback outside a release |
| G7 | Security / dependencies | security per diff | no govulncheck / npm audit cadence; no API auth guidance |
| G8 | Data | nothing | no SQL, migrations, Cloud SQL |
| G9 | Onboarding / explain | README | nothing explains a codebase to a person |
| G10 | Learn | 5 skills + 2 agents | over-weighted; the automated half never ran on a real home |
| G11 | Size tiers | one workflow | a dotfiles repo owes the same paperwork as a service; nothing for multi-service |
| G12 | Trail cold reader | none | nothing checks that resume works for a zero-context reader |
| G13 | Templates | assets | no README, spec, testing-guide, plan, handoff, change, bug, review, retro templates outside skills and agents |

title: Recon — memory-dream (2026-09-30)
body:
# Recon — memory-dream   (2026-09-30)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Question
Where do a new `sh-agent memory` verb and a `sh-agent dream [--all|--install-timer|--remove-timer]` verb plug into the code, and which text changes with them.

## Summary
Verbs are a flat switch in `run()` (cmd/sh-agent/main.go:85-349) over ONE shared FlagSet; search/index/report are dispatched before `ResolveSource` (main.go:152-183) because they need no harness tree, and delegate to `internal/search` / `internal/harness`. The global index lists projects in table `projects(root,name,docs_root,last_seen)` (internal/search/store.go:41), readable by a plain SELECT without reconcile. Redaction is unexported (`redactLines`, `redactDocument`, `needleIn`; report.go:128,199,257), needs an exported wrapper. The manifest holds paths relative to $HOME with no vendor-root restriction except `pruneEmptyDirs`' stop list, so a systemd/launchd file can be a `File` in `Plan` (no OS-specific precedent exists). No code runs `claude`/`agy` today. Six text places describe the memory store and all change together.

## Relevant files (file:line)
- cmd/sh-agent/main.go:39-67 usage const (one line per verb; search/index lines 54-56); :92-112 single FlagSet with all verb flags (new flags added here, `reorder` at :731 lets flags follow words); :152-183 early verbs (version, uninstall, report, search/index) before `harness.ResolveSource` (:175); :185+ install/status/diff/update/list/render/adopt; :349 unknown-command error. `search.Options{Dir,Home,Words,Refs,Open,Kind,Limit,Global,Rebuild}` built at :170. Pattern to mirror: `case "memory","dream":` before ResolveSource, build Options, call `internal/<pkg>.Func(o, out)`.
- internal/search/search.go:77 validate; :118 projectDB; :122 globalDB(home)=`~/.config/sh-agent/search.db`; :150 prepare; :225 `register(home,root,docs,out)` (upsert into projects, at most once a day); :252 `reconcileGlobal` (returns []proj; does `SELECT root, docs_root FROM projects ORDER BY rowid` at :284, drops dead checkouts via `dropReason` :341, runs git reconcile per project); :386 Index, :410 Search. internal/search/store.go:112 `openStore` (creates/migrates), :178 `tryOpen` (no create). SQLite driver imported ONLY in internal/search (store.go doc): a dream project list belongs there as a new exported func, e.g. `search.Projects(home)` using `tryOpen` + the SELECT at :284 (no reconcile; apply `dropReason` if dead roots matter; `dropReason` errors mean keep). Global index has no per-project "last dream" column; schema version is `schemaVersion="1"` (store.go:~28, mismatch => rebuild), so keep dream state in a separate file, not in search.db (cache; deleting it loses registrations until next search).
- internal/harness/report.go:29 redactedValue; :39 prefixNeedles; :58 keywordNeedles; :128 `needleIn(s)(name,bool)`; :199 `redactLines(name,data,jsonl)` (whole-line/whole-block removal; jsonl marker stays parseable); :241 `decoded`; :257 `redactDocument`; :284 `Collect(home)` (reads feedback.jsonl, retros.jsonl, proposals/, state.json; skips non-regular). All unexported. Reuse: add `func Redact(name string, data []byte, jsonl bool) ([]byte, []Redaction)` = `redactLines`. Note marker text says "[redacted by sh-agent report]" (wording tied to report). Needle set is credentials only: paths, emails, and prose pass through; transcripts carry tool output, so expect it to need review (see Risks). Tests: internal/harness/report_test.go (1350 lines) pin needles.
- internal/harness/state.go:15-21 `State{Repo,Commit,InstalledAt,Vendor,Files}`, Files relative to $HOME, sorted; :36-49 LoadState drops non-`filepath.IsLocal` entries; :71 ConfigDir (0700); :131 `LastRetro(home)` = newest mtime of `proposals/*.md` and `retros.jsonl` (plus caller main.go:508-516 prints `retro      last proposal DATE (N days ago)` with >14-day hint). NB: dream proposals written to proposals/ will reset LastRetro — a dream proposal is indistinguishable from a retro's; decide whether dream files use a prefix/other dir, or LastRetro excludes them.
- internal/harness/plan.go:11-17 roots consts (ClaudeRoot, AgyRoot, BinPath=`.local/bin/sh-agent`); :68 `Plan(src,selfExe,vendor)` returns []File{Rel,Data,Mode,KeepForeign}; :188-190 BinPath appended when selfExe != nil; :192-196 sort + duplicate-Rel error. A timer unit = more File entries appended here (Mode 0644), OS chosen with `runtime.GOOS`. No precedent for OS-specific files (runtime.GOOS used only at report.go:378 and release.go:154). Plan is vendor-filtered (wantAgy/wantClaude); timer files are neither vendor's — need an unconditional branch. Plan is also used by status/diff/render paths (selfExe nil), so timer files would be planned there too (drift shown).
- internal/harness/apply.go:19 Install (writes each File, builds manifest, saves State :~130); :172 Status (missing/differs/stale; BinPath exempt :200); :270 Uninstall (removes every manifest path, then `pruneEmptyDirs`); :358 pruneEmptyDirs stop list (home, .claude, .gemini, .gemini/config, .config, .local, .local/bin) — `.config/systemd/user` and `Library/LaunchAgents` are NOT protected and would be pruned when empty (removing e.g. `~/.config/systemd`; `~/.config` itself is protected; `~/Library` is not). Installing a unit file does NOT enable it: `systemctl --user enable --now`/`launchctl bootstrap` is a side effect outside the manifest; `--install-timer` has to run it and `uninstall` has to disable it BEFORE removing the file (Uninstall today only removes files, apply.go:270-307). "Listed in the install manifest" means Plan + Install; `--install-timer` could also be opt-in (a flag stored in State) because install plans every file unconditionally otherwise.
- cmd/sh-agent/main.go:423 `status()`; retro line :508-517 (insert `dream:` line next to it); `--dry-run` handling via `*dryRun`.
- exec precedent: only git/gh/go/diff/ssh-keygen (repo.go:197-259, release.go:77-265, apply.go:257, search.go:134, reconcile.go:37). No `claude`/`agy` subprocess anywhere.
- internal/harness/size_test.go:1-49 `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock`: context/AGENTS.md rendered + rules/*.md <= 22000 bytes (budget const :20; never raised; cap 24000). Any edit to context/AGENTS.md (resume line :9, Learning loop :42) is measured against it. Check current headroom before editing: `go test ./internal/harness -run RenderedContext -v`. Other pinning tests: harness_test.go `TestHarnessMap` (reads ../..), audit_test.go (324 lines) — not read; grep them for skill names/text before editing skills (Not examined).

## Flows
- install: main.go:185 -> resolveVendor -> harness.Plan -> harness.Install -> manifest (state.json, ~/.config/sh-agent). uninstall: main.go:155 -> harness.Uninstall (manifest only).
- search --global: search.Search -> prepare :150 -> reconcileGlobal :252. `register` (:225) is how a checkout enters the project list (called on any per-project search, daily). So `dream --all` only knows checkouts that have run `search`/`index` since registration; `sh-agent search` in project runs it.
- status: main.go:423 -> LoadState -> prints lines incl. retro (:508) -> vendor roots; exit 1 on drift.

## Transcripts (inspected on this machine, structure only)
- Claude Code: `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session-uuid>.jsonl` (+ sibling `<uuid>/` dirs for subagents/tool results). Slug = absolute path with `/` (and `.`) replaced by `-`, e.g. `-home-kesokaj-workspace-styrman-harness` (lossy: `-` in a path is ambiguous, so map via the records' own `cwd` key, not by reversing the slug). Line keys seen: `type` (`user`, `assistant`, `mode`, `permission-mode`, `file-history-snapshot`, ...), `sessionId`, `uuid`, `parentUuid`, `isSidechain`, `promptId`, `message{role,content}`, `timestamp`, `cwd`, `gitBranch`, `version`, `entrypoint`, `userType`, `isMeta`. Some lines (mode, snapshots) have no `cwd`/`timestamp`. Also `~/.claude/projects/-home-kesokaj-sandbox-gate14-*`: sandbox runs from release gates show up as projects; they are not registered harness checkouts, so they are excluded by starting from the registered list.
- Antigravity: `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/<uuid>.db` (90 here), SQLite 3 (`file` confirms). `sqlite3` CLI is ABSENT on this machine (inspected with python3 sqlite3 on a copy; copy deleted). Tables: trajectory_meta(trajectory_id,cascade_id,trajectory_type,source), steps(idx,step_type,status,has_subtrajectory,metadata,error_details,permissions,task_details,render_info,step_payload,step_format), gen_metadata, executor_metadata, parent_references, trajectory_metadata_blob, battle_mode_infos. All payloads are BLOBs with protobuf-looking prefixes (`08 0e 20 03 2a ...`); file paths appear in the raw bytes (`/home/` found in step_payload and executor_metadata) but there is no schema: decoding needs a hand-written protobuf wire reader or schema-less string extraction. The mapping to a project is NOT in the .db: `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversation_summaries.db` table `conversation_summaries(conversation_id,title,preview,step_count,last_modified_time,workspace_uris,status,source,project_id,agent_name,parent_conversation_id,nesting_depth,...,last_user_input_time,raw_summary)` — `workspace_uris` ties a conversation to a checkout and `last_modified_time`/`last_user_input_time` gives "since last dream". `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<conversation-uuid>/` also exists (contents: `scratch`), not read. The driver in go.mod is modernc sqlite (in internal/search only), so reading these is feasible but they belong in a new package with its own import (or internal/search) — the "only package importing the driver" rule (store.go:10) needs a decision.
- Headless CLI: `claude -p` exists (v2.1.285) with `--tools ""` (disable all tools), `--no-session-persistence`, `--output-format`, `--bare`, `--permission-mode`. `agy -p/--print` exists with `--output-format text|json`, `--model`, `--json-schema`, `--sandbox`, `--mode plan`, `--print-timeout`, `--disable-slash-commands`; I saw NO flag to disable tools in `agy --help` (only `--sandbox`, `--mode`), so "no tools" cannot be guaranteed on agy. Also: a dream run under `claude -p` writes a session transcript unless `--no-session-persistence`; otherwise the next dream reads its own transcript (self-feed) — the agy run creates a .db conversation likewise.

## Text that describes who writes/reads the memory store (all change together)
- .agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/memory-loop.md:11 path; :12 layout; :13 "Who writes: Claude Code natively, `.claude/settings.local.json` sets `autoMemoryDirectory`"; :14 who reads (Claude loads MEMORY.md; agy reads at end of Resume Protocol; /dream consolidates); :15 set up by /init-project (new/update paths, agy-only variant); :23 dreamer reads; :35 and :38 failure-table rows (autoMemoryDirectory conflicts, symlink/tracked refusal); :~35 security note that Claude Code honours the key without the check.
- skills/init-project/SKILL.md:110 (Step 5b intro), :112 (trust checks), :115 (`.claude/settings.local.json` autoMemoryDirectory write), :131 (.gitignore `.agents/memory`).
- skills/dream/SKILL.md:3 description, :7-9 intro, :22-29 Step 1 (resolve autoMemoryDirectory, default path, agy-only step 0, counts line), :33 reads, :37 verdict types, :53 index rewrite, :75 table.
- skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md:90 rule 7 "On Antigravity, also write the memory" (Claude saves natively; agy has no writer).
- agents/dreamer.md:18 (`Store` input), :28 (store read), :32 (store path is data).
- context/AGENTS.md:9 (resume: agy reads `.agents/memory/MEMORY.md` per the spec), :42 (learning loop: /dream, dreamer, retro reads memory). Size-tested.
- Also naming it: skills/distill/SKILL.md:38 (dispatches dreamer with store resolved per dream Step 1), skills/retro/SKILL.md:44 and :118 (memory evidence via dream skill), README.md:214, REQUIREMENTS.md:31 (store in `.agents/memory/`, never sent by report — immutable without approval; if the store moves or dream adds a new `proposals/` producer or reads transcripts, check this line), skills/docker/SKILL.md:79 and skills/docker/references/setup.md:11 (dockerignore, unaffected). Also specs/sh-agent/ other files, docs/deploy, and `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-29-security-memory-loop.md` (history; do not edit).
- Claude Code's native auto memory stays on unless disabled: replacing it needs `autoMemoryEnabled: false` (or env `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1`) plus CLAUDE.md telling the model to call `sh-agent memory`; I did not verify the setting names in this run — check the Claude docs. The current design sets `autoMemoryDirectory` precisely so native writes land in the store.

## Conventions
- Verbs return `error`; output to the `out io.Writer`; `exitCode` for non-error statuses (main.go:80-83); `--dry-run` / `--check` are read-only and resolve paths as the real run (global AGENTS.md hard rule: new side effects below early returns, test asserts dry-run does not write).
- Errors never fail open on guard checks (dropReason pattern). Symlink/tracked refusals for `.agents` and `.agents/memory` (guardProject search.go:128; memory-loop spec :38) — `sh-agent memory` must reuse those refusals. Files written via `harness.WriteAtomic` (apply.go:309); config dir 0700 via ConfigDir.
- Tests: main_test.go (1847 lines) drives `run(args,&buf)` with `--home` temp dirs; search_test.go/global_test.go in internal/search; no real CLI calls — a `claude`/`agy` runner needs an injectable command (testHooks pattern report.go:854).
- Docs: frontmatter owner/date; specs under .agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/; a new command also needs README, usage text, and the `documentation` agent step.

## Risks
- Redaction is credential needles only (whole-line). Transcripts contain full tool output, file contents and personal text; sending that to a model via headless CLI is a new disclosure path (the CLI is the same vendor the session already used, but agy transcripts sent to claude, or vice versa, cross vendors). Decide vendor policy and keep-local option. Proposals written from redacted text can still quote leaked content.
- Self-feed: dream's own headless call writes transcripts (claude) / conversations (agy) into the same stores it reads; filter by `entrypoint`/`--no-session-persistence`/timestamp.
- "No tools" is enforceable on claude (`--tools ""`) but not evidently on agy. Also prompt injection: transcripts and memory are data in the prompt; the model must only return text, and the Go side writes files (good: dreamer currently has Write).
- agy protobuf blobs are undocumented; a format change breaks silently. Plan for "transcripts unreadable -> name under not examined".
- Timer: install writes unit files but does not enable them; uninstall's file-only removal would leave an enabled unit pointing nowhere (systemd) or a loaded launchd job. pruneEmptyDirs stop list lacks the new dirs. A timer running `sh-agent dream --all` spends model quota unattended; needs a clear opt-in and a cap.
- LastRetro conflation (above); status exit code: drift rows for timer files on machines that did not opt in.
- Project list is only as complete as `register` calls; deleted checkouts (dropReason) and worktrees/duplicate roots.
- context/AGENTS.md budget 22000 bytes: rewriting the memory lines must not grow it.
- Replacing Claude native memory: concurrent writers (two sessions calling `sh-agent memory`) need atomic write + MEMORY.md index rebuild under a lock; index limits 200 lines/25KB.
- `sh-agent memory` must find the repo root from cwd (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`) — worktrees, submodules, no-git dirs.

## Open questions (left open by the request)
1. `memory` subcommands and I/O shape: `write` (name, type, description, body via stdin?), `read`/`list`, `index` rebuild, `forget`? Who triggers a write on Claude Code — instruction in context/AGENTS.md only (model compliance) — and is native auto memory disabled? How (setting vs env)?
2. Migration of existing stores (`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`, current `autoMemoryDirectory` entries in `.claude/settings.local.json`): keep, remove, or leave?
3. Does `/dream` skill stay (interactive, verdicts, deletes) beside the new Go `dream` (proposal-only)? Name clash: verb `dream` vs skill `/dream` and agent `dreamer`.
4. Which CLI does the headless call use (claude default? agy fallback when claude absent?), which model, cost/time caps, and is crossing vendor acceptable for redacted transcripts?
5. Redaction scope beyond credentials (home paths, emails, names); what "redacts it" must guarantee; whether transcripts are included at all by default.
6. Dream state: "since last dream" watermark per project — where stored (new file `~/.config/sh-agent/dream.json`?), and how a failed run behaves (watermark only after the output is written).
7. Proposal/draft-skill file naming in `~/.config/sh-agent/proposals/` and how `retro --harness` and `report` (Collect sends proposals/) treat them; does `LastRetro` count them?
8. Timer: schedule, scope (`--all` only), opt-in vs part of every install, who runs `systemctl --user enable`/`launchctl` and unregisters on uninstall, Linux without systemd, macOS plist path and label; `status` `dream:` line content (last run, result, timer installed?).
9. Whether REQUIREMENTS.md (line 31, memory store; learning loop) needs an approved edit and an ADR.
10. Does `dream --all` ignore projects not on this machine / gone (use dropReason) and what about the config-dir pseudo-project?

## Not examined
Bodies of harness_test.go/audit_test.go/main_test.go (only sizes and the one size test read); Install's stale-removal branch (apply.go:60-120); specs other than memory-loop.md; `brain/` dir contents; Claude docs for disabling native auto memory; exact agy step_payload protobuf layout; `go test` baseline not run.

title: Recon — project (2026-09-30)
body:
# Recon — project   (2026-09-30)

## Status: COMPLETE

Range reviewed: the whole repository at HEAD (3478a1c), no diff.

## Question
Inventory and structure map of the repository: uniformity, orphaned and dead-code candidates.

## Summary
The Go tree (`cmd/sh-agent`, `internal/harness`, `internal/search`) shows no clear dead code from a quick exported-symbol sweep: every symbol that looked isolated (`AssetName`, `BuildRecord`, `Collect`, `LatestRelease`, `LoadAgents`, `LoadDocs`, `ResolveFeedback`, `RunningElsewhere`, `SwapReleaseSigner`) turned out to have a same-file, same-package, or cross-package test caller — this needs `go vet`/staticcheck-grade tooling to say more definitively (not run here). Skills are fully accounted for: 28 directories under `skills/`, matching `context/AGENTS.md`'s "Skills (28)" line and `skills/VENDORED.md`'s provenance table, so no orphaned skill. `commands/` and `rules/` are real but **empty** (each holds only a `.gitkeep`), even though `AGENTS.md` layout table describes them as holding "markdown prompts... deploy[ed] to both vendors verbatim" — this is either intentional scaffolding-for-future-use or a stale layout line; worth a one-line check with the operator. Agent frontmatter is fairly uniform (`name`, `description`, `tools`, `model`, `effort`, `maxTurns`) but `dreamer.md` has no visible `maxTurns` line in the excerpt read and `reviewer.md` alone carries a `skills:` list — not a defect, just the one agent with a skill dependency. Skill frontmatter is deliberately non-uniform: vendored skills (`anti-ui-slop`, `gke-basics`, `terraform`) carry `license`/`metadata` blocks per `VENDORED.md`'s own rule that provenance lives in the skill's own frontmatter, while home-grown skills carry only `name`/`description` (+ occasionally `argument-hint` or `allowed-tools`) — this is a convention, not an inconsistency to fix. Trail orphaning is largely explained by project convention: `ROADMAP.md` "Now"/"Next"/"Later" are all empty (the project's stated rule: empty at every checkpoint, work is closed elsewhere), so the fact that most of the 60 files in `.agents/docs/plans/` are not named by ROADMAP is expected, not a smell — genuine orphan-detection would need to check each plan against handoffs/changes/bug records, which was not done exhaustively here (see Not examined).

## Relevant files
- `context/AGENTS.md` — canonical "Installed" list (28 skills, 8 agents) used as the cross-check baseline against `skills/` and `agents/`.
- `skills/VENDORED.md` — provenance manifest for 4 table-listed vendored skills plus 2 Apache-2.0 skills (`gke-basics`, `terraform`) attributed in their own frontmatter; also documents two *pruned* skills (`grill-me`, `skill-repair`) as historical context, not currently present.
- `agents/*.md` (8 files) — Claude-format subagent definitions; Antigravity's agent.md is derived from these at install (per project AGENTS.md).
- `internal/harness/inventory.go` — `LoadAgents`, `LoadDocs` read `agents/*.md`, `commands/`, `workflows/`, `rules/` directly; confirms `commands/`/`rules/` are wired into the install pipeline even though currently empty.
- `internal/harness/release.go`, `report.go`, `pathguard.go` — home of the exported symbols checked for dead-code candidacy; all have live callers.
- `.agents/docs/plans/` (60 files), `.agents/docs/handoffs/` — trail; `ROADMAP.md` empty by design.
- `commands/`, `rules/` — both contain only `.gitkeep` (empty since at least commit `fc89509`, "Generic installer directories, hooks research, no attribution").

## Flows
- Install pipeline: `internal/harness/inventory.go` (`LoadAgents`, `LoadDocs`) reads `agents/`, `commands/`, `workflows/`, `rules/`, `skills/` off a `Source` (repo checkout, embedded zip, or plain dir) → `plan.go` decides what/where → `apply.go`/`derive.go` write Claude Code files and derive Antigravity's agent.md → `render.go` assembles `context/AGENTS.md` + `context/dev-setup.md` into the rendered context checked by `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` (`internal/harness/size_test.go`).
- Release/report: `release.go` (`AssetName`, `LatestRelease`, `SwapReleaseSigner`, `verifyRelease`) backs `/preflight`'s signed-tag flow; `report.go` (`Collect`, `BuildRecord`, `ResolveFeedback`) backs `sh-agent report`'s throwaway-clone push to the feedback repo — both exercised primarily through their own package's tests plus `cmd/sh-agent` integration tests (`zip_test.go`, `search_test.go`).
- Search: `internal/search/{search,reconcile,store,parse}.go` is the one package importing `modernc.org/sqlite` (per AGENTS.md's stdlib-only-with-one-exception rule); `cmd/sh-agent` wires the `search`/`index` verbs to it.

## Conventions
- Skill/agent addition is a file drop, never a code change (project AGENTS.md, "Rules for working here") — so an "orphan" skill would be a directory present but absent from `context/AGENTS.md`'s Installed count; none was found (28 = 28).
- Vendored skills keep upstream frontmatter verbatim (license/metadata blocks); home-grown skills use a lean `name`/`description` (+ `argument-hint` for slash-invoked ones, `allowed-tools` for `bash`). This split is intentional per `VENDORED.md`, not inconsistency.
- Agent frontmatter fields in common use: `name`, `description` (one line, double-quoted when it contains a colon per AGENTS.md rule), `tools`, `model`, `effort`, `maxTurns`; `reviewer` additionally declares `skills: [review-standards]`.
- Trail files are append-only and dated `$(date +%F[-%H%M])-<slug>.md`; ROADMAP/TODO are kept empty at every checkpoint by rule, so "not named by ROADMAP" is not itself evidence of an orphan in this repo.

## Risks
- `commands/` and `rules/` are empty but load-bearing in the install code path (`LoadDocs` reads them unconditionally); an empty-by-design directory that the layout table describes as holding content is a documentation/reality mismatch worth flagging to the operator, though functionally harmless (empty dirs just mean zero commands/rules deployed).
- The dead-code sweep here was a shallow heuristic (exported symbols, same-package/test-caller check only); it does not cover unexported helpers, nor does it run `staticcheck`/`deadcode` tooling. A symbol used only by its own package's tests (no non-test caller) is common in this codebase's TDD style and was not flagged as dead, but a stricter definition might disagree — this is a judgment call, not a settled fact.
- Trail-orphan detection was done at the ROADMAP level only; individual plan files were not each checked against handoffs/changes/bug INDEX for a lingering reference, so some of the 60 plan files could be genuinely stale (never closed) vs. closed-but-unlisted (normal). Not distinguished here.

## Open questions
- Is the `commands/`/`rules/` emptiness intentional scaffolding for future content, or should the AGENTS.md layout table be corrected to say they are currently unused? (Operator call.)
- Should dead-code detection be re-run with `staticcheck ./...` or `deadcode ./...` for a authoritative (not heuristic) answer on `internal/harness` and `internal/search`?
- Among the 60 `.agents/docs/plans/` files, which (if any) were abandoned mid-way rather than closed — this recon only confirmed ROADMAP is empty, not that every plan's checkboxes are ticked.

## Not examined
- No `staticcheck`/`deadcode`/`go vet -unusedresult` style tooling was run; the dead-code claim rests on manual grep only.
- Unexported (lowercase) function call graphs in `internal/harness` and `internal/search` were not swept for dead code — only exported symbols were checked.
- Each of the 60 files in `.agents/docs/plans/` was not individually opened to confirm its checkboxes are all ticked or that it is referenced by a `changes/` entry or bug record.
- `.agents/docs/changes/`, `.agents/docs/reviews/`, `.agents/docs/testing/`, `.agents/docs/bugs/` directories were not inventoried for orphans (only `plans/` and `handoffs/` were sampled).
- Full text of `dreamer.md` past line 8 was not re-checked to confirm whether it truly lacks `maxTurns` (only the first 8 lines were read for all agents; `dreamer`'s excerpt ended without one, but the file may continue past what was shown — verify before reporting as a finding).
- `context/dev-setup.md` and the full contents of every `SKILL.md` body (beyond frontmatter) were not read.

title: Research brief: audit fixes — agent/skill formats, JSON API style, context size
body:
# Research brief: audit fixes — agent/skill formats, JSON API style, context size

All pages fetched 2026-09-30; none of the Antigravity pages carries a date.

## 1. Claude Code subagent frontmatter and the Agent Skills standard

**Subagent keys** — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents (seen 2026-09-30). The documented table: `name`, `description`, `tools`, `disallowedTools`, `model`, `permissionMode`, `maxTurns`, `skills`, `mcpServers`, `hooks`, `memory`, `background`, `omitClaudeMd` (v2.1.271+), `effort`, `isolation` (`worktree`), `color`, `initialPrompt`, `experimental.cacheTtl`.

- `skills:` — "The full content of each listed skill is injected into the subagent's context at startup. This field controls which skills are preloaded, not which skills the subagent can access: without it, the subagent can still discover and invoke project, user, and plugin skills through the Skill tool."
- `model` — `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, a full model ID, or `inherit`. When omitted: per-invocation `model` → `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` → the main conversation's model.
- `effort` — documented; `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`; "Overrides the session effort level when this subagent is active."
- `maxTurns` — documented; output "marked as partial" at the limit (marking needs v2.1.246+).
- Startup context of a non-fork subagent: its body, the task message, every CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md the main session loaded, a git snapshot, preloaded skills; not the skill-descriptions listing.

**Agent Skills spec** — https://agentskills.io/specification (seen 2026-09-30). Required: `name` (1–64 chars, lowercase/digits/hyphens, must match the directory), `description` (1–1024 chars, "should describe both what the skill does and when to use it"). Optional: `license`, `compatibility` (≤500 chars), `metadata` (string map), `allowed-tools` (space-separated, "Experimental"). Progressive disclosure: metadata ~100 tokens at startup for every skill; body "< 5000 tokens recommended"; "Keep your main `SKILL.md` under 500 lines." `disable-model-invocation`, `argument-hint`, `user-invocable` are **not** in the spec.

**Claude Code's SKILL.md superset** — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills (seen 2026-09-30): adds `when_to_use`, `argument-hint`, `arguments`, `disable-model-invocation`, `user-invocable`, `disallowed-tools`, `model`, `effort`, `context: fork`, `agent`, `background`, `hooks`, `paths`, `shell`. Description cap: "the combined `description` and `when_to_use` text is truncated at 1,536 characters in the skill listing" (configurable via `skillListingMaxDescChars`). Body: "Keep SKILL.md under 500 lines" and "Once a skill loads, its content stays in context across turns, so every line is a recurring token cost."

## 2. Antigravity CLI (`agy`)

**Agent file format** — https://antigravity.google/docs/subagents/ (seen 2026-09-30). Documented keys: `name` (required), `description` (required), `tools` (`string[]`, default `[]`), `mainAgent` (bool, default true), `subagent` (bool, default true), `model` (`inherit` | `flash` | `pro`, default `inherit`), `commandExecutionPolicy` (`off` | `auto` | `eager` | `sandbox`, default `sandbox`), `mcpServers`, `skills` / `plugins` (`string[]`, "Skill paths (e.g. `skills/my-helper-skill`) or plugin dependencies"). Locations: `.agents/agents/<name>.md` or `.agents/agents/<name>/agent.md`; global `~/.gemini/config/agents/<name>.md`. Known issue quoted on the page: "Specifying an unmapped or misspelled tool name in the `tools` list may cause the subagent process to hang" — the basis of the harness's fail-on-unmapped rule. Context: the subagent "does not inherit the parent's existing conversation history … starting with a clean slate" and inherits "the parent's allowed terminal command prefixes, file read/write directory scopes, and sandbox settings". Corroborated by https://atamel.dev/posts/2026/08-20_where_agy_agents/ (2026-08-20).

**Could not confirm**: (a) whether a subagent inherits the *global* skills directory or only what `skills:` names — the page is silent, and the skills page (https://antigravity.google/docs/skills/) documents only `name` and `description` and says nothing about agents; (b) how a `skills:` path resolves for a global agent (the example is workspace-relative `skills/…`); (c) any per-agent turn, effort or token limit — none is documented anywhere on the subagents, agents-command, reference or best-practices pages; (d) `toolPermission` is a **settings.json** key (`request-review` default, `proceed-in-sandbox`, `always-proceed`, `strict`; https://antigravity.google/docs/cli/reference/), not an agent frontmatter key.

**Rules size** — https://antigravity.google/docs/rules/ (seen 2026-09-30) now says: "24 KB (`24,000` bytes) per-file limit: Antigravity truncates any single rule file that exceeds 24,000 bytes" and "All active global and `always_on` rules share a 20,000-token budget separate from the customization budget", beyond which "Antigravity automatically demotes the largest rule files from inline text to lightweight pointers (`- <path>: <description>`)". Global paths listed: `~/.gemini/config/AGENTS.md`, `~/.gemini/config/GEMINI.md`, `~/.gemini/config/rules/*.md` (also `~/.gemini/AGENTS.md`). The "12,000 characters" figure in REQUIREMENTS.md § Known limits is the old page: agnostic-ai issue #1114 (2026-09-24) records the same page changing from 12,000 to 24,000 bytes. The harness's measured 24,000-byte block (BUG-085) now matches the vendor text, but the vendor says **per file**, while BUG-085 measured one block across files — that discrepancy stays as measured until re-tested on a current CLI. The new 20,000-token aggregate budget is a second ceiling the harness has not measured: 21,906 bytes of dense English is roughly 5,500 tokens, well under it.

## 3. Google API design (AIP) versus the 2012 JSON Style Guide

All AIP pages seen 2026-09-30. Note that https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors now 301-redirects to https://google.aip.dev/193: the AIPs are the single current home.

- **AIP-158 pagination** (https://google.aip.dev/158): request `int32 page_size` (0/absent → server default; over max → coerced; negative → `INVALID_ARGUMENT`), `string page_token`; response `next_page_token` ("If the end of the collection has been reached, the `next_page_token` field must be empty. This is the only way to communicate end-of-collection"), optional `int32 total_size` ("may be an estimate"); results field first.
- **AIP-193 errors** (https://google.aip.dev/193): `google.rpc.Status { code, message, details[] }`. HTTP JSON shape: `{"error": {"code": 404, "message": "...", "status": "NOT_FOUND", "details": [...]}}` — `code` is the HTTP status, `status` the `google.rpc.Code` name. `ErrorInfo { reason (UPPER_SNAKE_CASE, ≤63), domain (service name), metadata }` "required in all error responses"; each detail type at most once; `BadRequest.fieldViolations[]` for validation; `LocalizedMessage` for user-facing text.
- **AIP-140 names** (https://google.aip.dev/140): proto fields `lower_snake_case`, "mapped to an appropriate naming convention in JSON"; no prepositions; avoid language keywords; booleans drop `is_`; unit suffixes (`distance_km`).
- **Proto3 JSON mapping** (https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/json/): "Message field names are mapped to lowerCamelCase to be used as JSON object keys"; parsers must accept both forms; enums serialise as the enum **name** (string); `Timestamp` as RFC 3339, "Z-normalized with 0, 3, 6 or 9 fractional digits"; int64 as a string; `null` = unset.
- **AIP-142 time** (https://google.aip.dev/142): `google.protobuf.Timestamp`, field suffix `_time` (`create_time`, `update_time`; JSON `createTime`), `Duration` for spans, `google.type.Date` with `_date`.
- **AIP-203 field behavior** (https://google.aip.dev/203): `REQUIRED`, `OPTIONAL`, `OUTPUT_ONLY`, `INPUT_ONLY` ("rare"), `IMMUTABLE`, `IDENTIFIER`; every request field annotated.
- **AIP-126 enums** (https://google.aip.dev/126): first value `<NAME>_UNSPECIFIED`, `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`, strings on the wire; a `string` field instead when the set changes often.

**The 2012 guide**: https://google.github.io/styleguide/jsoncstyleguide.xml returned **404 on two fetches today** (both the bare URL and `?showone=error`); the skill's "Further Reading" link is dead. The text survives in the Chromium mirror (https://chromium.googlesource.com/external/github.com/google/styleguide/+/729557a4a28c1a74f01c23599e4f06ac533718fc/jsoncstyleguide.xml, "Revision 0.9"): envelope `apiVersion`/`context`/`id`/`method`/`params`/`data`/`error`; `error.errors[] {domain, reason, message, location, locationType, extendedHelp, sendReport}`; paging `currentItemCount`/`itemsPerPage`/`startIndex`/`totalItems`/`pageIndex`/`totalPages`/`nextPageToken`. No Google API published since the AIPs uses this envelope. What the skill keeps that still agrees with AIP: camelCase keys, enums as strings, RFC 3339 dates, omit nulls, plural arrays.

**Go struct tags**: with AIP over proto3 JSON, the wire is camelCase, so `json:"pageSize"`, `json:"nextPageToken"`, `json:"createTime"`. The golang skill's `references/golang-structure.md` lines 281–287 use `json:"user_id"`, `json:"created_at"` — snake_case, contradicting json-api-style rule 1 today, whichever guide it follows.

## 4. Instruction-file length: what the evidence says

- **Anthropic, memory page** (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, seen 2026-09-30): "Size: target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file. Longer files consume more context and reduce adherence. Move instructions that matter for only part of the codebase into path-scoped rules … Imports help you organize a long file but don't reduce its context cost." "Keep it to facts Claude should hold in every session: build commands, conventions, project layout, 'always do X' rules. If an entry is a multi-step procedure or only matters for one part of the codebase, move it to a skill or a path-scoped rule."
- **Anthropic, best practices** (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices, seen 2026-09-30): "For each line, ask: 'Would removing this cause Claude to make mistakes?' If not, cut it. Bloated CLAUDE.md files cause Claude to ignore your actual instructions!" "If Claude keeps doing something you don't want despite having a rule against it, the file is probably too long and the rule is getting lost." "If you emphasize many lines, none of them stands out." Failure pattern "The over-specified CLAUDE.md … Claude ignores half of it because important rules get lost in the noise."
- **Anthropic, skills page**: "Unlike CLAUDE.md content, a skill's body loads only when it's used, so long reference material costs almost nothing until you need it."
- **agents.md** (https://agents.md/, seen 2026-09-30): no length guidance at all; "just standard Markdown"; closest file wins; 60k+ projects.
- **Measurements**: IFScale (arXiv 2507.11538, 2025-07-15): 500 keyword instructions, "even the best frontier models only achieve 68% accuracy at the max density", three degradation patterns by model class, "bias towards earlier instructions". McMillan (arXiv 2605.10039, 2026-05-11), 1,650 Claude Code sessions varying a config file at 25/100/250/500 lines: file **size had no detectable effect** on compliance with the tested rule (affirmative null, BF₁₀ ≈ 0.10); presence vs absence was decisive (0 → 67.7 %); compliance fell ~5.6 % odds per additional function generated in the session. Agent-READMEs survey (arXiv 2511.12884): median production CLAUDE.md 485 words.

Reading: the 200-line target is a context-cost and attention rule, not a measured cliff. The one controlled study found no length effect up to 500 lines for a single rule; IFScale shows density effects at hundreds of *distinct* instructions plus a primacy bias. The harness context is 67 lines but 18.4 KB — roughly 150–200 imperatives, where IFScale's curves already bend and later rules lose to earlier ones.

## 5. Two small questions

(a) **`@AGENTS.md` and native support** — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory: "Reading `AGENTS.md` directly requires Claude Code v2.1.277 or later"; "Before v2.1.281, some sessions, such as those on Amazon Bedrock or with telemetry disabled, read `CLAUDE.md` files only" — so the harness's "before 2.1.277, Bedrock, telemetry off" exception should read "before 2.1.281 on Bedrock or with telemetry off; before 2.1.277 anywhere". It is a fallback: a `CLAUDE.md` or `CLAUDE.local.md` anywhere on the path suppresses AGENTS.md unless **Project instructions** is `claude-md-and-agents-md`; `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` does *not* count. The `@AGENTS.md` import is documented and safe to keep: "Keeping the import never makes Claude read `AGENTS.md` twice". v2.1.277 shipped 2026-09-18.

(b) **`/goal`** — documented at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/goal (seen 2026-09-30): `/goal <condition>` (≤4,000 chars), `/goal` for status, `/goal clear`; a Haiku-class evaluator judges the transcript after every turn; works with `claude -p "/goal …"`; unattended needs auto mode; unavailable when `disableAllHooks` is set or the workspace is untrusted. The evaluator "does not call tools, so it can only judge what Claude has already surfaced" — a check must print its result. The context's sentence is accurate; it could add "the check's output must appear in the transcript".

## Recommendations

### (i) derive.go: skills, effort, maxTurns on Antigravity

- **`skills:` — translate, do not drop.** Antigravity documents a `skills: string[]` agent key taking skill paths. The comment "markdown agents inherit the global skills anyway" is unsupported on either vendor: Claude Code's `skills:` is a *preload*, and Antigravity's docs say nothing about inheritance. Emit `skills: [<agy skills dir>/<name>, …]` using the path form the docs show; one agent (`reviewer` → `review-standards`) exercises it today. Gate: one behavioural run on agy proving the preloaded body reached the subagent (something only `review-standards` says), n of N, per the AGENTS.md testing rule; until that run, keep the current fallback of naming the skill path in the agent body (the `~/.gemini/config/skills/` rewrite already exists) and record the key as dashed.
- **`effort:` — drop, and say so.** No Antigravity equivalent exists (`model: pro|flash|inherit` is the only tier knob). Keep the drop, fix the comment.
- **`maxTurns:` — drop, and compensate in the dispatch.** No per-agent turn limit is documented for agy. The global rule already requires every dispatch to name a budget in the prompt; that is the only portable limit. Fix the comment.
- Add a test that pins what `DeriveAgy` emits and omits per key (today untested), and a `skills` mapping test that fails on a skill name not in the inventory.

### (ii) json-api-style: rewrite to AIP

Rewrite the skill on AIP-158/193/140/142/126/203 with proto3 JSON as the wire form; drop the `apiVersion`/`data`/`error.errors[]` envelope, `startIndex`/`itemsPerPage` paging, and the dead link. Shape: list responses `{ "<plural>": [...], "nextPageToken": "" , "totalSize"? }`; requests `pageSize`, `pageToken`; errors `{"error": {"code", "message", "status", "details": [ErrorInfo, BadRequest?]}}`; `createTime`/`updateTime` RFC 3339 Z; enums `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` strings with `_UNSPECIFIED`; int64 as string when precision matters; omit unset fields. Go tags camelCase (`json:"pageSize,omitempty"`), and the golang skill's `golang-structure.md` example changed to match in the same commit (the "vocabulary" rule in Hard rules: one grep for `json:"[a-z]*_` across `skills/`). Keep the reference file under `references/` and the SKILL.md well under 500 lines. Why AIP for a Go API + TypeScript SPA: camelCase is native to TS, `google.rpc.Status` is what gRPC-gateway and Connect emit, and the 2012 guide has no living home.

### (iii) Global context: target size and split rule

Target **≤ 12,000 bytes rendered** (≈ 35–40 lines of the current density, ≈ 3,000 tokens), with the test budget lowered to 14,000 and the 22,000 pin kept only as the vendor ceiling. Evidence: Anthropic's stated mechanism (long files "reduce adherence", rules "get lost in the noise", emphasis stops working when repeated), IFScale's density curve and primacy bias, and the harness's own bug trail (BUG-110: six passes; repeated "second round on the same mechanism" rules) — the symptoms Anthropic names. McMillan's null means length alone will not fix compliance, so the split must remove *instructions*, not bytes.

Split rule — a line stays in the context only if it is needed in **every** session before the first tool call: resume order and checkpoint moments; the classify-then-load table; the Definition of Done as five one-line rows naming the skill or agent that owns each; the Git backup rule and the secret-path stop; the scratch rule; the operator's interaction style; the environment stack in one paragraph; the canary. Everything else moves to the skill or agent that runs when it applies: the verification-evidence and mutation rules → `review-standards` and `verifier`; the read-only-mode, guard-on-error, both-direction-artifact and `&&`-chain rules → `review-standards` § checklists and the `bug` skill; the dispatch-text repetition rules → the `review` skill and agent definitions; the "behaviour change includes the text that describes it" rule → `review --docs` and `documentation`; GCP details → `cloud-run-deploy`/`gcloud-setup`; the learning-loop mechanics → `retro`/`distill`/`dream`. A rule that was learned from a bug lives where the bug's prevention rule points, with the context keeping one sentence that names the skill. On Antigravity, skills load by description only, so each receiving skill's description must name the trigger words the moved rule needs.

### (iv) Description length for skills and agents

Spec ceiling 1,024 chars (agentskills.io); Claude Code truncates the listing at 1,536. Rule: **150–500 characters**, one paragraph, "what it does", then "use when …", then one "do NOT use for" clause; `Lint` fails above 1,024 and warns above 600. Rationale: every description is paid at every session start on both CLIs (~100 tokens each × 29 skills + 8 agents ≈ 3–4 k tokens), and the harness's own descriptions already range from 296 (`bash`) to 1,007 (`cloud-run-deploy`, 17 bytes under the spec ceiling), with `review` 789, `dream` 705, `mermaid-syntax` 662 next. Agents run 405–613 and need no change beyond the ceiling.

title: Plan — Google skills catalog (2026-10-01)
body:
---
owner: main
date: 2026-10-01
---
# Plan — Google skills catalog   (2026-10-01)

## Why

Operator, 2026-10-01: "I want to add these skills to the harness: https://github.com/google/agents-cli all of the agents-cli skills and these https://github.com/google/skills/tree/main/skills/cloud and these https://github.com/google/skills/tree/main/skills/developers --- it is a big job." Installed as global skills the 141 candidates break skill selection on both CLIs (Antigravity lists 109 of 173 and drops 16 harness skills; Claude Code shows descriptions for the first 41 alphabetically and bare names for the rest) — `plans/2026-10-01-research-google-skills-catalog.md`. The operator took the thirteen recommendations: "Go all, with your recommendations".

## Scope

In: the 141 skills vendored verbatim at their pins as a catalog that is not installed as skills; one router skill that finds and follows the matching entry; provenance (manifest, checksums, licences) pinned by tests; a refresh script; the listing-budget test; a security review of the imported content; sandbox runs on both CLIs; docs.

Out: installing any of the 141 as a global skill; fetching Google's live catalog from the network inside a session; editing vendored text; a way to copy a catalog entry into a project's `.agents/skills/` (D8: deferred); retiring the `gke-basics` fork (D5: later).

Follow-ups noted, not built: project opt-in for catalog entries; replacing the `gke-basics` fork by the catalog's GKE set; the google/skills `ads`, `analytics`, `identity` directories (not asked for).

## Surfaces touched

- `skills/google-catalog/` (new): `SKILL.md`, `catalog/<141 entries>/…`, `catalog/INDEX.md`, `catalog/MANIFEST.md`, `catalog/CHECKSUMS`, `catalog/LICENSE-google-skills`, `catalog/LICENSE-agents-cli`, `scripts/refresh-catalog.sh`.
- `skills/cloud-run-deploy/SKILL.md` (description shortened), `skills/VENDORED.md` (a catalog section), `skills/review/scripts/restatement-grep.sh` (the catalog path counts as vendored).
- Tests that walk `skills/`: `TestSkillLinksResolve` (`internal/harness/skill_links_test.go`) and `TestNoTmpInHarnessProse` (`internal/harness/harness_test.go:1015`) skip a vendored subtree through one helper, `isVendoredPath(vendored map[string]bool, rel string) bool` beside `vendoredSkills` — `rel` is the slash-separated path relative to `skills/`, true when it equals a vendored key or lies under one; `TestNoTmpInHarnessProse`'s walker returns `filepath.SkipDir` for a directory whose `skills/`-relative path is a vendored key (its per-skill `vendored[filepath.Base(d)]` test alone never matches a path key). No other test walks skill prose (`zip_test.go:55`, `phase8_test.go:20` and `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go:295` walk the repository or the Go source for other properties: checked 2026-10-01). New `internal/harness/catalog_test.go` (`TestCatalogMatchesChecksums`, `TestCatalogIndexMatchesEntries`, `TestCatalogFilesAreCarryable`, `TestCatalogInstallsClean`, `TestRouterDescription`, `TestRefreshCatalogScript`), new `TestSkillListingBudget` in `internal/harness/size_test.go`, a catalog case in `internal/harness/restatement_script_test.go`.
- Docs: `README.md` § Skills and § Layout, project `AGENTS.md` § Layout and § Rules (third-party skills), `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md` (rows `catalog-route`, `catalog-no-leak`, `catalog-precedence`), `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md` § 4, `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` (release size), `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases (asset size note).
- No change to `cmd/`, `internal/harness` production code, `REQUIREMENTS.md` or the README map (D14).

## Interfaces

- **Router skill** `skills/google-catalog/SKILL.md`: `name: google-catalog`; `description` one double-quoted line of at most 300 characters that triggers on Google Cloud, Gemini, Agent Platform, ADK and agents-cli work the other skills do not cover and names what it must NOT be used for (Cloud Run deploys, Cloud SQL, Terraform, gcloud login, GKE day-0: their own skills). Body, four numbered steps: grep `catalog/INDEX.md` beside the file for the product or task words (never read the index whole); read the best match's `catalog/<name>/SKILL.md` and follow it, its relative paths resolved against that entry's directory; run an entry's scripts through their interpreter; the harness's rules win on conflict (Git rule, secrets, GCP defaults asked first, deploy guides) and a harness skill that covers the task wins over an entry. No match: say so in one line and continue without the catalog.
- **Entries** `skills/google-catalog/catalog/<name>/`: byte-identical to upstream at the pin, file modes 0644. Names are upstream's directory names; 141 at import: google/agents-cli `skills/` (7) and `extensions/langchain/template/.agents/skills/agents-cli-langchain` (1) at 2c39459; google/skills `skills/cloud` (131) and `skills/developers` (2) at d5d9052.
- **`catalog/INDEX.md`**: generated by the refresh script, committed: a three-line header, then exactly one line per entry, sorted by name: ``- `<name>` — <description>``, where `<name>` is the entry's directory name and `<description>` is what the harness's own `Parse` returns for the entry's `description`, cut at 220 characters (runes) with no ellipsis. The Go test re-derives every line this way, so the script's own frontmatter reader (python3, required; the script exits 1 without it) is checked rather than trusted.
- **`catalog/MANIFEST.md`**: frontmatter `owner: main`, `date:`; one table row per source — repository URL, path, commit pin, licence, fetched date, entry count — then "Local changes: file modes only (no executable bit)", then `## Excluded` (upstream paths the refresh refused, with the reason) and `## Notes` (the security review's per-entry notes; never edits to vendored text). The script rewrites the table rows, and the fetched date only in a row whose pin changed, so a re-run at the same pins changes nothing on any day; `## Excluded` and `## Notes` are written by hand and kept across a refresh.
- **`catalog/CHECKSUMS`**: `sha256sum` format, one line per vendored file — every file under an entry directory `catalog/<entry>/` and the two `catalog/LICENSE-*` files — paths relative to `catalog/`, sorted with `LC_ALL=C`. The three harness-written files (`INDEX.md`, `MANIFEST.md`, `CHECKSUMS`) are not covered: `INDEX.md` is pinned by its own test, and `MANIFEST.md` is edited by hand.
- **`scripts/refresh-catalog.sh`** (file mode 0644, run with `bash` from the harness checkout; never by a session in another project): `bash skills/google-catalog/scripts/refresh-catalog.sh [--dest <dir>] [--exclude <entry>]... <agents-cli pin> <google-skills pin>`. The four source sets are constants at the top: google/agents-cli `skills/*` and `extensions/langchain/template/.agents/skills/*`; google/skills `skills/cloud/*` and `skills/developers/*`. The two repository URLs default to GitHub and are overridable by the environment (`CATALOG_AGENTS_CLI_REPO`, `CATALOG_GOOGLE_SKILLS_REPO`) so a test points them at local fixture repositories; `--dest` (default `skills/google-catalog/catalog`) is where the catalog is written. It makes a full clone of each repository (no `--depth`, so any pin resolves) into `.agents/scratch/catalog-refresh/`, checks out the pins, and builds the new catalog in scratch first. It exits 1, naming the path and leaving `--dest` untouched, for the five classes it can see cheaply: a pin that does not resolve; an entry without `SKILL.md` frontmatter holding `name` and `description`; two source sets holding an entry of the same directory name; a symlink; a `go.mod` or `go.sum` (the embed would drop the directory). The operator then excludes the whole entry with `--exclude <entry>` and records it under `## Excluded`; a file is never altered. On success it replaces the entry directories under `--dest` (removing entries upstream dropped), clears exec bits, copies the two LICENSE files, regenerates `INDEX.md` and `CHECKSUMS`, updates the manifest rows, stages nothing, and prints the entry count per source set, the names added and removed, and the line `next: go test ./...`. What the script cannot see cheaply is caught by the suite it tells the operator to run: a secret-shaped name by `TestCatalogInstallsClean` (the installer's own `secretShaped` list, never a second copy in bash), a path git ignores by `TestEmbedHoldsOnlyTrackedFiles`. At import (2026-10-01, measured on the pins): 0 symlinks, 0 secret-shaped names, 0 ignored paths, 0 `go.mod`, 0 collisions; 141 entries.

## Failure modes

- A CLI denies or prompts for the read of a catalog file: a headless run needs a read grant (measured, Phase 0: with `Read`/`Grep` allowed on Claude Code and `read_file(*)` on Antigravity the reads succeed); whether a default interactive session prompts is not measured until Phase 4's operator box. Either way the router says which file it could not read and continues without the catalog.
- No entry matches: the router says "no catalog entry for <words>" and the session continues with the harness's skills.
- An entry tells the agent to do what a harness rule forbids (an unpinned `curl | sh`, a commit without staging by name, a public service by default): the router's step 4 says the harness rule wins; entries the security review flags are named in `MANIFEST.md` § Notes.
- A script needs the executable bit: run through its interpreter (step 3).
- The tree drifts from the pin (a hand edit, a partial refresh): `TestCatalogMatchesChecksums` fails and names the file.
- A future CLI version starts discovering nested `SKILL.md` files, or shrinks its listing budget: the matrix rows `catalog-no-leak` and the budget test catch it at the next release gate; the fallback is moving the entries' `SKILL.md` out of discovery by the refresh script (a D-row then).
- Refresh with a bad pin or an entry without frontmatter: the script exits 1 before touching the tree.

Open: (R3-2) where the refresh script clones — default: `--work <dir>`, defaulting to `$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.agents/scratch/catalog-refresh`; an existing clone is fetched and reused; the test passes a `t.TempDir()` work directory
Open: (R3-3) the suite fails on an unstaged catalog — default: the script's last line reads `next: git add skills/google-catalog && go test ./...`, and Phase 1's script box stages before the suite
Open: (R3-4) a `*.go` file in an entry would be compiled by the Go tool — default: the script and `TestCatalogFilesAreCarryable` refuse `*.go` beside `go.mod` and `go.sum`
Open: (R3-5) refresh details — default: `--exclude` clears four of the five refusal classes (not the unresolvable pin); the first run writes the manifest skeleton with empty `## Excluded` and `## Notes`, later runs keep both sections byte for byte; an excluded entry must be passed again on the next refresh, and the script prints the `## Excluded` names it was not given

title: Research — Google skills import: measurements and decisions (2026-10-01)
body:
# Research — Google skills import: measurements and decisions (2026-10-01)

Request (operator, 2026-10-01): add every skill of github.com/google/agents-cli and of google/skills `skills/cloud` and `skills/developers` to the harness.

## What was measured

- Candidates: 141 skills — agents-cli `skills/` 7 (pin 2c39459), its LangChain extension template 1, google/skills `cloud` 131 and `developers` 2 (pin d5d9052). Apache-2.0 both. 5.7 MB, 778 files (614 md, 74 py, 44 yaml, 20 sh). Descriptions all within 1,024 chars; 67,698 chars together (average 480).
- Harness lint on a scratch tree with all of them: 2 refused for `allowed-tools` (`agent-platform-alert-configuration`, `cloud-run-alert-configuration`); none for an unreadable frontmatter line; 26 files carry an exec bit (the embed test refuses those under `skills/`); one name clash, `gke-basics` (the harness's pinned fork). Rendered context with 173 skills: 19,548 bytes of the 22,000 pin.
- Installed into a sandbox home and asked each CLI what it sees (`~/sandbox/audit-fix/imp-*.out`):
  - **Antigravity 1.2.14 lists 109 of 173 skills.** Two runs agree. It drops the longest descriptions first (kept average 382 chars, dropped 690; about 44,000 characters of name plus description survive). 16 of the harness's own 34 are dropped: `feature`, `review`, `golang`, `spec`, `terraform`, `cloud-run-deploy`, `data-gcp`, `requirements`, `testing-strategy`, `project-memory`, `dream`, `explain-project`, `operate-gcp`, `api-auth-gcp`, `json-api-style`, `mermaid-syntax`.
  - **Claude Code lists all 186 names but descriptions for only the first 41 alphabetically** (through `data-gcp`), about 19,800 characters; every later skill — `feature`, `golang`, `handoff`, `init-project`, `preflight`, `review`, `terraform` — is a bare name with no description, so nothing tells the model when to load it.
