| Peak context per session, median / p75 / p90 / max (tokens) | 573,527 / 822,796 / 943,841 / 967,274 |
| Sessions whose peak passed 200K / 400K / 900K | 38 / 29 / 9 of 49 |
| Sessions with at least one compaction (total compactions) | 13 (16); max 3 in one session |
| Tool calls per session, median / p90 / max | 288 / 646 / 842 |
| Corrections logged per session, no-compaction vs compacted sessions | 0.06 vs 0.08 (3 events in all: under-logged, not a signal) |
| Escaped bugs per session, either bucket | 0.00 |
| Handoffs per session | 0.75 vs 1.15 |

Reading: on 1M-window models the sessions here run at half a million tokens for most of their life and compact at about 967K (the Claude Code default for native-1M models). The local store cannot yet show a quality difference between short and long sessions: it records corrections and escaped bugs, and both are near zero in the window.

### Published evidence

- Chroma, "Context Rot" (July 2025, 18 models incl. five Claude): "model performance consistently degrades with increasing input length"; "even a single distractor reduces performance relative to the baseline"; LongMemEval, 306 prompts: focused prompts of about 300 tokens beat full prompts of about 113K tokens "across all models", the Claude family showing the largest gap.
- Anthropic, "Effective context engineering for AI agents": context is "a finite resource with diminishing marginal returns"; degradation is "a performance gradient rather than a hard cliff"; the three long-horizon levers are compaction, structured note-taking outside the window, and sub-agents that return a condensed summary; "do the simplest thing that works".
- Claude Code docs, Best practices: "Most best practices are based on one constraint: Claude's context window fills up fast, and performance degrades as it fills"; "Use `/clear` frequently between tasks"; after two failed corrections, "`/clear` and start fresh with a more specific prompt"; after a spec is written, "start a fresh session to execute it. The new session has clean context focused entirely on implementation, and you have a written spec to reference."
- Claude Code docs, context window: what survives compaction (CLAUDE.md and rules re-injected; up to five recently modified files re-read; skill bodies capped at 5,000 tokens each, 25,000 total); `/autocompact <tokens>` sets an earlier pass (100K–1M); `/context` shows the live breakdown to the USER; nothing tells the MODEL its own usage.
- Antigravity: `agy --continue` and `agy --conversation <id>` exist (`agy --help`); no compaction control found; community reports describe compaction as aggressive and opaque with no token meter. Unverified beyond those reports.

### What the harness already has

- Global context: checkpoints "before the context gets long or the session may end (`/handoff`)"; Definition of Done step 5 "recommend a fresh session for the next task"; "progress that lives only in chat or a compaction summary is lost".
- `handoff` Step 7: "Start a new session and paste: `Read the handoff at <path> and continue the work.`" and "recommend a fresh session (`/clear` on Claude Code, a new conversation on Antigravity) for the next task". The paste line is generic: it names no phase, no approvals, no check.
- `feature` Step 4: one phase per checkpoint; an in-progress note when "the context may compact, the session may end"; nothing sizes a phase to a session or ends the session at the checkpoint.
- Sub-agents for large reads (explorer at 10+ files, verifier, reviewer): the main thread still runs a median 288 tool calls.
- `/review --resume`: the cold-read test that a fresh session can resume from the trail. This is the quality gate the feature needs and it exists.
- The learning loop already holds this correction once: feedback.jsonl 2026-10-21 19:04 (crew): "Start fresh sessions to keep the context small, and run autonomously with as few questions as possible: standing approvals in the prompt, ask only outside them or for critical failures." Today is its second occurrence; the retro cadence says a repeated correction graduates into a mechanism.

### Resume cost, measured

A fresh session's resume order on this project reads about 124 KB (roughly 30K tokens) before work: `bugs/INDEX.md` 50 KB, the active plan 27 KB, project `AGENTS.md` 18 KB, the rendered global context 16 KB, the handoff 4 KB, three changes 8 KB. Splitting a 600K session into three 200K sessions costs about 90K tokens of re-reads and saves nothing in tokens; the gain is quality, not cost. `INDEX.md` is 40% of the bill and grows with every bug.

## Stress test of the premise

- What the operator is not seeing: the gain they felt comes from two things at once, a fresh window AND the forced write-down of state into a prompt. The harness already forces the write-down (plan, handoff). The unmeasured part is the fresh window. Without a quality signal in the metrics the claim "fewer hallucinations" stays the operator's observation plus the literature; the plan must add the measurement, not assume it.
- Strongest counter-argument: a split mid-phase loses in-flight state the handoff cannot carry; Anthropic's own guidance ("sometimes you should let context accumulate because you're deep in one complex problem") and the resume cost both say split only at checkpoints, never on a token count.
- The model cannot see its context fill. A rule keyed on "when the context is long" is unobservable from inside; a rule keyed on a structural boundary (phase checkpoint, task done) is observable every time. Claude Code gives the OPERATOR a gauge (`/context`, status line); Antigravity gives none that was found.
- Over-splitting: Trivial and Task classes fit one session by definition; the rule is for Feature plans and for sessions that take a second unrelated ask (the "kitchen sink" pattern).
- Cross-CLI: anything that depends on `/clear`, `/autocompact` or a status line is Claude Code only; the structural rule and the kickoff prompt work on both.

## Items

### 1. Add it as its own feature plan, run before the EGM tasks

Different subject from EGM, a design question in it (where the always-on rule lives), and it changes how every later task is run. The EGM items (standards and naive-reader lens into `feature`; the `--drift` lens; the ADR-056a decision) become its first session-sized phases and its first measurement.

### 2. The always-on rule and where it lives

Rule: a session is one Task or one plan phase. At the phase checkpoint (or at Definition of Done step 5) the session writes the handoff with a kickoff prompt and ENDS; the next phase starts in a fresh conversation. A second unrelated ask in a session gets its own kickoff prompt instead of being done in place. Where: `rules/session-sizing.md` (always-on on both CLIs; the Antigravity block has 4,662 bytes of room). The hand-written context has 71 bytes of headroom, so a sentence there means removing one.

### 3. The kickoff prompt

The handoff gains `## Kickoff`: the exact prompt for the next conversation, written for a reader with no context: project path, the plan path and the ONE phase to do, the standing approvals it may act on without asking (the 2026-10-21 correction's words), what must pass before it stops (the phase's Checkpoint evidence; for an unattended run, the `/goal` condition), and the instruction to end with the next kickoff. The handoff's Step 7 report prints it in a fenced block, after "run `/clear` (Claude Code) or start a new conversation (Antigravity), then paste:". File-drop change to `skills/handoff/SKILL.md` only; no `sh-agent` verb.

### 4. Phase sizing in the feature skill

A phase is what one fresh session can finish and verify; the plan's cold reader (Step 3) gets a fourth question: "can each phase be finished by a fresh session that reads only the plan and the files it names?" A number for "finish" is not invented here: the metric in item 5 sets the target and `/retro` tunes the sizing.

### 5. Measure it

The metrics store already holds peak context per session (B3). Add one report row, "main sessions whose peak context passed the target (default 300K)", and the per-session peak in `show --json`, so `/retro` sees the trend; keep corrections and escaped bugs beside it. A small code change in `internal/metrics` (Task). Starting target 300K is a proposal, not a finding; the operator picks it.

### 6. Resume cost

`bugs/INDEX.md` (50 KB) is read in full by every fresh session. Options: resume reads only its open rows (`sh-agent search --open` already exists for plans) or a short `## Open` head the full table follows. A separate Task; it halves the cost of every split.

### 7. Claude Code knobs the operator can set today, outside the harness

`/autocompact 300k` (compaction before the gradient bites instead of at 967K), a status line with context percentage, `/clear` then `claude --resume` when a session must be revisited. Not harness changes (settings are a non-goal); recorded in `deploy/local.md` § Operator steps if the operator adopts them.

### 8. Not proposed

A token-count trigger for the model (unobservable); automatic `/clear` (no CLI exposes it to the model; hooks are refused, ADR-007); a `sh-agent next` verb (the handoff's fenced block does the job without code); per-project compaction instructions in CLAUDE.md (the project root holds `AGENTS.md` alone).

## Sources

- https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices · https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window · https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config · https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs
- https://discuss.ai.google.dev/t/frustrated-with-aggressive-context-compaction-before-plan-execution/167983 · https://agentpedia.codes/blog/managing-context-antigravity-sessions (community, unverified)

# Plan — session-sized work   (2026-10-23)

## Why
The operator (2026-10-23, their own turn): "we always use all context … split large context into smaller tasks or phases so we get less hallucinations" and "always splitting up things the operator asks into smaller chunks … when it is time to start a new conversation give me a new prompt. Then I run /clear and run the prompt again." The same correction was logged once before (feedback.jsonl 2026-10-21T19:04:11+02:00, crew: "Start fresh sessions to keep the context small … standing approvals in the prompt, ask only outside them or for critical failures"); a repeated correction graduates into a mechanism. Evidence and alternatives: `plans/2026-10-23-research-session-sizing.md` (49 main Claude Code sessions since 2026-09-01: median peak context 573K tokens, 38 of 49 past 200K; the harness ends a task with a generic "read the handoff" line and sizes no phase to a session). The EGM deltas approved the same day (`plans/2026-10-23-research-egm.md` items 4, 5, 6) are this plan's later phases: they are the first work run under the rule, and the first measurement of it.

## Scope
In: an always-on rule that a session is one Task or one plan phase and ends at its checkpoint with a kickoff prompt; the handoff's `## Kickoff` section and its paste-ready report; phase sizing and a fourth cold-reader question in the feature skill; a peak-context metric row and per-session peaks in `sh-agent metrics`; the EGM document standards and naive-reader lens in the feature skill's cold read; a `--drift` lens on `/review`; the operator's decision on reviewer isolation (ADR-056a) and its consequence; a harness-owned auto-compact backstop on Claude Code — `sh-agent install` sets Claude Code's own `autoCompactWindow` when absent — once the operator approves the `REQUIREMENTS.md` edit it needs (D25).
Out: a token-count trigger for the model (it cannot observe its context), an automatic `/clear` (no CLI exposes one to the model; hooks are refused, R3, ADR-007), a `sh-agent next` verb (the handoff's fenced block does the job), compaction instructions in CLAUDE.md (the root holds `AGENTS.md` alone), a wholesale EGM fork or plugin install (research-egm items 1–3, 7, 8), closed plans as drift targets by default (D7).
Follow-ups noted, not built: resume cost — `bugs/INDEX.md` (50 KB) is read whole by every fresh session; a Task later makes resume read its open rows or a short `## Open` head (research-session-sizing item 6). The operator declined to run knobs by hand (2026-10-23: "I dont want to run compact myself. I want something in this harness to monitor this and trigger"), so `/autocompact` became Phase 2b; a status line with context % is display only and stays optional for them; `/clear` then `claude --resume` is the Kickoff's path.

## Surfaces touched
- `rules/session-sizing.md` (new; deploys to `~/.claude/rules/` and `~/.gemini/config/rules/`, `internal/harness/plan.go:62`; shares the 22,000-byte Antigravity block, `internal/harness/size_test.go` `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock`, 17,338 used).
- `skills/handoff/SKILL.md` (Step 4 template, Step 7 report), `skills/feature/SKILL.md` (Step 2 template note, Step 3 brief, Step 4 checkpoint), `skills/review/SKILL.md` (Step 1 parse, Step 2 scope, Step 3 table and a `### Drift brief`, Step 6 report; `argument-hint`), `skills/feature/references/egm-standards/` (new: five standards and `LICENSE`, verbatim), `skills/VENDORED.md` (one row).
- `internal/metrics/show.go` (`ShowOptions`, `Efficiency`, `add`, `finish`), `internal/metrics/report.go` (one row), `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (`--context-target` on `metrics show|report`), their tests; `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/metrics.md` (§ Verbs, § Output, B3); `README.md` (the two metrics verb rows).
- `agents/reviewer.md` and, under D10 option (a), `internal/harness/inventory.go` (`agentKeys`), `internal/harness/derive.go`, their tests.
- `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` (ADR-058; ADR-059 under D10), `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md` (rows for the kickoff, the drift lens and the standards-citing cold read), project `AGENTS.md` (Layout line naming `rules/`), `README.md:278` ("one today: critical-thinking.md"), `README.md:264` and `skills/review/SKILL.md:3` (the lens vocabulary; the listing budget has 226 bytes, `--drift` costs under 10), `context/AGENTS.md:19` (DoD step 5 "recommend a fresh session for the next task" becomes "the session ends there (`rules/session-sizing.md`)": +6 bytes against 71 of headroom, pinned by `TestRenderedContextUnderTarget`), `internal/metrics/numbers.go:65` (the dream's numbers-only summary gains the over-target count; `session_peaks`, a list, is left out).

## Interfaces

**Rule file** `rules/session-sizing.md`, frontmatter `trigger: always_on` and a one-line quoted `description:` (the shape of `rules/critical-thinking.md`), body under 1,400 bytes:
> A session is one Task or one plan phase. A plan phase ends at its Checkpoint box: tick it, write the `changes/` entry, commit, push, then write the handoff with its `## Kickoff` and END the session; the next phase begins in a fresh conversation from that kickoff. A Task ends the same way at Definition of Done step 5. A second, unrelated ask arriving in a session that has done one gets its own Kickoff in the handoff instead of being done in place. Only the operator's own words in the same turn ("continue here") keep a session past its boundary. A Trivial change needs no kickoff. Why: a long context degrades on a gradient long before it compacts, and the model cannot see its own fill; the checkpoint is the boundary it can see.

**Handoff template** gains, after `## Next Steps` (in `SKILL.md` the outer fence is four backticks so the inner ```text fence does not close it):
````markdown
## Kickoff
```text
Project: <absolute path>. Read AGENTS.md, then <handoff path>, then <plan path>; do Phase <n> — <name> only.
Standing approvals (closed set): the phase's boxes marked who: AI and the tests they name; the checkpoint's `changes/` entry, commit and push; the closing handoff. Never: a who: user box, an Open: row, a release, a deploy, a real-home install, anything outside this repository. Ask only outside the set or on a critical failure.
Done when: <the phase's Checkpoint expect, verbatim>. Then write the handoff with the next Kickoff and end the session.
```
````
The template's Standing-approvals line is fixed text with the phase name filled in; the agent never adds to the set (D17). When nothing is queued the section holds one line: `Nothing queued; start the next task in a fresh conversation.` In an unscaffolded project (no `docs/` root, so no handoff) the kickoff is printed in chat only, same text, nothing saved. Step 7 becomes three items: (1) where the handoff was saved, (2) "Run `/clear` (Claude Code) or start a new conversation (Antigravity), then paste:" followed by the Kickoff block verbatim (the nothing-queued line when that is the case), (3) the one-sentence summary; the old item 4 is folded into (2). Paths inside the Kickoff are repo-relative except `Project:` (the template's existing rule).

**Feature skill.** Step 2, under `## Phases`: "A phase is what one fresh session, reading only this plan and the files it names, finishes and verifies, checkpoint included; a phase that would not be split here." Step 3 brief gains "(4) Sizing: could a fresh session finish and verify each phase from this plan alone? Name the phase that could not and why." and, after the three questions: "The rubric for (2) is `<feature skill dir>/references/egm-standards/zoom-out-standard.md` and for (3) `implementation-readiness-standard.md`; under (1), every term, acronym or name the plan uses without defining it or citing a file is a gap (the naive-reader check)." The skill directory is named the way the review skill names its own (`~/.claude/skills/feature` on Claude Code, `~/.gemini/config/skills/feature` on Antigravity, or the project's `.agents/skills/feature`, the first that exists). Step 4 checkpoint sentence ends: "then the handoff with the next phase's Kickoff, and the session ends (`rules/session-sizing.md`)."

**Metrics.** `ShowOptions.ContextTarget int64` (0 means 300000). `Efficiency` gains `ContextTarget int64 json:"context_target"`, `SessionsOverContextTarget map[string]*int json:"sessions_over_context_target"` (main sessions whose peak passed the target; a number for every vendor whose window holds a session with a context value — Antigravity's `gen_metadata` is stored at `agy.go:228` and read at `show.go:344` — and nil, named in `notes`, only for a vendor with no such session; `compactions` stays nil for Antigravity as today), `SessionPeaks map[string][]SessionPeak json:"session_peaks"` with `type SessionPeak struct { Session string json:"session"; Date string json:"date"; Peak int64 json:"peak" }`, main sessions only, sorted by peak descending, no content fields (D16: no per-session compaction count). Flag `--context-target N` (plain token count) on `metrics show` and `metrics report`; a non-positive value is the usage error `--context-target takes a token count above 0`. Report row `sessions over context target (<N>)` rendered `k of n`. Spec `metrics.md`: § Verbs row, § Output example, B3 row ("Also the sessions whose peak passed the context target, default 300K, and each main session's peak").

**Review `--drift`.** Runs alone, like `--resume` (another lens, `--all` or `--fix` beside it is the error `--drift runs alone`); takes no scope token except paths; scope text `Scope: the specs under <docs-root>/specs/ (or the named paths) against the code at HEAD (<short sha>), no diff.`; one `reviewer` dispatch PER SPEC FILE, in parallel, each with a 30-call budget and "write the artifact early, then update it", artifact `<docs-root>/reviews/<date>-review-<spec basename>-drift.md`; with more than one dispatch the main agent writes the merged record `<docs-root>/reviews/<date>-review-<scope>-drift-merged.md` per the skill's Step 4, `<scope>` `specs` or the first path's basename; named paths are spec files or directories of spec files, never code paths (D19). `--all` excludes `--drift` as it excludes `--resume`. Drift brief, one numbered list: (1) keep the report template, criteria `n/a — drift lens`; (2) for each spec, list every command, flag, file, field, shape and behaviour it states and find the code that implements each (`sh-agent search`, grep, reading); (3) finding shapes `missing: <spec file:line> — <what the code lacks>`, `partial: <spec file:line> → <code file:line> — <field, flag or branch absent>`, `divergent: <spec file:line> → <code file:line> — <different pattern or dependency>`, `unspecified: <code file:line> — <surface under a spec'd command that no spec names>`; (4) report only differences, never what matches; a spec with none gets the line `no drift detected`; (5) a statement that cannot be checked is `unverified:`; (6) a fixture or example value is not a claim. `--fix` is not accepted: the operator decides whether the spec or the code moves (research-egm item 6). Docs: the skill's `argument-hint` and Step 1 text, `skill-matrix.md` row `review-drift`.

**Reviewer isolation (D10, Open).** Option (a): `omitClaudeMd` joins a second list `tightenKeys` in `inventory.go` beside `agentKeys`, read by the same lint and by a new `TestDeriveDropsTightenOnlyKeys` that pins what `DeriveAgy` (`derive.go:40-71`, which already writes only name, description, subagent, mainAgent, model and tools) leaves out; no derive code changes; `agents/reviewer.md` sets `omitClaudeMd: true`; ADR-059 supersedes the part of ADR-056a that refuses a restriction one CLI drops, for keys that only tighten, and the same change rewrites the restatements of that rule: the comment at `inventory.go:225-231`, the project `AGENTS.md` agent-keys sentence, and ADR-056a's own text gets the `Superseded by ADR-059 (tighten-only keys)` mark; the README map stays (no delivery path moves) but `agents/reviewer.md` and the project `AGENTS.md` agent-keys rule say the Antigravity reviewer keeps the global context (an honest, named gap). Option (b): one paragraph in `agents/reviewer.md` under its description recording that the cold read runs with the global context loaded on both CLIs, and why.

## Failure modes
- A CLI ignores the rule: the § 4 behavioural run shows it (n of N), the log is FAIL, the phase stays open; on Antigravity ADR-050 records that the critical-thinking rule did not hold in one run, so this rule may not either — a FAIL there is reported, not hidden.
- The rules block passes 22,000 bytes: `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` fails; the rule is shortened, never the pin raised.
- A Kickoff a fresh session cannot act on: `/review --resume` (the existing trail lens) names what it had to guess; fixed at the source before the checkpoint.
- A Kickoff pasted into the same session: harmless; the session re-reads the handoff.
- `metrics show` for a vendor with no session carrying a context value in the window: that vendor's over-target count is `null` and `notes` says so; never 0. Antigravity does carry context (`agy.go:228`), so with Antigravity sessions in the window it gets a number.
- `--drift` with no `<docs-root>/specs/` and no paths: "no specs to check", stop, nothing written.
- Standards unreadable by the dispatched reviewer (wrong skill directory): the brief tells it to report an incomplete read instead of a verdict (EGM's own rule); the phase's behavioural run checks the report cites a standard.

## Verification
Tiers: unit (`gofmt -l cmd internal && go vet ./... && go test -race -timeout 30m ./...`, guide § 1, every phase: size pins, lint, embed, vendored-pin tests); harness self-check and scratch-home install (§ 2, § 3) for Phases 1, 3, 4, 5; metrics tier (§ 3g, Phase 2: canary tests, a real-data check from a copy under `.agents/scratch/metrics-home/`, the report opened in a browser); sandbox start of each CLI plus behavioural runs (§ 4) for every changed rule, skill and agent, logged `testing/<date>-verify-<slug>.md` with n of N; real home only through a later `sh-agent update`.
E2E criteria (yes/no, independent of how Interfaces are built):
- Golden path: a fresh conversation started with only the Kickoff from the previous phase's handoff (pasted) completes the next phase, ticks its checkpoint, and ends with a handoff whose Kickoff names the phase after it — observed for every phase after Phase 1 on Claude Code, and once on Antigravity in a sandbox for Phase 4 (skill text only, D20).
- Edge: a headless run given two unrelated tasks with the rule installed does the first, leaves the second undone and names it in its handoff's kickoff; the same run in a home without the rule does both (must-fail control, § 4).
- Metric: the per-session peaks printed by `sh-agent metrics show --json` for this plan's own sessions — identified by the `Session ID:` line of each handoff this plan writes, never by date, since `--since` takes a day and the research sessions share it — are every one under the target (300K). Baseline from the same store on the same day: 31 of 49 main Claude Code sessions since 2026-09-01 passed 300K (`.agents/scratch/egm-review/metrics/copy.db`, read-only). A session over the target is reported with its peak, not hidden.
- Drift: `/review --drift` against a fixture clone whose spec names a flag the code lacks reports `missing:` with both file:line; against the unchanged fixture it reports `no drift detected`.

Do not forget.", 2026-10-23).
D25 — 2026-10-23 — The harness may write Claude Code's `autoCompactWindow`; the `REQUIREMENTS.md` edit (§ Non-goals, third bullet, appended after the memory-keys clause) is approved as written: "…and, on Claude Code, the top-level `autoCompactWindow` key, which `install` writes only when absent, at 300,000 tokens: the model cannot observe its own context, hooks are refused (R3), and the CLI's own compaction at a window the harness sets is the one monitor-and-trigger the harness can own; the operator's `/autocompact` saves under `modelSettings` and takes precedence; Antigravity has no equivalent, recorded in memory-loop.md § Known differences (ADR-060)." — by: the operator ("D25 approved as written", 2026-10-23, the removal Task's kickoff turn). body:
# Plan — fyr: Antigravity only, no report path, renamed   (2026-10-24)

## Why
The operator (2026-10-24, their own turn): "I want to remove claude from styrman harness fully. Only focus styrman harness on agy and I want to rename it to something else." Then: "lets go with fyr. I also want to rename the styrman-harness to fyr and then remove the report back to styrman-harness-feedback repo. This should be removed also." `fyr` is Swedish for lighthouse, the fixed light a vessel steers by; the name check (GitHub, Homebrew, Debian, PyPI, npm, crates, DNS, the web) is in the conversation of 2026-10-24 and found no developer tool, company or package of weight; trademark registers were not checked. Recon: `plans/2026-10-24-recon-agy-only-fyr.md` (Claude Code in ~22 non-test Go files, ~340 test mentions; `report.go` 1,102 lines plus 1,584 of tests; `sh-agent` 491 mentions in 60 Go files and 88 in 20 skills; ~5,000 lines deleted or edited; the trail stays as history). Memory `agy-only-and-rename`; feedback log 2026-10-24T19:31:51+02:00.

## Scope

- F1 An old place runs `sh-agent update` after `v3.0.0` exists → today's code finds no `sh-agent-<os>-<arch>` asset (or, on a checkout, `go build ./cmd/sh-agent` finds no such package) and replaces nothing (today's rule); the place follows `deploy/remote.md` § Crossing to fyr by hand. Before `v3.0.0` exists, today's behaviour.
- F2 `fyr install` at a crossing: `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` is a symlink or under one, or was never in the old manifest → it stays (today's resync rule) and `fyr status` names it (F4); its removal fails (`os.Remove` error) → the install stops with the error as today, the operator removes the file by hand and runs `fyr install` again (D14).
- F3 `~/.config/fyr` and `~/.config/sh-agent` both exist at install → neither is touched; one line names both and says which one `fyr` reads (`~/.config/fyr`); the operator merges or removes by hand.
- F4 Both `sh-agent` and `fyr` on PATH after a crossing that left the old file (F2) → `fyr status` prints the `shadowed`-style line naming the leftover (BUG-079's path, extended to the old name).
- F5 The GitHub rename: `gh` API reads and `git` remotes follow the redirect until a repository named `styrman-harness` is created again under the account — the plan forbids that, in `deploy/remote.md`; a checkout place's `origin` is changed by hand (`git remote set-url`, § Crossing to fyr), never by `update` (D16).
- F8 A file under a directory that carries the old marker `.sh-agent-noindex` → still left out of every index (D12); a test with only the old marker proves it.
- F6 An agent file in the old Claude Code format left under `agents/` → the lint refuses the install naming the file (Phase 3a's test).
- F7 A project with a `.claude/` link tree made by the old `/init-project` → `fyr` ignores it and the skill no longer makes or removes one; the links are the operator's to delete (D16).

It was crossed from the checkout before the tag (a tree build), so its next `fyr update` follows main as a checkout place. Open: the work Mac, the home Mac and the second Linux host. **Work Mac: crossed, 2026-10-26. Home Mac: crossed, 2026-10-26. Second Linux host: crossed, 2026-10-26.** Each by the operator on that machine, by the operator's word (popup "Crossed, all clean": `fyr status` clean, no `sh-agent` binary, `~/.config/sh-agent` or timer left) — evidence: `TEST-2026-10-26-2233-verify-the-crossing-to-fyr-at-the-work-mac-the-h` (operator-attested; no `fyr status` line pasted, binary version and the `~/.config/fyr` migration half not recorded per place), 2026-10-26
- [x] Checkpoint — expect: every place runs `fyr`; `fyr status` clean at each; no `sh-agent` binary or `~/.config/sh-agent` left at any — evidence: every place crossed (dave TEST-2026-10-26-2217, the other three TEST-2026-10-26-2233, operator-attested), the feedback repo gone, 2026-10-26

## Risks
Assumptions: GitHub redirects `gh release view --repo kesokaj/styrman-harness` and `git fetch` from the old URL after a rename until the name is reused — checked by `gh api repos/kesokaj/styrman-harness --jq .full_name` right after the rename (Phase 6, first task). An old `sh-agent update` run after `v3.0.0` replaces nothing when the asset is missing — checked by reading `release.go` (download failure leaves the binary; today's rule) in Phase 4b; moot for the crossing, which is by hand at every place (D5a). The `agy` CLI reads `agents/<name>/agent.md` written natively with the keys `DeriveAgy` writes today — checked by Phase 3a's behavioural rows (it reads the derived files today, byte-shape identical). Any Claude Code on a crossed machine loses the harness files the manifest owned (D2) — stated, not checked. The `agy` CLI loads a project's root `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/skills/` — not shown by any run in the repo; checked by Phase 3b's row (D18).

## Decisions
D1 — 2026-10-24 — Approved as written ("go approved with my comments", 2026-10-24). The name is `fyr`: repository `github.com/kesokaj/fyr` renamed in place, module path the same, binary `fyr`, state `~/.config/fyr/`, unit `fyr-dream`, marker `.fyr-noindex`, env `FYR_*`; the operator chose the word ("lets go with fyr"; the name check found no developer tool, company or package of weight; trademark registers not checked) — by: the operator for the word; implementer for the derived names (Open below for the operator's veto).
D2 — 2026-10-24 — Antigravity only: every Claude Code path leaves the binary and the content; where the operator develops is not a harness decision ("Not develop in claude but the harness should only be tailored for antigravity only", 2026-10-24, read as: the question of the development CLI is theirs alone and the harness is tailored to Antigravity whatever they use). Consequence, stated: after a crossing, a Claude Code on that machine loses the harness files the manifest owned, and `~/.claude/settings.json` keeps its two keys until the operator removes them by hand (the handoff names them) — by: the operator ("remove claude from styrman harness fully. Only focus styrman harness on agy").
D3 — 2026-10-24 — Agents are authored natively as `agents/<name>/agent.md` in Antigravity's format; `derive.go` goes; the lint keeps the tool-name and frontmatter allow-lists — by: implementer; approved by the operator ("go approved with my comments", 2026-10-24). Rejected: keeping Claude Code's format as the authoring source with derivation — a translation layer for a vendor the harness no longer targets.
D4 — 2026-10-24 — Nothing replaces `report`: experience stays on the machine; the dreamer's harness-target proposals stay under `~/.config/fyr/proposals/dream/harness/` and reach the harness checkout only by the operator's own hands (`/retro --harness` in the checkout reads that box's queue); `feedback.jsonl` and `retros.jsonl` stay local inputs of `/retro`, the dream and the metrics; the `styrman-harness-feedback` repository is deleted, not archived — by: the operator ("remove the report back … This should be removed also"; "9.) delete"; "go approved with my comments", 2026-10-24) for the removal and the deletion; implementer for the residue. Rejected: a `fyr export` bundle — a new transport the operator did not ask for.
D5 — 2026-10-24 — Superseded by D5a. (Proposed: one bridge release publishing `fyr-*` and `sh-agent-*` assets, both markers and a `cmd/sh-agent` shim, removed in `v3.1.0` after every place crossed.)
D5a — 2026-10-24 — No bridge: `v3.0.0` (MAJOR: the installed command changes name) ships `fyr` only — one asset set, one marker, no shim; each of the four installed places is reinstalled by hand once (`deploy/remote.md` § Crossing to fyr), `fyr install` migrating the state dir and removing the old binary; an old `sh-agent update` after the release replaces nothing and the guide says what to do — supersedes D5 — by: the operator ("5.) change the fyr instead of sh-agent", 2026-10-24, read as: the release carries `fyr`, not `sh-agent`; an implementer's reading, quoted in the handoff for correction). Rejected: a new repository (loses the redirects for `git fetch` and `gh` reads that the by-hand procedure still relies on).
D6 — 2026-10-24 — Plan `2026-10-23-session-sized-work.md` closes at Phase 2b; its Phases 3–4 (EGM deltas) are re-queued as their own plan after this one, Phase 5 dropped (a Claude Code agent key), Phase 6 superseded by this plan's Phase 5 — by: implementer, from the operator's redirection; approved ("go approved with my comments", 2026-10-24); the EGM items are CLI-neutral and keep their value.
D7 — 2026-10-24 — Metrics: ingest reads Antigravity only; `cli=claude` rows already in a store are kept and shown as `claude (historical)` only when present; nothing deletes operator data — by: implementer; approved ("go approved with my comments", 2026-10-24).
D8 — 2026-10-24 — The historical trail is not rewritten: `changes/`, `handoffs/`, `reviews/`, `bugs/`, dated `testing/` logs, old plans and ADRs keep `sh-agent`, `styrman-harness` and Claude Code as they were (append-only; ~6,000 mentions); the living docs, specs, guides, skills, context and code change — by: implementer (project `AGENTS.md`: `changes/` and `DECISIONS.md` are append-only); approved ("go approved with my comments", 2026-10-24).
D9 — 2026-10-24 — The `REQUIREMENTS.md` replacement text is approved as proposed: the title, R0–R5, R7–R10, Known limits and Non-goals, the exact text of `.agents/scratch/fyr/requirements-edit.md` shown in chat and now in `REQUIREMENTS.md` at commit `92f5c8c` (verbatim, checked section by section) — by: the operator ("go all approved", 2026-10-24, over the Phase 0 report's six items: 1 the set, 2 R2 without a native-read claim, 3 the update timer deferred to Phase 6, 4 BUG-172 struck as obsolete, 5 the stale memory struck, 6 D2 and D5a confirmed).
D10 — 2026-10-24 — ADR-062 supersedes ADR-025 and ADR-060 and the report half of ADR-047a; it amends ADR-030, 033 and 038 (the binary's name; 033's report clause), ADR-047 (R10's scope), ADR-058 and 058a (the Kickoff wording naming `claude`) and ADR-061 (R0's "both CLIs"); Scope and Phase 0 now say the same — by: cold read round 1 (`reviews/2026-10-24-review-cold-read-fyr-agy-only.md`, the ADR-list finding).
D11 — 2026-10-24 — The hourly `sh-agent-update.timer` on the dev box: rebutted for Phases 1–5, kept for the crossing. The real home runs the v2.7.0 release binary, which refuses `--repo` (`journalctl --user -u sh-agent-update.service`, 2026-10-24 20:04: "this is the release binary v2.7.0 … --repo … is refused"), so the timer installs nothing from `main` and the Claude Code harness in `~/.claude` (the reviewer, verifier and security agents this plan's phases dispatch) stays as v2.7.0 left it until this box's crossing in Phase 6. The unit is the operator's own (the harness never installs it; `deploy/remote.md` shows it as an example) and execs `~/.local/bin/sh-agent`, so Phase 6 gains a who: user step to disable or rewrite it before the crossing, and § Crossing to fyr names it; a checkout place running such a timer would follow `main`, and § Crossing says to stop it first — by: cold read round 1 (`reviews/2026-10-24-review-cold-read-fyr-agy-only.md`, finding 1), rebuttal by evidence for its first half.
D12 — 2026-10-24 — `fyr` honours both `.fyr-noindex` and `.sh-agent-noindex` (F8): an old marker keeps excluding its directory from every index the dream reads, with a test holding only the old marker; nothing renames the operator's files — by: cold read round 1 (`reviews/2026-10-24-review-cold-read-fyr-agy-only.md`, finding 2); the safe direction for a privacy control.
D13 — 2026-10-24 — The state-dir migration runs first in every verb that writes under the state dir and never in a read-only verb or mode (the lists in Interfaces), which print one line instead (review-standards § 8: the side effect sits below the read-only returns, with a test that the dry run does not migrate); F3 (both dirs) leaves both and uses `~/.config/fyr`, no merge procedure is built (the operator's; default unchanged); the dream timer rename covers systemd `sh-agent-dream` and launchd `com.styrman.sh-agent-dream` under BUG-144's `UnitFor(home)` — by: cold read round 1 (`reviews/2026-10-24-review-cold-read-fyr-agy-only.md`, the migration finding, items 1–3).
D14 — 2026-10-24 — `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` leaves only through the existing resync (`apply.go:122-146`; the old manifest lists it when the old install wrote it, `plan.go:188-190`): a symlink or a path under a link stays, a removal error stops the install as today (F2); no new removal rule and no ownership check are written, so the "not-owned" test row goes (a non-root test cannot `chown(2)` to another uid: EPERM). The migration precedes the resync, which reads the previous manifest from the state dir. The old-manifest fixture is the real one: a v2.7.0 binary built from `git archive v2.7.0` into scratch and installed with `--home` — by: cold read round 1 (`reviews/2026-10-24-review-cold-read-fyr-agy-only.md`, findings 6 and 8).
D15 — 2026-10-24 — `fyr` reads `FYR_*` only; each set `SH_AGENT_*` variable gets one notice on stderr naming its `FYR_*` name, and § Crossing to fyr says to rename exported ones — by: cold read round 1 (`reviews/2026-10-24-review-cold-read-fyr-agy-only.md`, the migration finding, item 4); default chosen over silence because an ignored `SH_AGENT_REPO` changes which tree `update` installs.
D16 — 2026-10-24 — Struck: F5's automatic `origin` rewrite (no request, no mechanism, contradicts D5a's by-hand `git remote set-url`) and F7's link removal (the stub list it needs leaves in Phase 3b; a project's `.claude/` links are the operator's to delete) — by: cold read round 1 (`reviews/2026-10-24-review-cold-read-fyr-agy-only.md`, the F5/F7 finding).
D17 — 2026-10-24 — Native agents reproduce today's derived output byte for byte (generated into scratch before `derive.go` goes); `knownTools` is today's `toolMap` values; the inventory prints the `model` key as written; "a budget below the agent's `maxTurns`" becomes "a tool-call budget the dispatch names" in the context and the skills (Antigravity drops `maxTurns`); `KeepForeign`, `IsOurs` and the stub paths are deleted in Phase 2 as dead code, `ClaudeRoot` stays only in `pruneEmptyDirs`' stop map, the state's `Vendor` field is read only to be ignored — by: cold read round 1 (`reviews/2026-10-24-review-cold-read-fyr-agy-only.md`, the D3 and dead-code findings).
D18 — 2026-10-24 — The `REQUIREMENTS.md` set also covers the title, R3, R5, all of R4's leaving clauses, and Known limits 2 and 3, with one row added (no compaction window on Antigravity, moved from memory-loop.md § Known differences, which R10 stops citing); R2 makes no claim that Antigravity reads a project's `AGENTS.md` or `.agents/` natively — the repo holds no run that shows it — and Phase 3b adds the row that checks it — by: cold read round 1 (`reviews/2026-10-24-review-cold-read-fyr-agy-only.md`, the requirements-set and R2 findings); the exact text is D9's.
D19 — 2026-10-24 — A zip place takes its `fyr` binary from the release asset, downloaded by hand as a release-binary place does; `./fyr update --from-zip` then installs the tree and, as a plain-copy install, copies the running binary to `~/.local/bin/fyr` (`plan.go:188-190`); the zip replaces no binary (R9) — by: cold read round 1 (`reviews/2026-10-24-review-cold-read-fyr-agy-only.md`, the zip-place finding).
D20 — 2026-10-24 — E2E criterion 3 and the Phase 4a grep exempt, by name in the log: vendored-verbatim files and their `skills/VENDORED.md` rows (`find-skills`, `gke-basics`, `review-standards/references/prompt-audit`; project `AGENTS.md` forbids editing them), `.agents/docs/retros/` (trail, D8), the migration and historical-metrics code with their tests and fixtures, and `REQUIREMENTS.md`'s history clause; `internal/search/testdata/recall.tsv` is edited, not exempt, unless its rows test history; "and this plan" left the Phase 4 expectation because the pathspec excludes plans — by: cold read round 1 (`reviews/2026-10-24-review-cold-read-fyr-agy-only.md`, finding 3).
D21 — 2026-10-24 — Phase 3 splits into 3a (agents, lint, context, rules; 9 runs) and 3b (skills, kits, content runs); Phase 4 into 4a (the mechanical rename) and 4b (migration, timers, release, the crossing guide); each is one session under the session-sizing rule — by: cold read round 1 (`reviews/2026-10-24-review-cold-read-fyr-agy-only.md`, the sizing answer).
D22 — 2026-10-24 — Kept, with the reason the cold read asked for: the `StateDir` constant and its literal-grep test (the rename touches 21 files with the path, and a missed literal splits the state across two dirs silently); `internal/redact` (D4 deletes `report.go`, and a package keeps the dream off the installer's code for it); `diff` and `sync` unchanged; E2E criterion 1 worded by outcome, the asset download moved to Phase 6 — by: cold read round 1 (`reviews/2026-10-24-review-cold-read-fyr-agy-only.md`, the scope and E2E-1 findings), implementer.
D23 — 2026-10-24 — D2 and D5a are confirmed as read: where the operator develops is theirs, and `v3.0.0` ships `fyr` only with a by-hand crossing at each place; the Open row on D5a closes — by: the operator ("go all approved", item 6, 2026-10-24).
D24 — 2026-10-24 — Phase 2's checkpoint grep also exempts the two listing-budget comments, until the budget is measured on Antigravity (Follow-ups), and `internal/search/testdata/recall.tsv`, which D20 edits in Phase 4a; the box closes when Phase 3a removes the agent format (`derive.go`, `inventory.go`'s format comments, their tests); the budget number stays at 19,500 bytes until then — by: the operator ("Go all approved", 2026-10-24, over the Phase 2 report's items 1 amend, 2 defer, 3 defer to Phase 3b, 4 the Go SDK theirs).
D25 — 2026-10-25 — BUG-174 takes option (a): the context's post-dispatch check says its three git commands are three separate calls, because agy's grant store allows a simple command only; it lands in Phase 3b with its `context/` rows (the canary and every dispatch row re-run), and the kits keep their grants (no `command(*)`) — by: the operator ("Go all approved", 2026-10-25, over the Phase 3a report's items 1 (a) in 3b, 2 re-run in 3b, 4 fix in 3b, 5 defer to Phase 5).
D26 — 2026-10-25 — BUG-174's root cause was misread, and option (a) alone did not fix it: on agy 1.4.7 with the three commands run separately, `git log @{u}..HEAD` is still auto-denied on its own in 6 of 6 dispatch rows, while chained lines of granted commands ran (`git log -n 5 --stat && git status …`); a probe ran `git log --branches --not --remotes --oneline`, `git status -sb` and `git log origin/HEAD..HEAD` and was denied only `git log @{u}..HEAD` — the grant store refuses the `@{u}` form, and the Phase 3a chains all held it. The context's check names `git log --branches --not --remotes --oneline` instead (it also works where no upstream is set), keeps D25's "three separate commands" wording, and BUG-174 gets an addendum correcting its root cause; the kits gain `command(govulncheck)`, the `security` agent's own step, denied in its row — by: the operator ("Swap to --not --remotes", "Add command(govulncheck)", 2026-10-25, over `.agents/scratch/fyr/phase3b-bug174-decision.md`); supersedes D25's reading of the cause, not its wording.
D27 — 2026-10-25 — BUG-175 is fixed in Phase 3b's range, after its checkpoint: `skills/project-memory/SKILL.md`'s date line says to run `date +%F` as its own command and type the printed date into the body, and the save is the one `sh-agent memory add` command with nothing joined and no `$( )`, because agy's grant store refuses a command substitution; the `project-memory` row re-runs under the kit's named grants (no `command(*)`) — by: the operator ("Go all approved", 2026-10-25, over the Phase 3b report's items 1 BUG-174 done, 2 BUG-175 fix, 3 D18 done, 4 the test replaced, 5 `AGENTS.md:67` and the claude.ai wording defer, 6 the Go SDK theirs).
D28 — 2026-10-25 — Phase 4a's mechanical rename leaves to Phase 4b what 4b's own boxes test and change: the release asset name, `ReleaseRepo`, the sums marker and README's two install-from-release sections (4b's `release.go` box), and the dream unit names `sh-agent-dream` and `com.styrman.sh-agent-dream` (4b's timer box; the unit's text and binary path already say `fyr`). The repository name `styrman-harness` in clone URLs and the map's repository node waits for the rename in Phase 6. The catalog's marker file is renamed `.fyr-noindex` with `refresh-catalog.sh` writing it, because the marker is the harness's file and not an entry. The search header says `left out by a noindex marker:`, because each directory may hold either name. An empty `SH_AGENT_*` variable gets no notice. `fyr-matrix.md`'s dated records keep the old name under a note — by: implementer (`changes/2026-10-25-1039-fyr-phase4a-rename-in-the-tree.md` § Deviations); kept by the operator (D29).
D29 — 2026-10-25 — The Phase 4a report's five items: 1 BUG-176 (the `maxTurns` phrase left in `skills/bug/SKILL.md:55`) and BUG-177 (the trailer slip) recorded and the line fixed, a Phase 4b box; 2 D28 kept; 3 the kit guard watches both real state dirs until the crossing, a Phase 4b box; 4 E2E criterion 4 says exit 1, the code's behaviour since Phase 1; 5 the Antigravity runs under the new name stay Phase 5's (E2E 1 and the per-skill rows) — by: the operator ("Go all approved", 2026-10-25, over `.agents/scratch/fyr/phase4a-report.md`).
D30 — 2026-10-25 — Phase 4b's choices where the boxes and Interfaces left one open:
- A symlinked `~/.config/sh-agent`, with no `~/.config/fyr`, REFUSES a writing verb with the steps to move it by hand: a verb that ran on would start an empty state directory beside the operator's link, and the resync would never see the old manifest. A read-only verb names it.
- The read-only notice goes to stderr, because the stdout of `render`, `list` and `metrics show --json` is data. The `migrated …` line goes to stdout with the verb's other change lines.
- `install` replaces an old-named dream unit with the installing shell's PATH, as `--install-timer` does. The new unit goes in first and the old one comes out after. A refused new unit keeps the old one and fails the install, naming it.
- `LegacyTimerFiles` looks for the old bare names only, because no release wrote a bare fyr name under another home.
- Not built, named for Phase 5:
  - `uninstall` and `--remove-timer` do not remove an old-named unit;
  - F4's `status` line about a leftover `sh-agent` on PATH.
- `skills/bug/SKILL.md:55` says the dispatch "names a tool-call budget", `context/AGENTS.md:35`'s wording. The box's "a tool-call budget the dispatch names" would repeat its subject.
- The global `preflight` skill names the rule, not the tag: "an installed command that changes its name" is a MAJOR. `v3.0.0` itself is named in this repository's `deploy/remote.md` § Releases, because a harness skill deploys to every project. Step 6's bridge check had no `sh-agent` wording to drop.
- The crossing test (`TestCrossingFromV270`) builds v2.7.0 with no version stamp, so it starts from a plain-copy place. The checkpoint run builds it as a release binary (`-X main.version=v2.7.0`), so it starts from a release-binary place.
— by: implementer (`changes/` entry of Phase 4b § Deviations).
D31 — 2026-10-25 — Phase 5's review answers (reports `reviews/2026-10-25-review-v2.7.0-HEAD-code-docs.md` and `reviews/2026-10-25-security-v2.7.0-HEAD.md`, each with its `## Outcome`):
- `install` replaces an old-named dream timer only when the service manager says it is on. When the manager answers `disabled` or `masked` (systemd) or `Could not find service` (launchd), the old unit's files are removed and no fyr timer is turned on. A manager that cannot be asked counts as on. This is the security review's low finding and the round-2 fix. The operator chose "Fix, no round 3".
- The clone URL becomes `git@github.com:kesokaj/fyr.git` in Phase 5, not Phase 6 (D28 left it there with no box). The map's repository node is relabelled `fyr`. That is a label, not a path (rule 3), and the private map page is the operator's to refresh (rule 5). `TestOneRepositoryName` pins the URL.
- `.gitignore` stays without its `.claude` lines. The operator chose "Keep removed".
- The review skill's artifact sentence ("…with the Write tool") stays for the EGM follow-up plan.
— by: implementer, with the operator's two answers quoted.
D32 — 2026-10-25 — The Claude Code files on dave stay. The operator, in their own turn: "dont remove the claude skills and context on this machine. That should still be left on dave. But in the project we will only focus on antigravity going forward." Asked how, they chose "fyr never removes them": the resync skips the old manifest's `~/.claude` entries at every place, drops them from fyr's manifest and prints one keep line. Those files stay as v2.7.0 wrote them, and fyr never updates or deletes them again. This amends D2's stated consequence and D14's sweep of `~/.claude`; `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` still leaves by the resync. The work is Phase 5b, before Phase 6's crossing — by: the operator (2026-10-25; memory `keep-claude-files-on-dave`).
D33 — 2026-10-25 — D30 is kept as written. The operator chose "Keep D30 (Recommended)" when asked in this session, which closes D30's veto window. Phase 4b report items 2 and 3 (`uninstall` and `--remove-timer` leave an old-named unit; F4's `status` line) now live as boxes in plan `2026-10-25-harness-audit-fix.md` Phase 2 (audit TR9) — by: the operator (2026-10-25).
Open: whether `metrics show`'s historical `claude` column is wanted at all — default: shown only when rows exist (D7).
Open: how many installed places exist today (deploy/remote.md § The four places) — default: four; Phase 6 ticks each by name.

title: Recon — agy-only-fyr (2026-10-24)
body:
# Recon — agy-only-fyr   (2026-10-24)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Question
Inventory for: (1) drop Claude Code, Antigravity (`agy`) only; (2) drop `sh-agent report` and all sending to `styrman-harness-feedback`; (3) rename to `fyr` (module `github.com/kesokaj/fyr`, binary `fyr`, state `~/.config/fyr/`).

## Summary
Claude Code is woven through ~22 non-test Go files (about 150 mentions) and ~25 test files (about 340 mentions). The vendor switch is concentrated in `internal/harness/plan.go` (VendorAll/Claude/Antigravity), `settings.go`, `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`, `internal/metrics/claude.go` + `ingest.go`, `internal/memory`, and `internal/dream` (collect/dream/run). `report` is isolated: `internal/harness/report.go` (1102 lines) + `report_test.go` (1584 lines, 28 tests) + `runReport`/`report()` in main.go, BUT report.go also holds `Redact`/`RedactJSONL`, which `internal/dream/collect.go:157,254` uses, so the redactor must be moved, not deleted. The rename touches ~490 Go `sh-agent` mentions in 60 files, ~6,200 in docs (mostly historical trail) and 125 in context/README/REQUIREMENTS. The hard part is not the sed but the bridge release: the old binary `update` path hard-codes the repo, asset name `sh-agent-<os>-<arch>` and a `# styrman-harness vX` SHA256SUMS marker (release.go:24,35,51).

## 1. Claude Code surfaces in Go (non-test mention counts)
| File | Count | What it does / agy-only disposition |
|---|---|---|
| internal/harness/plan.go | 30 | Consts `VendorAll/Claude/Antigravity` (21-23), `ParseVendor` (~31-35), `ClaudeRoot`; `Plan` builds each file for `wantClaude` (73) and `wantAgy` (74): `~/.claude/{AGENTS.md,CLAUDE.md stub (KeepForeign),skills,agents,commands,rules}` vs `~/.gemini/config/{rules,skills,agents/<n>/agent.md,workflows}`. DROP all `wantClaude` branches (lines ~87-185 region: 27-30, 82-83, 96-97, 112-113, 121-122), keep agy; `--vendor` flag and `VendorAll` collapse. `claudeStub` const goes. |

## Flows
- Install: main.go `install` -> `harness.LoadSource` (source.go: embedded `styrman.Files` or checkout) -> `Plan(vendor)` (plan.go) -> `Install` (apply.go, pathguard/sweep) -> for Claude: `SettingSet` per `OwnedSettings` + `SettingsHint`; state.json manifest (state.go). agy-only: keep `~/.gemini/config/*`, derive agents, 22,000-byte rendered-context pin (size_test.go) stays; Claude-specific `TestRenderedContextUnderTarget` 15,000 stays.
- Update: checkout = git fetch/pull --ff-only + rebuild + reinstall (repo.go); release binary = `UpdateFromRelease` (release.go:69) `gh release view --repo ReleaseRepo` -> asset `sh-agent-<os>-<arch>` + SHA256SUMS with `# styrman-harness vX` marker -> replace binary -> exec `<dest> install`; zip = `--from-zip` (zip.go).
- Report: `report` -> `Collect(home)` -> `BuildRecord` -> `SendReport` -> clone `styrman-harness-feedback` throwaway -> push; also invoked by uninstall cleanup (main.go:1127).
- Metrics ingest: `metrics ingest --vendor` -> `ingestClaude` (claude.go reads ~/.claude/projects) and `ingestAgy` (agy.go) -> store.go SQLite `~/.config/sh-agent/metrics.db`; events.go reads feedback.jsonl for corrections.
- Dream: `dream` -> `collect` (claude transcripts + agy via internal/search/dream.go DB reads) -> `command(vendor)` runs `claude -p` or `agy ... -p` -> proposals under `~/.config/sh-agent/proposals/dream/{harness,...}` (harness-target ones were what `report` sent).

## Conventions to match
Tests first, `go test -race`; stdlib-only Go (one SQLite dep); ADR for any map/path change landing in ONE commit with code, docs and README map (AGENTS.md rules 3-5); `TestHarnessMap` pins README map vs binary verbs; delivery claim has one home (delivery.md § The model); `changes/` entries append-only, ADRs append-only; docs trail is historical: do NOT rewrite old plans/changes/reviews/bugs on rename (about 6,000 of the 6,187 doc `sh-agent` hits live there); embed pinned both ways to git (embed_test.go); size pins (22,000 / 15,000 bytes) and skill listing budget 19,500.

## Risks
1. BUG-bridge: places on old binary run `sh-agent update` which asks `gh release view --repo github.com/kesokaj/styrman-harness`. If the GitHub repo is renamed, `gh` follows the redirect for API reads, but the old binary then looks for an asset named `sh-agent-<os>-<arch>` and a `# styrman-harness vX` marker in SHA256SUMS; a release carrying only `fyr-*` assets makes every old place fail the update (and "nothing replaced" is the safe failure). A bridge release must ship BOTH names (a `sh-agent-*` binary that is really the new fyr build + a SHA256SUMS with the old marker), then the new code must migrate `~/.config/sh-agent` -> `~/.config/fyr`, the PATH binary name, the systemd update/dream timer unit names, and the old `~/.claude` files it wrote (uninstall for claude). AGENTS.md says a release after a bridge release waits for the operator's word that every place crossed it (BUG-161).
2. `gh` redirect on rename does not cover `git@github.com:kesokaj/styrman-harness.git` checkout remotes forever in all cases (GitHub redirects git too until a new repo takes the old name; do not create a new `styrman-harness`). Checkout places' `repo_origin_test.go` identity checks may reject a renamed origin.
3. Module path change: 30 Go files import the path (embed.go package `styrman` alias at source.go:12); root-package tests (embed_test, plan_test, init_project_test) reference it. `go:embed` itself has no path dependency, mechanical.
4. report.go holds the shared redactor (dream uses it); deleting the file breaks `internal/dream` and its redaction pins.
5. Removing `report` leaves harness-target proposals, `retros.jsonl`, and `feedback-log`/`retro --harness` flows with no transport; `/retro --harness` and queue dirs (`~/.config/sh-agent/proposals/`) become dead or must be redefined. Also R9's "improve the harness from reports" loop disappears (needs operator design call).
6. Dropping Claude Code removes the harness's own development CLI: the repo is developed in Claude Code today (this session; the global CLAUDE.md is Claude's `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` -> @AGENTS.md). After the change nothing deploys into `~/.claude`, so the operator's dev sessions would lose the harness unless they keep an old binary. The behavioural tests (ab-kit, seed-security, kit-preamble) run `claude -p` today; agy-only means agy runs only. The reviewer/verifier subagents here are Claude Code subagents.
7. Antigravity limits become binding: 24,000-byte global rules block (context pin 22,000 incl. inventory), no `autoCompactWindow`/compaction control (ADR-060 clause moves nowhere), no settings keys, no native memory switch (R10 memory hint), tool-name hang risk (toolMap), IDE unsupported. `.claude/` project symlinks (init-project Step 5) removed: project discovery for agy is `.agents/` natively.
8. Existing data: metrics.db rows `cli=claude`, state.json vendor values, `~/.claude/*` files left behind by old installs (uninstall sweep must still remove or the new binary must say so).
9. Mechanical rename of docs: sed over trail would falsify history; and `sh-agent` appears in skill text that models read (88 mentions in 20 skills + `~/.config/sh-agent` 27 in 7 skills) which must change in lock-step with the binary.
10. `sh-agent-matrix.md` and `kit-preamble.sh` assert fixtures (BUG-087..123); renaming silently breaks run kits unless the preamble greps are updated.

## Open questions
- Authoring format: keep Claude-format `agents/*.md` + derive, or switch to native `agent.md`? (affects derive.go, 8 agents, lint, REQUIREMENTS R1.)
- Bridge: how many places exist and are they all reachable to run one transitional `sh-agent update`? Ship dual-named assets for one release? Rename repo in place (redirect) or new repo?
- Does a `--home` / `--vendor` flag survive (agy only), or is vendor removed and state.json versioned for migration?
- Metrics: keep reading old claude rows? Keep `metrics ingest --vendor`?
- What replaces `report` as the way experience returns (nothing, manual, or `fyr export`)? Fate of `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl`, `/retro --harness`, `proposals/dream/harness`.
- Is the `attribution` off setting needed on agy (git commit trailers)? Not examined for agy settings.
- Whether `agy` supports commands/workflows dir names and `agent.md` keys unchanged (existing derive covers it today).
- Is `github.com/kesokaj/fyr` the same repo renamed or a new one (affects ReleaseRepo and old-binary behaviour)?

## Estimated change size
| Area | Files | Approx lines (delete+edit) |
|---|---|---|
| Delete Claude: plan.go, settings.go(+tests), derive comments, memory, main.go branches | ~10 + 5 tests | 1,200 (settings 272+tests ~300, plan ~80, main ~150, memory ~40, harness_test ~65 mentions) |
| Delete metrics/claude.go + ingest/show edits | 5 + 3 tests | 800 (claude.go 555 + claude_test ~600 + edits) |
| Dream: drop claude branch | 6 + 5 tests | 250 |
| Delete report (keep redactor move) | report.go, report_test.go, main.go, audit_test, TestHarnessMap | ~1,300 deleted + ~1,600 test lines (net after keeping redaction tests ~ -2,000) |
| Rename Go: module path, cmd dir, state dir, release asset/marker, env vars | ~60 Go files | ~700 mentions, mechanical, plus bridge logic ~100 new |
| Skills/agents/context/rules text | ~25 files | ~150 lines edited (init-project 26 mentions largest) |
| README/AGENTS.md/REQUIREMENTS/ROADMAP/delivery.md/deploy guides/specs | ~15 files | ~400 lines + 1 ADR (superseding 030/033/038/047/060) |
| Test kits (kit-preamble, ab-kit, agy-rel, seed-security, guide, matrix) | 7 | ~150 |
| Historical trail (plans, changes, reviews, bugs, testing) | ~1,200 files | untouched by design; add one change entry, ADR, handoff |

## Not examined
Per-line contents of pathguard.go/sweep.go/apply.go for `.claude` guards; internal/dream/timer.go unit names; search store paths beyond grep counts; skills' exact lines outside init-project/context; guide.md § 4/5 line detail; whether `Alive` in report.go is used outside report; the other agy behaviours (settings equivalents); ADR-030/033/038 text; internal/search marker behaviour; GitHub-side facts (redirect semantics are from general knowledge, not tested).

title: Plan — metrics fed at every checkpoint, joined to records (2026-10-25)
body:
# Plan — metrics fed at every checkpoint, joined to records   (2026-10-25)

## Why

Roadmap item 2 (`ROADMAP.md`, ADR-063 § Consequences: "Roadmap items 2–4 (metrics fed at checkpoints, …) build on it"). Two gaps, both left by the brain plan (`PLAN-2026-10-25-sqlite-trail`):

1. **The metrics join is blind on a migrated project.** `fyr metrics ingest` derives each main session's events (`SPEC-fyr-metrics` § Metric definitions, metrics A1–A5) from files: handoffs, `testing/*-verify-*.md`, `reviews/*.md`, `bugs/BUG-*.md` under the docs root (`internal/metrics/events.go:132-185`), and corrections from `~/.config/fyr/feedback.jsonl` (`events.go:252`). A migrated project has no docs root (its trail is records, R7), and `fyr record import --global` turns `feedback.jsonl` into global `feedback` records, so DoD closure (A1), verifier status (A2), review findings (A3), escaped bugs (A4) and corrections (A5) go to zero. First reads (metric C3) go blind too: it counts the trail kind of a session's first three `Read` steps (`internal/metrics/show.go:460`), and a migrated session reads its trail through `fyr record get|list`, a Bash call.
2. **Nothing feeds the store at a checkpoint.** Ingest runs inside `fyr dream` (`internal/dream/metrics.go:19`, R3's nightly exception) or when the operator types it, so `/retro`'s metrics step (`skills/retro/SKILL.md:50`) reads a store that can be a day stale or empty. R0: "The CLI asks it for help at the moments the context names: … at a phase end".

Terms: a **migrated** project is a checkout holding `.agents/trail.jsonl` (`SPEC-fyr-record` § Unmigrated project); **the file-wins load** is `SPEC-fyr-record` § Load (the checkout's `trail.jsonl` replaces the scope's rows when its hash changed); the **kit** is the Antigravity run kit, `.agents/kit/` (`GUIDE-testing` § 4); a **main session** is one with no parent (a subagent's is excluded, `SPEC-fyr-metrics` B2); **E2E** criteria are the end-to-end outcomes under Verification.

## Scope

In:
- S1. The event join reads a migrated project's handoff, testing, review and bug records; corrections come from the global feedback records for every project, migrated or not; an unmigrated project's other events keep the file join.
- S2. One event reference per trail item — the record ID, or for a file the ID the import gives it — and a rewrite of the store's existing file-name references to that form, so a project's migration adds no duplicate events.
- S3. C3 counts `fyr record get <ID>` (as the ID's kind) and `fyr record list` (as `list`) among a main session's first three trail reads.
- S4. The `handoff` skill runs `fyr metrics ingest` as its last call; `/retro` runs it before its metrics step (not under `--dry-run`); the context's checkpoint sentence names it once.
- S5. `SPEC-fyr-metrics`, `README.md` (the `fyr metrics` row), `GUIDE-skill-matrix` (handoff and retro rows) and `GUIDE-testing` § 3g say so.

S1, S2 and S4 are the two gaps of `## Why`; S3 is the C3 half of gap 1. Each was approved with this plan (D19).

Out:
- An ingest triggered inside the binary by `fyr record add` (Rejected, below).
- Ingesting Claude Code sessions (ADR-062: Antigravity only).
- `fyr check` and `fyr eval` (roadmap items 3, 4).
- Re-deriving events for sessions whose trail files the import dropped: their stored events stay (R4: the store is the only copy).
- Restoring commit references to imported closed bugs (D13).

Follow-ups noted, not built:
- An Antigravity conversation whose summary time is the zero time is stored with `ended_at` -62135596800000: BUG-181 (open; filed on the operator's approval, 2026-10-25).
- Remove the file join once every project the operator works in is migrated.

### The join (`joinEvents`), per project root

Order (today's order kept, `events.go:100-109`): corrections first, then the root-gone check, then commits, then trail events.

1. **Ref rewrite**, once per ingest before any root, in Go inside the join's transaction: every `handoff`, `verifier` or `review` event whose `ref` ends in `.md` gets `ref = ImportedID(<handoff|testing|review>, <ref without .md>)` (`UPDATE OR IGNORE`); a row the rewrite could not take because the ID-form row already exists for that session is deleted (it is a duplicate). Idempotent: once rewritten, no `.md` ref is left, and the file join (step 4) writes ID-form refs. No schema change.
2. **Corrections** (A5): `ForMetrics(home, root).Feedback` plus the `feedback.jsonl` lines about root (a home not yet imported). The ref is the entry's `ts` normalised to UTC RFC 3339 (`2026-10-21T14:39:54Z`), so one correction present in both, written `Z` or `+02:00`, counts once. A body that is not JSON or has no parsable `ts`: skipped.
3. Root gone or not git: a note as today; no trail events.
4. `Migrated` false → the file join as today (`events.go:132-185`), with `ref = ImportedID(kind, stem)` for handoff, testing and review files (a bug file is `BUG-NNN` as today).
5. `Migrated` true → the records join below. An error from `ForMetrics` (an unparsable `trail.jsonl`, a busy or newer `brain.db`) is a note `records not read: <root>: <reason>` (printed through `search.Printable`); the root gets no trail events this run; its stored events stay; ingest still exits 0.

**Record time.** The ID must match `^[A-Z]+-(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})-(\d{4})(-|$)` and parse with `time.ParseInLocation("2006-01-02 1504", …, time.Local)` (a minute like `2459` or a day like `02-30` fails). A record with such a time belongs to every main session whose window `[started_at, ended_at + 30 min]` overlaps `[stamp, stamp + 60 s)`. Anything else has no time. `updated` is never used (D3). Known limit, in the spec: a record added on a machine in another time zone is placed off by the zones' difference.

| Event | Records read | Value | Placed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `handoff` (A1) | `handoff` | `""` | record time |
| `verifier` (A2) | `testing` whose title matches `^Verif(ication\|y)\b` (the verifier's own title, `agents/verifier/agent.md:11`) and whose body has a line matching `statusLine` (`events.go:24`) | the status word | record time |
| `review` (A3) | `review` | `high=N,medium=N,low=N` from `finding` (`events.go:25`) over the body | record time |
| `bug` (A4) | `bug` | the full sha of the first hex run in the body that prefixes a commit owned by one session (as today) | that commit's session; `ts` = the record's `date` at 00:00 local, a stored stamp only |

A record with no time gives no `handoff`, `verifier` or `review` event. Bodies are read only for these patterns; no record text is stored. Scope rule: the trail is the scope of the main worktree root (`trail.Roots`), which every worktree of a repository shares; the session's own root may be a linked worktree (`events.go:63`).

### C3 — first trail reads

`agyTool` sets a Bash step's `target_kind` from its command line through a new `recordRead(cmd string) string`. It walks the command's segments with the same splitting and leading-word skipping `Verb` uses (`verb.go:107`: here-docs stripped, wrappers, `VAR=value` and keywords skipped) and takes the first segment whose program's basename is `fyr`, or whose words are `go run ./cmd/fyr`. After the program it skips `--home`/`--repo` with their value (`--home X` or `--home=X`) and any other word starting with `-`; the next word must be `record`, then:
- `get` → the first following word not starting with `-` (and not the value of `--home`/`--repo`): its kind by the brain's ID prefixes (`internal/brain/record.go:28-33`, `FEEDBACK` and `PROPOSAL` included), or `record` when the prefix is unknown or no ID word follows;
- `list` → `list`;
- anything else → `""`.

So `fyr-bin` or any other program name is not counted. Only the kind is stored, from that closed set plus `list` and `record`; the ID and every other word are dropped.

`show` (`show.go:460`): a main session's first-reads are its first three steps that carry a `target_kind` and are a `Read` or a `Bash` (today: `Read` only). Steps ingested before this change keep `target_kind` NULL on Bash.

## Failure modes

- `trail.jsonl` does not parse, or `brain.db` is busy or newer: the ingest's notes name `records not read: <root>: <reason>`; exit 0; earlier events stay.
- A record ID with no valid minute: no A1–A3 event for it; nothing printed.
- An imported closed bug: no A4 event (its body holds no commit, D13); events stored before the migration stay.
- A feedback body that is not JSON or has no parsable `ts`: skipped.
- The ref rewrite fails: the join's transaction rolls back, as any join error does today (ingest exit 1, the store as it was).
- `fyr metrics ingest` fails at a handoff: the chat report shows the line and exit status; the session ends as planned; the next ingest (next handoff, `/retro`, or the nightly dream) joins every session again.

## Trust boundaries and data handled

- Record bodies cross a boundary: a `trail.jsonl` pulled from git was written on another machine or by another contributor. Only regex matches are taken (a status word, severity counts, hex runs matched against known commits, an RFC 3339 time); no body text is stored or printed.
- Transcript command lines (Antigravity's conversation databases): only a kind from the closed set above is stored, never the ID or any word of the command (R4).
- `events.ref` holds record IDs, the same data class as the file names it held before (ADR-055).
- This touches input parsing (record bodies, command lines): `security` is due at Done.
