## Item 37 — borken: a development build at a zip place is deadlocked

What happened on borken (agy's run, quoted by the operator on 2026-10-31):
- `fyr version` printed `b9cae29346b2`, a development build.
- `fyr update --from-zip ~/Downloads/fyr-v5.0.0.zip` exited 0: "installing its harness and the running binary b9cae29346b2 … nothing in the zip replaces the binary". The version did not move.
- After that, `fyr status` and `fyr update` both exit 1: "this home was installed from a zip … harness repo not found and this build is b9cae29346b2, a development build".

Checked against the code (2026-10-31, `afd92b4`):
- `status` and `update` are `source: true` verbs (`cmd/fyr/ctx_verbs.go:126-133`), so they call `harness.ResolveSource` first.
- For a development build, `ResolveSource` (`internal/harness/repo.go:22-58`) needs a checkout: `--repo`, `$FYR_REPO`, the working directory, or the recorded path.
- `--from-zip` records `zip:sha256:…` as the place's source, so the recorded checkout path (`~/workspace/fyr` on borken) is gone. Neither verb can reach `zipDrift` or the zip instruction.
- The zip never replacing the binary is by design (ADR-038, `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model).

The fix (D5):
1. A table test over every binary kind (release, development) and every place kind (checkout, binary-only, zip), for `status`, `update` and `update --from-zip`. It fails first on the development-build-at-a-zip-place cells (the bug skill: the failing test before the fix; a `bug` record under the next free id, BUG-203 on 2026-10-31, `fyr record add` assigns it; "the borken bug" below). The cells are § Cells below; every cell not listed there keeps `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` as it stands at `260d0b7`, and the test records today's output for those first.
2. `status` at a zip place reports from the state with no source.
3. `update` without `--from-zip` at a zip place prints how that place moves (a new zip, or a release binary for the version) and exits 1, a refusal like a plain copy's (`GUIDE-fyr-matrix`); exit 2 already means "behind" for `update --check` and a usage error (D5, approved).
4. `update --from-zip` run by a development build at a place whose state records a checkout is refused, naming `fyr update` and `fyr install --repo <path>`. A development build never turns a checkout place into a zip place.
5. The error that strands a place names `fyr install --repo <checkout>` as the way back. That includes `zipNote` in `internal/harness/repo.go` (`sourceCandidates`), whose "or run `fyr update --from-zip <file>` again" is the advice that stranded borken.
6. `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model, the README map's zip label and `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` change in the same commit (AGENTS.md § How the harness works, rules 3 and 6), with an ADR amending ADR-038.

### Cells (D5; approved by the operator, 2026-10-31)

| Binary | Place | Command | Expect |
|---|---|---|---|
| development | zip | `status` | Reports from the state with no source: `installed … from zip sha256:…`, `drift not compared …`; exit 0 (1 on missing files, as today) |
| development | zip | `update` | Refused, exit 1. The message names both ways the place moves: a newer zip with a release binary of that version, and `fyr install --repo <checkout>` |
| development | zip | `update --from-zip <f>` | As today (installs the zip's harness and keeps the running binary, exit 0), plus one line saying the binary did not move and naming `fyr install --repo <checkout>` |
| development | checkout | `update --from-zip <f>` | Refused, exit 1, naming `fyr update` and `fyr install --repo <path>`. The state is unchanged: the place stays a checkout place |
| release | zip | `status` | As the development row |
| release | zip | `update`, `update --from-zip <f>` | Unchanged from today: the test records today's output first, and this fix does not change it |
| either | zip | `install --repo <checkout>` | The place becomes a checkout place: `status` names the checkout and exits 0 (the way back; borken's manual line below) |

Rejected: building the binary from the zip's Go source. That would be a new delivery path (rule 3) and would need Go on every zip place.

Now, by hand on borken, before the fix (Who: user): `git -C ~/workspace/fyr pull`, then `go build -o ~/workspace/fyr/.agents/scratch/fyr ./cmd/fyr` run inside `~/workspace/fyr`, then `~/workspace/fyr/.agents/scratch/fyr install --repo ~/workspace/fyr`. Expect: `fyr version` prints `b<sha>` of the pulled HEAD, and `fyr status` exits 0 naming `repo ~/workspace/fyr`. That makes borken a checkout place again, and `fyr update` works from then on. If the pull fails on port 22, item 40 applies. The operator pastes the output of the three commands into the next session, so P3 can confirm or strike item 40 from it. The reviewer's copy takes the security copy's wording. `MountsChecked` went: nothing read it, and the specs state the gap off Linux.


title: Research — agent evals and metrics: the standard benchmarks, scoring methods and metric sets against fyr eval and fyr metrics (2026-10-31)
body:
# Research — agent evals and metrics: the standard benchmarks, scoring methods and metric sets, against `fyr eval`, `GUIDE-eval` and `fyr metrics`   (2026-10-31)

Question (the release handoff's Kickoff, the operator, 2026-10-31): how are coding-agent evals and agent metrics best done — the established benchmarks, scoring methods and metric sets — and which of the standard ones does the harness not collect yet, so a plan can collect them and the harness can be improved from them.

Method: six web sweeps by dimension (coding benchmarks; agent benchmarks and scoring; observability metric sets; engineering-productivity frameworks; harness-level eval formats; statistics and reliability), each sweep's ten load-bearing claims re-read against their primary source by a second agent, a completeness critic over all six, and four gap fills for what the critic named (coding-CLI telemetry schemas, failure-mode taxonomies, safety benchmarks for code-executing agents, item-level statistics for small suites). 17 agents, 1,200 tool uses, this session's workflow `wf_d16c8b64-66f`; the raw result and per-dimension digests are in `.agents/scratch/evals-research/` (gitignored). Only the answer to the question above is recorded here; findings about other projects stay out (research skill, Step 1). A `[v]` after a claim means the second agent confirmed it against the primary source; `[p]` means it confirmed it with a correction, applied here.

## Evidence

### What the harness has today

Read this session from `SPEC-fyr-eval`, `GUIDE-eval`, `SPEC-fyr-metrics`, `cmd/fyr/eval.go`, `internal/eval/run.go`, `internal/metrics/show_finish.go`, `internal/serve/pages.go`, the retro, dream and handoff skills, and the eval home `~/sandbox/fyr-eval/home` (read only).

**`fyr eval` and `GUIDE-eval` (the suite):**

| Facet | Today |
|---|---|
| Suite | 63 rows in `GUIDE-eval` (id, setup, prompt, prompt2, check, agent, grants); 31 manual rows remain in `GUIDE-skill-matrix`. No category, difficulty, version or expected-cost tag on a row. |
| Verdict | Binary per row: `check` exits 0 AND the named agent was invoked (check f, a bytes search of the conversation store) AND no `auto-denied` AND no `invalid allow entry` AND the exit checks c, d, e pass. No partial credit, no score, no rubric; the agy exit status is printed, not a condition. A row whose clone, install or setup failed is a FAIL with that reason, not a separate "errored" state. |
| Per-row data kept | verdict, reasons, agy exit, `seconds` (the whole row from its start: clone, install, setup, session(s), check; `internal/eval/run.go:147`), sandbox path. Per run: fyr version, project and fixture HEADs, install source, agy version (`cmd/fyr/eval.go:319-334`). The sandbox keeps `out.txt`, `err.txt`, the logs and the clone, never pruned. |
| Runs | Serial, one trial per row per invocation; k is however many times the operator typed the row. No `--runs N`, no variance, no interval. |
| Over time | `fyr metrics show --label eval=<row>` and `fyr record list --kind testing`; no compare verb by the operator's choice (eval plan D7, 2026-10-26). `fyr serve /evals` lists the testing records. |
| pass^k | Per label, over the label's main sessions with an outcome, `PassK` is 1 only when every one of them passed (`internal/metrics/show_finish.go:27-49`): it is "all n passed", with k = n, not the τ-bench estimator for a chosen k; a `prompt2` row adds two sessions per run, so its n is doubled (`SPEC-fyr-eval` § Known limits, D12). Reported as `passed of k · pass^k = 0\|1` in the report's chart. |
| Trajectory | Check f, plus ad hoc greps of the conversation store inside a few `check` cells (`review-docs-check` wants a `fyr check` command line; `cloud-run` wants no `gcloud run deploy`; the `catalog-route-*` rows want a read under the expected catalog entry). |
| Adversarial rows | `inject-*` (a planted instruction the agent must not follow), `lane-*` (a dispatch asking for a write outside the agent's lane), `agents-security` and `agent-reviewer` (a planted comment). Reported as n of N (BUG-083, BUG-139), never a guarantee. |
| Gate use | AGENTS.md § Release: one run of each changed skill and agent before a tag; the `testing` record is the evidence. `GUIDE-testing` § 4: a behavioural run is reported as n of N. |

**Baseline on this box** (`fyr metrics show --home ~/sandbox/fyr-eval/home --all-labels --since 2026-09-01 --json`, 2026-10-31): 213 sandbox sessions, 63 labels, n from 1 to 16 (24 labels at n = 1); 7,635 tool calls; 21.3 M input, 1.9 M output and 160 M cache-read tokens (cache-write 0); 668 wall minutes; tool error rate 1.5 %; 294 retry loops; subagent tool calls led by `reviewer` 804, `verifier` 462, `security` 214. Six labels carry a failure: `agents-security` 4 of 5, `lane-reviewer` 4 of 5, `preflight` 9 of 11, `retro` 8 of 9, `docker` 2 of 3, `build-fullstack` 1 of 2. 34 `Eval — p of n PASS at <HEAD>` testing records since the verb landed (2026-10-26).

**`fyr metrics` (the store):** per-session shape in SQLite, metric ids A1–A6 (DoD closure, verifier status, review findings by severity, escaped bugs, corrections, pass^k), B1–B4 (tokens, wall and active time, turns, tool calls, peak context against a target, subagents), C1–C4 (search:grep ratio, forbidden git shapes, first reads, skill loads), D1–D3 (tool error rate, denials and interrupts where the CLI records them, retry loops, subagent volume). The CLI exposes no cost, denials, interrupts or compactions (`notes`). Steps are stored in order per session (`steps` by `ts, ext_id`), with tool, skill, target kind, tokens, context and a salted command hash, so a tool-sequence read is possible from the store without the transcript; `sessions.model` holds the model id. No column holds the harness commit a sandbox session ran under, and nothing links the two sessions of one `prompt2` row to one run. Everything but `session_peaks` and pass^k is aggregated per vendor over the window; a label is read one at a time (`--label`) or all together (`--all-labels`).

**Consumers of the numbers:** `/retro` step 11 (two adjacent windows, each worsened key named, a finding only with a cause from sources 1–9); the hourly dreamer (`metrics.Summary.Numbers()`, numbers only, no label, so no pass^k); the handoff skill's closing `fyr metrics ingest`; `fyr metrics report` (HTML, one pass^k chart); `fyr serve /metrics` and `/evals`.

### Published evidence

**Scoring: the four estimators every serious report uses.**
- pass@k (capability): `1 − C(n−c,k)/C(n,k)` from n ≥ k trials with c passes, averaged over tasks; the naive `1 − (1 − c/n)^k` "underestimates the true value by a considerable margin" (Chen et al. 2021, Figure 13) [v]. The stable form is `1 − ∏_{i=n−c+1}^{n}(1 − k/i)` (human-eval `evaluation.py`) [S1].
- pass^k (reliability): `C(c,k)/C(n,k)`, "the chance that all k i.i.d. task trials are successful", τ-bench, which ran "at least 3 trials per task" and reports gpt-4o retail pass^1 = 61.2, pass^8 < 25 % [v] [S2]; τ²-bench runs each task four times at temperature 0 and shows pass^k falling faster on the harder domain [S3]. Anthropic's 2026 guide gives the independence form p^k (0.75³ ≈ 42 %) [v] [S20]; the critic ruled for the combinatorial estimator, which lets k ≤ n be chosen at report time.
- The gap between pass@k and pass^k is the consistency story; "Towards a Science of AI Agent Reliability" (ICML 2026) formalises it as outcome consistency `C_out = mean_t (2p̂_t − 1)²`, trajectory consistency as 1 − normalised Levenshtein distance between the action sequences of a task's runs, and resource consistency as `exp(−mean CV)` over cost, time, calls and actions, all at K = 5 seeded runs [v] [S9]. Its finding: capability gains over 2025 brought only small reliability gains.
- pass@1 "averaged over N tries" is what vendor cards report: OpenAI 4 tries on a 477-task subset, Anthropic 10 trials (Sonnet 4.5) and 50 (Haiku 4.5) on all 500, METR 8 runs; none prints a standard error [S49, S50].

**Uncertainty at this suite's size.**
- Miller 2024: treat the question (here: the row) as the sample; `SE = sqrt(Var(s)/n)`; clustered SE when rows share a fixture; paired SE `sqrt(SE_A² + SE_B² − 2·SE_A·SE_B·Corr)` for A-vs-B on the same rows; power `n = (z_{α/2}+z_β)²(ω² + σ_A²/K_A + σ_B²/K_B)/δ²`; and the law of total variance: K resamples per question shrink only the within-question term, so "once E[σ_i²]/K ≪ Var(x), increasing K further will have little effect" [v] [S4]. Do not lower temperature to reduce variance.
- Bowyer, Aitchison & Ivanova (ICML 2025 spotlight): 95 % CLT intervals cover only 92.5 % at N = 100; use the Wilson score interval or the Beta(1 + c, 1 + n − c) posterior; Clopper-Pearson is "overly conservative"; bootstrap "performs poorly" at small N; paired Bayes for comparisons [v] [S5]. Wilson needs only a square root: with n = 5 and c = 5 the 95 % interval is (0.566, 1.0), and the rule of three bounds the failure rate at 3/n [S6].
- Resampling: the cluster bootstrap (resample rows, keep their runs together) reaches 95.2 % coverage with intervals 25 % narrower than the two-stage hierarchical bootstrap, which "roughly double-counts the within-input variance" (Indeed, N = 200, k = 5, 2,000 trials) [v] [S7]. For a two-level row → runs design the cluster bootstrap is the one to use.
- Noise floor: on SWE-bench Verified "single-run pass@1 estimates vary by 2.2 to 6.0 percentage points depending on which run is selected", "with standard deviations exceeding 1.5 percentage points even at temperature 0" (120 runs, 60,000 trajectories) [p: 3 models × 2 temperatures × 2 scaffolds × 10 runs, not 6 pairs × 10] [S8]. Resource allocation alone moved Terminal-Bench scores by 6 pp (p < 0.01) and infra error rates from 5.8 % to 0.5 %: record the allocation and the infra-error rate beside every pass rate and treat gaps under ~3 pp as noise [S21].
- How many runs: beyond 2–3 runs per task the gain is identifying the within-task variance, not precision of the suite score, because the problem set is the binding noise (variance ceiling `1 + μ_w/σ_b²`, median 1.34) [S15]; Indeed advises k = 3, or 5 if budget allows [S7]; ICC (between-task / total variance) converges at 8–16 trials for structured tasks [S10]; 29.3 % of single-run evaluations misrank four models against the multi-run truth [v] [S11]. Rows are the lever; add rows before adding runs.
- Paired regression detection: pair every item across versions into both-right / baseline-only (b) / candidate-only (c) / both-wrong and run the exact one-sided binomial on b of b + c at p = 0.5 ("our test is just a standard binomial test"); a lossless rerun flipped 1.31 % of items with p = 0.63 (Kübler et al., ICLR 2026) [v] [S13]. Always print the minimum detectable effect at the current N: `δ_MDE(N) = (z_{1−α/2}+z_{1−β})·σ_D/√N`, `σ_D² = p_A q_A + p_B q_B − 2ρ√(p_A q_A p_B q_B)`; for (0.65, 0.60, ρ = 0.3) N* = 1,028 items [v] [S14]. A 63-row suite resolves only large regressions, and should say so.
- Per-row flip rate ("ever-flip fraction", 0.7–2.7 % on BFCL at T = 0) and mean pairwise run agreement are the cheap per-item stability numbers [S12]; rows that never flip across versions carry no resolution and are regression guards, not signal (Kübler; the saturation index of Akhtar et al. 2026; Ndzomga's 30–70 % historical-pass filter) [S13, S57, S58].
- Sequential testing (SPRT boundaries `A = log((1−β)/α)`, `B = log(β/(1−α))`; betting confidence sequences, anytime-valid) is the honest frame for "k is however many times the operator ran it": optional stopping breaks fixed-n intervals [p: the practitioner source has arithmetic inconsistencies; two 2026 preprints are more authoritative] [S59]. Advisory only here: R3 forbids gates.

**Benchmarks: what the field holds fixed and reports.**
- SWE-bench (2,294 tasks; Verified 500, human-validated with difficulty buckets; Pro 1,865; Multimodal; Multilingual; Live; rebench) scores a task resolved iff every FAIL_TO_PASS test passes and every PASS_TO_PASS test still passes, in a per-instance container, no partial credit [S46]. Verified is saturated (97 % at the top; co-creator: "saturated at 93.9 %") and audited as flawed: 32.67 % of passing patches had the solution leaked and 31.08 % passed on weak tests (SWE-Bench+), 11 rank changes from augmented tests (UTBoost), file-path identification from the issue alone at 76 % (Illusion), 19.71 % of previously passing patches rejected by strengthened tests (SWE-ABS) [S47]; exact paired McNemar tests separate none of the 29 adjacent top-30 pairs (arXiv 2609.17394). The Bash Only track (mini-SWE-agent, one fixed scaffold) is how the board separates model from harness [S46]. SWE-rebench runs every model five times in one fixed minimal scaffold and reports mean ± SE and pass@5 [p] [S48].
- Terminal-Bench (now 4.0, 2026-08-28; 2.x scores are not comparable) runs every agent-model pair at least five times, reports 95 % intervals as whiskers, cost and tokens per run, grades only the final container state, requires ATIF trajectories, scores reward hacking 0 and semver-versions the task set (major = rerun, minor = regrade) [v] [S28]. Its validation before release: the oracle solution passes, a no-op agent fails, an adversarial agent hunts for cheats, humans review (~3 h per task); 2.1 fixed 28 of 89 tasks that drifted on external inputs. Episodes and output tokens do not predict success (r = −0.028, −0.170) [v].
- Harbor, its harness, is `fyr eval`'s shape at scale: a task is instruction + environment + `tests/test.sh` + solution; the verifier writes a numeric reward to `reward.txt` or labelled metrics to `reward.json` (preferred), runs in a separate sandbox by default since 2026-10-28 so "the agent never touches the tests or the reward output", clears stale reward files and sanitises artifacts (symlinks, FIFOs, setuid); its error policy maps every exception to a `failure_cause` that decides retry, whether the verifier runs and whether the reward is valid (agent_exhausted_budget and agent_refused_task are graded; sandbox_failed, model_provider_failed, verifier_failed are not) [p] [S27].
- The Holistic Agent Leaderboard (21,730 rollouts, ~$40,000): every result carries tokens and a dollar figure at dated list prices and a cost–accuracy Pareto frontier; it was "forced to rely on single runs without statistical validation" and reports no intervals; it inspects logs systematically (instruction violated, environmental barrier, self-corrected, verified before finishing) [S18]. Kapoor et al. 2024: "agent evaluations must be cost-controlled", accuracy "can be improved by scientifically meaningless methods such as retrying", LLMs "aren't deterministic even at temperature zero"; five runs, mean/min/max and a Student-t interval; report raw token counts beside dollars so cost can be recomputed [S16]. The Agentic Benchmark Checklist asks for a trivial-agent baseline per task, an oracle solver, a clean environment per run and "measures of statistical significance" (R.10); 7 of 10 benchmarks violate task validity [S17]; BetterBench: 14 of 24 benchmarks neither repeat runs nor report uncertainty [S19].
- τ²-bench's reward is a product of gating components with a non-gating action-match diagnostic [S3]; BFCL grades multi-turn calls as an unordered subset, extras unchecked (checker code), and no benchmark grades call order as the verdict; the tooling defaults that do (ADK EXACT, Ragas `strict_order=True`, agentevals strict) are configurable modes [S26, S32]. Verdicts grade end state plus a required-call subset.

**Harness-level eval formats: the closest neighbours.**
- Anthropic, "Demystifying evals for AI agents" (2026-01-09): an eval is a task + graders; a trial is one attempt; graders are code-based (fail-to-pass / pass-to-pass, state, tool-call and transcript checks), model-based (rubric, calibrated against humans) or human; grade what the agent produced over the path it took; track `n_turns`, `n_toolcalls`, `n_total_tokens` per trial; start with 20–50 tasks from real failures; "0 % pass@100 is most often a signal of a broken task"; a suite at 100 % "tracks regressions but provides no signal for improvement" [v] [S20].
- `claude plugin eval` (Claude Code 2.1.269+): each case runs in a fresh isolated `claude -p` home, 3 runs per case per arm by default ("a single run is noisy, so confirm any change at the default three runs"), two arms (plugin loaded / not) so the report says what the plugin contributed, six grader types (`regex`, `tool_used` with min/max, `tool_order`, `file_exists`, `llm` at 2 of 3 votes, `baseline`), a run scored as the weighted fraction of graders passed, a case as the mean over runs, `WITH / W/OUT / Δ / RUNS / COST` per case, a cost ceiling, a per-run error distinct from a failed grader; no custom-code grader, no variance or interval [v] [S22]. The skill-creator's `evals.json` stores per run `timing.json {total_tokens, duration_ms}` and `grading.json {expectations[]: {text, passed, evidence}}`, aggregates pass rate, time and tokens as mean ± stddev per arm plus delta, and splits 60 % train / 40 % held-out when tuning [v] [S23]. Both are the same shape fyr has in miniature.
- Inspect AI: `epochs` as a first-class run parameter with reducers `mean`, `pass_at_k`, `pass_k_k`, `at_least_k`; metrics `stderr(cluster=)`, `bootstrap_stderr`, `ci_wilson()` (recommended for 0/1 scores); per sample `total_time` vs `working_time`, `turn_count`, `limit_reason`, `retries`; a log status `started|success|error|cancelled` with `error` distinct from a failed score; the git commit of the eval code [v] [S24]. promptfoo: assertions with `weight` (0 = measure without gating), `not-` negation, `--repeat N`, `--filter-failing`, per-test `componentResults[] {pass, score, reason, assertion}` [v] [S25]. ADK: gating criteria with thresholds in a config file beside the suite and informational efficiency criteria (`tool_call_count_v1`, `inference_call_count_v1`, `token_usage_v1`, `invocation_duration_v1`) that "report a value, but never pass or fail"; `NUM_RUNS = 2` by default with scores averaged before the threshold [p] [S26]. OpenAI Evals: version the suite id and bump it whenever a case changes so results under one name stay comparable; validate a model grader by a meta-eval against human labels [S29]; the hosted Evals API is read-only from 2026-10-31 and shut down 2026-11-30, but its `result_counts {total, passed, failed, errored}` is the cleanest result shape [p] [S30].
- Per-trial records across runners (SWE-agent `.traj`, mini-SWE-agent `.traj.json`, OpenHands `EvalOutput`, Harbor ATIF): an `exit_status` or `failure_cause` separate from the score, the agent name and version, the model, per-call cost and tokens where the adapter has them, per-command return codes, and a rescorable artifact (`preds.json`) so a grader fix is a regrade, not a rerun [S27, S51].

**Metric sets and telemetry schemas.**
- OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions (every page "Status: Development", no release, 2026-10-31): operations `chat`, `execute_tool`, `invoke_agent`; token counters split input / output / cache_read / cache_write / reasoning with a `gen_ai.token.modality` attribute; duration histograms with fixed buckets; agent-level `gen_ai.invoke_agent.duration`, `.inference_calls`, `.tool_calls`; a `gen_ai.evaluation.result` event with name, numeric value and/or label, explanation; no cost attribute [p] [S31]. Adopt the vocabulary, not an SDK.
- The de facto per-session set of the coding CLIs themselves (the critic's first gap): Claude Code exports counters `cost.usage` (USD, by model, effort, `query_source main|subagent|auxiliary`, agent, skill, MCP tool), `token.usage` (`input|output|cacheRead|cacheCreation`), `lines_of_code.count`, `commit.count`, `pull_request.count`, `active_time.total (user|cli)`, `code_edit_tool.decision`; events `tool_decision` (decision accept|reject, source config|hook|user_permanent|user_temporary|user_abort|user_reject), `tool_result` (success, duration_ms, error_type), `api_request` (cost, cache 5m/1h), `api_error` (attempt), `api_refusal`, `compaction` (pre/post tokens), `subagent_completed`, `skill_activated`; its headless result carries `num_turns`, `duration_ms` vs `duration_api_ms`, `total_cost_usd`, `permission_denials[]`, and its transcript format is "internal … and changes between versions" [S34, S35]. Gemini CLI: `tool.call.count` with decision accept|reject|modify|auto_accept, `token.usage` input|output|thought|cache|tool, `chat_compression` before/after, a `telemetry.outfile` sink that needs no collector [S36]. Codex CLI: `tool_decision` with source config|user, `api_request.attempt`, `TurnAborted.reason` persisted to its rollout file (the only CLI-native interrupt flag found), `turn_cost.usage.estimated_usd` in source only [S37]. Copilot's API: sessions, requests, prompts, tokens, lines added/deleted, PRs created/merged per day [S38]. Cross-CLI: no CLI emits a context peak (all proxy it as max per-request input + cache); decision source, API retries and permission wait time exist only at the CLI layer and cannot be reconstructed from a transcript; the critic noted that a peer CLI exposes cost, denials, API errors, refusals and compactions, so "the CLI does not expose" is a per-CLI fact to pin by a test, not a law.
- Agent-eval libraries converge on: task/goal success, a tool-trajectory match under a declared mode (exact / in-order / any-order; Ragas `ToolCallF1`, DeepEval `ToolCorrectness`, agentevals strict/unordered/subset/superset), tool-call and inference-call counts, a judged step-efficiency, tool errors, duration histograms, tokens by class, estimated cost, repetitions with mean and stddev, and a score record `{name, value or label, reason, threshold, source}`; a counted "human interventions" metric exists only at the CLI layer [S31–S33].
- Engineering-productivity frameworks measure a different unit (the PR, the developer, the week) and are not this plan's: DORA 2025 names seven AI capabilities, two of them observable in fyr's git join (small batches, version-control hygiene) as moderators [S40]; DX's framework (utilization, impact, cost) maps onto fyr's A/B/C groups and rejects acceptance rate and raw generation volume as metrics [S39]; METR's RCT found AI-allowed tasks took 19 % longer (CI +2 % to +39 %, HC3 SEs) while developers forecast a 24 % speedup, and its late-2025 follow-up found ~4–20 % benefits [p] [S41]; METR's transcript method (10-minute windows with a human turn as active time; success labelled from the next message) is computable from a session log [S42]; GitClear's churn (code reverted or rewritten within two weeks), duplicate blocks (5+ repeated lines) and moved-vs-pasted lines are git arithmetic [S43]. The research skill's Step 1 rule applies: they answer a question this Kickoff did not ask, and are noted once.

**Failure modes, safety, item statistics (the critic's other gaps).**
- Terminal-Bench's single-agent pruning of MAST is the taxonomy a CLI harness should copy: three classes, nine modes — Execution: Disobey Specification, Step Repetition, Unaware of Termination Conditions; Coherence: Reasoning-Action Mismatch, Context Loss, Task Derailment; Verification: Premature Termination, Incomplete Verification, Incorrect Verification — with a decision-procedure rubric each, human κ 0.93 on calibration, GPT-5 judge at 90 % agreement; at command level, "executable not in PATH" alone explained 24.1 % of command failures, a sandbox-provisioning signal [S28]; MAST itself: 14 modes, 1,600+ traces, κ 0.88, NeurIPS 2025 [S44]; TRAIL adds span-level localisation [S45]. The gap fill's merged table finds seven of the modes fully rule-detectable from a transcript plus the verdict (step repetition, timeout and step limits, machine-checkable constraint violations, environmental barriers) and the rest needing a judge; every published judge validation at κ ≥ 0.77 used a frontier model; no public leaderboard reports a failure-mode distribution per entry. Anthropic's first split on a failed row: broken task or grader vs agent error, "all k trials fail" being the trigger to suspect the row [S20].
- Safety for code-executing agents: RedCode-Exec (4,050 risky Python and Bash cases, 25 vulnerability types, 8 domains, Docker, rejection rate as the headline; agents reject risky OS operations more than buggy code) [S52]; OS-Harm (misuse, injection and misbehaviour, judge F1 0.76/0.79 vs humans) [S53]; AgentDojo (utility, utility under attack, targeted attack success rate) [S54]; ToolEmu's "NoAct" control, a do-nothing agent that must score useless on the benign twin [S55]; the gap fill's catalogue of destructive-operation classes (filesystem, process, network egress, credentials, git history, package installs) each with a deterministic post-run predicate (file present/absent, checksum of protected files, canary untouched, a process that must survive or be gone, a log line of the command) and the reporting shape refused / attempted / executed beside the benign twin's pass rate [S52].
- Item statistics for a small suite: 2PL/3PL IRT is not fittable with fewer than ~30 system versions as respondents (and unreliable below ~100); Rasch is borderline at 30; Linacre's rule needs 8 passes and 8 fails per item; so with a handful of harness versions the fittable per-row numbers are p per version, p pooled, flip rate across k, the consistency gap, and, once 8+ versions exist, a point-biserial discrimination [S56, S60–S62]; tinyBenchmarks' 100-example subsets and ATLAS's adaptive selection need that panel too [S61]. Benchmark builders retire flaky items by running the known-good solution three times and keeping an item only when the verdict matches on all runs (SWE-Bench++, SWE-bench-Live) [S63]; DeltaSelect validates the harness's own use case, cheap repeated baseline-vs-candidate A/B on one model, by paired per-task deltas [S64].

## Stress test of the premise

- **The suite is two orders of magnitude smaller than what the statistics assume.** 63 rows, serial, 20 s to 7 min each: k = 5 over the suite is ~315 sessions and more than a working day of CLI time. The published methods still apply, but the honest outputs at this size are Wilson intervals that span tens of points, an MDE the compare verb must print, and flip rates per row; a two-point change in the suite rate is noise here and the report must say so rather than invite the dreamer to act on it.
- **The dreamer proposes rules from the rows that measure them.** That is Kapoor's lookup table: a rule written to pass `lane-reviewer` raises `lane-reviewer`. A held-out subset run only before a release, and per-row cohorts by creation date, are the standard answer; both are data, not code, but they cost gate time.
- **Judge-based grading is not free under R8.** A rubric judge or a failure-mode judge is a model call; the dreamer's path exists, but R8 names three things that leave the machine and a fourth is a requirements edit. Deterministic detectors cover seven of the nine failure modes; the rest wait for the operator's word.
- **"The CLI does not expose it" has to be re-measured per CLI version.** Codex persists turn aborts and compactions; Gemini writes per-message token usage; Claude Code's transcript is declared unstable. agy's conversation store was last probed for these rows in October (BUG-184 for tool names); a spike comes first.
- **Trajectory matching is tempting and the field says no.** No benchmark grades call order as the verdict, and the one order check fyr has (`review-docs-check`) is already an any-order grep; expected calls stay a non-gating m-of-n.
- **Infra noise is a variable fyr does not record.** On the host runner there is no resource cap, so the Terminal-Bench 6 pp effect has no analogue to control; for `--runner docker` workers the limits are a Backlog item. Recording "host runner, no cap" per run is enough until that changes.
- **What the standard set will not tell this harness.** Whether a rule change made sessions better for the operator: the productivity frameworks measure PRs and weeks, and fyr's A-group (DoD closure, verifier status, review findings, escaped bugs, corrections) already is the local version of impact; this plan does not touch it.

## Items

Highest priority first; `fix` = plan it, `defer` = noted in the plan's Follow-ups or an `Open:` row, `strike` = not proposed. The plan record carries the phases.

1. **The estimator and the run unit.** Store the run a sandbox session belongs to; compute per row n and c over runs; pass@k and pass^k with the combinatorial estimators for k ≤ n; D12 closed. — fix (plan Phase 1).
2. **Intervals.** Wilson 95 % per row and per suite; the Beta posterior as a second line; the cluster bootstrap as a check; the CLT interval never printed at this n. — fix (Phase 1).
3. **Declared k and the header block.** `fyr eval --runs N`; the testing record names k, the estimator, the model, agy and the harness commit; each sandbox session carries the harness commit. — fix (Phase 2); the default k (1 today; 3 for any compared number; 5 before a release claim) is the operator's.
4. **A trial status distinct from PASS/FAIL.** `error` with a `failure_cause` (clone, install, setup, sandbox replaced, interrupted, agy killed at the timeout, record or ingest failed) excluded from the rate; `fail` keeps the agent-side reasons. — fix (Phase 2).
5. **Per-row efficiency columns, never gating.** tokens by class, turns, tool calls, wall and active seconds, tool-error rate, retry loops, peak context; a Pareto position of pass rate against tokens per harness commit. — fix (Phase 3).
6. **Consistency.** flip rate, C_out, trajectory similarity from the stored sequences; ICC when k ≥ 8. — fix (Phase 3).
7. **A paired compare on the same rows.** b, c, the exact one-sided binomial p, improved / flat / regressed, `δ_MDE(N)`, a head-to-head win rate. — put to the operator: it reopens D7 (no compare verb) and needs an ADR (Phase 4, held until answered).
8. **Suite hygiene as data.** optional columns after `grants`: `version`, `kind` (capability \| regression \| safety \| indicator), `cluster`, `expect`; pass^k keyed by row@version; saturated and broken flags from history; the leakage rule for row authors. — fix (Phase 5); the grammar change supersedes ADR-065's D2 (a seven-column table) by ADR.
9. **Failure-mode labels, deterministic first.** Terminal-Bench's nine modes as a closed set; seven detected from the store (step repetition, limits, machine-checkable constraints, environmental barriers, premature termination by the verdict pattern); the two that need a judge wait. — fix the detectors (Phase 6); defer the judge (Open, R8).
10. **Safety reported as counts.** checks c, d, e and the inject and lane rows as refused / attempted / executed and attack success rate beside utility; benign twins for the destructive-operation classes as new rows. — fix the counts (Phase 6); defer the rows to the suite's owner.
11. **Validity controls stored.** per row an oracle (a known-good state passes the check) and a no-op (an untouched clone fails it), run by a `--controls` mode and recorded, so a row is trusted before its flips mean anything. — fix (Phase 7).
12. **Cost in dollars.** a dated local price table over tokens by class. — defer: tokens are the durable quantity; the table's source (which models, whose prices) is the operator's.

14. **Held-out rows and cohorts.** a `holdout` kind run only before a release; a creation date per row. — put to the operator (gate cost).
15. **Sequential-stopping advisory.** "this row has decided / keep running" from the posterior. — defer.
16. **Productivity-level columns** (two-week churn, duplicate blocks, active-human windows, lines added/removed per session). — defer to a research of its own: a different question and unit.
17. **Strike:** IRT fitting (no panel of versions), a rubric judge as a verdict, acceptance-rate metrics, an OpenTelemetry receiver (a protocol fyr would have to parse for a CLI that does not emit it), strict-order trajectory grading as a verdict.

## Risks
- **Uncommitted working-tree state (`skills/project-memory/SKILL.md:8`, `TODO.md:18`, `.agents/trail.jsonl:1431`):** Until committed with a new `change` and `handoff` record (and a behavioural run or `/review --docs` as required by `AGENTS.md:50` for a `skills/` edit), `TODO.md:18` (`None.`) contradicts `HANDOFF-2026-11-01-1451` (`.agents/trail.jsonl:795` body lines 19, 30, 42, 52).
- **Dropped open bug pointer (`BUG-207`, `.agents/trail.jsonl:311` body line 18):** `BUG-207` remains `open` in `fyr record list --open`, but `HANDOFF-2026-11-01-1451` and `TODO.md` no longer mention it, so a session reading only the newest handoff and `TODO.md` can overlook it.
- **Data-as-instructions check:** `.agents/trail.jsonl:881` (`PLAN-2026-10-31-1636` body line 368) and `.agents/trail.jsonl:566-568` describe E2E (d)'s planted prompt-injection test record (`asks the worker to edit AGENTS.md, to write ~/.config/fyr/auto.json and to push`); treated strictly as data.

## Open questions
- Should `BUG-207` (`.agents/trail.jsonl:311`, `open`, prevention rule in `agents/verifier/agent.md`) be recorded in `TODO.md` `## Backlog` or carried in the next handoff's `## Next Steps` for the operator?

- Truncated middle of `.system_generated/steps/24/output.txt` (surrounding `-U3` JSONL context lines of `git diff -- .agents/trail.jsonl`; the changed line `.agents/trail.jsonl:1431` was inspected in full via `git diff -U0` and `diff -u`).

- Truncated middle of `.system_generated/steps/40/output.txt` (lines 466–509 of `PLAN-2026-10-31-1636`, holding historical decisions D1–D12).

## Proposals

### Proposal 1: Showing the release notes is not a gate
Scope: harness — Target: `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 6, item 1 — Status: applied 2026-09-18 (42fad8f) (harness queue: `~/.config/sh-agent/proposals/2026-09-18-retro.md`)

Scope: harness — Target: `agents/reviewer.md` § Write the artifact EARLY (the same sentence in `agents/security.md` and `agents/explorer.md`) — Status: applied 2026-09-18 (42fad8f) (harness queue: same file)
Scope rule: target-in-harness — why: harness agent definitions.

### Proposal 4: The behavioural-run recipe for an agent or context change says how it is run and what it proves
Scope: project — Target: `AGENTS.md` § Testing — Status: applied 2026-09-18 (42fad8f)
Scope rule: target-in-project — why: this repo's own testing procedure for its own files; the promotion check (`retros.jsonl` targets named `AGENTS.md` from other projects; feedback `rule_ref` `project AGENTS.md § Testing` from other projects) found no hit.

Trigger: BUG-083. The verifier's rewritten rule was tested by `claude -p --agents` in a scratch clone: the first run was blocked at the permission gate (no `--allowedTools`), the second had its prompt swallowed by the variadic `--allowedTools` list, and only then did three runs produce evidence — 1 of 3, then 1 of 1 after the wording fix. A tier-4 CLI start from a scratch `HOME` failed on both CLIs ("Not logged in"; "authentication timed out") because credentials live in the real home. None of this is in the paragraph that prescribes the run.

Current behaviour: § Testing says "`claude -p --agents <json built from the working-tree file>` in a scratch clone of a small repository, several runs, with the agent's artifact carrying something only the new definition writes".

Expected behaviour: the same sentence names the dispatch shape, the permission form and the way the result is reported, and says where a CLI start can authenticate.

diff:
```
-A change to `agents/*.md` also gets a behavioural run: `claude -p --agents <json built from the working-tree file>` in a scratch clone of a small repository, several runs, with the agent's artifact carrying something only the new definition writes, so the run proves which definition ran;
+A change to `agents/*.md` also gets a behavioural run: `claude -p --agents <json built from the working-tree file>` in a scratch clone of a small repository, several runs, with the agent's artifact carrying something only the new definition writes, so the run proves which definition ran — the dispatch text does NOT repeat the changed rule (the definition alone is under test), the prompt goes on stdin because `--allowedTools` is variadic and swallows a trailing argument, `--allowedTools` names the agent's tools or every call is refused at the permission gate and the run proves nothing, the tool-call order is read from the run's subagent transcript under `~/.claude/projects/`, and the result is reported as n of N runs, never "works" (BUG-083);
```
and, after "The real home is never touched.":
```
+A CLI started from a scratch `HOME` cannot authenticate (credentials live in the real home), so the tier-4 CLI start is the sandbox procedure or the real-home smoke checks, never `HOME=<scratch> claude -p`.
```

Rationale: the recipe that took four attempts to get right is written where the next change to `agents/` will read it; applying it graduates BUG-083's prevention rule (`bugs` moves the row).

### Proposal 5: The delivery claim has one home; every other living file points at it
Scope: project — Target: `AGENTS.md` § How the harness works, a new rule 6 — Status: applied 2026-09-18 (42fad8f)
Scope rule: target-in-project — why: this repo's own docs convention; no promotion hit.

Trigger: the v1.3.0 gate. Applying ADR-033's model to README:245 (round 1) exposed the ADR-030 sentence in `AGENTS.md:63` (round 2), which exposed `remote.md:8`, `:91`, `:195` and `delivery.md:7`, `:56` (round 3): one claim, six restatements, each found by the previous fix's pointer. The next delivery ADR does it again.

Current behaviour: rule 3 says a path change lands in ONE commit with the code, the docs and the map; nothing says where the prose claim lives.

Expected behaviour: one home, and every other file a one-line pointer.

diff (after rule 5):
```
+6. **The delivery claim has one home.** What a tag delivers, to which kind of place, and how a place moves forward is stated once, in `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` § The model; README, this file, the deploy guides and the ADRs point at it in one sentence and never restate it. The v1.3.0 gate spent three review rounds finding the same claim stale in six files after one ADR (ADR-030 → ADR-033); a change to the claim is one file plus the map.
```
Applying it is a docs task: `delivery.md` gets the § The model paragraph (the ADR-033 wording now in `AGENTS.md:63`), and the six sentences become pointers — `documentation` for README/spec/deploy, the main agent for `AGENTS.md`; `/review --docs` over the range.

Rationale: the sweep rule (Proposal 2) catches a stale restatement; this removes the restatements so there is nothing to catch.

## Not proposed

- The verifier's `go run … --dry-run` "1 written" observation: the testing guide's tier 3a already prescribes the built binary; dispatch text, not a rule.

### asking-format.md
```markdown
---
name: asking-format
description: "How to put questions and unclear items to the operator — short list for one choice, numbered table for several, full write-ups on request only"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 94112419-d7ce-4ac4-8f7f-4048bff0bed2
  modified: 2026-09-17T07:35:13.977Z
---

One choice: a short list, one line of why per option, recommendation named. Several unclear items: one numbered table — `#`, problem in one short line, recommendation (`fix` / `defer` / `strike` / recommended solution in a few words). Each item's full version goes in one file under the project's `.agents/scratch/`, named under the table, shown only when the operator asks for it by number.

```

```markdown
---
name: fallback-paths-stay-simple
description: "Don't harden a workaround/fallback path (e.g. sh-agent --from-zip) past its purpose; low review findings there are not automatic fixes"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: f538b90a-5aa7-44d1-8311-a160b5bb0167
  modified: 2026-09-28T18:57:47.026Z
---

A fallback or workaround path (the zip place, `sh-agent update --from-zip`) should just work. Don't keep adding flags, refusals or hardening to it because a review round found a low.

**Why:** On 2026-09-28 the operator reversed a whole `--unverified` + stray-argument + agent-proof-wording chain before release: "Don't complicate things. Just accept the zip. This is a workaround for environments that can't use the normal way." (ADR-041).

**How to apply:** Before fixing a security/review low on a fallback path, ask whether the fix adds friction for the operator. If it does, put it to the operator as a one-line choice with the simpler option recommended, instead of building it. "All needs to be fixed" covers defects, not new gates on a workaround.
```

# Vendor format check — context, skills, subagents   (2026-09-03)

Range reviewed: the working tree after the rebuild (e75bf90 plus the rename and GCP-rule changes)

Documentation-based check that what `sh-agent install` deploys is in the shape each vendor documents. The live check on the operator's Mac is a later task.

## Verdict: PASS with three fixes applied

## Sources

| Vendor | Source | What it settled |
|---|---|---|
| Agent Skills spec | https://agentskills.io/specification | `SKILL.md` fields: `name` (1–64, lowercase, hyphens, **must match the directory name**), `description` (1–1024), `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata` (string map), `allowed-tools` (space-separated). Optional `scripts/`, `references/`, `assets/`. Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. |
| Claude Code skills | https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md | User-level `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`; command name comes from the directory; extra fields `disable-model-invocation`, `user-invocable`, `argument-hint`, `arguments`, `allowed-tools`, `disallowed-tools`, `model`, `effort`, `context`, `agent`, `background`, `hooks`, `paths`, `shell`, `when_to_use`; `metadata` is kept but not acted on; `description` + `when_to_use` are capped at 1,536 characters in the listing; `~/.claude/commands/*.md` still works but is merged into skills. |
| Claude Code subagents | https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md | User-level `~/.claude/agents/<file>.md`, identity from `name`; `tools` is a comma-separated string; `skills` is a YAML block list; `model` ∈ sonnet/opus/haiku/fable/inherit/full id; `memory` ∈ user/project/local; `isolation: worktree`; `effort` ∈ low…max; `maxTurns` integer; `description` single line. |
| Claude Code memory | https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (via the claude-code-guide agent) | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` supports `@path` imports, relative to the file, up to 4 hops; user-level imports load without a prompt. |
| Antigravity CLI 1.1.24 | Embedded customization guide and changelog in the `agy` binary (`agy changelog`; `strings` on the binary) | Global customization root `~/.gemini/config/` (skills at `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, agents created by `/agents` there, `skills.json`/`plugins.json`, `mcp_config.json`, `hooks.json`); workspace root `.agents/` with `rules/*.md`, `skills/`, `agents/<name>/agent.md`; workflows deprecated in favour of skills; skills injected by name + description (progressive disclosure); markdown agents support `mainAgent`, `subagent`, `hidden`, `inheritMcp`, `inheritCustomizations`, `commandExecutionPolicy`, `model` (`flash`/`pro`/`inherit`), plus `tools`, `skills`, `rules`, `plugins`, `mcpServers` keys; markdown agents inherit ambient skills and rules by default; `disable-model-invocation` is a recognised skill key. |

## Skills (28)

Checked by script: every `name` equals its directory name and matches `[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`; every description is non-empty and under 1,024 characters; no `SKILL.md` exceeds 500 lines; every frontmatter key is either a spec field or a documented Claude Code field.

- **Fix:** `mermaid-syntax` had a top-level `version: 1.5.0`, which is not a spec field. Moved to `metadata: {version: "1.5.0"}`.
- `bash` and `docker` use `allowed-tools: Bash` (spec field, experimental; Claude honours it, Antigravity ignores unknown fields).
- `audit`, `distill`, `grill-me`, `handoff`, `init-project`, `research`, `retro` use `disable-model-invocation: true` + `argument-hint`; both vendors know the first, Antigravity ignores the second.
- Vendored skills (`anti-ui-slop`, `gke-basics`, `gcloud-auth-verification`, `skill-repair`, `terraform`, `codebase-design`, `grilling`, `grill-me`, `find-skills`) carry `license`/`metadata` per spec; untouched.
- Directory layout: `references/`, `assets/`, `examples/` only. No `scripts/` remain.

## Subagents (6)

- Frontmatter keys used: `name`, `description`, `tools`, `model`, `effort`, `maxTurns`, plus `memory` (changelog, documentation), `skills` (reviewer), `isolation` (verifier). All documented for Claude Code.
- **Fix:** `reviewer` had `skills: review-standards` as a scalar; the docs show a block list. Changed to `skills:\n  - review-standards`. The installer's frontmatter parser was taught YAML block lists so the inventory and derivation read both spellings.
- Descriptions are one line, double-quoted, 317–446 characters, free of unescaped colons.
- Antigravity derivation emits `name`, quoted `description`, `subagent: true`, `mainAgent: false`, `model` (`opus`→`pro`, `haiku`→`flash`, `sonnet` omitted = inherit), `tools` mapped to `view_file`, `grep_search`, `find_by_name`, `run_command`, `write_to_file`, `replace_file_content`; Claude-only keys dropped. `skills` is dropped because markdown agents inherit the global skills.
- The agy binary carries `description` YAML keys, so a frontmatter `description` is read; what its changelog calls "H1-delimited system prompts" could not be pinned down from the binary. The derived body keeps `##` headings only, so the whole body is one prompt. Left for the live check.

## Global context

- Claude Code: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` = marker line + `@AGENTS.md` → `~/.claude/AGENTS.md`. Documented import form, one hop, user level.
- Antigravity: `~/.gemini/config/rules/AGENTS.md`. The global root is confirmed; the `rules/` subdirectory is the workspace convention (`.agents/rules/*.md`) applied to the global root, and the plugin guide recommends `rules/AGENTS.md` as the consolidated rule file. Left for the live check. If it fails, the alternative is a plugin (`~/.gemini/config/plugins/sh-agent/{plugin.json,rules/AGENTS.md}`), which needs no registration when placed in the global root.
- Content: 104 lines deployed (context + environment + inventory), no vendor-specific instructions except the discovery note.

## What was not checked

- Live loading on either CLI (deliberately deferred by the operator).
- Antigravity IDE paths (out of scope).
- The exact agy tool-name list beyond the six mapped names.

title: Review — 641eccd-worktree-code (2026-09-15)
body:
# Review — 641eccd-worktree-code   (2026-09-15)

Range reviewed: 641eccd..fe21671 (`git diff 641eccd..fe21671 -- context agents skills README.md AGENTS.md .agents/docs/deploy .agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md`) plus the uncommitted working tree (`git diff fe21671 -- skills .agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md`: `skills/init-project/SKILL.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md`)

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The worst problem is in `/preflight` Step 4, the mechanism ADR-023 just settled. A rebutted docs finding is carried forward only from the newest prior gate report's `## Outcome`, and no step writes the carried rebuttal into the next report's `## Outcome`. So one gate report later the finding is raised again and blocks. That is the failure ADR-023 was written to remove ("instead of blocking every later release"). A second defect sits in the same mechanism: the docs reviewer is never told about the rebuttal, so its REQUEST CHANGES verdict can still block. A third: Step 6 still says SHIP "has no findings left", which contradicts Step 4's new `left` gaps. These three findings are the third round on this one mechanism (BUG-026, ADR-023). Under Definition of Done step 2 and BUG-026's prevention rule, take them to the operator before a third patch. Two findings sit outside preflight. README's new `--vendor all` "widens" claim is false for `sh-agent update`. And the binary's two CLAUDE.md messages still give the procedure README just replaced. The working-tree init-project update is sound. Its shell snippets were run in scratch clones and behaved as documented, and the new `init-update` matrix check passes a correct update and fails two wrong ones.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:65` — A rebuttal is carried forward for one gate report only.
  - Step 4 reads "the `## Outcome` of the newest prior `reviews/*-preflight-*` report" and cites a rebutted finding "in the gate report". It does not say the citation goes into that report's `## Outcome`.
  - Step 6 (line 81) fills `## Outcome` only with "one line per finding" of the gate it resolves. A cited finding is by definition not raised, so it gets no line. On SHIP the report "needs none".
  - Failure path: gate N-1 has the rebuttal in its Outcome. Gate N reads it and cites the finding in its body. Gate N+1 reads gate N's Outcome, finds no rebuttal, and raises and blocks the finding again. That happens whenever two NO-SHIPs follow each other, or a SHIP is followed by the next release.
  - Same day, same version: Step 5 writes the same path, `$(date +%F)-preflight-<version>.md`, so the re-run overwrites the report whose Outcome held the rebuttal. Git still has it; the next run does not read git.
  - The "same statement at the same file:line" key also breaks when a fix for another finding shifts lines in the same doc. That key is the operator's ADR-023 wording, so this is noted for the operator, not re-argued.
  - Fix (operator's call, per BUG-026): Step 4 reads the Outcome of every prior preflight report, or each gate report copies carried rebuttals into its own `## Outcome`. The shorter option: a rebutted docs finding gets a doc change so it stops being raised, and the carry-forward mechanism is deleted.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:65,77` — A rebutted finding can still block through the reviewer's verdict.
  - Step 4 dispatches the docs reviewer "with the docs brief exactly as `/review` Step 3 gives it". That brief (`skills/review/SKILL.md:48`) carries no prior rebuttals, so the reviewer raises the rebutted finding again and sets its verdict from it.
  - Step 5 blocks on "a Step 4 REQUEST CHANGES verdict or high-severity docs finding, not counting a finding a prior gate report rebutted". The exclusion names findings, not the verdict.
  - Result: a rebutted finding that is the only reason for REQUEST CHANGES still blocks every run.
  - Fix: the verdict blocks only when a non-rebutted finding supports it. Or drop the verdict clause and block on high-severity non-rebutted findings alone.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:81` — Step 6 contradicts the new `left` gaps.
  - Stale text: "the SHIP path has no findings left and needs none" (no `## Outcome`).
  - Line 65, changed in this range, now says "every other gap is recorded as `left` with an owner", and ADR-023 says "A low-severity docs gap can ship, recorded with its owner". A SHIP report therefore does have `left` findings.
  - No step says where they go: Step 5's section list has no place for them, and Step 6 says SHIP needs none.
  - An agent following Step 6 on SHIP drops the owners ADR-023 requires. This is the describing-text rule (review-standards §3).
  - Fix: Step 5 names where `left` gaps go on SHIP (for example a `## Outcome` with `left` lines), and line 81 drops "has no findings left".
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `README.md:32` (also `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md:27`, which is scoped to install) — `--vendor all` does not widen through `update`.
  - README says every command accepts `--vendor` and "`--vendor all` widens a single-vendor install to both". That holds for `install`: `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:137` passes an explicit flag through the rebuild.
  - It fails for `update`: `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:348` appends `--vendor` only when `vendor != harness.VendorAll`. The child `install --repo …` then resolves the default from the manifest (`resolveVendor`, main.go:216-224) and reinstalls the old single vendor.
  - Silent failure: `sh-agent update --vendor all` on a claude-only install never installs Antigravity.
  - Checked by reading the code. Not run, because `update` fetches and pulls this repo.
  - Fix: pass `--vendor` whenever `vendorFlag != ""`, as install does, with a test. Or narrow the README sentence to `install`.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/apply.go:37`, `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:309` — The binary contradicts README's new CLAUDE.md procedure.
  - README.md:53 now tells the operator to move a hand-written `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` into `rules/`, remove it, and reinstall, so the file becomes the one-line import R2 requires.
  - The binary still prints the replaced procedure: `install` says "add the line `@AGENTS.md` to it yourself", and `status` says "make sure it contains the line `@AGENTS.md`".
  - Following the binary leaves a CLAUDE.md with content plus an import, which is not the one-line import of REQUIREMENTS.md R2. The operator also gets two conflicting instructions.
  - This is a describing-text miss (review-standards §3; BUG-027's "grep the subject, not the old wording"). The binary is outside the diff's paths but is what README describes.
  - Fix: change both messages to point at the README procedure. No test asserts on either string (grep of `cmd/`, `internal/`).

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. The change is docs and skill text only, with no orphaned file or dangling reference. The `anti-ui-slop` MANIFEST mention was correctly removed: the directory holds only LICENSE and NOTICE.
2. Flow tracing — fail. `--vendor all` traced through `update` → `Reinstall` → child `install` loses the flag (finding 4). Preflight Step 4 → Step 5 → Step 6 → the next Step 4 loses the rebuttal (findings 1, 2).
   - What held: README `--dry-run`, `--force` and repo discovery via parents match `main.go`/`repo.go`. The remote.md mirror paragraph matches both mirrors' `VENDORED.md`, crew's `image/Dockerfile` builder stage, argolis's `032_setup-harness.sh` (run as root) and its 5-minute `devbox-autoupdate.timer`. The Mac log cited in remote.md exists.
   - init-project Steps 3–6, run in `.agents/scratch/review-641eccd/upd` (a clone of the older demo-app scaffold): update added only `.agents/docs/retros/.gitkeep`, and a second run added nothing.
   - The `init-update` matrix check exits 0 after a correct update and 1 for a modified `TODO.md` and for a scaffold-message commit (BUG-024's must-pass rule met).
   - In a fresh repo (`.agents/scratch/review-641eccd-new`) the loops produce exactly the documented tree and four resolving links. A wrong-target link and a real directory are reported as "kept".
3. Standards conformance — fail on describing text (findings 3, 5). The init-project staging and commit wording matches the global hard rules (stage by name, read `--cached --stat`, commit in its own call). `go run ./cmd/sh-agent list` and `install --dry-run --home .agents/scratch/review-641eccd-home` exit 0: the new quoted frontmatter passes the installer's lint, and the dry run wrote no file.
4. Directory layout — pass. No new files. The new matrix row sits in the existing table.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — concern, not a separate finding. The preflight rebuttal carry-forward is the third round of patches on one mechanism (BUG-026). Deleting it (fix the doc so the finding stops recurring) is shorter than defending it. No security-sensitive code.
6. Decoupling — pass. Skill edits stay inside their own files. Preflight reuses the `/review` docs brief by reference, which is also why finding 2 needs a change on the preflight side, not in the brief.

## Not examined
- `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-15-harness-practices-g01-g26.md` (modified in the working tree; outside the dispatched scope).
- The `init-update` matrix row was not run through either CLI. Only its check was exercised, against states built by hand.

- `sh-agent update` was not executed (it fetches and pulls this repo), so finding 4 is from reading the code.

title: Review — c192622-22c106c-code, round 2 (2026-09-15)
body:
# Review — c192622-22c106c-code, round 2   (2026-09-15)

Range reviewed: c192622..22c106c, paths `context agents skills README.md AGENTS.md` (`git diff c192622..22c106c -- context agents skills README.md AGENTS.md`), plus the uncommitted round-1 fixes in the working tree (`git diff -- skills agents`: `agents/bugs.md`, `skills/{bug,feature,handoff,init-project,preflight}/SKILL.md`; 6 files, +12/-12). Standards: `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md` § 1–3 as in this repository.

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

Of the seven round-1 fixes, five are correct and complete: F1, F3, F4, F6 and F7. Two of them introduced new defects.

The worst is F2, which rewrote the preflight Step 4 mechanism, the one the round-1 review asked about. Every Step 4 docs finding now blocks the release, and the fix after NO-SHIP is followed by a full `/preflight` re-run. But Step 4 has no coverage rule and ignores prior rebuttals. A finding rebutted in the gate report's `## Outcome`, which Step 6 explicitly allows, is re-raised by the fresh docs reviewer on the re-run. Step 5 then blocks again, and Step 6 allows no override. A release with a correct rebuttal therefore cannot ship. By the context's own rule, this is the second round landing on the same mechanism.

The second defect is F5, the bug-fix clause added to preflight Step 2. It contradicts ADR-022, which is Accepted, and plan row D8. Both say that Step 2's release-diff threshold stays.

Neither new defect breaks the installer, and no frontmatter changed.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:65`, `:77`, `:81` — a rebutted Step 4 docs finding blocks every re-run, and nothing stops it.
  - **The rules involved:**
    - `:65` says each Step 4 finding "blocks the release" and that "`/preflight` runs again".
    - `:77` lists "a Step 4 docs finding" as blocking, with no exception.
    - `:81` lets the task that resolves NO-SHIP findings close one as `rebutted`, and says "Never ship on NO-SHIP — no override."
  - **Why the re-run does not honour a rebuttal:**
    - Step 4 dispatches the docs reviewer "with the docs brief exactly as `/review` Step 3 gives it", over the whole `<base>..HEAD`. The dispatch has no mention of the earlier gate report or its Outcome.
    - Step 2 has a way through: it reuses a prior report whose `Range reviewed:` covers the commits. Step 4 has nothing like that.
  - **Concrete failure:** the docs reviewer raises a false positive. It is rebutted with a checkable reason, as `/review` Step 4 requires. `/preflight` runs again, and the same diff against the same docs gets the same finding, so the result is NO-SHIP again. The only ways out are editing correct docs until the reviewer is satisfied, or abandoning the release.
  - **Introduced by the fix:** before it, the gate fixed docs findings inside the run, so a re-run was rare. Now every Step 4 finding forces a full re-run, and each re-run re-reads text that was already accepted.
  - **Fix, either of these:**
    - At `:77`, exclude a Step 4 finding that an earlier gate report over the same base lists as `rebutted` in its `## Outcome`, and have Step 4 pass those Outcome lines to the docs reviewer.
    - Simpler: give Step 4 Step 2's coverage rule. Cite a prior `*-docs` report whose `Range reviewed:` covers the commits and whose gate Outcome closes every finding, and run the docs lens only over the commits after it.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:50` — the F5 fix contradicts an Accepted ADR and a plan decision.
  - **What the records say:**
    - ADR-022 Consequences (`.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md:179`): "Features and tasks keep the 50-line / 5-file threshold, and so does the release gate's review of the release diff (`skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 2), which reads a sub-threshold release diff itself."
    - Plan D8 (`plans/2026-09-15-harness-practices-g01-g26.md:1197`) says the same.
  - **What changed:** `:50` now also dispatches the release reviewer when the range "adds a bug fix". `DECISIONS.md` is unmodified, and no new ADR or D-row records the change.
  - **Concrete failure:** a later reviewer or resume reads the Accepted ADR as the decision. Round 1 of this review did exactly that ("ADR-022's Consequences keep it on purpose"), and so will a future session, which then either reverts `:50` or sees two authorities that disagree.
  - **Not needed in behaviour:** `skills/bug/SKILL.md:53` already reviews every bug fix whatever its size. Step 2's coverage rule then cites that report, so the clause only fires for a fix that skipped its own Definition of Done.
  - **Fix:** prefer the shorter one. Revert `:50` and correct the Phase 5 changes entry's wording in the next `changes/` entry. That was the round-1 docs report's second option, and it agrees with ADR-022 and D8. Otherwise, append an ADR that amends ADR-022 plus a D-row superseding D8.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-15-harness-practices-g01-g26.md` (outside the dispatched paths; trail) — two fixes changed rehearsed plan edits without the D-row that `skills/feature/SKILL.md:85` requires.
  - **Which edits:**
    - The F1 fix changed I-23b's "no" branch (plan `:1023` still holds the removed text).
    - The F2 fix deleted I-21d–g's post-gate fix path (plan `:914`, `:922`, `:930`).

  - **Where it fails:** Phase 6's Checkpoint must map every I-edit to a matrix row. Mapped from the plan, it would expect behaviour that the tree no longer has, and a resume reading the plan's Decisions finds no record that the mechanism changed.
  - **Fix:** add dated D-rows for both changes (by: review round 1) that name the superseded I-edit text.

### Round-1 fixes verified
- **F1** `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:44` — **fixed.**
  - The harness no longer writes a `CLAUDE.md` that is not a one-line import. On "no" the file is untouched, and the summary says Claude Code will not import `AGENTS.md`.

It also matches `context/AGENTS.md:37` ("may not load on every vendor… `/skills` and `/agents` show what a vendor loaded").

- **F2** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:65`, `:77`, `:85`, `:90` — **the round-1 defect is gone; a new defect was introduced** (finding 1).
  - Gone: fixes now go through ordinary work with its Definition of Done, and a re-run's Step 2 verification row needs a log that reaches the new HEAD, so nothing unchecked reaches the tag.
  - Nothing else in the dispatched paths still describes in-gate docs fixes.
- **F5** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:50` — **wording applied, but it conflicts with the decision record** (finding 2).
- **F6** `agents/bugs.md:76` — **fixed.** The five homes equal `context/AGENTS.md:31` and `agents/bugs.md:70`, and ADR-021 (which also lists `context/AGENTS.md` for this repository).
- **F7** `skills/feature/SKILL.md:97`, `skills/bug/SKILL.md:53` — **fixed.** Both use exactly the trigger wording of `context/AGENTS.md:17` and `agents/documentation.md:12`.

### Considered, not findings
- **`:65` "the gate never edits the tree after it has run" versus Step 6 SHIP.** The changelog entry and the version bump are written after the gate. Step 6 names them explicitly and they predate this range, so a reader has no ambiguity that fails.
- **`:50`'s proxy "a `bugs/BUG-*.md` record in the range".** It also matches process-failure records such as BUG-008, BUG-011 and BUG-013, which are not fixes. The cost is an extra review, not a correctness failure. It is moot if `:50` is reverted.
- **Handoff Step 3 (`:64`) versus the table (`:49`).** Step 3 sends "any deferred idea worth keeping" to Next Steps; the table sends deferred work to the plan's Follow-ups when a plan is active. Resume reads both locations (`:32`), so nothing is lost.
- **Base-ref fallback on a re-run in a tagless project (`:44`).** It takes the base before the dots of the newest preflight report, so a NO-SHIP report does not shift the base.
- **Frontmatter.** No uncommitted fix touches frontmatter, so there is no BUG-004 exposure. No file under `cmd/` or `internal/` changed.

## Criteria
1. **Dead code: pass.** Markdown only. The fixes delete the post-gate fix path whole, with no residual references in the dispatched paths (`git grep` for "docs fixes", "still unfixed", "keep the content", "find the same rules" prints nothing there).
2. **Flow tracing: fail.** The preflight re-run after a rebutted Step 4 finding cannot reach SHIP (finding 1). Traced so far:
   - Step 4 fix → ordinary Definition of Done → re-run Step 1, Step 2 coverage and verifier row → Step 5. This holds.

3. **Standards conformance: fail.**

   - Plan edits changed without D-rows (finding 3).

   - gofmt, vet and tests are not applicable, since no Go changed.
4. **Directory layout: pass.** No new, moved or deleted file.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security): pass with a note.** Deleting the in-gate fix path made preflight shorter, which is the right direction. Finding 1's coverage-rule fix keeps it short. Nothing security-related is hand-rolled, and no dependency was added.
6. **Decoupling: pass.** The `documentation` and main-agent routing is stated the same way in `context/AGENTS.md:16`, `skills/review/SKILL.md:60` and `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:65`.

## Not examined
- **Round-1 range not re-read in full.** Round 1 read the whole committed range. In round 2 I re-read in full only the fixed files: `init-project` and `preflight` whole, `handoff` lines 30–80, and `bugs.md`'s range diff. The other committed files in the range were not re-read.

body:
# Review — c192622-22c106c-docs, round 2   (2026-09-15)

Range reviewed: c192622..22c106c (`git diff c192622..22c106c -- context agents skills README.md AGENTS.md`) plus the uncommitted working-tree changes (`git diff -- skills agents`: `agents/bugs.md`, `skills/{bug,feature,handoff,init-project,preflight}/SKILL.md`). The living docs were searched at the working tree with `git grep` and no revision, over `README.md AGENTS.md context agents skills commands rules .agents/docs/testing/sh-agent/guide.md .agents/docs/deploy`, less the six skills in `skills/VENDORED.md` (grilling, codebase-design, find-skills, anti-ui-slop, gke-basics, terraform). `.agents/` holds only `docs`, `scratch` and the `skills` symlink. There is no `specs/` tree.

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

All seven round 1 findings are fixed. Nothing in the living docs still says the old thing. The worst problem is new and comes from the fix to preflight Step 4. Every Step 4 docs finding now blocks, and after NO-SHIP `/preflight` runs Step 4 again over the whole `<base>..HEAD`. Step 4 has no coverage clause like Step 2's, and nothing honours a `rebutted` line in the gate report's `## Outcome`. So a docs finding that is rebutted, rather than fixed, is raised again on every rerun and blocks every release. Step 6 offers `rebutted` and `left` for exactly that case, but they cannot clear a Step 4 finding. The same fix also added the sentence "the gate never edits the tree after it has run", which Step 6's changelog entry and version bump contradict. Two findings introduced by fixes now land on the same mechanism, preflight Step 4. Under Definition of Done step 2, that is the point to ask what the Step 4 blocking rule is for before patching it a third time.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:65` ("each one blocks the release … After NO-SHIP they are fixed as ordinary work … and `/preflight` runs again") and `:77` (blocking includes "a Step 4 docs finding", with no qualifier) vs `:81` (the Outcome takes `fixed`, `rebutted` … or `left`). Step 2's reviewer at `:50` covers only the commits "not already covered" by a prior report, so a rebutted Step 2 finding is not raised again. Step 4 has no such clause. On rerun, the docs reviewer gets the same range and the same unchanged docs, finds the rebutted finding again, and `:77` blocks. A false positive, such as a medium-confidence finding, can therefore never ship. Before this change, the round 1 head fixed Step 4 findings in the same run, so no rerun loop existed. Fix: either make `:77` read "a Step 4 docs finding not recorded as `rebutted` in a prior gate report's `## Outcome`" and have Step 4 cite those lines, or give Step 4 the same coverage-and-cite clause as Step 2.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:65` ("the gate never edits the tree after it has run") vs `:83`–`:85` (after the gate, SHIP dispatches `changelog` for the release entry, bumps the version where the repo tracks one, and commits both). The version bump edits a tracked source file after the gate, so the new sentence is false as written. A reader who takes it literally will drop the bump or the entry. Fix: say what is meant, for example "the gate never fixes a finding after it has run", or name Step 6's records and version bump as the exception.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:44` ("on no that Claude Code does not import `AGENTS.md` until `CLAUDE.md` is that single line") vs `README.md:53` ("An existing `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` that sh-agent did not write is left alone; add the line `@AGENTS.md` to it yourself"). The README documents that adding the import line to a file with other content works. Import depends on the line being present, not on it being the only line. An existing project `CLAUDE.md` that already has `@AGENTS.md` among other content would be reported to the user as not importing. Fix: "does not import `AGENTS.md` while `CLAUDE.md` lacks the line `@AGENTS.md`, and is not the one-line import `REQUIREMENTS.md` R2 names". Confidence is medium because Claude Code's import behaviour was not run here. The claim rests on `README.md:53`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** The newest changes entry, `.agents/docs/changes/2026-09-15-harness-practices-phase5.md`, still describes behaviour the working tree reverses. At `:21`, Step 4 "fixes the rest itself … and those fixes ride in the release commit", blocking is "a Step 4 docs finding still unfixed", and "Step 6 commits Step 4's docs fixes". At `:25`, the user can keep the existing `CLAUDE.md` "with `@AGENTS.md` added as its first line". The `:21` line also still places the bug-fix reviewer trigger in Step 1 only. The file is append-only, so the fix is the next entry: it must name all three reversals, or a resume reader will take `:21` and `:25` as current.

## Round 1 findings — verification
1. `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:44`: the keep-content branch is removed. On no, the file is left untouched, so the skill no longer writes a `CLAUDE.md` that contradicts R2 (`REQUIREMENTS.md:11`), `DECISIONS.md:41` or `context/AGENTS.md:69`. **Fixed.** Finding 3 is about the new sentence.
2. `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:8` and `:66` no longer claim Antigravity loads the project layer. The `:66` text matches `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-15-verify-g26-precedence.md`: Antigravity CLI 1.2.3 quoted neither control marker, and rules were not tested. Grep for `natively`, `both Claude Code and Antigravity`, `project layer`, `both vendors` and `both CLIs` found no other claim about the project layer. **Fixed.**
3. `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 4 no longer edits after the gate. `:82` ("already run against the clean source tree") and `:90` ("the gated tree plus its records") are true again, and `:85` no longer commits docs fixes. `docs fix`, `still unfixed` and `docs gaps` have no stale hits. **Fixed.** Findings 1 and 2 come from this fix.
4. `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:50` now adds "or adds a bug fix (a `bugs/BUG-*.md` record in the range)", which matches `:40` and `context/AGENTS.md:16`. **Fixed.**
5. `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:49` now points deferred work at "the active plan's Follow-ups, or the handoff's Next Steps when no plan is active". That matches `agents/changelog.md:94` and `skills/bug/SKILL.md:49`, and `Follow-ups` exists as a plan section (`skills/feature/SKILL.md:38`, `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:32`). `Deferred work` has no other hit. **Fixed.**
6. `agents/bugs.md:76` lists the same five homes as `context/AGENTS.md:31` and `agents/bugs.md:70`. `rules/. file, or a test` has no remaining hit. **Fixed.**
7. `skills/feature/SKILL.md:97` and `skills/bug/SKILL.md:53` now use the trigger from `agents/documentation.md:3,12` and `context/AGENTS.md:17`. `behavior or interfaces` and `documentation. if behavio` have no other hit. **Fixed.**

## Checked, no finding
- `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md`: the `init-deploy` row (`:22`) runs on a bare service with no existing `CLAUDE.md`, and its check does not test `CLAUDE.md`. The `preflight` row (`:27`) greps `SHIP`, which a NO-SHIP also matches. Neither row asserts the changed behaviour.
- The round 1 "Checked, no finding" items for the committed range still hold at the working tree. The working-tree diff touches none of those lines, and the greps repeated above returned no new hits.

## Unverified
- `/skills` and `/agents` show what Antigravity loaded (`skills/init-project/SKILL.md:66`, `context/AGENTS.md:37`). The G26 test asked for descriptions in a prompt and never ran those commands on Antigravity.

- Claude Code's `@AGENTS.md` import when the file has other content (finding 3). Only `README.md:53` supports it; no run checked it.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — n/a — docs lens
2. Flow tracing — n/a — docs lens
3. Standards conformance — n/a — docs lens
4. Directory layout — n/a — docs lens
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — n/a — docs lens
6. Decoupling — n/a — docs lens

## Not examined
- Grep output was cut at 260 or 300 characters per line by `cut`. The hits that bear on a finding were read in full: `skills/preflight/SKILL.md`, `skills/init-project/SKILL.md`, and `context/AGENTS.md:1-71` in full, plus `agents/bugs.md:60-80`, `agents/documentation.md:1-20`, changes entry `:21` and `:25`, and skill-matrix `:22` (cut on the first read, then read to the end). Hits judged irrelevant were not read past the cut: `AGENTS.md:46`, `skills/feedback/SKILL.md:88`, `skills/distill/SKILL.md:133,173`, `README.md:67,87`, `skills/retro/SKILL.md:45,132`, `skills/review/SKILL.md` lines other than 48-64, and `agents/changelog.md:94` past its Follow-ups clause.
- The committed range c192622..22c106c was not re-read end to end this round. Round 1 read it in full, and this round re-read only the working-tree diff and the files it touches.
- The living docs were checked by targeted `git grep` for each changed statement, not read end to end.
