Remediation: (a) build release binaries from a clean export of the tag — `git -C <checkout> worktree add .agents/scratch/release-vX.Y.Z vX.Y.Z`, build there — instead of the operator's working checkout (D10 puts the build inside `/preflight` Step 6, not yet written, so this is the moment to fix it); (b) invert the embed test: walk `styrman.Files` and fail on any path that `git ls-files -- context skills agents commands rules` does not list, skipping when git is absent (stdlib `os/exec`, no dependency); (c) have the preflight build refuse when `git status --porcelain --ignored -- context skills agents commands rules` prints any `??` or `!!` line.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:477` — `knownCheckout` passes the manifest's repo value to `samePath`, which calls `filepath.EvalSymlinks` on it, so an `embedded:vX.Y.Z` value written by an embedded install (`internal/harness/apply.go:96`) is interpreted as a path relative to the process's working directory. `ResolveSource` was hardened against exactly this (`repo.go:42` skips `EmbeddedPrefix`; `TestResolveSource` plants an `embedded:v1.0.0` harness tree in the cwd and asserts it is not read as a path) — `knownCheckout` was not. Consequence in principle: on a machine whose install came from a release binary, the one guard that stops `install`/`update` from building a checkout the operator never named is satisfied when an entry named `embedded:<installed version>` in the working directory resolves to the walk-found tree (a symlink with an absolute target resolves to that target), after which the tree is `go build`-ed and executed (`main.go:153-166` → `repo.go:178-195`). Requires control of the directory the operator runs in, hence low. Remediation: refuse before comparing — `if strings.HasPrefix(st.Repo, harness.EmbeddedPrefix) { return fmt.Errorf("this install is the release binary %s; pass --repo %s to build and install from a checkout", …) }`, or require `filepath.IsAbs(st.Repo)` before `samePath`; add the planted-directory and planted-link cases to `TestKnownCheckout`, which today only covers absolute recorded paths.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/repo.go:24-31` — `--repo ""` and `SH_AGENT_REPO=` (set but empty) are treated as "not named" (`if named == "" { continue }`) and fall through to the directory walk, the recorded repo, and in a release binary to the embedded files. D15 promises a named path is used or refused, never replaced. A wrapper or systemd unit running `sh-agent install --repo "$HARNESS"` with `HARNESS` unset therefore installs whatever the walk finds, or the embedded release, instead of failing. Remediation: in `main.go`, detect that the flag was actually given (`fs.Visit`) and use `os.LookupEnv` for the variable, then refuse an empty value; `ResolveSource` cannot distinguish the two cases from a bare string.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:130-139` — the embedded install path `return installFiles(...)` before `knownCheckout` runs, so an embedded install never consults what the manifest records. Trigger: the manifest records a checkout, that path is no longer a harness tree (moved, renamed, mid-surgery) and the walk finds nothing → a release binary installs its own, possibly older, context/agents/rules over the checkout's newer ones with no confirmation, and `Install` prunes the files the older plan lacks — a silent downgrade of the text every session reads. Remediation: run `knownCheckout` (or an embedded-aware variant) on that path too, refusing when the manifest records a path source unless `--repo` or an explicit confirmation is given; the message can name the recorded checkout.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/repo.go:32-45` (the D14 ordering) — the working directory and its parents outrank the embedded files for every command, `install` included. For the release-binary audience (downloaded binary, no checkout, no manifest) that means: run it anywhere whose cwd or a parent holds `context/AGENTS.md` plus `skills/`, and that tree becomes the harness; with no manifest `knownCheckout` returns nil, and if the tree is its own git checkout with `go` on PATH, `Reinstall` runs `go build -o … ./cmd/sh-agent` inside it and executes the result. A plain copy (no `.git`) is not built, but its `context/` still lands in `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` and `~/.gemini/config/rules/AGENTS.md`, which every session reads — prompt-level persistence. The mechanism is pre-existing (`FindRepo` walked the same way), newly reachable by people who never intended to use a checkout. Remediation: when `IsReleaseVersion(version)` and no manifest exists, refuse to build or install a tree found only by the walk unless `--repo`/`SH_AGENT_REPO` names it.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/source.go:17-27` — the link refusals are keyed on `Source.Dir != ""` (`checkManagedTree` returns nil, `readRegular` uses `fs.Stat` instead of `os.Lstat`), and `Source` is exported with exported fields. A future `Source{FS: os.DirFS(p)}` with `Dir` unset therefore reads a tree on disk with every BUG-036 refusal silently disabled — fail-open by construction, and the tests already build `Source{FS: m}` literals. Production is safe today: the only constructors are `DirSource` and `EmbeddedSource` (`Source{` literals exist only in `source.go`, `repo.go`'s error returns and `main.go:265`'s empty value). Remediation: unexport the fields and construct only through the two helpers, or key the refusals on "this FS is not the embedded one" rather than on `Dir`. `fs.Lstat`/`fs.ReadLinkFS` would be the clean fix but arrived in Go 1.25 and `go.mod` says `go 1.24.4` — no pin, no dependency (ADR-029).

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/harness_test.go:526-577` — `TestResolveSource` is not hermetic: it chdirs into `t.TempDir()` and relies on the parent walk finding nothing, so with `TMPDIR` inside a harness checkout — which this project's own scratch rule makes the natural choice — every assertion inverts. Measured: with `TMPDIR=.agents/scratch/sec-review/tmp` the test fails 12 times (`version "" with no tree: err = <nil>, want harness repo not found`; `release binary with no tree: {Dir:/home/kesokaj/workspace/styrman-harness}`; `a development build must not read a recorded embedded:<version> as a path`), and the same run with the toolchain's default temp dir passes. The D14/D15 gate is thus only as strong as `$TMPDIR`, and a test that fails environmentally tends to get weakened rather than fixed. Remediation: assert up front that no parent of the cwd is a harness tree (`IsRepo`) and fail with that message, or let the test inject the walk's starting directory.

## Checked

- **Secrets** — no credential, token or key added in the diff; `var version` is the only new build-time value and it is a version string. The new exposure channel is the embed of ignored files (finding 1). `harness_version` in the report record is the regex-gated `vX.Y.Z`, so nothing arbitrary is written into the feedback repository.
- **Injection / unvalidated input** — no SQL or templates. Every `git`/`go` exec site was enumerated (`main.go:299,416,433,444`; `apply.go:100`; `report.go:353,413`; `repo.go:101,147,150,178,194,205`) and each is reachable only with `src.Dir != ""`: `install` returns early for the embedded source, `update` and `adopt` refuse it, `status` branches on `repo == ""`, `Install` and `BuildRecord` branch on `src.Dir != ""`. So Q4's answer is no — no `git -C ""` or `cmd.Dir = ""`, either of which would silently act on the process's own working directory. No test asserts the absence of a git process for an embedded source (a stray `git -C ""` would not fail loudly in a temp cwd), so that property rests on code reading. Path handling: `Source.path` is `filepath.Join(Dir, filepath.FromSlash(name))`; `os.DirFS` rejects non-`fs.ValidPath` names; `Skill.Dir` changed from an absolute path to an in-FS path and is read only by `fs.WalkDir`/`TrimPrefix` in `plan.go:99,123`; `Agent.Path`/`Doc.Path` have no readers anywhere in non-test code (unfiltered `grep -rn '\.Path\b' cmd internal` printed nothing) — so no in-FS relative path is mistaken for a disk path.
- **Authz/authn** — none in the harness. The trust boundary reviewed is "whose bytes become `~/.claude`/`~/.gemini` content and whose code gets built and executed": findings 2, 4 and 5.
- **Crypto** — nothing hand-rolled and nothing crypto-adjacent in range; `IsReleaseVersion` is a `regexp`, not a signature check, and is not presented as one. Signature/checksum verification of a downloaded release binary is Phase 4, outside this range.
- **Dependencies** — no new dependency; stdlib only (`embed`, `io/fs`, `path`). `govulncheck ./...` → "No vulnerabilities found" (go1.27.1, exit 0). `npm audit` not applicable — no JavaScript in this repository.
- **GCP surface** — untouched by this range (no IAM, no Cloud Run, no Secret Manager, no service-account material).
- **BUG-036, Q1 (symlink refusals for a tree on disk)** — hold on every read path, verified directly rather than inferred. A binary built into scratch (`go build -o .agents/scratch/sec-review/sh-agent ./cmd/sh-agent`) was run against eight scratch trees with a harmless canary file as the link target, in both must-pass and must-fail states: control (plain tree plus a linked `skills/<name>` with no inner links) → `diff` and `render` exit 0 with no refusal and no canary in the output; file link inside a LINKED skill directory → refused (`…/skills/linked/inner.md is a symlink — a skill ships regular files only`); `SKILL.md` a link inside a linked skill directory → refused by `readRegular` (`…/skills/linked/SKILL.md is a symlink — the repo ships regular files only`); a directory link nested inside a linked skill directory → refused; a `context/` entry link → refused; `agents/` itself a link → refused (`ships regular directories only`); `skills/` itself a link → refused; a `commands/` entry link → refused; a link inside a regular skill directory → refused. All eight exited 1 and the canary's content appeared in no output. The authors' own tests over the same ground pass (`TestManagedDirsRefuseSymlinks`, `TestSymlinkedSkillMdIsRefused`, `TestContextAgentsAndDocsRefuseSymlinks`, `TestSkillFilesAndAdoptCopiesRefuseSymlinks`, `TestRenderContextRefusesSymlinks`, `TestDirSourceFollowsLinkedSkillDir`, `TestFSSourceRefusals`, `TestPlanRefusesSecretShapedFiles`, `TestPlanDropsGroupAndOtherWrite`, `TestResolveSource*`, `TestReleaseBinaryWithoutCheckout`, `TestEmbeddedInstallStateAndRecord`, `TestFilesMatchTree`, `TestEmbeddedPlanEqualsCheckout`, `TestKnownCheckout` — one targeted run, all ok). The `Dir == ""` early return is sound for the embedded FS, which cannot hold a link (`go:embed` skips irregular files); its fail-open shape is finding 6.
- **Q2 (what can reach the embedded fallback)** — only a `vX.Y.Z` version. `version` comes from `-ldflags -X main.version` or, when empty, `versionFromInfo(debug.ReadBuildInfo())`, which prefers the VCS short revision (`+dirty` suffixed) and falls back to the module version, and the gate is `^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$` with Go's `$` meaning end of text (no trailing-newline match). No runtime flag, env var or file feeds it. `TestResolveSource` pins the rejected shapes (`""`, a revision, `+dirty`, `(devel)`, `v1.2.3-rc.1`, a pseudo-version, `1.2.3`, `v1.2`). A non-empty explicit `--repo`/`$SH_AGENT_REPO` that is not a harness tree is an error on both development and release builds and never falls through (`TestResolveSourceRefusesNamedNonRepo`, `TestReleaseBinaryWithoutCheckout`); the one gap is the empty-but-set case, finding 3.
- **Q3 (`embedded:<version>` as a path)** — three readers: skipped in `ResolveSource` (`repo.go:42`), display-only in `status` via `strings.CutPrefix`, and used as a path in `knownCheckout` (finding 2). The value is written only from the regex-gated version (`apply.go:96`), so its suffix cannot carry `..`, a leading `-`, or a separator. A pre-range binary reading a new manifest would treat the value as a relative candidate path, but the working-directory walk already grants an attacker who controls the cwd the same thing, so that adds no exposure.
- **Q5 (modes and secret-shaped files in what install deploys)** — no regression. Skill files keep `mode = info.Mode().Perm()&0o755 | 0o600`; `embed.FS` reports 0444, so the embedded plan yields 0644 — never wider than the checkout path, and group/other write is still masked off. An executable skill file would LOSE its exec bit from a release binary; `TestEmbeddedPlanEqualsCheckout` is the alarm for that (the plan records it firing on a mutation), but no tracked file under the five directories is `100755` or `120000` today (`git ls-files -s` shows only `100644`), so the "modes equal" claim is currently vacuous — worth saying plainly rather than reading as a guarantee. Context/agents/commands/rules files keep fixed `0o644`. The secret-shaped refusal runs on the same walk for both sources.

## Not examined

- Phase 3-5 work the plan references but this range does not contain: the throwaway feedback clone, `update`'s binary download with checksum/signature verification, README § Install without cloning, and the `/preflight` Step 6 build-and-upload step — which is exactly where finding 1's remediation belongs.
- `internal/harness/{adopt,state,apply}.go` beyond the lines the diff touched; the redaction machinery in `report.go` (unchanged here) was not re-reviewed.
- Test files read only in part: `harness_test.go` (526-580, 768-788), `main_test.go` (177-209, 1008-1099), `source_test.go` (98-217), `pathguard_test.go` (test names only), `plan_test.go` (not read — its content is taken from the plan's evidence line and from the targeted run passing).
- Not run: the full `go test -race ./...`, `gofmt -l cmd internal`, `go vet ./...` (verifier's tier); only the 16 targeted tests above, plus the eight scratch probes.
- How each vendor CLI consumes the deployed files (`derive.go` unchanged in range), and the behavioural CLI runs this repo's testing rules require for a `context/`, `agents/` or `skills/` change.
- Scratch left behind, all gitignored: `.agents/scratch/sec-review/` (built binary, eight probe trees, a probe Go module, and a nested probe git repository created with `git init` exit 0, every later command `git -C`). The real repository is untouched: `git status --short --untracked-files=all` shows only untracked review/testing docs, HEAD is 21ba8dc, and `git tag` lists only `v1.0.0`.

## Outcome

Read against the diff by the main agent, 2026-09-17. HEAD at the time: 21ba8dc.

**Fixed**

1. **[medium] `embed.go:9` — an untracked or gitignored file under the five directories is compiled into the released binary.** Reproduced: `printf 'TOKEN=canary\n' > rules/.env` (ignored by `.gitignore:12`) and the embedded set grew to hold it, while `TestFilesMatchTree` and `TestEmbeddedPlanEqualsCheckout` both still passed — the file is never planned or installed, only carried. Fixed by `TestEmbedHoldsOnlyTrackedFiles` in `embed_test.go`: the embedded set must equal `git ls-files` over the five directories, in both directions; it fails with `rules/.env is embedded but not tracked by git`, and skips (naming why) without git or outside a checkout. The release-time half — `/preflight` refusing a release when `git status --porcelain --ignored` names anything under the five directories, and building from the tag's own tree — is Phase 5, added as a task box with D23, because Step 6 does not exist yet on this branch.
2. **[low] `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` `knownCheckout` hands `embedded:vX.Y.Z` to `samePath`, which resolves it against the working directory.** Fixed: `knownCheckout` now refuses on `EmbeddedPrefix` before comparing, naming the release. `TestKnownCheckoutRefusesEmbeddedManifest` covers it; with the guard removed the test fails (the old message resolved the manifest value as a path).
3. **[low] `TestResolveSource` is not hermetic: with `TMPDIR` inside a checkout every case reads that tree.** Fixed: the test now probes the temp directory first and skips, naming why, exactly as the test it replaced did for the working directory.

**Rebutted, with reasons**

4. **[low] empty-but-set `--repo ""` / `SH_AGENT_REPO=` falls through to the walk.** Unchanged behaviour: `FindRepo` skipped an empty value the same way, and the harness's own tests neutralise the variable with `t.Setenv("SH_AGENT_REPO", "")`, which `os.LookupEnv` would turn into a hard error. D15 is about a value that NAMES something that is not a harness tree; an empty value names nothing. Out of scope for this change.
5. **[low] a release binary prefers a harness-shaped working directory or parent, and may `go build` and exec it.** That is D4's source order, chosen by the operator (scope item 3: `--repo`, a checkout found as today, then the embedded files), and the build is still gated by `knownCheckout` and `IsCheckout` exactly as for any binary. Changing the order is a design question, not a defect of this phase; the `knownCheckout` fix above closes the one case where the guard read a release as a path.
6. **[low] the embedded install path returns before `knownCheckout`, so it replaces and prunes a checkout install of the same home.** Behaviour as the plan's per-command table states it (install from `styrman.Files`, copy the running binary); whether a release binary should refuse a home that a checkout installed is a decision for the operator; asked 2026-09-17 and answered in their own turn, "Replace, as it does now" — recorded as plan decision D24, so the behaviour stands and the guard is deliberately not extended to the embedded path.
7. **[low] the refusals key on the exported `Source.Dir`, so a hand-built `Source{FS: os.DirFS(p)}` with no `Dir` would read a tree on disk with the link checks skipped.** `DirSource` is the only constructor for a tree on disk and both fields are documented; no caller builds a `Source` literal for a disk tree (`ResolveSource` and `DirSource` are the only producers, checked with grep). Noted rather than fixed: hiding the field would need an accessor for `main.go`'s `repo := src.Dir`, which buys nothing against a caller that ignores the constructor.
8. **[not a finding] the "modes equal" claim of `TestEmbeddedPlanEqualsCheckout` is vacuous today, since no tracked file under the five directories is `100755`.** Correct, and stated in the test's own comment: it exists so that adding an executable file, which `embed` records as `0444`, fails the test rather than shipping without its execute bit. `git ls-files -s` confirms all 133 files are `100644`.

Code review of the same range: `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-17-review-f7ee817-21ba8dc-code.md` (APPROVE, 0 findings; its one cosmetic observation — `Source.path` returning a bare slash path for the embedded source — is error text only and is left as is).

title: Security review — preflight v1.1.0 release gate (2026-09-17)
body:
# Security review — preflight v1.1.0 release gate   (2026-09-17)

Range reviewed: v1.0.0..086deab

## Verdict: FINDINGS (2 low, both ordering/hygiene in the release PROCEDURE; nothing blocks the gate)

No unreviewed code ships in this release, and no fix made after a prior review
introduced a regression: every fix the cited reports claim in their `## Outcome`
sections is present and whole at HEAD, verified by locating it in the shipping
source rather than by trusting the report. The worst thing found is an ORDERING
defect in the release procedure, not in the code: `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md`
§ Releases puts the `go:embed` contamination guard AFTER `git push origin
vX.Y.Z`, and `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 6 encodes the same order (6.4
pushes the tag, 6.5 builds artifacts). Because "a pushed tag is never moved", a
stray ignored file under the five embedded directories is caught only once the
version is public and unrecallable. The guard still stops the contaminated
binary from being PUBLISHED, so the blast radius is a burnt version number, not
a shipped secret — hence low. Ship is not blocked by either finding.

## Tree identity (verified here, not taken from the dispatch)

`git rev-parse 24d08a8^{tree} cd0bbcb^{tree}` → both
`da8d57d59eb1ff49ea3b96d2cdbb1183a5fb8b93`, and `git diff 24d08a8 cd0bbcb
--stat` is empty. The trees the prior reports reviewed and the tree shipping as
v1.1.0 are byte-identical. This premise is what licenses a delta review instead
of a repeat, so it was checked before anything else rather than accepted.

## Prior coverage cited, not repeated

- `sh-agent report` (feedback loop, redaction, push target):
  `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-17-security-6af54f7-015cf2d.md` (8 findings),
  `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-17-security-015cf2d-012b4ca.md` (8 findings)
- Embedded source and `ResolveSource`: `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-17-security-f7ee817-21ba8dc.md`
- Throwaway clone and `RemoveKeptClone`: `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-17-security-73f2c36-83f3cf6.md`
- `update` from a signed release: `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-17-security-dab2565-4d45155.md`
- Also in range and counted as coverage, though the dispatch did not name them:
  `-security-012b4ca-worktree.md` and `-security-012b4ca-worktree-final.md`
  (the redaction round-3 probes).

## Part 1 — are the claimed fixes present and whole at HEAD?

**All present. None found partially applied.** Each was located in the shipping
source.

### Report round 1 (`-security-6af54f7-015cf2d.md`)
| Claim | At HEAD | Whole? |
|---|---|---|
| F1 wider needles, no bare `sk-` | `report.go:38-57` — `prefixNeedles` (19 vendor shapes, shortest `sk-ant-`/`glpat-`; no bare `sk-`), `keywordNeedles` (4 case-insensitive regexps) | yes |
| F2 no key path in `report.json` | `report.go:94-100` — `Redaction` has `File/Line/Pattern/Lines/Unterminated` and **no `Path` field at all**: the leak is structurally impossible, not merely unset | yes, strongest form |
| F3 push target + env redirects | `report.go:598` `gitRedirects` = the five vars, consumed `617-621` in `SendReport` **before** `Collect`; `verifyFeedback:579-594` requires `rev-parse --show-toplevel` to `EvalSymlinks`-equal `dir`, and `remote.origin.url` to equal the URL exactly | yes |
| F4 block rule before JSON; `blockEnd`; rewritten dashes | `report.go:159` the block rule is the FIRST branch of the loop; `blockEnd:104-133` searches from the header's offset and re-opens on a header following a footer; `blockOpen:63` matches `BEGIN[A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY` | yes |
| F6 `runDir` refuses a linked `reports` | `report.go:775-779` — `os.Lstat` on `reports` and `reports/<host>`, refuses `!IsDir()`, before any `MkdirAll` | yes |

### Report round 2 (`-security-015cf2d-012b4ca.md`)
| Claim | At HEAD | Whole? |
|---|---|---|
| F1 push to the URL, not origin | `report.go:851` — `gitOutC(dir, "push", "--quiet", "-u", url, "HEAD:main")`; no remote name decides the destination | yes |
| F2/F3 per-value JSON walk deleted | `report.go:149-181` `redactLines` — the walk is gone; `decoded()` (`191+`) is used for MATCHING only and the whole line goes. The retirement is stated in the doc-comment at `145-148` | yes — mechanism deleted, not patched |
| F4 origin not echoed | `report.go:589-592` — names the expected URL only, with the reason in a comment | yes |

### Embed / source (`-security-f7ee817-21ba8dc.md`)
| Claim | At HEAD | Whole? |
|---|---|---|
| F1 `TestEmbedHoldsOnlyTrackedFiles` | `embed_test.go:54`; skips explicitly without git or outside a checkout (`55-59`) | yes |
| F2 `knownCheckout` refuses `EmbeddedPrefix` | `source.go:42` defines it; `main.go:341` and `main.go:515` both `CutPrefix` before comparing paths; `repo.go:42` also excludes an embedded manifest from `ResolveSource`'s candidates | yes, at all three sites |
| F1's deferred release-time half (D23) | present in `remote.md` § Releases step 0 (`git status --porcelain --ignored --untracked-files=all -- context skills agents commands rules` + the test) | present but **mis-ordered** — Finding 1 |

### Clone / update (`-security-73f2c36-83f3cf6.md`)
| Claim | At HEAD | Whole? |
|---|---|---|
| F1 `RemoveKeptClone` fails closed | `report.go:558` `rev-list --count --all --not --remotes`; `509` `filepath.Abs(home)`; `538` `status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored` | yes |
| F2 `update --check` deletes nothing | read the whole function: the two `checkOnly` returns are `main.go:430` (`return nil`) and `435` (`exitCode(2)`); `RemoveKeptClone` is at `459`, below both, and below the dirty-tree guard as well (so a dirty checkout removes nothing either — fail-safe) | yes |
| F3 `sweepInterruptedClones` | defined `report.go:409`, called `report.go:701` at the start of the throwaway path | yes |
| F4 `scrubCredentials` | `report.go:494`, applied to both the URL and git's message at `472` | yes |
| F5 `LC_ALL=C` for the recognised message | `report.go:849-852` — `gitOutC` for that one push; the match covers `rejected` and `non-fast-forward` | yes |

### Release consumption (`-security-dab2565-4d45155.md`)
| Claim | At HEAD | Whole? |
|---|---|---|
| F1a tag validated before argv | `release.go:101-103` — `IsReleaseVersion(tag)` before the switch and before gh sees it | yes |
| F1b never backwards/sideways | `release.go:104-118` — `==` up to date; a non-release running binary left alone; `compareRelease < 0` refused | yes |
| F1c version inside the signed bytes | `release.go:47` `sumsVersionMarker`, checked `249-255` **after** `verify.Run()` at `243`. Nothing in the file is believed before the signature holds | yes, correctly ordered |
| F2 `sshKeygen` prefers a system path | `release.go:299-316` — `/usr/bin`, `/bin`, then PATH | yes |
| F3 random 0700 dir, stale siblings cleared | `release.go:138-147` — glob-and-remove `release-*`, then `os.MkdirTemp` | yes |
| F4 `checksumFor` strict | `release.go:272-295` — 64 chars, hex-only, refuses two DIFFERENT hashes, tolerates an exact duplicate | yes |
| F5 stderr captured | `release.go:190-209` — `strings.Builder` stderr; "no asset" distinguished by `os.Stat` | yes |
| F6 `readCapped` | `release.go:52-53` (256 MiB / 1 MiB), used at `203` and `222` | yes |

Two properties no prior report states, confirmed here: (a) `verifyRelease`'s
order is signature → version marker → checksum → byte compare, and the
downloaded bytes are never made executable or run until `writeAtomic`
(`release.go:165`), which runs only after `verifyRelease` returns nil — so the
`exec.Command(dest, "install")` at `172` cannot execute unverified bytes; (b) the
release branch of `update` passes only `installPassArgs(*homeFlag, home,
*vendorFlag)` — the operator's own flags — to the new binary, so no external
input reaches that argv.

## Part 2 — release-diff paths no security report names

`git diff v1.0.0..HEAD --name-only` (148 paths) minus every path and basename
appearing in the seven in-range `-security-*.md` reports leaves **97 paths, of
which none is Go source and none is a skill**: trail markdown
(`bugs/BUG-051..072`, `changes/`, `handoffs/`, `plans/`, `retros/`, non-security
`reviews/`, `testing/`) plus `ROADMAP.md` and three agent definitions
(`agents/changelog.md`, `documentation.md`, `verifier.md`). Every Go file in the
release diff is named by at least one prior security report whose tree is
byte-identical to HEAD. The uncovered paths were read for the surface that
applies to them — see Part 3.

## Part 3 — secrets, credentials, private data, instruction-shaped text

Added-line scan over the whole 13,690-line release diff for
`ghp_|gho_|ghs_|ghu_|github_pat_|glpat-|sk-ant-|sk-proj-|xox[baps]-|AKIA|ASIA|AIza|ya29.|GOCSPX-|-----BEGIN|PRIVATE KEY|BEGIN SSH SIGNATURE`
returns hits only inside redaction documentation and test-fixture discussion.
Every one is a deliberate placeholder or a vendor's published example:
`AKIAFAKEVALUE`, `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE` (AWS's own doc example), `ghs_FAKETOKEN`,
`FAKEVALUE`, `MIIEvFAKEbody`, and `secret123` (pre-existing in the vendored
`skills/terraform/references/security-compliance.md`, not added here).
**No live credential is added by this release.** No `.env`, `*.pem`, `*.key`,
`*.tfvars`, `*.tfstate` or credential JSON appears in the diff.

Two things that look like secrets and correctly are not:
- `release.go:39` and `remote.md` § Releases carry
  `ostling.simon@gmail.com ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3Nza…62NCR`. A PUBLIC key, and its
  presence IS the control — the allowed-signers line must be compiled in rather
  than read from disk. `release.go:26-38` says so, including what it does not
  pin (ssh-keygen itself).
- `remote.md` names the private key's PATH (`~/.ssh/id_ed25519`) and its
  fingerprint. A path and a fingerprint are not key material.

The signing procedure does not expose the key: `ssh-keygen -y -f
~/.ssh/id_ed25519 | ssh-keygen -lf - | cut -d' ' -f2` derives the PUBLIC
fingerprint for comparison, so the private half is never printed, never placed
in a variable and never written to a file; `tag -s` and `-Y sign` both take the
key by path. Nothing in the procedure prints anything sensitive. Finding 2
covers the one residue it leaves.

**Instruction-shaped text.** This release changes `context/AGENTS.md`, nine
skills and three agent definitions, plus ~90 trail files, all of which ship to
every machine that clones this repository — a real delivery vector, so it was
read for it. Nothing found that redirects an agent to exfiltrate data, reach the
network, touch `~/.ssh` or a real `$HOME`, weaken a permission setting, or treat
an agent message as consent. The changes are the operator's own harness rules
and they *strengthen* controls rather than relax any:
- `context/AGENTS.md` — BUG-058's rule that a finding counts as fixed only when
  every trigger it names has a test failing without the fix; the "second round
  on the same mechanism → stop and ask" rule; the stop-sign checklist after any
  dispatch that can write (`git status`/`log`/`tag`, BUG-044/045).
- `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` — stage by name, never `.env*`/`*.pem`/`*.key`/
  `*.tfvars`/`*.tfstate`/credential JSON, and `gitleaks git --staged` (with an
  explicit needle-scan fallback) refusing on a hit before the release commit.
- `agents/verifier.md`, `documentation.md`, `changelog.md` — guide-path change
  (ADR-032), app resolution (BUG-062), guide-write duty (BUG-063), and BUG-061's
  every-claim-traces-to-the-diff rule.
- **Checked specifically:** `--dangerously-skip-permissions`,
  `bypassPermissions` and `acceptEdits` appear **nowhere** in `skills/`,
  `context/`, `commands/`, `rules/`, `AGENTS.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md` or
  `testing/guide.md`. The flag occurs only inside dated testing logs under
  `.agents/docs/testing/`, each as a record that the operator approved it for
  specific Antigravity runs and that `settings.json` was not modified. Nothing
  prescribes it. No finding, but worth recording as an explicit negative
  because a prescribed bypass here would have shipped everywhere.

Related code check (no prior report covers it): `attributionSet`
(`main.go:615-701`) is the only vendor setting the installer writes. It is
unchanged in this release — only its call site moved into a helper — and it
cannot weaken an operator's `permissions` key: it writes only an ABSENT
`attribution` key, refuses a symlinked `settings.json` (`Lstat`), creates with
`O_EXCL` so a planted link between the two calls fails rather than being written
through, caps at 1 MiB, and inserts textually with a re-parse instead of
re-encoding the operator's file. `permissions` appears nowhere in the Go source.

## Part 4 — does the release procedure produce artifacts the shipping code accepts?

Traced end to end, `remote.md` § Releases against `release.go`. **It does.**

| Procedure produces | Code requires | Match |
|---|---|---|
| `printf '# styrman-harness %s\n' vX.Y.Z > SHA256SUMS` | `sumsVersionMarker` = `(?m)^#\s*styrman-harness\s+(v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)\s*$`, then `named == tag` | yes — regex checked against the exact literal emitted |
| `sha256sum <three binaries> >> SHA256SUMS` (two-space separator) | `checksumFor` cuts at the first space, `TrimSpace`s the name, strips a `*` | yes; the `#` marker line cannot be misread as a hash line (its name field never equals an asset name) |
| `ssh-keygen -Y sign -n sh-agent-release SHA256SUMS` | `ReleaseNamespace = "sh-agent-release"`, `-Y verify -n` the same | yes |
| signer line written to a local `allowed_signers` | `releaseSigner` compiled in; identity cut at the first space | yes — and the procedure states in as many words that its own file is only a pre-upload check |
| assets `sh-agent-{linux-amd64,darwin-arm64,linux-arm64}` | `AssetName(runtime.GOOS, runtime.GOARCH)` | yes for those three; any other host (e.g. darwin/amd64) gets the clean refusal `release vX.Y.Z has no sh-agent-<goos>-<goarch>` — a coverage gap, not a security defect |
| `-trimpath`, `CGO_ENABLED=0`, `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`, `-X main.version=vX.Y.Z` | `version` is what `UpdateFromRelease` compares; `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` is consistent with ADR-029's no-`toolchain`-directive decision | yes |
| `gh release create … --verify-tag` | n/a (publish side) | consistent |

The version marker is the one that mattered: a v1.0.0-era `SHA256SUMS` carries
no marker, so `update` correctly refuses it (`release.go:251`) — the procedure
is the only thing that can make a release installable, and it writes the line.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases (binaries block, step 0) and `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 6.4-6.5 — **the `go:embed` contamination guard runs after the tag is pushed, which is the one irreversible step.** The documented order is: clean-tree test → `git tag -s` → verify tag → `git push origin main` → `git push origin vX.Y.Z` → *then* `test -z "$(git status --porcelain --ignored --untracked-files=all -- context skills agents commands rules)"` and `go test -run TestEmbedHoldsOnlyTrackedFiles`. The skill encodes the same sequence (6.4 "Push the branch and the tag", 6.5 "Release ARTIFACTS") and even anticipates the failure: "stop with the tag pushed and say so". Exploitable in principle: an ignored or untracked file under the five embedded directories — `.gitignore` covers `.env`, which `all:` embeds, which is BUG-066's own reproduction — is compiled into every released binary, and the guard that catches it fires only once `vX.Y.Z` is public and, by this repo's own rule ("a pushed tag is never moved"), unrecallable. The guard does prevent PUBLISHING the contaminated binary, so no secret ships; the cost is a burnt version number and a tag with no assets. The earlier clean-tree test does **not** close this: `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` without `--ignored` cannot see an ignored file. Remediation: move step 0's two commands above the `git tag` line in `remote.md` § Releases — they read only the working tree and nothing the tag creates — and add one sentence to `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 6.5 saying a deploy guide's artifact PRECONDITIONS run before 6.3's tag, not with the build. No code change, no dependency.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases — **the procedure writes an `allowed_signers` file in two places and removes neither**, leaving `.agents/scratch/allowed_signers` behind after every release plus one in the build directory. This is not key material (a public key) and `.agents/scratch/` is gitignored, so it cannot be committed. It is worth a line because a signer file resting on disk is precisely the artifact `release.go:26-38` argues must never decide what a genuine release is, and a later reader who finds one may wire something to it. Confidence medium: a maintenance trap rather than a reachable weakness today. Remediation: append `rm -f .agents/scratch/allowed_signers` after the `verify-tag` line and `rm -f allowed_signers` after the pre-upload `-Y verify`, each with its one-line reason.

No high or medium findings. Neither finding blocks the gate.

## Checked

- **Secrets** — added-line scan of the full release diff (13,690 lines) for 19 vendor token prefixes, PEM headers and SSH signature armor: all hits are documented fake fixtures or a vendor's published example. The compiled-in and documented `ssh-ed25519` line is a public key and is the control. The operator's email appears as the signer identity, which is its purpose. No secret-shaped path in the diff.
- **Injection** — the release path's only external inputs are gh's tag string and the release assets. The tag is regex-gated to `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+$` before reaching argv (`release.go:101`), so no `-`-leading or shell-meaningful tag survives; asset names derive from `runtime.GOOS`/`GOARCH`, not input. `SHA256SUMS` parsing is length- and charset-strict and refuses ambiguity instead of resolving it. Every git and gh call is `exec.Command` with separate args — no shell anywhere in the codebase. `hostDir` reduces a hostname to one path element; `runDir` `Lstat`-refuses a non-directory `reports`/`reports/<host>`; `Source.readRegular` refuses a symlink or non-regular file, and embed cannot store a link.
- **Authz/authn** — no endpoints, no request handling. The two authorization decisions that exist are "is this release the operator's" (compiled-in allowed-signers line + namespace + in-signature version marker) and "is this checkout the feedback repository" (`verifyFeedback` + pushing to the URL literally). Both fail closed: a failed `gitOut` yields `""`, which never equals the expected URL.
- **Crypto** — nothing hand-rolled, and nothing in this release comes close. `crypto/sha256` used as a checksum (`release.go:260`); signature verification delegated to OpenSSH's `ssh-keygen -Y verify`; transport is git over SSH. No cipher, MAC, KDF, RNG, token format, session or auth flow is implemented or composed here. The one place a home-grown construction could have crept in — binding a version to signed bytes — is solved by requiring a comment line INSIDE the signed file rather than by inventing a signature format, which is the correct answer.
- **Dependencies** — `go.mod` requires nothing beyond the stdlib (the repo's stdlib-only rule) and this release adds none. `govulncheck ./...` on go1.27.1: **"No vulnerabilities found."** `gofmt -l cmd internal *.go` clean; `go vet ./...` clean. No npm ecosystem in the repo, so `npm audit` does not apply — not faked, simply absent.
- **GCP surface** — none. No IAM binding, service account, `--allow-unauthenticated`, Cloud Run flag, Secret Manager reference or service-account key file anywhere in the release diff. The only remote service is GitHub, reached via `gh` (carrying the operator's own credential, deliberate per R8/D7) and git over SSH.

`internal/harness/source.go` (all 86), `internal/harness/report.go` lines 1-200
(the redaction walk), `internal/harness/repo.go` lines 1-70 (`ResolveSource`,
`IsRepo`), `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` lines 180-215, 420-475 and 612-701,

all nine changed skills.

fix present and whole", but NOT a full re-review:
`internal/harness/report.go` lines 200-860 (guard lines of `Collect`,
`BuildRecord`, `cloneThrowaway`, `commitAndPush`, `RemoveKeptClone` read; their
full control flow not re-traced), the remainder of `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` and

`render.go` (only their `EmbeddedPrefix`/`secretShaped` sites). All are named by

Not read, and therefore named rather than cleared:

title: Review — audit fix round, 160aa16..3209cf3 (2026-09-18)
body:
# Review — audit fix round, 160aa16..3209cf3   (2026-09-18)

Range reviewed: 160aa16..3209cf3 (`git diff 160aa16..3209cf3 -- . ':!.agents/docs'`)
Map: `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-18-review-harness-merged.md` §§ Findings, Outcome — 19 findings, 15 marked fixed here, 2 left by decision, 2 to `documentation`.

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Every fix marked **fixed** in the merged record is present, does what the record claims, and is covered by a test. Nothing in the diff is wrong for the platforms this project ships (Linux, macOS). The worst item is a portability regression that is invisible here: `internal/harness/pathguard.go` now imports `syscall` and dereferences `syscall.Stat_t`, so `GOOS=windows go build ./...` fails at head where it succeeded at 160aa16 — no Windows asset is built or supported, so this is a nit, not a blocker. The remaining items are advisory-message and lifecycle edges, all low.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/pathguard.go:8,142` — `syscall.Stat_t` is not defined on Windows; `GOOS=windows go build ./...` fails at head (`undefined: syscall.Stat_t`) and succeeded at 160aa16 (verified by building a `git archive` of the base under `.agents/scratch/rev-base`). `os.Getuid()` also returns `-1` there, so even a compiling variant would read every file as not-owned. No Windows asset exists (`AssetName` is called with `runtime.GOOS` only; the operator is macOS/Linux), so this costs nothing today. Fix, if portability is wanted: put `ownedByCaller` in `pathguard_unix.go` (`//go:build unix`) with a `pathguard_other.go` returning `true`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/pathguard.go:118` — `filepath.Clean(real) != filepath.Clean(home)` is a *lexical* identity test for a directory. `$HOME` with a trailing slash is handled (both sides are Cleaned, and `run` now runs `filepath.Abs`), but a symlinked home is not: with `$HOME=/home/x` symlinked to `/data/x`, `sh-agent update --home /data/x` suppresses the note although that *is* the real home. `$HOME` unset likewise suppresses it (`os.UserHomeDir` errors). Both are false negatives on an advisory line, never wrong advice, so the failure mode is benign — but `os.SameFile` on `os.Stat(real)` and `os.Stat(home)` is the correct identity for "the same directory" and is the same three lines.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/pathguard.go:131` — `ownedByCaller` answers "do I own this file", but the question the remedy asks is "can I replace this name". `ln -sfn` needs write on `filepath.Dir(from)`, not ownership of `from`; and `os.Lstat` deliberately stats the symlink, whose uid is not what governs the relink either. Two skews follow: a caller-owned file in a root-owned directory still gets "point it at the installed binary (`ln -sfn`)", which will fail with EPERM, and the old text's "when that path is root-owned, prefer removing it" hint is gone from that branch. Advisory only; the fix is `unix.Access(filepath.Dir(from), W_OK)` or simply keeping the old root-owned clause in the owned branch.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/apply.go:223-226` — `Diff` is a report-only verb, and it now creates `~/.config/sh-agent` (`MkdirAll`) as a side effect, inside the per-file loop, whenever a file differs. On a home the caller cannot write, `sh-agent diff` now returns an error where it previously produced output via `/tmp`. The global rule "a new side effect goes BELOW a read-only mode's early returns" points the other way. Low because the directory is this tool's own, the mkdir is skipped entirely when there is no drift, and every real place has that directory already.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/apply.go:230-233` — `Diff` returns without `os.Remove(tmp.Name())` when `tmp.Write` fails (pre-existing shape, new consequence): the orphan now lands in `~/.config/sh-agent/` rather than `/tmp`, and nothing ever sweeps it — `UpdateFromRelease`'s stale-sweep globs `release-*` only, so a `sh-agent-diff-*` file accumulates in the operator's config directory. `defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())` inside the loop body (or a small closure) closes it.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/source.go:54-65`, `internal/harness/repo.go:34` — informational, as the dispatch asks. A binary stamped `v1.02.2` is now `IsReleaseVersion == false` everywhere. `ResolveSource` therefore treats it as a *development build* and looks for a tree on disk (`--repo`, `$SH_AGENT_REPO`, the walk, the recorded repo) instead of installing its embedded harness — the exact silent-tree behaviour ADR-034 forbids for a release binary. `report` (`main.go:312`) falls to `ResolveSource` and, if that errors, sends a record with a zero `Source` (the BUG-077 null shape); `status`/`version` (`releaseFromInfo`, `main.go:933`) fall back to the VCS stamp. All unreachable in practice: `/preflight` cuts canonical `vX.Y.Z` tags, and Go itself refuses a non-canonical module version, so `info.Main.Version` cannot carry one. No change requested — recorded so the next reader of `ResolveSource` knows the release branch is gated on a *canonical* spelling now.

## Verification of each point the dispatch named

- **`IsReleaseVersion`'s int-fit loop** — correct and the check is necessary-but-narrow. The regex `^v(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$` admits only ASCII digits, no sign, no leading zero, no empty component, so `strconv.Atoi` can fail for exactly one reason: `ErrRange` (a component wider than `int`). Confirmed — `Atoi`'s other error, `ErrSyntax`, needs a non-digit, a sign or an empty string, none of which survive the regex. The loop is therefore the overflow guard finding 6 asked for, and it makes `releaseParts`' silent `[3]int{}` fallback unreachable from `compareRelease` (both arguments are validated before that call), which is what the finding was about.
- **`compareRelease(tag, version) <= 0` — is the equal case reachable?** No. `UpdateFromRelease`'s switch tests `tag == version` first, and by the time the third case runs both strings have passed `IsReleaseVersion`, i.e. both are canonical; canonical spelling is a bijection with the numeric triple, so `compareRelease == 0` implies `tag == version`, already returned. The `<=` is defence in depth with no live branch — harmless, and the wording change ("is not newer than") is accurate for the branch that does fire. Note this means the `<=` half of fix 6 is carried entirely by the canonical regex; the test `TestNonCanonicalTagNeverReachesTheDownload` asserts the right thing (the tag never reaches the download) rather than the equality.
- **Callers of `IsReleaseVersion` that now see `false`** — enumerated: `release.go:102` (tag from the GitHub API → refusal naming the tag, correct), `release.go:113` (running version → "not a release; leaving it alone", correct), `repo.go:34` `ResolveSource`, `main.go:312` `report`, `main.go:933` `releaseFromInfo`. The last three are the low finding above.
- **`NoteRunningElsewhere`'s home compare** — see the two low findings. `$HOME` unset → suppressed; trailing slash → handled; symlinked home → false negative.
- **`ownedByCaller` on macOS** — compiles. `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 go build ./...` succeeds at head; `syscall.Stat_t` on darwin carries `Uid uint32`, so `int(st.Uid)` is correct there. The release cross-build is safe.
- **`Diff`'s `MkdirAll(…, 0o700)` over an existing 0755 dir** — fine. `MkdirAll` returns nil and does not chmod an existing directory, so a pre-existing `~/.config/sh-agent` keeps 0755; the rendered harness is protected by `os.CreateTemp`'s own 0600 on the file, and the same non-enforcement already exists at `release.go:136`. No finding.
- **`filepath.Abs(home)` at `main.go:105-107`** — placed after the `--home`/`os.UserHomeDir` resolution and before every consumer, so `ResolveSource`, `knownCheckout`, `samePath`, `installPassArgs`, `Reinstall` and `NoteRunningElsewhere` all see the same absolute, Cleaned path. No comparison is weakened: `samePath` and `knownCheckout` compare *repo* paths, not the home, and `st.Repo` is unaffected; the home was previously passed through verbatim, so anything that already worked with an absolute home is unchanged and only the relative case moves (which is BUG-080's point). `err != nil` from `Abs` leaves `home` as it was — `Abs` fails only when `os.Getwd` fails, and falling through with the relative path is the old behaviour, not a new hazard.
- **The `readSettings` bound vs `attributionOff`** — correct and this is the fix's whole value: `attributionOff` (`main.go:890`) now inherits the size check, so `attributionHint` — the `status` path — reports an oversized settings file instead of silently reading its first megabyte and judging truncated JSON. `attributionSet`'s own `case info.Size() > 1<<20` is gone and the `!IsRegular` arm's comment was updated to say so. One behaviour delta worth naming and correct as chosen: `install` no longer prints its own "larger than 1 MiB" line, it now returns silently and `attributionHint` prints the single shared note.
- **`plainCopyOf`** — see § Tests.
- **`scratchClone`** — see § Tests.

## Tests

`gofmt -l cmd internal` clean, `go vet ./...` clean, `go test ./...` and `go test -race ./...` both green (three packages). Every new test was read and traced to the behaviour it pins; each would fail against a revert:

- `TestIsReleaseVersionIsCanonical` covers all three leading-zero spellings, the overflow case (`v99999999999999999999.0.0`, the only input the regex admits and `Atoi` rejects) and four negatives — it fails on the old regex.
- `TestNonCanonicalTagNeverReachesTheDownload` asserts the refusal, that the installed binary's bytes are unchanged, and that no `release-*` directory exists — the strongest of the set, because it pins "never reached the download" and not just the message.
- `TestNoteRunningElsewhereOnlyForTheRealHome` drives both arms (`$HOME` elsewhere → silence; `$HOME == home` → the note) with a real symlink on a real `PATH`. `TestOwnedByCaller` covers own uid, another uid, and the no-`Stat_t` fallback; a typed-nil `(*syscall.Stat_t)(nil)` is handled by the code and not exercised, which is fine.
- `TestAdoptStripsGroupAndOtherWrite` and `TestThrowawayParentIsPrivate` both defeat umask correctly (an explicit `os.Chmod` after `WriteFile`; `0o700 &^ 022` is still `0700`) and both skip under root, which is the honest thing to do.
- `TestDiffUsesTheHomeNotTmp` points `TMPDIR` at a non-existent directory, so it fails on the old `os.CreateTemp("")`, and additionally asserts no `sh-agent-diff-*` is left behind. `TestCellIsRuneSafe` sweeps `max` from 5 to 119 over an 81-rune string, crossing both branches of the cut. `TestYamlQuoteEscapesControlCharacters` carries the literal `\u0001` escape in its expectation (the BUG-057 hazard the Outcome names) — confirmed present as two characters in the source, not as the control byte.
- CLI side: `TestUpdateOnPlainCopyNamesTheAlternative`, `TestAdoptOnPlainCopySaysWhereToCommit`, `TestAdoptOnReleaseBinaryNamesTheAlternative`, `TestStatusOnPlainCopyNamesTheRefusal`, `TestSyncIsInstall`, `TestDiffVerbShowsDrift`, `TestStatusWarnsOnOversizedSettings` and `TestRelativeHomeResolvesAgainstTheInvokingDirectory` close exactly the four recon gaps plus findings 2, 8, 10, 11. The BUG-080 test asserts both halves — the install landed under the invoking directory AND no `rel-home` appeared inside the repository — which is what makes it a regression test rather than a happy-path one. `TestAttributionSet`'s changed assertion traces to the source change (the bound moved into `readSettings`, so install now emits the shared `attributionHint` note instead of its own `settings:` line) — a legitimate expectation change, not a loosened one.

### The two new fixtures

- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go:1596-1629` `plainCopyOf` — correct today and fragile tomorrow. `filepath.WalkDir` does not follow symlinks and reports one with `d.IsDir() == false`, so the body calls `os.ReadFile` on it; a symlink to a directory then fails with EISDIR and the helper `t.Fatal`s with a raw errno. Verified there is no symlink anywhere under `context/ skills/ agents/ commands/ rules/` today (`find … -type l` is empty) — the repo's symlink is `.agents/skills → skills/`, which is outside the five walked roots, and `skills/` itself is a real directory, exactly as the dispatch supposed. The fragility is real though: `AGENTS.md` invites `npx skills add` to land third-party skills in `skills/`, and one containing a symlink would break three CLI tests with a message that names neither the symlink nor the helper. One line closes it: skip `!d.Type().IsRegular()` entries, or copy the link with `os.Readlink`/`os.Symlink`.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go:1631-1652` `scratchClone` — **no risk to this checkout**, as the dispatch supposed, and worth recording why. `git clone <src> <dst>` only reads the source: it opens refs and objects, takes no lock on the source worktree, and writes nothing there. Its local-transport optimisation hardlinks `.git/objects/**` into the clone, which is safe because git treats loose objects and packs as immutable (mode 0444, content-addressed, never rewritten in place); a later `git gc` inside the clone or the `t.TempDir()` cleanup only drops a link, leaving the source's own link and refcount intact. The clone's environment is scrubbed of `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR` and every `GIT_CONFIG*` (`gitCleanEnv` plus `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`), so no ambient variable can redirect the clone's writes back at this repository — the BUG-045 shape (a probe repository whose commands fell through to the real one) is guarded against, not merely avoided by luck. The test that uses it then rebuilds with `go build` inside the clone; nothing it does reaches `../..`. Both `git` and `go` are checked with `LookPath` and the test skips without them.

## Criteria

1. **Dead code** — pass with one note. `releaseParts`' `return [3]int{}` on `Atoi` failure is now unreachable from `compareRelease`; it is a two-line defensive fallback in an unexported helper, not a finding. The duplicated comment at `main.go:557-562` was removed (finding 18). The seven copies of the settings format string collapsed into `settingsUnwritable` (finding 12) with no call site left behind — grep confirms five uses and no stragglers.
2. **Flow tracing** — pass. Each changed declaration was re-read with its callers: `IsReleaseVersion` (5 call sites, all enumerated above), `compareRelease`/`releaseParts`, `NoteRunningElsewhere` (2 call sites: `release.go:178`, `main.go:522`, both after a binary was written), `readSettings` (2 callers: `attributionSet`, `attributionOff`), `settingsUnwritable` (5), `ownedByCaller` (1), `copyTree`, `cell`, `yamlQuote`, `Diff`, `cloneThrowaway`, `errPlainCopy`. `home` after `filepath.Abs` traced through `run`'s whole switch. No stub, no caller left on an old signature; no signature changed.
3. **Standards conformance** — pass. `gofmt -l cmd internal` clean; `go vet ./...` clean. Errors are returned, not swallowed; the two new bare `return err`s (`apply.go:225`, from `MkdirAll`) carry the syscall's own path in the message. The describing-text rule holds: `attributionSet`'s `!IsRegular` comment was updated in the same hunk that moved the bound, `readSettings`' doc-comment now says "read or rewrite", and `errPlainCopy`'s new text is mirrored in README and the delivery spec by the `documentation` fixes in the same commit. Stdlib only; no new dependency.
4. **Directory layout** — pass. `ownedByCaller` sits beside `NoteRunningElsewhere` in `pathguard.go`; `settingsUnwritable` beside `abandonTemp` in `main.go`; the new tests beside the code (`internal/harness/audit_test.go`, `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go`). The one layout question the audit raised — the ~220-line settings editor in the entrypoint (finding 5) — is explicitly **left** by the main agent's decision, recorded in the merged record's Outcome, and is not re-litigated here.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security)** — pass. No hand-rolled primitive or protocol: the release path still verifies through `ssh-keygen` and `crypto/sha256` used as designed. `yamlQuote`'s `\uXXXX` escaping is string rendering, not crypto. Every fix is smaller or the same size as what it replaced except `yamlQuote` (+19 lines, buying a strict-parser guarantee the two `ReplaceAll`s did not give) and `NoteRunningElsewhere` (+ownership branch, which finding 7 asked for).
6. **Decoupling** — pass. No new cross-package reach-in; `ownedByCaller` is unexported and consumed where it is declared; `settingsUnwritable` is a private helper in the entrypoint. `internal/harness` gained no dependency on `cmd/`.

## Not examined

- `.agents/docs/**` — excluded from the range by the dispatch's own pathspec; the merged record was read as the map, not reviewed.
- The `documentation` fixes (3, 4, 19) are in `README.md` within this range, and README was read in full and is consistent with the code (the `keep` line, the `knownCheckout` refusal, the canonical-tag wording, the "not newer than" message, `diff`'s new temp location, the oversized-settings note, both `adopt` messages). `delivery.md`, `local.md` and `remote.md` live under `.agents/docs`, excluded by the dispatch's pathspec, and were NOT read here — the docs lens (`reviews/2026-09-18-review-160aa16-3209cf3-docs.md`) reports them clean over the same range; that is its verdict, not mine.
- A repo-wide grep for the superseded wordings ("is older than this binary", "commit and push the repo", the old `adopt` refusal, the old 1 MiB line) found only append-only trail (`testing/2026-09-17-release-binary-e2e.md:73` quotes what a past run printed) and the audit reports themselves — no live restatement left standing. `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/`, `rules/` and `context/` are untouched by this range and were not otherwise reviewed.
- Nothing was run on macOS: the darwin claim is a successful `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 go build ./...` cross-compile here, not a darwin test run.
- `govulncheck` was not run (no network in this dispatch).

## Outcome

Written by the main agent after round 2 of the Phase 2 fix round, in its commit.

- [low] `syscall.Stat_t` broke `GOOS=windows go build ./...` — **fixed**: `ownedByCaller` lives in `owned_unix.go` (`//go:build unix`, internal/harness/owned_unix.go:17) with a `!unix` twin that reads every file as owned (internal/harness/owned_other.go:8); `GOOS=windows go build ./...` and `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 go build ./...` both succeed. (`GOOS=windows go vet` still fails on a pre-existing `syscall.Mkfifo` in `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` — tests, not the build; not in scope.)
- [low] lexical home compare misses a symlinked `$HOME` — **fixed**: `os.SameFile` on the two directories (internal/harness/pathguard.go:123); `TestNoteRunningElsewhereThroughASymlinkedHome` (internal/harness/audit_test.go:235); a mutation back to `Clean` fails it.
- [low] `Diff` leaks its temp file on a write error — **fixed**: `diffOne` removes it with a `defer` on every path (internal/harness/apply.go:242).
