title: Review — 42840fb..30f7488 (release gate v1.2.3, the one uncovered commit)
body:
# Review — 42840fb..30f7488 (release gate v1.2.3, the one uncovered commit)

Range reviewed: `git diff 42840fb..30f7488 -- . ':!.agents/docs'` — `internal/harness/state.go`, `internal/harness/audit_test.go`, `README.md` (HEAD 30f7488, tree frozen and clean).

## Verdict: APPROVE

Nothing in this commit is broken. The two `note:` lines are pure output on paths that already returned without touching anything; the guard order is correct, the new note is pinned by a test that fails without it, and both README restatements match the code. The one thing worth recording is a sentence in `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` that the earlier symlink guard (42840fb) made inaccurate and that this commit's README rewording did not carry over — low severity, docs-only, not a release blocker.

## Answers to the gate's questions

1. **Can a regular FILE at that path fall into a note that calls it a directory?** No. `state.go:105` (`if !info.IsDir() || info.Mode().Perm()&0o077 == 0 { return }`) runs *before* the not-owned note at `state.go:108-111`, so a plain file returns silently; the `%04o` note is reached only for a real directory. One residual edge: a **symlink** is noted at `state.go:100-103` before the `IsDir` test, so a symlink pointing at a regular file (or a dangling one) prints "its target's mode is yours to set". The text is imprecise there, but the ordering is deliberate and correct — `Lstat` cannot see through the link and `Stat`-ing it would be the reach-through the guard exists to avoid. The subsequent install failure on such a path (`ConfigDir` → `os.MkdirAll` returns `ENOTDIR`/`EEXIST`) is pre-existing behaviour from before this range, unchanged by the diff, and not a finding against it.
2. **Does the symlink note print on a dry run?** Yes, and it should: `state.go:100-103` returns before the `dryRun` check at `state.go:114`, so a dry run prints the note and changes nothing. Consistent with the `mode` line, which a dry run also names (`audit_test.go:246-266`).
3. **Can either note print more than once per install?** No — one call site, one per process. `TightenConfigDir` is called only from `apply.go:30` inside `Install`; `Install` is called once per command from `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:286` (`installFiles`), which itself has two mutually exclusive call sites (`main.go:145` release-binary path returns; `main.go:182` checkout/plain-copy path). On the rebuild path the parent returns `harness.Reinstall(...)` at `main.go:173` without reaching `installFiles`, so the child prints the note exactly once and the parent prints none.
4. **Is `%04o` of an unowned dir an information leak?** No. The value is the permission bits of a directory under the home the caller passed, which any process that can `Lstat` the path can already read; it carries no content, no owner uid, no path beyond the fixed literal `~/.config/sh-agent`. Naming the mode is what makes the "ask its owner for 0700" advice actionable. No finding.
5. **Is README's clause true to the code?** Yes. Tightening requires: not a symlink (`state.go:100`), a directory with group/other bits set (`state.go:105`), and owned by the caller (`state.go:108`). "when it is yours and not a symlink" names exactly the two conditions that can produce a refusal, and "(either case gets a `note:` instead)" is true of both — symlink at `state.go:101`, not-owned at `state.go:109`. The unstated conditions (already 0700, or not a directory at all) are silent no-ops that the sentence does not claim anything about. Both occurrences (README.md:74 and the install row, README.md:162) carry the identical clause.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md:51` — "`~/.config/sh-agent/` is created 0700 and every install tightens it to 0700 when it is looser and the directory is the caller's own" is now false for a symlinked runtime dir whose target is looser and is the caller's own: `state.go:100-103` declines and notes instead. The condition landed in 42840fb and this commit is the one that reworded both twin sentences in `README.md` without carrying the change here (review-standards § 3, the every-restatement rule; the repo's own BUG-003/007/027 family). Fix: append the symlink case and the two notes, e.g. "… when it is looser, is a real directory and is the caller's own; a symlinked or foreign-owned directory gets a `note:` and is left alone." Docs-only, no behaviour at risk — safe to fold into the next docs pass rather than block v1.2.3.

## Criteria
1. **Dead code** — pass. Nothing added is unreferenced; nothing was left behind. The refactor split one compound `if` into three guards with no orphaned branch: every guard is reachable (`err != nil`, symlink, non-dir/already-tight, not-owned, tighten).
2. **Flow tracing** — pass. Single caller (`apply.go:30`), single process per install (question 3 above). The function returns nothing and writes only to the `io.Writer` the caller already passes, so no error path, no resource, no caller signature changed. The new test at `audit_test.go:294-296` fails if the note is reverted (the string exists only in `state.go:101`); the not-owned note has no test and cannot get one without a second uid — that gap is already recorded honestly in `reviews/2026-09-18-security-e7fec88-42840fb.md:333`, so the coverage claim is not overstated.
3. **Standards conformance** — one low finding above. Otherwise pass: `gofmt -l cmd internal` silent, `go vet ./...` clean, `go test -run TestInstallMakesTheConfigDirPrivate -count=1 ./internal/harness/` ok; the doc-comment at `state.go:85-92` still describes the behaviour it guards; the `note:` prefix matches install's existing convention (`apply.go:56`). No `REQUIREMENTS.md` clause touched — R4's "never changes another key" and R6's scratch-home rule are unaffected; no recorded bug reintroduced.
4. **Directory layout** — pass. Code in `internal/harness/state.go`, its test beside it in the same package, README at the root. No new files.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security)** — pass. Two `fmt.Fprintf` calls and an `if` split; stdlib only, no dependency, no abstraction. No primitive or protocol implemented here; `os.Lstat`/`os.Chmod`/uid comparison via `ownedByCaller` is filesystem permission handling, not hand-rolled crypto or auth.
6. **Decoupling** — pass. `TightenConfigDir`'s signature is unchanged, so `apply.go` and `cmd/` are untouched by this commit; the ownership test stays behind the build-tag split (`owned_unix.go` / `owned_other.go`) and is not reached into.

## Not examined
- The other nine commits in `v1.2.2..30f7488`: covered by the existing reports named in the dispatch, read only as far as the one `Outcome` line cited above.
- `.agents/docs/**` in this range (excluded by the dispatch's pathspec), except `specs/sh-agent/delivery.md:51` and the security report line read for the coverage claim.
- Runtime behaviour on a not-owned directory and on a symlink-to-file: reasoned from the code, not executed (both need a second uid or a deliberately broken home; no install into a real `$HOME` was attempted, per the dispatch's hard limits). The full suite (`go test -race ./...`) was not run here — the verifier's Phase 2/3 logs cover it at this tree.

title: Review — BUG-078 PATH-shadow guard, round 2 (4cdc0b5..8ce58a0)
body:
# Review — BUG-078 PATH-shadow guard, round 2 (4cdc0b5..8ce58a0)

Range reviewed: 4cdc0b5..8ce58a0

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

Both round-1 findings are genuinely fixed and well tested (verified by reading the code and by re-running the test suite): the two-definitions-of-"on PATH" split between `binOnPath`/`PathShadows` is gone (one function, one walk), and hard links are now correctly recognised as "not a shadow" via `os.SameFile`. But the fix introduces a new instance of the exact class of bug round 1 flagged, now *inside* `PathShadows` itself: the function uses two different notions of "reaches the same binary" in the same walk — a strict lexical `filepath.Clean(dir) == binDir` string comparison to decide `onPath` (pathguard.go:29), and `os.SameFile` identity (which follows symlinks) to decide "not a shadow" (pathguard.go:49). When PATH reaches the bin dir only through a symlinked directory component (e.g. `~/bin -> ~/.local/bin`, a common dotfiles/devbox pattern — exactly the kind of aliasing that caused the original BUG-078 incident), `PathShadows` correctly finds an earlier real shadow but returns `onPath=false`, and `status`'s report is gated by `if onPath` (main.go:390) — so the genuine shadow is computed and then silently dropped, never printed. I reproduced this with a standalone repro against the built package (see below): `shadows=[.../earlier/sh-agent]`, `onPath=false`. This is the identical failure mode ("status reported drift none/nothing about a binary the shell does not run") the whole change exists to close, just moved one level down.

## Reproduction

```go
// PATH: earlier/sh-agent (a real, different shadowing binary), then an
// alias directory that is a symlink to the real bin dir (not the bin dir's
// own literal path).
shadows, onPath := harness.PathShadows(path, target)
// shadows: [/tmp/.../earlier/sh-agent]   <- correctly found
// onPath:  false                         <- wrong; PATH does reach target here
```
`status`'s shadow loop (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go:389-393`) only runs `if onPath`, so in this state it prints nothing — no `shadowed` line — even though a real, earlier shadow was found and is sitting in the `shadows` slice the same call just returned.

## Findings

- **[high / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/pathguard.go:29` vs `:49` (`PathShadows`), gated by `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:390` (`status`) — `onPath` is decided by lexical `filepath.Clean` string equality on the PATH entry's directory, which does not follow a symlinked directory component, while "is this candidate the same binary" is decided by `os.SameFile`, which does. A PATH entry that reaches the installed binary only via a symlinked directory (not the binary's own literal directory string) makes `PathShadows` return `onPath=false` even when it has just correctly found and populated `shadows` with an earlier, genuine shadow — and `status`'s entire shadow-report loop is gated on `onPath`, so the warning is silently dropped. Reproduced live (see above). Fix: derive `onPath` from whatever the function's own loop actually used to decide "this entry reaches the target" — i.e., set `onPath = true` whenever the loop reaches the end of PATH having found (via `executableAt` + `SameFile`) that some entry *is* the target file, not only when the entry's raw directory string equals `binDir`. This is the same root cause round 1 named for `binOnPath`/`PathShadows` (two disagreeing definitions of "reaches the target"), now internal to one function instead of split across two.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/pathguard_test.go` — no test covers a PATH entry reaching the bin dir through a symlinked directory (only a symlinked *binary file* is tested, pathguard_test.go:287). The finding above would have been caught by such a case.

## Round-1 findings verified fixed

- Two definitions of "on PATH" (`binOnPath` vs `PathShadows`'s `Clean` comparison): **fixed** at the surface level — `binOnPath`, `shadows`, `shadowHint` deleted; both `pathHint` and `status` now read one `PathShadows` call (main.go:390, main.go:648). `grep -rn 'ResolveExecutable|binOnPath|shadowHint' --include=*.go --include=*.md .` returns nothing outside dated trail docs under `.agents/docs/reviews/` and `.agents/docs/testing/`, which is expected. See above for the residual, narrower recurrence inside the consolidated function.
- Hard link wrongly reported as shadow: **fixed and tested**. `os.SameFile` on `os.Stat` results correctly identifies hard links; `pathguard_test.go:315` ("a hard link to the installed binary is not a shadow") passes.
- README "for an hour" claim: **fixed**, now says "installed a stale tree this way and every command said it had succeeded (BUG-078)" (README.md:124), consistent with the bug record's root cause.

## Verification performed

- `gofmt -l cmd internal` — clean.
- `go vet ./...` — clean.
- `go test -race ./internal/harness/... ./cmd/sh-agent/...` — all pass.
- `go.mod` `go 1.24.4` — satisfies `t.Chdir` (added Go 1.24), used by the new empty-PATH-entry test case.
- `grep -rn 'ResolveExecutable\|binOnPath\|shadowHint' --include=*.go --include=*.md .` — only dated trail files under `.agents/docs/reviews/` and `.agents/docs/testing/` remain; no leftover source or living-doc reference.
- Confirmed `strings` import in `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` is still used elsewhere (not left orphaned by the `TrimSuffix` removal).

## Criteria

1. **Dead code** — pass. `binOnPath`, `shadows`, `shadowHint`, and the old injected `resolve`/`ResolveExecutable` are all gone with no remaining references; nothing orphaned.
2. **Flow tracing** — fail: see the high finding. `PathShadows` → `status`'s `if onPath` gate is a broken hop for symlinked-directory PATH entries; `pathHint`'s `switch` degrades more gracefully in the same situation (falls into the `case len(shadows) > 0` branch and still prints a mislabeled but present warning), so only `status` silently loses the signal entirely.
3. **Standards conformance** — pass. gofmt/vet/test clean; comments describing the guarantee were updated to match the new single-function design; message strings match doc quotes in README/remote.md/local.md.
4. **Directory layout** — pass, no change from round 1.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security)** — pass, and improved: dropping the injected `resolve` function in favor of directly calling `os.Stat`/`os.SameFile` is a net simplification with no loss of testability (tests build real files instead of a fake).
6. **Decoupling** — weak, and this is the root of the new finding: `PathShadows` now internally conflates two different equivalence relations ("same literal directory" vs "same file by identity") without them agreeing, which is the same shape of bug round 1 flagged between two separate functions. Fix on the finding above resolves this too.

## Not examined

- The security-review round from round 1 (`.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-18-security-4cdc0b5-52574a0.md`) was not re-run against this diff; only the code reviewer's findings were re-verified here, per the dispatch brief.
- `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-18-verify-bug078-path-shadow.md` and `...-2.md` are untracked (not part of `4cdc0b5..8ce58a0`) and were not read in full; only grepped for leftover-name references.
- Did not test on macOS; PATH/symlink semantics were verified only on this Linux box, matching the deploy docs' own Linux-first verification story.
- The `~` / unexpanded env-var PATH-entry forms named in the dispatch were reasoned through, not found to independently cause a masked shadow (an unexpanded `~` or `$VAR` component resolves to nothing real for either the shell or `PathShadows`, so both agree it is not "on PATH" — no divergence). The symlinked-directory form is the one that does diverge, and is the finding above.

## Outcome

Written by the main agent after the round-3 change, in its commit. This was the second round to land on the same mechanism — how "on PATH" is decided — so under the context's Definition of Done rule the mechanism was put to the operator rather than patched again. Their choice: define it by the one identity the rest of the walk already uses.

- [high] lexical `onPath` vs `os.SameFile` disagree on a symlinked directory — **fixed** by deleting the lexical comparison rather than extending it: the walk now stops at the first PATH entry whose `sh-agent` IS the installed file by `os.SameFile` (internal/harness/pathguard.go:48); `filepath.Clean` no longer appears in the file, and the doc-comment says why (internal/harness/pathguard.go:12). A missing installed file now yields `onPath == false` with every executable of that name a shadow, which is the correct reading and is asserted (internal/harness/pathguard_test.go:348). Must-fail: identity by path string in place of `SameFile` fails `TestPathShadows`.
- [low] no test for a symlinked directory on PATH — **fixed**: two cases, the round-2 repro with an earlier shadow (internal/harness/pathguard_test.go:329) and the alias first (internal/harness/pathguard_test.go:330).

title: Review — BUG-078 PATH-shadow guard, round 3 (final, 4cdc0b5..b029ea1)
body:
# Review — BUG-078 PATH-shadow guard, round 3 (final, 4cdc0b5..b029ea1)

Range reviewed: 4cdc0b5..b029ea1 (round 3's own delta is 8ce58a0..b029ea1: `internal/harness/pathguard.go`, `internal/harness/pathguard_test.go`, `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` comments only, plus README.md and remote.md install-block formatting)

## Verdict: APPROVE

The round-2 high finding — `onPath` decided by a lexical `filepath.Clean(dir) == binDir` comparison while "is this a shadow" was decided by `os.SameFile` identity, so a PATH entry reaching the bin dir only through a symlinked directory made a real shadow silently disappear from `status`'s report — is fixed correctly and completely, per the operator's directive to stop patching the mechanism and define "on PATH" by one identity. The lexical comparison is deleted outright rather than extended; the walk now has exactly one notion of "reaches the target" (`os.SameFile` on `os.Stat` results), used for both halves of the return value. This closes the class of bug, not just the reported instance.

## Findings

None. No correctness, security, or requirements-violating defect found in this round's diff.

## Verification performed

- `grep -n 'filepath.Clean\|binDir' internal/harness/pathguard.go` — empty, as the dispatch required. `binDir` and the lexical comparison are gone from the function entirely; only `main.go`'s unrelated `binDir` local (used for message text, not identity) remains, outside this file.
- Whether stopping at the first `SameFile` match can suppress a later entry that matters: **cannot, by PATH semantics** — a shell resolving an unqualified command runs the first match on PATH and never even attempts a later one, so `PathShadows` returning as soon as it finds the target (having already appended every earlier non-matching candidate to `shadows`) matches what the shell actually does. Confirmed by reading the loop (`internal/harness/pathguard.go:33-54`): every entry before the match is unconditionally appended, so no genuine earlier shadow is lost by the early return.
- Whether `install`'s write to `~/.local/bin` makes `pathHint` see `onPath == true` trivially: read `internal/harness/apply.go` and `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:638-658`. `pathHint` calls `PathShadows(PATH, bin)` where `bin` is the literal `home/.local/bin/sh-agent` just written; when that same directory is itself on PATH, the walk's candidate at that entry is the identical path, so `os.Stat` resolves to the identical device/inode as `target` and `SameFile` is true regardless of whether the file was written by copy or link — not a defect, just the base case working as intended. `TestInstallAndStatusNameAPathShadow` (`cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go:1378`, unchanged by round 3, still green) exercises the adjacent case — an earlier PATH entry holding a different binary — end to end through `install` and `status`, and confirms both go quiet once the earlier entry becomes a symlink to the installed file.
- Whether the `seen` de-duplication can hide a shadow under two spellings: `seen` is keyed on `cand := filepath.Join(dir, name)`, and `filepath.Join` cleans (`/a` and `/a/` produce the same key), so two spellings of the *same* directory correctly collapse to one report instead of double-counting — this is correct, not a suppression of a distinct shadow. Two different directories that happen to alias the same file via a symlinked directory are each stat'd independently through `executableAt`/`SameFile`, not deduped by their `cand` string, so a genuine shadow reachable under two distinct PATH spellings is still detected on each entry, not hidden. No defect found.
- `gofmt -l cmd internal` — clean. `go vet ./...` — clean. `go test -race ./internal/harness/... ./cmd/sh-agent/...` — all pass, including `TestPathShadows`'s two round-2-repro cases (`internal/harness/pathguard_test.go:329-330`: alias after an earlier shadow, alias first) and the missing-target case now asserting `onPath == false` (`internal/harness/pathguard_test.go:348-354`), consistent with the new doc-comment guarantee.
- README.md and remote.md install blocks (round-2's low finding, operator's option 2): both are now single `&&`-chained commands, so a failed verification step stops the move; read end to end, the chain is correctly ordered (download → write allowed-signers → verify signature → verify checksum → chmod+run the *file* → move → cleanup) with no step reachable after a prior failure.

## Criteria

1. **Dead code** — pass. No leftover lexical-comparison code, no orphaned identifiers; `grep` confirms.
2. **Flow tracing** — pass. `status` and `pathHint` both derive their message solely from one `PathShadows` call (main.go:390, main.go:648); the two can no longer disagree on what "on PATH" means, closing the round-2 hop that broke.
3. **Standards conformance** — pass. gofmt/vet/test clean; the doc-comment on `PathShadows` explicitly documents the two prior rounds' failure modes and why the fix is "one identity, one walk," matching the describing-text rule.
4. **Directory layout** — pass, unchanged from prior rounds.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security)** — pass. Deleting the lexical comparison rather than reconciling two notions is the simpler and more correct fix; no new dependency.
6. **Decoupling** — pass. The function now has a single internal equivalence relation instead of two disagreeing ones — the round-2 finding's root cause is removed rather than patched around.

## Not examined

- The security-review round from round 1 was not re-run against this round's diff; this round's changes are non-security-relevant (a comparison semantics fix and doc/comment text), so no new security surface.
- macOS-specific PATH/symlink behavior was reasoned through but not executed on macOS; verified only on this Linux box, consistent with prior rounds' verification story.
- `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-18-verify-bug078-path-shadow-3.md` (untracked, not part of the committed range) was not read.

title: Review — v1.2.2 release gate, post-b029ea1 delta (b029ea1..f91257c)
body:
# Review — v1.2.2 release gate, post-b029ea1 delta (b029ea1..f91257c)

Range reviewed: b029ea1..f91257c (`git diff b029ea1..f91257c -- . ':!.agents/docs'` — `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`, `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go`, `README.md`, `ROADMAP.md`; 39 insertions, 10 deletions). The preceding range 4cdc0b5..b029ea1 is covered by `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-18-review-4cdc0b5-b029ea1.md` (APPROVE), which I read; nothing in this delta reopens it.

## Verdict: APPROVE

Nothing in this delta is broken. The `!dryRun` gate is the correct shape for the rule it satisfies (a new side effect — here a *claim*, which is the same thing for a read-only mode — placed below the read-only path, with a test asserting the read-only mode does not make it), it changes no non-dry-run path, and its test is not vacuous: I removed the gate in a scratch copy of HEAD and the test failed. The README browser chain is a correct single `&&` chain — every failing check stops the `mv`, including the pipeline case, and the `rm` runs only after a successful `mv`. One low finding, on the browser chain writing and deleting inside the user's `~/Downloads` rather than a scratch directory.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `README.md:119-125` — the browser route runs in `~/Downloads`, a directory the user owns and shares with unrelated downloads. Two concrete effects: `printf … > allowed_signers` (line 120) truncates any pre-existing `~/Downloads/allowed_signers` without a guard, and the closing `rm allowed_signers SHA256SUMS SHA256SUMS.sig` (line 125) deletes three fixed names there — a `SHA256SUMS`/`SHA256SUMS.sig` pair the user downloaded earlier for an unrelated project is destroyed by a chain that never mentions it. The gh route above deliberately avoids exactly this (`D=$(mktemp -d)`, and its own comment says "everything is verified in a scratch directory"), so the two routes disagree about a rule one of them states. Concrete fix, keeping the one-chain property: `D=$(mktemp -d) && mv ~/Downloads/sh-agent-darwin-arm64 ~/Downloads/SHA256SUMS ~/Downloads/SHA256SUMS.sig "$D" && cd "$D" && <the same verify/chmod/run/mv steps> && cd ~ && rm -r "$D"`. Not a security defect: nothing unverified can reach `~/.local/bin` either way.

No other correctness, security, or project-rule defect found.

## Answers to the dispatch's specific questions

**1. Does the `!dryRun` gate change any non-dry-run path? No.** `pathHint` has exactly one call site in the repository: `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:277`, inside `installFiles` (`grep -rn pathHint cmd/ internal/` returns that call, the function at `main.go:650`, its doc-comment, and one comment in `main_test.go` — no other caller, no test calling it directly). `installFiles` itself has two callers, `main.go:138` (`install`) and `main.go:175` (`update`), both passing `*dryRun`. The gate's body is entered whenever `dryRun == false`, so both non-dry-run paths reach `pathHint` exactly as before, with the same argument and the same error propagation (`return err`). The only behaviour that changed is `install --dry-run` / `update --dry-run`, which now print nothing about PATH. Nothing downstream consumes `pathHint`'s output — it is written to `out` and not parsed — so no caller needs updating.

**2. Does the dry-run assertion pin the behaviour, or pass vacuously? It pins it — verified by mutation, not only by reasoning.**
- Reasoning: at that point in the test `PATH` is still `elsewhere` (set at `main_test.go:1444`), which holds an executable `sh-agent` (`other`), and the `fresh` home's bin dir is not on it. So `PathShadows` returns `shadows=[other], onPath=false`, and `pathHint` takes the `case len(shadows) > 0` branch (`main.go:657`), whose text contains "so `sh-agent` runs" — one of the three asserted phrases. The assertion therefore cannot pass with the gate removed.
- Measured: `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C .agents/scratch/review-gate` gave a pristine copy of HEAD (the real tree was never touched; no git command that writes the working tree was run). Baseline `go test ./cmd/sh-agent/ -run TestOffPathInstallNamesWhatAnswersAndDoesNotWarnTwice` → `ok`. I then asserted the gate text `if !dryRun {` occurs **exactly once** in `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (count = 1, abort otherwise), saved a copy, removed the gate so `pathHint` is called unconditionally, and re-ran: **FAIL**, with the dry-run output containing `note: …/003/.local/bin is not on PATH, so \`sh-agent\` runs …/002/sh-agent instead`. Restored from the saved copy and confirmed the scratch copy is byte-identical to the real tree's `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (`diff -q`). The test is a real must-fail check for this gate.
- The three phrases are also correctly chosen: they are the bin-dir sentences only (`main.go:653,657,660`), so the unrelated "`go` is not on PATH" warning that a one-directory PATH legitimately produces does not make the assertion fire, and the comment at `main_test.go:1481-1482` says so.

**3. README browser chain — does every failing check stop the `mv`, and does the `rm` run only after a successful `mv`? Yes to both.**
- The whole block is one `&&` chain from `cd ~/Downloads` (line 119) to the final `rm` (line 125), so any non-zero status aborts everything after it. `cd` failing (no `~/Downloads`) stops before anything is written; the signature check (`ssh-keygen -Y verify`, line 121) failing stops before the checksum check; the checksum check failing stops before `chmod`/`mv`.
- The pipeline question: `&&` sees the **last** command's status, i.e. `shasum -a 256 -c - --ignore-missing`, not `grep`'s (no `pipefail` in a copy-pasted interactive shell). That is the safe half of the asymmetry, and I probed the degenerate cases on this box rather than assuming: a `SHA256SUMS` of comment lines only makes `grep` exit 1 and feeds empty input to the checker, which exits **1** ("no properly formatted checksum lines found") on both `sha256sum` (coreutils) and `shasum` 6.04; a `SHA256SUMS` whose every listed file is absent exits **1** ("no file was verified") under `--ignore-missing` on both. So a truncated, emptied or renamed-away input cannot produce a passing checksum step, and `--ignore-missing` cannot silently verify nothing. The file the checksum step verifies is the same name that is then `chmod`ed, executed and `mv`ed (`sh-agent-darwin-arm64`), so there is no verify-one/move-another gap.
- The trailing `rm allowed_signers SHA256SUMS SHA256SUMS.sig` is joined by `&&` to `mv sh-agent-darwin-arm64 ~/.local/bin/sh-agent` on the same line, so it runs only after the `mv` succeeds. A failed `mv` (e.g. `~/.local/bin` does not exist) leaves all four files in place for a retry — the fail-safe ordering. (The separate concern about those three names belonging to the user's `~/Downloads` is the finding above, not a chain-ordering defect.)

## Criteria

1. **Dead code** — pass. Nothing orphaned: `pathHint` still has its caller, no branch of it became unreachable (all three `switch` cases remain reachable from the non-dry-run path), no commented-out code, no leftover debug output. The README's old one-line browser instruction was deleted rather than left beside the new fence.
2. **Flow tracing** — pass. `pathHint`'s single call site traced to both `installFiles` callers (`install`, `update`); error propagation unchanged (`return err` preserved inside the gate); no caller parses the suppressed text. `install --dry-run` still reaches `attributionSet(home, dryRun, out)` and `attributionHint` below the gate, so the gate suppresses only the PATH claim and does not short-circuit the rest of the function. The new test can fail (proved by mutation, above); it asserts behaviour through `run(...)`, not source text.
3. **Standards conformance** — pass. `gofmt -l cmd internal` clean, `go vet ./...` clean, `go test -race ./... -count=1` all three packages `ok` (run on the pristine scratch copy of HEAD so the real tree stayed frozen). The describing-text rule is satisfied in both directions: the new comment at `main.go:272-274` states why the dry run says nothing, and the README fence's own prose ("the same checks as the gh route … as ONE chain") matches what the chain does. The restatement check for the renamed `allowed-signers` → `allowed_signers` file: `grep -rn 'allowed-signers'` leaves hits only in `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` and past review reports, and in each the hyphenated form is English prose for the OpenSSH concept ("the allowed-signers line"), never a filename in a command — the two places that name the file in a command, `README.md` and `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md`, both use `allowed_signers`, as does `internal/harness/release.go`. No live restatement left stale. The global read-only-mode rule ("a new side effect goes BELOW that mode's early returns, and the test asserts the read-only mode does NOT perform it") is followed exactly, including the test half.
4. **Directory layout** — pass. No new files; the test sits in `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` beside the code it covers, appended to the test function that already owns the off-PATH situation rather than opening a parallel one.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security)** — pass. A four-line guard is the simplest correct fix; no new dependency; no crypto or auth primitive is implemented here — the release chain delegates to `ssh-keygen -Y verify` and `sha256sum`/`shasum`, which is consuming vetted tools, not hand-rolling.
6. **Decoupling** — pass. The gate sits in the caller, so `pathHint` keeps its single responsibility ("say what PATH does about a binary that exists") and gains no `dryRun` parameter it would have to reason about; `status`'s use of `PathShadows` is untouched.

## Not examined

- `ROADMAP.md` — read (the "Now" entry deleted, `Last reviewed:` moved to 2026-09-18, matching `date +%F`); it is a records file with no behaviour to verify, and the AGENTS.md rule that ROADMAP sections are empty at a checkpoint is satisfied.
- `.agents/docs` was excluded from the range by the dispatch, so the handoff, changes entry and testing logs committed in f91257c were not reviewed; `/review --docs` over the same range covers them (`.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-18-review-v1.2.1-f91257c-docs.md` exists but was not read).
- **macOS was not exercised.** All shell probes ran on this Linux box with `shasum` 6.04. Whether the `shasum` shipped in macOS's Perl (Digest::SHA 6.02) accepts `--ignore-missing` was not verified — no network, no Mac. If it does not, the flag is rejected with a non-zero status and the chain stops before `chmod`, so the failure mode is a broken instruction, never an unverified binary reaching `~/.local/bin`. Worth one command on the work Mac before the tag: `shasum --help | grep ignore-missing`.
- `sh-agent status` from an installed home (the AGENTS.md "binary line without a warning" check after a `cmd/` change), and any install into a real `$HOME`, were not run — out of scope for a reviewer and forbidden by the dispatch; that is the verifier's row.
- The scratch copy used for the mutation is at `.agents/scratch/review-gate/` (gitignored) and was restored to HEAD content; `main.go.orig` sits beside it in `.agents/scratch/`. The real working tree was not modified by any command in this review.

title: Review — sh-agent-works-everywhere Phase 1 (2026-09-18)
body:
# Review — sh-agent-works-everywhere Phase 1 (2026-09-18)

Range reviewed: b393525..028a43b -- . ':!.agents/docs' (`internal/harness/apply.go`, `internal/harness/harness_test.go`, `README.md`)

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The diff does what the plan's Interfaces section and D4/D6–D9 describe: per-file `add`/`update`/`mode`/`remove` lines on every run including `--dry-run`, `mode` correction probed unconditionally and gated only on `!dryRun`, `remove` now printed on the real run too, and the seven-case test (`TestInstallNamesEveryChange`) exercises all of it and passes (verified: `go test ./...`, non-root, all green; `gofmt`/`go vet` clean). Nothing broken enough to block. One real edge case the plan's own rationale (D6) doesn't fully cover: a directory sitting where a file is expected prints a success-shaped `update` line and then the install aborts with an error, which I confirmed by reproducing the syscall.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/apply.go:68-76` — When `readErr != nil` and is *not* `fs.ErrNotExist` because the destination is a directory (`EISDIR` from `os.ReadFile`), the code prints `update ~/<rel> (previous file unreadable: <err>)` (line 69) *before* attempting the write, then `writeAtomic`'s final `os.Rename(tmp, dest)` fails because you cannot rename a file onto an existing directory. I reproduced this directly: `os.Rename` on a plain file over a directory returns `IsADirectoryError(21, 'Is a directory')` — i.e. `EISDIR`, not `EEXIST` as the plan's D9 states. Practically: `Install` returns the wrapped error immediately, so (a) the transcript already shows an "update" line implying the write is in progress/succeeding for a path where the write in fact never happens, and (b) every file later in `files` that hasn't been processed yet gets no line at all and is silently left unvisited — the operator only learns something failed from the trailing error, with no summary of what did or didn't happen. D6's rationale ("a previous file that exists but cannot be read is written over") does not hold in this specific sub-case, and the plan's own D9 acknowledges the install "would refuse rather than write" but doesn't address the message-order/silent-truncation consequence, only the test fixture. Not a data-loss bug (nothing is corrupted, the directory is left alone) and the plan already treats the residue as accepted, so this is low severity — but the report is worth having on record since it was explicitly asked for and the error text propagated (`EEXIST`) in the plan doc is factually wrong.

Everything else checked came back clean:
- `errors.Is(readErr, fs.ErrNotExist)` correctly covers both "no previous file" and "parent directory missing" (both surface as `ENOENT` from `os.ReadFile`), matching D6's "add" case.
- A dangling symlink at `dest`: `os.ReadFile` follows it, gets `ENOENT`, labelled `add`; `writeAtomic`'s final `os.Rename` replaces the symlink's directory entry (not its stale target) with the real file — correct and safe, just worth knowing the label doesn't distinguish "nothing there" from "a broken link was there."
- `mode` lines only fire from the `bytes.Equal` branch (apply.go:39-58), never alongside `add`/`update`, so `--dry-run` never prints a `mode` line for a file that a real run would actually be adding/updating instead of chmod'ing — verified against `TestInstallNamesEveryChange` cases 6/7.
- `%04o` formatting on `Perm()` (apply.go:51-52) strips setuid/sticky/setgid bits by design (both sides of the comparison use `.Perm()`), so a special-bit-only difference is neither detected nor printed — consistent with how the rest of the codebase treats file modes (0644/0755 only); no finding.
- `TestInstallNamesEveryChange`'s `t.Skip` for root (harness_test.go:1731-1733) sits after cases 1–3 (first install, second identical install, changed-source update) and before cases 4–7 (mode correction, unreadable-file write-over, dry-run variants), all of which do need non-root (root bypasses the `0666`/`0000` permission checks the assertions depend on). Ran the suite as `kesokaj` (non-root) to confirm cases 1-3 execute unconditionally and 4-7 also ran (no skip triggered) — matches D9.
- `grep -rn 'no longer in the repo\|remove  ~/'` outside `.agents/docs` found only the two `apply.go` producers, no caller parsing the old "no longer in the repo" wording or the `remove` line format — the wording change (D-consistent) has no broken consumer.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass: diff is additive (new switch arms, new test cases); old `write   ~/%s` string is gone with no remaining references anywhere in the tree.
2. Flow tracing — pass with the one low-severity gap above (EISDIR ordering); every other changed branch traced end to end (Install → writeAtomic → caller in cmd/sh-agent/main.go, which surfaces the returned error and does not swallow it).
3. Standards conformance — pass; errors wrapped with `%w` and context throughout; comments citing the plan's D-numbers are accurate except D9's `EEXIST` (a plan-doc claim, out of this diff's scope since `.agents/docs` is excluded from the range).
4. Directory layout — pass; no new files, changes stay in the existing `internal/harness` package and `README.md`.
5. Simplicity — pass; no new dependency, no new abstraction; the three-way `switch` on `readErr` is the simplest expression of the three cases D6 names.
6. Decoupling — pass; single function's internal control flow, no new seam, no cross-package reach-in.

## Not examined
`.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` and the plan document's own prose beyond the Interfaces/D4/D6–D9 section named by the dispatch (out of scope: `.agents/docs` excluded from the diff range). Did not test the EISDIR path through the actual `Install`/`writeAtomic` call chain in this repo's test harness (only reproduced the underlying `os.Rename` syscall behavior standalone in scratch, since the fixture is explicitly out of scope per D9 and I must not add a test). Did not exercise `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`'s top-level error printing for the EISDIR case end-to-end (traced by reading, not run).

## Outcome

Written by the main agent, in the Phase 1 checkpoint commit.

- [low] a directory at a destination gets an `update … (previous file unreadable)` line, then the rename fails and the install aborts — a line for a change that did not happen — **fixed**: the per-file line is built first and printed only after `writeAtomic` succeeds (internal/harness/apply.go:80); a directory case in `TestInstallNamesEveryChange` asserts the install errors and prints no line for it (internal/harness/harness_test.go:1809); a must-fail mutation that moves the print back before the write fails it. The plan's D9 now says `EISDIR`, as measured, not `EEXIST`.
- Everything else checked clean per the report; no change.

# Review — c868ed4-bc745dc-docs (2026-09-18)

The one real gap is `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md`, which still describes the release-binary `update` path as "replaces the binary and reinstalls" with no mention of the running-vs-installed distinction this scope just spent three files establishing — a reader who trusts the delivery model alone would not learn that the binary they invoked may not be the one just replaced. Nothing in the diff reroutes a line on the README `How it works` map: the new `note:` line is diagnostic output inside the existing `update` node, not a new edge or node.

"replaces the binary" is unqualified and, read next to the now-detailed Verify sections, invites the wrong reading (that the invoked binary itself is replaced). This is pre-existing wording the scope did not touch, but the scope was specifically asked to check it against the new BUG-079 nuance and it has not been updated to say "replaces `~/.local/bin/sh-agent`" or otherwise flag the running-binary distinction. title: Review — harness-code (audit phase, sh-agent-works-everywhere Phase 2) (2026-09-18)
body:
# Review — harness-code (audit phase, sh-agent-works-everywhere Phase 2)   (2026-09-18)

Range reviewed: `internal/harness` and `cmd/sh-agent`, all non-test `.go` files, read whole in the working tree (not a diff), per `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-18-sh-agent-works-everywhere.md` Phase 2. Files read: `internal/harness/{apply,plan,repo,source,release,state,inventory,pathguard,frontmatter,adopt,derive,render,report}.go` and `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` — all 14 non-test `.go` files in scope (≈4,240 lines). No `*_test.go` file read in full (spot-checked with `grep` only, see Not examined).

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The code is unusually careful — nearly every non-obvious decision carries a dated review comment explaining a prior failure mode it closes. I found no correctness or security defect that reaches a silent no-op or a false success. I found two places where the operator's own stated rule for this audit — "refuses with a message naming the cause **and the alternative**" — is only half met: `update` on a plain copy gives the cause with no next step, and `adopt` on a plain copy succeeds but tells the operator to do something (commit and push) that the place cannot do. Neither is a silent failure; both are message-quality gaps the audit was explicitly commissioned to find.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:461` (`update`) + `internal/harness/repo.go:118-119,153` — `update` on a plain copy (a tree with no `.git`) surfaces the bare `errPlainCopy`: `"sh-agent: not its own git checkout; a plain copy cannot be updated with git"`. This names the cause but not the alternative, unlike every other refusal in this codebase (compare `ResolveSource`'s release-binary refusal, which says "unset it, or build sh-agent from that tree"; `Pull`'s dirty-tree refusal, which says "commit or stash them"). The plan's own Failure-modes rule for this audit is explicit: "refuses with a message naming the cause and the alternative (the BUG-076 rule)". `status` on the same place kind (`main.go:351`) is a little better — "plain copy, not its own git checkout; update is refused" — but still names no alternative (re-clone as a real checkout, or move to a release binary and use `sh-agent update` there). Fix: wrap the error at the `update()` call site (or in `Behind`/`Pull`) with the alternative, the way every sibling refusal in this file does. No CLI-level test exercises this path today (confirmed by grep — only `Behind`/`Pull` unit tests hit `errPlainCopy`; `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` has no plain-copy `update` case), which is also flagged, independently, as a Phase 2 test-gap item in the plan itself.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:245-257` (`adopt` case) — `adopt` does not check whether `repo` is a git checkout before running. On a plain copy (no `.git`) it succeeds and unconditionally prints `"next: review it, run \`sh-agent install\`, then commit and push the repo"` — an instruction the operator cannot follow, because there is no git repository to commit or push in a plain copy. This is the "a wrong message ... is a finding" case the dispatch names: a reported success carries a next step that does not apply to the place kind it ran on. Compare the release-binary path, which correctly refuses adopt outright (`main.go:249-251`, "adopt needs a harness checkout; this install is a release binary") — the plain-copy path has files to adopt into but no git to finish the workflow, and nothing in `Adopt` or its caller says so. Fix: gate the "commit and push" sentence on `harness.IsCheckout(repo)`, or refuse adopt on a plain copy the same way it is refused on a release binary.

- **[note, not a finding / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/source.go:44-51` — `IsReleaseVersion`'s regex `^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$` accepts non-canonical spellings such as `v1.02.2` or `v01.2.2` (leading zeros). This is not exploitable as a downgrade or confusion vector today — `compareRelease`/`releaseParts` uses `strconv.Atoi`, which parses `"02"` as decimal `2`, and the tag string itself is only ever compared for exact-equality against the signed `SHA256SUMS` marker (`release.go:282`), never used as a numeric identity elsewhere. Flagging only because the plan's own Phase 2 checklist already names this exact gap ("`IsReleaseVersion` rejects a non-canonical spelling") as unchecked/pending — this review confirms the current regex still admits it, so the pending item is real and not stale.

## Criteria

1. **Dead code** — pass. No unused exported function, type, or leftover debug output found across the 14 files; every helper (`gitOutC`, `firstLineOfError`, `hostDir`, etc.) has a live caller.
2. **Flow tracing** — pass with the two findings above. Traced `Install`/`Status`/`Diff`/`Uninstall` (apply.go) against `Plan` (plan.go) and `main.go`'s dispatch for every verb × place-kind combination named in the dispatch (checkout / release binary / plain copy). Error paths are wrapped with context almost everywhere (`fmt.Errorf(...: %w, err)`); the two exceptions above are the only bare/under-specified propagations found. `writeAtomic` (apply.go) and the settings-file write (main.go) both sync-then-rename correctly, so a crash mid-write cannot leave a truncated file. Resource lifetimes (temp files, cloned dirs) are closed/removed on every path I traced, including `defer os.RemoveAll` in `cloneThrowaway`/`Reinstall`/`Adopt`'s staging.
3. **Standards conformance** — pass. Go idioms observed throughout: context-wrapped errors, no naked panics, `context` not needed here (no long-running I/O beyond `exec.Command`, which is bounded by the OS). Comments describing security-relevant behavior (secret redaction, symlink refusals, signature verification) are consistent with the code they sit beside — no stale doc-comment found.
4. **Directory layout** — pass. `cmd/sh-agent/` holds only the entrypoint; `internal/harness/` holds all private logic; no stray files.
5. **Simplicity / DIY-except-security** — pass. Release verification uses `ssh-keygen -Y verify` (a vetted external tool, not a hand-rolled signature check) and `crypto/sha256` as designed — both conform to the security exemption. No hand-rolled auth, crypto, or session logic anywhere in scope. Stdlib-only throughout (`go.mod` per `AGENTS.md` carries no dependency), consistent with the project's stated constraint.
6. **Decoupling** — pass. Clean seams: `harness` package owns all filesystem/git/release logic; `main.go` is thin wiring plus two operator-facing pieces of state (`--home`/`--vendor` resolution, `attribution*` for Claude's settings.json) that arguably could live in `internal/harness` but are small and self-contained — not a finding, no second caller exists to justify moving them.

## Not examined

- Test files (`*_test.go`) in both directories were not read in full — only grepped for specific coverage questions (plain-copy `update`, `Adopt` scenarios). The dispatch scoped this review to the non-test `.go` files; test-coverage completeness is Phase 2's separate verifier-mapping task.
- Did not run `go build`/`go vet`/`go test` — this review is a static read, per the hard limits (no network, no `--home` outside `.agents/scratch/`, no tree-changing git commands); I did not invoke any Go tooling since it was not requested and risked no scope violation either way, but no build/vet/test confirmation is claimed here.
- The recon matrix `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-18-recon-sh-agent-audit.md` was named as background by the dispatch and not independently re-verified line-by-line against the source; this review's findings were derived from reading the source itself, not from trusting the recon's claims.
- `linux/arm64` and darwin-specific code paths: none exist in the reviewed files (no `//go:build` tags in scope), so nothing was skipped there — noted for completeness only.

title: Review — harness-docs (2026-09-18)
body:
# Review — harness-docs (2026-09-18)

Range reviewed: `internal/harness` and `cmd/sh-agent`, read whole as they stand in the working tree (docs lens — not a diff), compared against `README.md`, `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/{local,remote}.md`, and the newest `.agents/docs/changes/` entry (`2026-09-18-install-names-every-change.md`).

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The docs are unusually well kept — almost every command, flag, and refusal message I checked in `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` and `internal/harness/*.go` is quoted or paraphrased accurately in README § Daily commands, the deploy guides, and the delivery spec, including recent additions (the per-file `add`/`update`/`mode`/`remove` lines, the BUG-078/079 shadow and stale-binary notes, the release verification chain). Two gaps are real, both narrow: `install`'s `keep`/`kept` output for a foreign `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is undocumented, and README's "so `sh-agent update` works from anywhere" overstates what the checkout-discovery fallback actually does — it can refuse.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/apply.go:35` and `:143` (the `keep    ~/%s (not written by sh-agent; …)` line and the `%d kept` count in `Install`'s summary line) — no living doc names either. README.md:162 (install row of § Daily commands) documents the per-run output as `add` / `update` / `mode` / `remove` plus "counts the unchanged," and `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md:43` repeats the same four-category description ("added, updated …, corrected the mode of, or removed, with the unchanged as a count"). Neither mentions the fifth category: when an unmanaged `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` exists and differs from the harness stub, every install run prints a `keep` line for it and folds it into a separate `kept` count in the summary (`%d written, %d unchanged, %d removed, %d kept — %d files managed`). A reader following the docs and then running `sh-agent install` sees an unexplained line and count. Fix: add `keep` to the README/delivery.md description, or point at the existing "existing ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md … is left alone" paragraph (README.md:196) and note that install now also prints and counts it per run.

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:546` (`knownCheckout`) — install and update refuse to build from a checkout that was only found by walking up from the working directory (or from the manifest's recorded path) when a *different* checkout is already the one on record; the two refusal messages ("this home was installed from the release binary …, not from a checkout …" and "checkout … is not the installed one (…); pass --repo … to build and install from it") appear nowhere in a living doc. README.md:171 and `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:77` both describe the discovery order ("finds the checkout from `--repo`, then `$SH_AGENT_REPO`, then the working directory or any of its parents, then the path recorded at the last install") and README specifically concludes "so `sh-agent update` works from anywhere" — which is true only when the discovered checkout matches the installed manifest's recorded repo, or `--repo`/`$SH_AGENT_REPO` is set explicitly. On a second-or-later install/update run from an unregistered checkout-shaped directory (an unpacked copy under review, a second clone) the command refuses instead of "working," and no doc says so. Fix: add one line to README § Daily commands (or `remote.md` § First install) naming the refusal and its two messages.

- **[low / confidence: low, unverified]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:301-303` — `report` on a release binary prints `report: --repo is not used here; this release binary reports the harness built into it` when `--repo` is passed; not documented in README's `report` row or `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md` § Report back. Narrow edge case (passing `--repo` to `report` specifically on a release-binary install); I did not check whether this is deliberately left out as too minor to document elsewhere.

## Criteria

Docs lens: criteria 1-6 are the language/code-quality lens and do not apply to this dispatch.

1. Dead code — n/a — docs lens
2. Flow tracing — n/a — docs lens
3. Standards conformance — n/a — docs lens
4. Directory layout — n/a — docs lens
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — n/a — docs lens
6. Decoupling — n/a — docs lens

## Not examined

- `internal/harness/adopt.go`, `frontmatter.go`, `derive.go`, `state.go`, `source.go`, `pathguard.go` (beyond `NoteRunningElsewhere`/`PathShadows`), `report.go`'s full redaction-shape list, and `release.go`'s edge-case messages (`"this binary reports version %q, which is not a release; leaving it alone"`, the stale `release-*` cleanup note) were not individually diffed against every doc line — spot-checked only via grep for their exact wording; I did not find contradictions but did not exhaustively re-read each doc paragraph against each message.
- `README.md` sections beyond § Daily commands, § Install, § Install without cloning, § The loop, and § What gets installed where were not read in full (e.g. § Adding things by hand's full table, anything past line ~220).
- `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` beyond line ~120 (the rest of § Releases, any sections after it) was not read.
- `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md` was read in full and cross-checked against `apply.go`'s dry-run/rebuild messages; no discrepancy found there.
- I did not run any command (per hard limits: no network, no real-`$HOME` install, no `sh-agent report`), so all comparisons are static text-vs-text, not observed output.

title: Review — harness, every lens (2026-09-18)
body:
# Review — harness, every lens     (2026-09-18)

Range reviewed: the named files as they are in the working tree, read whole — not a diff: internal/harness cmd/sh-agent. Tree at 160aa16 (Phase 1 of `plans/2026-09-18-sh-agent-works-everywhere.md` closed). The audit phase of that plan, run as `/review internal/harness cmd/sh-agent --all`: five agents, one per lens, each given the scope text and its brief, reading the same frozen tree. The explorer's matrix (`plans/2026-09-18-recon-sh-agent-audit.md`) is background: no silent cell across ten verbs × three place kinds; four coverage gaps.

## Verdicts

| Lens | Agent | Verdict | Artifact |
|---|---|---|---|
| code | `reviewer` | APPROVE WITH NITS — 1 medium, 1 low | `reviews/2026-09-18-review-harness-code.md` |
| security | `security` (opus) | FINDINGS — 1 medium, 7 low (one low/low) | `reviews/2026-09-18-security-harness.md` |
| simplify | `reviewer` | APPROVE WITH NITS — 1 medium, 3 low | `reviews/2026-09-18-review-harness-simplify.md` |
| docs | `reviewer` | APPROVE WITH NITS — 2 medium, 1 low | `reviews/2026-09-18-review-harness-docs.md` |
| tests | `verifier` | PASS — 2 coverage gaps; 77.1% / 86.9% | `testing/2026-09-18-verify-harness.md` |

No high anywhere. No FAIL. The release verification chain — signature, namespace, in-band version marker, hash over the exact bytes written — was read end to end and found sound (security).

## Findings, worst first

Each carries the lens, severity, confidence, and the disposition the fix round takes; `## Outcome` below records what happened.

1. **[security, medium/high]** `internal/harness/adopt.go:168` `copyTree` keeps group/other write bits (`Perm()|0o600`) where `plan.go:138` strips them (`&0o755|0o600`): an adopted third-party skill lands group-writable in the tree every install ships; git records only the x bit. → **fix**: plan.go's expression; test.
2. **[code, medium/high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:461`, `repo.go:118-119,153` — `update` on a plain copy surfaces `errPlainCopy` with no alternative named, unlike every sibling refusal (the BUG-076 rule). No CLI-level test. → **fix**: name the alternative (a checkout or a release binary; `install` still deploys it as it is); CLI test (recon gap 1).
3. **[docs, medium/high]** `apply.go:35,143` — the `keep` line and the `kept` count are undocumented; README `install` row and `delivery.md` list add/update/mode/remove only. → **fix** (`documentation`).
4. **[docs, medium/medium]** `main.go:546` `knownCheckout` refuses an install/update from a checkout found by walking up from cwd when a different one is on record — undocumented, and README's "works from anywhere" reads as a contradiction. → **fix** (`documentation`): describe the refusal and qualify the claim.
5. **[simplify, medium/medium]** `main.go:676-895` — a ~220-line `settings.json` editor lives in the entrypoint, not `internal/harness`. → **left** (main agent): a move with no behaviour change, during an audit whose purpose is behaviour; a Follow-up of the plan.
6. **[security, low/high]** `release.go:106,116` — `v1.02.2`, `v01.2.2`, `v1.2.02` pass `IsReleaseVersion`, compare equal, reach the download (the signed marker stops substitution); `releaseParts` reads an overflowing component as `v0.0.0`. → **fix**: canonical spelling only, `compareRelease <= 0` refuses, overflow is an error; tests for all four (Phase 2 box).
7. **[security, low/high]** `pathguard.go:112-121` — the BUG-079 note is `--home`-blind: run with `--home <scratch>` it calls the scratch home's binary "the installed binary" and may send the reader to relink their real one at it; and `ln -sfn` is offered before ownership is known. → **fix**: the note prints only for the default home; "remove it" alone when `from` is not the caller's; tests (Phase 2 box).
8. **[code, low/high]** `main.go:245-257` — `adopt` on a plain copy prints "commit and push the repo" with no `.git` present. → **fix**: the message depends on `IsCheckout`; test.
9. **[recon/tests]** `adopt` on a release binary refuses without naming the alternative; `status` on a plain copy's "update is refused" line untested; `sync` never invoked by name; `Diff`'s body 0% (the one `diff` test has no drift). → **fix**: four tests, `adopt`'s message names a checkout.
10. **[verifier, Phase 1]** a relative `--home` with `--repo` resolves against the repo dir on a real install (`Reinstall` sets `cmd.Dir = repo`) and against cwd on `--dry-run`. → **fix** (`bug` skill, BUG-080): absolutize `--home` at entry; test.
11. **[simplify, low/medium]** `main.go:691,732-733` vs `readSettings` — the 1 MiB settings bound enforced two ways; `status` never warns on an oversized file. → **fix**: one bound in `readSettings`.
12. **[simplify, low/high]** the `settings: %s could not be written (%v); add the key by hand` format string ×7. → **fix**: one helper.
13. **[security, low/high]** `report.go:400-402,453-458` — the throwaway clone's parent created `0o755` where `release.go` uses `0o700`. → **fix**: `0o700`.
14. **[security, low/high]** `apply.go:220-237` `Diff` writes the rendered harness to `os.CreateTemp("")` — `/tmp`. → **fix**: the temp file under `~/.config/sh-agent/` (the home's runtime dir), removed after.

17. **[security, low/high]** `repo.go:74-82` + `main.go:546-570` — `LoadState` sanitises `Files` but not `Repo`; `knownCheckout` compares `st.Repo` with a repo `st.Repo` itself chose. → **left** (main agent): the manifest is written by `sh-agent` as the user; a prior write as the user is the attacker already holding the user's rights; `knownCheckout`'s purpose (a DIFFERENT checkout found from cwd) still holds when the walk finds one.

19. **[docs, low/unverified]** `report: --repo is not used here` on a release binary undocumented. → **fix** (`documentation`), one clause.

- No lens ran on a machine other than this one; the Mac and devbox cells are Phase 4's.

title: Review — harness-simplify (2026-09-18)
body:
# Review — harness-simplify   (2026-09-18)

Range reviewed: internal/harness and cmd/sh-agent (whole-file read, not a diff): all non-test `.go` files in `internal/harness` (adopt.go, apply.go, derive.go, frontmatter.go, inventory.go, pathguard.go, plan.go, release.go, render.go, repo.go, report.go, source.go, state.go) and `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`.

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing here is broken. The codebase is unusually well-defended (every non-obvious choice carries a comment naming the bug or review round that produced it) and I found no dead exported code, no case of two functions silently disagreeing on the same question (the brief's `binOnPath`/`PathShadows` and lexical-vs-`os.SameFile` pairs are already gone — `PathShadows` and `RunningElsewhere` both use `os.SameFile` identity consistently, one call each). The one real issue is `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` carrying a self-contained ~220-line settings.json editor that has nothing to do with CLI orchestration, plus a small cluster of literally-duplicated message strings inside that same code. Everything else is either already minimal or a single-purpose helper with one caller.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:676-895` (`attributionSet`, `attributionHint`, `attributionOff`, `readSettings`, `abandonTemp`) — a self-contained JSON-file editor (read `~/.claude/settings.json`, insert one key, atomic rename) with no dependency on flag parsing or command dispatch. It sits in the 945-line entrypoint file next to install/update/status orchestration, so it and the CLI wiring share one file and one diff for unrelated changes. Every other piece of logic this size in the repo (install, plan, state, release, report) lives under `internal/harness` and is called once from `main.go`; this cluster is the outlier. Shorter version: move these five functions verbatim into a new `internal/harness/attribution.go`, export the two entry points (`AttributionSet`, `AttributionHint`) and call them from `installFiles`/`status` as already written — deletes ~220 lines from `main.go` with no behavior change.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:703,711,716,721,725,784,816` — the exact format string `"settings: %s could not be written (%v); add the key by hand\n"` is repeated verbatim at seven call sites inside `attributionSet`/`abandonTemp`, and `"settings: %s could not be edited safely (the result would not parse); add the key by hand\n"` is repeated at two more (lines 756, 775). A wording change (there have already been several review rounds touching this file) has to be made in up to nine places to stay consistent. Shorter version: one `settingsWriteFailed(out io.Writer, path string, err error)` helper (3 lines) replacing the 7 identical `fmt.Fprintf` calls, and a second one-line helper for the "could not be edited safely" pair — net deletion of roughly a dozen duplicated lines.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:691,732-733` vs `internal/harness` pattern in `readSettings` (main.go:822-843) — the 1 MiB bound on `settings.json` is enforced twice, two different ways: `attributionSet` does its own `os.Lstat` + `info.Size() > 1<<20` check and refuses with a message, then falls through to call `readSettings`, which does its *own* `os.Stat` of the same path and silently truncates via `io.LimitReader(f, 1<<20)` instead of rejecting. `attributionOff` (used by `status`) reaches `readSettings` directly and never gets the oversized-file message `attributionSet` gives — the same file is judged two different ways depending which command reads it. Shorter version: make `readSettings` itself reject a file over the bound (return the "is larger than 1 MiB" problem string) and delete `attributionSet`'s separate Lstat-and-size branch (lines 730-735) along with the duplicate `1<<20` constant; one bound, one message, checked once per read instead of twice.

- **[low / confidence: low]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:557-562` — the comment on `knownCheckout` explaining why a manifest's `EmbeddedPrefix` value is not handed to `samePath` is printed twice, back to back, identically. Harmless (not user-facing text) but is a straightforward accidental duplication; delete one copy.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. Every exported function in `internal/harness` and every unexported helper in both packages has at least one real (non-test) caller; checked by grepping each identifier's call sites. `redactDocument` initially looked uncalled because it is passed by reference (`add("state.json", redactDocument)`), not called by name — confirmed live.
2. Flow tracing — not in this lens
3. Standards conformance — not in this lens
4. Directory layout — not in this lens
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — one finding: the settings.json editor is a correctly-scoped, dependency-free implementation (no library needed for a one-key JSON patch), but its size-bound check is implemented twice with different outcomes (reject vs. silent truncate). No hand-rolled crypto/auth; `crypto/sha256` and `ssh-keygen -Y verify` in `release.go` are used as designed, not DIY.
6. Decoupling — one finding: the attribution/settings-file cluster in `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` is an independent module living in the wrong package, making the entrypoint file a grab-bag of CLI dispatch plus an unrelated file-editing concern. Everything else split cleanly: each `internal/harness` file owns one concern (state, plan, release, report, pathguard) with small interfaces at the seams (`Source`, `File`, `Report`).

## Not examined
- Every `*_test.go` file (out of scope per the dispatch: non-test `.go` files only).
- `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l` were run and are clean, but no deeper static analysis (staticcheck, golangci-lint) was run — not installed in this sandbox.
- Runtime behavior was not exercised (no `sh-agent install`/`update`/`report` invocation, per the hard limits: no real-`$HOME` install, no network, no `sh-agent report`).
- Criteria 2 (flow tracing), 3 (standards conformance) and 4 (directory layout) were not evaluated at all, per the brief's scope restriction to criteria 1, 5, 6 plus reuse/efficiency.

title: Review — plan-sh-agent-works-everywhere-cold-read-3 (2026-09-18)
body:
# Review — plan-sh-agent-works-everywhere-cold-read-3   (2026-09-18)

Range reviewed: plan file, round 3 — `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-18-sh-agent-works-everywhere.md` (with D8) and `internal/harness/apply.go`

## (1) Gaps

- **BLOCKING (new)** Phase 1 task 1's chosen fixture for "previous file unreadable" (`apply.go:33-62`, D6) is "a directory in its place, which `ReadFile` refuses". I verified with a standalone `os.Rename` probe (regular file → existing directory) that this fails with `EEXIST`/`file exists`, not a silent overwrite. In the default branch, `writeAtomic` ends with `os.Rename(name, dest)` (`apply.go:298`); when `dest` is a directory, that rename errors, and `Install` returns `fmt.Errorf("writing %s: %w", dest, err)` (`apply.go:61`) instead of printing `update ~/<rel> (previous file unreadable: …)` and succeeding. The plan's own claim — "lists `update … (previous file unreadable: …)` and is written" (Phase 1, line 47) — cannot be true for the fixture it names; the install would instead return an error (or, if `writeAtomic` is extended to `RemoveAll` a directory first, that is new behavior the plan never decides). Either the fixture must change (e.g. a regular file that returns a non-`ErrNotExist` read error some other way — permission bits are unreliable as root/CI often bypass them) or `writeAtomic` must gain directory-removal handling the plan doesn't currently authorize. This blocks Phase 1 task 1 as written: two implementers would diverge on whether the test asserts success or an error.
- **Resolved from round 2**: D8 plus the added Phase 1 clause ("`--dry-run` over a deployed file `chmod`ed to 0644 lists the `mode` line and leaves the mode as it was") closes round 2's blocking gap about the `os.Stat` probe being trapped inside `if !dryRun`. Confirmed against `apply.go:49-55`, which today wraps both `Stat` and `Chmod`, matching D8's cited line range.
- **Carried over, still low severity**: Phase 1's checkpoint (line 49) still states "260 at the time of writing" for the add-line count with no re-derivation caveat beyond the parenthetical already there — acceptable as written, not blocking.

## (2) Scope vs Why

No new endpoints, verbs, flags, or config keys found beyond rounds 1-2. D1-D8 each carry an attributed operator quote or an implementer note with citation; nothing in the plan builds beyond the `## Why`/`## Scope` request.

## (3) Readiness

1. **BLOCKING** — Does the "previous file unreadable" test fixture (a directory standing in for the deployed file) actually exercise the `update … (unreadable)` line, or does `os.Rename` over a directory error out first? Verified: it errors first. Not stated; the plan asserts an outcome ("is written") that contradicts what the named fixture produces with today's `writeAtomic`.
2. **NON-BLOCKING** — Exact wording/formatting of the `mode` line's `(0644 -> 0755)` old→new values (octal vs `-rwxr--r--` style) — Verification line 40 makes wording non-binding; a reasonable implementer follows the interface line's literal example.
3. **NON-BLOCKING** — The "260 add lines" checkpoint figure will drift with unrelated content changes; a reasonable implementer re-derives it at run time.

## Verdict

`design needs revision` / `implementation not ready`: one new BLOCKING gap. D8 correctly closed round 2's finding, but Phase 1 task 1's own added test fixture for the D6 "unreadable file" case is internally inconsistent with `apply.go`'s rename-based `writeAtomic` — verified by direct `os.Rename` probe (file over existing directory → `EEXIST`). The plan needs either a working fixture for "read fails but write can proceed" or an explicit decision that this case is instead a refusal/error path.

## Not examined

Did not re-read `main.go`, `plan.go`, `repo.go`, `source.go`, `release.go`, `report.go`, `adopt.go`, `state.go`, `render.go`, `inventory.go`, `derive.go`, `pathguard.go`, `apply_test.go`, or any docs surface (`README.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/{local,remote}.md`, `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md`); Phase 2-5 content beyond re-confirming D8 against `apply.go`. This round re-verified round 2's fix (D8) and probed the one new fixture Phase 1 added since round 2, given the 20-tool-call budget.

All five round-3 fixes are correct, and the delivery mechanism is now consistent everywhere the one prescribed grep reaches: no sentence in `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/*.md` or `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/*.md` still says a tag delivers nothing or that every machine follows `main`. That is a false NO-SHIP, not a false ship, so it does not block a release; it should be qualified in the same file.

## Findings (round 4)

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:77` vs `:52` — `:52` now distinguishes the two non-PASS cases: a FAIL or BLOCKED log "is carried to Step 5 as it is and blocks there — never replaced by a re-run cited alone", while "only one left IN PROGRESS" sends the gate to a fresh dispatch. `:77` did not gain the matching qualifier and still blocks on "a verifier log whose Status is still IN PROGRESS (a run cut off before it finished; BUG-083)" — unqualified, so the superseded log the gate was just told to replace still satisfies a blocking condition. Fix: at `:77`, say "the verifier log cited for the Verification row, or any FAIL or BLOCKED log in the range" — keeping the FAIL/BLOCKED case deliberately range-wide (that asymmetry is right, and `:52` states it) while letting a replaced IN PROGRESS log go.

## Verification of the round-3 fixes

- **`.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:8`** — "Git is the transport for a checkout place and a signed release download for a binary-only one (§ Releases), both on the operator's own credentials", now citing R8, R9, ADR-030 and ADR-033. Correct and complete: it matches `:128` ("Then the release's binaries, which is how a binary-only place updates (R9, ADR-033)"), `README.md:154`, `deploy/local.md:43`, and `REQUIREMENTS.md` R9; the "no push-based deploy, no CI, no hooks, no service" tail is preserved, so nothing the old sentence guaranteed was dropped.
- **`.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:91`** — "A checkout place never installs from a tag; a binary-only place installs only from one (§ Releases)." Correct, and it keeps the timer paragraph's point intact (the timer is a checkout mechanism, so the first clause is the one that governs there). No longer contradicts `:95`, `AGENTS.md:63` or R9.
- **`.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:195`** — "There is no deploy step after the push: a checkout place picks the commit up, and a binary-only place the release, with `sh-agent update` when the operator runs it." Correct; the "no deploy step" invariant that R9 and ADR-030 D2 protect survives the split.
- **`.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md:7`** — now names R8 and R9, ADR-030 and ADR-033, with a parenthetical for the release binaries. Correct; consistent with `:33` and `:76`, which already carried ADR-033.
- **`.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md:56`** — the withdrawn-channel bullet keeps its history and gains "ADR-033 later restored a narrower channel: the binaries published with a tag, which a binary-only place updates to after verifying their signed checksums — an asset the place fetches, never a push to a machine." Correct, and the "never a push" clause keeps the bullet's original point (the section is "What is deliberately NOT being built", and what is still not built is a push channel) — the addition does not turn the bullet into a contradiction of its own heading.
- **`skills/preflight/SKILL.md:52`** — the FAIL/BLOCKED re-dispatch path that round 3 flagged is closed, with the "never replaced by a re-run cited alone" clause naming the exact failure mode. Correct; see the one nit above for the `:77` half.
- **The prescribed grep** (`grep -nE 'ADR-030|tag' README.md AGENTS.md .agents/docs/deploy/*.md .agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/*.md`) — every hit read. Nothing still says a tag delivers nothing or that every machine follows `main`. The remaining ADR-030-only citations are all historically correct as written: `AGENTS.md:74` (now naming both ADRs), `remote.md:56` (ADR-030 D1, per-machine credentials — untouched by ADR-033), `remote.md:91` (the timer's trust root — untouched), `delivery.md:43` (ADR-030 D4, a dependency the spec is arguing against).
- **G10 check** — the replaced sentences exist nowhere else; no orphaned copy of "a tag is never what a machine installs from", of the old `remote.md:8` transport claim, or of the unconditional Verification row survives anywhere the grep reaches. The `README.md` map (lines 8-45) already draws both paths — `harnessRepo -- "clone once, update pulls" --> checkoutPlace` and `releases -- "update downloads and verifies" --> binaryPlace` — so the project `AGENTS.md` rule 3 (a delivery change whose diff does not touch the map is incomplete) is satisfied by a map that was already correct; the `tags: release markers` node label is paired with a separate `Releases` node and is not the withdrawn claim.

## Criteria (round 4)

1. **Dead code** — pass. Every replaced sentence is gone, not duplicated; no stale copy left beside its replacement.
2. **Flow tracing** — pass. The ADR-033 delivery claim now reaches `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` (prose and map), `deploy/remote.md`, `deploy/local.md` and `specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` consistently; the verifier Status vocabulary reaches both `/preflight` rows, with the one unqualified reference named above.
3. **Standards conformance** — pass with the one nit. No BUG-004 frontmatter hazard; no agent `description:` touched in this range.
4. **Directory layout** — pass. Each fix landed in the file that owns its claim; trail artifacts under `.agents/docs/` in the right directories.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security)** — pass. No code, no dependency, no security-sensitive surface anywhere in v1.2.3..10a9fe2; `go.mod` untouched.
6. **Decoupling** — pass. The verifier/`preflight` seam and the requirements/docs seam are each consistent in both directions.

## Noted, out of round

- `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:93`, the section heading "Releases — signed tags, as release markers", is now narrower than the section's own first sentence (a tag also carries the binaries). Not a contradiction and not in this round's scope; worth a word if the section is edited again.

## Trail claims checked against the code (rounds 1-3, still valid)

- `BUG-078`/`BUG-079`/`BUG-080`/`BUG-081`/`BUG-082` graduated-to claims all resolve to sentences present in `context/AGENTS.md`; the Graduated rows match; `BUG-083` (`open`) points at the § Work dispatch sentence, which exists and carries the round-2 wording; `BUG-084`'s record file and INDEX row exist (text not read).

## Not examined

- `gofmt -l cmd internal`, `go vet ./...`, `govulncheck`, `go test ./...` — not re-run this round; no Go source changed anywhere in v1.2.3..10a9fe2, and round 2 read a bare green `go test ./...` at 94bec82, whose Go tree is identical to 10a9fe2's.

- Round-1 "Not examined" still stands for the rest of the trail markdown in the range (the retro, three handoffs, two cold-read plans, the changes entry, the worktree-retro review, two testing logs, the works-everywhere plan).

## Outcome

- Finding 1 (`skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md:48` schema line without `redirection`): fixed at `skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md:48`.
- Finding 2 (`agents/verifier.md:71` template Status without `IN PROGRESS`): fixed at `agents/verifier.md:71`.
- Finding 3 (`agents/verifier.md:18` "FIRST command" unsatisfiable before Pre-flight): fixed at `agents/verifier.md:18` ("the FIRST verification command … once the docs root is resolved") and the matching dispatch sentence at `context/AGENTS.md` § Work.
- All three in the pre-gate commit that follows 3b5b71a; recorded as BUG-084 (a value added to a vocabulary in prose but not in the file's own schema/template lines).
- Round 2 (over 3b5b71a..94bec82): all three verified fixed; two findings raised — `/preflight`'s blocking list did not know the new `IN PROGRESS` status, and `AGENTS.md:63` still carried the ADR-030 delivery claim the README fix superseded.
