- Round 4 (this review, over 8e1b044..10a9fe2, at the operator's call): all four round-3 findings verified fixed at `remote.md:8,91,195`, `delivery.md:7,56` and `preflight:52`; the prescribed grep over `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `deploy/*.md` and `specs/sh-agent/*.md` finds no surviving "a tag delivers nothing" or "every machine follows `main`" claim. ## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `agents/reviewer.md:20` and `agents/security.md:18` — both still read "Write your report file as soon as you have one finding worth recording, then UPDATE it as you go...", the exact phrasing `agents/verifier.md` just replaced with the per-command IN-PROGRESS-log rule. Criterion 3 ("every other restatement of a changed rule is changed with it") applies: these are the same "write the artifact early" rule for sibling read-only agents, now inconsistent with the verifier's stricter version. `agents/explorer.md:17` carries the same old wording too but explorer writes a brief, not a pass/fail log, so it is the weaker case of the three — still worth a decision either way, not a silent skip. `restated: agents/reviewer.md:20, agents/security.md:18 (also agents/explorer.md:17) still say the old thing; agents/verifier.md:18-19 has the new thing.`

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md:28-29` (new triggers 6 "Redirection" and 7 "A missed filing") vs. the Signal Types table (`skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md:73-78`, values `correction|override|restatement|format|gap`) — neither new trigger maps cleanly to an existing signal value. Trigger 6 ("the user changes what is being built... even when no word of it is 'no'") is closest to `override` but `override` is documented narrowly as "User changed agent's choice to something else" (tool/pattern), not scope/direction. Trigger 7 ("the user asks for something a rule says should already exist... the ask IS the correction") is closest to `gap` ("Agent lacked knowledge it should have had") but the trigger's own text says the agent *did* know the rule and just didn't file it — that's not a knowledge gap. Since `rule_ref`/`signal` values are the controlled vocabulary `/retro` matches on across projects, an entry logged under triggers 6/7 will be coerced into a signal that doesn't describe it, or left ambiguous. Either add `redirection` and a value for trigger 7 to the table, or the SKILL.md states explicitly which existing value each maps to.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `context/AGENTS.md` Hard rules — of the four sentences this scope changes, two cite BUG ids that exist (`BUG-078`, `BUG-079` on the "verified by the shell" sentence; `BUG-080` on the "read-only mode" sentence — both confirmed present in `.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md`). Dispatch `bugs`") applies to both: three rounds on one mechanism and four mutations misread as passing are exactly the failure classes that rule names.

title: Security review — fix round for the Phase 2 audit (160aa16..3209cf3)
body:
# Security review — fix round for the Phase 2 audit (160aa16..3209cf3)

Range reviewed: 160aa16..3209cf3 (`git diff 160aa16..3209cf3 -- . ':!.agents/docs'`, plus the four docs in the dispatch)

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Seven of my eight audit findings are closed as written. One is not: the `0o700`
on the throwaway clone's parent is **inert on every machine that has run
`install`**. `SaveState` writes `~/.config/sh-agent/state.json` through
`writeAtomic`, whose `os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dest), 0o755)` (`apply.go:291`)
creates that directory first, and `os.MkdirAll` returns nil for an existing
directory without touching its mode — measured, twice: a scratch probe
replicating the two calls in order prints `-rwxr-xr-x` after both, and
`~/.config/sh-agent` on the operator's own box is **0755** right now. So
`report.go:457`, `apply.go:224` and the older `release.go:136` all no-op. I also
have to correct my own earlier framing of that finding, and `release.go`'s
comment with it: 0755 grants group and other **r-x, not w**, so nobody can
pre-create `report-<pid>` as a symlink there — the exposure the 0700 actually
closes is READ exposure, and that is the one still open: every local account can
traverse `~/.config/sh-agent` and read the feedback log, the retro proposals, and
the transient clone of the **private** `styrman-harness-feedback` repository
while `report` runs (and after a SIGINT, until the next sweep). Everything else
in the round does what its finding asked, and two of the new tests
(`TestNonCanonicalTagNeverReachesTheDownload`, `TestDiffUsesTheHomeNotTmp`) are
genuine must-fail checks of the behaviour they pin.

## Status of the eight prior findings — checkable statements

1. **`copyTree` mode — CLOSED.** `adopt.go:175` is now
   `writeAtomic(target, data, info.Mode().Perm()&0o755|0o600)`, identical in
   effect to `plan.go:138`: 0666 lands 0644, 0775 lands 0755. Directories in the
   same walk are `MkdirAll(target, 0o755)`. `TestAdoptStripsGroupAndOtherWrite`
   asserts `Perm()&0o022 == 0` on the adopted file (skipped as root, correctly).
3. **Canonical tags + `<= 0` + overflow — CLOSED.** `source.go:46` is
   `^v(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$`, which rejects
   `v1.02.2`, `v01.2.2`, `v1.2.02`; the added `strconv.Atoi` loop rejects
   `v99999999999999999999.0.0` before `releaseParts` could read it as `v0.0.0`.
   `release.go:116` is `compareRelease(tag, version) <= 0` with the message "is
   not newer than". `compareRelease` has exactly **one** production caller
   (`release.go:116`, confirmed by grep across the module) and both its operands
   are gated by `IsReleaseVersion` above it (`:102` for `tag` from the GitHub
   API, `:114` for the running `version`), so `releaseParts`' surviving
   `return [3]int{}` is unreachable from production code. The guard moved to the
   entry rather than to the parse; that is equivalent **here and only here**, and
   a second caller of `compareRelease` would have to repeat the gate. The doc
   comment at `release.go:369-370` ("Both are known to match") says so, which is
   the mitigation.
4. **The BUG-079 note — CLOSED for `--home`, PARTIAL for ownership.**
   `pathguard.go:118` returns unless `filepath.Clean(os.UserHomeDir()) ==
   filepath.Clean(home)`, and `TestNoteRunningElsewhereOnlyForTheRealHome`
   exercises both directions by setting `HOME`. `ownedByCaller` downgrades the
   remedy. Two residuals, findings B and C below.
5. **Throwaway parent `0o700` — NOT CLOSED.** Finding A.
6. **`Diff` out of `/tmp` — CLOSED for `/tmp`; the leak survives.**
   `apply.go:223-227` writes under `filepath.Join(home, ".config", "sh-agent")`,
   and `TestDiffUsesTheHomeNotTmp` proves it by setting `TMPDIR` to a
   non-existent path and requiring `Diff` to succeed — a real must-fail check.
   The `tmp.Write` error path at `:231-233` still returns without
   `os.Remove(tmp.Name())` and without `Close`, so a write failure leaks the file
   and its fd; the remediation that removed the temp file entirely (`diff … -`
   with `cmd.Stdin`) was not taken. Severity drops from "debris in a shared
   directory" to "debris in the operator's own directory at 0600". Finding E.
7. **`yamlQuote` — CLOSED.** `frontmatter.go:167-189` escapes `\`, `"`, `\n`,
   `\t` and every rune `< 0x20` or `== 0x7f` as `\uXXXX`. `\u` + four hex digits
   is a valid double-quoted escape in YAML 1.1 (`ns-esc-16-bit`) and YAML 1.2, so
   the rendered `agent.md` parses; DEL is included. Better than the finding
   asked: the reachable case is not the hypothetical newline (`entries()` splits
   on `\n`, `TrimRight`s `\r` and joins continuations with a space, so `Parse`
   cannot return a value containing a line break) but a **mid-line** control — a
   raw ESC, NUL or DEL inside a vendored skill's `description:`, which `keyLine`'s
   `(.*)` matches, `TrimSpace` preserves, and `Lint` does not refuse. That case
   was live and is now escaped. One residual, finding D.
8. **`cell` — CLOSED.** `inventory.go:396-402` converts to `[]rune` and takes
   `string(r[:max])`; every later index is a byte offset into that already
   rune-aligned prefix, so neither the space cut (ASCII boundary) nor the
   `cut = len(head)` fallback (the whole prefix) can split a rune.
   `TestCellIsRuneSafe` sweeps `max` from 5 to 119 over a multi-byte string and
   checks `utf8.ValidString`.

## The two findings left — do the reasons hold

**17 / `LoadState` does not sanitise `Repo`.** Two halves, two answers.

- *"a prior write as the user is the attacker already holding the user's
  rights"* — **sound for the default home and the default threat model, but it
  claims more than it proves and should be recorded narrower.** `state.json` is
  a file, not a live process; it arrives by any route that populates
  `~/.config`, and two of those are not "the attacker already has your rights":
  (a) a dotfiles repository or a restored backup carrying
  `~/.config/sh-agent/state.json` — a normal way for `~/.config` to be seeded,
  which makes `repo` an input from off the machine; (b) `--home <dir>` where the
  directory is shared or group-writable — and on this very box `~/.config` is
  **0775**, so the user's group is already a wider set than the user. In both,
  the `repo` field selects the directory `Reinstall` runs `go build` in and then
  executes. The disposition (leave it) is defensible — high cost, blast radius is
  the operator's own account — but write the reason as: *"no path writes
  `state.json` except `sh-agent` running as the user; a `state.json` that arrives
  from a backup, a dotfiles sync or a shared `--home` is out of model."* Closing
  it for real is still one `IsCheckout(st.Repo)` call before a build.
- *"`knownCheckout`'s purpose (a DIFFERENT checkout found from cwd) still holds
  when the walk finds one"* — **holds; verified against the resolution order.**
  `ResolveSource` (`repo.go:22-70+`) takes `--repo`, then `$SH_AGENT_REPO`, then
  the cwd walk, and only then the recorded manifest. So whenever the walk (or a
  flag) supplies `repo`, `st.Repo` is an independent value and
  `samePath(st.Repo, repo)` is a real comparison that refuses the mismatch — the
  case the guard exists for. The circularity bites only where nothing else
  supplied a repo and `st.Repo` was itself the selector, which the guard never
  claimed to cover. The claim is accurate as written.

## Findings — new surface from the fixes

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/report.go:457`,
  `internal/harness/apply.go:224`, `internal/harness/release.go:136` — **the
  `0o700` never applies.** `os.MkdirAll` is a no-op returning nil when the
  directory exists, and `~/.config/sh-agent` always exists by the time any of
  these run, created 0755 by `writeAtomic` under `SaveState` during the first
  `install` (`report`, `update` and `diff` all presuppose an install). Measured
  two ways: a scratch probe (`.agents/scratch/security-phase2/mkdirmode.go`,
  gitignored, no harness import, replicating `MkdirAll(dir,0o755)` then
  `MkdirAll(dir,0o700)`) prints `-rwxr-xr-x` for both; and `stat` on the
  operator's own `~/.config/sh-agent` returns **755** today. Why it matters, with
  the threat corrected: 0755 grants group and other r-x, **not w**, so the
  symlink-planting story in `release.go:132-134`'s comment and in my own earlier
  finding is wrong for this directory — nobody else can create an entry in it.
  What 0755 does leave is read access for every local account to
  `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl`, `proposals/*.md`, `state.json`, and — for the
  duration of `report`, and indefinitely after a SIGINT until the next
  `sweepInterruptedClones` — a working clone of the **private**
  `styrman-harness-feedback` repository holding this machine's reports. On a
  single-user box that is nothing; on the devbox or any host with a second
  account it is a disclosure. Remediation: one `ensureConfigDir(home)` helper —
  `os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o700)`, then when the directory already exists and
  `ownedByCaller` says it is the caller's, `os.Chmod(dir, 0o700)` — called from
  `SaveState` and from the three sites above; stdlib `os` only, no dependency.
  The test to add is the arrangement the current one avoids: `TestThrowawayParentIsPrivate`
  uses a bare `t.TempDir()` home with no prior install, which is the **one**
  arrangement in which the fix works, so it passes while the shipped behaviour
  does not; the new test must `Install` first (as `TestDiffUsesTheHomeNotTmp`
  already does, where the 0700 is provably inert and unasserted) and then assert
  the mode.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/pathguard.go:131` — the note
  decides "yours to relink" from `os.Lstat(from)`, but the operation it advises
  (`ln -sfn <installed> <from>`) is governed by **write permission on
  `filepath.Dir(from)`**, not by the ownership of the file at `from`. The two
  disagree in the case that actually occurs on these machines: a `sh-agent` the
  operator owns sitting in `/usr/local/bin`, a root-owned directory —
  `ownedByCaller` reads true, the note says "point it at the installed binary
  (`ln -sfn`)", and the command fails with EACCES. My audit's remediation said
  "stat `from` **and its directory**"; the directory half was not implemented. On
  the brief's symlink question: `Lstat` is the **right** call of the two — a
  symlink replacement is a directory operation, and on a sticky directory the
  link's own uid is what governs it, so following to the target's owner would be
  strictly worse — but neither `Lstat` nor `Stat` is sufficient without the
  parent. Remediation: also require `filepath.Dir(from)` to be the caller's (or
  writable by them) before offering `ln -sfn`. Advice-only surface; filed because
  a wrong remedy in a security-relevant note is what sends an operator to `sudo`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/pathguard.go:141-147`
  (`ownedByCaller`) — the brief's root question, answered: for **root** (uid 0) a
  user-owned `from` (uid 1000) reads as *not* the caller's, so root running
  `update` gets "it is not yours to relink — remove it, with the rights that own
  it". The direction is the conservative one and the resulting advice is not
  harmful (root relinking a file inside a user's `~/.local/bin` is not advice to
  give), but the sentence is false as stated for root, who owns everything by
  capability. The realistic shape is `sudo sh-agent update` with `$HOME` left as
  the user's: the real-home gate at `:118` passes, `os.Getuid()` is 0, and every
  file in that home reads as foreign. No security consequence — the note writes
  nothing and touches nothing. Reword to "not owned by the user this process runs
  as". Separately, `os.Getuid()` (real uid) is the weaker of the two for a "can I
  write this" question; sh-agent is not setuid so it does not matter today, and
  `os.Geteuid()` is the one-word change that keeps it not mattering.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/frontmatter.go:178-183` —
  `yamlQuote` escapes C0 and DEL but not the **C1** controls (U+0080–U+009F,
  notably U+0085 NEL) or U+2028/U+2029. In YAML 1.1 — libyaml, PyYAML, what most
  embedded parsers implement — those are line-break characters, so a description
  carrying one renders as a raw break inside the double-quoted scalar. This is
  **not** injection: a double-quoted scalar ends at its closing quote, so the
  worst case is a fold to a space or a parse error, never a second mapping key.
  Filed only because the fix's own rationale ("a raw control character ends a
  double-quoted YAML scalar for a strict parser") applies verbatim to these four
  runes. Remediation: extend the guard to
  `r < 0x20 || (r >= 0x7f && r <= 0x9f) || r == 0x2028 || r == 0x2029`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/apply.go:220-234` — `Diff`, a
  read-only verb, now **writes into the home**: it creates `~/.config/sh-agent`
  when absent and drops a temp file there. Confined to sh-agent's own directory
  and only on drift, so this is a note rather than a defect against the read-only
  rule (which is scoped to `--check`/`--dry-run`), but `sh-agent diff --home <a
  home you are merely inspecting>` now mutates it. The `tmp.Write` error path at
  `:231` leaks the file and its fd (no `Remove`, no `Close`), and README's new
  `diff` row asserts "removed after" without qualification — a description one
  error path wider than the behaviour. Remediation closes all three at once and
  is the one the audit gave: `exec.Command("diff", "-u", "-L", …, dest, "-")`
  with `cmd.Stdin = bytes.NewReader(f.Data)`, and no temp file at all.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go:1599-1629`
  (`plainCopyOf`, new in this range) — the fixture copies `context/`, `skills/`,
  `agents/`, `commands/` and `rules/` out of this checkout by walking the
  **working tree**, not `git ls-files`, into `t.TempDir()` (i.e. under `$TMPDIR`,
  which this project's rules put off limits for generated files). Today nothing
  leaks: `git status --untracked-files=all` and `git ls-files --others --ignored`
  over those five directories are empty, and a `find` for symlinks and
  secret-shaped names (`.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.tfvars`, `id_*`,
  `*credential*`) returns nothing — so the copy is all tracked content. The
  mechanism is the one `AGENTS.md` names as sharp ("an artifact built from the
  WORKING TREE rather than from git is pinned to what git tracks — `go:embed`
  compiled a gitignored `.env` into a release binary"): a gitignored credential
  dropped into `skills/` by a vendored skill would be refused by `secretShaped`
  at `install` and at `adopt`, and copied raw by this fixture. Exposure is
  bounded — `t.TempDir()` roots are 0700 — so it is a test-hygiene finding, not a
  shipping one. Remediation: drive the walk from `git ls-files -- <dir>`, or
  reuse `secretShaped` as a skip in the fixture; and point the fixture's root at
  `.agents/scratch/` rather than `$TMPDIR` if the project wants its own rule
  honoured in tests too.

## Checked

- **Secrets:** clean in the diff. No credential, token or key added in any
  changed file; `release.go:40`'s compiled-in **public** signer line is untouched
  by this range. The new test bodies were grepped for PEM headers and
  `ghp_`/`sk-ant-`/`AKIA`/`AIza`/`xoxb-`/`ssh-rsa`/`ssh-ed25519` shapes —
  nothing. Secrets in *output*: the two new message strings (`errPlainCopy`, the
  `adopt` refusal) embed only the public clone URL; the new `settingsUnwritable`
  helper prints `path` and `err` and no file content, exactly as the five sites it
  replaced did; `readSettings`' new size branch returns a fixed sentence and no
  bytes. The `plainCopyOf` fixture is the one secret-adjacent mechanism, above.
- **Injection:** no new shell, no new `exec.Command`, no new argv construction.
  The only argv-relevant change (`release.go:116`, `source.go:46-62`) *narrows*
  what can reach `gh`. `filepath.Abs(home)` at `main.go:106` runs before every
  path join and removes a class of relative-path surprise (BUG-080) rather than
  adding one. `Diff`'s new `filepath.Join(home, ".config", "sh-agent")` uses no
  external input. Path traversal from the manifest is unchanged: still one choke
  point at `LoadState`'s `filepath.IsLocal` filter over `Files` (and still not
  over `Repo` — finding 17, left).
- **Authz/authn:** not a service. The one new authorization-shaped predicate is
  `ownedByCaller`, which gates **no operation** — it only chooses the wording of
  an advisory line. `knownCheckout` is unchanged by this range except for the
  removal of a duplicated comment.
- **Crypto:** nothing hand-rolled and nothing added. The release chain
  (`ssh-keygen -Y verify` over `SHA256SUMS` in a pinned namespace with the signer
  compiled in, then `crypto/sha256` over the asset bytes) is untouched except for
  the version gate, which only tightens it. `yamlQuote` is an encoder, not a
  primitive. No finding.
- **Dependencies:** unchanged and best case — `go.mod` still has **zero**
  third-party requires. The three new imports are stdlib: `syscall`
  (pathguard.go), `strconv`/`strings` (source.go); `fmt` was already imported in
  frontmatter.go. `go vet ./...` exits 0 and `gofmt -l cmd internal` is empty, so
  the range builds. `npm audit`: not applicable, no JavaScript in the repository.
  `govulncheck ./...`: **not run** — it queries `vuln.go.dev` and this dispatch
  forbids network; I did not fake it. Residual is small: zero third-party
  modules, so the only surface is the standard library, and this box runs
  go1.27.1, above both advisories `AGENTS.md` records as fixed in
  go1.24.6/go1.25.8. One command closes it.
- **GCP surface:** none in range — no IAM binding, service account,
  `--allow-unauthenticated`, Secret Manager call, or service-account key file.
  The only remote endpoints are GitHub via `gh` and `git`.
- **Docs in the dispatch** (`README.md`, `deploy/local.md`, `deploy/remote.md`,
  `specs/sh-agent/delivery.md`): read whole for this range. They match the code —
  the canonical-tag rule, the "not newer than" refusal, the `--home` gate on the
  BUG-079 note, the ownership-aware remedy, the `knownCheckout` refusal with its
  exact message, and the `keep` line are each described accurately, and
  `remote.md` now tells the operator never to cut a tag with a leading zero.
  One inaccuracy, named above: README's `diff` row says the temporary copies are
  "removed after" without the `tmp.Write` exception.

## Not examined

- `govulncheck ./...` — not run (network prohibited). Exact command above.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` was **not read line by line**: I read the diff's
  new test functions and the two helpers (`plainCopyOf`, `scratchClone`) in full,
  plus `TestRelativeHomeResolvesAgainstTheInvokingDirectory` and
  `internal/harness/audit_test.go` whole. The ~1590 pre-existing lines of
  `main_test.go` and the unchanged `harness_test.go`, `report_test.go`,
  `pathguard_test.go`, `source_test.go` were scanned for secret material only.
  I make no coverage claim beyond the individual tests I name here; the `--tests`
  lens owns the coverage map.
- No verb was executed against any home, real or scratch, and no install was
  performed. The only thing run was `.agents/scratch/security-phase2/mkdirmode.go`
  — a standalone `package main` with no harness import (the Go tool skips
  dot-prefixed directories, so it is invisible to `./...`), plus read-only `stat`,
  `go vet`, `gofmt -l` and `git` queries. `git status --untracked-files=all`
  confirms the working tree is unchanged apart from review artifacts.
  `sh-agent report` was not run, as the dispatch requires.
- The **runtime** behaviour of the two consumer CLIs is out of scope: the YAML
  claims about `\uXXXX` rest on the YAML 1.1/1.2 specifications and on reading
  `DeriveAgy`, not on feeding a generated `agent.md` to the Antigravity CLI. That
  behavioural run is the project's own testing procedure and belongs to the
  verifier.
- The unchanged parts of `report.go` (the redaction list, `Collect`, the push
  path) and of `release.go` (download, `verifyRelease`, `checksumFor`) were not
  re-read in this range; they were audited on 2026-09-18 in
  `reviews/2026-09-18-security-harness.md` and are untouched here apart from the
  two lines in the diff.
- Nothing in `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/` or `rules/` changed in
  this range, so their content was not audited; for `plainCopyOf` I enumerated
  them only for untracked, ignored, symlinked and secret-shaped entries.

## Outcome

Written by the main agent after round 2 of the Phase 2 fix round, in its commit.

- [low] finding 5 not closed — `MkdirAll(…, 0700)` no-ops on a dir every install had already created 0755 — **fixed**: `ConfigDir(home)` (internal/harness/state.go:76) creates the runtime dir 0700 or tightens an existing one (internal/harness/state.go:86), and every writer of it goes through it: `SaveState` (so every install tightens it), `cloneThrowaway`, `Diff`, the release download. `TestInstallMakesTheConfigDirPrivate` (internal/harness/audit_test.go:200) covers a fresh home and a pre-existing 0755 one; `TestThrowawayParentIsPrivate` now pre-creates the dir 0755 — the arrangement the earlier version of the fix could not pass; mutations for the chmod and for `SaveState` bypassing `ConfigDir` fail them. The operator's own dir tightens on their next `install`/`update`.
- [low] relinking is governed by the directory's owner, and root should read `Geteuid` — **fixed**: the advice is keyed on `os.Stat(filepath.Dir(from))` (internal/harness/pathguard.go:141) and `ownedByCaller` compares with `os.Geteuid()` (internal/harness/owned_unix.go:17); the sentence says "with the rights that own its directory". Not pinned at the note level: no non-root test can make a directory it does not own; `TestOwnedByCaller` pins the predicate with a fake `Stat_t`.
- [low] `Diff`'s write-error leak and README's unqualified "removed after" — **fixed** (the `defer`, internal/harness/apply.go:242); README's clause is now true on every path. `plainCopyOf` copying the working tree rather than `git ls-files` — **left** (main agent): a test fixture under `$TMPDIR`, removed by the test; the five directories hold nothing untracked today, and the embed test (`TestEmbedHoldsOnlyTrackedFiles`) fails the build if that changes.
- finding 17's `left` reason — **narrowed** in the merged record: a `state.json` from a dotfiles sync, a restored backup or a shared `--home` is not an attacker with the user's rights; what holds is that `knownCheckout` compares the cwd-walk result against the manifest (a real comparison), and a `Repo` value that names no harness is refused by `ResolveSource` before anything builds.

title: Security review — BUG-078 PATH shadow warning, round 4 (4cdc0b5..28e4747)
body:
# Security review — BUG-078 PATH shadow warning, round 4 (4cdc0b5..28e4747)

Range reviewed: 4cdc0b5..28e4747

Round 4 is the one bounded extra round granted at the three-round cap. It re-reads the range with attention
to the three round-3 fixes (`install --dry-run` prints no PATH hint; the README's three install routes in
three fences; one `allowed_signers` spelling) and to the two findings the main agent chose to leave, and
asks of each: is the fix correct, is it complete, and did it introduce anything. Every fix was checked by
running or by enumeration, not by reading alone.

## Verdict: FINDINGS — all low, nothing that reopens the work

**All three round-3 fixes are correct and complete, and none introduced a defect in the Go code.** The
dry-run fix is the right shape and I validated its test in both states: unmutated, the test runs and passes
(`--- PASS`, verbose, so it is not a `-run` filter matching nothing); with the gate mutated back to
`if true`, it fails on the exact needle — `main_test.go:1485: install --dry-run made a PATH claim about a
binary it did not write ("so \`sh-agent\` runs")`. Completeness is by enumeration: `pathHint` has exactly one
call site (`main.go:277`), and on every non-dry-run path the installed binary really is written, because
`installFiles` errors out unless `selfExecutable()` returns bytes (`main.go:262-265`, `:632-640`, which has
no `return nil, nil`), so `Plan`'s `if selfExe != nil` guard (`plan.go:188`) cannot be skipped there. The
`allowed_signers` rename is one spelling in both documents, matches `internal/harness/release.go:234`, and
repairs the broken pointer round 3 named. The three fences are well formed and a whole-fence paste now runs
exactly one route.

The worst remaining item is a **residual sharpened by the fence split, not introduced by it**: the browser
route is now an independently copy-pasteable fence whose only executable content is `chmod +x` + `mv` of an
unverified download into `~/.local/bin/sh-agent`, with its three checks stated as prose above them
(`README.md:116-119`). The property the round-2 fix established for the `gh` route — unverified bytes cannot
become `~/.local/bin/sh-agent` — is the one property that fence lacks, and it is now the easiest fence to
paste alone. Everything else is bookkeeping about the record: the rewritten hung-mount reason **now holds**
with one refinement, `left` reason 1 holds on its first clauses and **fails on its fourth**, and `left`
reason 2 holds for the case it names but leaves two other cases in the same silent branch.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `README.md:116-119` — the browser route's fence is a standalone
  copy-pasteable block with no verification in it. Its executable content is exactly one line,
  `chmod +x ~/Downloads/sh-agent-darwin-arm64 && mv ~/Downloads/sh-agent-darwin-arm64 ~/.local/bin/sh-agent`;
  the three checks it depends on live in the comment above it ("run the same three checks as the gh route on
  them (signature, checksum, version), then"). The round-3 fix is right and I would keep it — a whole-fence
  paste running the `gh` route and then overwriting its verified output with a browser download was the
  worse shape — but splitting the fences gave this route its own copy button, and it is the route with no
  `&&` chain, no `ssh-keygen -Y verify`, no `sha256sum -c`. Not newly introduced: those lines were prose in
  the combined fence too. Why it is on the record: `README.md:82-89` and `remote.md:24-26` both now state,
  in their fence comments, that a failed check stops the move, and `README.md:129` tells the reader `install`
  and `status` will name a shadow — a reader who has just been promised verification everywhere is the one
  most likely to treat a fence as self-contained. It is also the only route naming `darwin-arm64`, i.e. the
  macOS path. Remediation, concrete: give it the same chain over `~/Downloads` — `cd ~/Downloads && printf
  '%s\n' '<the signer line>' > allowed_signers && ssh-keygen -Y verify -f allowed_signers -I
  ostling.simon@gmail.com -n sh-agent-release -s SHA256SUMS.sig < SHA256SUMS && shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS
  --ignore-missing && chmod +x sh-agent-darwin-arm64 && ./sh-agent-darwin-arm64 version && mv
  sh-agent-darwin-arm64 ~/.local/bin/sh-agent` — so every fence in the section has the property; or delete
  the route's `mv` line and end the prose with "then finish with the `gh` fence's checks in `~/Downloads`".
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:395` with `internal/harness/pathguard.go:30,48` —
  `left` reason 2 ("`binary unknown (installed file has no build info)` already says the file is not
  there") holds for the case it names and leaves two others in the same silent branch. `status` prints a
  `shadowed` line only inside `if … ; onPath {`, and `onPath` is false whenever `executableAt(binPath)`
  fails **or** no PATH entry holds that file. Case (i): the installed file exists, has build info, and has
  lost its execute bit — `binaryLine` is built from the build info and prints the **normal, healthy**
  version line (`main.go:373`'s "unknown (installed file has no build info)" is only the fallback), and no
  `shadowed` line is printed, while an unqualified `sh-agent` runs whatever else is on PATH. The reason's
  premise ("the binary line already says the file is not there") is false in that case. Case (ii): the bin
  dir is not on PATH at all and shadows exist — healthy binary line, no `shadowed` line, and no note either,
  because notes are `install`-only (`main.go:277`). Case (ii) is deliberate, pinned by a test
  (`main_test.go:1469`) and mitigated by `local.md:87`'s added "unqualified `sh-agent version` must match
  what was just installed"; case (i) is covered by nothing. Severity stays low: `install` writes the binary
  0755 (`plan.go:189`), so losing the bit takes an external `chmod`, an `rsync -r` without `-p`, or a
  restore. It is on the record because BUG-078's whole shape is "every command reported success about a
  binary that was not running", and this is the one path still able to print that. Remediation (optional,
  unchanged from round 3): print the shadows whenever `len(shadows) > 0` and let the `binary` line carry
  whether the file is installed — the code gets shorter, since the `onPath` condition leaves the call site.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:147,161` vs the round-3 `## Outcome`'s
  `left` reason 1 — the fourth clause of that reason does not hold. It says § Releases' rule "is about the
  SIGNING key's neighbourhood, not a verifier's temp dir". What § Releases says is not scoped to the signing
  machine: `:147` — "a signer file left on disk is the artifact `release.go` refuses to trust" — and `:161`
  — "a file on **any machine** cannot decide what a genuine release is — which is exactly why this
  procedure does not leave one lying about". A verifier's temp dir is on a machine. The conclusion (leave
  the finding unfixed) is nonetheless sound and stands on the reason's other clauses, which I checked: the
  chain does leave `$D` on any failure (`rm -r "$D"` is the last link, `README.md:96`, `remote.md:35`);
  nothing in `$D` is secret (the asset, `SHA256SUMS`, `SHA256SUMS.sig`, and an `allowed_signers` holding the
  **public** ed25519 line already published at `release.go:40`); and a failed verification leaves the asset
  **non-executable**, because `chmod +x` sits after both checks. The "cleaned by the OS" clause is measured
  true **on this box only**: `/tmp` is `tmpfs` (cleared at reboot), `/usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/tmp.conf` carries
  `q /tmp 1777 root root 10d`, and `systemd-tmpfiles-clean.timer` is `static` and **active**. That is a
  property of this machine, not of the procedure, and it was not measured on macOS, which the same block
  targets. Remediation: none to the code; if the reason is cited again, cite the first clauses only.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/pathguard.go:28-54` — the rewritten hung-mount reason
  **holds**, with one refinement worth having on the record. The rewrite ("the walk `stat`s every PATH entry
  ahead of the installed file, which is MORE than the shell does — the shell stops at its first match, so a
  shadow short-circuits it; the exposure is bounded by those entries and is the cost of naming every shadow
  rather than the first") is checkable against the code and true: `PathShadows` returns at the first
  `os.SameFile` match (`:48-50`), so with a reachable installed file it stats the entries up to and
  including the one holding it, while a shell finding a shadow at entry 1 stats one. This answers round 3's
  objection exactly. The refinement: the bound "entries ahead of the installed file" presumes PATH reaches
  the installed file. When `binPath` is missing, is a directory, or has no execute bit, `haveTarget` is
  false (`:30`), no early return can fire, and the walk stats **every distinct PATH entry** — the same worst
  case as a shell that finds no `sh-agent` anywhere, still on the operator's own PATH on the operator's own
  command, so the conclusion (accepted availability cost, no code change) is unaffected. `status`
  (`main.go:395`) shares the bound.

## Confirmed fixed and correct (round-3 findings)

- **`install --dry-run` makes no PATH claim — fixed, correct, complete, and the test proves it.**
  `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:270-282`: the whole `pathHint` call sits inside `if !dryRun`, with a comment naming
  why. Three separate checks:
  1. *No second path.* `grep -rn "pathHint\|PathShadows" cmd/ internal/` gives exactly two production call
     sites — `main.go:277` (install) and `main.go:395` (status) — and `status` takes no `--dry-run`.
  2. *The remaining (non-dry-run) path cannot print the false message.* The message was false only when the
     installed file was absent. `installFiles` calls `selfExecutable()` first and returns its error
     (`main.go:262-265`); `selfExecutable` (`:632-640`) returns `os.ReadFile`'s slice or an error and has no
     `return nil, nil`, so `Plan`'s `if selfExe != nil` (`plan.go:188`) always appends `BinPath` at 0755 and
     `harness.Install` errors rather than silently skipping it. So whenever `pathHint` runs, the file it
     asks about exists and is executable.
  3. *Must-fail validated by mutation, in a scratch copy of the tree* (`.agents/scratch/security-bug078/
     mustfail/`, a `tar` copy excluding `.git`; the anchor was asserted unique before the edit, the file
     restored from a saved copy afterwards and `diff`-confirmed identical to the source; the real working
     tree was never touched and `git status`/`git tag` after the probe showed nothing of mine but this
     report). Unmutated: `--- PASS` under `-v`, so the test really ran. Mutated `if !dryRun {` → `if true {`:
     `--- FAIL`, at `main_test.go:1485`, on the needle `"so \`sh-agent\` runs"`.
  The chosen fix (print nothing) is the better of the two remediations round 3 offered: a third message
  would have had to make a true statement about a binary that does not exist. The assertion round 3 asked to
  keep — the exact `note: … is not on PATH, so \`sh-agent\` runs … instead; put … ahead of it` string for a
  genuinely off-PATH home — is unchanged and still passes.
- **The new assertion's needles are complete.** `main_test.go:1473-1488` installs `--dry-run` into a
  **fresh** `t.TempDir()` while `PATH` is still the single `elsewhere` directory holding a 0755 decoy
  `sh-agent` (`:1444-1448`), so a re-enabled `pathHint` lands in the `case len(shadows) > 0` branch — which
  is what the mutation run demonstrated. Matching the three needles against `pathHint`'s three branches
  (`main.go:655-662`): `warning: %s comes before %s on PATH, so \`sh-agent\` runs that one` is caught twice
  ("comes before", "so \`sh-agent\` runs"); `note: %s is not on PATH, so \`sh-agent\` runs %s instead` by
  "so \`sh-agent\` runs"; `note: %s is not on PATH; add it so \`sh-agent\` is available everywhere` by "add
  it so \`sh-agent\` is available everywhere". Every branch is covered, so no `pathHint` regression can slip
  past this assertion as a silent no-op.
- **No description outlived the behaviour.** Grepped the living docs for claims about this output
  (`README.md:129`, `local.md:87`, `remote.md:44,191`, `BUG-078-*.md:28,34`): each describes what `install`
  and `status` print on a **real** install, and none promises a PATH hint from `--dry-run`, so the gate
  contradicts no documented behaviour. `pathHint`'s own doc comment (`main.go:642-649`) still describes the
  two situations it prints and is accurate for the paths that reach it.
- **One `allowed_signers` spelling — fixed, and the pointer resolves.** `README.md:92,93` and
  `remote.md:25,31,32` all use the underscore form; `grep -rn "allowed-signers"` finds no hyphenated
  **filename** left in `README.md`, `remote.md`, `internal/`, or `cmd/`. `remote.md:25`'s "the signer line
  is § Releases' `allowed_signers` line" now points at a file that section creates twice (`:113` as
  `.agents/scratch/allowed_signers`, `:145` in the release check), and the name matches
  `internal/harness/release.go:234` (`filepath.Join(dir, "allowed_signers")`). The rename changes nothing
  about the chain's security: the file is written and consumed by adjacent links of the same `&&` chain in a
  `mktemp -d` directory, and named on both command lines. The one hyphen left in the deploy guides is
  `local.md:43`, "the allowed-signers line compiled INTO the binary", which describes a *line*, not a file —
  a cosmetic inconsistency, not a broken pointer.
- **Three fences — fixed, and each is well formed.** `README.md:89-97` (gh), `:100-114` (`go install`),
  `:116-119` (browser). Each opens with ```` ```bash ```` and closes with ```` ``` ````; the `gh` fence ends
  at `mv … && cd ~ && rm -r "$D"` with nothing after it, so a whole-fence paste runs one route and cannot
  reach the `go install` or `chmod ~/Downloads` lines. The scenario round 3 measured — a verified binary
  overwritten by an unverified browser download in a single paste — is no longer available from the copy
  button.
- **Nothing else in the Go delta.** `git diff b029ea1..28e4747` over `cmd/` and `internal/` is the four-line
  `if !dryRun` gate plus its comment and the sixteen-line test addition. `internal/harness/pathguard.go` is
  **byte-identical** to the round-3 version (re-read end to end here, 67 lines): identity walk,
  `os.SameFile` at `:48`, dedupe before the executable check at `:40-43`, POSIX empty-entry handling at
  `:35-39`, `os.Stat` and `path/filepath` only, nothing opened, read, or executed.

## Checked

- **Secrets** — nothing added in this delta. The only key material in range is the **public** ed25519
  allowed-signers line, unchanged in content, at `README.md:92` and `remote.md:31,113,145`; it is the blob
  compiled in at `internal/harness/release.go:40` and publishing it is its purpose. The private half is
  never referenced. No `.env`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.tfvars`, `*.tfstate` or credential JSON in range. The
  dry-run change *reduces* what is printed; nothing new is echoed to logs.
- **Injection** — the Go delta adds no sink; it removes a call. The `printf '%s\n' '<literal>' >
  allowed_signers` rename changes a redirect target to another literal: no expansion, no external input. In
  the shell blocks every expansion is still double-quoted (`"$D"`, `"$ASSET"`, `"./$ASSET"`).
  `PathShadows` still splits PATH with `filepath.SplitList`, joins with `filepath.Join`, and every sink is
  `fmt.Fprintf` with a constant format string and the path as an argument.
- **Authz/authn** — none in range: no endpoint, session, identity decision or privilege change. The one
  trust decision is release-artifact verification, and this delta changes only the signer file's *name*, not
  the structure of the `&&` chains that guard it. `sudo` appears only as prose on `remote.md:38`.
- **Crypto** — nothing hand-rolled, nothing added, in this delta or the range. The documents *consume*
  `ssh-keygen -Y verify` and `sha256sum -c` as designed, under the pinned namespace `sh-agent-release` and
  the compiled-in identity, signature **before** checksum — the correct order.
  `internal/harness/release.go` is unchanged across the whole range. No primitive, token, session, KDF, RNG
  or auth flow is implemented or composed here.
- **Dependencies** — none added; `go.mod` and `go.sum` untouched across `4cdc0b5..28e4747`. `pathguard.go`
  imports `os` and `path/filepath` only. No remediation above adds a dependency (the README one is shell
  commands already used in the adjacent fence). `govulncheck` is installed
  (`/home/kesokaj/.go/bin/govulncheck`) but was **not run**: it queries `vuln.go.dev` and this review is
  under a no-network limit. Per `AGENTS.md` it is clean on the go1.27.1 SDK this box runs, and this range
  adds no dependency and no new stdlib surface, so a run would add no signal about this diff — re-run it in
  a networked gate. No npm ecosystem here, so `npm audit` is not applicable.
- **GCP surface** — nothing in range: no IAM binding, service account, Cloud Run flag,
  `--allow-unauthenticated`, secret-as-env-var, or service-account key file. This repository has no GCP
  deploy path.
- **Markdown for secrets, private data and instruction-shaped text** — the delta's README and `remote.md`
  hunks read with context; no added private data, no credential, no text instructing an agent to act outside
  the documented procedure. `remote.md:161` keeps the standing note that this repository's trail names
  internal hostnames and machine paths — fine privately, a separate decision before publication.
- **Tests, run by me** — `go test ./cmd/sh-agent/ -run
  TestOffPathInstallNamesWhatAnswersAndDoesNotWarnTwice -count=1 -v` in the scratch copy: PASS unmutated,
  FAIL mutated (transcript summarised above). No other test was run by me.
- **Temp-directory cleanup, measured** — `/tmp` is `tmpfs`; `/usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/tmp.conf` has
  `q /tmp 1777 root root 10d` and `q /var/tmp 1777 root root 30d`; `systemd-tmpfiles-clean.timer` is
  `static` and `active`; `TMPDIR` unset. This box only.

## Not examined

- `govulncheck ./...` — not run (no-network limit, reason above). `npm audit` — not applicable. `gofmt`,
  `go vet` and a full `go test -race ./...` were **not** run by me; the round-4 verifier log
  `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-18-verify-bug078-path-shadow-4.md` exists and I did not read it.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (≈975 lines) was not read end to end. Read across rounds 3-4: the full diff of the
  range, `:235-285` (`installFiles` and the gated call), `:355-420` (`status`, the binary line, the shadow
  block), `:626-690` (`selfExecutable`, `pathHint`, the head of `attributionSet`), plus greps for
  `pathHint`, `PathShadows`, `binOnPath`, `EvalSymlinks`, `selfExe`, `no build info`, `BinPath`. Both call
  sites are enumerated; the rest of the file is unread.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` (≈1489 lines) was not read end to end. Read: `:1425-1489` — the tail of
  `TestInstallAndStatusNameAPathShadow` and all of
  `TestOffPathInstallNamesWhatAnswersAndDoesNotWarnTwice` including the new dry-run block. Lines 1-1424 are
  unread. `internal/harness/pathguard_test.go` was read in round 3 from `:260` to the end; `:1-259` (other
  tests in the same file) remain unread, and `git diff b029ea1..28e4747` shows the file unchanged this
  round. `internal/harness/plan.go` was read only at `:66-80` and `:170-200`.
- `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` was read at `:20-40` and `:84-92` this round, with grep context at
  `:44`, `:113-115`, `:145-147`, `:161`, `:191`; the rest was not read end to end.
  `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md` was read only at `:43`, `:67` and `:87` via grep context — its one-line
  change in this range was reviewed in round 3. `README.md` was read end to end in round 3 (227 lines);
  this round only `:74-129`.
- `internal/harness/` beyond `pathguard.go`, `plan.go` and greps of `apply.go`/`release.go` was not
  re-read; `release.go` was last read in round 2 and is unchanged in range.
- The shell chains were **never executed**: no `gh release download`, no network, no release fetched,
  nothing moved to `~/.local/bin`, nothing written to the real `$HOME`, and `sh-agent report` was never run.
  `gh`'s exit status on a non-matching `--pattern` and on a missing tag is taken from its documented
  behaviour, not measured. macOS was not exercised at all: `shasum` was probed on Linux at 6.04 in round 3,
  and macOS `/tmp` cleanup was not measured. `os.SameFile` was exercised on Linux only.
- Trail artifacts inside the range were not read: the four `2026-09-18-review-*.md` code/docs reports and
  the four `2026-09-18-verify-bug078-path-shadow*.md` logs. Only the round-3 SECURITY report was read in
  full, for its `## Outcome`.
- Scratch: `.agents/scratch/security-bug078/mustfail/` (the 6.4 MB tree copy used for the mutation) was
  deleted after the probe. `.agents/scratch/security-bug078/` still holds round 3's `probe/`, a decoy
  `fakebin/sh-agent`, a scratch `home/` and `stashed-binary` — gitignored, safe to delete.

## Outcome

Written by the main agent at the close of the work. This was the one extra round granted at the cap; the dispatch said only a HIGH reopens, and none is.

- [low] the browser fence's only executable lines moved an unverified file — **fixed** as a docs-only edit under ten lines (Definition of Done: steps 4 and 5): the fence is the same `&&` chain as the `gh` route over the files in `~/Downloads`, ending in the one `mv` and the removal of the three helper files (README.md:119). The macOS `shasum -a 256 -c - --ignore-missing` form is written from its manual, not run on a Mac — named in the handoff.
- [low] `left` reason 2 (no `shadowed` line when the installed file is missing) had holes — reason **narrowed** to what holds: `onPath == false` means PATH does not reach an executable that is the installed file, so `status` names no shadow of it; a present file with no execute bit is a broken install whether or not anything shadows it, and the next `install` rewrites it; the bin-dir-off-PATH-with-shadows case is the tested, deliberate one, said by `install`'s note and by `local.md` § Verify. Still `left` (main agent).
- [low] `left` reason 1's clause about § Releases' rule scoping — clause **withdrawn**, the rest stands: a failed chain leaves `$D` for inspection, nothing in it is secret, and the temp dir is cleaned by the OS (measured on this box, `q /tmp … 10d`; not measured on macOS — handoff). Still `left` (main agent).
- [low] hung-mount reason — holds; the refinement (with the installed file missing or non-executable the walk `stat`s every distinct entry, the shell's own worst case) is accepted as written and changes nothing.

title: Security review — BUG-078 PATH shadow warning (4cdc0b5..52574a0)
body:
# Security review — BUG-078 PATH shadow warning (4cdc0b5..52574a0)

Range reviewed: 4cdc0b5..52574a0

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Nothing in the Go change is exploitable: `PathShadows`/`ResolveExecutable` only `Lstat`/`Stat` PATH candidates,
never open or execute one, and print strictly less than `which -a` (the candidate path, never the
`EvalSymlinks` target, and only entries ahead of the install dir). The worst problem is in the docs half of
the diff: `README.md:86` tells a first-time installer to build the release trust anchor themselves from a
placeholder (`'YOUR_EMAIL ssh-ed25519 AAAA…'`) when the genuine line is already sitting in this repository at
`internal/harness/release.go:40` and `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:80`, and it leaves that `allowed-signers`
file permanently in `~/.local/bin` — a user-writable trust anchor in a PATH directory, which is exactly the
artifact `remote.md` § Releases deletes on the signing side ("a signer file left on disk is the artifact
release.go refuses to trust"). A reader with no key source named will take it from the release page that also
serves the artifact, which makes the signature check self-certifying. Secondary: the same fenced block still
offers two install routes with no verification at all beside the newly verified one. Everything else is low:
advisory output that cannot be the integrity check the docs nearly read as, and message-correctness edges.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `README.md:86-88` — the only place a NEW machine can bootstrap trust names
  no key. The snippet writes `allowed-signers` from a literal placeholder into `~/.local/bin` (a PATH
  directory), never says where the real signer line comes from, and never removes the file. Two distinct
  weaknesses. (a) *Unspecified trust anchor*: the obvious source for the missing key is the release page that
  serves `SHA256SUMS.sig`, so signature verification certifies the channel with the channel's own key. A
  literal paste fails loudly (`ssh-keygen -Y verify` rejects `AAAA…`), so there is no silent bypass — the
  realistic failure is a reader who fetches the key from whatever page is in front of them, or skips the step.
  (b) *Durable writable anchor*: `remote.md` § Releases removes `allowed_signers` immediately after each use
  and says why; the README instead leaves one in a PATH dir and tells the reader to repeat these steps on
  every update, so anyone who can write `~/.local/bin/allowed-signers` (any process running as the operator,
  any earlier compromise, any sync tool) makes a forged `SHA256SUMS` verify from then on. Remediation: print
  the real line and its fingerprint in the README —
  `ostling.simon@gmail.com ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIBkx0BICH1xG18f0a0F/02Vw0OvBTfSOVNXkPkO62NCR`,
  `SHA256:5HpYQJjpG+yE1xXBTOIZPsTkbkgkVnV8z0eG8hBawyU` (a public key, not a secret; it is already in this
  repository twice, compiled into the binary at `internal/harness/release.go:40` as `releaseSigner` and
  documented at `remote.md:80`) — add one line saying it must not be taken from the release page, write the
  signer file to a temp dir, and `rm -f` it after the verify. The in-binary copy cannot bootstrap the *first*
  install, which is why the README must carry the key rather than point at it. Secondary: `remote.md:26` also
  names `allowed-signers` without pointing at line 80 for its contents and without deleting it afterwards.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `README.md:88-105` — the same fenced block that now verifies route 1 leaves two
  unverified routes beside it, with nothing marking the difference. The browser-download route
  (`chmod +x ~/Downloads/sh-agent-darwin-arm64 && mv …`) has no checksum and no signature step at all, and the
  `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine` note below it reads as an endorsement of that route on macOS. The
  `go install` route with `GOPRIVATE='github.com/kesokaj/*'` disables both `GONOPROXY` and `GONOSUMDB` for that
  path (verified with `go env`: `GOPRIVATE` is their default), so it fetches source directly over SSH with the
  checksum database switched off and performs no release-signature check either — its entire trust basis is
  GitHub plus a tag, and "a pushed tag is never moved" is this project's policy, not an enforced property.
  Both are plausible in principle against a compromised GitHub account or session, which is precisely the
  threat `SHA256SUMS.sig` exists to cover. Remediation: repeat the two verification lines for the browser
  route, and label the `go install` route as unverified-by-design in one clause so a reader chooses knowingly.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `README.md:110,115` and `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:31,35` — `sh-agent version`
  unqualified is presented as the check that "matters"/"comes first on purpose", but the binary that answers it
  is the one under suspicion: a shadowing `sh-agent` prints any version string it likes, and so does a
  shadowing binary asked for the new `warning:`/`shadowed` lines (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go:393,683`) — the guard
  runs inside the artifact it vouches for. The unqualified check separates STALE from FRESH, never GENUINE
  from FORGED. Both documents do the authentic check correctly (signature + checksum over the file, then
  `./sh-agent-<os>-<arch> version` by path, before the `mv`); the exploitable gap is only that a reader may
  substitute the cheap check for the real one on a later update. Remediation: one sentence saying the
  unqualified check detects the wrong binary winning, not a tampered one, and that the file checks are what
  establish authenticity.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:182` — Verify now accepts "`sh-agent status`
  with … no `shadowed` line", but the absence of that line is not evidence. `status` emits it only when
  `binOnPath(home)` is true (`cmd/sh-agent/main.go:391`), and `binOnPath` (`main.go:656-665`) is an exact
  string match with a single `TrimSuffix(p, "/")`, while `PathShadows` normalises with `filepath.Clean`
  (`internal/harness/pathguard.go:32`). Two normalisations for one question: a PATH entry spelled
  `~/.local/bin//`, a `$HOME` reached through a symlink, a case-different entry on macOS, or an install into a
  system path all silence the check, and `main.go:651` then prints "is not on PATH" about a directory that is.
  Separately `os.Getenv("PATH")` is this process's PATH, not the operator's interactive shell's (differs under
  `sudo`, `env -i`, login vs non-login shells, and a shell whose `hash` table caches an older location), so a
  quiet `status` says nothing about what the next prompt will run. Remediation: make `binOnPath` use
  `filepath.Clean` — the same comparison `PathShadows` already uses — and keep `sh-agent version` unqualified
  as the deciding line in § Verify, with the `shadowed` line marked corroborating rather than a pass condition.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/pathguard.go:60-66` — `install` and `status` now walk every
  PATH entry with `EvalSymlinks` + `os.Stat` where they previously did a pure string comparison. The FIFO and
  device-node concern is moot: `stat(2)` does not open the file and does not block on either. A hung
  NFS/autofs/FUSE mount on PATH does block `os.Stat` uninterruptibly, so `sh-agent install` and `sh-agent
  status` can hang where they previously could not. Input is the operator's own PATH, impact is availability
  of the operator's own command, and every shell PATH lookup already has the same property — accepted-risk
  shaped, recorded for the record rather than for a fix. Symlink loops and 255-deep chains return an error and
  are handled.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/pathguard.go:51`, `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:393,648,683` — a
  candidate path is printed to the terminal verbatim. A PATH entry may hold any byte but `:` and NUL,
  including ESC, CR and newline, so a directory named with an ANSI sequence can rewrite the warning line (hide
  it, or forge a reassuring one). The precondition — an attacker-controlled directory on the operator's PATH
  holding an executable `sh-agent` — is strictly worse than the escape, since that attacker already gets code
  execution the next time the operator types `sh-agent`; this is an amplifier, not a way in. No leak beyond
  `which -a`: only the candidate is printed, the resolved target never is, and `sh-agent report` collects
  files (`state.json`, the feedback log), not command output, so these paths do not reach the feedback
  repository. Remediation (cheap): print with `%q`, which escapes control bytes and, as a bonus, fixes the
  next finding's ambiguity.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/harness/pathguard.go:29-30,47` — an empty PATH entry correctly becomes
  `.` (POSIX), but `filepath.Join(".", "sh-agent")` yields the bare relative name, so the message reads
  "warning: sh-agent comes before /home/u/.local/bin/sh-agent on PATH". That is unactionable text for the one
  case where a planted `./sh-agent` is most likely — the working directory. Remediation: report `./sh-agent`
  or the absolute path; the current form is pinned by `pathguard_test.go` ("an empty PATH entry means the
  working directory"), so the test moves with the fix.

Not findings, checked and sound: the shadow walk never executes a candidate — the only `exec` reachable from
`cmd/sh-agent/main.go` is the pre-existing `exec.LookPath("go")` at line 153 for the rebuild decision, outside
this range and unchanged; no shell, no user-controlled format string; `--dry-run` only reads; a dry run on a
home with no installed binary yet loses the same-file suppression, but a link to a not-yet-existing target is
dangling and therefore unresolvable, so it cannot produce a false shadow. `haveTarget && got == target`
correctly silences a symlink to the installed binary and is covered both in unit and end-to-end tests. The
README's verify → run → `mv` order runs the downloaded binary only after its signature and checksum pass.
`grep -v '^#' SHA256SUMS | sha256sum -c - --ignore-missing` cannot pass vacuously — measured here, GNU
`sha256sum` and Perl `shasum` both exit 1 with "no file was verified" when every listed file is absent, and
both accept `--ignore-missing`. One divergence worth knowing but not a finding: on a malformed checksum line
GNU exits 1 and `shasum` exits 0, unreachable here because the file is signature-verified before it is parsed.
Stripping the `# styrman-harness vX.Y.Z` line does mean the manual path never binds `SHA256SUMS` to the
version asked for, the way `sh-agent update` does (D26); `gh release download vX.Y.Z` pins the assets, so this
is a hardening note only — `grep -q '^# styrman-harness vX.Y.Z' SHA256SUMS` before the `-c` would close it.

## Checked
- **Secrets** — no credential, token or key added. The signer public key and operator email in `remote.md:80`
  and `internal/harness/release.go:40` are public material and predate this range; `README.md:86` adds only a
  placeholder. No `.env`, `*.pem`, `*.key` in range; nothing echoed into logs beyond PATH-derived paths the
  operator already knows (finding 6). Neither markdown file gained private data or instruction-shaped text
  that would steer an agent — every added command is a verification or a move, and the two placeholder forms
  (`…/sh-agent-<os>-<arch>`, `AAAA…`) fail loudly rather than silently doing something else.
- **Injection** — no shell, no `exec`, no SQL, no template. PATH is split with `filepath.SplitList` and each
  entry joined with `filepath.Join`; the only sink is `fmt.Fprintf` to an `io.Writer` with a constant format
  string. Terminal-control injection in the printed path is finding 6.
- **Authz/authn** — none in range; no endpoint, no identity decision. The one trust decision is release
  signature verification, covered by findings 1, 2 and 3.
- **Crypto** — nothing hand-rolled and nothing added. The diff consumes `ssh-keygen -Y verify` and
  `sha256sum -c` as designed, in the namespace (`sh-agent-release`) the signing procedure uses and the binary
  compiles in (`ReleaseNamespace`, `release.go:25`); no primitive, token, session or auth flow is implemented
  or composed here.
- **Dependencies** — none added; `go.mod`/`go.sum` untouched in the range, stdlib only (`os`, `path/filepath`,
  `fmt`, `strings`), consistent with the repo's stdlib-only rule. `govulncheck` is installed
  (`/home/kesokaj/.go/bin/govulncheck`) and the toolchain is go1.27.1, but it was NOT run: it fetches
  `vuln.go.dev` and this review is under a no-network limit. Per `AGENTS.md` it reports clean on go1.25.8+, so
  a run here would add no signal about this diff; re-run it in a networked gate. No npm ecosystem in this repo.
- **GCP surface** — nothing in range: no IAM binding, service account, Cloud Run flag, or secret-as-env-var.

## Not examined
- `govulncheck ./...` — not run, no-network limit (see above). `npm audit` — not applicable.
- macOS behaviour of the changed docs: `shasum` was measured with the Perl `Digest::SHA` build on this Linux
  box, not the binary macOS ships; the option-support claim is inferred for macOS, not observed.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (955 lines) and `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` (1472 lines) were read through the diff
  plus targeted greps, not end to end: every call site of `shadows`, `binOnPath`, `shadowHint`, `os.Getenv`
  and `exec.` was enumerated, so the new code's blast radius inside main.go is established, but unrelated
  regions of both files were not read.
- `internal/harness/release.go` and `internal/harness/report.go` were grepped, not read: enough to establish
  the compiled-in signer and namespace and that `report` collects files rather than command output, not enough
  to vouch for either file's own logic.
- No runtime probe of `install`/`status` against a scratch home with a hostile PATH: the existing tests cover
  the shadow and off-PATH cases, and constructing an escape-sequence PATH entry would have been exploit-shaped.
- `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-18-verify-bug078-path-shadow.md` (untracked, outside the range) was not read.

## Outcome

Written by the main agent after the fix, in the fix's commit; the fix itself is the re-dispatch's input.

- [medium] placeholder signer, and a signer file left in a PATH dir — **fixed**: the README's block now carries the real line, the one compiled into `internal/harness/release.go` and printed in `remote.md` § Releases, with the instruction to take it from a checkout or a binary already trusted and never from the release page (README.md:91); every file is downloaded and verified in a `mktemp -d` directory that is removed after the one `mv` of the binary (README.md:85). `remote.md`'s block says the same of its `$D`.
- [low] browser and `go install` routes unlabelled — **fixed**: the `go install` comment names what that route trusts and that neither the checksum database nor a release signature is checked (README.md:100); the browser route now says to fetch the two checksum files and run the same three checks before the `mv` (README.md:112).
- [low] `sh-agent version` and the new lines are the suspect binary's own output — **fixed**: README (README.md:124) and `remote.md` (.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:35) both say it tells stale from fresh, never genuine from forged, and that authenticity is the file checks before the move.
- [low] `remote.md` Verify's "no `shadowed` line" could pass vacuously through `binOnPath` — **fixed** with the code reviewer's high finding: one definition of "on PATH" (internal/harness/pathguard.go:22); `local.md` § Verify says the same now (.agents/docs/deploy/local.md:87).
- [low] `stat(2)` on every PATH directory; a hung network mount would hang `install` and `status` — **rebutted**: the same `stat` is what the shell does to resolve `sh-agent` at all, and what `which -a` does; a PATH entry on a hung mount already hangs every command lookup on that machine, so this adds no hang that was not there. No code change.
- [low] control bytes in a printed PATH entry — **rebutted**: the printed strings are the operator's own `PATH` entries, printed exactly as `which -a` prints them; nothing untrusted reaches them, and quoting would make the path unusable for copy-paste, which is what the line is for. No code change.
- [low] an empty PATH entry printed as a bare `sh-agent` — **fixed**: it prints as `./sh-agent` (internal/harness/pathguard.go:37), asserted by `TestPathShadows` (internal/harness/pathguard_test.go:349) with `t.Chdir`.

title: Security review — BUG-079 stale-running-binary note, round 3 (2026-09-18)
body:
# Security review — BUG-079 stale-running-binary note, round 3   (2026-09-18)

Range reviewed: c868ed4..a078848

## Verdict: FINDINGS

No high. The round-2 medium is closed on the release path: all fifteen returns of
`UpdateFromRelease` that install nothing now come BEFORE `NoteRunningElsewhere`
(`internal/harness/release.go:178`, each traced below), so the branch that had just proved the
running file newer than every release can no longer advise replacing it, and the message no
longer asserts staleness — it states file identity, which is what the code knows. Tracing that
gate, however, put the ordering guard it leans on under the lamp, and the guard has a
normalization hole that is the worst thing in this report: `IsReleaseVersion` accepts leading
zeros (`^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$`, `internal/harness/source.go:44`) while `releaseParts` runs
each field through `strconv.Atoi` (`release.go:384-391`), so `v1.02.2` and `v1.2.2` compare
EQUAL though the strings differ — the switch's three `return`s are all skipped and the update
proceeds. The signed payload is the `SHA256SUMS` content only (`verifyRelease:239-244` feeds it
to `ssh-keygen -Y verify`; asset names are tag-independent), so a previous release's binary,
`SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig` republished under a tag spelled `v1.02.2` verifies genuinely
and installs over a running `v1.2.2` — a rollback the comment at `release.go:109-112` says the
guard exists to prevent, needing GitHub write access and no signing key. That code is
pre-existing and outside the diff; it is in the blast radius because the round-2 fix's entire
argument is "past this switch the installed file is newer". The rest is low: the checkout path
prints the note after a `Reinstall` that is not proven newer, and `NoteRunningElsewhere` is
`home`-blind, so under `--home` it offers to point a PATH-resolved `sh-agent` at a scratch-tree
binary or remove the real one. Exporting `NoteRunningElsewhere` widens nothing outside the
module. Nothing in the range touches secrets, auth, hand-rolled crypto, dependencies or the GCP
surface.

## Answers to the four checkable questions

1. **Is the medium closed? On the release path yes, subject to finding 1 — traced.**
   `UpdateFromRelease` (`internal/harness/release.go:90-180`) reaches the note at line 178 only
   past every other exit: `gh` missing (92), `LatestRelease` error (96), non-`vX.Y.Z` tag (103),
   `tag == version` (107-108, round-2 state (b)), running version not a release (114-115),
   `compareRelease(tag, version) < 0` (117-118, round-2 state (a)), `checkOnly` (121-122),
   `sshKeygen` (129), `MkdirAll base` (137), `MkdirTemp` (146), download (153), verify (157),
   `MkdirAll` of `dest`'s directory (164), `writeAtomic` (167), and the new binary's own
   `install` (176). So it prints only after `home/.local/bin/sh-agent` was replaced by a
   signature- and checksum-verified binary of a tag `T` for which the switch established
   `T != version`, `version` is a release, and `compareRelease(T, version) >= 0`. That `>=`
   rather than `>` is finding 1: with a leading-zero tag the relation is `== 0` and the running
   file can be the newer one after all. Two further residues: the checkout path has no such
   proof at all (finding 2), and after a successful `writeAtomic` whose subsequent child
   `install` FAILS (176) the installed file is new, the running one is behind, and nothing says
   so — fail-silent, not a weakness, recorded for completeness.
2. **Is the `ln -sfn` ownership concern addressed or only softened? Softened.**
   `internal/harness/pathguard.go:119` still offers `ln -sfn` FIRST and unconditionally and then
   conditions only the *preference* on a fact the program does not check although
   `RunningElsewhere` holds `from`'s `FileInfo`; "root-owned" is also not the whole risk class
   (finding 3).
3. **Does exporting `NoteRunningElsewhere` widen anything? Not outside the module.**
   `internal/harness` is an `internal/` package of module `github.com/kesokaj/styrman-harness`
   (go.mod, untouched in range), so the toolchain refuses any import from another repository;
   `grep -rn` finds exactly two call sites, `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:509` and `release.go:178`, plus
   tests. The function takes neither PATH nor exe from its caller — it reads `os.Getenv("PATH")`
   and `os.Executable()` itself — so a caller can influence only `home` and `out`, and the
   function only stats and prints: it never writes, removes or execs. The one thing a caller can
   get wrong is `home`, which is finding 4.
4. **Can the note be lost or misattributed after a noisy install? Not lost; misattributable.**
   The child's stdout and stderr both go to the same `out` (`release.go:174`) and `cmd.Run` →
   `Wait` does not return until those copies finish, so the note is always the last line on that
   path; with `out` an `*os.File` the child writes the descriptor directly and has already
   exited — same ordering. Nothing can interleave inside the note, which is one `Fprintf`. The
   residual is human: it follows the installed binary's own install output, including that
   binary's `warning: … comes before … on PATH` line about the same file, so a reader may take
   "note:" for part of the install. It self-identifies with "this update ran from", and a pasted
   log preserves the order. No finding.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/source.go:44` with
  `internal/harness/release.go:105-119,384-391` (pre-existing, in the blast radius of the gate
  the round-2 fix relies on) — the "never sideways or backwards" guard can be walked past with a
  leading-zero tag, which turns `update` into a rollback channel for anyone who can publish a
  release without holding the signing key. `IsReleaseVersion` accepts `v1.02.2`; `releaseParts`
  `Atoi`s each field, so `compareRelease("v1.02.2", "v1.2.2") == 0`; the switch returns only on
  `==` by string, a non-release running version, or `< 0`, so execution falls through to the
  download. `verifyRelease` signs nothing tag-specific — `ssh-keygen -Y verify` is fed the
  `SHA256SUMS` bytes, whose lines are `<hash>  sh-agent-linux-amd64`, identical across releases —
  so the attacker republishes an older release's three assets verbatim under the new tag and
  every check passes. Result on each binary-only place that runs `update`: an older genuine
  binary replaces the newer one and then installs its own older embedded context, skills and
  agents; the new note then tells the operator their newer running copy is "not the installed
  binary" and offers to remove it. Prerequisite is GitHub write access to the release repository;
  the yield is limited to previously signed artifacts, which is why this is medium and not high.
  Remediation, one character plus its message: make the guard strict —
  `case compareRelease(tag, version) <= 0:` — so only a strictly greater release installs, and
  additionally reject a tag whose text is not its own canonical form (compare `tag` with
  `fmt.Sprintf("v%d.%d.%d", parts...)`) so a non-canonical spelling can never name a release at
  all. Stdlib only; no dependency, nothing to justify. Longer term, bind the tag into the signed
  payload (a line in `SHA256SUMS`), which also kills asset replay across releases.
  Validated in both directions with a scratch probe that copies `releaseVersion`, `releaseParts`
  and `compareRelease` verbatim (`.agents/scratch/security-bug079-3/probe.go`, gitignored, no
  network, nothing published): `tag=v1.02.2 running=v1.2.2 -> isRelease=true cmp=0
  fallsThroughToInstall=true` (must-fail state), against `v1.2.2/v1.2.2 -> false`,
  `v1.2.1/v1.2.2 -> false` and `v1.02.1/v1.2.2 -> false` (must-pass states). It exercises a copy
  of the predicates, not the package's own unexported ones — a reviewer may not add a test to
  `internal/harness`.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:461-509` — on the checkout path the note
  prints after `Reinstall` with no evidence that the installed binary is newer than the process
  that ran the update, and then offers `ln -sfn`/removal against that process's file. `update`
  prints "up to date with upstream" (467) and, when `!checkOnly`, falls through to `Reinstall`
  (508) and the note (509); `Reinstall` rebuilds from the working tree, so a binary is always
  written and the operator's D2 gate ("only after a binary was actually written") holds — but
  "written" is not "newer". Concrete state: a copy on PATH built from a local commit ahead of
  `origin/main`, or from a branch never pushed, runs `sh-agent update`; the checkout
  fast-forwards to the older `origin/main`, `Reinstall` writes that older build, and the note
  advises pointing the newer file at it or removing it. `ResolveSource`
  (`internal/harness/repo.go:22-48`) keeps a RELEASE binary off this path entirely — it always
  returns `EmbeddedSource` — so the running process here is a development build, which is also
  why the round-2 remediation is awkward: `buildinfo` gives such a build a VCS stamp, not a
  version. Narrow, hence low; confidence medium because I did not exercise it. Remediation:
  compare the two builds' VCS revisions (`main.go:377` already reads the installed file's build
  info) and drop the remedy clause unless the installed one is ahead; or, simpler and shorter,
  keep only the first sentence of the note — the identity fact plus `hash -r` — and delete the
  remedy from both paths.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/pathguard.go:119` — `ln -sfn` is still offered
  first and unconditionally for a path whose ownership the program has already stat'ed and
  chooses not to read. Following it on the BUG-079 machine means
  `sudo ln -sfn ~/.local/bin/sh-agent /usr/local/bin/sh-agent`, after which a root-owned,
  system-wide PATH entry resolves to a file inside one user's home that that user — and every
  agent this harness dispatches as that user — can overwrite, so anyone running `sh-agent` from
  the system path (another account, `sudo sh-agent …`, a unit, a cron job) executes
  user-writable content. The added clause lowers the chance of that but leaves the unsafe option
  first and delegates the decision to the reader's knowledge of a fact the program holds.
  Root-ownership is not the whole class either: a package-manager path, `/opt/devbox/bin`, or a
  path owned by another non-root account weaken the same way. Low because the step is the
  operator's own on single-operator machines. Remediation: decide it in code — offer `ln -sfn`
  only when `from` is under `os.UserHomeDir()`, otherwise name removal alone (or say the path is
  the operator's to decide, and what changes if they link it). A lexical home check needs no
  build tags; `info.Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t).Uid` is the alternative if ownership is preferred
  over location.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/pathguard.go:112-120` with
  `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:509` — the note is `home`-blind: it calls `filepath.Join(home, BinPath)`
  "the installed binary" for whatever `home` the run used, so under `--home` it recommends
  wiring a PATH-resolved `sh-agent` to a binary outside the real home, or removing the real one.
  Reachable with the ordinary checkout-place setup this repository mandates: `~/.local/bin/sh-agent`
  is a development build (so `ResolveSource` takes the checkout path) and a PATH entry reaches it
  by name (the gate); the operator runs `sh-agent update --home .agents/scratch/x` to exercise an
  install, `Reinstall` writes `.agents/scratch/x/.local/bin/sh-agent`, and the note names THAT as
  the installed binary and offers `ln -sfn` it over — or removal of — their real
  `~/.local/bin/sh-agent`. `.agents/scratch/` is gitignored and written by every agent this
  harness dispatches, so the link version moves a PATH-resolved name onto an agent-writable path
  (and a dangling symlink as soon as scratch is cleaned); the removal version deletes the working
  install. Exploitable without an attacker (self-inflicted) and with one (any writer of
  `.agents/scratch/`). Low because the step is the operator's own with both paths printed in
  front of them, and because the pre-existing `PathShadows` warnings share the class — the note
  extends it rather than inventing it. Remediation: print the note only when `home` equals
  `os.UserHomeDir()` (stdlib, already used in home resolution) and stay silent otherwise, or keep
  the identity sentence and drop the remedy when it does not.

### Rebuttals and round-2 items re-checked

- **Raw `%s` of PATH-derived paths — still rebutted.** `from` comes from the operator's own PATH
  entries and `installed` from `--home`/`$HOME`; no untrusted producer reaches either, and `%q`
  would stop the output matching `which -a`/`type`, which the docs tell the reader to compare
  against. Round 2's log-injection caveat is unchanged and unacted on, as its Outcome says.
- **`os.Executable()` only stat'ed — still rebutted.** `exe` is consumed once
  (`pathguard.go:80`) and the returned value is always `cand`, built from a PATH entry; a
  `" (deleted)"` or stale-relative `exe` makes the `Stat` fail and the function returns
  `"", false` — fail-closed, pinned by the `exe missing` case.
- **`ln -sfn` argument order** — unchanged, and unchanged in consequence: `writeAtomic` replaces
  a symlink at `dest` by rename rather than writing through it, so a reversed link cannot
  redirect a later install out of `--home` (carried over from round 2's reading of `apply.go`).
- **`RunningElsewhere` stats PATH candidates without `executableAt`'s directory and exec-bit
  checks, unlike `PathShadows` — checked, no finding.** The comparison is `os.SameFile` against
  a file this process is executing; a directory or a mode-0 inode cannot be the same inode as a
  running executable, and hard and symbolic links share the inode's mode. No TOCTOU either: the
  result is printed, never acted on.
- **`--check` on both paths — silent, and tested in the must-be-silent state.**
  `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go:1543` (release path, up to date, with and without `--check`) and the
  `--check` assertion inside `TestCheckoutUpdateNamesTheBinaryItRanFrom`. The side effect sits
  below every read-only early return on both paths.

## Checked

- **Secrets** — none added: no credential, token or key in the eight changed files; no `.env*`,
  `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.tfvars`, `*.tfstate` or credential JSON in the range; no high-entropy
  literal. The note discloses only paths; a `$HOME`-derived path leaks the username into a pasted
  log exactly as every existing `sh-agent` line does.
