- **Injection** — nothing in the range execs, queries or templates; `from` and `installed` are
  stat'ed and printed only. The pre-existing exec of the downloaded binary (`release.go:173`) is
  unchanged and still behind the verification gate — whose bypass for a non-canonical tag is
  finding 1, an input-validation defect at the one boundary where unsigned GitHub metadata
  (`tag`) decides what gets installed. The new tests' fake `gh` lives in `t.TempDir()` behind
  `t.Setenv("PATH", …)`, and `t.Chdir(t.TempDir())` keeps the empty-PATH-entry probe out of the
  repository.
- **Authz/authn** — no auth path in range. The authorization-adjacent effects are the message
  inviting a privileged `sudo ln -sfn`/`sudo rm` (finding 3) and finding 1's reliance on release
  publishing rights rather than the signing key.
- **Crypto** — nothing hand-rolled and nothing crypto-adjacent added; the new code makes no
  crypto call. `ssh-keygen -Y verify` over `SHA256SUMS` with a compiled-in allowed-signers line is
  a vetted tool used as designed, and it still runs before any replacement. The weakness in
  finding 1 is not the primitive but the payload's lack of tag binding plus the version
  comparison — recorded there, not as a crypto finding.
- **Dependencies** — `go.mod`/`go.sum` not in the range; the added code imports only `fmt`, `io`,
  `os`, `path/filepath`. Stdlib-only rule held; both remediations above are stdlib. `govulncheck`
  IS installed at `/home/kesokaj/.go/bin/govulncheck` but was NOT run: it fetches vuln.go.dev and
  this dispatch forbids network. `npm audit` not applicable (no JavaScript in the repository).
- **GCP surface** — nothing in range: no IAM binding, service account, key file, Cloud Run flag,
  `--allow-unauthenticated`, or secret-as-env-var.
- **Binary/escape check** — `git diff --numstat c868ed4..a078848` shows no `-`/`-` pair; nothing
  in the range is binary.
- **Build and tests** — `gofmt -l cmd internal` clean, `go vet ./...` clean, and
  `go test -run 'TestRunningElsewhere|TestUpToDateUpdateSaysNothingAboutTheRunningBinary|TestCheckoutUpdateNamesTheBinaryItRanFrom|TestUpdateFromReleaseReplacesAndInstalls' ./cmd/sh-agent ./internal/harness`
  passes on both packages (no `-race`, no full suite — see Not examined).

## Not examined

- `govulncheck ./...` — not run (network forbidden). `AGENTS.md` claims clean on go1.25.8+ since
  2026-09-17; not re-verified this round.
- `go test -race ./...` in full — not run: tests outside this range can reach the network and the
  real home. Only the four named tests ran, without `-race`.
- Read end to end at `a078848`: the complete diff of all eight changed files,
  `internal/harness/pathguard.go`, and `internal/harness/release.go:80-191,219-264,371-391`.
  **Not** read end to end: `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (the diff hunks plus lines 188-232, 455-515,
  899-911 and grepped lines 50, 116-269, 334-431, 545-547; roughly 780 lines unread),
  `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` and `internal/harness/pathguard_test.go` (added blocks in full; the
  ~1486 and ~405 preceding lines unread), `internal/harness/release_test.go` (added hunk only),
  `README.md` and `ROADMAP.md` (changed hunks with context).
- Blast radius partially read: `verifyRelease`'s tail past line 264 and `downloadRelease`
  (`release.go:184-218`) — so finding 1's replay step rests on the signed payload being the
  `SHA256SUMS` bytes (read) and on `gh release download --pattern` fetching whatever the release
  holds (not read); `Reinstall`'s body, `harness.Install`/`plan.go` beyond `BinPath`,
  `Behind`/`Pull`/`Inspect`, `apply.go` (carried over from round 2), `status`'s `shadowed` line,
  `report.go`. **Consequently unverified:** that `Reinstall` always writes
  `home/.local/bin/sh-agent` in the non-fixture case — if it does not, the note is silent, so
  that direction is fail-safe.
- Finding 1's END-TO-END path was NOT exercised: no release was published, downloaded or
  verified, and no tag was created anywhere (the hard limits forbid network, and a real probe
  would have to touch the release repository). Its arithmetic was validated in both states by
  the scratch probe named in the finding; the replay step and `gh release download`'s behaviour
  rest on reading. No probe directory was created under `.agents/scratch/security-bug079-3/`; no exploit
  was built. Findings 2 and 4 were likewise established by reading, not by running.

## Outcome

Written by the main agent at the close of BUG-079 (three review rounds, the cap). No high; the BUG-079 medium is closed on both paths (finding 1). The rest is outside this fix and goes to the audit phase of `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-18-sh-agent-works-everywhere.md` (Phase 2), each as its own box there:

- [medium, pre-existing] `v1.02.2` passes `IsReleaseVersion` and compares equal to `v1.2.2`, skipping the not-newer refusal — **left, owner Phase 2 audit**, with one correction to the finding's blast radius: the rollback channel as described stops at `verifyRelease`'s marker check (internal/harness/release.go:283), which requires the SIGNED `SHA256SUMS` first line to equal the tag string exactly — an older release's signed file names its own version, and nobody without the key can sign `# styrman-harness v1.02.2`. What remains is that a non-canonical tag reaches the download at all, and that `compareRelease` treats it as equal; Phase 2 rejects a non-canonical spelling and uses `<= 0`, with a must-fail test for `v1.02.2` and `v01.2.2`.
- [low] `ln -sfn` offered first regardless of who owns the path — **left, owner Phase 2 audit**: `RunningElsewhere` holds `from`'s `FileInfo`; the note can say "remove it" alone when the file or its directory is not the caller's.
- [low] the note is `--home`-blind: with `--home .agents/scratch/x` it calls a scratch binary "the installed binary" — **left, owner Phase 2 audit**: print the note only for the default home, or name the home in it.
- [low] the checkout path rebuilds and notes when `behind == 0` — **left** (main agent): the note's statements stay true (the process is not the file just written; that file is a fresh build); no wrong advice follows from it.
- (4) exporting `NoteRunningElsewhere` widens nothing outside the module — confirmed. (5) ordering after a noisy install — deterministic, no finding.

title: Security review — BUG-079 stale-running-binary note (2026-09-18)
body:
# Security review — BUG-079 stale-running-binary note   (2026-09-18)

Range reviewed: c868ed4..bc745dc

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The note `update` now prints is an instruction an operator executes, and it fires in states where its premise is false. `UpdateFromRelease` has three `return nil` branches that install NOTHING (`up to date (V)`, "this binary reports version … leaving it alone", "the newest release … is older … nothing installed`), and `main.go` gates the note only on `!*check` and a nil error — so a run that changed nothing still prints "this update ran from `<X>`, which update never replaces; the installed binary is `<home>/.local/bin/sh-agent` … — or remove it". `RunningElsewhere` swallows the `os.Stat(binPath)` error, so the named "installed binary" need not exist: on a place installed by hand into `/usr/local/bin` (the README "Install without cloning" route — the exact devbox shape in BUG-079), the note names a file that is not there as the replacement and tells the reader to remove the machine's only, current `sh-agent`. This is the asserted behaviour, not a hypothesis: `TestUpdateNamesTheBinaryItRanFrom` drives the `tag == version` path with a `t.TempDir()` home holding no `.local/bin/sh-agent`, and passes. Nothing in the range touches crypto, auth, secrets or dependencies; the release signature/checksum gate is untouched and still runs before this note.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:654-663` with `internal/harness/release.go:105-119` and `internal/harness/pathguard.go:82` — the note fires after an update that installed nothing, and can name a non-existent file as "the installed binary" while ending in "or remove it". Three branches of `UpdateFromRelease` return nil without writing `home/.local/bin/sh-agent`; the caller's only guards are `!*check` and `err == nil`. `RunningElsewhere` ignores the `os.Stat(binPath)` error rather than treating a missing installed file as "nothing was replaced, say nothing" — the harness's own test case `installed file missing: a reachable other copy still reported` (pathguard_test.go:450) fixes that as intended. Exploitable in principle as self-inflicted destruction on the program's own advice: the operator is told the binary they are running is superseded when it is the newest and possibly the only one, and the remedy is `rm`. No attacker is needed; a plain `sh-agent update` on an up-to-date binary-only place is the trigger. Remediation: have `UpdateFromRelease` report whether it actually wrote `dest`, and print the note only then; additionally require `os.Stat(installed)` to succeed inside `RunningElsewhere` (an installed file that does not exist cannot be behind anything) and state the version of each side, so the premise is shown rather than asserted.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:661` — "or remove it" is unqualified and names the PATH-entry spelling, not the running file. The path reported may be root-owned (`/usr/local/bin/sh-agent`, the BUG-079 path: the `rm` needs `sudo`), manager-owned and read-only (`/nix/store/…`, a Homebrew link, `/opt/devbox/bin`), or a symlink under another name to the stale binary — the function's own test `reached only through a link: reported at the PATH entry, not the exe path` (pathguard_test.go:449) makes that the documented output, in which case removing what is named deletes the link and leaves the stale binary in place while the reader believes it is gone. README.md and `deploy/remote.md` qualify the parallel advice ("point the earlier one at this binary (`ln -sfn`) or remove it — a link to the same file is not a shadow"); the program's own note does not. Remediation: name the exe path and the PATH spelling when they differ, put the non-destructive fix first (`ln -sfn <installed> <from>`), and offer removal only for a path under the user's home.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/pathguard.go:86-91` — `RunningElsewhere` drops the empty-PATH-entry convention its sibling handles on purpose. `PathShadows` maps a `""` entry to `./sh-agent` (pathguard.go:35-39) precisely because "Join would print it as a bare name that reads like a command, not a file". Here `filepath.Join("", "sh-agent")` is `"sh-agent"`, statted against the cwd and printed bare, so with a PATH carrying an empty element (`PATH=$PATH:` out of a sloppy profile) and a link to the running binary in the cwd the note reads "this update ran from sh-agent … or remove it" — a token that reads as a command name, and a reader acting on it runs `rm sh-agent` in whatever directory they are in by then. A local user who can write the operator's cwd can plant that link. Remediation: reuse the `"." + separator + name` mapping, or skip empty entries; either way the two functions should agree.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:661` (same shape pre-existing in `pathHint`, main.go:672+, and in `status`'s `shadowed` line) — environment-derived paths are printed raw with `%s` into an advisory that contains shell commands. `from` comes from `PATH` and `installed` from `--home`/`$HOME`; `filepath.SplitList` splits on `:` only, so a PATH element may contain `\n`, `\r` or ESC. A directory whose name carries a newline, holding a link to the running binary, forges an extra line of `sh-agent`'s own output; with ESC it rewrites the line in a terminal or in a pasted verification log. The note is the thing an operator acts on and it is copied into `.agents/docs/testing/` logs, so a forged line outlives the run. Remediation: print env-derived paths with `%q` — Go quoting escapes control bytes and makes a trailing space visible. Stdlib only; no dependency, nothing to justify.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/pathguard.go:78-88` — `os.Stat(exe)` re-resolves a path string rather than the running inode, and `os.Executable()` returns a path, not a handle. On Linux Go returns `readlink("/proc/self/exe")` with a literal `" (deleted)"` suffix trimmed, so a binary replaced or deleted during the run yields a path whose current occupant is a *different* file — that occupant is what gets statted and compared — and a genuine path ending in `" (deleted)"` is mangled. On darwin `os.Executable` resolves `_NSGetExecutablePath` against the process's initial cwd, so a relative-path exec followed by a move yields a stale path; macOS is a first-class place for this harness. The consequence is confined to the advisory's accuracy — the program mutates nothing on the basis of these stats. Answering the two cases the dispatch asked about, neither is a finding: `exec -a` rewrites argv[0] only and cannot move `/proc/self/exe`, and a process started through a symlink gets the resolved target while the PATH walk reports the spelling a shell uses (covered by pathguard_test.go:449). Remediation: none required for the Linux path beyond finding 1; treat the returned path as advisory and say "the binary at …" rather than "this update ran from …" if precision is wanted.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-18-recon-bug-079-diagnosis.md:21` — the committed doc contains `warning`: two U+0646 ARABIC LETTER NOON inside an ASCII word. Arabic letters are strong RTL, so a bidi-aware renderer reorders the run around them. Nothing here is source and the surrounding meaning is unaffected, but `.agents/docs/` is read back as agent input, and unexpected strong-directional non-ASCII in text an agent consumes is the trojan-source class. Remediation: correct the word; a non-ASCII grep over `.agents/docs/` outside the intended typography set (em dash, curly quotes) catches the next one. `git diff --numstat` shows no `-`/`-` pair, so nothing in the range is binary.

**TOCTOU between the stats and the message — moot as an exploit, not as correctness.** Between the two `os.Stat` calls and the `Fprintf` the program acts on nothing: no unlink, no exec, no write, no trust decision. There is no window in which a racing local user gains anything from the code itself. The race only widens the interval in which the printed text is wrong, and a human executes the remedy — which is findings 1, 2 and 5, not a separate one.

## Checked

- **Secrets** — none: no credential, token or key in the eight changed files; no `.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.tfvars` or credential JSON added; no high-entropy string in the diff. The new output prints only paths; a `$HOME`-derived path discloses the username in a pasted log, which every other `sh-agent` line already does. `gh auth login` appears in prose only.
- **Injection** — nothing in the range execs, queries or templates. The only injection-shaped surface is terminal/log injection of `PATH`- and `$HOME`-derived text into the advisory (finding 4); `filepath.Join` on a PATH entry cannot escape anywhere that matters because the result is only statted and printed, never written or removed by the program. The new test's fake `gh` is confined to a `t.Setenv("PATH", …)` and a `t.TempDir()`.
- **Authz/authn** — no auth path in range. The one authorization-adjacent effect is the remedy inviting a privileged `sudo rm` of a system path (finding 2).
- **Crypto** — nothing hand-rolled and nothing crypto-adjacent added; the new code has no crypto call. `release.go`'s `ssh-keygen` signature and checksum gate is outside this range and untouched, and the note prints after it, changing no trust decision. No finding.
- **Dependencies** — `go.mod`/`go.sum` untouched; the added code imports `os` and `path/filepath` only, holding the repo's stdlib-only rule. `gofmt -l cmd internal` clean, `go vet ./...` clean, and `go test -run 'TestRunningElsewhere|TestUpdateNamesTheBinaryItRanFrom|TestCheckoutUpdateNamesTheBinaryItRanFrom'` passes on both packages (that pass is what pins finding 1). `govulncheck` IS installed at `/home/kesokaj/.go/bin/govulncheck` but was **not run**: it fetches the database from vuln.go.dev and this dispatch forbids network. `npm audit` not applicable — no JavaScript in this repository.
- **GCP surface** — nothing in range: no IAM binding, service account, key file, Cloud Run flag, `--allow-unauthenticated`, or secret-as-env-var.

## Not examined

- `govulncheck ./...` — not run (network forbidden by the dispatch). `AGENTS.md` claims it is clean on go1.25.8+ and has reported none since 2026-09-17; I did not re-verify that.
- `go test -race ./...` in full — not run: tests outside this range can reach the network and the real home, both forbidden here. Only the three named tests were executed.
- Read end to end: `internal/harness/pathguard.go`, `internal/harness/pathguard_test.go`, and all four markdown files' changed hunks via the complete diff. **Not** read end to end: the unchanged bodies of `README.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md` and `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` (changed hunks plus context only); `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (lines 180-240, 480-530 and 600-700 plus the diff — roughly 900 further lines unread); `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` (the 106 added lines and their context only — the preceding ~1486 lines unread).
- Blast radius not read: `internal/harness/release.go` beyond lines 90-150 (the download/verify/`writeAtomic` tail is unread), `internal/harness/plan.go`, `install.go`/`Reinstall`, `status`'s `shadowed` line, `report.go`. **Consequently unverified:** whether `Reinstall` can succeed on the CHECKOUT path without writing `home/.local/bin/sh-agent` (a skipped or non-fatal binary step). If it can, finding 1 applies to that path too, not only to the release path.
- No runtime probe of the real release `update` path (it needs `gh` and network); no probe directory was created under `.agents/scratch/`, and no exploit was built.

## Outcome

Written by the main agent after the round-2 change, in its commit.

- [medium] the note fires after an update that installed nothing, into a home with no installed binary, and names a file that does not exist while telling the reader to remove their only binary — **fixed**: `RunningElsewhere` returns nothing unless the installed file exists (internal/harness/pathguard.go:86); pinned by a fresh-home release-path case (cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go:1524) and the unit case (internal/harness/pathguard_test.go:450), and by a must-fail mutation that swallows the `Stat` error again. On an "up to date" run into a home that DOES hold an installed file the note still prints — the running file is still not that one, a shell hash pointing at it is still the hazard for the next update — and the wording now says only what is true in both cases (cmd/sh-agent/main.go:661).
- [low] "or remove it" unqualified, naming a path that may be root-owned, manager-owned or a link — **fixed**: the message says the file "stays as it is" and offers `ln -sfn` to the installed binary before removal (cmd/sh-agent/main.go:661); README and both deploy guides already carried the qualified form.
- [low] empty PATH entry printed as a bare `sh-agent` — **fixed**: `./sh-agent`, as `PathShadows` prints it (internal/harness/pathguard.go:93).
- [low] raw `%s` printing of PATH-derived paths — **rebutted**, as for BUG-078: the strings are the operator's own `PATH` entries and home, printed as `which -a` and `type` print them; nothing untrusted reaches them. No change.
- [low] `os.Executable()` path-vs-inode edge cases — **rebutted**: the function uses `exe` only to `Stat` it and reports the PATH entry it matches by identity, never `exe`'s spelling, so a ` (deleted)` suffix or a relative darwin form changes nothing the reader sees. No change.
- [low] two U+0646 characters in the explorer's diagnosis brief — **fixed**: removed by character code (the first attempt matched the escape text, not the character — BUG-057's class, caught by `grep` for the character itself).
- TOCTOU — moot as the finding says; advisory output only.
- Unverified in the report (checkout path succeeding without writing the installed file): it can, in the test fixture whose fake install writes a marker — and with the gate the note is then silent there, which is the intended reading; the checkout test plants an installed file to exercise the note.

title: Security review — Phase 2 round 3, the `TightenConfigDir` split (e7fec88..42840fb)
body:
# Security review — Phase 2 round 3, the `TightenConfigDir` split (e7fec88..42840fb)

Range reviewed: e7fec88..42840fb (`git diff e7fec88..42840fb -- . ':!.agents/docs'`; HEAD `42840fb`, tree frozen)

## Verdict: FINDINGS — four low, **no high, nothing reopens the work**

Round 2's **medium is closed, and closed structurally rather than by
measurement**: `TightenConfigDir` (state.go:93) has **no error return at all**,
`Install` calls it as a bare statement before the first write (apply.go:30), and
the only chmod-failure branch writes a `note:` line and falls through
(state.go:106-108). No value flows from that chmod into `Install`'s result — a
failed tighten cannot abort a deployment, whatever the filesystem does. The
operator's option 1 is implemented as specified and measured on all six paths
(fresh, loose, dry run, second run, symlink, `diff`/`status`).

The worst thing left is a **documentation guarantee the code does not keep**:
README line 74 says the runtime directory "is created 0700 and **tightened to it
by every install**", and line 162 repeats "tightened to 0700 **on every
install**". Measured false — a symlinked `~/.config/sh-agent` is left at 0755
with **zero output** and `install` still exits 0 (probe E) — and false by code
for a directory the caller does not own (state.go:99). The two silent skips plus
the absolute claim combine into a false assurance about the privacy of the
feedback log and the retro proposals: the operator whose arrangement is skipped
is told, in writing, that it was fixed. That is a doc sentence and a `note:`
line to close, not a defect in the mechanism.

## The brief's questions, as checkable statements

1. **Is the medium (a failed tighten aborting after every write) closed?
   YES — by construction, which is stronger than a probe.**
   `func TightenConfigDir(home string, dryRun bool, out io.Writer)` returns
   nothing (state.go:93); `apply.go:30` discards nothing because there is
   nothing to discard; the chmod error is consumed by
   `fmt.Fprintf(out, "note: could not correct the mode of ~/.config/sh-agent (%v)\n", err)`
   (state.go:107) and control falls off the end of the function. There is no
   path from that `Chmod` to a non-nil `Install` error. Bounding measurements:
   probe **E** (the tighten skipped entirely, symlinked dir) → `rc=0`, manifest
   written into the target; probe **J** (a *different* failure, below) → the
   only surviving abort is `writeAtomic`, not the chmod.
   **I could not force `chmod` to fail as this user, and say so plainly:**
   `chattr +i` needs `CAP_LINUX_IMMUTABLE` and returned
   `chattr: Operation not permitted` (probe H); no read-only bind mount is
   available here; no root was used, per the dispatch. So the `note:` line
   itself was **never observed executing** — the closure rests on the
   signature and the control flow, which I read end to end, not on seeing it
   print. That branch is also untested (finding 4).
2. **Does `left` reason 3 hold (`~/.config` created 0700 when absent)? YES.**
   Measured (probe A, fresh home): `.config` **700**, `.config/sh-agent`
   **700**, and **no `mode` line** — the directory was created private, not
   tightened, which is exactly what the split promises. The reason given
   ("when `~/.config` does not exist yet the whole path is sh-agent's to
   create") holds and is now *stronger* than at e7fec88: because `ConfigDir`
   no longer tightens, an **existing** `~/.config` (0775 on this box) is left
   alone, so the surprise is confined to a home where sh-agent made the
   directory itself. Same uid throughout; no exposure, no lockout. The doc
   comment (state.go:71) says "created 0700 when absent", which matches.
3. **Does `left` reason 4 hold (the contents' modes)? YES, unchanged.**
   Measured read-only on the operator's real home, today: `~/.config` **775**,
   `~/.config/sh-agent` **755**, `feedback/` **drwxrwxr-x**, `proposals/`
   **drwxrwxr-x**, `feedback.jsonl` **-rw-rw-r--**, `retros.jsonl`
   **-rw-rw-r--**, `state.json` 0644. Their next `install` (or `update`, which
   reinstalls) tightens the parent to 0700, and a 0700 parent denies `x` to
   group and other, so the local-account read the finding named is closed —
   traversal is the gate, not the leaf modes. The acknowledged residual is
   unchanged: the loose modes travel with a backup, an archive or a dotfiles
   sync. One nuance the reason should carry: the tighten is **install-only**,
   so a machine that only ever runs `report`, `diff` or `status` keeps a 0755
   runtime directory indefinitely — measured (probes F, G: mode stayed 755
   across both). Every machine kept current with `update` reinstalls, so this
   bites only a machine nobody updates.
4. **Does `left` reason 5 hold (ownership vs writability)? YES — and it is
   untouched by this range.** `pathguard.go:141` is byte-identical at
   e7fec88 and 42840fb. `ownedByCaller` still gates **wording only**, never an
   operation, and errs toward the stronger remedy. Nothing here changed it.
   Note the same predicate is now load-bearing in a *second* place
   (state.go:99), where it gates an actual operation rather than a sentence —
   correctly, since `chmod(2)` requires ownership, and `Geteuid` is the right
   uid for "will the kernel let me".
5. **Should the not-owned skip print a note? YES — print one.** (Advice only;
   this is finding 2, low.) `install`'s whole output contract is that it names
   what it changes, and it already has the precedent for naming what it
   *declines* to touch: the `keep ~/…` line for a managed path holding a
   foreign file (apply.go:40). A loose, foreign-owned runtime directory is the
   same situation — sh-agent sees a privacy problem in its own directory,
   decides it is not its to fix, and says nothing, while the README says it
   was fixed. The branch only fires when the directory is **both** loose and
   not the caller's, so the note is rare and every printing of it is
   actionable. Same argument, slightly weaker, for the symlink skip. Suggested
   text: `note: ~/.config/sh-agent is 0755 and is not yours to change; leaving
   its mode alone (it holds the feedback log and the retro proposals)`.
6. **Can the dry run's `mode` line mislead? NO.** Measured (probe B): the dry
   run printed `mode    ~/.config/sh-agent (0755 -> 0700)`, left the directory
   at **755**, and closed with `[dry-run] 0 written, 260 unchanged, 0 removed,
   0 kept`. That is exactly the per-file `mode` contract (apply.go:52-59, plan
   D7/D8): the probe runs on a dry run so it names the same line the real run
   prints, the line itself carries no `[dry-run]` prefix — no per-file line
   does — and the prefixed summary is the marker. The predicate is identical
   on both paths (`Lstat`, symlink, `IsDir`, loose, owned all checked *before*
   the print), so a dry run cannot name a change the real run would skip. The
   one residual asymmetry is that the real run may additionally print a
   `note:` when the chmod fails, i.e. the dry run can promise a tighten that
   does not happen — the identical asymmetry the per-file lines already have,
   and it is announced at the time. No finding.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `README.md:74` and `README.md:162` — **the
  README states an unconditional guarantee the code does not keep.** Line 74:
  "`~/.config/sh-agent/` is created 0700 and **tightened to it by every
  install**"; line 162: "`mode` (… and also the runtime directory
  `~/.config/sh-agent`, **tightened to 0700 on every install**)". Both are
  false for two arrangements the code deliberately skips: a **symlinked**
  runtime directory (state.go:96) and one the caller **does not own**
  (state.go:99). Measured for the first (probe E): `~/.config/sh-agent` →
  a 0755 target, `install` exits **0**, target stays **0755**, and the output
  contains **no line at all** about it. Why this matters in principle: a
  dotfiles-symlinked `~/.config/sh-agent` is a normal arrangement, the
  directory holds the feedback log, the retro proposals and — briefly — a
  clone of the *private* feedback repository, and the operator who reads this
  README has been told in writing that every install makes it private. A
  guarantee that is read as a control and is not one is worse than no
  sentence. This is also the behaviour-change-includes-its-description rule:
  the code moved in this commit, the two sentences did not. Remediation: one
  clause on each line — "…tightened to it by every install, except a
  symlinked directory or one owned by another user, which it leaves alone" —
  plus finding 2's note so the exception is visible at the moment it applies.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/state.go:96,99` — **both skips
  are silent, so the one case where the privacy problem persists is the one
  case the operator is never told about.** `Lstat` failure, a symlink, a
  non-directory and a foreign-owned directory all `return` with nothing
  written to `out`. The loose-and-foreign case is precisely a runtime
  directory that is world-readable, holds the feedback log and proposals, and
  that sh-agent has decided not to fix. `install` already prints a line when
  it declines to touch a managed path (`keep ~/…`, apply.go:40), so the
  pattern and the output budget both exist. Remediation as in question 5: one
  `note:` before each `return`, gated on the directory actually being loose so
  it cannot become noise. Stdlib only; no dependency, no new syscall.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/state.go:95-108` — **`Lstat`
  then path-based `Chmod` is a TOCTOU window; `os.Chmod` follows symlinks and
  the `Lstat` guard does not survive the gap.** An account that can create
  entries in the target `~/.config` can replace `sh-agent` with a symlink
  between the two calls and the `Chmod` follows it. The impact is bounded in
  the safe direction and I state that explicitly: `chmod(2)` succeeds only on
  a target the caller owns (or with `CAP_FOWNER`), and 0700 only *clears*
  bits, so the worst a non-root install yields is one of the caller's own
  directories tightened to 0700 — availability, never a widening, never
  another user's files. Under a **root**-run install the same race can tighten
  any directory on the box. The precondition (write access to the victim's
  `~/.config`) already implies a deeper compromise — that same access plants a
  skill or a `settings.json` — which is why this is low and not higher. On this
  box `~/.config` is `775 kesokaj` and the group has no second member, so it
  is not reachable here. Remediation if it is ever worth closing:
  `os.OpenFile(dir, os.O_RDONLY|syscall.O_DIRECTORY|syscall.O_NOFOLLOW, 0)`
  then `f.Chmod(0o700)` — `fchmod` on the descriptor that was inspected, pure
  stdlib `os`/`syscall`, no dependency — at the cost of a build-tag split like
  the existing `owned_unix.go`/`owned_other.go` pair. **My recommendation is
  to leave it and keep this line as the record**: a build-tag split for a race
  whose precondition is already game-over buys defence, not safety, and the
  shorter code is worth more. Second-order note, same site: `os.Chmod(dir,
  0o700)` is absolute, so it also clears **setgid/sticky** on the runtime
  directory, while the printed line shows `Perm()` (`%04o` of 0755) and never
  names those bits — a setgid-inherited runtime dir is silently de-setgid'd.
  Tightening again, impact ~nil, mentioned so it is on the record.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/state.go:99` and
  `state.go:107` — **the two security-relevant branches this commit adds have
  no test, and the suite cannot reach either.** `ownedByCaller` is unit-tested
  only through a fake `Stat_t` (`owned_unix_test.go:21-27`); grep shows no
  test anywhere referencing the `!ownedByCaller` skip inside
  `TightenConfigDir`, and none referencing the `note: could not correct the
  mode` string. Reaching them needs a second uid or a way to make `chmod`
  fail, neither of which exists in a `go test` on one account — so this is a
  gap in the *evidence*, not a defect in the code, and I name it because the
  rest of the mechanism is well covered and a reader could take that as
  coverage of the whole. What **is** pinned, and pinned bidirectionally:
  `audit_test.go:239-242` asserts the `mode` line is present for a 0755
  directory and **absent** for a fresh one (`has != (pre == "0755")`);
  `:246-266` asserts the dry run prints the line and does **not** change the
  mode; `:268-294` asserts the symlink target keeps 0755 and that **no** line
  claims otherwise; `:131-140` and `:175-177` assert `report` and `diff` leave
  the mode alone. Those are genuine must-fail checks of the behaviour they
  name. Remediation: none available in-process; the honest move is a line in
  the testing guide saying the not-owned and chmod-failure branches are
  covered by reading, not by running.

### Carried, pre-existing, and **not** a regression of this range

- `internal/harness/apply.go:30` / `state.go:68` — **an unwritable runtime
  directory still leaves a fully deployed home with no manifest.** Measured
  (probe J: `~/.config/sh-agent` present, `0500`, owned by me):
  **260 files written**, `state.json` **ABSENT**, exit 1,
  `sh-agent: saving manifest: open …/.sh-agent-1876906526: permission denied`.
  `TightenConfigDir` correctly skips it (0500 is already private), so this is
  `writeAtomic`, not the chmod, and the same probe produces the same end state
  against e7fec88's code — **this range does not make it worse, and for the
  not-owned-but-writable directory it makes it strictly better** (that case
  aborted at e7fec88 and now succeeds). Round 2's medium named the *chmod*
  mechanism and that mechanism is gone. The class survives: the manifest is
  "the only thing uninstall trusts" (state.go:13-15) and `Uninstall` removes
  nothing without it (apply.go:271-274). It is now cheap to close, since
  `Install` has a hook at the top where it did not before: a writability probe
  beside `TightenConfigDir(home, dryRun, out)` that fails **before** the first
  write. Out of range; recorded so it is not lost.
- `internal/harness/apply.go:226` — `sh-agent diff`, a read-only verb, still
  *creates* `~/.config/sh-agent` (and `~/.config` when absent) to render a
  temp file. It no longer changes an existing directory's mode — measured
  (probe F: 755 before, **755** after, no leftovers) and pinned
  (`audit_test.go:175-177`), which is round 2's finding 6 fixed. The residual
  creation is unchanged from round 1, does not touch `--check`/`--dry-run`,
  and the smaller remedy is still `cmd.Stdin = bytes.NewReader(f.Data)` with
  `-` as the second operand, deleting the temp file and the `ConfigDir` call
  outright.

## Checked

- **Secrets:** clean. No credential, token or key added in the four changed
  files. The only new output strings are the fixed literal
  `mode    ~/.config/sh-agent (%04o -> 0700)` and the `note:` with `%v` of an
  `*os.PathError` — a path and an errno, never file content. No new file is
  created in the runtime directory; `state.json` is still 0644 via
  `writeAtomic`, and `diffOne`'s temp file is `os.CreateTemp`'s 0600. New test
  bodies grepped for PEM headers and `ghp_`/`sk-ant-`/`AKIA`/`AIza`/`xoxb-`
  shapes — nothing. My probe logs under `.agents/scratch/` hold paths and
  modes only.
- **Injection:** no new `exec.Command`, no new argv element, no new parsing
  boundary in range. `TightenConfigDir`'s only input is `home`, already made
  absolute at `main.go` before any verb runs (BUG-080), and the path is a
  program-chosen `filepath.Join(home, ".config", "sh-agent")` — no external
  string reaches a shell, a format verb's *verb* position, or a filename.
  `LoadState`'s `filepath.IsLocal` choke point over `Files` is untouched.
- **Authz/authn:** not a service. The one authorization-relevant operation is
  the `Chmod`, and the check behind it is the kernel's; `ownedByCaller` is a
  *pre*-check that avoids a guaranteed EPERM, not a home-grown gate — the
  kernel still decides. Correctly keyed on `Geteuid` (the uid `chmod(2)` is
  judged by) and `sh-agent` is not setuid, so real and effective coincide.
  Read-only modes verified again by reading control flow **and** by
  measurement: `--dry-run` returns before the `Chmod` (state.go:103-105, probe
  B), `status` never calls either function (probe G: 755 in, 755 out),
  `update --check` returns at `release.go:123-126` before `ConfigDir` at
  `:135`.
- **Crypto:** nothing added and nothing hand-rolled in this range — no cipher,
  hash, MAC, signature, KDF, RNG, token or session format is implemented or
  composed here. The release chain (`ssh-keygen -Y verify` over a signed
  `SHA256SUMS` with the signer compiled in, then the checksum over the asset
  bytes) is untouched. Re-checked in the blast radius because this commit
  changed what `ConfigDir` does for `release.go:135`: the download directory is
  a random `MkdirTemp` under a possibly-loose parent, but `downloadRelease`
  reads the asset into memory (`readCapped`), `verifyRelease` checks **those
  bytes**, and `writeAtomic(dest, data, 0o755)` writes **those same bytes** —
  so no file is re-read between verification and installation and there is no
  swap window, whatever the staging directory's mode. The `SHA256SUMS` swap is
  covered by the signature. **Not a finding.**
- **Dependencies:** `go.mod` unchanged, still **zero** third-party requires; no
  import added anywhere except stdlib `io` in `state.go` (for the
  `io.Writer` parameter) and `strings`, already present, in the test. Any
  remediation above is stdlib-only, named as such, and rejects nothing.
  `gofmt -l cmd internal` → empty; `go vet ./...` → rc 0; `go test -race
  -count=1 -run 'ConfigDir|Throwaway|DiffUsesTheHome|OwnedByCaller|NoteRunningElsewhere|HarnessMap'
  ./internal/harness/` → **ok, 1.155s**. `govulncheck ./...`: **not run** — it
  queries `vuln.go.dev` and this dispatch forbids network. Not faked. Residual
  is small: zero third-party modules and this box runs **go1.27.1**, above both
  stdlib advisories `AGENTS.md` records. `npm audit`: not applicable, no
  JavaScript in the repository.
- **GCP surface:** none in range — no IAM binding, service account,
  `--allow-unauthenticated`, Secret Manager call or service-account key file.
  The only remote endpoints remain GitHub via `gh` and `git`.
- **Files in the diff, read end to end:** `internal/harness/state.go`,
  `internal/harness/apply.go`, `internal/harness/audit_test.go`,
  `README.md` (the diff hunks in full plus every line naming the runtime
  directory or a mode — lines 29, 60, 74, 161-163, 168, 184, 194 — over a
  245-line file). Blast radius also read: every `ConfigDir` call site
  (`state.go:65`, `apply.go:226`, `report.go:455`, `release.go:135`),
  `owned_unix.go`, `owned_other.go`, `pathguard.go:141`, and
  `release.go:100-215` (the update-from-release path that consumes
  `ConfigDir`'s changed contract).
- **Measurements** (probes A-J, `.agents/scratch/security-phase2-3/`,
  gitignored, binary built from the frozen tree; umask 0002, so every 0700
  observed is the explicit code, not the umask): **A** fresh → `.config` 700,
  `.config/sh-agent` 700, no line. **B** 0755 + `--dry-run` → line printed,
  mode stays **755**, `[dry-run] 0 written, 260 unchanged`. **C** 0755 + real
  → line printed, mode **700**, `state.json` present 0644. **D** already 0700
  → **no** line. **E** symlinked dir → target stays **755**, **no** line,
  rc **0**, manifest in the target. **F** `diff` over a drifted file → 755
  before, **755** after, no leftover temp files. **G** `status` → **755**
  after. **H** `chattr +i` → `Operation not permitted` (no root used). **J**
  0500 runtime dir → 260 files, manifest **ABSENT**, rc 1. **I** the
  operator's real home, read-only `stat` only, nothing installed there.

## Not examined

- `govulncheck ./...` — **not run**; the dispatch forbids network. One run on
  a connected session closes it; the command is in `AGENTS.md` § Setup.
- **The `note: could not correct the mode` branch (state.go:107) and the
  `!ownedByCaller` skip (state.go:99) were never observed executing.** I could
  not make `chmod` fail as this user (probe H) and used no root, and I cannot
  produce a directory owned by another uid without one. Both are reasoned from
  the source, which I read end to end, not measured. Finding 4 records the
  matching test gap.
- **Non-unix runtime:** `owned_other.go` (`ownedByCaller` → always `true`, so
  `TightenConfigDir` always attempts the chmod on Windows) is unchanged in this
  range and was neither compiled nor run this round. On Windows the `Perm()`
  bits are a fiction and the tighten is close to a no-op; I make no claim about
  its behaviour there beyond what the round-2 report recorded.
- **Unchanged files not re-read this round:** the remainder of `report.go`
  (redaction list, `Collect`, the push path), the remainder of `release.go`
  (`verifyRelease`'s body, `checksumFor`, `downloadRelease`'s callers),
  `plan.go`, `derive.go`, `source.go`, `main.go`. None is touched by this
  range; all were audited on 2026-09-18 and in round 2.
- **Test files outside the diff** — `main_test.go`, `harness_test.go`,
  `report_test.go`, `pathguard_test.go`, `source_test.go`, `owned_unix_test.go`
  (grepped for `ownedByCaller` only, not read end to end). I make no coverage
  claim about them; the `--tests` lens owns the coverage map.
- No behavioural run of either consumer CLI, and no `sh-agent report` (both
  excluded by the dispatch); no install into the real `$HOME` — the only touch
  of it was a read-only `stat`/`ls`.
- **Housekeeping:** probes left on disk under
  `.agents/scratch/security-phase2-3/` (`sh-agent`, `home1/`, `home2/`,
  `target2/`, `home3/`, `ro/`, `*.log`), all gitignored, none removed by me.
  `git status --short --untracked-files=all` shows no source, test or config
  file changed by this review — only untracked files under `.agents/docs/`,
  of which exactly one is mine (this report). `git log @{u}..HEAD` is empty,
  `git tag` ends at v1.2.2 (unchanged), HEAD is `42840fb`. No git command that
  changes the working tree was run.

## Outcome

Written by the main agent at the close of Phase 2. No high; the round-2 medium closed structurally, as the report measures.

1. [low] README's false assurance — **fixed** (README.md:74), as the reviewer's identical finding.
2. [low] the two skips are silent — **fixed**: the symlink skip prints `note: ~/.config/sh-agent is a symlink; its target's mode is yours to set (0700 keeps the feedback log private)` (internal/harness/state.go:102), pinned at internal/harness/audit_test.go:295; the not-owned skip prints `note: ~/.config/sh-agent is not yours to tighten (mode NNNN); ask its owner for 0700 — the feedback log lives there` (internal/harness/state.go:109), which no non-root test can reach and is recorded as unpinned.
3. [low] `Lstat` then path-based `Chmod` — **left**, as the finding recommends: the window is bounded (chmod succeeds only on a directory the caller owns, and only clears bits).
4. the two unreachable branches — recorded, not covered; the chmod-failure branch is a note by construction (no error value reaches `Install`).
- The caveat that the tighten is install-only (a machine that runs only `report`/`diff`/`status` stays loose) — recorded: every `update` runs an install, and a place that never updates is a place that never receives anything.
These lines were written after the third round, the cap; they are not re-reviewed in a fourth round — Phase 4's `/preflight` reviews the whole range with reviewer and security, which is where they get their independent read.

title: Security review — harness (2026-09-18)
body:
# Security review — harness   (2026-09-18)

Range reviewed: the named files as they are in the working tree, read whole — not a diff: internal/harness cmd/sh-agent

## Verdict: FINDINGS

No break in the release verification chain, which is the sharpest surface here and
reads as sound end to end: a signature over `SHA256SUMS` in a pinned namespace against
a compiled-in signer, the release version carried *inside* the signed bytes, then the
asset's own hash over the exact bytes that get written, with no re-read between hash
and write. What is wrong is smaller and all of one kind — hardening that was reasoned
out carefully in one file and not carried to its twin in another. The worst of it is
`Adopt`'s copy, which deploys a third-party skill's permission bits into the harness
repo without the group/other-write mask that `Plan` applies on the way out and
explains at length; a skill adopted from `~/.agents/skills` at 0664 lands
group-writable inside `skills/`, which is the tree `Reinstall` compiles and `install`
ships to every machine. Second is a circular guard: `knownCheckout` defends the source
directory against the cwd walk by comparing it to `state.json`'s `repo` field — the
same field that selected it — so the one input it cannot validate is the one it reads,
while its sibling field `files` in that same file is sanitised.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/adopt.go:168` (`copyTree`) — `writeAtomic(target, data, info.Mode().Perm()|0o600)` keeps the source file's group and other **write** bits. `internal/harness/plan.go:138` does `info.Mode().Perm()&0o755 | 0o600` for the same bytes on the way out, and says why: "A repo file that is 0664 or 0666 — a loose umask, a copied archive — would otherwise land group-writable in `~/.claude`, where its contents are instructions every session reads: another local account could rewrite the harness without touching the repo." `adopt` is the entrance for exactly such a file: its whole purpose is to copy a skill directory the operator did not write (`npx skills add -g` into `~/.agents/skills`, an unpacked archive) into the repo's `skills/`, and it already carries the symlink refusal and the secret-shaped refusal from that same review series — the mode mask is the one that was not carried over. A skill whose files are 0664/0666 therefore sits group- or world-writable inside the harness checkout, which is the tree `Reinstall` runs `go build` in and the tree every later `install` reads; git records only the execute bit, so review and `git status` never show it, and the deployed copies look correct because `Plan` masks them. Another local account edits the file in `skills/`, and the next `sh-agent install` on that machine ships the edit to both vendor directories. Remediation: use plan.go's expression verbatim — `info.Mode().Perm()&0o755 | 0o600` — in `copyTree`, and add a test adopting a fixture file created 0666 that asserts the copy in `skills/` is 0644/0755. No dependency involved; this is one expression.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/repo.go:74-82` with `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:546-570` (`knownCheckout`) — `LoadState` deliberately filters `s.Files` through `filepath.IsLocal` before any caller may `Lstat` or `os.Remove` through it ("a non-local entry … is dropped HERE, once, never followed by any caller", `state.go`), and deliberately leaves `s.Repo` alone. `s.Repo` is the more dangerous field: `ResolveSource` falls back to it, `IsRepo` accepts any directory holding `context/AGENTS.md` and a `skills/` dir, and on a development build `install`/`update` then hands that directory to `Reinstall`, which runs `go build ./cmd/sh-agent` **in it** and executes the result. `knownCheckout` is the guard, and against the cwd-walk leg it works — but against a tampered manifest it cannot: it loads `st.Repo` and checks `samePath(st.Repo, repo)` where `repo` is the directory `st.Repo` itself just selected, so the comparison is the field against itself and always passes. `SaveState` writes the file 0644 under the operator's own home, so the precondition is prior write access as that user — this is a persistence and escalation step, not a first-order break, which is why it is rated low; it is worth closing because the cost is one `IsCheckout` call and because `--home` weakens the precondition further (a home another account can write is a home that chooses the operator's compiler input). Remediation: (1) require the recorded repo to still be a git checkout (`IsCheckout`) before it may be *built*, or restrict the `st.Repo` fallback to the read-only verbs (`status`, `list`, `diff`, `render`) and require `--repo`/`$SH_AGENT_REPO` for a build; (2) print the resolved source and **where it came from** (`--repo` / `$SH_AGENT_REPO` / cwd walk / recorded manifest) before `Reinstall` builds, since today `building sh-agent from <repo>` prints after the decision and names no provenance; (3) stop the cwd walk at the first `IsCheckout` boundary rather than continuing to `/`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/release.go:106,116` — `IsReleaseVersion` accepts non-canonical spellings and the sideways guard is `< 0`, so a release tagged with a different spelling of the version already installed reaches `gh release download`. Measured, not read: with the running binary at `v1.2.2`, `v1.02.2`, `v01.2.2` and `v1.2.02` all pass `IsReleaseVersion`, all fail the `tag == version` string compare at `release.go:106`, and all give `compareRelease(tag, version) == 0`, so the `< 0` branch does not fire and the download proceeds (probe: `.agents/scratch/security-audit/verprobe.go`, gitignored, pure logic, no network). It does **not** reach a downgrade or a substitution: `verifyRelease` requires the signed `SHA256SUMS` marker to equal `tag` exactly (`release.go:278-284`), and a signed file naming `v1.02.2` needs the operator's key — that marker is the control that holds this line and should be named as such in the fix's rationale. This confirms the plan's Phase 2 box; the scheduled fix (`<= 0` plus canonical-spelling rejection) is right. Extend it by one item: `releaseParts` returns `[3]int{}` on any `strconv.Atoi` failure, so `v99999999999999999999.0.0` — which also passes `IsReleaseVersion` — is silently read as `v0.0.0`; the probe shows today's caller refuses it, but only because the zero value happens to fall on the safe side of this particular comparison. Make the parse failure an error rather than a zero value.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/pathguard.go:112-121` (`NoteRunningElsewhere`) — confirms both Phase 2 boxes, and the first is worse than the box states. The note measures against `filepath.Join(home, BinPath)`, so a run with `--home .agents/scratch/x` compares the operator's **real** `sh-agent` against a *scratch* install and tells them their `/usr/local/bin/sh-agent` "stays as it is" and needs `hash -r` — a false alarm about a real binary, produced entirely by a test-only home, and the harness's own testing procedure runs every verb that way. Second, `ln -sfn` is offered unconditionally with ownership demoted to trailing advice ("when that path is root-owned, prefer removing it"), where the plan wants ownership decided before the suggestion is made. Remediation as the plan has it: suppress the note (or name the home in the line) when `home` is not the default, and stat `from` and its directory for caller ownership before suggesting `ln -sfn`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/report.go:400-402,453-458` — `throwawayDir` is the predictable `report-<pid>` and `cloneThrowaway` creates its parent with `0o755`, while `release.go:135-147` treats precisely this risk as worth `MkdirAll(base, 0o700)` plus `os.MkdirTemp`, with the reasoning written down: "a predictable name is one another local account can pre-create as a symlink for these writes to follow." Two paths, one threat, one of them argued. The obvious version is closed — `os.RemoveAll(dir)` before the clone removes a planted symlink rather than following it — but a TOCTOU window remains between that removal and `git clone`, and the directory mode is what decides whether anyone can stand in it. Remediation: `0o700` on `~/.config/sh-agent` in the report path too (it is sh-agent's own directory, and `SaveState` already puts the manifest there), keeping the pid name that `sweepInterruptedClones` depends on.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/apply.go:220-237` (`Diff`) — `os.CreateTemp("")` writes the rendered harness content into `/tmp`, which this project's rules forbid outright ("every generated or temporary file goes there, never `/tmp`"); mode is 0600 so the exposure is small, but two error paths (`tmp.Write` failing, `tmp.Close` failing) return without removing the file, so a failing `sh-agent diff` leaves debris in a shared directory. Remediation that removes both problems at once and adds nothing: give the planned bytes to `diff` on stdin (`diff -u -L … <dest> -` with `cmd.Stdin = bytes.NewReader(f.Data)`) and delete the temp file entirely.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/harness/frontmatter.go` (`yamlQuote`) with `derive.go` (`DeriveAgy`) — `yamlQuote` escapes `\` and `"` and nothing else, and `DeriveAgy` uses it to render an agent's `description` into the frontmatter of the generated `~/.gemini/config/agents/<name>/agent.md`. It is safe today only because of an unstated invariant elsewhere: `entries` works line by line and joins continuation lines with a space, so `Parse` cannot return a value containing a newline. Nothing states that `DeriveAgy` depends on it, and nothing tests it, so a future change to `Parse` that preserves a line break turns a skill or agent description into arbitrary injected YAML keys in a file an agent CLI reads as configuration. Rated low confidence because I found no input today that produces it. Remediation: either a one-line guard in `yamlQuote` (refuse or escape `\n`, `\r`, and other control characters) or a comment on `Parse` naming `DeriveAgy` as the dependent, plus a test that a description with an embedded line break does not produce a second frontmatter key.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/inventory.go:394-403` (`cell`) — robustness, not exploitable: `s[:max]` and `s[:cut]` slice a UTF-8 description by **bytes**, so when `cut` falls back to `max` (`cut < max/2`) a multi-byte rune is split and invalid UTF-8 goes into `sh-agent list`. Descriptions come from skill files including vendored third-party ones, so the input is not the operator's. Named here because it is in the audited scope and cheap to fix: cut on a rune boundary (`utf8.DecodeLastRuneInString`, or slice `[]rune`).

## Checked

- **Secrets:** clean. No credential, token or key material anywhere in either directory, tests included — a targeted scan for PEM headers, `ghp_`/`sk-ant-`/`AKIA`/`AIza`/`xoxb-` shapes and `ssh-rsa`/`ssh-ed25519` lines returns only labelled fakes in `report_test.go` (`FAKEVALUE`, `FAKEBODY`, AWS's own documented `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE`, a PEM body reading `MIIEpAIBAAKCAQEAsecretbody`) and the one real hit, `release.go:40`, which is a **public** key line, compiled in deliberately and correctly argued. Secrets in *output* were designed against and hold: `scrubCredentials` strips `user[:pass]@` from every URL before it reaches a message, `verifyFeedback` never prints an origin, `readSettings`/`attributionHint` never echo a byte of the operator's `settings.json` (a JSON error string would carry the input it choked on), and `Redaction` records the needle's *name*, never the matched text. `secretShaped` refuses credential-shaped filenames at both ends, adopt and install.
- **Injection:** no shell anywhere — every external command is `exec.Command` with an argv (`git`, `gh`, `go`, `diff`, `ssh-keygen`), so there is no metacharacter surface at all. Argv-injection was considered where it counts: `tag` is validated by `IsReleaseVersion` before reaching `gh` as a positional, with the `-`-leading-tag case written down (`release.go:98-104`); `git add`/`commit` pass paths after `--`; `RemoveKeptClone` deliberately does not interpolate the clone path into the text it prints. Path traversal from the manifest is closed at one choke point, `LoadState`'s `filepath.IsLocal` filter, which `Install`'s resync, `Uninstall` and `Status` all inherit; every other deployed path element goes through `validName`/`identLike`, one local segment of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`. Symlink handling is systematic and was the subject of its own bug (BUG-036): refused in `checkManagedTree`, in `Source.readRegular`, in `Plan`'s walk, in `copyTree`, in `Collect`, in `runDir`, and `attributionSet` Lstats *and* opens `O_EXCL`. `hostDir` strips both separators and refuses `""`, `.`, `..`. The residual is the mode-mask gap above, not a traversal.
- **Authz/authn:** not a service. The two trust decisions are "which tree do I install" (finding 2) and "is this release the operator's" (sound, above). Root/`sudo` is worth one line of honest scope: there is no `Geteuid` check, no warning and no refusal anywhere in either directory, so `sudo sh-agent install` would build as root inside the checkout, execute the result as root and leave root-owned files in `~/.claude` and `~/.config/sh-agent`. I am not filing that as a finding — nothing in the code or docs invites it, and the harness's `sudo` rule is about host setup, not this binary — but it is unguarded, and the BUG-079 note's own "when that path is root-owned" clause shows the situation does arise on the operator's machines.
- **Crypto:** nothing hand-rolled, no finding. `crypto/sha256` + `encoding/hex` used as designed for a checksum; signature verification is delegated whole to `ssh-keygen -Y verify`, a vetted external tool, with the namespace pinned and the signer compiled in rather than read from disk. `checksumFor` requires 64 lowercase hex digits and refuses two differing hashes for one name rather than resolving by order. The comment at `release.go:36-39` already concedes the one real limit — a machine whose PATH or system directories an attacker owns can defeat any check this binary makes — and `sshKeygen` prefers `/usr/bin` and `/bin` accordingly.
- **Dependencies:** best case. `go.mod` declares `go 1.24.4` and **zero** third-party requires; the only import outside the standard library is the module's own `github.com/kesokaj/styrman-harness` embed package. Nothing to justify against stdlib-first, no known-vulnerable version to flag. `npm audit` is not applicable (no JavaScript in scope). `govulncheck` **was not run**: it is installed (`/home/kesokaj/.go/bin/govulncheck`) but it queries `vuln.go.dev`, and this dispatch's hard limits include "no network" — I did not fake it and did not work around it. Context for whoever runs it: with no third-party modules the only surface is the standard library, this box is on go1.27.1, and the project's `AGENTS.md` records the two stdlib advisories as fixed in go1.24.6/go1.25.8, both below that. One command closes it: `govulncheck ./...`.
- **GCP surface:** none in scope — no IAM binding, no service account, no Cloud Run flag, no Secret Manager call, no credential file on disk. Nothing to report.

## Not examined

- `govulncheck ./...` — not run; the dispatch prohibits network. See the dependencies line for why the residual risk is small and for the exact command.
- The `_test.go` files in both directories (`main_test.go` 1592, `harness_test.go` 1812, `report_test.go` 1230, `release_test.go` 645, `pathguard_test.go` 464, `source_test.go` 247 — about 6000 lines) were **not read line by line**; they were scanned only for embedded secret material, which came back clean. No claim is made here about what is or is not covered by a test, including for the findings above — each remediation names the test it needs, and the `--tests` lens in the plan's Phase 2 owns the coverage map.
- No verb was executed and no install was performed. The only thing run was `.agents/scratch/security-audit/verprobe.go`, a pure-logic probe of `IsReleaseVersion`/`compareRelease` with no network and no filesystem effect (gitignored; `git status` confirms the working tree is unchanged apart from review artifacts). The release download path, the `report` push path and `RemoveKeptClone` were read, never run — `report` in particular is prohibited by the dispatch.
- Dynamic behaviour of the consumers (what Claude Code and the Antigravity CLI actually do with a deployed file) is outside this scope, so the *impact* claims about a rewritten instruction file rest on the harness's own stated model, not on measurement.
- Files outside the two named directories — `embed.go`, `.gitignore`, the release workflow in `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md`, `context/`, `skills/` — were not audited. `embed.go` was read incidentally (it embeds `all:context all:skills all:agents all:commands all:rules`); note for whoever picks up the release lens that `all:` includes dot-prefixed files, so what lands in a release binary is decided by what git tracks in those directories, which I did not enumerate.

title: Security review — release gate v1.2.2 (v1.2.1..f91257c) (2026-09-18)
body:
# Security review — release gate v1.2.2 (v1.2.1..f91257c)   (2026-09-18)

Range reviewed: v1.2.1..f91257c

## Verdict: FINDINGS — all low; nothing here blocks the gate

Nothing in this range hand-rolls crypto, adds a dependency, commits a secret, or introduces an
injection sink. `govulncheck ./...` on go1.27.1: **No vulnerabilities found** (run by me, this tree).
The public ssh-ed25519 signer line is byte-for-byte identical in all seven places it appears —
`internal/harness/release.go:40` (`releaseSigner`), `README.md:92,120`, `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:31,91,113,145`
— measured, not eyeballed: SHA-256 of each occurrence is `2b5cdc207c04e554790bd70bcb590bbb1ac5b49c0382f0e73df01bfb2220fcca`,
one distinct value across all seven, and `TestReleaseSignerMatchesTheDeployGuide` (`internal/harness/release_test.go:431`)
pins the `remote.md` copies to the compiled-in one. It is a PUBLIC key whose identity is the operator's
own email, which is its purpose, not a leak.

The worst item is a **downgrade gap in the newly documented MANUAL install chains**: both strip the
`# styrman-harness vX.Y.Z` marker out of `SHA256SUMS` with `grep -v '^#'` and never assert it, so the
human route does not bind the signed hashes to the version being installed — the exact check
`internal/harness/release.go:277-283` makes for `sh-agent update`, and the one `sumsVersionMarker`'s own
comment says exists because "serving an older release's assets under a newer tag would pass every check".
It was named as a hardening note in round 1's report and never carried into any `## Outcome`, so it is
still open. Low, because it needs an actor who can serve release assets without holding the key.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `README.md:94`, `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:33` — the documented chains
  verify `ssh-keygen -Y verify` over `SHA256SUMS`, then pipe `grep -v '^#' SHA256SUMS` into
  `sha256sum -c - --ignore-missing`. The `#` line discarded there is `sumsVersionMarker`, the only thing
  binding a signed checksum file to a release; `verifyRelease` checks it (`internal/harness/release.go:277-283`,
  "the signed SHA256SUMS says %s but this is release %s"), the human chain does not. Exploitable in
  principle by anyone who controls what the release endpoint serves but not the signing key: hand the
  operator an older, genuinely signed `SHA256SUMS` + `SHA256SUMS.sig` + binary and every step of the
  documented chain passes — a silent downgrade to a release with known defects. Sharper for `README.md:90`,
  which passes no tag at all (`gh release download --repo … --pattern …` takes the newest release), so the
  reader has nothing at all tying the bytes to a version. `remote.md:29` at least names `vX.Y.Z` to `gh`,
  but never checks that the signed file agrees. Remediation, no new dependency, one extra `&&` link before
  the checksum step: `grep -qx '# styrman-harness vX.Y.Z' SHA256SUMS` (README: the version the reader meant
  to install), keeping the existing `grep -v '^#'` filter afterwards for `sha256sum -c`'s benefit.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `README.md:119-124` — the browser-route chain, added in the closing
  commit of this range, is the one verification chain in the repository that has never been executed on
  the platform it targets. It is written for macOS (`shasum -a 256 -c - --ignore-missing`), and the
  handoff in this same range says so in as many words: "Not run on a Mac: the README browser route's
  `shasum -a 256 -c - --ignore-missing` form (written from the manual)"
  (`.agents/docs/handoffs/2026-09-18-bug-078-closeout.md`). This repository's own BUG-075 prevention rule
  — "a doc command is RUN as written before the release that documents it, not read" (`bugs/INDEX.md`) —
  is what v1.2.2 would be publishing against. Risk direction is honest: I measured both plausible
  implementations on this Linux box and both FAIL CLOSED with nothing verified — GNU coreutils
  `sha256sum -c - --ignore-missing` exits 1 (`'standard input': no file was verified`) and Perl
  `shasum` 6.x exits 1 with the same message — and an implementation that rejects the flag exits non-zero
  too, stopping the chain before `chmod +x`. The version macOS actually ships was not measured by me or by
  any prior round. Remediation: run the fence once on the Mac before or immediately after cutting the tag
  and record the result in `.agents/docs/testing/`, or drop `--ignore-missing` (the signed file lists
  three assets, so `-c` without it will report the two absent ones and fail — which is why the flag is
  there; if it is dropped, the chain must select the one line instead).
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:395` with `internal/harness/pathguard.go:30,48` —
  `status` prints its `shadowed` line only inside `if … ; onPath {`, and `onPath` is false whenever
  `executableAt(binPath)` fails: the installed file is missing, is a directory, or has lost its execute
  bit. In that state the walk has already collected real shadows and drops them silently, while
  `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:191` and `local.md:87` both list "no `shadowed` line" as a Verify pass
  condition — so a shadowed machine can be recorded as passing. This is the BUG-078 shape (every command
  reporting success about a binary that is not the one running) surviving in one branch. Known and twice
  dispositioned `left` by the main agent (rounds 3 and 4), with real mitigations I confirmed: a missing
  file also prints `binary unknown (installed file has no build info)` (`main.go:373` fallback), and both
  guides now additionally require an unqualified `sh-agent version` matching what was installed. The
  uncovered case remains a present-but-non-executable binary, where the `binary` line prints normally.
  Recorded, not a gate blocker. Remediation (makes the code shorter): print the shadows whenever
  `len(shadows) > 0` and let the `binary` line carry whether the file is installed.
- **[low / confidence: high]** trail markdown in this range — `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-17-release-binary-e2e.md`,
  `.agents/docs/bugs/BUG-078-*.md`, `.agents/docs/handoffs/2026-09-18-bug-078-closeout.md` and the verifier
  logs record internal machine identifiers: account names on other hosts (`/home/admin`, `/Users/spgo`),
  internal hostnames (`spgo-mac.roam.internal`, `devbox`, `dave`), provisioning paths (`/opt/devbox/bin`,
  `/opt/devbox/deploy/harness`), and the local home path throughout. No credential, token, private key or
  `.env` content anywhere — the only key material is the public signer line and the public fingerprint
  `SHA256:5HpYQJjpG+yE1xXBTOIZPsTkbkgkVnV8z0eG8hBawyU`. The repository is private (confirmed in the e2e
  log by `gh repo view --json visibility` → `PRIVATE`), and `remote.md:161` already carries the standing
  note that the trail names internal hostnames and machine paths. Exploitable only as reconnaissance if
  the repository is ever published, which is why it is low and informational. Remediation: none needed
  now; treat it as a checklist item for any decision to open the repository, as `remote.md:161` says.

### Considered, not raised as findings

- **Terminal control bytes in the new `shadowed`/`warning:` output** (`main.go:397,657`, paths printed
  verbatim with `%s`). Raised in rounds 1 and 2 and rebutted twice; I checked the rebuttal and concur:
  the only variable part is an element of the operator's own `$PATH`, the resolved target is never
  printed, `which -a` does not escape either, and anyone who can put an executable `sh-agent` on that
  PATH already gets code execution the next time `sh-agent` is typed. `%q` is Go quoting, not shell
  quoting, so it is not the right instrument. No new information since; no code change asked for.
- **`os.Stat` on every PATH entry hanging on a dead NFS/autofs mount.** Availability only, on the
  operator's own command, bounded by the entries ahead of the installed file (and by every distinct
  entry when the installed file is absent). Rebutted across rounds 2-4 with the reason finally stated
  correctly; I agree.
- **`sh-agent report` leaking the new path output.** It does not: `internal/harness/report.go` `Collect`
  reads files under `~/.config/sh-agent` (`feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl`, `proposals/`, `state.json`)
  and redacts them; it never captures `status` or `install` stdout, so these paths do not reach the
  feedback repository. Verified by reading `report.go`'s `Collect`/`redactLines`/`redactDocument`.

## Checked

- **Secrets** — the only credential-shaped string in range is the PUBLIC allowed-signers line, identical
  to `releaseSigner` by hash across all seven occurrences and pinned by a test. Greps over every added
  markdown line for `password|secret|token|api[_-]?key|private key|BEGIN .*PRIVATE|bearer|ghp_|github_pat_|
  AKIA|xox[baprs]-|client_secret|\.pem|\.key|id_rsa|id_ed25519|GOOGLE_APPLICATION|service.account`: no
  hits other than prose in the prior security reports discussing the absence of secrets. No `.env`,
  `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.tfvars`, `*.tfstate` or credential JSON in the range; `git diff --numstat` shows
  no binary file (no `-`/`-` row), so nothing is hidden from a reviewer.
- **Injection** — `PathShadows` splits `$PATH` with `filepath.SplitList`, joins with `filepath.Join`,
  and never opens, reads or executes a candidate (`os.Stat` only). Every sink is `fmt.Fprintf` with a
  constant format string and the path as an argument; no shell, no `exec`, no template, no SQL added in
  range. In the markdown half the commands are run by a human: every expansion is double-quoted
  (`"$D"`, `"$ASSET"`, `"./$ASSET"`), the chains are single `&&` chains so a failed check cannot be
  outrun by the `mv`, and `chmod +x` sits after both checks so a failed verification leaves a
  non-executable file. The one pipeline (`grep … | sha256sum -c -`) has the deciding command at the end,
  so the `&&` chain reads the right status — and I measured that `sha256sum` cannot exit 0 without
  verifying a real file (empty input → exit 1, nothing present → exit 1).
- **Authz/authn** — no endpoint, session, identity decision or privilege change in range. The one trust
  decision is release-artifact verification; `internal/harness/release.go` is unchanged across the whole
  range, the compiled-in signer and the `sh-agent-release` namespace are intact, and the documented
  chains verify the signature BEFORE trusting the checksum file — the correct order. The gap between the
  documented route and the code route is finding 1.
- **Crypto** — nothing implemented or composed here. The change consumes `ssh-keygen -Y verify` and
  `sha256sum`/`shasum` as designed; `os.Stat`/`os.SameFile` are not crypto. No cipher, hash, MAC,
  signature, KDF, RNG, token or session format is hand-rolled anywhere in range.
- **Dependencies** — none added; `go.mod`/`go.sum` untouched across `v1.2.1..f91257c`. `pathguard.go`
  imports `os` and `path/filepath` only. `govulncheck ./...` → `No vulnerabilities found.`, exit 0,
  go1.27.1 (run by me on this tree; prior rounds could not run it under a no-network limit). No npm
  ecosystem in this repository, so `npm audit` does not apply.
- **GCP surface** — nothing in range: no IAM binding, service account, Cloud Run flag,
  `--allow-unauthenticated`, secret-as-env-var, or service-account key file. This repository has no GCP
  deploy path.
- **Trail markdown (secrets, private data, instruction-shaped text)** — all 21 markdown paths in the
  range read end to end (the four prior security reports, four code/docs reviews, five testing logs, the
  bug record, the changes entry, the handoff, two plan diffs, `INDEX.md`, `README.md`, `ROADMAP.md`,
  `local.md`, `remote.md`). Greps for injection-shaped text (`ignore previous|disregard|new instructions|
  system prompt|override|curl … | sh|rm -rf|chmod 777|--dangerously|--no-verify|skip the review|
  force-push|git config --global|eval|base64 -d`) found no added line that instructs an agent to act
  outside the documented procedure or reads as a prompt override; the only `rm -rf` hits are review prose
  discussing a remediation and the `rm -r "$D"` cleanup. `sudo` appears only in prose on `remote.md:38`
  and in the bug record quoting what the operator did. Private data is finding 4.

## Not examined

- **macOS.** Every measurement here is on Linux (`Linux 6.12.107+deb13-amd64`, go1.27.1, GNU coreutils,
  Perl `shasum` 6.x). The README browser fence's `shasum -a 256 -c - --ignore-missing` form and the
  quarantine behaviour were not run on macOS by me or by any prior round (finding 2).
- **The shell chains were never executed end to end**: no `gh release download`, no network, no release
  fetched, nothing moved into any `bin` directory, nothing written to the real `$HOME`, and
  `sh-agent report` was never run (hard limits). `gh`'s exit status on a missing tag or non-matching
  `--pattern` is taken from its documented behaviour, not measured, so finding 1's threat model rests on
  reading `release.go` and the chains, not on an observed downgrade.
- **Files outside the release diff, read only in part**: `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (~975 lines) was read
  through the full diff plus `:370-400` (`status`), `:260-285` (`installFiles`) and `:640-665`
  (`pathHint`), with greps enumerating every `PathShadows`/`pathHint` call site (exactly two, both in
  range) — the rest is unread. `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go` was read through its 117 added lines only.
  `internal/harness/release.go` was read at `:20-50` and `:218-290`; `report.go` at its `Collect`/redaction
  functions; `pathguard_test.go` in full. No other file in `internal/` was read.
- **No runtime probe of `install`/`status` against a hostile PATH** — constructing an escape-sequence or
  attacker-owned PATH entry would be exploit-shaped; the control-byte item rests on reading the format
  strings. The only probe run was a checksum-tool behaviour measurement under
  `.agents/scratch/security-gate-v122/` (gitignored, safe to delete).
- **Every path in the release diff was read end to end**; no release-diff path is named here.

title: Security review — release gate v1.2.3 (v1.2.2..30f7488)
body:
# Security review — release gate v1.2.3 (v1.2.2..30f7488)

Range reviewed: v1.2.2..30f7488

80 files, 5767 insertions / 112 deletions: 21 source and test files, `README.md`, `ROADMAP.md`,
and 57 trail files under `.agents/docs/`. HEAD `30f7488`; the tree was frozen and no git command
that touches the working tree was run. Every path in the release diff was read (source and tests
from the diff and the surrounding functions; all 57 trail files end to end via a concatenation
under `.agents/scratch/security-gate-v123/`).

## Verdict: FINDINGS — six low, no medium, no high. **Nothing here blocks the v1.2.3 gate.**

The release is a net security improvement over v1.2.2 on every surface it touches: the release-tag
comparison is canonical and refuses a sideways install (`<= 0` plus a `strconv.Atoi` overflow
guard), the adopted-file mode mask stops a group-writable third-party skill landing in the tree
every install ships, `yamlQuote` no longer lets a raw control byte end a YAML scalar, `Diff`'s temp
file leaves the system temp directory and is removed on every path, `TightenConfigDir` makes
`~/.config/sh-agent` private in a way that cannot fail an install, and the by-hand install chains in
README and `remote.md` now bind the download to a version the operator names from outside the
download — closing the real hole in the human route, which was that a genuinely signed OLDER
release passes signature and checksum unchanged. The compiled-in `releaseSigner` is byte-for-byte
identical to all six copies in the docs, and `TestReleaseSignerMatchesTheDeployGuide` pins it.
`govulncheck ./...` is clean.

The worst thing left is **an integrity hole in `install` that this range brings into its own blast
radius without closing**: a runtime directory that exists and is unwritable makes `install` deploy
all 260 files and then fail at `SaveState`, leaving a fully deployed home with **no manifest** — and
the manifest is documented as "the only thing uninstall trusts", so `uninstall` then removes
nothing, `status` can never report a stale file, and every later `install`'s resync prunes nothing.
The prior round measured it (probe J), recorded it as pre-existing, and noted that `Install` now has
a hook at the top where it did not before. Low, because the trigger is an unusual directory state
and nothing is destroyed — but it is a silent loss of the one record `uninstall` depends on.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/apply.go:30,135` with `internal/harness/state.go:64-68` — **an unwritable `~/.config/sh-agent` leaves a fully deployed home with no manifest.** `TightenConfigDir` runs first and correctly skips a directory that is already private (`0500` passes the `Perm()&0o077 == 0` test at state.go:100), so nothing checks that the directory can be *written*; the run proceeds through every file and fails only at `SaveState` → `ConfigDir`/`writeAtomic`, with `saving manifest: … permission denied` after 260 files are on disk. `State` is documented at `state.go:12-14` as "the only thing uninstall trusts: a path not listed here is not sh-agent's to delete", and `Uninstall` (`apply.go:271-274`) prints "nothing installed" and removes nothing when the manifest is absent — so the home holds 260 sh-agent-written files that sh-agent will never account for or remove. Exploitable in principle as a self-inflicted, silent loss of the uninstall record: any `--home` whose `.config/sh-agent` exists and is not writable (a handed-over home, a directory a previous `sudo` run created, a dotfiles symlink into a foreign tree) triggers it, and the failure is announced only after the deployment is complete. Measured by the round-3 reviewer (`reviews/2026-09-18-security-e7fec88-42840fb.md` § Carried) and recorded there as out of range; it is in range now because `TightenConfigDir` put a hook at the top of `Install` and this is the call that belongs beside it. Remediation: a writability probe beside `TightenConfigDir(home, dryRun, out)` — `ConfigDir(home)` plus an `os.CreateTemp(dir, ".probe-*")`/`os.Remove` on a non-dry run — so an unusable runtime directory fails the run **before** the first write. Stdlib `os` only; no dependency.
