- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/state.go:76-91` + `internal/harness/report.go:455`, `internal/harness/apply.go:225` — **the 0700 tightening is bound to `install`, not to the commands that put private data in the directory.** `ConfigDir` creates 0700 when absent and, by design (operator's option 1, round 3), leaves an existing directory's mode untouched; only `TightenConfigDir` corrects it and only `Install` calls it (`apply.go:30`). `cloneThrowaway` (`report.go:455`) clones the private `styrman-harness-feedback` repository under that directory, and `Diff` (`apply.go:225`) writes rendered source there. On a machine upgraded to v1.2.3 whose `~/.config/sh-agent` is still 0755 from an older install, `sh-agent report` before any `install` exposes the throwaway clone — that machine's own redacted feedback — to every local account for the life of the clone. **Disposition on record:** the round-3 report's `## Outcome` (`reviews/2026-09-18-security-e7fec88-42840fb.md`, last bullet) already accepts this — "every `update` runs an install, and a place that never updates is a place that never receives anything". Filed again because the acceptance rests on an operator ordering (`install` before `report`) rather than on a check, and `report` is the one verb that clones a private repository. Remediation if it is ever worth closing: call `TightenConfigDir` from `report` too (it has no error return, prints what it changes, and is a no-op on a dry run) — one call, no dependency.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/frontmatter.go:167-189` (`yamlQuote`) — the new escaping covers `\`, `"`, `\n`, `\t`, `r < 0x20` and `0x7f`, which closes the raw-control-byte hole the audit found. It does **not** cover U+0085 (NEL), U+2028 (LS), U+2029 (PS), or the C1 range U+0080–U+009F. A YAML 1.1 parser (libyaml, and the Python/JS parsers built on it — the likely readers of Antigravity's derived `agent.md`) treats NEL/LS/PS as line breaks and most of C1 as non-printable, so a description carrying one can still terminate or corrupt the double-quoted scalar and, in the line-break case, put author-chosen text at the start of a new frontmatter line. The trust boundary is repo-authored `agents/*.md` (`yamlQuote`'s single caller is `derive.go:36`, on `a.Description`; `adopt` lands third-party content in `skills/`, not `agents/`), which is why this is low. **This is the unfixed residual of the round-1 finding** (`reviews/2026-09-18-security-160aa16-3209cf3.md`, finding 4), which proposed the exact one-line guard and was not carried into any later round's Outcome. Remediation: extend the arm to `r < 0x20 || (r >= 0x7f && r <= 0x9f) || r == 0x2028 || r == 0x2029`, and add the code points to the table at `internal/harness/audit_test.go:201`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:104-109` — `--home` is absolutized with `if abs, err := filepath.Abs(home); err == nil { home = abs }`, and a failure is swallowed. `filepath.Abs` fails only when `os.Getwd()` fails (the working directory was removed or is unreadable), and on that path `home` stays relative and BUG-080 recurs exactly as before: the checkout route runs the rebuilt binary's install with `cmd.Dir = repo`, so a relative `--home` lands **inside the repository**, while `--dry-run` reports against a different directory. Silent divergence between what a dry run says and what a real install writes is the whole shape of BUG-080, and the round-1 reviewer's note ("falling through with the relative path is the old behaviour, not a new hazard") is true of the code and not of the guarantee the fix now advertises. Remediation: return the error (`return fmt.Errorf("resolving --home %q: %w", home, err)`).
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:34`, `README.md:129,153` vs `internal/harness/release.go:48` — the human route and the binary route disagree on what counts as the version marker, and nothing pins them together. The docs check `grep -qxF "# styrman-harness $V"` (one space, exact line, no trailing whitespace); the code matches `(?m)^#\s*styrman-harness\s+(v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)\s*$`, which also accepts `#styrman-harness  v1.2.3 `. The publishing step at `remote.md:148` (`printf '# styrman-harness %s\n' vX.Y.Z`) produces the strict form, so the three agree today and the divergence fails safe (the human chain refuses a marker `update` accepts). It is unpinned: no test ties the doc's `grep -qxF` needle to the publisher's `printf` or to the regex, so a future reformatting of the marker breaks the documented human install with no failing test. Note also that the code's `\s` spans newlines under `(?m)`, so the regex can match across lines — inert, because it runs only on bytes the operator's key has already signed. Remediation: one test asserting the three forms agree, as `TestReleaseSignerMatchesTheDeployGuide` already does for the signer line.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-18-security-c868ed4-bc745dc.md:25` — **two U+0646 ARABIC LETTER NOON inside an ASCII word survive in the release diff.** The round-1 finding that reported them (`warننning` in the explorer's diagnosis brief) was fixed in the brief — I re-scanned every trail file in this range and `plans/2026-09-18-recon-bug-079-diagnosis.md` is clean — but the report that quoted the defect carries the characters verbatim and is itself in the release diff. Arabic letters are strong RTL, so a bidi-aware renderer reorders the run; `.agents/docs/` is read back as agent input, which is the trojan-source class the original finding named. Nothing ships: `embed.go` embeds `context skills agents commands rules` only, so no release binary carries `.agents/docs/`. The original remediation ("a non-ASCII grep over `.agents/docs/` outside the intended typography set catches the next one") is exactly the check that was not run on the fix's own commit. Remediation: replace the two characters by code point (never by typing the escape — BUG-057's class), and add the sweep to the release gate.

### Verified clean, explicitly (the surfaces the dispatch named)

- `IsReleaseVersion` / `compareRelease` / `UpdateFromRelease` — the regex is canonical (`^v(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$`) and the `strconv.Atoi` pass rejects a component too large for `int`, so `releaseParts`' zero-on-error fallback is unreachable from `UpdateFromRelease`: both `tag` (`release.go:102`) and `version` (`release.go:113`) are proven canonical before `compareRelease` runs at line 116. `<= 0` makes equal and older both refuse. The whole gate — `ssh-keygen -Y verify` against the compiled-in signer in namespace `sh-agent-release`, then the signed in-band version marker, then the asset's own SHA-256 over the exact bytes `writeAtomic` writes, with no re-read between hash and write — is untouched and still runs before anything is replaced. `allowed_signers` is written 0600 into an `os.MkdirTemp` 0700 directory; the download directory is random-named and `defer os.RemoveAll`'d, with stale `release-*` siblings swept first; the new binary is placed by `writeAtomic` (`CreateTemp` 0600 → `Chmod` → `Sync` → rename), so there is no window at a wider mode. No hand-rolled crypto: `crypto/sha256` used as designed, signature verification delegated to `ssh-keygen` preferring `/usr/bin` and `/bin` over PATH. The rollback channel the BUG-079 round-3 report raised (`v1.02.2` comparing equal) is closed twice over: by the canonical regex and by the signed marker check.
- `releaseSigner` — `internal/harness/release.go:40` compared against `README.md:97`, `README.md:131`, `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:32,99,121,153` by exact string match (Python line dump, no normalisation): `ostling.simon@gmail.com ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIBkx0BICH1xG18f0a0F/02Vw0OvBTfSOVNXkPkO62NCR` is identical in all seven places. It is a **public** key and the operator's own email, compiled in on purpose so no on-disk signer file can decide what a genuine release is. Not a secret; one principal, one key, no `cert-authority`, no `namespaces=` (the namespace is bound by OpenSSH into the signed blob).
- The `V=` binding in the by-hand chains — `README.md:123,148` and `remote.md:17`. `V` is set at the head of an `&&` chain (a bare assignment exits 0), `gh release download "$V"` is quoted, and two independent checks tie the download to it: `grep -qxF "# styrman-harness $V" SHA256SUMS` runs **after** `ssh-keygen -Y verify` (so the marker is believed only once the signature holds — the same ordering the code uses), and `test "$(./sh-agent-… version)" = "sh-agent $V"` runs **after** the checksum check, so the binary is executed only once verified. `-qxF` is the fixed-string form, so the round-2 BRE-dot finding is closed. The `grep -v '^#' SHA256SUMS | sha256sum -c -` pipeline is a filter *feeding* the verifier, so the `&&` chain reads `sha256sum`'s status, not `grep`'s — the safe orientation of the harness's own rule. `--ignore-missing` cannot make an empty check pass: with no line verified both GNU `sha256sum` and BSD `shasum` exit 1. The browser route's `ls … >/dev/null` guard stops the chain before `mv`, `xattr -d … 2>/dev/null || true` is best-effort and fails closed at the `version` link, and `rm -r "$D"` with a quoted empty `D` is an error, not a wildcard.
- `PathShadows` / `RunningElsewhere` / `NoteRunningElsewhere` / `ownedByCaller` — identity by `os.SameFile` throughout, never a lexical path comparison; `RunningElsewhere` requires `os.Stat(binPath)` to succeed, so a home with no installed binary is silent; the empty-PATH-entry convention (`./sh-agent`) matches `PathShadows`, closing the "reads as a command name" finding; `NoteRunningElsewhere` fires only when `--home` is the real home **by `os.SameFile`** (so a symlinked or bind-mounted `$HOME` counts), and only after a binary was actually written (`release.go:178` past fifteen earlier returns; `main.go:517-521` after `Reinstall`), so no branch that installed nothing reaches it and `--check` is silent on both paths. The `ln -sfn` advice is withheld for a directory the caller does not own, keyed on the **directory's** owner via `ownedByCaller` → `Stat_t.Uid == os.Geteuid()` (`owned_unix.go:17`), with the `!unix` twin returning true because there is no ownership to read. `ownedByCaller` gates no operation on that path — wording only. Output discloses paths only.
- `ConfigDir` / `TightenConfigDir` — `TightenConfigDir` has no error return at all and `Install` calls it as a bare statement before the first write (`apply.go:30`), so a failed chmod cannot abort a deployment; the only chmod-failure branch prints a `note:` and falls through. `os.Lstat` + a symlink arm means the target of a dotfiles symlink is never chmodded, and both skips now print a `note:`. A dry run names the change and touches nothing (verified in both the must-print and must-not-change states by `audit_test.go:246-266`). README:74 and the `install` row of the Daily commands table now state the guarantee with both carve-outs, so the earlier false assurance is closed. The `Lstat`-then-`Chmod` TOCTOU is bounded in the safe direction (chmod succeeds only on a directory the caller owns, and 0700 only clears bits) and was explicitly left with that reasoning — I agree; no finding. A 0700 parent denies traversal, so the 0775 `feedback/` and `proposals/` children need no separate fix.
- `copyTree` modes — `info.Mode().Perm()&0o755|0o600` (`adopt.go:172`) is `plan.go:138`'s expression verbatim, so a 0664 or 0666 adopted skill file lands 0644 and cannot be rewritten by another local account inside the tree `install` ships. `FileMode.Perm()` masks to 0777, so setuid/setgid/sticky cannot survive either. Pinned by `TestAdoptStripsGroupAndOtherWrite` (skipped as root, correctly).
- `Diff`'s temp file — `diffOne` (`apply.go:235`) `defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())` on every path including a failed write, a failed close (folded into `werr`) and a `diff` that cannot run; `os.CreateTemp` makes it 0600 under the home's own runtime directory rather than `/tmp`. `Diff` still *creates* `~/.config/sh-agent` through `ConfigDir` — a side effect in a read-only verb — but it creates a private directory and no longer changes an existing one's mode (pinned at `audit_test.go:175-177`). Recorded, not a finding.
- `cell` (`inventory.go:395`) — the cut is by rune, `strings.LastIndex` returns a byte index at a space (a valid boundary in an already rune-aligned prefix), and the no-space fallback is `len(head)`, so no slice can split a multi-byte character or panic.
- `errPlainCopy` / the `adopt` messages — the added text embeds a public SSH clone URL and prose only; no credential, no path outside the repo. Both name the cause and the alternative, as the audit's refusal rule asks.
- `readSettings`' bound — the 1 MiB check moved into `readSettings` (`main.go:845`), so `install` and `status` apply one bound and say one thing; the `problem` strings carry no byte of file contents, and `attributionSet` still writes with `O_EXCL` and sync-then-rename.
- Tests in range — `audit_test.go`, `owned_unix_test.go`, `pathguard_test.go`, `release_test.go`, `harness_test.go` and `main_test.go` additions were scanned for credential material (clean: only labelled fakes such as `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE` in the untouched `report_test.go`) and for real-home / network / destructive operations. Every `t.Setenv("HOME", …)` points at a `t.TempDir()`, every install goes to `t.TempDir()`, and the root-sensitive mode tests skip under `os.Geteuid() == 0` rather than passing vacuously.
- Trail markdown (all 57 files, read end to end) — no credential, token, key material, `.env`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.tfvars` or credential JSON. The only credential-shaped strings are the public signer line and the key fingerprint `SHA256:5HpYQJjpG+yE1xXBTOIZPsTkbkgkVnV8z0eG8hBawyU`, both public by design. Private-data content is exactly what `remote.md` § Releases already declares and accepts for a private repository: hostnames (`spgo-mac.roam.internal`, `devbox`, `dave`), home and machine paths (`/opt/devbox/deploy/harness`, `/Users/spgo/…`), the operator's email, a Claude session id in the handoff, and one `report.json` body with no secret in it. No instruction-shaped text aimed at a future agent reader was found — the operator quotes and the "remediation" paragraphs are addressed to the reader of the record, and no file contains an imperative that would redirect an agent's behaviour. One bidi residual: finding 6 above.

## Checked

- **Secrets** — clean. Every added line in the range grepped for `ghp_`/`github_pat_`/`gho_`/`ghs_`/`AKIA`/`ASIA`/PEM armor/`api_key`/`client_secret`/`xox[baprs]-`/`sk-…`/`Authorization:`/bearer/password/token: the only hits are prose in the prior review records discussing those shapes. The one credential-shaped string is the `ssh-ed25519` **public** key in the allowed-signers line, unchanged from v1.2.2 and identical in all seven places. No secret-shaped path added anywhere in the range. Nothing is echoed into a log; the new messages print paths, modes and errnos only.
- **Injection** — the parsing boundaries in range are the release tag (canonical regex + `Atoi`, validated before it reaches `gh`'s argv, so a `-`-leading tag cannot be read as a flag), `SHA256SUMS` (`checksumFor` requires 64 lowercase hex and refuses two different hashes for one name, reached only after the signature verifies), the settings JSON (bounded, `encoding/json`), and agent frontmatter (`yamlQuote` — finding 3). No `exec.Command` in range takes a shell; every argument is a separate element and `f.Rel` reaches only `diff`'s `-L` labels, as data. Manifest path traversal is still closed at one choke point, `LoadState`'s `filepath.IsLocal` filter over `Files`; `Repo` remains unfiltered, which the merged record's item 17 left with a narrowed reason I read and find accurate. `diff` and `gh` resolve through PATH and `ssh-keygen` prefers `/usr/bin` — pre-existing and documented at `release.go:36-39`.
- **Authz/authn** — no endpoints, no sessions, no tokens. The authorisation-shaped decisions are `ownedByCaller` (`Stat_t.Uid == Geteuid()` — a pre-check that avoids a guaranteed EPERM, with the kernel still deciding; used to withhold advice and to skip a chmod, both fail safe) and the real-home gate on the BUG-079 note (`os.SameFile`, not string comparison). No `Geteuid` guard against `sudo sh-agent install` exists anywhere, as the audit already recorded; nothing in the range invites it and I do not file it.
- **Crypto** — no hand-rolling. `crypto/sha256` + `encoding/hex` used as designed for a checksum; signature verification delegated entirely to OpenSSH's `ssh-keygen -Y verify` with a compiled-in allowed-signers line and a bound namespace. No cipher, MAC, KDF, RNG, token or session format is implemented or composed anywhere in the range. `yamlQuote` is a string encoder, not a primitive.
- **Dependencies** — none added. `go.mod` is untouched by the range and still carries **zero** third-party requires; the new code adds stdlib `strconv`/`strings` to `source.go`, stdlib `io` to `state.go`, and `syscall` in `owned_unix.go`. `govulncheck ./...` on go1.27.1: **"No vulnerabilities found"** (exit 0). `gofmt -l cmd internal` and `go vet ./...`: clean. `npm audit` not applicable — no JavaScript in this repository. None of my remediations adds a dependency: each is stdlib `os`/`fmt` or a test.
- **GCP surface** — nothing in range: no IAM binding, service account, service-account key file, Cloud Run flag, `--allow-unauthenticated`, Secret Manager reference, or secret passed as an env var. The only remote endpoints are GitHub via `gh` and `git`.
- **Binary/escape check** — `git diff --numstat v1.2.2..30f7488` shows no `-`/`-` pair: nothing in the range is binary. A bidi/invisible-character sweep over every trail file, `README.md` and `ROADMAP.md` in the range returned exactly the two characters in finding 6.

## Not examined

- **Not reached by any command here, and named rather than claimed:** the real release endpoint. No release was published, downloaded or verified in this review — no network was used, no `gh` call was made. The release verification chain's behaviour against a real GitHub response (`gh release download` exit statuses, `--pattern` matching nothing, `--clobber` interacting with `--dir`) rests on reading `release.go` and on the prior e2e logs, not on measurement in this dispatch.
- **macOS is unmeasured, here as in every prior round:** the README browser chain, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine`, Gatekeeper on a quarantined ad-hoc-signed arm64 binary, and `shasum -a 256 -c - --ignore-missing`. The `linux/arm64` asset has never been executed on any machine. The darwin swapped-signature edge of `update` is proven on Linux only. All three are named as remainder in `testing/sh-agent-matrix.md` and in the handoff.
- **The not-owned and chmod-failure branches of `TightenConfigDir` (`state.go:99,107`) were not observed executing** and have no test — a non-root process can neither create a directory it does not own nor make `chmod` fail on one it does. They are reasoned from source I read end to end. The round-3 report reached the same limit by measurement (its probe H) and recorded it; I did not use root and did not retry.
- **`owned_other.go`'s runtime behaviour** (`ownedByCaller` → always true on Windows, so `TightenConfigDir` always attempts the chmod there) was not exercised; no Windows or macOS machine here. I make no claim beyond "it compiles", which the prior rounds' cross-builds establish.
- **`go test -race ./...` was not run in this dispatch** — the verifier owns that and its logs for this range (`testing/2026-09-18-verify-sh-agent-works-everywhere-phase-{1,1-2,2,2-2,2-3,3}.md`) record PASS at 250/0/0 at `42840fb`. I ran `gofmt`, `go vet` and `govulncheck` only. I make no coverage claim; the `--tests` lens owns the coverage map, and its own log names `harness.Diff` at 0% and the verb string `sync` as untested by name.
- **`report.go` and `release.go` outside the diff hunks and their immediate callers** — the redaction list, `Collect`, the push path, `downloadRelease`'s error handling and `verifyRelease`'s tail were read where the range touches them (`cloneThrowaway`, `UpdateFromRelease` whole, `verifyRelease` whole, `checksumFor`, `sshKeygen`, `readCapped`) but the remainder of `report.go`'s ~900 lines is unchanged in this range and was not re-audited; it was audited on 2026-09-18 in `reviews/2026-09-18-security-harness.md`.
- **No release-diff path is unread.** All 21 source and test files, `README.md`, `ROADMAP.md` and all 57 `.agents/docs/` files in `git diff v1.2.2..30f7488 --name-only` were read. No tool result used for this report came back truncated: two oversized outputs were re-read in full from their saved paths, and the trail was read in chunks from `.agents/scratch/security-gate-v123/trail.txt` with every line from 1 to 5281 covered.
- **Housekeeping:** one scratch file created, `.agents/scratch/security-gate-v123/trail.txt` (gitignored), not removed. No probe repository was created. No git command that changes the working tree was run; `sh-agent report` was not run; nothing was installed into the real `$HOME`; no network was used.

title: Cold-reader check — context-consolidation plan (round 1) (2026-09-21)
body:
# Cold-reader check — context-consolidation plan (round 1)   (2026-09-21)

Range reviewed: `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-21-context-consolidation.md` (plan file, not a diff), plus the code/doc surfaces it names: `internal/harness/render.go`, `internal/harness/inventory.go` (`RenderInventoryCompact`, `checkManagedTree`), `internal/harness/harness_test.go:165` (`TestInventoryAndRender`), `internal/harness/source.go`, `internal/harness/source_test.go:43` (`TestPlanFromFSSource`), `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go:1341` (`TestHarnessMap`), `skills/retro/SKILL.md` §Step 2 target table, `agents/bugs.md` §Rules and its `tools:` frontmatter, `REQUIREMENTS.md` §Known limits, `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` header, `README.md` deployment table, `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-03-verify-real-home.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md` §5, plus (per the plan's Why clause) `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-21-context-audit-assessment.md` and `2026-09-21-context-audit-prompt.md`, and `.agents/docs/bugs/BUG-085-...md`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: DESIGN NEEDS REVISION / IMPLEMENTATION NOT READY

Two concrete gaps block a first-pass implementer, both in Phase 2 ("Stop the regrowth" — the phase whose whole point is to close the loop that caused BUG-085): (1) the new rule text for `agents/bugs.md` asks the `bugs` subagent to determine whether a Go test *would fail*, but that agent's `tools:` list has no Bash/`run_command` — it structurally cannot execute `go test`; (2) the new retro-table row that routes "rule scoped to a file type or path" findings to `rules/<name>.md` is added now even though the plan itself defers building any `rules/` file, the cited assessment explicitly says this exact row belongs "in the same commit as the first rule file," and the new size-test gate (Step 2 item 5) is worded to cover only `context/AGENTS.md`/`context/dev-setup.md`, not `rules/` — which shares the same 24,000-byte block per the row's own text. Phase 2 as written reopens the regrowth vector it claims to close. A third, lower-severity issue: D9 cites a test (`TestEmbeddedPlanEqualsCheckout`) that does not exist anywhere in the repo to justify not testing the embedded/release-binary path.

## (1) Gaps

- **`agents/bugs.md` new bullet requires an execution capability the agent does not have.** `agents/bugs.md:1-7` frontmatter: `tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write` — no Bash/`run_command`. The plan's Interfaces text (line 40) adds: "A recommended permanent home is never `context/AGENTS.md` or `context/dev-setup.md` when `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` **would fail** with the sentence added…" Determining whether a test *would* fail requires running it (or reproducing its byte-counting logic by hand from files the agent can `Read`/`Grep` — not specified). Nothing in the plan's Surfaces-touched list mentions adding Bash to this agent's `tools:` (that omission would itself need `internal/harness/derive.go`'s `toolMap`, per this repo's `AGENTS.md` rule on adding a tool). Phase 2's verification for this task ("the record's Related must name the size test") only checks that the test is *named*, not that the agent correctly determined pass/fail — so the behavioural check as designed cannot catch an agent that names the test but guesses wrong. This is a real interface gap between the new rule and the calling agent's capabilities, not decided anywhere in the plan.
- **Phase 2's new retro-table row is not gated the way Phase 2's own new gate is worded, and contradicts the cited assessment's sequencing.** Plan Interfaces (line 39) adds the row `| Rule scoped to a file type or path | .agents/rules/<name>.md | rules/<name>.md (shares Antigravity's 24,000-byte block with the context — REQUIREMENTS § Known limits) |` and, separately, Step 2 item 5: "Before a harness proposal adds to `context/AGENTS.md` or `context/dev-setup.md`, run `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock`…". Item 5's trigger names only those two files — a proposal that creates `rules/<name>.md` is not covered by its own wording, even though the row it sits beside says that file shares the very same byte block. Read `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-21-context-audit-assessment.md` §"The `rules/` question": "Rules do not change the growth engine. The retro target table and the `bugs` graduation rule route every new rule into the context; a `rules/` row and a delete/merge action in that table are what change the next retro's output, and they **belong in the same commit as the first rule file**." That section's own Recommendation is "later" — after pruning shows whether MOVE-TO-SCOPED residue exists, "with a smoke check per rule file on both CLIs before any content depends on it." The plan under review explicitly puts "any `rules/` file" Out of scope (line 15: "deferred: the block cap makes a split worthless until the context has room") yet adds the routing row anyway, ahead of the file it's meant to accompany, with no smoke check and no size gate reaching it. No D-row addresses this divergence from the assessment's explicit sequencing. BUG-085's own probe result (quoted in the bug record) found a second rules file was silently dropped once the block filled, with no error — exactly the failure mode this ungated row could reintroduce on the very next retro.
- **D9 cites a test that does not exist.** "a release binary renders the same bytes (`TestEmbeddedPlanEqualsCheckout`) — by: implementer." `grep -rn "TestEmbeddedPlanEqualsCheckout"` over `cmd/` and `internal/` returns nothing; the only embedded-related tests are `TestEmbeddedInstallStateAndRecord` (`source_test.go:217`) and `TestKnownCheckoutRefusesEmbeddedManifest` (`main_test.go:1048`), neither of which compares rendered bytes. The underlying claim is plausibly true by construction (`EmbeddedSource` reads `styrman.Files`, a `go:embed` of the same tree the checkout test reads, so a release binary built from a given commit embeds the identical `context/*.md` bytes that commit's checkout test would see) — but the plan asserts this via a citation to a nonexistent test rather than stating the construction argument, so a reader has no way to check the claim as written. Low severity (the reasoning holds once traced), but it is an assumption asserted, not checked, exactly as it stands in the file.
- **E2E edge criterion names an ambiguous test fixture.** Verification §E2E "Edge": "with `context/AGENTS.md` padded by 2,100 bytes **in a scratch copy of the repo**, `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` fails naming the excess." But the test's own Interfaces spec (line 37) hardcodes `DirSource(filepath.Join("..", ".."))` relative to the `internal/harness` package directory — it can only ever read the checkout it is compiled from. "A scratch copy of the repo" therefore either means (a) a full second git clone under `.agents/scratch/`, with `go test` invoked from *within that clone's* `internal/harness`, so its own `../..` resolves correctly — a nontrivial, unstated mechanism — or (b) an in-place edit of the live `context/AGENTS.md` with a saved backup, matching this repo's already-established must-fail-mutation protocol (`AGENTS.md` Hard rules: "restored from a saved copy… `git diff` read to confirm nothing else moved"), in which case "in a scratch copy of the repo" is loose wording for "with a copy kept in scratch." These are materially different procedures and the plan does not say which.

## (2) Scope

Everything the plan's Scope §In lists traces to the operator's approval ("Go with your recommendations" over the assessment's Recommendation §0–4 and the audit prompt's method) via D1–D9. I found no endpoint, config surface, or extra shape built beyond what Why/D1 names. The one item worth flagging under this heading is not extra *scope* but a **sequencing** divergence from the plan's own named source (see Gap 2 above): the retro-table `rules/` row is listed in Scope §In ("a `rules/` row… in the retro skill's target table") so it is nominally authorized, but its *content and timing* (added now, unguarded, ahead of any rule file) diverges from what the cited assessment recommended for that same row, with no D-row acknowledging the divergence.

## (3) Readiness

Questions a first-pass implementer would have to ask before starting:

1. **BLOCKING** — How does the `bugs` agent (no Bash tool) determine whether `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` would fail with a proposed sentence added? Do we add Bash to its `tools:` (a `derive.go` `toolMap` change not in Surfaces touched), or reword the rule to not require execution?
2. **BLOCKING** — Does the new retro-table `rules/` row go in now (Phase 2), unguarded by the size test, ahead of any actual rule file — or does it wait, as the cited assessment recommends, until the first `rules/` file and its smoke check land in the same commit? Two implementers would build genuinely different retro-skill text.
3. **BLOCKING** — For the E2E must-fail mutation, is "a scratch copy of the repo" a second full clone (test run from inside it) or an in-place edit-and-restore of the live `context/AGENTS.md`? The mechanisms differ materially and the size-test's hardcoded `../..` path makes the first non-obvious to implement.
4. NON-BLOCKING — `TestEmbeddedPlanEqualsCheckout` doesn't exist; a reasonable implementer drops the false citation or replaces it with the construction argument (`go:embed` of the same tree) without asking.
5. NON-BLOCKING — Plan's cited line numbers are off by one in two places (`skills/retro/SKILL.md:52-59` — table actually starts line 53; `README.md:208` — context row is actually line 209); trivially found by content match.

## Not examined

I did not read: the full `context/AGENTS.md` / `context/dev-setup.md` prose line-by-line against the audit prompt's Step-4 classes (not needed to answer the three questions posed); `internal/harness/plan.go`, `apply.go`, `derive.go`, `pathguard_test.go` beyond the grep confirming `EmbeddedSource`/`rules/` support exists; the full `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-21-context-audit-assessment.md` §Measured/§Recommendation tables beyond what bears on the findings above; `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md` outside §5; `skills/retro/SKILL.md` Steps 3 onward; `agents/bugs.md` Records/Output sections. I did not read the operator's chat of 2026-09-21 that the plan's Why and D1 cite as holding "the findings table" rows 1–8 — that table is not present in either file the plan names as its source, so those specific row approvals are not independently verifiable from the trail alone; this is noted as context for Gap 2, not asserted as a separate defect.

body:
# Cold-reader check — context-consolidation plan (round 2)   (2026-09-21)

Range reviewed: `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-21-context-consolidation.md` (plan file, not a diff), read fresh; round-1 report (`reviews/2026-09-21-coldread-context-consolidation-r1.md`) read only to see what was raised, judged against the plan as it now stands. Code/doc surfaces checked: `internal/harness/render.go`, `internal/harness/harness_test.go:165-212`, `internal/harness/source_test.go:1-93`, `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go:1341-1360` (`TestHarnessMap`), `embed.go`/`embed_test.go:47-`, `internal/harness/plan.go:175-190`, `agents/bugs.md`, `skills/retro/SKILL.md` (full), `REQUIREMENTS.md` § Known limits, `README.md:180-210`, `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-03-verify-real-home.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md` §§3/5, `.agents/docs/bugs/BUG-085-...md`, `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-21-context-audit-assessment.md`, `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-21-context-audit-prompt.md` §§0,4,5.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: DESIGN NEEDS REVISION / IMPLEMENTATION NOT READY

Round 1's three findings are resolved as written: D9 now cites tests that exist (`TestEmbedHoldsOnlyTrackedFiles`, the `TestHarnessMap` pattern — confirmed present and doing what's claimed); D10 rewrites the `bugs` rule to something the agent's Read/Grep/Glob/Edit/Write tools can actually judge (no execution needed); D12 gives the E2E edge mutation an explicit save/restore protocol. But two new gaps of the same shape (an instruction a first-pass implementer cannot execute as written) surface in the surfaces D9-D12 didn't touch: the retro skill's new gating step names a mechanism ("run the test with the addition in place") that nothing in the retro workflow supports before Step 6 actually writes files, and lands as "item 5" in a step that already has five items; and the pruning-review's class list includes MOVE-TO-SCOPED with no defined disposition once the plan defers all `rules/` file creation, so the one class built for exactly this situation has nowhere to go.

## (1) Gaps

- **Retro `SKILL.md` Step 2 "item 5" is a numbering collision and a sequencing gap.** Plan Interfaces (line 39): "Step 2 gains item 5: 'Before a harness proposal adds to `context/*.md` or `rules/*.md`… run `go test ./internal/harness -run TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock -count=1` with the addition in place…'" But `skills/retro/SKILL.md` Step 2 already has five numbered items (`SKILL.md:49` item 1 through `SKILL.md:71` item 5, "Write the rule that fired on every proposal"), so the plan's "item 5" would literally collide with an existing item 5 — a reasonable implementer renumbers it item 6, but the plan doesn't say so (minor, non-blocking on its own). The larger problem: Step 2 is the per-finding *target/scope classification* loop, which runs before Step 3 drafts the exact diff and before Step 6 ever writes a file to disk. "Run the test with the addition in place" cannot execute during Step 2 — there is no addition yet, and nothing is on disk until Step 6's apply. Two implementers would build genuinely different things here: one inserts the sentence verbatim into Step 2 (where it cannot be literally followed — no drafted text exists to test), another moves the check to Step 3 (after drafting, testing against a scratch/mutated copy — needing the same save-restore protocol D12 gives the E2E edge, which this instruction doesn't reference), a third folds it into Step 6's existing "run the project's checks" (where it would be redundant with `go test -race ./...` already running the same test post-hoc, not pre-emptively as "before… adds" implies). The plan does not decide which, nor how "the addition" gets onto disk to be measured without either already committing it (defeating the "before… adds" gate) or an unstated mutate/restore step.
- **Pruning-review class `MOVE-TO-SCOPED` has no defined disposition, and the plan's own scope forecloses its natural one.** Interfaces (line 38) requires every paragraph classified into `{KEEP, DERIVABLE, VAGUE, COMMON-KNOWLEDGE, MOVE-TO-SCOPED, MOVE-TO-SKILL, MOVE-TO-ENFORCEMENT (always "n/a: R3"), DUPLICATE, CONFLICT, STALE}`. `MOVE-TO-ENFORCEMENT` gets an explicit forced default ("n/a: R3") precisely because this plan does no enforcement work. `MOVE-TO-SCOPED`'s natural destination — a `rules/<name>.md` file — is explicitly Out of scope in this same plan (line 15: "any `rules/` file (deferred…)"), and Phase 1's "Apply approved actions" task (line 73) only names two actions: "deletions; merges land in the named skill in the same commit." Nothing says what happens to a row classified MOVE-TO-SCOPED: does it stay in `context/AGENTS.md` untouched (in which case it still counts against the 22,000-byte budget Phase 1 must hit, and the class was pointless to compute), or is it deleted now with no destination file (content lost from the live docs, recoverable only via `git log`, with the future `rules/` file left to reconstruct it from memory)? The Follow-ups line ("the retro table's `rules/` row, which lands in the same commit as the first rule file") implies deletion-now-rebuild-later is intended, but this is nowhere stated for the pruning-review's own Apply step, and it is exactly the kind of implementation choice two engineers would resolve differently — one keeps MOVE-TO-SCOPED rows (correct but blows the budget), the other deletes them (hits budget but silently orphans content the class was invented to protect).

## (2) Scope

No endpoint, config surface, or extra shape beyond what `Why`/D1 name; everything in Scope §In traces to the operator's "Go with your recommendations" via D1–D12, consistent with round 1's finding. The MOVE-TO-SCOPED gap above is a gap in what's decided, not extra scope — the class itself is authorized by Scope §In ("the pruning of… using the prompt's Step 4 classes").

## (3) Readiness

1. **BLOCKING** — Does the new retro Step 2/item-5 test-gate run against a scratch mutation (needing its own save/restore protocol), fold into Step 6's existing "run the project's checks," or move to Step 3? And does it become item 6, since item 5 already exists?
2. **BLOCKING** — When Phase 1's pruning review classifies a paragraph MOVE-TO-SCOPED, what does "Apply approved actions" do with it, given no `rules/` file is built in this plan? Delete now (orphaning content) or keep now (missing the budget)?
3. NON-BLOCKING — Citation drift, larger than round 1's off-by-ones: the README context row (plan: `README.md:209`) is at `README.md:190`; the retro target table (plan: `SKILL.md:53-59`) starts at line 52; the verify-real-home context-questions row (plan: line 17) is at line 12. A reasonable implementer finds these by content match, as round 1's finding 5 already noted for two of these files.
4. NON-BLOCKING — The E2E edge's fixed 2,100-byte padding (Verification §Edge) is chosen without knowing Phase 1's actual post-pruning size; if pruning lands well under 22,000, 2,100 bytes may not cross the budget. Self-correcting at Phase 4 (the checkpoint would just fail to fail, and the implementer pads further) — a reasonable implementer decides this alone.

## Not examined

The full prose of `context/AGENTS.md` / `context/dev-setup.md` paragraph-by-paragraph against the audit prompt's Step 4 classes (not needed to answer the three questions posed, and Phase 1 hasn't run). `internal/harness/derive.go`'s `toolMap`, `apply.go`, `pathguard_test.go` beyond what confirms `r.Raw` and the Agy rules-deploy line (`plan.go:184`, confirmed accurate). `agents/bugs.md` sections beyond §Rules. `skills/retro/SKILL.md` Steps 3-6 beyond what bears on the item-5 gap. `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` (not read this round; nothing in the plan hinges on its existing content, only on an ADR yet to be written into it). The operator's underlying chat approving "rows 1-8" (same limitation round 1 noted: not independently verifiable from the trail alone, not re-asserted as a defect here).

title: Cold-reader review — project-agents-md-native plan, round 1 (2026-09-21)
body:
# Cold-reader review — project-agents-md-native plan, round 1   (2026-09-21)

Range reviewed: `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-21-project-agents-md-native.md` and the surfaces it names (`skills/init-project/SKILL.md`, `context/AGENTS.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md` ADR-005, `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md`, `internal/harness/size_test.go`, `internal/harness/plan.go`, `internal/harness/render.go`).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: implementation not ready

Two blocking gaps, both about surfaces the plan's own "Surfaces touched" section never names.

## (1) Gaps

- **[high / confidence: high]** `REQUIREMENTS.md:11` (R2 — "Standards, not vendor formats") states: "The context follows the agents.md standard and is named `AGENTS.md` at every level (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` **and a project's `CLAUDE.md`** are one-line imports)." This is the exact claim the plan reverses (a project's `CLAUDE.md` no longer exists), and it is a named, numbered requirement — immutable without the operator's explicit approval per the global rule ("propose the exact edit → approval → ADR → update `REQUIREMENTS.md` and `ROADMAP.md` in one commit"). The plan's "Surfaces touched" list (lines 19-24) never mentions `REQUIREMENTS.md` or R2, its Decisions section carries no D-row proposing an R2 edit or citing the operator's approval of that exact text, and Phase 1's grep clause ("grep `AGENTS.md`/README for a claim that this repo has one") does not include `REQUIREMENTS.md`. Shipping this plan as scoped either leaves R2 stale (a description outliving the behaviour it describes, and a violation of the immutable-requirements rule) or requires an out-of-process edit nobody proposed. This is also a live recurrence risk of **BUG-025** (`.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md:26`): "I-23b's edit left project `CLAUDE.md` not a one-line import, violating REQUIREMENTS.md R2" — its prevention rule ("a plan's cold-reader check and rehearsal compare every edit against REQUIREMENTS.md before it lands") is exactly what this check is catching now.
- **[high / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md:22`, the `init-deploy` row, is the fixture the plan's own Verification section names for its behavioural tier ("`/init-project` headless in a fresh scratch repo … answers in the prompt as the matrix's `init-deploy` row"). Its prompt text explicitly instructs the agent: "Do everything the skill says, including the `.claude` symlinks, **`CLAUDE.md`**, `.gitignore` lines, and the commit." After this plan's `SKILL.md` edit, the skill no longer writes `CLAUDE.md` — so the fixture's own prompt now conflicts with the skill it is meant to exercise, and directly contradicts the plan's stated success criterion at line 39 ("`ls CLAUDE.md` afterwards must fail"). This is a test fixture in a verify clause that no longer produces (and actively works against) the condition the plan's E2E criterion claims. The plan does not list `skill-matrix.md` as a surface touched, so nothing directs an implementer to update this row before running the behavioural tier.
- **[low / confidence: low]** The `Why` section's evidence ("Verified today on this box … as the memory page documents") is not backed by any file in this repo — `HERON-4412`/`2.1.277` appear nowhere else under `.agents/docs/`. Not blocking (it is background rationale, not an implementation detail), but worth a one-line testing/change record so the claim is checkable later rather than living only in chat memory.

## (2) Scope

Everything built (SKILL.md edits, this repo's own `CLAUDE.md` removal, the `context/AGENTS.md` Project layout line, ADR-036, v1.6.0 MINOR) is covered by a D-row citing the operator's "Your recommendation. Approved." (D1, D2) or the implementer's own measurement (D3). No unapproved scope creep found.

## (3) Readiness

Could a first-pass implementer ship without asking? No — two BLOCKING questions:

- **BLOCKING**: Does R2 (`REQUIREMENTS.md:11`) get edited in the same commit as ADR-036, and what is the exact proposed wording — has the operator approved that specific text (not just the general "Your recommendation. Approved." on the Why paragraph, which never quotes an R2 edit)?
- **BLOCKING**: Is `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md:22`'s `init-deploy` prompt updated to drop the `CLAUDE.md` instruction before the plan's own behavioural verification tier runs, and is that update in scope for Phase 1 or a prerequisite?
- **NON-BLOCKING**: Should a testing/ log record the 2.1.277 native-read verification cited in `Why`, so it's checkable outside chat memory?

## Criteria (per the six-point lens, applied to the plan document)

1. Dead code — n/a to a plan file; the plan does correctly identify `skills/init-project/assets/CLAUDE.md` for deletion (`git rm`).
2. Flow tracing — traced correctly through `SKILL.md` Step 3's loop/bullet and the update-rule at `:22`; missed the R2 and skill-matrix restatements above.
3. Standards conformance — fails the global "every other restatement of a changed rule is changed with it" rule (`REQUIREMENTS.md` R2) and the project's own immutable-REQUIREMENTS rule.
4. Directory layout — n/a; no new files proposed outside existing conventions (ADR under `architecture/DECISIONS.md`, review under `reviews/`).
5. Simplicity — appropriately minimal; correctly rejects a `--claude-stub` flag as unneeded code.
6. Decoupling — n/a; single-skill, single-doc change with clean boundaries.

## Not examined

`internal/harness/harness_test.go` and `pathguard_test.go` (opened only enough to confirm the size-test budget mechanics, not read end to end — out of scope for this plan since global stub is Out). `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-21-*` historical verification logs (spot-checked for the `20,205` figure only). `skills/init-project/assets/CLAUDE.md` and other `assets/` templates were not opened (not needed beyond confirming the deletion target exists in the plan's own citation). Did not run any command, per the read-only instruction.

title: Review — v1.4.0-HEAD-code (2026-09-21)
body:
# Review — v1.4.0-HEAD-code   (2026-09-21)

Range reviewed: v1.4.0..c7e178e1cb22d873add9903519f91875da0538c8 (`git diff v1.4.0...HEAD`)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing in this range is broken. The release is the BUG-085 fix: a fixed canary line appended last to the rendered context, a size test that pins the rendered context plus `rules/*.md` under 22,000 bytes against Antigravity's observed 24,000-byte block cap, and the pruning of `context/AGENTS.md` / `context/dev-setup.md` that brings it to 20,205 bytes. The Go change is small, traced, and covered by two tests that can fail. The one defect I found is latent rather than live: the size test counts only the BYTES OF THE FILES, while this project's own BUG-085 probe measured roughly 300 bytes of per-file block overhead that the test does not count — harmless today because `rules/` is empty, a silent overflow once several rules files exist. `gofmt -l cmd internal`, `go vet ./...` and `go test -race ./...` are all clean on this head (three packages `ok`).

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/size_test.go:38-44` — the block accounting undercounts per-file overhead. `total = len(ctx) + Σ len(r.Raw)` treats Antigravity's `<user_rules>` block as the concatenation of file bytes, but BUG-085's own probe (`.agents/docs/bugs/BUG-085-…md`, Probe 2026-09-21) measured a 45-byte second rules file costing `AGENTS.md` 342 additional bytes — i.e. ~300 bytes of wrapper/overhead per file that this sum ignores (the store shows each file wrapped as `<RULE[path]>…</RULE[path]>`). With `rules/` empty the test is exact today; with six `rules/*.md` files it would report ~1,800 bytes less than the CLI builds, which is most of the 2,000-byte margin the budget is made of, and the failure mode is a silent truncation with no test red. Concrete fix: add a measured per-file allowance in the sum (`total += len(r.Raw) + rulesFileOverheadBytes` with `rulesFileOverheadBytes = 350`, citing the probe), or state in the test comment that the count is exact only while `rules/` is empty. Also affects the claim in `README.md:207` and `REQUIREMENTS.md:50` that `rules/` files "share the block"/"count toward the budget" — true, but they cost more than their own size.

Not findings, recorded for the record: `skills/cloud-run-deploy/SKILL.md:37` inserts an unnumbered `-` bullet directly after numbered Pre-flight item 5, so the service-account precondition reads as part of "Registry auth" rather than as its own step — formatting, no failure mode, and step 1 now names the service account and says "all six" (the fix recorded in `reviews/2026-09-21-review-worktree-docs-3.md` § Outcome). `README.md:72` still points at "context § Git" for the attribution mechanics, and the pruned context § Git no longer restates the settings key — the RULE it points at (author is the local git config only, the CLI's reminder defers to it) is still there, and the mechanics are in `README.md:72`, `REQUIREMENTS.md:19,59`, `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md:87` and `remote.md:19`, so BUG-039's prevention rule still holds somewhere a reader lands.

## Criteria

1. **Dead code** — pass. The Go diff adds one exported const (`Canary`), referenced by `render.go:60` and `harness_test.go:205`; no function, branch or import is orphaned. Prose deletions in `context/` are covered by the earlier `reviews/2026-09-21-review-worktree-code.md`, which traced each moved row to its stated destination; I re-checked the two highest-risk deletions myself: the subagent git-write rule (BUG-038) is present in all four Bash-holding agents (`agents/{reviewer,explorer,verifier,security}.md`; the other three have no Bash), and the attribution-key mechanics are in `README.md:72` and `REQUIREMENTS.md:19,59`, so the pruning table's stated homes hold.
2. **Flow tracing** — pass. `RenderContext` has exactly three callers (`internal/harness/plan.go:80`, `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:245` `render`, `size_test.go:35`); the canary is appended after `RenderInventoryCompact`, so both vendor targets (`.claude/AGENTS.md`, `.gemini/config/rules/AGENTS.md`, `plan.go:86-96`) get identical bytes and the drift/status comparison stays a byte compare — no consumer parses the tail. No error path is introduced or swallowed. Both new tests can fail: `harness_test.go:205` asserts the suffix (a removed or non-last canary fails it), and the size test's must-fail mutation is logged in `testing/2026-09-21-context-consolidation-phase-4.md` / commit 94a6596. `size_test.go` fails rather than skips outside a checkout (`fs.Stat` → `t.Fatalf`), matching `TestHarnessMap`. The installer-as-caller question is answered by ADR-035's rejected alternatives: no install-time size check, deliberately, because a binary-only place installs what its tag rendered.
3. **Standards conformance** — pass with the one finding above. Go: stdlib only (`io/fs`, `path/filepath`, `testing`), errors handled, `max` is the 1.21 builtin and `go.mod` is `go 1.24.4`. Restatement sweep for the changed rules: the 22,000/24,000 figures and `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` agree verbatim across `REQUIREMENTS.md:50`, `AGENTS.md:24-25,62`, `README.md:190,207,241-243`, `skills/retro/SKILL.md:133`, `agents/bugs.md:77`, `DECISIONS.md` ADR-035 and `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md:126`; `GANNET` appears in exactly the four living files the plan names plus the trail. The rules moved out of the context (mutation protocol → `review-standards § 2`, destructive-guard idiom → `golang`, embedded-artifact both-directions → `review-standards § 2`) are each cited from the context's short form (`context/AGENTS.md:57,58,60`) and present at the destination (`skills/review-standards/SKILL.md:33,36`, `skills/golang/SKILL.md:20`), with `skills/{bug,feature}/SKILL.md` pointing at the same section. REQUIREMENTS was changed the sanctioned way: ADR-035 and the § Known limits bullet land in one commit (5e08629) with operator-approved text.
4. **Directory layout** — pass. `internal/harness/size_test.go` sits beside the package it measures, next to the existing `harness_test.go`/`map_test.go`; no new file elsewhere.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security)** — pass. No new dependency, no new abstraction; the canary is a const and one `WriteString`. Nothing in the range touches auth, crypto, hashing, sessions or JWT/OIDC; no hand-rolled primitive. `plan.go`'s existing symlink and secret-shaped-file refusals are untouched by this diff.
6. **Decoupling** — pass, and improved: rules that only apply inside Go work or review work now live in the skill that loads for that work instead of the always-on context, which is what the byte budget is forcing. `size_test.go` consumes only exported API (`DirSource`, `LoadInventory`, `RenderContext`, `Inventory.Rules[].Raw`) and reaches into no other package.

## Not examined

- The `context/` diff is ~43 KB and the tool result was truncated; I read the POST-state of `context/AGENTS.md` and `context/dev-setup.md` in full and spot-checked deletions by grep, but did not read every removed hunk line by line. The Phase 1 pruning deletions are covered row-by-row by `reviews/2026-09-21-review-worktree-code.md` (APPROVE), Phase 2 by `-docs-2.md` (APPROVE), and the Phase 3 gap-closing edits by `-docs-3.md` (APPROVE WITH NITS, its one finding fixed in the same phase); I did not re-derive the pruning table's per-row byte arithmetic.
- No CLI was started and no installer was run (per the dispatch): the canary's behaviour on Antigravity, the "no `<truncated` marker" result, and the real-home smoke are taken from `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-21-verify-real-home-smoke-5.md` and `-verify-sandbox-pruned-context.md`, not reproduced here. The Mac (Antigravity-only place) is explicitly unexercised by those logs and remains an operator step in the handoff.
- Handoff Next Step 2 tells the operator to ask for the canary word "from the real home" without naming a working directory; `GANNET` is in this repo's `README.md:190` and `AGENTS.md:62`, so a run started inside a harness checkout could answer from the project context rather than the global one. The real-home procedure in `2026-09-03-verify-real-home.md` uses a throwaway demo clone and is sound, so this is a caution on the operator instruction, not a defect in the range — not investigated further.
- The `.agents/docs/` trail in the range (plans, changes, handoffs, cold-read reports, testing logs — ~1,500 of the 1,833 inserted lines) was read selectively for the claims cited above; it was not reviewed as deliverables.
- `skills/` files outside the six named in the dispatch, and `agents/*.md` other than `bugs.md` (read only for the BUG-038 rule), were not reviewed.

title: Review — v1.4.0-HEAD-docs (2026-09-21)
body:
# Review — v1.4.0-HEAD-docs   (2026-09-21)

Range reviewed: `v1.4.0..c7e178e1cb22d873add9903519f91875da0538c8` (HEAD), docs lens per `/preflight` Step 4. Diff: `git diff v1.4.0...HEAD` (53 files, mostly under `.agents/docs/`, plus `README.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `context/`, `agents/bugs.md`, six `skills/*/SKILL.md`, `internal/harness/{render,harness_test,size_test}.go`).

This report re-verifies both prior findings against the final HEAD state (not just the working tree snapshot each was written against) and covers the files those three did not: `README.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `internal/harness/{render,harness_test}.go`, `.agents/docs/architecture/DECISIONS.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md`, `.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md` (full diff), and the rest of `context/AGENTS.md`'s diff (Project layout, Work-classify, Learning loop, Git sections) not walked line-by-line in the prior reports.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The consolidation is what it claims to be: `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, the testing guide, `internal/harness/size_test.go` and `render.go`, and ADR-035 are mutually consistent on the canary line, the 22,000/24,000-byte budget, and the `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` test name and location — every claim I could check against code checked out true. `worktree-docs-3`'s one finding (cloud-run-deploy step-1 missing the service account) is fixed at HEAD. One thing remains broken: `worktree-docs`'s Finding 1 — a dropped rule about how a reviewer must handle a saved-diff dispatch — has no home anywhere in the living docs at HEAD either, confirmed by re-grepping the final tree, not just the working-tree snapshot the earlier report saw. `worktree-docs`'s Finding 2 (the self-hosting-suite/port-bound example) did resolve later in the range: it now lives in `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md` § 2, and `context/AGENTS.md`'s trimmed instrumentation bullet points there ("The mutation protocol is `review-standards` § 2").

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `context/AGENTS.md:16` (Definition of Done step 2, "Review") — dropped, still unresolved at HEAD: the clause "a saved diff file only when the tree will stand still, and the reviewer pins the blobs it read" is gone from the rewritten step 2, which now reads only "given the diff only (a git range or a path list, never the intent)". `git grep -n "pins the blobs\|tree will stand still\|saved diff"` across `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `context/`, `agents/`, non-vendored `skills/`, `.agents/docs/specs/`, `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/` returns nothing at HEAD. `agents/reviewer.md`'s own description ("Give it the diff or the plan only, never the intent") does not carry the frozen-tree/blob-pinning condition either. This is a real procedural rule, not incident narration (unlike several other trims in this same diff that were legitimately incident-only and correctly dropped, e.g. the BUG-070/BUG-080 anecdotes in the read-only-mode bullet, whose actual rule text survives intact). This review's own dispatch text had to restate the missing clause verbatim to work at all ("a saved diff file only when the tree will stand still, and the reviewer pins the blobs it read") — direct evidence the rule has no surviving home to point to. Fix: restore the clause in `context/AGENTS.md` step 2, or fold it into `agents/reviewer.md`.

## Verified consistent (no finding)

- `README.md` § How it works table: canary line and `rules/*.md` budget-sharing row both added, matching `render.go`'s `Canary` constant and `size_test.go`'s inclusion of `inv.Rules` in the byte total. The map's labels change (rule 3 concern) but add no new path — consistent with the brief's framing.
- `REQUIREMENTS.md` § Known limits: new bullet on the 24,000-byte Antigravity block matches `BUG-085`'s record and ADR-035 exactly (numbers, test name, mechanism).
- `AGENTS.md` (project) Setup commands and § Testing/§ Release: size-test pointer and the new `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Steps 1–5 parenthetical both verified against the actual files (`grep -n "^## Step" skills/preflight/SKILL.md` returns Steps 1–6 matching the description given).
