body:
# Review — dreamer-memory-loop-coldread-r2   (2026-09-29)

Range reviewed: `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-29-dreamer-memory-loop.md` (plan, cold read, post round-1 revision), with `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/memory-loop.md` as its spec. Prior review: `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-29-review-dreamer-memory-loop-coldread-r1.md` (gaps G1–G3, D8–D10 claim to resolve them). This is a plan/spec review, not a diff review; code surfaces named by the plan (`internal/harness/derive.go`, `internal/harness/report.go`, `internal/harness/size_test.go`, `skills/init-project/SKILL.md`, `skills/dream/SKILL.md`, `skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md`, `skills/retro/SKILL.md`, `skills/distill/SKILL.md`, `context/AGENTS.md`, `.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md`, `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md`) were read and cross-checked against the plan's claims.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

D10 (byte-for-byte edit technique) is cleanly resolved and matches the file it touches. But two things remain undecided in a way a first-pass implementer cannot resolve alone, both worse than what round 1 flagged because they are now internal contradictions inside the plan/spec pair rather than open questions: (a) the spec's own "Candidate tests" paragraph (still describing the dreamer running an independent "backed by two sources" judgement over memories) was never reconciled with D8's "the dreamer does not re-derive `/dream`'s verdicts" — so the actual algorithm `agents/dreamer.md` must implement is stated two incompatible ways in the same document set, and the `dreamer` matrix row's own expected check cannot be satisfied under the stricter reading without an unstated step; and (b) D9, which round 1 required to fix the silent-migration-mismatch problem, was written as a Decision but never threaded into the Interfaces Step 5b text or the Failure modes table it should have changed — the buildable spec for the migration still says "when `old` is absent or empty, nothing," contradicting D9's "prints 'no default store at `<old>`' ... and lists a hint."

## (1) Gaps

- **G4 — spec's Candidate tests vs. D8's "does not re-derive promote" are unreconciled [medium-high severity, high confidence, BLOCKING].** `specs/sh-agent/memory-loop.md:22` ("Dispatch text") says: "The dreamer does not re-derive `/dream`'s verdicts: the promoted files are its rule-candidate inputs, one candidate row per memory file" — i.e., for memories, the dreamer's job is a pass-through: one candidate row per file already named in `Promoted:`. But `specs/sh-agent/memory-loop.md:24` ("Candidate tests") still reads as an independent judgement the dreamer performs on any memory: "a **rule** when a `feedback` or `user` memory ... is recorded nowhere loaded and is backed by two sources (two memories, a memory and a trail row, or a bug row that recurs)" — a test that can combine "a memory and a trail row" the `Promoted:` list has no way to express (`/dream` only ever flags memory-vs-memory or memory-vs-`feedback.jsonl` pairs; it never sees the trail). Plan Interfaces (line 48, D8) restates the pass-through reading for `/retro`'s wiring ("its rule candidates are the promoted memories ... bug rows whose prevention rule is written nowhere, and trail rows"), but the plan never edits the spec's Candidate-tests paragraph, so an implementer writing `agents/dreamer.md`'s actual prompt text has two different algorithms to choose between: (a) trust `Promoted:` verbatim and do no independent test on memories, or (b) run the "backed by two sources" test on every memory in the store regardless of what `Promoted:` says. These produce different agents. It also breaks the plan's own acceptance check: the `dreamer` matrix row (plan line 50) seeds "two `feedback` memories on one fact from two sessions" directly into the store and dispatches the dreamer with "dispatch text as the contract" — with no `/dream` run first to compute a `Promoted:` list, and no stated rule for what value the matrix-row author puts in the `Promoted:` field of that dispatch. Under reading (a), if the matrix row's dispatch text sets `Promoted: none` (the honest value, since no `/dream` ran), the dreamer would produce **no** rule candidate for the memory pair — failing the row's own stated check ("a rule candidate naming the memory pair"). Under reading (b) the row passes, but then D8's "does not re-derive promote" is false for memories. Decide which reading is correct and: if (a), rewrite spec line 24 to describe promoted-memory pass-through, not an independent test, and state how the matrix row computes its `Promoted:` value for a fixture that bypasses `/dream`; if (b), correct D8 and the plan's Interfaces (lines 22/48 restatement) to say the dreamer *does* re-run the two-source test on memories (and decide what, if anything, `Promoted:` then adds).

- **G5 — D9's migration-visibility fix is not written into the buildable Interfaces/Failure-modes text [medium severity, high confidence, BLOCKING].** D9 (line 111) states: "`/init-project`'s migration prints 'no default store at `<old>`' when the directory is absent, so a mismatch is visible, and lists any `~/.claude/projects/*/memory` directory whose name ends with the repository's last path component as a hint." This is the resolution to round 1's G1 (slug-formula mismatch could silently no-op). But the actual migration text an implementer builds from, Interfaces Step 5b item 3 (line 40), still reads: "when `old` is absent or empty, nothing" — no print, no hint, exactly the silent behaviour G1 flagged and D9 was supposed to replace. The Failure modes table (lines 54–61) has no row for this case either. Two implementers, one working from Interfaces/Failure-modes (silent) and one from the Decisions log (verbose + hint), build different Step 5b scripts, and neither the Phase 1 verify clause (line 77, "behavioural tier, `init-memory` runs") nor the `init-memory` matrix row (line 50) exercises the absent-`old` case at all (its fixture always seeds two files in the default store), so the discrepancy would ship unnoticed either way. Fix: rewrite Interfaces item 3 to match D9's language, and add a Failure-modes row and a matrix-row (or Phase-1 task) case for "no default store at `<old>`, hint printed" so the behaviour D9 promises is actually built and checked.

- **G1/G3 (round 1) — resolved.** D10's "one inserted line with the Edit tool ... never `jq`" matches Interfaces item 2 (line 39) verbatim; closes G3 cleanly. G2 (round 1's one BLOCKING item, `dream`'s `promote` vs. the dreamer's own rule test double-firing) is resolved by D8 and correctly threaded into Interfaces lines 48–49 ("source 7's `promote` findings are replaced by the dreamer's rows for the same memory files, one row per memory, so no memory appears twice") — this part of D8 *is* reflected in the buildable text, unlike D9. The slug-formula verification half of round-1 G1 (a path with a dot) is resolved: D9's rule and the two worked examples on line 36 (`.../styrman-harness` and a `.agents/scratch/.../clone` path with a dot) were checked against this box's real `~/.claude/projects/` names (confirmed by `find ~/.claude/projects -maxdepth 2 -iname '*styrman-harness*'`: the plain-path entry is exactly `-home-kesokaj-workspace-styrman-harness`, matching the plan's claim).

- **No new docs-clause gaps.** Every command/config surface changed still documents itself (its own skill file); confirmed unchanged from round 1's finding. `README.md`/`delivery.md` "nothing" still holds (no map line moves).

- **Byte budget checked and correct.** `go test ./internal/harness -run TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock -v` on the current tree: 21,643 of 22,000 bytes — matches the plan's "headroom 357 bytes" (line 26) exactly; the ~140-byte Resume clause fits.

- **Line-number citations checked and correct.** `skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md` `## Behavior Rules` is at line 80 (plan line 27, exact). `skills/init-project/SKILL.md` Step 5 at line 79, Step 6 at line 94, Step 7 at line 106 (plan line 25's ranges match). `context/AGENTS.md` § Resume at line 9 (plan line 26, exact). `internal/harness/derive.go`'s `toolMap` (lines 15–22) already maps `Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write` (plan line 29's claim holds). `internal/harness/report.go`'s allowlist (lines 262–288) sends only `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl`, `state.json`, `proposals/*.md` — D1's citation holds, memory is not in it.

## (2) Scope

- Nothing new beyond round 1's assessment: the split-store check and migration remain necessary engineering for the operator-chosen design (D6, D9), each with a D-row. D9's added "hint" mechanism (directories ending with the repo's last path component) is scope not named in `## Why`, but is covered by a D-row (D9) responding to the round-1 review, same pattern round 1 already accepted for the split-store check — not a fresh violation, though see G5: as written it exists only in the Decision, not in the build.
- No second shape for the same operation beyond the retro-source-7/source-8 overlap, which D8 resolves at the wiring level (one replaces the other) — see G4 for the unresolved question of whether the *agent's own logic* still duplicates `/dream`'s judgement.

## (3) Readiness

Questions a first-pass implementer would have to ask:

1. **BLOCKING** — Does `agents/dreamer.md` treat `Promoted:` as the *entire* input for memory-based rule candidates (pass-through, per D8), or does it run its own "backed by two sources" test over every memory in the store regardless of `Promoted:` (per spec line 24)? These are different prompts and produce different artifacts on the same fixture. (G4)
2. **BLOCKING** — For the `dreamer` skill-matrix row, which seeds a memory pair directly (no `/dream` run), what value does the dispatch's `Promoted:` field hold, and who computes it? If the matrix-row author manually decides "these two count as promoted" by eyeballing the fixture, that duplicates `/dream`'s own logic outside `/dream`, which is exactly what D8 was written to avoid. (G4, G5's sibling — this is the acceptance-test half of the same undecided question)
3. **BLOCKING** — In `/init-project` Step 5b's migration, when `old` is absent or empty, does it print anything (per D9) or nothing (per Interfaces line 40, still unedited)? Two implementers diverge on whether Step 5b ever prints "no default store at `<old>`" or lists the last-path-component hint. (G5)
4. NON-BLOCKING — Exact position of the Resume clause in the reading-order chain: still unambiguous (append after `bugs/INDEX.md`), as round 1 found.
5. NON-BLOCKING — JSON-edit technique: resolved by D10, matches the file.

**design needs revision** (G4 and G5 are undecided/contradictory) — **implementation not ready** (three BLOCKING questions: G4 twice over, once for the agent's own logic and once for the acceptance test that is supposed to prove it, plus G5 for the migration's visibility behaviour).

## Not examined

- `agents/dreamer.md`, and `skills/retro/SKILL.md` beyond Step 1/Step 2's target table, `skills/distill/SKILL.md` beyond Step 1's current (pre-change) text, `skills/init-project/SKILL.md` Steps 1–4 — not yet written (pre-implementation) or read only to the extent needed to confirm the plan's line-number and content claims.
- The actual contents of this checkout's real memory store (`~/.claude/projects/-home-kesokaj-workspace-styrman-harness/memory/`) beyond confirming the directory name; E2E criterion 2's second half (the "read-neighbours" memory as evidence) was not verified against the live store's file contents.
- `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-29-research-memory-subagents.md` — read only for D-row context in round 1, not re-audited here.
- Claude Code's actual documented slug algorithm for paths with a space or a repeated separator — still unverified beyond the dot case (round 1's residual note, not re-raised as its own finding since D9 covers the dot case and adds a detection fallback for the rest).
- The behavioural/E2E runs themselves — no code exists yet to execute.

title: Review — dreamer-memory-loop-coldread-r3 (2026-09-29)
body:
# Review — dreamer-memory-loop-coldread-r3   (2026-09-29)

Range reviewed: `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-29-dreamer-memory-loop.md` (plan, cold read, post round-2 revision: D8–D12), with `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/memory-loop.md` as its spec, cross-checked against `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-29-review-dreamer-memory-loop-coldread-r2.md` (G4, G5). This is a plan/spec review, not a diff review; not authored by this reviewer. Code/doc surfaces read: `internal/harness/derive.go` (`toolMap`), `internal/harness/report.go` (send allowlist, lines 262–288), `skills/init-project/SKILL.md`, `skills/dream/SKILL.md` (Steps 1–3), `skills/retro/SKILL.md` (Steps 1–2), `skills/distill/SKILL.md` (Step 1/usage), `context/AGENTS.md` § Resume, `agents/reviewer.md` and `agents/bugs.md` (frontmatter shape for `effort`/`maxTurns`), `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md`. `agents/dreamer.md` does not exist yet (pre-implementation, as expected).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES (one new BLOCKING gap; G4/G5 confirmed resolved)

D11 and D12 land as claimed: the spec's Candidate-tests paragraph now reads as pure pass-through for `Promoted:` files (no re-derivation of `/dream`'s two-memory test), Interfaces Step 5b item 3 and the Failure modes table carry the "no default store at `<old>`" print + hint, and the `dreamer` matrix row states its `Promoted:` value explicitly rather than deriving it — G4 and G5 are genuinely closed, not just claimed closed. But the round's own new text introduces one edge case that breaks the buildable spec: Interfaces item 2's JSON-edit technique ("add the key... as one new line after the opening `{`" with a trailing comma) produces invalid JSON when `.claude/settings.local.json` exists as an empty object (`{}`), and the plan states a parse check but never a recovery step when it fails. A second, smaller item: D12's "default store empty at `<old>`" message is written into Interfaces but has no Failure-modes row and no verify/matrix coverage, contrary to D12's own claim that it is "in Interfaces, the Failure modes and the `init-memory-absent` runs."

## (1) Gaps

- **New — Interfaces item 2's insert-after-`{` technique produces invalid JSON for an empty settings file, and no recovery step is named for a failed parse check [medium-high severity, high confidence, BLOCKING].** Plan Interfaces, Step 5b item 2 (line 39): "present without the key → add the key with the Edit tool as one new line after the opening `{` (`"autoMemoryDirectory": "~/.config/sh-agent/memory/<slug>",`), touching no other line... then `python3 -c 'import json,sys; json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))' .claude/settings.local.json` to prove it still parses." When the existing file is `{}` (a freshly created or otherwise empty settings file — a real case: "present without the key" explicitly includes this), inserting a comma-terminated line right after the opening `{` yields `{\n  "autoMemoryDirectory": "...",\n}` — a trailing comma before `}`, which is invalid JSON and would fail the very parse check the plan specifies. The plan states the check but never what to do when it fails: retry with no comma, insert before the closing `}` instead, or a different technique for the empty-object case specifically. A literal implementation of the instruction as written is a bug that the plan's own verification step would catch at test time (if the fixture happens to include an empty `{}` case) but has no defined fix path — an implementer hitting this has to invent a recovery on the spot, and the init-project SKILL.md's Step 5b description (the actual buildable text an implementer edits) inherits whatever they invent. Fix: state the rule for the empty-object case (e.g., "when the file's only content is `{}`, write `{"autoMemoryDirectory": "...")}` with no trailing comma" or a general "look at the next non-whitespace character after the insertion point; add a comma only when it is not `}`"), and state what happens when the post-edit parse check still fails (abort and report the file's raw content for the user to fix, per the existing headless-refusal pattern).

- **D12's "empty store" message has no Failure-modes row or verify coverage, despite D12's claim [low-medium severity, high confidence, NON-BLOCKING for implementation, but a real verification gap].** D12 (line 115) says the "default store empty" behaviour is "in Interfaces, the Failure modes and the `init-memory-absent` runs." Checked against the actual text: Interfaces item 3 (line 40) does state it ("when `old` exists and is empty, print `default store empty at <old>`"). But the Failure modes table (lines 54–61) has only a row titled "No default store at the computed path... `no default store at <old>` plus the hint list" — nothing for the empty-but-present case — and the `init-memory-absent` matrix row's base is explicitly "the `init-memory` base **without the seeded default store**" (i.e. the absent case, not an empty-but-present one) with a check that only greps for `no default store at`. So the "empty store" message is specified once (Interfaces) and never exercised by any stated verify clause or matrix row — it could ship silently broken (wrong message text, wrong trigger condition) and nothing in the plan's Verification section would notice. Since the text in Interfaces is unambiguous, this is not a fork-in-implementation risk (NON-BLOCKING), but it is a coverage gap worth a Phase-1 task or a third matrix-row variant before this is called tested.

- **G4/G5 (round 2) — confirmed resolved.** Spec `Candidate tests` (memory-loop.md:24) now reads as pure pass-through for `Promoted:` files plus two independently-judged tests (recurring bug rows, trail-restated memories) that never overlap `/dream`'s memory-vs-memory domain — matches D8/D11 and the Interfaces restatement (plan line 48). The `dreamer` matrix row (plan line 50) states `Promoted: <the two feedback files>` directly, labelled "(what `/retro` passes after `/dream`)" rather than deriving it by running `/dream` on the fixture — this answers round 2's Q2 cleanly. Interfaces Step 5b item 3 (line 40) and the Failure modes table's "No default store" row both carry the "no default store at `<old>`" print + hint list — matches D9, closing G5's "absent" half.

- **No new docs-clause gaps beyond the above.** Every command/config surface changed documents itself in its own skill file; `README.md`/`delivery.md` "nothing" still holds.

- **Frontmatter fields checked.** `agents/dreamer.md`'s planned `model: sonnet`, `effort: medium`, `maxTurns: 40` match the shape used by `agents/reviewer.md` and `agents/bugs.md` — no new field, no gap.

## (2) Scope

- Nothing new beyond round 1/2's assessment. D9's hint mechanism and D12's "empty store" message are both scope beyond a literal reading of `## Why`, but each carries its own D-row responding to a prior cold-read gap — the established, already-accepted pattern (round 2 §2). No second shape for the same operation was introduced by this round's edits.
- The dreamer's "trail row restates a memory" candidate test (spec line 24, second half) is new judgement the agent performs on its own — not a re-derivation of `/dream`'s promote logic (which never reads trail files), so it does not reopen G4; it is in scope under the operator's original request ("something in the project/conversation highlights to generate a skill/rule or procedure").

## (3) Readiness

1. **BLOCKING** — When `.claude/settings.local.json` exists as `{}` (no existing key, no existing content), does the "insert one line after the opening `{`" technique omit the trailing comma, or is a different insertion point used? And when the post-edit `json.load` check fails for any reason, what does Step 5b do (abort and report raw content, retry a different way, something else)? Two implementers who follow Interfaces item 2 literally without noticing the empty-object case will ship the same latent bug; an implementer who does notice must invent the fix, and different invented fixes diverge. (new)
2. NON-BLOCKING — Whether the "default store empty at `<old>`" message gets its own Failure-modes row and matrix/verify coverage, or is left to the general Interfaces text: a reasonable implementer adds a row/case since D12 already commits to it; this is a testing-completeness gap, not a build ambiguity. (new)
3. NON-BLOCKING — G4/G5 from round 2: resolved, no outstanding question.
4. NON-BLOCKING — Exact `Promoted:` line format (comma list vs. one per line) for the dispatch text template: freeform text handed to an LLM dispatch, any reasonable implementer's choice works the same.

**design needs revision** (the empty-`{}` JSON edge case is an undecided gap in the buildable Interfaces text) — **implementation not ready** (one BLOCKING question: the settings-file edit technique's failure mode).

## Not examined

- `agents/dreamer.md`, `.agents/rules/`, `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-29-research-memory-subagents.md` — not re-read this round (out of scope for a targeted G4/G5-follow-up + fresh pass; round 1/2 already covered them).
- `skills/retro/SKILL.md` beyond Steps 1–2's target table, `skills/distill/SKILL.md` beyond its Step 1/usage header — read only enough to confirm the plan's claims about where source 8 and the dreamer-first dispatch land, not the full files.
- The live `~/.claude/projects/-home-kesokaj-workspace-styrman-harness/memory/` contents, and the actual current `.claude/settings.local.json` in this checkout (whether it is empty, absent, or populated) — not checked, so whether the new BLOCKING gap will actually fire on this checkout's own E2E run is unverified.
- Any code, since `agents/dreamer.md` and the `init-project`/`dream`/`feedback-log`/`retro`/`distill` edits are pre-implementation; nothing to run.
- `.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md` full contents (grepped only for JSON/settings-edit-related prior bugs; none found).

title: Review — f41e5c0-c872598-code (2026-09-29)
body:
# Review — f41e5c0-c872598-code   (2026-09-29)

Range reviewed: f41e5c0..c872598

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing is broken. The two security fixes in `internal/search/store.go` (`prepareFiles`) are correct, and they apply to both indexes because every open goes through `tryOpen`. The `--rebuild` paths unlink a planted link, and that is safe. The error text matches the spec's failure-mode row. The new tests fail without the fix: in a scratch copy of c872598 I replaced the `prepareFiles` call with `_ = prepareFiles`. The code compiled, and both `TestRefuseSymlinkedDatabase` and `TestDatabaseIsPrivate` failed on every sub-case (see finding 1 for the exact output). The worst problem is a test-quality gap. `TestRefuseSymlinkedDatabase`'s "wrote through the symlink" assertion cannot fail for `search.db` in the fixture it uses, so it gives no evidence that nothing was written. Separately, the `O_EXCL` comment in `prepareFiles` implies more protection than the code gives. The preflight Step 5 sentence matches BUG-105's prevention rule. It conflicts with no other restatement, and no code parses the verdict line's position.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/search/security_test.go:230-249` (`TestRefuseSymlinkedDatabase`, the `search.db` case)
  - **What is wrong:** the victim file holds `"keep me"`, which is not a SQLite database. In the mutation run described below, SQLite hit NOTADB. `openStore` printed "unreadable … rebuilt", and `removeDB` unlinked the link and left the victim alone.
  - **Why it matters:** the only assertion that failed there was the refusal-string check (`security_test.go:245`). The `data != "keep me"` assertion stayed silent. It cannot fail in this arrangement, so it does not prove that nothing was written through the link.
  - **The measured arrangement:** the security finding this test answers (`2026-09-29-security-aae16af-f41e5c0.md`, finding 1) used an EMPTY target, which grew from 0 to 86,016 bytes. The global rule wants the test built on the arrangement the finding measured.
  - **Impact:** the trigger itself is still covered, because the refusal assertion fails without the fix.
  - **Fix:** give the `search.db` case (and the global case) an empty victim file, and assert that it is still 0 bytes. The write-through assertion then fails without the fix.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/search/store.go:160-168` (`prepareFiles`)
  - **What is wrong:** the comment "O_EXCL never follows a link put there since the check above" is true of `OpenFile` itself. But on `ErrExist` the function returns nil without looking again. A link planted between the `Lstat` loop and the `OpenFile` makes `OpenFile` return `ErrExist`, the link is accepted, and `sql.Open` then follows it.
  - **Why it matters:** the comment implies that window is closed, and it is not.
  - **Practical impact: negligible.** The attacker needs concurrent write access to the user's own `.agents/scratch` or `~/.config/sh-agent`. A swap of an existing regular file between check and open is inherent to opening by path.
  - **Fix:** on `ErrExist`, `Lstat` the path again and refuse a non-regular file. Otherwise reword the comment so that it claims only what the code does.

## Criteria

1. **Dead code: pass.** `prepareFiles` is called from `tryOpen`, and nothing is left behind.
2. **Flow tracing: pass.**
   - `tryOpen` is the only open path. It is reached from `openStore`, from `prepare` (project), `register` (global), and `reconcileGlobal` (global, plus the direct `tryOpen` in the rebuild count).
   - A refusal is neither NOTADB nor stale, so `openStore` wraps it as `search: <path>: <file> is not a regular file…` and never falls into `removeDB`. This matches the spec's new failure-mode row.
   - Under `--rebuild`, `removeDB` unlinks a planted link with `os.Remove`, which does not follow it.
   - `Chmod` runs only after `Lstat` has shown a regular file.
   - The companion files inherit 0600: `TestDatabaseIsPrivate` checks them, and it failed under the mutation.
   - `gofmt -l cmd internal` is clean, `go vet ./internal/search/` is clean, and `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/search/` passes (6.6 s, on the tree at c872598).
3. **Standards conformance: pass, with the two lows above.**
   - The code is stdlib only, and errors are returned to a caller that wraps them.
   - The spec (`search.md` § Where the indexes live, § Failure modes) was updated in the same range.
   - The preflight sentence restates BUG-105's prevention rule. A grep over `context/`, `agents/`, `skills/*/SKILL.md`, `commands/`, `rules/`, `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` for "VERDICT: SHIP", "verdict line" and "What was not checked" found no conflicting restatement. `AGENTS.md:75`'s Antigravity rule is exactly the "project's own" condition the new sentence tells the gate to read.
   - BUG-105 moved to the Graduated table in `INDEX.md`.
4. **Directory layout: pass.** The test sits beside the code, and the new function sits in `store.go` with `tryOpen`.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security): pass.** It uses `Lstat`, `Chmod` and `OpenFile(O_EXCL, 0600)`, with no dependency and no crypto.
6. **Decoupling: pass.** The file-level check lives in the store, so both indexes get it. `guardProject` keeps its directory checks. No reach-ins.

## Not examined

- **Trail files, not read beyond their diff stat:**
  - `2026-09-29-review-aae16af-f41e5c0-code.md`
  - `2026-09-29-review-abbaddc-1634787-docs.md`
  - the security report `2026-09-29-security-aae16af-f41e5c0.md`, apart from its Findings, Not examined and Outcome sections
  - `testing/2026-09-29-search-adoption.md`
  - `testing/2026-09-29-search-agy-gate.md`
  - `testing/2026-09-29-verify-real-home-search.md`
  - `testing/2026-09-29-verify-search-release-readiness.md`
  - `changes/2026-09-29-2326-search-release-readiness.md`
  - the diffs of the plan `plans/2026-09-29-search-release-readiness.md`, `testing/skill-matrix.md` and the BUG-083 record
- **Read in full:** `changes/2026-09-29-2336-preflight-verdict-last.md`. **Read through line 42:** `testing/2026-09-29-preflight-verdict-last-behavioural.md`.
- **Tests:** the full `go test ./...` was not run, only `./internal/search/`. `govulncheck` was not run, but `go.mod` is unchanged in the range.
- **Behaviour I did not probe myself:**
  - macOS behaviour of `prepareFiles` and of SQLite's companion-file mode;
  - the preflight rule on either CLI. The behavioural log says the verdict itself did not tell the arms apart; only the order did.

## Outcome

Both fixed before the tag (v1.13.0 gate, 2026-09-30), so the verification row is re-run on the fixed head.

- 1. [low] `TestRefuseSymlinkedDatabase`'s write-through check could not fail for `search.db` — fixed: the link's target is an empty file (which SQLite accepts as a new database and the old code wrote into, 86,016 bytes in the security probe), and the test asserts it stays 0 bytes, for the three names and the global index.
- 2. [low] the `O_EXCL` comment promised a recheck the code did not make — fixed by rewording: the comment says a file that appears between the check and the create is opened as it is, and why (closing that window would take a lock the rest of the index does not hold; whoever can race there already writes to the directory). A recheck was tried and dropped: no test could make it fail.

body:
# Review — search-index-code-r2   (2026-09-29)

Range reviewed: 565bb1e..aae16af

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE

The diff is the recorded security-round-2/round-3 fix set (D32–D35) plus its docs. Each fix is narrowly scoped, has a targeted test in `internal/search/security_test.go`, and the accompanying `README.md`/spec/`AGENTS.md`/`DECISIONS.md` text was updated in the same commits. `go build ./...` and `go test ./internal/search/...` pass. Nothing is broken; the two points below are low-severity and don't block.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/search/search.go:322` (`dropReason`) — the "no longer a git checkout" branch is detected by `strings.Contains(err.Error(), "not a git repository")`, i.e. by matching git's English stderr text. `git` localizes this message under `gettext` catalogs on a non-C locale, so on such a machine a genuinely-gone checkout would never match, fall into the generic `err != nil` branch, and the registration would be kept forever with a recurring "note: skipped … this time" rather than ever being dropped. This doesn't leak anything (the safe/keep direction is the one taken on ambiguity, matching D35's intent), but it silently defeats the intended cleanup path on such machines. Low impact given this is a single-operator Linux/macOS CLI tool that in practice runs `git` under `LANG=C`/no gettext catalogs installed, so I'm not blocking on it — worth a one-line note if it's ever seen in practice.

- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/search/search.go:602-603` — the `printable` doc comment says "Tabs and newlines are folded to spaces by the callers first," but most call sites (`sc.label`/`rawLabel`, the `--refs` note/hint lines, `dropReason`'s note lines, the rebuilt-DB note) pass raw, unfolded text straight into `printable` — only `cleanSnippet` and `markTarget` actually fold whitespace first. `printable` still neutralizes a raw `\n`/`\t` (both are `< 0x20`, mapped to `?`), so there's no functional/security gap — the comment just overstates what upstream folding happens before most calls. Not a correctness issue, so borderline as a "finding" at all; noting it since the project's own rule treats a comment that no longer matches the code it documents as reportable.

## Criteria

1. **Dead code** — pass. No orphaned functions; `docsRootOf` still has a live caller (`prepare`'s local-scope path), the old `hash-object`-based loop was fully replaced (not left dangling), and the removed `strings.ContainsAny(p, "\n")` filter was only needed for the newline-joined `git hash-object --stdin-paths` protocol that this diff deletes — its removal is correct, not a regression (paths are now read individually via `os.ReadFile`/`filepath.Join`, immune to embedded `\n`, and any raw `\n` that reaches an output line is still neutralized by `printable`).
2. **Flow tracing** — pass. `blobID`'s SHA-1 git-blob hash is computed directly from `os.ReadFile` bytes and threaded through `entry.oid` into `store.apply`/`diffCount` exactly as the old `hash-object` output was. The new `dropReason`/`register` gate on `.agents/docs` is applied consistently at both registration (`prepare`, gated on `os.Stat(.agents/docs)`) and reconciliation (`reconcileGlobal` → `dropReason`), and `docsRootOf` vs. the hardcoded `".agents/docs"` in `reconcileGlobal` don't diverge because the gate already guarantees `.agents/docs` exists whenever `docsRootOf` is called on a registered root. `printable` is applied at every output site that carries indexed/attacker-reachable content (label, snippet, refs rows, hints, drop/skip notes, rebuilt note); the `TestOutputStripsControlCharacters`/`TestHintAndNotesArePrintable`/`TestRebuiltNoteIsPrintable` tests exercise this concretely, each with a real failing condition (verified `go test ./internal/search/...` passes). `dsn()` correctly percent-encodes `?`/`#`/`%` in the path via `net/url`, verified against the driver's DSN-splitting behavior. Every new test can fail (each plants an attacker-shaped fixture — a `\x1b` byte, a secret-shaped name, a missing `.agents/docs` — and asserts the specific defect is absent), consistent with the review-standards bar.
3. **Standards conformance** — pass. `secretShaped`'s case-insensitive match and the `.git-credentials`/`credentials` additions are mirrored in `.gitignore` and in `README.md`'s `search` row, so the "every restatement of a changed rule" grep is satisfied for this vocabulary. `AGENTS.md`'s `govulncheck` line and `DECISIONS.md` ADR-045a were updated together in-range, consistent with the "describing text moves with behaviour" rule.
4. **Directory layout** — pass. `SecretShaped` lives in `internal/harness` (the package that already owns the credential-shape list for the installer) and is consumed by `internal/search` through an exported function, not a reach-in; tests stay beside their packages.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security)** — pass. `crypto/sha1` is used only to reproduce git's own blob-ID scheme for content addressing (not a security primitive), which is stdlib-as-designed, not hand-rolled crypto. No new dependency was added for this fix set; `go.mod`/`go.sum` churn is `modernc.org/sqlite` moving from indirect to direct plus its own transitive build deps (`go mod tidy`), not a new functional dependency.
6. **Decoupling** — pass. `internal/search` depends on `internal/harness` only through the one exported `SecretShaped` function, sized to what it needs; no new cross-package reach-ins were introduced.

## Not examined

- The three review-report markdown files added in this range (`reviews/2026-09-29-review-search-index-code.md`, `reviews/2026-09-29-security-search-index.md`, `reviews/2026-09-29-review-8ee5d70-HEAD-docs.md`) — out of the dispatch's named scope (Go source + README/AGENTS/.gitignore/spec), and they are other reviewers' own artifacts, not source to critique.
- `internal/search/parse.go`, `store.go`'s `ensureSchema`/`applyLocked`, and the rest of `search.go` outside the diffed hunks — unchanged in this range, not re-reviewed.
- Behavioural verification beyond `go build ./...` and `go test ./internal/search/...` (both green); no manual CLI smoke test was run against a real `~/.config/sh-agent`, per the dispatch's code-only scope.
- Locale-dependent git stderr text (finding 1 above) was reasoned about, not empirically reproduced under a non-C locale.

## Outcome

The reviewer stopped at its turn limit after writing this report (Status COMPLETE).

- 1. `dropReason` matched git's English stderr — fixed at `internal/search/reconcile.go` (`git`): every git call runs with `LC_ALL=C` and an empty `LANGUAGE`; `TestDropReasonIgnoresLocale` (a fake `git` that answers in German unless `LC_ALL=C`: failed before the fix, passes after).
- 2. `printable`'s doc comment said callers fold whitespace — fixed at `internal/search/search.go` (`printable`): the comment says tabs and newlines become `?` except in snippets.

body:
# Review — v1.10.0-1d03e7a-code   (2026-09-29)

Range reviewed: v1.10.0..1d03e7a

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The worst problem: round 2's finding 2 was only half resolved. 1d03e7a struck the verifier shared-call rule, and the changes entry gives the reason: "the prescribed form was refused by the permission gate". The kept long-suite bullet (`agents/verifier.md:42`) still prescribes that same form, `> <file> 2>&1; echo <name>=$?`. The echo is unquoted and comes after a redirect, and the probe gate refused both of those constructs. The echo is also unnecessary, because the foreground suite runs as its own call. This is the third round on this mechanism.

The second problem: no behavioural run has exercised the final long-suite text (redirect plus echo, the `kill -0` check, the tool's own stop), as project `AGENTS.md` § Testing requires for an `agents/*.md` change. The only probe ran d3cc2b7's `tee` + `jobs` text. The round-3 gate verify log is untracked and still IN PROGRESS.

Otherwise:
- Every other earlier finding is fixed or struck.
- The struck text is fully gone: `skills/feature/SKILL.md` lines 15, 55 and 80 match v1.10.0, and `agents/verifier.md:41` matches v1.10.0.
- No repository history leaked into the deployed text.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `agents/verifier.md:42` — The foreground long suite is still written as `> <file> 2>&1; echo <name>=$?`.
  - In the probe (`testing/2026-09-28-verify-retro-apply.md`, the paragraph under the table), the permission gate refused every unquoted `=$?` ("Contains simple_expansion", 6 of 6) and every redirect ("needs approval"). This form has both.
  - 1d03e7a struck the shared-call rule for that exact reason (`changes/2026-09-29-0623-retro-strikes.md`: "the prescribed form was refused by the permission gate"), but left the same construct in the bullet it kept. The strike's own rationale therefore contradicts the kept text.
  - The echo buys nothing. The foreground suite is its own call, so the call's exit status is already the suite's.
  - Failure mode: under a gate like the probe's, a verifier that follows the text literally loses a turn on the one call that matters most. That is the turn exhaustion that the new `maxTurns: 45` answers.
  - Confidence is medium because the operator's real permission settings may allow the construct.
  - Fix, and the shortest one: `> <file> 2>&1` alone, then read the call's own exit status. Otherwise quote it: `; echo "<name>=$?"`.
  - Context § DoD step 2 applies: this is the third round on this mechanism, so it is put to the operator, not fixed on this report's word.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `agents/verifier.md:42` — No behavioural run covers the final long-suite rule. The changed behaviours are: foreground with a raised timeout, redirect with the status echo, background only past the tool maximum, `kill <pid>` then `kill -0`, and the tool's own stop.
  - Project `AGENTS.md` § Testing: "A change to `agents/*.md` also gets a behavioural run … reported as n of N runs".
  - The only probe (`testing/2026-09-28-verify-retro-apply.md`) ran the d3cc2b7 definition, which still had `tee` and `jobs`.
  - The round-2 gate log (`testing/2026-09-28-verify-v1.11.0-gate-r2.md`, Not examined) says no behavioural run was done.
  - 1d03e7a's entry lists only `go test` and the size test.
  - `testing/2026-09-29-verify-v1.11.0-gate-r3.md` exists untracked, with Status IN PROGRESS, so it could not be checked.
  - Fix: run the behavioural probe on the 1d03e7a verifier definition, per BUG-083's procedure, with a suite long enough to take the foreground path, and report n of N. This closes if the round-3 log carries that run.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/reviews/2026-09-28-review-v1.11.0-gate-r2.md` — Committed in 1d03e7a without a `## Outcome` section.
  - Context § DoD step 2 says findings are fixed or rebutted "in the report's `## Outcome`", and `skills/review/SKILL.md:62` says "The record ends with its `## Outcome`".
  - Its three findings are struck (1), half struck (2, see above) and moot (3), and none of that is recorded. The missing ledger is how finding 2's second half went unnoticed.
  - Fix: append `## Outcome` with one line per finding (struck at 1d03e7a / left: operator / moot) when this round is resolved.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `context/AGENTS.md:16` vs `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:84` and `:86` — Two rules give different paths for a low finding whose fix adds a flag, refusal or step.
  - The new clause says such a finding "is put to the operator as a one-line choice".
  - Preflight's SHIP path says a non-blocking finding is either "fixed NOW" or "accepted and named in the release entry with the reason". It also says that, apart from item 4's optional confirmation, the run does not stop ("showing is not a gate … item 4's confirmation … is the only stop").
  - During a release, one agent will stop and ask mid-SHIP. Another will accept the finding into the release entry without asking.
  - Fix: one clause in either file. For example, in the context clause: "(at `/preflight`, it is accepted and named in the release entry)". Or have preflight's non-blocking paragraph list the ask as a third outcome that stops before item 1.

## Earlier findings against the final text

| Round / # | Finding | State at 1d03e7a |
|---|---|---|
| R1-1 | `tee` hides the suite's status | Fixed. `verifier.md:42` says "never `tee`". |
| R1-2 | `jobs` check cannot fail | Fixed. It now uses `kill -0 <pid>` failing, or the tool's own stop. |
| R1-3 | Cold-read early exit contradicts the gate | Struck. `feature/SKILL.md` lines 15, 55 and 80 are byte-identical to v1.10.0. The only in-range diff to the file is line 72 (grouped inputs). |
| R1-4 | Verify log counted attempts | Fixed in the log (round 2 checked the arithmetic). |
| R1-5 | No state for "put to operator" | Fixed. `left: operator — <choice>` appears in both `context/AGENTS.md:16` and `review/SKILL.md:62`. |
| R1-6 | `&&` ambiguity in shared calls | Struck with the shared-call rule. `verifier.md:41` is at its v1.10.0 text. |
| R1-7 | Claude-Code-only wording | Fixed. The verifier says "up to the tool's maximum". The context says "Claude Code: `TaskStop`; elsewhere the CLI's own stop". |
| R2-1 | Early exit widened past its scope | Struck (as R1-3). |
| R2-2 | Unquoted `; echo <name>=$?` refused by the gate | Half struck. Line 41 is gone. Line 42 still carries it: finding 1 above. The "no behavioural run" part is finding 2 above. |
| R2-3 | "Shared calls executed" column mislabelled | Moot: the mechanism it measured is struck. The trail log is not amended, and no deployed text depends on it. |

## Criteria

1. Dead code — pass. Rule text only.
   - The struck text has no surviving restatement in `context/`, `agents/`, non-vendored `skills/`, `commands/`, `rules/` or `README.md`: the feature skill is back to its v1.10.0 gate list, box and tick rule, and verifier line 41 is at v1.10.0.
   - `maxTurns: 30` for the verifier is not restated anywhere. `context/AGENTS.md:33`, `skills/review/SKILL.md:43` and `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:48` say "below the agent's `maxTurns`", without a number.
2. Flow tracing — fail (findings 1 and 2).
   - Status reading is correct: the redirect keeps the suite's status, with no `tee`.
   - The prescribed form is the one the measured gate refused, and the final text has had no behavioural run.
   - The new context sentence on stopping a still-running agent (`:33`) agrees with the verifier's own "every background job is ended before the hand-back" (`verifier.md:42`).
3. Standards conformance — fail (findings 2, 3 and 4).
   - Project rule § Testing is unmet for the `agents/` change. A review record has no Outcome. The context and preflight disagree on low findings at release.
   - `left: operator` agrees between `context/AGENTS.md:16` and `review/SKILL.md:62`, and preflight's NO-SHIP Outcome vocabulary (`fixed` / `rebutted` / `left`) already includes it.
   - The Git "is it live" sentence agrees with the `/preflight` trigger rule in the same paragraph, and with dev-setup's "nothing goes to a cloud unless the user says so", since it is only an offer.
   - The research bullet agrees with Steps 2–4: its second sentence scopes "only".
   - The grouped-inputs clause (`feature/SKILL.md:72`) conflicts with nothing in the golang, docker or cloud-run-deploy skills or in dev-setup. Secret Manager governs delivery, not the command's interface.
   - History leak: the added deployed lines were grepped for `BUG-`, `ADR-`, `styrman`, a year prefix, `retro`, `sh-agent` and `GANNET`, with no match.
   - The rendered context is unchanged since cb6cf73 (1d03e7a does not touch `context/`), where the round-2 log measured 21,517 bytes ending with GANNET.
4. Directory layout — pass. The only new files are trail files under `.agents/docs/{bugs,changes,handoffs,retros,reviews,testing}`.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass, apart from finding 1's redundant echo. No code, no dependencies. Striking the two mechanisms is the shorter fix the context prefers.
6. Decoupling — pass. Each rule stays in the file that owns its actor: verifier, feature, research, the review flow, and the context DoD and Git sections.

## Not examined

- `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-29-verify-v1.11.0-gate-r3.md` (untracked, IN PROGRESS): read only for its Status line and headings.
- In-range trail files not read in full:
  - `bugs/BUG-095-*.md`
  - `bugs/INDEX.md`
  - `changes/2026-09-28-2222-retro-apply.md` and `changes/2026-09-28-2228-retro-apply-fixes.md`
  - `handoffs/2026-09-28-2057-v1.10.0-released.md`
  - `retros/2026-09-28-retro.md`
  - `reviews/2026-09-28-review-v1.10.0-d3cc2b7-docs.md`
  - `testing/2026-09-28-verify-v1.11.0-gate.md`
- Not run by this review: `go test`, `go vet`, `sh-agent render` and the probe transcripts. The byte count and the refusal counts are taken from the round-2 logs.
- Whether Claude Code's notification wording and the `TaskStop` tool name in `context/AGENTS.md:33` match the current CLI.
- Antigravity behaviour of every changed rule.

## Outcome

1. **Long-suite rule, third round on the mechanism: struck.** The operator struck retro proposal 7 for this release ("Go all" on the strike table, 2026-09-29). `agents/verifier.md:42` is back to its v1.10.0 text, so the verifier's diff against v1.10.0 is `maxTurns: 45` alone. Proposal 7 returns to the harness queue as `queued`, to be applied with a behavioural run designed for it.
2. **No behavioural run of the long-suite text: resolved by 1.** No verifier prose changes now; `maxTurns` is frontmatter, checked by the install and `sh-agent list`.
3. **Low, a `left: operator` finding would stop a release: fixed.** `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 6 now says such a finding is accepted into the release entry, recorded `left: operator`, with the choice in the handoff's Next Steps, and the run does not stop.
4. **Low, the round-2 review had no `## Outcome`: fixed** in the same commit.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

No defect in the deployed text blocks this release. The deployed diff is exactly the one the dispatch expects: 6 files, +8/-7. Two of the three context sentences have had no behavioural run, and neither have their `/review` and `/preflight` restatements, which project `AGENTS.md` § Testing requires for a `context/` change. The gap is disclosed in the logs, not hidden (finding 1). The "is it live" sentence is absolute, so it misdirects in a case it did not foresee: released but not yet updated at a place (finding 2).

A single `claude -p --append-system-prompt` run handed a review record containing one low finding of that shape reproduces it: does the agent apply the finding, or record `left: operator` and ask?

Name sentence 8 under Not exercised in the gate report. Alternatively, per preflight Step 6, accept the gap and name it in the release entry.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `context/AGENTS.md:45` — "A question whether a change is live, when it is not, is answered with that fact and a one-line offer to run `/preflight` — never with the deploy steps listed as the operator's work." The rule assumes every deploy step is something `/preflight` performs. That is false when a release exists but a place has not taken it.
  - In this repository, a place moves forward only by the operator's own `sh-agent update`, and project `AGENTS.md` says deploying to the real home is the operator's job.
  - The same is true of a root step without the standing-permission record: `context/dev-setup.md:8` says "hand the step back with the exact command".
  - It also clashes with DoD step 4 (`context/AGENTS.md:18`): "an action only the operator can take goes in the handoff's Next Steps".
  - Failure mode: asked "is v1.11.0 live on my laptop?" after the tag exists, an agent following the text must offer `/preflight`, which has nothing to release or would cut a needless version, and must not name `sh-agent update`.
  - The only probe covered the Cloud Run case, where `/preflight` does the whole deploy.
  - Fix: scope it in one clause, for example "… never with the steps `/preflight` performs listed as the operator's work".

## Earlier findings against the final text (740ca80)

| Round / # | Finding | State at 740ca80 |
|---|---|---|
| R1-1 | `tee` hides the suite's status | Struck. The verifier's long-suite bullet (`agents/verifier.md:42`) is at its v1.10.0 text. |

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The range is small (three commits, records plus a ten-line source/skill change) and mostly self-consistent, but the one new behavioural sentence in `skills/init-project/SKILL.md` Step 1 — "Every write this skill makes — a root file, a template copy, a `.gitignore` line, the settings file, the store — first checks that the target path and its directory are not symlinks" — overstates what the file actually implements two steps later: Step 3's root-file loop and Step 4's `.agents/` tree loop carry no `test -L` check at all, only Step 5b (settings/store) and Step 6 (`.gitignore`) do. Given this project's history with exactly this class of defect (ADR-043, BUG-098–103), a claim of blanket coverage that the adjacent code does not back up is worth flagging even though nothing else in the range is broken.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:26` vs `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:44-48,58-68` — the new sentence names "a root file" and "a template copy" as covered by the symlink check, but Step 3's copy loop (`for f in AGENTS.md REQUIREMENTS.md TODO.md ROADMAP.md; do [ -e "$f" ] || cp "$ASSETS/$f" "$f"; done`) and Step 4's `.agents/` tree loop (`[ -e "$d" ] && continue … mkdir -p "$dir" && cp …`) have no `test -L` guard on the target path, its directory, or (for Step 4) `.agents` itself — the very directory Step 5b later checks specifically for the store. If `.agents` is a symlink, Step 4 populates the entire scaffold (rules, skills, agents, workflows, commands, docs) through it, unchecked, before Step 5b ever runs. The associated changelog entry (`2026-09-29-1609-post-release-checks.md`) claims this sentence closes "the older writes the security round had named as out of range," which the code does not bear out for Steps 3–4. Fix: either add the same `test -L` guard to Steps 3 and 4's loops, or narrow the Step 1 sentence to the writes it actually covers (settings file, store, `.gitignore`).
- **[low / confidence: low, unverified]** `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-29-verify-real-home-v1.12.0.md` (Claude Code table, `init-memory-linked-store` row) says "the five default-store files untouched," but the matrix row it is reporting on (`skill-matrix.md`'s `init-memory-linked-store`, built on the `init-memory` base) seeds the default store with "two memories and a `MEMORY.md`" — three files, not five. The five-file count matches this same log's unrelated general Fixture section (a different `.agents/memory` seed used for the context/dream/retro checks), so the number may simply have been copied from the wrong paragraph, or the operator ran a differently-seeded fixture than the row specifies. Not independently reproducible from the record alone — listed as a docs-consistency gap, not asserted as a defect.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — n/a — docs lens (the one code change, `harness_test.go`'s glob→stat swap, removes the old assertion cleanly; nothing dead left behind).
2. Flow tracing — n/a — docs lens (see Finding 1: the described "flow" of Step 1's blanket check does not reach Steps 3–4's callers).
3. Standards conformance — n/a — docs lens; the changed-rule grep for "the Antigravity run before a tag" rule found no other restatement needing a matching update: `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` already generalizes "a project's `AGENTS.md` may add blocking conditions; it cannot remove these" (line 77), so the new project-level NO-SHIP condition in this repo's root `AGENTS.md` § Release needs no companion edit there; `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases covers the tag/sign/version mechanics only and does not restate gate blocking conditions, so it is not stale either. `context/AGENTS.md` (the deployed global context) has no `## Release` section, so the project-specific rule correctly stays out of it.
4. Directory layout — n/a — docs lens; all new/changed files (bug record, two `changes/` entries, one handoff, two testing logs, matrix edit) land under their conventional `.agents/docs/` subdirectories.
5. Simplicity — n/a — docs lens.
6. Decoupling — n/a — docs lens.

## Other checks performed
- README.md map: unchanged in this range (confirmed via `git diff --stat`) — correct, per the rule that the map does not move without a design decision.
- `/init-project` symlink sentence vs `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/memory-loop.md`: the spec's existing rows (lines 15, 35, 38) already describe symlink refusal specifically for the settings file and the store; the new Step 1 sentence in the skill is consistent with those rows for the writes they name (settings, store, `.gitignore`) — the mismatch is only that the skill's sentence claims wider coverage (root files, template copies) than either the skill's own later steps or the spec describe.
- Matrix rows changed (`dream`, `init-memory-linked-store`) checked against the logs they cite (`2026-09-29-verify-real-home-v1.12.0.md`): the `dream` row's exact-path change matches the store's actual location claims in the log; the `init-memory-linked-store` row's dropped `.gitignore` assertion matches Step 6's actual (unconditional-on-symlink-only) behavior. Only the file-count wording noted above did not line up.
- `AGENTS.md` § Release new sentence cross-checked against `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Steps 2 and 5 and `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` § Releases — no disagreement found (see Criterion 3).
- BUG-104 record and INDEX row read against `internal/harness/harness_test.go`'s actual diff — description matches the code change exactly (own-pid stat replacing a shared glob).

## Not examined
- Full text of `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` § The model (read only via grep, not in full) — no change in this range touches it, so it was not read end to end.
- `internal/harness/harness_test.go` was read only as a diff, not run; the verifier's own log (`2026-09-29-verify-post-release-v1.12.0.md`, present in this range) already reports the mutation-protocol evidence for BUG-104 and was taken as read rather than independently re-run.
- The claimed Antigravity/Claude Code real-home runs themselves (their actual transcripts) were not available to inspect — only the written logs describing them; the file-count discrepancy noted above could not be resolved further without those transcripts.
- `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md` rows other than `dream` and `init-memory-linked-store` (the only two this range touches) were not re-audited.

## Outcome
- `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:26` claims every write is symlink-guarded while Steps 3 and 4 had none — fixed: Step 3's loop skips a symlinked root file; Step 4 refuses a symlinked `.agents` before the loop (an if/else, after a first `&& false ||` form that would have run the loop anyway) and skips a symlinked file or directory inside it; the shell blocks parse and the guard was exercised on a linked `.agents` in scratch.
- `testing/2026-09-29-verify-real-home-v1.12.0.md` "five default-store files" — clarified: that fixture seeds four memories plus the index; the matrix row's generic base seeds two.

title: Review — v1.12.1-c872598-docs (2026-09-29)
body:
# Review — v1.12.1-c872598-docs   (2026-09-29)

Range reviewed: v1.12.1..c872598 (git diff v1.12.1...c872598); release gate for v1.13.0, Step 4 (docs freshness). Two prior docs-lens reports (8ee5d70-HEAD, abbaddc-1634787) already covered parts of this range and their findings were fixed; this report concentrates on cross-document contradictions at the head and the release-facing docs (README install/command table, deploy/local.md, deploy/remote.md, specs/sh-agent/delivery.md) named in the dispatch.

## Status: COMPLETE (within the call budget — see Not examined for what a fuller pass would still cover)

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The release-facing docs are internally consistent at the head: README's install paragraph, its `search`/`index` command-table rows, `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md`'s plain-copy build note, `REQUIREMENTS.md` R4, and `go.mod` all agree on "one dependency, `modernc.org/sqlite`, go 1.24.4" (the two prior docs-lens reports already fixed the version-number and advisory-count mismatches in this area). `specs/sh-agent/search.md`'s ranking description ("chunks holding every word rank first … filled with any-word hits"), registration rule (only a checkout with an `.agents/docs` directory registers; a plain `docs/` never does), and the 0600 file-mode claim all match `internal/search/search.go` and `store.go` exactly, code and doc read side by side. `specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` (unchanged in this range) is silent on `search.db` rather than contradicting anything — `REQUIREMENTS.md` R4 and R7 deliberately keep "harness state" (manifest, feedback log, proposals, `retros.jsonl`) distinct from the search indexes, which every doc calls a "cache" `report` never sends, so delivery.md's "R7 keeps that as the one place harness state lives" is not narrowed by omission. One real defect: the final commit (c872598) flipped BUG-083's and BUG-105's frontmatter `status:` from `open` to `fixed` without touching either record's own body text, so each file now contradicts itself.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/bugs/BUG-105-verdict-contradicted-what-was-not-checked.md:5` vs `:16` — commit c872598 changed the frontmatter to `status: fixed`, but the `## Fix` section, left untouched, still reads "Not fixed as a rule... no file yet stops the next gate report from writing a verdict before checking it against its own 'What was not checked' list." That statement is now false: this same commit added exactly that stop (`skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 5, "Write the verdict line LAST..."), and the commit message itself says "BUG-105 fixed and graduated." A reader of the record alone (or `sh-agent search --refs BUG-105`) sees a `fixed` status next to prose asserting no fix exists. Fix: append a line under `## Fix` (bug records are append-only) noting the Step 5 rule that closed it and the date.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/bugs/BUG-083-verifier-early-write-rule-not-followed-every-run.md:5` vs `:30` — same pattern: frontmatter flipped `open` → `fixed` in c872598, but the `## Prevention` section still reads "Status stays `open` in the sense that more behavioural runs would still be useful; it leaves the main INDEX table because the rule it names is now graduated." That sentence was accurate when written (against the old `status: open`) and is now a direct contradiction of the frontmatter two lines above it, in the same file, both current as of this commit. Fix: append a line noting the 2026-09-29 measurement (31 of 31 verifier dispatches) that justified the flip, or soften "Status stays open" to say so explicitly.

Both are append-only trail records (project rule: the `bugs` subagent's status-flip is "the one edit a past record allows"), so the fix is an addition, not a rewrite — but as they stand at `c872598` each record's own two halves disagree about whether the bug is fixed, which is exactly the kind of self-contradiction this release gate is meant to catch, even though bug records are outside the "grep other living docs for stale restatements" corpus the brief names (that exclusion is about searching *other* files for a changed rule's old wording, not about a record contradicting itself).

## Criteria
1. Dead code — n/a — docs lens
2. Flow tracing — n/a — docs lens
3. Standards conformance — n/a — docs lens
4. Directory layout — n/a — docs lens
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — n/a — docs lens
6. Decoupling — n/a — docs lens

## Verified matches (no finding)
- README.md § install paragraph, its `search`/`index` command-table rows, and `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md`'s plain-copy note all state "one dependency, `modernc.org/sqlite`" and Go 1.24+, matching `go.mod` (`go 1.24.4`, `require modernc.org/sqlite v1.46.1`) and `REQUIREMENTS.md` R4's rewritten text.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`'s `-h` usage text for `search`/`index` (word-for-word: flags, `--global` description, the `.agents/scratch/search.db` path) matches README's command-table rows and `specs/sh-agent/search.md`.
- `specs/sh-agent/search.md`'s registration rule ("A checkout with an `.agents/docs` directory registers itself... a third-party clone with a plain `docs/` never registers") matches `internal/search/search.go`'s `prepare()` (registers only when `os.Stat(filepath.Join(root, ".agents", "docs"))` is a directory).
- The 0600/0700 file-mode claims in `specs/sh-agent/search.md`, README, and `REQUIREMENTS.md` R8/delivery.md match `internal/search/store.go`'s `os.Chmod(p, 0o600)` and the existing `~/.config/sh-agent/` 0700 code.
- `context/AGENTS.md`'s Resume Protocol ("...→ `.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md` → `sh-agent search --open`...") and `skills/handoff/SKILL.md`'s Resume-Protocol restatement both carry the same `sh-agent search --open` step, consistent with each other (already verified by the abbaddc-1634787 report for the `--open`/`--global` clause split; re-checked here for the exact ordering, which matches).
- `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md` § 3d, `sh-agent-matrix.md`'s new `search`/`index` rows, and `skill-matrix.md`'s `search-first`/`search-agents` rows are consistent with each other and with the spec/code.
- `ROADMAP.md` and `TODO.md` are empty (headers only) at `c872598`, correct per the project rule for a closed checkpoint; the newest `changes/` entry (`2026-09-29-2336-preflight-verdict-last.md`) accurately describes the diff it covers (`skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 5, the two bug-status flips, the INDEX.md graduation move) — except that it does not flag the self-contradiction the flips left behind in the bug files themselves (see Findings).
- `specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` (untouched this range) makes no claim about the binary having "no dependency" and does not claim `~/.config/sh-agent/` holds only the pre-search-index files; its silence on `search.db` is consistent with R4/R7's deliberate state-vs-cache distinction, not a contradiction.

## Not examined
- `internal/search/reconcile.go`'s 14-day blob-GC and freshness steps were read only in the section already spot-checked (lines 60-90); the rest of the reconcile path and the full failure-mode table in `specs/sh-agent/search.md` were taken on the prior reports' word, not independently re-verified line by line against the code in this pass.
- `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` and `gcp.md` have no diff in this range; only a targeted grep (for "offline"/"module proxy"/"dependenc") was run against `remote.md`, which found nothing, so their release-build steps were not read start to end for a subtler contradiction (e.g. whether the signed-tag build step still has network access for the one Go module fetch on a fully offline release machine).
- The full `git diff v1.12.1...c872598` (94 files, ~6,800 insertions) was not read in full; this pass targeted the release-facing docs and the cross-document claims the dispatch named (word-search ranking, registration, file mode, resume order, the delivery model) rather than every changed file's prose.
- Plan files, `reviews/`, `handoffs/`, and `retros/` entries added in this range (e.g. `plans/2026-09-29-search-index.md`, the coldread rounds, the security reports) were not read; per the brief they are excluded from the stale-restatement grep, and this pass did not separately check them for self-contradiction the way BUG-083/BUG-105 were checked.
- `agents/*.md` and `skills/*/SKILL.md` diffs in this range (small, 1-4 lines each per the stat) were not individually re-diffed against the code paths they describe beyond the `preflight`/Step-5 change already covered.

## Outcome

- 1. and 2. [medium] BUG-105's and BUG-083's bodies still say "not fixed" / "stays open" beside `status: fixed` — rebutted: a bug record's body is history as written at the time, and its status is the one later edit the rules allow (`context/AGENTS.md` § Work: "set the record's status in both files — the one edit a past record allows"); the docs lens's own brief excludes bug records from the living docs it searches (`skills/review/SKILL.md` Step 3, the `--docs` row: "never in … bug records or dated logs"). The status in the frontmatter and in `bugs/INDEX.md` is the living value; the evidence for both closures is in `testing/2026-09-29-preflight-verdict-last-behavioural.md` and `changes/2026-09-29-2336-preflight-verdict-last.md`.

# Review — worktree-code (2026-09-29)

Range reviewed: working tree (unstaged + staged) — `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md`, `skills/VENDORED.md`, `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md`, `skills/review/SKILL.md`, `skills/review-standards/references/prompt-audit/LICENSE.txt` (new), `skills/review-standards/references/prompt-audit/prompt-audit.md` (new)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing broken. This wires a new `/review --prompts` lens onto a verbatim-vendored Anthropic reference file: the vendoring is correctly pinned (digest matches, file untouched), the installer places both new files under the right skill directory on both vendors (verified with a scratch install), the dispatch text's paths for both CLIs are correct against `internal/harness/plan.go`'s `AgyRoot`/`ClaudeRoot`, and `go build`/`go vet`/`go test ./internal/harness/...` are clean. The one real gap is in the new skill-matrix test row itself: its check script only asserts 3 of the 4 fixture facts the scenario sets up, so a regression in the most basic pattern group (Group 1a pressure language) could pass this scenario silently.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md:31` (`review-prompts` row) — the scenario commits four fixture facts (a Group 1a pressure-language line `CRITICAL: You MUST ALWAYS run gofmt...`, a stale path `cmd/nothing/main.go`, a Group 2 conflicting-instructions pair `make test` vs `go test ./...`, and a provenance-protected BUG-001 line), but the `check` column only asserts three: `## Proposed diff`, `cmd/nothing`, `make test`, plus the negative BUG-001/remove check. Nothing in the check requires the report to mention or act on the `CRITICAL: ... gofmt` line at all. If the `--prompts` lens implementation (or the vendored file's Group 1a section) regressed and stopped detecting pressure language, this scenario would still PASS. Add an assertion (e.g. `grep -qi "CRITICAL" "$f"` plus a check that it's flagged, not just quoted) so the row actually exercises the fixture it sets up. This is the AGENTS.md "changed code without covering test is a FAIL" rule applied to a test spec that doesn't cover part of what it claims to.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md:14` — the new `prompt-audit` bullet is appended under the "Language deep-dives (load only for the languages present in the diff)" heading, but it is not a language deep-dive and is explicitly *not* loaded that way — its own text says `/review --prompts` hands it to the reviewer and "nothing else loads it". The bullet's own wording resolves the ambiguity for a careful reader, so this doesn't cause a wrong load, but the heading's scoping rule no longer covers the list under it. Consider a second one-line heading (e.g. "Special-purpose references, loaded only when named:") rather than folding it into the language list.

## Vendoring check (as scoped)

- `skills/VENDORED.md`'s new row pins `github.com/anthropics/skills` at `8a1541c`, digest `c33200da…1878f2`. `sha256sum` of the working-tree file: `c33200da181e10f1f31bd4625059cd30bc6922940aac49017d8ab0c2721878f2` — matches the row's prefix/suffix exactly.
- `LICENSE.txt` beside it is the stock Apache-2.0 text (spot-checked header); not reviewed further per instructions.
- No network access in this sandbox, so the fetched-content-matches-upstream direction could not be independently re-verified against `raw.githubusercontent.com`; only the local digest-matches-file check was possible. Noting this as a scope limit, not a finding.
- Not reviewed: the prose of `prompt-audit.md` itself (per instructions) — noted only that it internally references `shared/model-migration.md` and `shared/prompt-caching.md`, two sibling files from the same upstream skill that are not vendored here. The `/review --prompts` dispatch brief in `skills/review/SKILL.md` only ever points the reviewer at `prompt-audit.md` and never asks it to open those two files, so nothing in this diff's own flow breaks on their absence — flagged here only as a fact for the operator, not a finding.

## Criteria

1. **Dead code** — pass. No removed callers, no orphaned exports; the new files are the sole additions and both are referenced (from `review-standards/SKILL.md` and `review/SKILL.md`).
2. **Flow tracing** — pass, with the one test-coverage gap above. Traced: `review/SKILL.md`'s new `--prompts` row (Step 3) → `review-standards/SKILL.md`'s new bullet → `references/prompt-audit/prompt-audit.md` → both vendor paths (`~/.claude/skills/review-standards/...`, `~/.gemini/config/skills/review-standards/...`), confirmed against `internal/harness/plan.go`'s `ClaudeRoot`/`AgyRoot` constants and a live scratch install. The `--fix` step's `--prompts` handling (apply hunks, run `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` only for `context/`/`rules/` edits) matches the project AGENTS.md's own scoping of that test. The new skill-matrix row's check under-asserts one of its four fixtures (finding above).
3. **Standards conformance** — pass. Frontmatter in `skills/review/SKILL.md` is double-quoted (contains a colon), no unquoted `#` (BUG-004). Grepped `README.md`, `skills/preflight/SKILL.md`, `context/AGENTS.md` for other restatements of the lens list (`--docs`, `--simplify`, etc.) — none found, so no other restatement needed updating for the new `--prompts` flag.
4. **Directory layout** — pass. `references/prompt-audit/{prompt-audit.md,LICENSE.txt}` sits under the existing `review-standards/references/` convention beside `go-review.md`/`typescript-review.md`; `skills/VENDORED.md`'s header rule ("never edit vendored content in place") is honored — the file is untouched from its pinned fetch.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security)** — pass. No new dependency; this is a markdown reference file plus two doc/skill edits wiring it in. No security-relevant code touched.
6. **Decoupling** — pass. The new lens is additive to `review/SKILL.md`'s existing per-lens table/dispatch pattern; no existing lens's brief or table row was restructured, only appended to.

## Not examined

- Did not re-fetch `prompt-audit.md` from `raw.githubusercontent.com` to confirm the local copy matches upstream byte-for-byte (no network in this environment) — verified only that the local file's digest matches the row's recorded digest, and that the file is unedited relative to that pin (no diff-in-place indicators).
- Did not execute the `review-prompts` skill-matrix scenario itself (that is a live-CLI behavioural run per `AGENTS.md` § Testing, out of scope for a static review of the spec row).
- Did not review the prose content of `prompt-audit.md` beyond the passages needed to confirm it does not embed obviously wrong internal references — per the dispatch's explicit instruction not to review vendored prose.

## Outcome
- `skill-matrix.md:31` check asserts 3 of 4 seeds — fixed: the `review-prompts` row now greps `CRITICAL`, `reviewer-go` and `reviewer-ts` as well (seven greps); run against the four round-2 clones in `.agents/scratch/prompts-probe/runs/{4,5,6,ctl}`, PASS in each (`testing/2026-09-29-prompts-lens-behavioural.md`).
- `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md:14` bullet under the language-deep-dives heading — fixed: the bullet now sits under its own line, "Lens reference (not a language; loaded only when `/review --prompts` names it in the reviewer's brief)".
- Not examined, upstream byte check — done by the main agent: `sha256sum` of the vendored file equals the file fetched from `raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/skills/8a1541c4a3ffa5a20a5a91de0dcf3f0bab1d1ef4/skills/claude-api/shared/prompt-audit.md` (`c33200da…1878f2`, 48,983 bytes).

title: Review — worktree-docs (2026-09-29)
body:
# Review — worktree-docs   (2026-09-29)

Range reviewed: working tree — changed files: .agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md, skills/VENDORED.md, skills/review-standards/SKILL.md, skills/review/SKILL.md; new/staged: skills/review-standards/references/prompt-audit/LICENSE.txt, skills/review-standards/references/prompt-audit/prompt-audit.md

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The change adds a fourth review lens (`--prompts`, vendoring Anthropic's `prompt-audit` reference) and is documented consistently everywhere the harness enumerates `/review`'s lenses: the skill's `description`, `argument-hint`, usage block, Step 1's flag list, the Step 3 lens table, and Step 5's per-lens fix behaviour in `skills/review/SKILL.md` all now include `prompts`/`--prompts`. `README.md`, `context/AGENTS.md`, `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` and `agents/*.md` do not enumerate the lens set at all (they reference `--docs` once, for a specific unrelated rule, or "lens" in the six-criteria sense), so none of them needed an update. The vendored file is byte-identical to upstream at the pinned commit (verified by re-fetching `8a1541c` and comparing sha256: `c33200da…1878f2` matches) and the `VENDORED.md` row's path, pin, and license are all correct. The one real gap is a paraphrase in `skills/review/SKILL.md`'s `--prompts` brief that silently drops a qualifier the vendored source states explicitly, which would make the reviewer skip the sub-agent-roster check in the single most common case this lens is used for.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/review/SKILL.md:52` — the `--prompts` brief says "Its Group 4 is `not applicable` unless the scope holds request-building code," but the vendored source it summarizes (`skills/review-standards/references/prompt-audit/prompt-audit.md:173`) says Group 4 is not applicable when there's no request-building code "**except the sub-agent roster check, which applies to those agents' definition files**." Since `--prompts` scope is most often exactly `agents/*.md` / `.agents/agents/` with no request-building code (the harness's own primary use case per the new skill-matrix scenario, which scopes to `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/rules`), the brief's flattened wording tells the reviewer to skip the redundant-sub-agent-roster check in the case it was written for. Fix: restate the brief's Group 4 sentence to keep the roster-check exception, e.g. "Its Group 4 is `not applicable` unless the scope holds request-building code, except the sub-agent roster check, which still applies to any agent definition file in scope."

- **[low / confidence: low]** `.agents/docs/testing/skill-matrix.md:31` — the new `review-prompts` row grants `--add-dir <home>/.claude/skills/review-standards`, but no other `/review` scenario in this file (`review`, `review-shadow`, `review-shadow-name`, `review-project`, rows 26–30) grants that directory even though they equally dispatch the `reviewer` agent with the `review-standards` skill (which itself loads `references/go-review.md` / `references/typescript-review.md`). If skill references are normally reachable without `--add-dir`, this row's grant is either unnecessary scaffolding or evidence the other rows are under-permissioned for their own reference reads. I could not run the sandbox to settle which; flagging as unverified rather than asserting a defect.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — n/a — docs lens
2. Flow tracing — n/a — docs lens
3. Standards conformance — n/a — docs lens
4. Directory layout — n/a — docs lens (the new reference lands under `skills/review-standards/references/prompt-audit/`, consistent with the existing `references/go-review.md` / `references/typescript-review.md` siblings and with `AGENTS.md`'s "Third-party skills are vendored verbatim... never edit them in place" rule — this is vendored verbatim as a reference, not a skill, and `VENDORED.md` records it)
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — n/a — docs lens (stdlib/dependency question doesn't apply to a markdown reference; no new code dependency introduced)
6. Decoupling — n/a — docs lens

## `git grep` sweep for restatements of the changed lens set

The diff changes the enumerated lens list (`--code|--security|--simplify|--docs|--tests|--all` → adds `--prompts`) in four places, all in `skills/review/SKILL.md` itself (already updated together, verified above). Grepping the living docs (`README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `context/`, `agents/`, every skill dir under `skills/` not in `skills/VENDORED.md`, `commands/`, `rules/`, `.agents/docs/specs/`, `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md`, `.agents/docs/deploy/`) for the old lens enumeration or for `--docs|--tests|--all` lens lists found no other restatement — no `dropped:` or `narrowed:` findings beyond the Group-4 paraphrase above, which is not a restatement of the *lens list* but a restatement of the *vendored file's own Group-4 rule*.

No rule, command, flag, or caveat was removed by this diff (it is purely additive except for the four places where the lens token list gained one more item in-line) — no `dropped:` findings.

## Not examined

- Whether `.agents/docs/testing/2026-09-29-verify-prompts-lens.md`'s in-flight verifier run (Status: IN PROGRESS at time of this review) or the concurrent behavioural probe in `.agents/scratch/prompts-probe/` actually confirm the `--prompts` lens works end to end — that is the verifier's job, not this docs review's, and its log was still IN PROGRESS when read.
- The `skill-matrix.md` `--add-dir` question above (low finding) — would need a sandbox run to confirm whether it's redundant or the other rows are missing it.
- `skills/review-standards/references/prompt-audit/LICENSE.txt` was not byte-verified against upstream (fetched the wrong URL, got a 404 from GitHub); its content is a standard Apache-2.0 license text with "Copyright 2026 Anthropic, PBC.", consistent with `VENDORED.md`'s Apache-2.0 claim, but the exact source URL was not located and confirmed.
