- **[medium / confidence: high]** `plan:144` and Surfaces `plan:36` ("`Collect` excludes `proposals/dream/`"). `Collect` already reads only the top-level `.md` entries of `proposals/` (`report.go:331-339`), and a directory named `dream` is neither `.md` nor read recursively. The Phase 4 unit test therefore passes before any change, so it cannot fail. Say that it is a regression pin for existing behaviour, not a code change. Separately, `redactLines` is at `report.go:199`, not `:128`, which is `needleIn`.
- **[high / confidence: high]** `plan:20,128` — the new skill `skills/memory/` takes the name of Claude Code's built-in `/memory` command. This is BUG-065's class exactly (`bugs/INDEX.md:51`: "a skill/agent/command name never shadows a built-in slash command of either CLI"). Rename it, for example to `memory-log` or `project-memory`, and check agy's built-in list too.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `plan:117-121` vs `REQUIREMENTS.md:31` (R7) and `context/AGENTS.md:42` ("every retro, distill and dream leaves a record in `.agents/docs/retros/`"). `sh-agent dream` writes its per-project output only to `~/.config/sh-agent/proposals/dream/`, and D3 says it "never edits a project". R7 says a project's dream records live in the project's trail. The plan lists `context/AGENTS.md:42` as touched but does not say whether the verb's output is a "dream record" under R7 (D10 keeps the two names on purpose). Stale restatements to fix as well: `README.md:212` ("a dream leaves its record in the project's `retros/` and no line here"), `README.md:30` (the map's `configDir` contents omit `proposals/dream/`, `dream-state.json`, `dream.log`, `dream.lock` and `dream-work/`), and `README.md:214` (the report list).
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `plan:23` vs `AGENTS.md:15` (rule 3: adding a line to the map needs the operator, an ADR and one commit) and `REQUIREMENTS.md:47` (R9: the procedures and the map change together). The job adds a producer into `configDir` and an edge to `retroHarness` (`README.md:15,30,51`), yet the plan's docs list names `README.md:214` and the verbs table but not the map. Decide whether dream is on the map. If it is, the operator's word and `TestHarnessMap` belong in the same commit.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `plan:23`, D6 — the consumer is undefined in three places:
  - (a) `/retro --harness` lists proposals by their `**Status:**` line (`skills/retro/SKILL.md:48`), but dream files carry frontmatter plus `## Proposals` and no Status line. Nothing says how one is marked applied or rejected, so each file is re-listed forever.
  - (b) A proposal whose target is a project (kinds `rule`/`memory`) has no consumer. `/retro --harness` runs in the harness checkout and applies harness targets, and project-level `/retro` never reads `proposals/dream/`.
  - (c) On binary-only and zip places, `/retro --harness` never runs ("same machine only", `README.md:51`), and D6 keeps dream files out of `report`. Their output is never seen.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** D3 (`plan:165`) — the R3 exception text says the job writes "to `~/.config/sh-agent/proposals/` only". The design also writes `dream-state.json`, `dream.log`, `dream.lock` and `dream-work/` (`plan:58,71,74,76`). The operator would be approving text that the implementation breaks on its first run. Reword it before asking, for example "writes only under `~/.config/sh-agent/`, and its proposals and draft skills only to `proposals/`".
- **[medium / confidence: high]** Scope items 1 and D1–D6 cite "dreamer table item N" and "memory table item N". The dreamer table exists only in the gitignored `.agents/scratch/2026-09-30-dream-background-options.md`; the memory table was not found anywhere. The approved decisions are therefore not in the trail. The plan also departs from approved items without saying so:
  - item 4 said `proposals/<date>-dream-<project>.md` (top level, "the existing queue") and `proposals/drafts/<name>/SKILL.md`; the plan uses `proposals/dream/` with inline drafts (D6);
  - item 5 said Read/Grep/Write tools with a dedicated agy settings file; the plan goes tool-free (D4);
  - item 1 said "the manifest lists it"; the plan is silent (see the R4 finding above).

  Copy both tables into the plan, and mark each departure as one that needs the operator's word.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `plan:89` — `/init-project` Step 5b. Every project already scaffolded falls in the branch "present with the key → keep the file as it is" (`skills/init-project/SKILL.md:115`), so "same insertion method" does not say how `autoMemoryEnabled` gets into a file that already holds `autoMemoryDirectory`. Also, Non-goals (`REQUIREMENTS.md`, the "Editing `settings.json` or any vendor setting … never another key" bullet) is not reconciled with a second vendor-setting key written by a skill. The plan's Out list cites Non-goals only for permissions.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `plan:58-66` — the watermark. The plan does not say whether "advances" means run start or write time. With write time, anything changed during a 10-minute run is lost. Memory is collected whole ("every memory file"), so the plan also needs to say what makes a project "unchanged" (E2E 3 depends on it). Claude transcripts also need a rule: file mtime or per-line `timestamp`.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** Risks do not name a cost of R-parity. With native memory off, loading memory needs a `Bash`/`run_command` call to `sh-agent memory show` at every session start, and writing needs one per memory. Both ask for permission because Non-goals bar writing a permission. In headless runs without a grant, the call is refused and memory silently never loads. Either list this as a known difference or accept it in a D-row.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** Cross-vendor disclosure. With manifest vendor `all`, Antigravity transcripts are sent to Claude (recon risk 1). No D-row decides it; the Open row covers only redaction scope.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `plan:44`. The frontmatter drops `node_type: memory` and `originSessionId`, which `skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md:90` and `memory-loop.md:12` name. `/dream` and `dreamer` read that shape, so say that the spec rewrite changes it.
- **[low / confidence: high]** Docs clauses missing:
  - project `AGENTS.md` Layout (`:36-46`) for `internal/memory` and `internal/dream`;
  - `AGENTS.md:59`, if the driver question moves;
  - the `uninstall` row in README and `deploy/local.md` for the timer removal;
  - `README.md:212,214,30` (see above).
- **[low / confidence: high]** Phase 0 box 1 (`plan:118`) is already done in d6e396a (R10 at `REQUIREMENTS.md:49`, ADR-047 at `DECISIONS.md:501`) but is not ticked. The context budget is 21998 of 22000 bytes (`go test -run RenderedContext -v`), so the Phase 2 resume edit has 2 bytes of headroom; the plan does say it pays in the same edit.
- **[low / confidence: high]** E2E 6 (`plan:112`) applies `--cli`, a `dream` flag, to criterion 1, which is about memory sessions. Reword it as "criterion 1 on the claude and agy homes; criterion 3 with `--cli claude` and `--cli agy`".

### Scope (question 2)
Items the plan builds that `## Why` did not name, with the D-row status of each:
- `sh-agent dream <dir>` (a second, single-project form of the operation): no D-row. It is useful for tests, but the plan should say so or drop it.
- `memory add --title`: an optional value the slug already covers. No D-row, and the memory table that might hold it is not in the trail.
- `--cli claude|agy`: in the approved options item 5 ("overridable with `--cli`"), but that record is scratch only, so it needs a D-row.
- `status` line and `dream.log`: approved options item 6, same record caveat.
- `--dry-run`: required by the global read-only rule. Not a gap.

### Readiness (question 3)
BLOCKING (two careful implementers would build different things):
1. Where does the SQLite read of Antigravity's databases live, given R4 and AGENTS.md:59: an `internal/search` export, or a requirements change?
2. Is the timer in the manifest? How does `uninstall` remove it without breaking R4, and how does `install` avoid deleting it as stale?
3. How does the unit find `claude`/`agy` (PATH or an absolute path captured at install), and which `sh-agent` path goes into `ExecStart`?
4. How is a dream proposal marked consumed, who applies project-target proposals, and what happens to the output on places without a harness checkout?
5. What is the watermark's value (run start or write time), and what counts as "changed" when memory is collected whole?
6. Is "`.gitignore` lacks `.agents/memory`" a literal-line check or `git check-ignore`? A `.agents/` line gives opposite results.
7. How does Step 5b add `autoMemoryEnabled` to a settings file that already holds `autoMemoryDirectory`, and how is Non-goals' "never another key" reconciled?
8. What is the skill named, given the collision with the built-in `/memory` (BUG-065)?
9. Is the dream job on the README map (AGENTS.md rule 3, R9), and is its output an R7 "dream record"?
10. What is the stale rule for `dream.lock`?
11. How is the timer verified without the real systemd manager and the real home (R6)?

NON-BLOCKING (a default is stated, or a reasonable implementer can decide):
- Does `memory add` wait on a held `.lock` or fail at once?
- Claude transcripts from a session started in a subdirectory of the root: exact `cwd` match per `plan:64` misses them; accept that.
- Frontmatter fields `node_type` and `originSessionId`.
- Whether agy needs a workspace-trust entry for `dream-work/`. If so, that is a vendor-setting edit; the D7 fallback covers it.
- Whether to use redaction marker wording other than "[redacted by sh-agent report]".
- Cross-vendor transcript policy (the Open row defaults to none).

`design needs revision` — `implementation not ready`

## Criteria
1. Dead code: not applicable to a plan. One planned change is a no-op: the `Collect` exclusion already holds (`report.go:331-339`).
2. Flow tracing: **fail**. Timer → manifest → `install` stale removal → `uninstall` is untraced. Unit → PATH → CLI fails. Proposal → consumer is undefined for project targets and non-checkout places.
3. Standards conformance: **fail**. R4 (driver outside `internal/search`, uninstall beyond the manifest), R6 (timer verification), BUG-065 (skill name), and R7 and restatements left standing (`README.md:30,212,214`, `context/AGENTS.md:42`). R10 is satisfied in intent. AGENTS.md § Testing (`:65-73`) is cited for the sandbox runs (BUG-115 exists); E2E 3's real `claude -p` under `--home` must keep the real `HOME` in the child's environment (AGENTS.md:65, "a CLI started from a scratch HOME cannot authenticate"), which the plan does not say.
4. Directory layout: pass. `internal/memory` and `internal/dream` fit, but AGENTS.md Layout has no clause for them.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security): pass with notes. The Antigravity protobuf string extraction (D8) is not crypto. The `<dir>` form and `--title` are unrequested surface. No new dependency, unless question 1 resolves to one.
6. Decoupling: pass with a note. The exported `harness.Redact` and `search.ListProjects` seams are clean. The timer's reach into `Uninstall` couples `internal/harness` to `internal/dream`; decide which package owns timer removal.

## Not examined
- `agents/dreamer.md` and `skills/dream/SKILL.md`: not read line by line; the plan's cited lines were taken from the recon.
- `skills/distill:38`.
- `internal/search/{search,store}.go` bodies: `tryOpen`'s behaviour on a schema mismatch, relevant to `ListProjects` and "missing db → empty".
- `main.go` status at :508.
- `testing/skill-matrix.md` and `testing/sh-agent-matrix.md`.
- agy's built-in slash-command list.
- Whether `autoMemoryEnabled` is a real Claude Code setting key: not checked against the Claude docs, and still unverified in the plan too.
- macOS launchd behaviour: not tested, since this is a Linux box.

# Preflight — v1.13.0   (2026-09-30)

Range reviewed: v1.12.1..c63f736

Release request: the operator, 2026-09-29, in their own turn: "Cut new version update docs. This is dod", and the version "v1.13.0 (Recommended)". A MINOR release: new verbs (`sh-agent search`, `sh-agent index`), one dependency, nothing an existing place must react to.

## Findings, worst first

None blocking. Every finding below was fixed before the tag or accepted by the operator, with its Outcome in the report it came from.

| Severity / confidence | Finding | Where | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| low / high | a work-tree rename misparsed; a path outside the checkout indexed | gate security, finding 1 (`reviews/2026-09-29-security-v1.12.1-c872598.md`) | fixed at 505732d (`--no-renames`, BUG-108), test failed first |
| low / high | a skip-worktree file under a symlinked directory read outside the checkout | security check of the fixes, finding 2 (`reviews/2026-09-30-security-c872598-505732d.md`) | fixed at de1a88f (every read through an `os.Root`), test failed first; the check of that fix found no other way out |
| low / high | a `search.db` copied in with a project directory is trusted | gate security, finding 2 | left: operator — "Document the limit (Recommended)"; spec § Failure modes |
| low / high | GO-2026-4970 on `os.Root.Open` for a Go before 1.25.12 | security check of fix 2 (`reviews/2026-09-30-security-505732d-de1a88f.md`) | left: not exploitable (an `Lstat` of the same path precedes every open); the two known advisories named in `AGENTS.md` and README at c63f736 |
| low / high | the symlink test could not fail on its write-through check; an `O_EXCL` comment overpromised | gate code review (`reviews/2026-09-29-review-f41e5c0-c872598-code.md`) | fixed at 505732d |
| low / high | the read-through test covered one trigger shape | security check of fix 2, finding 2 | fixed at c63f736 (both shapes) |
| low / medium | the `gitView` root has no test of its own | security check of fix 2, finding 3 | left: git lists a modified or untracked file only where the path is a regular file, so no fixture reaches that read; recorded, not hidden |
| medium / high (docs, advisory) | two closed bug records' bodies still say "not fixed" | gate docs lens (`reviews/2026-09-29-review-v1.12.1-c872598-docs.md`) | rebutted: a record's body is history, its status the one later edit; the lens's brief excludes bug records |

## Rows

- **Reviewer** (`model: opus` on the gate dispatch): `reviews/2026-09-29-review-search-index-code.md` (c04f2d7..565bb1e, APPROVE), `-code-r2.md` (565bb1e..aae16af, APPROVE with Outcome), `reviews/2026-09-29-review-aae16af-f41e5c0-code.md` (APPROVE), `reviews/2026-09-29-review-f41e5c0-c872598-code.md` (APPROVE WITH NITS, fixed). v1.12.1..c04f2d7 is text only (R4, ADR-045, three doc lines), read by the docs lens `reviews/2026-09-29-review-8ee5d70-HEAD-docs.md`. c872598..c63f736 (the three gate-fix commits: 100 lines of Go and tests, two doc lines) is under the reviewer threshold and was read by the main agent and by the two security checks named below.
- **Security**: `reviews/2026-09-29-security-v1.12.1-c872598.md` read all 94 paths of the release diff, nothing under Not examined; `reviews/2026-09-30-security-c872598-505732d.md` and `reviews/2026-09-30-security-505732d-de1a88f.md` read the gate-fix diffs end to end. de1a88f..c63f736 (a test widened, `configView` back on the plain reads the first report read, two doc lines) had no security dispatch: it reverts to code that report covered.
- **Verification**: `testing/2026-09-30-verify-v1.13.0-gate-r4.md`, PASS at c63f736 (366 pass with subtests, 0 fail, 2 skips with reasons; three cross-builds and the Go 1.24.4 build; embed and context tests; govulncheck); the earlier gate logs at c872598, 505732d and de1a88f PASS.
- **Docs freshness** (Step 4): `reviews/2026-09-29-review-v1.12.1-c872598-docs.md` APPROVE WITH NITS, the nits rebutted above; the earlier docs lenses over the range fixed three nits (ADR-045a) and found nothing else.
- **Trail freshness**: pass — the newest `changes/` entry (`2026-09-30-0505-v1.13.0-gate-fixes.md`) describes the release's last work; no future `date:`; `changes/` gained eight additions and no modification; `DECISIONS.md` gained ADR-045 and ADR-045a and the status marks on ADR-002 and ADR-029, the one edit a past ADR allows; `ROADMAP.md` and `TODO.md` were touched four times since the base and are empty.
- **The project's own blocking condition** (`AGENTS.md` § Release: one Antigravity run of each changed skill and agent): `testing/2026-09-29-search-agy-gate.md` (10 of 10 scenarios), `testing/2026-09-29-preflight-verdict-last-behavioural.md` (the preflight skill, one Antigravity run), `testing/2026-09-29-search-index-behavioural.md` (`reviewer`, `explorer`, `documentation`, `bugs`, `changelog` on Antigravity). The gate-fix commits changed no skill, agent or context. Real-home smoke on both CLIs: `testing/2026-09-29-verify-real-home-search.md`, PASS.

## What was not checked

- The Mac and the devbox: installed after the release by the operator's `sh-agent update` there; `linux/arm64` and `darwin/arm64` binaries were built, not run.
- Interactive sessions on either CLI; every behavioural run was headless.
- Antigravity's `$(…)` auto-denial in headless mode with narrow grants: two skills ran there with the per-run skip flag inside the sandbox; from the real home the limit does not apply.
- A release range in which the old preflight text would have written SHIP against its own unchecked items; the new rule's ordering effect was measured, its verdict effect was not distinguishable on the fixtures.
- `gitView`'s root read (finding above), unreachable by a fixture.
- Efficiency over days of work in one project; the measured runs are single sessions and three-session lanes.

Every item above was read against the blocking conditions: a verifier FAIL, BLOCKED or IN PROGRESS log (none: r4 is PASS); a high security finding (none); a missing security report, or one naming a release-diff path under Not examined (none); a reviewer REQUEST CHANGES or high finding (none); a `REQUIREMENTS.md` violation (none: R4 as amended, R7, R8 hold); a project agent shadowing a review agent (none); the project's Antigravity-run rule (met for every changed skill and agent, the preflight skill included). None of the unchecked items is named by a blocking condition.

VERDICT: SHIP

title: Review — cb799ff-f1ca525-code (2026-09-30)
body:
# Review — cb799ff-f1ca525-code   (2026-09-30)

Range reviewed: cb799ff..f1ca525 (source part: `git diff cb799ff..f1ca525 -- cmd internal skills agents context`; go.mod/go.sum unchanged)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The worst problem: with the Antigravity vendor on Linux, `sh-agent dream` passes the whole prompt (cap 256 KiB) to `agy` as one argv element. Linux refuses any single argument over 128 KiB (MAX_ARG_STRLEN = 32 pages), so every project whose prompt is over that size fails with E2BIG. Its watermark never advances, so the next night's window is larger and it fails again, permanently. Also: failures before the first project exit 1, not 2, and leave nothing in `status`. An unreadable state file silently resets every watermark. Both lock files have staleness races: the memory one can drop an index line, and the dream one can leave the job wedged. `go vet` and `go test ./internal/memory ./internal/dream ./internal/search` are green, but no test covers any of these paths.

## Findings

- **[high / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/run.go:137-142` (with `dream.go:23`, `dream.go:163`): for `agy`, the prompt replaces `<prompt>` in argv. `maxPrompt` is 256 KiB. Linux caps a single execve argument at 131072 bytes (checked on this host: `/bin/true "$(head -c 200000 …)"` → "Argument list too long", exit 126; PAGE_SIZE 4096). So `exec` fails for any agy prompt over 128 KiB and the project is logged `fail`. Its watermark stays (run.go:99-104), the next run collects a larger window, and that fails too. The project is never dreamt again on Linux + antigravity, which is a supported operator setup (macOS has no per-argument limit). A second effect: argv is world-readable through `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` for up to 10 minutes, so the redacted memory and transcripts are visible to other local users. `TestRunAgyGetsThePromptAsArgument` uses a small prompt and cannot catch this. Fix: use a per-vendor cap under 128 KiB for agy (or pass the prompt through stdin or a file if agy supports it), plus a test with a prompt over 128 KiB and a fake agy.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/dream.go:63-66` and `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:212-219`: the plan (Interfaces, "Exit") says a pre-project failure exits 2 and writes the run log line and `last_run.error`. Errors from `targets()` are returned as plain errors instead: `ListProjects` failing on an unreadable or corrupt global index, a `--project` that is not a checkout, and `--all` together with `--project`. `main` exits 1 on these, and nothing reaches `dream.log` or `dream-state.json`. So when the nightly timer hits a broken index, it exits 1 and `sh-agent status` keeps showing the previous successful run. Fix: wrap `targets()` errors as `&ExitError{2,…}`. After the lock is taken, record them through `finish` (or record them before the lock for the usage cases), and add a test.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/state.go:28-37` and `run.go:117-118, 329-333`: plan line 45 counts "state unreadable" as a pre-project failure (exit 2, `last_run.error`). `readState` instead treats a corrupt or unreadable `dream-state.json` as a first run. Every project's watermark silently drops to t0−14 days, which re-sends and re-proposes two weeks of input and duplicates proposals (`-2` files). The next `saveState` then overwrites the old watermarks for good. `TestReadStateFallback` (collect_test.go:337) pins this contradicting behaviour. Separately, `saveState` throws away its write error. If the state cannot be written, the run still exits 0 while the watermark is not persisted, breaking the "advance only after the write" rule. Fix: distinguish ENOENT (first run) from other errors (exit 2), return the `saveState` error and count it as a project failure, and change the test.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/memory/memory.go:246-283`: the comment at line 133 claims "two writers never lose a line", but the lock does not guarantee it. (a) A lock file exists but is still empty between `OpenFile(O_EXCL)` and `Fprint(pid)`. A concurrent `stale()` reads "", `Atoi` fails, so the lock counts as stale and gets removed while its owner proceeds. (b) Two waiters that both judge a dead lock stale: B removes it and creates its own, then C's `os.Remove` deletes B's fresh lock and C creates one too. (c) `unlock` removes the path unconditionally, so it can delete another holder's lock. In each case two `memory add` calls (for example two sessions, or `feedback-log` plus `project-memory`) read and modify MEMORY.md concurrently, and one index line is lost while its memory file stays on disk unindexed. No test runs concurrent adds. Fix: write the pid through a temp file plus `os.Link` (atomic create-with-content), or treat an unreadable pid as live until `lockAge`. Before removing a stale lock, re-read it and compare, and make unlock remove only a file that still holds our pid. Add a concurrent-add test that fails without the fix.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `internal/dream/run.go:337-356`: the dream lock has no age bound, and `harness.Alive` counts EPERM as alive. A `dream.lock` left by a crashed or killed run (OOM, reboot mid-run) can hold a pid that a later process reuses, which is likely after a reboot. From then on every nightly run prints "already running" and exits 0, so the job has stopped with no error in the log, `last_run` or `status`. The same empty-file window as the memory lock (an empty file reads as stale) lets a timer run and a manual run both proceed, racing `saveState` with whole-map writes. Fix: add an age bound as `memory.lock` has (the maximum run length follows from the 10-minute CLI timeout × projects, or record the start time in the lock), apply the same atomic pid write, and report a held lock older than the bound.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `internal/dream/collect.go:82-85` and `run.go:117`: an error from `AgyConversationText` (for example the copy of `conversation_summaries.db` plus `-wal` being inconsistent because Antigravity checkpointed between the two copies at search/dream.go:246-253, or one conversation db failing to open) only goes to `Dropped`. The project continues, and on success its watermark advances past every Antigravity conversation of that window, so they are lost for good after a transient error. Plan line 163 advances the watermark only after success. A transcript that could not be read is not the cap's deliberate drop. `sessionText` also ignores `sc.Err()` (collect.go:306-331), so a line over 16 MB silently truncates the session with the same effect. Fix: fail the project (watermark kept) on a collection error that is not a trust refusal, and check `sc.Err()`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:199-208`: `sh-agent dream --install-timer --dry-run` installs and enables the timer, and `--remove-timer --dry-run` removes it. `--dry-run` is parsed for every command and its help says "change nothing". `uninstall --dry-run` respects it for the same timer, but these branches ignore it. This breaks the global rule that a new side effect goes below the read-only mode's early return. Fix: have both branches print what they would do under `*dryRun`, with a test that asserts no unit file is written.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/memory/memory.go:148-155`: an index line is matched by the substring `(slug.md)`. If another entry's description contains `(slug.md)` (for example "supersedes (old-name.md)"), that line is overwritten too, so the other memory loses its index line and the index holds two copies of the new one. Fix: match the line prefix `- [slug](slug.md)`.

## Criteria
1. Dead code: pass. `harness.alive` was exported as `Alive` and all callers were updated. No leftover debug output or commented-out blocks. `memory.Store` is a thin wrapper around `trusted`, but it has a real caller (collect.go:50).
2. Flow tracing: fail. Findings 1-6. The `dream` exit-code path and the state read/write path do not match the plan. Both lock protocols have races. The collection error path advances the watermark. The `--dry-run` of `dream` itself does not write the dream state, lock or proposals (ListProjects and AgyConversationText create temp dirs under `~/.config/sh-agent` and remove them, and `TestDryRunWritesNothing` covers that). Slug and draft names are checked by an anchored Go regexp before any path is built (memory.go:105, run.go:196), and the model's `file` field is never used as a path. Deleting a failure only removes regular files, older than 30 days, from `dream-failed/`.
3. Standards conformance: fail on finding 7 (global read-only-mode rule) and on the comment at memory.go:133, which claims a guarantee the lock does not give (describing-text rule). The spec and plan rows for "state unreadable" and pre-project exit 2 are not implemented (findings 2 and 3). Restatements of the memory store in context/AGENTS.md, agents/dreamer.md and skills/project-memory agree with the code.
4. Directory layout: pass. `internal/memory`, `internal/dream`, the sqlite reads kept in `internal/search/dream.go` (the driver's package, ADR-047a), and tests sit beside their code.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security): pass. No new dependency (go.mod unchanged), and no auth or crypto code. Redaction reuses `harness.Redact`.
6. Decoupling: pass. `dream` consumes `memory.Root`/`memory.Store` and `search.ListProjects`/`AgyConversationText` through small exported functions. The two lock implementations are near-copies with the same defects. Merging them is not required, but a fix must be applied to both.

## Not examined
- Test files were read only in part: the lock, state and memory-verb tests and the test names. `internal/harness/report_test.go` (212 lines changed), `internal/search/dream_test.go`, `internal/dream/timer_test.go` and most of `run_test.go`/`collect_test.go` were not read line by line.
- Text changes in `skills/{distill,dream,feedback-log,init-project,retro}/SKILL.md` were not read. The docs lens is a separate report (`…-docs.md`).
- `harness.redactLines` itself (only the new `Redact` wrapper was read); `harness.WriteAtomic`'s fsync behaviour.
- `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`'s `status` path beyond the added dream line; `resolveVendor` when no manifest exists.
- Real `systemctl --user` / `launchctl` behaviour, and systemd specifier expansion of `%` in the captured PATH (not tested).

## Outcome
1. high, agy prompt on argv (128 KiB): fixed. agy gets the prompt on stdin as one stream-json message (`agy --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --mode plan -p ""`), and the answer is read from the `result` event. Probed on this box; `TestRunAgyPrivateHomeAndStdin` asserts the argv carries no prompt.
2. medium, pre-project errors exit 1 with no record: fixed. Usage errors are refused in `Run` before anything is written. Every other pre-project failure (index, no CLI, no login) is exit 2, with a run log line and `last_run.error`: `TestRunPreProjectFailureIsExit2AndRecorded`, `TestDreamVerb`.
3. medium, a corrupt state silently reset: fixed. `readState` returns an error; the run exits 2 and leaves the file untouched (`TestReadState`, `TestRunCorruptStateIsExit2AndKept`). `saveState` errors are exit 2 at the end of the run.
4. medium, memory lock races: fixed. `flock` on `.agents/memory/.lock`: the kernel drops it on exit, and two waiters cannot both hold it (`TestLeftoverLockFileIsNoLock`, `TestHeldLockRefusesAfterRetry`).
5. medium, dream lock with no age bound and a reused pid: fixed. `flock` on `dream.lock`: a dead run's lock is released by the kernel (`TestRunLock` holds a real flock, then releases it).
6. medium, an Antigravity read error advanced the watermark: fixed. It fails the project, so the watermark stays. A Claude Code transcript read error is named as left out.
7. low, `--dry-run` ignored with the timer flags: fixed (`TestDreamTimerDryRun`).
8. low, the index matched a description's `(slug.md)`: fixed. The match is the line's link target (`TestIndexMatchIsTheLinkTarget`). A full index is now refused before the lock file is created, so the refusal still writes nothing.

title: Review — e2cffc1-a275b96-code (2026-09-30)
body:
# Review — e2cffc1-a275b96-code   (2026-09-30)

Range reviewed: e2cffc1..a275b96 (source: `git diff e2cffc1..a275b96 -- internal/`; the round-2 Outcomes of `reviews/2026-09-30-review-f1ca525-e2cffc1-code.md` and `reviews/2026-09-30-security-f1ca525-e2cffc1.md`, checked against code and tests)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The worst problem: the security round-2 medium fix, "a reply's tool-call arguments are dropped", does not hold on real data. The filter drops a run only when it starts with `{"`. In a real protobuf payload, the byte right before a length-delimited string is its varint length, and for many lengths that byte is itself printable. `textRun` then joins it to the front of the run, so the run starts with, for example, `` `{"`` and passes the filter. I confirmed this on the probe copies already in `.agents/scratch/`, which include the gate18 conversation the Outcome cites. The test fixture cannot catch it, because it writes a fixed non-text length prefix whatever the payload's length. The other round-2 Outcome claims hold. There is one stale spec row.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/search/dream.go:240` (`strings.HasPrefix(s, `{"`)`), with `textRun` at `:92`: Antigravity tool-call arguments still reach the other vendor's model.
  - **Mechanism.** A protobuf string field is `tag, varint length, bytes`. `textRun`'s first character class is `[\x20-\x7e\xc2-\xf4]`, and its later classes also admit `\x80-\xbf`. Two length ranges put a printable byte in front of `{"`:
    - 33 to 126 bytes: the one-byte varint length is printable ASCII. A length of 32 is a space, which `TrimSpace` removes.
    - 4096 to 16383 bytes: the second varint byte is `0x20`-`0x7e`. A first byte of `0xc2`-`0xf4` can even start the run, and `ToValidUTF8` then deletes it, leaving one printable character in front.

    The run then begins `<char>{"…`, fails the prefix check, and is sent whenever it has 3 or more spaces. That covers short shell commands (`CommandLine`) and whole written files of 4 to 16 KB (`CodeContent`), which are exactly what the finding was about.
  - **Evidence.** I ran a read-only scan (`mode=ro&immutable=1`, metadata only printed) with the same regex and filter over step types 14 and 15 of the conversation copies under `.agents/scratch/**/conversations/`:
    - `gate18-agy/…/15776d24….db`: a run starting `0x7e 0x7b 0x22` (`~{"`, a length of 126) holds `{"AbsolutePath":…`, a view_file argument. It is kept.
    - `agysmoke/…/e85bf990….db`: this is the database with "32 dropped", matching the Outcome's count. A run starting `` 0x60 `` (a length of 96) holds `{"Action":"list"…`. It is kept, and is counted among the Outcome's "21 prose runs".
  - **Test.** The fixture `blob()` (`internal/search/dream_test.go:119-126`) always writes `0x0a 0x8f 0x01` before each part. The byte `0x01` is non-text, so every fixture run starts cleanly at `{"`. This is not the arrangement a real payload has, so `TestAgyConversationText` passes with the leak present.
  - **Describing text now overclaims.** `specs/sh-agent/dream.md:39` says "a reply's tool-call arguments … are dropped". Plan D29 (`plans/2026-09-30-parity-memory-dream.md:342`) records the operator's "keep both, filtered" choice, and names the residual risk as only "an unknown field type". That choice was made on the premise that this filter works.
  - **Fix.**
    - Make `blob()` write the part's real varint length, and add a 33-126-byte argument case and a 4096-16383-byte argument case. Both must fail against the current code.
    - Then either drop a run whose `{"` appears within its first 2 characters after trimming, or, cleaner, walk the protobuf wire format (tag, varint and length are stdlib-simple) so that each string field is taken whole and its prefix is exact.
    - Correct spec :39 in the same change, and put the D29 premise back to the operator.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/specs/sh-agent/dream.md:60`: the table row still says a killed run's copies are removed as "any leftover … at the start of the next". Since this range, `removeCopies` (`internal/dream/run.go:301-314`) removes only copies older than an hour.
  - Round-1 code finding 3 asked for the spec row to be corrected along with the comment. The comment was fixed; the row was not.
  - Fix: state the one-hour bound, and why (a dry run takes no lock), in that row.

### Round-2 Outcome claims checked against code and tests
Code review (f1ca525..e2cffc1) Outcome:
1. Antigravity read error test: **holds.**
   - `TestRunAgyReadErrorKeepsWatermark` feeds a garbage `conversation_summaries.db`. Putting back the `Dropped` append would give exit 0 and an advanced watermark, so the test can fail.
   - `TestCollectNamesAnUnreadableTranscript`: `bufio.Scanner`'s limit is max(80 KiB, 64 KiB cap), so a 100 KiB line gives `ErrTooLong` as the test claims.
2. State-write failure: **holds.** `writeState` is the only write path used by `saveState`. The test asserts exit 2 and "could not be saved".
3. Cleanup spares a live dry run: **holds in code.** `removeCopies` has one call site (`run.go:85`, under the lock). The dry run never calls it, and no copy outlives `cliTimeout` (10 min), far below the hour. The spec row is stale (finding 2).
4. Unreachable `targets()` branches: **holds.** They are removed. `Run` refuses both and neither before `realRun` or `targets` (`dream.go:63-68`), and `TestRunUsage` asserts exit 2 with nothing written.
5. Step types 14/15 source: **holds.** Plan D8b records it.
6. `.agents` link: **holds.** `linked` now `Lstat`s each component. `TestCollectDoesNotFollowALinkedAgentsDir` would fail under the old two-path check, because `Lstat(root/.agents/docs)` resolves the intermediate link. Files are also `Lstat`ed (`mdFiles`, `readFile`).
7. `--setting-sources local`: left and documented at `specs/sh-agent/dream.md:37`. Accepted.

Security review (f1ca525..e2cffc1) Outcome:
1. Tool-call arguments dropped: **does not hold** (finding 1).
2. `.agents` link: **holds** (as code item 6 above).
3. Remaining gaps:
   - Absolute-only PATH: **holds.** `TestInstallTimerKeepsOnlyAbsolutePath` fails without `absolutePath`.
   - SUCCESS required: **holds.** The real stream outputs in `.agents/scratch/sj-*.out` carry `"status":"SUCCESS"` and `"status":"ERROR"`, and the fake at `run_test.go:143` emits SUCCESS.
   - Explicit `toolPermission`: **present in code.** The sandbox claim was not re-run.

## Criteria
1. Dead code: **pass.** The dead `targets()` branches and the test lines that pinned them are gone, and the `errors` import was removed with them. `transcriptLineMax` and `writeState` are test seams with callers.
2. Flow tracing: **fail** (finding 1).
   - The rest traces cleanly. The usage refusal happens before the lock. The read-error path is collect → `fmt.Errorf` → project failure with the watermark kept. The state-write error becomes exit 2. `removeCopies` ignores an `Info()` error, which keeps the data.
   - The package-level test seams are safe, because no test in `internal/dream` uses `t.Parallel`.
3. Standards conformance: **fail** (low).
   - `specs/sh-agent/dream.md:39` restates a guarantee the code does not give (finding 1), and `:60` is stale (finding 2).
   - `removeCopies`' comment is now accurate.
4. Directory layout: **pass.** Changes stay in `internal/dream` and `internal/search`, with the tests beside the code.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security): **pass.** There is no new dependency, and no auth or crypto code. Walking the protobuf wire format for finding 1 is stdlib byte parsing, not a security primitive.
6. Decoupling: **pass.** `search` still owns the sqlite reads, and `dream` owns the run, the lock and the state.

## Not examined
- I did not run `go test`, `go vet`, or any mutation. The claims that mutations were "restored byte-identical" were judged only by reasoning about whether each test can fail, not by re-running them.
- The real `agy` runtime with the explicit `toolPermission: request-review` (the security Outcome's sandbox run), `claude` under the new flags, and macOS launchd.
- Protobuf field layouts beyond the 30 conversation copies in `.agents/scratch/`. Only step types 14 and 15 were scanned. JSON found deep inside long prose runs (for example `{"autoMemoryDire…` at offset 11582, and the dream's own `{"proposals"…` answers) was not classified.
- The trail files in the range: BUG-116..122, the INDEX rows, the change entry, and both verifier logs. The plan diff was read only at D8b and D29, and the spec only in the rows cited.

## Outcome
1. medium, the JSON-argument filter did not hold on real data: fixed. The scan is replaced by a protobuf wire-format decoder (plan D30); see `reviews/2026-09-30-security-e2cffc1-a275b96.md` § Outcome 1 for the tests and the 95-database measurement. The fixture's `blob()` now writes real framing.
2. low, the spec row on leftover copies: fixed (only copies older than an hour; a dry run takes no lock).

title: Review — f1ca525-e2cffc1-code (2026-09-30)
body:
# Review — f1ca525-e2cffc1-code   (2026-09-30)

Range reviewed: f1ca525..e2cffc1 (round 2: the fixes for round 1's code review, plus the security and docs round-1 fixes in the same commit; source part `git diff f1ca525..e2cffc1 -- cmd internal`)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The code changes for all eight round-1 findings are correct as written, and I found no new high-severity defect. `go vet ./...` is clean, and `go test ./internal/dream ./internal/memory ./internal/search ./cmd/sh-agent` passes on this box. The blocking gap is test coverage, because under the project's Definition of Done a finding counts as fixed only when a test fails without the fix. Two Outcome claims have no such test:
- Round-1 finding 6: an Antigravity read error now fails the project and keeps its watermark, but no test drives that path.
- Round-1 finding 3, second half: a `saveState` failure now gives exit 2, but no test drives that path.

Reverting either fix leaves every test green. The other findings below are low: a false "under the lock" claim that lets a real run delete a concurrent dry run's copies, two targets() branches now unreachable, an unrecorded source for the step-type mapping, a symlink check that misses `.agents` itself, and a possible auth loss from `--setting-sources local`.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/collect.go:94-97`, and `collect.go:86-90` with `:361`: round-1 finding 6 is fixed in code but has no test.
  - No test in `internal/dream` creates an Antigravity database: a grep for `conversation_summaries` in `internal/dream/*_test.go` finds nothing, and the Outcome line names no test.
  - So putting back the old `c.Dropped = append(...)` at line 96 leaves every test green, and the watermark-advance defect could come back unnoticed.
  - The new `sessionText` → `sc.Err()` → `Dropped` path (a transcript line over 16 MB) is untested as well.
  - Fix: add a Run-level test with a corrupt `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversation_summaries.db` in the fixture HOME. Assert exit 1, `st.Projects[root].IsZero()`, and a `fail reading Antigravity's conversations` log line. Add a collect test with an over-long transcript line that asserts the `claude transcript …` Dropped entry.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/run.go:146-157`: Outcome 3 says "`saveState` errors are exit 2 at the end of the run", but no test makes the state write fail.
  - Changing the `stateErr` handling back to ignoring the error passes the whole suite.
  - Fix: add a test where the state write fails after the lock is taken. For example, pre-create `dream.lock`, `dream.log` and `dream-work`, then make `~/.config/sh-agent` 0o500 so that `WriteAtomic`'s temp file cannot be created.
  - Assert exit 2 with "watermarks could not be saved", and assert that the project's proposals were still written.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/run.go:295-297` (`removeCopies`): the comment says "It runs under the lock, so no live run owns them". That is false for `sh-agent dream --dry-run`.
  - The dry run takes no lock, yet it creates `dream-projects-*` (`internal/search/dream.go:55`) and `dream-agy-*` (`internal/search/dream.go:109`) in the same directory.
  - A real run (the timer, or a second shell) that starts during a dry run deletes those live copies, and the dry run then fails with a read error.
  - Fix: only remove directories older than a bound (for example `cliTimeout`, since no copy outlives a run), or have the dry run take the lock too. Also correct the comment and the spec row at `specs/sh-agent/dream.md:51`, which repeats "under the lock".
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/dream.go:87-88` and `:102`: the `--all`-with-`--project` branch and the usage branch of `targets()` are now unreachable.
  - `Run` refuses both cases at `dream.go:64-68` before any caller reaches `targets()`.
  - `collect_test.go:227-229` pins the dead "not both" branch.
  - The dead usage text has also drifted from the live one: it lacks `--install-timer | --remove-timer`.
  - Fix: delete both branches and the test lines. `targets()` then only handles `o.Project` and `o.All`.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/search/dream.go:221-223`: the comment attributes step types 14 and 15 to "the D8 probe", but D8a (`plans/2026-09-30-parity-memory-dream.md:296`) records no step types and no `step_type` column. The mapping has no recorded source anywhere in the trail I read.
  - The test fixture (`internal/search/dream_test.go:98-111`) encodes the same assumption, so it cannot catch a wrong mapping. The verifier's mutation (a) only proves that the filter exists.
  - Failure mode if the mapping is wrong: every Antigravity transcript comes back empty and silently, with no error. If a conversation database lacks the column, that project instead fails every night.
  - I could not check a real conversation database; the read was denied. See Not examined.
  - Fix: record the probe (the step-type counts from one real conversation) in D8a or in a testing log, and point the comment at that record.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/dream/collect.go:116-120` (`linked`): `os.Lstat` only tests the last path element. When the docs root is `.agents/docs`, a committed `.agents` symlink is followed.
  - For example, `.agents -> ../other/.agents` sends another checkout's trail to the model under this project's name.
  - `memory.Store` refuses exactly this shape for the store, so the two readers disagree.
  - Fix: also `Lstat` each element of `docs` (here `root/.agents`), and extend `TestCollectDoesNotFollowLinkedTrail` to cover it.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/dream/dream.go:181`: `--setting-sources local` skips `~/.claude/settings.json`, including its `env` block and any `apiKeyHelper`.
  - An operator whose Vertex/Bedrock switch or key helper lives there would get an auth failure on every project, every night (exit 1).
  - The probe ran on a box where authentication comes from elsewhere.
  - Fix: confirm which settings the dream call needs. If user-level auth settings matter, state the limitation in `specs/sh-agent/dream.md`, or pass the auth environment explicitly.

### Round-1 Outcome lines checked against code and tests
1. agy prompt on stdin: **holds**. `command()` has no prompt in argv, and `call()` writes one `{"event":"user",…}` line. `TestRunAgyPrivateHomeAndStdin` asserts that argv lacks the prompt and that stdin decodes. The real agy probe was not re-run.
2. Pre-project exit 2 and record: **holds**. Usage is refused before the lock (`TestDreamVerb` asserts that nothing is written). Index failures go through `fail()` (`TestRunPreProjectFailureIsExit2AndRecorded`). An unreadable state logs a line and deliberately leaves the state unwritten; `StatusLine` reports it.
3. Corrupt state: **holds for `readState`** (`TestReadState`, `TestRunCorruptStateIsExit2AndKept`). **Untested for `saveState`** (finding 2).
4. Memory lock: **holds**. flock on a separate descriptor per call. `TestHeldLockRefusesAfterRetry` holds a flock on an empty file, which the old pid-file code would have judged stale, so that test fails without the fix. There is no concurrent-writer test, but flock semantics rule out the three races structurally.
5. Dream lock: **holds**. `TestRunLock` holds a real flock on an empty file, which the old code also treated as stale.
6. Antigravity read error: **code holds, untested** (finding 1). Claude Code transcript errors deliberately go to "left out" while the watermark advances. I accept that as stated, because a deterministic `ErrTooLong` would otherwise wedge the project for good, which was round 1's argv failure shape.
7. Timer flags with `--dry-run`: **holds**. `TestDreamTimerDryRun` fails without the fix, because `InstallTimer` returns an error when no binary is present and the remove path never prints "[dry-run] would".
8. Index link-target match: **holds** (`TestIndexMatchIsTheLinkTarget`). The pre-lock full-index refusal is re-checked under the lock.

## Criteria
1. Dead code: **fail** (low). The `targets()` branches at dream.go:87-88 and :102 are unreachable, and collect_test.go:227-229 pins one of them. The memory `lockAge`/`stale` code, the `strconv` import and `harness.Alive` in the lock paths were removed cleanly.
2. Flow tracing: **fail** on coverage (findings 1 and 2). Otherwise the paths traced cleanly:
   - The order lock → readState → finish/fail → saveState is consistent. The error paths return ExitError 2 or 1 as the spec table says, and `fail()` ignores a second saveState error only on a path that already exits 2.
   - `answer()` treats `denied_actions` as no answer, which becomes a failure plus a kept watermark (`TestRunAgyDeniedToolIsNoAnswer`).
   - The private HOME is removed by `defer cleanup()` on every path after it is created, and leftovers are removed at the next start (but see finding 3).
   - `call()` sets `cmd.Env = nil` for claude, so claude inherits the environment.
3. Standards conformance: **fail** (low). The `removeCopies` comment and `specs/sh-agent/dream.md:51` claim "under the lock" (finding 3). The step-type comment cites a probe that does not record the mapping (finding 5). Also, `specs/sh-agent/dream.md:24` still says "the child keeping sh-agent's own environment", while line 26 gives agy a private HOME; that one is for the docs lens. gofmt/vet are clean.
4. Directory layout: **pass**. Nothing new is outside `internal/dream`, `internal/memory`, `internal/search` and `cmd/sh-agent`, and the tests sit beside their code.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security): **pass**. There is no new dependency, and `syscall.Flock` is the stdlib lock. No auth or crypto code is written here: copying the operator's OAuth token file into a private HOME only consumes the CLI's own login and implements no protocol. `GOOS=windows go build` now fails on `syscall.Flock` in `internal/memory`, but Windows is not a release target (`release_test.go:488` expects no windows asset), so this is not a finding.
6. Decoupling: **pass**. `search` owns the sqlite reads, and `dream` owns the CLI call, the lock and the state. The two flock helpers are small near-copies. That is acceptable at this size, but a future change to one must be applied to the other.

## Not examined
- The real Antigravity conversation schema (the `step_type` column and its values). The read-only query against `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/*.db` was denied by the permission classifier, so finding 5 stays at low confidence.
- The real `agy` stream-json exchange and the real `claude --setting-sources local` behaviour. I did not re-run either CLI; the Outcome and BUG-119 claim probes on this box.
- The docs, spec, README and skill text changes in the range (`.agents/docs/**`, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `skills/{init-project,project-memory,retro}/SKILL.md`). That is the docs lens's job, and I read only the spec rows cited above.
- `internal/dream/timer.go`'s `%%` escaping on a real systemd, and the macOS launchd path, which does not use the `%` rule. Only the unit test was read.
- Whether Antigravity's OAuth token is file-based on macOS. `agyHome` requires the file, and if the Mac keeps the login elsewhere, every Mac agy run fails with exit 2 "no Antigravity login".

## Outcome
1. medium, the Antigravity read-error fix had no test: fixed. `TestRunAgyReadErrorKeepsWatermark` sets up a garbage `conversation_summaries.db`; undoing the fix compiled and failed it, restored byte-identical. `TestCollectNamesAnUnreadableTranscript` covers `sessionText`'s error path. The limit is a variable, `transcriptLineMax`, and the scanner's own 64 KiB floor means the test line exceeds it.
2. medium, the state-write failure had no test: fixed. `writeState` is a variable, and `TestRunStateWriteFailureIsExit2` makes it fail; dropping the error compiled and failed the test, restored byte-identical.
3. low, the start-of-run cleanup could delete a live dry run's copies: fixed. Only copies older than an hour are removed (`TestRemoveCopiesKeepsFreshOnes`).
4. low, unreachable branches in `targets()`: fixed. Removed; `Run` refuses both and neither before anything is written (`TestRunUsage`).
5. low, the source of step types 14/15 was unrecorded: fixed (plan D8b, from two real conversation databases).
6. low, the symlink check missed `.agents` itself: fixed. Every component from the root down is checked (`TestCollectDoesNotFollowALinkedAgentsDir`).
7. low, `--setting-sources local` may lose settings-based auth: left, documented. The spec's Known limit names it; a CLI login works, and a machine using `apiKeyHelper` sees the failure logged per project.

title: Review — plan audit-fix, cold read (2026-09-30)
body:
# Review — plan audit-fix, cold read   (2026-09-30)

Range reviewed: `.agents/docs/plans/2026-09-30-audit-fix.md` (cold read, no diff), checked against the code and files it names.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The plan is not implementation ready. The worst problem is the C1 headline: the listed context moves cannot reach "render <= 14,000 bytes". They save about 4,600 bytes from 21,906, which gives about 17,300, and no further cut is named. Nearby, the plan contradicts itself on `/goal` and on the warn threshold, and several verify clauses cannot produce the condition they claim (tools not installed, a flag the code rejects, a grep that matches by design). Most of the remaining gaps are NON-BLOCKING.

## (1) Gaps

- **[high / high]** C1 arithmetic. `context/AGENTS.md` render is 21,906 bytes (`sh-agent render | wc -c`). The plan needs -7,906. The lines it names are 16 (1,400 B), 34 (1,156), 52 (941), 56 (796), 57 (567), 58 (687), 59-62 (1,356), and each is cut to a stated size. That sums to about -4,600, and the G11 paragraph adds back about 250. The Phase 3 verify ("render <= 14,000") will fail, and the implementer must pick further rules to drop, which is an operator-level choice. Fix: list the extra cuts, or set the target at about 17,500, or name which whole rules leave.
- **[high / high]** `/goal` contradiction. Interfaces (line 36), D17 and the `C15` note say keep `/goal`. The Phase 3 task (line 110) says "`/goal` dropped".
- **[medium / high]** Warn threshold stated three ways. Interfaces and Phase 3 say 15,000. Failure modes says 18,500. D2a says the 18,000 target is superseded. `TestRenderedContextTarget` "warns, not fails", so it cannot fail and its verify ("prints the byte count") verifies nothing. The test is extra scope with no one asking (D2: "implementer"). The `render | wc -c` check already covers it. Fix: drop the test, or pin one number.
- **[high / high]** Phase 6 verify `grep -rn 'python\|anti-ui-slop' context skills/*/SKILL.md README.md` expects "only the frontend Do-NOT line". It already matches `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:115` (python3, which D13 keeps and WS3 documents more) and `skills/gke-basics/SKILL.md:49` ("kubernetes python"). It cannot reach the expected result. Fix: anchor the grep to the skill names (`/python`, `skills/python`, `anti-ui-slop`).
- **[high / high]** `--kind spec,plan` (research skill, Phase 5 WS10). `internal/search/search.go:84-92` accepts exactly one kind and errors on a comma list. The plan either needs a code change and a docs row in `specs/sh-agent/search.md`, or should read `--kind spec` and a second call.
- **[medium / high]** AG12b / "the one skill over 600 today (cloud-run-deploy, 1,007)". Not true. Single-line descriptions of `skills/dream` (691), `skills/project-memory` (629) and `skills/review` (775) also exceed 600, measured on the first `description:` line. The Phase 4 verify "`sh-agent list` expect no note" then fails unless those are trimmed. Nothing in the plan trims them. There is also a consistency trap: `Lint` failing at > 1,024 makes `install` refuse any vendored skill that is over the limit, and vendored skills may not be edited in place (AGENTS.md § Rules). The plan does not measure the vendored ones.
- **[medium / high]** IN2 (Phase 1). "manifest saved after each successful write", expect "manifest lists 1..N-1". `apply.go:95-110` removes stale files before writes and only saves state once at line 140. A manifest of just the written files drops the old install's not-yet-rewritten files from the manifest while they remain on disk: orphans, the defect the task is meant to fix. The manifest after a failure should be (old entries still on disk) ∪ (written). `SaveState` per file is also O(n) rewrites; saving once in an error path would do. The expected result and the approach both need stating.
- **[medium / high]** Tools not installed. `terraform`, `tflint` and `gcloud` are MISSING on this machine (`command -v`). Phase 6 verifies `terraform validate` and `gcloud run deploy --help`, and the Risks section says gcloud flags are "checked by `gcloud run deploy --help`". Those cannot run. Fix: a step to fetch them into scratch, or say those rows are reported as unverified.
- **[medium / medium]** Antigravity `skills:` key (D5, AG5/AG15). Phase 4 says "the agy behavioural run below proves the skill loads", but no agy behavioural run exists below in Phase 4; only `claude -p --agents` runs and a sandbox start. Phase 9's matrix covers skills, not the derived agent key. D5's "drawn solid only after one agy behavioural run" has no task. The reviewer would also carry two mechanisms for one operation (the `skills:` key and the explicit `~/.claude/skills/review-standards/SKILL.md` read). Antigravity hangs on unrecognised agent keys (AGENTS.md § Rules, toolMap), so a wrong `skills:` path form is a hang risk; the sandbox-start task sits last in the phase. Fix: move it first and add the agy run row.
- **[medium / medium]** C1 moves rules an author follows into `review-standards` (lines 56-62, "a review checks and an author follows"). `review-standards` is loaded by reviewers only. The four Go-flavoured rules also go to `skills/golang`, but TypeScript, bash and docs authors get none. State where the author-side copy lives for non-Go work, or say it is deliberately review-side only.
- **[medium / medium]** The derive/Lint changes alter `install` behaviour (refusal over 1,024; a `note:` line in `list`; `LoadAgents` refusing descriptions), and Phase 1 changes exit codes and refusal output (IN11-IN13). No docs clause names `specs/sh-agent/*.md`, README, or `.agents/docs/testing/guide.md` for any of these. Phase 5 adds `/review --resume` and `distill --from-log/--global` with no docs clause either (Phase 7 does have README rows for new skills).
- **[low / medium]** Phase 4 verifier behavioural check "log carries 'Step 4' marker". Nothing in the plan says the new definition instructs the agent to write a step marker. Without it the run proves nothing (AGENTS.md § Testing: the artifact must carry something only the new definition writes). The same applies to the changelog check (the agent would have to name the SHA it was given; spelled out there, but not for the verifier).
- **[low / medium]** SD7 `VACUUM INTO` "on a read-only connection". The earlier design copies the DB files so the operator's live Antigravity DB is never opened. A read-only WAL connection may still create or touch `-shm`. The plan needs a statement that the live DB is not modified, and a fixture that proves it (`TestCopyDBWhileWriting` only checks the copy opens).
- **[low / medium]** IN8. The flock helper moves from `internal/dream/run.go:514` into `internal/harness`. `internal/harness` has a `!unix` stub file (`owned_other.go`), so a non-unix stub is needed. Lock path, blocking or not, and behaviour on contention are undecided. Release builds are only linux/darwin (remote.md:139), so this is low.
- **[low / medium]** Interfaces text left as thinking-out-loud: "`sh-agent memory init-settings <root>`? — NO", "a `.agents/rules/` line is not global; ... ? No: ..." (grilling, WS21). The final decision is recoverable but the content to write for the VENDORED note and the keep-list is unstated; the claimed "(D-row.)" for grilling does not exist (D13 covers init-project only).
- **[low / medium]** `TestSkillLinksResolve`: "See <Title>" pointer rule is undefined, and it walks `skills/**/*.md`, including vendored skills that cannot be edited. Say which dirs it skips.
- **[low / medium]** TR1 `restatement-grep.sh`: inputs, output format and "living files" list are unspecified; the installed path on Antigravity (`~/.gemini/config/skills/review/scripts/`) differs from Claude's and skill bodies are not rewritten by derive (only agent bodies are, `derive.go:25,63`). "`kit-preamble.sh` sourced by every kit in guide § 4": kits there are prose procedures, not scripts.
- **[low / low]** E2E (a)/(b): AGENTS.md § Testing says a CLI started from a scratch HOME cannot authenticate; (a) and (b) say "both CLIs start and answer" / run `/init-project` then `/spec` then `/feature` without saying the home (the sandbox procedure or the real home after Phase 9). E2E (c) "sandbox `dream --project`" runs with fake CLIs on PATH per guide § 3e; say so.
- **[low / low]** Re-audit "published as Styrman Harness Audit III", verified by "page URL in the changes entry": the mechanism ("the same way as the two before") and a fallback if the external service is unavailable are not stated.
- **[low / low]** "Grep -c 'Write the artifact EARLY' ... expect 5 identical blocks": the "one shared wording (13 lines)" is not in the plan, and `explorer.md` has none today; the AG9 sentence "security is pinned to pro" likewise has no text to copy. NON-BLOCKING; the implementer writes it.
- **[low / low]** AGENTS.md says deploying to the real home is the operator's job; D15 cites "You can update the local harness everything you need it" as the authority. One line in the plan saying this is a one-time exception (and does not amend the rule) would close it.

## (2) Scope — built beyond the request in `## Why`

The Why names: fix all findings, add features from the audit, phases, verified, a PRIORITY_TODO, re-audit. Covered by "add new features from your audit report": the seven new skills (D7), `--resume`. Not named and with no D-row naming who asked:
- `TestRenderedContextTarget` (warn-only test; D2 is "implementer") — see above; it cannot fail.
- Two thresholds (`Lint` fails > 1,024 AND `list` notes > 600) for the same property: a second shape for one check (D19 cites the format brief, not a request).
- Two mechanisms for the agent-to-skill link on Antigravity (`skills:` key AND a body read-path AND the Budget prose line), when the Budget prose line duplicates `maxTurns` that the dispatcher already names per the context.
- `explain-project`, `testing-strategy` and `operate-gcp` write to `docs/onboarding.md` etc.; fine as audit features, but `explain-project` (a human walkthrough) has no audit ID cited in the plan (D7 lists G1, G2, G5-G9 only).

## (3) Readiness — questions I would have to ask

1. BLOCKING. C1: which additional rules leave the always-loaded context to reach <= 14,000, given the listed moves reach about 17,300? Or is the target 17,500?
2. BLOCKING. `/goal`: kept (Interfaces, D17) or dropped (Phase 3)?
3. BLOCKING. IN2: what must the manifest list after a failure on file N (old entries on disk plus written), and is it saved per file or once in an error path?
4. BLOCKING. `--kind spec,plan`: change `search.go` to accept a list (then a test, a spec row, and a docs clause), or use one kind?
5. BLOCKING. Phase 6 python/anti-ui-slop grep: expected result is unreachable as written; what should it match?
6. BLOCKING. AG12b: trim `dream`, `project-memory`, `review` (and any vendored over 1,024) or raise the note threshold? What happens when a vendored skill is over 1,024?
7. BLOCKING. Where does the agy behavioural run for the derived `skills:` key live, and what is its pass criterion? What if the vendor key form is wrong (hang risk)?
8. NON-BLOCKING. Terraform, tflint and gcloud are missing: fetch to scratch or report unverified? (Plan default: verify clauses assume they exist.)
9. NON-BLOCKING. Warn threshold number (15,000 or 18,500) and whether the test stays.
10. NON-BLOCKING. SD7: does the live Antigravity DB get opened even read-only? IN8: lock path and contention behaviour. SD9 "a non-JSON string argument corpus test": what corpus?
11. NON-BLOCKING. Content for grilling's VENDORED note, the AG9 "security is pinned to pro" sentence, the early-write block, the verifier step marker.
12. NON-BLOCKING. `TestSkillLinksResolve` "See <Title>" rule and skipped dirs; `restatement-grep.sh` interface and Antigravity path.
13. NON-BLOCKING. Which home E2E (a)/(b) run in; docs clauses for exit codes, `list` note, `install` refusal, `--resume`, `--from-log`.
14. NON-BLOCKING. Re-audit publish mechanism and fallback.

## Criteria (applied to the plan as a design document)

1. Dead code — no dead code yet; the plan strikes `python`/`anti-ui-slop` and deletes dead pointers; `TestRenderedContextTarget` is a test that cannot fail.
2. Flow tracing — fail: IN2 manifest semantics, `skills:` derive chain has no agy run, lint/install refusal of vendored skills not traced.
3. Standards conformance — fail: docs clauses missing for changed commands/exit codes; `/goal` restated both ways; AGENTS.md real-home rule needs an explicit exception line.
4. Directory layout — pass: `skills/review/scripts/`, `assets/agents-tree/docs/specs/`, `.agents/docs/testing/kit-preamble.sh` are where conventions put them (Antigravity path for scripts to confirm).
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — mixed: stdlib flock reuse and no new dependency is right; duplicate mechanisms (two thresholds, `skills:` key plus read path plus Budget line) are the simplicity risk. `api-auth-gcp` names vetted libraries only (no hand-rolled crypto).
6. Decoupling — pass: Phases 1, 3-7 and 8 touch separate files; Phase 8 rewrites `main.go` after Phase 1 edits it (serialized, stated by order).

## Not examined

The recon brief and the five research briefs were read only where needed to check cited facts (not line by line); the research briefs' technical claims (Terraform, Cloud Run flags, Tailwind, Vitest versions) were not verified. The Graduated row count "46 rows" (TR1) was not reliably counted. `skills/**` vendored description lengths over 1,024 were not measured. The real content of G1-G13 and WS/AG IDs was not cross-checked against the recon brief beyond IN2, IN3, IN4, IN8, IN10, SD7 and C1.

title: Review — project-code (2026-09-30)
body:
# Review — project-code   (2026-09-30)

Range reviewed: the whole repository at HEAD (3478a1c), no diff.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE

Nothing broken found. This is a mature, heavily security-reviewed codebase:
almost every non-trivial function in `internal/harness` and `internal/search`
carries an inline comment citing the specific past review round, BUG-NNN, or
security-review finding that shaped it (path-escape guards, zip-slip guards,
redaction adversarial cases, git-redirect-env refusals, TOCTOU-safe renames,
os.Root-scoped reads). I read the highest-risk surfaces in full
(`report.go`'s redaction/push pipeline, `zip.go`'s unpack path, `pathguard.go`,
`internal/search/reconcile.go` and `search.go`, `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`,
`derive.go`, `adopt.go`) and found no regression of a recorded bug and no new
correctness or security defect. `gofmt -l cmd internal`, `go vet ./...`,
`go build ./...`, and `govulncheck ./...` all ran clean (the one reported
module vulnerability is the known, unreached `golang.org/x/sys` advisory
`AGENTS.md` already names). `deadcode ./...` flagged one function
(`SwapReleaseSigner`, `internal/harness/release.go:422`) as unreachable; it is
a documented test-injection seam called from `cmd/sh-agent/zip_test.go` in a
different package, so the tool's static-reachability pass misses it — not a
real dead-code finding.

One layout observation, not raised to a finding: `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`
(1199 lines) carries a full second feature's business logic in the entrypoint
package — reading, parsing, and atomically rewriting Claude's `settings.json`
(`attributionSet`/`attributionHint`/`attributionOff`/`readSettings`, main.go:805-1031)
— where the golang skill's checklist says "`cmd/` stays thin — flag business
logic in main.go." It is well-tested and correct as far as I traced it, so I
am not filing it as a blocking finding, but a reviewer on the next change to
this area should ask whether it belongs in `internal/harness` beside
`report.go`/`zip.go`, which own comparable one-off, carefully-hardened file
mutations.

## Findings

None that meet the bar (correctness, security, or a stated requirement/rule
violation). Nothing found regressing any of the ~90 recorded bugs in
`.agents/docs/bugs/INDEX.md`, several of which target exactly the files read
here (report.go redaction/push-target checks BUG-053–060/074; zip unpack
BUG-093/094; search's work-tree-rename parsing BUG-108, fixed today).

## Criteria

1. **Dead code** — pass. No unused exported symbols with real production
   callers missing; the one `deadcode` hit (`SwapReleaseSigner`) is an
   intentional cross-package test seam, documented as such.
2. **Flow tracing** — pass on everything read. `report.go`'s redaction feeds
   `SendReport` end to end (`Collect` → `BuildRecord` → `writeAndPush`), every
   git-redirect env var is checked before every write path that could be
   redirected, every push/clone path scrubs credentials before printing.
   `internal/search/reconcile.go`'s `gitView` uses `--no-renames` and reads
   through `os.Root` (the BUG-108 fix, confirmed in place). `zip.go` validates
   every entry name, size, and kind before writing anything, and removes the
   temp directory on every error path. `cmd/sh-agent/main.go`'s command
   dispatch (`run`) correctly routes `--from-zip` ahead of every other flag
   combination and refuses it outside `update`.
3. **Standards conformance** — pass with the one soft note above
   (`cmd/` not staying thin in `main.go`'s settings-editing code). `gofmt`,
   `go vet`, `go build`, `govulncheck` all clean. R4's one-dependency rule
   holds (`go.mod`: one direct require, `modernc.org/sqlite`). `toolMap` in
   `derive.go` covers every tool actually used across `agents/*.md`
   (Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Edit, Write) — no agent risks the Antigravity
   hang the project rule warns about.
4. **Directory layout** — pass, with the `cmd/`-not-thin note above as the
   one deviation from the stated convention; entrypoints stay in
   `cmd/sh-agent/`, private logic in `internal/harness` and `internal/search`,
   tests beside their sources throughout.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security)** — pass. No hand-rolled crypto/auth:
   `crypto/sha256`/`sha1` are used only as checksums/content IDs (never as a
   MAC, KDF, or signature primitive), SSH-signing and verification for
   releases go through `git`/`ssh-keygen -Y verify`. No dependency beyond the
   one justified SQLite driver.
6. **Decoupling** — pass. `internal/search` and `internal/harness` interact
   through a small, one-directional import (`search` imports `harness` for
   `SecretShaped`), no reach-into-internals. Small interfaces at the seams
   (e.g., `report.go`'s `redact func(string, []byte) ([]byte, []Redaction)`).

## Not examined

Given the scope (whole repo, ~16,700 lines of Go plus ~1,000 tracked
non-scratch files) and the tool-call budget, I read the highest-risk and
highest-churn Go source files in full but did not read every file. Not
examined in this pass:
- `internal/harness/apply.go`, `frontmatter.go`, `inventory.go`, `plan.go`,
  `release.go` (beyond the `deadcode`/`SwapReleaseSigner` spot check),
  `render.go`, `repo.go`, `source.go`, `state.go`, `owned_unix.go`/`owned_other.go`.
- `internal/search/parse.go`, `store.go`.
- `embed.go` and its generated-counterpart guarantee (`plan_test.go` at repo
  root asserts embedded-plan-equals-checkout; I read its doc comment but not
  its body or a full trace of the embed build).
- All test files (`*_test.go`) — read none in full; relied on `go build`,
  `go vet`, `gofmt`, and `govulncheck` passing rather than re-deriving test
  coverage by hand. `go test ./...` (with `-race`) was not run in this pass
  (time/tool-budget tradeoff against a ~16.7k-line Go tree); a change-free
  review leans on the fact that HEAD's own CI-equivalent (verifier/preflight)
  already gates merges, but this means I cannot personally attest the test
  suite is currently green.
- All markdown: `context/AGENTS.md`, every `skills/*/SKILL.md` and its
  `references/`, `agents/*.md` bodies (frontmatter and tool lists were

Proposed: one `internal/harness` helper returning `error`, with `attributionSet` wrapping it. |

The two sibling sweeps (`report.go:419`, `main.go:1171`) already use `os.ReadDir` plus a prefix match. Proposed: the same, plus a test with a metacharacter in the home path. |
| 3 | low / high | security | `internal/harness/repo.go:197,225,241` | A checkout place builds and runs the tip of `main` after `git pull --ff-only` with no signature check; release places verify SSHSIG. By design (R9, AGENTS.md rule 3). Operator choice: record as accepted risk in an ADR line (recommended), or verify commit signatures after the pull. |
| 4 | low / medium | security | `internal/harness/report.go:39-58` | The report redaction deny-list misses JWTs, `sk_live_`/`rk_live_`/`whsec_`, `npm_`, `hf_`, `pypi-`, legacy `sk-` keys, Slack webhook URLs and `https://<token>@host` without a colon. Destination is the operator's private repository, hence low. Proposed: anchored `regexp` needles, each with a test that fails without it. |
| 5 | low / high | security | `skills/VENDORED.md` (Apache-2.0 table) | `gke-basics` and `terraform` have no recorded source, pin or digest; every other vendored row has one. Proposed: re-vendor from a pinned upstream commit and record the pin. |
| 6 | low / low | security | `internal/harness/report.go:901-914` | Push errors return git's stderr unscrubbed, while the clone failure path wraps the same kind of message in `scrubCredentials`. Proposed: wrap both push-error returns. |
| 7 | low / low | simplify, code | `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (1199 lines) | The entrypoint holds the settings.json attribution editor (~230 lines) and the PATH-shadow reporter, neither CLI-dependent; the golang skill's "cmd/ stays thin" item. Both lenses call it non-blocking; the single-file grouping is also defensible. |

Observations that are not findings, recorded once:
