- **Untested fix.** The close-before-rename order in `WriteAtomic` is right, but no test would catch it being reverted.
- **Stale guide.** The operator's guide still lists the needle set from before this range.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/report.go:46,49,74,80` — what is left of round 2's finding 1, plus shapes from the same classes. **Probe:** `.agents/scratch/sec-worktree-r3/mut/internal/harness/zz_probe_test.go` calls `redactLines` on a copy equal to the live code, in text mode and in JSONL mode. Its positive control was redacted and its negative control (`ssh://git@…`) was not. Each of these came back **unredacted in both modes**:
  - `https://HOOKS.SLACK.COM/services/…`. Prefix needles match case-sensitively (`needleIn`, `strings.Contains`), and the host is not case-sensitive. Carried from round 2.
  - A 17-character bare userinfo, `https://FAKEVALUEFAKEVALU@host`. `url token` needs 20 or more characters. Carried from round 2.
  - A bare userinfo carrying `=` padding, `https://…FAKE==@host`. `=` and `+` are outside the `url token` class, and both appear in base64 tokens. New this round.
  - `https://hooks.slack.com/triggers/…`, Slack's workflow-trigger webhook path. New this round; my confidence that this path is live is medium.
  - An OpenAI `sk-None-…` key, the prefix of user keys created without a project. The `openai key` regex needs 32 alphanumerics straight after `sk-`. New this round; my confidence in the vendor format is medium.

  Each would reach the feedback repository verbatim. **Remediation:** put it to the operator as one choice.
  - **(a) Recommended: close the classes, not the instances.** This leaves one needle fewer than today, each with a `TestReportRedactShapes` case.
    - Replace both Slack prefixes with one keyword needle, `(?i)hooks\.slack\.com/`. It covers every path and every letter case.
    - Change `url token` to `://[^/\s:@]{16,}@`. That is any userinfo alphabet and 16 or more characters; `ssh://git@` still passes.
    - Add `sk-None-` as a prefix needle.
  - **(b) Record `left: operator — deny-list residue accepted`.** `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md:67` already tells the operator "Anything that matches no shape IS sent".
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/apply.go:331-342` — the close-before-rename fix is correct by reading, but no test pins it.
  - **Mutation O1** moved the `Rename` block back above the `Close` block, as round 2 had it. It compiled, and no test in `internal/harness` or `cmd/sh-agent` failed.
  - The one failure was `TestRelativeHomeResolvesAgainstTheInvokingDirectory`, which fails the same way in the unmutated copy (`git clone` of a copy that is not a checkout). It is environmental and passes on the live tree.
  - Under the global Definition of Done, a finding counts as fixed only when a test fails without the fix. Pinning this order needs a close seam in `WriteAtomic`, which is more code than a window of one syscall warrants.

  **Remediation:** record `left: operator — order pinned by reading; no seam`. Separately, a comment nit: `abandon`'s inline comment (`apply.go:350`) says the file is "already closed on the rename branch", but after this fix it is also closed on the close-failure branch.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md:66` — the guide's "The shapes:" list still describes the needle set from before this range.
  - **What it lists:** vendor prefixes only up to `xoxs-`, plus the four keyword shapes.
  - **What it omits:** every shape this range added:
    - the prefixes `sk_live_`, `rk_live_`, `whsec_`, `sk_test_`, `rk_test_`, `sk-svcacct-` and `sk-admin-`;
    - both PyPI prefixes;
    - the Slack `services/` and `workflows/` hosts;
    - the `jwt`, `openai key`, `npm token`, `hugging face token` and `url token` regexes.
  - **Impact:** it understates coverage, which is the safe direction, so nothing leaks. It is still the operator's reference for what `report` catches, and it is an enumeration of a vocabulary this change grew without updating (the global "every enumeration of it" rule).

  **Remediation:** replace the list with a pointer to `prefixNeedles` and `keywordNeedles` in `report.go`, which is shorter and cannot drift; or update it in the same change. Route it to `documentation`.

## Fix by fix
- **Prefixes `sk_test_`, `rk_test_`, `sk-svcacct-`, `sk-admin-` and `hooks.slack.com/workflows/` (`report.go:49`): closed.**
  - Mutations P1-P5 each deleted one of the five needles. Each compiled, and each time `TestReportRedactShapes` failed.
  - A side effect, not a finding: the new prefixes also match ordinary identifiers, and the probe drops the whole line for `see task-admin-panel`, `network_test_helpers.py` and `framework_test_utils.py`. That is the safe direction.
    - Unlike `ASIAN food`, no such case is pinned in the benign list.
    - The comment at `report.go:36-38` ("a bare `sk-` would match every "task-"") implies that `task-` words survive, and `sk-admin-` breaks that.
    - If this is accepted, pin one case among the benign lines so that a change to it is deliberate.
- **`%` in `url token` (`report.go:80`): closed.** Mutation P6 removed `%` from the class. The code compiled and `TestReportRedactShapes` failed. The change can only add matches, so it cannot cause a miss.
- **`WriteAtomic` closes before the rename (`apply.go:331-342`): correct, untested** (the second finding).
  - **Every error path leaves `dest` alone.** Write, chmod, sync, close and rename all go through `abandon`.
  - **The second `Close` is harmless.** In `abandon`, `Close` on a file that is already closed returns `os.ErrClosed`, which is discarded. `tmp.Name()` is still valid after the close.
  - **Every caller reports failures truthfully again.** The five callers are `Install` (`apply.go:79`), `UpdateFromRelease` (`release.go:170`), `SaveState` (`state.go:68`), `copyTree` (`adopt.go:175`) and `attributionSet` (`main.go:907`). With this order, their "failed" messages are true again: round 2's false failures are gone.
  - **The ETXTBSY window is closed.** The inode is closed before it is renamed into place.
- **A young `release-*` survives (`release_test.go:654`): closed.** Mutation A1 set the age at `release.go:147` to `time.Duration(0)`. The code compiled and `TestUpdateFromReleaseSweepStaysInHome` failed. The test now pins the threshold between the test's own duration and 2 h: a threshold of 3 h would leave `release-old` in place and fail too.
- **`VENDORED.md` split date: closed.** The blob-less upstream clone (`.agents/scratch/sec-worktree/gskills.git`) gives these commits:
  - `5d9d054`, dated 2026-06-23 (author and committer), "Refactor GKE basic skill into individual skills".
  - The first commit touching `skills/cloud/gke-basics` after the pin `6f0b877` (2026-04-23) is `626910e` (2026-05-11), so "unchanged upstream through 2026-05-10" is true.

## Checked
- **Secrets:** the diff adds only placeholder values (`FAKEVALUE`, `FAKEPW`). No secret-shaped path is in scope or untracked. `git status` after all my runs is identical to its state at the start, with no new commit and no new tag.
- **Injection:** no new exec, SQL or template. The regexes are RE2.
  - `SweepStaleDirs` matches names from `ReadDir` by prefix and skips symlinks and non-directories.
  - The parent directory is `~/.config/sh-agent`, created 0700, so `RemoveAll` targets only the owner's own entries (the rule from BUG-037).
- **Authz/authn:** no endpoint or credential flow is touched.
  - **Settings write:** `attributionSet` now writes through `WriteAtomic`. The Lstat symlink refusal and the non-regular refusal still come first, and the rename replaces the path without ever writing through a link. Only the owner can write to `~/.claude`.
  - **`pushError`:** it scrubs both branches, and `errors.Is(err, errPushRejected)` still works because that branch keeps `%w`. The other branch no longer wraps its cause, and no caller unwraps it: `report.go:761` and `:787` test only `errPushRejected`. `TestPushErrorScrubsCredentials` covers both branches.
- **Crypto:** nothing composed here.
- **Dependencies:** `go.mod` and `go.sum` are unchanged. `govulncheck ./...` exited 0 with "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities", plus 1 vulnerability in a required module that the code does not call. `AGENTS.md` names that one as GO-2026-5024; the default output does not print the ID. `npm audit` does not apply because there is no `package.json`.
- **GCP surface:** none in the range.
- **Tools on the live tree (go1.27.1):**
  - `gofmt -l cmd internal` printed nothing.
  - `go vet ./...` exited 0.
  - `go test -race -count=1 ./...` exited 0, with all four packages ok. This closes round 2's gap for the whole suite with `-race`.
- **Mutations:** all ran in `.agents/scratch/sec-worktree-r3/mut`, a tar copy of `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`, with `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` set so that git inside the copy cannot reach the real repository.
  - **Copy checked:** `cmp` found six files equal to the working tree.
  - **Baselines:** the targeted tests passed there first. The unmutated full baseline fails only the environmental BUG-080 test.
  - **Each mutation:** the diff was checked non-empty and the code compiled (`go test -run '^$'`) before the named test ran, and each file was restored and checked with `cmp` afterwards.
  - **Summary:** P1-P6 and A1 failed their named tests; O1 survived.
- **Past bugs (`sh-agent search --refs … --kind bug`):**
  - BUG-053 covers the needle list, the same mechanism as the first finding.
  - BUG-079 covers binary replacement, consistent with the ETXTBSY reasoning.
  - BUG-080 is the test that is environmental in the copy.
  - BUG-037 is the `RemoveAll` validation rule, which `SweepStaleDirs` meets.
  - `sweep.go`, `VENDORED.md` and `state.go` have no bug references.

## Not examined
- **Other filesystems:** `WriteAtomic` on NFS or other network filesystems. The claim "an error always means dest is unchanged" was checked by reading, for local filesystems only.
- **JSONL that fails to decode:** a line that fails to decode partway was not probed; the probe fed well-formed JSONL.
- **BUG-080 test under O1:** `TestRelativeHomeResolvesAgainstTheInvokingDirectory` cannot run in the scratch copy, so for `cmd/sh-agent`, O1's survival rests on that package's other tests.
- **`VENDORED.md` rows:** the `terraform` row, unchanged since round 1 checked it. For `gke-basics`, only the split date and the upstream log between the pin and the split were re-verified.
- **Zip path:** `updateFromZip`'s `parent` and the zip sweep's call site were not re-read; they are unchanged since round 2.
- **Search:** `internal/search` beyond the `-race` run.
- **Other agents' artifacts:** `review-worktree-code` and `verify-review-fixes` were grepped for `left: operator` records, not read whole.
- **Scratch left on disk:** `.agents/scratch/sec-worktree-r3/` (the mutation copy, the probe, the logs and the govulncheck output) and `.agents/scratch/sec-worktree-r3-live-test.log`. Both are gitignored and can be deleted.

title: Security review — worktree-redaction (2026-09-30)
body:
# Security review — worktree-redaction   (2026-09-30)

Range reviewed: Scope: working tree — changed files: internal/harness/report.go internal/harness/report_test.go; read the diff with git diff HEAD -- internal/harness/report.go internal/harness/report_test.go.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Three findings, all low. Nothing leaks that leaked before.

- **The fix works.** A probe of the live patterns shows that each of the five shapes round 3 named is now redacted, in text mode and in JSONL mode. Mutations M1-M5 each removed or weakened one new rule. Each compiled, and each was caught by `TestReportRedactShapes`.
- **The over-redaction question: yes, the `url token` rule goes past what the written policy covers.** It does so in two ways, both in the safe direction:
  - it redacts usernames of 16 or more characters;
  - it redacts text that is not a userinfo at all, because its match can run out of a URL that has no path and into the text beside it.
- **The second kind is not new.** HEAD's unchanged `url credentials` rule already does the same thing.
- **The cost:** a whole line of a proposal, or a whole correction record in `feedback.jsonl`, is dropped.
- **Residuals.** Five shapes in the same two classes still pass: three Slack host variants, a GovSlack host, and a token with an empty password. This is the fifth pass over this deny-list, so it is an operator choice. Two small edits, one of them shorter than today's rule, close all five; a copy of the code with those edits was probed.
- **Stale comment.** One comment in `report.go` still describes a list entry this diff moved.
- **The working tree moved during this review, but not the two files in scope.** Someone else edited `.agents/docs/deploy/local.md:66` to describe the new rules, and a verifier log appeared. I made neither change. After every run, `report.go` and `report_test.go` were still `cmp`-equal to the copy I probed.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/report.go:76-81` — `url token` (`://[^/\s:@]{16,}@`) over-redacts beyond the written policy.
  - **The written policy.** Three places state it: `report_test.go:122-123` (the `ASIAN` pin), `report.go:70-71` (a word that ends in `sk-`), and `deploy/local.md:66` ("tokens: 3", "ASIAN"). All three name only lexical collisions: text that looks like a needle.
  - **Probe.** Each of these benign lines was redacted, in both modes:
    - **(1) A lexical collision: a username of 16 or more characters in the userinfo.**
      - `clone https://simon-ostling-dev@bitbucket.org/ws/repo.git` (Bitbucket clone URLs carry the username);
      - `https://contoso-engineering@dev.azure.com/…` (Azure DevOps clone URLs carry the organization);
      - `ssh://firstname.lastname@host/repo.git`;
      - `postgres://reporting_readonly_user@db/x`;
      - `docker://ubuntu-with-extra-tools@sha256:abc`.

      This is the same kind of over-redaction as `ASIAN`. But the comment says "a username (`ssh://git@`) stays", which is true only below 16 characters. The old rule already dropped usernames of 20 or more characters. This change widens that to 16-19 characters, and to usernames with characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9_.%-]`.
    - **(2) Structural: the match leaves the URL.** The class admits `"`, `,`, `?`, `#`, `)`, `]` and any non-ASCII character. A userinfo holds none of them unescaped. RE2's `\s` is ASCII-only, so a non-breaking space pasted from a chat is not a space to it. A match therefore starts in a URL with no path and runs on to the next `@` in the text beside it:
      - `origins = ["https://app.example.com","ops@example.com"]`
      - `ALLOWED=https://app.example.com,ops@example.com`
      - `https://example.com?email=me@example.com`
      - `see [docs](https://docs.example.com)@simon`
      - `the url https://example.com#frag@anchor`
      - three words joined by U+00A0 non-breaking spaces

      The written policy names no case like these. It is not new in kind, though: HEAD's unchanged `url credentials` rule (`report.go:63`) crosses the same way. The probe redacted `{"url":"https://app.example.com","by":"ops@example.com"}` under `url credentials`.
  - **What the comment gets wrong.** "Anything a userinfo may hold" and "a username stays" both overstate: the class is wider than a userinfo alphabet, and only short usernames stay.
  - **Not over-redacted:** `ssh://git@…`, `ssh://ostling.simon@gmail.com@source.developers.google.com:2022/…`, `…/golang.org/x/sys@v0.20.0`, `git+https://github.com/org/repo@v1.0`, `https://unpkg.com/react@18`, and a URL followed by a space before an email.
  - **Remediation:** put it to the operator as one choice.
    - **(a) Recommended: accept it.**
      - Reword `report.go:76-78` to say what else goes: a username of sixteen characters or more, and text after a URL with no path when an `@` follows with no space between.
      - Pin one case of each among the benign lines, expected redacted, as `ASIAN` is pinned.
      - Add the username case to the over-redaction examples in `local.md:66`.
    - **(b) Narrow the class to a token alphabet, `[A-Za-z0-9._~%+=-]`.** Not recommended. `url credentials` crosses the same way and would need the same narrowing, so two rules get longer to protect usefulness, not secrecy. It also still drops long usernames.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/report.go:81,83` — residual shapes in the same two classes. The probe of the live code left each of these **unredacted in both modes**:
  - `https://hooks.slack.com:443/services/T0/B0/…` (an explicit port);
  - `https://hooks.slack.com./services/…` (a trailing-dot fully qualified name);
  - `url=https%3A%2F%2Fhooks.slack.com%2Fservices%2F…` (a webhook embedded in another URL or in a form body, where the `/` after `com` is `%2F`);
  - `https://hooks.slack-gov.com/services/…` (the GovSlack webhook host; medium confidence in the vendor format);
  - `https://TOKEN:@host/r` (a userinfo token with an empty password). `url credentials` needs at least one password character, and `url token` stops at the colon. Some registries document this form, for example Gemfury's `https://TOKEN:@pypi.fury.io/…` (medium confidence).

  Not counted as residuals:
  - a 15-character userinfo, which falls under the threshold by design;
  - a scheme-relative `//TOKEN@host`, which is rare. JSONL mode catches it only by accident, because `decoded` prints `key:value` and so creates a `://`; text mode misses it;
  - a JSONL line that fails to decode and carries `https:\/\/` escapes. That limit is older than this diff, applies to both URL rules, and is `decoded`'s documented limit.

  **Remediation:** this is the fifth pass over this list, so the global rounds rule applies: put it to the operator as one choice.
  - **(a) Recommended: two edits.** Each gets a `TestReportRedactShapes` row.
    - `slack webhook` becomes `(?i)hooks\.slack`, dropping `\.com/` (five characters shorter).
    - `url token` becomes `://[^/\s:@]{16,}:?@` (two characters longer).

    I probed both edits in the scratch copy only:
    - all five residuals were then redacted in both modes;
    - `TestReportRedactShapes` still passed, every positive and benign row;
    - the benign URL lines stayed unredacted.

    After these edits, record any further residue as `left: operator — deny-list residue accepted`.
  - **(b) Record all of it as accepted residue now.** `local.md:66` already calls the list "a safety net, never a guarantee".
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/report.go:43-44` — the prefix-list comment says its entries include "a Slack webhook URL". This diff removed both Slack prefixes from that list; the webhook is now the `slack webhook` rule at `:83`. **Remediation:** delete "and a Slack webhook URL" from the comment in the same change (the global rule on text that describes a behaviour).

## Checked
- **Secrets:** the diff adds only `FAKEVALUE` placeholders. `git status` shows no secret-shaped path.
- **Injection:** the only new logic is RE2 regexes, which run in linear time, with no exec, SQL or template.
  - **What `report.json` records:** `needleIn` returns the rule name (`slack webhook`) or the needle literal (`sk-None-`), never the matched text (BUG-054 still holds).
  - **Callers:** only `Collect` (`report.go:286-314`) calls the redactors, before `--dry-run` output and before the push. It sends:
    - `feedback.jsonl` and `retros.jsonl` in JSONL mode;
    - `state.json` whole, written by `MarshalIndent`, so whitespace separates its values;
    - `proposals/*.md` in text mode.
- **Superset check:** every line that contains one of the two removed prefixes also contains `hooks.slack.com/`. Only the recorded pattern name changes.
- **Authz/authn:** nothing touched.
- **Crypto:** nothing composed.
- **GCP surface:** none.
- **Dependencies:** `go.mod` and `go.sum` are unchanged.
  - `govulncheck ./...` exited 0: "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities", plus 1 vulnerability in a required module that the code does not call (GO-2026-5024 per `AGENTS.md`).
  - `npm audit` does not apply: there is no `package.json`.
- **Tools on the live tree (go1.27.1):** `gofmt -l cmd internal` printed nothing; `go vet ./...` exited 0; `go test -race -count=1 ./...` exited 0, with all four packages ok.
- **Probe:** `zz_probe_test.go` calls `redactLines` in text mode and in JSONL mode, in a `tar` copy of `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard`. `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` was set, and `git rev-parse` inside the copy failed as it should. `cmp` showed `report.go`, `report_test.go`, `go.mod` and `go.sum` equal to the working tree.
  - The positive control (`AKIA…`) was redacted, and the negative control (`ssh://git@…`) was not.
  - Every round-3 shape was redacted by the intended rule: `slack webhook` ×2, `url token` ×2, `sk-None-`.
- **Mutations:** each was applied to a copy, its diff checked non-empty, compiled with `go test -run '^$'`, then run against `TestReportRedactShapes`, and the file restored and checked equal with `cmp`.
  - **Killed, each by the intended row:**
    - M1 dropped `sk-None-`;
    - M2 dropped `(?i)`;
    - M3 raised the threshold to `{17,}`;
    - M4 removed `=` from the class;
    - M5 deleted the Slack rule;
    - M7 lowered the threshold to `{10,}` (the benign `deploy-bot` row caught it);
    - M8 changed the Slack rule to `(?i)slack\.com/` (the benign `slack.com/apps` row caught it).
  - **Survived:** M6 (`{11,}`). The benign pin is 10 characters long, so the threshold can fall to 11 unnoticed. That is the over-redaction direction, so it is not a finding; a benign username of exactly 15 characters would pin the threshold exactly.
- **Past bugs** (`sh-agent search --refs`):
  - BUG-053 and BUG-110 cover this deny-list mechanism.
  - BUG-056, BUG-058 and BUG-059 cover structure and the decoder, which this diff leaves unchanged.
  - BUG-057 covers escapes in fixtures; the new rows hold none.
  - Round 3's side note, pinning one case like `task-admin-panel`, was not taken up. It is outside this diff and not a finding.

## Not examined
- **Dry-run tier:** the end-to-end `sh-agent report --dry-run` tier (`testing/guide.md` § 3b), which the verifier's log `testing/2026-09-30-verify-redaction-rules.md` reports running. I did not re-run it, and I read only that log's header.
- **Concurrent `local.md` edit:** read as a diff only, not reviewed as a document.
- **Other living docs:** a grep found no other description of the changed thresholds. `delivery.md` § The loop back was not re-read.
- **Coverage beyond round 3:** vendor webhook and token formats other than Slack and OpenAI, and any deny-list kind round 3 did not name.
- **Slack host behaviour:** whether `hooks.slack.com` accepts an explicit port or a trailing dot. I reasoned from URL syntax and did not probe the vendor.
- **Scratch left on disk:** `.agents/scratch/sec-worktree-redaction/` (the copy, the probe, the pristine `report.go`, `live-test.log`, `govulncheck.log`). It is gitignored and can be deleted.

## Outcome
- 1 over-redaction of `url token` — fixed: accepted in the safe direction, the comment reworded at `report.go` (`url token`), one case of each pinned in `TestReportRedactShapes` (a long username, a pathless URL with an unrelated `@`).
- 2 five residual shapes — fixed at `report.go`: `(?i)hooks\.slack` and `://[^/\s:@]{16,}:?@`, the rules this report proposed; five rows in `TestReportRedactShapes`, mutation fails ten lines.
- 3 stale comment — fixed at `report.go` (prefix list comment).

title: Preflight — v2.0.0 (2026-10-01)
body:
# Preflight — v2.0.0   (2026-10-01)

Range reviewed: v1.16.2..9c6c3ed

Requested in the operator's own turn: "Update the architecture page, readme and all supporting files that this is the new stable state and make sure the REQUIREMENTS is fully updated, then /preflight v2.0.0". Version: MAJOR at the operator's word; the rule's test holds too — a v1.16.x place reacts to this release: two skills it had (`python`, `anti-ui-slop`) are gone, and a flag passed to the wrong `sh-agent` verb now exits 2 instead of being accepted.

## Findings, worst first

No blocking finding. Every medium found by the gate was fixed before the tag; every low is recorded with an owner.

| # | severity / confidence | finding | where | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | medium / high | `internal/memory`'s `git ls-files` ran a project's `core.fsmonitor` hook, so the nightly dream executed project code at 03:00 (security code slice) | `internal/memory/memory.go:85` | fixed d26de97 (`storeTrackedArgs`, `TestStoreTrackedArgs`; the agent's hook probe: old binary 1 run, new binary 0) — reviewer APPROVE WITH NITS: the test pins the arguments, a behavioural hook test is `left: next task — main agent` |
| 2 | medium / medium | `allowed-tools: Bash` in the bash and docker skills let every shell command run unprompted on Claude Code while the skill was active (security harness-text slice) | `skills/bash/SKILL.md:4`, `skills/docker/SKILL.md:9` | fixed 89f3308 (lines deleted; no other skill carries the key) — BUG-143 |
| 3 | medium / medium | golangci-lint installed by `curl … \| sh`; gcloud tarball fetched with no checksum step (security harness-text slice) | `skills/golang/references/service.md:404`, `skills/gcloud-setup/SKILL.md:49` | fixed 89f3308 → 19d3467 → 9c6c3ed over three reviewer rounds (download chain wrong on macOS and landing in the project root; then my rewrite deleted the usage sentence): now `go install …@v2.14.0` verified by the checksum database, the release-binary path as one sentence, the gcloud SHA256 through `sha256sum -c -`; reviewer round 3 APPROVE; security Outcome: closed — BUG-143 |
| 4 | medium / high | `deploy/remote.md` said `sh-agent list` shows 27 skills and 7 agents (docs lens) | `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md:203` | fixed in this release commit (34 and 8) |
| 5 | low / medium | the frozen-tree rule lost its reason and the fix-that-cannot-wait clause; `review` Step 5 omitted `docs/onboarding.md` (docs lens) | `context/AGENTS.md:15`, `skills/review/SKILL.md:105` | fixed 89f3308 (render 15,137 / hand-written 14,252 bytes) |
| 6 | low / high | the dream timer's `systemctl`/`launchctl` calls are not scoped by `--home`: a scratch `uninstall` or `--remove-timer` disables the real timer (security code slice) | `internal/dream/timer.go:112,116,171` | `left: operator` — one-line choice in the handoff (a per-home unit name, or refusing the service-manager calls for a non-real home) |
| 7 | low / high | the dream redacts raw `feedback.jsonl` lines without `report`'s JSON-decoding pass; `memory show` follows a symlinked `MEMORY.md` (security code slice) | `internal/dream/collect.go:65,148`, `internal/memory/memory.go:243` | `left: next task — main agent` |
| 8 | low / low | R3's "no tools" for the Antigravity dream child rests on plan-mode behaviour no recorded probe verified (security code slice) | `internal/dream/dream.go:166` | `left: next task — main agent` (one recorded agy probe settles it) |
| 9 | low / medium | data-gcp's default role sits in `cloudsqlsuperuser` (CREATEROLE/CREATEDB unnamed); docker builder images on mutable minor tags; `feature` reads issue bodies with no data-only clause; an older `npx -y`, a Makefile deploy without `--project`, `commit -am` in a README sample (security harness-text slice) | `skills/data-gcp`, `skills/docker`, `skills/feature`, `skills/find-skills`, README | `left: next task — main agent` (the mutable tag is Phase 6 D26, by research brief, not an operator rebuttal) |
| 10 | low / medium | the kit preamble's real-home guard is a string compare and fingerprints one directory; `command(*)` rows run in a HOME-only sandbox with the operator's uid (security trail slice) | `testing/kit-preamble.sh:24,47`, `testing/skill-matrix.md:14` | `left: operator` — accept as the sandbox's design (recommended) or ask for real isolation; recorded in the handoff |

## Rows of the Definition of Done

- **Dirty source before the gate (Step 1):** none at the start besides the README repair, committed as 0b1b5b8 with its entry. The gate then fixed its own findings in four commits — 89f3308, d26de97, 19d3467, 9c6c3ed — each with a `changes/` entry, a reviewer round and a verifier re-run; the verifier that was in flight when d26de97 and 9c6c3ed landed was stopped and re-dispatched (BUG-142's rule), never cited.
- **Verification:** `testing/2026-10-01-verify-v2.0.0-gate.md` PASS at 0b1b5b8; `-r2` PASS at 89f3308; `-r3` stopped (tree moved, not cited); `-r4` PASS at 19d3467; `-r5` PASS at 9c6c3ed — gofmt clean, vet clean, six packages ok with `-race`, 342 top-level tests, both size pins (14,252 / 15,137), `TestEmbedHoldsOnlyTrackedFiles`, scratch install 34 skills / 8 agents / drift none, govulncheck 0 affecting, the coverage map of every changed Go file (r1). Status at every cited log: PASS.
- **Reviewer:** the nine phase commits are covered by their phase reports, each `## Status: COMPLETE` with a `Range reviewed:` line over the working tree that became the commit (`reviews/2026-10-01-review-worktree-p5..p9-{code,docs,prompts}.md`, `review-4764c5f-worktree-code*.md`, `review-c62e064-*`, `review-329a99b-*`, `review-1430d53-*`); the parity commits of 2026-09-30 by `review-cb799ff-f1ca525-*`, `review-f1ca525-e2cffc1-code.md`, `review-e2cffc1-a275b96-code.md` (the `review-a275b96-head-code.md` left IN PROGRESS is not cited: that commit is covered by the v1.17.0 gate re-verify and the Phase 1 code review); ddac2d8 (3 files) and 0b1b5b8 (docs) read by the main agent, below the threshold; the gate-fix commits by `reviews/2026-10-01-review-0b1b5b8-89f3308-code.md` (three rounds: REQUEST CHANGES → REQUEST CHANGES → APPROVE, Outcomes per round) and `reviews/2026-10-01-review-89f3308-d26de97-code.md` (APPROVE WITH NITS). The Phase 6 code review hit its three-round cap and was decided by the operator (D40).
- **Security:** three slices over the whole range, each `## Status: COMPLETE`, each `## Not examined` naming no release-diff path after the follow-up reads: `reviews/2026-10-01-security-v1.16.2-0b1b5b8-{code,harness-text,trail}.md`, with `## Outcome` sections for the fix commits (the code slice re-probed the fsmonitor hook against the new binary; the harness-text slice ran the new install path and the gcloud check). No high finding.
- **Docs lens:** `reviews/2026-10-01-review-v1.16.2-0b1b5b8-docs.md`, APPROVE WITH NITS; its three findings are rows 4 and 5 above (fixed) — the "GitHub Container Registry only on explicit request" clause it reported dropped stands in `skills/cloud-run-deploy/SKILL.md:19`.
- **Documentation agent:** not dispatched — the docs changes of this gate are the docs-lens findings and the two release-state lines (`specs/sh-agent/delivery.md` § Where things stand → v2.0.0; `deploy/remote.md` count), applied by the main agent and read against the diff.
- **Bugs:** BUG-143 (the two security mediums in skills; fixed). BUG-142 (open, this plan) applied twice in this gate as the rule it names.
- **Changelog:** six entries by the main agent (`changes/2026-10-01-1229-…`, `-1244-…`, `-1247-…`, `-1249-…`, `-1251-…`, and the release entry).

## Trail freshness (Step 3)

title: Review — 0b1b5b8-89f3308-code (2026-10-01)
body:
# Review — 0b1b5b8-89f3308-code   (2026-10-01)

Range reviewed: 0b1b5b8..89f3308 (7 files: `context/AGENTS.md`, `skills/bash/SKILL.md`, `skills/docker/SKILL.md`, `skills/gcloud-setup/SKILL.md`, `skills/golang/references/service.md`, `skills/review/SKILL.md`, `.agents/docs/changes/2026-10-01-1244-v2.0.0-gate-fixes.md`). Working tree for `context/` and `skills/` confirmed identical to 89f3308 (`git diff --quiet 89f3308 -- context skills`).

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The worst problem is the new golangci-lint recipe's macOS variant. As written, "`shasum -a 256 -c`" drops `--ignore-missing`. The checksums file lists every release asset, so on a Mac the check exits 1 and the `&&` chain stops before `tar`. The install fails on one of the operator's two platforms, and an agent blocked there may go back to `curl | sh`. The fix is one token. The recipe also downloads the tarball and the checksums file into the current directory, which is the project root when an agent follows it. That breaks the global scratch rule. The other five files are correct: the context sentence stays under its pin, both frontmatters still parse, and the review lane now matches `agents/documentation.md`. The Linux path of the recipe works: asset names, `sha256sum -c --ignore-missing` and the one-member `tar --strip-components=1` extraction were all checked in a scratch fixture.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/golang/references/service.md:404`: the parenthetical "(macOS: the `darwin-arm64` asset and `shasum -a 256 -c`)" replaces `sha256sum -c --ignore-missing` without `--ignore-missing`. golangci-lint's `-checksums.txt` lists every asset in the release (all OS/arch archives, plus the .deb and .rpm packages). Only one of them is downloaded, so `shasum -a 256 -c` reports every other line as `FAILED open or read` and exits 1. I reproduced this in `.agents/scratch/review-golangci` with Perl `shasum`. A checksums file with one present and one absent entry gave `shasum -a 256 -c` exit 1, while `sha256sum -c --ignore-missing` gave exit 0. The chain ends at `&&` and nothing is installed. The same `shasum` prints `--ignore-missing  don't fail or report status for missing files` in its help. Fix: write `shasum -a 256 -c --ignore-missing`. I could not confirm that macOS's bundled Digest::SHA version has the flag; that part is medium confidence. If any doubt remains, use `grep ' golangci-lint-2.14.0-darwin-arm64.tar.gz$' …checksums.txt | shasum -a 256 -c`. The macOS line also needs the tar member renamed to `golangci-lint-2.14.0-darwin-arm64/golangci-lint`. "The `darwin-arm64` asset" implies this but does not say it.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/golang/references/service.md:404`: `gh release download` has no `-D`, so it writes `golangci-lint-2.14.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz` and `golangci-lint-2.14.0-checksums.txt` into the current directory, which is the project root when an agent follows the recipe. Neither file is removed afterwards. The global context's hard rule says "every generated or temporary file goes there [`.agents/scratch/`], never `/tmp`, never beside source." The old `curl | sh` form left nothing behind, so this is a regression against the rule. Fix: download into scratch and run the check there, because `sha256sum -c` resolves the listed names against the current directory and `-D` alone would break the check. For example: `d=.agents/scratch/golangci-lint && gh release download … -D "$d" && (cd "$d" && sha256sum -c --ignore-missing golangci-lint-2.14.0-checksums.txt) && tar -xzf "$d/golangci-lint-2.14.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz" …`.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/golang/references/service.md:404`: `tar -C "$(go env GOPATH)/bin"` fails when that directory does not exist yet. In scratch this gave `tar: …: Cannot open: No such file or directory`, exit 2. On a fresh machine where nothing has been `go install`ed, `$GOPATH/bin` is absent. The old `install.sh -b` created its target directory (godownloader scripts run `install -d`); I recall this rather than checked it, hence medium confidence. The failure is loud, not silent. Fix: put `mkdir -p "$(go env GOPATH)/bin" &&` in front of the `tar`.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `agents/changelog.md:66` (outside the diff, a restatement of the lane the diff changed): `skills/review/SKILL.md:105` now lists `docs/onboarding.md` among the documentation agent's files, matching `agents/documentation.md:3`. The changelog agent's "Which of README, specs, testing guides, deploy guides, and the project AGENTS.md changed" still leaves it out, so a task that changes `onboarding.md` will not have that change reported in its `changes/` entry. Fix: add `docs/onboarding.md` to that enumeration (review-standards § 3, restatements).

## Correctness checks the brief asked for

- **Asset names (no network):** golangci-lint's goreleaser naming is `golangci-lint-<ver>-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz` for archives and `golangci-lint-<ver>-checksums.txt` for checksums. The version has no `v`; the tag does (`v2.14.0`). The archive is wrapped in a `golangci-lint-<ver>-<os>-<arch>/` directory that holds the binary, LICENSE and README.md. The recipe matches these conventions as I know them. I did not confirm that a v2.14.0 release exists; the version pin was already there before this diff.
- **`sha256sum -c --ignore-missing`:** this is the right form for a multi-file checksums file. In scratch, GNU coreutils 9.7 gave exit 0 when the downloaded file matched and the others were absent, and exit 1 with `FAILED` and `no file was verified` when the tarball had been tampered with. When no listed file is present it also exits 1 (`no file was verified`), so a misnamed download cannot pass the check silently.
- **`tar -xzf … --strip-components=1 -C <bin> <dir>/golangci-lint`:** GNU tar 1.35 matches the member against its full archive path before stripping. A fixture archive with LICENSE and README.md beside the binary put only `golangci-lint` into the bin directory, executable bit kept, exit 0. Not tested with macOS's bsdtar; see Not examined.
- **Context size:** `go test ./internal/harness -run 'TestRenderedContext|TestLint|TestAgentDescription|TestSkill' -count=1 -v` passed on 89f3308. It reported the hand-written context at 14,252 bytes against a 15,000 target, and the render at 15,137 bytes against 22,000, matching the changes entry.
- **Frontmatter after removing `allowed-tools`:** `skills/bash/SKILL.md` is left with `name` plus a double-quoted `description`. `skills/docker/SKILL.md` is left with `name` plus a block-scalar `description: |`, closed by `---`. Both are valid, and `go run ./cmd/sh-agent list` lists `bash` and `docker` with their descriptions. A grep finds no `allowed-tools` anywhere in `skills/*/SKILL.md`, `agents/`, `context/` or `README.md`, which supports the changes entry's "no other skill carries the key."
- **gcloud tarball step:** the Cloud SDK install page publishes a SHA256 for each archive, and the sentence correctly says TLS is the only authenticity guarantee. The URL is the unversioned `rapid` "latest" archive, so a release landing between page and download gives a mismatch. That failure is loud, which is the safe direction, so this is no finding.

## Criteria

1. **Dead code: pass.** These are text-only edits. Two frontmatter keys were deleted and nothing else was orphaned.
2. **Flow tracing: fail (finding 1).** I traced the golangci-lint chain step by step. On Linux the `&&` chain gets from download through check to extract. On macOS the check step fails as written, and a missing `$GOPATH/bin` fails the extract (finding 3). The context sentence's `TaskStop` → commit → re-dispatch matches `skills/feature/SKILL.md:101`, and `TaskStop` is already used elsewhere in the context. The review Step 5 lane matches `agents/documentation.md`. The changed behaviour is instruction text, and no test was expected for it. BUG-143's candidate lint test, which would refuse `allowed-tools`, was not added. That is a graduation candidate, not a requirement of this diff.
3. **Standards conformance: fail (finding 2, finding 4).** The download into the working directory breaks the global scratch rule. The changelog agent still restates the documentation lane without `onboarding.md`. The frozen-tree restatements in `skills/feature/SKILL.md:101` and `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:46` agree with the new context sentence. No `curl … | sh` or `| bash` is left in `skills/`, `context/` or `agents/`. The remaining `curl … | sudo gpg --dearmor` at `skills/gcloud-setup/SKILL.md:42` imports an apt key and executes nothing. None of the changed skills is vendored (`skills/VENDORED.md`), so editing them in place is allowed.
4. **Directory layout: pass.** No new files. The changes entry is in `.agents/docs/changes/` with the `YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM-<slug>` name and `owner:`/`date:` frontmatter.
5. **Simplicity (DIY-except-security): pass.** The recipe uses `sha256sum` as designed, which is no hand-rolled crypto. `gh` was already a harness tool. The checksums file comes from the same release as the tarball, so the check protects against corruption and truncation, not a compromised release. That meets BUG-143's "checksum or signature" prevention rule as written.
6. **Decoupling: pass.** The documentation lane's single source stays `agents/documentation.md`, and review now points at the same list. The skills changed are independent of each other.

## Not examined

- macOS itself: I did not run the bsdtar `--strip-components` + member-name form on macOS (no bsdtar on this box). libarchive matches members before stripping as far as I know, but that is low confidence. I also could not run the macOS `/usr/bin/shasum` version for `--ignore-missing` support.
- Network: I did not confirm that the golangci-lint v2.14.0 release or its exact asset names exist (no network). I did not check whether golangci-lint publishes a signature over its checksums file (cosign or an attestation) that the recipe could verify instead of a same-origin checksum.
- The gcloud install page's current checksum table was not fetched.
- The changes entry's references to other review and testing artifacts (untracked at review time) were not opened.

Scratch fixture used: `.agents/scratch/review-golangci/` (removed after the run).

## Round 2

Range reviewed: d26de97..19d3467 (`skills/golang/references/service.md` § Lint, `skills/gcloud-setup/SKILL.md` § 1, `agents/changelog.md` § Docs, `.agents/docs/changes/2026-10-01-1249-v2.0.0-gate-fix-lint-recipe.md`). Working tree for `skills/` and `agents/` confirmed identical to 19d3467.

### Verdict (round 2): REQUEST CHANGES

The fix to the lint recipe deleted the sentence that told the reader how to use golangci-lint. 89f3308 had: "Run `golangci-lint run` and `golangci-lint fmt`; `golangci-lint config verify` checks the file. The minimal config for a stdlib-first service, `.golangci.yml` at the module root:". 19d3467 replaced the whole line, and that sentence is gone. The YAML block now follows "never a script piped into `sh`" with no file name, no location and no run command. A grep finds no `.golangci.yml` and no `golangci-lint run|fmt|config verify` left anywhere in `skills/`, `context/` or `agents/`, except a Makefile sample in `skills/bash/references/makefile-patterns.md:101`. All three round-1 findings on the recipe itself are resolved, and the other two files are correct.

### Outcome of round-1 findings

- Finding 1, macOS `shasum -a 256 -c` without `--ignore-missing`: **fixed.** `go install` is now the primary path. The release-binary sentence gives `--ignore-missing` on both platforms (`service.md:404`).
- Finding 2, downloads landing in the project root: **fixed.** `go install` writes nothing into the tree, and the release-binary sentence names `.agents/scratch/` (`service.md:404`).
- Finding 3, `tar -C` into a `$GOPATH/bin` that may not exist: **fixed, by removal.** `go install` creates `GOBIN`/`$GOPATH/bin` itself. The release-binary sentence is prose and names no extract command.
- Finding 4, `agents/changelog.md:66` without `docs/onboarding.md`: **fixed** (`agents/changelog.md:66`).

### Round-2 findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/golang/references/service.md:404`: the round-2 rewrite dropped the run, fmt and config-verify commands and the label for the YAML block that follows (`.golangci.yml` at the module root). `skills/golang/SKILL.md:22` sends the reader to § Lint for staticcheck through golangci-lint. That section now shows a config with no file name or location and no command to run it, so an agent following it cannot place the file or run the linter from this text. The change entry does not mention the deletion, so it is collateral damage. Fix: put the deleted sentence back after the install sentence: "Run `golangci-lint run` and `golangci-lint fmt`; `golangci-lint config verify` checks the file. The minimal config for a stdlib-first service, `.golangci.yml` at the module root:".
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/golang/references/service.md:404`: the go-install caveat is understated. Before this round the file said the golangci-lint project documents that `go install` "is not guaranteed to work". The new text says only that the project "prefers its release binaries for reproducible version information". As I recall the golangci-lint install docs (not fetched, offline), they warn that `go install` builds are not guaranteed to work and are not covered by their CI, and version information is only one of the reasons they give. A failed `go install` still fails loudly, and the release-binary fallback is named in the next clause, so there is no silent failure. Fix: keep the original words "not guaranteed to work" in the clause that names the fallback.

### Checks the coordinator asked for

- **Module and command path:** `github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.14.0` is right as far as I can tell offline. The v2 line moved to the `/v2` module path, the binary's main package is `cmd/golangci-lint`, and this is the form the project's v2 docs give for `go install`. I did not confirm that tag v2.14.0 exists (no network). Because the version is pinned, `go install pkg@version` checks the module against `sum.golang.org` under the default `GOFLAGS`/`GONOSUMDB`, as the text says.
- **gcloud `printf '%s  <file>\n' <sha> | sha256sum -c -`:** correct. Two spaces is the GNU text-mode format. In scratch, a matching hash gave `OK`, exit 0, and a hash with one character changed gave `FAILED` and `computed checksum did NOT match`, exit 1. GNU coreutils 9.7 also accepts a single space, so the form is not fragile. The recipe is Linux-only because the URL is the `linux-x86_64` archive, so `sha256sum` is the right tool.
- **`agents/changelog.md`:** the Docs list now matches `agents/documentation.md:3` and `skills/review/SKILL.md:105`.
- **Criteria for this round:** 1 dead code pass. 2 flow tracing fails (the round-2 medium finding: § Lint is cut off where `golang/SKILL.md:22` sends the reader). 3 standards pass apart from the low finding; no `curl | sh` reintroduced. 4 layout pass. 5 simplicity pass: one `go install` line replaces a four-step chain, and the checksum database is a vetted mechanism used as designed. 6 decoupling pass.

### Not examined (round 2)

The golangci-lint install docs and the v2.14.0 tag (no network). The changes entry's mention of a verifier r3/r4 was not checked against the testing logs.

## Round 3

Range reviewed: 19d3467..9c6c3ed (`skills/golang/references/service.md` § Lint, `.agents/docs/changes/2026-10-01-1251-v2.0.0-gate-fix-round-3.md`). Working tree for `skills/` confirmed identical to 9c6c3ed.

### Verdict (round 3): APPROVE

The round fixes both round-2 findings and changes nothing else in the line. § Lint now gives, in order: the pinned `go install` command, the golangci-lint project's own caveat with the release-binary fallback, then the run, fmt and config-verify sentence and the label for the YAML block that follows. No new findings.

### Outcome of round-2 findings

- Round-2 medium (usage sentence and `.golangci.yml` label deleted): **fixed** at `skills/golang/references/service.md:404`. "Run `golangci-lint run` and `golangci-lint fmt`; `golangci-lint config verify` checks the file. The minimal config for a stdlib-first service, `.golangci.yml` at the module root:" is identical to the text at 89f3308 (`git show d26de97:…` line 404) and sits directly above the YAML block.
- Round-2 low (go-install caveat understated): **fixed** at `skills/golang/references/service.md:404`. It now reads "The project documents that `go install` is not guaranteed to work and prefers its release binaries", the wording the file used before round 2, followed by the fallback.

### Criteria (round 3)

All six pass. Only the one line and a changes entry moved. No `curl | sh` was reintroduced, and the fallback still names `.agents/scratch/` and `--ignore-missing` on both platforms.

### Not examined (round 3)

Same gaps as round 2: no network access, so neither the golangci-lint docs nor the v2.14.0 tag were checked.

## Status: COMPLETE

title: Review — 1430d53-worktree-code (2026-10-01)
body:
# Review — 1430d53-worktree-code   (2026-10-01)

Range reviewed: working tree against 1430d53, `git diff 1430d53 -- internal/harness/derive.go internal/harness/inventory.go internal/harness/frontmatter.go internal/harness/harness_test.go`

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing blocking. The new checks work on the real tree (the four named tests pass; the longest real description is under 800 characters). Worst problem: `Lint` measures a block-scalar description 2 to 3 characters longer than `Parse` and the Agent Skills limit see it, so the limit is enforced slightly too tight for `|`/`>` blocks. Five lows in total, none a defect that fires on today's files.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/frontmatter.go:111` — `joined := TrimSpace(unquote(e.val))` starts from `e.val`, which for a block scalar is the indicator itself (`|`, `>-`). The loop then yields `"| first second"`, so the count includes the indicator and a space (2 to 3 runes), while `Parse` (`strings.Join(cont, " ")`) and the spec measure only the text. A block description of 1,023 to 1,022+ characters is refused wrongly. Fix: start `joined` empty when `isBlockIndicator(e.val)`. The test margin (1,100 vs 1,024) hides it; add a case at 1,023 as a block.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/frontmatter.go:99-108` — the `descriptionLimit` const was inserted between `Lint`'s doc comment and `func Lint`, with no blank line, so the "Lint rejects ..." comment now documents the const and `Lint` has no doc comment; neither text mentions the new description rule. Describing-text rule: move the const above the comment and add the limit to Lint's comment.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/inventory.go:250` — `strings.Contains(fm["description"], "\n")` is dead: `Parse` joins continuation lines with spaces and `unquote` does not decode `\n`, so `fm["description"]` can never hold a newline. `descriptionIsMultiLine` carries the whole check. Delete the first operand. (`descriptionIsMultiLine` itself is correct: it uses the same `entries()` as `Lint`, so a `|` block, a `>` block and a wrapped plain or quoted scalar all show `val` as indicator or `len(cont)>0`; blank continuation lines are skipped by `entries` in both.)
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/inventory.go:289` (and `LoadSkills` 189, `LoadAgents` 234) — `Lint` is called for skills (yes: the claim holds), agents, AND commands/rules, so the 1,024 limit also refuses a command or rule description. AGENTS.md:59 says "any skill or agent description". Harmless today, but the restatement is narrower than the behaviour; say "any description" or limit the check to skills and agents.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/harness_test.go` `TestAgentDescriptionRules` — no control case: the fixture agent `x` is never loaded with a valid description, so a refusal from another cause (name, tools) would pass the test; error text is not asserted either. Add one accepted `x` agent or match the error substring.

## Per-hunk tests (fails without the hunk?)
- `inventory.go` multi-line check: TestAgentDescriptionRules "two lines" (block joins with spaces, only `descriptionIsMultiLine` catches it); banned-phrase loop: the other two cases. Yes.
- `frontmatter.go` Lint limit: TestLintDescriptionLimit (quoted 1,029, block ~1,101 refused; 1,019 accepted). Yes, no boundary case at 1,024/1,025.
- `derive.go`: comment only, no code change; the claim about the probe (3/3, 2/2) is not verifiable from the diff and is cited to an untracked log. TestDeriveAgy's added `maxTurns:` assertion pins existing behaviour (DeriveAgy builds from a whitelist) and would pass without a code change; TestDeriveAgyRealReviewer likewise pins existing rewrite on the real file. Both can fail if the behaviour regressed; they do not need a source hunk.
- Rune count: `len([]rune(joined))` counts characters, matching the spec's "characters"; invalid UTF-8 bytes count one each (conservative).

## Criteria
1. Dead code — one dead operand (inventory.go:250), see findings.
2. Flow tracing — pass: Lint reaches skills, agents, commands/rules; `descriptionIsMultiLine` and `Lint` share `entries`; errors wrapped with the agent/skill name. Off-by-indicator in Lint (finding 1).
3. Standards conformance — nit: Lint's doc comment displaced; AGENTS.md:59 restatement narrower than behaviour.
4. Directory layout — pass: code and tests beside each other in internal/harness.
5. Simplicity — pass: stdlib only, no new dependency.
6. Decoupling — pass: no new cross-package reach.

## Not examined
Everything outside the four Go files (agents/*.md, skills, AGENTS.md beyond the one restated line, the untracked verify log, the probe evidence quoted in the derive.go comment). Full `go test ./...`, gofmt and vet not run (only the four named tests, which pass). No mutation runs.

## Outcome

All five lows fixed in the phase: the `|`/`>` indicator is no longer counted (an under-the-limit block case added to TestLintDescriptionLimit); `descriptionLimit` sits above `Lint`'s doc comment; the dead newline check is gone; AGENTS.md § Rules says the limit covers skills, agents, commands and rules; TestAgentDescriptionRules has a valid-fixture control. The derive hunk is comment-only by design (D5b: the key is not emitted; the probe is the evidence).

body:
# Review — 329a99b worktree, docs lens   (2026-10-01)

Range reviewed: working tree against 329a99b (`git diff 329a99b` plus untracked files)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

Nine stale restatements of changed claims survive in living files (no high; 6 medium, 3 low). The worst: `skills/handoff/SKILL.md` still carries the old resume order and the old "both empty" rule, so a handoff's cold read runs a different protocol from the context; `AGENTS.md` rule 1 still says the dream timer "sends nothing off" the machine while the README map now draws and ADR-049 records its prompt to the model provider; the two size pins are named only once in three places. All claims in the lens list were checked with `restatement-grep.sh`; the ones that hold are listed under "Checked, no finding".

## Findings
- **[medium / high]** `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:168` — cold-read step: "AGENTS.md → TODO.md → this handoff → ROADMAP.md "Now" → ... → `bugs/INDEX.md` → `sh-agent search --open`". The context (context/AGENTS.md:9) now reads `AGENTS.md` → handoff → ROADMAP "Now" → plan → changes → `bugs/INDEX.md` → `TODO.md` → `search --open` → `memory show`. Change the chain to the new order (add `memory show`), so the check a handoff must pass is the protocol the next session runs.
- **[medium / high]** `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:66` — "both are empty (headers only) at every checkpoint, not just at Done". New rule: TODO empty; ROADMAP holds only "Now" naming the plan while one is open. The sentence's own tail ("while a plan is in progress "Now" names it") contradicts its head. # Review — 89f3308-d26de97-code   (2026-10-01)

Range reviewed: 89f3308..d26de97 (internal/memory/memory.go, internal/memory/memory_test.go, .agents/docs/changes/2026-10-01-1247-v2.0.0-gate-fix-fsmonitor.md)

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The fix does what it says. Nothing is broken. A scratch probe on git 2.47.3 confirmed it: in a repository whose `core.fsmonitor` points at a hook, the old `git -C <root> ls-files -- .agents/memory` ran the hook and the new argument list did not. The output was the same either way (`.agents/memory/a.md`). The one weak spot is the test. `TestStoreTrackedArgs` pins what the helper returns. It does not check that `trusted()` uses the helper. If line 85 went back to the old inline call, the helper would become dead code and the test would still pass, so the behaviour could regress with the suite green (low).

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/memory/memory_test.go:350` (`TestStoreTrackedArgs`): the test checks the helper's return value, not the hook-free behaviour of `Store`/`trusted`. Restoring the old `exec.Command("git", "-C", root, "ls-files", ...)` at `memory.go:85` would still compile, since Go allows an unused unexported func, and the test would pass with the hook running again. That fails review-standards § 2 ("would it still pass if the behaviour it names were reverted?"). Fix: add a behavioural test. Make a temp repo, `git config core.fsmonitor <script that touches a marker>`, call `Store(root)`, and assert the marker is absent. Before trusting it, show the marker does appear with the old argument list (the probe below shows this setup works on Linux git 2.47.3). The sibling `trailStatusArgs` pin in internal/dream has the same shape. That file is outside this range, so it is noted here and is not a finding.

## Checks asked for in the brief
- **Argument order**: correct. `--no-optional-locks` and `-c core.fsmonitor=false` come before `-C root ls-files`. In the probe, putting `--no-optional-locks` after the verb gave exit 129 (`unknown option`).
- **`--no-optional-locks` semantics for `ls-files`**: no change to output. The probe printed the same path with and without it. It has no effect on `ls-files`, which takes no optional index lock, so it is only there to match the sibling. `-c core.fsmonitor=false` is the guard that matters: on its own it kept the hook from running, and `--no-optional-locks` on its own did not.
- **Test string equals the return value**: yes. `strings.Join` of the slice is exactly `--no-optional-locks -c core.fsmonitor=false -C /r ls-files -- .agents/memory`.
- **`go test -race -count=1 ./internal/memory`**: ok (1.236s). `gofmt -l internal/memory` and `go vet ./internal/memory` are clean.
- **Duplication with `internal/dream/collect.go` `trailStatusArgs`**: acceptable. The two slices share a four-token guard prefix and then use different verbs and pathspecs, in two packages. Today they carry the same guards, so the duplication hides no divergence. Sharing a helper would make `internal/dream` export one, or make `internal/memory` export one for `dream`, and that coupling costs more than two slices of eight to ten tokens.

## Probe (scratch, removed afterwards)
Setup: a repository under `.agents/scratch/review-fsmon` with `core.fsmonitor=<hook appending to a marker>`. Results:
- old `ls-files`: hook ran
- new args: quiet
- `-c core.fsmonitor=false` alone: quiet
- `--no-optional-locks` alone: hook ran
- `rev-parse --git-common-dir` (`memory.Root`, which the dream also reaches): quiet
- the dream's `git log --name-only` (collect.go:209): quiet
- hardened `status`: quiet
- `check-ignore -q` (memory.go:128): hook ran

`check-ignore` is reached only from `memory.Add`, which runs only from an interactive `sh-agent memory add`. The nightly run gives the model no tools (run.go:251-276), so it never reaches `Add`. The changes entry says the nightly job runs no project hook from the memory store, and that holds for every git call the nightly path makes. Outside this range, and not a finding: if `Add` is ever reached unattended, `check-ignore` needs the same guard.

## Criteria
1. Dead code: pass. `storeTrackedArgs` has one caller (`trusted`) and the test; nothing was left commented out.
2. Flow tracing: pass. The nightly dream reaches the change through `collect.go:56` `memory.Store` → `trusted` → `storeTrackedArgs`. The error path is unchanged (refusal wrapping `err`), and the dream turns a refusal into `Dropped`. The test gap is the finding above.
3. Standards conformance: pass. Stdlib only, gofmt and vet clean, and the doc comment says why. Restatements: `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:116` names a plain `git ls-files .agents/memory`, but that is an interactive step in the operator's own project, not the nightly path, so it is not stale. The changes entry matches the diff: a nil body returns "" and fails the test, so the red run it cites compiled.
4. Directory layout: pass. The helper sits in memory.go, and its test is beside it in memory_test.go.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security): pass. A literal argument slice with no new dependency and no security primitive.
6. Decoupling: pass. Each package owns its git call. Neither imports the other's helper, and `dream` already depends on `memory`, not the other way round.

## Not examined
- Antigravity and the macOS builtin-fsmonitor case (`core.fsmonitor=true`): the probe ran only on Linux git 2.47.3 with a hook path. `-c core.fsmonitor=false` should cover the builtin daemon too, but that was not run.
- The full `go test ./...` and `govulncheck` across the repository: only `./internal/memory` was run.

## Status: COMPLETE

README has no skills table and does not enumerate lenses (it says only "`review` is the review command on both CLIs", README.md:263), so nothing in README is stale, but the clause cannot be met as written. VENDORED notes: find-skills no longer names `skill-repair` (no hit), grilling's note matches prompts brief item 4 and `skills/grilling/SKILL.md:26`. Context resume line names `project-memory`; `TestRenderedContext*` size pins pass.

title: Review — worktree-p5-prompts (2026-10-01)
body:
# Review — worktree-p5-prompts   (2026-10-01)

Range reviewed: working tree — the changed instruction files, read whole as they are in the working tree: context/AGENTS.md, agents/documentation.md, skills/bug/SKILL.md, skills/distill/SKILL.md, skills/dream/SKILL.md, skills/feature/SKILL.md, skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md, skills/handoff/SKILL.md, skills/init-project/SKILL.md, skills/preflight/SKILL.md, skills/research/SKILL.md, skills/retro/SKILL.md, skills/review-standards/SKILL.md, skills/review/SKILL.md (diff against HEAD: `git diff HEAD -- <files>`; findings may land anywhere in these files)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES (four Group 2 findings, none a safety defect; all proposed only, nothing applied)

The worst problem: `skills/review/SKILL.md:105` and `skills/retro/SKILL.md:143` tell the main agent to run only `TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock` (22,000-byte pin) after a `context/` or `rules/` edit, while the project `AGENTS.md` Setup commands name two pins and `internal/harness/size_test.go` has a second, tighter one (`TestRenderedContextUnderTarget`, 15,000 bytes). An edit applied under `--fix --prompts` or a retro can pass the instructed check and fail `go test ./...`. The other three findings are an init-project root that disagrees with the Go store root, an instruction to a shell-less agent to run `ls`, and a dangling cross-reference to "the review loop cap". Every conflict you asked me to check came back consistent except these (list under Criteria).

## Step 0: assumptions, inventory, provenance
- Scope: the 14 files named above. Skipped: everything else (no user-level files read; `~/.claude/skills/review-standards/references/prompt-audit/prompt-audit.md` read as the method).
- Target models: Claude and Gemini (every model that reads the files). A finding whose only reason is one model's documented behaviour is `flag`; Group 2 stale-fact and conflict findings are actionable as written.
- Inventory: 1 global context, 1 agent definition (`documentation`), 12 skills (all `SKILL.md` only; no reference files in scope except the prompt-audit reference used as method). No tool descriptions, no request-building code, no few-shot blocks beyond format-pinning templates.
- Provenance: `bugs/INDEX.md`, `plans/2026-09-30-audit-fix.md`, `git blame` (the init-project 5b block and the "moved from" notes are uncommitted in the tree; HEAD had the `--show-toplevel` root too). Prohibitions in these files trace to bug rows or plan decisions and were kept (keep-list 5); the "moved from the global context 2026-10-01" notes are allowed by the plan (earlier reviews 329a99b-worktree-prompts and -r2 recorded that) and are a flag only.
- Volatile specifics checked by reading (no commands run): paths `skills/init-project/assets/{AGENTS,REQUIREMENTS,ROADMAP,TODO}.md` and `agents-tree/`, `skills/review/scripts/restatement-grep.sh` (flags `-i`, `--all`, `--` match the usage block), `skills/review-standards/references/prompt-audit/prompt-audit.md`, `architecture/DECISIONS.md` all exist; `sh-agent` flags `--open`, `--kind`, `--refs`, `--global` and `--vendor` are defined in `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:107-117`; the `"vendor": "antigravity"` probe in init-project and dream matches `state.go` (`MarshalIndent`, `VendorAntigravity`); both size-pin test names exist.

## Summary
Group 2 (brittle configuration files): 4 findings, all actionable. Group 1 (dated prompt text): 0 actionable; low-confidence flags only. Group 3 (tool descriptions): not applicable. Group 4: not applicable (no request-building code); sub-agent roster check over `agents/documentation.md`, the only agent in scope: 0 findings (no near-duplicate agent in scope).

## Findings

### F1 — one size pin run where the project has two
- **Location:** `skills/review/SKILL.md:105`; `skills/retro/SKILL.md:143`
- **Evidence:** review: "a `context/` or `rules/` edit runs `go test ./internal/harness -run TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock -count=1` bare before the commit"; retro: "run `go test ./internal/harness -run TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock -count=1` bare after the edit and before the commit". Project `AGENTS.md` Setup: "must also pass the two size pins in internal/harness/size_test.go … under 22,000 bytes … under 15,000 bytes". `size_test.go:26` and `:59` define both.
- **Pattern:** Group 2, instruction files that disagree on one point (a restatement narrower than its source).
- **Why obsolete:** the second pin (ceiling 15,000, rendered context measured at 14,882 bytes in the phase 3 commit message) is the binding one; the instructed `-run` filter cannot match it, so the check can be green while the suite is red.
- **Confidence:** high (the repository contradicts it).
- **Action:** rewrite (diff below).

### F2 — init-project resolves the store root differently from the code and the dream skill
- **Location:** `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:112` (sub-step 1); also feeds `:113`, `:116`, `:120`
- **Evidence:** "`root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)`". `internal/memory/memory.go:60-72`: "Root is the main worktree's top level … so every worktree of a repository shares one store (D26)" via `--git-common-dir`; `skills/dream/SKILL.md:22`: "`root` is the main worktree's top level, the parent of `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`".
- **Pattern:** Group 2, two instruction files ruling differently on the same point; the code sides with dream.
- **Why obsolete:** run from a linked worktree, init-project creates `.agents/memory`, appends the gitignore lines and writes `autoMemoryDirectory` for the worktree's own path, while `sh-agent memory add`, `dream` and `nativeOn` (reads `<root>/.claude/settings.local.json`, `memory.go:230`) use the main worktree: two stores, settings the Go side never reads, and a migration that moves files into the wrong one.
- **Confidence:** medium. The code and the dream text are verified; that Claude Code's `~/.claude/projects/<slug>` name follows the directory the session ran in (so `slug` should keep `--show-toplevel`) I did not verify.
- **Action:** rewrite (diff below). Direction assumed: the newer, code-backed rule (D26) wins.

### F3 — an agent without a shell is told to run `ls`
- **Location:** `agents/documentation.md:37`
- **Evidence:** "the single `cmd/<app>` directory (`ls -d cmd/*/` printing exactly one)"; frontmatter `tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write`; `skills/bug/SKILL.md:55`, `feature/SKILL.md:111`, `preflight/SKILL.md:44` all say the agent "has no shell".
- **Pattern:** Group 2, volatile specifics: a command the agent's tool list cannot run.
- **Why obsolete:** the instruction is unexecutable as written; Gemini, which hangs on an unrecognised tool, or Claude would improvise or guess `<app>`, and the rule's last clause ("never left literal in a path you write") is the one it protects.
- **Confidence:** high (tools list contradicts it).
- **Action:** rewrite (diff below).

### F4 — "the review loop's cap" is referenced where no loop is described
- **Location:** `skills/bug/SKILL.md:15` ("a review loop that hits its three-round cap (Step 5)"); `skills/feature/SKILL.md:15` ("a review loop that hits its cap")
- **Evidence:** bug Step 5 (`:55`) dispatches `reviewer` once and describes no rounds; feature Step 6 (`:113`) likewise. The cap is in `skills/review/SKILL.md:112` ("**The cap** is the third round") and the rounds rule in `review` Step 4 (`:94`), which `context/AGENTS.md:16` points at.
- **Pattern:** Group 2, a cross-reference that no longer resolves to what it names.
- **Why obsolete:** a fresh session following bug Step 5 finds no cap to hit; whether the gate waits depends on it knowing `review` owns the loop.
- **Confidence:** medium (the intended target is clear; the wording is the only defect).
- **Action:** rewrite (diff below).

### Flags (low confidence or decided elsewhere; no diff)
- **[flag, low]** `skills/review/SKILL.md:94`, `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:26`, `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:31`, `skills/bug/SKILL.md:21`, `skills/retro/SKILL.md:32`, `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md:43,76,84`, `skills/feature/SKILL.md:85`: "moved from the global context 2026-10-01" and "the ADR was the changelog agent's until 2026-10-01" are migration-relative phrasing (Group 1d, history narratives): a diff against a prior version no reader saw. The plan allows the note (earlier reviews 329a99b recorded it); left as a flag so the operator can strike the nine parentheticals once the move has settled.
- **[flag, low]** `agents/documentation.md:3` names `docs/onboarding.md` in the description but the lane tree (`:24-35`) and Records line do not list it; `:34` cites "(G13)", an id nothing in the repository resolves for the reader; `:59` calls `architecture/DECISIONS.md` a "root file".
- **[flag, low]** `context/AGENTS.md:64` "(the harness's REQUIREMENTS R2 lists them)": an id only this repository's checkout can resolve; earlier review 329a99b flagged the same.
- **[flag, low]** `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:36,154` and `agents/changelog.md:81` call the context section "the Resume Protocol"; its heading is "Resume, then checkpoint" (`context/AGENTS.md:7`).
- **[flag, low]** `skills/dream/SKILL.md:3,36-42` enumerates five verdicts; Step 4 and the failure table add `index` (rows for index lines, not memories). Vocabulary enumeration differs; both are readable.
- **[flag, low]** `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:121` (sub-step 6): "the store is still created" holds only if sub-step 2's `.gitignore` append and `mkdir` ran; the headless guard names the settings write only.
- **[flag, low]** `skills/feedback-log/SKILL.md:24,30` encode single sessions as rules (the "Is it not retro first, then handoff?" quote; "A missed filing"); recency-trap pattern, kept because they are signal definitions the retro matches on.

## Proposed diff

```diff
--- a/skills/review/SKILL.md          # F1
+++ b/skills/review/SKILL.md
-a `context/` or `rules/` edit runs `go test ./internal/harness -run TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock -count=1` bare before the commit.
+a `context/` or `rules/` edit runs `go test ./internal/harness -run 'TestRenderedContext(FitsAntigravityBlock|UnderTarget)' -count=1` bare before the commit.
--- a/skills/retro/SKILL.md           # F1 (same finding, second restatement)
+++ b/skills/retro/SKILL.md
-run `go test ./internal/harness -run TestRenderedContextFitsAntigravityBlock -count=1` bare after the edit and before the commit
+run `go test ./internal/harness -run 'TestRenderedContext(FitsAntigravityBlock|UnderTarget)' -count=1` bare after the edit and before the commit
```

```diff
--- a/skills/init-project/SKILL.md    # F2
+++ b/skills/init-project/SKILL.md
-1. **Root.** `root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)`; when that fails or is empty, stop Step 5b and say so.
+1. **Root.** `root` is the main worktree's top level, the parent of `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`, so every worktree shares one store, as `sh-agent memory` and the `dream` skill resolve it; when that fails or is empty, stop Step 5b and say so. Sub-step 5's `slug` is computed from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (the directory Claude Code ran in), not from `root`.
```
(and in sub-step 5 `slug=$(printf '%s' "$root" | …)` becomes `slug=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel | sed 's#[^A-Za-z0-9-]#-#g')`; verify the slug rule before applying — the one unverified premise of F2.)

```diff
--- a/agents/documentation.md         # F3
+++ b/agents/documentation.md
-`<app>` in `specs/<app>/` is the single `cmd/<app>` directory (`ls -d cmd/*/` printing exactly one), which a heading or title in `AGENTS.md` does not override,
+`<app>` in `specs/<app>/` is the single `cmd/<app>` directory (Glob `cmd/*/` matching exactly one), which a heading or title in `AGENTS.md` does not override,
```

```diff
--- a/skills/bug/SKILL.md             # F4
+++ b/skills/bug/SKILL.md
-a review loop that hits its three-round cap (Step 5)
+a review loop that hits its three-round cap (`review` Step 5, "The cap")
--- a/skills/feature/SKILL.md
+++ b/skills/feature/SKILL.md
-and a review loop that hits its cap.
+and a review loop that hits its cap (`review` Step 5, "The cap").
```

## Criteria
1. Dead code — n/a — prompts lens
2. Flow tracing — n/a — prompts lens
3. Standards conformance — n/a — prompts lens
4. Directory layout — n/a — prompts lens
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — n/a — prompts lens
6. Decoupling — n/a — prompts lens

## Conflict checks you named (all read, results)
- review Step 1 (`--all` excludes `--resume`) vs description and usage block: consistent (description names `resume` as its own lens; usage says "never part of --all"; argument-hint lists both).
- review Step 3 table vs its three brief subsections: consistent (docs item 7 under `--project` exists; prompts and resume rows, slugs and artifact names match the closing paragraph).
- preflight Step 1 vs 2 vs 5: consistent; `## Status: COMPLETE` is required in Step 2 for a covering reviewer and security report and in Step 5's blocking list; a verifier log IN PROGRESS blocks in both.
- handoff § Cold-reader check vs review § Resume brief: same order, same six questions; the only wording differences are "Any/Every" and Q6's phrasing, none changes the question.
- init-project Step 5b sub-steps against each other: consistent except F2 (root) and the low flag on sub-step 6; sub-steps 3/4/5 chain (trust check, keys, migration only when the key is held) agrees, as do the Antigravity-only skips with Step 1.
- distill `--from-log` vs feedback-log: consistent (the log is the user's words; distill never appends; `retros.jsonl` is its index; `signal` values `gap` and the category field exist in the log format).
- context resume order vs handoff § Cold-reader check and review § Resume brief: identical sequence; the "open plan that postdates the handoff outranks it" clause appears in all three.

## Not examined
Nothing in scope was left unread. Not done: Step 7 of the audit (behavioural probes of a removal) is out of the report-only brief; no model was run on any rule. Not read: files outside the 14 (e.g. `agents/changelog.md`, other skills) except the lines cited above; `skills/review/scripts/restatement-grep.sh` and `internal/harness/restatement_script_test.go` (changed in the tree but not instruction prose; outside this lens's scope list). F2's slug premise is unverified.

## Outcome
- F1 [high] one size pin named where the project has two — fixed at `skills/review/SKILL.md:105`, `skills/retro/SKILL.md:143`, `README.md:275` (`-run TestRenderedContext`, both pins)
- F2 [medium] init-project Step 5b root differs from `internal/memory/memory.go:62` and the dream skill — fixed at `skills/init-project/SKILL.md:112,118` (root = main worktree via `--git-common-dir`; `top` from `--show-toplevel` serves only the migration slug, since Claude Code names `~/.claude/projects/<slug>` after the directory the session ran in — the premise the finding left unverified is accepted as the Claude Code convention the `init-memory` matrix row already measures)
- F3 [high] documentation agent told to run `ls` with no shell — fixed at `agents/documentation.md:37` (a Glob for `cmd/*/main.go`); behavioural runs p5d2 and p5d3 after the edit, both dispatched (p5d3's ROADMAP lane result is BUG-139, unrelated to this line)

# Review — worktree-p8-code   (2026-10-01)

Range reviewed (round 1): working tree (uncommitted) vs HEAD 7c2e30a: cmd/sh-agent/main.go, main_test.go, search_test.go; internal/harness/{apply,frontmatter,inventory,pathguard,release,repo,report,zip}.go; README.md; .agents/docs/testing/sh-agent-matrix.md; untracked internal/harness/{settings.go,settings_test.go,phase8_test.go,repo_origin_test.go}

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

No correctness or security defect found. `go vet`, `gofmt -l` and `go test -race -count=1 ./...` are clean on this tree (all six packages ok). The refactor keeps the verbs' outputs; the worst problem is one user-visible exit-code change (a flag error now exits 2, was 1) that collides with `update`'s documented exit 2, and two new tests that cannot fail for the behaviour they name.

## Findings
- **[medium / high]** `cmd/sh-agent/main.go` (`run`, the `c.fs.Parse` error branch) — a flag the verb does not define now returns `exitCode(2)` with nothing on stderr; the old single FlagSet returned the parse error, so `main` printed `sh-agent: flag provided but not defined` and exited 1. Measured with a built binary: `install --bogus` rc=2 (was 1), `update --bogus` rc=2. `update --check` documents exit 2 as "behind", so a script cannot tell a typo from "update available". Plan D9/D30 says verbs unchanged; the matrix row and README say "usage error" but not the code change. Fix: return the parse error (exit 1), or state exit 2 in the README/spec/plan and accept the collision on `update` — operator's choice.
- **[medium / high]** `cmd/sh-agent/zip_test.go:470-485` `TestUpdateFromZipDryRunCleansTempDir` (not in the diff, made stale by it) — comment and check still say the dry run unpacks under the system temp directory. Since IN10 the unpack is beside the zip, so the test watches a directory nothing writes to. Intended by IN10 and removed on every exit path (I checked each: defer in both, and the unpack dir by `updateFromZip`'s defer), but it is a behaviour change on the fallback path for exactly the machines that cannot take another way in. Operator decision; fallback to `~/.config/sh-agent` (which the real run creates) would keep scratch out of /tmp.
