title: Security review — v1.16.2-0b1b5b8-code (2026-10-01)
body:
# Security review — v1.16.2-0b1b5b8-code   (2026-10-01)

Range reviewed: v1.16.2..0b1b5b8 (slice: cmd/, internal/, go.mod, go.sum, embed.go)

Read from the working tree, whose HEAD moved to 89f3308 (a skills/context commit) during the review; `git diff --stat 0b1b5b8 89f3308 -- cmd internal go.mod go.sum embed.go` is empty, so the slice read is byte-identical to 0b1b5b8. Follow-up the same day: the fsmonitor fix d26de97, and every modified test file of the slice, read at HEAD 19d3467, whose slice equals d26de97.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Worst first: the nightly dream still runs a project's configured `core.fsmonitor` command. The range hardened the dream's `git status` against exactly that (security review 2026-10-01 rounds 2 and 3; `trailStatusArgs`, `TestTrailStatusArgs`), but one call earlier in the same project pass, `memory.Store` runs `git ls-files`, which reads the index and fires the hook. Measured on a scratch probe: plain `status` 1, hardened status 0, `rev-parse` 0, `log` 0, `ls-files` 1, `check-ignore` 1. So the control the code and its test claim does not hold at 03:00. After that: `--home` does not scope the service manager the timer verbs drive (on macOS a test `--install-timer --home <scratch>` loads a real nightly job over the real home); the dream redacts `feedback.jsonl` lines more weakly than report redacts the same file (measured); `memory show`/`add` follow a symlinked MEMORY.md; and for Antigravity, R3's "a CLI with no tools" rests on vendor permission behaviour this slice cannot show. Nothing high. No committed secret, no hand-rolled crypto, no new dependency; govulncheck reports only the known GO-2026-5024.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/memory/memory.go:85`, reached every night from `internal/dream/collect.go:56` (`memory.Store`), in `--dry-run` too. `trusted()` runs `git -C <project> ls-files -- .agents/memory` without `-c core.fsmonitor=false`. `ls-files` reads the index, so a `core.fsmonitor` command set in that project's `.git/config` (or a file it includes) runs unattended, for every indexed project, every night. That defeats the hardening at `collect.go:238-244` ("it runs no fsmonitor hook the project may have configured"), which covers only the status call. Measured on a scratch probe (`.agents/scratch/sec-probe-fsmon`, hook set with `-c`, a marker counted per command): plain `status` fired 1 (must-fire control), `trailStatusArgs` status 0 (must-not-fire), `rev-parse --git-common-dir` 0, `log --name-only` 0, `ls-files` 1, `check-ignore` 1. Precondition: someone can write that project's git config. A clone does not carry it; a copied or unpacked repository does, and so does a tool that writes repo config. The project's own reviews judged this vector worth closing. Remediation: one helper for every git call on the dream path (`memory.Root`, `memory.trusted`, `trailDates`) that puts `--no-optional-locks -c core.fsmonitor=false` before the verb, plus a test that runs each of those calls against a probe repository whose fsmonitor hook writes a marker, with plain `status` as the must-fire control. `check-ignore` in `memory.Add` and `search.guardProject` (`internal/search/search.go:134`) also fires the hook, but it runs in the operator's own interactive session. Not an issue if: the operator rules every indexed project's `.git/config` trusted. Then the `trailStatusArgs` hardening and its comment's claim should be withdrawn too, not kept.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/timer.go:112,116,171,175` via `cmd/sh-agent/main.go:298-305,341-350`. `--home` scopes where the unit files go, but not the service manager: `systemctl --user` and `launchctl … gui/<uid>` act on the operator's real session. On Linux, `uninstall --home <scratch>` or `dream --remove-timer --home <scratch>`, with a timer file in the scratch home, runs `systemctl --user disable --now sh-agent-dream.timer`. That disables and stops the REAL nightly timer, while the output says the scratch one was removed. On macOS, `dream --install-timer --home <scratch>` runs `launchctl bootstrap gui/<uid> <scratch plist>`. That loads a real job into the login session whose ProgramArguments are `<scratch>/.local/bin/sh-agent dream --all`, with no `--home`. The job then dreams over the REAL home's projects and sends their content to the model, from a command meant as a test. This breaks the project rule that development never runs against the real `$HOME`, and the consent R3 ties to `--install-timer`. The tests use a fake manager, so they never see it. Remediation: when `home` is not the real user home (the `os.SameFile` check `NoteRunningElsewhere` already makes, `internal/harness/pathguard.go:113-121`), write or remove the files only and skip the manager calls, or refuse the verb, saying which. Test it with the fake manager recording no call under a scratch home. Not an issue if: `--home` is declared unsupported for the timer verbs and refused.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/collect.go:65-67,148-154` with `internal/harness/report.go:277-283`. The dream sends each `feedback.jsonl` line raw through `harness.Redact`, which calls `redactLines(..., jsonl=false)` and so skips the decoded pass report runs on the same file (`report.go:264-266`). Measured with a synthetic line (`.agents/scratch/sec-probe-redact`, `json.Marshal` of `…?api-version=1&sig=FAKEVALUE…`): Go's encoder writes `&sig=`, report redacts the line, and the dream's `Redact` keeps it, so it would reach the CLI's model. `Redact`'s doc ("removes from text every line report would redact") is false for JSONL input; `TestRedactText` feeds plain text only. Remediation: judge each feedback line by `needleIn(decoded(line))` too, as report does, in `feedback()` or in a JSONL-aware `Redact`. Extend `TestRedactText` to run every `shapeSecrets` entry through `json.Marshal` and `scrub`. Not an issue if: feedback lines are never written by an HTML-escaping encoder. Nothing guarantees that; the writer is whatever the session uses.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/memory/memory.go:243-261` (`readLines`, used by `Show` and `Add`) and `:230` (`nativeOn`). MEMORY.md is opened with `os.Open` and a symlink is followed. `trusted()` refuses a linked `.agents`/`.agents/memory` and tracked content, but not a linked file inside the store. An untracked link (an unpacked archive, another tool) makes `memory show` print the target's non-empty lines into the session, and `memory add` copy them into the rewritten MEMORY.md. `nativeOn` reads `.claude/settings.local.json` through links and with no cap. The dream's reader of the same store refuses non-regular files (`collect.go:186-201,246-256`), so the two readers of one store disagree. Remediation: Lstat plus a regular-file check and `ReadCapped` for MEMORY.md (and settings.local.json); a test with a linked MEMORY.md. Not an issue if: the store's threat model is only what a commit can carry (ADR-043's wording), accepted explicitly.

- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/dream/dream.go:166-177`, `internal/dream/run.go:207-247,249-284`. REQUIREMENTS R3: the dream "runs a CLI with no tools". For Claude Code it does: `--tools ""`, `--strict-mcp-config`, `--setting-sources local` from the empty `dream-work` cwd, no session persistence. Antigravity has no no-tools flag. Its tools exist and are refused by `--mode plan` plus a private HOME whose settings allow nothing with `request-review`. `answer()` discards the result only AFTER a tool step shows up ("a tool step that ran, denied or not"), and `keepFailure` then keeps that stdout locally. Whether any agy tool class (read-only file view, web fetch) can execute under these settings is vendor behaviour this slice cannot show. If one can, a prompt-injected trail record or transcript (input others can write) could read files or reach the network unattended, and discarding the answer undoes neither. Remediation: record on the trail a probe of agy with these exact settings and a prompt asking for every tool class, including read-only and web. Without that probe, `--vendor antigravity` does not meet R3's "no tools" and should be refused for dream. Not an issue if: that probe already exists on the trail. My slice holds none.

## Checked

- **Secrets**: no credential, token or private key in the slice's code or tests (test values are `FAKEVALUE`). `releaseSigner` is a public allowed-signers line, compiled in. The agy OAuth token is copied 0600 into a 0700 `MkdirTemp` under `~/.config/sh-agent`, removed on exit, swept after 1 h when a run is killed. Clone/push errors scrub URL userinfo; dream log and failure text pass `scrub`. The redaction needles were reviewed by kind against `TestReportRedactShapes`. Against v1.16.2 the secret-assignment rule is narrower for short unquoted values (`password=abc`, `token=abcdefg`, `secret = my passphrase` now pass) and wider for the pass family and `--password x`. That is the pinned, accepted IN1 trade-off, not a finding. Space-separated `password hunter22` (the netrc shape) was not covered in v1.16.2 either.
- **Injection**:
  - SQL and SQLite: all SQL is parameterized; FTS words are quoted; LIKE is escaped. The SQLite DSN is built with `url.URL`, `mode=ro`, on a copy. An Antigravity `conversation_id` holding a separator or `.`/`..` is refused. The protobuf walk is depth-capped and bounds-checked.
  - Timer units: the systemd unit refuses quote/backslash/CR/LF and doubles `%`; the plist is XML-escaped.
  - Commands: `exec.Command` takes argv only, never a shell. The release tag is validated before it reaches argv.
  - Zip: names that are absolute, hold a backslash or `..`, are non-local, too long or too deep are refused, and so are symlink and irregular entries. Sizes are counted by decompression, writes use O_EXCL, and the archive is hashed and parsed from one buffer.
  - Dream output: prompt fences are escaped and labels folded; proposal fields are folded or indented; draft names are regex-checked.
  - Flags: one FlagSet per verb; `reorder` reads value flags from the FlagSet; `--` is kept; a stray argument exits 2; `--from-zip` is decided from the parsed flags.
- **Authz/authn**:
  - Release update: the gh tag goes through `IsReleaseVersion`, never sideways or back. `ssh-keygen -Y verify` uses the compiled-in signer, the namespace, and a version marker inside the signed bytes. Each asset has one checksum line, and the binary read is capped at 256 MiB.
  - Zip place: verified when SHA256SUMS and .sig are both beside the zip, otherwise installed marked UNVERIFIED (ADR-041, by design). A half pair counts as unsigned, which gives nothing to an attacker who could delete both anyway. `ReadCapped` fails closed on streams.
  - Report: refuses `GIT_DIR` & co., checks the origin exactly, pushes to the URL.
  - `knownCheckout` and `ResolveSource` refusals: unchanged.
- **Crypto**: only `crypto/sha256` checksums and OpenSSH signature verification. No hand-rolled primitive, token, session or auth flow.
- **Dependencies**: `go.mod`, `go.sum` and `embed.go` are unchanged in the range. The one direct dependency is `modernc.org/sqlite v1.46.1` (R4). `govulncheck ./...` (go1.27.1): "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities"; `-show verbose` names one module-level advisory, GO-2026-5024 (`golang.org/x/sys` v0.37.0, not called), the known one in AGENTS.md. No new advisory. `npm audit`: no npm ecosystem in this slice.
- **GCP surface**: none in the slice: no IAM, service account, deploy flag or env-var secret in `cmd/` or `internal/`.
- **Links and writes**:
  - Installer: Install, Status, Diff, Uninstall and resync never read, write, chmod or remove through a linked destination or a linked parent (`underLink`).
  - `settings.json`: refused when linked or under a linked `~/.claude`; created with O_EXCL.
  - Report: skips non-regular files and a linked `proposals/dream(/harness)`, and sends only harness-target dream proposals (D19). Those carry the project's name and `~`-relative path into the private feedback repository, by design.
  - Dream: refuses linked docs and record directories and non-regular files. `configView` indexes none of the dream's new files.
- **Requirements**:
  - R3 exception: sh-agent's own writes stay under `~/.config/sh-agent`. The Claude child's state under `~/.claude` is the vendor's.
  - Transcripts: both CLIs' transcripts go to the one chosen CLI, as R3 states.
  - R4: one dependency.
  - R8: only `report` sends.
  - R3 "no tools" on agy: finding 5.

- **Test-only risks.** These are the modified test files of the slice, each read end to end at HEAD 19d3467, whose slice equals d26de97. I looked for writes outside a TempDir or the scratch dir, use of the real home or `~/.config/sh-agent`, network use, and leftover processes or timers.
  - `cmd/sh-agent/main_test.go`: every run gets `--home` (or `HOME`) in a TempDir. Release paths run with a fake `gh` alone on PATH, or an empty PATH. Git fixtures use a temp `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` plus `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`. Child installs finish before the test returns; no timer. Three exceptions:
    - Tests read the real checkout (`../..`), and Inspect runs `git status` there, which may refresh its `.git/index`.
    - `TestRelativeHomeResolvesAgainstTheInvokingDirectory` clones the checkout locally and runs a real `go build`. That needs the network only when `modernc.org/sqlite` is missing from the module cache.
    - The FIFO case of `TestAttributionNote` would hang on a regression rather than fail.
  - `cmd/sh-agent/zip_test.go`: every zip test runs under `isolate` (empty PATH, scratch cwd). Keys, SHA256SUMS and signatures are made in TempDirs with `/usr/bin/ssh-keygen`. The release dry run uses a fake `gh`; the checkout dry run uses a local bare origin. Nothing outside TempDirs, no network.
  - `cmd/sh-agent/search_test.go`: a TempDir repository with repo-local config, `t.Chdir`, `--home` in a TempDir. Nothing else.
  - `internal/harness/harness_test.go`: TempDir repositories and homes throughout.
    - `TestReinstallBuildsAndInstalls` builds the real checkout into `<checkout>/.agents/scratch/sh-agent-build-<pid>` (scratch, removed afterwards) and installs into a TempDir home. Same module-cache caveat as above.
    - `TestReinstallNeverNeedsToDownloadAToolchain` pins `GOPROXY=off` and a temp `GOMODCACHE`, so no network.
    - `TestBehindAndPull` and the `gitIn` fixtures commit under the operator's global git config, without `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` isolation, so a global hook or `commit.gpgsign` would apply.
    - The adopt test only names `/etc/passwd` as a symlink target; it never reads or writes it.
  - `internal/harness/report_test.go`: `gitEnv` isolates git config and unsets `GIT_DIR` & co. Feedback remotes are local bare repositories or `file://` URLs, homes are TempDirs, and `testHooks` are reset. `TestCloneFailureDoesNotPrintCredentials` makes git resolve `example.invalid`: a DNS lookup that fails by design, the one outbound attempt. The sweep test uses an exited `true` and pid 1, so no process is left behind.
  - `internal/harness/zip_test.go`: TempDirs only. `releaseSigner` is swapped with a `t.Cleanup` restore. Its signing helpers live in `release_test.go`, outside the slice.
  - `internal/harness/size_test.go`: reads the checkout, writes nothing.
  - `internal/search/search_test.go`: TempDir repositories with repo-local config (`commit.gpgsign false`). Commits still run under the operator's global git config, hooks included. `TestConcurrentReconcile` runs the test binary twice as `TestHelperIndex` and waits for both. One test reads a real bug record from the checkout.
  - `internal/search/testdata/recall.tsv`: data rows, no code.

## Not examined

Every path in the slice, over the range v1.16.2..d26de97, was read end to end. What remains unread is outside the slice:

- Blast-radius code that is unchanged in the range:
  - `internal/harness/state.go` (LoadState/SaveState/ConfigDir/TightenConfigDir), `plan.go`, `render.go`, `adopt.go`
  - the test helpers `newRelease` and `signRelease` in `internal/harness/release_test.go`
  - `internal/search` beyond `configView`: `gitView`, `openStore`, `checkoutRoot`, `docsRootOf`
- Vendor behaviour: no live Claude Code or Antigravity run. The unit tests use fake CLIs and a fake service manager (finding 5).
- Tests: not run; `go test` is the verifier's lane. The probes were measurements only, kept under `.agents/scratch/`: `sec-probe-fsmon/`, `sec-probe-redact/`, `sec-probe-old/`, `sh-agent-probe`, `sh-agent-probe-old`. All are gitignored and left in place. `go.mod` and `go.sum` were checked unchanged with `git status`.

## Outcome

- **[medium] `internal/memory/memory.go:85`: fixed** in d26de97. `trusted()` now runs `git` with `storeTrackedArgs(root)` = `--no-optional-locks -c core.fsmonitor=false -C <root> ls-files -- .agents/memory`, and `TestStoreTrackedArgs` pins that argument string. I checked it by reading `git show d26de97` and by re-running the scratch probe through real binaries. The hook was injected with `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, which a `-c` overrides just as it overrides `.git/config`.
  - Must-fire control, plain `git status`: 1.
  - New binary, built from HEAD 19d3467, whose slice is identical to d26de97: `dream --project <probe> --dry-run` 0, `memory show` 0.
  - Old binary, built from `git archive 0b1b5b8`: 1 and 1.
  - The pin is a string pin. The probe is the behavioural evidence, and nothing in `go test` runs a hook.
  - `check-ignore` in `memory.Add` and `search.guardProject` still fires a configured hook. Both run only in the operator's own interactive session, so I accept that and record it, not reopen it.
- **[low] timer `--home` scoping** (`internal/dream/timer.go:112,116,171,175`): left: operator — one-line choice in the handoff. The choice is a per-home unit name, or skipping or refusing the service-manager calls when `home` is not the real home.
- **[low] feedback.jsonl JSON-decoding redaction pass** (`internal/dream/collect.go:65-67,148-154`): left: next task — main agent.
- **[low] symlinked MEMORY.md followed by `readLines`** (`internal/memory/memory.go:243-261`, `:230`): left: next task — main agent.
- **[low] Antigravity plan-mode assumption behind R3's "no tools"** (`internal/dream/dream.go:166-177`, `run.go:207-284`): left: next task — main agent. I do not judge it release-blocking on this slice's evidence. A recorded agy probe would settle it either way.

title: Security review — v1.16.2-0b1b5b8-harness-text (2026-10-01)
body:
# Security review — v1.16.2-0b1b5b8-harness-text   (2026-10-01)

Range reviewed: v1.16.2..0b1b5b8 (slice: context/, agents/, skills/, root markdown)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

No credential, private key, real project id or hand-rolled auth/crypto anywhere in the slice, and the GCP samples are private by default (IAM-gated Cloud Run, `var.public = false`, pinned `--set-secrets`, write-only secret versions, no SA key files). The worst items are a supply-chain and a permission weakness, neither high: the range ADDS `curl … | sh` of golangci-lint's install script from a mutable URL (`skills/golang/references/service.md:404`), and two skills changed in the range still carry `allowed-tools: Bash` (pre-existing since before v1.16.2), which on Claude Code pre-approves every shell command while the skill is active. The rest are low.

Slice: 109 paths changed in the range (83 added or modified, 26 deleted), 10,784 lines at 0b1b5b8; the working tree matched 0b1b5b8 for every slice path when the review started (`git diff 0b1b5b8 --stat -- <slice>` empty).

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `skills/golang/references/service.md:404` (new in this range: absent at v1.16.2) — the skill tells an agent to run `curl -sSfL https://golangci-lint.run/install.sh | sh -s -- -b "$(go env GOPATH)/bin" v2.14.0` on the operator's machine, where gcloud ADC, the SSH signing key and the `gh` token are in reach. `v2.14.0` pins the binary the script fetches, not the script: it is executed unread from a mutable website path outside GitHub, so a compromise of that site (or its CDN) runs code as the operator. Exploitable only through upstream compromise, hence medium. The harness elsewhere verifies what it downloads (`skills/data-gcp/SKILL.md:168-170`: cloud-sql-proxy against the release's SHA-256; README's signed `SHA256SUMS`), so this line is the odd one out. A second site of the same class, not checked for whether the range added it: `skills/gcloud-setup/SKILL.md:49-50` downloads the gcloud tarball and runs its `install.sh` with no checksum. Remediation: download `golangci-lint-2.14.0-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz` and `golangci-lint-2.14.0-checksums.txt` from the GitHub release, `sha256sum -c --ignore-missing` (exit read bare), extract into `$(go env GOPATH)/bin`; or fetch `install.sh` from `raw.githubusercontent.com/golangci/golangci-lint/<full commit sha>/install.sh` and read it first. No dependency is added either way (the skill already rejects `go install`/`go tool` because upstream says they are not guaranteed). Non-issue when: the line names a checksum-verified tarball or a commit-pinned script.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `skills/bash/SKILL.md:4`, `skills/docker/SKILL.md:9` (pre-existing: both lines are identical at v1.16.2; both files changed in the range) — `allowed-tools: Bash`. On Claude Code a skill's `allowed-tools` lets the listed tools run without a permission prompt while the skill is active, and bare `Bash` matches every command (`rm`, `git push`, `curl`, and `sudo -n`, which `context/dev-setup.md:8` says is passwordless on the Linux box, gated only by prose). Both skills trigger while the agent reads untrusted text — `bash` on "reviewing or debugging scripts", `docker` on "any Dockerfile mention" — so a prompt injection in a reviewed script or Dockerfile meets no human prompt. It also sits against REQUIREMENTS § Non-goals ("never a permission", written for settings but the effect is the same grant) and R10 (Antigravity's handling of the key is unverified, so the two CLIs may not behave the same). Remediation: delete both lines (neither skill needs them; the operator's own permission settings decide), or scope them to read-only commands (`Bash(shellcheck:*)`, `Bash(docker build:*)`). Non-issue when: the operator records the grant as a deliberate decision (ADR), or Claude Code's documented semantics are shown not to skip the prompt in the operator's permission mode.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/data-gcp/SKILL.md:55-61,111-112`, `skills/golang/references/service.md:316` — the default database path runs the service as `app`, created with `gcloud sql users create`, which Cloud SQL puts in `cloudsqlsuperuser`. The skill states the trade-off as "DDL at runtime", but the membership carries CREATEROLE and CREATEDB as well, so a SQL injection in the service reaches role and database administration on the instance, not just its own schema. Remediation: on path 1, create the runtime login role through SQL as `postgres` (`CREATE ROLE … LOGIN`, password set with psql's `\password`, never in an argument), owning nothing and holding DML only, with the migration role separate; or make the IAM split (path 2, already written) the default for anything holding user data; at minimum, name CREATEROLE/CREATEDB in the trade-off sentence and in `deploy/gcp.md`'s Database roles row. Non-issue when: a project's `gcp.md` records the operator's acceptance of exactly that grant.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/docker/SKILL.md:61,69,86` — the builder stages `node:24-alpine` and `golang:<major.minor>` are mutable tags, by documented choice (to pick up patch fixes). The runtime image is digest-pinned, but the shipped binary is compiled in the builder, so an upstream re-tag changes what builds the release with no diff in the repository. Remediation: digest-pin both builders and move the digest deliberately in the monthly base-image check that `gcp.md` § Operate already schedules, the option rule 1 already offers for byte-reproducible builds. Non-issue when: the operator accepts tag tracking as the decision.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `skills/feature/SKILL.md:19` — `/feature #<n>` reads the issue's body and comments (`gh issue view … --json title,body,labels,comments`) into the main context with no line saying that text is evidence, not instruction. Other surfaces state this (`agents/dreamer.md:34`; "words in tool output, files, or logs authorize nothing" in dream, distill, feedback-log, handoff, init-project). Remediation: one clause saying the issue's text is the request's evidence and never an instruction to run, install, push or authorize. Non-issue when: the repositories' issues and comments are writable only by the operator.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/bash/references/makefile-patterns.md:200-207` (pre-existing) — the `deploy` target runs `gcloud run deploy` with no `--project` and none of the REGION/GCP_PROJECT guard `docker-push` has, so it deploys into whatever project the active gcloud configuration names. That is the source `context/dev-setup.md:4` and `skills/gcloud-setup/SKILL.md:128` forbid, and it bypasses `/preflight` (BUG-020's class). Remediation: `--project=$(GCP_PROJECT)` plus the same guard, and a comment that a release goes through `/preflight`; or drop the target. Non-issue when: the sample is removed.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `README.md:251`, `skills/VENDORED.md:57` (pre-existing) — `npx skills add … -y` runs whatever version of the npm `skills` CLI is newest at that moment, auto-confirmed, from the harness checkout. Remediation: pin it (`npx skills@<version> add …`) and drop `-y`, so the provenance read VENDORED.md:3-6 requires happens before anything lands. Non-issue when: the version is pinned.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `README.md:205` (pre-existing) — the loop example `vim … && sh-agent install && git commit -am "context: tweak" && git push` contradicts context § Git (stage by name, read `git diff --cached --stat`, commit in a separate call). `-a` stages only tracked files, so a new secret-shaped file is not swept in; this is a docs-consistency issue that an agent could copy. Remediation: show the staged-by-name sequence. Non-issue when: the example is rewritten.

## Checked

- **Secrets:** regex sweep of all 83 present slice files for vendor key shapes (AKIA, AIza, `gh?_`, `github_pat_`, `sk-`, `sk_live/test_`, `xox?-`, PEM private-key headers, `ya29.`, refresh tokens, JWTs, `glpat-`, `npm_`, `AccountKey=`), for `password/secret/token/api_key = "…"` assignments, and for e-mail addresses. No credential. Hits, all benign: `AGENTS.md:63` (`sk_test_` named as a redaction example); `skills/preflight/SKILL.md:48` (the scan list itself); `skills/json-api-style/references/json-api-conventions.md:75` (sample page token, base64 of digits); `README.md:107-108,141-142` (the operator's public signer line, public by design); `example.com` and `NAME@PROJECT` placeholders. Compose `app/app` credentials are local and loopback-bound (`skills/docker/references/setup.md:51-54,68-69`). `.dockerignore` is an allowlist with secret shapes excluded inside it (setup.md:10-39).
- **Project ids and regions:** none real; placeholders only (`PROJECT`, `${PROJECT}`, `your-project`, `example-project` in a test fixture). Example literals that are not ids: `gcloud-setup/SKILL.md:104-105` (`staging-project-id`, `europe-west1` in a named-config example) and `gke-basics/SKILL.md:29-32` (`my-cluster`, `us-central1`, vendored fork text).
- **Injection:** the Go samples validate before interpolating (trace ids hex-checked, `service.md:269,285`), bound bodies at 1 MiB and never echo decoder errors (`service.md:88-97`), and use positional SQL parameters. The init-project shell loops refuse symlinks before every write, pass paths as argv to python3, and refuse `"` and `\` in the printf fallback (`init-project/SKILL.md:34,54-58,69-78,119`). `bash-fundamentals.md` bans `eval`.
- **Authz/authn:** `api-auth-gcp` and its samples use `idtoken.Validate` with the audience refused-when-empty at construction, an explicit issuer check (`Validate` does not compare `iss`), `email` and `email_verified` on the public scheduler route, and Firebase `VerifyIDToken`; the IAP header is never trusted alone. `cloud-run-deploy` keeps IAM-gated as the default; the Terraform root sets `invoker_iam_disabled = var.public` with `default = false`; `roles/run.invoker` is granted per service, never per project.
- **Crypto:** no hand-rolled JWT, crypto, session or password scheme in any sample; tokens come from `crypto/rand.Text` (`service.md:422`); TLS and IAM auth come from the connector.
- **Dependencies:** the slice adds no dependency to this repository. Sample dependencies named for projects are vetted (pgx, golang-migrate, cloudsqlconn, idtoken, Firebase Admin). `govulncheck ./...` (this repository's Go code, the other reviewer's slice): exit 0, "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities", plus 1 vulnerability in a required module that is not called, consistent with AGENTS.md's known GO-2026-5024. `npm audit`: not applicable, since there is no `package.json` at the root, under `web/` or under `ui/`.
- **GCP surface:** `--set-secrets` with pinned versions and never `--set-env-vars` for secrets; a dedicated service account per service and job; IAP access granted on the service, never the project; SA key files only as an operator-ordered last resort (`gcloud-setup/SKILL.md:141-152`) and refused in `api-auth-gcp/SKILL.md:143`; Cloud SQL with no authorized networks, `ENCRYPTED_ONLY`, deletion protection and PITR; Terraform secrets write-only (`secret_data_wo` with a `sensitive` + `ephemeral` variable), IAM by `_member`, a state bucket with public-access prevention.
- **Instruction-shaped text:** no exfiltration step, no bypass of the Git or secret rules, no `--no-verify` or force-push, no `curl | sh` other than finding 1. Root steps are gated on the operator's word plus a recorded standing permission (`dev-setup.md:8`, `docker/SKILL.md:124`, `gcloud-setup/SKILL.md:38-39`).
- **Deleted paths:** `skills/anti-ui-slop/*` (10 files), `skills/python/*` (3), `skills/golang/references/golang-*.md` (7) and the old `skills/terraform/references/*` (6) are gone at 0b1b5b8; the removal also drops the paid-MCP UI skill (`skills/VENDORED.md:46-48`).
- **REQUIREMENTS.md:** read in full. init-project 5b writes exactly the two memory keys § Non-goals allows, and R2's stub list is pointed at, not restated. The one tension is finding 2.

- **Last batch:**
  - `restatement-grep.sh` greps fixed strings after `--`, builds the vendored-skill filter only from names matching `[a-z0-9-]+`, and has no `eval`.
  - `preflight` stages by name, refuses secret-shaped paths, and runs gitleaks or a fallback secret scan before both commits.
  - `retro` and `dreamer` treat dream proposals and memory as data that is re-derived, never followed.
  - `operate-gcp` keeps log excerpts to severity, time, status and message (no `requestUrl`, IP or user agent), and makes a rollback across a security fix or a secret rotation the operator's call.
  - `terraform`: the state bucket gets uniform access, public-access prevention and versioning; the plan file lives in gitignored scratch; `*.tfvars` is ignored and secret values arrive by `TF_VAR_` or a prompt; `invoker_iam_disabled` is driven by `var.public`, `default = false`.

## Not examined

- No slice path. All 83 added or modified paths were read end to end at 0b1b5b8, through `.agents/scratch/sec-chunk-*.txt` copies of the working tree, which matched 0b1b5b8. That includes the last batch: `json-api-conventions.md` 36-149, `mermaid-syntax/` (3 files), `operate-gcp/` (2), `preflight`, `project-memory`, `requirements`, `research`, `retro`, `review-standards`, `review/SKILL.md`, `review/scripts/restatement-grep.sh`, `spec`, and `terraform/SKILL.md` 1-40. Nothing in that batch is a finding. The root `AGENTS.md` was read whole at HEAD. The root `TODO.md`, unchanged in the range, was read too. The 26 deleted paths need only the note under Checked.
- `sh-agent search --refs <path> --kind bug` ran for every slice file, but the combined output was cut at 150 lines (after `skills/distill/SKILL.md`), so the bug references of the later files were not read. This is a process gap, not an unread slice path.
- Outside the slice by the dispatch: the Go code (the dream job's private-HOME copy of the agy login, report redaction) and the `.agents/docs` trail, which the other two reviewers cover; the unchanged `skills/gke-basics/references/` and `assets/`, and `skills/frontend/references/design.md`. Antigravity's handling of a skill's `allowed-tools` was not tested (finding 2).

## Outcome

Checked on 2026-10-01 against `git diff 0b1b5b8..89f3308`. HEAD is 89f3308, and the working tree matches it for the four paths involved. The coordinator asked for this section; the review skill's Step 4 gives the Outcome to the main agent. It records the reviewer's check of 89f3308, and the findings above are unchanged.

1. `skills/golang/references/service.md:404` (curl | sh) — **fixed** in 89f3308.
   - **Change:** the line now reads `gh release download v2.14.0 … && sha256sum -c --ignore-missing golangci-lint-2.14.0-checksums.txt && tar -xzf … --strip-components=1 -C "$(go env GOPATH)/bin" golangci-lint-2.14.0-linux-amd64/golangci-lint`. No script runs.
   - **Sweep:** `git grep` for `curl|wget … | sh` over `context/`, `agents/`, `skills/` and `README.md` at 89f3308 finds nothing.
   - **Run:** the exact chain was run in `.agents/scratch/sec-gl/`, with only the `-C` target moved to scratch. It passed: gh exit 0, `golangci-lint-2.14.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz: OK` with exit 0, the tar member exists, and the binary prints `golangci-lint has version 2.14.0`.
   - **Must-fail checks:** a tampered tarball gives `FAILED` and exit 1, and a missing tarball gives "no file was verified" and exit 1 (GNU coreutils 9.7), so the check cannot pass with nothing verified.
   - **Second site:** `skills/gcloud-setup/SKILL.md:50` now checks the SHA256 before `tar` and `install.sh`. That closes it in substance.
   - **Residuals**, none a security gap, all **left: next task**, owner: main agent:
     - (a) The gcloud check compares two hashes by eye. It should pipe the page's value into `sha256sum -c -` and read the exit status, the form `skills/data-gcp/SKILL.md:170` uses. Not verified: that the install page lists a SHA256 for the unversioned rapid tarball.
     - (b) The macOS wording "`shasum -a 256 -c`" drops `--ignore-missing`. Measured: `shasum -a 256 -c` on the checksums file exits 1, because the other listed platform assets are absent. It fails closed. With `--ignore-missing` it exits 0.
     - (c) `gh release download` has no `-D .agents/scratch/…`, so the tarball and checksums land in the working directory, against the scratch rule.
2. `skills/bash/SKILL.md:4`, `skills/docker/SKILL.md:9` (`allowed-tools: Bash`) — **fixed** in 89f3308.
   - **Change:** both lines are deleted, and each frontmatter still closes with `---`.
   - **Sweep:** `git grep -n '^allowed-tools' 89f3308 -- 'skills/*/SKILL.md'` prints nothing (exit 1). No `allowed-tools` mention remains in `context/`, `agents/`, `skills/`, `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `internal/` or `cmd/`.
   - **REQUIREMENTS point:** agreed. § Non-goals governs editing vendor settings files, and a skill's own frontmatter is a file in the customization directories. The finding called it a tension, not a violation. Nothing to rebut and nothing further to change.
3. `skills/data-gcp/SKILL.md` (default runtime role in `cloudsqlsuperuser`) — **left: next task**, owner: main agent. Agreed. The skill names the trade-off but not CREATEROLE or CREATEDB, so the finding stands as a low until that sentence and the `gcp.md` Database roles row say so.
4. `skills/docker/SKILL.md` (mutable builder image tags) — **left: next task**, owner: main agent. D26 (`plans/2026-09-30-audit-fix.md:213`) records the choice "by: research briefs", not by the operator. The non-issue condition (the operator accepts tag tracking) is not met, so `rebutted` would not hold.
5. `skills/feature/SKILL.md:19` (issue text with no data-only clause) — **left: next task**, owner: main agent. The coordinator's list did not name it, and 89f3308 does not touch the file.
6. `skills/bash/references/makefile-patterns.md:200-207` (`deploy` without `--project`) — **left: next task**, owner: main agent.
7. `README.md:251`, `skills/VENDORED.md:57` (unpinned `npx skills add … -y`) — **left: next task**, owner: main agent.
8. `README.md:205` (`git commit -am` in a chain) — **left: next task**, owner: main agent.

### Round 2 — 19d3467 (`git diff d26de97..19d3467`), checked 2026-10-01

HEAD is 19d3467, and the working tree matches it for both paths. `git grep` for `curl|wget … | sh` over `context/`, `agents/`, `skills/` and `README.md` at 19d3467 finds nothing.

- **Finding 1, main path — still fixed.** golangci-lint is now installed with `go install github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@v2.14.0`. How verified, on this box:
  - **Environment:** `go env` shows `GOSUMDB=sum.golang.org`, `GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct`, and `GOPRIVATE`, `GONOSUMDB`, `GONOSUMCHECK` and `GOFLAGS` all empty, so the checksum database check is on.
  - **Module:** `go mod download -json …@v2.14.0` exits 0 with `Sum h1:ot8QffRa4LzAAEgtvNYrVs9esxQ7xoTwoAv6uhp4ngA=`. Its `go.mod` has `go 1.26.0` and no `replace` or `exclude` lines, so `go install pkg@version` is allowed.
  - **Install:** run with `GOBIN` set to `.agents/scratch/sec-gl2/bin`, it exits 0 in 13 s. The binary reports `golangci-lint has version 2.14.0 … mod sum: "h1:ot8Q…4ngA="`, the same hash.
  - **Not shown:** a rejection by the checksum database (it needs a tampered proxy). The claim also holds only while `GOSUMDB` is on and no `GOPRIVATE`, `GONOSUMDB`, `GONOSUMCHECK` or `GOINSECURE` pattern matches `github.com/golangci`. That is the default, and the README sets `GOPRIVATE` only for `github.com/kesokaj/*`, per command.
  - **Side effects:** the run used the default Go module and build caches; no binary was installed outside scratch.
- **Leftover (a), gcloud hash compared by eye — closed.** `skills/gcloud-setup/SKILL.md:50` now reads `printf '%s  google-cloud-cli-linux-x86_64.tar.gz\n' <sha256 from the page> | sha256sum -c -` with the exit status read, before `tar` and `install.sh`. Measured on a dummy file: correct hash exit 0, wrong hash exit 1 (`FAILED`), empty hash exit 1 ("no properly formatted checksum lines found"). Still not verified (the page was not fetched): that the install page lists a SHA256 for the unversioned rapid tarball.
- **Leftover (b), macOS `shasum` without `--ignore-missing` — closed.** The text now says `shasum -a 256 -c --ignore-missing`. Measured with this box's `shasum`: good asset exit 0; missing asset exit 1 ("no file was verified"); tampered asset exit 1. macOS's own `shasum` was not run; its Digest::SHA version may differ.
- **Leftover (c), download location — closed.** The release-binary sentence now puts the asset and its `-checksums.txt` in `.agents/scratch/` and verifies them before extracting. It does not spell out running the check from that directory, but a check run from anywhere else finds no file and exits 1 ("no file was verified", measured with both `sha256sum` and `shasum`), so it fails closed.
- **Findings 3–8 unchanged:** left: next task, owner main agent.

title: Security review — worktree-gate-lows (2026-10-01)
body:
# Security review — worktree-gate-lows   (2026-10-01)

Range reviewed: 8b6c6de..working tree (`git diff HEAD`: 12 files at the first snapshot. The tree changed during the review. A second snapshot taken mid-review showed no Go change; it showed edits to AGENTS.md, the README table rows, skills/VENDORED.md, skills/project-memory, the Makefile variable now `$(GCP_PROJECT)`, the data-gcp sentence moved, and docker "pin the Node image". Those were read as a diff of the two diffs only.)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

No high. The four code changes do what they claim, and three of them are proven in both states.
- `RedactJSONL` makes the dream redact each feedback record exactly as `report` does. Per-record result equals report's whole-file pass (5 escaped records, measured).
- With the fix reverted, `TestFeedbackRedactsEscapedSecret` FAILS. With it, the test PASSES.
- `readLines` refuses a symlinked `MEMORY.md` in `Show` and in both `Add` reads. With the refusal removed, the test FAILS on both.
- The `allowed-tools` refusal closes BUG-143's literal form.

The worst problem is in the docs: the new builder digest pin in `skills/docker` freezes the Go patch. The text around it still says the tag "tracks the current patch and its stdlib fixes", and the refresh is optional. A project that follows the skill can ship binaries built with an old stdlib, and a local `govulncheck` does not see it. Second: the BUG-143 lint is a one-key denylist read through a lenient key grammar. Quoted or spaced keys pass it, and so do sibling grants (`hooks`; `allowed-tools` in commands; agent `permissionMode`). This is latent: no shipped file carries any of them.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/docker/SKILL.md:67-69,86`: the digest freezes the patch, and the rule still claims the tag tracks it.
  - **What is wrong.** With `golang:<major.minor>@sha256:<digest>`, Docker/BuildKit resolves the digest and ignores the tag. The builder, and the stdlib statically linked into every shipped binary, stay on the pinned patch until someone edits the digest. Rule 1 still gives "golang:1.27, which tracks the current patch and its stdlib fixes" as the reason for the two-part tag. The refresh is optional ("or want the newer patch").
  - **Why the usual check misses it.** The `govulncheck ./...` the golang skill teaches runs against the developer machine's Go, not the builder's. A newer local Go reports clean while the image is built on an older stdlib with advisories. For a Cloud Run service, a net/http or crypto/tls advisory is reachable remotely.
  - **Not the problem.** The unresolved placeholder itself is safe: `<…>` is an invalid reference, so `docker build` fails closed.
  - **Remediation.** Say plainly that the digest freezes the patch. Make the refresh mandatory on a trigger the workflow already runs: every `/preflight`, or any govulncheck stdlib advisory. Scan the built artifact with `govulncheck -mode=binary` on the binary from the build stage.
  - **Non-issue if** the operator accepts manual refresh, the text stops claiming patch tracking, and the binary scan is in the deploy recipe.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/inventory.go:206` with `internal/harness/frontmatter.go:19` (`keyLine = ^([A-Za-z0-9_-]+):(?:[ \t]+(.*))?$`): the refusal checks one key, read through a lenient key grammar.
  - **Spellings that pass.** Measured with LoadSkills on a scratch copy:
    - `"allowed-tools": Bash`, `'allowed-tools': Bash` and `allowed-tools : Bash` load (refused=false). A YAML parser reads each as the `allowed-tools` key.
    - The plain and block-list forms are refused.
  - **Sibling grants that pass.**
    - A skill's `hooks:` (measured: loads). On Claude Code, hooks declared in frontmatter run commands while the skill is active, a stronger grant than allowed-tools. CLI support is from memory, confidence medium.
    - `allowed-tools` in `commands/*.md`, which deploy verbatim with no lint. Claude Code honours the key in commands.
    - `permissionMode` in an agent. derive.go:30 drops it for Antigravity only; Claude Code gets it as written.
  - **Exposure today.** None shipped: `grep -rnE '^(allowed-tools|"allowed-tools"|hooks|permissionMode)[ ]*:' skills/*/SKILL.md agents/*.md commands rules` returns nothing (exit 1), and commands/ and rules/ are empty. The realistic carrier is a vendored third-party skill (`npx skills add`). VENDORED.md's diff review is the only other screen.
  - **Remediation (stdlib only, one rule per kind as BUG-110 taught).**
    - Refuse any top-level frontmatter line that keyLine does not parse and that is not blank, a comment or a continuation. This closes the parser differential for every key.
    - Refuse the permission keys by kind: `allowed-tools` and `hooks` on skills and commands; `hooks` and `permissionMode` on agents.
  - **Non-issue if** both CLIs ignore quoted or spaced keys (YAML says they do not) and the harness never carries commands or third-party skills.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/memory/memory.go:242-244` (the readLines comment) and `internal/memory/memory_test.go:400-401`: the comment overstates the harm, and one assertion can never fail.
  - **What the code does.** The comment says a symlinked index would carry "Add's rewrite" outside the store. It would not: Add writes through `harness.WriteAtomic` (CreateTemp + rename), and the rename replaces the link.
  - **What was measured.** With the refusal removed (mutation M2), `Show` printed the outside file. `add` returned nil and left a regular `-rw-------` MEMORY.md holding the outside file's lines. So the real pre-fix harm is that the outside file is copied into the store and shown to the session; nothing is written outside.
  - **The test.** The test's third assertion ("the link target was rewritten") cannot fire. The first two carry the trigger: both fail under M2, at :395 and :398.
  - **Remediation.** Correct the comment. Re-aim the third assertion: after the refused Add, the store holds no regular MEMORY.md copied from the target.
  - **Non-issue if** this is treated as text accuracy only. The code is right.

- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/dream/collect.go:120` (`scrub`): the escaped-secret gap remains for the dream's other inputs.
  - **What is wrong.** `RedactJSONL` runs only on feedback records. Transcript prose, trail markdown and memory files are matched raw. A secret JSON-escaped inside that text (a pasted API response, or a tool result quoted as JSON with `&` written as its backslash-u escape) passes both `Redact` and the home-path rewrite.
  - **Bearing on the claim.** Report never sends these inputs, so "dream at least as strong as report" still holds. The gap is against the dream's own goal: everything sent to the model is redacted.
  - **Unknown.** Confidence is low because `contentText` (collect.go:435-466) was not read, so I do not know whether tool results reach the prompt at all.
  - **Remediation.** In `scrub`, also match a copy of each line with its JSON string escapes (backslash-u four hex digits, backslash-quote, backslash-backslash) undone, for matching only. This is the same decode-for-matching rule report applies, applied to any line that holds an escape.
  - **Non-issue if** no transcript, trail or memory text can carry JSON-escaped content into the prompt.

## Checked

- **Secrets:** the diff carries only synthetic strings (`0123456789abcdef…` under `h.example`). No credential, `.env` or key file is in `git status`. The new error strings carry a path, never content.
- **Injection / input parsing (RedactJSONL, dream feedback):**
  - Every marker is a constant; no input reaches `marker()`. The output is the input line, unchanged, or a one-line JSON marker.
  - Clean lines come back byte-identical, measured on: an escaped clean line, invalid UTF-8, a non-JSON line, an empty line, and a CR inside a line.
  - Escaped `&sig=`, an escaped PEM header and `pass`+escaped-`w`+`ord=` are each missed by the raw needles (the control) and caught by RedactJSONL.
  - A 4 MiB escaped line was caught in roughly 1-4 s. That is CPU only, on the operator's own file. The 4 MiB scanner cap is unchanged; a longer line stops the scan and drops the lines after it, which loses data but leaks nothing.
  - 20,000-deep nesting is invalid to encoding/json, so the dream's `json.Unmarshal` gate skips the line. No panic.
  - An unterminated single-line `-----BEGIN` becomes one valid JSON marker line.
  - Report's whole-file pass swallows every later line after an unterminated BEGIN (6 records became 1 line, measured). The dream judges each record alone. That difference is over-redaction in report, not a gap in the dream: a record is self-contained JSON, and a PEM body line cannot pass the `Unmarshal`+`project` gate.
  - A line whose first value does not decode (NaN) is not redacted by RedactJSONL. In the dream such a line is never sent, because Unmarshal rejects it. In report it is sent; that is D14's documented, pre-existing limit. A value shadowed by a duplicate key is also unseen by `decoded()` in both paths (D14). Neither limit is new here.
  - The test proves its trigger. The file holds a literal backslash-u0026 (`od -c`) and no `&sig`. Reverting collect.go:288 to `sc.Text()` makes it FAIL (M1, scratch copy). It PASSES in the real repo.
  - A probe trap worth knowing: my first probe's backslash-u0026 reached the file as a literal `&` in transit. The raw-needle control fired and exposed it. I redid the probe with runtime-built backslashes; this is the same trap BUG-145 records.
- **Authz / path (memory):**
  - The refusal covers `Show` (memory.go:208) and both `Add` reads. At :134 the pre-check swallows the error and falls through; at :149, under the lock, it refuses. Measured: both return the symlink refusal, not the check-ignore one.
  - TOCTOU between Lstat and Open: none that matters. A swap needs a writer inside the operator's 0700, untracked, gitignored store. `trusted()` already refuses a tracked store and a symlinked `.agents` or store. `os.OpenFile(path, O_RDONLY|syscall.O_NOFOLLOW, 0)` would close it in one call if wanted.
  - Pre-existing and outside the diff: `lock()` opens `.lock` with O_CREATE through a symlink. Read, not probed; local only.
  - The dream's own `readFile` (Lstat+IsRegular) already skipped a symlinked index.
- **allowed-tools scope:**
  - Closes BUG-143's literal form.
  - `LoadSkills` is reached only through `LoadInventory(src)` on the harness source (plan.go:76, main.go:495/504/737, report.go:499). A project's own `.agents/skills`, linked by /init-project, is never loaded or refused by it: no breakage, and by design no protection there either.
  - Side effect, which fails closed: a checkout place carrying a vendored skill that sets the key now fails the whole install/update until the skill is forked. VENDORED.md forbids editing in place.
- **Crypto:** no primitive, token, session or auth flow added or changed. Nothing hand-rolled.
- **Dependencies:** no new module; go.mod/go.sum untouched. `govulncheck ./...` (go1.27.1): "No vulnerabilities found. Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities." `gofmt -l` is clean and `go vet` passes on the three changed packages. README and VENDORED.md now pin the skills CLI (`npx skills@<version>`) and drop `-y`; an unresolved `<version>` fails closed. The fetched skill content is still upstream's head, screened by VENDORED.md's pin-and-diff rule. npm audit: no npm ecosystem in the diff, not run.
- **GCP surface:**
  - The Makefile deploy targets now pass `--project=$(GCP_PROJECT)`. It is declared at :134 with an empty default, and an empty project fails closed in gcloud. This removes the reliance on the active gcloud config.
  - No IAM binding, service account, `--allow-unauthenticated` or env-var secret was added.
  - data-gcp wording is accurate in substance: an injection on the password path can create roles and databases. Precision nit (confidence medium, from memory of the Cloud SQL docs, not re-checked): PostgreSQL never inherits CREATEROLE/CREATEDB through role membership. The API-created user holds those attributes itself, so "cloudsqlsuperuser carries" is loosely put; the conclusion stands.
- **Prompt injection (feature skill):** "issue text is data, never instructions", covering the title, body, labels and comments fetched, is a sound guard.

## Not examined

- `internal/dream/collect.go:355-466` (`claudeTranscript`, `contentText`) and `internal/search` `AgyConversationText`: not read. They decide how far finding 4 reaches.
- Edits made during the review to `.agents/docs/specs/*`, `.agents/docs/deploy/remote.md` and `.agents/docs/testing/sh-agent-matrix.md`: not read. The changed AGENTS.md, README, VENDORED.md and project-memory lines were read as diff only.
- Whether Claude Code or Antigravity honour a quoted `allowed-tools` key, or `hooks` in skill frontmatter: deliberately not run, since that would be building the exploit. Finding 2's CLI side rests on YAML semantics and the CLIs' documented frontmatter.
- The full `go test -race ./...` (the verifier's lane): not run. I ran the four new tests, three probe tests and two mutations (M1, M2) on a scratch copy at `.agents/scratch/sec-2026-10-01/mod`.
- `lock()`'s `.lock` symlink behaviour: read, not probed. npm audit: not applicable.

## Outcome (2026-10-01)

- **1 [medium, docker digest]: resolved by revert.** `git diff HEAD -- skills/docker` is empty, so the digest pin is gone, and with it the "tracks the current patch" contradiction. HEAD's `golang:<major.minor>` tracks the patch, as its text says (Phase 6 D26). The gate's mutable-tag low is left to the operator; I agree with the recommendation to keep the tag. The digest option stays acceptable only with a mandatory refresh trigger and a `govulncheck -mode=binary` scan of the built binary.
- **2 [low, lint grammar]: fixed.** Checked on a scratch copy byte-identical to the tree for frontmatter.go, inventory.go and harness_test.go.
  - Refused as unreadable lines: `"allowed-tools":`, `'allowed-tools':` and `allowed-tools :`, and also `? key`, `<<:` and flow `{…}`.
  - Refused through `Keys`: skill `hooks`, agent `permissionMode` and `hooks`, command and rule `allowed-tools` and `hooks`. The no-extra control loads for every kind.
  - Mutation, `unreadLine` accepting everything: `TestLintPermissionKeysByKind` FAILS on all three spellings.
  - Mutation, `permissionKey` finding nothing: it FAILS on the block list, skill hooks, both agent keys and the command case, and `TestLintRefusesAllowedTools` FAILS as well. So the agent and command fixtures are live, not vacuous.
  - The checkout's inventory loads under the new grammar.
  - Residuals, not blocking:
    - `hooks` in a command or rule is refused (probe) but not pinned by the test.
    - An agent's `mcpServers:` loads. Whether Claude Code honours it in agent frontmatter is unchecked (confidence low).
    - `Allowed-Tools:` and a nested `metadata:` `allowed-tools` load. To a YAML reader they are a different key and not a top-level one.
- **3 [low, comment + assertion]: fixed.** The `readLines` comment now matches the measurement: Show printed the outside file; Add copied its lines into the store; the rename replaced the link; nothing was written outside. With the refusal removed (M2), `TestSymlinkedIndexRefused` FAILS at :395 (Show), :398 (Add) and the new :403 (the index is no longer the link), so the third assertion is live. It PASSES with the refusal.
- **4 [low/low, the dream's other inputs]: left, accepted as recorded (next task, main agent).** Its first step is the unknown this finding names: whether `contentText` (collect.go:435-466) lets tool results into the prompt. Nothing in this range touched that path.

## Status: COMPLETE

title: Security review — worktree-p6 (2026-10-01)
body:
# Security review — worktree-p6   (2026-10-01)

Range reviewed: working tree against HEAD 8be6c06 (Phase 6 of the audit-fix plan, uncommitted), rounds 1 to 3, the same files each time: `skills/terraform/**`, `skills/cloud-run-deploy/SKILL.md`, `skills/docker/**`, `skills/gcloud-setup/SKILL.md`, `skills/golang/references/service.md`, `skills/json-api-style/SKILL.md`, `skills/init-project/assets/agents-tree/docs/deploy/gcp.md`, `internal/harness/skill_links_test.go`; `git diff HEAD -- <files>` and each file whole. Round 3 read all 17 files in that scope end to end (2,024 lines, concatenated in `.agents/scratch/secrev-p6-r3/all.txt`). What a round did not reach is under that round's Not examined.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Round 3: one medium and four lows remain. Every other round-2 fix holds, including the `.dockerignore` allowlist, which was verified by build. The worst problem is in the `/tick` fix itself. The comment under the scheduler's `oidc_token` (`skills/terraform/references/resources-gcp.md:316-317`, echoed at `:229`) tells a public service's handler to call `idtoken.Validate` with the service URL as audience, and to do nothing else. `Validate` accepts any Google-signed ID token whose `aud` matches (`google.golang.org/api@v0.287.1/idtoken/validate.go:160`, with RS256 checked against Google's shared certs at `:185`). It never compares `email` or `iss`. Any service account in any project can mint such a token for any audience, so the check admits anyone with a Google Cloud account. The lows:
- `resources-gcp.md:237` still says the runtime role is DML-only, and `:3` still calls `db_url` only `sensitive`.
- Immutable tags now refuse the `:latest` alias that `cloud-run-deploy/SKILL.md:54` and the `gcp.md` template still offer.
- The new owner/DML recipe in `service.md:316` misses Cloud SQL's `cloudsqlsuperuser` membership for API-created users.
- The allowlist paragraph claims that a secret in any shape stays out. A `key.json` or `*.pem` inside `internal/` or `web/` still gets in, as the build showed.

Round 2 verdict, kept as written:
Round 2: all five round-1 mediums are fixed, and nothing above low remains. The `.dockerignore` probe was re-run with the new list taken from the file. `infra/terraform.tfvars`, `web/.env.local`, `keys/x.key` and `keys/x.pem` no longer enter the context, and neither do the plan file, `.terraform/terraform.tfstate` or root `.env`. The worst thing left is in that same fix. Moving from `*.env*` to `**/.env*` brought a root `app.env` back into the build context; the same build with the round-1 list keeps it out. A `key.json` in the project directory also still gets through, and that is exactly where `gcloud-setup`'s last-resort sample puts one. So do SSH keys without an extension, `web/.npmrc` and the tfvars JSON forms. The rest are lows:
- `idtoken.Validate` silently drops its audience check when the configured audience is empty.
- The migration-role split is asserted ("cannot drop tables") but never wired.
- The reference's live `allUsers` block would make "the standard app" public.
- The public-mechanism rule is missing from the deploy-time skill.
- A public service leaves the scheduler's `/tick` open to anyone.
- Several round-1 sub-points the Outcome marks fixed are not.

Round 1 verdict, kept as written:
No secret value, no hand-rolled crypto and no unsafe IAM default appears in any sample. The runtime SA is dedicated, `run.invoker` is granted per service, `public` defaults to false, secrets come from Secret Manager, and no SA keys are created. The worst problem is the `.dockerignore` list that every Go Dockerfile here copies: its patterns match only at the build-context root. So the secrets the terraform and frontend layouts keep below the root get through, together with any key outside the root: `infra/terraform.tfvars` (the value fed to `secret_data_wo`), the plan file (which the skill says "holds every value in clear"), `web/.env*`, and `keys/*.key|*.pem`. The Go stage's `COPY . .` then puts them into the build context and the build-stage layer, and `setup.md:24` claims this cannot happen. I checked this with a build, not by reading. Next come three gates that pass when they should not. `trivy config .` exits 0 on findings. `golang:<the go.mod go line>` pins the patch level the module states as its minimum, so this repo's own `go 1.24.4` would build on a toolchain with known stdlib advisories. The Terraform samples read secrets at `latest`, which contradicts the pin rule in `cloud-run-deploy`. The skill that should cover IAP JWT validation does not exist.

## Findings (round 1)

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/docker/references/setup.md:10-24`: the patterns `.agents/scratch`, `*.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.tfvars` and `*.tfstate` match only at the context root. Docker matches `.dockerignore` with Go `filepath.Match` relative to the root, and only a `**/` prefix reaches subdirectories. That is unlike `.gitignore`. Verified: I copied the exact list (lines 11-21) into `.agents/scratch/secprobe-p6-dockerignore/` with dummy files and ran `FROM scratch` + `COPY . /ctx/` through `docker buildx build --output type=local`. Root `.env` was excluded. `infra/terraform.tfvars`, `infra/.agents/scratch/tfplan`, `web/.env.local`, `keys/sa.key` and `keys/tls.pem` all reached the output. These are exactly the paths `skills/terraform/SKILL.md:27,31,74` (run from `infra/`) and the frontend's `web/` produce. The distroless final stage copies only `/app`, which keeps the runtime image clean. The secrets still sit in the build context sent to the daemon or Colima VM and in the Go stage's cached layer. They also travel with any `--target build` image or `--cache-to … mode=max` export. Line 24 promises otherwise. Fix: an allowlist (`*`, then `!go.mod`, `!go.sum`, `!cmd/`, `!internal/`, `!web/`, then re-exclude `**/.env*`). Otherwise prefix every entry with `**/` and add `**/*.tfvars.json`, `**/*.tfstate*`, `**/.terraform`, `**/tfplan`. Either way, correct the claim on line 24.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/terraform/SKILL.md:70,76`, `skills/terraform/references/checks.md:3,11`: both say to run each check bare and read its exit status. But the command given is `trivy config .`, and trivy exits 0 whatever it finds unless `--exit-code 1` is passed. The table's exit-code column mentions the flag, but neither command does. The one misconfiguration scanner in the procedure ("public buckets, missing deletion protection, plaintext secrets") therefore always reads as clean. Fix: `trivy config --exit-code 1 .` in both places.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/docker/SKILL.md:60,75,115`: `FROM golang:<the go.mod go line>` takes the module's `go` line as the image tag. That line is a minimum language version, and since Go 1.21 it is usually three-part. This repo's own `go.mod` says `go 1.24.4`. Following the rule here gives `FROM golang:1.24.4`, a frozen patch that `AGENTS.md` says carries the `os`/`os/exec` stdlib advisories fixed in 1.24.6. The official image sets `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`, so nothing upgrades it. Every stdlib CVE fixed after the module's floor ends up compiled into the static binary. Fix: `golang:<major.minor>`, taken from the go line (`go 1.24.4` → `golang:1.24`, which tracks the latest patch). Never use a patch tag, and run `govulncheck -mode=binary` on the built binary as part of the smoke test.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/terraform/assets/example/main.tf:64-71,81-84` and `skills/terraform/references/resources-gcp.md:155-158`: the Cloud Run env var reads its secret at `version = "latest"`. This contradicts `skills/cloud-run-deploy/SKILL.md:101` ("Pin the version (`:3`), not `:latest`, for env vars") and the template's "pinned versions" row (`gcp.md:39`). With `latest`, a principal holding only `secretmanager.versions.add` decides what the next instance of a running revision reads. That needs no deploy and no `run.services.update`. Instances of one revision can also disagree, and a rollback does not roll the secret back. The example has a second defect: the service does not depend on `google_secret_manager_secret_version.app`, so the first apply can start a revision before any version exists. Fix: `version = google_secret_manager_secret_version.app.version`, which pins and orders in one reference. Do the same in resources-gcp.md.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/cloud-run-deploy/SKILL.md:96,100`: "The app still validates `x-goog-iap-jwt-assertion` (`api-auth-gcp` skill)" and "Connection code: `data-gcp` skill" point at skills that do not exist (`ls skills/`). Phase 7 is meant to write them. An agent with nothing to read will compose the ES256 signature, `aud`, `iss` and expiry checks itself. That is hand-rolled JWT verification, which the global context bans as high severity. This was also raised by the p6 code, docs and prompts reviews; it is recorded here for the security angle. Fix: name the vetted library in the cell, for example `google.golang.org/api/idtoken.Validate(ctx, token, audience)` with the audience Google documents for IAP on Cloud Run. The stdlib alternative, composing JWT/ES256 verification over `crypto/ecdsa`, is rejected because it is the banned hand-rolling. Otherwise ship Phase 6 and 7 together. The same row should also say where `roles/iap.httpsResourceAccessor` is granted: on the service's IAP resource, not the project, where it opens every IAP-protected resource.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `skills/terraform/references/resources-gcp.md:174-181`: the Direct VPC egress sample hardcodes `network = "default"`, `subnetwork = "default"`. The auto-mode default VPC carries `default-allow-internal` (every port from 10.128.0.0/9) and SSH/RDP open to 0.0.0.0/0, so the service joins a flat network with every VM in the project. Many organisations also delete that network (`compute.skipDefaultNetworkCreation`). Phase 6 deleted `security-compliance.md`, whose "DON'T: Use Default VPC" was the only caution, and the new sample does the opposite. The same sample also pairs public-IP Cloud SQL (`:113-115`) with `vpc_access`, against `SKILL.md:63` ("no `vpc_access` at all without a private target"). Fix: a dedicated `google_compute_network` (`auto_create_subnetworks = false`) and a `/26`+ `google_compute_subnetwork` passed in by variable. Set `network_tags` on the service for egress firewall rules, add `google_service_networking_connection` for private Cloud SQL, and comment out the block in the public-IP sample.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/cloud-run-deploy/SKILL.md:95,139-142`, `skills/terraform/SKILL.md:53`, `assets/example/main.tf:54-55`: the two skills make a service public by different mechanisms. Terraform uses `invoker_iam_disabled = true`; gcloud uses `--allow-unauthenticated`, which writes an `allUsers` binding. The IAM-gated path is "omit the flag", which leaves an existing `allUsers` binding or a disabled invoker check in place. Verify calls the unauthenticated 403 "proves nothing", yet for `Public: no` that 403 is the one probe that proves the gate. A service recorded `Public: no` can stay public across deploys with every Verify step green.
