- Not examined (no `-race` run, no mutation, no `fyr search --refs` pre-flight): covered by the main thread — `go test -race -timeout 30m ./...` at the checkpoint, and every new test run in its must-fail state (the change record lists each mutation).

title: Security review — ledger Phase 8 (2026-10-28)
body:
# Security review — ledger-phase-8   (2026-10-28)

Range reviewed: 012d34f..working tree (HEAD 105796d, the uncommitted changes in 25 tracked files, and 7 untracked files: areas_test.go, cmd/fyr/eval_register.go, cmd/fyr/eval_register_test.go, internal/check/skipped_test.go, internal/dream/collect_nested_test.go, internal/search/dream_workspace.go, internal/search/dream_workspace_test.go)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The worst problem: `registerClone` registers the eval clone under whatever `--home` the run has, and `fyr eval` does not refuse the default home (the real `$HOME`). A run without `--home` therefore uses the real `~/.config/fyr/registration.key` (or creates it), seals the clone with the operator's real key, and the metrics join (`brain.ForMetrics` -> `openForSearch` -> `session.sync`) then loads the agent-written `.agents/trail.jsonl` into the real brain.db as a project scope. Because sandboxes stay, that scope stays. The code comment says the opposite ("the seal names the eval home's key, never the real home's"), and nothing enforces it. The impact is limited: `loadLocked` holds the records to the clone's scope, refuses the global kinds (feedback, proposal, memory) and caps the file at `maxTrail`. The remaining findings are low: a check-then-use window in `registerClone`, and two places where the dream's workspace filter can still send a conversation.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `cmd/fyr/eval_register.go:17-19,50` (called from `cmd/fyr/eval.go:265`). The comment promises the seal "names the eval home's key, never the real home's". Neither `registerClone` nor `evalSetup`/`eval.Preflight` (`internal/eval/run.go:71-83`, `guard.go:62-92`) refuses `home == os.UserHomeDir()`. `checkRoots` only refuses the real home itself or a parent of it, and `~/.config/fyr/eval` is neither. When `fyr eval` runs without `--home`: (1) `trail.Register` calls `ensureKey` on the real state directory; (2) the clone becomes a checkout registered under the operator's real key; (3) `ForMetrics` syncs the agent-authored trail.jsonl into the real brain.db. The agent ran with `command(*)` and wrote that trail. Any consumer that trusts registered checkouts sees that content as one of the operator's projects. That breaks SPEC-fyr-eval's invariant "nothing eval does writes the real home outside the sandbox root". The metrics ingest into the real metrics.db already broke it before this change; the brain store and the key are new. I did not run eval against a real home: this comes from reading the code, hence medium confidence. **Remediation:** in `registerClone`, or before any row runs, refuse registration when the resolved `home` equals the resolved `os.UserHomeDir()`. Report it the way `regErr` is reported. Add a test that sets HOME to the eval home and asserts no marker and no brain scope. Or require an explicit `--home` for `fyr eval`.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `cmd/fyr/eval_register.go:35-50`. The containment check (first `git rev-parse`) and `trail.Register`'s own `roots()` (second `git rev-parse`, then `CreateTemp` + `rename` into the common dir) resolve the git directory separately. `ingestRow` returns early on `ReasonProcs` and `ReasonReplaced` (`eval.go:258`), which closes the window only where processes are checked. `eval.ProcsChecked` can be false (it is reported in `evalBody`). On such a box, an agent process left running could swap `app/.git` between the two calls, and the marker plus a temp file would land in another repository's git dir. The payload is small: a marker sealed under the eval home's key; `Register` refuses non-regular files and replaces by rename. **Remediation:** do the containment check on the same rev-parse output that `Register` writes through, for example a `trail.RegisterWithin(stateDir, root, boundary)` that fails when `common` or `top` resolves outside `boundary`. Or skip registration when `!eval.ProcsChecked`.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/search/dream_workspace.go:52-55`. `judge` skips URIs that are not `file:`: they count as neither under nor outside. A conversation whose workspaces are the registered root plus a remote or other non-file workspace is kept, and its whole text goes to the model. This is unchanged from the old `inWorkspace` and consistent with the comment ("Every file URI"). It is still a fail-open edge in a filter that otherwise fails closed (unreadable -> left out, outside -> left out). **Remediation:** treat a non-file URI as `outside`, so the conversation is named and not sent. Add a test row for `[file root, non-file]`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/search/dream_workspace.go:41-43,79-87`. Known, documented limit: when a nested checkout is deleted after its session, the session is judged by the nearest surviving parent, reads as the target's own, and is sent. A nested directory whose `.git` was removed but whose files remain behaves the same way. Recorded here as accepted residual risk, with no new fix asked for. If it is ever closed, the conversation's own recorded repository identity is the signal to use, not the current disk state.

## Checked
- **Secrets:** no credential in the diff or the untracked files. The secret-shaped matches in the `.agents/trail.jsonl` diff are bare vendor prefixes (`xoxb-` and similar, 5 characters) and one `fake` placeholder inside plan and review text. The new redactor test rows use `FAKEVALUE`. The `record add --id` warning (`cmd/fyr/record_redact.go:25-28`) prints only a fixed message, never the ID. stdout still prints the ID as add's output, which is the operator's own input; acceptable.
- **Injection / input parsing:** `dream_workspace.judge` parses JSON and `url.Parse`, runs `filepath.Clean` (`..` is collapsed and percent-decoding happens before the prefix test), compares as a prefix with a separator (the sibling `root-other` case is tested), and resolves links through `trail.Roots`. A symlink inside root that points at another checkout resolves to that checkout's main root and is left out as nested. I traced this; no test covers it. Left-out conversations are named only by `Printable(id)` plus a fixed reason, never by path (tested in `collect_nested_test.go`). Antigravity generates the IDs, so naming them in the prompt discloses only an opaque ID. The dream now runs `git rev-parse` (via `trail.Command`: fsmonitor off, repository variables dropped, optional locks off) in the directory of every conversation under root, nested unregistered checkouts included, from the nightly timer. I know of no code-execution path in rev-parse with those flags; informational only.
- **Authz/authn (registration seal):** `registerClone` refuses a linked `app`, and a common dir or top level that resolves outside `app` (a `.git` file, `commondir`, `core.worktree`). `trail.roots` also checks that a worktree is registered. `Register` refuses a non-regular marker and writes by rename, so a hard link or symlink at the marker name is replaced, never followed. Tests cover the `.git`-file case only. The link, `core.worktree` and `commondir` branches are untested.
- **trail.Dirty top-level check** (`internal/trail/dirty.go:30-32,187-208`): both callers fail closed. `brain/import.go:130` refuses the import on error; `eval.go:298` labels the source "dirty: unknown". Comparing with links resolved is sound.
- **`--repo` ignored warning** (`run_dispatch.go:91-95`): prints the verb name only. **dream usage refusals** moved before the lock/log (`verb_dream.go`), and `dream.Run` keeps a guard for other callers. No security impact.
- **Redactor test change** (`internal/redact/needles_test.go`, `redact_test.go`): test-only. `TestEveryKeywordNeedleBinds` requires every keyword needle to have a row that only it catches, which strengthens the mutation coverage of the redactor. No runtime change.
- **Crypto:** no new primitive. Registration uses stdlib `crypto/hmac` + `crypto/sha256` as designed (existing `trail/register.go`, unchanged). Not hand-rolling.
- **Dependencies:** `go.mod` and `go.sum` are not in the diff; no new dependency. govulncheck (`$(go env GOPATH)/bin/govulncheck ./...`): "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities". One vulnerability is reported in required modules, not called; it is the known GO-2026-5024. npm audit was not run: the range touches no `web/` or `ui/` or package manifest.
- **GCP surface:** not touched by the range.
- **Past bugs** (`fyr search --refs <path> --kind bug`, scratch home): BUG-188 (Dirty false clean, fixed) on `dirty.go` and `eval.go`; BUG-181 (agyTime) on `search/dream.go`. Neither regressed by this diff, as far as I can tell from reading it.

## Not examined
- Running `fyr eval` end to end, with or without `--home`: finding 1 comes from reading the code, not from a run.
- What else consumes `trail.Registered` beyond the metrics join (for example whether `fyr dream --all` or cross-project search would include a clone registered under the real home). I did not trace them, so the full blast radius of finding 1 is unconfirmed.
- `internal/metrics/events_join.go` beyond its call to `brain.ForMetrics`; `brain.readRecords` and `parseLine` validation of a hostile trail.jsonl; `brain.guardExportPath`.
- The untracked `areas_test.go` and `internal/check/skipped_test.go` in detail. I skimmed their test names and their exec/git use only; they are tests and change no runtime surface.
- `cmd/fyr/checkout_test.go`, `help_test.go`, `metrics_test.go`, `record_redact_test.go`, `internal/search/dream_arms_test.go`, `dream_test.go` and `internal/trail/dirty_test.go`, beyond the diff stat.
- The `.agents/trail.jsonl` record bodies, which I scanned only for secret shapes; README and help text for accuracy (a docs-lens job).
- `go test`, `go vet` and gofmt were not run (the verifier's lane).

## Outcome

- Finding 1 (medium, a real-home `--home` registers under the real key and loads the agent's trail into the real brain store): fixed — `cmd/fyr/eval_register.go` `registerClone` refuses a `--home` that resolves to the real home (`samePath` with `os.UserHomeDir`); `TestRegisterCloneRefusals` fails with the refusal removed; SPEC-fyr-eval § State says so.
- Finding 2 (low, the check and `Register` resolve the git directory apart): fixed by refusal — `registerClone` takes `eval.ProcsChecked` and registers nothing where check e does not run, so no process a row left can swap the directory in between; on Linux check e runs and a row with processes left is never ingested (`cmd/fyr/eval.go` ingestRow). A `RegisterWithin` was not built: `Register` itself resolves and writes in two steps, so it would not close the window either. Pinned by `TestRegisterCloneRefusals` (must-fail with the check removed).
- Finding 3 (low, a non-file workspace URI was neither under nor outside): fixed — `internal/search/dream_workspace.go` judge counts a non-file or unparsable URI as outside, so the conversation is named and not sent; two `TestWorkspacesJudge` rows fail with that line removed; SPEC-fyr-dream says so.
- Finding 4 (low, a nested checkout deleted after its session): left, accepted — the documented known limit in SPEC-fyr-dream § the transcripts input and in `judge`'s doc comment.

title: Security review — ledger Phase 8, round 2 over the fixes (2026-10-28)
body:
# Security review — ledger-phase-8-round-2   (2026-10-28)

Range reviewed: working tree on HEAD 105796d, limited to the round-1 fixes: cmd/fyr/eval_register.go (read in full), cmd/fyr/eval.go (the ingestRow hunk, lines 251-283), cmd/fyr/eval_register_test.go (read in full), internal/search/dream_workspace.go (read in full) with its test row, and the SPEC-fyr-eval and SPEC-fyr-dream record text. Round-1 file: .agents/scratch/agents/security-2026-10-28-1317.md.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The fixes close round-1 findings 1 (its key and brain parts), 2 and 3. Two new low-severity weaknesses come with them. The worst: the real-home guard compares only the `--home` directory itself (`cmd/fyr/eval_register.go:32`). It never compares the state directory the seal and the brain store actually use, `<home>/.config/fyr`. So a separate `--home` whose `.config` or `.config/fyr` is a link to the real one passes the guard, and the clone is still sealed under the real key. Only the operator sets `--home`, and the agent does not, so this is a misconfiguration path rather than one an agent can trigger. The second: off Linux, every row's ingest now fails, so `fyr eval` there always exits 1. That trains the operator to ignore exit 1, which is also how the safety checks report a real failure. Nothing new is high or medium.

## Round-1 findings, one by one

1. **Real home used as `--home` (medium): partly fixed. The escalation is closed; one residual overclaim remains.** `cmd/fyr/eval_register.go:32-34` refuses when `samePath(home, os.UserHomeDir())` is true, before anything is written. `eval.go:265` passes the result on, and the refusal is reported at `eval.go:279-281`. `ForMetrics` loads the trail only for a root that is `trail.Registered` under the home (`internal/brain/dream.go:141`). So an unregistered clone gets no `ensureKey` on the real state directory, no seal under the real key, and none of the agent-written trail.jsonl in the real brain.db. All three parts round 1 named are closed. The guard fails open when `os.UserHomeDir()` errors, but `evalSetup` refuses that case first (`eval.go:127-130`), so `runEval` never reaches it. Two things are still open. (a) With `--home` set to the real home, `metrics.Ingest` still reads the agent-written conversation databases into the real metrics.db (`eval.go:266-272`). That existed before this change and round 1 named it. (b) SPEC-fyr-eval's line "Invariant: nothing eval does writes the real home outside the sandbox root" (Interfaces section) still overstates for that case. See finding N3.
2. **Race between the containment check and Register (low): fixed for the window round 1 described.** `cmd/fyr/eval_register.go:35-37` refuses when `procsChecked` is false. On Linux, `eval.go:256` skips registration and ingest for any row with `ReasonProcs`, `ReasonExists` or `ReasonReplaced`, so neither the ingest nor `registerClone` runs. The residual is the one SPEC-fyr-eval already documents (Known limits: "A process that escapes check e …"): such a process can still swap `app/.git` between the rev-parse at line 46 and `trail.Register` at line 61. The payload has not changed (a marker sealed under the eval home's key, written by rename). Accepted as documented. The stronger fix, a single resolution shared by the check and the write, was not made.
3. **Non-file workspace URI (low): fixed.** `internal/search/dream_workspace.go:51-57` treats a URI that fails to parse, or whose scheme is not `file`, as outside. A conversation that has the root plus a remote workspace is therefore named `whyOutside` and not sent. The test row is at `internal/search/dream_workspace_test.go:41` (`vscode-remote://…`, want `whyOutside`). SPEC-fyr-dream line 23 matches the code ("a remote or unparsable one counts as outside").
4. **Deleted nested checkout (low): accepted, not fixed (as stated in the dispatch).** It is documented in the comment at `dream_workspace.go:40-43` and in SPEC-fyr-dream line 23 ("Known limit: …"). Nothing more to add.

## Findings (new in round 2)

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `cmd/fyr/eval_register.go:32`: the guard compares the wrong path. `samePath(home, real)` compares the two home directories. Everything the guard protects lives one level lower: the seal key and brain.db sit in `filepath.Join(home, harness.StateDir)` (`.config/fyr`, `internal/harness/state.go:34`), which line 61 passes to `trail.Register`. Take an eval home that is not the real home but whose `.config` or `.config/fyr` is a link to the real one, for example a scratch home set up by linking config across. It passes the guard, and `Register` then seals under the real key while the join loads the agent's trail into the real brain.db. That is exactly what finding 1 was meant to stop. Only the operator controls `--home`, hence low severity. **Remediation:** resolve and compare the state directories, `samePath(filepath.Join(home, harness.StateDir), filepath.Join(real, harness.StateDir))`, and keep the home comparison too. Add a test where `<home>/.config` is a link to `<realHome>/.config`. (`samePath` falls back to comparing raw strings when the state directory does not exist yet. The real one normally exists, and `resolveHome` makes `home` absolute at `run_dispatch.go:111`, so the fallback does not hide the link case.)
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `cmd/fyr/eval_register.go:35-37` with `cmd/fyr/eval.go:279-281` and `recordEval` (`eval.go:170-172`): off Linux, every eval always fails. There `ProcsChecked` is the constant `false` (`internal/eval/procs_other.go:13`), so every started row's ingest returns the "not registered" error, `failed` is set, and `fyr eval` exits 1 even when every row PASSes. Eval reports a credential found, real config changed, or processes left through that same exit 1. An exit code that is always 1 on macOS gets ignored, which wears away that signal on the platform that already lacks check e. **Remediation:** off Linux, report the skipped registration as a notice, printed and written into the testing record next to the existing "skipped process check" line, rather than as a failed ingest. Or get the operator to accept and record "always exit 1 off Linux" as intended in SPEC-fyr-eval's failure-modes table, which at present lists only "an ingest fails → exit 1".
- **[low / confidence: high]** SPEC-fyr-eval, Interfaces section, "Invariant: nothing eval does writes the real home outside the sandbox root; check c fails the row when something did": this is a restatement that is still false. If `--home` is the real home (or `--home` is omitted, since `resolveHome` falls back to `os.UserHomeDir()`), eval writes the real `~/.config/fyr/metrics.db` (the ingest) and the real brain.db (the testing record, `eval.go:183`). Check c fingerprints `~/.config/fyr` minus `eval/`, but only up to step 14, before the ingest, so it does not see these writes. The registration fix removed the agent-controlled part, but the sentence remains a claim the code does not keep. **Remediation:** either require an explicit `--home` that is not the real home for `fyr eval` (refused in `evalSetup`, which would also fix N1 and close the metrics leftover from finding 1), or narrow the invariant to "… outside the sandbox root and the `--home` stores".

## Checked

- Secrets: none in the scoped files or tests. The test identities are `t@e.invalid`. No error message echoes a key or token. The refusal message prints the real home's path (`eval_register.go:33`), which is the operator's own path in the operator's own terminal and not a secret.
- Injection: `trail.Command(app, "rev-parse", …)` uses fixed arguments, and `app` is a path eval built from `r.Dir`, not a shell string. `url.Parse` plus `filepath.Clean` in `judge` handles `..` in a `file:` path lexically. A link inside the root is caught by the `trail.Roots` main-root comparison.
- Authz/authn: the real-home guard and the procs guard are in place and ordered before any write (`eval_register.go:32-37`). Mutation reasoning on `TestRegisterCloneRefusals`: removing either guard makes the matching assertion fail, because the clone is otherwise valid and would register. The real-home refusal has the test; the linked-state-directory case (N1) has none.
- Crypto: nothing hand-rolled in scope. The seal is made inside `trail.Register`, which this diff did not change. Not re-reviewed.
- Dependencies: `git diff --stat go.mod go.sum` is empty, so no new dependency. I did not run govulncheck because the round-2 scope changes no module. Round 1's run stands.
- GCP surface: none in scope.
- Tests run (from the repository root, not under `-race`): `go test -count=1 -v -run 'TestRegisterClone|TestEvalIngest' ./cmd/fyr/` passed 4 of 4 (JoinsSandboxTrail, RefusesForeignGitDir, RegisterCloneRefusals, SkipsReplaced). `go test -count=1 -v -run Workspace ./internal/search/` passed `TestWorkspacesJudge`.

## Not examined

- `trail.Register` / `ensureKey` / the seal's construction (`internal/trail`): reached by the fix but not changed by it, and not re-read in round 2.
- The `readsRepo: true` added to the eval verb (`cmd/fyr/eval.go:39`, `cmd/fyr/run_dispatch.go:92`) is in the same diff but outside the dispatched scope. Not reviewed.
- A `file://<host>/path` URI with a non-local host is treated as the local path `p.Path`, and I did not test it. The likely effect is in the safe direction, because a path that is not under the root counts as outside, but it is unverified.
- The full `go test -race ./...` and gofmt/vet were not run (the verifier owns them). I did not run eval end to end against a real home: findings N1 and N3 come from reading the code.
- Every other file in the working-tree diff that is outside the round-2 scope.

## Outcome

- Finding 1 (low, a separate `--home` whose `.config` links to the real one passes the home comparison): fixed — `registerClone` also compares `<home>/.config/fyr` with the real state directory, both resolved (`cmd/fyr/eval_register.go`); `TestRegisterCloneRefusals` builds that link and fails with the second comparison removed.
- Finding 2 (low, off Linux every ingest would fail and every run exit 1): fixed — with `ProcsChecked` false `registerClone` registers nothing and returns nil: no record events there, a known limit stated in SPEC-fyr-eval § State, never a failed ingest; `TestRegisterCloneRefusals` fails if the skip returns an error.
- Finding 3 (low, the invariant "nothing eval does writes the real home" is false for a `--home` left out or the real home): the text fixed, the refusal left — SPEC-fyr-eval's invariant now says what holds (nothing a row's agent does; eval itself writes `--home`'s metrics and brain stores, never the real home's with a separate `--home`; a `--home` left out puts `eval=<row>` sessions in the real metrics store, as before this phase, and no clone is ever registered there). Requiring a separate `--home` changes `fyr eval`'s refusals: left for the operator, recommended, in the handoff's Next Steps.

title: Review — ledger Phase 9: the map, the ADRs and the docs, with D37's eval --home refusal (2 rounds, code and docs)
