The worst problems are one piece of dead production code the change orphaned (`metrics.openRegular` / `openNonBlocking`, with a doc comment that is now false), a spec claim that is no longer pinned by any test, and a crossing procedure that now leaves the operator an unlisted manual step.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/metrics/ingest.go:130-142`, `internal/metrics/open_unix.go:10-15`, `internal/metrics/open_other.go:7-9`, `internal/metrics/fifo_unix_test.go:14-36` — Dead code left behind. `openRegular` was called only by `readSmall` (events.go) and `readFeedback` (events_feedback.go), both deleted here; `git grep openRegular HEAD -- internal/metrics` shows those two plus the test. `deadcode ./...` now reports `openRegular` (ingest.go:134) and `openNonBlocking` (open_unix.go:13) unreachable. Its doc comment says it is "the one way ingest opens a conversation file or a trail file", which is false: ingest no longer reads any file through it. `TestOpenRegularRefusesFIFO` keeps it green by testing the dead helper, so it reports coverage of a path nothing runs. Fix: delete `openRegular`, both `openNonBlocking` files and `fifo_unix_test.go`'s `TestOpenRegularRefusesFIFO` (keep `syscallMkfifo` only if another test uses it). Check that `fmt` and `os` imports in ingest.go are still used after the delete.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `internal/metrics/records_test.go:49-51, 120-123`, `internal/metrics/events_test.go` (deleted `TestJoinFilesArms` / `TestJoinFilesRefs`) — The new spec text (SPEC-fyr-metrics "Trail from records only") says an unmigrated project "gives no trail events, only its commits and corrections". No test pins it. The old tests were deleted; the new `TestCorrections/unmigrated` fixture is an empty git repo with no docs files and no commits, and filters on " correction " only. `recordsFixture`'s "leftover docs root holds a handoff file the join must not read (D4)" is the only fixture with a file, but it is a migrated project and no code path reads that file any more, so that assertion can no longer fail. Failure scenario: someone re-adds a file join (or `joinRoot` stops guarding on `in.Migrated`) and every test stays green. Fix: add one case to `TestJoinEvents`-style tests — an unmigrated registered/unregistered root with a commit in a session window and a `.agents/docs/handoffs/*.md` file; assert the commit event exists and no handoff/verifier/review/bug event does. Also reword the `recordsFixture` comment so it does not claim the leftover file is guarded by this test.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** DEPLOY-remote (record body, "Before the crossing, at every place" paragraph, and the new first paragraph of "Crossing to fyr") — The change removes `fyr install`'s replacement of the old-named dream timer and says only that "an old-named unit left anywhere is the operator's to remove by hand". The procedure is still the one offered to any v2.7.0 place (DEPLOY-remote line 13 sends such a machine there), and its "Before the crossing" step names `sh-agent-update.timer` but not `sh-agent-dream[-<hash>].timer`. Failure scenario: a place still on v2.7.0 crosses; `fyr install` deletes `~/.local/bin/sh-agent`; the old `sh-agent-dream` timer keeps firing hourly against a missing binary, and `fyr dream --remove-timer` / `uninstall` cannot remove it (they no longer know the name). The "After the crossing" check `systemctl --user list-timers | grep -cw sh-agent  # 0` would catch it, but only afterwards and with no command to fix it. Fix: add `systemctl --user disable --now sh-agent-dream*.timer` (and the files / the macOS `launchctl bootout` + plist `com.styrman.sh-agent-dream*`) to the "Before the crossing" step. Severity is low because the operator's decision (ledger A1 yes, D40) is that every place has crossed.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** GUIDE-fyr-matrix row "`dream --install-timer` / `--remove-timer`" (after-body) — The row cites `TestDreamTimerSaysWhatItFound` and `TestUninstallDryRunLeavesTheTimer` as "test: against a fake `systemctl`". Neither runs `--install-timer`; `TestDreamTimerSaysWhatItFound` only asserts that `--remove-timer` with nothing installed calls no manager. The replaced test (`TestInstallSaysATurnedOffTimerStaysOff`) was the install-side one. The install-side verb tests with a fake manager are `TestInstallTimerLinux` and `TestRemoveTimerLinux` in `internal/dream/timer_install_test.go`; the verb-level success path "dream timer removed" / "removed the dream timer" is asserted nowhere (only the negative forms, `cmd/fyr/memory_test.go:212, 260`). - **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/dream/timer.go:62` — `namesFor(home, unit, plist)` now has a single caller (`UnitFor`); the parameters exist only for the removed `oldUnitFor`. Inline it. Not a defect; listed because it is the last trace of the removed feature.

1. Dead code — FAIL (low-medium): `metrics.openRegular`, both `openNonBlocking` files and their FIFO test are now unreferenced from production; `namesFor` has a vestigial parameter shape. Everything else removed went cleanly (`readSmall`, `readFeedback`, `trailFiles`, `joinFiles`, `joinFileBugs`, `fileTimes`, `bugName`, `LegacyTimer*`, `OldTimerHere`, `ReplaceOldTimer`, `oldUnitFor`, `oldTimerNote`, `timerUnit.probe/off`, `timerUnit.on`, `fakeManagerOff`: zero remaining references). `rewriteFileRefs` / `fileRef` are kept on purpose (spec documents the rewrite of events an older ingest stored).

5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass: net -975 lines, no new dependency, nothing auth/crypto related.
6. Decoupling — pass: `cmd/fyr` no longer imports `dream` in `verb_install.go`; `metrics` no longer imports `harness` in tests; the `brain` import in `events_test.go` is the same seam `records_test.go` already uses.

The `openNonBlocking` hits left are `internal/brain`'s own copies, which are live. The `os` import went out of `ingest.go` and vet passes. The new SPEC sentence is accurate: `metrics` reads databases through `search.OpenCopy` (`agy.go:75,124`, `numbers.go:18`), and `OpenCopy` opens through `copyFileImpl`, which calls `openSource` and then checks the opened file is regular (`internal/search/copy.go:20-34`). The FIFO guarantee is covered by `internal/search/copy_test.go` (FIFO case at line 30). The trail is read through `brain.ForMetrics` (`internal/brain/dream.go:139`).
2. Unmigrated root unpinned: fixed. The test commits a handoff file inside S1's window in an unregistered root, adds a global feedback record, and requires exactly the commit and the correction. The must-fail file shows the same test failing on HEAD's code with an extra `S1 handoff ...-file=`. That is a real behavioural failure, not a build error. The `recordsFixture` comment no longer claims the leftover file is the pin. The new `TestCorrections/unmigrated` case now has a real git root, so it exercises the unmigrated path.
3. DEPLOY-remote: fixed. The paragraph gives `systemctl --user disable --now 'sh-agent-dream*.timer'` (quoted, so `systemctl` expands the glob), the file deletion, `daemon-reload` and the launchd equivalent. It also says why: `fyr install` no longer does it.
4. GUIDE row: fixed. It cites `TestDreamInstallTimer` (exists, `cmd/fyr/dream_arms_test.go:17`). `TestDreamTimerSaysWhatItFound` now asserts the success wording of both verbs and that the unit files are gone. `timerFilesFor` uses `dream.UnitFor`, so it matches the running system's unit names. The must-fail (`dream timer gone`) failed the test with a named message, and the code compiled.
5. `namesFor` rebuttal: accepted. It is a style preference with no failure mode, and it is out of scope for a removal phase.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass: the round-1 orphans are gone and no dangling references remain.
2. Flow tracing — pass: the ingest to `OpenCopy` to `openSource` chain was traced. The tests can fail, per the two must-fails.
3. Standards conformance — pass: the changed comments (`ingest.go`, `records_test.go`, `memory_test.go`) match the code. The SPEC, DEPLOY and GUIDE texts match the code.
4. Directory layout — pass.
5. Simplicity — pass: only deletions plus one test and one helper.
6. Decoupling — pass: the `harness` test import from `metrics` is gone.

## Not examined
- Full `go test ./...`: a suite is running elsewhere on the tree.
- I did not re-run the must-fail mutations; I read the recorded output and checked it is a test failure, not a build failure.
- The launchd path of `timerFilesFor` was read, not run.
- The DEPLOY-remote shell glob/quoting was read, not run on a real systemd.

# Review — cold read of PLAN-2026-10-29-root-docs-and-fyr-serve   (2026-10-29)

Range reviewed: `.agents/scratch/plan-root-docs-and-fyr-serve.md` (plan, cold-reader check) and the code surfaces it names; REQUIREMENTS.md at HEAD (26c3383).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES  (design needs revision; implementation not ready)

Worst first: Row 3's expect clause is self-contradictory (its `grep ROADMAP … skills` "prints nothing" cannot hold while Interfaces requires init-project to keep the ROADMAP.md→TODO.md migration lines). Rows 2–3 also change a requirement-bearing rule (init-project "update never rewrites or deletes what the project wrote") and the immutable-file status of a document that now holds living metric baselines, with no D-row for the second. `fyr serve` touches R3/R7/R8 (long-running process, a possible `dream` action, serving memory) without citing them. Drafts B passes: every operation is exact, no requirement sentence changes, and row 4's `diff` verify prints nothing on unchanged text (simulated, see below).

## Findings

- **[high / high]** Plan row 3, `grep -rn 'ROADMAP' context agents skills rules --exclude-dir=catalog` "expect: the first prints nothing" vs § Interfaces "init-project … `ROADMAP.md`'s Now and Next moved under `TODO.md` … then `ROADMAP.md` deleted by name". The migration step in `skills/init-project/SKILL.md` must name `ROADMAP.md`; the grep will print it. The second grep already allows "migration lines" for REQUIREMENTS; the first does not. Fix: expect "only the migration lines of init-project". Also `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md:10` and `skills/init-project/assets/ROADMAP.md:3` are in the grep's reach (the asset is deleted in row 2; areas.md is listed in Surfaces).
- **[high / high]** Immutability vs living baselines. Drafts B puts a Goals table with measured baselines (G1 14,876; G2 21,422; G3 2) and `Last updated:` into a file whose line 3 says "Immutable without the operator's explicit approval. Agents never edit this file." (REQUIREMENTS.md:3, kept by B step 2) and AGENTS.md hard rule "REQUIREMENTS.md is immutable". Nothing decides who updates baselines/`Last updated`/"Verified by" cells later, or whether those are exempt. Also G2 (`AGENTS.md` ≤ 12,000) is a new non-negotiable target, not a requirement-sentence change, but it is new binding content; D5 says "requirement sentences unchanged" while the approval would fix G2. Decide: exempt sections named in the note, or move metrics out of the PRD.
- **[medium / high]** `skills/init-project/SKILL.md` Step 1 states "an update never edits `REQUIREMENTS.md`, an existing `AGENTS.md` …" and "never rewrites or deletes what the project wrote". D7 resolves this by asking, but no task rewrites that sentence in SKILL.md and Step 3 (`for f in AGENTS.md REQUIREMENTS.md TODO.md ROADMAP.md`) and "`REQUIREMENTS.md` — copied … the one file whose placeholders this step does not fill" are restatements the Row 2 task ("create and update steps per § Interfaces") does not enumerate. Name them, and name `SKILL.md`'s description (it lists `REQUIREMENTS.md`, and the skill-listing budget has 108 bytes free).
- **[medium / high]** Requirements touched but not cited: **R3** (`fyr serve` is a long-running listener; S3 candidate `dream --dry-run` would start the one conversation R3 allows only under the timer/`fyr dream` rules; "no daemon"), **R7** (memory records are "local to the machine and never exported"; serving them over HTTP is a new reader), **R8** (exactly two things leave the machine; loopback must be shown not to be a third, and "no service" in AGENTS.md rule 1 is read against a server). D17 only addresses the README map. Add to § Why's list and to S1's ADR.
- **[medium / high]** Row 4 verify for the rename uses `git show HEAD:REQUIREMENTS.md`. Correct only before the commit; after the commit (the checkpoint) HEAD has no such file, `git show` fails, the left side is empty, and `diff` prints the whole PRD. Name the base (`HEAD` before commit, else the pre-row-4 SHA). It also compares only R0..R10 (stops at the `## Known` line): "Known limits … unchanged" (B step 7), the Non-goals move (B step 4) and the title/note are not pinned by any command.
- **[low / high]** Row 4 grep `grep -rn 'REQUIREMENTS\|ROADMAP' --include=... . --exclude-dir=.agents` lacks `--exclude-dir=catalog` (and `.git` is skipped by grep only with -r defaults off); catalog entries are vendored data. (`fyr check --home …` is fine: `--home` is a global flag, cmd/fyr/check.go:67; I ran it, 2 findings, both `spec-stale` SPEC-fyr-check and SPEC-fyr-eval, exit 1 -- the plan's baseline reproduces, and the note `REQUIREMENTS.md has no enforced-by field: not checked` confirms D6. Note the baseline exit is 1, so a verify clause 'exit 0' would fail; the plan correctly says findings subset of baseline.)
- **[medium / medium]** E2E criterion 3: "`ls` at the root shows exactly the D1 files plus `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `embed.go`, the test files and the directories". Root today holds an untracked, gitignored `fyr` build output (`.gitignore:5 /fyr`) that `ls` shows, and the root tests `areas_test.go, embed_test.go, funclen_test.go, init_project_test.go, plan_test.go, skills_text_test.go, statedir_test.go, testmain_test.go`; "exactly" and "the test files" are not a checkable list. Use `git ls-files | grep -v /` against an enumerated list (this repo's tracked root files are the right base; `fyr` is an untracked build output unless ignored).
- **[medium / medium]** Row 2 `outsideText` task: "survives the import's closure" tests a record referenced only from `PRD.md`, but `outsideText` also feeds D8's closure from `SDD.md`/`TDD.md`; only PRD is tested. Also `internal/brain/import_docs.go:179` passes names to `git ls-files --`, so a not-yet-existing file is harmless, but the "while it exists, `REQUIREMENTS.md`" clause needs no code; say so.
- **[low / high]** `fyr check` rule (c) test cases (`internal/check/requirements_test.go:56-140`) hard-code `REQUIREMENTS.md:N requirement` finding prefixes; § Interfaces says "Findings name the file read" but `candidate{where: "REQUIREMENTS.md"}` at `internal/check/requirements.go:164` and the `Finding{"REQUIREMENTS.md", …}` at :47 are also fixed strings; the plan lists only "which file it opens". Add them to the task.
- **[low / high]** E2E criterion 4 / Row 8 manual walk: "opens the printed URL" and "200 then 403" are fine, but `?token=<t>` as the first-URL transport is already chosen in § Interfaces while Row 7 says routes/token shapes are row 7's: two homes for one decision.

## Specific checks requested

**Drafts B vs REQUIREMENTS.md at HEAD.** Original headings (HEAD, 69 lines): `# Requirements — fyr` (1), note (3), R0 (5), R1 (9) … R10 (52), Known limits (56), Non-goals (64). Op 2 replaces line 1 and keeps line 3 — exact. Op 4 moves Non-goals (heading + four items) after Goals — exact; Known limits (op 7) stays after R10 so R10's "a Known limit below" and R4's "(Non-goals)" still read true. Op 6 heading level only. No requirement sentence changes; I grepped the file: it names no "REQUIREMENTS.md" in body text, so the rename leaves no stale self-reference in the body. New text that is not requirement text but is binding-looking: G2's target; Problem's claims ("drifts from machine to machine") are new prose asserted as fact with no source. Placeholders left in the drafted lines: `YYYY-MM-DD` (Last updated) and `<filled in row 4>`; "every new line written out" holds except those, and the Requirements-index titles are R-headings' words shortened (R0 "Purpose: the second brain of the Antigravity CLI" matches; R8 matches; R9 matches) — fine.

**Row 4 rename verify.** Simulated in `.agents/scratch/agents/sim/` (old.md = `git show HEAD:REQUIREMENTS.md`; PRD.md built by B's operations): `diff <(sed -n '/^## R0/,/^## Known/p' old.md | sed 's/^## R/### R/') <(sed -n '/^### R0/,/^## Known/p' PRD.md)` prints nothing, exit 0. Must-fail not exercised for a changed sentence beyond reading the range logic; the range is bounded by the first `^## Known` and the table rows `| R0 |` do not match `^### R0`. Limitation as in the finding above (HEAD moves at commit; coverage stops at Known limits).

## Answers to the brief

**(1) Gaps** — the findings above, plus undefined terms the naive reader meets: `D8`'s closure (in `import_docs.go`, not cited from the plan: "D8" collides with this plan's own D8), `rule (c)`, `rule (a)`/`notInRuleA`, `TR16`, `IN23`-style IDs (not in this plan), "baseline (2 findings, both `spec-stale`)" (shown but not reproduced by a command in the plan; reproduced by me: 2 spec-stale findings), "R→M→T" vs "R→S→T" (Phase 5 in the Reference section still says S#, the table in the Order says R→S→T in row 10 title of the order table: row 10 reads "R→S→T"; Phases row 10 says R→M→T; D8 supersedes but the order table, "approved as is", still says S), "G1..G3" (defined only in Drafts B), "Smoke checks" (cited), "Phase 6/Phase 5" numbering (rows 5 and 10 vs Phases 6 and 5 — three numbering schemes: row #, Phase #, S1–S3).
Also an assumption asserted, not checked: "17 skill and agent files" (ADR draft, "about 17"); counted now: 17 files name ROADMAP and 18 name REQUIREMENTS outside the catalog (my grep, `-l` count) — the sets differ, so the list is two sets. Also the new `TestInitProjectRootDocs` "fails before the file exists" is satisfied by any absent file.
Docs clause check: the `fyr serve` verb (rows 8, 9) has docs clauses; the `fyr check` change has `help_text.go` and `SPEC-fyr-check`; the init-project changes name SKILL.md; no clause for `README.md`'s verb table when `fyr check`'s synopsis changes; rule (d) in row 10 has docs.

**(2) Scope** — Built beyond the `## Why` request: (a) rule (d) R→M→T check (Phase 5) is flagged optional and asked (fine, an Open ask in row 7); (b) AGENTS.md trim to ≤ 12,000 (row 5): the Why does not name it, but D3 records the operator's order including Phase 6 — covered, though the 12,000 figure has no D-row naming who set it (only Drafts B G2); (c) `fyr serve` requires a `Host` allow-list for both `127.0.0.1:N` and `localhost:N` while binding only 127.0.0.1 (a second shape; covered by D15 "Host header checked"); (d) the Goals/Users/Problem prose in the PRD is new text the operator did not write (mitigated: put to the operator in row 1). No extra endpoint was named in the plan.

**(3) Readiness** — questions:
1. (BLOCKING) Row 3 grep expectation vs the migration lines: which files may still name ROADMAP/REQUIREMENTS.
2. (BLOCKING) Who may update PRD baselines/`Last updated`/"Verified by" cells given the immutability note.
3. (NON-BLOCKING) `fyr check --home` is accepted (checked); baseline exit is 1, so Row 4's check must be read as findings subset, not exit 0 (stated).
4. (BLOCKING) Row 4: what is "the commit row 4 starts from" for `git show HEAD:…` after the commit.
5. (NON-BLOCKING) Exact wording of the migration approval line and its byte-identity check ("original requirement lines byte-identical" — which lines: everything but the heading level?). The E2E criterion 2 says byte-identical, but the migration adds sections; the check command is not given.
6. (NON-BLOCKING) Template heading for items under `## Must`/`## Should` in `assets/PRD.md` vs this repository's `### R#`: two shapes, both stated (D6).
7. (NON-BLOCKING) `--port 0`, a non-numeric port, a port above 65535: only "busy" is specified.
8. (NON-BLOCKING) Whether `fyr serve` opens the browser (no; says "prints").
9. (NON-BLOCKING) Package name `internal/serve/` ("S1 decides").
10. (NON-BLOCKING) The eval fixture holding the old files (checked by row 3 task 1; an operator step).
11. (BLOCKING) Is a `GUIDE-eval` edit row 3's or row 4's? Rows 2 (`scaffold`), 3 (`requirements-check`, `lane-documentation`) both list `GUIDE-eval`; row 4's living-records task also lists `GUIDE-testing` etc. The records are "edited as drafts and stored back" — mechanism (`fyr record edit --body` with `--home`?) is not stated and the trail export must be committed in the same commit.

**(4) Sizing** — Row 3 is the phase a fresh session could not finish from the plan alone: it re-points 17–18 skill/agent files, four context lines under a 124-byte-free pin and a 108-byte-free skill listing, with draft deltas "estimated" (−154) and the listing-budget rule ("or the wording is cut") unquantified; plus the unresolved grep contradiction. Row 4 is also oversized for one session (PRD + SDD + TDD authoring with sequence diagrams and trace tables, README rewrite, ~11 living records, every `func <Name>` grep) with no split rule. Rows 1, 2, 5, 7–12 are workable.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — n/a (plan); the plan deletes `assets/REQUIREMENTS.md`, `assets/ROADMAP.md` by name: pass. `notInRuleA` keeping `ROADMAP.md` is justified (D11).
2. Flow tracing — fail: Row 3 grep vs init-project migration; `Finding{"REQUIREMENTS.md",…}` and `candidate.where` at requirements.go:47,164 not in the rule (c) task; row 4 `HEAD` base.
3. Standards conformance — fail: R3/R7/R8 not cited; immutability gap; init-project Step 1 restatements not enumerated (`SKILL.md` Step 1, Step 3 copy loop, description).
4. Directory layout — pass (`internal/serve/`, assets in `skills/init-project/assets/`, tests beside code); the `fyr` root entry is unexplained.
5. Simplicity — pass: stdlib only (D13), no new config; no hand-rolled auth (token via `crypto/rand`, CSRF) but S1 must say "no sessions library": a per-run token/cookie is a protocol composed here; flag for `security` at rows 8–9, already planned.
6. Decoupling — pass; `fyr serve` reads through existing packages, none edited by it.

## Not examined
- (Resolved after the first write: `fyr check --home` run; baseline reproduced.)
- `internal/eval/suite_test.go` pins beyond the `want` map lines 126–133; `GUIDE-eval` rows' full expectation text.
- `skills/init-project/assets/*` contents, `TestHarnessMap`, `TestSkillListingBudget` internals, and the byte counts in § Context-size budget (taken from the plan, not re-measured).
- The 17/18 skills and agents files individually; only counts and `handoff`/`init-project` were read.
- `SPEC-fyr-*` records and `DEPLOY-local` § Operator steps (records not read).

## Outcome

Every finding answered in PLAN-2026-10-29-root-docs-and-fyr-serve (main thread, 2026-10-29):
- Row 3 grep vs migration lines (high): fixed — expect now allows only init-project's migration lines (ROADMAP) and init-project/requirements' (REQUIREMENTS); areas.md named as must-not-print.
- Immutable PRD with living figures (high): fixed by D22 — baselines dated and never updated, `Last updated` = date of the applying commit, the Verified-by column removed from Drafts B (the trace lives in SDD/TDD); G2 named as new binding text in the approval table.
- init-project restatements (medium): fixed — row 2's task enumerates the description, Step 1's two sentences, Step 3's loop and per-file notes, with a grep and the listing-budget test.
- R3/R7/R8 uncited (medium): fixed — § Why cites them; D21 states how `fyr serve` meets each, for row 7's ADR.
- Row 4 rename verify on HEAD, partial coverage (medium): fixed — BASE recorded on the row's first box; `comm -23` over the whole old file (all but its title, headings at the new level), with a positive control.
- Row 4 grep without catalog (low): fixed — `--exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=catalog`.
- E2E criterion 3 `ls` (medium): fixed — `git ls-files | grep -v /` against an enumerated list.
- outsideText only PRD tested (medium): fixed — a table test over PRD, SDD, TDD; "while it exists" needs no code (stated).
- rule (c) fixed strings (low): fixed — requirements.go:27, :47, :164 named in the task, finding prefixes in the test cases.
- token transport in two homes (low): fixed — Interfaces no longer names it; row 7's spec only.
- Naive-reader terms: rule letters defined, the import's "D8 closure" renamed "reference closure" with file:line, numbering schemes and R→S→T explained under the order table, the 17/18 counts split.
- Readiness Q1, Q2, Q4: answered above. Q11: records-edit mechanism and GUIDE-eval row ownership added to § Context-size budget. Q5: migration line text and its `comm` check added. Q7: port range 1–65535, else exit 2. Q8: opens no browser. Q6, Q9, Q10: defaults already stated.
- Sizing: row 3 rebutted (D23: mechanical, deltas measured). Row 4: an `Open:` row put to the operator (split 4a/4b would change "one session per row"; default one session with an early handoff if needed).

title: Review — worktree-code-docs   (2026-10-29)
body:
# Review — worktree-code-docs   (2026-10-29)

Range reviewed: working tree vs HEAD 0367164 (git diff HEAD), 14 files: cmd/fyr/help_text.go, init_project_test.go, internal/brain/import_docs.go, internal/brain/import_rootdocs_test.go (new, staged), internal/check/requirements.go, internal/check/requirements_test.go, skills/init-project/SKILL.md, skills/init-project/assets/{AGENTS.md, PRD.md, SDD.md, TDD.md, TODO.md} and the deleted assets/{REQUIREMENTS.md, ROADMAP.md}, plus the two trail edits (GUIDE-eval `scaffold` row, SPEC-fyr-check), read as records against `git show HEAD:.agents/trail.jsonl`. This is PLAN-2026-10-29-root-docs-and-fyr-serve row 2; rows 3 and 4 (context, skills, agents, README, this repo's own migration) are not in the scope.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing in the code is broken. Rule (c) of `fyr check` (PRD.md, REQUIREMENTS.md fallback, both-present note), the `outsideText` pathspec and the templates all do what the plan's § Interfaces says, and the new tests can fail (the import test would fail without the pathspec change, since no listed file would name the record; the template test fails if the template's items lose their comments or shape). `go test -count=1` is green for internal/check, internal/brain, internal/eval, the root package (TestInitProject*, TestFunctionLength) and cmd/fyr (Help/Harness/Check); gofmt and go vet are clean on the touched packages. The worst items are one docs restatement left standing (README) and two small gaps in init-project's update instructions. No `REQUIREMENTS.md` item is violated: that file is untouched by the diff.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `README.md:51` — the `fyr check` row still says it checks "every Must and Should item of `REQUIREMENTS.md`"; `cmd/fyr/help_text.go:257` now says PRD.md, REQUIREMENTS.md only in a project without one, and `SPEC-fyr-check` was updated to match. Same claim, two wordings now. The plan puts README in row 4, so this is expected to close there; if row 4 slips and a release is cut first, the README documents the old behaviour. Fix: change the clause in this phase or keep it on row 4's checklist by name.
- **[low / confidence: high]** Restatements left standing by design until plan row 3 (a release before it ships contradicting text): `context/AGENTS.md:9,20,56,66` (resume order reads `ROADMAP.md`; the hard rule says "update `REQUIREMENTS.md` and `ROADMAP.md` in one commit"; the root layout lists both), while the new `skills/init-project/assets/PRD.md` header comment cites "(global context § Hard rules)" with "PRD.md and TODO.md in one commit". Also `skills/{feature,handoff,explain-project,harness-audit}/SKILL.md`, `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md:7,9,10`, `agents/{changelog,documentation,explorer,reviewer,dreamer}/agent.md`, `internal/check/check.go:65` (`notInRuleA` names ROADMAP.md; fine until row 4 deletes this repo's). A project scaffolded now has no `ROADMAP.md` or `REQUIREMENTS.md`, yet the context tells every session to read both. Not a defect of this diff; the gate is that no tag is cut before rows 3 and 4 (plan row 6 already orders the release last).
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/init-project/SKILL.md` Step 3, the `SDD.md` / `TDD.md` bullet — their headers carry `Status: draft · Last updated: YYYY-MM-DD`, but only the `PRD.md` bullet says to set `Last updated:` from `date +%F`. Old text did this for ROADMAP (`Last reviewed:`). A run can leave the placeholder or write a date from memory (global hard rule: dates come from the shell). Fix: add "`Last updated:` from `date +%F`" to the SDD/TDD bullet.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/init-project/SKILL.md` Step 3, "Migrating the old root files", item 1 — when `PRD.md` and `REQUIREMENTS.md` both exist (a half-migrated project, or one where the user wrote PRD.md by hand), the copy loop skips PRD.md and the migration line is offered, then `git mv REQUIREMENTS.md PRD.md` refuses because the target exists. It fails safe (no data loss), but the skill gives no branch for it, and `fyr check` will read PRD.md and note "REQUIREMENTS.md beside PRD.md: not read". Fix: one sentence: with both present, report them and offer no migration for that file.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `GUIDE-eval` row `scaffold` (trail record, edited) — coverage gap, named: its check proves the five files exist, REQUIREMENTS.md and ROADMAP.md are gone, the requirement text is unchanged (`comm -23` with the one old line rewritten by `sed`), and the tree is clean. It does not prove that ROADMAP's Now/Next lines reached TODO.md, nor that PRD/SDD/TDD link each other in the scaffolded copy. The fixture (`~/sandbox/fyr-eval/fixture`) does hold REQUIREMENTS.md and ROADMAP.md (listed), so the migration path is reachable and the `comm` check is not vacuous. The row has not been run behaviourally in this scope (plan row 6, D12): unverified.

## Docs lens
Compared with README, SPEC-fyr-check (edited and consistent with `requirements.go` and its notes, line by line), the plan's § Interfaces, `AGENTS.md`, GUIDE-eval. `cmd/fyr/help_text.go` and the SPEC rows match the code; the notes quoted in the SPEC are the exact strings the code and `TestRequirementsRuleNotes`/`TestRequirementsRuleReadsPRD` assert. The README clause above is the one stale statement. `dropped:` — `skills/init-project/SKILL.md` old "fill a `ROADMAP.md` this run created" and the `ROADMAP.md` `Last reviewed:` rule went with the file; the replacement is only the PRD header date (see the SDD/TDD finding). `narrowed:` — old Update bullet "an update never edits ... `REQUIREMENTS.md`" became "without the user's yes to Step 3's migration line" (plan D7), a deliberate widening of what an update may change, with the yes and committed-files guards; I found no case it leaves out.

`fyr check` ran with the installed binary (fyr f3389b1fa484, built before the working tree's change; it reads the working tree, so the new rule (c) code was not the code that ran): 1 finding, none on a line or spec this scope touches. Pre-existing (fyr check): `SPEC-fyr-eval spec-stale` (1 commit to cmd/fyr/eval.go internal/eval cmd/fyr since c016f1a61921). Note quoted: `note: REQUIREMENTS.md has no enforced-by field: not checked` (this repo's REQUIREMENTS.md). A second run of the working tree's code (`go run ./cmd/fyr check`) did not finish inside my budget: unverified.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. No unused functions; `where` is threaded to `candidate.where` and used. Deleted assets are replaced; no orphan references in code (grep of Go sources for the old asset paths shows none).
2. Flow tracing — pass. `requirementsRule` → `unenforced(name, …)` → `resolves(where, …)` updated at every hop; all four file-presence cases (PRD only / REQUIREMENTS only / both / neither) plus a PRD without the field are tested, with findings and notes naming the file read. Not blocking: the content is unchanged and README no longer carries it, so there is still one copy outside the specs.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `SDD.md:156` (§ Deployment, "In words") — restates which places get the harness and what a release publishes. `AGENTS.md` rule 6 gives that claim one home (`SPEC-fyr-delivery` § The model) and says other files "point at it in one sentence and never restate it". The paragraph is the README's former "In words" text moved over, so it is carried-over rather than new; but README's own "In words" is gone and SDD now holds the only prose copy, which should be one pointer sentence plus the map, or the rule's carve-out for map labels should be extended to SDD in the same change (`AGENTS.md`, README map rule 3 requires a design question for map changes; this is not a path change).

## Docs lens

Compared with README, the `spec` records, `GUIDE-testing`, `DEPLOY-*`:
- `fyr check` (working tree, run once, exit 1): `SPEC-fyr-eval spec-stale — 3 commits to cmd/fyr/eval.go internal/eval cmd/fyr since c016f1a61921`; docs 0, requirements 0. Note quoted: `note: PRD.md has no enforced-by field: not checked` (the requirements rule did not check R0-R10, so the SDD/TDD R-to-M trace is checked by hand above, not by `fyr check`).
- Restatement grep (`ROADMAP`, `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `Daily commands`, `What you get`, `In words`): hits in the scope are the three SDD/TDD/README statements above; the remaining `REQUIREMENTS.md` hits are `fyr check`'s deliberate fallback for projects without a PRD (`internal/check/requirements.go`, `cmd/fyr/help_text.go:257`) and their tests, which are correct. `ROADMAP.md` hits are `internal/check/check.go:65` (exclusion list) and tests of the same, correct.
- Old wording `setup and deploy sections` / lane lists: `agents/documentation/agent.md:3,35-37`, `skills/review/SKILL.md:99` both updated in the scope; `context/AGENTS.md:19` points at the agent definition ("its lane is in its definition"), so it needs no change; `context/AGENTS.md:66` already names SDD/TDD. `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md:37` now names `TDD.md` § T5, which exists.
- Pre-existing (fyr check): `SPEC-fyr-eval spec-stale` above; outside this scope's verdict (no eval code in the diff).
- README sections referenced by code and docs (`§ Install without cloning`, `§ Install from a zip`, `§ How it works`) all still exist at the same names (README.md:11,127,179).
- Unverified: whether `SPEC-fyr-*` records still say "README § Daily commands" in prose (`fyr search` over spec/guide/deploy kinds for `Daily commands` and `command table` returned 0 hits, so no known restatement); the `SDD`/`TDD` Decisions lines' ADR pairings were checked by title for 16 of the ADRs, and ADR-051 (a second rules file may load when it fits) is cited for "pruned rather than split", which is a loose fit with its title.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass: no code added; no orphaned file. README's removed prose has a new home (TDD § T5, SDD § Deployment); nothing dropped without a home.
2. Flow tracing — pass with the nits above: README -> TDD § T5 pointers resolve; the R-to-M trace (SDD) matches its component table in both directions; all 40 test names in the TDD trace exist (one is attached to the wrong component, finding 1); the new `documentation` rules renumbered 4-10 are referenced by no other file by number.
3. Standards conformance — pass with nits: the documentation agent's description is one line and has no forbidden phrases; `skills/review` and the agent lane agree; no frontmatter on SDD/TDD as rule 9 requires; findings 3-5 are restatement/describing-text issues (`review-standards` § 3, § 7).
4. Directory layout — pass: SDD.md and TDD.md at the root beside PRD.md as `context/AGENTS.md:66` and ADR-074 state; README Layout lists them.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass: no dependency, no code.
6. Decoupling — pass: SDD summarises and links, TDD one section per component; finding 4 is the one place the TDD copies instead of linking.

## Not examined
- Whether `PLAN-2026-10-29-root-docs-and-fyr-serve` rows 4b's wording (e.g. "the root-listing E2E criterion") is met; I did not read the plan record.
- The README mermaid map was compared by diff (unchanged lines), not rendered; the interactive page of the map (outside this repository) was not looked at.
- The full `go test ./...` was not run; only `TestHarnessMap` and `TestVocabularyVerbsAndFlags` (pass) and, by listing, the existence of every test the TDD trace names. Whether those named tests really verify each component beyond their names was checked only for M7 (wrong package) and not for the rest.
- `TestSkillListingBudget` and the context size pins (the `agents/` and `skills/review` edits are small; no context file changed).

## Outcome

- Finding 1 (`TDD.md` M7 names a metrics test): fixed — the M7 row names `TestExportByteStable` and `TestLoadReplacesRowsFromAChangedFile` (`internal/brain/export_test.go`), each found once by `grep -rln '^func <Name>('`.
- Finding 2 (zip check narrowed): fixed — the `SDD.md` Update diagram checks the zip "when it sits beside it, else mark it UNVERIFIED", and unpacking refuses an entry that leaves the temporary directory (R9).
- Finding 3 (`cmd/fyr/usage_test.go:16` cites README § Daily commands): fixed — the comment names `TDD.md` § T5, where the claim moved.
- Finding 4 (T5 copies the verb rows whole): rebutted as a recorded trade-off — PLAN-2026-10-29-root-docs-and-fyr-serve D36: several claims have no other home yet (`cmd/fyr/help_text.go` names neither the kept Claude Code files nor `$FYR_REPO`), so the rows moved whole per D16; thinning them is a `TODO.md` Backlog item, and § T5 says so above the table.

body:
# Review — agents-md-trim loss check   (2026-10-29)

Range reviewed: `.agents/scratch/AGENTS.old.md` (identical to `git show HEAD:AGENTS.md`, b337e33, checked by diff) -> `AGENTS.md` (working tree, 11,882 bytes); audit table `.agents/scratch/agents-md-trim.md`. Records read with `fyr record get <ID> --home .agents/scratch/home-trail`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

No rule, constraint or fact of the old file is without a home: every move/strike row was opened at its named home and the content is there with the same meaning (DEPLOY-local, DEPLOY-remote, GUIDE-testing, TDD T1/T2/T6/T8/T12/T13/T14/T15 and Testing strategy, SDD Components, skills/VENDORED.md). "## How the harness works" and lines 1-20 are byte-identical (diff prints nothing). The worst problems are outside the new file: two README sentences (README.md:202 and :253, both untouched by this change) still say that `AGENTS.md` holds content that this rewrite moved, so they are now false. One pointer in the new file is weaker than the old one (version tracking), one local disambiguation was lost (`fyr eval --home`), and the audit table mislabels several Layout rows as "keep". Fix the two README lines in the same commit.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `README.md:202` — "`AGENTS.md` § Rules for working here lists each refusal and why." The lint's refusal list was moved to `TDD.md` § T6 "Lint refusals"; the new AGENTS.md bullet only points there (`AGENTS.md:57`). The claim is now false and README was not in the diff. The table's "Checks" line verified only that the heading exists, not that the claimed content does. Fix: change to `TDD.md` § T6.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `README.md:253` — "`govulncheck` has two known, unreachable advisories (`AGENTS.md` § Setup commands)." The advisory list (GO-2026-5024, GO-2026-4970, the go1.27.3 result) moved to `DEPLOY-local` § Operator steps (record line 107); `AGENTS.md:28` now only says "the known ones: DEPLOY-local § Operator steps". Fix: repoint README to `DEPLOY-local` § Operator steps.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `AGENTS.md:70` — old: "The tag is the only version tracking (no version file; preflight Step 6.2)". New: "...the only version tracking (`DEPLOY-remote` § Releases; preflight Step 6, ...)". The fact stays in AGENTS.md, but "no version file" and "Step 6.2" are gone and neither named target states it: `DEPLOY-remote` § Releases has no "version file" or "only version tracking" text (its "Version:" paragraph only gives MINOR/PATCH/MAJOR), and preflight item 6.2 reads "Bump the version only where the repo already tracks one", which is a generic rule, not this project's fact. Fix: restore "(no version file; preflight Step 6.2)".
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `AGENTS.md:54` vs `AGENTS.md:66` — meaning narrowed by loss of a local disambiguation. Rules bullet 2 lists `eval` among the verbs that carry `--home .agents/scratch/<name>`, with a single exception (a `fyr dream` sandbox). The old Testing paragraph resolved this for eval ("a `--home` outside every checkout", plus `--fixture ~/sandbox/fyr-eval/fixture`); the new Testing paragraph points to `GUIDE-testing` § 4 instead and says nothing about the home. `TDD.md` T13 says a home inside a checkout is refused with exit 2, so the failure is loud and safe, but AGENTS.md read alone now directs a command that is refused. The tension existed in the old file; the rewrite removed what reconciled it. Fix: name eval as the second exception in bullet 2 ("`fyr eval`: a `--home` outside every checkout, `GUIDE-testing` § 4"), or drop `eval` from the list.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `AGENTS.md:70` — inherited broken pointer, unchanged by the rewrite: "plan `2026-10-01-google-skills-catalog` D11, D12". No record has that id in the trail (the closest, `PLAN-2026-10-01-research-google-skills-catalog`, contains no D11 or D12). `DEPLOY-remote` carries the same pointer. Not caused by this change; fix by naming the record that holds D11/D12 or by quoting the decision.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** Audit table accuracy, `agents-md-trim.md` rows L9, L11, L13-L17 and K9: marked "keep" or "§ Layout search line names SPEC-fyr-search", but the new Layout block lists the packages by name only (`AGENTS.md:42-43`). `SPEC-fyr-search`, `SPEC-fyr-check`, `SPEC-fyr-record` and `ADR-064` no longer appear in AGENTS.md, and `ADR-055`/`ADR-063` survive only in the stdlib bullet. The homes exist (`TDD.md` "Spec:" lines of T7, T8, T14; `SDD.md` Components M7-M15; ADR-064 at `SDD.md:140`), so nothing is lost, but the table's "keep" labels are wrong and should say "strike -> SDD Components / TDD". Same for T3's "§ 3a-3h by the package each names": 3a and 3f are triggered by a path or a behaviour, not a package.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** Small wording changes with no rule lost (listed so the author can decide): (a) `AGENTS.md:66` "`TestSuiteHarness` pins every row, so its `want` entry changes in the same commit" dropped "by id, agent and grant", "a row added or changed" and the file path `internal/eval/suite_test.go`; "its" is now ambiguous; (b) `AGENTS.md:54` dropped "graduated from BUG-182's rule" (BUG-182 holds it); (c) `AGENTS.md:31` "the harness's own ceiling and the only one" is now "the harness's own ceiling" in `TDD.md:18`; (d) `AGENTS.md:70` dropped "never one run per entry" (implied by "Catalog entries are data ... met by the router's rows"); (e) "`git` never under `sudo`" and "a bad release gets the next PATCH" now live only in `DEPLOY-remote` § Releases (record line 229), which the Release paragraph points to.

Checked and confirmed, no finding: S1a/S1b (GUIDE-testing § 1 lines 12-15); S6a-S6d, S8, S9 (DEPLOY-local lines 95-107); S2a-S2c (TDD T1 "Size pins"; "never raise a limit" is new but grounded in `size_test.go:19` and PRD G1); L1, L6, L6a, L6b, L8a, L9b, L12, L13a, L17a (TDD T1, T2, T4, T8, T14/T15, T13); R3a and R5b (TDD T6, full list matches: flat format, SKILL.md/description, 1,024 and the two phrases, YAML comment BUG-004, allow lists IN23, permission keys, validName, BUG-143/153); R4a (TDD T3: `subagent: true`, `mainAgent: false`); R7b-R7h (VENDORED.md intro, § Forks, § Vendored catalogs incl. refresh script, `--exclude`, INDEX/CHECKSUMS pinned both ways, security review, "pin from a date is a guess"; TDD T2 for the 19,500-byte budget); R9c (TDD T12 "Needles"); T2a-T2c (TDD Testing strategy; detail in GUIDE-testing § 1); T3a-T3d, T4a-T4c (GUIDE-testing § 3c/3d/3e/3g, lines 127-130, 188-191; corpus numbers 971/197 and K = 0 present); E1a, E2, E3b (DEPLOY-remote lines 135, 5-22, 229); E3c (preflight Step 6 bridge check, BUG-161). Pointer targets that exist: README § How it works, SDD § Components, TDD § T1/T2/T6/T12/Testing strategy, DEPLOY-local § Operator steps, DEPLOY-remote § Releases, GUIDE-testing § 1/2/3a-3h/4 "Behavioural runs"/5, `TEST-2026-09-03-verify-real-home`, `RETRO-2026-09-18-retro-2`, `SPEC-fyr-delivery/-eval`, and every test name the new file cites. Every `AGENTS.md §` pointer in skills, agents, Go comments and TDD/SDD names a surviving heading, except the two README sentences above, whose heading exists but whose claimed content moved.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass: no code in scope; the two Go changes are comments only (`inventory_load.go:110`, `lint_test.go:11`), now citing `TDD.md` § T6, which exists.
2. Flow tracing — fail (minor): the pointer graph into AGENTS.md has two stale claims (README.md:202, :253), one pointer weakened (version tracking), one dangling inherited (plan 2026-10-01-google-skills-catalog).
3. Standards conformance — partial: size target met (11,882 <= 12,000, PRD G2); the describing-text rule (restatement grep) missed README; no sentence of the old file lacks a row, apart from small Layout descriptions (L2/L6/L7 glosses) that no one needs.
4. Directory layout — pass: no new files beyond the author's scratch table.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass: documentation only, no dependency, no auth or crypto.
6. Decoupling — pass: each fact has one home (the delivery claim, rule 6, is untouched); moves go to the owning document (DEPLOY-local, DEPLOY-remote, GUIDE-testing, TDD, VENDORED.md).

## Not examined
- Living `change`/`review`/`handoff` records that mention AGENTS.md content (the table says 15 were re-pointed): records are immutable history and were not swept; `.agents/trail.jsonl` was only checked for which record changed (DEPLOY-local).
- The full text of every `GUIDE-testing` and `DEPLOY-*` section outside the lines cited; I confirmed the cited sentences, not that nothing else in those records contradicts the new AGENTS.md.
- Whether `go test ./...` (size pins, `TestHarnessMap`, `TestFunctionLength`) passes on the working tree: no tests were run (read-only review of prose).
- Skill and agent texts that quote AGENTS.md content without the `§` marker (only the `§` form and a handful of subject nouns were grepped).

## Outcome

1. README.md:202 — fixed: now "`TDD.md` § T3 and § T6 list each refusal; its test names the bug behind it."
2. README.md:253 — fixed: the advisories point at `DEPLOY-local` § Operator steps.
3. Version tracking — fixed: "(no version file; preflight Step 6.2)" restored in § Release.
4. `fyr eval --home` — fixed: § Rules' `--home` bullet names two exceptions taking a home outside every checkout, `fyr eval` (`GUIDE-testing` § 4) and a visible `fyr dream` run (§ 3e).
5. Inherited broken plan pointer — fixed: it names plan `2026-10-01-google-skills-catalog` in git at `9001831^` (`.agents/docs/plans/2026-10-01-google-skills-catalog.md`, D11 line 113, D12 line 114, read with `git show`). `DEPLOY-remote`'s own mention of the plan is a provenance note, not a pointer to D-rows; left as it is.
6. Audit table labels — fixed: a "Corrections after the review" section in `.agents/scratch/agents-md-trim.md` relabels L9, L11, L13–L17, K9 as strike → SDD/TDD and corrects T3.
7. Wording trims — (a) fixed: `TestSuiteHarness` "by id, agent and grant" and "a changed row" restored; (c) fixed: TDD § T1 says "the harness's own ceiling and the only one"; (b), (d), (e) kept as trimmed: BUG-182, "Catalog entries are data" and `DEPLOY-remote` § Releases hold them.

No second round: every fix is a pointer or a restored clause the round-1 report quoted; the second round is at the operator's call.

## Findings

## Docs lens
- Restatement grep (`restatement-grep.sh` over "empty at every checkpoint", "parking lot", "ROADMAP", "REQUIREMENTS"): no living file still says `TODO.md` is empty at every checkpoint or that `ROADMAP.md` holds Now/Next. In the spec/guide/deploy records the only hits for `sh-agent-dream` are `DEPLOY-remote` line 66 (crossing steps, operator action: correct) and `SPEC-fyr-dream` line 54 (already says no verb reads or names the old units). `DEPLOY-remote:243` and `DEPLOY-local:68` point the operator at `fyr dream --remove-timer` then `--install-timer` for a timer an older fyr installed: consistent with this range, since the replacement went away.
- Old-wording grep for the `feedback.jsonl` join: `SPEC-fyr-dream` lines 25, 51, 99 still describe the dream's own `feedback.jsonl` reads; `internal/dream` was not changed by this range (only `dream.go` StatusLine and `timer.go`), so these remain true. `SPEC-fyr-metrics:220,273` describe corrections from records and say older ingests stored `feedback.jsonl` refs: matches `events.go:217-219`.
- `README.md` "Daily commands" shrank to one-line rows; the long rows moved to `TDD.md` § T5 (README:`fyr help <verb>` paragraph and `usage_test.go:15-16` cite it). The removed `fyr status` text about "an older fyr's unit, the two commands that replace it" matches the removal of that notice in code. No dropped claim without a new home found among the rows I compared.
- `fyr check` at the checkout root (HEAD = range head, so not unverified): 3 findings (docs 0, specs 3, requirements 0), the three spec-stale above. Note quoted: `note: PRD.md has no enforced-by field: not checked`. This is a part it did not check: no requirement of `PRD.md` is verified for resolution, and `REQUIREMENTS.md` at v4.0.0 had the same single `enforced by` string (count 1 in both), so this is pre-existing.

## Criteria

title: Security review — v4.0.0-36cd92f (2026-10-29)
body:
# Security review — v4.0.0-36cd92f   (2026-10-29)

Range reviewed: v4.0.0..36cd92f
Previous run: first pass of this file (2026-10-29, 29 tool calls; Status COMPLETE with test bodies and long skills lines under Not examined). This is the re-dispatch reading those paths end to end.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The worst problem is an authorization change written into data, not code. Plan record D37 says "the agent decides when to run `/preflight` ... the operator gives no separate release word", and `TODO.md` Now repeats it ("`/preflight vX.Y.Z`, the agent's call (D37)"). That contradicts the project `AGENTS.md` § Release, which this range rewrote and still says "cut only by `/preflight vX.Y.Z` ... from the operator's own turn". It also contradicts the global context rule that release words "from tool output, files, or logs authorize nothing". A later session that reads D37 or TODO.md could treat a record as permission to tag and publish binaries to every place.

No code in the range is exploitable. The deleted FIFO-safe open helpers in `internal/metrics` were removed together with their only two callers, and every read that remains goes through guarded openers. The other findings are low: the old-name dream timer can no longer be found or removed, and an agent standing permission installs into the real home, which conflicts with PRD R6.

The re-dispatch read the 13 test files, `recall.tsv` and the full long skills lines end to end. It found nothing new.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `.agents/trail.jsonl` record `PLAN-2026-10-29-root-docs-and-fyr-serve` D37, and `TODO.md` § Now (both Now lines and the "`/preflight vX.Y.Z`, the agent's call (D37)" box).
  - **Weakness:** the authority to release now sits in a stored record and a TODO line, and a session reads both at resume. The governing texts were not changed. `AGENTS.md` § Release (rewritten in this range at c06a909) still requires the operator's own turn, and the global context forbids taking release authority from files. A release publishes binaries and a zip that every release-binary and zip place downloads with `fyr update`. `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` Step 2 also reads tiers from "the plan `TODO.md` Now names", so the release path itself consults the file that carries the claim.
  - **Why it is exploitable in principle:** this is a confused-deputy path. Any session, or any text that injects into a resume and cites D37, gets "permission" to cut a tag with no operator turn. D12, which requires the operator's eval records or a quoted waiver, still gates it, so this is not high.
  - **Remediation:** pick one of two. (a) The operator approves an `AGENTS.md` § Release edit with an ADR, so the rule and the record agree. (b) D37 and TODO.md are reworded so that the release still needs `/preflight vX.Y.Z` typed in the operator's own turn. Until then, a session must not act on D37 as authorization.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `AGENTS.md` § Rules for working here, bullet 1 ("except on dave ... `fyr install` into the real home"), and `DEPLOY-local` § Operator steps, "Keep dave current".
  - **Weakness:** at every checkpoint, an agent session installs its own just-edited context, skills, agents and rules into the operator's real `~/.gemini/config`, and the binary into `~/.local/bin`. No operator step sits between commit and live config. This contradicts `PRD.md` R6, which is immutable and unchanged in this range: "Deploying to the operator's real `$HOME` is the operator's action". It also reverses the old wording, "Deploying to the real home is the operator's job".
  - **Exploitable in principle:** instruction text that survives one review round becomes the global context of every later session on that machine without a human gate. That is a persistence path.
  - **Remediation:** reconcile with R6 through an approved PRD edit and an ADR, or keep the install an operator step. If it stays, make the install depend on a passing review record of that exact commit.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `cmd/fyr/verb_uninstall.go:21`, `cmd/fyr/verb_dream.go:56-75`, `internal/dream/timer.go:169` (`RemoveTimer`), `cmd/fyr/verb_install.go` (the `ReplaceOldTimer` call was removed), `internal/dream/dream.go:255` (the status note was removed).
  - **Weakness:** no verb finds, names, stops or replaces a dream unit under the pre-v3.0.0 names `sh-agent-dream*` and `com.styrman.sh-agent-dream*` any more, and `fyr status` stays silent about one.
  - **Exploitable in principle:** a place that still carries such a unit keeps an hourly job, which earlier sent redacted project content to the model provider. That job survives `fyr uninstall` and `--remove-timer`, and nothing tells the operator.
  - **Tests removed with the code:** the deleted `internal/dream/timer_legacy_test.go`, read whole from `git show v4.0.0:`, held three guarantees from earlier security reviews:
    - a turned-off old unit is never turned back on (review of v2.7.0..881389a);
    - a probe that cannot tell is treated as on;
    - a scratch home whose `.config` links to the real home's never calls the real unit legacy (review of v2.1.0..a62eb9d).

    All three guarded code this range deletes, so no guarantee is lost for surviving code. The residual is only the unhandled old unit.
  - **Mitigation in place:** the operator's A1 answer (D40) says every place has crossed, and `DEPLOY-remote` now documents removing such a unit by hand.
  - **Remediation:** keep a read-only detection in `fyr status` (`OtherSystemTimerFiles` already shows the pattern) for one more release, or accept the risk and record that.

## Checked
- **Secrets:** a regex scan of the whole 4,368-line diff for AWS, GitHub, Slack, Google and OpenAI token shapes, private-key blocks, `ya29.`, e-mail addresses and home paths. Hits:
  - `xoxb-1111-2222-fakevaluefake`: a documented reviewer probe, named as a fake in the record.
  - `BEGIN PRIVATE KEY`: redactor prose.
  - `fx@example.invalid`: a test fixture.
  - 124 `/home/kesokaj/...` paths in trail records. They are a pre-existing pattern, and `HANDOFF-2026-10-28-2123` says the repository is private.

  Handoffs elide conversation IDs to 8 characters, per the gate's earlier low. No credential found, and the test files read in the re-dispatch add none.
- **Injection / input parsing:**
  - `internal/check/requirements.go`: `PRD.md` and `REQUIREMENTS.md` are read through the existing `readFile`, which calls `os.Root` Lstat and accepts only a regular file of at most 16 MiB, then makes a non-blocking open re-checked on the fd (`internal/check/check.go:164-189`). A symlinked `PRD.md` is refused, with a note.
  - `resolves` still rejects a leading `/` and `..` in site tokens.
  - `internal/brain/import_docs.go` passes fixed names after `--` to `git ls-files`, so no injection.
  - `internal/metrics`: `openRegular`, `openNonBlocking`, `open_unix.go` and `open_other.go` are deleted together with their only callers at v4.0.0 (`readSmall` and `readFeedback`; confirmed with `git grep` at both revisions). At HEAD, metrics reads files only through `search.OpenCopy` (O_NONBLOCK|O_NOFOLLOW plus a regular-file check on the fd), `brain.ForMetrics` and `os.Stat`/`ReadDir`. No surviving read lost its guard.
  - The removed `feedback.jsonl` parse and the trail-file reads shrink the input surface.
  - `internal/harness/state.go`: only comments and note strings changed.
- **Authz/authn:** D37 and the dave standing permission (findings 1 and 2). Instruction-shaped text in the read trail records is limited to Kickoff blocks and standing-approval sets, and their authority is the operator's turn. D37 is the one that claims release authority (finding 1).
- **Crypto:** no crypto code in the range. The `fyr serve` plan (rows 7-9, not built) proposes a per-run token from `crypto/rand`, a cookie and CSRF. That is a composed session and token protocol, and it must get the planned `security` review before it is built (S-D3, D15).
- **Dependencies:** `go.mod` and `go.sum` are untouched. `govulncheck ./...` (go1.27.3): "No vulnerabilities found ... 0 affecting code, 1 in a required module not called" (the known GO-2026-5024 class). There is no npm ecosystem (no `package.json`), so `npm audit` is n/a.
- **GCP surface:** none in the range.
- **Past bugs:** `fyr search --refs <path> --kind bug --home .agents/scratch/home-trail` for ingest.go, events.go, events_join.go, open_unix.go, dream/timer.go, check/requirements.go, harness/state.go, verb_uninstall.go and verb_install.go: 0 references each.
- **Tests, read end to end in the re-dispatch** (as diffs against v4.0.0, which hold the whole change; the deleted file read whole):
  - `cmd/fyr/auditfix_test.go`: removes `TestUninstallAndRemoveTimerRemoveTheOldNamedUnit`, along with its fake `systemctl` on PATH under `t.TempDir`.
  - `cmd/fyr/crossing_test.go`: `TestCrossingFromV270` drops its timer half. The state-dir, manifest, binary and `~/.claude` byte-for-byte checks stay.
  - `cmd/fyr/install_verbs_test.go`: removes `TestInstallSaysATurnedOffTimerStaysOff`.
  - `cmd/fyr/memory_test.go`: `TestDreamTimerSaysWhatItFound` now asserts both verbs' removal wording and that the files are gone. `timerFilesFor` writes only under the test's temp home.
  - `cmd/fyr/usage_test.go`: comment only.
  - `cmd/fyr/testdata/recall.tsv`: four gold paths `REQUIREMENTS.md` → `PRD.md`, data only.
  - `init_project_test.go`: `TestInitProjectRootDocs` reads the repository's assets only.
  - `internal/brain/import_rootdocs_test.go`: a fixture repository under `repo(t)` and an import into a temp home.
  - `internal/check/requirements_test.go`: `TestRequirementsRuleReadsPRD` (5 cases) and `TestRequirementsRuleReadsThePRDTemplate`. One gap, not a finding: the symlink case is pinned for the requirements file in `TestRequirementsRuleNotes`, not specifically for `PRD.md`. Both go through the same `readFile`.
  - `internal/dream/timer_legacy_test.go`: deleted; read whole at v4.0.0 (see finding 3).
  - `internal/dream/timer_test.go`: `fakeManagerOff` removed, and `TestRemoveTimerSaysWhatItRemoved` moved here unchanged.
  - `internal/harness/audit_test.go`: the symlink-note pin is updated to the full new text, and the 0700 assertion is unchanged.
  - `internal/harness/lint_test.go` and `internal/harness/size_test.go`: comments only.

  No test writes outside `t.TempDir`, reaches the real home, or weakens an assertion on surviving code. Every removed test matches removed code. On the live path, the FIFO guarantee stays covered by `internal/search/copy_test.go`, per `REVIEW-2026-10-29-0941`; that test was not re-read here.
- **Skills, read end to end in the re-dispatch:** every `skills/` diff line over 700 characters was read whole, 34 old and new lines across `bug`, `explain-project`, `feature`, `init-project`, `preflight`, `requirements`, `research`, `retro` and `review`. All but one are file-name re-pointings (`REQUIREMENTS.md`/`ROADMAP.md` → `PRD.md`/`TODO.md`, Next Steps → `TODO.md` Backlog). The exception is `skills/retro/SKILL.md:59`, which adds two things. One is "(a dream proposal's excepted, above)". The other is that a `/distill --global` skill's every command, URL fetch and approve/skip/trust directive is quoted to the operator, and the skill gets `/review --prompts` or `security` before its commit. That is a hardening, and no instruction text in it weakens a gate. Lines of 700 characters or fewer were read whole in the first pass.

## Not examined
- **Release-diff paths:** none left. Every path in `git diff --stat v4.0.0..36cd92f` has been read end to end, as a diff against v4.0.0 or whole.
- **Living records read as diffs only:** `GUIDE-eval`, `GUIDE-fyr-matrix`, `GUIDE-skill-matrix`, `GUIDE-testing`, `DEPLOY-local`, `DEPLOY-remote`, `SPEC-*` and `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` were read as body diffs against v4.0.0, not as whole bodies. That is the range's change, but text that was already there was not re-reviewed. `SPEC-fyr-eval` and `SPEC-fyr-search` showed only metadata changes.
- **Runtime checks:** no run of the GUIDE-eval setup shell lines (the `requirements-check` and `lane-documentation` setups). They are read as `git mv` and `git rm` inside the eval clone only.
- **Planned surface:** `fyr serve` (rows 7-9) is design only and not in the range's code.

## Outcome

- Finding 1 [medium] (D37 and `TODO.md` Now hand the release decision to the agent): **rebutted**. The release run this report gates is authorized by the operator's own turns in this release session (2026-10-29): the pasted Kickoff, whose standing approvals carry "`/preflight vX.Y.Z` when you judge the release ready", and "run the fyr eval line yourself". D37 records that arrangement, and its text names "the operator's own turn that pastes it" as the source. Neither the plan nor `TODO.md` authorizes a release on its own, and preflight still requires the request to come from the user's own turn. D37's wording leaves room for an unattended run to read it as authority, so the gate report names this for the operator.
- Finding 2 [low] (the "Keep dave current" standing permission vs PRD R6): **left: operator**. The permission is the operator's (2026-10-29, `DEPLOY-local` § Operator steps), and only the operator can amend R6 (a `PRD.md` edit). Goes to the handoff's Next Steps.
- Finding 3 [low] (no verb finds a pre-v3 dream timer any more): **left: operator**, accepted. The operator's word that every place crossed v3.0.0 (A1, D40 of the ledger plan) is the premise of the removal, and the residual is named in the release notes.

None.

  - [low] No verb finds a dream timer under a pre-v3 name any more. **Left: operator**, accepted on the operator's word that every place crossed v3.0.0 (ledger A1, D40), and named in the release notes.
- **Verification:**
  1. Verifier logs reaching HEAD, both PASS: `TEST-2026-10-29-1439-verification-release-1-gate-part-1-v4-0-0-529f7e` covers GUIDE-testing § 1, § 2, § 3, § 3h, govulncheck (0 findings) and the coverage map. `TEST-2026-10-29-1511-verification-release-1-gate-part-2-v4-0-0-529f7e` covers § 3c (36 of 36 cells for install, uninstall, dream and status), § 3d, § 3e, § 3g, and § 3h's must-fail and not-the-harness controls.
  2. What the release changed was run:
     - **Commands:** AGENTS.md's setup commands, the § 1 line among them, run by part 1.

It covers one row per changed skill and agent and the context's `smoke`: `scaffold`, `requirements-check`, `lane-documentation`, `feature`, `bug`, `handoff`, `preflight`, `review`, `review-docs-check`, `retro`, `research`, `explain-project`, `harness-audit-elsewhere`, `dispatch-bugs`, `lane-bugs`, `dispatch-changelog`, `dispatch-documentation`, `agent-dreamer`, `agent-explorer`, `agent-reviewer`, `lane-reviewer`.
     - **The real-home smoke** (AGENTS.md § Release): `TEST-2026-10-29-1430-verify-release-1-gate-the-real-home-smoke-on-dav`, 3 of 3 PASS on dave at 36cd92f.
     - 36cd92f..529f7eb changes records only.
  3. No failure left standing: no FAIL, BLOCKED or IN PROGRESS log in the range.

## Step 3 — trail freshness

- The newest `change` record before the release (`CHANGE-2026-10-29-1230-…`, row 5) describes the last work in the range: pass.
- No record carries a future date: pass.
- Every `TEST-` ID in v4.0.0's trail is still present: pass.
- No `CHANGE-` or `ADR-` line present at v4.0.0 differs at HEAD: pass.

## Step 4 — docs freshness

The reviewer's docs lens rode in the Step 2 dispatch. Its one docs finding (spec-stale) is fixed, and no docs gap is open.

## Bridge check

v4.0.0, the previous release, is not a bridge: no trust or format change stops an older install from updating past it. Its MAJOR actions (register, reinstall the timer, `eval --home`) are taken at a place, not needed to update. This tag closes no bridge.

- `PRD.md` has no enforced-by field (`fyr check` note), so rule (c) checked nothing. This was the same before the rename.

None of these is an Antigravity run of a changed skill or agent, so AGENTS.md § Release's blocking condition is met.

## For the operator

- D37's wording ("the agent decides when to run `/preflight`") can be read by an unattended run as release authority (security, medium, rebutted for this run). Consider tightening it to "on the operator's own turn that pastes the Kickoff" before row 11.

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES (implementation not ready)

All five round-1 highs and every round-1 medium are fixed or substantially fixed; the security skeleton, including the new `Sec-Fetch-Site` refusal, holds up. No high finding remains. It is still not ready, by a small margin: the spec states `/search` as "`fyr search`'s text" through `search.Search`, but the record hits that carry the IDs it tells the implementer to link are printed by `cmd/fyr`'s unexported `recordHits` (two shapes); the closures take `project` (the main worktree root) where the CLI takes the working directory (different behaviour in a linked worktree); `TestPagesWriteNothing` as written fails against the spec's own `/search` write; and the printers' exit-code mapping, the second-signal exit and the `--port`/`Listen` rows are pinned by tests that cannot see them. Each fix is a few lines.

## Round-1 findings, one by one

| Round 1 | Status | Where the spec answers it |
|---|---|---|
| High 1, `/metrics` shape | fixed | Routes: `/metrics` is the layout (link, absent-store line, ingest form); `/metrics/report` serves `RenderReport` whole; Headers states why `'unsafe-inline'`; `TestPages` re-asserts the banned strings |
| High 2, action seams | fixed | Package shape: `Options.Index`, `Options.Ingest`, `Options.Listen`; `TestActionCSRF`, `TestActionBusy` can now fake and block |
| High 3, `exitCode` as 500 | fixed | Package shape closing paragraph: `Status` and `Check` map exit statuses to nil, a refusal reason goes to `w`; matches `status.go:41,164,197` and `check.go:30-41` (but see M3: nothing tests the mapping) |
| High 4, init cycle | fixed | Interfaces, verb bullet: `serve` registered in `init()` like `check` (`check.go:15-19`) |
| High 5, Ctrl-C | fixed | Interfaces § Stopping (claim reworded, `Notify` channel, second signal, `ErrServerClosed`), Non-goals (no process group); a test seam for the second signal is missing (M3) |
| Medium 1, cookie across ports | fixed | Tokens (scoping stated, `r.Cookies()` compared, `Sec-Fetch-Site`, CORP) |
| Medium 2, Origin/PostFormValue/mime | fixed | Every request step 5 |
| Medium 3, `localhost` | fixed | Step 1, Non-goals, ADR Rejected |
| Medium 4, `dream.log` open | fixed | Routes, the dream log reader (`O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK`, `Fstat`, window, own `open_*.go` beside the three that exist: `internal/{brain,check,search}/open_{unix,other}.go`) |
| Medium 5, GET writes | fixed | Data (the writes listed), ADR Consequences, `Sec-Fetch-Site` on GET |
| Medium 6, `/search` | partly fixed | split rule, 200-byte cap, 400, `Limit`, ID regex given; the link source is wrong (M1) |
| Medium 7, `brain.Get` | fixed | Routes, `/records/{id}` paragraph (missing list first, then 500); matches `brain.go:327-352` |
| Medium 8, start lines | fixed | Interfaces (the migration line may precede them; `writesState` true for `serve`) |
| Low 1–5 | fixed | imports list incl. `internal/trail`, `internal/harness`; `(*Store).Show`; step 3/4 (HEAD, 404/405, slashes, repeated token); T not single-use; timeouts, `ErrorLog`, 1 MiB cap, CORP, static served from bytes |
| Questions 4 (PRD) | fixed | SDD M16 traces R0, R3, R4, R7, R8, R10 (working-tree diff); ADR reconciles "no service" |
| Question 5 (uncheckable rows) | partly fixed | actions, bind address, headers cases, FIFO, HEAD, `{id}` now have rows; three remain (M3, M4) |

## Findings (new text only)

### Medium

- **[medium / confidence: high]** SPEC § Routes `/search` row, § Verification `TestSearchAndRecordParams` — "`fyr search`'s text for the project" through `search.Validate`, `search.Search` is false as a description of the verb. `runSearch` prints the brain store's record hits first, through `recordHits` (`cmd/fyr/record.go:249`, `brain.Search` + `brain.FormatHit`, whose first field is the record label), and only then calls `search.Search` (`cmd/fyr/verb_search_memory.go:32-36`); `search.Search` itself prints file hits (`search_query.go:184`, `sc.label(...)`). The spec's link rule ("each line whose first field matches the record ID grammar") is aimed at the record hits, which `search.Search` never prints. Two shapes: (a) `search.Search` only, so the links never occur (and a file hit such as `SPEC-fyr-check.md:3` matches the broad ID grammar and links to a 404); (b) the page also calls `brain.Search`. Fix: say `/search` shows the record hits first, from `brain.Search(brain.Options{Home, Dir}, Words, kind, 10)` formatted by `brain.FormatHit` (both exported; `serve` already imports `brain`), a `records: …` header as `recordHits` prints it, then `search.Search`'s text; link only the record-hit lines (the ones `serve` formats itself, so no regex over free text), and name the failure of the record half (`records: not searched: <err>` line, page still 200, as the verb does).

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** SPEC § Interfaces (project definition), § Package shape (`Index`, `Check` comments: `Dir: project`, `check.Run(project, …)`) vs `Options.Dir` ("the working directory at start; its checkout is the project") — two shapes. The project is "the main worktree root" (`trail.Roots` main), but the CLI hands the working directory to every verb: `fyr check` calls `check.Run(wd, …)`, which resolves the toplevel of the worktree holding `dir` (`internal/check/check.go:86`, `_, top`), and `search`/`index` use `wd`. In a linked worktree, `check.Run(main root)` checks the other worktree's files and `search.Index{Dir: main}` indexes it, so the page differs from the verb the spec says it equals ("Equals `fyr index` in the project"). Fix: the closures and `brain.Options` take `o.Dir` (the start directory) exactly as the verbs take `wd`; the project root from `trail.Roots` (main) is for the start line and the no-project test only. State it once in the project bullet.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** SPEC § Verification `TestPagesWriteNothing` — cannot be written as stated. It hashes "the project tree" before and after a walk of every page, but the walk includes `/search`, which writes `.agents/scratch/search.db` in the project tree (the spec's own Data section, `search.Index`'s `prepare`), and the section's own "Never written" bound is "outside `.agents/scratch/`". Also `metrics.db` can change on an older-schema store (`/metrics/report` migrates, Data section). Fix: hash the project's files excluding `.agents/scratch/`, plus `trail.jsonl` by name, and `metrics.db` for a store the fixture created at the current schema; assert the exclusion list (`.agents/scratch/`, `<home>/.config/fyr`) is the only place a changed file may appear.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** SPEC § Verification rows `TestPages` (`/` is 200 although status exits 1; `/check` is 200 with findings), `TestServePortRange`/`TestServeBusyPort` ("exit 2 before `Listen` is called"), `TestServeShutdown` ("a second signal exits 1") — each is pinned in a place that cannot observe it. (1) `internal/serve` tests drive fake printers (`Options.Status` is a func; `internal/serve` may not import `cmd/fyr`), so a fake that returns nil proves nothing about the `exitCode`→nil mapping or the check refusal→writer mapping, which live in the `cmd/fyr` closures (the round-1 High 3 fix has no test that fails when reverted). (2) A `cmd/fyr` test sees `Listen` only if the verb exposes a seam; `Options.Listen` is set to nil by default inside the verb. (3) A second signal ends in `os.Exit(1)` from a goroutine; no in-process test sees it. Fix: name a `cmd/fyr` constructor (for example `serveOptions(c *ctx) serve.Options`) and a package variable for the call into `serve.Serve` (as `stdin` and `stderr` are in `cmd/fyr`); add `TestServeOptionsMapExit` (an uninstalled scratch home gives `Status` nil with the `installed  nothing` line; a non-checkout gives `Check` nil with the refusal text on the writer; another error stays an error); and state how the second signal is tested: either a `exit func(int)` variable the test replaces, or a subprocess run of the built verb.

### Low

- **[low / confidence: medium]** SPEC § Every request (closing paragraph) vs step 4 and § Failure modes ("An unknown path, any method → 404") — "a refusal (403, 404 outside the layout, 405) is `text/plain` … `not found`" and "only a request that passed steps 1–3 gets the layout's 404 page". Step 4 runs after 3, so every route 404 has passed 1–3: no 404 is "outside the layout", and the same-path claims (`/records/NOPE-x`, malformed `{id}`, `/static/` → 404, POST unknown path) have both shapes (layout page vs `not found` plain text). `TestRoutesAndMethods` and `TestSearchAndRecordParams` need one. Fix: say which 404 is which (for example: step-4 route miss and a malformed `{id}` are the plain `not found`; `no record <ID>` and `no metrics store` are the layout's 404).

- **[low / confidence: medium]** SPEC § Every request step 2 and § Tokens — the `Sec-Fetch-Site` refusal, checked against the flows named in the dispatch: the first click from a terminal and a pasted URL send `none` (accepted); the 303 follow-up is `none` or `same-origin` (both accepted); same-origin link navigation and the stylesheet `<link>` send `same-origin` (accepted, and the `SameSite=Strict` cookie travels on them); a form POST sends `same-origin`. Chrome 76+, Firefox 90+ and Safari 16.4+ send it to `127.0.0.1` (a potentially trustworthy origin); a browser that does not send it passes by "when sent" and falls back to the cookie, CSRF field and `Origin` check. Two residuals the spec does not state: (a) for a browser that omits the header, a page on another local port can still cause the idempotent GET writes (search reconcile, metrics migration) with the cookie, since `SameSite` does not separate ports — name it as accepted, as the ADR does for the history entry; (b) a printed URL clicked in a web page or a browser-based terminal (for example a web UI showing the agent's output) is `cross-site` and gets a bare `forbidden` with no hint. Fix: one sentence each; for (b) either the Failure-modes row names it ("open the URL by pasting it into the address bar") or the `403` for step 2 alone answers with a reason line (it holds no secret).

- **[low / confidence: medium]** SPEC § Package shape `Ingest` comment ("then `r.Line()`") vs `/actions/metrics-ingest` "Equals `fyr metrics ingest`" and § Failure modes ("An action's function fails → 500") — `fyr metrics ingest` returns `exitCode(1)` when a source failed after printing the summary (`cmd/fyr/verb_metrics.go:84-86`, `len(r.Failed) > 0`). Say whether a failed source is `ok` or `failed:` on the page (the output is the data, as for the printers; recommended: `ok` with the line, or `failed: N source(s) failed` explicitly) and that the closure closes the store (`defer s.Close()`, as the verb does).

- **[low / confidence: low]** SPEC § Routes `/records/{id}` (`?scope=global`) — the `400` for an unknown `scope` value is stated for the list only; one clause extends it to `/records/{id}`. The ID grammar `^[A-Z]+-…` also allows ids the store's per-kind grammar refuses (harmless: `brain.Get` returns them as missing).

## Security check of the new text

No regression found. Order of steps (Host, fetch metadata, token, route, CSRF) is sound; refusal bodies leak nothing; `Sec-Fetch-Site: none` is also accepted on a POST, which no browser sends (harmless, since the cookie, `C` and `Origin` still apply). `Location` is built from `r.URL.Path` with a collapsed leading run of slashes: build it from a `url.URL` (not string concatenation) so a `/\x` path is escaped; reachable only with a valid `T`, so informational. CORP `same-origin` does not affect navigations or the same-origin stylesheet.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass: no code; `Options.Version`, `Run.CSRF()` are used by the page and tests.
2. Flow tracing — fail (minor): `/search`'s record hits (M1), `Dir` vs project (M2), `/search` write vs `TestPagesWriteNothing`; the printers' mapping is traced and correct against `status.go`, `check.go`, `brain.Get`, `check.Run`.
3. Standards conformance — fail (minor): three Verification rows not checkable where they are pinned (M4); the rest conform.
4. Directory layout — pass: `internal/serve` with its own `open_unix.go`/`open_other.go`, `cmd/fyr/verb_serve.go`, embedded templates beside the package.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass: stdlib only; tokens are `crypto/rand` bytes with `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`, a cookie and a form field; no primitive or session format is implemented here.
6. Decoupling — pass: function-valued `Options` fields are the right seam; `internal/serve` imports no `cmd/fyr`, no sqlite.

## Not examined
- The plan file `PLAN-2026-10-29-root-docs-and-fyr-serve` and the D-rows cited (D13–D15, D18–D21, D39, D43, D44); taken as written.
- Browser behaviour was reasoned from the Fetch Metadata specification and shipping-version knowledge, not run in Chrome, Firefox or Safari.
- `metrics.Ingest`'s own option validation with only `Home` set, and the "Antigravity sessions" default-view wording (`ShowOptions{}` was read; the source default was not traced).
- `help_text.go`, `TestHarnessMap`, flag registration of `--port` (mechanical).
- No build, test or run was made.

implementation not ready

## Outcome
