All eight fixed in the stored spec: `/search` names its record half (`brain.Search`, `brain.FormatHit`, linked by the hit's ID) and its file half; every call takes `Options.Dir`, the main root only for the start line and the no-project test; `TestPagesWriteNothing` excludes `.agents/scratch/` and fixes the metrics schema; `cmd/fyr` gets `serveOptions`, `serveRun` and `serveExit`, with `TestServeOptionsMapExit`, `TestServePortRange` and `TestServeSecondSignal` there; the plain and layout 404s are named; the step-2 403 carries a pasting hint and the no-header residual is stated as accepted; an ingest with failed sources is `failed:` with a 500 and the store is closed; `scope` is checked on `/records/{id}`; `Location` is built as a `url.URL`. No third round (review Steps 4–5: at most two); these fixes are unreviewed, and row 8's `reviewer` and `security` read the code built against them.

title: Review — fyr serve row 8, code and docs, round 1 (2026-10-29)
body:
# Review — fyr-serve-row8   (2026-10-29)

Range reviewed: uncommitted working tree on main, .agents/scratch/row8.diff (internal/serve, cmd/fyr/verb_serve.go and its wiring, AGENTS/README/SDD/TDD, cmd/fyr/help_text.go), against SPEC-fyr-serve (stored record) and the revised draft .agents/scratch/SPEC-fyr-serve.md

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing in the code is broken against the spec. I read every non-test file of `internal/serve` and `cmd/fyr/verb_serve.go` line by line against the spec's request order (Host, Sec-Fetch-Site, token/cookie, route), the five headers, the 303 Location construction, the record-ID grammar, the dream-log reader and the exit/signal behaviour. `go vet`, `gofmt -l`, `go test -race ./internal/serve`, `go test ./cmd/fyr` (full), the root pins `TestFunctionLength` and `TestGitTestPackagesDropGitVariables`, and the vocabulary/help/lint pins all pass. A live run on port 39871 against `.agents/scratch/home-trail` matched the spec: 403 `forbidden` without a token, 303 plus `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict` cookie, 200 on every read page with the cookie, `localhost` Host 403, `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` gets the paste-the-URL line, POST on a page 405, `/static/` and `/records/` 404, all five headers present. What remains is documentation drift: one project rule that lists state-writing verbs omits `serve` (the same family as BUG-182), one TDD sentence about `--repo` is now wrong for `serve`, and a few spec-draft and help-text statements are stale or incomplete.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `AGENTS.md:54` — the rule "Every `fyr` verb that writes state (`record`, `memory add`, `index`, `search`, `metrics ingest`, `dream`, `eval`) carries `--home .agents/scratch/<name>`" does not list `serve`, yet this diff makes `serve` write state (`cmd/fyr/run_dispatch.go` `writesState` answers true: brain store loads trail.jsonl, `/search` reconciles `search.db`, `/metrics/report` can migrate `metrics.db`). Failure: the next session's "manual walk" or a Kickoff runs `fyr serve` without `--home` and writes the real `~/.config/fyr` — exactly BUG-182/BUG-006's family, which this rule exists to prevent. Fix: add `serve` to that list in the same commit (and to any Kickoff template that names verbs).
- **[low / confidence: high]** `TDD.md:73` — "a verb that does not read [`--repo`], every verb but `install`, `sync`, `status`, `diff`, `update`, `list`, `render`, `adopt` and `eval`, says on stderr that it ignored it". `serve` is registered `source: true` (`cmd/fyr/verb_serve.go:23`) and passes `c.src` to `status` and `render`, so it reads `--repo` and gives no warning (checked: `fyr serve --repo . --port 0` prints none). The list is now wrong by one verb. Fix: add `serve` to the list.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/scratch/SPEC-fyr-serve.md:3` — the draft header still says "Code to be: `internal/serve`, `cmd/fyr/verb_serve.go`" while the status line above it says the read pages are built. Also `§ Package shape` says `serveOptions(c *ctx) serve.Options`; the code is `serveOptions(c *ctx) (serve.Options, error)` (os.Getwd can fail) and adds a third test seam, `serveNotify`, next to `serveRun` and `serveExit`, which the spec names only two of. Fix: "Code:", the real signature, name `serveNotify`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/help_text.go:265-272` — the `serve` page never states the default port (3000), though README, TDD T16 and the spec do, and the flag line reads "the port N on 127.0.0.1, 1-65535". An operator reading only `fyr help serve` cannot tell what a bare `fyr serve` binds. Fix: add "(default 3000)" to the flag description or the about text.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** records outside the diff: `GUIDE-testing` has no section for `internal/serve` (its § 3a–3h are chosen "by the package each names"; none names `serve`) and `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` has no `serve` rows, though § 3d says "a new or changed verb also gets its rows in GUIDE-fyr-matrix". A verifier dispatched over this range will run only § 1. Not a code defect; name them in the row's remaining boxes or the change record so they are not silently skipped.

Observation, not a finding: `.agents/trail.jsonl` became modified during my review (mtime 16:06:56; SPEC-fyr-delivery's `updated` bumped). I ran only `record get`/`list`/`search` against the scratch home, and re-running them did not touch the file, so I believe another writer (the main thread) did it; it is not in row8.diff. Check it is intended before staging.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. `Run.CSRF()` and the drawn CSRF token are used only by tests until row 9; the spec names them as row 9's, so not dead, but remove them if row 9 slips.
2. Flow tracing — pass. Host, fetch-metadata, token, route order matches the spec; the 303 Location is a `url.URL`, leading slashes collapsed (a `//evil.example` target gives `/evil.example`); every cookie of the run's name is compared; `exitCode` from `status` is mapped to nil; check refusals go to the writer; the first signal cancels, the second calls `serveExit(1)`; store errors fail only their page (TestStoreErrorIsolated); `/metrics` Lstat-checks before `metrics.Open`. The report-defaults claim holds: `ShowOptions{}` equals the CLI's defaults. Tests could fail: each has its precondition (FIFO, symlink, absent store, held port).
3. Standards conformance — pass for Go (errors wrapped, no ignored errors except body writes after the header, `-race` clean, no function over the 50-line pin). Docs: fail on the restatements listed in the findings.
4. Directory layout — pass: `internal/serve` with `assets/`, tests beside code, one verb file in `cmd/fyr`, registered in `init()` like `check`.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Tokens are `crypto/rand` bytes, compared with `crypto/subtle`; no hand-rolled crypto or session format; no new dependency; no SQLite import of its own.
6. Decoupling — pass: `internal/serve` imports brain, search, metrics, dream, trail, harness, never `cmd/fyr`; the printers arrive as functions.

## Not examined
- `fyr check` (instructed not to run; it takes about 4 minutes): whether the spec's 14 names of the unbuilt verb now resolve, and any `spec-stale` finding for the revised draft, are unverified.
- Full `go test ./...` and the race run of the other packages (only the subsets named above ran).
- `/check` end to end through the HTTP server for a 3-4 minute handler (the 30 s `ReadTimeout` against a long handler: I reasoned that the response is still written, but did not run it).
- Concurrent requests against the brain store while `/check` runs (SQLITE_BUSY behaviour).
- Mutation runs on the new tests (no must-fail protocol was executed).
- Row 9 (actions, CSRF, Origin, 409, output cap): not in the diff, so none of the spec's POST claims were reviewed; the spec's Verification rows for them are marked row 9 in the draft.

## Outcome

- Medium, `AGENTS.md:54` (`serve` missing from the `--home` list): fixed. `serve` added; `AGENTS.md` is 11,982 bytes, under G2's 12,000.
- Low, `TDD.md:73` (`--repo` readers): fixed. `serve` added to the list.
- Low, the spec draft's "Code to be", the `serveOptions` signature and the third seam: fixed in the stored spec. "Code:" now; `(serve.Options, error)`; `serveNotify` named.
- Low, `fyr help serve` lacked the default port: fixed. The flag now reads "1-65535 (default 3000)".
- Low, the `GUIDE-testing` and `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` sections: fixed. § 3i and § `serve` are stored with this change.
- Observation, `.agents/trail.jsonl` modified: intended. It was the main thread's `SPEC-fyr-delivery` edit, made after `TestDeliverySpecCurrent` failed in the full suite.

title: Review — fyr serve row 8, code and docs, round 2 over the fixes (2026-10-29)
body:
# Review — fyr-serve-row8-round2 (2026-10-29) Range reviewed: the delta .agents/scratch/row8-round2-delta.txt over .agents/scratch/row8-round2-full.diff (uncommitted tree on main, round 2 of row 8), the code it names read in full (internal/serve guard.go, routes.go, serve.go, view.go, pages.go check handler, assets/layout.html), and the drafts SPEC-fyr-serve, ADR-075a, GUIDE-testing § 3i, GUIDE-fyr-matrix § serve, SPEC-fyr-delivery under .agents/scratch/ ## Status: COMPLETE ## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS Every round-1 finding is closed and the fixes are correct. Nothing in the code is broken. The cookie is `Path=/s/

` and the routing, every nav link, record link, search action and the stylesheet link carry the prefix. A path outside the prefix is the plain 404 after the token check, as ADR-075a says. `/check` takes a `TryLock` and answers 409 while one runs. The start line passes `search.Printable`, and the backslash redirect cases are pinned. `gofmt -l`, `go vet ./internal/serve ./cmd/fyr`, `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/serve` and the cmd/fyr serve/vocabulary/help tests pass. I mutated six guards through `go test -overlay` (no source touched). Five are caught by a named test: cookie `Path` back to `/`, the prefix check dropped from `rel`, the nav prefix dropped, `Printable` dropped from the start line, and the check lock disabled. The sixth is not caught, and it is an equivalent mutation (finding 3). What remains is three documentation nits: one stale pointer to the guide's sections, one spec/plan gap, and one over-broad coverage claim. ## Findings - **[low / confidence: high]** `AGENTS.md:66` — "`GUIDE-testing`: § 1 for every change, § 3a–3h by the package each names" is a restatement of the guide's section list. The drafted guide adds § 3i (`fyr serve`), and the diff changes AGENTS.md only at lines 54 and the layout line. Failure: a verifier or reviewer routed by AGENTS.md picks § 3a–3h, skips § 3i, and never runs the serve walk, which is the round-1 gap ("a verifier dispatched over this range will run only § 1") reopened through the pointer. Fix: change to "§ 3a–3i" in the same commit as the GUIDE-testing edit (grep for `3a–3h` found no other copy in AGENTS.md, TDD.md, SDD.md, README.md, PRD.md, agents/, skills/, context/). - **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/scratch/SPEC-fyr-serve.md` § Package shape (the `Run` method listing, ~line 140) lists `NewRun`, `Handler`, `Token`, `CSRF`, `Serve` but not `func (r *Run) Base() string`, which the code (`serve.go`, used by the tests) exports and the Tokens section relies on. Also, code comments (`serve.go`, `guard_test.go`), the spec and ADR-075a cite "plan D48, D49", but the stored `PLAN-2026-10-29-root-docs-and-fyr-serve` body has no D48 or D49 row (its last D-rows seen are D43-D46). Failure: the spec and ADR point at decisions a reader cannot find. Fix: add `Base()` to the listing, and add the D48 (path prefix) and D49 (one /check at a time) rows to the plan in the same commit. - **[low / confidence: high]** `.agents/scratch/GUIDE-testing.md:176` (§ 3i, "Security claims are mutation-checked") — says each guard, "the prefix check" among them, "has a test that fails when it is removed". Mutation: in `internal/serve/routes.go` `rel()`, deleting the `!strings.HasPrefix(rel, "/")` half leaves `go test ./internal/serve` green. It is an equivalent mutation, since every `pages` key and `idPath` begins with `/`, so `/s/

x/records` is a 404 either way, and `rel`'s other users (nav, logf) are harmless. The `CutPrefix` half is caught (`TestCookieScopedToPrefix`). Fix: either delete the redundant half of the condition (the `pages` lookup already refuses it), or narrow the claim to "the prefix cut" and name the slash check as defence in depth that no test can observe. ## Closed from round 1 (checked) - reviewer 1 (`AGENTS.md` writes-state list): `serve` added, line 54. Closed. - reviewer 2 (`TDD.md:73` `--repo` list): `serve` added. Closed. - reviewer 3 (spec header, `serveOptions` signature, `serveNotify`): header says "Code:", signature has the `error` result, `serveNotify` named. Closed. - reviewer 4 (default port in the help): the flag line reads "1-65535 (default 3000)", printed by `fyr help serve` once (no duplicate from the flag printer). Closed. - reviewer 5 (GUIDE-testing section, matrix rows): § 3i and `serve` matrix rows drafted; their pointer from AGENTS.md is finding 1. - security 1 (cookie reaches every port): prefix `/s/

`, `TestCookieScopedToPrefix` uses a real cookie jar (precondition: the jar sends under the prefix) and checks `/`, `/records`, `/s/`, `/s/other/`, `x/` get nothing. The mutation to `Path: "/"` fails it and `TestTokenSetsCookieAndRedirects`. Every page's links and forms are asserted under the prefix in `TestPages`. Closed. - security 2 (`/check` stacking): `TestCheckOneAtATime` blocks the first call, asserts 409, asserts another page serves, releases, asserts the next runs. Closed. The disconnect case (run continues after the client leaves) is not covered, and the spec still calls the cost a property of `fyr check`. - security 3 (start line raw): the second line goes through `Printable`; `TestStartLinePrintable` (mutation caught). Closed. - security 4 (backslash redirect): `/\evil.example` and `/%5C%5Cevil.example` added. Closed. ## Criteria 1. Dead code — pass. `Run.CSRF()` is still test-only until row 9 (the spec names it as row 9's). The `HasPrefix(rel, "/")` half in `rel()` is redundant (finding 3). 2. Flow tracing — pass. Host, fetch metadata, token or cookie, then route. The 303 `Location` is built from the full request path, so a valid token on a path outside the prefix sets the cookie and redirects there; the next request is a 403 (no cookie is sent outside the prefix). That is consistent with ADR-075a ("404 after the token check"), harmless, and not worth a rule. The `/check` lock is taken after the no-project return, released by defer. `Shutdown` still waits for a running check (unchanged, named in the spec). 3. Standards conformance — pass for code. Docs: README row, SDD security line, TDD T16 (security, trace row, ADR-075a), help text, spec, ADR-075a and matrix agree on the printed URL shape (`/s/

/?token=`), the cookie `Path=/s/

` and the routes relative to the prefix. A grep for `?token=`, `Path=/` and `127.0.0.1:N/` over living files finds only the stored `SPEC-fyr-serve` record (to be replaced by the draft) and the cold-read review records (history, not rewritten). Fail only for the AGENTS.md:66 pointer (finding 1). 4. Directory layout — pass; nothing moved. 5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. P is a third `crypto/rand` value in the existing `newToken`; no new primitive, no dependency. 6. Decoupling — pass; `internal/serve` still imports no `cmd/fyr`, the prefix is internal to `Run`. ## Not examined - `fyr check` (told not to run it): whether the spec draft's names resolve and the `spec-stale` result. - Full `go test ./...` and the race run of other packages; only `./internal/serve` (race) and the `Serve|Vocabulary|Help` tests of `./cmd/fyr` ran. - A live browser or `curl` walk of the final build; the matrix's evidence and the walk text in § 3i are the author's, read for consistency only. - A real browser's cookie-path matching and the CSP in a browser (the `net/http/cookiejar` test stands in for the path rule). - Concurrent `/check` plus other pages against the brain store (SQLITE_BUSY); client disconnect during a check. - SPEC-fyr-delivery beyond the one added clause and the grep above; the stored plan's other rows. - Row 9 (actions, CSRF, `Origin`, the 409 for actions). ## Outcome - Low, `AGENTS.md:66` "§ 3a–3h": fixed, now "§ 3a–3i". - Low, the spec's `Run` listing lacked `Base()`, and D48/D49 were not in the stored plan: fixed. `Base()` is listed; D45–D49 are stored in the plan in this change. - Low, the redundant `HasPrefix(rel, "/")` in `rel()`: removed. `rel` now returns "" only when the path does not begin with the prefix; a path that merely begins with it names no page. Its remaining guard is mutation-checked: removing it is caught by `TestCookieScopedToPrefix`.

title: Review — fyr serve row 8, security, round 1 (2026-10-29)
body:
# Security review — fyr serve, row 8 (2026-10-29) Range reviewed: HEAD (2fdd3a9)..working tree (uncommitted), as captured in .agents/scratch/row8.diff — internal/serve/*, cmd/fyr/verb_serve.go, cmd/fyr/{ctx_verbs,main,run_dispatch,help_text}.go, and the code they reach for rendering (internal/metrics/report*.go, internal/search printable, internal/brain FormatGet/FormatHit/Search snippets). ## Status: COMPLETE ## Verdict: FINDINGS No high-severity finding. The guard chain (Host, Sec-Fetch-Site, token exchange, cookie) works as the spec says. I probed it live on 127.0.0.1:3911, and the escaping is sound. The worst problem is a design property: the session cookie that carries T is sent to EVERY port on 127.0.0.1, because browsers scope cookies by host and not by port. Any other listener on 127.0.0.1 that the operator's browser sends a request to while that browser session lasts gets T in its `Cookie` header. With T it can read every page with a plain client. A plain client sends no `Sec-Fetch-Site` and can set `Host: 127.0.0.1:`, so neither check stops it. ADR-075 § Consequences says the token "guards against other users' processes and browser-borne requests". Another user's process listening on a loopback port is exactly the actor that receives T this way. The spec notes that the cookie reaches other ports, but the defences it lists (Sec-Fetch-Site, CSRF, Origin) only protect requests sent TO fyr serve. None of them stops T itself from leaking. The other findings are low. ## Findings - **[medium / confidence: high (mechanism), medium (exploitability)]** `internal/serve/guard.go:65` — `http.SetCookie(... Name: fyr_serve_, Value: T, Path: "/" ...)`. The cookie has no port scope, so the browser attaches `fyr_serve_=T` to every request it makes to `http://127.0.0.1:/`. This covers top-level navigations the operator makes and same-site subresource loads from pages on 127.0.0.1. Scenario: another local account, or any process the operator does not trust (a dev server, a tool's local callback listener, a compromised dependency's server), listens on 127.0.0.1:X. The operator opens 127.0.0.1:X in the same browser session. That listener reads T from the request headers and then runs `curl -H 'Host: 127.0.0.1:' -b fyr_serve_=T http://127.0.0.1:/records?scope=global` (and /memory, /context, /records/{id}, /search). HttpOnly does not help because the leak happens on the server side. SameSite=Strict does not help because the request is same-site or top-level. T stays valid for the whole run (spec § Tokens), so the read access lasts that long too. Cookie planting was also checked and does not work: cookieOK compares every cookie, so a planted cookie cannot replace T. Fix, in order of preference: 1. Serve every page under a per-run, unguessable path prefix (a third `crypto/rand` value, e.g. `/s/

/...`) and set the cookie with `Path=/s/

/`. Browsers then send T to other ports only for that path, which a foreign listener cannot learn: CORP, no-referrer and no CORS keep it from reading it. 2. If that is rejected, state this exact consequence in ADR-075 § Consequences and in SPEC-fyr-serve § Tokens' accepted residual: "T is disclosed to any 127.0.0.1 listener the browser visits during the run". Also print a hint on the start line to close the browser session after Ctrl-C. Binding a separate loopback address such as 127.0.0.2 is not portable: macOS does not configure it by default. I rejected it for that reason. - **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/serve/pages.go:43-47` → `cmd/fyr/verb_serve.go:111` — each GET /check runs a full `check.Run`, measured at 3–4 minutes in this checkout. Concurrency is unbounded, the run ignores client disconnects (it takes no `req.Context()`), and `Shutdown(context.Background())` at `serve.go:145` waits for all runs to finish. Reloading or opening several tabs stacks up CPU-heavy runs. A browser that sends no `Sec-Fetch-Site` lets a page on another local port trigger the same thing with the cookie (an `/check>`). The spec's accepted residual names the idempotent writes but not this resource cost. Fix: let one /check run at a time, with the same pattern as row 9's 409 for actions, or reuse an in-flight result. Pass `req.Context()` through if `check.Run` can take one. Or name this cost in the accepted residual. - **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/serve/serve.go:135` (and `:78`, `:80`) — the second start line writes `projectLine()` (o.Dir, or `trail.Roots`' error text) and `o.Home` to the terminal raw. Every other operator line in this verb goes through `search.Printable`: `runServe` prints `Serve` errors with it at `verb_serve.go:53`, and `logf` uses it too. A directory name that contains ESC or OSC sequences (for example a checkout cloned into a name taken from an untrusted URL or archive) would be interpreted by the terminal. Fix: put the line through `search.Printable` before printing. The HTML side is already escaped. - **[low / confidence: high — test gap, not a live defect]** `internal/serve/guard_test.go:16` — the open-redirect test covers `//evil.example`, but nothing pins the backslash form. Today it is safe only because `net/url`'s encoding table escapes `\`. Probed live: `/%5Cevil.example/x?token=T` and the raw `/\evil.example` both give `Location: /%5Cevil.example...`. Browsers treat `/\host` as protocol-relative, so if the Location building changes (concatenation, `RawPath`) the redirect would turn into an open redirect without any test failing. Fix: add the `/\evil.example` and `/%5C%5Cevil.example` cases to `TestTokenSetsCookieAndRedirects`. Informational, no finding: - An absolute-form request target (`GET http://127.0.0.1:N/ HTTP/1.1` with `Host: evil.example`) is answered 200, because Go takes `req.Host` from the target. Browsers never send absolute-form to an origin server, so DNS rebinding cannot reach this. - With duplicate `Sec-Fetch-Site` headers, the first one wins. Page script cannot set `Sec-*` headers, so this is not exploitable. ## Checked - **Secrets** — none in the diff. T and C exist only in memory. T appears once on stdout (the printed URL, by design) and never in logs. `logf` logs `req.URL.Path` without the query, refusals are fixed strings, and the 303 Location drops `token` (verified live: `Location: /%5Cevil.example/x?a=1`). Referrer-Policy is no-referrer. - **Injection** — html/template escapes every page value. Every `href` is built by serve from a fixed path or `url.URL{Path: "/records/"+ID}`, which always starts with `/`, so a `javascript:` URL is impossible. Record bodies, hits and log lines go through `search.Printable` (C0/C1, Zl/Zp, Cf including bidi and zero-width characters, variation selectors). `/metrics/report` is html/template, plus hand-built SVG cast to `template.HTML`. I traced every `%s` in that SVG: each one goes through `esc` (`template.HTMLEscapeString`) except `s.Class`, which only ever holds the constants `s1` and `s2` (report.go:35-37). FTS words are quoted by `search.FTSQuery`. The `{id}` grammar is enforced by a regexp; `

title: Review — fyr serve row 8, security, round 2 over the fixes (2026-10-29)
body:
# Security review — fyr serve, row 8, round 2 (fixes only) (2026-10-29) Range reviewed: HEAD (2fdd3a9)..working tree (uncommitted), limited to the fixes since round 1 (.agents/scratch/row8-round2-delta.txt against .agents/scratch/agents/security-2026-10-29-1605.md): internal/serve/{guard,routes,serve,view,pages}.go, their tests (guard_test.go, pages_test.go TestCheckOneAtATime, serve_test.go TestStartLinePrintable, fixture_test.go helpers), and the drafts .agents/scratch/ADR-075a.md and .agents/scratch/SPEC-fyr-serve.md (the lines on the prefix, the 409 and logging). ## Status: COMPLETE ## Verdict: FINDINGS (low only; all four round-1 findings closed) All four round-1 findings are closed, and each fix has a test that fails without it. I checked that with five overlay mutations (`go test -overlay`, so the source was not edited); the results are under Checked. I found no new leak of P. The 303 Location and the Set-Cookie only go back to a client that already holds T. Every response sends Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, and no page renders an href outside `/s/

`. Log lines show the path relative to the prefix. The cookie path-match edges hold: `/s/

x/`, `/s/`, `/` and other prefixes get no cookie. Two low items remain. First, no test pins the order of checks for requests outside the prefix. Second, the spec draft says a test covers the security headers on a 409, and that test does not exist. ## Findings - **[low / confidence: high — test gap, not a live defect]** `internal/serve/guard.go:50-54` with `internal/serve/routes.go:35-39`. The prefix check runs after `cookieOK`, which is correct, so an unauthenticated client gets the same 403 inside and outside `/s/

`. ADR-075a's Decision also says the 404 comes "after the token check". But every case in TestRefusals (`guard_test.go:72-91`) is built with `bare`, which puts the request under the prefix. The only requests outside the prefix (`guard_test.go:203-208`) carry the valid cookie. Scenario: a refactor moves the `rel` or 404 check ahead of `cookieOK`, for example to cut work on unknown paths. An unauthenticated client then gets 404 outside the prefix and 403 under it. That turns the response into a membership oracle on P, and it runs the non-constant-time `strings.CutPrefix` on unauthenticated input. No test would fail. Practical exploitability is negligible because P is 256 bits, but it would quietly undo the ordering that the ADR states. Fix: add `"no cookie, outside the prefix": {raw("GET", "/"), 403, lineForbidden}` and `raw("GET", "/s/other/records")` to TestRefusals. - **[low / confidence: high — doc/test claim]** `.agents/scratch/SPEC-fyr-serve.md:222` says TestSecurityHeaders pins the five headers on a `409`. TestSecurityHeaders (`internal/serve/guard_test.go:135-158`) has cases for 200, HEAD, 303, 400, 403, 404, 404 p, 405, 500 and css, and none for 409. The code itself is fine: the headers are set at `guard.go:34-36` before routing, so the 409 does carry them. The problem is that the spec claims a test that does not exist. Fix: add a 409 case, built the way TestCheckOneAtATime blocks a check, or remove `409` from that row. Informational, no finding: - The `/check` lock is held across the response write (the `defer` at `pages.go:53` covers `r.page`), and the server has no WriteTimeout. A client holding T that stops reading a large `/check` response keeps the lock until the connection breaks. Only a client with T can do this, and Shutdown already waits for handlers that are still running. - A page on another port of 127.0.0.1 can still set many cookies for the host, and that can push `fyr_serve_` out of the browser's cookie store (cookie jar overflow). The effect is a logout, not a leak. Opening the printed URL again restores the session, because T is still valid. This predates the fix and is not a new risk. ## Checked - **Finding 1 (cookie across ports): closed.** `guard.go:65` sets `Path: r.base`, and `r.base = "/s/" + P` comes from a third `crypto/rand` 32-byte value (`serve.go:76-80`). - Live probe on 127.0.0.1:3912 (now stopped; port confirmed free) showed `Set-Cookie: fyr_serve_3912=; Path=/s/

; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict` and `Location: /s/

/`. - With the cookie, `/s/

/` returned 200. `/s/

`, `/s/

x/`, `/`, `/s/`, `/s/

/../`, `/s/

/%2e%2e/records`, `/s/

//records` and `/s/

/records/../check` all returned 404. Without the cookie, `/`, `/s/

/` and `/nope` all returned 403. - RFC 6265 path-match with `Path=/s/

` and no trailing slash excludes `/s/

x`. TestCookieScopedToPrefix pins this through `net/http/cookiejar`, which ignores the port, the same way browsers do. - Mutation `Path: "/"` makes TestCookieScopedToPrefix and TestTokenSetsCookieAndRedirects fail. - **P leakage.** - Location: the 303 echoes the requester's own path. A token exchange outside the prefix (`/elsewhere?token=T`) answers `Location: /elsewhere` plus a Set-Cookie that names the Path. That reveals P only to a client that already holds T. - Referer: `no-referrer` is set on every response. The live `/records` page had no href or action outside the base, and TestPages (`pages_test.go:52`) checks every href and action. - Logs: `logf` uses `r.rel(req)`. Mutating it back to `req.URL.Path` makes TestSecurityHeaders' log assertion fail. Nothing reached stderr during the live probe. - Start line: P and T appear only in the printed URL, by design. - **Order of checks**: Host, then Sec-Fetch-Site, then token, then cookie, then prefix, then route, then method. The comparison against P only runs after the constant-time cookie check. The missing pin is reported under Findings. - **Finding 2 (/check stacking): closed.** - `TryLock`, then a 409 page, then `defer Unlock` (`pages.go:49-53`). The defer runs on a panic, because net/http recovers per connection after the handler's defers have run, and on HEAD, which goes through the same handler. The noProject check runs before the lock. - Live: a second GET while a HEAD `/check` was running returned 409. - Mutation that bypasses TryLock: TestCheckOneAtATime fails with "a second /check: 200". - The cross-port `` trigger from round 1 now also needs P. - **Finding 3 (start line): closed.** `serve.go:150` passes the line through `search.Printable`. Removing that call makes TestStartLinePrintable fail: raw `\x1b]0;title\a` reaches the output. - **Finding 4 (`%5C%5C` redirect): closed.** The case is at `guard_test.go:24`. When the Location is built by concatenation, both backslash cases fail (`"/\\\\evil.example"`, which should be `"/%5C%5Cevil.example"`). - **Secrets**: none in the fixes. **Injection**: the new hrefs are `base` (base64url) plus fixed paths or `url.URL{Path}`. **Crypto**: `crypto/rand` and `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare` from the standard library, used as designed. This is not hand-rolling and is no finding. - **Dependencies**: `git diff --stat go.mod go.sum` is empty, so nothing new. I did not re-run govulncheck: the round-1 result stands for an unchanged module graph. `npm audit` does not apply. - **GCP surface**: none. - **Tooling**: - `go vet ./internal/serve ./cmd/fyr`: clean. - `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/serve`: ok. - The mutated copies and the probe binary are in `.agents/scratch/sec-r2-mut/` (gitignored). ## Not examined - I did not wait out the live run to see the lock released after a HEAD `/check` finished, because a full `fyr check` takes minutes. Release after GET is pinned by TestCheckOneAtATime. Release after HEAD and after a panic rests on `defer` semantics and is not tested. - I did not test in a real browser. I relied on Go's cookiejar and RFC 6265 path-match for how browsers scope the cookie by path. - ADR-075a and SPEC-fyr-serve: I read only the lines about the prefix, the 409 and logging, not the full text. - I did not review the `cmd/fyr/serve_test.go` address regex beyond the line shown in the delta. - I did not re-review the docs and trail parts of the delta (README, SDD, TDD, AGENTS.md, trail.jsonl), and I did not re-review round-1 surfaces that the fixes did not touch. - I did not run `fyr search --refs` (no state-writing fyr calls). ## Outcome - Low, the cookie-before-prefix order was unpinned: fixed. `TestRefusals` adds `raw("GET", "/")` and `raw("GET", "/s/other/records")` without a cookie, each expecting 403. Mutation-checked: moving the prefix check ahead of the cookie check was caught. - Low, `TestSecurityHeaders` claimed a 409 it lacked: fixed. A 409 case from a blocked `/check` (`busyCheck`) was added. - Not tested (accepted): the `/check` lock's release after a panic. It is a `defer`, and `net/http` recovers a handler panic after the deferred `Unlock` runs. A HEAD takes the same handler path as a GET.

title: Review — cold read of PLAN-2026-10-29-workers (2026-10-29): design needs revision, implementation not ready, 8 BLOCKING
body:
# Review — plan-workers cold read   (2026-10-29)

Range reviewed: /home/kesokaj/workspace/styrman-harness/.agents/scratch/plan-workers.md (plan file, cold-reader check; code surfaces read: internal/eval/*.go (run, row, row_prepare, row_session, row_after, row_env, guard, procs_linux, fakeagy_test), cmd/fyr/eval.go, eval_home.go, eval_register.go, internal/brain/export.go, skills/handoff/SKILL.md, README/AGENTS/SDD/PRD greps)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

design needs revision / implementation not ready. The worst problem: the lead's loop and the handoff skill contradict each other on what a worker does at its end. A worker told to run the handoff skill is required to edit `TODO.md` (skills/handoff/SKILL.md Step 3.3) and a Checkpoint "Done when" that includes push and a real-home install, while the plan forbids both and its scope check (D18) fails any path outside `Files:` — so a correctly behaving worker will routinely FAIL "changed outside its Files". Second: the lead's loop never commits between waves, but D13 refuses a dirty tree and every `fyr record` write dirties `.agents/trail.jsonl` — the second wave of the four-phase E2E cannot start. Third: `--kill <stamp>` needs a stamp that nothing prints before the run ends, and its unit test cannot run in-process.

## Findings (gaps, worst first)

- **[high / confidence: high]** `plan-workers.md:166,170-174` vs `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:66-67,134,187` — Worker end-of-session procedure is undecided. The handoff skill (which the Kickoff's "Then write the handoff" invokes) tells the agent to bring `TODO.md` current (Step 3.3), to push and to run `fyr metrics ingest`; the Kickoff template's `Done when:` is "the phase's Checkpoint expect, verbatim", and this plan's own Checkpoints say "commit, push, the real-home install on dave". D23/work step 3 say Never TODO.md, never push, no real-home install. Nothing in the plan changes the handoff skill's Step 3.3 or says how the lead rewrites `Done when:` (and who then runs install, `fyr metrics ingest`, `TODO.md` tick). The lead's loop (steps 7-11) also omits `TODO.md` entirely though D29 / handoff Step 3.3 require it ticked in the plan-tick commit. Fix: a D-row stating a worker-mode Kickoff (the exact Standing-approvals and Never lines, a Done-when that drops push/install/TODO), the handoff skill edit that matches, and the lead steps for TODO.md, install and metrics ingest.
- **[high / confidence: high]** `plan-workers.md:112,170-174` + `internal/brain/export.go:368-405` (every write re-exports trail.jsonl) — dirty-tree deadlock between waves. The loop ticks the plan (step 8) and stores drafts (step 9) — both rewrite `.agents/trail.jsonl` — and commits only at step 11. The next `fyr work` (loop step 2 again) is refused by Refusal 2 (D13), and a worker clone sees only committed records, so the plan record the Kickoff tells the worker to read would be stale. `git status` at the start of this very session shows `M .agents/trail.jsonl`. Fix: the loop commits (and the plan/TODO tick with it) at the end of every wave, before composing the next Kickoffs; say so, and add a test of refusal 2 with a dirty trail.jsonl.
- **[high / confidence: high]** `plan-workers.md:154,247` — `--kill <stamp>` is unusable as specified: `<stamp>` is `%F-%H%M%S` of the invocation, but the contract prints only at worker end and the stamp appears in no line until the `drafts` line (only when n>0). The lead has no way to learn it while the run is going except `ls`. Fix: print `work: stamp <stamp>` as the first line (and count it in the 80-line E2E criterion), or let `--kill` take no argument and find the newest pid file. Also two invocations in one second share `<stamp>/pid`; say which wins.
- **[high / confidence: high]** `plan-workers.md:247` — the `--kill` unit test cannot produce its condition in-process. The verb writes the test process's pid into the pid file; `--kill` then refuses it because `/proc/<pid>/exe` is `work.test`/`cmd.test`, not `fyr` (cmd/fyr/eval.go:25-26 already notes "the test binary is not a fyr"), and if the check were bypassed it would SIGTERM the `go test` process itself. The test needs a built `fyr` binary run as a subprocess; the plan must say so (and how it is built under `.agents/scratch/`).
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `plan-workers.md:110,240` — exit statuses contradict the instruction to copy eval's. `cmd/fyr/eval.go:64-148` returns exit 2 for every refusal (`evalRefuse`) and 1 only for a failed run; the plan says refusals exit 1 and usage 2 while Phase 2 task 3 says "the exit statuses of eval's verb". Decide one and pin it.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `plan-workers.md:122` vs `cmd/fyr/eval_home.go:19-31` — eval refuses a missing `--home` and any home sharing real state (`evalHomeRefused`, ledger D37, with a security review behind it: the run's agent holds `command(*)` and could link `--home`'s state to the real one). `fyr work` defaults to the real home and never says whether `sharesRealState` / the post-run re-check (eval.go:134-139) apply. With the real home as default, `Root(home,"work")` is `~/.config/fyr/work`, which D7 calls "beside eval's" though eval never runs there. Decide what the real-home path re-checks after the run, before the fetch and the drafts copy write into the checkout.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `plan-workers.md:131` — scope check as written misses cases: `git diff --name-only` without `--no-renames` lists only the new path of a rename (the old path's deletion is outside `Files:` and goes unseen); without `-z`, core.quotePath quotes non-ASCII or special names and they never match an entry; `<base>` is never defined (the checkout's HEAD at invocation, recorded once); and a worker that rewrote history (reset, orphan branch) makes `<base>..<head>` not what `git merge` will bring — require `merge-base --is-ancestor <base> work/<name>`. Also the by-record test needs the rule for a record that existed at base and is deleted on the branch.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `plan-workers.md:147-148,230-241` — "timed out" has no source: eval's timeout is only a note, `agyExit` returns -1 for any signal-killed agy (row_session.go:117-123), and `Session` returns an int. `killed` (ctx) and `timed out` are indistinguishable from the signature. Also agy's own `--print-timeout` expiry (timeout minus 5m) exits non-zero first and is neither. Specify the return value (a reason or a Has() call) and the `--print-timeout` string format (eval passes `20m`; a `time.Duration` formats `20m0s`).
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `plan-workers.md:73-88` vs `row_session.go:119-140`, `row_env.go`, `row.go` — the Interfaces list does not cover the helpers eval keeps needing after the move: `printable` (row.go:153; used by eval's `resultLine` and by the work contract; a test pins it equal to `search.Printable`), `openRegular`, `bash` (row_session.go:131, used by eval's steps 5 and 13), `fyrEnv`/`checkEnv`/`setupEnv` (eval's step 3 `record list` and step 5/13 need `Home()`, the directory and the env), `withoutGit`, `shellQuote`, `stopGrace`/`agyTimeout` (test seams; `stopGrace` has no Config field). "Moved verbatim" is not true until these are assigned. Also `After()` (steps 11-12) returns early on `!intact` and on `ctx.Err()` (row_after.go:15-33) — eval must replay those guards before step 13; `Intact()` is exported but the ctx guard is not.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `plan-workers.md:131,146-150` — what the lead reads is worker-written text printed verbatim into the lead's context (handoff sections, change titles), and the lead's merge decision ("Next Steps ask nothing") rests on it. The Trust section covers control characters (`printable`) but not instruction-shaped text, nor redaction. Also a worker that fails "credentials left in the sandbox" is still fetched (step 6), its drafts copied into the checkout (step 8) and its handoff printed. Decide: no fetch/copy/print on that reason, or run `internal/redact`; and say that the work skill treats the contract as data.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `plan-workers.md:127,165-166` — the Kickoff text starts `Project: <absolute path>`; the lead writes its own checkout path, the worker's project is the clone. Eval's prompt prefix ("ignore any other checkout") is the only guard against a worker editing the lead's real tree, which neither the scope check nor the after-checks see. State whether the verb rewrites `Project:` or relies on the prefix, and keep the prefix text in `Session`.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `plan-workers.md:270,193` — Risks accept only the dream timer as a source of "real config changed", but check c fingerprints the whole `~/.config/fyr` (guard.go:117-120 skips only `eval/`): any `fyr` write by any other session during a 25-minute run (a `fyr record add`, `metrics ingest`, `index`) changes `brain.db`/`metrics.db` and fails the worker, which is then "never merged". The lead itself is the likeliest writer: D6 has it polling between turns. The work skill must forbid fyr write verbs while a run is in flight, and the Risks row should say what a false FAIL costs (a 25-minute rerun). Also the D10 test claim "failing on the old `watched`" holds only for the `work/` side; the `eval/` side passes on old code.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `plan-workers.md:108` — the name regex admits invalid git ref names (`a..b`, `x.lock`, `x.`); `git checkout -b work/x.lock` fails at step 2 after the sandbox exists, so it is a late FAIL, not a refusal. Tighten the regex or run `git check-ref-format --branch` in Refusal 4.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `plan-workers.md:135-144` — contract undefined for: several change records (one line each? only the first?), no change record, which sections are cut first when over 40 lines, and what `<k> commits` counts. The 40-line unit test cannot be written without it. Same for the pid file's format ("pid and start time").
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `plan-workers.md:98,128` — install source undefined: `Config.Repo` "" means the harness embedded in Self, but eval resolves `--repo`/`FYR_REPO`/checkout through `harness.ResolveSource` after its own refusals (cmd/fyr/eval.go:119-123, `readsRepo`), and a development build has no embedded harness (harness/repo.go:48-52). Does `fyr work` take `--repo`, and which skills does a worker see on dave when the range changes `skills/`?
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `plan-workers.md:55,233` — claimed scope of the move is larger than listed: eval's verb also owns `ingestRow` and `registerClone` (cmd/fyr/eval.go:211-260, eval_register.go) which the plan puts Out of scope for work; say so in SPEC-fyr-work, and check that nothing in `sandbox` depends on them (they read `r.Dir/home`, `r.Dir/app`: `Dir` must stay observable, but `Box` exposes only `App()` and `Home()`).
- **[low / confidence: high]** Restatement missed: `SDD.md:150` ("two things leave the machine … the operator's `fyr eval` runs (R8)") is not in the plan's docs list (only SDD M13, M17, M18). Also `README.md:13` is listed, `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md:45` asks "what leaves the machine" and is not. `TestHarnessMap` (cmd/fyr/harnessmap_test.go:24) names R9 as the requirement for the map; the plan edits the map and cites no R9.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `plan-workers.md:208-211,229` — fixture `~/sandbox/fyr-work/fixture` is described as "a small Go module with a trail" but not as having `.agents/scratch/*` in `.gitignore`; without it, the drafts copy (D21) and `.agents/scratch/work/kickoffs/` dirty the tree and the next `fyr work` is refused (D13). Also `docker/` does not exist and AGENTS.md § Layout names no such directory (Phase 5 layout decision).
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `plan-workers.md:239` — the fake agy's "adds a handoff and a change record to trail.jsonl" must write strict 7-key lines that `brain.parseLine` accepts (the verb decodes with `encoding/json`, but the lead's next `fyr record` call uses the strict parser); the plan does not say the fake runs the real `fyr record add` through the sandbox wrapper.

## Scope (question 2): built beyond what the request named

The Why/brief names: the verb, one then N Kickoffs at once, `--kill`, `--model`, `--timeout`, `--keep`, `.gitattributes`, the skill and feature-skill lines, the PRD edits, Docker last. Built beyond that, with a D-row that says "implementer" rather than naming who asked:
- D18 the scope check (a second mechanism beside the overlap refusal), with its own FAIL reason `changed outside its Files`.
- D19 the cap of 4 files (a constant no one asked for) and the sequential mode "one after another" (adds a second run shape; its only difference from `--parallel` is timing, since all clone the same HEAD).
- D21 the drafts copy with its three caps (1 MiB, 50 files, 0600) and the `.agents/scratch/work/<stamp>/<name>/` tree.
- D16 `Files:` line instead of the flags the operator expected (`--branch`, `--files`), plus the record-ID entry form (D17) and the 64 KiB / 63-char limits.
- The pid-file shape of `--kill` (D26), the `--timeout` floor of 10m.
- The Status line says "the eight items found reading the code (D9–D29)" were approved with "Go all approved", but D9-D29 are 21 rows and D14, D16, D18, D19, D21 are marked "implementer" with no matching item number. Confirm with the operator which of these he asked for, or record each as approved.

## Readiness (question 3): questions an implementer must ask

BLOCKING
1. What exactly is the worker's Kickoff in worker mode: Standing-approvals, Never, `Done when:`; and does the handoff skill's Step 3.3 (TODO.md), Step 6 (push, `fyr metrics ingest`) change for a worker? (finding 1)
2. When does the lead commit between waves, and who ticks `TODO.md`? (findings 1, 2)
3. How does the lead learn the stamp for `--kill`, and how is the `--kill` test run against a real `fyr` process? (findings 3, 4)
4. Exit status for refusals: 1 or 2? (finding 5)
5. Real-home default: which of eval's `--home` refusals and post-run re-checks apply to `fyr work`? (finding 6)
6. The scope check's exact git invocation and `<base>`. (finding 7)
7. How "timed out" is detected and returned from `Session`. (finding 8)
8. Does a worker that fails "credentials left" / "processes left" / "real config changed" get its branch fetched, drafts copied, handoff printed? (finding 9; the plan says fetch whenever `Intact()`, and that such a worker "is never merged")

NON-BLOCKING (a reasonable implementer decides, plan has a nearby default)
9. Name regex vs git ref rules (default: add `check-ref-format`). 10. Contract details: multiple change records, cut order, `<k> commits`, pid-file format. 11. `--repo` for `fyr work` (default: mirror `evalSetup`). 12. Rewrite of `Project:` in the Kickoff. 13. Helper ownership after the move (`printable`, `openRegular`, `bash`, `fyrEnv`, `withoutGit`, test seams). 14. Whether 25 minutes is a workable default for a whole plan phase (it was sized for an eval row; the lead can pass `--timeout`). 15. Two invocations in the same second (shared `<stamp>/pid`). 16. Fixture `.gitignore`. 17. `--print-timeout` string format.

## Sizing (question 4)

- **Phase 2 could not be finished and verified in one fresh session from this plan**: it carries `internal/work` (nine steps, the scope check, drafts copy, contract, one test per refusal/reason/line), the verb, SPEC-fyr-work, the ADR, PRD R8/Non-goals/Known limits, the README map, AGENTS rules 1/4/Rules, SPEC-fyr-delivery, GUIDE-testing, SDD, TDD, help text, matrix, then `reviewer --code --docs`, `security`, verifier, install and handoff. Split into code (with SPEC-fyr-work) and ADR/PRD/map/restatements (rule 3 requires one commit, so the split would have to be a branch or the second half stays unmerged: decide).
- **Phase 3 could not be finished from dave alone**: task 3 needs a Mac run ("who: both", output pasted into a D-row) in the same session; the real-agy risk checks (a), (b) also come first and a "no" on (b) rewrites the phase.
- **Phase 4**: the E2E measure ("the lead's peak context") is polluted if the implementing session is itself the lead; the E2E needs a separate fresh lead session started by the operator, and `fyr metrics ingest` for that session before `fyr metrics show`. Say so.
- **Phase 5** is explicitly not plannable from this plan (its first task writes the plan); that counts as a gap here by the check's definition.
- Phase 1 is sizeable but finishable: 8 source files and 8 test files moved, no behaviour change; each step has a verify.

## Criteria (cold-reader adaptation)

1. Dead code — n/a for a plan; the plan moves `Reason*` constants into sandbox and keeps aliases in eval (OK, but name who deletes the aliases).
2. Flow tracing — fail: the lead-loop to verb to handoff-skill chain breaks at the end-of-session procedure, the commit between waves and the stamp (findings 1-3).
3. Standards conformance — fail: SDD.md:150 and R9 restatements missed; handoff skill's closed Standing-approvals rule is changed by the plan (Never extended, push removed) without naming the restatement.
4. Directory layout — `docker/work.Dockerfile` has no home in AGENTS.md § Layout (Phase 5); `internal/sandbox`, `internal/work` fine.
5. Simplicity — sequential mode, the 4-file cap, record-ID entries and the drafts caps are additions beyond the request (see Scope). No security primitive is hand-rolled.
6. Decoupling — `sandbox` exports a 20-method `Box` that mirrors eval's row struct; helper ownership is unassigned (finding on `printable` et al.).

## Terms used without definition or citation (naive-reader check)

"check c / d / e / f", "guard a / b", "gap O1" (named in the plan only as `guard.go`/`procs_other.go`; SPEC-fyr-eval § One row is cited, but the lettered checks are not defined here); "dave" (the operator's Linux box; AGENTS.md only); "Open N", "Step 1 item N", "brief Decided N" (defined by the appended brief, but the plan never says the numbering is the brief's); `<REVIEW- ID>` (a placeholder); "ADR-058 (5)", "ADR-067", "ADR-075" (cited by number only); "the real-home install" (`DEPLOY-local` § Operator steps, cited only in Phase 1); "Intact" (defined in code, not in the plan); `GUIDE-skill-matrix` (record exists; not cited with a section).

## Not examined

- Mac-side behaviour (`ps -o comm=`, Colima) and `procs_other.go`; `internal/eval/creds.go` (check d internals) and the `*_test.go` files beyond `fakeagy_test.go`/`testmain_test.go`.
- `SPEC-fyr-eval` § One row step numbering was taken from the plan's citation and the code, not read as a record; SPEC-fyr-delivery, GUIDE-testing § 3-4, GUIDE-fyr-matrix, GUIDE-eval row text and `TDD.md` T5/T13 were not read.
- `agy` flags (`--model`, `--mode`, `--print-timeout`) were not run; the plan's claim of agy 1.4.10 was not checked.
- The union merge driver's behaviour on a re-sorted trail.jsonl was reasoned from `export.go`, not run.

title: Review — workers Phase 1, internal/sandbox extracted: APPROVE WITH NITS, 3 fixed
body:
# Review — workers-phase1-sandbox-extract   (2026-10-29)

Range reviewed: uncommitted working tree vs HEAD e1c59aa (diff at .agents/scratch/workers/phase1.diff). The live tree moved while I read: internal/sandbox/box.go, box_test.go and session.go changed at 17:45 (after the saved diff; they cite "security review of Phase 1, findings 2 and 3"). I read both versions and judge the live ones; where the saved diff differs it is said.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

No behavioural regression found in the live tree. Every step, note string, reason string, note order and early return of the old internal/eval code was compared line by line against internal/sandbox and the new internal/eval/row.go and run.go, including the prompt2 path, ctx cancel, timeout, sandbox replaced between sessions, and the token-link failure. The saved diff had one real difference (a spurious "WARNING  is no longer a regular file" note with an empty path after a token-link failure, because the token path was recorded only after the link succeeded); the 17:45 edit fixes it and pins it with TestBoxTokenLinkRefused. What remains is a doc finding that breaks this repo's own `fyr check` rule (SPEC-fyr-eval names `fyr work`, a verb that does not exist yet) and a stale Verification section in the same spec. gofmt, `go vet ./...`, `GOOS=darwin go vet` on both packages, and `go test -race` of internal/sandbox, internal/eval and cmd/fyr, plus `go test .` and internal/harness, all pass on the live tree.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** SPEC-fyr-eval record (`.agents/trail.jsonl`, line 78 of the body, check c) — the edited text says "where every sandbox of `fyr eval` and `fyr work` is written". `go run ./cmd/fyr check --home .agents/scratch/review` now exits 1: `SPEC-fyr-eval:78  verb  \`fyr work\`: fyr has no verb work` (docs 1 finding; HEAD's text does not hold the line, so it is the range's own, GUIDE-testing § 3h BUG-193). GUIDE-testing § 3h requires this checkout to pass its own check with `check: 0 findings` before a completion claim. Fix: reword so the verb is not named as a command (for example "the workers verb's sandboxes, PLAN-2026-10-29-workers D10") in SPEC-fyr-eval and in the GUIDE-testing § "fyr eval makes the setup proofs itself" bullet, and rerun `fyr check`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** SPEC-fyr-eval § Verification (record, `## Verification`, first bullet) — still says `go test -race ./internal/eval/` runs "each safety check with its kit cases (`TestGuard*`, `TestCreds*`, `TestProcs*`, `TestInvoked`)". Those tests moved to internal/sandbox; `go test ./internal/eval` no longer runs TestCreds*, TestProcs*, or the fingerprint tests, so a reader following the spec skips the safety-check tests. Fix: name `go test -race ./internal/sandbox ./internal/eval` (as GUIDE-testing § 3j already does) and split the test names by package. The spec's Code header ("Code: `cmd/fyr/eval.go`, `internal/eval/`") also omits `internal/sandbox/`.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/sandbox/guard.go:176` with SPEC-fyr-eval § Data "Invariant" — the one intended change (check c skips `work/` as well as `eval/`) means an eval row's agent can now write `~/.config/fyr/work/...` in the real home without failing `real config changed`, while the spec's Invariant ("check c fails the row when something did") is stated without that exception. It is the plan's D10 and is pinned both ways by TestGuardFingerprintSkipsSandboxRoots (the `work/x` case fails on an eval/-only skip; `worker/x` and `sub/work/x` still change), so this is a doc nit: add the exception to the Invariant or Known limits.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/eval/run_proc_test.go:184` — the positive control in TestRunRealFyrBaseline no longer asks the credential scanner whether it sees a private-key finding in the sandbox's brain.db (old: `scanCreds(...).kinds["private-key"] == 0`); it matches a copy of the regexp (`keyHeader`) against the raw bytes. The condition it proves (the header is in the store) still holds today and the pattern is identical to creds.go:26, but the copy can drift from the scanner, and a scanner skip rule for that file would no longer be noticed. Acceptable given eval cannot reach the unexported scanner; no fix required unless sandbox exports a test hook.

## Behaviour preservation (what was compared)
- Step order in prepare: clone, open sandbox, records-before, fingerprint, setup, install (+ wrapper), wide-grants note, settings, baseline, ctx check. Identical to the old `prepare`; the "runs with command(*)" note is still printed after a successful install and before settings.json is written.
- Notes: old `printable("eval: "+ID+": "+Sprintf(...))` equals new `Printable(Prefix+": "+Sprintf(...))` for ids from `a-z0-9._-`. The no-/proc line keeps `eval:` through `verb()`.
- Sessions: first session truncates err.txt, second appends (`sessions > 0` equals the old `appendErr` flag); prompt2 still needs rc 0, live ctx and an intact sandbox (eval checks Intact, and the live Session checks it again); a failed token link returns -1 and the check still runs, as before; timeout is a note, agy alone is killed, `TimedOut` is new and used by no eval verdict.
- After steps: unlink, Intact, denial and invalid-allow counts, then eval's ctx check, check, check f: same order as the old `afterSession`. ExitChecks body unchanged except the `leftoverProcs` signature.
- Preflight: same error strings (`the sandbox root: ...`, BUG-106 text, `... is not a git checkout`).
- Result lines, reasons and Seconds unchanged.
- check c: `rel == "eval"` became `slices.Contains(["eval","work"], rel)` under the state dir, directories only. Nothing else in guard.go changed beyond the exported `WithoutGit`.

## Test coverage
No test function was lost (old set is a subset of the new set by name). Moved verbatim or with package/identifier renames only: creds, creds_table, guard, open, procs_linux, testmain. TestGuardPreflight and TestInvokedSkipsAnOversizedDatabase moved to eval (they need eval's Options and maxScan), TestPrintableMatchesSearch and TestNoSQLiteDriver gained a sandbox copy (eval keeps its own TestNoSQLiteDriver, which still covers sandbox through imports). prepare_arms_test rewritten onto a Box rig with the same cases (real home, inside a checkout, four obstacle writes, replaced err file, deaf agy, process group) plus a `TimedOut` assertion; the old records-baseline case lives in eval/prepare_records_test.go. New: TestBoxSession (args, env, identity, cwd, link, settings, appended err.txt), TestBoxTimedOut, TestBoxMakeAndNote, TestBoxTokenLinkRefused, TestBoxLaterSessionNeedsIntact, TestGuardFingerprintSkipsSandboxRoots. No assertion weakened except the positive-control note above. Not mutation-tested by me.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. `Box.verb`, `TimedOut`, `Root`, `CheckRoot` each have a caller or test; `sessions`/`tok` are used. Nothing commented out.
2. Flow tracing — pass on the live tree (fail on the saved diff: the empty token path, fixed at 17:45). Callers in cmd/fyr/eval.go compile; reasons propagate through `Reasons()`.
3. Standards conformance — fail on one item: the `fyr work` doc line breaks the "checkout passes its own check" rule (finding 1); the stale Verification restatement (finding 2). AGENTS.md "3a–3j" matches the new GUIDE-testing § 3j; SDD M5–M17, M13/M17 rows, R6/R8 rows and TDD T13/T17 and the coverage row match the code (T17 interfaces, imports harness and trail only, no SQLite).
4. Directory layout — pass; internal/sandbox is a new package listed in AGENTS.md Layout.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass; stdlib only, no new dependency, no crypto/auth code.
6. Decoupling — pass; Config and Box expose the steps, eval keeps only setup, records baseline, check, agent check and verdict; the import is one-way eval -> sandbox. `Config.Timeout == 0` would fire the timer at once (only `StopGrace` has a default): a trap for the next caller, not a defect today.

## Not examined
Mutation runs of the new tests; `fyr eval` against a real agy (the spec's blocking condition for a release, not run by me); cmd/fyr tests beyond the passing `go test -race ./cmd/fyr`; GUIDE-testing and PLAN record bodies beyond the diffed paragraphs; the TEST-2026-10-29-1744 record added in trail.jsonl; Windows/macOS runtime (only `GOOS=darwin go vet`).

## Outcome

- **Finding 1 (SPEC-fyr-eval names a verb fyr lacks): fixed.** Check c's clause now names "the two sandbox roots: eval's, and the workers' of `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers`" with no verb span; `fyr check` is rerun before the claim. GUIDE-testing's edit names no verb (`(minus `eval/` and `work/`)` only).
- **Finding 2 (§ Verification's stale test list): fixed.** It now names `./internal/eval/ ./internal/sandbox/` and which `Test*` families live where, and the spec's Code line names `internal/sandbox/`.
- **Finding 3 (the invariant's unstated exception): fixed.** § Data's invariant now says check c watches its paths and that the real state directory's `eval/` and `work/` are not watched (also security finding 1).
- **The weakened positive control in `TestRunRealFyrBaseline`: rebutted.** The control proves that the fixture's `brain.db` holds a key header, so that the leak case after it tests something. Whether the scanner matches that shape is pinned in `internal/sandbox` by `TestCredsEveryPattern` (hit and near-miss per kind). Eval cannot reach the unexported scanner after the move, and exporting it only for a test was rejected.
- The live-tree change the reviewer saw at 17:45 is the security round's fixes (findings 2 and 3 there); the reviewer judged that version.

title: Security review — workers Phase 1, internal/sandbox extracted: 3 low, 2 fixed, 1 rebutted
body:
# Security review — workers phase 1, internal/sandbox extraction   (2026-10-29)

Range reviewed: e1c59aa..working tree (uncommitted; `.agents/scratch/workers/phase1.diff`), internal/eval → internal/sandbox

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Nothing high or medium. Almost all of the moved code is verbatim: Box/OpenRegular/soleLink/Printable/guard/creds/procs match HEAD apart from renames, and the step order in `runRow` matches HEAD (clone → openSandbox → recordsBefore → fingerprint → setup → install → settings → baseline → session(s) with Intact before prompt2 → After → ExitChecks). The real change is the one D10 approved: check c no longer watches `~/.config/fyr/work/`. Nothing reads that directory yet, so the risk lands in Phases 2–4, when `fyr work` fetches worker branches from there into the operator's checkout. There is also a small regression on the token-link failure path: it now prints an empty-path WARNING about the real login.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/sandbox/guard.go:151`, `:176` — Check c now skips the whole `~/.config/fyr/work/` subtree. The skip applies to every verb, eval included. It also covers a `work/` directory that did not exist before the row (it used to be reported as `real config changed`). An eval-row agent runs under the operator's uid, and wide rows hold `command(*)`, named rows `write_file(*)`/`cp`/`ln`. Such an agent can now create or change anything under `work/` without a FAIL. Today nothing reads `work/` (grep: only `sandbox.Root`'s comment and `sandboxDirs`), so Phase 1 itself exposes nothing. Under the plan (Phase 2 steps 6–7, Phase 4 `--kill`), `fyr work` fetches `work/<name>` from `work/<stamp>/<name>/app` into the operator's checkout and reads `work/<stamp>/pid`. Scenario: an eval row runs at the same time as a worker. Its agent commits into the worker's clone, changing a file the worker's `Files:` names. The scope check passes it, the worker's `Intact()` only resolves directories, check c skips `work/`, and the lead merges it. Mitigation: check c never watched the operator's checkout itself, so the same agent could write there directly. The delta is real but modest, and D10's reason (concurrent sandboxes would fail each other) is valid. Remediation: in Phase 2, skip only the sandboxes of live runs and not the whole verb directory. For example, Config carries the skip set: this box's own Dir, plus the stamp directories whose `pid` file holds a live flock. Alternatively, `fyr work` refuses to fetch while an eval run is live. Either way, record the residual risk in SPEC-fyr-work § Security. Also reword `SPEC-fyr-eval` § Data's invariant ("nothing a row's agent does writes the real home outside the sandbox root; check c fails the row when something did"). Check c watches four paths, and now not even all of `~/.config/fyr`.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/sandbox/after.go:44-45` with `internal/sandbox/session.go:19-24` — `unlink` now checks `b.tok`, which is set only after `os.Symlink` succeeds. When the link fails (ReasonToken), eval still calls `After()` (`internal/eval/row.go:122`), so `os.Lstat("")` fails and the box prints `WARNING  is no longer a regular file`. That is a false alarm about the operator's real login, with an empty path. HEAD passed the caller's `tok` (`HEAD:internal/eval/row_after.go:61`) and printed nothing in this case. This contradicts "eval's behaviour and output are unchanged" (`SPEC-fyr-eval` § One row, plan Phase 1). Remediation: keep `tok` in the Box before the Symlink, or skip the regular-file check when `!b.linked`. Add a test on the token-link-failure path that pins the output.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/sandbox/session.go:17-28` — The rule that a later session runs only on an intact sandbox used to sit inside `row.session` (`HEAD:internal/eval/row_session.go:34`). It now lives only in the caller (`internal/eval/row.go:113`), so the exported `Box.Session` accepts a second call on a replaced sandbox. It then opens `<Dir>/<outName>` and `err.txt` by path. `OpenRegular`'s `O_NOFOLLOW` covers only the last component, so if the first session swapped `Dir` for a link, the creation and the truncation of a sole-link regular file follow that link. A future `fyr work` caller that runs more than one session per box would inherit this. Remediation: `Session` checks `b.Intact()` itself when `b.sessions > 0` (or always after Clone), and a test pins it.

## Checked
- Secrets: no credential, token or key in the diff. Token paths are only ever named; `cleanName` and `Printable` still sanitise process names and notes. `Note` now passes the prefix as data, not as part of the format string (HEAD built `"eval: "+ID+": "+format`), which is slightly safer.
- Injection: the wrapper still `ShellQuote`s SB and the binary path (`prepare.go:140`, verbatim). The git identity now comes from `Config.GitName`/`GitEmail` (`env.go:40-41`). It goes into exec's env slice element by element, so a value cannot add a variable. An empty value makes git refuse to commit (fails closed). Eval passes the HEAD constants, which `box_test.go` pins. `outsideCheckout`/`WithoutGit`/`FyrEnv` are unchanged apart from names.
- Authz/authn: the token is linked once per Box (`session.go:18-24`). It is removed through the held `os.Root` in `After` and again in `ExitChecks`, and the root is closed only at the end of `ExitChecks`, the same lifetime as at HEAD. Make failing → no root and no link; Clone failing → root nil, linked false, ExitChecks still runs. The token link is still made by path, not through the root (`session.go:19`). That predates this diff, and no agent has run at that point.
- OpenRegular: verbatim (O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, regular-file check, sole-link check on both the fd and the name, truncation after the check).
- Check e: the new `verb` parameter is unused on Linux (`procs_linux.go:24`). On other systems it only prefixes a note, and it comes from the caller's constant Prefix, never from the agent. SIGTERM/SIGKILL targets are unchanged: approved resolved roots, an exact `HOME=` match, own ancestors skipped, and the final SIGKILL limited to the agy pgids this box started.
- Crypto: `crypto/sha256` used as designed for the fingerprint; nothing hand-rolled.
- Dependencies: none added (`slices` is stdlib). `govulncheck ./...`: 0 vulnerabilities affecting the code; 1 in a required module, not called (the known one, DEPLOY-local). npm is not applicable here.
- GCP surface: none touched.
- Tests: `go vet ./internal/sandbox ./internal/eval ./cmd/fyr` clean; `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/sandbox ./internal/eval` pass. `TestGuardFingerprintSkipsSandboxRoots` pins the eval/work skip and the near-misses `worker/` and `sub/work/`.
- `fyr search --refs --kind bug`: BUG-106, BUG-107, BUG-123, BUG-160, BUG-163, BUG-185 and BUG-087/090/091 name the old paths. Their mechanisms (checks b, c, d, e, the wrapper and the credential scan) moved intact.

## Not examined
- The content of the new and moved test files (`box_test.go`, `rig_test.go`, `prepare_arms_test.go`, `printable_test.go`, `testmain_test.go`, `internal/eval/*_test.go`) beyond greps; only that they pass.
- The doc diffs in `AGENTS.md`, `SDD.md`, `TDD.md` and the `GUIDE-testing`/`SPEC-fyr-eval` record bodies, apart from the SPEC lines quoted above.
- The body of `creds.go`, beyond confirming it is a verbatim move (diff: package name and one comment).
- `go test ./...` across the whole module and `cmd/fyr`'s tests were not run, and no real `agy` row was run.
- `procs_other.go` (macOS) was only diffed, not exercised.

## Outcome

- **Finding 1 (work/ unwatched by eval's check c): rebutted in design, doc fixed.** Skipping `work/` is D10, the operator's (Step 1 item 2): without it every concurrent eval row fails "real config changed", and parallel workers fail each other. The threat model is eval's accepted one (`GUIDE-testing` § 4): an agent under the operator's uid with `command(*)` can already write the lead's checkout or anything else check c never watched, so a worker clone under `work/` is not a new class of reach. The point stands for Phase 2: before `fyr work` fetches a branch from a clone a concurrent run could have written, Phase 2's scope check (D36) and its own exit checks are the guard; carried to the handoff as a Phase 2 note. `SPEC-fyr-eval` § Data's invariant is reworded: it now says check c watches its paths and that the real state directory's `eval/` and `work/` are not watched.
- **Finding 2 (empty token path warning): fixed.** `Session` records the token before the link (`internal/sandbox/session.go`). `TestBoxTokenLinkRefused` failed before the fix (`WARNING  is no longer a regular file`) and passes after; its second half pins that a real token that is gone still warns with its path.
- **Finding 3 (Session's own integrity check): fixed.** A later `Session` returns -1 on a sandbox that is not intact, before any file is opened. Eval keeps its own `Intact()` check before prompt2, so its exit status is unchanged (rc stays the first session's). `TestBoxLaterSessionNeedsIntact` failed before the fix (agy ran twice) and passes after.

title: Review — workers Phase 2: internal/work, one worker
body:
# Review — workers-phase2-internal-work   (2026-10-29)

Range reviewed: uncommitted change on main (HEAD a7f8645): `.agents/scratch/workers/phase2-source.diff` (tracked changes in internal/sandbox, AGENTS.md, SDD.md, TDD.md, .agents/trail.jsonl) plus the untracked `internal/work/` (all 17 files) and `internal/sandbox/config_test.go`. Read against `SPEC-fyr-work`. `gofmt -l`, `go vet ./...` and `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/work ./internal/sandbox` all pass (run by me, read-only).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The code is mostly sound and matches the spec closely: the refusal order, the fetch command, the scope check, the os.Root draft copy, the cut order and the line bounds all trace through. Two places do not do what SPEC-fyr-work says. (1) A worker whose session never started because the token link failed (or `agy` failed to exec) is treated as having run: its empty branch is fetched, the worker fails with an extra `no commits`, and its sandbox is removed, where the spec's failure table says no fetch and sandbox kept. (2) `parseTrail` accepts a trail line with missing keys and any kind, although the spec says "exactly the seven keys" and the test header says "as fyr record refuses it"; the worker can PASS with a trail line that makes every later `fyr record` call refuse. Nothing else is high; the rest is low.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/work/worker.go:60-62` (with `internal/sandbox/session.go:25-31`, `:53-56`) — `w.ran = true` is set before `Session` and never cleared when `Session` returns -1 without starting agy (token symlink failure `ReasonToken`, or `cmd.Start` failure, which only notes). `collect()` then sees `ran`, passes `unsafe()` (token link is not a safety reason), fetches the clone's branch (it exists, zero commits), `scope()` adds `no commits`, `fetched` becomes true, and `remove()` deletes the sandbox. Observed result: `FAIL (token link; no commits) ... work/x <base>..<base> (0 commits)` with the sandbox gone. SPEC § Failure modes row 2 ("a setup step fails (... token): FAIL with the sandbox's reason; no session or fetch; sandbox kept") and § One worker step 6 ("fetch runs only when the session started") say otherwise. `TestRunUnfetchedKept` covers install-fail and delete-branch only, so nothing pins it. Fix: have the sandbox report whether agy was started (e.g. `Box.Started()` set at `cmd.Start` success) and set `w.ran` from that; add a test with the token link made to fail.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/work/records.go:56-72` — spec step 8 requires "one object per line, exactly the seven keys"; `parseTrail` uses plain `string` fields with `DisallowUnknownFields`, so a line with a missing key (e.g. no `status` or `date`), an invalid kind, a bad ID grammar, an invalid date or a non-RFC3339 `updated` is accepted. `internal/brain/export.go:parseLine` (the reader of the merged trail) uses pointer fields and refuses all of these ("no %q key", kind, ID grammar, status, date, RFC 3339). Failure: a worker that hand-edits `.agents/trail.jsonl` (the wide grant allows it) gets PASS with a handoff it printed, and after the lead merges, every `fyr record` call refuses the whole trail. `TestParseTrail` has no missing-key case, and its header claims "as fyr record refuses it". Fix: require all seven keys (pointer fields or a map decode) at least, and add the missing-key row; ideally share the strict parse with `internal/brain` rather than restate it (the no-SQLite-driver constraint, ADR-063, decides where it can live).

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/sandbox/after.go:134-141` (`Box.Remove`) — `os.RemoveAll` fails on a tree with read-only directories. A worker that runs `go test` or `go mod download` in a Go project (this harness's own target) fills `<sandbox>/home/go/pkg/mod` with 0555 directories, so the removal of a PASS (and of every fetched worker) fails with a permission error, leaves a partly deleted sandbox, and the result line says `kept <dir>`. Not unsafe, but the spec's "removed" step is not reliable for the repo's main language. Fix: before `RemoveAll`, walk the resolved dir and `chmod u+w` directories (not following links), or note that the sandbox is partly removed. Not tested (the tests' sandbox holds no read-only directory).

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/drafts.go:41-63` with `internal/work/worker.go:121-128` — drafts exist only in the clone (gitignored). When `writeDraft` fails (exists, disk full) or `readDir` fails, `drafts()` notes and returns, but `fetched` is already true, so `remove()` deletes the sandbox and the uncopied drafts are lost; the same happens silently when `OpenRoot` of the draft directory fails. Spec only accepts loss for the skipped kinds (over 1 MiB, non-regular, past 50). Fix: have `drafts()` report failure and keep the sandbox in that case.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/preflight_test.go:17` (83 lines), `internal/work/run_test.go:18` (62 lines), `internal/work/kickoff_test.go:12` (63 lines) — functions over the 50-line limit of `~/.claude/rules/code-modularity.md`. The first and third are tables; `TestRunPass` could split its assertions into helpers. All files are under 400 lines; no non-test function exceeds 50.

- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/work/records.go:29-33` — `trailAt` treats any failure of `git cat-file -s <rev>:.agents/trail.jsonl` as "no records". For the branch that is harmless (it then fails `no handoff`), but for `<base>` an unreadable object (corruption, not a missing file) gives an empty base set, so the "changed or vanished base record must be named" guard passes open (review-standards § 8: a guard keeps the data when its check errors). Distinguish a missing path (`git cat-file -e` or `ls-tree`) from an error. Realistic trigger is a damaged lead repository only.

## Observations (not findings)

- `SkipStores` (D45) makes check c blind to the operator's real `brain.db`, `metrics.db`, `search.db` and `state.json`, so a worker with the wide grant can write them undetected. This is the approved trade-off and `TestGuardFingerprintSkipStores` pins that only the top-level names are skipped; stated here so the decision stays visible.
- The handoff sections are printed verbatim, so a worker's handoff can contain a line shaped like a contract line (`work: x  PASS ...`). The spec's non-goal ("not redacting the contract") covers the text; Phase 5's `work` skill must read only the first result line per worker.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. No unreferenced exports found (`ParseKickoff`, `Run`, `Result.Block`, `Box.Remove`, `Config.Model`, `Config.SkipStores` are all used by the package or its tests; the verb is Phase 3's). No commented-out code.
2. Flow tracing — fail. Findings 1 and 2: `ran` is set without the session having started, and the trail decode does not match the strict reader it claims to match. The rest traced clean: `Run` → `preflight` → `newWorker.run` → `Make/Clone/Fingerprint/Install/Settings/Baseline/Session/After/ExitChecks` → `collect` (lead check, fetch, scope, records, drafts) → `remove`; `fingerprint(…, skipStores)` is updated at all three call sites; `fit` cannot index out of range and stays within 40 lines.
3. Standards conformance — pass with a low finding (test functions over 50 lines). Error paths wrap or note; no ignored errors that hide a failure except the one in finding 6. TDD T17/T18, SDD M17/M18, AGENTS.md layout and the R8 row agree with each other and with the code. SPEC test table names tests that exist (`TestBoxRemove`, `TestBoxSessionModel`, `TestBoxSkipStoresExitChecks`, `TestGuardFingerprintSkipStores` are in `internal/sandbox/config_test.go`).
4. Directory layout — pass. `internal/work/` and tests beside the code; `config_test.go` beside `internal/sandbox`.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only, no new dependency, no hand-rolled auth or crypto; `TestNoSQLiteDriver` pins the driver ban. Fetch uses `fetch.fsckObjects`, `--no-tags`, `--no-recurse-submodules`; the drafts copy goes through `os.Root` with `O_NOFOLLOW`/`O_EXCL`.
6. Decoupling — pass. `work` depends on `sandbox` and `trail` only; sandbox additions are additive (`Model`, `SkipStores`, `Remove`) and eval's arguments are unchanged. The trail decode is a second copy of `internal/brain`'s parse (finding 2), a drift risk by construction.

## Not examined
- `internal/work/kickoff_test.go` body (only its length checked); `internal/sandbox/guard_test.go` diff beyond the signature updates; `.agents/trail.jsonl` diff (records, not code).
- The "31 mutations, all red" claim of the spec was not re-run; no mutation was performed (read-only review).
- No real `agy`, installer or `fyr` verb against a real home was run; behaviour with a real Antigravity CLI (flags, `--model`, `--print-timeout`) is unverified here.
- macOS paths (`procs_other.go`) were not read.

---

# Round 2
