Range reviewed: round 2, the fixes only: `.agents/scratch/workers/phase2-r1-to-r2.diff` over `.agents/scratch/workers/phase2-source-r2.diff` (uncommitted on main, HEAD a7f8645); source read for context. `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/work ./internal/sandbox` passes (run by me); `GOOS=darwin go vet` and `go build` of both packages pass. No file other than this report was written.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Every medium finding of both round-1 reports is fixed, with a test that can fail. The worst thing left is a latent one, no defect today: the drafts destination requires `<stamp>` to be a directory this run made, but the stamp is "taken once per invocation" and Phase 4 runs several workers under one stamp, so the second worker's drafts copy will fail and its sandbox will be kept (finding 1, low, forward-looking). Next, the fix for the lead-checkout hooks and replace refs is real (I confirmed a planted `reference-transaction` hook runs on a bare `git fetch` and does not under the new flags), but `trail.Dirty`, which runs first, still reads the lead without them, and the comment and SPEC step 6 say a little more than that is guarded (finding 2, low). Nothing the fixes introduced is medium or higher.

## Round-1 findings, one by one

Reviewer report:

1. `ran` set before the session started (medium) — **fixed.** `Box.started` is set only after `cmd.Start` succeeds (`internal/sandbox/session.go:62`); `worker.go:58` sets `w.ran = w.b.Started()`; `collect` returns on `!w.ran` (`fetch.go:21`). Pinned by `TestRunUnfetchedKept` with the new `token-block` row (`run_safety_test.go:153-169`: reason `ReasonToken`, `Head == ""`, sandbox kept). The exec-failure branch (`session.go:57-59`) takes the same path; it has no row of its own, but it is the same two lines.
2. `parseTrail` accepted lines with missing keys (medium) — **fixed for the keys, dates and sizes; partly for the kind, ID, status, title and body tables, by design.** `records.go:parseLine` uses pointer fields and refuses a missing key, a non-real date, a non-RFC 3339 `updated` and a line over `maxLine` (`6<<20 + 64<<10`, equal to `brain.maxLine` = `6*maxBody + 64<<10`, `internal/brain/export.go:29`). Pinned by `TestParseTrail` rows `missing key`, `bad date`, `bad updated`, `long line`. The kind, ID grammar, status and title/body text tables stay in `internal/brain`, which work cannot link (ADR-063); the comment at `records.go:79-82` and SPEC step 8 say so. A worker can still PASS with a handoff of a kind or status `fyr record` refuses after the merge; that fails closed in the lead and is a named limit, not a defect. Evidence the stricter parse does not reject the real base trail: I checked all 1445 lines of `.agents/trail.jsonl` (seven keys, real dates, RFC 3339, no duplicate IDs, longest line 173,725 bytes): 0 rejected. `TestRunPass` also runs the real `fyr record list` over the merged trail, but only for the valid case.
3. `Box.Remove` and read-only directories (low) — **fixed.** `after.go:Remove` walks the resolved sandbox with `WalkDir` and `chmod 0700` on every directory before `RemoveAll`; `WalkDir` calls the function on a directory before reading it, so a 0000 directory is opened up first, and it reports a link as a link, so no chmod goes through one. `TestBoxRemove` now builds a 0555 `go/pkg/mod/m@v1` tree (`config_test.go`) and the test passes.
4. Drafts lost when the copy fails (low) — **fixed.** `drafts()` returns false on a read-directory, `OpenRoot` or `writeDraft` error; `collected` (`worker.go:23-26,66`) gates `remove()`; `TestRunDraftsNotRedirected` asserts the sandbox is kept and a note names the drafts. One silent path stays (finding 3 below).
5. Test functions over 50 lines (low) — **fixed.** `refusalCases` is a package variable, `TestRunPass` is split into `wantWorkerSaw`/`wantContract`, `TestParseKickoff` is split. A scan for any function over 50 lines in `internal/work/*.go` (tests included) finds none; the largest file is `run_safety_test.go` at 250 lines.
6. `trailAt` treats an unreadable base as empty (low) — **fixed.** `ls-tree -z <rev> -- <path>` distinguishes a missing path (empty output, no records) from an error (returned, so `records()` notes it and fails `no handoff`); a non-blob or symlink entry is an error. `TestTrailAtFailsClosed` covers an unknown rev (error), HEAD (one record) and a rev without the file (zero records, no error).

Security report:

1. Drafts destination followed links (medium) — **fixed.** `draftsDest` (`drafts.go:112-135`) works through an `os.Root` on the lead: `.agents`, `.agents/scratch` and `.agents/scratch/work` must each be an existing non-link directory or are made; `<stamp>` and `<name>` must not exist and are made with `Mkdir`; `writeDraft` opens through the destination `Root` with `O_EXCL`. `Lstat` on an `os.Root` does not follow the last component, so a planted link is refused. Pinned by `TestRunDraftsNotRedirected` (both plants, `name` and `work`: the outside directory stays empty, the sandbox is kept). The review's step 2 (re-run check c after the copy) is not done and is not needed once the writes cannot leave the checkout. Residual: finding 1 below.
2. Scope read only the net diff (medium) — **fixed.** `changedPaths` = `rev-list base..ref` fed to `diff-tree --stdin -r -m --root --no-renames --name-only -z --no-commit-id`, each commit against each parent (`fetch.go:68-88`). `TestRunEveryCommitInScope` (add then remove `outside.txt`) expects `ReasonOutside` and the file named in the notes. Not done from the review: scanning added blobs with check d's patterns (a secret committed then removed); the remediation offered it as an alternative to squash-only merging and the spec records neither, so it stays an open decision for Phase 5's skill, not a regression.
3. Handoff sections forged contract lines (medium) — **partly fixed.** Every section line is now printed as `work: <name> | <line>` (`contract.go`, after `fit`, so the line counts and the 1000-byte clip are unchanged; `TestBlockCutOrder` and `wantContract` updated to the prefix). SPEC `## Compatibility` now says a reader takes the one unprefixed `work: <name>  ` line, and that the printed `## Kickoff` is data, not an instruction (D38). Still open: no test or eval row shows a worker's Kickoff is not run without the operator's own turn; that is Phase 5's skill. Accepted as phase-appropriate.
4. Lead `.git` hooks and replace refs (medium) — **fixed for hooks and replace refs; the claim is narrower now but not fully accurate** (finding 2 below). `leadGit` adds `--no-replace-objects -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null` and is used for the HEAD check, fetch, rev-parse, rev-list, merge-base, diff-tree, ls-tree and cat-file. I ran it by hand in a scratch repo: with a `reference-transaction` hook planted, a plain `git fetch ... refs/heads/work/x:refs/heads/work/x` creates the marker, and the same fetch with `leadGit`'s flags does not, so `TestRunLeadHooksOff` can fail and its condition holds. `.git/config` and `.git/info/` are neither hashed nor neutralised; the spec's wording (step 6) now states which paths are not seen.
5. `state.json` / `dream-state.json` in `SkipStores` (low) — **not fixed.** `guard.go` is untouched since round 1. This is D45's approved trade-off; I found no rebuttal in the diff or the spec. If it stays, record the rebuttal in the report's `## Outcome`.
6. `parseTrail` differences, memory, double resolve (low) — **fixed except the case-insensitive key match, which is not a difference:** `brain.parseLine` uses the same `encoding/json` with `DisallowUnknownFields` (`export.go:249-253`), so `"ID"` passes both. The blob is resolved once (`ls-tree` → `cat-file blob <oid>`) and read through `LimitReader(maxTrail+1)`; the cap is still 256 MiB, read whole, then split: a smaller spike than before, not removed.
7. Hard-linked draft (low) — **fixed.** `readDraft` refuses `Stat_t.Nlink != 1` (`drafts.go:88-90`); `hard.md` is in the planted set and in the skipped list of `TestRunDrafts*` (`run_safety_test.go:2138` of the diff). The test fails without the check (the file would be copied). Builds for darwin.
8. Relative `Root`/`Home` (low) — **fixed.** `Run` makes `Root`, `Home` and `RealHome` absolute before `preflight` (`work.go:90-98`); `TestRunRelativePaths` runs with a relative `lead`/`home` under `t.Chdir`, which would fail the fetch before the fix.
9. `--model` starting with `-` (low) — **fixed** in `preflight` (refusal 9, SPEC line 53; row `model-flag` in `refusalCases`). The `Box` itself still passes the value as given; `Run` is its only caller that sets it.

## Findings (new, from the fixes)

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/drafts.go:106-123` (`draftsDest`), with SPEC `SPEC-fyr-work` line 59 and 92 — `<stamp>` is required to be absent ("a directory this run made"), but the stamp is one per invocation and Phase 4 starts several workers under it (`Phase 4 adds several files`; the stamp line already says `1 workers`). The first worker with drafts makes `.agents/scratch/work/<stamp>`; the second finds it, `fresh` is true for that path, and `draftsDest` returns `... exists and is not a directory this run made`. Result: the second worker's drafts are not copied, a note says so, and its sandbox is kept, with no safety concern behind it. Fix before Phase 4 (cheap, safe): treat `<stamp>` like `.agents`, `scratch` and `work` (an existing non-link directory is accepted, one is made otherwise) and keep `<name>` as the only must-be-fresh component; a session that plants a real directory there changes nothing, since `<name>` is still refused when it exists and a link is still refused by the `Lstat`. Add a test with two workers sharing a stamp. Not a defect in Phase 2 as it stands.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/fetch.go:41-47` (comment), `internal/work/fetch.go:48-55` (`leadUnchanged`), SPEC step 6 — `leadUnchanged` runs `trail.Dirty`, which uses `trail.Command` (`internal/trail/dirty.go:36`), not `leadGit`; a `refs/replace/<HEAD tree>` the session planted can make `Dirty` read a replaced tree. The comment ("leadGit and the drafts' os.Root guard those") and SPEC step 6 ("every git call in the lead from here on runs with ...") are broader than what is true: `Dirty` is a git call in the lead run without the flags, and a planted `.git/config` or `.git/info/attributes` (a `clean` filter) is read by `Dirty`'s `git` calls in any case. This is inside the stated model (same uid; the session can plant `~/.bashrc`), so it is a claim fix, not a blocker: either say "except `trail.Dirty`" in the comment and the SPEC, or pass `--no-replace-objects` into `Dirty`. Not tested.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/work/drafts.go:30-38` — three exits return `true` without a note: `os.OpenRoot(w.b.App())` failing, and `src.Lstat(draftsRel)` failing for any reason, not only "does not exist". A session that left `.agents/scratch` unreadable (a parent at mode 000) makes the drafts uncopied and the sandbox removed, with nothing said. This is the one silent path left of round-1 finding 4. Fix: treat only `errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist)` as "no drafts"; note and return false otherwise.

## Criteria

1. Dead code — pass. The new `Started`, `leadGit`, `changedPaths`, `parseLine`, `draftsDest`, `copyDrafts` are all called; nothing commented out; `fetched` is gone from the package (grep).
2. Flow tracing — pass. `Session` → `agy` → `started` → `Started()` → `ran` → `collect`; `collect` → `leadUnchanged` → `fetch` → `scope` (`changedPaths`, `records`) → `drafts` → `collected` → `remove` → `Box.Remove`. Errors are noted or returned at every hop; `trailAt` fails closed. The new tests can fail: the hook by my hand experiment; the others by what they assert (see round-1 table). I did not run any mutation.
3. Standards conformance — pass with the low claim finding. No function over 50 lines. SPEC steps 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, the compatibility section, the failure table and the test table, SDD M17, and the doc comments on `Remove`, `drafts` and `scope` agree with the code; the restatement grep (`net diff`, `MkdirAll`, `.fetched`, `ran = true`) found no stale copy. The one overstated claim is finding 2.
4. Directory layout — pass. No new files outside `internal/work` and `internal/sandbox`; tests beside code.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only; no hand-rolled crypto or auth; `os.Root`, `ls-tree`, `diff-tree` instead of new parsing code; `TestNoSQLiteDriver` still holds.
6. Decoupling — pass. The trail line parse remains a second copy of `brain`'s, now with the same key, date, RFC 3339 and length rules; the tables it cannot share are named in the comment. `Box.Started` is additive.

## Not examined

- No mutation was run; "31 mutations, all red" and any new mutation claim are not re-run.
- `internal/sandbox` diff beyond `after.go`, `session.go`, `box.go` as shown in the round diff; `guard.go` (finding 5 was only confirmed unchanged), `creds.go`, `procs_*.go`, `prepare.go` were not re-read.
- The fake agy script (`rig_test.go`) beyond the `token-block`, `plant`, `hook` and `add-remove` branches and the `hard.md` line.
- `.agents/trail.jsonl`, `AGENTS.md`, `SDD.md` and `TDD.md` beyond the greps above; the interactive map and `GUIDE-testing`.
- No real `agy`, installer or `fyr` verb against a real home was run; `fyr record get` ran with `--home .agents/scratch/workers` only.

## Outcome

Round 1 (`reviewer-2026-10-29-1841.md`), each fixed with a test that failed before the fix, unless rebutted:
1. `ran` without agy started — fixed: `Box.Started`, `w.ran = w.b.Started()`; the token-link case of `TestRunUnfetchedKept`.
2. `parseTrail` looser than the strict reader — partly fixed: the seven keys, a real date, RFC 3339 `updated` and brain's line cap (`TestParseTrail`'s new rows). The kind, ID grammar and status tables stay `internal/brain`'s, which `internal/work` cannot link (ADR-063). The lead's `fyr record list` after the merge checks them. Sharing the parser through a SQLite-free package is put to the operator.
3. `Box.Remove` on read-only directories — fixed: they are made writable first; `TestBoxRemove` plants a 0555 module cache.
4. A failed drafts copy removes the sandbox — fixed: `collected` keeps it; `TestRunDraftsNotRedirected` (a planted destination).
5. Test functions over 50 lines — fixed: `TestParseKickoff` split, `TestRunRefusals`' table a package variable, `TestRunPass`'s checks in two helpers.
6. `trailAt` fails open — fixed: `ls-tree` tells a missing file from an error; `TestTrailAtFailsClosed`.

Round 2 (`reviewer-2026-10-29-1858.md`):
1. A fresh `<stamp>` breaks Phase 4 — fixed: an existing non-link `<stamp>` is used, and `<name>` must be new; `TestRunDraftsStampExists`, and the `namedir` case of `TestRunDraftsNotRedirected`.
2. The `trail.Dirty` claim — fixed in wording: the comment and SPEC step 6 say that its git calls run without `leadGit`'s options.
3. A drafts `Lstat` error that is not ENOENT lost silently — fixed: noted, and the sandbox is kept. No test: no portable way to make that `Lstat` fail.

The mutation pass over the final code: 47 mutations, all red.

title: Security review — workers Phase 2: internal/work, one worker
body:
# Security review — workers phase 2 (internal/work, internal/sandbox changes)   (2026-10-29)

Range reviewed: a7f8645 (HEAD)..working tree (uncommitted; `.agents/scratch/workers/phase2-source.diff`: tracked changes to `internal/sandbox/{after,box,guard,guard_test,prepare,session}.go` plus the new `internal/sandbox/config_test.go` and `internal/work/`)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The worst problem is the drafts copy. It writes files into the lead checkout through a path the agent can redirect, and it does so after check c has already run. `writeDraft` (`internal/work/drafts.go:91-104`) calls `os.MkdirAll` on `<root>/.agents/scratch/work/<stamp>/<name>`, and `MkdirAll` follows links. Only the final file name gets `O_NOFOLLOW`. That directory is gitignored (`.gitignore:40` `.agents/scratch/*`), so `trail.Dirty` never sees it, and the leadUnchanged check (D35) does not catch a link the agent planted there. The agent can predict the path exactly: `<stamp>/<name>` is in its own working directory, which the prompt prefix names. `worker.run` calls `collect()` after `ExitChecks()` (`internal/work/worker.go:62-69`). So a session that plants `.agents/scratch/work/<stamp>/<name> -> ~/.gemini/config/<dir>` gets up to 50 files of its choosing, 1 MiB each, created in a path check c watches. fyr itself creates them, after the fingerprint was compared, and nothing reports them. Eval has no such write-back. This is new exposure beyond the threat model's "guards detect what a run leaves in the watched paths", not inside it.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/work/drafts.go:91-104` (`writeDraft`) and `internal/work/worker.go:62-69` (order) — The drafts destination follows links in any of its components except the last. It sits under a gitignored path that the D35 check does not cover, and the copy runs after check c and check e. 4. The lead's `.git` — fixed for hooks, replace refs and, in round 2, grafts: `leadGit` (`TestRunLeadHooksOff`, the graft case of `TestRunEveryCommitInScope`). The rest of `.git/config` is rebutted as inside eval's threat model, and the claim is narrowed in the code and SPEC step 6.
5. `state.json` and `dream-state.json` in `SkipStores` — not changed: D45 is the operator's row. Put to them, with what each choice accepts, in SPEC § Open questions.
6. The trail parse — partly fixed, as the review's finding 2. The blob is named once and read through a capped stream. The case-insensitive key match was withdrawn in round 2: brain decodes the same way.
7. Hard-linked drafts — fixed: `Nlink != 1` is refused (`TestRunDrafts`, `hard.md`).
8. A relative Root or Home — fixed: `Run` makes them absolute (`TestRunRelativePaths`).
9. A `--model` flag injection — fixed: a leading `-` is refused (`TestRunRefusals/model-flag`).

Round 2 (`security-2026-10-29-1858.md`):
1. Grafts bypass the per-commit check — fixed: `GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null` in `leadGit`. The graft case failed before the fix, and a hand probe gave 1 commit with the graft and 4 with the variable.
2. The `.git/config` claim — fixed in wording, as above.
3. The `Box.Remove` chmod race — rebutted: it needs a process alive after check e, which eval's threat model accepts. `os.Root.Chmod` is Go 1.25, above the module's 1.24 line.
4. `<stamp>` in Phase 4 — fixed: an existing non-link `<stamp>` is used, `<name>` must be new, and links are refused at every level.
5. The `SkipStores` question — fixed: the Open question now says what each choice accepts.

The mutation pass over the final code: 47 mutations, all red.

title: Cold read — workers re-plan after the addendum
body:
# Review — workers re-plan cold read   (2026-10-29)

Range reviewed: `.agents/scratch/replan/plan-body.md` (body of PLAN-2026-10-29-workers; the parts the re-plan changed, per the dispatch). Phases 1–2 not reviewed. Code surfaces read: `internal/sandbox/guard.go`, `internal/dream/run.go`, `internal/dream/run_files.go`, `internal/brain/export.go`, `skills/feature/SKILL.md`, `skills/handoff/SKILL.md`, `rules/session-sizing.md`, `internal/harness/size_test.go` (run with -v), ADR-058, GUIDE-eval (feature, handoff rows), PRD G1. Status reads and `go run ./cmd/fyr record ...` used `--home .agents/scratch/replan-home`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES   (`design needs revision`, `implementation not ready`)

Worst first: D64's `SkipStores` list is incomplete. The dream appends to `<state dir>/dream.log` on every real run (`internal/dream/run.go:45`, `run_files.go:44-51`). Check c still fingerprints it, so the hourly dream during a worker's run, which is the premise of D64, still fails the worker "real config changed". Phase 3's tests, as written, would pass without catching it. Next: the plan's own branch-name rule cannot name a branch for most real plans in this trail (plan IDs run to 69 characters, the name cap is 63, `-phase-n[-r2]` is added), the fix-up Kickoff has no way to reach the branch it is meant to fix, `.gitattributes` `merge=union` is built only for this repo so the Phase 6 fixture conflicts on `trail.jsonl` at the second squash, and Failure modes says a refusal exits 1 where Interfaces and D34 say 2. Phase 6's timeout fixture and closed-set fixture do not produce the conditions they claim.

## Findings (gaps, worst first)

Numbering: F# = finding. B = BLOCKING for the phase named, N = non-blocking.

- **F1 [high / confidence: high] BLOCKING, Phase 3.** `SkipStores` omits `dream.log`. `internal/dream/run.go:45` and `run_files.go:44-51` open `<conf>/dream.log` with `O_APPEND|O_CREATE` on each run; `<conf>` is `~/.config/fyr`, which `watched` (`internal/sandbox/guard.go:146`) fingerprints. D64 and the Phase 3 box list only `dream-state.json` and `dream.lock`; the tests-first clause names those two, so it would be green with `dream.log` unhandled. `dream-state.json` is also written through `harness.WriteAtomic` (`run_files.go:56`): the temp file's name appears in the directory for a moment, which a walk can catch. Decide: skip everything the dream owns (`dream.*` prefix, or list `dream.log`), and add the test row for it. Also check that nothing else writes the state dir while the operator's agy session runs (it holds `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl`, `proposals/`, `reports/` on this box; the dream reads `feedback.jsonl`, `internal/dream/collect.go:187`). The plan asserts "only install writes state.json" without a grep (`internal/harness/state.go:37` is the only writer I found, so that part holds).

- **F2 [high / confidence: high] BLOCKING, Phases 3, 5a, 6.** Branch names cannot be built for real plans. The name rule is `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$` (63 chars max). The branch is `work/<plan-slug>-<phase>` and the retry `-r2` (Interfaces step 4, D61). `<plan-slug>` and `<phase>` are never defined (is "5a" `phase-5a` or `5a`? is the slug the ID minus `PLAN-`, lowercased?). This trail's own plan IDs are 68–69 characters (`PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-plan-fyr-eval-the-antigravity-run-kit-as-a-verb`, 68; slug 63), so adding `-phase-3` already fails refusal 4 ("bad name"), and `-r2` makes it worse. Decide the slug rule (a shortening: date plus first words, or the plan's own `slug:`), the phase token, and that `<slug>-<phase>-r2` stays under 63; state that the lead checks it before writing the file.

- **F3 [high / confidence: medium] BLOCKING, Phase 5a.** The fix-up Kickoff after a conflict or a red squash (Interfaces step 7.5, D24, Failure modes) has no source for the change it is to fix. The branch is kept unmerged in the lead's checkout, but the worker's clone runs `git remote remove origin` (step 2, D14), which deletes the `origin/*` tracking refs, so `work/<name>` is not reachable by name in the new clone; the lead's HEAD does not hold the change. The red-test case cannot even be reproduced at HEAD. Decide: does the fix-up Kickoff carry the `<head7>` SHA to merge (the objects arrive with `git clone`, but nothing says they survive or that the worker may use them), or is the fix-up a redo from the printed result? Also name the file: D61 only defines `-r2`; a fix-up for a PASS that conflicted is neither a retry nor a first attempt, and "a phase failed twice" counting is unstated for it.

- **F4 [high / confidence: high] BLOCKING, Phase 5b and 6.** `.gitattributes` `merge=union` lands only in this repo (Scope; Phase 5b box 3). The mechanism is for every project the lead leads. Without it, two branches that each append records to `.agents/trail.jsonl` (the golden path: both handoffs and both change records) conflict at the second `git merge --squash`. Neither `/init-project`, the work skill, nor the Phase 6 fixture box adds the file (`grep gitattributes skills context agents` is empty). Decide who ensures the line: the lead's loop step 1 (check, add and commit before the first wave), `/init-project`, or the fixture only. Add it to the fixture box either way.

- **F5 [high / confidence: high] contradiction, Phase 3.** Failure modes first bullet: "A refusal (Refusals 1–10): one line, exit 1, and nothing is created." § Interfaces refusals and D34: "exit 2 … a FAIL is exit 1". Pick one (D34, eval's, is 2) and fix the bullet.

- **F6 [medium / confidence: high] BLOCKING, Phase 5a.** The closed-set and loop-ending rule is stated four ways that disagree:
  1. § Interfaces closed set and Failure modes: an item "ends the loop" only when an unrun phase depends on it, through `after:` or its boxes; otherwise it is collected.
  2. The same paragraph, step 4, and the E2E timeout edge: "a phase failed twice" ends the loop, unconditionally. A phase failed twice is on the closed-set list, so rule 1 should apply to it. It does not say whether an independent sibling phase still runs.
  3. Step 7, A FAIL: a safety FAIL "ends the loop", unconditionally. A safety FAIL is not on the closed-set list at all.
  4. D60 / step 2: "the next phase that is ready does not qualify, the loop ends", even if the reason is a `who: user` box nothing depends on (which rule 1 would collect). Also unsaid: do the qualifying phases of the same wave run before the loop ends? D50 and the addendum say a closed-set item "ends the loop" with no dependence qualifier; D58 added it (operator approved).
  Also unspecified: an `-r2` that again ends in a question (no `-r3`, and a PASS-with-question is not a FAIL, so "failed twice" does not apply). Decide one rule: ends the loop iff a not-yet-run phase is `after:` it, transitively, or depends on its boxes; otherwise collected and the loop continues; say it for failed twice, safety FAIL, a second question, and a non-qualifying ready phase.

- **F7 [medium / confidence: high] BLOCKING, Phase 5b.** D56 / Step 3: "in a planning session that may lead, a BLOCKING question only the user can settle is not asked". "May lead" is undefined, and the cold read comes before the workers decision, so the session cannot know yet. Read literally, every `/feature` planning session may lead, so the feature skill's user gate (Step 3, the gate rule) is waived for all plans, including those that end up `no`. Decide a testable condition (for example: the plan has two or more phases with only `who: AI` boxes and pairwise-disjoint `files:`), and say what happens to the `Open:` row when the decision is `no` (the question must then be asked, or go to the handoff).

- **F8 [medium / confidence: high] BLOCKING, Phase 6.** Two fixtures do not produce the condition they claim.
  1. Timeout edge: `sleep 900` under `--timeout 10m`. `PrintTimeout` is `<timeout−5>m` = 5m (§ Interfaces step 4, D37), so agy's own print timeout ends the session at 5m, before the verb's kill at 10m; D37 says the result is then `no commits` / `no handoff`, not `timed out`. The criterion ("killed as eval kills") and Failure modes ("fails `timed out`") name the verb's kill; the fixture reaches agy's. It is also unchecked whether agy's print timeout interrupts a running `sleep`. Decide the expected reason (accept either, with the unit test of `Box.TimedOut` carrying the verb's path), or use a test seam.
  2. Closed-set edge: the fixture rule covers only "a worker that must name a public CLI flag stops". Nothing makes the store phase's worker stop for the format ADR; its Never line says "store an adr: draft it under `.agents/scratch/agents/`", i.e. continue, so it can draft and PASS. The edge is not produced. Add a fixture rule ("a persisted format is a structural decision: stop at the gate"). The store phase is also last, so by rule 1 of F6 the item is collected, not loop-ending; the criterion says "the loop ends". Say what is being tested.
  3. Flag edge: the fixed request says "behind one new flag" without naming it; the planner may name it in the plan, so the worker never needs to ask. The fixture rule does not force the question.

- **F9 [medium / confidence: high] contradiction, Phase 5b.** Failure modes bullet "The same record edited on two branches …": "The lead aborts that merge." The merge is a squash (D63): there is nothing to abort; the recovery is `git reset --hard HEAD`. A restatement of D24's old `--no-ff` claim left standing. Also D15's body still says `git branch -d` and D24's `--no-ff` (both headed "amended by D63"; acceptable, but the `restatement-grep` over "abort" and "merge --no-ff" belongs to Phase 5a's verify clause, which names only "the D-rows it cites").

- **F10 [medium / confidence: high] BLOCKING, Phase 5a.** Loop step 11: "the lead's own context nears its target: write the lead's handoff". The model cannot observe its own context (ADR-058 Context: "The model cannot observe its own context"; `rules/session-sizing.md` Why). The trigger is not usable. Decide an observable boundary (for example: a handoff after each wave, or after N waves, or N tool calls) and say who measures the 300,000 target (the E2E measure, post hoc).

- **F11 [medium / confidence: high] NON-BLOCKING, Phase 5a.** Step 8 "copying the evidence the worker's handoff names onto each box": the verb prints only `## Open / In Progress`, `## Next Steps` and `## Kickoff` and step 6 says "Read only what the verb prints". The Completed section and evidence are not printed, so the lead must `fyr record get` the handoff after the merge (D4 allows it). State that, and bound it (the lead reads the Completed section only), since the read counts toward the context being measured.

- **F12 [medium / confidence: high] NON-BLOCKING, Phase 5a.** The first wave cannot start from the planning session: the plan record was just written, `.agents/trail.jsonl` is dirty, and refusal 2 (D13) refuses. Step 10 commits only "at the end of a wave"; the feature skill's "commit and push the plan" sentence is the one the exception drops. Add a step before the first dispatch: commit and push the plan (and `.gitattributes`, F4), by name.

- **F13 [medium / confidence: medium] NON-BLOCKING, Phase 5a.** Step 6's reason for "no state-writing `fyr` verb while a run is going" cites check c (D45). After D45/D64 check c no longer sees `brain.db`, so a `fyr record add` does not trip it. The real failure is D35: any write to a tracked file (a `trail.jsonl` rewrite) makes every worker fail `lead checkout changed`. Say so in the skill: the rule is also "no commit, no tracked-file edit, no `fyr record` write while the run is going" and cite D35. Same for resume (below).

- **F14 [medium / confidence: medium] NON-BLOCKING, Phase 5a.** Resume (`/work PLAN-ID`) "rejoins the loop at step 2" but does not look for existing `work/*` branches. A lead stopped after a PASS and before its merge leaves `work/<slug>-<phase>`; the resumed lead dispatches the same file name and meets refusal 4. Add: list `git branch --list 'work/*'`, treat each as an attempt (merge or `-r2`), and do not depend on a handoff existing.

- **F15 [medium / confidence: medium] NON-BLOCKING, Phase 5b.** The `files:` line format is not specified (one line, comma-separated, paths and `/`-ended dirs and record IDs, no globs) although the Kickoff's `Files:` takes it "verbatim" and refusal 3 rejects anything else. A planner writing `internal/work/*.go` produces a Kickoff refused at dispatch. The disjointness test in D48 should cite D17's intersection rule (equal, or one a dir-prefix of the other).

- **F16 [low / confidence: high] NON-BLOCKING, Phase 5b.** D8 says "G1: nothing enters `context/` or `rules/`; the loop is a skill" and cites it as decided; D57 adds a clause to `rules/session-sizing.md`. D57 is the operator's, but it does not say it amends D8's G1 line, and PRD G1 (`PRD.md:21`, context ≤ 15,000) is not cited among the PRD items. Measured: the rules block is 20,906 of 22,000 bytes (`size_test.go:51`, run -v), room for the clause. Also stale and not in the grep list: the rule's frontmatter `description` ("a session is one Task or one plan phase and ends at its checkpoint…") and the rule's second sentence of bullet 1 ("A plan phase ends at its Checkpoint box … END the session"), which the clause leaves true only for non-lead sessions. Add both to the restatement grep and decide whether the clause also covers them.

- **F17 [low / confidence: high] NON-BLOCKING.** Stale cross-references after the box reorder and the Phase 1 move: D11 and Risks say the fixture is made / checked by "Phase 3's third task" and "Phase 3, task 3"; it is now the fifth box. Risks cites `internal/eval/guard.go:144`; the file is `internal/sandbox/guard.go`. Surfaces touched lists `guard.go` / `watched` at :146 under `internal/eval` (history, but read as current).

- **F18 [low / confidence: medium] NON-BLOCKING, Phase 6.** Verification vs Phase 6: the E2E timeout edge says "the lead re-dispatches it once as `-r2`; a second timeout ends the loop", but Phase 6 box 3 says the `-r2` retry after a timeout "is not exercised". A criterion that is promised and knowingly not run: split it (verb-level edge: yes; lead retry: not run), so the `testing` record's n of N is honest. The golden path "stdout under 80 lines for the two" also does not follow from "at most 40 lines per worker" plus the stamp line (81 maximum); say "at most 41 per worker" or "typically".

- **F19 [low / confidence: medium] NON-BLOCKING, Phase 5a/6.** The skill file ships to every machine, yet § Interfaces writes its rules with plan D-row cites (D38, D47, D48, D60, D61, D63). The skill must be self-contained: state each rule in words. Phase 5a's verify clause ("restatement-grep over the D-rows it cites") should say the skill carries no plan-local D-row numbers. The global git rule is also missing from step 10 and step 7.3: the push is preceded by `check-trailers.sh` (global AGENTS Git), and a staged-by-name `git diff --cached --stat` read precedes the squash commit (global AGENTS "stage by name … read git diff --cached --stat"). The lead's standing approval to run `git reset --hard HEAD` and `git branch -D` is new destructive git; it is in the fixed text of the skill, which is the right place; state the clean-tree guard check (`git status --porcelain` empty) before each reset.

- **F20 [low / confidence: medium] NON-BLOCKING, Phase 3.** Phase 3 box 1 documents (help text, README verb table, GUIDE-fyr-matrix) a verb with "exactly one file", while § Interfaces' synopsis lists `--max-workers` and `--kill`, built in Phase 4. Say whether Phase 3's help text and flag set omit them (my reading: yes; `--keep` stays). Box 1's verify clause is "unit, go test -race ./cmd/fyr": name the cases (each refusal's exit 2, a FAIL exit 1, SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP each ending a fake-agy worker `killed` with the token link removed), tests first.

## Scope (question 2)

Everything in the plan traces to a D-row naming the operator, a cold-read round, or the implementer under an approval, except these, which have no D-row saying who asked:
- The Kickoffs directory `.agents/scratch/work/kickoffs/` (loop step 4): D54/D61 fix the file names only.
- The fixed text of the `/feature` request and the fixture's AGENTS.md rules (D62: "by implementer, under that approval"; acceptable).
- The loop's step 11 `fyr metrics ingest` as the lead's last call (copied from the handoff skill; acceptable).
- `Box.Remove`, `Started` etc. are Phase 2 (not reviewed).
No extra endpoints, flags or configuration beyond what D30 (`--max-workers`), D26 (`--model`, `--kill`) and D37 (`--timeout`) give. Nothing the requirements forbade is built (`--effort`, a serve page, a GUIDE-eval edit remain Out). One item reverses the brief and carries its D-row: the README map's new line (D9). One more reverses the brief's G1 line (F16).

## Readiness (question 3)

Questions an implementer would have to ask the author:
1. [BLOCKING, P3] Which dream-owned files does `SkipStores` skip: only two, or `dream.log` and temp files too? (F1)
2. [BLOCKING, P3/5a/6] What are `<plan-slug>` and `<phase>`, and how is a long plan ID kept under the 63-char name rule with `-r2`? (F2)
3. [BLOCKING, P5a] How does a fix-up worker get the conflicting or failing change, and what is the file name? (F3)
4. [BLOCKING, P5b/6] Who puts `.gitattributes` into a project other than the harness? (F4)
5. [BLOCKING, P5a] When does an item end the loop versus get collected: failed twice, safety FAIL, a second question, a non-qualifying ready phase? Do the qualifying phases of the same wave run first? (F6)
6. [BLOCKING, P5b] What is "a planning session that may lead" in Step 3, and what happens to the `Open:` row when the decision is `no`? (F7)
7. [BLOCKING, P6] What reason does the timeout fixture produce, and what makes the store worker stop for an ADR? (F8)
8. [BLOCKING, P5a] What observable boundary stands in for "the lead's context nears its target"? (F10)
9. [NON-BLOCKING] Where does the lead read the evidence for each box? (F11) Commit and push the plan before wave 1? (F12) Resume: existing `work/*` branches? (F14) `files:` format? (F15) Phase 3's flag set? (F20)

Not BLOCKING (checked): the worker Never line versus Done when is consistent: `Never wins` is fixed text, and the Checkpoint expects of Phases 3–7 (push, real-home install, ingest, reviewer/verifier records) match the lines the Never list names or the closed-set records the by-hand Kickoff already uses. `git reset --hard HEAD` after a failed squash does not resurrect rejected records in the lead's brain: `loadLocked` (`internal/brain/export.go:326-366`) reloads from the file when its SHA differs ("the file wins"), and the next `fyr record` call is the duplicate-ID guard. `rules/session-sizing.md` clause fits (20,906 + at most 120 < 22,000).

## Sizing (question 4)

- **Phase 3:** finishable but at the upper edge: the verb, the ADR, the PRD edits, the map, 12 restatements through `documentation`, `SkipStores`, a real-agy first worker and `reviewer --code --docs` plus `security`. It can be done from the plan alone once F1, F2 and F5 are fixed. The `who: user` box is correctly outside the Checkpoint (D69).
- **Phase 5a:** finishable once F2, F3, F6, F10 are decided; the skill text depends on them. Its risk check (`who: both`) needs an operator message two minutes after the start: write that into the box so the session does not stall. No behavioural run of the new skill until Phase 6; the Checkpoint should say what is not covered ("the loop is exercised only by Phase 6"), per the global rule on coverage claims.
- **Phase 5b:** finishable; heavy (two skills, a rule clause with byte math, an ADR, three docs, `.gitattributes`, two `fyr eval` rows). The `feature` row says "Stop after the plan record and the cold-reader check", so a `yes` workers decision in the row would still stop; note that the row will not exercise the new branch (Phase 6 does). Needs F4, F7, F16 decided.
- **Phase 6:** not finishable from the plan alone as written: F8 (fixtures produce the wrong conditions), F4 (fixture lacks `.gitattributes`), and the E2E is an LLM run whose edges (the flag question, the ADR question) happen only if the planner's plan leaves them open.

## Contradictions (question 5)

- Closed set and loop-ending rule: disagree (F6). The squash merge and branch deletion agree with each other (step 7: squash, tests on the uncommitted squash, commit, then `-D`; D63; D15's header "amended"), except F9's stale "aborts that merge" and the unamended bodies of D15 and D24.
- Worker `Never` versus `Done when`: agree (`Never wins`; D59; the fixed text matches the D59 list item for item).
- `-r2` naming versus the verb's refusals and name rules: the regex and `check-ref-format` accept the suffix, and refusal 4 does not meet the kept first branch (D61), but the name length breaks for real plan IDs (F2) and the resume case meets refusal 4 (F14).
- Failure modes versus Interfaces on the refusal exit status: F5.
- D8 versus D57 on "nothing enters rules/": F16.
- Verification versus Phase 6 on the `-r2` timeout retry: F18.

## Criteria (the six review criteria, applied to a plan document)

1. Dead code — pass: nothing built here. Stale pointers noted in F17.
2. Flow tracing — fail: the fix-up path (F3), the first wave's dirty tree (F12), the evidence read (F11), resume (F14).
3. Standards conformance — fail: F5, F9 are restatements left behind; F16; global git rules missing from the lead's steps (F19).
4. Directory layout — pass: `internal/sandbox`, `internal/work`, `skills/work`, `cmd/fyr/verb_work.go`, `.agents/scratch/work/` all follow the stated layout.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass: stdlib, no new dependency; no auth or crypto implemented (the only secret handling is eval's token link).
6. Decoupling — pass, with one note: the shared strict trail parser is deferred (D65) and `internal/work` keeps its own copy of brain's parse (D47); accepted by the operator.

## Not examined

- Phases 1, 2 and 4 (out of scope per the dispatch); § Interfaces § `internal/sandbox`'s other lines than `SkipStores`.
- `internal/work` and the rest of `internal/sandbox` code beyond `guard.go`; I did not verify D47's claims about it.
- Whether agy's `--print-timeout` interrupts a running shell command (F8.1): not run; stated as unchecked.
- ADR-058's items (1) and (4) are the rule and the feature skill's checkpoint sentence as the plan says; I read the ADR only.
- `GUIDE-skill-matrix`'s existence and `TestSkillListingBudget` headroom for a new skill's description (Phase 5a): not checked.
- Whether `git clone --no-hardlinks` keeps the unreferenced objects reachable by SHA after `git remote remove origin` (F3): not run; the finding is that the plan does not say.

## Final line

design needs revision
implementation not ready

## Outcome

Every finding was answered in PLAN-2026-10-29-workers by a D-row (cold read round 1), and none was rebutted:
- F1 → D70; F2 → D71; F3 → D72; F4 → D73; F5 → D77; F6 → D75; F7 → D76; F8 → D78 and D85; F9 → D84; F10 → D74
- F11 → D79; F12 → D80; F13 → D81; F14 → D82; F15 → D83; F16 → D86; F17 → D87; F18 → D85; F19 → D88; F20 → D89
- Sizing (question 4) → D90
- Scope (question 2): the kickoffs directory is the lead's scratch path under the global scratch rule; no D-row is needed.

D72 (amends the operator's D24), D74 (no wave limit) and D75 (refines the operator's D58 and D60) are named in the session's report, for the operator to override.

title: Review — workers Phase 3: the fyr work verb, ADR-076, PRD and map (code and docs, two rounds)
body:
# Review — workers-phase3-fyr-work-verb   (2026-10-29)

Range reviewed: uncommitted working tree vs HEAD 0c24e92 (`.agents/scratch/workers/p3.diff`): `cmd/fyr/verb_work.go` + `verb_work_test.go` (new), `ctx_verbs.go`, `help_text.go`, `main.go`, `internal/sandbox/{guard,box,config_test}.go`, `internal/work/{contract,contract_test}.go`, AGENTS/PRD/README/SDD/TDD/TODO, `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md`, and the changed records (ADR-076 new; SPEC-fyr-work, SPEC-fyr-delivery, GUIDE-testing, GUIDE-fyr-matrix, DEPLOY-local, DEPLOY-remote). Lenses: code and docs.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing blocks. The worst problem is that the new verb is not in `writesState`, so on a machine that still holds the pre-rename `~/.config/sh-agent`, a first `fyr work` creates `~/.config/fyr/work/…` before any migration and turns a later `fyr install` into the "both directories present, nothing moved" case. Second, `--timeout 0` silently becomes 120m instead of the documented refusal. The verb itself is thin, its refusal order matches SPEC-fyr-work, the signal test exercises the real path, and the claim "three things leave the machine" was found and changed in every living restatement the grep and a record scan turned up. The README map edge count (linkStyle 17..23) is right. `go vet`, `gofmt -l`, `TestWorkVerb*`, `./internal/sandbox`, `./internal/work` and the root-package map test pass.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `cmd/fyr/run_dispatch.go:177` (`writesState`) — `work` is missing from the verb table, and eval, the other verb that makes sandboxes under `<home>/.config/fyr/`, is in it. `migrateStateDir` therefore takes the read-only branch for `work` (prints the notice, moves nothing), and then `work.Run` creates `~/.config/fyr/work/<stamp>` (`internal/sandbox/prepare.go:29`, MkdirAll 0700), and the default `--home` is the real home. On a pre-rename machine that makes `~/.config/fyr` exist beside `~/.config/sh-agent`; `harness.MigrateStateDir` (`internal/harness/migrate.go:48`) then leaves both alone for good ("both present is the operator's to merge"), and the next `fyr install` resyncs without the old manifest, the failure the comment at `migrate.go:35-40` describes. Fix: add `"work"` to `writesState` (as eval's case: true unless the run is a refusal that precedes any write; true always is also safe and matches the comment "errs early on purpose"), plus a test that `work` against a home holding only `.config/sh-agent` migrates first.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/work.go:84` with `cmd/fyr/verb_work.go:22` — `Run` treats `Timeout == 0` as "default", and the verb passes the flag value straight through, so `fyr work --timeout 0 <file>` runs a 120m worker. SPEC-fyr-work and the flag text say "whole minutes, at least 10m" and the test table pins only `9m`. Fix: refuse a non-positive `--timeout` in the verb (or in `preflight`, keeping 0 as the default only for the library), and add a `--timeout 0` row to `TestWorkVerbRefusals`.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. `storeFiles` was replaced by `storePrefixes`/`storeNames`/`storeEntry`, all used; no leftovers.
2. Flow tracing — pass with the finding above. Traced verb -> `trail.Roots` -> `ResolveSource` -> `work.Run` -> exit mapping; a `Run` error is exit 2, a non-PASS verdict is exit 1 with the contract printed, a signal ends the context and `killed` is reported (`TestWorkVerbSignals`). `storeEntry` is top-level only (separator test) and `SkipDir` on a skipped directory is right. The 39-line pins use the literal 39, so reverting `maxLines` to 40 fails `TestBlockBounds`. `TestGuardFingerprintSkipStores` pins both skip and non-skip, both modes, including `state.json`, `proposals.bak`, `xdream.log`.
3. Standards conformance — pass. Restatements of "two things leave the machine" are changed in AGENTS rules 1 and 4 and the `--home` bullet, PRD (Non-goals, delivery paragraph, Known limits), README (intro, olive row, verb row), SDD (M18, Security), TDD (verb row, M17/M18, T-table), SPEC-fyr-delivery (three places), SPEC-fyr-work, DEPLOY-local, DEPLOY-remote, GUIDE-testing, harness-audit areas. The "40 lines" and "no verb yet" restatements in SPEC-fyr-work, SDD and TDD are changed; no stale copy found. The help page, TDD row, README row and SPEC agree on the synopsis and flags. Rules 3 and 5 (map change plus ADR plus code in one change, map pinned by test) are met by the diff; ADR-076 is present.
4. Directory layout — pass. `cmd/fyr/verb_work.go` and its test sit beside the other verbs; the logic stays in `internal/work`.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. No new dependency; no auth/crypto code. The token handling reuses the existing sandbox link.
6. Decoupling — pass. The verb touches `internal/work`, `harness`, `trail` and `search.Printable` only; `ctx` gained three fields; `workSelf` is a test seam like `evalSelf`.

## Not examined
- The real-Antigravity run on dave cited in SPEC-fyr-work and GUIDE-fyr-matrix (1 of 1 PASS, agy exit 0 in 233s): its `testing` record was not read, so the claim is unverified here. The same cells state "not run on the Mac" honestly.
- The full test suite (another run was in progress; only single packages and named tests were run).
- `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers` D-rows cited (D34, D35, D40, D64, D70, D85, D89) were not read; the diff was judged against the specs, not the plan.
- `.agents/trail.jsonl` lines other than the seven changed records; ADR-065 and earlier records are history and were not checked.
- Behaviour on macOS and with a symlinked `~/.config/fyr`.


# Round 2 (over the fixes only)

Range reviewed: round-1 diff vs the working tree (`.agents/scratch/workers/p3-fixes.interdiff`): `cmd/fyr/run_dispatch.go`, `cmd/fyr/migrate_test.go`, `cmd/fyr/verb_work.go` + test, `internal/sandbox/guard.go` + test, and the restating docs (TDD.md, SPEC-fyr-work, GUIDE-testing, GUIDE-fyr-matrix). Lenses: code and docs.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Both round-1 findings are closed in code: `work` is in `writesState` (always true) with a `TestStateDirMigrationByVerb` row, and the verb refuses `--timeout` <= 0 with a `zero timeout` row. SIGQUIT is caught and tested in `TestWorkVerbSignals`. The skip list in `guard.go` matches the real writers (checked against `os.MkdirTemp` / `CreateTemp` call sites and fixed names). The targeted tests pass under `-race` (`cmd/fyr`, `internal/sandbox`). One documentation restatement was left standing: SPEC-fyr-work still says the skip is "by name prefix", the claim the fix reversed. Also, a D-row cited in the new text does not exist in the plan.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** SPEC-fyr-work record, § Open questions, the `SkipStores` bullet (3rd bullet from "## Open questions", ~line 187) — says "The skip is by name prefix at the top of the state directory, so an unseen write by a session to a file named like one of them is accepted." The fix reversed this: the skip is by exact writer name or digit-suffixed regexp, and a file named like one is still watched (`guard.go:165-170`, step 3 of the same spec at ~line 97, TDD.md:172, GUIDE-testing § 3k). Same stale claim in `TODO.md:14` ("`Config.SkipStores` by prefix"; a ticked history line, so lower weight). Fix: reword the Open-questions bullet to say the accepted cost is a write to one of the exact listed names, and the TODO line to "by exact writer name".

- **[low / confidence: medium]** TDD.md:172, SPEC-fyr-work (~line 97) and GUIDE-testing § 3k cite "D91", but `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers` holds no D91 (its last row is D90; `fyr record get` grep for `D91` returns 0). A dangling decision reference in three living docs. Fix: add the D91 row to the plan recording the exact-names decision (the security review's finding 4), or cite the review record instead.

## Round-1 findings

1. `work` missing from `writesState` — closed. `run_dispatch.go:181-183` returns true; `migrate_test.go` row `{"work", "absent.md"}` sits in the verbs-that-migrate list and passes. Returning true even for a refusal is the safe direction.
2. `--timeout 0` becomes 120m — closed. `verb_work.go` refuses `c.workTimeout <= 0` (before the checkout and install-source steps, so no sandbox), row `zero timeout` pins `--timeout 0s`. SPEC-fyr-work (line 38, flag row line 26), TDD verb row, GUIDE-testing § 3k and GUIDE-fyr-matrix `work` table all state it consistently.

## Checks on the fixes

- Skip list vs writers: `brain.db`/`search.db`/`metrics.db` (+ `-wal`, `-shm`, `-journal`); `dream.log`, `dream.lock`, `dream-state.json` (`dream/state.go:31`), `dream-failed`, `dream-work` (`harness.DreamWork`), `proposals`; MkdirTemp prefixes `dream-agy-home-`, `dream-agy-`, `dream-projects-`, `dream-metrics-`, `dream-brain-`, `metrics-agy-` (all digit suffixes); `WriteAtomic`'s `.fyr-*` (`harness/apply.go:285`). Regexps are anchored, so `brain.db.bak`, `metrics.json`, `dream-config.json`, `.fyr-noindex` stay watched (test rows). `atomicTemp` applies to files only; `.fyr-456/x` stays watched. Matches the docs in all four places that enumerate it (SPEC step 3, TDD.md:172, GUIDE-testing § 3k, plus the `guard.go` comment).
- Signals: `verb_work.go:71` lists INT, TERM, HUP, QUIT; SPEC (line 45, 171, 202), TDD verb row and 3k, GUIDE-fyr-matrix all list the four. No remaining three-signal list found in living files.
- Not a regression: `.config/fyr/reports/` (metrics report output) is not skipped under `SkipStores`, same as in round 1; it is written only by an operator-run verb.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. `storePrefixes` is gone; `storeFile`, `storeNames`, `storeTemps`, `atomicTemp` are all used by `storeEntry`.
2. Flow tracing — pass. `storeEntry(rel, d.IsDir())` is the only caller; the `SkipDir` path for a skipped directory is unchanged. The `writesState` -> `migrateStateDir` -> verb order is traced and tested.
3. Standards conformance — pass with the two low findings (one stale restatement, one dangling D-row).
4. Directory layout — pass.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib `regexp` only; no auth or crypto.
6. Decoupling — pass; `guard.go` keeps the writers' names as data and does not import `dream`, `search` or `metrics`. The names are copied by hand, so a new writer needs a new entry (accepted, the spec says so).

## Not examined
- Full test suite (only the three named test groups were run).
- GUIDE-fyr-matrix's and SPEC-fyr-work's remaining prose outside the lines a grep for the skip list, the signals and `--timeout` turned up.
- The plan's D-rows beyond a search for `D91`.
- A real Antigravity run of the fixed verb; `gofmt`/`go vet` were not re-run.

## Outcome

- Round 1, finding 1 (`writesState` lacks `work`): fixed. `cmd/fyr/run_dispatch.go` returns true for `work`; the `{"work", "absent.md"}` row of `TestStateDirMigrationByVerb` failed before the fix (the migration line printed 0 times) and passes.
- Round 1, finding 2 (`--timeout 0` runs 120m): fixed. The verb refuses a `--timeout` of 0 or less; the `zero timeout` row of `TestWorkVerbRefusals` exited 0 before the fix and exits 2.
- Round 2, finding 1 (SPEC-fyr-work's "by name prefix"; TODO.md:14): fixed in both.
- Round 2, finding 2 (D91 cited but absent): fixed. D91 is added to `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers` in this checkpoint.

title: Security review — workers Phase 3: the fyr work verb and check c's skip list (two rounds)
body:
# Security review — workers-phase3-fyr-work-verb   (2026-10-29)

Range reviewed: 0c24e92..working tree (uncommitted; `.agents/scratch/workers/p3.diff`). Code hunks: `cmd/fyr/verb_work.go`, `cmd/fyr/verb_work_test.go` (new); `cmd/fyr/ctx_verbs.go`, `help_text.go`, `main.go`; `internal/sandbox/guard.go`, `box.go`, `config_test.go`; `internal/work/contract.go`, `contract_test.go`. The dispatch described the change as two new files, but the diff also widens safety check c in `guard.go`. That widening is the most security-relevant part of the range.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The worst problem is in `internal/sandbox/guard.go`. Safety check c now skips everything at the top of the real `~/.config/fyr` that starts with `dream` or `metrics`, plus the whole `proposals` entry. That blinds the only escape detector the worker has, and it does so for paths that persist into the operator's later sessions. A worker runs agy with `command(*)` as the operator's uid (`internal/work/worker.go:15`), so it is not confined to its clone, and check c is the only thing that would notice a write to the real state directory. After this change, a worker steered by injected text in the repo or the Kickoff can do two things without check c failing it. It can drop a proposal or a draft `SKILL.md` under the real `~/.config/fyr/proposals/`, which is the input `/retro --harness` and `/retro` step 9 read. It can also rewrite files inside a live `dream-agy-home-*`, whose `settings.json` is what keeps the dream's agy grant-less. Before the diff, both kinds of write failed the worker. This is the plan's own decision (D64/D70: false FAILs from concurrent writers), so the finding argues for a narrower list, not a revert. No secret, injection or dependency problem was found in the verb itself.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/sandbox/guard.go:162-163,204-209`: the `proposals` name and the bare `dream` prefix are now skipped whole. Directories get `SkipDir`, so all of `proposals/**` and every `dream*` directory goes unseen: `dream-agy-home-*` (the dream's private agy home: a copy of the token plus a grants-nothing `settings.json`, `internal/dream/agy_home.go:71,103`), `dream-work`, `dream-failed`, `dream-projects-*`, `dream-brain-*`.
  - Scenario: a worker that has read a poisoned file in the clone runs `command(*)` and writes `~/.config/fyr/proposals/dream/drafts/x/SKILL.md` or `proposals/foo.md`. `brain.ImportGlobal` (`internal/brain/import_global.go:143`) and `/retro` pick it up as a queued proposal or skill candidate. Check c reports nothing and the worker can PASS. Alternatively, while a dream is running, it rewrites `dream-agy-home-*/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` to allow tools. `dream-work` is partly covered, because `workAlone` (`internal/dream/agy_visible.go:95`) sends a non-empty `dream-work` to the private branch.
  - Mitigations already in place: retro step 9 says to treat proposal text as data, and `brain.db`, which holds the global proposal records, memory and feedback, was already unwatched before this diff (D45).
  - Fix: replace the bare `dream` prefix with the exact writer names: `dream.log`, `dream.lock`, `dream-state.json`, `dream-failed`, and the temp prefixes `dream-agy-`, `dream-projects-`, `dream-metrics-`, `dream-brain-`, `metrics-agy-`. Keep `dream-agy-home-*` and `proposals/` fingerprinted, but report a change there as a printed `WARNING <paths>` note instead of a FAIL. The operator then sees it without the false FAIL that D64 avoids. The safest form also cross-checks a `dream.log` append in the same window: a `proposals/` change with no dream run during the session is a FAIL.

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** Context, not new in this diff: what check c does not watch at all (`internal/sandbox/guard.go:148`), combined with `cmd/fyr/verb_work.go:556-559` making the real home the default. `fyr eval` refuses the real home (`cmd/fyr/eval_home.go:21`). `fyr work` is the first verb that pairs the `command(*)` grant (`internal/work/worker.go:15`) with the real home by default.
  - Check c watches only `~/.config/fyr`, `~/.config/sh-agent`, `~/.gemini/config` and the CLI's `settings.json`. A worker that writes `~/.local/bin/fyr` (the binary the operator and the dream timer run), `~/.bashrc`, `~/.config/systemd/user/*`, `~/.gitconfig` or `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` gets a PASS. Its sandbox also sits in the real state directory's `work/`, which check c skips by design.
  - ADR-065/076 accept same-uid writes. I flag this so the trade is written down for the real-home default, not because it is a regression.
  - Fix, either or both: add `.local/bin/fyr` and the dream timer's unit or plist path to `watched` (cheap, and they have no concurrent writers), and state in `SPEC-fyr-work` that check c is a narrow tripwire, not containment.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/sandbox/guard.go:162`: the prefixes `metrics`, `dream` and `.fyr-` have no separator, so they also cover entries no writer was named for. Examples: `.fyr-noindex` (`internal/trail/trail.go:31`, an index-exclusion marker), and any future `dream-*.json` or `metrics*` configuration file. A config file added later under one of those names is silently unwatched, with no test failing. Fix: list exact names and exact temp prefixes (`.fyr-` only as WriteAtomic's `CreateTemp(".fyr-*")` pattern, regular files only). Add a test that fails when a new top-level state file matches a skip prefix but is not in an explicit list.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/verb_work.go:592-593`: the signal handling has three edge cases.
  - (a) Once the first signal has cancelled the context, further SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP are swallowed until `stop()`. If cleanup hangs (a fetch, `After`, `Remove`), the operator can only stop it with SIGKILL, which leaves the token link in the sandbox home.
  - (b) SIGQUIT (Ctrl-\) is not handled. Go's default dumps goroutines and exits, so the token link is not removed. agy, in its own process group, runs on unattended with `command(*)`, bounded only by `--print-timeout` (Timeout minus 5m).
  - (c) Registering SIGHUP replaces a `nohup` ignore, so `nohup fyr work …` is killed at logout. That is a reliability problem, not a security one.
  - Fix: add `syscall.SIGQUIT` to the list. On a second signal during cleanup, remove the token link and exit instead of swallowing it, for example with a second `signal.Notify` channel after `sig.Done()`.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** The result contract `internal/work/contract.go` prints into the lead session is untrusted text. Its "## Next Steps" and "## Kickoff" sections are written by the worker. `search.Printable` strips control characters (pinned by `TestBlockBounds`), but 39 × 1000 bytes of worker-authored text can carry instructions such as "go all approved" into the lead agent's context. The per-line `work: <name> |` prefix labels the source. Fix: have the first contract line state that the sections are the worker's text, to be read as data. The lead's `handoff`/`feature` skill should say not to act on Next Steps from a worker without the operator's turn.

## Checked

- **Secrets:** none in the diff or tests; the test token is the literal `"token"` under a temp `real` home. The token link's lifecycle (`internal/sandbox/session.go:18-30`, `after.go:34-57`) is unchanged, and `TestWorkVerbSignals` asserts the link is gone after SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP. Gaps: no SIGQUIT and no second-signal escape (findings above).
- **Injection:** the Kickoff parser (`internal/work/kickoff.go`) reads only a regular file (`OpenRegular`), caps it at 64 KiB, requires one `Files:` line, refuses absolute paths, `..`, globs and control characters, and limits the name to `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$` (branch `work/<name>`), so neither a flag nor a ref can be injected. `--model` reaches agy as a separate argv element (`session.go:43-44`), comes from the operator and is not passed through a shell. `--timeout` is validated in `internal/work` (test "short timeout"). The fetch-back (`internal/work/fetch.go`) uses `--no-replace-objects`, `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, `GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null`, `fetch.fsckObjects`, `--no-tags` and `--no-recurse-submodules`; that is Phase 2 code and unchanged here.
- **Authz/authn:** the verb adds no auth surface. `RealHome` is `os.UserHomeDir()` ($HOME only), as in eval; eval's `realHomes()` also uses the account database, which `checkRoots` in work does not. Low, same as eval, not raised as a finding.
- **Crypto:** check c's `crypto/sha256` file fingerprint is stdlib used as designed. No hand-rolled primitive.
- **Dependencies:** `go.mod` and `go.sum` are unchanged; the new imports are stdlib and internal only. `govulncheck ./...` reports 0 vulnerabilities affecting the code, and 1 in a required module that is not called (known, `DEPLOY-local`). No npm ecosystem in this range.
- **GCP surface:** none touched.
- **Tests run:** `go test -count=1 -run TestGuardFingerprintSkipStores ./internal/sandbox` passes. The full suite was not run, per the dispatch.
- **Past bugs:** `fyr search --refs <path> --kind bug --home .agents/scratch/workers` for `guard.go`, `verb_work.go` and `contract.go` found 0 references.

## Not examined

- `internal/sandbox/creds.go`, `prepare.go` (beyond the settings write), `procs_linux.go`, `open.go`, `after.go` (beyond the unlink lines), `box.go` (beyond its grep): these were read only in part or by grep.
- `internal/work/work.go`, `preflight.go`, `drafts.go`, `records.go`, and the rest of `contract.go`: not read. Their Phase 2 behaviour was reviewed earlier (`outcome-security.md`), and this diff changes only the `maxLines` constant there.
- `cmd/fyr/run_dispatch.go` (how `readsRepo` and the `--home` default resolve), `harness.ResolveSource`: not read.
- The `trail.Command` hardening flags and git's handling of an untrusted local-path upload-pack config on fetch: not re-verified (Phase 2 scope).
- `verb_work_test.go` was read but not run (`TestWorkVerb*`), to avoid disturbing the concurrent suite run.
- The doc and trail hunks of the diff (`AGENTS.md`, `PRD.md`, `README.md`, `SDD.md`, `TDD.md`, `TODO.md`, `.agents/trail.jsonl`, `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md`): not reviewed for content, apart from the D64/D70 text.


# Round 2 (over the fixes only)

Range reviewed: round-1 tree (`.agents/scratch/workers/p3.diff`) .. current uncommitted tree; interdiff `.agents/scratch/workers/p3-fixes.interdiff`, full diff `.agents/scratch/workers/p3-round2.diff`. Fix hunks: `internal/sandbox/guard.go:151-216` (storeEntry and its vars), `internal/sandbox/config_test.go` (TestGuardFingerprintSkipStores rows), `cmd/fyr/verb_work.go:41-43,71` (zero timeout, SIGQUIT), `cmd/fyr/run_dispatch.go:181-183` (writesState), `SPEC-fyr-work` § Signals, § One worker step 3 and § Open questions. Round 1: `.agents/scratch/agents/security-2026-10-29-2017.md`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Only low findings remain, and they sit in the record text, not the code. The code fixes close what they claim to close. Round-1 finding 4, the bare prefixes, is closed: each skipped name is now an exact writer name or a real `MkdirTemp`/`CreateTemp` prefix followed by digits, and the tests pin the near-miss names. Finding 3(b), SIGQUIT, is closed as well. The deferral to the operator is where the gaps are:

- `SPEC-fyr-work` § Open questions still describes the skip as "by name prefix", which contradicts the fix.
- Two of the round-1 items the dispatch says were written into Open questions are not there: 3(c), `nohup`, and finding 5, the contract as untrusted text.
- The `proposals/` bullet names only two of the unwatched dream entries.

None of this changes what the operator is being asked to decide. It does mean the record they will decide from is partly stale and partly incomplete.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `SPEC-fyr-work` § Open questions, second bullet (the stored record at `.agents/trail.jsonl:1142`, line 187 of the `record get` output): "The skip is by name prefix at the top of the state directory, so an unseen write by a session to a file named like one of them is accepted." This is no longer true.
  - The same record's § One worker step 3 (line 97, D91) and the code at `internal/sandbox/guard.go:163-170` now use exact names. Prefixes appear only in a temporary-directory form anchored to `[0-9]+$`.
  - A stale restatement of a security property misleads the operator about what check c misses. Under the project's restatement rule it should have been caught in this change.
  - Fix: replace the sentence with "The skip is by exact writer name, or a writer's temporary prefix followed by digits, at the top of the state directory only (step 3); a write by a session to one of those names is accepted."

- **[low / confidence: high]** The dispatch says findings 3(a), 3(c) and 5 are written into § Open questions for the operator. That is only partly true.
  - 3(a), the swallowed second signal, is recorded accurately, though in § Signals (line 45) rather than Open questions: "a hung cleanup stops only with SIGKILL, which leaves the token link". That is acceptable.
  - 3(c) appears nowhere in the record (`grep -i 'nohup|hangup|logout'` finds nothing): `nohup fyr work …` is still killed at logout, because `verb_work.go:71` registers SIGHUP.
  - Finding 5 is not recorded as an open question either. Line 147 restates D38 for the Kickoff section, and line 130 makes the lead hold back a PASS whose Next Steps ask a question. Nothing records that the printed contract carries no in-band "worker-authored, read as data" marker, or that the lead's skill does not tell it to leave Next Steps alone. The operator therefore never sees either item as a decision.
  - Fix: add one Open questions bullet each for 3(c) and 5, with their defaults.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** The third bullet of § Open questions (line 188) names only `proposals/` and `dream-agy-home-*` as the unwatched paths a worker can write without a FAIL. Under `SkipStores` the same is true of other entries:
  - `dream-state.json`: the dream's per-project watermarks. A worker can advance them so the next dream skips a project's recent content, or roll them back.
  - `dream.lock`, `dream.log` (rendered by `fyr serve`'s dream page, through `Printable`), `dream-failed`, `dream-work`, and every `dream-*-<digits>` and `metrics-agy-<digits>` directory.
  - `storeEntry` (`internal/sandbox/guard.go:176-182`) matches those names without a type check; only `.fyr-<digits>` is restricted to files. A worker can therefore also replace `proposals` with a symlink unseen. `dream-work` is still guarded at dream time, because `internal/dream/agy_visible.go:95-101` refuses a non-empty directory.
  - The second bullet points at "the other top-level entries listed in step 3", but frames them as stores that "a session writes". This is a completeness gap in what the operator is asked to accept, not a new weakness.
  - Fix: have the third bullet cover every step-3 entry, naming `dream-state.json` explicitly, rather than the two examples.

## Round-1 findings, status after the fixes

- **Finding 4 (bare prefixes): CLOSED.**
  - `guard.go:165-170`: `storeFile` is `^(brain|search|metrics)\.db(-wal|-shm|-journal)?$`, `storeNames` is an exact list, `storeTemps` is the six prefixes followed by `[0-9]+$`, and `atomicTemp` is `^\.fyr-[0-9]+$` for files only. A name containing a separator is never skipped.
  - Each prefix matches a real temporary-file writer: `internal/dream/agy_home.go:71`, `internal/search/dream.go:55,103`, `internal/dream/dream.go:319`, `internal/dream/metrics.go:57`, `internal/metrics/agy.go:46`, `internal/harness/apply.go:285` (`.fyr-*`, reached for `dream-state.json` through `dream/run_files.go:56`). Go's `MkdirTemp`/`CreateTemp` suffix is decimal, so `[0-9]+` matches what they write.
  - The new near-miss rows (`dream-config.json`, `metrics.json`, `.fyr-noindex`, `.fyr-456/x`, `dream-agy-x/`, `proposals.bak`, `xdream.log`, `brain.db.bak`, `state.json`) are watched, and the test passes.
- **Finding 1 (`proposals/`, `dream-agy-home-*` skipped):** still open in code: `proposals` is in `storeNames`, and `dream-agy-home-` is in `storeTemps`. The deferral bullet (line 188) states it accurately, apart from the completeness gap above.
- **Finding 2 (narrow tripwire):** deferred. The bullet (line 189) is accurate. Its claim that watching `~/.local/bin/fyr` "would change eval's check c too" is true: `watched` (`guard.go:149`) is shared, and eval calls `fingerprint(real, false)`.
- **Finding 3(b) (SIGQUIT): CLOSED.** `cmd/fyr/verb_work.go:71`; the SIGQUIT row of `TestWorkVerbSignals` passes.
  - I also checked the sibling case, SIGPIPE on a closed stdout. It is not a gap: `internal/work/work.go:105-110` writes to `Out` only before the sandbox exists (the stamp line) and after `w.run` has finished its cleanup.
- **Finding 3(a):** recorded in § Signals, accurately.
- **Finding 3(c):** not recorded (finding above).
- **Finding 5:** not recorded as an open question (finding above).

## Checked

- **Secrets:** no new secret-shaped value in the fix hunks. The test rows write empty or literal files under a temporary `real` home.
- **Injection:** no new input surface. `--timeout <= 0` is now refused at `verb_work.go:41-43` before anything is made, the "zero timeout" row of `TestWorkVerbRefusals` covers it, and a negative value takes the same branch.
- **Authz/authn:** `writesState` returning true for `work` (`run_dispatch.go:181-183`) makes the verb migrate `~/.config/sh-agent` before its usage refusals, as every state-writing verb does (the comment at `run_dispatch.go:148-158` accepts this). This adds no new privilege.
- **Crypto:** unchanged. Check c's `crypto/sha256` is stdlib used as designed.
- **Dependencies:** none added. `regexp` is stdlib, and `go.mod`/`go.sum` are unchanged in the fixes. `govulncheck` was not re-run: the round-1 result stands, since there is no module change.
- **GCP surface:** none.
- **Tests run:** `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/sandbox ./cmd/fyr -run 'TestGuardFingerprintSkipStores|TestWorkVerb'` gave `ok` for both packages. That is a green run only. I did not do a mutation check of the new rows; the record says they failed on the old code.

## Not examined

- The non-code hunks of the interdiff (`.agents/trail.jsonl`, apart from the SPEC-fyr-work record, plus `AGENTS.md`, `PRD.md`, `README.md`, `SDD.md`, `TDD.md`, `TODO.md`, `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md`). The interdiff file (202 KB) came back as a preview only and was not read in full; I reviewed the fixes from the live tree and `git diff` of the named code files instead.
- `brain.ImportGlobal` and `search/config_view.go`'s handling of a `proposals` symlink. A same-uid worker with `command(*)` can read those paths directly, so I judged this to add no capability, but it was not traced.
- The PLAN record's D91 text: not read. I relied on the SPEC's step 3 citing it.
- The full test suite and `govulncheck`: not run, per the dispatch's scope.

## Outcome

- Round 1, finding 1 (`proposals/` and `dream*` unwatched): partly fixed, partly to the operator. The bare `dream` and `metrics` prefixes are gone: check c now skips the writers' exact names and `<prefix><digits>` temporary names (finding 4's fix). `proposals/` and `dream-agy-home-*` stay skipped, because the hourly dream writes both while a worker runs (`internal/dream/proposals_write.go:23`, `agy_home.go:71`), and watching them is the false FAIL D64 and D70 remove. The proposed alternative, a printed warning instead of a FAIL, changes check c's verdicts; it is written into `SPEC-fyr-work` § Open questions and put to the operator in the handoff.
- Round 1, finding 2 (narrow watched set with the real home as default): rebutted as a code change in this phase and recorded. Watching `~/.local/bin/fyr` and the dream timer's unit changes eval's check c too; `SPEC-fyr-work` § Open questions states check c is a tripwire, not containment, and the handoff puts the widening to the operator.
- Round 1, finding 3: (b) fixed, SIGQUIT is caught; `TestWorkVerbSignals/quit` killed the test binary before the fix and passes. (a) recorded in `SPEC-fyr-work` § Interfaces (signals), as in eval. (c) recorded in § Open questions.
- Round 1, finding 4 (prefixes too broad): fixed. `storeEntry` matches exact names and patterns; `TestGuardFingerprintSkipStores`'s rows for `brain.db.bak`, `metrics.json`, `dream-config.json`, `dream-agy-x/`, `.fyr-noindex` and a `.fyr-<digits>` directory each failed on the prefix list and pass.
- Round 1, finding 5 (the contract is worker-written text): recorded in `SPEC-fyr-work` § Open questions; D38 holds, and the `work` skill (Phase 5a) states it.
- Round 2, findings 1–3: fixed in `SPEC-fyr-work`: the "by name prefix" line, findings 3(c) and 5 written in, and the skip bullet widened to every skipped entry, `dream-state.json` among them, with the name-not-type match stated.

title: Review — workers Phase 4: several Kickoffs, --max-workers, --kill (code and docs, two rounds)
body:
# Review — workers-phase4-several-files-and-kill   (2026-10-29)

Range reviewed: uncommitted working tree vs 645492d, as `.agents/scratch/workers/p4-review.diff` (README, SDD, TDD, cmd/fyr, internal/work incl. new slots.go, slots_test.go, several_test.go) and the three record drafts under `.agents/scratch/workers/p4docs/`. Lenses: code and docs.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing blocking. The implementation is sound: `go test -race` over `./internal/work` and the `TestWorkVerb*` tests pass, `-count=6` over the new tests is stable, gofmt and `go vet` (linux and GOOS=darwin) are clean, `fyr check` reports 0 doc findings, and every claim the docs make about `fyr work` that I traced matches the code (refusal order 0-11, 2s poll, pid-file format, setup-failed on a slot-count error, mutex scope, exit statuses, help text). The worst problems are test gaps that I proved by mutation in a scratch copy (a changed behaviour no test pins), one small dispatch race, and a few stale describing comments.

I did not run any `fyr` verb that writes state and no real `agy`; mutations ran in a copy under `.agents/scratch/` (removed afterwards); no source was touched.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/work/preflight.go:~135` (`intersect`) — the direction "first file's entry is a directory, the second file's entry lies under it" is pinned by no test. Mutation (scratch copy): `return a == b || under(b, a)` (drops `under(a, b)`) compiled and left `TestRunSeveralRefusals` and `TestWorkVerbRefusals` GREEN. Every dir-prefix case in the tests puts the file first (`pkg/b.go` then `pkg/`). Failure scenario: someone "simplifies" `intersect` to one direction; `fyr work one.md(Files: pkg/) two.md(Files: pkg/b.go)` is no longer refused and two workers change one path (D17). The claimed "15 mutations, all red" in SPEC/GUIDE-testing did not include this one. Fix: add the reversed pair to `TestRunSeveralRefusals` ("dir-prefix-reversed").
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/run_dispatch.go:182` — `writesState` now returns `c.workKill == ""` so `--kill` skips the state-dir migration (SPEC draft states it), but `TestStateDirMigrationByVerb` (`cmd/fyr/migrate_test.go`) has no `{"work", "--kill", ...}` row in its read-only list. Reverting to `return true` passes every test. review-standards § 8: a read-only mode's test asserts it does NOT do the side effect. Fix: add a read-only row for `work --kill <stamp>`.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/work.go:154-170` (`dispatch`) — `ctx.Err()` is not consulted before `take()`; `stopped` is only set when the select picks `<-stop`. If the context ends while a worker is finishing, `select` can pick `done` (both ready, random), and the next loop turn takes the freed slot and starts a still-waiting file with a dead context. Result: a sandbox directory is made and kept and the worker fails `killed` without the `never started` note, contrary to SPEC ("a file still waiting never starts ... no sandbox", D26). Fix: `for next < len(ws) && !stopped && ctx.Err() == nil`; the next select then sees `stop` and `neverStarted` runs. No test covers a kill that arrives while a slot frees.
- **[low / confidence: high]** coverage claims name no gaps (review-standards § 7): GUIDE-testing and SPEC say each Phase 4 test was "validated red under a mutation". Not covered by any test: the slot-count error path (`take` error -> `setup failed`, listed in the SPEC failure table; grep finds no test), `slots.lock` mutual exclusion between two runs (the "two runs never take the last slot" claim), `give`'s error path. Name them as uncovered in the GUIDE-testing note, or add tests.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/slots.go:~80-105` — accounting leaks on error: `take` increments `r.running` before `r.write()`, and returns `(true, err)` on a write error, which `dispatch` treats as "setup failed" without a `give`; `give` skips the decrement when `lockSlots` fails. The run then believes a slot is in use for good; with `--max-workers 1` the next waiting file never starts and the run loops on the 2s tick until a signal. Fix: decrement `r.running` in memory unconditionally in `give`, and roll back on a failed write in `take`.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/slots.go:~131` (`liveRuns`, via `take`'s `others, _ :=` and `atLimit`) — `filepath.Glob` interprets the work-root path as a pattern. A home path containing `[`, `*` or `?` (e.g. `/home/a[1]`) matches nothing or errors, the error is dropped in `take`, so the machine-wide limit is silently not enforced (fail-open; the dispatch comment says "fail closed"). Fix: `os.ReadDir(work)` and open `<stamp>/pid` per entry, and return `take`'s liveRuns error.
