- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/work/slots.go:~64` (`openRun`) — `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB` on the brand-new pid file fails if another run's `liveRuns` holds its transient `LOCK_SH` on it in the microseconds between `O_CREATE` and the flock; the whole run is then refused ("the run's pid file: locking ...") before anything prints. Very small window; a blocking flock (or one retry) closes it.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** weak red under mutation: with `take`'s limit check disabled (`if false && n+r.running >= r.max`), `TestRunSeveralWaits` failed 3 of 3 runs but `TestRunCountsOtherRuns` failed only 2 of 3 (it detects overlap by a `running-*` file count at worker start, so it depends on timing). A regression there can pass CI intermittently. Fix: assert non-overlap with the `together` barrier (the workers must NOT meet) rather than a race.
- **[low / confidence: high]** stale describing text (global "describing-text" rule): `internal/work/work.go:1` ("Package work runs one Kickoff as a worker"), `internal/work/drafts.go:123` and `internal/work/run_safety_test.go:241` ("Phase 4's workers share <stamp>", future tense; the SPEC draft already rewrote this line to "the workers of one run share <stamp>").
- **[low / confidence: medium]** docs: `fyr work --kill` looks under the invocation's own `--home` (default: the real home), but the repo's own testing procedure (GUIDE-testing § 3k, AGENTS.md "Rules for working here") starts development runs with `--home ~/sandbox/fyr-work/home`. Neither the help page, README, TDD nor SPEC says `--kill` needs the same `--home`; without it the user gets `no run <stamp>: open ...: no such file`. One sentence in the SPEC `--kill` paragraph, the help text and GUIDE-testing § 3k.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. No unused code found; `first()` in run_safety_test.go is used by rig and tests; `MaxMaxWorkers`/`DefaultMaxWorkers` are used by the verb.
2. Flow tracing — pass with nits. Callers of `Run`/`preflight` all updated (`first()` in tests, the verb loops the results); the dispatch loop has no goroutine leak (every started worker sends on `done` and the loop only ends when all results are set); `r.running` is touched only by the dispatch goroutine, so no data race (`-race` clean); fds are CLOEXEC so agy cannot inherit the flock; `held()` semantics hold across processes. Nits: the ctx-end race and the error-path accounting above.
3. Standards conformance — nits. Findings above (read-only-mode test, coverage claims, stale comments). Docs: README row, TDD verb table and T18 list, SDD M18, help text, `fyr check` (0 doc findings) and the three record drafts agree with the code; the restatement grep over living files found no remaining "one file only" claim (TODO.md:10 still describes Phase 4 as pending, which is the active-plan pointer, not a restatement). The two comment restatements are the exception.
4. Directory layout — pass. `slots.go`/`slots_test.go`/`several_test.go` sit beside the code in `internal/work/`; each file is under the size limits (slots.go 235, several_test.go 220).
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only (`syscall.Flock`, `regexp`); no auth/crypto involved. The pid-file/flock scheme is the simplest thing that gives a machine-wide count without a daemon.
6. Decoupling — pass. Slot accounting is isolated in `slots.go`; `worker.run` takes the collect mutex as a parameter; the verb only calls `work.Run` and `work.Kill`.

## Not examined
- A real Antigravity run of two workers in one `fyr work` invocation (the docs say so themselves; only two separate runs were exercised on dave). Whether worker A's real-home fingerprint can see worker B's token rewrite as "real config changed" was not tested; the docs' dave smoke is the only evidence.
- The "15 mutations, all red" claim: I re-ran four mutations (limit check off, other-runs count off, intersect one direction, and the findings above) and did not reproduce the other eleven.
- The stored (non-draft) records' text outside the three diffs; PRD.md/AGENTS.md prose beyond the grep hits; `internal/sandbox` beyond the leftover-process and OpenRegular reads; macOS runtime behaviour (only `GOOS=darwin go vet`).
- `fyr search --refs ... --kind bug` and `fyr record list --kind bug` were not run (they may write the index); no recorded-bug cross-check was done.

## Round 2


Range reviewed: the interdiff `.agents/scratch/workers/p4-r2.diff` (r1 reviewed tree to the working tree), the full current text of `internal/work/slots.go`, the `dispatch` loop in `work.go`, `preflight.go`, `rig_test.go`, and the two changed record drafts `.agents/scratch/workers/p4docs/SPEC-fyr-work.md` and `GUIDE-testing.md` (§ 3k). Round-1 inputs: `reviewer-2026-10-29-2108.md` and `security-2026-10-29-2101.md`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing blocking. Every round-1 code finding that the dispatch lists is fixed by the interdiff, and each of those has a test that I made fail by a mutation in a scratch copy (a build-clean mutant, a named test red). The at-limit rebuttal is confirmed: `go test -count=3 -run TestRunSeveralRefusals ./internal/work` passes (ok, 1.3s); the full `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/work ./cmd/fyr` passes (22s and 64s); gofmt and `go vet` are clean, also with GOOS=darwin. The worst remaining problem is a stale restatement: `TDD.md:179` still says a slot is "taken and given back under `slots.lock`", which round 2 reversed for `give`. The rest are fixes with no test (the accounting rollback, the glob-to-ReadDir change, the blocking pid-file lock, the lock-test error branch), three round-1 security items that are neither fixed nor recorded as accepted, and one SPEC claim of coverage.

No `fyr` verb that writes state and no real `agy` were run (one `fyr search --refs` and one `fyr record list --kind bug` read at the start; the latter showed no bug touching this area). The mutation copy lived under `.agents/scratch/reviewer-r2-mut/` and was deleted; the tree was not touched.

## Round-1 findings, one by one

Mutations: sed/python edit of exactly one occurrence (count asserted = 1), copy restored from the tree and compared with `cmp`; each mutant compiled and the named test failed.

| Round-1 finding | Fixed by | Test red without it |
|---|---|---|
| review: `intersect` one direction unpinned | new row `dir-prefix-first` | yes: drop `under(a,b)` makes `TestRunSeveralRefusals/dir-prefix-first` fail |
| review: `--kill` migration unpinned | row `{"work","--kill",...}` in the read-only list | yes: `writesState` -> `return true` makes `TestStateDirMigrationByVerb/reads_work_--kill_...` fail |
| review: ctx end races a worker's end | `&& ctx.Err() == nil` in `dispatch` | yes: removed, `TestRunDeadContextStartsNothing` fails (sandboxes made, no "never started" note). The test uses a context dead from the start, a deterministic stand-in for the select race; the random-select interleaving itself is not exercised |
| review: coverage claims name no gaps | GUIDE-testing § 3k and SPEC now list the slot-count error path, `slots.lock` exclusion, a `held` error | docs; see finding 4 for gaps still unnamed |
| review: accounting leaks on error | `take` rolls back `running` on a failed write; `give` always decrements | no test (finding 2) |
| review: `filepath.Glob` on a home path | `os.ReadDir` in `liveRuns` | no test (finding 2): no test path holds `[ * ?` |
| review: `openRun` `LOCK_NB` on a fresh file | blocking `LOCK_EX` | no test (finding 2); the window is microseconds |
| review: weak red in `TestRunCountsOtherRuns` | `apart` barrier (`running-` files) and `wantApart` | yes: limit check off (`if false && ...`) fails `TestRunSeveralWaits` and `TestRunCountsOtherRuns` 3 of 3 runs; others-count off (`n += 0*c`) fails `TestRunCountsOtherRuns` 3 of 3. The rig removes `running-$me` at the end of each worker, so correct sequential workers never see two `running-` files |
| review: stale comments | `work.go:1`, `drafts.go`, `run_safety_test.go` rewritten | n/a |
| review: `--kill` needs the same `--home` | help text, SPEC `--kill` paragraph, GUIDE § 3k last sentence | n/a (TDD.md:70 does not say it; not required) |
| security 1: pid over `pid_max` wraps in `kill(2)` | `maxPid = 1<<22` in `readPid`; `stampRe` capped at 7 digits | yes: each half alone fails `TestPidBounds` (maxPid check removed: red; stampRe back to `+`: red via the Kill "not a stamp" assertion; both: red) |
| security: `at-limit` fails | rebutted | confirmed, see above |
| security: `liveRuns` fails open (open error, `held` error) | open error and `held` error count as the whole limit | open error: yes (`continue` instead makes `TestLiveRunsFailClosed` fail). `held` error: no test (mutant passed the whole `Test(Run\|Live\|Kill\|Slot\|Pid)` set); the SPEC names this as uncovered, which is honest |
| security: blocking `lockSlots` | `LOCK_NB`, busy -> retry at next poll | yes: blocking again makes `TestRunSlotsLockBusy` fail ("the run hung on slots.lock", 20.7s) |
| security: `Kill` signals a planted pid (no identity check) | not changed; SPEC adds an accepted TOCTOU residual only | not fixed, not recorded as accepted for the planted-file case (finding 3) |
| security: worker can rewrite its run's pid file | not changed | not fixed, not recorded (finding 3) |
| security: `atLimit` reads before `CheckRoot` | not changed | not fixed, not recorded (finding 3) |

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `TDD.md:179` — stale restatement of a claim round 2 reversed: "A slot is taken and given back under `slots.lock`, counting every other live run's `running`, so two runs never take the last slot". After the fix, `give` takes no lock and `take` never waits for it (SPEC line 105 says so; `slots.go:90-123`). Failure scenario: an engineer reading TDD T18 believes `give` is serialized by `slots.lock` and adds code that relies on that. Fix: "A slot is taken under `slots.lock`, which is never waited for (a busy lock means no slot is free this poll); it is given back without the lock, since a lower count only frees a slot."
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/slots.go:106-111` (`take`), `:119-123` (`give`), `:147-` (`liveRuns` ReadDir), `:71` (`openRun` blocking lock) — four round-1 fixes have no test that fails without them. Mutating `take` to drop the `r.running--` rollback, `give` to skip the decrement, `liveRuns` back to `Glob`, or `openRun` back to `LOCK_NB` leaves every test green (no test has a write error, a glob metacharacter in the home path, or a concurrent shared lock on a fresh pid file). The dispatch asked for a test that fails without each fix. Failure scenario: a later "simplification" restores `filepath.Glob`, and a home such as `/home/a[1]` silently stops enforcing the machine-wide limit again. Cheap tests: `TestLiveRunsBracketHome` (work root under `t.TempDir()/a[1]/work` with a held stand-in run, `atLimit` must refuse), and a `take` with `r.pid` closed to force a write error asserting `r.running` is unchanged. The race windows (`openRun`) can be named as untestable.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `.agents/scratch/workers/p4docs/SPEC-fyr-work.md:106` and `GUIDE-testing.md` § 3k "Not covered" — the SPEC states "(`os.ReadDir`, so a home path with `[`, `*` or `?` is no pattern)" as behaviour, and the "Not covered" lists omit the glob case, the `take` rollback/`give` accounting and the blocking pid-file lock (review-standards § 7: a coverage claim names what is not covered). Fix: add those three to the "Not covered" sentences in both drafts, or add the tests above. The test-table row for `TestStateDirMigrationByVerb` (SPEC line 242) also still reads only "the verb migrates ... first", though its new row pins that `--kill` does NOT migrate; add "and `--kill` does not".
- **[low / confidence: medium]** security items not fixed and not recorded as accepted: (a) `slots.go` `Kill` signals whatever pid a held, planted, same-uid pid file names, as long as the pid equals the stamp's, with no check that it is a `fyr` process (SPEC § The verb records only the pid-reuse TOCTOU as residual); (b) a worker can rewrite its own run's `pid` line, because the file is its sandbox's grandparent (`<work>/<stamp>/pid`), which lowers or inflates the machine-wide count; (c) `atLimit` (refusal 6) reads the work root before `CheckRoot` (refusal 8). Failure scenario for (a): a worker plants `<work>/<stamp>-<editor pid>/pid`, holds its lock, and `atLimit`'s refusal lists the stamp with "fyr work --kill <stamp>". These are within the same-uid model that SPEC § Open questions already accepts for clones (line 222), so they are low; but the round-1 report asked for either a fix or a recorded decision. Fix: one bullet in § Open questions naming (a) to (c) as accepted under that model, or a `/proc/<pid>/exe` check for (a).
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/work/slots.go:~164` — the comment "the run ended since the glob" now describes code that uses `os.ReadDir`. Trivial; fix with the next edit.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. `slotPoll`, `maxPid`, `wantApart`, `fastPoll` are all used; no commented-out code added.
2. Flow tracing — pass. `take` -> `lockSlots` (busy returns `(false, nil)`, `dispatch` breaks and waits for the poll or `stop`); `take` error -> `unstarted(setup failed)`; `give` runs once per `done`, so the running count stays balanced; `ctx.Err()` guard feeds `neverStarted`; `held` now returns an error to `liveRuns` (fail closed) and `Kill` (refusal exit 2). `maxPid` flows through `readPid` to `liveRuns`, `Kill`. New tests were mutated red (table above), apart from the four gaps in finding 2.
3. Standards conformance — pass with nits. gofmt, vet (linux, darwin) clean. Restatement grep over README, SDD, TDD, help text, SPEC and GUIDE for `slots.lock`, pid file, glob, `--kill`, `--home`: one stale copy (`TDD.md:179`, finding 1). Record text matches the code on: pid bounds (4194304 allowed, 7-digit stamp), `--kill` reads and does not migrate, `--home` for `--kill`, never-waited `slots.lock`, ReadDir, fail-closed rules, dead-context rule, exit codes. Help text reworded and no longer says "before anything ran"; the 39-line/exit lines are consistent with SPEC.
4. Directory layout — pass. No new files in round 2.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only. `give` without the lock removes a lock acquisition; `LOCK_NB` plus the existing poll replaces a blocking wait with no new mechanism. No auth or crypto surface.
6. Decoupling — pass. Slot accounting stays in `slots.go`; `dispatch` takes `ctx.Err()` through the existing parameter; the rig change (`apart`) is local to the fake agy script.

## Not examined
- The interleaving where `select` picks a worker's end over `ctx.Done()` while a slot frees; only the dead-from-start context is tested. Reasoned from the `for` condition, not run.
- The claim "22 mutations, all red": I reproduced 14 (intersect, writesState, ctx guard, maxPid x3, open-error, held-error [green, as noted], blocking lockSlots, limit check off x3, others-count off x3 repeat runs). The other mutants were not run.
- A real two-worker Antigravity invocation, and macOS runtime behaviour (only `GOOS=darwin go vet`).
- The stored (non-draft) records' text, the `orig/` copies of the drafts, `GUIDE-fyr-matrix.md`, and `internal/sandbox` (not in the interdiff).
- `go test` of packages other than `./internal/work` and `./cmd/fyr`; `fyr check`.

## Outcome

Round 1:
1. `intersect` reversed direction untested — fixed: `TestRunSeveralRefusals/dir-prefix-first`; the one-way mutation is red.
2. `--kill` and the state-dir migration — fixed: a `work --kill <stamp>` row in `TestStateDirMigrationByVerb`'s read-only list; reverting `writesState` is red.
3. `dispatch` could start a waiting file on a dead context — fixed: `ctx.Err()` checked before each slot; `TestRunDeadContextStartsNothing` (a dead context at the start, the same condition) is red without it.
4. Coverage claims name no gaps — fixed: `SPEC-fyr-work` § Verification and `GUIDE-testing` § 3k name the uncovered paths.
5. Slot accounting leaks on error — fixed: `take` rolls back on a failed write; `give` decrements with no lock. `give`'s decrement is pinned (`TestRunSeveralWaits` red when it keeps the slot); the rollback's write error has no test and is named as uncovered.
6. `filepath.Glob` on the home path — fixed: `os.ReadDir`; `TestLiveRunsGlobChars` is red under a glob.
7. `openRun`'s lock race — fixed differently: the pid file is locked under `pid.new` and renamed, so no count opens it before it is locked; named as uncovered by a test.
8. `TestRunCountsOtherRuns` timing-dependent — fixed: the fake agy's `apart` barrier; the "others ignored" mutation is red.
9. Stale comments — fixed (`work.go`, `drafts.go`, `run_safety_test.go`).
10. `--kill` needs the run's `--home` — fixed: the help page, `SPEC-fyr-work` and `GUIDE-testing` § 3k say so.

Round 2:
1. `TDD.md` T18 Slots wording — fixed.
2. Four fixes with no test — `give` and `ReadDir` now pinned (above); the rollback and the `pid.new` rename named as uncovered.
3. Three round-1 security items unrecorded — `atLimit` before `CheckRoot`: fixed, the count now follows the root check (`TestRunRootBeforeLimit`, red when reordered); `Kill` cannot prove a `fyr` process and a worker can rewrite its run's pid file: accepted, stated in `SPEC-fyr-work` § Open questions and D92.

27 mutations of the pinned branches, all red. The full test command exit 0 after the fixes (own call).

title: Security review — workers Phase 4: the pid file, the slots and --kill (two rounds)
body:
# Security review — fyr-work-phase4-several-kickoffs   (2026-10-29)

Range reviewed: 645492d..working tree, the uncommitted diff as snapshotted in `.agents/scratch/workers/p4-code.diff` (21:00), plus the new files `internal/work/slots.go`, `slots_test.go`, `several_test.go`. The tree moved during the review: `cmd/fyr/verb_work.go`, `internal/work/preflight.go` and `internal/work/work.go` were rewritten at 21:07–21:08, and README.md, SDD.md and TDD.md were added to the diff. I compared the code changes against the snapshot. They split functions (`workRun`, `prepared.session`, `neverStarted`, `printReady`) and change no behaviour that I could see. `slots.go` is byte-identical to the snapshot. Tests below ran against the 21:08 tree.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The worst problem is in `--kill`. The pid it signals comes from a pid file, and the only bound on it is `pid > 1`. On Linux the kernel truncates the `kill(2)` pid argument to 32 bits. I confirmed this with a harmless signal-0 probe: `kill(2^32+self, 0)` returned 0. So a held pid file whose stamp and line both say `4294967295` makes `fyr work --kill` call `kill(-1, SIGTERM)`, which signals every process of the operator's uid. `4294967296` makes it `kill(0)`, which signals the caller's own process group. The precondition is a same-uid process that plants the directory and holds its flock. Under the accepted threat model a worker agent already has that power, and it could signal those processes directly. So this is defence in depth, not an escalation. But the hazard is cheap to remove, and `atLimit`'s refusal lists every live stamp next to the hint "fyr work --kill <stamp>", so the operator would be shown a planted stamp and told to kill it. The second problem is functional, and it is security-adjacent: refusal 5 (`atLimit`) does not fire in the package's own test (3 of 3 runs plus one `-race` run). The machine-wide limit still holds because `take()` makes the run wait, so the limit is not breached.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/work/slots.go:179` and `:231`: the pid is parsed with `strconv.Atoi` and only `pid <= 1` is refused. The stamp regex `([0-9]+)` places no bound on the pid either. `syscall.Kill(pid, …)` passes `uintptr(pid)`, and Linux truncates that to `pid_t`. **Failure scenario:** a worker agent (same uid, `command(*)`) creates `<work>/2026-10-29-120000-4294967295/pid` containing `4294967295 0`. A detached child holds `flock(LOCK_EX)` on the file. Every later `fyr work` refusal-5 message names that stamp as a live run and suggests `--kill`. When the operator runs it, every process of their uid gets SIGTERM, including the desktop session, editors and the other workers. With `4294967296+N` the signal goes to pid N, and with `2^32` to the caller's process group. **Remediation:** parse with `strconv.ParseInt(s, 10, 32)` and require `1 < pid <= 1<<22`, which is Linux's maximum `pid_max` and covers macOS's 99999. Apply this in `readPid`, so `liveRuns` gets the same bound. Add a test row for `4294967295` and `4294967296` that fails without the bound.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/slots.go:214-235`, `Kill`: the only thing that ties the signalled pid to a `fyr work` run is that the file is locked by someone and that the pid string matches the stamp. Both are chosen by whoever planted the file. A held, planted file that names any live same-uid pid, such as the operator's editor, sends that process SIGTERM. There is also a TOCTOU window between `held()`/`readPid` and `syscall.Kill`. If the run ends and the pid is reused in that window, an unrelated process is signalled. The window is microseconds. **Remediation:** before signalling, check that the pid is a `fyr` process. On Linux, compare `/proc/<pid>/exe` with `os.Executable()`. Alternatively, take a process-associated lock (`fcntl F_SETLK`) on the pid file and read the holder with `F_GETLK`, which returns `l_pid`, then signal only that pid. Note that POSIX locks drop when any fd on the file in that process closes, and `liveRuns` never opens its own run's file, so this is workable.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/slots.go:192-208` with `preflight.go:47-50`: `TestRunSeveralRefusals/at-limit` fails deterministically on this tree. The output is `err <nil>, want "the machine already runs 2 workers, at --max-workers 2: …"`. It failed 3 of 3 times without `-race` and once with `-race`, and each run took about 122 s. That matches the stand-in holder's 2-minute self-exit (`slots_test.go` `holdRun`). So `Run` passed preflight, then waited in `take()` until the holder exited. `take()` and `atLimit` call the same `liveRuns`, and the logic reads the same to me. I checked separately that the holder's lock is held and its line is `"<pid> 2\n"`: a Python `LOCK_SH|LOCK_NB` probe against a manually started stand-in got `BlockingIOError`. I did not isolate the root cause within budget. Separately, `liveRuns` fails open on two paths: an `OpenRegular` error is `continue`, and a `held()` error other than `EWOULDBLOCK` (EINTR, ENOLCK on NFS) counts as not held. **Consequence:** the documented refusal does not happen, and a run blocks silently for as long as the other runs hold slots (the cap still holds). **Remediation:** find out why the pin is red before commit. Make the `held()` error and the open error fail closed: count the whole limit, as an unreadable line already does.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/slots.go:107-117`, `lockSlots`: this is a blocking `LOCK_EX` on `<work>/slots.lock`, with no context and no timeout, called from `take()` and `give()` on the dispatch goroutine. Go installs SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers with SA_RESTART, so `--kill` or Ctrl-C does not interrupt it. **Failure scenario:** a same-uid process (a leftover worker child, or a SIGSTOPped `fyr work` caught inside the microsecond window) holds `slots.lock`. Every run's dispatch loop then hangs. Workers that finish block forever on the unbuffered `done` send, `r.close()` never runs, and only SIGKILL ends the run. Cleanup that has already run inside each worker, such as the token link removal, is unaffected. **Remediation:** poll with `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB` and a short sleep, giving up on `ctx.Done()` or after a bound. On give-up, fail closed: no slot taken, and `give()` records the miss.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/slots.go:121-126` together with the sandbox layout `<work>/<stamp>/<name>/`: the run's pid file is the parent directory's entry of every worker sandbox in that run. A worker agent can rewrite its own run's `pid` line, for example to `<pid> 0`. Other runs then undercount it, and the machine-wide cap (D30) is exceeded. Or it can leave a held file behind after the run, which counts as 8 and blocks every later run until it is killed. Both fall within SPEC-fyr-work § Open questions' accepted same-uid model (line 192 of the record). This is listed because the count is a new trust channel that agents can write and that other runs read. **Remediation (optional):** keep the pid files outside the directory that holds the sandboxes, e.g. `<work>/.runs/<stamp>`, or record this in the spec's accepted-risk list.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/preflight.go:47-50`: `atLimit` globs and opens files under the work root before `sandbox.CheckRoot` has approved that root. These are reads only, through `OpenRegular` with `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK`, so a FIFO cannot block them. But a `--home` inside a checkout, or a work root that is a symlink, gets read before it is refused. **Remediation:** move `atLimit` after `CheckRoot`. That reorders the refusal numbering in the spec, so it is the operator's call. Alternatively, leave it as is and note it.

- **[info]** `cmd/fyr/run_dispatch.go:182`: `--kill` is classed as not writing state. That is correct: `Kill` only opens the pid file read-only and takes and releases a shared flock. `Kill` gets no `CheckRoot`, and the stamp regex rules out path traversal in the one joined component.

## Checked

- **Secrets:** none added in code, tests or help text. The `--kill` output and errors print only the stamp, the pid and the path, through `search.Printable`.
- **Injection:** the stamp is anchored by a regex before any path join, so there is no traversal. The pid file is read with `LimitReader(64)`, `Fields`, `Atoi`, and the stamp and pid strings must match. Kickoff names come from `nameRe` (`[a-z0-9-]{1,63}`) and stay unique per run (`branchesFree`), so the sandbox paths and branches are disjoint, and the leftover-process roots (`<dir>/app`, `<dir>/home`, matched with a trailing separator) of one worker cannot match a sibling's. `disjoint`/`intersect` is consistent with `Kickoff.covers`: an entry without a trailing `/` is a file. The fetch is a non-forced `ref:ref` with fsck, so two runs that share a Kickoff name across processes cannot overwrite each other's branch.
- **Signals and processes:** `kill(-1)`/`kill(0)` truncation (finding 1). `pid <= 1` rules out -1, 0 and 1 as typed. The pid file fd is `O_CLOEXEC`, the Go default, so no child inherits the lock and keeps a dead run looking live. The SIGTERM handler is installed before the pid file exists and outlives it, because `r.close` is deferred inside `Run`. Per-worker `pgids` keep the group sweeps per worker.
- **Concurrency:** `collect` mutex serializes fetch, scope and drafts per process. Drafts go to `.agents/scratch/work/<stamp>/<name>`, distinct per worker. Clones use `--no-hardlinks` (`internal/sandbox/prepare.go:56`), so no worker shares object inodes with the lead. Cross-worker writes into a sibling's clone are an accepted risk (SPEC-fyr-work, line 192). Check c skips `work/`, so the new `slots.lock` and pid files cause no false failures. `go test -race` showed no data race in the tests that ran.
- **Lock semantics:** `flock` is per open file description on Linux and macOS, so `held()` works across processes and within one. On NFS, Linux emulates flock with POSIX locks: still correct across processes. Non-EWOULDBLOCK errors fail open (finding 3).
- **Authz/authn:** no auth surface. `--kill` signals only within the uid, by kernel rule.
- **Crypto:** none touched. Nothing hand-rolled.
- **Dependencies:** `go.mod`/`go.sum` are unchanged and the change is stdlib only. `govulncheck ./...`: "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities" (1 in a required module, not called; the known one per AGENTS.md). `npm audit`: not applicable, no JS in range.
- **GCP surface:** none in range.
- **Tests run:** `go vet ./internal/work ./cmd/fyr` is clean. `go test -race ./internal/work -run 'Several|Kill|Slot|CountsOther|Run'` gives FAIL (at-limit only). `go test ./internal/work -run 'TestKill|TestRunCountsOtherRuns|TestRunSeveralRefusals/(name-twice|dir-prefix|max-9)$'` gives PASS. The truncation probe used signal 0 to the probe's own pid and nothing else.

## Not examined

- The root cause of the `at-limit` failure. I had no strace and no way to instrument without editing source.
- `cmd/fyr` tests were not run (`TestWorkVerb*`), and neither was the full `./internal/work` suite outside the patterns above.
- `internal/work/fetch.go` and `drafts.go` beyond their outlines, which this diff does not change apart from the `collect` lock.
- `internal/sandbox/session.go`'s per-worker behaviour under several concurrent boxes, beyond the pgid list.
- macOS: not run. The `syscall.Kill` truncation on darwin/arm64 was not probed, though the remediation bound covers it either way.
- The docs added to the diff after the snapshot (README.md, SDD.md, TDD.md, help_text.go wording).

## Round 2


Range reviewed: the round-1 tree to the working tree. This round covers the fixes only: the interdiff `.agents/scratch/workers/p4-r2.diff` (slots.go, slots_test.go, several_test.go, work.go, rig_test.go, migrate_test.go, help_text.go, and comments in drafts.go and run_safety_test.go), read against the current `internal/work/slots.go` (271 lines, read whole) and the `dispatch` loop of `internal/work/work.go`. The round-1 findings are in `.agents/scratch/agents/security-2026-10-29-2101.md`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Round-1 findings 1, 2 and 3 are fixed, and each fix has a test that fails when the fix is reverted. I checked this with mutations on a scratch copy; the table is below. Nothing high or medium is left. The remaining findings are all low.

The worst one is a gap left by the fix to finding 3. `openRun` now waits on a blocking `LOCK_EX` of its new pid file, with no bound and no context. `take()` was changed so it never waits for the same reason, and `openRun` keeps that pattern.

The other gaps are these:
- Two of the fail-closed branches named in finding 2 have no test: the `held()` error path in `liveRuns`, and the same path in `Kill`.
- The fail-closed count turns a planted or unreadable stamp-named entry into a permanent "machine already runs 8 workers" refusal. The `--kill` hint in that refusal cannot clear it.

All three need a same-uid process or the operator's own leftovers. Under SPEC-fyr-work's accepted same-uid model they are hardening and test gaps, not escalations.

### Round-1 findings: status

| Round-1 # | Fix | Test | Mutation check (scratch copy `.agents/scratch/sec-r2-mut`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 pid wrap in kill(2) | `maxPid = 1<<22` checked in `readPid` (slots.go:213); `stampRe` limits the pid to 1–7 digits (:38) | `TestPidBounds` | Regex reverted to `[0-9]+`: FAIL. `pid > maxPid` removed: FAIL. **Fixed.** |
| 2 fail-open: open error | `OpenRegular` errors other than ENOENT count as `MaxMaxWorkers` (:167-172) | `TestLiveRunsFailClosed` (symlinked pid file) | Branch reverted to "count nothing": FAIL. **Fixed.** |
| 2 fail-open: `held()` error | `held` returns its error; `liveRuns` counts the run as full (:174-175) and `Kill` refuses (:258-259) | **none** | Each branch reverted to "count nothing" or "proceed": both PASS. **Fixed in code, untested** (finding B). |
| 2 at-limit pin red | n/a | `TestRunSeveralRefusals/at-limit` | `go test -count=3 -run 'TestRunSeveralRefusals\|…' ./internal/work`: ok in 33 s in total. In round 1 each run took about 122 s and failed. Consistent with the dispatch's explanation (a concurrent mutation run); I cannot verify what happened in round 1 itself. |
| 3 blocking `slots.lock` | `lockSlots` uses `LOCK_EX\|LOCK_NB`; busy means "no slot, poll again" (:125-138); `give()` no longer takes the lock | `TestRunSlotsLockBusy` | `LOCK_NB` removed: FAIL (hung 20 s, `t.Fatal`). **Fixed.** |
| (dispatch) dead ctx starts workers | `ctx.Err() == nil` guard on the start loop (work.go) | `TestRunDeadContextStartsNothing` | Passes on the tree; not mutated (not my finding). |

### The fixes add no new weakness in these respects

- **`give()` without `slots.lock`:** `take` and `give` both run only on the `dispatch` goroutine, so there is no data race on `r.running`. `give` only lowers the count. Another process that holds `slots.lock` reads either the old or the new value, and both are at least the true value, so any error is in the safe direction. The write is a single `pwrite` at offset 0 with a fixed length: `running` is 0–8, one digit, because `take` keeps it below `max` (at most 8) and `give` follows only a started worker. A failed `write()` in `give` leaves the higher count on disk, which is also the safe direction.
- **`take()` never waits:** busy returns `(false, nil)`, so the worker stays queued and `ctx.Done()` and the ticker still reach the loop. An error from `lockSlots` or `liveRuns` fails the worker as `ReasonSetup`, never started. Both fail closed. `take` now undoes `running++` when the write fails, so no phantom slot is held.
- **`liveRuns` with `os.ReadDir`:** this is a fail-open fix in its own right. A home path that contains glob metacharacters (`[`, `*`, `?`) previously matched no pid files, so it counted zero runs. A stamp entry that is a symlink to a directory is still followed into its `pid` file, which is no change from the glob. The last component is opened with `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK` (`OpenRegular`), so a FIFO cannot block it. ENOENT, a run that ended between the listing and the open, is skipped correctly.
- **`--kill` in `migrate_test.go`'s read-only list:** it runs with `--home <temp>`, where no pid file exists, so it signals nothing.

## Findings

- **A. [low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/slots.go:72`. `openRun` takes a blocking `LOCK_EX` on its freshly created (`O_EXCL`) pid file, with no context and no bound. `verb_work.go:81` captures SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGQUIT with `signal.NotifyContext`, and Go's handlers restart the syscall, so neither Ctrl-C nor `--kill` breaks the wait. `--kill` would in any case report the file as stale, because nothing holds `LOCK_EX` on it yet. Legitimate contention is only the momentary `LOCK_SH|LOCK_NB` probe in another run's `held()`. **Failure scenario:** a same-uid process, for example a leftover worker child watching `<work>/` with inotify, opens the new pid file and holds `LOCK_SH`. The run then hangs before it prints its stamp, and only SIGKILL ends it. It leaves `<work>/<stamp>/pid` behind, which other runs count as 0 because it is unlocked. This is the same class as round-1 finding 3, now at a single call site. **Remediation:** poll `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB` with a short sleep and a bound (for example 50 ms × 100), then fail with "the run's pid file: locked by another process". A test can hold `LOCK_SH` on an `O_EXCL` file in the rig (this needs a seam, since the path is created inside `openRun`) and require the error.

- **B. [low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/slots.go:174-175` (`liveRuns`) and `:258-259` (`Kill`). The `held()` error branches, which are half of round-1 finding 2's fail-open remediation, have no test. With either branch reverted on the scratch copy, the full `TestPidBounds|TestLiveRunsFailClosed|TestRunSlotsLockBusy|TestRunDeadContextStartsNothing|TestKill` set passes. Under the review rule that "a finding is fixed only when every trigger it names has a test that fails without the fix", finding 2's `held()` trigger (EINTR or ENOLCK) is not yet fixed. **Remediation:** make the flock call a package variable (as `slotPoll` already is) or pass a `held` func, then add one row where it returns `ENOLCK`: `atLimit` must refuse, naming the stamp, and `Kill` must return an error without signalling.

- **C. [low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/slots.go:167-172` with `:241` and `:248-256`. Failing closed is correct, but its refusal is misleading and has no way out. Any entry under `<work>/` whose name matches `stampRe` and whose `pid` cannot be opened makes every later `fyr work` refuse with "the machine already runs 8 workers … fyr work --kill <stamp>". The entry might be a regular file (ENOTDIR), a mode-000 directory (EACCES), or a `pid` that is a symlink (ELOOP). For the same entry, `--kill` then fails with "no run <stamp>: …", and no message names the path to remove. This is availability only, and it needs a same-uid plant or a hand-edited work root. **Remediation:** carry the reason and the path for each failed entry, and have the refusal say "<stamp>: <path> unreadable (<err>); remove it if no run owns it" instead of counting it as 8 live workers.

- **D. [info]** Round-1 findings 2 (signal a live non-fyr pid / TOCTOU), 5 (pid file inside the sandbox parent) and 6 (`atLimit` before `CheckRoot`) are not addressed in this interdiff. They were optional or accepted-risk items, and I list them here only so the record shows they are still open.

## Checked

- **Secrets:** none added. The new error strings carry only a stamp, a path, a pid and an errno.
- **Injection:** the stamp regex is tighter (1–7 digit pid) and is still anchored before any path join. `ReadDir` names are filtered by `stampRe` before the join, so there is no traversal.
- **Signals/processes:** a `--kill` pid is now at most `1<<22` (4194304), below 2^31, so `kill(2)` cannot wrap it to -1, 0 or a process group. `pid <= 1` is still refused. Both bounds are tested.
- **Concurrency/locks:** the locking claims are under "The fixes add no new weakness" above. `openRun`'s blocking `LOCK_EX` is finding A.
- **Authz/authn:** no auth surface.
- **Crypto:** none touched.
- **Dependencies:** the interdiff adds only `io/fs` from the stdlib, and `go.mod` is unchanged. I did not re-run `govulncheck` this round: there is no dependency change, and round 1 got "affected by 0".
- **GCP surface:** none.
- **Tests run:** `go test -count=3 -run 'TestRunSeveralRefusals|TestPidBounds|TestLiveRunsFailClosed|TestRunSlotsLockBusy|TestRunDeadContextStartsNothing|TestKill|TestRunCountsOther|TestRunSeveral' ./internal/work` gave ok (33.3 s). There were six mutations on the scratch copy `.agents/scratch/sec-r2-mut`, with the baseline green first. Four were caught (M1a, M1b, M2a, M3). Two survived, `held()` error in `liveRuns` and in `Kill` (finding B). The copy's `slots.go` was restored and checked with `cmp`.

## Not examined

- `-race` was not run this round, and neither were the full `./internal/work` suite outside the patterns above nor `cmd/fyr` tests (`TestWorkVerb*`, the migrate row).
- I did not trace the `rig_test.go` `apart` barrier change and the `wantApart` rewrite in `several_test.go` closely enough to confirm that `wantApart` fails when two workers overlap. They are test-only. I did no mutation on `take`'s limit comparison for them.
- macOS: not run. The `pid_max` bound is above macOS's 99999, so the bound holds there too.
- Round-1 finding 3's assertion that the round-1 at-limit failure came from a concurrent mutation run: I could not verify it. I confirmed only that the pin is green now, 3 of 3.
- The docs (README.md, SDD.md, TDD.md) are outside this interdiff and were not read.

## Outcome

Round 1:
1. Pid truncation in `kill(2)` (medium) — fixed: a pid over 1<<22 is refused in the line, and the stamp's pid is at most seven digits; `TestPidBounds`, red under either mutation.
2. `at-limit` red, and two fail-open paths — the red test is rebutted: it ran while a mutation script patched `atLimit` in the same tree; it passes 3 of 3 (both round-2 reports confirm). The fail-open paths are fixed: an unopenable pid file and a lock test that errors each count as the whole limit (`TestLiveRunsFailClosed`, `TestHeldErrorFailsClosed` through a `flock` seam), each red without its fix.
3. Blocking `slots.lock` — fixed: never waited for (`TestRunSlotsLockBusy`, red when it blocks); `give` takes no lock.
4. `Kill` cannot tie the pid to `fyr` — accepted: the limit is a resource guard among the operator's own processes; stated in `SPEC-fyr-work` § Open questions and D92.
5. A worker can rewrite its run's pid file — accepted, as 4.
6. `atLimit` reads before `CheckRoot` — fixed: counted after it (`TestRunRootBeforeLimit`).

Round 2:
1. `openRun`'s waiting `LOCK_EX` — fixed: `pid.new` locked without waiting, then renamed.
2. `held()` error branches untested — fixed: `TestHeldErrorFailsClosed`.
3. An unreadable entry blocks every run unnamed — fixed: the refusal names each path counted as full (`TestLiveRunsFailClosed` checks the path).

`govulncheck`: no new findings.

title: Review — workers Phase 5a, the work skill (code and docs)
body:
# Review — workers Phase 5a, the work skill (code and docs)   (2026-10-29)

Range reviewed: working tree vs HEAD (bc245f8): README.md (2 lines), skills/work/SKILL.md (new, staged, read whole), .agents/trail.jsonl (one record, GUIDE-skill-matrix, edited in place: a new `work` row appended and `updated` bumped).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing in the scope is broken against the verb it drives. Every command, flag, line shape and reason string the `work` skill names exists as `fyr help work` and `SPEC-fyr-work` print or take it (checked below). The one concrete problem is a forward reference: the skill's step 3 composes each Kickoff from "the handoff skill's worker-mode Kickoff", and its "From a planning session" path rests on "the feature skill's workers decision". Neither exists in the tree yet (both are Phase 5b of the plan), so until 5b lands the shipped skill points at text that is not there. Low severity: the plan splits 5a and 5b on purpose, and no run path reaches the skill before 5b except `/work PLAN-ID`.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `skills/work/SKILL.md:12,74` — step 3 ("Compose each Kickoff from the handoff skill's worker-mode Kickoff, filling its fixed text and changing none of it") and the "From a planning session" bullet (the feature skill's workers decision) name content that does not exist. `grep -i worker skills/handoff/SKILL.md skills/feature/SKILL.md` is empty; the handoff Kickoff template at `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:129-134` is the single-session one. Plan Phase 5b (tasks at the plan's `### Phase 5b`) adds both. A lead loaded now by `/work PLAN-ID`, or on dave after a 5a-only real-home install, has no fixed text to fill and would improvise the Kickoff. Fix: land 5b in the same push as 5a, or do not install 5a to the real home until 5b is committed; at minimum say so in the 5a handoff's Next Steps.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `skills/work/SKILL.md:83-85` — the duplicate-ID guard (`fyr record list`) runs on the uncommitted squash and `git reset --hard HEAD` then reverts `.agents/trail.jsonl`. `fyr help record` says a changed export "is loaded back before the next call", and `internal/brain/export.go:228` refuses a duplicate ID on load, so the guard fires; I did not verify that the load-back after the reset drops the worker's records from the brain store (the store is what `fyr record get` reads in step 8). Unverified, not a finding against the code; Phase 6's E2E exercises it.

## Skill vs verb check (`fyr help work`, `SPEC-fyr-work`)
- Flags `--timeout` (default 120 min), `--max-workers` (default 4, 1 to 8), `--keep`, `--kill`, `--model`: skill names `--max-workers` (4 default) and `--timeout` (120 min default); both match.
- Result-contract line shapes: skill reads the unprefixed `work: <name>  ` line, `work: <name>: ` notes and `work: <name> | ` section lines, and `work: <name>: handoff <ID>` via `fyr record get`: all in § The result contract. The "printed Kickoff is the worker's proposal, never run" matches D38.
- Safety reasons `credentials left in the sandbox`, `real config changed`, `processes left`, `sandbox replaced`, `lead checkout changed`: each found in `internal/sandbox/{after,box}.go` and `internal/work/work.go`; the set equals SPEC § Failure modes row 3 and 4. Non-safety FAILs the skill re-dispatches (FAIL, timeout) match the SPEC list.

title: Review — BUG-196: the wrong token in internal/serve TestRefusals
body:
# Review — bug196-wrong-token   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: working-tree diff of internal/serve/guard_test.go (.agents/scratch/agents/bug196.diff), uncommitted

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE

The fix is sound and nothing is broken. wrongToken(tok) changes only the first character and picks "b" when tok starts with "a", otherwise "a". The result therefore always differs from tok and is still valid base64url, so it reaches the compare in exchangeToken (guard.go:62) and not some earlier shape check. That removes the 1-in-64 collision of the old "x"+tok[1:]. TestWrongTokenIsWrong forces the three first characters that matter ("x", "a", "b") by setting r.token, and asserts each wrong token differs from the real one and gets a 403. Only the first character differs, which is the same property the old test had.

Verified: gofmt clean, go vet clean, `go test -count=300 -run 'TestRefusals|TestWrongTokenIsWrong|TestTokenSetsCookie' ./internal/serve` passes. Must-fail was checked by reasoning only, not by a mutation run: reverting wrongToken to "x"+tok[1:] makes the "x" case hit the `wrong == Token()` Errorf. Returning tok unchanged fails every case.

## Findings
(none blocking)
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/serve/guard_test.go:126-128` — the test sets `r.token` directly (same package, unexported field). That is fine here: cookie name and base come from other fields, and each test builds its own Run. It breaks silently if Run later derives the cookie or base from the token. No action needed now.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/serve/guard_test.go:87` — "token beside a cookie" still uses the literal `?token=x`. It is safe because the real token is 43 characters and never equals "x", so BUG-196's collision cannot occur there. Noted only so a later reader does not mistake it for a second instance.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass: no unused additions. wrongToken has two callers, the precondition in TestRefusals and TestWrongTokenIsWrong.
2. Flow tracing — pass: wrong token -> bare() -> serveHTTP -> exchangeToken -> equal() -> 403 with lineForbidden. The tests can fail: the precondition checks plus the "x" case would catch a revert. The unusual condition (the token starting with a, b or x) is established by assignment and is then checked against the real value.
3. Standards conformance — pass: the precondition-check rule (review-standards §2) is applied. The comment cites BUG-196 and is accurate (6 bits of first character, so 1/64). The BUG-196 record is still open, which is a records step for the main thread.
4. Directory layout — pass: tests stay beside guard.go.
5. Simplicity — pass: stdlib only, a 6-line helper.
6. Decoupling — pass: the helper is test-local and uses only exported accessors and the same-package field.

## Not examined
The full test suite (excluded by the dispatch). No mutation run of the reverted helper. serve.go and fixture_test.go were read only around the token and request helpers. pages and records tests were not read; they are unrelated to the diff.

## Outcome

- Finding 1 (low, `r.token` set directly): accepted, no change. The cookie name is derived from the port and the base from its own `newToken()` (`internal/serve/serve.go:65-80`), so setting the token moves nothing else. If that derivation changes, the test fails on its 403 assertion rather than passing silently, because the guard still compares against `r.token`.
- Finding 2 (low, `?token=x` at `:87`): no change needed. The reviewer's own reason holds: a 43-character token never equals "x".
- Must-fail evidence the reviewer did not run: the main thread ran `TestWrongTokenIsWrong` with the helper still written as `"x" + tok[1:]` before the fix. It failed with `guard_test.go:130: token x…: the wrong token is the real one`, then passed after the fix.

body:
# Review — worktree-code-docs   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: working tree vs HEAD (bfdfdc6): .agents/trail.jsonl (ADR-077, DEPLOY-local), AGENTS.md, SDD.md, TDD.md, rules/session-sizing.md, skills/feature/SKILL.md, skills/handoff/SKILL.md; untracked .gitattributes. Agreement target: skills/work/SKILL.md (not in the diff), SPEC-fyr-work, PLAN-2026-10-29-workers § Interfaces § The skills and § Phase 5b.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing in the scope breaks a build or a pinned test: `go test ./internal/harness .` passes (size pins, lint, listing budget), and the rule grows by exactly 118 bytes, as ADR-077 states. The worst problems are three places where the new skill text does not agree with the verb or the work skill it feeds, each of which can make a lead misbehave on a real plan: the `files:` grammar is delegated to a section that does not define it (finding 1), the `after:` default exists only in the feature skill (finding 2), and the "planning session ends here" paragraph is only half conditioned on the workers decision (finding 3). All are text fixes; none needs a design decision. No REQUIREMENTS.md violation found (the repo's requirements file is PRD.md; no item touched). No recorded bug is reintroduced.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `skills/feature/SKILL.md:79` — the new `files:` paragraph says entries follow "the Kickoff `Files:` grammar (`handoff` skill)", but the handoff skill defines no grammar (grep for "grammar" in `skills/handoff/SKILL.md` is empty; its new `Files:` line only says "verbatim"). The grammar lives in SPEC-fyr-work § Kickoff: a record ID `^[A-Z]+-[0-9A-Za-z-]+$`, or a repo-relative file or `/`-ended directory; refused: absolute, `..`/`.`/empty segment, glob characters, control characters, and `.agents/trail.jsonl` itself. The feature text lists only "no globs, no absolute paths". A planner who writes `files: .agents/trail.jsonl, ./x` (natural for a phase that stores records) produces a plan whose Kickoffs the verb refuses with exit 2 before anything is made, and `skills/work/SKILL.md` step 5 has no remedy for a refusal. Fix: state the full refusal list in the feature paragraph (or in the handoff `Files:` bullet and point at that), and say a phase never names `.agents/trail.jsonl`.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `skills/feature/SKILL.md:79` vs `skills/work/SKILL.md:73` — the feature skill makes "waits for the previous phase" the default for a header with no `(after: …)`, but the work skill's wave rule says only "whose `after:` phases are all ticked". `/work PLAN-ID` loads the work skill alone (work:11-13), so a lead resuming a plan reads a phase with no `after:` as having no dependency and can dispatch it beside its predecessor whenever their `files:` are disjoint, breaking dependency order. The same default also means the workers decision (feature:104) says "yes" for a plan whose phases are all implicitly chained, which buys one-worker waves. Fix: one clause in work step 2 ("a phase with no `after:` waits for the previous phase").
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `skills/feature/SKILL.md:106` — only the first sentence got the "unless the workers decision says yes" exception. The next sentence still reads unconditionally: "With the box closed, commit and push the plan, write the handoff with Phase 1's Kickoff, and end the session ... never in the session that wrote the plan." On a yes the lead must not write a Phase 1 Kickoff handoff and stop. Line 15 has the same overstatement: a cold-read question "becomes an `Open:` row instead" in a session that may lead, while line 102-104 say it is asked after all when the decision is no. Fix: begin the second sentence with "On a no,", and make line 15 say "becomes an `Open:` row, asked after the workers decision if that is no".
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:162` — the worker-mode carve-out skips Step 3.3, Step 6's push and ingest, then says "Everything else holds". Step 5's cold-reader checks 3 and 4 (handoff:182-183) compare the handoff to `TODO.md` and tell the session to fix `TODO.md` "at the source" (handoff:187), which the worker's Never line forbids; Step 7 items 3 and 4 (handoff:200-201) still require the `fyr metrics ingest` line and a paste-ready next Kickoff for a session that ingests nothing. Fix: name Step 5 items 3-4, Step 7 item 3 as skipped and item 4 as the worker's Kickoff-proposal, in the same paragraph.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:147` vs `AGENTS.md:53`, `DEPLOY-local` § Operator steps — DEPLOY-local records dave's `fyr install` as a standing by-hand procedure, and handoff:147 says Next Steps never list such a procedure ("listing it reads as a question"), while the lead rule (work:57,100; ADR-077) puts exactly that install line into the closing handoff's Next Steps. No one is named as running it. Fix: say in handoff:147 (or AGENTS.md) that a lead's closing handoff is the one place the line is listed, and who runs it.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `skills/feature/SKILL.md:17` — the new gate-rule sentence ("In a lead session, the `work` skill's judgement rule answers a question in the user's place, except an item of its closed set") is not named in ADR-077, and the closed set (work:46) does not list the feature skill's own gates (scope confirmation, review cap). The lead starts after Step 1, so the scope gate is moot in practice, but the sentence reads as waiving gates by session shape rather than by the user's words, which the paragraph's first half forbids. Fix: add the sentence to ADR-077's decision text, and say the scope confirmation is not waived.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. No code in the scope; no orphaned text found. Every new rule has a consumer in `skills/work/SKILL.md`.
2. Flow tracing — fail (nits). Traced feature `files:`/`after:`/workers decision -> work loop steps 2-3 -> handoff worker Kickoff -> `fyr work` (SPEC-fyr-work Kickoff grammar, result contract, drafts at `.agents/scratch/agents/` -> `.agents/scratch/work/<stamp>/<name>/`) and the worker handoff's `## Completed`/`## Next Steps` sections exist. Breaks are findings 1-3. The drafts path and the `Never` line agree with the spec.
3. Standards conformance — pass with nits. Restatement grep ("one Task or one plan phase", "planning session ends", "END the session", "ends here", "metrics ingest") listed every copy: rules/session-sizing.md (bullet and description), SDD.md:146, TDD.md:15, feature:106, handoff:135 (generic Kickoff, correctly unchanged) and context/AGENTS.md:11 (unchanged, still true). Leftover: findings 3-5. Verified rule growth 1311 -> 1429 bytes = 118, matches ADR-077 and the plan's "at most 120".
4. Directory layout — pass. `.gitattributes` at the root is where git reads it; the project layout block does not list it, which is not a finding.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. No code, no dependency; `merge=union` is git's own driver.
6. Decoupling — pass with nits. The worker Kickoff is one home (handoff skill) that the work skill points at, not copies; the `files:` grammar is the exception (finding 1).

## Docs lens
- `fyr check` (run at the checkout root against the working tree; HEAD is a0b05bd+uncommitted): `check: 3 findings (docs 0, specs 3, requirements 0)`; note: `PRD.md has no enforced-by field: not checked`.
- Pre-existing (fyr check), outside the verdict: SPEC-fyr-check spec-stale (2 commits to internal/check, cmd/fyr/check.go ... since 2fc4656cdb9c); SPEC-fyr-eval spec-stale (3 commits since d66d7cfe3eee); SPEC-fyr-serve spec-stale (3 commits since cd001539eed6). None touches the scope's files.
- `restatement-grep.sh` run with the keywords above; hits read; no file restates the old claim except as listed under criterion 3.
- `fyr search` over `spec`, `guide`, `deploy` records for the old session-sizing wording: 0 hits. README.md and PRD.md: no restatement (PRD.md:110 cites ADR-058 as the mechanism, still true).
- DEPLOY-local and AGENTS.md:53 agree with each other and ADR-077 on the dave-install deferral; the conflict with handoff:147 is finding 5.
- ADR-077 numbering of ADR-058's clauses (1), (4), (2)(3)(5) matches ADR-058's text.
- Stale test: none found. `go test ./internal/harness .` passes. The `feature`/`handoff` eval rows were not run (a concurrent run is out of scope; ADR-077 states the yes branch is first exercised in Phase 6).

## Not examined
- `go test ./...` in full and `go vet`: only `./internal/harness` and the root package were run.
- `fyr eval` rows `feature` and `handoff`, and any behavioural run of the changed skills: not run, and not checked against a `testing` record.
- Whether `merge=union` on `.agents/trail.jsonl` behaves as ADR-077 says for an edited line on two branches: not exercised, taken from the ADR.
- Plan-record wording beyond § Interfaces § The skills and § Phase 5b; GUIDE-testing and GUIDE-eval row contents were not read in full.
- The `fyr check` output beyond the three findings and the note (the earlier lines were not shown by the tail I read; the summary line reports docs 0).

## Outcome

- Finding 1 (`files:` grammar delegated to a section that defines none): fixed at `skills/feature/SKILL.md`, the `files:` paragraph: it names the entries and every refusal of `fyr work` (absolute, `.`/`..`/empty segment, glob, `.agents/trail.jsonl`), and records are named by ID.
- Finding 2 (the `after:` default only in the feature skill): fixed at `skills/work/SKILL.md` step 2, and the blocked-phase rule (round 2's nit 1). The second half (an all-chained plan qualifies and runs one-worker waves) is rebutted: that is D48's test as the operator approved it (`PLAN-2026-10-29-workers` D48).
- Finding 3 (the "ends here" paragraph only half conditioned; line 15): fixed at `skills/feature/SKILL.md`: "On a no, with the box closed, …", and line 15's gate waits as an `Open:` row, asked only when the decision is no.
- Finding 4 (worker mode vs Step 5 and Step 7): fixed at `skills/handoff/SKILL.md` § The worker-mode Kickoff: Step 5's checks read `TODO.md` and never edit it; Step 7 reports the skipped ingest and gives the Kickoff as a proposal for the lead.
- Finding 5 (the standing-procedure bullet vs the lead's install line): fixed at `skills/handoff/SKILL.md`, the Next Steps bullet: the lead's closing handoff is the exception, one line for the operator.
- Finding 6 (the gate-rule sentence not in ADR-077; scope gate): fixed in ADR-077's Decision and `skills/feature/SKILL.md` § The gate rule ("it never waives the scope confirmation", round 2's nit 2).
- Round 2 (`REVIEW-2026-10-30-0739-review-workers-phase-5b-round-2-over-the-fixes`): every fix verified; its three low nits fixed after it, at the cap, with no third round: `skills/work/SKILL.md` § blocked phases ("explicit, or the previous phase by default"), `skills/feature/SKILL.md` § The gate rule ("a worker's question"; "it never waives the scope confirmation"), and ADR-077's matching wording. `go test ./internal/harness .` ok after them.

title: Review — workers Phase 5b, round 2 over the fixes
body:
# Review — worktree-code-docs round 2   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: round 2, the fixes only, working tree vs HEAD: skills/feature/SKILL.md (lines 15, 17, 79, 106), skills/work/SKILL.md (line 73), skills/handoff/SKILL.md (line 147, § The worker-mode Kickoff, Worker mode paragraph), ADR-077 (`fyr record get ADR-077 --home .agents/scratch/review`). Round 1 report: .agents/scratch/agents/reviewer-2026-10-30-0730.md.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

All six round-1 findings are fixed as the coordinator described, and the fixes introduced no broken reference or build/test failure (`go test ./internal/harness .` passes; `rules/session-sizing.md` still 1429 bytes, unchanged by round 2; ADR-077 appears once in the trail, no duplicate ID). Two small residues remain: the implicit `after:` chain added to work step 2 is not carried to the blocked-phase rule at work:53, and the new "never waived" wording can be read as overriding the user's own waiver.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/work/SKILL.md:53` (and `:36`) — round 1 finding 2 is fixed at step 2 (work:73: "a phase header with no `after:` waits for the previous phase"), but the blocked-phase rule still says "neither is any phase whose `after:` reaches it, directly or through other phases". A later phase with no explicit `after:` has only the implicit edge, so when its predecessor is blocked it is literally not "reached", and step 11's closing-handoff list ("every blocked phase with its reason") can omit it. It is never dispatched anyway (its predecessor is never ticked), so the failure is a handoff that does not name it, not a wrong dispatch. Fix: at work:53 write "whose `after:` (explicit, or the previous phase by default) reaches it".
- **[low / confidence: low]** `skills/feature/SKILL.md:17` — "the scope confirmation (Step 1) is never waived" sits in a sentence about the judgement rule, but the paragraph's first half lets "the user's own words in the same turn" waive a named gate. Read plainly, "never" also forbids that. Fix: "is never waived by the judgement rule".
- **[low / confidence: low]** ADR-077 Decision says the work skill's judgement rule "answers a worker's question in the user's place", feature:17 says "answers a question". Same meaning for the work skill (work:40 lists "the answer to a worker's question") but the two wordings differ; the ADR is the narrower. Fix by using the skill's words in the ADR, if it is still editable before commit.

## Round 1 fixes, checked
1. `files:` grammar (feature:79) — fixed. The paragraph now names file, `/`-ended directory, record ID, and the verb's refusals (absolute path, `.`/`..`/empty segment, glob, `.agents/trail.jsonl`). Matches SPEC-fyr-work § Kickoff. Not listed (control character, the record-ID regex `^[A-Z]+-[0-9A-Za-z-]+$`): a record ID in a normal plan (`ADR-077`, `BUG-196`) passes it; acceptable. The template placeholder at feature:63 agrees. No remaining "grammar" cross-reference in feature, handoff or work.
2. `after:` default (work:73) — fixed at step 2; residue above.
3. "planning session ends here" (feature:106) — fixed: "On a no, with the box closed, …". Consistent with the workers-decision paragraph (feature:104) and with work step 1, which commits and pushes the plan on a yes. Line 15 now agrees with lines 102-104 ("waits as an `Open:` row, and is asked only when the workers decision is no").
4. Worker-mode carve-out (handoff, Worker mode paragraph) — fixed for Step 5 (read, never edit `TODO.md`) and Step 7 (skipped ingest reported, Kickoff given as a proposal). Step 5's "fix at the source (plan, `TODO.md`…)" line (handoff:187) is overridden by the paragraph's "never edit it"; acceptable because "the Kickoff wins" is stated.
5. Next Steps exception (handoff:147) — fixed: "A lead's closing handoff (`work` skill) is the exception: it lists the real-home install it deferred, for the final tree, as one line for the operator." Agrees with work:57/:100, AGENTS.md:53 and DEPLOY-local § Operator steps. The restatement grep for "standing procedure" shows no other copy.
6. Gate rule / ADR (feature:17, ADR-077) — fixed; ADR-077 now names D55 and the scope confirmation. Residue above.

Orphans check: no declaration was moved or re-declared by the fixes; each edit is an in-place sentence. Nothing left with no caller.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. No text orphaned by the fixes.
2. Flow tracing — pass with a nit. feature `after:`/`files:` -> work steps 2, 3, 11 -> handoff worker Kickoff -> verb grammar now agree, except work:53 (first finding).
3. Standards conformance — pass. Restatements of the changed sentences found and consistent; ADR-077 matches the skill text up to the wording nit.
4. Directory layout — pass. No files added in round 2.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. No code or dependency.
6. Decoupling — pass. The `files:` rules now live in the feature skill and the verb's spec, not a dangling pointer into the handoff skill.

## Not examined
- Full `go test ./...` and `go vet`; `fyr eval` rows for the changed skills; `fyr check` was not re-run (round 1 reported docs 0 findings; round 2 touched no path or verb name).
- Round-1 low-confidence behaviours not re-tested: `merge=union` on `.agents/trail.jsonl`, and a live lead run (first exercised in Phase 6 per ADR-077).

title: Review — BUG-197 fix, code and docs (2026-10-30)
body:
# Review — bug197-union-duplicate   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: working tree against HEAD 3fa2705 (`.agents/scratch/bug197/fix.diff` incl. new `internal/brain/union_test.go`; docs lens `.agents/scratch/bug197/docs.diff`: SPEC-fyr-record, SPEC-fyr-work, PLAN-2026-10-29-workers)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing is broken. The fix does what BUG-197 fix (a) / D99 says: `readRecords` (internal/brain/export.go) and `parseTrail` (internal/work/records.go) read a byte-identical second line of one ID as the same record, and a same-ID pair that differs is still refused with both line numbers. Every reader of trail.jsonl goes through these two (load, ReadTrail, ParseTrail, work's trailAt); no third duplicate-ID site for trail lines exists (internal/eval/suite.go:66 is the GUIDE-eval table, unrelated). The one real gap is a docs/plan consequence: the committed squash keeps the duplicate line until the next record write (finding 1).

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers` golden path (record body lines ~343 and ~915: "trail.jsonl holds both handoffs and both change records, with no duplicate record ID") and `skills/work/SKILL.md:83-84` (step 3 `fyr record list` as "the duplicate-ID guard", step 4 commit) — after the fix, the lead's squash is committed with the byte-identical duplicate line still in the file: reading drops it in memory, only the next `fyr record add/edit` rewrites the export (`exportLocked`, export.go ~395; `list` is read-only). A rerun check that counts IDs in the file (rather than via `fyr record list`) fails on the first squash commit, and the duplicate persists in history until the lead's next record write. Not a runtime failure (every later read tolerates it, and a union merge on top of a base holding the duplicate stays clean). Fix: state in the plan's golden-path row how "no duplicate record ID" is checked (after the lead's change/handoff write, or via `fyr record list`), and either say in SKILL.md step 3/4 that an identical duplicate is tolerated and dropped by the next record write, or accept it explicitly in D99. The docs.diff sentence "the next export drops the copy" is accurate; the plan's golden-path text is the restatement left untouched.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/brain/union_test.go`, `internal/brain/export_test.go` — SPEC-fyr-record now claims "byte-identical ... after its line ending is trimmed". The work test covers a CRLF/LF pair (`records_test.go`), but no brain test covers it, nor a duplicate as the last line with no trailing newline (the `continue` skips the loop's EOF check; it terminates correctly on the next empty read). I ran both by hand in a scratch copy: CRLF/LF pair and no-final-newline pair give 1 record, no error; a pair differing by a trailing space is refused. Behaviour is right; only the test is missing (the doc claim of coverage is not backed in brain).

## Evidence run (scratch copy under .agents/scratch/bug197/mut, removed afterwards; source untouched)
- Targeted `go test ./internal/brain ./internal/work -run ...` on the working tree: pass.
- Mutation 1 (HEAD's export.go and records.go with the new tests): `TestUnionMergeOfSortedExports`, `TestDuplicateLines`, work `TestParseTrail` all FAIL with the old duplicate refusal (compiled, named tests failed). The union test builds its fixture with the real generator and asserts the repro precondition (2 copies) before the fix path, so it proves its condition.
- Mutation 2 (fixed code, hash/bytes comparison disabled): `TestLoadRefusals`, `TestParseTrail`, `TestLoadTakesALongValidLine`, `TestDuplicateLines`, work `TestParseTrail` FAIL, so the "differs is still refused" half is pinned. The changed existing-test inputs (export_test, readtrail_test, records_test) each trace to the behaviour change.
- No aliasing bug: `seenLine` stores a SHA-256 of the line (the `long` buffer is reused across lines); work stores a slice of the immutable input.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass; `seenLine` is used, nothing orphaned.
2. Flow tracing — pass; load (`loadLocked` inserts the deduped `recs`, stores the file's hash), ReadTrail, ParseTrail (eval, check) and work `trailAt` all share the two parsers. Finding 1 is the end-of-flow consequence (file keeps the copy until a write).
3. Standards conformance — pass with nits; describing text updated in code comments, test headers, SPEC-fyr-record (Status, ID rule, Export refusal list, Read-without-store), SPEC-fyr-work step 8, PLAN risks row (`export.go:232` is the correct line). Left standing: plan golden-path row and SKILL.md step 3/4 (finding 1). Other "duplicate ID" restatements (PLAN lines ~243, 245, 312, 693, D72; SKILL.md:85) still hold, since they concern a differing duplicate or a refusal that still exists.
4. Directory layout — pass; `union_test.go` beside `export.go`.
5. Simplicity — pass; stdlib `crypto/sha256` as a checksum, no new dependency (the brain/work duplication of the rule is the standing ADR-063 split).
6. Decoupling — pass; brain and work stay unlinked, each states the same rule locally.

## Not examined
Whole-tree `go test ./...` (told not to run it); the Phase 6 rerun itself; BUG-198; whether the full-tree `TestHarnessMap`/size pins are affected (no context/ or skills/ file is in the diff).

## Outcome

- Finding 1 — rebutted, with the text made explicit. The lead's loop (`skills/work/SKILL.md` step 7.4) commits the squash with the copy, but step 8 stores the plan with `fyr record edit <PLAN-ID> --body`, a write whose export drops the copy, before step 10 commits and pushes; the golden path's "no duplicate record ID" is read at the end of the wave. Stated in `BUG-197` § Fix (Not covered) and the plan's Edge cases row; the skill is unchanged.
- Finding 2 — fixed: `TestDuplicateLines` gained a CRLF first copy and a last copy with no final newline; it fails with the `\r` trim removed from `readRecords` (mutation run, file restored and compared).

title: Security review — BUG-197 fix, the two trail readers (2026-10-30)
body:
# Security review — bug197-duplicate-trail-lines   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: HEAD (3fa2705)..working tree, as `.agents/scratch/bug197/fix.diff` (internal/brain/export.go, export_test.go, readtrail_test.go, union_test.go [new]; internal/work/records.go, records_test.go). Blast radius followed: `internal/brain/export.go` (ReadTrail, ParseTrail, readRecords, parseLine, loadLocked, exportLocked), `internal/work/records.go` (trailAt, parseTrail, parseLine), `internal/work/fetch.go` (scope, records, added), consumers `internal/check/check.go:99`, `cmd/fyr/eval.go:215-240`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

No record can be shadowed, replaced or dropped through the change. Both readers accept a second line of an ID only when it is byte-identical to the first, after both have run the full `parseLine` validation on it. So the copy decodes to the same record, and which copy is kept makes no difference. The record-scope check in `fetch.go` compares parsed `Record` values, so it cannot be bypassed. A changed copy next to a stale one is still refused by both readers. The two readers agree on what "identical" means: brain hashes the line after `TrimRight("\r\n")`, and work compares it after splitting on `\n` and `TrimRight("\r")`. Both compare leading and trailing spaces as raw bytes, and both refuse a lone-`\r` separator as two JSON values. The only weakness is one low-severity widening on the work side. A worker branch can now carry a hand-added copy of an out-of-scope record and still pass the scope check. That tolerance is only needed at the base. Below that are two gaps in test coverage. Memory and CPU stay bounded: the 256 MiB cap and the per-line cap are unchanged, the cost is linear (one SHA-256 or one `bytes.Equal` per line), and no line bytes are kept past their buffer. Brain stores hashes only, which is correct because `ReadSlice` and `long` reuse their buffers. Work keeps subslices of a blob that is in memory anyway.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/records.go:85-91` (as called from `internal/work/fetch.go:151` for the branch tip). The tolerance is applied to the worker's branch tip as well as to the base. Before the change, a tip whose trail held a second line of an existing ID failed the run (`ReasonNoHandoff`, `trailRel` named as outside). Now a worker can hand-add a byte-identical copy of any record line, including one outside its `Files:`, and pass. Nothing is noted, because `after[id] == before[id]` and `trailRel` is exempt from the path check (`fetch.go:108`). The content does not change, so this is not a scope bypass. But the merged trail is non-canonical. If the lead's branch changed that record after the base, the merge yields `X'` next to a stale `X`. Every `fyr` verb then refuses with "renumber one of the two lines by hand", and that advice, followed literally, turns the stale copy into a phantom record. A legitimate tip should never carry a duplicate: the worker's mandatory handoff write goes through `exportLocked`, which rewrites the whole file in canonical form and so drops any copy inherited from a union base. The BUG-197 case is the base (`trailAt(root, w.p.base)`). Remediation: tolerate byte-identical copies only when reading the base, and refuse them (or at least `Note` them) on the branch tip. One way is a `parseTrail(b, allowDup bool)` parameter, set by `records()` per side. Add a test in which a tip carrying a copy of an unnamed record fails.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/records_test.go` / `internal/work/fetch_test.go`: no test pins the scope check in `fetch.go` (`records()`/`added()`) against a trail that contains duplicates. Neither a union base with a copied line nor a tip with a copied out-of-scope line is tested. The only coverage is the unit test on `parseTrail`, so the behaviour the lead actually sees is unpinned. If the finding above is rebutted rather than fixed, pin the accepted behaviour instead.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/brain/union_test.go:51-62`: `TestDuplicateLines` does not pin the CR edge for brain. The work test covers a `\r\n` line paired with a `\n` copy (`records_test.go:22`), but no brain test shows such a pair is accepted. Nor does any test show that a pair differing only inside a string, past a trailing `\r`, is refused. If someone changes the brain trim set, the two readers could drift apart without a test failing, and agreement between them is the point of the fix. Remediation: add both CR cases to `TestDuplicateLines`, mirroring the work test.

Non-security note, outside this review's lane: fix (a) covers only an unchanged line inside a union hunk. If one side edits an existing record whose line sits between the other side's new CHANGE and HANDOFF lines, union still produces `X'` next to `X`, and both readers refuse, correctly. That is the same failure as BUG-197 in another shape. A worker that edits an in-scope existing record of a kind sorting between CHANGE and HANDOFF (DEPLOY, FEEDBACK, GUIDE) will meet it.

## Checked
- Secrets: none in the diff or tests. The fixtures are synthetic records. Error messages carry only the ID and line numbers (unchanged).
- Injection / parsing: both readers still run full `parseLine` on every line, copies included, before the duplicate check, so no validation is skipped for a copy. Duplicate JSON keys (`"id"` twice) cannot split the two readers, because byte-identical input decodes deterministically. Equality is a SHA-256 match in brain (collision is negligible) and `bytes.Equal` in work. CR, leading and trailing whitespace, and long lines (brain's `long` path) are handled the same way by both. The other trail consumers (`check.go:99`, `eval.go:215/229` `findRecord` first match) see identical content whichever copy is kept.
- Authz (work record scope): `records()` compares parsed `Record` structs per ID, before against after. A copy cannot hide a changed record, because a differing second line is still refused. Handoff and change counting in `added()` sees one record per ID, the same as a clean trail. The one widening is finding 1.
- Load path: `loadLocked` stores the hash of the duplicated file as `export_sha` and inserts each ID once (no SQLite PK conflict, since the copy is skipped before the insert). The next write's `exportLocked` rewrites the file in canonical form. No new path for a "file wins" overwrite.
- DoS: the caps are unchanged (brain `maxTrail` through `capped`, `maxLine` per line; work 256 MiB `LimitReader`, `maxLine` per line). Accepting copies means a whole capped file is now parsed where the first copy used to stop it, but that is the same cost a file of distinct IDs already had.
- Crypto: `crypto/sha256` is used as a content checksum, standard-library use as designed, so it is not hand-rolling. It was already imported in `export.go`.
- Dependencies: none added (`go.mod`/`go.sum` untouched). `govulncheck ./internal/brain/... ./internal/work/...` found no vulnerabilities in called code and one in a required module that is not called (the known one per `AGENTS.md`). `npm audit` does not apply (no JS in the range).
- GCP surface: not touched.
- Tests run (targeted, per the dispatch): `go test -count=1 ./internal/work -run TestParseTrail` ok. `go test -count=1 ./internal/brain -run 'TestDuplicateLines|TestUnionMergeOfSortedExports|TestParseTrail|TestLoadRefusals|TestReadTrailRefusals'` ok. I did not use `-v`, so I did not confirm that each named test ran.
- `fyr search --refs --kind bug` (scratch home `.agents/scratch/secreview-home`): `export.go` gave BUG-197 only. `records.go` and `fetch.go` gave none.

## Not examined
- `internal/work/fetch_test.go` and the wider work test suite. I did not check whether an existing test already covers duplicates at the scope level (finding 2 assumes not, from the diff and `records_test.go`).
- `govulncheck` over the whole tree. It was scoped to the two changed packages because a whole-tree run is in progress.
- `internal/search/reconcile.go` and `internal/dream/collect.go`. Grep shows they do not parse trail lines themselves (dream only `Lstat`s the file). I did not read them in full.
- I did not run a mutation check of the new tests (must-fail state).
- I did not verify that a worker's tip is always written through `exportLocked` (the basis of finding 1's confidence: medium). I inferred it from `exportLocked`'s unconditional canonical rewrite and the mandatory handoff write.

## Outcome

- Finding 1 — rebutted. A worker's branch inherits the base's bytes until its first `fyr record` write; tolerating a copy only at the base would fail a branch over a line it never touched (a base that holds an unexported union squash). A byte-identical copy parses to the same record, so `records()`'s before/after comparison and the `Files:` scope check see the same map either way; before the fix such a branch failed `no handoff` for an unreadable trail, not as a scope signal. Both readers now apply one rule.
- Finding 2 — fixed: `TestTrailAtFailsClosed` commits a trail whose line is doubled and reads it through `trailAt` (ls-tree, cat-file, parse): one record, the guide. It fails with HEAD's `records.go` (mutation run, file restored and compared).
