Stamp (`work.go:121`, `%F-%H%M%S-<pid>`) and Name (`nameRe`) are docker-name-safe, and the label filters match exactly. `mountable` refuses `,`, `"`, control characters and relative paths, covering docker's CSV `--mount` syntax (a `=` inside a value is safe: split on the first `=`). Image and env gaps: finding 4.
- **Authz/process control:** `docker kill`/`stop` go by exact name. That name contains non-hex characters, so it can never resolve as an ID prefix of another container. The labels are set at create and cannot be changed from inside the container (no socket). Cross-run label collision needs the same second and the same pid, so it is not feasible. The client runs in its own group: timeout → kill → StopGrace → SIGKILL group; cancel → `stop -t ceil(StopGrace)` → SIGTERM (proxied to the container by the default `--sig-proxy`) → SIGKILL. Exit 125–127 or no cid → not started → `w.ran=false` → no fetch (`fetch.go:22`): fail-safe. `containersLeft` fails closed on a ps/rm error, an unreadable line, any state but exited/dead, and a container still listed after rm. It runs before the process scan and the credential scan. Hardening present: `--user` uid:gid (no supplementary groups), `--cap-drop ALL`, `no-new-privileges`, `--read-only`, `--init`, `--pull never`, no socket, no `--privileged`, no host network. Docker 29.7.2 rootful with apparmor + builtin seccomp (`docker info`). The clone is `--no-hardlinks` (`prepare.go:55`), so no inode is shared with the lead's objects. The fetch by path runs `upload-pack` on a container-written `.git`. That is pre-existing and was reviewed in Phase 2, but it is now the container boundary.
- **Crypto:** none added or hand-rolled.
- **Dependencies:** none added (stdlib only). `govulncheck ./internal/sandbox/...`: "No vulnerabilities found" (scoped to the package, not `./...`). `npm audit`: N/A, no JS in range. `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/sandbox`: ok (9.7s).
- **GCP surface:** none in range. dave is not GCE; GCE metadata reach noted in finding 8.
- `fyr search --refs <file> --kind bug --home .agents/scratch/workers` for the five changed files: 0 references each.

## Not examined
- `go test ./internal/eval` and the full `go test ./...`; `govulncheck ./...` over the whole module.
- `internal/sandbox/{guard,creds,open}.go` and `procs_linux.go` beyond the lines named; `internal/work/{drafts,records,contract,slots,preflight}.go` beyond the grep.
- `docker/work.Dockerfile` and its ignore file (reviewed in 7a, D107).
- Real docker behaviour: no container was run. The `-e NAME` client-env copy, the pflag handling of a leading-`-` image and the create-start race are from docker's documented semantics, not observed. No mutation runs: source edits were out of scope, so finding 3 is reasoned.
- The Mac/Colima path (7d).

## Outcome (main thread, 2026-10-30)

Each finding is answered in plan D109:
- the medium is fixed: only the clone and the home are mounted;
- the cid collision, the `dockerArgs` refusals, the token's `Lstat`, the check before `After`, and the sweep are fixed;
- the run-level container sweep, image-ID pinning, mountable paths before any sandbox, and `DOCKER_HOST` move to 7b-2's boxes;
- memory and CPU limits and the icc network are put to the operator;
- the token's content was accepted by D106.

Round 2 follows: `security-2026-10-30-1254.md`.

title: Security review — workers Phase 7b-1, round 2 over the fixes
body:
# Security review round 2 — workers Phase 7b-1 fixes   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: HEAD (eb15019)..working tree, the fixes only (`.agents/scratch/phase7/diff-7b1-r2.patch`; `internal/sandbox/docker.go` and `docker_test.go` as on disk), against round 1 (`security-2026-10-30-1243.md`) and D109.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The medium is closed. The container now gets `<dir>/app` and `<dir>/home` as separate bind mounts and never `<dir>` itself. `TestDockerArgs` pins the exact argv, so a mount of the worker directory would turn it red. From inside the container, `<dir>` is an empty directory on the read-only rootfs, so `err.txt` and `out.txt` cannot be reached. The split opens nothing new that I found. The new issues are two lows: the note shown when `docker ps` fails tells the operator to remove containers by the `fyr.worker` label alone, which also matches a concurrent run's worker of the same name; and `TestContainersLeftOnlyAfterARun` now passes trivially and pins nothing. One more low gap: the token check has no time-of-check/time-of-use (TOCTOU) protection, a race window between `Lstat` and docker's own resolution of the path.

## Round-1 findings, one by one

| # | Round-1 finding | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | medium: the worker directory mounted read-write, so `err.txt`/`out.txt` were rewritable | **fixed** | `docker.go:76-79`: four mounts (app, home, token, agy read-only); `TestDockerArgs` pins the argv exactly |
| 2 | low: `cid-<name>` collides with a worker directory | **fixed** | `docker.go:46`: `<name>.cid`. `nameRe` (`kickoff.go:33`) has no `.`, and the stamp directory's only other file is `pid` (`slots.go:41`), so nothing collides |
| 3 | low: the cid's location was not pinned by a test | **fixed** | `TestDockerSession` asserts `--cidfile <parent>/w1.cid` in the argv and that the path is not under `b.Dir()`. D109 reports that mutant red; I did not rerun it |
| 4a | low: an image ref read as a flag | **fixed** | `docker.go:62`: empty, leading `-`, a space or control character refused; `TestDockerArgsRefuses` covers `""`, `-v`, `--privileged`, a space and a tab |
| 4b | low: an env entry without `=` | **fixed** | `docker.go:65-69`, which also refuses an empty key; tested with `GH_TOKEN` and `=x` |
| 4c | low: the token's file type | **fixed** (TOCTOU left, see N3) | `docker.go:126-131`: `Lstat`, a regular file or `ReasonToken`, before docker runs; `TestDockerTokenNotRegular` covers the symlink case only (a directory fails the same `IsRegular`) |
| 5 | low: a container created or started after the check is orphaned; no run-level sweep | **moved** to 7b-2 | D109: remove every `fyr.work=<stamp>` container at the run's end and at `--kill`, even when the run's process is gone. Using `docker create` + `start -a` was not adopted, so the in-flight create race inside one session stays (low/medium, unchanged) |
| 6 | low: `After()` ran before the container was confirmed gone | **fixed** | `docker.go:158-160`: `containersLeft` runs inside `dockerAgy` once `waitDocker` returns, before `After`; `TestSessionListsContainers` sees `ReasonProcs` at `Session`'s return. When `ps` fails, a container may still be live while `After` runs, but it fails closed and the evidence files are now out of its reach |
| 7 | low: no memory/CPU limits | **deferred**, put to the operator | D109 |
| 8 | low: bridge network with inter-container traffic on (`enable_icc=true`) | **deferred**, put to the operator | D109 |
| 9 | low: the real token's content can be replaced by a worker | **not fixed**, accepted (D106) | D109 restates the acceptance |
| 10 | low/low: the reaped client's pgid in the sweep | **fixed** | `docker.go:154-156`: kept out of `b.pgids`; `docker.go:256-262`: the SIGTERM is skipped once `done` has fired. A window of microseconds between the check and `Kill` remains, negligible |

### 7b-2's list (D109 moved these): accepted as written
Run by image ID resolved at the version check; check the token and every sandbox path as mountable before any sandbox; refuse a `DOCKER_HOST` that is not a local unix socket; sweep containers by stamp at a run's end and at `--kill`. Round 1's other 7b-2 items still stand (runner values, image missing or at another version, `(devel)`, the agy checks).

## Do the separate mounts open anything new?

No, from what I read:
- **Symlinks inside app or home pointing at the worker directory** resolve in the container's mount namespace. There `<dir>` is an empty mountpoint parent on the read-only rootfs, so `../err.txt` gives ENOENT and is never the host file. A hard link would need a reachable source, and fails across vfsmounts with EXDEV anyway.
- **Mount sources** are resolved by docker when it creates the container. App and home are made by host code (Clone, Install, Settings) before any agent code runs, so a worker cannot redirect a source.
- **app and home are now mountpoints in the container**, so the container cannot rename them or replace them with links (EBUSY; their parent is read-only). The replacement that `Intact()` guards against can no longer come from inside the container, which is an improvement.
- **The host's reads and writes in app and home after the session** are unchanged by the split:
  - `unlink` and `removeInSandbox` go through `os.Root`;
  - `Remove` uses `RemoveAll` and a `WalkDir` chmod, neither of which follows links;
  - `countLines`/`OpenRegular` use `O_NOFOLLOW`;
  - drafts go through `os.Root`;
  - the fetch is `upload-pack` with `leadGit`'s options.

  One host-mode-era leftover: `newestLog` follows an intermediate symlink (`home/.gemini/antigravity-cli/log` → anywhere). It only reads `cli-*.log` files, and the worst it can cause is a spurious fail, so it is not a new finding.

## New findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/sandbox/docker.go:209` — when `docker ps` fails, the note says "remove label fyr.worker=<name> by hand". That label alone matches every run's worker with that Kickoff name, so an operator following it literally (`docker rm -f $(docker ps -aq --filter label=fyr.worker=<name>)`) can remove a concurrent run's live container. Remediation: name both labels (`fyr.work=<stamp>` and `fyr.worker=<name>`), or the container name `fyr-work-<stamp>-<name>`, and pin the note's text in `TestContainersLeft`'s ps-fails case.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/sandbox/docker_test.go:372` — `TestContainersLeftOnlyAfterARun` calls only `ExitChecks`, which no longer calls docker at all. It passes for any implementation and pins nothing; the "no client, no docker call" property now lives on `dockerAgy`'s early returns. Remediation: drive `Session` through an early return (the token not regular, `dockerArgs` refusing) with `ps-fail` set, and assert there is no `ps` call and no `ReasonProcs`. Or delete the test and its TDD row.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/sandbox/docker.go:126` — `Lstat` checks only the token path's last component, and only at check time. A host process (another host-mode worker, the lead's agy) can swap the file for a link before docker resolves the source, and a symlink in a parent component (`~/.gemini` itself) is followed by docker unchecked. Docker workers cannot do this: rename over a bind-mounted file fails with EBUSY. Remediation (optional): resolve with `filepath.EvalSymlinks`, require the result to equal the path, and pass that path as the source. The race window stays.

## Checked
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/sandbox ./internal/eval`: both ok (10.0s, 14.8s).
- Every `containersLeft` caller (one: `docker.go:160`); `containerRan` is gone.

body:
# Review — fyr work --runner docker (Phase 7b-2)   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: uncommitted diff /home/kesokaj/workspace/styrman-harness/.agents/scratch/phase7/diff-7b2.patch (HEAD 634e199 plus working tree), read in full; the new files read from disk; records SPEC-fyr-work, GUIDE-testing, GUIDE-fyr-matrix, PLAN-2026-10-29-workers (D108, D109) read from `fyr record get --home .agents/scratch/workers`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The worst problem: `go test .` is red. `TestFunctionLength` (funclen_test.go:52) reports `internal/work/work.go:Run is 52 lines, over 50`; the diff grew `Run` from 44 to 52 lines. That is the code-modularity rule and the repo's completion gate (AGENTS.md Setup commands), so the change cannot be committed as it stands. Beyond that, the refusal order and the fail-closed design hold up in the code I traced, and the author's mutation suite is honest (I re-ran it in a copy: 25 of 25 red, plus the two verb mutations). But the suite misses several things the docs promise: the sweep line's "only when" and "never with host" claims, and the `--image` and `--agy-linux` flags reaching `Options`. One test is environment-dependent and fails under `DOCKER_HOST=tcp://...`, and three docs claim "refused before any docker call" for the dev-build refusal, which the code does not do. Two docs restatements are stale (TDD.md:70, SPEC-fyr-work refusal-list footnote).

Verification I ran (real tree): `gofmt -l cmd internal` clean; `go vet` clean on cmd, internal/work, internal/sandbox; `go test -race ./internal/work ./internal/sandbox` ok; `go test ./cmd/fyr -run 'TestWork|TestHelp|TestVerb'` ok; `go test .` FAIL (finding 1). The full `go test ./...` was not run. Mutations were run in copies under `.agents/scratch/agents/mut` and `mut2` (not in the real tree; git status unchanged by me). Those copies can be deleted.

## Findings

- **[high / confidence: high]** `internal/work/work.go:123` (`Run`) — `Run` is now 52 lines; `go test .` fails `TestFunctionLength` ("over 50, rules/code-modularity.md item 1"). The diff added 8 lines (the sweep block, work.go:138-145 in the patch). Fix: move the block to docker.go as a small function, for example `func (o Options) sweepRun(stamp string)` that does the `Runner` check, calls `sweepContainers` and prints the line, and call it from `Run`. Then re-run `go test .`.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/work/docker.go:251-266`, `cmd/fyr/verb_work_test.go:~200`, `SPEC-fyr-work` § Interfaces (the verb-refusals test row), `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` § work (the `(devel)` row) — three places claim the dev-build refusal (16) is made "before any docker call, so on a machine with or without docker". In the code, `dockerRefusals` runs `exec.LookPath("docker")` (13) and `localDaemon()` (14, which runs `docker context inspect`) first, as the spec's own order (13-20) says. The claim is false. The cmd test (`docker from a dev build`, want `work: --runner docker`) is therefore environment-dependent. I reproduced it: `DOCKER_HOST=tcp://10.0.0.1:2375 go test ./cmd/fyr -run TestWorkVerbRefusals` fails with `work: DOCKER_HOST=tcp://10.0.0.1:2375: --runner docker needs the local daemon...`. It also reaches a real docker if one is installed. A remote `DOCKER_CONTEXT` fails it the same way. Fix: either move the version check (16) ahead of 13/14 in `dockerRefusals` and renumber or restate the order in the spec, or keep the order and drop the claim. In both cases make the cmd test not depend on the machine (an empty PATH, or assert the specific text `development build`), and assert in `TestRunDockerRefusals` the claim you keep (an empty `docker.calls` for the dev-build case, if you move it first).

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/work/work.go:138-145`, `internal/work/docker_test.go` — the sweep line's contract is stated in the spec ("never appears with `--runner host`", "only when it removed one or failed") and the host output is claimed byte-identical, but no test pins either. Mutations in a copy, all GREEN (not caught): the `o.Runner == RunnerDocker` guard replaced by `true` (a host run would then call docker and print `... error exec: docker not found` on every run on a machine without docker); the print condition `err != nil || n > 0` replaced by `true` (a zero-removed line always printed). `TestRunDockerPass` only checks the one positive case. Fix: a host-runner PASS test with the fake docker on PATH that asserts no `docker.calls` and no sweep line; a docker PASS with `docker-ps-run` empty that asserts no sweep line.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/verb_work.go:81-82`, `cmd/fyr/verb_work_test.go` — nothing tests that `--image` and `--agy-linux` reach `Options`. Mutations: dropping `Image: c.workImage` and dropping `AgyLinux: c.workAgyLinux` are both GREEN. A verb that drops `--image` silently runs the default image (the operator named another and gets no signal); a dropped `--agy-linux` silently uses the host agy. The cmd tests only cover refusals. Fix: a verb test with a fake docker on PATH and a `--image other:1` run that asserts the `image inspect ... other:1` call (the `internal/work` rig has this; the cmd rig is smaller), or at least a refusal that names the passed image (`--image x:1 --runner docker` must print the image ref in its error, which only holds if `Image` arrives).

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/docker.go:397-401` (`sweepContainers`) — it returns at the first failed `docker rm -f`, so the containers after it in the list are not attempted. The sweep exists for containers that escaped check e (running agents with the token mounted read-write); a stuck first container leaves the rest running, and the sweep line reports only one error. Fix: continue the loop, count removals, and return the joined error (`errors.Join`). Untested: the mutation "rm error ignored" is GREEN, so there is no test on the failure branch either. Add one (the fake docker has no way to fail `rm`, so a control file is needed).

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/docker.go:278`, `:261` — two checks are unpinned: dropping the agy and token entries from the mountable list (leaving only the work root) stays green, since `comma-home` covers only the root; dropping the space and control-character half of the `--image` ref test stays green (`--privileged` covers only the `-` prefix; my first mutation did not compile, the second, `unicode.IsControl(r) && false`, stayed GREEN). A comma in `--agy-linux` or the token path reaches only the per-worker `dockerArgs` refusal (a worker FAIL, not a refusal before anything is made). Fix: add cases `agy-comma` and `image-space` to `TestRunDockerRefusals`. Likewise `len(f) != 2 || f[0] != "fyr"` in `imageVersion` could be loosened to `len(f) < 2` with no test failing.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `Kill`'s guard `localDaemon() == nil` at `internal/work/slots.go:286` — removing it is GREEN (the fake endpoint is always `unix://`). The spec says a stale `--kill` with a remote daemon must not sweep. Fix: a `TestKillStaleSweeps` case with `docker-endpoint` set to `tcp://...` that asserts no `rm -f` and the plain `is stale` text.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `TDD.md:70` — the § T5 verb row still reads `fyr work [--timeout D] [--model M] [--max-workers N] [--keep] <kickoff-file>...` and says nothing of `--runner`, `--image`, `--agy-linux`, the sweep line or the stale-`--kill` sweep; README.md:125 was updated in this diff and this row was not (same subject nouns, review-standards § 7). Fix: add the three flags and one clause on docker mode and the sweep to that row.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `SPEC-fyr-work` § Interfaces, paragraph after refusal 20: "The Go comment above `dockerRefusals` says 'refusals 11-16'; the numbers here are the record's." The code comment now says "refusals 13-20 of SPEC-fyr-work, after refusal 11". The sentence is stale and describes a state that no longer exists; delete it.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/docker.go:33` (`BuildLine`) — the SPEC says "the `BuildLine` constant in `internal/work/docker.go` is this text" (the Dockerfile build line), but no test compares the two; an edit to either one drifts silently, and three refusals print the constant. Fix: a root or work test that reads the build line from the SPEC fence, or from `docker/work.Dockerfile`'s header, and compares. Low severity because the 7a pins already cover the Dockerfile itself.

## Criteria

1. Dead code — pass. No unused function or export: `RunnerHost`, `RunnerDocker`, `DefaultImage`, `BuildLine`, `Mountable` all have callers; the `sandbox.Docker.Image` comment still says "the image REF the verb checked" while work passes the ID (harmless).
2. Flow tracing — pass with findings. Traced: flags -> `Options` -> `preflight` (unknown runner after the limit and before `session`, matching SPEC refusal 12 "after 8, before 9") -> `session` skips `LookPath("agy")` in docker mode and `p.agy` stays empty (only `Session(ctx, w.p.agy, ...)` reads it; I did not read the docker branch of `Session` to confirm it ignores that argument; see Not examined) -> `dockerRefusals` (13-20, fail-closed: every error returns before `p.docker` is set, no side effect before it) -> `dockerPlan` -> `newWorker` -> `sandbox.Config.Docker` -> labels `fyr.work`/`fyr.worker` -> the run-end sweep by the same stamp. The sweep runs on the `Background` context, so SIGINT does not skip it. `Kill` validates the stamp with `stampRe` before using it as a label filter. The image is run by ID. Findings 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 are tracing and test-power gaps; the fail-closed behaviour itself (a failing check ends in a refusal, never in a fallback to the host runner) holds.
3. Standards conformance — fail (findings 1, 2, 8, 9). Go idiom is fine (errors wrapped with context, `exec.CommandContext` with a deadline, no ignored errors except the deliberate `docker("rm", "-f", c)` in the check cleanup). Docs lens: the docs that name the flags are README.md:125 (updated, correct), help text (updated, correct), SPEC-fyr-work (updated; two defects above), GUIDE-testing § 3k and GUIDE-fyr-matrix (updated; the "before any docker call" row is wrong), SDD M17/M18 (updated), TDD § T18 (updated) but TDD.md:70 (not). `skills/work/SKILL.md` does not name the flags and defers to `fyr help work`; its step 6 reads the unprefixed `work: <name>  ` line, the `work: <name>: ` notes and the `work: <name> | ` lines. The sweep line `work: the run's container sweep (label ...)` cannot match any of the three, since a Kickoff name is `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$` (kickoff.go:33), so the skill's parsing survives. The skill never tells the lead what to do with a removed-container warning (the spec calls it "worth reading"); not a finding, but a lead that reads only the three patterns will not see it. The README map is right to be unchanged: AGENTS.md rule 3 covers paths to a machine and what leaves it; docker mode adds neither (the container's agy reaches the same provider, the olive dashed line is unchanged), `TestHarnessMap` passes, and the README verb row, which changed, is not the map. Rule 6 (the delivery claim): none of the diff states what a tag delivers; the pre-existing sentence in SPEC-fyr-work § The worker image ("A release-binary place builds from a checkout or the zip of the same tag") is outside this diff and not examined.
4. Directory layout — pass. `docker.go` and `docker_test.go` sit beside `work.go` in `internal/work`; the verb stays in `cmd/fyr`; the one export in `internal/sandbox` (`Mountable`) is used by exactly the one new caller.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only (`debug/elf`, `os/exec`, `regexp`); no new dependency; no auth, crypto or session code. The image ID is a shape check, not a hash computation.
6. Decoupling — pass. `internal/work` reaches `internal/sandbox` only through exported API (`Docker`, `Mountable`, `FyrEnv`, `Printable`, `Root`); the docker refusals are in their own file; `Config.Docker` is nil on the host path. Code-modularity: new files are 224 and 259 lines; `dockerRefusals` is under 50 lines; `Run` exceeds the function limit (finding 1); `slots.go` is 303 lines, under the ceiling.

## Not examined

- A real docker daemon, a real linux agy in a container, and macOS: none are run (the record names them as Phase 7c/7d). I judged only the fake-docker behaviour.
- The docker branch of `sandbox.Box.Session` (`internal/sandbox/session.go` or wherever `Session` dispatches), to confirm it ignores the host-agy argument that `worker.go:68` passes as `w.p.agy` (empty in docker mode). The sandbox's own tests (`TestDockerSession`) pass, which is indirect evidence only.
- The full `go test ./...` (only `internal/work`, `internal/sandbox`, a `cmd/fyr` subset and the root package ran); `govulncheck`; the eval/behavioural tier (`GUIDE-testing` § 4); the `.agents/trail.jsonl` diff (3 lines) beyond its existence.
- `GUIDE-testing` § 3k and `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` beyond the docker rows (grep for the docker/runner words, not a full read); PLAN-2026-10-29-workers beyond D108 and D109 and the 7b-2 task rows.
- The sentence in SPEC-fyr-work § The worker image about where a release-binary place builds from (AGENTS.md rule 6), pre-existing and outside this diff.
- `docker/work.Dockerfile` (read only its `USER` and absence of `ENTRYPOINT`, which is what `imageVersion`'s `fyr version` needs).

## Outcome (main thread, 2026-10-30)

Every finding is answered in plan D110:
- the high: the sweep moved to `Options.sweepRun`, and `TestFunctionLength` passes;
- the mediums: the dev-build refusal is first, before any docker call, and is pinned by an empty `docker.calls`; the sweep's quiet cases and the flags reaching the run are tested;
- the lows: the sweep continues and is tested; the mountable agy and token and the image-ref characters are pinned; the `--kill` local guard is tested; TDD.md:70 is updated; the stale SPEC sentence is removed; `BuildLine` is pinned to the Dockerfile.

The suite is 37 of 37 red. Round 2 follows: `reviewer-2026-10-30-1347-r2.md`.

Every round-1 finding is fixed or partly fixed, none is open as a defect in the code. 1. High, `Run` 52 lines (`TestFunctionLength`) — **fixed.** The sweep is `Options.sweepRun(stamp)` in docker.go, `Run` calls it in one line; `go test .` passes.
2. Medium, dev-build refusal "before any docker call" — **partly fixed.** The code now checks the version first in `dockerRefusals` (docker.go, before `LookPath`), and `TestRunDockerRefusals` asserts `docker.calls` is empty for `devel` and `unknown`; mutant `devel-first` is red. It also asserts no sandbox is made.

(`imageVersion`'s `len(f) != 2 || f[0] != "fyr"` shape check is still not pinned by a named mutant in the suite; I did not re-test it; low.)

9. Low, stale "11-16" sentence in SPEC — **fixed** (sentence removed).

Low, `BuildLine` not pinned — **fixed.** `TestBuildLinePinned` compares the constant to a `# Build:` line in `docker/work.Dockerfile` (comment-only change to the Dockerfile; it is now two places that must match, but the test pins one of them; the SPEC fence is still unpinned, accepted); mutant `buildline` red.

Security's second low (the cleanup after a failed version check ignored its errors) is **fixed:** `imageVersion` joins the `ps` and `rm` errors and appends `the check's container (label ...) may be left` to the refusal; mutant `check-cleanup` red. ## New findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `SPEC-fyr-work` § Failure modes table row "a docker-mode refusal (12–20)": "refusals 16, 17 and 18 print the build line". After the renumbering the refusals that print it are 13 (dev build), 17 and 18; 16 is the image-ref refusal, which prints none (docker.go:~66). Also `SPEC-fyr-work` § The worker image: "the verb refuses a `(devel)` or `unknown` host in docker mode and names `fyr install` (refusal 16)" should say 13. Fix both numbers.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/verb_work_test.go` (`TestWorkVerbDockerFlags`) and `internal/work/docker_test.go` (`dockerRig`) — the tests do not clear `DOCKER_HOST` (nor `DOCKER_CONTEXT`), so a machine whose environment points at a remote daemon fails them; reproduced above. The tests that set `DOCKER_HOST` on purpose (`docker-host`) set it after.

If it keeps `\n`, a two-failure sweep prints more than one line, against "a run-level line". Not run; check `Printable`.

2. Flow tracing — pass. The version check now runs first; the new order of refusals 13-20 is the same in code, the docker.go header comment, TDD.md:191 and SPEC refusals; `Kill` returns a distinct message for an unswept stale stamp.

4. Directory layout — pass.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass; `errors.Join` is stdlib.

- The full `go test ./...` and `-race` on `./cmd/fyr` (only `TestWorkVerb*` were run there); `govulncheck`.
- `sandbox.Printable`'s handling of newlines (finding 4); the failing-cleanup message path of `imageVersion` has no test I could find and I did not mutate it.
- GUIDE-testing § 3k beyond grep for refusal numbers and "before any docker call"; GUIDE-fyr-matrix beyond the same grep and the new `--kill` remote-daemon row.

## Outcome (main thread, 2026-10-30)

1. Fixed. `SPEC-fyr-work` names refusals 13, 17 and 18 as the ones that print the build line, and calls the dev-build refusal 13.
2. Fixed. `dockerRig` and `TestWorkVerbDockerFlags` clear `DOCKER_HOST` and `DOCKER_CONTEXT`; the tests pass with `DOCKER_HOST=tcp://10.0.0.1:2375` set.

# Security review round 2 — workers phase 7b-2 fixes (2026-10-30) Range reviewed: 634e199..working tree (uncommitted), as `.agents/scratch/phase7/diff-7b2.patch`. This round covers only the fixes to round 1's findings (`security-2026-10-30-1318.md`), read in: `cmd/fyr/verb_work.go` (the `runWork` hunk), `internal/work/docker.go` (`localDaemon`, `imageID`, `inspectImage`, `imageVersion`, the `linuxAgy` comment), `internal/work/slots.go` (`Kill`), and the new tests in `docker_test.go` and `verb_work_test.go`. ## Status: COMPLETE ## Verdict: FINDINGS (low only) Round 1's medium is fixed. `localDaemon()` asks the docker CLI which endpoint it will use. On this machine I saw it follow `DOCKER_HOST` (`tcp://127.0.0.1:1` printed back), `DOCKER_CONTEXT`, and a `DOCKER_CONFIG` whose `currentContext` names an unknown context. That last case exits 1, so the refusal fails closed. Three low findings are fixed and one is accepted (D110). The fixes add two new low issues: a stale `--kill` skips its sweep without saying so when the daemon is not local, and the cleanup after a failed version check ignores its own errors. ## Round-1 findings 1. **[medium] The docker context bypassed the `DOCKER_HOST` check — FIXED.** `docker.go:291-303` runs `docker context inspect --format {{.Endpoints.docker.Host}}` under `FyrEnv()`, the same environment every later docker call uses. It requires `unix://`. An inspect error is a refusal, not a pass. The check is called from `dockerRefusals`, after LookPath and before the image checks, and from `Kill`. Test `remote-context` covers a `tcp://` endpoint. CLI behaviour verified read-only on dave: the default context gives `unix:///var/run/docker.sock`; with `DOCKER_HOST=tcp://127.0.0.1:1` the default context gives `tcp://127.0.0.1:1`; `DOCKER_CONTEXT=` exits 1; a `DOCKER_CONFIG` whose `currentContext` is unknown exits 1. Residual risk: a `unix://` socket that is itself forwarded to a remote host (`ssh -L`) still passes. That is the operator's own plumbing and is out of reach of any endpoint check. 2. **[low] `--image`/`--agy-linux` were ignored without `--runner docker` — FIXED.** `verb_work.go:115-125` checks `fs.Visit` for `--image` and non-empty for `--agy-linux`, and refuses with exit 2 before any sandbox. Both are tested (`image without docker`, `agy-linux without docker`). A typed `--agy-linux ""` counts as unset, which is harmless. 3. **[low] The agy was checked once and mounted at each session (TOCTOU) — ACCEPTED** as the operator's own file, in the comment at `docker.go:383-384`. That comment cites D110, and D110 does not exist yet. It must be written in the same commit, or the comment points at nothing. 4. **[low] The version-check container had no label or limit — FIXED.** `docker.go:326-338` adds `--label fyr.work.check=` and `--pids-limit 64`. On any error, including the client being killed at `dockerTimeout`, it lists containers with that label and runs `rm -f` on each, every call under a fresh timeout. Test: `TestVersionCheckCleansUp`. A pid label is unique among live processes on this host, and a leftover from a dead process with a reused pid is only a check container, so removing it is safe. 5. **[low] The image ID was not validated — FIXED.** `docker.go:307,316` requires `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$` before the ID reaches `docker run`. The test fixtures use a 64-hex ID. 6. **[info] The version is a build-arg string, `elf` checks only `e_machine`, `--image ""` falls back to the default** — unchanged, as expected. This is accepted design (plan § Which image). ## New findings - **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/slots.go:286` (diff line 754) — When `localDaemon()` refuses (a remote context, or a `context inspect` error), `Kill` skips the sweep and returns the plain "`

` is stale: no run holds it". The operator is not told that no container was looked for. A docker-mode run on a remote daemon is already refused at preflight, so containers left behind there are unlikely. The silence is still the fail-quiet shape: the same message means both "swept, none found" and "not swept". Remediation: append the reason when the sweep was skipped because of `localDaemon`, for example `; its containers were not swept: `, and add a test with a `tcp://` endpoint. - **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/docker.go:332-336` — The cleanup after a failed check discards the `ps` error and every `rm -f` error. If cleanup fails, the refusal is still returned (fail closed for the run), but a check container may be left running with nothing said. Remediation: put the cleanup's failure in the returned error, for example `…; its check container was not removed: `. ## Checked - **Fail-open review of the new code:** `localDaemon` refuses on an inspect error, on a non-`unix://` endpoint, and on an empty output (`HasPrefix("", "unix://")` is false). The `imageID` regexp is anchored. The verb's refusal runs before `trail.Roots` and every docker call. - **Injection:** the endpoint string goes to output through `sandbox.Printable` only. The label value is decimal digits only. - **Tests:** `go test -count=1 ./internal/work` ok (19.3s). `go test -count=1 -run TestWorkVerb ./cmd/fyr` ok (1.1s). - **Secrets, crypto, dependencies, GCP:** no change in the fixes. No new import except `regexp` and `flag` (stdlib). govulncheck was not re-run: the fixes add no dependency, and round 1's `./...` run stands. ## Not examined - The rest of the diff beyond the fix hunks: round 1 covered it. I did not diff round 1's patch against round 2's line by line, so a change outside the five named fixes would not have been seen. - The full `go test ./cmd/fyr` and `-race`. No real container was run: the label-removal path is exercised only by the fake `docker`. - Whether D110 exists: it does not yet, by the coordinator's own note. ## Outcome (main thread, 2026-10-30) 1. Fixed. A stale `--kill` with a daemon that is not local says `its containers were not swept: ` (`TestKillStaleRemoteDaemon`). 2. Fixed. The version check's cleanup errors join the refusal's error (`TestVersionCheckCleansUp`). D110 is written in the same commit. No third round.

title: Security review — workers Phase 7b-2, the work runner
body:
# Security review — workers phase 7b-2 (`fyr work --runner docker`)   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: 634e199..working tree (uncommitted), as `.agents/scratch/phase7/diff-7b2-code.patch`: cmd/fyr/{ctx_verbs,help_text,verb_work,verb_work_test}.go, internal/sandbox/docker.go (the `Mountable` export only), internal/work/{preflight,slots,work,worker}.go, new internal/work/docker.go and docker_test.go. Blast radius: preflight.go 1-110, slots.go `Kill`/`openRun`, work.go `Run`, sandbox/docker.go 1-100 (`dockerArgs`, `Mountable`), sandbox/env.go `FyrEnv`, sandbox/box.go:110, kickoff.go `nameRe`, cmd/fyr/verb_work.go, docker/work.Dockerfile (grep), PLAN-2026-10-29-workers § Interfaces § `--runner docker` and D109, the 7b-1 review's "What 7b-2 must refuse".

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

No high-severity problem. The worst one is that refusal 11, "the daemon is local", only reads `DOCKER_HOST`. The docker client the run calls gets `FyrEnv()`, the whole caller environment (sandbox/env.go:12-19). So a remote daemon chosen through a docker context gets past the refusal: `DOCKER_CONTEXT`, `DOCKER_CONFIG`, or `currentContext` in `~/.docker/config.json`. The plan relies on contexts on purpose ("so Colima's context and socket are found", § Interfaces). A remote one is therefore a supported path, and on it the bind sources name the remote machine's files. The rest of the fixed list from the 7b-1 review is met; it is mapped item by item under Checked. The other findings are low: fail-open UX, TOCTOU windows, and hardening.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/docker.go:181-183` — The `DOCKER_HOST` check is the only locality check. A docker context with an `ssh://` or `tcp://` endpoint passes it. The context can come from `DOCKER_CONTEXT`, from `DOCKER_CONFIG` pointing at another config, or from `docker context use`. Every later call uses the same `FyrEnv()`: the image inspect, the version check, the session's `run`, 7b-1's fail-closed `ps`/`rm` and the sweep. All of them then talk to the remote daemon. In principle the remote host mounts its own files at the clone, home and token paths, and receives the prompt, git identity and env as argv/`-e`. The host-side fetch and checks then read the local, untouched clone. That gives a FAIL in the normal case, but the refusal's stated guarantee is false. The same gap applies to `Kill`'s stale sweep (`slots.go:624`), which has no locality check at all. Remediation: resolve the endpoint the client will actually use, with `docker context inspect --format '{{.Endpoints.docker.Host}}'` under `FyrEnv()`. That honours `DOCKER_HOST`, `DOCKER_CONTEXT` and `DOCKER_CONFIG` in docker's own precedence. Require `unix://` and keep the `DOCKER_HOST` check as a fast path. Add a test with `DOCKER_CONTEXT` set to a fake context whose endpoint is `ssh://`. Run the same check before `Kill`'s sweep.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/verb_work.go:56-58` and `internal/work/preflight.go:59-63` — `--image` and `--agy-linux` are silently ignored unless `--runner docker` is given. Because `--image` defaults to `DefaultImage`, a typed `fyr work --image fyr-work:local k.md` cannot be told apart from an untyped one. That command runs every session on the host runner, without the container the operator asked for. This is a fail-open of intent, not of a check: the host runner is the approved default with its own sandbox. Remediation: in `runWork`, use `c.fs.Visit` to refuse (exit 2) an explicitly set `--image` or `--agy-linux` when the runner is not docker. Test both flags.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/docker.go:261-283` and `internal/work/worker.go:677` — The linux agy is checked once in preflight but bind-mounted by path at every session. With `--max-workers` below the file count, a session can start hours later. Between check and mount, the file, or a directory on its resolved path, can change. Examples: an agy self-update, or a deleted version directory. Docker's bind source follows symlinks, so whatever the path names at mount time is what gets mounted read-only at `/usr/local/bin/agy`. Exploiting this needs write access to the operator's own agy directory, so it is not a privilege boundary. The usual outcome is a session failure, which fails closed. Remediation (pick one): re-run `linuxAgy` per session; copy the checked binary into the run's stamp directory (mode 0555, outside every mount) and mount the copy; or record the device/inode and size at check time and compare them before each `run`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/docker.go:233-236` — The version-check container has no `--label fyr.work=…`, no `--name`, no `--pids-limit` and no `--init`. On a hang, `CommandContext` kills only the client after `dockerTimeout` (1 min). `--rm` acts only on exit, so the container stays running, unlabelled and outside every sweep. The image is the operator's own and runs with `--network none`, so the risk is a leaked process, not exposure. Remediation: add a unique `--name` (for example `fyr-work-check-<pid>-<unix nanos>`) and `--pids-limit`. On error, `docker rm -f` that name under a fresh context.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/docker.go:224-228` — The image ID from `image inspect` is checked only for being non-empty. It is then used as a positional argument in `docker run … <id> fyr version` (line 235) and as `Docker.Image`. `dockerArgs` refuses a leading `-` and whitespace for the session, but the version-check argv has no such check. The value is daemon-written, so this is a defence-in-depth gap. Remediation: require `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$`, and check `arch` against `elfMachine` there, before any use.
- **[info / confidence: high]** `internal/work/docker.go:201` and `docker/work.Dockerfile:28-29` — The version check compares a string stamped from the `FYR_VERSION` build argument. The image's fyr is built from whatever tree is the build context. An image built from a dirty or different tree with the right argument passes. The plan states this (§ Which image), so it is accepted design, and it is listed here so nobody cites the check as integrity. Two smaller points: `elf.Open` checks `e_machine` but not OS/ABI or `e_type`, and `--image ""` falls back to the default rather than being refused. Both are harmless, because the default is still inspected and version-checked.

## Checked

- **The 7b-1 review's list of what 7b-2 must refuse:**
  1. Unknown `--runner`: met (`preflight.go:59-63`, before `session`, so before any sandbox). `fyr eval` has no runner (`grep -rn Docker internal/eval` is empty).
  2. `--image` with a leading `-`, whitespace or control characters: refused (`docker.go:191`). Empty falls back to the default (info above). The tag is resolved to its ID at inspect, and the version check and the session both run by that ID (`dockerPlan.image`, test `docker-image-ran`): met.
  3. Missing image, another version, `(devel)`/`unknown`/a version with spaces: refused, and all three fail closed (`err != nil || got != o.Version`).
  4. Linux agy: missing (Abs/EvalSymlinks error or LookPath), not regular, not executable, not ELF, wrong `e_machine`, unknown arch, a path `Mountable` refuses (checked after EvalSymlinks): met.
  5. Token: `Lstat` regular, non-symlink, in `session` before `dockerRefusals` (test `token-link`), and `Mountable`: met.
  6. Work root: `Mountable`. dir/app/sb are `<root>/<stamp>/<name>/{app,home}`, with stamp matching `stampRe` (digits and `-`) and name matching `nameRe` (`[a-z0-9-]`), so the root's check covers them by construction: met.
  7. `DOCKER_HOST`: met. Docker context: not met (the medium finding).
  8. Sweep at the run's end (`work.go:653-659`, under a fresh 1-min context, while the pid lock is still held) and on stale `--kill` (`slots.go:622-629`): met. A live `--kill` relies on the run's own end-sweep, and a second `--kill` after a SIGKILL takes the stale path.
- **Sweep scope:** `label=fyr.work=<stamp>` is an exact match in docker's label filter. `Kill` validates the stamp against `^…-[0-9]{1,7}$` before the path or filter is built. The stamp holds a second plus a pid, so another run's containers cannot share it. A stale stamp needs a pid file under the same `--home`. Removal is by the ID that `ps` printed. No too-wide match was found.
- **Secrets:** none in code, tests or the diff. Docker stderr and the `fyr version` output reach errors only through `sandbox.Printable` or `%q`.
- **Injection:** every docker call is argv, with no shell. The ref, the stamp and the label values are validated or follow their flag. `Mountable` is applied to agy, the token and the work root. The `fyr version` output is compared for exact equality and never interpreted. The inspect output is split once on a space, and arch is looked up in a two-entry map.
- **Authz/authn:** no new trust boundary beyond 7b-1's container. The version-check container has `--user` uid:gid, `--cap-drop ALL`, `no-new-privileges`, `--network none`, `--read-only`, `--pull never`, no mounts and no `-e`. The Dockerfile has no ENTRYPOINT, so `fyr version` is the command.
- **Crypto:** none added. Nothing hand-rolled.
- **Dependencies:** none added (`debug/elf` is stdlib). `govulncheck ./...` (Go 1.27.3): "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities". There is 1 vulnerability in a required module that the code does not call (the known one). `npm audit`: N/A, no JS in range.
- **GCP surface:** none in range.
- **Tests:** `go test -count=1 ./internal/work`: ok (18.8s).
- **`fyr search --refs <file> --kind bug --home .agents/scratch/workers`** for all nine changed files: 0 bugs, except `cmd/fyr/ctx_verbs.go`, which names BUG-193 (a verification-process bug, not relevant to this surface).

## Not examined

- `go test ./cmd/fyr` and `-race`: not run (budget). `cmd/fyr/verb_work_test.go` was read in the patch only.
- Real docker behaviour: no container, build or pull was run. These are from docker's documented semantics, not observed: the precedence among context, `DOCKER_HOST` and `DOCKER_CONTEXT`; `docker run sha256:<id>` resolving as an ID; label filters matching exactly; bind sources following symlinks at mount time. This machine's context is `default`, at `unix:///var/run/docker.sock` (`docker context ls`).
- No mutation run: source edits were out of scope, so the findings are reasoned and no failing test was shown.
- `slots.go` beyond `Kill` and `openRun`'s open line; `internal/sandbox/{after,session,guard,creds}.go` (reviewed in 7b-1); the `SPEC-fyr-work` doc text.
- The Mac/Colima path (7d).

## Outcome (main thread, 2026-10-30)

- The medium is fixed: `localDaemon()` checks `DOCKER_HOST` and the docker context's endpoint.
- The lows: `--image` or `--agy-linux` without docker is refused; the version-check container is labelled, limited and removed on failure; the image ID's shape is checked; the agy check-then-mount window is accepted (D110).
- The info item is already stated in the plan.

Round 2 follows: `security-2026-10-30-1326-r2.md`.

title: Cold read — workers Phase 8, a model per worker
body:
# Review — workers plan, Phase 8 cold read   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: `.agents/scratch/p8/plan.md` (body of PLAN-2026-10-29-workers), Phase 8 parts only: § Interfaces § A model per worker, Phases 8/8a/8b, D103, D113-D117 and the Rejected rows citing them, the Failure-modes, Trust-boundaries and Risks lines naming Phase 8 or `agy models`. Checked against internal/work/*.go, internal/sandbox/session.go and env.go, cmd/fyr/verb_work.go, help_text.go, the three skills, SPEC-fyr-work, GUIDE-eval, PRD R8/R10, ADR-076, and a real `agy models` run on dave (agy 1.4.11).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES (design needs revision; implementation not ready: 1 BLOCKING question)

The plan's core is sound and its code claims mostly check out (agy models prints `<id>\t<name>` on stdout, spinner on stderr, exit 0, 13 lines, verified here; session.go:66 is agyArgs; the Files: parser is the right precedent). The worst problems: (1) the `work` skill has no text for a refused `fyr work` (exit 2), and Phase 8 makes a whole-wave refusal routine (typo, offline, login lapse); 8b's skill edits do not say what the lead does (BLOCKING). (2) 8b claims "3 of 3 PASS" covers the changed skills, but no row observes the feature skill's `model:` line, the `-r2` carry-over, or the chain from plan line to the verb. (3) ADR-080 is to "amend ADR-076, whose `--model` was one model per run", but ADR-076 never mentions `--model` or `--effort`. (4) D115 and D116 are the implementer's, not the operator's, and D115 narrows an existing flag.

## Findings (gaps, Q1/Q2)

- **[BLOCKING / high]** `skills/work/SKILL.md:72-77` and plan "Phase 8b" box 1 — the skill has no rule for exit 2 (the only "refus" in the skill is :72, about a dirty tree). Phase 8 adds the first refusal a lead can hit routinely: a `model:` line with a typo or an ID agy dropped, `agy models` failing offline or without a login. The whole wave is refused with nothing made (plan Failure modes :412). Two implementers would write different step 5/6 text (stop the loop; block that phase and rerun the rest; drop the Model: line). Decide it in a D-row and put it in 8b box 1, plus a test or note for it.
- **[gap / high]** plan :627 (8b box 1) — "step 7.6 keeps it on `-r2`". `skills/work/SKILL.md` has three `-r2` paths: :86 (7.6, merge/test failure), :89 (a worker question), :92 (a FAIL). The plan's own rule is "a `-r2` re-dispatch keeps the phase's line" (:365). Name all three, or say "every `-r2`".
- **[gap / high]** plan :628-629 (8b boxes 2-3) — the coverage claim "3 of 3 PASS" for feature, handoff and `work-kickoff-model` overstates. The existing `feature` row's check (GUIDE-eval) never looks for a `model:` line; the `handoff` row exercises the by-hand Kickoff, which gets no Model: line; `work-kickoff-model` stops before `fyr work` and never runs `-r2`. Not covered: the feature skill's `model:` sentence, `-r2` keeping the line, the lead's copy feeding the verb end to end. Name them in the box and in the `testing` record (AGENTS.md: claims of coverage name what is not covered), or add the check to the feature row (a change to an existing row, which D-Rejected rules out, so name the gap instead).
- **[gap / medium]** plan :618 (8a box 1) and :1188 (D113 item 6) — "amends ADR-076, whose `--model` was one model per run". `fyr record get ADR-076` holds no `--model` and no `--effort`; the `--model` decision is D26 and SPEC-fyr-work. Restate what ADR-080 amends (D26, SPEC-fyr-work § The verb) and what it only extends in ADR-076 (the one network-visible act of `fyr work`).
- **[gap / medium]** plan :1196-1197 (D115, D116) — both `by: implementer`. D115 refuses `--model "a b"` and any ID outside `modelRe`, which the verb accepted before; D116 decides R8 (a Must item, immutable) needs no edit although R8 says no verb sends anything and three things leave, "which only the operator's own session starts". Per the D45 precedent, ask the operator for both, or cite the D113 item that approves them (items 3-4 do not mention `--model`'s pattern; D116 follows from item 2 only as an opinion).
- **[gap / medium]** plan :623 (8a box 6) — the verify clause does not say two runs. One `fyr work` with both Kickoffs cannot give "first PASS" and "second refused": refusal 21 refuses the whole run, so the first never starts. Also "nothing made under `~/sandbox/fyr-work/home/.config/fyr/work/`" is false after the PASS run (a stamp directory and a pid file were made there). Say: the refused run first on an empty work root, or compare listings before and after; the PASS run separately.
- **[gap / medium]** plan :620 (8a box 3) — existing tests break and the plan does not say how: `internal/work/run_test.go:168-177` (`TestRunModelAndKeep`, `o.Model = "gemini-x"`) now triggers refusal 21 against a fake agy that has no `models` branch. As written the fake would run its whole session body for `agy models` (commit, record add) in the caller's cwd. Decide the fake's default `models` output (list `gemini-x` and the test IDs), and that the `models` branch exits before `printf ... > $CTL/args` (the plan has this) and before every git command. `internal/work/preflight_test.go:74` (`--mode=auto`, expects "--model") still matches the new message but should be pinned to `not a model ID`.
- **[gap / medium]** plan :379 — `agy models` has no `cmd.Dir`. Left unset it runs in the lead's cwd (in tests, the package directory), where agy may read workspace config; set it to a neutral directory (fyr's home or `os.TempDir()`), and say so. Also unbounded: stderr is read for "its last stderr line" with no cap (cap it); `CommandContext` kills only agy, so a child agy forked would outlive the deadline (accepted or process group, decide).
- **[gap / low]** plan :396 (D116) — "carries no prompt and no project content" is asserted, not checked. Running `agy models` here on dave wrote `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/log/cli-*.log`, `cache/onboarding.json` and `conversation_summaries.db-wal/-shm`. These are outside check c's watched paths (`.gemini/config`, `settings.json`; `guard.go:146`), so no false "real config changed" FAIL for a run in flight: checked. State the real-home writes in `SPEC-fyr-work` § Data, and add the check of the request's content (agy's log or a proxy) to 8a's integration box, or name it "not checked".
- **[gap / low]** plan :365 — the plan-level `model:` line has no syntax beyond "beside `files:`": exact prefix, one per phase, what the lead copies when the line carries a note (`model: x  (cheap)`), what a second line means. The Kickoff side is exact (`modelRe`), so a "verbatim" copy of a noted line makes a whole-wave refusal (see BLOCKING). Say "the value after `model:`, trimmed" and that the planner writes nothing else on the line.
- **[gap / low]** plan :369-372 — `modelRe` is stricter than the authority the plan names ("the list below is the authority"): an ID with `/` or `:` would be refused offline. Fine for the 13 IDs seen; say where it is widened (one constant) so the next release does not need a design pass. A fix-up `-r2` Kickoff that quotes test output beginning `Model:` at column 0 makes `2 Model: lines` and refuses the wave; the same exposure as `Files:` (D16), and the skill's quoting rule (`skills/work/SKILL.md:86`) should indent quoted output.
- **[gap / low]** plan :623 (8a box 6), :629 (8b box 3) — fixtures `~/sandbox/fyr-work/fixture`, `~/sandbox/fyr-work/home`, `~/sandbox/fyr-eval/{home,fixture}` are assumed present; no first task checks them (Risks lists only the `agy models` assumption). Add them to Risks with the check.
- **[gap / low]** plan :628 — the new row's grant is undecided (wide vs named). `TestSuiteHarness` (internal/eval/suite_test.go:128-132) pins `{agent, wide}` per row; the other `work`/`handoff` rows are wide. Name it, and why (a named grant list is the safer default; the row writes files and runs `fyr record get` only).
- **[gap / low]** plan :378, :623 — docker-mode runs that name a model now need a host `agy` on PATH; the plan accepts it. `dockerRig` (docker_test.go:65-82) takes the host agy off PATH; the box's "with docker and a host agy, the check runs" needs the rename-back that `TestRunSweepQuiet` (:299-300) does; say so.
- **[gap / low]** citations: `internal/work/docker.go:233` for `FyrEnv()` is :237 today. The plan's own Failure-modes lead line :400 says "Refusals 1-10"; refusals 11-21 exist.
- **[gap / low]** Verification (§ :438-446) holds no Phase 8 yes/no criterion; the 8a/8b boxes name implementation choices (`modelsTimeout`, 64 KiB). Add one yes/no E2E: "a model named on a plan phase reaches that worker's agy argv, and a model agy does not list stops the run before any sandbox", independent of how it is built.

## Q2 — Scope

Not named by D103: (a) `--model` itself now needs the network and a login (D113 item 4, operator-approved: in scope); (b) `modelRe` on `--model` (D115, implementer, no operator word: gap above); (c) the `model default` field on every line, including a never-started worker (D113 item 5, operator-approved); (d) `modelsTimeout` as a variable, `WaitDelay`, the 64 KiB cap: hardening for tests, no extra surface. No extra endpoint, flag or second shape found. Rejected rows cite D103/D113 correctly.

## Q3 — Questions to ask the author

1. What does the lead do on a refused wave (exit 2) from the model check or a bad `model:`? **BLOCKING** (two skill texts possible).
2. Which `-r2` paths keep `Model:`: all three of the skill's? NON-BLOCKING (the plan's rule says all).
3. What does ADR-080 amend, given ADR-076 holds no `--model`? NON-BLOCKING.
4. Does the operator approve D115 and D116 as written? NON-BLOCKING (D115 narrows a flag; D116 reads R8).
5. Two runs or one in the real-worker box, and how is "nothing made" measured? NON-BLOCKING (a reasonable implementer runs two).
6. Default `models` output of the fake agy; `cmd.Dir` and stderr cap of the call? NON-BLOCKING.
7. Grant of `work-kickoff-model`: wide or named? NON-BLOCKING.
8. Plan-level `model:` line syntax and noted values? NON-BLOCKING.

## Q4 — Sizing

8a: finishable and verifiable from the plan alone (one new file, one parser, one field, docs list is long but mechanical; the docs list spans SPEC, README, GUIDE-fyr-matrix, TDD, SDD, GUIDE-testing and help text, which is the heaviest part; if it runs long, the docs box is the one to hand to `documentation`). 8b: could not finish its first box without question 1 (the refusal text) and would overclaim in its third box (finding on coverage). Fix both and it is one session.

## Q5 — Parallelism

None, by D117: 8b needs 8a's SPEC, and 8b's `after: Phase 8a` is present. 8a's boxes share `internal/work/kickoff.go`, `preflight.go` and the contract tests, so they stay serial. Phase 7d (the Mac) shares no file with Phase 8 but waits on the operator (D112); no `after:` is missing. `PRD.md` items touched: R8 and R10 are cited (D113 item 2, D116); no other item is touched.

## Criteria (the six lenses, applied to the plan text)

1. Dead code — pass: nothing orphaned; refusal 11's old `strings.HasPrefix(o.Model, "-")` branch (preflight.go:90) is replaced, not kept beside the pattern.
2. Flow tracing — fail (minor): `Kickoff.Model` to `prepared.k` to `newWorker` (`worker.go:51`, `Config.Model: o.Model` must become the worker's model) to `agyArgs` to `Result.Model` to `line()` traces; `session()` has only `o`, so refusal 21 (needs every Kickoff) is a new step in `preflight` after `p.session`, not in `session()`: the plan does not say so. The `-r2` paths and the refusal path at the lead are not traced (findings).
3. Standards conformance — fail: coverage claim in 8b; ADR-076 misdescription; D115/D116 by implementer on an immutable PRD item. Restatement grep on `--model` found plan :79, :117, :147, :837 (history, unchanged) and SPEC-fyr-work flag table; the docs list covers the SPEC, README:125, help text.
4. Directory layout — pass: `internal/work/models.go` beside `docker.go`; no new directory.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass: stdlib `os/exec`, no new dependency, no auth or crypto handled; cache and `--effort` rejected.
6. Decoupling — pass: the check lives in its own file in `internal/work`, `sandbox.Config.Model` is unchanged; the one coupling is `FyrEnv` from sandbox, already used by docker.go.

## Not examined

Not run: the unit and integration steps (nothing built). Not read: `fyr work` Interfaces text of the plan outside Phase 8 (read only to match lines :79, :117, :147), D-rows other than D26, D103, D113-D117, `GUIDE-fyr-matrix`, `TDD.md` T18, `SDD.md` M18, `GUIDE-testing` § 3k (named by 8a's docs box; not opened), `internal/work/run_test.go` beyond lines 160-180, `skills/feature/SKILL.md` outside :56-104. title: Review round 2 — workers Phase 8a fixes
body:
# Review — phase 8a round 2, the fixes   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: the fixes since round 1, in the live tree: internal/work/models.go, preflight.go, work.go, rig_test.go, models_test.go, plus records SPEC-fyr-work (refusal 21, Verification), GUIDE-testing 3k model bullet. Interdiff .agents/scratch/p8a/round2-interdiff.txt used as a map only.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE

Every fix is correct and every named test fails without its fix. `go vet` and `go test -race ./internal/work` pass, and so does the root `TestFunctionLength`. I found no defect introduced by a fix. The two security rebuttals hold.

## Mutations
Method: five scratch copies of models.go, each applied through `go test -overlay`, so the tree was untouched. The target text was unique (asserted in the script). Each mutant compiled, and a named test failed.
- A: the deadline derived from `context.Background()` instead of the run. `TestRunModelCheckEnds` FAILS (30 s: the call outlives the run's end).
- B: post-call group kill removed. `TestRunModelCheckOnlyWhenNamed` FAILS (the `models-helper` child survives).
- C: `sandbox.FyrEnv()` instead of `rootEnv()`. `TestRunModelRefusals` FAILS (the PWD assertion).
- D: lastLine's carriage-return clause removed. `TestRunModelRefusals` FAILS (the `call-fails` case).
- E: the `run.Err()` case removed from the switch. `TestRunModelCheckEnds` FAILS (the error text).
Not mutated: the dirty-tree ordering case and the `models-bigerr` stderr-drop case (read, not run red; both are straightforward asserts).

## Findings
None blocking. Notes, not findings:
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/models.go` post-call `syscall.Kill(-pid, SIGKILL)` after the leader is reaped. The kernel keeps the pgid reserved while any member lives, so it cannot hit a reused ID unless the group is empty AND the pid has wrapped AND the new process became a group leader inside microseconds. If the group is empty, the call is ESRCH. Not worth a change.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `TestRunModelCheckOnlyWhenNamed` polls `kill(pid,0)` for the helper. In a container whose PID 1 does not reap orphans, the killed `sleep` stays a zombie and the poll would time out. This is an environment flake, not a product defect.

## Checks on the named concerns
- Group kill ordering: Cancel and the post-call kill both skip a nil Process, and a start failure is handled. Correct.
- PWD is read on linux only: that is the test (guarded by `runtime.GOOS == "linux"`). `rootEnv` itself is portable. The other new tests use only `syscall.Kill` and are portable.
- Error switch order: `stdout.full`, then `run.Err()`, then `DeadlineExceeded`. The run's own deadline lands in `run.Err()` before the local one, which is right. A call that succeeded in the instant the run ended is refused, which is harmless because the run is ending anyway.
- Context flow: `Run` passes ctx to `preflight`, `checkModels` and `listModels`, and `listModels` derives its deadline from it. `parseAll` keeps refusal 3's order, and the model check stays last.
- Records: SPEC refusal 21 (PWD=/, no OLDPWD, group kill after the call, stderr past the cap dropped, the CR rule, the "run ended" message), the Verification list and the Options.Model comment all match the code.

## Security rebuttals
1. agy's stderr line in the refusal: ACCEPTED. It is printed only on the operator's terminal through `sandbox.Printable`, like `docker()`, and it is agy's own text about the operator's own login.
2. Full verb environment to agy: ACCEPTED. agy needs its login and config, it is the same environment as every other host call, and PWD and OLDPWD are now scrubbed. The agy binary comes from the operator's PATH, the same trust as the sessions.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass.
2. Flow tracing — pass: ctx, group lifetime and error ordering traced above.
3. Standards conformance — pass: the restatements (SPEC, GUIDE-testing, Options comment) agree with the code.
4. Directory layout — pass.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass: stdlib only, no crypto or auth.
6. Decoupling — pass: models.go is self-contained, with one seam, `checkModels(ctx, o, ks)`.

## Not examined
Full `go test ./...` outside internal/work and the root TestFunctionLength; the plan and ADR-080 text beyond item 6 (not re-read); the dirty-tree and models-bigerr mutations (not run).
