# Review — p8a-work-models   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: uncommitted change in /home/kesokaj/workspace/styrman-harness, `.agents/scratch/p8a/review.diff` (code, tests, README/SDD/TDD, SPEC-fyr-work, GUIDE-fyr-matrix, GUIDE-testing, ADR-080) read against the live tree.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

One real defect: the new `agy models` call cannot be cancelled by the operator. Everything else is low severity (a stale doc-comment, two untested branches, one transient `fyr check` finding). Verified by running: gofmt/vet clean; `go test -race -run 'Model|Block|Refusals|ParseKickoff' ./internal/work` ok; `go test ./cmd/fyr -run 'Help|Work|Usage|Verb'` ok; root `TestFunctionLength`/areas pins ok (untracked models.go counted). The process control is sound: Setpgid + Cancel kill of the group + WaitDelay, null stdin, cwd `/`, 64 KiB caps that end the child's pipe (the over-cap test returns in about 1s), error text carries exit/timeout/last stderr line. Mutation in a scratch copy (.agents/scratch/p8a/mut): removing Setpgid/Cancel makes `TestRunModelRefusals/timed-out` fail (5.3s > 3s); so the group kill is pinned.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/work/models.go:70`, `internal/work/preflight.go:28`, `internal/work/work.go:122` — the model check is not cancellable. `listModels` uses `context.Background()` and `preflight` takes no ctx, but the verb has already installed `signal.NotifyContext` for SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGQUIT (`cmd/fyr/verb_work.go:91`), so those signals no longer terminate fyr; the child sits in its own process group (`Setpgid`), so a terminal Ctrl-C does not reach it either. Scenario: agy hangs on the network, the operator hits Ctrl-C, and nothing happens for up to 60s + 5s WaitDelay; the run then proceeds into `dispatch`, prints a stamp line and fails every worker `killed`. No stamp existed during the wait, so `--kill` cannot help. Before this change preflight was offline and instant, so the "signals fail each worker killed" contract had no such window. Fix: pass Run's ctx into `preflight`/`checkModels`/`listModels` as the parent of the deadline context (Cancel already kills the group), return a refusal when ctx ends, and add a test with a cancelled ctx plus `models-sleep`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/work.go:33` — `Options.Model` still reads `// agy --model; "" passes none`; SPEC-fyr-work's copy of the struct was updated to "for a worker whose Kickoff has no Model: line" in this change, the code comment was not (describing-text rule). Fix: reword the comment to match.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/models.go:131-133` (`lastLine`'s carriage-return clause) and `models.go:116-118` (stderr cap, `over == nil` branch) — no test fails without them. Mutation in the scratch copy: deleting the CR clause leaves `TestRunModelRefusals` green; making stderr overflow return an error also leaves it green. The fake's `models-exit` case prints `spinner\n<err>` with no `\r`, and no case floods stderr. SPEC-fyr-work § Refusal 21 states both behaviours ("past any carriage return", "stderr capped at 64 KiB"). Fix: print `spinner\r<err>` in the fake and flood stderr in one case (exit 1, assert the message and the elapsed time), or drop the claim. Note the authors already name `WaitDelay` as unpinned; these two are not named.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `SPEC-fyr-work:362` — `fyr check` (run here with `--home .agents/scratch/workers`) reports "path `models.go`: no tracked file is named models.go", because `internal/work/models.go` is untracked at review time. It should clear once the file is staged and committed; re-run `fyr check` after `git add` and before the checkpoint commit. The other five findings (`docker/references/*`, three stale specs) are not from this change.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** ordering claim, SPEC-fyr-work § Failure modes and refusal 21 ("made once, after every offline refusal") — pinned only for refusal 11 (`model-flag`, whose message differs if the check ran first); no test shows that a docker refusal (13-20) or refusals 9/10 with a named model make no `agy models` call. The code is correct by construction (`checkModels` is the last statement of `preflight`); the claim of coverage "each before anything is made" is wider than the tests. Optional: assert `modelCalls()==0` in `TestRunDockerRefusals` for a Kickoff with `Model:`.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. `prefixed` is used by both parsers; `capped`, `lastLine`, `errModelsOver` all used; no leftovers.
2. Flow tracing — fail on one point: ctx does not reach the new call (finding 1). Otherwise Kickoff `Model:` -> `newWorker` -> `sandbox.Config.Model` -> `--model` and `Result.Model` -> result line is traced and tested (`TestRunModelPerWorker`, override of `--model` per worker); unstarted workers keep `Model` (`unstarted` reuses `w.res`). Error text and fail-closed behaviour are right; the pipe-cap stops the child (verified by timing).
3. Standards conformance — pass with nits. Docs lens: README row, SDD M18, TDD verb row + T18 Interfaces/Errors, help text, verb flag text, SPEC (flags, struct, Kickoff file, refusals 3/11/21, step 4, contract, compatibility, data, failure modes, verification table), GUIDE-fyr-matrix, GUIDE-testing and ADR-080 agree with the code (regex, caps, timeout, cwd, tab parse, order, result-line shape, error strings checked one by one). Restatement grep (`restatement-grep.sh` over "not a flag", "refusals 1", "starts with", "Model:", "every worker", "Files: line", plus `agy exit` and `--model`) found no other living copy made false; `skills/work/SKILL.md:77` reads the unprefixed result line and its verdict, which the new field does not move (SPEC says the skill's text is 8b). Stale: `work.go:33` (finding 2). The `help work` text dropped the docker mount/build-line sentences to make room; the flag table still points to SPEC for the build line.
4. Directory layout — pass. `models.go` and `models_test.go` beside `preflight.go`; no new package.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only; no auth/crypto. The `capped` writer is small and justified by the pipe-cap requirement.
6. Decoupling — pass. One new seam (`checkModels(o, ks)`), called once from `preflight`; the sandbox gets only the resolved model string.

Code shape: models.go 134 lines, longest function (`checkModels`) about 45, `TestFunctionLength` passes.

## Not examined
- A real `agy models` run (format "id<TAB>name", the claims about files it writes under `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/`, and that the request carries no project content): the diff itself names the last as not checked; I did not call the network. I did confirm `watched` in `internal/sandbox/guard.go:149` excludes the log/cache paths the SPEC names.
- The 12-mutation claim: I re-ran 3 (group kill, CR clause, stderr cap), not the others.
- The brain-store records were read as diff only (not re-read from the store); `.agents/trail.jsonl`'s 7-line change is consistent in count with one new and three changed records, content not diffed.
- The full `go test ./...` (only the packages and patterns above), the Mac/darwin build, `--runner docker` against a real daemon.

## Outcome

1. **Fixed.** `preflight(ctx, …)` → `checkModels(ctx, …)` → `listModels(run, …)`: the deadline's context derives from the run's, so the verb's caught signal kills the group at once; error `the run ended before it answered`. Test `TestRunModelCheckEnds` (cancelled run, a 30 s sleeping fake, refused in under 3 s, nothing made); red when the deadline derives from `context.Background()` again.
2. **Fixed.** `work.go`'s `Options.Model` comment names the new rule. `lastLine`'s carriage-return clause is pinned by `call-fails` (stderr `⠋ loading\rnot logged in` → `not logged in`), red without the clause; the stderr cap's "dropped, not refused" by `models-bigerr` (200 000 bytes of stderr, the run passes) in `TestRunModelCheckOnlyWhenNamed`, red when stderr refuses past the cap.
3. **Fixed / answered.** "After every offline refusal": `TestRunModelCheckOnlyWhenNamed` now runs a named model on a dirty tree (refusal 2): refused with 0 `agy models` calls; red when the check runs before `leadClean`. `fyr check` is re-run after staging (the checkpoint).
Also fixed outside the findings: `TestFunctionLength` (root package) failed on `preflight` at 52 lines; the parse loop is `parseAll`.

title: Security review — workers Phase 8a, a model per worker
body:
# Security review — p8a-model-per-worker   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: HEAD (8cc1783)..working tree, as `.agents/scratch/p8a/review.diff` (978 lines: README, SDD, TDD, cmd/fyr/help_text.go, cmd/fyr/verb_work.go, internal/work/{contract,kickoff,preflight,work,worker,models}.go and their tests, records SPEC-fyr-work, GUIDE-fyr-matrix, GUIDE-testing, ADR-080)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Nothing high. The new input surface is tight. The `Model:` value and `--model` are both held to `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`. Go's `$` without `(?m)` is end-of-text, the value is trimmed first, and it reaches agy as a separate argv element after `--model` on the host and after the image in `docker run`, never through a shell. Every refusal line goes out through `search.Printable`. The worst problem is in the new `agy models` subprocess. `cmd.Dir = "/"` keeps it away from the project, but `cmd.Env = sandbox.FyrEnv()` is an explicit Env, and with an explicit Env `os/exec` does not rewrite `PWD`. The child therefore inherits `PWD` (and `OLDPWD`) pointing at the lead's checkout. The test checks the fake's `pwd`, and bash's builtin resets an inherited `PWD` that does not match the real cwd, so it cannot see this. The other findings are low: Ctrl-C is held off for up to a minute during the check; the subprocess gets the operator's whole environment; any process it leaves behind is not reaped; agy's stderr goes into the refusal without redaction; and ADR-080 states as fact a "no project content" claim that the SPEC marks unverified.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/models.go:497-498` (`cmd.Dir = "/"`, `cmd.Env = sandbox.FyrEnv()`). The design intent (D125, SPEC refusal 21: "the call runs in `/`") is to keep `agy models` away from the project. But `os/exec` sets `PWD` to `Dir` only when `Env == nil` (GOROOT `src/os/exec/exec.go:1222-1237`, go.dev/issue/50599). `FyrEnv()` (`internal/sandbox/env.go:12`) copies `os.Environ()`, so the child gets `PWD=<lead checkout>`, the directory `fyr work` must be run from (`verb_work.go` `trail.Roots(wd)`), plus `OLDPWD`. This is certain. What agy does with it is not known. Many CLIs resolve their workspace as `$PWD || cwd` to keep symlinked paths. If agy does, it could load project-level settings (for example MCP servers started at launch) or attach workspace metadata or content to the list request. That would undo both the "runs in /" isolation and ADR-080 item 6's "no project content". The test cannot catch it: `rig_test.go:364` records bash's `pwd`, which ignores an inherited `PWD` that does not match the cwd. Remediation: drop `PWD`/`OLDPWD` from the env and append `PWD=/`. Pin it in the fake by writing `$PWD` (not `pwd`) to `models-cwd`, and check the test fails without the fix.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/models.go:494` (`context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), …)`) and `internal/work/preflight.go:311`. The verb traps SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGQUIT into `signal.NotifyContext` (`cmd/fyr/verb_work.go` `workRun`), but `preflight` takes no ctx. The child runs in its own process group, so the terminal's SIGINT does not reach it either. During the check, Ctrl-C does nothing for up to `modelsTimeout` (1m) plus `WaitDelay` (5s). An operator who escalates to `kill -9` on fyr leaves `agy models` orphaned with no deadline, running with the real HOME. Nothing is made and the context is checked after preflight, so the effect is availability and a stray process, not a bypass. Remediation: pass `Run`'s ctx into `checkModels` and derive the timeout from it, so a trapped signal kills the group at once.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/work/models.go:496-516`. A process that `agy models` leaves behind is never reaped. `Cancel` (the group SIGKILL) runs only when the deadline hits. On a normal exit, a helper still in the group (agy wrote `conversation_summaries.db-wal`/`-shm`, per SPEC § Data, which hints at more than a list print) keeps running under the real HOME. If it holds stdout, it is cut loose after `WaitDelay`. Unlike the worker sessions (check e, `processes left`), this call has no process check. Remediation: after `Run`, send `syscall.Kill(-pid, SIGKILL)` to the group unconditionally (ESRCH when empty). Note that a helper that calls `setsid` escapes any group kill, so say so in the SPEC rather than imply it is covered.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/work/models.go:511-514`. When the call fails, agy's last stderr line is put into the refusal verbatim. `search.Printable` neutralises control and format characters, but nothing redacts. An auth failure that echoes a token, a signed URL or an account identifier gets printed, and it lands in the lead session's transcript, which goes to the model. Remediation: pass the line through `internal/redact` before it joins the error, or print only the exit status and point to agy's log.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/models.go:498`. `agy models` gets the operator's full environment minus `GIT_*`, `FYR_REPO` and `FYR_CHILD`: cloud credentials, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, any `*_API_KEY`. The worker session gets `agyEnv`'s allowlist (`internal/sandbox/env.go:24`). This is the operator's own CLI with no model in the loop, so the exposure equals typing `agy` by hand, which is why the severity is low. But nothing needs that breadth. Remediation (operator's call): an allowlist of PATH, HOME, LANG, TERM, USER, LOGNAME, proxy variables and `PWD=/`, which also closes finding 1.
- **[low / confidence: high] (docs claim)** `record/ADR-080` Decision 6 (review.diff:977) says the call goes out "with no prompt and no project content (D116)" and on that basis concludes R8, the README map and `SPEC-fyr-delivery` are unchanged. `SPEC-fyr-work` § Data (review.diff:871) and § Trust boundaries (review.diff:888) say "That it carries no project content was not observed: not checked." Given finding 1, the unverified version is the honest one. Remediation: make ADR-080 item 6 conditional ("assumed, not observed"), or observe the request (for example agy's own log at debug level) before the claim is made, so rule 1's "three things leave the machine" is not resting on an assumption.

## Checked
- **Secrets:** no credential, token or key in the diff. The token path is unchanged. The stderr-to-refusal path is finding 4.
- **Injection:** `Model:` is parsed at column 0 only, at most one line, trimmed, with the regex anchored at end-of-text (verified: Go RE2 `$` without `(?m)`). It refuses a leading `-`, spaces, control characters and over 64 characters, and is held offline before any call. `--model` gets the same check (`preflight.go:323`). The value reaches agy as a discrete argv element (`internal/sandbox/session.go:66-72`) and in docker mode after the image (`internal/sandbox/docker.go:86`). No `sh -c` is on this path; `Box.Bash` is eval's only. The value is used in no path or label. IDs read from agy are only looked up in a map, never executed. Refusal text, including the up-to-64-KiB ID list and the Kickoff path, is printed through `search.Printable` (`verb_work.go` `workRefuse`). Result-line `Model` comes only from the two validated sources.
- **Process control:** `exec.LookPath` refuses relative PATH entries (ErrDot). stdin is the null device. `Setpgid` is set, and `Cancel` kills the group on deadline. `WaitDelay` is 5s. stdout is capped at 64 KiB with a returned error, which closes the pipe and fails closed (`stdout.full` is checked first); stderr is capped and the rest dropped. There is no data race: Run waits for the copy goroutines. The real agy cannot be reached from the tests (`dockerRig` strips every PATH directory holding `agy`; HOME is the rig's temp dir). Gaps: findings 1-3.
- **Authz/authn:** the Kickoff is lead-written. It can pick any model `agy models` lists, which is by design (ADR-080); the list is the authority and fails closed. The Kickoff is read once into memory and that same `Kickoff` value feeds both the check and the worker, so there is no TOCTOU.
- **Crypto:** none touched. Nothing hand-rolled.
- **Dependencies:** `go.mod` and `go.sum` are unchanged (stdlib plus the existing `modernc.org/sqlite`). `govulncheck ./...`: "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities"; 1 in a required module, not called (a known one, per DEPLOY-local).
- **GCP surface:** none touched. The new egress is one authenticated `agy models` request to the CLI's provider (finding 6). Under the real home it writes agy's log, cache and summaries files, none under check c's watched paths (`internal/sandbox/guard.go:149`: StateDir, OldStateDir, `.gemini/config`, `.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json`), so it should not false-trip a concurrent run's check c.
- **Past bugs:** `fyr search --refs <path> --kind bug --home .agents/scratch/workers` returned 0 references for models.go, kickoff.go, preflight.go, worker.go, contract.go, verb_work.go and sandbox/session.go.

## Not examined
- A real `agy models` run: what it sends, whether it reads `$PWD`, whether it spawns helpers. Not observed (no network capture). This is the open question behind findings 1, 3 and 6.
- The Mac (darwin) path for `--runner docker` with a host agy.
- `internal/sandbox/docker.go` beyond the argv append (unchanged, reviewed in Phase 7).
- The rest of `SPEC-fyr-work` outside the diff hunks. Trust boundaries were read only as far as the diff shows them.
- `npm audit`: no JavaScript ecosystem in this change.

## Outcome

1. **Fixed.** `rootEnv()` drops `PWD` and `OLDPWD` from the verb's environment and adds `PWD=/`. Pinned on linux: the fake reads its initial environment from `/proc/$$/environ` (bash rewrites `$PWD` itself) and every `TestRunModelRefusals` case wants `PWD=/` alone; red with `sandbox.FyrEnv()`.
2. **Fixed.** The run's context reaches the call (the reviewer's finding 1): `TestRunModelCheckEnds`.
3. **Fixed (docs).** ADR-080 item 6 now says "given no prompt and no project file … by design, not observed (D122)".
Lows: **a leftover helper — fixed**: the group is SIGKILLed after every call; `models-helper` (a background `sleep 30` with its output closed) must be gone within 2 s, red without the kill. **agy's stderr in the refusal — rebutted**: the line goes only to the operator's terminal, through `sandbox.Printable`, as `docker()`'s stderr does (`internal/work/docker.go`); it is agy's own text about the operator's own login. **The full environment — rebutted**: it is the verb's environment, as every other host call of the verb (`docker()`, D125); agy needs its config and login, and `FYR_REPO`/`FYR_CHILD` and the git variables are already removed by `FyrEnv`.

title: Review round 2 — workers Phase 8b fixes
body:
# Review — workers Phase 8b round 2 (fixes over round 1)   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: ab6879b..68f55d2 as captured in .agents/scratch/p8b-round2.patch (skills/handoff/SKILL.md, skills/work/SKILL.md, GUIDE-eval row `work-kickoff-model`, SPEC-fyr-work line 252). Commit 68f55d2 also adds a `testing` record (Eval 3 of 3 PASS at ab6879b) to the trail; the working tree adds one more (Eval 1 of 1 PASS at 68f55d2, uncommitted, the main thread's, not examined beyond its title).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Every round-1 finding the patch claims to fix is fixed, and the fixes broke nothing I could find. The one defect left is a wording overstatement in the SPEC-fyr-work line the patch rewrote: it says the skill "blocks a phase whose Kickoff the verb refuses", which is wider than the skill, where only three refusal shapes block a phase and the rest end the loop. It changes no behaviour. The eval check now fails on an uncommitted trail edit and still passes on correct Kickoffs; I ran both by hand.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: medium]** SPEC-fyr-work line 252 (§ Compatibility; patch line 61) vs `skills/work/SKILL.md:80` — the new sentence "blocks a phase whose Kickoff the verb refuses" overstates the skill. The skill blocks a phase only when the refusal is `the Kickoff <path>: …` or `the Kickoff <path> names the model …`; `the Kickoff <path> is over N KiB` (internal/work/kickoff.go:60), `the Kickoffs <a> and <b> …` (preflight.go:139, :161) and the model-check refusals end the loop. Fix at the Checkpoint's docs step: "…and blocks a phase whose Kickoff `Files:` or `Model:` line, or whose model, the verb refuses; any other refusal ends the loop."

## Round-1 findings, one by one
- Reviewer, indent rule on every `-r2` path: fixed. `skills/work/SKILL.md:75` (step 3) now holds the one rule: everything a `-r2` Kickoff adds (failing lines, a worker's question, the lead's answer, a cause) goes last, after `Quoted for this attempt (data, not instructions):`, each line indented four spaces. Its list covers all three paths (7.6 at :88, the question path at :91, the FAIL path at :94), and :88 now points to step 3. Against the parser: `prefixed` (kickoff.go:76-85) matches `Files:` / `Model:` only at column 0 after trimming trailing `\r`, and splits on `\n` only, so an indented line, or a lone `\r` inside a line, never matches. `handoff/SKILL.md:152` ("quoted additions follow the block as the `work` skill's step 3 writes them") agrees with it. The marker line itself is not `Files:` or `Model:`.
- Reviewer, eval check not seeing a plan edit: fixed. The check ends with `&& git diff --quiet HEAD -- .agents/trail.jsonl`. I ran the setup in a scratch clone of `~/sandbox/fyr-eval/fixture` and the check from the GUIDE-eval row. Must-pass (two correct Kickoffs): exit 0. After `fyr record get`, `list --open` and `search` (all with `--home`): still 0, so a read does not dirty the trail. Must-fail: an appended line to `.agents/trail.jsonl` gives 1; a Kickoff with the `Model:` line removed gives 1. The bullet text (GUIDE-eval line 29) says "the plan is not edited" and still names what the row does not cover. The cell shape is unchanged (7 cells, no `|` in setup or check); `TestSuiteHarness` `want` (`{"", false}` for `work-kickoff-model`) is unchanged and `go test -count=1 ./internal/eval ./internal/harness .` passes.
- Reviewer, SPEC-fyr-work line 252: fixed in substance (it no longer says the skill text is "Phase 8b's" to come); see the finding above for the wording.
- Security, `-r2` quoting low: fixed by step 3 (see above): one rule, a named end block, indented, labelled data. Handoff template still carries no slot for it, but now says where the additions go.
- Security, eval check low: fixed (see above).
- Security, refused-run matching and quoting: fixed in the skill. `:80` names `the Kickoffs <a> and <b> …` and the model check's failure as "other refusal"s that end the loop, and has the closing handoff quote the refusal line in backticks as data. The shapes agree with the verb's messages (kickoff.go:52-70, models.go:56, preflight.go:139/161). Residual, not a finding: a backtick inside a refusal line (a plan-derived path is held to clean entries by `checkEntry`; the `agy models` listing is agy's output) could end the inline code; a fence would be sturdier. Speculative, so left out.
- Security, `--model` flag: fixed. `:75` adds "runs `fyr work` with no `--model`". Step 5 passes none; `feature/SKILL.md:80`'s "the run's `--model`, else agy's default" describes the verb and does not contradict it. No other living file says the lead may pass `--model` (grep over skills/, context/, agents/, README.md).

## Whole-file reads at HEAD (nothing broken by the fixes)
- `skills/work/SKILL.md`: step numbers and cross-references hold (step 3 → step 7 paths; step 6 → refusal rules; step 11 "blocked phase with its reason" still fits a quoted refusal line). The phrase "step 6" at :52 (blocked: verb refused) and :42 still resolves. Resume section unchanged.
- `skills/handoff/SKILL.md`: the worker-mode block still carries `Model:` right after `Files:` (what the row's awk adjacency check expects); the by-hand Kickoff template (lines 131-136) has no `Model:` line, as :141 says. Worker-mode paragraph unchanged.
- GUIDE-eval row against `internal/eval/suite.go`: header `id | setup | prompt | prompt2 | check | agent | grants` (suite.go:34, 42) matches the 7 cells; grant `named`; id matches `validID`.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass: nothing added that nothing uses; the old 7.6 indent sentence was replaced, not left beside the new rule.
2. Flow tracing — pass: step 3 rule → all three `-r2` paths in step 7 → Kickoff file → `prefixed`/`filesLine`/`modelLine`; refused-run branches traced to the verb's messages; the eval check can fail (ran must-pass and two must-fail by hand).
3. Standards conformance — pass with the SPEC wording nit above; restatement grep over the quoting rule and the `--model` rule found no other living copy (the plan record's D120 wording is decision history). Listing-budget and lint tests pass.
4. Directory layout — pass: no new files.
5. Simplicity — pass: text only; no code, no dependency, no security primitive.
6. Decoupling — pass: the lead still composes only; the verb alone decides what is a valid `Files:`/`Model:`.

## Not examined

No third round (review Steps 4–5: at most two); the one-sentence edit was read against `skills/work/SKILL.md` step 6 by the main thread.

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing is broken. The skill text agrees with what `fyr work` does: the `Model:` line is read at column 0, at most one per Kickoff, trimmed, held to `modelRe` (internal/work/kickoff.go:35-40, 87-99); refusal 21 is last, per Kickoff in file order, then `--model` (internal/work/models.go:29-62); the two per-Kickoff message shapes the work skill quotes are the real ones (kickoff.go:52-67, models.go:56). Two low-severity gaps are below; neither is a stated-requirement violation.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/work/SKILL.md:88` (loop step 7.6) vs `:90-91` and `:94` (the question-answer path and the FAIL path) — the "no quoted line starts with `Files:` or `Model:`" rule (D120) is written only for the merge/test-failure fix-up. The other two `-r2` paths also put derived text in a Kickoff ("with the answer in its Kickoff"; "unless the result line names a cause the lead can answer"). A line in such text that starts at column 0 with `Files:` or `Model:` makes the file carry two such lines; the verb refuses it (`2 Model: lines; give one`, kickoff.go:83-86) and, under the new step-6 rule, the phase is then BLOCKED, with no way out since the lead may not edit a `Model:` line. Fix: state the four-space-indent rule once, at the point every `-r2` Kickoff is composed (step 3 or step 4: "any text quoted or added to a Kickoff is indented so no line starts with `Files:` or `Model:`"), and let 7.6 point to it. Not a bug in today's text as long as the lead quotes only command output, hence low.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/eval` row `work-kickoff-model` (GUIDE-eval, last column of the row; check cell) — the check does not enforce two of the prompt's own prohibitions: "do not edit the plan" (an uncommitted `fyr record edit` rewrites `.agents/trail.jsonl`; the check looks only at `git log -1` and branches) and "no `fyr work`" beyond the absence of `work/*` branches (a refused `fyr work` leaves none). It cannot pass on a wrong Kickoff (see below), so the row's stated claim (the two Kickoff files) holds; but its description in the record ("nothing is committed or branched") reads as covering an unedited plan too. Fix, if wanted: append `&& git diff --quiet HEAD -- .agents/trail.jsonl` to the check (first confirm in a scratch clone that a read-only `fyr record get` leaves it clean) and say so in the bullet. Low because the plan edit would be a skill violation the row was not written to detect.

## Verified, no finding
- Docs lens, skill text against code:
  - `skills/work/SKILL.md:80` ("a refused run exits 2, prints one `work: <reason>` line and no result line, made nothing") = SPEC-fyr-work lines 44, 266-268. "`the Kickoff <path>: …`" = refusal 3's prefix; "`the Kickoff <path> names the model …`" = models.go:56. `the model check: agy models: …`, `agy models listed no model`, `--model X: …` are correctly left to "any other refusal".
  - `skills/feature/SKILL.md:80` ("checked by `fyr work` before anything is made; left out, the run's `--model`, else agy's default") = SPEC lines 32, 93, 121. `model: <ID>` with nothing else on it is D126; the `Model:` value is trimmed by the verb as the skill says.
  - `skills/handoff/SKILL.md:141,152,157`: the by-hand Kickoff template (lines 131-136) has no `Model:` line, as the new rule says; the worker-mode block carries it right after `Files:`, which is what the row's awk check expects.
  - Result-line change (`model <ID>|default`) does not touch what step 6 reads (the unprefixed `work: <name>  ` line and verdict), as SPEC line 252 says.
- Restatements: `bash skills/review/scripts/restatement-grep.sh` over `files:` line, `Files:` line, worker-mode, Kickoff, plus a grep for `Files:|files:` across context/, agents/, rules/, skills/*/SKILL.md. No living restatement of the Kickoff fields or the refusal handling is left unchanged. README.md:125, SDD.md:49, TDD.md:70/186 and `fyr help work` already carry the `Model:` line (Phase 8a). The cold-read prompt (feature skill line 99, item 5) names `files:` only for disjointness and needs no `model:`. Pre-existing text that is now slightly dated, not a finding: SPEC-fyr-work line 252 says "the skill's own text is Phase 8b's" (this change makes it so; reword at the Checkpoint's docs step).
- GUIDE-eval row, run by hand in a scratch clone of `~/sandbox/fyr-eval/fixture` (.agents/scratch/p8b-rev/): setup exit 0, one commit `trail: the greet-models plan`, the plan loads in the store (`fyr record get PLAN-2026-10-29-greet-models`). Check: must-pass 0 with two correctly composed Kickoffs; must-fail (exit 1) for a wrong model, a missing `Model:`, two `Model:` lines, a Phase 1 Kickoff present, and `Model:` not on the line after `Files:`; restored copy 0 again. The cell columns are `| id | setup | prompt | prompt2 | check | agent | grants |` as `ParseSuite` expects (suite.go:42); no `|` in the setup or check cells; the grant is `named` (D128) and `TestSuiteHarness` `want` carries `{"", false}` for it. `go test ./internal/eval ./internal/harness .` passes.

The refused-run rule and the `-r2` rule therefore have no behavioural run; the plan's 8b box 3 must say so in its `testing` record.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass: nothing left behind; no orphaned text (the placeholder lines in the handoff block are used by the lead).
2. Flow tracing — pass: skill step 3 -> Kickoff file -> `ParseKickoff`/`modelLine` -> `checkModels` -> result line traced; the three `-r2` paths and the refused-run branch traced to the verb's messages (see the first finding for the one gap). The row's check can fail (mutations above).

## Not examined

Run both after the eval ends.
- The ADR-080 body, plan §Interfaces § A model per worker and 8a's code beyond kickoff.go/models.go (8a is out of this range).

Covered by text only: no row runs a `-r2` path (D130).

Validated both ways: exit 0 on the real run's kept clone (`~/sandbox/fyr-eval/home/.config/fyr/eval/2026-10-30-152459/work-kickoff-model/app`, whose lead ran `fyr record get` and left the trail clean), exit 1 on a scratch clone with a line appended to the trail, exit 0 again once restored.

title: Security review — workers Phase 8b: the model: line in the skills, the work-kickoff-model row
body:
# Security review — workers Phase 8b, model: lines in skills + eval row   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: ea7cfd7..working tree (uncommitted; `.agents/scratch/p8b-diff.patch`, 113 lines: skills/feature, skills/handoff, skills/work SKILL.md, internal/eval/suite_test.go, GUIDE-eval body)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

No high-severity problem. The parser holds: `fyr work` reads `Files:` and `Model:` only at column 0 (`internal/work/kickoff.go:77-85`), refuses a second line of either (`kickoff.go:94-95`, `:110-111`), checks each model ID against `modelRe` (`kickoff.go:40`, so no leading `-`, space or control character), and passes it to agy as one argv element (`internal/sandbox/session.go:70`) only after `agy models` lists it, failing closed (`internal/work/models.go:29-63`). The worst problem is in the skill text. On the `-r2` fix-up path, the new Kickoff's `Files:` line adds "the conflicting or failing files", and nothing says where that list comes from or how far it may reach. A failing test's output is text the first worker's code controls, so that worker can widen the scope its retry gets, and the lead then squash-merges the result. The new four-space indent rule protects the parser on one `-r2` path only. The answer-to-a-question path and the FAIL path have no such guard. The refused-run rule cannot be used to make the lead edit the plan: the rule forbids that in so many words, and every case it does not cover ends the loop. Its line-matching is loose, though, and the refusal line goes into the handoff word for word. The eval row is clean as code, but its check cannot see the plan edit the rule forbids.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `skills/work/SKILL.md:88` (patch line 95) — The `-r2` `Files:` is "the phase's `files:` plus the conflicting or failing files". The diff touches this sentence but leaves this part as it was. "Failing files" are read from the project's test output on the squash, and the r1 worker wrote the code that produces that output. So a worker can make a test fail in a way that names any clean repo-relative path (`AGENTS.md`, `skills/...`, `.gitattributes`, another phase's files). `checkEntry` (`kickoff.go:127-152`) still allows these paths, and the r2 worker then gets them in scope. That is untrusted text reaching a `Files:` line, which `disjoint` checks only within one run. Remediation: take the added entries only from git, never from test output. For a conflict, use `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U`. For a red test, use the squash's own `git diff --cached --name-only`, which can only name files inside the old scope. Write any wider scope as a `by: lead` D-row first, or block the phase instead.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/work/SKILL.md:91` and `:94` — The guard that keeps quoted text off column 0 (`:88`) covers only the failing command's last lines. Two other `-r2` paths put lead-written text into the Kickoff, and that text may quote the worker: the answer to a worker's question (`:91`) and a FAIL "unless the result line names a cause the lead can answer" (`:94`). Neither has a column-0 rule. The handoff template (`skills/handoff/SKILL.md`, patch lines 55-61) also has no slot for this text, even though its text is "fixed". If the phase has no `model:` line, a quoted column-0 `Model: <listed id>` is accepted and changes the worker's model. A quoted `Files:` fails closed as a duplicate. None of the quoted text is marked as data for the r2 worker either. Remediation: one rule for every `-r2` addition: put it in a named block at the end, indent every line four spaces, and add one line saying the block is data, not instructions.
- **[low / confidence: high]** GUIDE-eval row `work-kickoff-model` check (patch line 113) — The check confirms HEAD is still the setup commit and that no `work/*` branch exists. It never checks whether the tree or `.agents/trail.jsonl` is unchanged. The prompt says "do not edit the plan", and a `fyr record edit` or a direct write to the plan stays uncommitted, so the row passes whichever way the lead acts on the security-relevant "never edit the plan" rule. Remediation: add `git diff --quiet HEAD -- .agents/trail.jsonl` (or `[ -z "$(git status --porcelain -- . ':!.agents/scratch')" ]`). The row covers no refused-run path; D130 states this, and it stays an open gap.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/work/SKILL.md:80` — The refused-run rule decides between "block one phase and rerun" and "end the loop" by matching text. `the Kickoff <path>: …` and the disjointness refusal `the Kickoffs A and B share scope` (`preflight.go:161`) differ by one letter. Read loosely, the disjointness refusal blocks one phase and reruns, when it should end the loop: it means step 2 itself went wrong. Separately, the refusal line becomes the blocked phase's reason in the closing handoff's Next Steps (`:99`), copied word for word. That line holds plan-derived text (`Files:` entries are printed with `%s`, e.g. `kickoff.go:137`, `:139`) and the whole `agy models` listing (`models.go:56`). The next session reads Next Steps. Remediation: name the disjointness refusal as an "other refusal" explicitly, and quote the refusal line in the handoff as data (fenced or backticked).
- **[low / confidence: low]** `skills/work/SKILL.md:75` — "The lead never chooses, changes or adds a model" does not mention the run's `--model` flag. A phase with no `model:` line falls back to that flag (`internal/work/worker.go:46-49`), so a lead could still choose that phase's model through the flag. Remediation: say step 5 passes no `--model` unless the plan names one.
- **[low / confidence: low, outside the diff]** `skills/work/SKILL.md:96` — Step 9 stores each merged worker's drafts with "the kind and title its draft names". The only kind excluded is `adr`. A worker draft that names `plan` or `handoff` can therefore put plan-shaped text (`files:` / `model:` lines) or Kickoff-shaped text into the store through the lead. Remediation: allow `bug` and `change` drafts only (whatever the Kickoff's Never line allows), and treat any other kind as a closed-set item.

## Checked

- Secrets: none in the diff. The eval row's model IDs are names, not credentials. The setup uses only fixture git identities (`row.go:155-159`).
- Injection: the parser is column-0 and fails closed on duplicates and malformed IDs. The model ID reaches agy as argv, not through a shell, and `modelRe` rules out a flag. The eval setup is `set -e`; `python3 -I` with the record built in Python and dumped as JSON; the path passed quoted as argv; an append to the clone's own trail; `git add`/`commit` in the clone (`session.go:148-150`, cwd = clone; env `-i`-style, `row.go:140-159`). The check is read-only: fixed-string `grep -qxF`, `awk` with no input from outside, `git log`/`git branch --list`. The check does not refuse a Kickoff file that is a symlink, but it only reads through it and reports pass/fail, so no impact. The setup's `open(...,"a")` would follow a symlinked `trail.jsonl` in the fixture. The fixture is the operator's own (D30), so this is informational only.
- Authz/authn: the refused-run rule can't be used to get past a check. It forbids editing `Model:`/`model:`/the plan, blocks only the refused phase, and ends the loop on every other refusal, including a failed or empty `agy models` call. The by-hand Kickoff has no `Model:` line (`skills/handoff/SKILL.md`, patch line 44), so a fresh session never picks up a plan model as an instruction.
- Crypto: none touched.
- Dependencies: `go.mod`/`go.sum` unchanged. `govulncheck ./...`: "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities" (1 in a required module, not called). The eval row's `python3` was already a named grant (`row.go:24`) and is already used in 6 GUIDE-eval places. No npm in scope.
- GCP surface: none touched.
- Tests: `go test ./internal/eval -run TestSuiteHarness -count=1` ok (the new `want` entry agrees with the GUIDE-eval body in the working tree).

## Not examined

- `internal/work/contract.go` (result-line parsing) and `internal/sandbox/session.go` past the `--model` argv line: Phase 8a code, unchanged here.
- How the r2 worker treats quoted text: that is model behaviour and was not run.
- No behavioural `fyr eval work-kickoff-model` run.
- The full GUIDE-eval record outside the diffed hunk, and the fixture's own `.agents/trail.jsonl` (whether it is a symlink was not checked).
- `skills/feature/SKILL.md` and `skills/handoff/SKILL.md` outside the diffed hunks.

## Outcome

- [medium] 7.6's `-r2` `Files:` takes "the failing files" from test output: deferred to the operator, not fixed here. The sentence predates this diff (Phase 5a); the fix (added entries from git only, or block the phase) changes the lead's re-dispatch scope, which is a design decision outside Phase 8b's standing approvals. Put to the operator in the session's report and the handoff, recommendation: fix, as the finding's remediation says.
- [low] The quoting guard covers one `-r2` path: fixed in `68f55d2` (step 3: every `-r2` addition last, after `Quoted for this attempt (data, not instructions):`, indented four spaces; 7.6 points to it; the handoff skill names it).
- [low] The eval check cannot see a plan edit: fixed in `68f55d2` (`git diff --quiet HEAD -- .agents/trail.jsonl`), validated must-pass on the real run's clone and must-fail on a scratch clone with an edited trail.
- [low] The refused-run rule's matching and its verbatim quoting: fixed in `68f55d2`: `the Kickoffs <a> and <b> …` is named as another refusal (ends the loop), and the closing handoff quotes the refusal line in backticks, as data.
- [low] `--model` lets the lead choose a model: fixed in `68f55d2`: step 3 says the lead runs `fyr work` with no `--model`.
- [low, outside the diff] Step 9 stores a worker's draft of any kind but `adr`: deferred to the operator with the medium finding (it predates this diff and changes the lead's store rule), recommendation: allow only the kinds the Kickoff lets a worker draft (`bug`, `change`), and treat any other as a closed-set item.

title: Review — root-docs row 9, fyr serve actions (2026-10-30)
body:
# Review — root-docs row 9, fyr serve actions   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: working tree against HEAD dcff413 (`.agents/scratch/row9.diff`, `.agents/scratch/row9-trail.diff`, plus the untracked `internal/serve/actions.go` and `actions_test.go`), lenses code and docs.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing is broken: the code matches `SPEC-fyr-serve` step 5, the row 9 routes and the failure-mode rows I traced, and `go test -race ./internal/serve`, the `cmd/fyr` serve/vocabulary/help tests, `TestFunctionLength*` and gofmt/vet pass. One real gap: the spec's order guarantee (D52: CSRF, then no-project, then the lock, so a refused request learns nothing about a running action) is stated in the spec and the plan's "12 of 12 mutants caught" evidence, but no test pins it. I moved the `TryLock` block to the top of `act` in a scratch copy (outside the repo, deleted afterwards); it compiled and every `internal/serve` test still passed. A request without the CSRF token would then get 409 and reveal a running action, with a green suite.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/serve/actions.go:35-47`, `internal/serve/actions_test.go:112-150` (TestActionBusy), `internal/serve/pages_test.go` (TestNoProject) — the order step 5, then the no-project line, then the lock is the spec's D52 reading (`SPEC-fyr-serve` § Routes — row 9, last paragraph) and a security-flavoured claim (a 403-class request must not learn that an action runs). No test sends a bad-CSRF POST while an action blocks (expect 403, not 409), and none sends an index POST outside a checkout while one blocks (expect the no-project 200, not 409). Mutation evidence: lock moved above `csrfOK` compiled and all `./internal/serve` tests passed. Fix: in TestActionBusy, while the first action blocks, POST `/actions/index` with no/wrong `csrf` and assert 403 `forbidden`; add the no-project variant to TestNoProject or a busy no-project case. Because GUIDE-testing § 3 now lists the one-action lock as mutation-checked, that wording and the plan's "12 of 12" cover removal of the lock, not its position; narrow the claim or add the test.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `.agents/trail.jsonl` (GUIDE-testing, PLAN row 9 evidence) — "Mutation check: 12 of 12 mutants of `actions.go` caught" is cited without the list of mutants, so a reader cannot see that the order mutant was or was not among them. Name the mutants in the plan evidence (the order mutant evidently was not).

## Checked and sound (evidence, not findings)
- `csrfOK`: token query refused; `mime.ParseMediaType` with charset allowed; `Origin` must be a single header equal to `http://`+host; `MaxBytesReader` at 4 KiB; `PostForm` only (never the query). Each refusal case in TestActionCSRF can fail: the 5 KiB body would pass without the cap (Go's own limit is 10 MiB), the query-only csrf would pass with `FormValue`, the second Origin would pass without the `len != 1` check.
- `capped`: exactly 1 MiB is not truncated, over is, later writes are dropped without error; the action stays `ok`. Covered by the three sizes in TestActionOutputCapped.
- `cmd/fyr`: `Index` is `search.Index` with `{Dir: wd, Home: home}`, the same options `runSearch` builds for a bare `fyr index` (no register, global or rebuild). `ingestInto` keeps the old ingest sequence (open, ingest, summary line) and `metricsIngest` still exits 1 on failed sources; TestServeActions covers both the verb and the closure with a real corrupt source.
- Docs and restatements: README row, TDD verb table, T16 interfaces/errors/test table, help page, SDD M16 row (already said "two maintenance actions") and the spec's rows all say "read-only" no longer for `serve`. The remaining "read-only" hits in README/TDD are `fyr check`. `grep` for "row 9" left only code comments naming the row (`serve.go:44`, `actions.go:13`) and TDD T16; these are historical labels, not stale claims. Older handoff/change records say "read-only pages" about row 8 and are correct for their date.
- Sizes: no file over 600 lines (largest touched: `pages_test.go` 269, `guard_test.go` 281); `TestFunctionLength*` pass with the untracked `actions.go` read.

## Criteria

title: Security review — root-docs row 9, fyr serve actions (2026-10-30)
body:
# Security review — fyr serve row 9 actions   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: HEAD (dcff413)..working tree — `.agents/scratch/row9.diff` plus the untracked `internal/serve/actions.go` and `internal/serve/actions_test.go`; blast radius read: all of `internal/serve/*.go` non-test production files touched (actions, guard, routes, serve, pages, view, layout.html, dreamlog's printableText), `cmd/fyr/verb_serve.go`, `cmd/fyr/verb_metrics.go`, the CLI's `fyr index` path (`verb_search_memory.go`, `verb_index_register.go`), `search.Options`/`search.Index`, `search.printable`, `metrics.Options`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Nothing at medium or above. Row 9 does what `SPEC-fyr-serve` § Every request step 5 and § Routes row 9 say, in the spec's order (CSRF, then no-project, then the lock). The CSRF check refuses a `token` query on a POST, any media type except `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (parsed with `mime.ParseMediaType`), a `csrf` field that appears only in the query, an `Origin` of `null`, a foreign one or a repeated one, and a body over 4 KiB. It runs after the guard's Host, `Sec-Fetch-Site` and cookie checks. A same-site or rebinding page has three things in its way: it does not know `P`, so it cannot address the route; it does not know `C`; and its `Origin` and `Sec-Fetch-Site` are refused. The actions take no input from the request: `act` passes only `Options` to the closure. The closures in `cmd/fyr` build `search.Options{Dir, Home}` and `metrics.Options{Home}` with every flag field left at its zero value, so `--register`, `--global`, `--rebuild`, `--source`, `--label` and `--outcome` cannot be reached, and neither can any other verb. Both actions run in-process (no subprocess, no shell). Their output is capped at 1 MiB, passes through `search.Printable` line by line (C0, C1, DEL, the Cf/Zl/Zp classes and ignorables become `?`), and is HTML-escaped by `html/template` inside a `<pre>`. Neither action page carries `C`. The worst issue is availability only and was already there in row 8 (finding 1). The other two are test gaps and a small hardening inconsistency.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/serve/serve.go:150` (`MaxHeaderBytes: 64 << 10`) with `internal/serve/guard.go` (row 8, but row 9's actions sit behind it): cookie tossing can deny service. Browsers do not separate cookies by port. A page on another `127.0.0.1` port (same-site) can set many large `Path=/` cookies for `127.0.0.1` (Chrome allows about 180 × 4 KiB per host). Every request to `fyr serve`, including the action POSTs, then carries a `Cookie` header over 64 KiB and gets `431` until the operator clears the cookies. Nothing can be read and nothing runs, but the console cannot be used. This is not in the spec's "Accepted residual". Remediation: add it to `SPEC-fyr-serve` § Every request "Accepted residual", naming the recovery (clear 127.0.0.1 cookies, or use a fresh browser profile). Raising `MaxHeaderBytes` only moves the threshold and costs memory per connection; I do not recommend it.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/serve/actions_test.go:46-104` (test gap):
  - `TestActionCSRF` sends every refusal case to `/actions/index` only, so nothing shows that `/actions/metrics-ingest` is refused the same way. The code path is shared (`act`), so the risk is regression only.
  - No action POST carries `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site` or `cross-site`. Only GET exercises step 2 (`TestRefusals`).
  - No action test pushes `<`, `&`, ESC or a multibyte rune cut at the 1 MiB boundary through the action page. `TestBodyEscaped` covers read pages, not `act`'s `Pre` and `failed:` lines.

  Remediation: add a `metrics-ingest` refusal row and two `Sec-Fetch-Site` rows (asserting the step-2 line and zero calls). Make one fake action write `<script>\x1b[2J` and fail with an error holding the same, then assert both are escaped.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/serve/actions.go:77`: `req.PostForm.Get("csrf")` takes the first of several `csrf` fields, so `csrf=C&csrf=junk` passes. Step 3 refuses a repeated `token` outright ("exactly one value"). This cannot be exploited without `C`. It is hardening, for the same rule on both tokens. Remediation: require `len(req.PostForm["csrf"]) == 1` and add a test row. That means a spec edit to step 5 and to § Failure modes first.

## Checked
- **Secrets:** no credential-shaped strings in the diff (grep for key, token and private-key shapes). `T`, `C` and `P` are drawn at runtime by `crypto/rand` and never logged. `logf` writes the path without the prefix or query. `C` appears only on `/` and `/metrics` (`TestPages`), never on an action's response page or `/metrics/report`.
- **Injection:**
  - No command, SQL or path input reaches the actions: the request is never passed to `fn`.
  - The `Href` in a form is `r.base + const`. Template values are escaped by `html/template`. Output goes through `printableText`, then `search.Printable`.
  - A query with `;` makes `Query().Has("token")` miss the pair, but a POST still needs the cookie and `C`, so it changes nothing.
- **Authz/authn:**
  - Order verified in code: guard (Host, Sec-Fetch-Site, then token or cookie; a token exchange only on GET/HEAD) → route (405 `Allow: POST` for other methods) → `csrfOK` → no-project → `TryLock`.
  - `PostForm` reads only the body. `MaxBytesReader` is applied before `ParseForm`.
  - `Origin` passes only when absent or equal to exactly one `http://127.0.0.1:<N>`.
  - CSP `form-action 'self'` and `frame-ancestors 'none'`, plus CORP `same-origin`, prevent framing and reading `C` back. CSS exfiltration of the hidden input is blocked: `default-src 'none'` leaves no `img-src` or `font-src`, and no attacker markup reaches a page that holds `C`.
- **Crypto:** `crypto/rand` 32 bytes, base64url; `crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`. That is the stdlib as designed, not hand-rolled. Nothing new in the diff.
- **Dependencies:** `go.mod` and `go.sum` unchanged; stdlib only. `govulncheck ./...` (go1.27.3): "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities". It reported 1 vulnerability in a required module that the code does not call (the known ones are listed in `DEPLOY-local`). `npm audit` does not apply (no JS ecosystem in the range).
- **GCP surface:** none (a loopback-only local server; no IAM, service accounts or deploy changes).
- **Resource use:**
  - One lock across both actions, so a concurrent POST gets 409 and runs nothing (`TestActionBusy`). The lock is released by `defer`, a panic included.
  - Output is capped at 1 MiB before printableText. Expansion from U+FFFD and HTML escaping bounds a page at a few MiB.
  - `capped` is not goroutine-safe, but neither `search.Index` nor `metrics.Ingest` writes from goroutines (grep found no `go func` or `WaitGroup` in either package).
  - There is no `WriteTimeout`, by spec. An action is not cancelled when the client disconnects, and Shutdown waits for it; the second signal exits, as the spec describes.
- **Writes:** `Index` = `search.Index(Options{Dir: wd, Home: home})`, identical to the CLI's bare `fyr index` (`verb_search_memory.go:25-30`). `Ingest` = `ingestInto(metrics.Options{Home})`, the same function `fyr metrics ingest` runs. The serve path skips `o.Validate()`, which is harmless for the zero options. Both write only what the bare verbs write: the project's `.agents/scratch/search.db` (refused when not gitignored), the global index registration as `fyr index` does it, and `<home>/.config/fyr/metrics.db`.
- **Tests:** `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/serve` ok. `go test -race -count=1 -run TestServe ./cmd/fyr` ok (it uses `t.TempDir()` homes, not the real home).
- **Past failures:** `fyr search --refs <path> --kind bug` (scratch home) on each changed production file found only BUG-196 (on `serve.go`: a flaky wrong-token construction). Row 9's tests guard against it with `wrongToken` plus a precondition (`actions_test.go:49`).
- **Data as instructions:** nothing in the diff, the spec or the ADRs read as an instruction to this review.

## Not examined
- Whether an action can run alongside `/check` (it has its own mutex) or a `/search` reconcile when both write `search.db`: SQLITE_BUSY behaviour, at worst a 500, not a security issue. I did not read `search.prepare`.
- Escaping inside `metrics.RenderReport` (`/metrics/report`, row 8, unchanged), whose data the ingest button now refreshes.
- How `metrics.Ingest` finds its sources beyond `Options` (it reads under `<home>/.gemini/...`, per `TestServeActions`).
- No live-browser run: real `Sec-Fetch-Site`, `Origin` and cookie-jar behaviour, and the cookie-tossing limit in finding 1, were reasoned from browser behaviour, not observed.
- No mutation run of the step-5 checks (source edits are out of my lane). The full `go test ./...` was not run, per the dispatch.
- The diff's doc and trail edits (`README.md`, `TDD.md`, `TODO.md`, `.agents/trail.jsonl`): read only for their changed lines.

## Outcome

1. [low] fixed as documentation: `SPEC-fyr-serve` § Every request gains a second accepted residual, the `431` a cookie flood from another local port causes (availability only, present since row 8). Raising `MaxHeaderBytes` was rejected because it only moves the line (plan D53).
2. [low] fixed: `TestActionCSRF` runs every refusal case against both actions (`refusedPosts`) and adds `Sec-Fetch-Site` `cross-site` and `same-site` (the step-2 line), two `csrf` fields and the no-media-type case; the new `TestActionOutputEscaped` pins `<script>` escaped, ESC as `?`, and a UTF-8 character cut at 1 MiB as U+FFFD before `[output truncated]`.
3. [low] fixed: `csrfOK` requires exactly one `csrf` field in the body (plan D53, spec step 5 and § Failure modes updated); the mutant that accepts a second field is caught by `TestActionCSRF`.

title: Security review round 2 — root-docs row 9, the fixes (2026-10-30)
body:
# Security review — fyr serve row 9 actions, round 2 (fixes only)   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: `.agents/scratch/row9-fixes.diff` — `.agents/scratch/r1/{actions.go,actions_test.go}` → working tree `internal/serve/actions.go`, `internal/serve/actions_test.go`, and the `cmd/fyr/serve_test.go` line (on top of HEAD dcff413). Checked against the `## Outcome` of `reviewer-2026-10-30-1629.md` and `security-2026-10-30-1630.md`, and `SPEC-fyr-serve` § Every request step 5, § Failure modes, § Verification. Lenses: security and code correctness.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: CLEAR

Every fix does what its Outcome claims. The new and changed tests fail without the code they cover: 8 mutants run on a scratch copy of the module, 8 caught. The fixes introduce no new defect at low severity or above. There are two informational notes, neither a defect in the code.

## Findings
- **[info / confidence: high]** `internal/serve/actions_test.go:173-190` (the second half of `TestActionBusy`): if the ingest POST is ever refused before `o.Ingest` runs (for example, a CSRF regression), `<-entered` blocks. The test then hangs until `go test -timeout` instead of failing with a message. The first half of the test has the same pattern, so this is not new to the fix. A `select` with `time.After` on `entered` would make such a failure readable. Not required.
- **[info / confidence: high]** `.agents/scratch/row9-fixes.diff`, from about line 186: the `cmd/fyr/serve_test.go` part has no `---/+++/@@` header. Its lines run on after the `TestActionFails` context, so the diff reads as if they were added to `TestActionFails`. The working tree is correct: `TestActionFails` does not hold them (`actions_test.go:255`), and they sit in `TestServeActions` (`cmd/fyr/serve_test.go`, `harness.StateDir`). There is no r1 copy of `serve_test.go`, so I reviewed the current `TestServeActions` instead of a one-line delta. This is a problem with how the review input was made, not with the code.

## Fix-by-fix
- **Security 3 (exactly one csrf):** `actions.go:79-80` now reads `vs := req.PostForm["csrf"]; len(vs) == 1 && equal(vs[0], r.csrf)`. It reads only the body. With no field, `len` is 0 and `vs[0]` is never indexed, so there is no panic. Mutant `>= 1` (the old `Get` behaviour): `TestActionCSRF` fails on "two csrf fields" for both paths. Spec step 5 and § Failure modes line 180 say the same.
- **Security 2 (test gaps):** `refusedPosts` runs for `/actions/index` and `/actions/metrics-ingest`. It covers `Sec-Fetch-Site` cross-site and same-site (expecting `lineFetchSite`), two csrf fields, and no media type (`Content-Type: ""`, which `ParseMediaType` rejects). Mutant "metrics-ingest skips csrfOK": 13 failure lines, all on the metrics-ingest path. Mutant "guard checks Sec-Fetch-Site on GET only": `TestActionCSRF` fails. The new `TestActionOutputEscaped` has two checks:
  - Mutant "no printableText": both assertions fail. ESC is not escaped, and the output keeps a raw `\xc3` (invalid UTF-8). So the U+FFFD comes from `search.Printable`, as claimed.
  - Mutant "no newline before `[output truncated]`": the tail assertion fails.
- **Security 1 (cookie-flood residual):** the spec line 69 carries the residual, which is availability only. There is no code change, as the Outcome says.
- **Reviewer 1 (order of step 5, then no-project, then the lock):** `TestActionBusy` adds a 403 POST without csrf while an action runs, and a no-project 200 outside a checkout while an ingest runs. Mutant "lock above csrfOK": fails. Mutant "lock above noProject": fails. The live order in `act` is csrf → noProject → TryLock.
- **Reviewer 2 (evidence and docs):** only the spec § Verification rows 225-226 were read; they match the tests. The plan text and `GUIDE-testing` § 3i are outside this lens and were not read.

## Checked
- **Secrets:** none in the fix diff.
- **Injection:** there is no new input path. The escaping test confirms `html/template` plus `printableText` on the action page.
- **Authz/authn:** step 5 is tightened (one csrf field). The order is pinned by mutants.
- **Crypto:** unchanged (`equal`, which is `crypto/subtle`).
- **Dependencies:** the only new import is `unicode/utf8` (stdlib, test only). `go.mod` is untouched. `govulncheck` was not rerun, because round 1 ran it and no dependency changed.
- **GCP surface:** none.
- **Tests:** `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/serve` ok. `go test -race -count=1 -run TestServe ./cmd/fyr` ok. Mutants were run in `.agents/scratch/mut-r2` (a tar copy without `.git`, removed afterwards). The working tree was not touched. The baseline on the copy was green before and after.

## Not examined
- Code that is not part of the fixes, per the dispatch (round 1 covered it).
- The r1 version of `cmd/fyr/serve_test.go` (no copy exists), so the exact one-line delta could not be confirmed. Only the current `TestServeActions` was read, and it passes.
- The plan record (D52, D53 evidence) and `GUIDE-testing` § 3i text.
- The full `go test ./...`, per the dispatch.

## Outcome

1. [info] fixed: the second half of `TestActionBusy` waits on `entered` or `done` in a `select`, failing with a precondition message when the ingest returns without blocking, as the first half does.
2. [info] no change: a note on the scratch diff's shape; the working tree was reviewed.

title: Review — root-docs row 10: fyr check rule (d), R → M → T traces (2026-10-30)
body:
# Review — check-row10 traces   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: working tree vs 9ab49a0 (git diff + intent-to-add internal/check/traces.go, traces_test.go), as captured in .agents/scratch/row10.diff, plus .agents/scratch/row10-spec.diff (SPEC-fyr-check). Note: the working tree moved after row10.diff was written (17:07): cmd/fyr/help_text.go (reworded paragraph) and internal/check/check.go (Run's rule (c)/(d) calls moved into `rootDocsRules`) changed at 17:09. I reviewed the CURRENT tree for those two files; the rest matched the diff byte for byte.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing in the new code is broken: rule (d) parses the template shape correctly, the `verificationLines` refactor onto `unfenced` is behaviour-identical (line-by-line against the old loop: same fence rule, same first/second case order, same `0,0` / `from,1<<30` / `from,n` returns), the summary-line change is complete in code and in both tests that pin it, `go test` of internal/check, cmd/fyr, internal/serve, internal/harness and the root package is green, gofmt and vet are clean, and the function-length pin passes. The worst problems are (1) a heading match that is looser than the spec says, giving a concrete false negative, and (2) three behaviours the spec states or the diff changes that no test would notice reverting (confirmed by mutation). Everything else is stale describing text.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/check/traces_test.go` (whole file) and `cmd/fyr/check_test.go:161,173` — three changed or specified behaviours survive a mutation. Each mutation was applied to a scratch copy of the tree (`.agents/scratch/agents/mut`, since deleted), compiled, and the named tests ran green:
  1. Summary-line order: swapping `r, t` to `t, r` in `printCheck`'s `Sprintf` (cmd/fyr/check.go:58) passes `TestCheckVerb` and every other cmd/fyr check test, because both pinned summaries have requirements 0 and traces 0. Failing input: a checkout with one `requirement` finding prints `requirements 0, traces 1`. `TestFindingsSorted` pins `Counts`, not the printed order. Fix: one cmd/fyr case with a requirement finding and a trace finding (or a `printCheck` unit test over a hand-built Report).
  2. "The first row with a key wins" (`tableRows`, traces.go:323; spec § Rule (d)): changing it to last-wins passes all of `TestTracesRule*`. No fixture has a duplicate key. Failing input: SDD trace `| R4 | none |` then `| R4 | M1 |` is a finding today and would not be after the change.
  3. "To the next level-one or level-two heading" (`tableRowList`, traces.go:301-304): replacing `in = strings.HasPrefix(...)` with `in = in || strings.HasPrefix(...)` passes all tests, because in every fixture `## Trace` is the last section. Failing input: a `## Risks` table after `## Trace` with a row `| R9 | M1 |` would then count as a trace row. Fix: add a section after `## Trace` holding a row for an otherwise-untraced item.
  (Mutations that DO fail the suite, so those parts are pinned: dropping the fence handling fails `TestTracesRule` and `TestVerificationFileNames`; disabling the names-a-component check fails `TestTracesRule`.)

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/check/traces.go:301,306` — the section match is a prefix match (`strings.HasPrefix(l, "## "+heading)`), but the spec says "every `## <heading>` section" and TDD/SDD wording says "`## Trace`". Failing input (run in the scratch copy): TDD.md with `## Traceability matrix` holding `| M1 | T1 |` and a real `## Trace` holding only `| M2 | T2 |` gives no finding for M1, although M1 has no row in `## Trace`. Same for `## Components …` in SDD.md. Fix: compare the whole heading text (`strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(l, "## ")) == heading`), or say "begins with" in the spec.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` (current `guide` record, table row `check`, Checkout column) — still states the exact output `check: 0 findings (docs 0, specs 0, requirements 0); fyr d0494224331c` and lists only the `REQUIREMENTS.md has no enforced-by field` note. After this change a matrix run prints `…requirements 0, traces 0)` and an added `note: no SDD.md: traces not checked`. `fyr check` does not read this string, so no gate fails; the next person following the guide compares against stale text. Restatement left standing, found by grepping the summary line across current `guide`/`spec`/`deploy`/`testing` records (the other hits are `change`/`testing` history, which are never rewritten).

- **[low / confidence: high]** Stale describing text left by the change: `internal/check/check.go:1-2` (package doc: "docs, specs and requirements") does not name traces; `PRD.md:114` still lists "Whether `fyr check` verifies the R → M → T traces" as an open question. The PRD edit needs the operator's approval (propose it; do not make it silently). `cmd/fyr/main.go:22` ("drift check of this checkout's docs") is generic and was already looser than the verb.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/check/traces.go:232` via `requirement­Items` (requirements.go:71-102) — items are read without fence handling, while the tables are read with it. Failing input: a PRD.md `## Must` holding a fenced example `- **R9** — example.` yields `R9: no row in SDD.md's trace` (reproduced). The behaviour is inherited from rule (c) and the spec says "Items are rule (c)'s", so it is consistent, but the Known limits do not name it for rule (d). Either note it in the spec's Known limits or leave it; not a regression.

- **[low / confidence: low]** `traces_test.go:495-504` — only a symlinked SDD.md is tested; the spec's row says the same holds for PRD.md and TDD.md. The code path is the same `rootDoc` helper, so the risk is small; the spec's claim of coverage is wider than the test.

## Criteria

1. Dead code — pass. `unfenced` is used by both `tableRowList` and `verificationLines`; no leftover helpers; `rootDocsRules` has one caller. The old duplicate fence loop in verification.go is gone.
2. Flow tracing — pass. `Run` → `rootDocsRules` → `tracesRule` → `rootDoc`/`requirementItems`/`tableRowList`; `Counts` has one caller (cmd/fyr/check.go) and both callers of its old 3-value form were updated (compiles; internal/serve renders through `printCheck`, its tests pass). Notes on every unreadable half are emitted, never a silent pass; the symlink/oversize path goes through `readFile` (Lstat + opened-file check under `os.Root`). Finding text interpolates only `it.id` (`[A-Za-z][0-9]+`) and `M[0-9]+`, so nothing a document holds reaches the terminal unprinted (and `printCheck` runs `search.Printable` anyway). `verificationLines` refactor verified equivalent.
3. Standards conformance — fail on describing text only (findings 3 and 4); README, SDD, TDD (verb row, T14 interfaces, trace row), help text, skills/review/SKILL.md step 3 and SPEC-fyr-check all agree with the code. Spec Output/Counts/notes rows match `traces.go` and the notes strings verbatim. Tests: see finding 1.
4. Directory layout — pass. `traces.go`/`traces_test.go` beside the rule files in internal/check; `check.go` is 362 lines (< 600), `traces.go` 154, `traces_test.go` 167; `Run` stays under the 50-line function pin (`TestFunctionLength` green).
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only (`regexp`, `strings`, `errors`, `io/fs`); no auth/crypto involved.
6. Decoupling — pass. Rule (d) reuses `requirementItems`, `fenceMarker` and `readFile` from the package; the only new shared seam is `unfenced`, which the fence rule now has one home for.

## Not examined

- A full `fyr check` run finished after the report was drafted: `check: 4 findings (docs 2, specs 2, requirements 0, traces 0)`, notes `PRD.md has no enforced-by field: not checked` and `PRD.md has no Must or Should items: requirements not traced`. The summary line prints the new field; no component of SDD.md lacks a TDD.md trace row (no trace finding); the two spec-stale findings (SPEC-fyr-check, SPEC-fyr-eval) are the expected pre-commit state, since the spec edit is in the trail but not yet committed, and the two docs findings (`docker/references/*.md` paths in skills) pre-date this change. This repo's PRD has no items, so the PRD to SDD half of rule (d) is not exercised on it.
- `go test ./...` in full (ran internal/check, cmd/fyr, internal/serve, internal/harness, the root package, plus `go vet` and `gofmt -l` on the changed packages).
- Behavioural `fyr eval` rows (no agent, skill behaviour or rule text other than skills/review/SKILL.md step 3's one clause changed; its wording was read against the code, not run).
- The rest of SPEC-fyr-check beyond the diff hunks and the grep for restatements; `docs.go`/`specs.go` behaviour is untouched.

## Outcome

1. Fixed. `TestTracesRule` gains a duplicate `R2` row (`none yet`, then `M1`; the first wins, so R2 is still a finding), a `## Risks` section after `## Trace` holding `| S1 | M1 |` (S1 is still a finding), and a TDD `## Traceability matrix` holding `| M3 | … |` (M3 is still a finding). `TestPrintCheckSummaryOrder` (cmd/fyr) prints a report with specs 1, requirements 2 and traces 3. Each of the four mutations named here (last-wins, a section never ending, a prefix heading match, `r, t` swapped) was applied by hand and failed its test, then reverted.
2. Fixed. `tableRowList` compares the whole heading text (`## Traceability matrix` is not `## Trace`); the spec says so.
