# Security review — work-lead-input-hardening-2 (D139/D140)   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: 4eac588..working tree (uncommitted). That is `.agents/scratch/h2/source.diff` (`internal/work/{fetch,records,worker}.go`, `internal/work/{records,rig,run}_test.go`, `cmd/fyr/verb_work_test.go`, `internal/eval/suite_test.go`, `skills/{work,handoff}/SKILL.md`), plus `spec.diff` (the SPEC-fyr-work body), `plan.diff` (D140), and `guide-eval.diff` with `setup.sh` and `check.sh` (the `work-squash-r2` row). The blast radius I followed: `internal/brain` ordering, its trail parser and its schema (`brain_input.go:100`, `export.go:255-298`, `store.go:38-50`, `record.go:98-110,238-249`), and the eval row runner (`internal/eval/row.go:82-171`, `internal/sandbox/session.go:149-151`).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The worst problem: the new window check compares `updated` as an instant, but the store ranks records by `updated` as text. So a worker can still outrank the lead's closing handoff on the same day. This is the "same-day `updated`" half of the prior review's finding 1, and it stays open.

How it works:
- `window.outside` (`internal/work/records.go:148`) accepts any RFC 3339 offset. `TestWindowOutside` even pins `+02:00` as accepted (`records_test.go:96`).
- `internal/brain` stores `updated` verbatim in a `TEXT` column (`store.go:48`; `export.go:296` checks only that it parses). It sorts `ORDER BY date DESC, updated DESC, id DESC` (`brain_input.go:100`), which is a byte comparison.
- The lead's own `fyr record` always writes UTC `Z` (`brain.go:308`).
- So suppose a worker stores its handoff with today's `date` and an in-window instant written with a large positive offset, such as `2026-10-31T08:29:00+14:00` for 18:29Z, or `+23:59`. Its `updated` string then sorts after every `Z` stamp the lead writes under the same `date`. Squashed and pushed, it is "the newest handoff, the live one" (`skills/handoff/SKILL.md:173-175`) for the rest of the lead's day, ahead of the lead's step-11 closing handoff.
- The same holds for "the three newest change records".

I checked this with a scratch probe that copies `outside` unchanged (`.agents/scratch/sec-probe-2026-10-30-1951/main.go`). The control `2026-10-30T18:29:00Z` is in the window and does not sort after the lead's `2026-10-30T18:45:00Z`. Both `+14:00` and `+23:59` are in the window and do sort after it.

The fix's own text says this cannot happen: `fetch.go:174`, `run_test.go:210`, and the SPEC's step 8 ("a worker's handoff can never be dated after the run, and so outrank the lead's closing handoff"). All three are wrong.

The cross-day half of the prior finding 1 (a far-future `date`) is closed, except for the documented west-of-UTC case (finding 2). The other findings are low.

## Prior findings (REVIEW-2026-10-30-1926-security-review-work-lead-input-hardening-d138)

- **F1 [medium] worker-chosen `date`/`updated` on added handoff/change: PARTLY CLOSED.**
  - A future or past `date` (2099-12-31, 2000-01-01) is now refused (`records.go:151-155`), and so is an out-of-window instant (`records.go:148`). `TestRunAddedRecordDates` covers this, and the plan states each case was seen red. I ran `go test ./internal/work -run 'TestWindowOutside|TestRunAddedRecordDates' -count=1` and it passed.
  - Open: the same-day outrank through the text form of `updated` (finding 1). The next-day `date` for a lead west of UTC after UTC midnight (finding 2, documented as not closed in D140). Edited records named in `Files:` are not date-checked (documented, finding 5).
  - The optional binding of a handoff ID to its date is not done (finding 4).
- **F2 [low] refused ID unbounded in the note: CLOSED.** It is `%.128q` (`fetch.go:193,197`). The new notes cut `updated` with `%.128q` (`records.go:149`). `date` uses `%q`, but `parseLine` has already made it exactly `YYYY-MM-DD` (`records.go:123`). A fraction 300 digits long is cut at 128 (probe).
- **F3 [low] step 8 body mechanism: CLOSED in an earlier round.** The file tool plus `--body <` is at `skills/work/SKILL.md:96`. Residual, step 8's line-break list: U+2028 and U+0085 are now named and CLOSED in prose, but U+2029 is not (finding 3). The step-8 awk is still not fence-aware; it is not in this diff and was not re-examined.
- **F4 [low] step 9 title edited to fit: CLOSED.** It is in prose: "its draft's first line with the `# ` removed, exactly as written … never edited to fit: its draft is not stored and is a closed-set item" (`skills/work/SKILL.md:97`). Nothing enforces it mechanically. It is the remediation the prior review asked for.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/work/records.go:148` with `internal/brain/brain_input.go:100` and `internal/brain/store.go:48`: `updated` is checked as an instant but ranked as text, so a positive offset outranks the lead's closing handoff (and change records) for the rest of the day. The evidence is above.
  - **Remediation, in the verb:** refuse an added handoff or change whose `updated` is not in the canonical form `fyr record` writes. That means `u.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339) == r.Updated`: UTC `Z`, no fraction, no offset. It fails `changed outside its Files` like the rest of D140.
  - **Defence in depth, in the store:** normalise `updated` to UTC on load (`export.go:296`), or order by `julianday(updated)`. A store change is a design question for the operator (ADR-063 scope).
  - **Tests:** flip `records_test.go:96` to a refused case. Add `TestRunAddedRecordDates` rows with an in-window `+14:00` and an in-window fractional `updated`, each seen red before the fix.
  - **Text to correct:** `fetch.go:174`, `run_test.go:210`, the SPEC's step 8 sentence "So a worker's handoff can never be dated after the run…", and D140 (`updated` "compared as an instant, whatever its offset" is the very gap).
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/records.go:151-155`: the UTC day is accepted for every lead. So for a lead west of UTC whose window ends after UTC midnight, any worker may date its handoff tomorrow, and a docker worker (UTC) does so unasked. That handoff outranks the lead's closing handoff until the lead writes one dated the next day. D140 and the SPEC name this as not closed. It is accepted, not fixed. The operator's own zone (UTC+1) does not hit it; a lead west of UTC would.
  - **Remediation:** give the worker the lead's zone (a `TZ` entry in the agy allowlist and the docker env, from the lead's `time.Local`), then accept only the lead-local day. Or accept the UTC day only for `--runner docker` and only when it is not after the lead's local day at the window's end.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/work/SKILL.md:96`: the step-8 "no line break" list names LF, CR, U+2028 and U+0085, but not U+2029 (PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR). U+2029 passes `bodyText` (`internal/brain/record.go:241-249`: only < 0x20 and 0x7f are refused, so VT and FF are already refused) and is a mandatory break to Unicode-aware readers. A worker's `## Completed` evidence holding U+2029 could start a `files:` or `model:` line for such a reader of the plan body.
  - **Remediation:** name the Unicode mandatory breaks as a class (LF, CR, VT, FF, U+0085, U+2028, U+2029), or say "any character other than printable text and spaces leaves the evidence off".
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/brain/record.go:98-110`: an added handoff's ID is not bound to its `date`. `validID` takes any slug, so `HANDOFF-2099-12-31-2359-x` dated today passes the verb and the store. The ranking does not use the ID's stamp except as the last tie-break. But an agent reading `fyr record list --kind handoff`, or a handoff named in Next Steps, may take the ID's stamp as the recency.
  - **Remediation (optional, as in the prior review):** in `added()`, require a handoff or change ID of the form `<KIND>-<date>-<HHMM>-<slug>`, with that date equal to the `date` key.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/work/fetch.go:156-158`: a base record that the Kickoff names in `Files:` and that the worker edits is not date-checked. A worker could re-date a named change or handoff into the future. This is documented in D140 and the SPEC. A lead naming a record ID in `Files:` is unusual.
  - **Remediation:** apply `win.outside` to changed records of kind handoff or change whose `date` or `updated` moved.

## Checked

- **Secrets:** none in the diff, the tests or the eval row. The fixture records and identities are dummies (`GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=f@localhost` from `row.go:168`).
- **Injection:**
  - The new notes are bounded and quoted (`%.128q`), and the date is pre-validated. Notes pass through `Printable` (relied on from the prior review, not re-read).
  - Eval row `work-squash-r2`: the setup is constants only, with no external input interpolated. It runs with `cwd` = the clone (`sandbox/session.go:150`), `HOME=SB` (`row.go:146`) and an `env -i`-style environment. It writes only `$CLONE/.agents/trail.jsonl`, the clone's `.gitattributes`, branches and `.agents/scratch/work/...` in the clone, and `$SB/setup-head` / `$SB/p2-head`. No `|` appears in the setup, so the table cell is safe.
  - The check's `fyr` calls run with `HOME=SB`, so they never touch the real `~/.config/fyr`. `records-before.txt` is written by the runner (`row.go:85-103`); if it were missing, `grep -f` would exit 2 and fail closed. The `while read -r h` loop takes IDs from `fyr` output, used quoted.
  - The row exercises the skill against a fabricated `result.txt`, not the verb, so it does not cover the D140 check (expected: the Go tests do).
- **Authz/authn:**
  - The window's clock is the wall clock (`time.Now`). `from` is cut to whole seconds, which strips the monotonic reading. A backward clock step during the run shrinks or inverts the window and fails closed. `to` is taken at the scope check under the collect mutex, so time spent waiting widens it. It still ends before the lead's step-11 handoff.
  - `w.start` is set only in `run()` (`worker.go:71`), the sole path to `added()` (`fetch.go:114,160,176`), so a zero start cannot open the lower bound.
  - The two-handoff path still fails.
  - The outrank gap is finding 1.
- **Crypto:** none touched.
- **Dependencies:** `go.mod` and `go.sum` unchanged. The new import is the stdlib `time`. `govulncheck ./...` (full path): "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities" (1 in a required module, not called), so nothing new. No npm in scope.
- **GCP surface:** none touched.

## Not examined

- `internal/sandbox` `Printable` and the docker runner's clock and env: relied on from the prior review.
- The `skills/work/SKILL.md` steps outside 8 and 9, and the fence-awareness of step 8's awk.
- The full `skills/handoff/SKILL.md` worker Kickoff, beyond the changed Never line.
- I ran no `fyr eval` (the dispatch forbids it), so the `work-squash-r2` row's behaviour on Antigravity is unverified.
- I ran only the two new Go tests, not the full suite.

## Outcome

- [medium] `updated` checked as an instant but sorted as text. Fixed: `window.outside` refuses an `updated` that is not `u.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)` (`internal/work/records.go`). Tests: `TestRunAddedRecordDates` rows `offset-updated` (+14:00, in the window) and `fraction-updated`, and `TestWindowOutside`'s `+02:00` and `.5Z` rows, each seen red against the first fix (`.agents/scratch/h2/red2.txt`) and green after. The texts the finding named (`fetch.go`'s `added` comment, `run_test.go`'s header, the SPEC's step 8, D140) are corrected. Closed in round 2.
- [low] UTC day accepted for a lead west of UTC. Deferred to the operator: the fix gives the worker the lead's `TZ`, an `internal/sandbox` change outside this Task's approved set. Stated in the SPEC and D140.
- [low] U+2029 missing from step 8. Fixed (the class is named). Closed in round 2.
- [low] An added handoff's ID is not bound to its `date`. Deferred to the operator (a new check, not D139 item 2's window). Stated in the SPEC and D140.
- [low] A named, edited record is not date-checked. Deferred to the operator. Stated in the SPEC and D140.

title: Review — plan audit of the three open plans against the code, the trail and TODO.md (D141 item 4, 2026-10-30)
body:
# Plan audit — the three open plans against the code, the trail and TODO.md (2026-10-30)

Scope: `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers`, `PLAN-2026-10-29-root-docs-and-fyr-serve` and `PLAN-2026-10-30-ui-skills`, as asked by `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers` D141 item 4. The audit was read-only: no source, plan body or record was edited. Tree: `0cbf714` (clean). The plans were read whole from `fyr record get … --home .agents/scratch/workers`, saved to `.agents/scratch/plan-audit/`.

## Summary

None of the three plans can close today without the operator's input. Two findings matter most:

- Release 2 owes more behavioural runs than D141 item 1 names. It lists 3 rows; the range since `v4.1.0` changed 7 skills and 1 rule.
- The worker TZ Task (D141 3a) has two open design questions. It should run as workers Phase 9, starting with its own Step 1, and land before Release 2.

Everything else is stale text, deferrals missing from `TODO.md` Backlog, or operator items that were never answered.

## The table

| # | Problem | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Release 2's owed runs are incomplete. D141 item 1 names `work-squash-r2`, `work-kickoff-model` and `handoff`, but the range since `v4.1.0` also changed `review`, `testing-strategy`, `cloud-run-deploy` and `harness-audit`, and none of their rows has run since. | fix: row 11's Kickoff lists all 8 rows plus the real-home smoke (item 1 below) |
| 2 | It is unclear who starts `fyr eval`. D12 and D38 say the operator. PRD R8 today says "only the operator's own session starts", and workers 5b and 8b ran the rows `who: AI`. The UI plan's Phase 2 is `who: AI` too. | ask once: may the release session run the owed rows itself? Record the answer as a D-row in root-docs |
| 3 | The TZ Task (D141 3a) is not a plain Task. dave has no `TZ` (`/etc/localtime` → Europe/Stockholm), so there is no "lead's TZ" to pass. It is also unverified whether the docker image has zoneinfo. | fix: workers Phase 9, with a two-question Step 1, before Release 2 |
| 4 | The PRD Must/Should reshape (D55 (2)) is drafted but has no box in any plan. Until it lands, rule (d) does not cover this repository ("no Must or Should items: requirements not traced"). | approve `PROPOSAL.md` 1–5, then a root-docs row 10b Task before Release 2 |
| 5 | The workers plan's text contradicts its boxes. The Status line, 7a box 1's tail ("stays open", but it is `[x]`) and 7b-2's checkpoint ("PRD box stays open", but it is ticked, D112) are stale. D102's `Open:` row was answered by D112 but never marked closed. § Risks still names agy 1.4.10. | fix: one D-row, then the edits, in the hygiene Task |
| 6 | The root-docs Status line is still row 1's. D9's follow-up (a check that `TODO.md` Now mirrors the plan's boxes, "asked in row 7") was never asked. | fix the status; put D9's follow-up in Backlog |
| 7 | `TODO.md` Now says the workers plan is "done except Phase 7d". Phase 4's Mac box is also open. | fix in the hygiene Task |
| 8 | Eight deferrals are in no Backlog (D10 says they belong there): D141 3b and 3c; D138 item 5 (step 7.3); D109's container limits; the workers Scope's 3 follow-ups; D9's mirror check. | fix: one Backlog line each |
| 9 | Two Backlog items approved on 2026-10-29 ("go all approved") are still not done. One is the stale canary claim in `GUIDE-testing` § 5, which is still there (line 243 of the record). | fix: in the hygiene Task (docs only) |
| 10 | D109's "put to the operator" items (`--memory`, `--memory-swap` and `--cpus` per container; a run network with `enable_icc=false`) were never answered. | defer: Backlog, through the operator's word |
| 11 | BUG-198 is still open with no decision (D101: "watch the next loop run"). | defer: keep it open as a watch in Backlog; do not let it block closing the plan |
| 12 | The Mac items gate closing the workers plan: Phase 4's `go test` on the Mac (`who: user`) and 7d's two boxes (agy search and build; the Mac smoke). | operator's call: run them in one Mac session, or defer both to Backlog with a closing D-row |
| 13 | UI plan Open 1 understates the overrun. `frontend-ui-economist`'s description is 1,016 bytes (not about 900) and `-modern`'s is 822, so the listing goes over by about 1,280 bytes, not 1,100. Option (a) would cut each description to about 280 bytes. Provenance is also unclear: a skill named `frontend-ui-modern` appears in this Claude Code session's skill list. | ask in Step 1: confirm the skills are the operator's own (editable) or vendored |
| 14 | The UI plan has no release row, and its runs would add to whichever release comes next. | defer: start it after Release 2, and add a release row (Release 3) in Step 1 |
| 15 | Outside the repo: this Claude Code session loaded `~/.claude/AGENTS.md`. It is a pre-ADR-062 copy that `fyr` keeps (`internal/harness/apply.go:254`), and it still names `ROADMAP.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md` and "TODO.md empty". | the operator's: refresh or remove it; the harness itself is unaffected |

## Details by number

### 1 — The runs Release 2 owes
These are the skill and rule files changed in `git diff --name-only v4.1.0..HEAD -- skills agents rules context` (catalog excluded). For each, the last commit and the `GUIDE-eval` rows that test it:

| Unit | Last change | Last eval run after it | Rows owed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skills/work` | `1079cff` | none (`work-kickoff-model` ran at `68f55d2`, before D136, D138 and hardening-2) | `work-kickoff-model`, `work-squash-r2` (never run) |
| `skills/handoff` | `1079cff` | none (last run `68f55d2`) | `handoff` |
| `skills/feature` | `ab6879b` | `TEST-2026-10-30-1539-…` at `ab6879b` | covered |
| `skills/review` | `dab94f6` (step 3, one line) | none | `review`, `review-docs-check` |
| `skills/testing-strategy` | `c98d4b9` (one path) | none | `testing-strategy` |
| `skills/cloud-run-deploy` | `c98d4b9` (one path) | none | `cloud-run`, `catalog-precedence` |
| `skills/harness-audit` (`references/areas.md`) | `4dccb7a` | none | `harness-audit-elsewhere` |
| `rules/session-sizing.md` | `c3cc1a8` | every later run renders it (`TEST-…-1539`, `-1553`) | covered |

The AGENTS.md § Release rule names each changed skill, so 8 rows plus `TEST-2026-09-03-verify-real-home`'s smoke are owed. A waiver for the four one-line path edits is the operator's to give, quoted (D33).

### 2 — Who starts `fyr eval`
- PRD.md R8 (current text): "the runs of `fyr eval` and the workers of `fyr work`, which only the operator's own session starts".
- Root-docs D12 and D38 read the older wording, "only the operator starts". D38 says row 11's runs are the operator's "unless they say otherwise".
- Workers 5b and 8b ran `fyr eval` as `who: AI` boxes, inside the operator's sessions.
- D141 item 1: "stay the operator's".

One D-row settles which reading row 11 and the UI plan's Phase 2 follow.

### 3 — The TZ Task, placed
Measured on dave: `TZ` is unset, and `/etc/localtime` links to `Europe/Stockholm`. A host-runner worker inherits `/etc/localtime`, so for it the gap is only a lead whose `TZ` is set and differs (D140). A docker worker most likely runs in UTC. The image is `golang:<minor>-trixie` with no `tzdata` step, and whether it holds `/usr/share/zoneinfo` was not checked.

The touch points are `internal/sandbox/env.go` (the agy environment, `LANG` at :32), the docker argv in `internal/sandbox/docker.go`, `internal/work/records.go:148-162` (drop the `time.UTC` zone from the date loop), and `SPEC-fyr-work` step 8. It changes no skill, so it adds no eval rows before Release 2.

Step 1 has two questions:
- (i) Which zone name is passed when `TZ` is unset? Recommendation: `$TZ`, else the zone named by `/etc/localtime`'s link target, else refuse docker mode with a line.
- (ii) How does the zone reach the container? Recommendation: `-e TZ=<name>`, plus a test that the image resolves it (a `date` check in the 7a image test), or `/etc/localtime` mounted read-only.

D141 3b and 3c stay deferred (item 8).

### 4 — The PRD reshape
The draft is in `.agents/scratch/prd-reshape/`: `PROPOSAL.md` (decisions 1–5) and `PRD.diff` (+49/−44). It was validated in a scratch clone: 0 findings as written, and 2 findings on a mutant. On approval, one commit holds the edit, its ADR, `SPEC-fyr-check`'s `### R0` line and `TODO.md`.

It has no row in root-docs' order of work. D55 (2) needs a row (10b) added by a D-row; the order is the operator's (D3).

### 5–7 — Stale plan text
- Workers line 4 (Status) lists "7a's box 1 … 7b-2's PRD box" as left, and calls Phase 8 "placed and planned". 8a and 8b are built, and D136–D141 are absent from it.
- Line 558: "Box 1 stays open" on a `[x]` box (D111 ticked it).
- Line 595: "The PRD box above stays open" (ticked, D112).
- Line 1087 `Open:` (the linux agy for the Mac): answered by D112 item 1, with no closing line, unlike root-docs' "Closed (D34 …)".
- § Risks line 638: agy 1.4.10 (dave runs 1.4.11; D102 noted it).
- Root-docs line 8 (Status) is the row-1 text. Line 39's follow-up says it was "asked in row 7", but row 7's table (D39–D42) did not ask it.
- `TODO.md` Now: "done except Phase 7d" leaves out Phase 4's Mac box (workers line 485).

These are plan-body edits, so the next Kickoff needs them in its standing approvals.

### 8 — Backlog lines owed
These are dated deferrals that `TODO.md` Backlog lacks:
- D141 3b: bind an added record's ID stamp to its `date`.
- D141 3c: date-check a named, edited record.
- D138 item 5: step 7.3's test run outside the sandbox. It is a design question for when docker becomes the default runner.
- D109: per-container `--memory`, `--memory-swap` and `--cpus`, and `enable_icc=false` (item 10).
- Workers § Scope follow-ups: worker session metrics; agy `--settings` in place of a written `settings.json`; the shared strict trail-line parser (D65).
- Root-docs D9's check that `TODO.md` Now mirrors the boxes.
- BUG-198's watch (item 11).

### 9 — Approved Backlog items not done
- `GUIDE-testing` § 5 still says the canary word is written in this repo's README and AGENTS.md (record line 243). `grep -n 'GANNET\|canary' README.md AGENTS.md` prints nothing.
- The home for the catalog plan's D11 and D12 is still only in git at `9001831^`.

Both were approved on 2026-10-29, and both are docs-only.

### 10–12 — Operator items with no answer
- D109's limits (item 10).
- BUG-198 (record open; its Fix reads "None yet … a question for the operator").
- Phase 4's Mac box, and 7d's two boxes (D112 chose the route; the linux-arm64 search needs the web, so the next session cannot do it from this repository alone).

### 13–14 — The UI plan
Its claims were checked and hold:
- The listing is 19,499 of 19,500 bytes over 37 skills (`TestSkillListingBudget -v`).
- The hand-written context is 14,744 of 15,000, and the block is 21,032 of 22,000.
- `skills/frontend` is 88K.
- 15 files name `frontend`.
- Both zips are in `.agents/scratch/ui-skills/`.

What it gets wrong or leaves out:
- The overrun is about 1,280 bytes, as measured in item 13.
- The `who:` is missing on its Phase 1 and Checkpoint boxes.
- It has no release row.
- Phase 2's `who: AI` eval runs depend on item 2.

`frontend-ui-economist`'s SKILL.md names the simulator "also published at claude.ai" (its Open 6).

### 15 — The Claude Code context
`internal/harness/apply.go:19` and `:254` (`keptClaude`): an install made before ADR-062 left Claude Code's files under `~/.claude`, and `fyr` keeps them. This session's loaded context comes from that copy. It gives a resume order through `ROADMAP.md` and a DoD with "`TODO.md` is empty at every checkpoint", which root-docs D1 and D10 reversed. `context/AGENTS.md` in the repo names neither file (row 3's grep). The fix is outside this repository.

## One ordered path

Each step is one session unless marked as the operator's.

1. **The operator** answers items 2, 3 (i and ii), 4 (`PROPOSAL.md` 1–5), 10, 11, 12 and 13, plus UI Open 1–7.
2. **Hygiene Task**: items 5–9.
   - Plan-body edits: Status lines; stale tails; D102's `Open:` closed by a D-row; § Risks.
   - `TODO.md`: Now, and the Backlog lines.
   - The two approved docs items.
   - Standing approvals needed: plan-body edits and the `GUIDE-testing` record.
3. **Workers Phase 9, the TZ Task** (item 3): code, `SPEC-fyr-work`, red-first tests, `reviewer` and `security`, real-home install.
4. **Root-docs row 10b, the PRD reshape** (item 4), if approved. It is independent of step 3, so steps 3 and 4 can swap.
5. **The owed runs** (item 1), by whoever item 2 names: 8 rows and the real-home smoke, as `testing` records. Root-docs row 11 box 1 is ticked on them.
6. **Release 2**: `/preflight` from the operator's own turn, which pastes row 11's Kickoff (D41). This ticks row 11 box 2.
7. **The operator**: row 12's smoke checks. Then **root-docs closes** (a closing D-row and the status set to done).
8. **Workers closes**: Phase 4's Mac box and 7d are done on the Mac, or deferred to Backlog by the operator's D-row (item 12). BUG-198 stays a Backlog watch. Then a closing D-row and the status set to done.
9. **UI skills**: Steps 2–3 (cold read), Phase 1, Phase 2 and the Checkpoint, then a Release 3 row at the operator's word. It runs after step 6, so its skill changes do not enlarge Release 2's owed runs.

## What was not checked

- `fyr check` was not rerun. The last run was at `db38c01` (0 findings, per the newest handoff), and HEAD `0cbf714` changes only the handoff.
- Whether `golang:1.27-trixie` holds `/usr/share/zoneinfo` (no container run).

title: Cold read — workers Phase 9, the worker's zone
body:
# Review — workers Phase 9 cold read (the worker's zone)   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: no diff. The plan record `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers`, Phase 9 alone: § Interfaces § The worker's zone (plan lines 400-446 of the saved copy `.agents/scratch/agents/plan-workers.txt`), § Phases § Phase 9 (lines 683-692), D27, D140, D141, D143, D144, and `SPEC-fyr-work` § Refusals and § One worker step 8 (`spec-work.txt`), checked against the code the dispatch names. Probes: `.agents/scratch/agents/gocheck/` (Go's `time.LoadLocation` and `TZ` behaviour; glibc via `date`).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS (no BLOCKING item; 6 GAPs to answer before the code box)

Phase 9 is buildable from its text and fails closed everywhere I traced: the date check only ever accepts a calendar day of the lead's own zone, so no case accepts a date that the old check refused. Go's and glibc's zone behaviour is stated correctly (`TZ` unset, set-but-empty, an unknown name, `Local`, and `LoadLocation`'s refusal of POSIX rule strings all reproduced). What would make two implementers build different things or leave a red suite: a cited D-row that is not the one meant (G1), a test row placed where it cannot be reached (G2), a work suite that depends on the developer's `TZ` (G3), refusal 22's position behind a container start (G4), a restated claim in SPEC step 8 that the docs list does not name (G5), and a TDD pin list that the docs list names by the wrong words (G6).

## Findings

### BLOCKING
none.

### GAP

- **G1 [medium / high] "D27's allowlist" names the wrong plan's D-row.** `plan-workers.txt:414`, `:444`, `:687` (Step 1 box ii) and `D144` say "amends D27's allowlist (`run.sh`:220-222)". In THIS plan D27 is "The PRD edits, applied in Phase 2" (`:807`), and says nothing of an environment. The allowlist is D27 of `PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-plan-fyr-eval-the-antigravity-run-kit-as-a-verb` (its text: "The agy environment is exactly `PATH` ... `STYRMAN_SKIP_CRED_PULL=1` (`run.sh:220-222`)"); `internal/sandbox/env.go:22` cites a bare "D27" for it. A cold reader following the plan finds the PRD edits. Fix: write "the eval plan's D27 (`PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-…`)" in the Interfaces text, the Step 1 box and the `agyEnv` comment. Related: that comment says "exactly the allowlist"; after Phase 9 it is exact for eval (pinned by `internal/eval/run_verdicts_test.go:66`, which stays green only because eval leaves `Zone` ""), and exact plus `TZ` for work. The plan says the comment is edited but not to what; name it so the comment does not stay false for one of the two callers.

- **G2 [medium / high] The "`--runner docker` with no name" test row cannot live in `TestRunRefusals`.** `plan-workers.txt:429` puts it there. `TestRunRefusals` (`internal/work/preflight_test.go:99`) runs the host rig; `--runner docker` there stops at refusal 13 (a test binary is a development build: `Options.Version` is empty) and never reaches 22. The docker refusals need the docker rig (`internal/work/docker_test.go:98`: `o.Runner, o.Version, o.AgyLinux = RunnerDocker, "vtest", self`, a fake `docker`), i.e. `TestRunDockerRefusals` (`docker_test.go:151`). Only the host-runner invalid-`TZ` row belongs in `TestRunRefusals`. Fix: move the row, and say the docker case passes refusals 13-20 first.

- **G3 [medium / high] The existing `internal/work` suite becomes a function of the developer's shell, and the plan does not pin it.** Every `Run`-based test (`run_test.go`, `several_test.go`, `docker_test.go`, `cmd/fyr/verb_work_test.go`) goes through `preflight`, so after Phase 9 each one meets refusal 22 when the machine's `TZ` is `:/etc/localtime`, `:Europe/Stockholm`, a POSIX string, or `Local` (all valid for the shell), and `TestRunAddedRecordDates` et al. then redden for a reason unrelated to the test. `newRig` (`rig_test.go:159-160`) already pins `HOME` and `PATH` with `t.Setenv`; the plan names only `TestLeadZone` as setting `TZ`. Fix: `newRig` sets `TZ` to a fixed valid name (or `localtimeLink` to a temp link) so every test starts from a known zone; say so in the code box. Also: the tests need tzdata on the test machine (`LoadLocation` of `Europe/Stockholm`, `America/Los_Angeles`); say whether a missing zone skips (`t.Skip` on `LoadLocation` error) or fails, so a tzdata-less builder does not read as a regression.

- **G4 [low / medium] Refusal 22 runs after refusals 17-18, which start a container, though it is a pure offline check.** `plan-workers.txt:410` places it "after `p.session`"; `p.session` ends in `p.dockerRefusals(o)` (`preflight.go:112-113`), whose refusal 18 runs `docker run … fyr version` (SPEC-fyr-work § Refusals 18). So `--runner docker` with no zone pays a container start before it is told to set `TZ`. `preflight.go:79-80` states the principle "every offline refusal is made before the one network call"; refusal 22 is offline. The stated reason for the number (keep 21's citations) does not require this position. Either compute `leadZone` before `p.session` (the host-runner invalid-`TZ` refusal then sits after 11 as SPEC says for 21; the docker no-name refusal needs `o.Runner`, already known) or name the container start as accepted.

- **G5 [medium / high] The docs list misses restatements that Phase 9 reverses.** Grep over the living docs and code (`fyr search`, `grep` over `*.md` and `*.go`):
  - `SPEC-fyr-work` step 8 (spec line 183 of the saved copy): "none can carry a later `date` than the run's **but the case below**". The case below is the west-of-UTC case, which Phase 9 closes, so the exception clause becomes false. The plan names "the zone sentence" and "D140's Not closed list less its first two cases" but not this clause. Also in step 8: the three note formats, of which the third (`… , local or UTC)`) becomes `… in <loc>)` (plan `:416` states the new text, but the docs box does not list the format line); and "The verb sets no zone for the worker (the agy allowlist has no `TZ`)" appears in step 8 and in D140 (D140 stays, being a record).
  - `SPEC-fyr-work` § Refusals: line 110 says "Refusal 21 ... is the last of all, after 20"; the intro line before refusal 12 and the "twelve to twenty"/"1-21" counts. Also `internal/work/preflight.go:26` "refusals 1-21" and the plan's own Failure modes lead (`:450` "Refusals 1-21", set by D131). The docs box lists "§ Failure modes" for the SPEC but neither the plan's `:450` nor the `preflight.go:26` comment.
  - `internal/work/records_test.go:86-92` (the `TestWindowOutside` header: "a day of the window in the lead's zone or UTC ... no local zone (UTC-12 to UTC+14) holds them") and `SPEC-fyr-work` Verification row (spec line 344: "a `date` two days off refused whatever the local zone"): both describe the old rule. The plan lists the row; the test header is not listed.
  - `internal/work/records.go:139-141` (the `window` comment) is listed; `records.go:162` (the note) is the code.
  Fix: add these to the docs box; the `restatement-grep.sh` run of `/review --docs` will find them, but the plan should not depend on it.

- **G6 [low / high] "`SDD.md` M18 and `TDD.md` T18 where they name the window or the allowlist" is vacuous.** Neither file names the window, `agyEnv` or the allowlist (grep: no hit in `SDD.md`, `TDD.md`, `README.md`). What `TDD.md` does carry are the "Pinned by" lists at `TDD.md:180` (sandbox: `TestDockerArgs`, …) and `:193` (work: `TestRunDockerPass`, …) and the T18 test table at `:237`; `TestLeadZone`, `TestRunZone` and `TestImageZoneGuard` belong in them. Name those lines. `GUIDE-testing` § 3k is a record (not a file in the tree); say `fyr record edit` and who.

### NIT

- **N1** `TestRunZone` (`plan-workers.txt:429`): "Whether the fake records the environment is the implementer's to check first." It does: `internal/work/rig_test.go:37` writes `env > "$CTL/env"`. The test reads `$CTL/env` for a `TZ=` line; no new rig work.
- **N2** "`loc` ... the same zone as the lead's `time.Local` by construction" (`:412`) is slightly overstated. `LoadLocation` honours `ZONEINFO` first, which `time.Local`'s initialisation does not; and in case 3 the name is a string cut from the link target, loaded from the platform's zone directories, not the file `/etc/localtime` points at (a link into a private zoneinfo tree gives a different zone). Both are far-fetched and fail closed; "by construction" can say "for a stock system".
- **N3** The no-name `loc.String()`: the plan says "`Local` when there is none". `time.Local.String()` is `Local` only when `/etc/localtime` loaded; with the file missing it is `UTC` (probe, `gocheck/`: `TZ` unset gives `Local`; `TZ=Local` gives `UTC`). Say "`Local` or `UTC`, whatever `time.Local` calls itself".
- **N4** `Local` is refused because `LoadLocation("Local")` returns `time.Local` with no error. Confirmed (probe). The stated cause is "the host's zone"; when the lead's own `TZ=Local`, Go has already read it as UTC (probe: `TZ=Local` gives `time.Local = "UTC"`), so `LoadLocation` returns UTC there. The refusal is right either way. Same class, not refused by the pattern: `localtime` (Debian's `/usr/share/zoneinfo/localtime -> /etc/localtime`; `TZ=localtime date` prints CET here and `LoadLocation("localtime")` loads the host's zone) and `posixrules`. A worker given `TZ=localtime` in the image reads the image's `/etc/localtime` (UTC), so it fails closed. Add `localtime` beside `Local` in the refusal list and in `TestLeadZone`, or accept it.
- **N5** Valid shell values refused on the HOST runner as well: `TZ=:/etc/localtime` (a widespread setting, chosen to save a `stat`), `TZ=:Europe/Stockholm` and POSIX rules like `CET-1CEST,M3.5.0,M10.5.0/3` now make every `fyr work` exit 2 until `TZ` is unset. Step 1 (i) says "refused unless `time.LoadLocation` loads it and it is an IANA name" with no runner qualifier, and D144 approves it, so this is within the approval; the line it prints ("set TZ=<Area/City>, or unset it") is adequate. Put it in `SPEC-fyr-work` § Failure modes in those words so an operator who hits it reads it there.
- **N6** The image guard's position: "after its `COPY` and before `USER`" (`:418`); the final stage has `COPY`, then `ENV PATH`, then `USER`. Before or after the `ENV`? Both satisfy the text; `TestImageZoneGuard` as specified (after the last `FROM`) cannot tell. Say "after `ENV PATH`, before `USER`" or accept either. The guard checks `Etc/UTC` only, so a name the image lacks (Debian trixie moved the legacy aliases such as `US/Pacific` to `tzdata-legacy`; not measured here, no docker) still runs the worker in UTC unseen; the plan states that case ("Still not closed") and it fails closed.
- **N7** `window{from, to, loc}`: a zero `window` (nil `loc`) panics in `Time.In(nil)`. The only constructors are `fetch.go:177` and the test; no finding, but a nil guard or a constructor keeps a later literal from panicking inside the scope check.
- **N8** "Both lines go through `sandbox.Printable`, the value cut to 128 characters" (`:410`): the second line has no value; and after `%q` a control character is already escaped, so `Printable` is a no-op there. Specify the form (`%.128q` as `fetch.go:196` does), so two implementers agree.
- **N9** "A mutation of each refusal branch, red": `leadZone` has five (pattern, 64 bytes, `Local`, `LoadLocation`, and the empty-to-`UTC` branch) plus the docker no-name refusal. List them; "each refusal branch" is countable only by reading the code.

## What I checked and found sound (not findings)

- Go: unset `TZ` gives `time.Local.String() == "Local"`; `TZ=Europe/Stockholm` gives that name; `TZ=` (empty) and an unknown name and `TZ=Local` give UTC without error; `LoadLocation("Local")` loads; POSIX strings (`CET-1CEST`, `UTC0`, `GMT+5`) are refused by `LoadLocation`; `zoneRe` as a Go regexp has `$` as end-of-text, so `Europe/Stockholm\n` is refused (probe). glibc: `TZ= date +%Z` prints `Universal` (offset 0, UTC), `TZ=Local` an offset-0 zone named `Local`, an unknown name a zone with an empty abbreviation. So the plan's "set-but-empty is UTC for both" holds. D143's claim for the image (`TZ=No/Such_Zone date` prints UTC) differs from dave's host (empty abbreviation) only in the label.
- Fail-open trace: the new loop accepts a date only when it lies between the lead-zone day of `from` and of `to`. Every accepted date is one the old loop accepted, so nothing new is accepted. A docker image without the name gives a UTC date, accepted only when it equals a lead-local day of the window. A worker that sets its own `TZ` on a command line can only produce a date, which the same check bounds.
- `Config.Zone` has two constructors, `internal/work/worker.go:55` (set) and `internal/eval/row.go:45` (unset, as stated); `agyEnv` has no other caller than `hostCmd` (`session.go:80`) and `containerEnv` (`docker.go:108`), which filters only `PATH=`, so `TZ` reaches both; `dockerArgs` already refuses a `-e` entry without `=`; the `fyr` wrapper (`prepare.go:23`) does not scrub the environment. `TestHostCmdUnchanged`/`docker_test.go:161` compare against `b.agyEnv()` and stay true.
- The `prepared` copy loop (`preflight.go:78-82`) copies `p` into each `ps[i]`, so a `zone` set before it reaches every worker.
- `TestImageContextAllowList` reads `COPY`/`ADD` lines only; a `RUN` line does not disturb it; `TestBuildLinePinned` is unaffected. The guard runs as the build's default user (root), before `USER 65532`.

## Criteria (for a plan)
1. Dead code: pass. The `time.UTC` branch and the `local or UTC` note are named for removal; nothing else is left behind.
2. Flow tracing: pass with G2, G3, G4: `leadZone` -> `prepared.zone` -> `newWorker` -> `Config.Zone` -> `agyEnv` -> host `cmd.Env` / `containerEnv` -> `-e` argv; and `prepared.zone.loc` -> `window.loc` -> `outside`. Eval untouched.
3. Standards conformance: gaps G1, G5, G6 (citations and restatements).
4. Directory layout: pass. `internal/work/zone.go` is the package's pattern (one concern per file); no new package.
5. Simplicity: pass. Stdlib only (`regexp`, `os.Readlink`, `time.LoadLocation`); bind-mounting `/etc/localtime` and a per-run probe are rejected with reasons. Nothing hand-rolled in the security sense.
6. Decoupling: pass. `Config.Zone` is the one seam between `work` and `sandbox`; `sandbox` stays zone-agnostic (it passes a string); the pattern check lives in `work`, and `dockerArgs`'s `=` check is the second line of defence.

## Not examined
- `docker` was not run (instructed); the Debian trixie `tzdata`/`tzdata-legacy` split is from memory, not measured (N6).
- `internal/work/docker.go` beyond what `preflight.go` calls (`dockerRefusals`' internals), `cmd/fyr/work*.go`, `cmd/fyr/verb_work_test.go` beyond the date line, and the `fyr work` help text (whether it lists refusals) were not read.
- `README.md` map and `SPEC-fyr-eval`/`SPEC-fyr-sandbox`-style records that may restate "exactly the allowlist": `fyr search` found no record restating it besides `SPEC-fyr-work`, the eval plan and `GUIDE-testing` (which concerns eval's `env -i` start); I did not read `GUIDE-testing` § 3k itself.
- Phase 9's boxes 4-5 (real docker worker on dave, Checkpoint): not checkable before the code exists; box 4's expectation (committed `CET`/`CEST`, handoff dated the Stockholm day) is checkable as written, but it does not say what `TZ` the lead runs with: D143 says dave has `TZ` unset, so the run goes through case 3 (link name), which is the case to exercise; a second run with `TZ=Europe/Stockholm` would exercise case 1.

## Outcome

Answered by D145 of `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers` (the main thread, 2026-10-30). Every item is fixed in the plan's text: § Interfaces § The worker's zone and Phase 9's boxes. None is rebutted, and none is put to the operator.
- G1: the eval plan's D27 is cited, and `agyEnv`'s new comment is named.
- G2: the docker no-name row is in `TestRunDockerRefusals`.
- G3: `newRig` pins `TZ=UTC`, and the tests import `time/tzdata`.
- G4: refusal 22 is made in `prepared.session` after refusal 11, before any docker call.
- G5 and G6: the docs list is extended, with lines named.
- N1–N9: each is fixed in the text. N4 adds `localtime` to the refused names. N5 goes in SPEC's § Failure modes. N7 adds a nil-`loc` guard. N9 lists the eight branches.
- "Not examined", box 4: a second run, with `TZ=America/New_York` in the lead, exercises case 1.

title: Security review — 2a58fd8   (2026-10-30)
body:
# Security review — 2a58fd8   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: 2a58fd8^..2a58fd8

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: CLEAR

The commit has no security weakness. The new input is the lead's own `TZ`, or the text after the last `zoneinfo/` in the `/etc/localtime` link target. Both come from the operator or root, and the worker cannot set either. `asZone` (`internal/work/zone.go:62`) caps the value at 64 bytes and checks it against an ASCII-only regexp anchored at both ends. Go's `$` without the `(?m)` flag matches only at the end of the text, so a value with a trailing newline is refused. The regexp refuses `/`, `:`, `.`, `,`, `=`, space and control characters, and `Local` and `localtime` are refused by name. `time.LoadLocation` must also accept the value, and it refuses `..` and a leading `/` on its own. The value that passes reaches the child process in one place: `TZ=<name>` in `agyEnv` (`internal/sandbox/env.go:44`). With `--runner docker` it becomes one `-e` argv element through `exec.Command("docker", args...)`, with no shell (`internal/sandbox/docker.go:83,174`). Because the element always starts with `TZ=`, a name starting with `-` or `+` (the regexp admits both) cannot be read as a docker flag. The refusal message prints the value with `%.128q` (`zone.go:49`), so it is cut and Go-quoted. `TestLeadZone` checks that an ESC byte does not come through. The docker no-name refusal (`zone.go:78`) does not echo the link target. Nothing reaches eval: `internal/eval/row.go:45` sets no `Zone`, `agyEnv` adds `TZ` only when `Zone` is not empty, and `TestAgyEnvZone` pins that eval gets no TZ even when the caller has one set. The date check in `window.outside` (`internal/work/records.go:160-165`) now holds a date in one zone instead of "Local or UTC", so it is stricter. A nil zone refuses the date, so the check fails closed. The zone comes only from the lead and is checked on the lead's side, so a worker cannot widen it.

## Findings
None at any severity.

## Observations (not security weaknesses, recorded for the author)
- **[informational / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/zone.go:66` — A name passes when the lead's Go can load it. Without a `time/tzdata` import in production code (only `zone_test.go:9` imports it), Go looks in `$ZONEINFO` first, then in the system tzdata. The worker's lookup can fail where the lead's succeeded. On the host, `agyEnv` does not pass `ZONEINFO`. A docker image may have older tzdata without a newer zone name, and the Dockerfile guard only checks that `Etc/UTC` exists. When the lookup fails, glibc in the worker silently uses UTC, which is the case D144 was meant to stop. This fails closed for security: the window check uses the lead's zone, so worker dates written in UTC near midnight are refused, not admitted. It is a correctness and usability gap, not something an attacker can use. A possible remediation, which is the author's call: check the name against the image's own `/usr/share/zoneinfo/<name>` during the docker preflight, as `--pull never … test -f` beside the version check.
- **[informational / confidence: low]** `zone.go:22` — The regexp admits `posix/…` and `right/…` names. glibc applies leap seconds for `right/…` zones, and Go may not read them the same way, so the lead and the worker can disagree on the day for about 27s around midnight. Same as above: fails closed, not a security weakness.

## Checked
- Secrets: no credentials, tokens or keys in the diff. TZ is not secret, and the refusal message prints only the operator's own value, cut and quoted.
- Injection: TZ and the link-target text are checked with an anchored ASCII regexp, a 64-byte cap and LoadLocation. The value enters docker's argv only as `TZ=<name>` through `exec.Command` (no shell), and `dockerArgs` also refuses an entry with no `name=value`. No path is built from the zone name in fyr's own code: LoadLocation and glibc join it under their own zoneinfo directories, and `.` and a leading `/` are refused. The record `Date` in the new `outside` message is `%q`, and the zone is the checked name.
- Authz/authn: the trust boundary is unchanged. The zone comes from the lead's environment or root's `/etc/localtime`, never from the worker. `localtimeLink` and `loadLocation` are package variables that only tests replace. The date check is stricter, and fails closed when there is no zone.
- Crypto: none touched, nothing hand-rolled.
- Dependencies: go.mod is unchanged. `time/tzdata` is standard library and imported only in a test. `govulncheck ./...` (Go 1.27.3; run with GOCACHE under .agents/scratch and GOPROXY=off): 0 vulnerabilities affecting the code, plus 1 in a required module that the code does not call (the known one, per DEPLOY-local § Operator steps). npm is not relevant: no web/ change.
- GCP surface: none touched. The Dockerfile change is one root `RUN test -f` before `USER 65532:65532`, with no new privilege, network or secret.
- Past failures: `fyr search --refs <path> --kind bug` over the eight changed source files found only BUG-197 (`records.go` merge=union duplicates), which this diff does not touch. The scratch index called zone.go "untracked" and the others "modified", which looks like a stale index, not a finding.
- Data read as data: TDD.md and the trail.jsonl diff were scanned for directive text and none was found.

## Not examined
- I did not read the full `.agents/trail.jsonl` diff. I scanned it only for keywords (ignore, skip, approve, security, reviewer, instruction).
- I did not read the rest of the record bodies, or `internal/work/records_test.go` beyond its stat.
- Not run, per the dispatch: `go test`, docker, `fyr work`, `fyr eval`. Whether a real image's glibc honours the passed TZ is therefore not verified here.
- I did not check how the release binary's LoadLocation behaves on macOS against the `/var/db/timezone` layout. The parsing is covered by the `link-mac` test row.

title: Review — 2a58fd8-code-docs   (2026-10-30)
body:
# Review — 2a58fd8-code-docs   (2026-10-30)

Range reviewed: 2a58fd8^..2a58fd8 (code + docs lens)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The worst problem is test hermeticity: `newRig` pins `TZ=UTC` only for `internal/work`, but `cmd/fyr`'s work-verb tests also reach `work.Run` -> refusal 22 and do not, so a developer with `TZ=:/etc/localtime` (valid in a shell, the case refusal 22 itself names) gets 6 failing `TestWorkVerb*` tests; the spec/GUIDE text claims the opposite. The code is otherwise sound: the zone name is regex-restricted before it reaches env or docker argv, order of refusals matches the spec, and `go vet` plus `go test -count=1 ./internal/work ./internal/sandbox` pass.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/verb_work_test.go:90-92,353-355` (stale claim: `SPEC-fyr-work` § Verification line "`newRig` pins `TZ=UTC`, so the developer's own `TZ` ... never reaches a `Run`-based test"; `internal/work/rig_test.go:161-163`) — the pin is in `internal/work`'s rig only. Verified: `TZ=:/etc/localtime go test -run TestWorkVerb ./cmd/fyr` fails 6 tests with `work: TZ=":/etc/localtime": not a zone name ...`; with TZ unset they pass here only because `/etc/localtime` links to `zoneinfo/Europe/Stockholm`. `TestWorkVerbDockerFlags` (docker runner) also fails on any host whose `/etc/localtime` is not a zoneinfo link and TZ is unset (refusal 22's no-name case). Fix: `t.Setenv("TZ", "UTC")` in both setup blocks of `verb_work_test.go` (and say in the docs that the pin is per package), or correct the sentence.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/docker.go:50` — doc-comment "dockerRefusals are refusals 13-20 ..., after refusal 11" no longer matches `SPEC-fyr-work` (13-20 are checked after 22; `preflight.go:112-117` calls `runZone` before `dockerRefusals`). Say "after refusal 22".
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `cmd/fyr/help_text.go:251-266` (`fyr help work`) — a new user-visible refusal (every `fyr work` exits 2 while `TZ` is set but not a zone name, and `--runner docker` with no zone name) is not mentioned; help says only "Exit ... 2 refused". The spec is the home for the full rule, so this is a nit, but a lead with `TZ=:/etc/localtime` gets no pointer from help.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. No unused symbols; `loadLocation` and `localtimeLink` are test seams with callers.
2. Flow tracing — pass with the finding above. `leadZone` -> `runZone` -> `prepared.zone` -> `Config.Zone` -> `agyEnv` -> `containerEnv` (inherits TZ via `agyEnv`) and `window.loc` in `fetch.go` all agree; the nil-loc guard fails closed; eval sets no Zone (`TestAgyEnvZone`). Only construction of `window` is `fetch.go:177` (plus tests).
3. Standards conformance — fail (low): stale comment `docker.go:50`; the test-hermeticity claim above. Package tests `internal/work`, `internal/sandbox` pass with `go test -count=1`; gofmt not run by me.
4. Directory layout — pass. `zone.go` beside the other `internal/work` files; tests beside code.
5. Simplicity — pass. Stdlib only; `time/tzdata` imported in test files only. No crypto/auth.
6. Decoupling — pass. `sandbox.Config.Zone` is one additive string field; work-side logic stays in `internal/work/zone.go`.

## Docs lens
- SPEC-fyr-work, GUIDE-testing, TDD.md and the Dockerfile comment agree with the code on: refusal 22 text and order, `TZ` in `agyEnv`/`containerEnv`, the window wording `in <loc>` and the nil-zone note, the tzdata guard and its test. `internal/work/preflight.go:27` was updated to 1-22. # Review — v4.1.0-5b716dd-code-docs   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: v4.1.0..5b716dd

HEAD is 5b716dd, so the working tree is the range head. Every `fyr` call carried `--home .agents/scratch/workers`. Nothing was written under `~/.config/fyr`, `~/.gemini` or `~/sandbox`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

I found no high or medium defect in the code I read. `fyr check` finished late with 0 findings, but two of its notes show that the new trace rule and the requirement rule checked nothing on this repo (finding 1). The pre-flight recorded-bug search came back empty for six changed files (`referenced by 0`), and no change reintroduces a bug I could match. The read covered the worker runner, slots, docker mode, zone, fetch and scope checks, drafts, the serve guard, actions and records, the sandbox guard and after-steps, and the verb wiring. It also covered the brain duplicate-line fix (BUG-197) and the trace rule in `check`. It does not cover the whole range (see "Not checked"), so this is a bounded APPROVE WITH NITS, not a full release clearance.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/check/traces.go` (new rule d) — `fyr check` at HEAD printed two notes: `PRD.md has no enforced-by field: not checked` and `PRD.md has no Must or Should items: requirements not traced`. So on this repository the new R → M → T trace rule (requirements half) and the existing requirement rule both checked nothing. "0 findings (docs 0, specs 0, requirements 0, traces 0)" is therefore weak evidence for the trace rule here. This range's `SDD.md` trace edits (R0, R3, R4, R6, R7, R8, R10 rows) are not machine-checked. Either `PRD.md` should use the `Must`/`Should` item form the rule reads, or the release record should say the requirements half of rule (d) did not run. The components half (SDD M# to TDD trace) ran without a note.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/check` spec-stale rule (not changed by this range) — `fyr check` took over 10 minutes wall time here. At one point its child was `git log -G '"id":"SPEC-fyr-metrics".*"updated":"…"' --format=%H -- .agents/trail.jsonl`, about 30 s per spec record, which is one pickaxe over the whole trail history per spec. The trail grew by about 90 commits in this range, and `fyr eval` was running on the machine at the same time, so load may have added to it. It is not a correctness failure, but a release gate that takes this long is easy to cut off. Fix: resolve each spec's last-changed commit in one pass, or bound the history walk.

- **[low / confidence: low]** `skills/work/SKILL.md` standing approvals (`git reset --hard HEAD`) with open bug BUG-198 — BUG-198 ("the work lead committed to its checkout during a fyr work run, then reset to a named commit outside its approvals") is listed as `open`. The skill now narrows the reset to `HEAD` on a tree that was clean before the squash, and says no commit happens while a run is going. That is prose only: no mechanism enforces it, and I did not check whether BUG-198's prevention rule is met by this range. Check that the BUG-198 status matches what the range does before the release record says it is closed.

- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/sandbox/docker.go` (`dockerArgs`, token mount) — the operator's real login token file is bind-mounted read-write into the container, with the wide `command(*)`, `read_file(*)` and `write_file(*)` grant. The code checks that it is a regular file (`dockerCmd`). The comment cites D106 as the decision, so this is an accepted trade-off and not a defect. I list it only so the release record names the residue: a worker can overwrite the real login, and `ExitChecks` does not fingerprint the token (`watched` leaves it out by design).

## Docs lens

1. `fyr check` at the checkout's root, HEAD 5b716dd: it completed with `check: 0 findings (docs 0, specs 0, requirements 0, traces 0); fyr 9284cae9b19b`. The binary's stamp is 9284cae, not 5b716dd. 5b716dd is a handoff-only commit on top of it, so the code is the same, but the stamp differs from HEAD. Notes quoted verbatim: `note: PRD.md has no enforced-by field: not checked` and `note: PRD.md has no Must or Should items: requirements not traced`. See finding 1.
2. Restatements compared by hand (`restatement-grep.sh` exists at both candidate paths but I did not run it; hand `git grep` stood in, so coverage is partial):
   - "two things leave the machine" is restated consistently as three in `AGENTS.md:14`, `README.md:76` and `SDD.md:152`. `git grep` found no surviving "two things" or "the other is `fyr eval`" wording in the living docs.
   - README skill count "37 of them" matches `skills/` (38 entries, minus `VENDORED.md`).
   - README's `fyr work` flags match `cmd/fyr/verb_work.go` (`--timeout --model --keep --max-workers --kill --runner --image --agy-linux`), and the defaults match (4, at most 8).
   - README's `fyr serve` default `127.0.0.1:3000` matches `cmd/fyr/serve_test.go:154`.
   - The "at most 39 lines per worker" contract matches `internal/work/contract_test.go:64`.
   - `AGENTS.md` Layout lists `docker/` and the new `internal/` packages.
   - `PRD.md` and `SDD.md` carry the sandbox/work/serve trace rows (R8: M16–M18).
3. The `skills/work`, `handoff` and `feature` changes agree with the code on the points I compared: the verb's accepted record kinds (`internal/work/fetch.go` `added`: handoff and change only), the draft-name regexp `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,80}\.md$` (`drafts.go`), and the `Files:` / `Model:` line handling.
4. `stale test` / `dropped` / `narrowed`: none found in what I compared. `TDD.md`, `GUIDE-testing`, the `spec` records and the `DEPLOY-*` records were not read (see "Not checked").
5. Pre-existing (`fyr check`): none; it reported 0 findings.

## Criteria

1. Dead code — pass. Nothing orphaned in the files read. The eval guard/creds/procs code moved to `internal/sandbox` and the old copies were deleted (no duplicate left behind).
2. Flow tracing — pass for the paths read. `dispatch` hands out slots, `give` runs on every `done`, and the unstarted workers fail `killed`. `waitDocker` and `containersLeft` fail closed when `docker ps` errors. `fetch` and `scope` run only after the lead-unchanged check. `leadZone` refusal 22 comes before every docker call. Not traced: the eval refactor into `sandbox` beyond its guard, `invoked.go` and the moved files' call sites.
3. Standards conformance — pass with the caveats above. Errors are wrapped or noted, contexts flow, and the guards keep the data when a check errors (`Kill`, `liveRuns`, `containersLeft`, `localDaemon`). gofmt, vet and tests were not re-run by me.
4. Directory layout — pass. New packages are under `internal/`, the Dockerfile and its ignore file are under `docker/` (documented in `AGENTS.md` Layout), and tests sit beside their code.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only. The serve token and cookie use `crypto/rand` bytes and `crypto/subtle` compare as designed, which is stdlib use and not hand-rolled crypto.
6. Decoupling — pass. `serve.Options` takes printer closures from `cmd/fyr`, so there is no import back. `sandbox` is the shared seam for eval and work. `work` depends on `sandbox` and `trail` only.

## Not checked

- The `restatement-grep.sh` script (hand `git grep` was used instead).
- `TDD.md` (+52/−5), `TODO.md`, the `GUIDE-testing`, `GUIDE-eval`, `SPEC-*` and `DEPLOY-*` records, and the newest `change` record.
- `internal/eval/row.go`, `run.go` and `invoked.go` (the refactor into `internal/sandbox`) beyond a glance, and the moved `creds.go` and `procs_*`.

- `internal/serve`: `pages.go`, `view.go`, `dreamlog.go`, the other page handlers, and the templates and CSS.
- `cmd/fyr`: `verb_serve.go`, `help_text.go`.
- All `_test.go` files, so no assessment of whether the new tests can fail, and no mutation evidence examined.
- The `docker/` image build itself, which was read but not built.
- `skills/work` beyond what is cited above; `skills/handoff` and `skills/feature` were checked by diff only.
- Behavioural runs (`fyr eval`), the real-home smoke, and `govulncheck`. The AGENTS.md release blocking condition (an Antigravity run of each changed skill and agent) is not something this review can satisfy.

## Outcome

- 1. `fyr check` printed that PRD.md has no enforced-by field and no Must or Should items, so the requirements rule and half of the trace rule checked nothing (low): left: operator. The PRD.md Must/Should reshape waits for the operator's approval (root-docs D55 (2)); named in the v5.0.0 gate report's What was not checked.
- 2. `fyr check` took over 10 minutes (low): left. TODO.md Backlog already holds it (fyr check's CPU time, added 2026-10-29). It finished: exit 0, 0 findings.

title: Security review — v4.1.0..5b716dd (release v5.0.0 gate) (2026-10-31)
body:
# Security review — v4.1.0-5b716dd (2026-10-31) Range reviewed: v4.1.0..5b716dd ## Status: COMPLETE ## Verdict: FINDINGS The worst issue is a policy one. `fyr serve` composes its own authentication and session flow: a one-time URL token is exchanged for a path-scoped cookie, and a second CSRF token goes in every form body (`internal/serve/guard.go`, `internal/serve/actions.go`). The global context bans hand-rolled auth and sessions outright, so this is high severity even though no exploitable flaw turned up. Host pinning, Sec-Fetch-Site, constant-time compares, SameSite=Strict, a random per-run path, CSP `default-src 'none'` and html/template escaping all look correct. The worst *technical* risk is the `work` skill. The lead runs worker-written code (the project's full test command on the squash) directly on the host and then commits and pushes it without a human reading it. That bypasses the `--runner docker` isolation entirely. `fyr work`'s scope check also misses file modes: a worker can land a symlink inside its `Files:` scope. The README and SDD both claim a worker's data can only reach the model because its clone "has no remote". That is false, because the worker has `command(*)` and network access. Nothing secret was found in code, tests or the trail. govulncheck reports nothing reachable. **The gate is blocked by `## Not examined`:** the 53 test files were scanned by pattern, not read line by line. ## Findings - **[high / confidence: medium]** `internal/serve/guard.go:33-86`, `internal/serve/actions.go:63-81`, `internal/serve/serve.go:69-111` — a hand-rolled auth and session flow. A bearer token from `crypto/rand` is exchanged via `?token=` (303) for a cookie `fyr_serve_` scoped to `/s/

`. Every request is authenticated by comparing that cookie. A separate CSRF token sits in each POST body, with an Origin check. The token bytes are stdlib as designed, so they are not the issue. The session and CSRF protocol built around them was composed here, which the hard rule ("never hand-roll auth … sessions") forbids regardless of correctness. In review the flow held: an exact Host match defeats DNS rebinding, a duplicate-cookie plant is refused, a token in a POST query is refused, and every page carries `no-store` and `no-referrer`. Remediation is the operator's decision, because a vetted library would add a dependency the project's R4 forbids. Either (a) record an explicit exception to the hard rule as an ADR naming this flow, building on ADR-075/075a, or (b) replace the CSRF half with stdlib `net/http.CrossOriginProtection` (Go 1.25+) and keep only the per-run bearer token. The stdlib has no session library. - **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/work/SKILL.md:86` (step 7.3), `:25`, `:98` — the lead runs "the project's full test command" on the uncommitted squash of a worker branch. That executes worker-written code on the host as the operator, with the operator's credentials and network, after the session's sandbox checks are over. A PASS then gets committed and pushed (steps 7.4 and 10) with no human reading the diff. A worker that was prompt-injected (for example by repository text it read) only needs to put a malicious `_test.go` or build step inside its own `Files:` scope. This bypasses `--runner docker` entirely. `TODO.md` Backlog already records the issue as deferred ("Step 7.3 … runs the worker's code outside the sandbox"). Remediation: run step 7.3 in the same hardened container image with `--network none` and only the clone mounted. Until that exists, require the operator's review before the lead pushes a squash, or stop pushing merged worker code until the closing handoff. - **[medium / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/fetch.go:102-113` and `:124-144` (`changedPaths` uses `diff-tree --name-only`) — the scope check validates paths only, not file modes. A worker branch can add a symlink (mode 120000) or a gitlink (160000) at a path its `Files:` line covers. After the squash-merge (pushed by the lead, finding 2), a symlink in the lead's tree pointing at `~/.ssh/` or `~/.config/gcloud/` lets later tools, builds and agents read or write outside the checkout through an ordinary-looking repo path. Remediation: use `diff-tree --raw -z` and fail `changed outside its Files` on any added or changed mode 120000/160000 unless the Kickoff names that path explicitly. Add a test that fails without the fix. - **[medium / confidence: high]** `README.md:76` ("whose clone has no remote, so nothing it holds goes anywhere but to that model"), `SDD.md:152`, `cmd/fyr/help_text.go:44` and `cmd/fyr/main.go:21` ("sandboxed agy workers") — these overstate the security boundary. On `--runner host` the worker gets `command(*)` (`internal/work/worker.go:16`) as the operator's uid with network access. Removing the git remote does not stop `curl` or `git push `, and the operator's credentials (`~/.ssh`, gcloud ADC) are readable. On `--runner docker` the container still has the default network. `SkipStores: true` (`internal/sandbox/guard.go:156-180`, workers D45) also means a host worker that calls a fyr binary by absolute path with the real home can write the real `brain.db`/`search.db`/`metrics.db` without check c noticing. That is persistent poisoning of memory and records. The design accepts most of this (D20, D45, GUIDE-testing § 4), but the docs state a guarantee the code does not give. Remediation: correct the README and SDD sentences ("the clone has no remote; the agent can still reach the network"). Say "isolated only with --runner docker" in the help line. Consider making docker the default. - **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/sandbox/docker.go:78`, `internal/sandbox/guard.go:149` — the real Antigravity OAuth token is bind-mounted read-write into the worker container (D106), and check c deliberately does not fingerprint it. A worker that has been subverted could replace the token file with a valid token for another account. The file stays a regular file, so `unlink` (`internal/sandbox/after.go:45`) only warns on a type change and misses this. The operator's later agy sessions would then run on that account, which receives their prompts and code. Host mode has the same capability through the symlink, but there the agent already holds the uid. Docker mode is where the token is the one writable host file outside the clone. Remediation: before the session, record the token's account identity field (a JSON field read for comparison, not verified as a credential). Fail `real config changed` if it differs afterwards. Alternatively, mount a copy and write back only a refresh for the same account. - **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/sandbox/docker.go:70-86` — the session container has no `--network` restriction and no `--memory`/`--cpus` limit (only `--pids-limit 4096`). Network access is required for agy to reach its model, so exfiltration from inside the container is possible. Resource exhaustion of the host or VM is also possible. Already in `TODO.md` Backlog (D109, put to the operator, unanswered). Remediation: add memory and CPU limits and an `enable_icc=false` run network, as the backlog item proposes. - **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/contract.go:27-71`, `internal/work/fetch.go:176-211`, `skills/work/SKILL.md:96-97` — worker-authored text reaches the lead model's context and, after a merge, the lead's trail. That text includes handoff sections, change titles, and bug drafts the lead stores "unreviewed" (step 9). After the merge, a worker's handoff with a `## Kickoff` is instruction-shaped text in the trail that resume reads. Prefixing, `Printable`, the 39-line cap, the kind allow-list and the D139/D140 date window stop spoofing and outranking. They do not stop injected content. The skill tells the lead to treat these lines as data, which is the right mitigation. Remediation: have resume's handoff selection skip handoffs whose title or body marks them as a worker's (worker mode), or have the lead re-title them on merge. ## Checked - **Secrets:** grepped every added line of the non-trail diff for key and token shapes (PRIVATE KEY, AKIA, AIza, ya29., sk-ant-, ghp_, xox, password=): none. Trail: covered by pattern grep of all 196 added `.agents/trail.jsonl` lines (not read line by line). The hits are `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE` (AWS's published example key, quoted in `REVIEW-2026-10-30-1225-…` as finding prose), `BEGIN PRIVATE KEY`/`ya29.` as pattern names in a handoff, and `-----BEGIN` in `SPEC-fyr-delivery` redactor prose. No real secret. Instruction-shaped text: "approved by the operator" appears in 5 records (`CHANGE-2026-10-30-0958`, `CHANGE-2026-10-30-2042`, `PLAN-2026-10-29-root-docs-and-fyr-serve`, `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers` ×2). Each is a self-attested approval note in the trail's own records, read as data and not acted on; none is addressed to a reviewer. Private data: `git@github.com:kesokaj/fyr.git` and the host name `dave` appear in DEPLOY and GUIDE records, both already public in the repo's own docs. Added record kinds: adr 8, bug 4, change 33, deploy 2, guide 4, handoff 43, plan 4, review 60, spec 8, testing 29. Logs: serve's `logf` omits the query (no token). The work refusal and notes go through `Printable`. The models check strips PWD. - **Injection:** serve escapes everything through html/template, has no script, validates the record ID with a regex, caps `q` at 200, validates kind against `brain.Kinds()`, and builds the Location as a `url.URL` with leading slashes collapsed. Docker argv: `Mountable` refuses comma, quote and control characters; the image ref refuses `-`, whitespace and control characters; the run uses the image ID (`sha256:` + 64 hex); `-e` needs `k=v`; TZ and model are regex-validated; the Kickoff name is `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$` plus `check-ref-format`. `Files:` refuses `..`, globs, absolute paths and control characters. git in the lead runs with `--no-replace-objects`, `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, `GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null` and `fetch.fsckObjects`. The trail parser in work has strict keys, line and size caps, and dedupes only byte-identical lines (BUG-197). The brain export now accepts byte-identical duplicate IDs (sha256 of the line) and refuses others. The wrapper script uses `ShellQuote`. Drafts are copied through `os.Root` with a single-link check and an O_EXCL write. - **Authz/authn:** serve, see finding 1. The guard order is Host → Sec-Fetch-Site → token/cookie → route; POSTs need CSRF and Origin. `fyr work --kill`: stamp regex, pid matched to the stamp, pid bounds, flock-held check. Sandbox checks: guard a/b (`CheckRoot`), `Intact`, `OpenRegular` (O_NOFOLLOW, single link), leftover processes, fingerprint, credentials scan. - **Crypto:** `crypto/rand` 32-byte tokens, `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`, sha256 for duplicate-line equality: stdlib as designed. The serve session/CSRF protocol is finding 1. No other primitive was composed. - **Dependencies:** `go.mod`/`go.sum` unchanged in the range. `govulncheck ./...`: "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities"; 1 vulnerability in a required module is not called. No `package.json`, so npm audit does not apply. New image base `golang:${GO_MINOR}-trixie`, unpinned by digest: the operator builds it locally and the run pins the built image ID (low; not a finding). - **GCP surface:** no IAM, service account, `--allow-unauthenticated` or Secret Manager change. `skills/cloud-run-deploy/SKILL.md` changed one reference path only. - **Dockerfile / dockerignore:** default-deny context; secret-shaped excludes; named COPYs; `FYR_VERSION` validated; non-root `USER 65532`; no secrets in layers. - **fyr search --refs --kind bug** (with `--home .agents/scratch/workers`) for `internal/serve/guard.go`, `internal/sandbox/docker.go`, `internal/work/fetch.go`, `internal/work/drafts.go` (0 each) and `internal/brain/export.go` (BUG-197, fixed; the dedupe change read and consistent with it). The other changed paths were not queried individually (tool-call budget). ## Not examined - **Test files: pattern scan only, not read line by line. Per the dispatch, this blocks the gate.** 53 `*_test.go` files in the range (+6437 lines): `cmd/fyr/{check,migrate,serve,testmain,verb_work}_test.go`; `internal/brain/{export,readtrail,union}_test.go`; `internal/check/{check,traces}_test.go`; `internal/eval/{fixture,invoked,prepare_records,row_replaced,run_proc,run,suite}_test.go`; `internal/sandbox/{box,config,creds_table,creds,docker,env,guard,imagepath,open,prepare_arms,printable,procs_linux,rig,testmain}_test.go`; `internal/serve/{actions,dreamlog,dreamlog_unix,fixture,guard,pages,serve,writes}_test.go`; `internal/work/{contract,docker,kickoff,models,preflight,records,rig,run_safety,run,several,slots,testmain,zone}_test.go`; and the deleted `internal/eval/prepare_arms_test.go`. Covered only by: the secret-shape grep (none), and a scan for real-home, network, `docker` and HOME use. HOME is always set to the rig's fake real home, fake docker and agy scripts sit on PATH, and the only "real" network strings are `http://evil.example` header fixtures. - `.agents/trail.jsonl`: covered by pattern grep and kind counts as described in Checked, not read record by record. - The deleted bodies of `internal/eval/row_prepare.go` (lines after the wrapper script) and `internal/eval/row_session.go` were not read line by line. They are removals; their replacements in `internal/sandbox/{prepare,session}.go` were read in full. - Not re-read in full, only as diffs: unchanged code these changes call: `internal/brain` (List/Get/Search/FormatGet), `internal/metrics.RenderReport` (served whole at `/metrics/report`, so whether its HTML escapes session-derived strings was not checked; CSP `default-src 'none'` blocks script either way), `internal/sandbox/creds.go` beyond its 2-line rename diff, `trail.Dirty`/`trail.Command`. - No dynamic test: serve and work were not run; `go test` was not run (the verifier's lane). ## Outcome - 1. fyr serve's own session (high, policy): rebutted. The operator accepted it as the named exception in their own turn of the release session, quoted in ADR-075b ("Accept the exception (Recommended)", 2026-10-31). - 2. The work skill's step 7.3 runs worker tests on the host (medium): left: operator. TODO.md Backlog (workers D138 item 5), a design question; named in the v5.0.0 release notes as a known limit. - 3. The scope check ignores modes (medium): fixed. `internal/work/fetch.go` `links`, with `--ignore-submodules=none` after round 2; `TestRunLinks`; BUG-200. - 4. The docs overstate a worker's isolation (medium): fixed. README.md:76, SDD.md:152, cmd/fyr/help_text.go:44, cmd/fyr/main.go:21, SPEC-fyr-work § Purpose, SPEC-fyr-delivery § What stays on the machine; BUG-202. - 5. The agy token is mounted read-write, and an account swap goes unseen (low): left: operator. TODO.md Backlog (the token's account check). - 6. No network, memory or CPU limits on the container (low): left: operator. TODO.md Backlog (workers D109, unanswered). - 7. A worker's handoff in the lead's trail is instruction-shaped text (low): left: operator. TODO.md Backlog. - Not examined (the test files): covered end to end by the part A and part B reports, both with `## Not examined: none`.
