| 26 | `internal/metrics/report.go` is 402 lines. Phase 3 adds the per-row table to the report. | fix in Phase 3's Kickoff: the table goes in a new file (code-modularity pre-edit rule) |

## Details by number

### 1 — `replaced`: graded or not
- What the code does: `internal/eval/cause.go:14-24` maps `replaced` to ERROR. D30 puts a safety check first, so a swap that also leaks a credential or leaves a process is a FAIL. The plan's § Interfaces cause table (line 106) and `SPEC-fyr-eval` step 15 both name `replaced` as an ERROR.
- The reviewer's low finding 4 (`REVIEW-2026-10-31-0855-…`): `TestRunSecondSessionAfterSwap` has the agent itself move the directory. That trial leaves n, so pass^k is computed without it.
- The case against FAIL: some infrastructure failure could also change the sandbox's identity. Nothing in `internal/sandbox` does that today. A swap means a process inside the sandbox replaced it, and the only such process is the agent.
- The cost: one map entry, `TestClassifyEveryReason`'s want, the cause table, `SPEC-fyr-eval` step 15, and a D-row.
- Why before 2b: 2b's goldens print the cause, so doing it in 2b means changing the formats once instead of twice.

### 2 — Phase 2b
Its boxes are lines 220–223 of the plan:
1. The verdict and summary lines, the record's title suffix, the header block, and the per-trial and per-row tables.
2. `GUIDE-testing` § 4, `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` § eval, and `TDD.md` § T13.
3. The E2E on this box, `who: both`.
4. The Checkpoint.

Checked: no Wilson interval is printed by `cmd/fyr` today (`grep -ln Wilson cmd/fyr/*.go` finds nothing). The E2E needs agy runs under `~/sandbox/fyr-eval/home`, so the Kickoff must name that home, per AGENTS.md's eval exception.

### 3 — The real-home install lag
- `fyr version` on PATH is `35b75f2f40f0`, and `fyr help eval` does not mention `--runs`.
- `git log v5.0.0..HEAD` holds 7 commits.
- AGENTS.md § Rules for working here: "on dave … a session's checkpoint ends with `fyr install` into the real home from a clean, pushed tree".
- The Kickoffs of Phase 1, Phase 2a and this audit all listed "a real-home install" under Never.
- Effect: `fyr check` from PATH reports `--runs: fyr eval does not take it` five times, at README.md:124, SPEC-fyr-check:7, SPEC-fyr-eval:18, SPEC-fyr-serve:7 and TDD.md:69 (the Phase 2a review's Not examined). Every session has to remember to use a tree binary.

### 4 — The PRD reshape
- The draft is `.agents/scratch/prd-reshape/` (`PROPOSAL.md` with decisions 1–5, `PRD.diff` +49/−44), drafted against `db38c01`.
- `PRD.md` has not changed since `db38c01`, and `git apply --check .agents/scratch/prd-reshape/PRD.diff` exits 0 at `b9cae29`.
- v5.0.0's preflight records: "`fyr check`'s requirements rule and the requirements half of its trace rule: they ran and checked nothing".
- It is a requirements change, so the order is: your approval of `PROPOSAL.md` 1–5, a D-row adding row 10b to root-docs (D3: the order is yours), then one commit holding the edit, its ADR, `SPEC-fyr-check`'s `### R0` line and `TODO.md`.

### 5 — `fyr check` time
- Measured with a tree binary at `b9cae29` (`go build -o .agents/scratch/audit/bin/fyr ./cmd/fyr`), running `time fyr check --home .agents/scratch/workers`:
  - real 5m16.5s, user 5m13.6s, sys 2.8s;
  - `check: 0 findings (docs 0, specs 0, requirements 0, traces 0)`, plus the two PRD notes (item 4).
- The Backlog's figure is 3m22s with the pre-row-8 binary (`99e4a0c`, 2026-10-29).
- So it is CPU-bound, with almost no I/O wait, and it grew by more than half in two days while the trail grew. That looks superlinear in the number of records or files.
- Every Definition of Done runs it: the verifier, the preflight, and `fyr serve`'s `/check`. The last two handoffs told sessions to background it.
- The hot path was not profiled, since that is outside a read-only audit. A `-cpuprofile` run is the first step of the fix Task.

### 6 — Closing root-docs
- Status (line 8): "As of 2026-10-30 (D56) … Left are row 11, Release 2 … and row 12". Row 11 is `[x]` with v5.0.0's evidence.
- Row 12 (line 198): "The operator's Antigravity checks, once, over everything (`DEPLOY-local` § Operator steps) — who: user".
- No `Open:` row is left. D31 and D34 closed both.
- To close: your word on row 12, recorded in a handoff (or a D-row deferring it), then a closing D-row and the status set to done.

### 7 — Closing workers
- The boxes left are line 559 (Phase 4's `go test -race ./internal/sandbox ./internal/work ./cmd/fyr` on the Mac), line 684 (7d: a linux agy for the Mac; the search needs the web) and line 685 (the Mac container smoke). All three are `who: user` or need the Mac.
- The Status line is current: D142 brought it in line with the boxes, and Phase 9 is recorded (D143–D147).
- The PRD's Known limits already cover docker on macOS (ADR-079), so deferring loses nothing a reader is not told.

### 8 — BUG-198
- One occurrence in two lead loops (Phase 6 and its rerun, D99 and D100).
- v5.0.0's gate ran one docker worker directly, not as a lead loop, so the watch has had no new data.
- `leadUnchanged` (`fetch.go:50`) checks that HEAD equals the base and that the tracked tree is clean, after the session. The lead's commit followed by `git reset` passes both.
- The mechanical guard: read `git reflog -1 --format=%H%gd` (or the reflog's line count) for HEAD before the run, and refuse when it differs after.
  - Step 6 of the skill forbids every git write mid-run, so a legitimate run never moves the reflog.
  - It is test-first and touches `internal/work` only, so it owes no eval row.
- The case for keeping it a watch: one occurrence. The global rule graduates a recurring rule into a mechanism. But the guard is small and catches exactly the failure the text did not stop.

### 9 — The UI skills
- Still true, measured today:
  - The listing is 19,499 of 19,500 bytes (`TestSkillListingBudget`).
  - The context is 14,744 of 15,000, and the block is 21,032 of 22,000.
  - `skills/frontend` is 88K.
  - Both zips and their unpacked trees are in `.agents/scratch/ui-skills/`.
- New: this Claude Code session's skill list carries `anthropic-skills:frontend-ui-modern`. If that is the same skill, it is third-party, so `skills/VENDORED.md`'s verbatim rule applies and its description cannot be shortened (Open 1 (b): make room elsewhere).
  - `frontend-ui-economist` is not in that list.
  - Whether the two `frontend-ui-modern`s are the same was not compared: the Claude Code copy was not read.
- Risk: `.agents/scratch/` is gitignored, so the zips exist on dave only.
- Still missing from the plan: `who:` on Phase 1 and its Checkpoint, and a release row (prior audit items 13 and 14).

### 10 — O1–O8
- O1 holds Phase 4 (`compare.go`, `SignTest`, `MDE`). The interim is `metrics evals --harness <key>` run twice.
  - For: the `harness` key (D15, D31) exists only so that two versions can be compared.
  - Against: a compare needs 3 or more trials per row per key (O4) to say anything, and that means agy runs.
  - Recommendation: yes.
- O2, O3, O5, O6, O7 and O8 have the default "not built", and O4 "as written". One D-row taking them closes six open rows and keeps the plan's open list honest.

### 11 — The parallel-dispatch probe
- TODO Next: "first one agy run that puts two subagent dispatches in one turn". The trail has no record of such a run: the only "parallel dispatch" in `.agents/trail.jsonl` is a 2026-09-28 review's aside.
- It needs an agy session outside this repository's tree, and lands only in `skills/feature` and `agents/explorer`, never `rules/` (21,032 of 22,000).

### 12–17 — The workers deferrals
Each was checked against the code as not done:
- 12: `internal/sandbox/docker*.go` passes no `--memory`, `--cpus` or `--pids-limit`. The only `--network` match is a test's refusal list.
- 13: `skills/work/SKILL.md` step 7 still runs the merged code's tests on the host (security medium in v5.0.0's preflight, "left: operator").
- 14: `internal/work/contract.go` prints the handoff's three sections. The merged handoff record keeps its own title.
- 15: no account read in `internal/sandbox` or `internal/work`.
- 16: `records.go` `window.outside` checks `updated` and `date` only, not the ID's stamp, and only for added records.
- 17: `parseTrail` and `parseLine` (`records.go:74-127`) are separate from `internal/brain`'s import and export parsing.

### 18 — The TODO mirror check
Prior audit item 7 found drift once, and it was fixed by hand in the hygiene Task. `TODO.md`'s own header and the root-docs D9 rule make the plan record win on a conflict. A `fyr check` rule would have to parse free prose in Now. Strike it, and say so in the Backlog with a D-row.

### 19 — TDD § T5
Lines 42–75: 19 rows, averaging 491 characters, the longest 1,860. Eval-metrics Phases 2b–6 still edit the `eval` and `metrics` rows, so thinning them now would mean doing it twice.

### 22 — The stale catalog pointer
`AGENTS.md:71` says "(D11, D12 of plan `2026-10-01-google-skills-catalog`, in git at `9001831^`)". `fyr record get PLAN-2026-10-01-google-skills-catalog` holds both D11 and D12 (closed 2026-10-30). This is the second half of prior audit item 9, approved 2026-10-29. The first half (the `GUIDE-testing` § 5 canary claim) is fixed: the guide now names `internal/harness/render.go`.

### 23 — The `pass_k` warning
`secretRe` (`internal/redact/redact.go:44`) reads `pass_k` as a key in the pass family, so the bare value `{"k":…` is redacted. `cmd/fyr/record_redact.go` only warns on stderr, and the record is stored as written. The dreamer's prompt would be redacted there, which is the safe direction. AGENTS.md: "over-redaction in the safe direction is pinned there, never argued about".

### 25 — Release 3
- `git diff --stat v5.0.0..HEAD -- . ':!.agents'`: 42 files, +1,948/−328.
- `git log v5.0.0..HEAD -- skills agents rules context` is empty, so the project's NO-SHIP rule owes no Antigravity run today.
- If the UI skills land before the tag, that range owes their rows plus the removed `frontend`'s routing.

### 26 — `report.go`
`internal/metrics/report.go` is 402 lines. `rules/code-modularity.md` item 2: before adding to a file over 400, the new logic goes in a new file. Phase 3's box 2 adds the per-row table and the Wilson whisker to the report.

## One ordered path

1. **You:** answer items 1, 3, 4, 7, 8, 9 (provenance first), 10 and 12.
2. **Phase 2b**, with item 1's answer, item 26's note for later, and the real-home install in its standing set (item 3).
3. **Hygiene Trivial/Task:** item 6's Status line, item 22's pointer, the D-rows for items 10 and 18, and the closing D-rows from item 7. These are plan-body edits, so the Kickoff must approve them.
4. **Row 10b, the PRD reshape** (item 4), if approved.
5. **The BUG-198 guard** (item 8), if approved.
6. **The `fyr check` profile and fix** (item 5): one Task, any time; it speeds up every later step.
7. **Phase 3**, then Release 3 (item 25) on your word.
8. **The UI skills**, after Release 3, once Step 1 is answered.

## What was not checked

- The full test suite was not run. Only the three size pins were run, and they pass.
- The agy-side facts: whether agy has `--settings` (item 21), and whether two dispatches run at once (item 11).
- Whether `anthropic-skills:frontend-ui-modern` is byte-identical to the zip (item 9).
- The workers plan's D1–D141 were not re-read against the code. The previous audit covered them, and only D142–D147 are new.
- The scripts in the UI zips.

title: Review — PLAN.md cold read (2026-10-31)
body:
# Review — PLAN.md cold read   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: `PLAN.md` at the repo root (203 lines, read in full; the cold-reader check, no diff). Claims checked against the code and these records, read with `--home .agents/scratch/workers`: PLAN-2026-10-31-0300 (eval metrics), PLAN-2026-10-30-ui-skills, BUG-198, BUG-199, ADR-038, ADR-079, SPEC-fyr-check, SPEC-fyr-eval, GUIDE-testing § 3k.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

Two blocking defects. Rule 3 makes every Checkpoint write a handoff whose Kickoff is "the fixed one in § Kickoff", and PLAN.md has no such section. P3 and § Item 37 file the new bug as BUG-199, but BUG-199 is already stored as a different, fixed bug. Both are cheap to fix. The larger risks are:
- D5's behaviour is never tabulated, so P3's "every cell matches GUIDE-fyr-matrix" has no stated expected values.
- P5 reshapes the PRD so that test names become enforced, and P10 then deletes or renames tests those names point at.
- Several boxes have no Verify or Expect that can fail.
- P13 closes the plan before the release gate has run.

Many code claims were checked and are true; they are listed under Verified.

The working tree moved during the review: `AGENTS.md`, `internal/check/check.go`, `check_test.go` and `.agents/trail.jsonl` are modified, and the root `fyr` binary is gone. P1 is evidently being executed by another thread, so this report describes the plan as read at HEAD `260d0b7`.

## Findings

### BLOCKING
- **[BLOCKING / confidence: high]** `PLAN.md:28` — Rule 3 says "The handoff's Kickoff is the fixed one in § Kickoff". No `## Kickoff` heading exists. The headings are: the operator's words, Rules, Items, Item 37, Phases, Decisions, Risks. `grep -n Kickoff PLAN.md` returns only line 28. Thirteen sessions each write a handoff from that Kickoff, and a fresh session cannot reconstruct it. Fix: add § Kickoff as a fenced block giving the read order, the `--home .agents/scratch/workers` flag for every `fyr record` call (AGENTS.md § Rules for working here), "run phase N, Checkpoint, end", and the standing approvals. Or delete the reference and say that the handoff skill's default applies.
- **[BLOCKING / confidence: high]** `PLAN.md:97` and `PLAN.md:122` — "a `bug` record, BUG-199" and "BUG-199 stored". `fyr record get BUG-199` returns an existing, fixed bug ("A background test run reported as passed from the notification's exit code…", 2026-10-30). The highest stored bug is BUG-202, so the next id is BUG-203, assigned by `fyr record add`. A session following the plan literally either cites the wrong record or overwrites the numbering. Fix: write "the next BUG id (BUG-203 at 2026-10-31)", and use "the borken bug" in D5, § Item 37 and P3.

### MAJOR
- **[MAJOR / confidence: high]** `PLAN.md:97-102`, `PLAN.md:123` — The matrix test is the core of item 37, yet the plan never states the expected outcome of any cell. 2 binary kinds × 3 place kinds × 3 invocations is 18 cells, and the plan gives only prose for the failing ones. P3 box 2 says "every cell matches `GUIDE-fyr-matrix`", but box 3 is the one that changes GUIDE-fyr-matrix, so the reference is circular and a fresh session decides the cells itself. Fix: put the cell table (exit code and key message per cell) in § Item 37 or in a D-row, and make box 2's Expect "equals the table". Two related points:
  - Fix 3 uses exit 2 for "update at a zip place". `update --check` already uses exit 2 for "behind" (`cmd/fyr/ctx_verbs.go`), so an informational refusal sharing the code needs a stated reason.
  - `internal/harness/repo.go:102` currently tells a development build at a zip place to "run `fyr update --from-zip <file>` again". That is the instruction that stranded borken. It is not in the P3 list of strings to change, and fix 5 should name it.
- **[MAJOR / confidence: high]** `PLAN.md:134` (P5) against `PLAN.md:155` (P10) — The reshape adds `enforced by:` test names to the PRD, so rule (c) starts to bind. `.agents/scratch/prd-reshape/PROPOSAL.md` states this: "Any later edit of a test named in an `enforced by:` … is then a `fyr check` finding on PRD.md". The names include `TestSearchRanksARecordAboveAFile` (`cmd/fyr/record_test.go`) and `TestLoadReplacesRowsFromAChangedFile` (`internal/brain`), and P10 reworks exactly the file-era search and load code those tests probably cover. `TestUpdateFromZipVerifiedAndTampered` (R8 and R9) is in P3's area. Only P1, P5 and P12 expect `fyr check` to be clean. Fix: either run P5 after P10, or add to P5 and to each of P3, P4 and P10 the line "a renamed or removed test named in PRD.md's enforced-by is fixed in the same commit by an approved PRD edit"; and add `fyr check` to the Checkpoint of those phases.
- **[MAJOR / confidence: medium]** `PLAN.md:138` (item 1, P6) — The box names only `TestClassifyEveryReason` and `SPEC-fyr-eval` step 15. Several other places assert or describe `replaced` as an ERROR:
  - `internal/eval/row_replaced_test.go:53,76` and `internal/eval/run_sandbox_test.go:90`, which expect `StatusError` for `ReasonReplaced`;
  - `internal/eval/cause_test.go:46`;
  - `internal/eval/cause.go:15`, the comment on `errorCauses`, and the `errorCauses` map itself;
  - SPEC-fyr-eval's status table (the ERROR row lists `replaced`).
  No Verify or Expect is given, and the box does not say to grep restatements of "ERROR … replaced" (AGENTS.md describing-text rule). Fix: list these files, add `go test -race ./internal/eval ./cmd/fyr`, and Expect: "`TestRunSandboxReplaced` now asserts FAIL, and the SPEC table moves `replaced` to FAIL".
- **[MAJOR / confidence: medium]** `PLAN.md:139` (item 2, P6) and `PLAN.md:122-123` — Phase 2b's E2E box in the eval-metrics plan says "who: both" and needs a logged-in agy. P6 marks the whole box "Who: AI". It points at "the four boxes as written there", and those boxes are `[-]`. The golden-path and edge criteria live in that record's § Verification, a different section from § Interfaces. A fresh session has to open a closed record and stitch three sections together. Fix: inline the two E2E criteria and the Verify/Expect of each box, or name the exact record sections, and mark which step needs the operator or an agy login.
- **[MAJOR / confidence: medium]** `PLAN.md:155-156` (P10) — Item 33 is six removals across `internal/search`, `internal/dream`, `internal/brain`, `internal/harness` (state.go), `internal/trail` and a skill script, plus a behaviour change: "a migrated project registers for `--global`" and "the dream reads only records". It sits in one session with "test first where a behaviour changes", with no list of which behaviours change. `internal/search/global.go:70` (`globalDocsRoot = ".agents/docs"`) and `scope_prepare.go:123` show the global index registers only projects that carry `.agents/docs`. What replaces that condition is a design question the plan never answers. Also:
  - the Expect "only the import path and its tests name `.agents/docs`" will fail on `internal/trail/trail.go:132` (`DocsRoot`) and `internal/brain/brain.go:88` (`unmigrated`), both of which D4 keeps;
  - the Verify line says `scripts/restatement-grep.sh`, which does not exist at the root (the script is `skills/review/scripts/restatement-grep.sh`, as the box's own earlier sentence says);
  - item 34 should name `fyr record import --global` (`internal/brain/import_global.go`) and the proof (a dry run listing no problem, the line counts 33, 17 and 6 proposals matched to records).
  Fix: split P10 in two, or write the replacement rule for the global registration into the ADR box before the code.
- **[MAJOR / confidence: medium]** `PLAN.md:170-173` (P13) — Box 2 stores this file as a closed `plan` record and removes it from the root before box 3 runs `/preflight`. Rule 2 says a problem found during the run is added to § Items found during the run. After box 2 no plan exists, so a NO-SHIP finding or a failed gate has no home, and the last box (borken moves, Who: user) happens after the plan is closed. Also, box 1 and `/preflight` Step 6 write their own records and commit. Fix: reorder to behavioural runs, preflight, then close the plan and delete it, or state that a NO-SHIP reopens the plan. The final borken box is a post-release check outside the plan's life; say so.
- **[MAJOR / confidence: medium]** `PLAN.md:129-130` (P4, item 13) — The container work is under-specified for a security change.
  - The network: `docker network create` with `enable_icc=false`. Nothing says one network per run versus per worker, how it is labelled, how it is swept when the run is killed or `--kill` is used (the existing sweep is by label `fyr.work=<stamp>`, ADR-079), or what happens when creation fails (refuse versus run on the default bridge).
  - `--pids-limit` is 4096 today (`internal/sandbox/docker.go:74`). The plan lowers it to 1024 with no evidence that `go test -race` builds fit inside it.
  - Item 13's box does not list SPEC-fyr-work § Docker runner, an ADR amending ADR-079, or TDD § T17, although these are a restatement of container limits (rule 3 of the repo's describing-text rule). Only item 12's box mentions the SPEC.
  - "`internal/sandbox/docker*.go`" matches one file, `docker.go`; the run command is built by `dockerArgs` there.
  Fix: add the failure semantics and the docs list; and have the real docker worker run be a `go test`-bearing Kickoff so the pids limit is exercised.
- **[MAJOR / confidence: medium]** `PLAN.md:106` ("Now, by hand on borken") — Three commands for the operator on a machine the AI cannot reach, with no Verify, no Expect and no `Who:` label. Their effect is not tested: no test or record shows that `install --repo` over a zip-origin home turns it back into a checkout place (`cmd/fyr/update_checkout.go:129` suggests it is accepted, but only for `update`). Nothing says what the operator should see afterwards (`fyr version` prints a `b<sha>`, `fyr status` exits 0). Fix: label it Who: user, add the expected output, and add "report the output to the next session" so item 40 can be confirmed from it.
- **[MAJOR / confidence: medium]** `PLAN.md:195` (D5) — D5 is "by: implementer, as recommended to the operator". The table verdict (fix) is the operator's, but the design is not: exit codes, the refusal in fix 4, and the rejection of "build from the zip's source" were never approved in the operator's own turn. Rule 4 says an item's verdict changes only by the operator. Fix: either get the operator's "approved" on D5 in P1 (the cold read is the natural place), or mark P3's start as "needs the operator's approval of D5".

### MINOR
- **[MINOR / confidence: high]** `PLAN.md:122-126` — P3 box 4 (item 40) has no Verify or Expect. "Reproduce a fetch failure against an unreachable remote in a scratch checkout" is a command, but "names the way out" is never defined (the SSH-over-443 setup? `ssh.github.com:443`?). `internal/harness/repo.go:242` is the `git fetch --quiet` call. Fix: write the expected message text, or the condition ("the message contains `ssh.github.com`").
- **[MINOR / confidence: high]** `PLAN.md:165-168` (P12) — Box 1 verifies "rows thinned, each claim kept" with `fyr check`, which cannot fail on a lost claim (it checks spec freshness and links). Box 2 (prune) and box 3 (item 35) have no Verify or Expect. Item 35 names no command (`fyr render`? `fyr install --home ~/.claude`?). Fix: state each box's check, such as the rendered text diff for item 35 and a before/after `du` and listing for item 32. The prune also lists `workers/` as the keep-set but not `agents/`, which holds the Checkpoint artifacts. Say whether `agents/` is kept; `.agents/scratch/evalm` does not exist yet (P9 creates it), which is fine but worth a word.
- **[MINOR / confidence: medium]** `PLAN.md:118` (P2) — "under 30 s of CPU here" pins a machine-specific number with a "timed test", which is flaky; "the same findings as before on a mutated tree" does not say which mutated tree (the prd-reshape `check-mutant` fixtures exist, but are not named). 3m22s versus 5m16s shows large variance, so the baseline needs several runs. Fix: pin an operation count or a work-done bound in the test, and name the mutation.
- **[MINOR / confidence: medium]** `PLAN.md:160-162` (P11) — Open 5 of D3 ("each orphan put to the operator") is a user step inside a box with no `Who: user`. Box 1's comparison with "the published `anthropic-skills` copy when one is on this box" has no command and no Expect, and the fallback is a judgement the AI makes alone about vendoring a third-party skill (AGENTS.md: vendored skills are never edited, the pin comes from a `git archive` and `diff -r` check). Also `security` is named for "the new scripts", but P11 has no step reading them. UI-plan Phase 2 (the behavioural runs) is not in P11 and is deferred to P13, which is workable but should say so.
- **[MINOR / confidence: medium]** `PLAN.md:112` (P1 box 2) — `go test ./internal/check` lacks `-race` (rule 3 runs the full command at the Checkpoint, so it is harmless). SPEC-fyr-check line 61 already says "a `PLAN.md` while one exists" is outside rule (a), so the spec is ahead of the code and needs no edit; say so, or the session may add a duplicate.
- **[MINOR / confidence: medium]** `PLAN.md:203` (Risks) — "The installed `fyr` on dave refuses `metrics.db` schema 4 until P1's install" is not checked against the code and the box text for P1 does not say which binary the Checkpoint's `fyr record add` and `fyr metrics ingest` use before the install. State the binary (the tree binary) and the `--home` flag.
- **[MINOR / confidence: low]** `PLAN.md:36-77`, the closed eval plan — its `[-]` boxes say "closed 2026-10-31 (D33, `PLAN.md`)". `PLAN.md` has D1 to D5 only and D33 lives in the closed plan's record. The pointer is wrong; the UI plan's records say "D1, `PLAN.md`" and the other two say D33. No action needed beyond knowing it.
- **[MINOR / confidence: low]** `PLAN.md:171, 199` — P13 box 1 asks for "one `fyr eval` row per changed skill and agent" in `v5.0.0..HEAD`. At 260d0b7 that range has no change under `skills/`, `agents/`, `context/` or `rules/` (`git diff --stat v5.0.0..HEAD -- skills agents context rules` is empty), so the Risks list of "at least `init-project`, `review`…" is a forecast. P13 should compute the list with the `git diff --name-only` at that time and cover P8/P9's `GUIDE-eval` rows and P3's help text.

## Verified (claims in the plan that are true)
- AGENTS.md:71 holds "in git at `9001831^`".
- The root `fyr` is gitignored (`.gitignore:5: /fyr`); `skills/init-project/assets/agents-tree/docs/deploy/` is an empty untracked directory.
- `cmd/fyr/ctx_verbs.go` marks `status` and `update` as `source: true`; `internal/harness/repo.go` `ResolveSource` and `sourceCandidates` behave as § Item 37 says.
- `internal/metrics/report.go` is 402 lines.
- `notInRuleA` exists in `internal/check/check.go:65` with `ROADMAP.md` and `TODO.md`.
- `.agents/scratch/prd-reshape/PRD.diff` passes `git apply --check` at HEAD (exit 0).
- The four plans named in rule 1 are all `closed`.
- BUG-198 is open; ADR-038 and ADR-079 exist.
- GUIDE-testing § 3k covers the worker, including the docker tier.
- `fyr record import --global` already migrates `feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl` and `proposals` (`internal/brain/import_global.go`).
- The keep-set directories exist except `evalm/`.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — n/a for a plan. P10 and P1 delete the right things; the item 33 list is not tied to a grep that proves "no other reader".
2. Flow tracing — fail. The missing § Kickoff, the BUG-199 collision, the circular GUIDE-fyr-matrix reference, the P5-before-P10 enforced-by hazard and the P13 box order break the chain from one phase to the next.
3. Standards conformance — partial. The plan follows AGENTS.md's Checkpoint, security and record rules. It omits the restatement and describing-text obligations for items 1 and 13, and the `--home` rule for record writes.
4. Directory layout — pass. The new eval report code goes in a new file; the root `PLAN.md` and its removal are handled by items 38 and 39.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. D5 rejects building from the zip's source for a sound reason; no new dependency. Item 13's network and ICC handling should say it uses docker's own mechanism.
6. Decoupling — partial. P10 bundles six packages and P3 touches `cmd/fyr`, `internal/harness` and four docs in one commit, which is workable but leaves P10 oversized.

## Not examined
- The contents of `REVIEW-2026-10-31-0920` and the operator's full table beyond what the plan quotes.
- `PLAN-2026-10-29-root-docs-and-fyr-serve` and `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers` records (the D1 closing rows were assumed).
- `TDD.md` § T5, `SPEC-fyr-serve`, `GUIDE-skill-matrix` and `skills/VENDORED.md`.
- Whether the `fyr check` hot path (item 21) and `internal/serve`'s evals page exist as the plan assumes; `GOOS=darwin` builds.
- `fyr status` and `update` bodies beyond the lines quoted; the 18 matrix cells were not run.
- The in-flight P1 edits to `AGENTS.md` and `internal/check`, made by another thread during this review.

## Outcome

Answered by the P1 session on 2026-10-31, in `PLAN.md` (the same commit as this record's storage):

- BLOCKING `PLAN.md:28` no § Kickoff — fixed: `PLAN.md` § Kickoff added, the operator's fixed block verbatim.
- BLOCKING BUG-199 collision — fixed: § Item 37 fix 1 and P3 box 1 name "the next free BUG id (BUG-203 on 2026-10-31)", "the borken bug".
- MAJOR matrix cells unstated — fixed: § Item 37 § Cells (proposed), P3 box 2's Expect equals it and `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` at `260d0b7` elsewhere; fix 3's exit is 1, not 2; fix 5 names `zipNote` in `internal/harness/repo.go`.
- MAJOR P5 enforced-by vs P10 — fixed: D6 (tests named in `PRD.md` enforced-by are not renamed or removed; `fyr check` 0 findings at every Checkpoint from P5). Moving P5 after P10 instead — left: operator (an order change, rule 4).
- MAJOR item 1 restatements — fixed: P6 box 1 lists `cause.go`, `cause_test.go`, `row_replaced_test.go`, `run_sandbox_test.go`, the SPEC table, the grep, Verify and Expect.
- MAJOR P6 E2E who/sections — fixed: P6 box 2 names § Phases § Phase 2b, § Interfaces and § Verification, and the operator's agy login.
- MAJOR P10 oversized / registration rule / Verify path / Expect / item 34 — fixed: the script path, the Expect's kept names (`unmigrated()`, `trail.DocsRoot`), item 34's `fyr record import --global --dry-run` proof. The replacement registration rule (proposed: a project with `.agents/trail.jsonl`) and splitting P10 — left: operator (questions in the P1 handoff).
- MAJOR P13 closes before preflight — fixed: D7 (a NO-SHIP reopens the plan; borken's box is a post-release check carried by the handoff).
- MAJOR P4 item 13 under-specified — fixed: P4 box 2 (one labelled network per run swept by ADR-079's label sweep, refuse on create failure, pids 1024 exercised by a `go test -race` worker, the SPEC, ADR and TDD § T17 docs).
- MAJOR borken manual line — fixed: Who: user, Expect, output pasted to the next session; P3's last cell pins `install --repo` from a zip place.
- MAJOR D5 not the operator's — left: operator. D5 now says "awaiting the operator's approval"; P3 carries a gate line.
- MINOR item 40 Verify — fixed: P3 box 4's Expect (the remote URL and git's stderr).
- MINOR P12 Verify/keep-set/item 35 command — fixed: P12 boxes (claims map, `du` before/after, `agents/` kept, `diff <(fyr render) ~/.claude/AGENTS.md`).
- MINOR P2 timed test — fixed: P2 box 2 pins a work count; the mutated tree is `.agents/scratch/prd-reshape/clone` with `check-mutant.txt`.
- MINOR P11 user step / provenance — fixed: P11 boxes (`diff -r`, the orphans Who: user, `security` reads the scripts, Phase 2's runs at P13).
- MINOR P1 box 2 `-race` and spec "already ahead" — rebutted: the spec line was edited by this same P1 session while the review ran (`.agents/trail.jsonl` in the P1 diff), and the Checkpoint runs the full `-race` command.
- MINOR Risks binary — fixed: § Risks names the tree binary and `--home`.
- MINOR D33 pointer — rebutted: D33 is the closed eval plan's own closing D-row in `PLAN-2026-10-31-0300-…`, so "(D33, `PLAN.md`)" reads "closed by D33, superseded by `PLAN.md`"; it does not point into `PLAN.md`'s D-rows.
- MINOR P13 list forecast — fixed: P13 box 1 computes it with `git diff --name-only`.

No BLOCKING item is left unanswered.

title: Review — worktree-code-docs   (2026-10-31)
body:
# Review — worktree-code-docs   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: working tree vs HEAD (260d0b7): AGENTS.md, internal/check/check.go, internal/check/check_test.go, .agents/trail.jsonl (one edit: SPEC-fyr-check body, read with `fyr record get --home .agents/scratch/workers`)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE

Nothing is broken in the diff. `PLAN.md` joins `notInRuleA` beside `TODO.md` and `ROADMAP.md`, the spec sentence (SPEC-fyr-check, rule (a) exclusions) is changed in step, and the test now has a PLAN.md and a TODO.md fixture whose fyr-verb text must produce no finding. I ran a must-fail mutation in a scratch copy (`.agents/scratch/mut`): removing `"PLAN.md": true` makes `TestDocsRuleVerbs` fail with findings on PLAN.md; removing `"TODO.md": true` makes it fail with a finding on TODO.md. Both mutants compiled. The real tree passes `go test ./internal/check`, `go vet`, `gofmt -l`.

## Findings
None blocking.

## Docs lens
- SPEC-fyr-check line 61 now reads "`TODO.md`, a `PLAN.md` while one exists, and `ROADMAP.md` ...": matches the code (the code skips PLAN.md whenever present; "while one exists" is the same thing).
- Restatement grep over ROADMAP/TODO/"outside rule"/"not built yet": no other living file (README, SDD, TDD, skills, agents, GUIDE-*) restates the rule (a) exclusion list. AGENTS.md § Layout gains the PLAN.md row; README.md:225-238 root-file listing does not name PLAN.md. Not a finding: PLAN.md is temporary (its rule 5 / P13 removes it and the Layout row together).
- AGENTS.md Release: `(D11, D12 of plan `2026-10-01-google-skills-catalog`, in git at `9001831^`)` became `(D11, D12 of `PLAN-2026-10-01-google-skills-catalog`)`. title: Review — P2 code and docs, round 1 (2026-10-31)
body:
# Review — p2-check-speed (2026-10-31) Range reviewed: working tree vs HEAD 2da906b (`git diff` plus the two untracked files `internal/check/trailhistory.go` and `trailhistory_test.go`), read through `.agents/scratch/p2-check-speed/review.diff` and `review-records.diff`. ## Status: COMPLETE ## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES The bisection itself is sound, and I found no wrong answer against the old `git log -G` behaviour. The worst problem is a consequence nobody ran: committing this tree makes `fyr check` report 6 `spec-stale` findings. The one-line comment edit in `internal/serve/pages.go` counts as a commit to `internal/serve`, and six current specs name that directory and were not re-stamped (reproduced below). Next, PLAN.md says "P1 and P2 done" while every P2 box is unticked, and the kickoff re-runs the first phase with an unticked box. Then, D8 claims the pre- and post-fix findings match, but the pre-fix evidence files are still empty. Lastly, the new code reads historical blobs with no size cap. ## Findings - **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/serve/pages.go:46` — The comment-only edit makes `fyr check` fail after the commit. Reproduced: I cloned the repo into `.agents/scratch/p2-check-speed/review/clone`, copied in the 7 changed files, committed, and ran the post-fix binary from `.agents/scratch/p2-check-speed/fyr-postfix`. It gave `6 findings (specs 6)`: SPEC-fyr-dream, -eval, -memory-loop, -metrics, -record and -search, each "1 commit to internal/serve ... since ". Rule (b) counts any commit to a span-named path, and the rule's own known limit says the remedy is a re-read. Item 41 re-stamped only SPEC-fyr-serve and SPEC-fyr-work, and P2's checkpoint expects `fyr check` clean. Fix: either re-read those six specs against `pages.go` and re-stamp them (add them to item 41), or drop the `pages.go` comment edit. Dropping it leaves "each run takes minutes" stale, so re-stamping is the honest route. - **[medium / confidence: high]** `PLAN.md:3` and `PLAN.md:131-133` — The status line says "P1 and P2 done", but the three P2 boxes are `[ ]`, and so is the checkpoint box. The Kickoff (`PLAN.md` § Kickoff) says "do the first phase of PLAN.md that has an unticked box". If this tree is committed as is, the next session re-does P2. Fix: tick the boxes and write the bound into the Checkpoint, in the same commit as the status line. Also, the item 21 row (`PLAN.md:58`) says "5m16s of CPU", while D8, Risks and `SPEC-fyr-check` say 5m26s. Make them agree. - **[medium / confidence: medium]** `.agents/scratch/p2-check-speed/{check,mutant,stale}-prefix.*` and `PLAN.md` D8 — D8 asserts "Pre- and post-fix findings match on the mutated clone and on a stale fixture clone". At review time (10:26) `check-prefix.log`, `mutant-prefix.txt` and `stale-prefix.txt` are all 0 bytes, and 8 `fyr-prefix check` processes started at 10:17 are still running. Only the postfix side exists (`mutant-postfix.txt`, 4 lines; `stale-postfix.txt`, 11 lines). The claim is not yet evidence. Do not store D8 or the SPEC's "3.7 s after" until `diff` of each prefix and postfix pair is printed. The equivalence claim is a risk in its own right, because the bisection changes meaning in the cases below. - **[medium / confidence: medium]** `internal/check/trailhistory.go:270` — `cat-file blob` goes through `Output()`, so a historical `trail.jsonl` blob of any size is buffered whole. Every other read in this package and in `brain` is capped: `maxTrail`, and `maxLineRead` at 16 MiB. `fyr check` and the `/check` page read a checkout that may not be the operator's own, and old revisions are exactly where a hostile repo can plant a 2 GB blob. The old `git log -G` kept that memory inside git. Scenario: a clone with one huge historical `trail.jsonl` makes `fyr check` OOM, or the serve process with it. Fix: take the size from `ls-tree -l` (the line already read), treat a blob over `maxTrail` as a read error so the existing "trail history unreadable" note applies, and add a test with a stand-in blob. - **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/check/trailhistory.go:10`, `trailhistory_test.go:343`, `SPEC-fyr-check` (cost and Known limits), `SPEC-fyr-serve`, `GUIDE-testing`, `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` — They cite "PLAN.md item 21" and "PLAN.md D8". PLAN.md is stored as a plan record and removed from the root at P13, so these pointers dangle in living specs and in code comments. Cite the plan record id, or state the fact (a 13 MB trail, 399 revisions) without the pointer. - **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/check/trailhistory_test.go` — The SPEC's cost paragraph says the same bound holds "down a merged side", and cites the three tests. No test covers: a nested merge on the side (the recursion); an octopus merge; an error or a missing blob on the merged side (`search` returns it as a note); a merge whose own trail blob adds the line (the evil merge, which relies on the side search returning `""` and falling back to the merge); or the read count when a side is searched. The tests name nothing of this as not covered. I judge the code correct for these by reading, so this is a coverage gap, not a defect. ## Checks that found no fault - **Git invocation:** every argument built from data is a 40-hex id taken from `rev-list`, `rev-parse` or `ls-tree` (`found^@`, `^`, `cat-file blob `), after `--`-guarded pathspecs. `HEAD` is a literal. I found no injection route. - **textconv:** `ls-tree`, `rev-list`, `rev-parse` and `cat-file blob` start no textconv driver or external diff, and `cat-file` without `--textconv` applies no filter. - **Lazy fetch:** `trail.Command` sets `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, and `historyNote` still gates partial clones before `specsRule` runs. The `trail.Log` `Readable` check that the removed function carried is covered by that gate. A missing object fails and becomes a note (`TestSpecRuleGitFailureIsANote`). - **Bisection:** it is correct when the line stays once added, which is the documented limit. `sort.Search`'s `err` branch makes errors return `true` and surface through `ferr`. A root commit gives an empty parent list and the loop is skipped. - **Tests:** they can fail. `TestSpecCommitBisects` fails on a linear scan (40 reads against its bound of 19). `TestSpecRuleMergedLine` fails without the merge descent, because the count since the merge would be 0. `go test -count=1 ./internal/check` passes (2.9 s). - **Restatements:** I grepped the code, the SPEC records and the guide records. ADR-064, ADR-075a and the old CHANGE record still say `git log -G` and "3–4 minutes". Those records are never rewritten, so they are no finding. `TestSpecRuleRunsNoTextconv` can no longer fail through the new code, only through a future `git log`, which its own plain-`git log` precondition makes a live probe. That is acceptable. ## Criteria 1. Dead code — pass. `specCommit` and the `regexp` import are removed with their last caller, and `trail.Log` still has other callers (`dream`, `metrics`). 2. Flow tracing — fail on the two plan and evidence points above. The code flow (`specsRule` → `commitOf` → `search` → `holds` → `read`) is consistent, with errors propagated and cached per commit. 3. Standards conformance — fail. Describing text: the `pages.go` edit stales six specs, PLAN.md status and boxes disagree, and the 5m16s/5m26s figures disagree. No unbounded blob read exists elsewhere in the package. 4. Directory layout — pass. `trailhistory.go` and its test sit beside `specs.go` in `internal/check`, and each file is well under the line limits. 5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. It is stdlib only, with no new dependency and no security primitive. The bisection is warranted by the measurement: 5m26s against 3.7 s. 6. Decoupling — pass. `trailHistory` is a private type behind `commitOf`, and `specsRule` is its only consumer. ## Not examined - The pre-fix findings for the equivalence claim (the prefix files were empty at review time). - A mutation of the bisection or merge descent (not run; the tests were judged by reading). - Real behaviour of `rev-list --first-parent

^` when the side forked from a branch that was merged earlier (the exclusion may not follow non-first parents). I reasoned it returns extra but non-oldest commits, so the answer is unchanged, but I did not run it. - The record diff of SPEC-fyr-work (unchanged body, re-stamp only) beyond what `review-records.diff` shows. - `TDD.md` and `SDD.md` for statements about rule (b)'s git calls (none found by grep). ## Outcome 1. `pages.go` stales six specs: fixed. The six (`SPEC-fyr-dream`, `-eval`, `-memory-loop`, `-metrics`, `-record`, `-search`) were re-read against the two-line comment, which none of them describes, and re-stamped in the same commit. PLAN.md item 41 names them. A clone of the committed tree gives `check: 0 findings`. 2. PLAN.md status and boxes: fixed. The P2 boxes are ticked in the commit. The 5m16s and 5m26s figures are reconciled in D8: 5m16s was the audit's run (item 21's row), 5m26s was P1's `check.log`. 3. D8's equality claim without evidence: fixed. Pre- and post-fix findings, notes and exit codes are identical on this checkout, on the mutated clone (equal to `check-mutant.txt`), and on a stale fixture clone with 7 stale specs and a commit that only moves a line. The final binary was re-run against the pre-fix output on both clones. 4. Unbounded historical blob read: fixed (security round 1, finding 1). `ls-tree -l` size refusal, a `LimitReader` on the read, and `TestSpecRuleBlobOverCap`. 5. Dangling `PLAN.md item 21` and `D8` pointers: fixed. The living specs, the guides and the code comments state the date and the fact instead. 6. Merge coverage gap: fixed in part. `TestSpecRuleNestedMerge`, `TestSpecRuleMergeAddsTheLine` and `TestSpecRuleMergeDepth` were added, each mutation-checked (the nested test also at the second level alone). The octopus merge and an unreadable merged side are named as not tested in `SPEC-fyr-check`.

title: Review — P2 code and docs, round 2 (2026-10-31)
body:
# Review — p2-check-speed, round 2   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: the fixes since round 1, as `.agents/scratch/p2-check-speed/review-round2.diff` (trailhistory.go round 1 → round 2, the new `trailhistory_guard_test.go`, the PLAN.md diff, four record body diffs, seven re-stamps), read against the working tree (cmp'd identical to `commit-sim` for every file except PLAN.md, which is newer than the sim).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The worst problem is new and comes from the fix for security's S×N finding. The one-pass `index` in `trailhistory.go` no longer skips to the end of a line after a miss, and it scans to the line's end once per `"id":"` occurrence. A past `trail.jsonl` of 1 MiB made of `"id":"SPEC-a"` repeated with no newline took 49 s in a verbatim copy of the loop, and the cost grows with the square of the blob size, so the 256 MiB cap bounds nothing. Round 1's `holdsLine` was linear on the same input, so this is a regression introduced by round 2. The other open item is that PLAN.md says "P1 and P2 done" while the three P2 boxes are still `[ ]`. Everything else from round 1 is fixed or answered (table in Findings), and `go test -count=1 ./internal/check` passes (3.3 s), `go vet` and `gofmt -l` are clean.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/check/trailhistory.go:186-207` — `index` is quadratic in the length of a line. After each `"id":"` hit it sets `rest = rest[i+len(key):]` (it no longer jumps to the line end, as round 1's `holdsLine` did with `rest = rest[end:]`), then runs `bytes.IndexByte(rest, '\n')`, which scans to the end of the line, once per `"id":"` occurrence. This happens before the ID is looked up, so the ID need not be a spec. Failing scenario: a hostile clone has a past commit whose `.agents/trail.jsonl` is under 256 MiB, with no newline, made of `"id":"` repeated (it packs to a few KB). Measured: I copied the loop verbatim into `.agents/scratch/p2-check-speed/review2/probe/main.go` and fed it `"id":"SPEC-a"` repeated to 1 MiB. It took 49 s on this machine (loaded by the prefix runs); time grows with the square of the size. The bisection probes about log2(n) such commits, so `fyr check` or the `/check` page of `fyr serve` hangs (and `serve` then answers 409 to every later run). This is the same threat as security finding 1 and the new code reopens it by another route. The `maxTrailBlob` cap does not help, because the blob is under it. Fix: read the line end once per line and match only what the export writes. For example, process line by line, take the first `"id":"` of the line only (Known limits already says rule (b) matches `"id"` before `"updated"`, the export's order), and look up the stamp once. If several ids per line must be kept as `-G` allowed, bound the work, for example skip any line over 1 MiB. Add a test whose blob has one 4 MiB line of repeated `"id":"` and a work or time bound loose enough not to flake, and re-run the security lens on the replacement.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `PLAN.md:3` and `PLAN.md:131-133` — round 1's second finding is only half fixed. The status line now reads "P1 and P2 done", but the two P2 boxes and the P2 Checkpoint box are still `[ ]`. The Kickoff says "do the first phase of PLAN.md that has an unticked box", so a session started from this commit re-runs P2. Fix: tick the three boxes in the same commit (the Checkpoint box with its bound named), or word the status line "P2 in review" until they are ticked. The 5m16s/5m26s mismatch is answered: D8 says 5m26s is P1's `check.log` and 5m16s is item 21's row, the audit's run.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `PLAN.md:224` (D8) — "Pre- and post-fix findings, notes and exit codes are identical on this checkout, on the mutated clone ... and on a fixture clone" is still a claim without a printed `diff`. I was told to ignore the prefix files, so I did not check it (they have been written since, at 10:27–10:30). Do not store D8 until the three prefix/postfix pairs are diffed and the diffs read. D8's own list of what changes in meaning (re-added line, NUL byte) is accurate against `SPEC-fyr-check` § Known limits.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/check/trailhistory.go:115-119` — the `visited` set cannot fail any test and has no reachable path. `mergedSide` returns `found` or an error, never `""`, so a revisit of the same (merge, spec) key only happens in a cycle. With `--no-replace-objects` and `GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null` a cycle cannot form. `TestSpecRuleMergeDepth` pins the depth bound only. Mutating `visited` away changes nothing. Either remove it (the depth bound alone ends any descent) or keep it and say in its comment that it is untested defence. Not blocking.

## Round 1 findings, one by one

| Round 1 finding | State |
|---|---|
| Reviewer 1: `pages.go` comment stales six specs | Fixed. The six are re-stamped. `fyr-postfix2 check` in `commit-sim` (same trail, code and tests as the working tree) gives `0 findings`, in 2.2 s. The comment edit no longer claims "minutes", and `SPEC-fyr-serve`, `GUIDE-testing` and `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` carry the new figure. The old figure is left only as history ("3–4 minutes on 2026-10-29"). |
| Reviewer 2: PLAN.md status vs boxes; 5m16s vs 5m26s | Boxes: NOT fixed (finding 2). Figures: answered by D8. |
| Reviewer 3: D8 evidence | Open (finding 3); not examined by instruction. |
| Reviewer 4 / Security 1: unbounded blob read | Fixed by `ls-tree -l` size, over-cap blob becomes a read error and the existing note. `TestSpecRuleBlobOverCap` lowers the cap after proving the finding exists without it, and would fail if the check were removed (the stale finding would appear and the note would not). |
| Reviewer 5: dangling "PLAN.md item 21 / D8" pointers | Fixed. No such text in `internal/check`, `internal/serve` or any SPEC/GUIDE record (grep; the only left is `check.go:65` "PLAN.md item 38", not in the diff). |
| Reviewer 6: merge coverage gap | Fixed or named. Tests added for nested merge, merge that adds the line, depth. `SPEC-fyr-check` § cost now says an octopus merge and an unreadable merged side are not tested. |
| Security 2: cyclic merge descent via replace refs / grafts | Fixed. `h.git` adds `--no-replace-objects` and `GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null` (the env is non-nil from `trail.Command`, so `PATH` is kept), plus a depth bound. `TestSpecRuleIgnoresReplaceRefs` proves its graft takes effect before it asserts. The `rev-list --count` arm in `specs.go` still runs through `k.git` with replace refs live; that is the old behaviour and not a hang route, so no finding. |
| Security 3: S×N blob scan | Fixed in intent by `index`, but see finding 1: it traded S×N for a quadratic line scan. |
| Security 4: `Readable` guard gone | Fixed. `commitOf` checks `trail.Readable` before the first read. |
| Security 5: binary-blob meaning change | Fixed. Named in Known limits and D8. |

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass, with the `visited` note: unreachable defence, low. The `regexp` and `specCommit` removals from round 1 stand.
2. Flow tracing — fail on the `index` loop (finding 1). Errors for oversize, depth and a missing blob all reach `specsRule` as the "trail history unreadable" note. The new tests can fail; I read each against the code.
3. Standards conformance — fail on PLAN.md's boxes (finding 2). The describing text for the changed rule (`SPEC-fyr-check` § Its commit, § Its cost, § Known limits; the `pages.go` comment; the timing figures in the SPEC-fyr-serve, GUIDE-testing and GUIDE-fyr-matrix records) agrees with the code.
4. Directory layout — pass. The new test sits beside `trailhistory.go`, and all three files are far under the line limit.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only, no security primitive written here.
6. Decoupling — pass. `trailHistory` stays private behind `commitOf`; the only added import is `internal/trail`, already used by `check`.

## Not examined
- The prefix/postfix equivalence of findings (D8), by instruction.
- A mutation run of the new guard tests (judged by reading; I did not edit source).
- Whether the six re-stamped specs were truly re-read against their code: I checked their bodies for the stale timing claim only. No record body was diffed beyond the four in the diff.
- The probe measured a verbatim copy of `index`, not the packaged function inside `fyr check`; a real `fyr check` over a crafted history was not run.
- The octopus-merge path and an unreadable merged side (named untested in the SPEC).

## Outcome

1. Quadratic `index`: fixed in round 3. `values` scans each line once and restarts at the closing quote, so a key that opens at a value's quote is still found. `TestIndexMatchesTheRegex` compares it with the regular expression `-G` compiled over 10 edge lines and 5000 generated ones; it fails on a no-restart mutation and on `>` in place of `>=`. `TestIndexIsLinearOnALongLine` reads 8 MiB of `"id":"SPEC-a"` in 0.3 s; the quadratic mutation did not finish in 300 s.
2. PLAN.md status and boxes: fixed. The boxes are ticked in the commit.
3. D8's diffs: fixed (see round 1's Outcome, item 3). `visited` untested and unreachable: removed. The depth bound is the only limit, with a comment saying why.

Round 3 is not re-reviewed: the review rule allows at most two rounds. Its fixes are covered by the tests above, each with its mutation run.

title: Security review — P2 trail-history bisection, round 1 (2026-10-31)
body:
# Security review — p2-check-speed (rule (b) trail-history bisection)   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: HEAD 2da906b..working tree, as given in `.agents/scratch/p2-check-speed/review.diff` (PLAN.md, internal/check/{specs.go,hardening_test.go,trailhistory.go,trailhistory_test.go}, internal/serve/pages.go)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The worst problem is that a historical `trail.jsonl` blob is now read whole into the fyr process with no size limit. `trailhistory.go:125` runs `git cat-file blob <sha>` through `Cmd.Output()`, which buffers the whole blob in Go memory. HEAD's trail is capped at 256 MiB (`brain/export.go:25` `maxTrail`), but nothing caps the blobs in history. A crafted clone can carry a highly compressible multi-GB `trail.jsonl` blob in a past commit, which is a few MB in the pack. The bisection then makes `fyr check` allocate gigabytes, and `fyr serve`'s check page does the same in-process (`cmd/fyr/verb_serve.go:84,126`). The `git log -G` it replaces did not do this: pickaxe `-G` skips binary blobs, and a blob over `core.bigFileThreshold` counts as binary, so it was not loaded. The second problem is that the new merge descent can recurse with no bound when the history is cyclic. The checkout's own replace refs or grafts can make it cyclic, and `trail.Command` does not disable either one, although `internal/work/fetch.go:44-47` already does for the same reason. Textconv, lazy fetch and argument injection are all clear: `cat-file blob`, `ls-tree`, `rev-list` and `rev-parse` run no textconv or filter driver. Rule (b) is gated off for partial and shallow clones (`check.go:118`, `specs.go:15-23`). And only hex object names reach git's argument parser: the record ID and stamp are no longer passed to git at all.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/check/trailhistory.go:125` — the historical blob read has no size limit. **Scenario:** someone else's clone has a past commit whose `.agents/trail.jsonl` is a 4 GB blob of repeated bytes, a few MB compressed. HEAD's trail is small, so it passes `maxTrail`. The bisection probes that commit, and `Output()` buffers 4 GB, so the operator's machine OOM-kills `fyr check` or the long-running `fyr serve`. The probe point is predictable (the midpoints of the first-parent trail commits), and the attacker can put a bomb in every trail commit. This is a regression: git's `-G` skipped such a blob as binary. **Remediation:** get the size in the same call with `git ls-tree -l` (or `cat-file -s`), and when a blob is over `maxTrail` treat the commit as unreadable. Record it in `h.failed` and give the existing "trail history unreadable: spec not checked" note, never a silent pass. Or read through `StdoutPipe` with `io.LimitReader(maxTrail+1)` and refuse past the cap. Pin it with a test that lowers the cap, the way `brain/security_test.go:73` does.

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `internal/check/trailhistory.go:68-78` — the merge descent in `search` has no visited set and no depth limit. **Scenario:** the checkout's `.git` holds a `refs/replace/*` entry or an `info/grafts` line that rewires an ancestor on a merge's second-parent side to have that merge as its parent. `rev-list --first-parent P1 ^P0` then lists the merge M itself. The bisection lands on M again (it holds the line), `rev-parse M^@` returns the same parents, and `search` recurses into the same side forever. Every level starts two git processes and reads no blob, because `held` is cached, so it does not crash fast: it hangs for hours. While it hangs, `fyr serve`'s check page answers 409 to every later run (`pages.go:52`). `trail.Command` strips `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS` and `GIT_GRAFT_FILE`-style overrides from fyr's caller but passes no `--no-replace-objects`. The checkout's own replace refs and grafts therefore stay live. The repository already treats this as a threat for a checkout an agent wrote (`internal/work/fetch.go:38-47`). I did not build a cyclic fixture to confirm this (no exploit), so the confidence is medium. **Remediation:** run the history reads with `--no-replace-objects` and `GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null`, as `leadGit` does. Also give `search` a per-spec visited set of merge commits already descended, plus a depth limit that ends in the "unreadable" note. Even an acyclic history with many nested merges currently costs a `rev-list` per level per spec, with no cache.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/check/trailhistory.go:130` with `:141` — every blob read is scanned once per spec (`bytes.Index` over the whole blob for each of S specs), so the cost is S×N per blob. HEAD's trail can be up to 256 MiB, which allows on the order of 10^5–10^6 minimal spec records. A crafted trail of many tiny `current` specs plus a large blob makes one probe cost about 10^14 byte comparisons. This is not worse in order than the `S × n diffs` of the old `git log -G`, so it is not a regression, but it is still not bounded. **Remediation:** index each blob in one pass. Find each `"id":"`, take the ID up to the closing quote, look it up in a map of spec ID to stamp, and check the stamp on the rest of that line. That is O(N) per blob whatever S is.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/check/trailhistory.go:68,74,117,125` — some defence in depth is gone. The old `trail.Log` refused a partial clone on a git older than 2.44 itself (`trail.go:186`). The new reads go through `k.git` (`trail.Command`), which sets `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` but does not check `Readable`. Today `check.go:118` gates rule (b) on `historyNote`, and that covers `PartialClone || !Readable`, so nothing can fetch now. A future caller of `trailHistory` outside `specsRule` would lose the guard. **Remediation:** check `trail.Readable(k.top)` once in `trailHistory`/`commitOf` and return an error, or note that dependency in a comment on `trailHistory`.

- **[info / confidence: medium]** `internal/check/trailhistory.go:125-134` — the meaning changed for binary blobs. `-G` skipped a blob git classed as binary (a NUL byte, or over `bigFileThreshold`); `holdsLine` now matches any blob. This does not affect security beyond the first finding, but PLAN.md D8 says "pre- and post-fix findings match", and that is not true for such blobs. It may belong in `SPEC-fyr-check` § Known limits.

## Checked

- Secrets: none in the diff. The PLAN.md, test and comment text holds no credential-shaped strings.
- Injection: the git arguments are fixed verbs plus object names that `rev-list`/`rev-parse`/`ls-tree` output (hex). `found+"^@"` and `"^"+parents[0]` come from those. The record ID and stamp now go only to `bytes.Index`, never to git, and `validID` limits the ID's characters. `ls-tree`'s output is split on whitespace, and `f[1]=="blob"` excludes gitlinks. A symlink entry is a small blob (its target path), which is harmless.
- Program execution from the checkout: `cat-file blob` (no `--textconv`/`--filters`), `ls-tree`, `rev-list` and `rev-parse` read no diff driver, textconv or filter. `trail.Command` keeps `core.fsmonitor=false` and `log.showSignature=false`. `TestSpecRuleRunsNoTextconv` still proves its driver is live with a plain `git log -G` before it asserts that fyr check does not start it.
- Lazy fetch: rule (b) does not run on a partial or shallow clone (`check.go:118`, `specs.go:15-23`), and `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` is on every call. git here is 2.47.3.
- Authz/authn: no surface touched. `pages.go` changes only a comment, and the TryLock single-run guard is unchanged.
- Crypto: none touched, nothing hand-rolled.
- Dependencies: `go.mod`/`go.sum` are unchanged, and the `regexp` import was dropped. `govulncheck ./...` reports 0 vulnerabilities affecting the code, plus 1 in a required module that is not called (the known one).
- GCP surface: none touched.

## Not examined

- No probe repository: the replace-ref/graft cycle (finding 2) and the blob-size bomb (finding 1) were reasoned from git's documented behaviour and not reproduced, by design (no exploits).
- I did not run `go test` on the changed tests; that is the verifier's lane.
- `brain.readRecords` record validation beyond `validID` (whether `Updated` is format-checked) was not read in full; it affects correctness only, not this boundary.
- The rest of `internal/check` (docs, traces, requirements rules) was not read because the diff does not change them. The rule (b) `rev-list --count` arm (specs.go:46-60) is unchanged and was not re-reviewed.
- `npm audit`: not applicable, because the diff touches no JS ecosystem.

## Outcome

1. Unbounded historical blob read: fixed. The size comes from `ls-tree -l` before the read, a blob over 256 MiB (`maxTrailBlob`, brain's trail cap) is refused with the spec's "trail history unreadable" note, and the read itself goes through `io.LimitReader`. `TestSpecRuleBlobOverCap` fails with the size check removed.
2. Merge descent unbounded or cyclic: fixed. The history reads run with `--no-replace-objects` and `GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null`, plus `core.commitGraph=false` from round 2, and the descent is bounded at 64 merges. `TestSpecRuleIgnoresReplaceRefs` and `TestSpecRuleMergeDepth` fail with each guard removed. A visited set was added in round 2 and then removed as unreachable: without replace refs and grafts the history is acyclic, and each level is older.
3. The S×N scan per blob: fixed, as one pass per line. Round 2 found the first one-pass index quadratic; round 3 replaced it (see the round-2 record).
4. The `Readable` guard: fixed. `commitOf` checks `trail.Readable` itself before the first read.
5. Binary blobs no longer skipped: answered. `SPEC-fyr-check` § Known limits says so, and PLAN.md D8 lists it among the changes in meaning.

title: Security review — P2 trail-history bisection, round 2 (2026-10-31)
body:
# Security review — p2-check-speed round 2 (fixes only)   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: the round-1 findings (`.agents/scratch/agents/security-2026-10-31-1023.md`) against `.agents/scratch/p2-check-speed/review-round2.diff`, which takes `internal/check/trailhistory.go` from round 1 to round 2 and adds `internal/check/trailhistory_guard_test.go`. The working tree is on HEAD 2da906b. I also re-read `internal/check/specs.go:1-90`, `internal/trail/trail.go:151-190` and `internal/work/fetch.go:38-47`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The worst problem is new and comes from the fix for round-1 finding 3. The "one-pass" index in `trailhistory.go:186-208` is quadratic in line length. For every `"id":"` it finds, it scans forward to the end of that line (`bytes.IndexByte(rest, '\n')`, `:195`), and when the ID is a known spec it also runs `bytes.Contains` over the rest of the line (`:202`). It then moves forward only past the key, not past the line. A past `trail.jsonl` blob under the 256 MiB cap, made of one line that repeats `"id":"x"`, holds about 3×10^7 keys. Each key scans a mean of 128 MiB, about 4×10^15 bytes in total: days of CPU in `fyr check`, or in `fyr serve`, where the TryLock answers 409 to every later run until it ends. All four round-1 findings are otherwise fixed:
- The size cap is checked before the read, and the test lowers it.
- Replace refs and grafts are off on every read in `trailhistory.go`.
- The descent has a visited set and a depth bound.
- `Readable` is checked in `commitOf`.

The `rev-list --count` in `specs.go:48-55` still runs with replace refs live, so the bisection and the count read two different histories. That lets a checkout's own replace ref turn a stale spec clean. It is a lint-integrity issue, not a DoS.

## Round-1 findings: status

- **F1, blob size cap — fixed.** `read` (`trailhistory.go:163-181`) runs `ls-tree -l` and refuses a size over `maxTrailBlob`, or one that does not parse, before `cat-file`. The refusal goes into `h.failed`, so the spec gets the "trail history unreadable" note and never a silent pass. `TestSpecRuleBlobOverCap` lowers the cap to 64 and gets the note. Without the check, the 64-byte cap would not trip and the spec would be reported stale, so the test fails without the fix.
- **F2, replace refs, grafts, descent bound — fixed for the bisection, not for the count.** All three history reads in the file (`rev-list` `:136`, `rev-parse ^@` `:107`, `ls-tree`/`cat-file` `:164,175`) go through `h.git`. `h.git` adds `--no-replace-objects` as a global option before the subcommand and sets `GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null`. `trail.Command` sets `cmd.Env` to a non-nil value, so the append keeps the rest of the environment. The visited key `found+" "+r.ID` cannot fire falsely on an acyclic graph, because each level descends one side only. `maxMergeDepth` alone already ends a cycle. `TestSpecRuleIgnoresReplaceRefs` fails without the fix: with the graft live, the bisection lands on HEAD, the count is 0, and the spec comes out clean. The count arm that is still live is finding 2 below.
- **F3, one-pass index — S×N removed, but replaced by something worse in the worst case** (finding 1 below).
- **F4, `Readable` guard — fixed** at `trailhistory.go:70-72`, before the first history read.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/check/trailhistory.go:189-206` — the index is quadratic in line length. This is new in round 2. **Scenario:** a cloned repository has a past commit whose `trail.jsonl` is one line of about 250 MiB that repeats `"id":"x"`. That is under the cap and compresses to almost nothing. The bisection probes that commit, which is predictable because the probes are the midpoints of the first-parent trail commits. Each of about 3×10^7 iterations calls `IndexByte` to the line's end, so the run takes days. Repeating a real spec ID adds a `bytes.Contains` over the same remainder each time. A crafted HEAD trail is not needed. **Remediation:** split the blob into lines once (`IndexByte` once per line) and handle every key within that line before moving past it. To keep the `-G` semantics of `"id":"<ID>".*"updated":"<stamp>"` linear, scan each line from right to left and keep the set of `"updated":"<s>"` values seen so far. Then mark an ID when `stamps[id]` is in the suffix set at its position. That is O(line) whatever the number of keys or specs. A cheaper alternative: refuse (note) any line with more than a small number of `"id":"` keys. Pin it with a test that times or counts the work on a one-line blob of many keys, the way `reads` is counted now.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/check/specs.go:48-55` — the `rev-list --count <commit>..HEAD` still uses `k.git`, with replace refs and grafts live. The bisection ignores them, so the two arms of rule (b) read different histories. **Scenario:** an agent session that can write the checkout's `.git` (the threat `internal/work/fetch.go:38-47` names) adds a replace ref. The ref maps HEAD to a commit that has the spec commit's tree and the spec commit as its parent. The bisection, reading the real objects, finds the spec commit. The count, reading the replaced HEAD, sees no code change and gives 0, so a stale spec is reported clean. The comment at `trailhistory.go:51-53` ("the history read is the one the commits record") and the test header at `trailhistory_guard_test.go:37-40` claim more than the rule does. This is not a DoS: `rev-list` ends on a cycle through its SEEN flags. **Remediation:** run the count through the same graft-free, replace-free git as `h.git`, for example by moving `git` to the checker or passing `h.git` to the count. Add a test with a `git replace` of HEAD that leaves the spec stale.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/check/trailhistory.go:54-58` — `--no-replace-objects` and `GIT_GRAFT_FILE` do not cover `.git/objects/info/commit-graph`. git trusts the parent lists in that file when it parses a commit. A forged graph can rewire parents for the bisection and for the count alike: a false clean or a false stale, bounded by the depth limit. `leadGit` has the same gap, and its comment accepts "the rest of the lead's .git" under the operator-uid threat model. So this is consistent with the precedent, and it is recorded here only so the comment's claim is not read as complete. **Remediation, if wanted:** add `-c core.commitGraph=false` to `h.git` (and to `leadGit`), or narrow the comment.

- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/check/trailhistory.go:172-175` — the cap depends on `ls-tree -l`'s size, read in a separate call, while `cat-file blob` is still read whole by `Output()`. git checks that the inflated length of a loose or packed object matches its header. The size is therefore trustworthy for one consistent object store, and with replace refs off both calls resolve the same OID. What is left is a race: a writer that swaps the loose object file for that OID between the two calls (git does not re-hash on read) gets an unbounded read again. **Remediation:** read `cat-file` through `StdoutPipe` and `io.LimitReader(maxTrailBlob+1)`, and refuse past the cap. The bound then does not depend on a second process.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/check/trailhistory.go:120-127` — `rev-list` is not cached in the descent. Each spec, at each of up to 64 levels, runs one `rev-list` per merged parent until one holds the line. An octopus merge with P parents costs P processes per level per spec, so a crafted tree of nested octopus merges costs about S × 64 × P git processes. It is bounded, which round 1 was not, and blob reads are cached. **Remediation:** memoise `commits(p, "^"+parents[0])` by its arguments, so the cost no longer grows with S.

- **[info]** `ls-tree` output parsing (`:168-171`) is sound. The path is fixed, and ls-tree matches it literally (no wildcard, no prefix-of-name match). The OID and size come from the same line, even when a crafted tree has duplicate entries. A tree, a gitlink or a missing entry gives "holds none", which is the same as a deleted file. Path quoting changes only the fifth field and later ones. The visited set has no test (no cyclic fixture), but `TestSpecRuleMergeDepth` pins the depth bound, and that bound alone ends a cycle.

## Checked

- Secrets: none in the fix diff or the new test.
- Injection: git arguments are still fixed verbs plus hex OIDs from git's own output, and `--no-replace-objects` is a global option placed before the subcommand. No record ID or stamp reaches git.
- Authz/authn: no surface touched.
- Crypto: none touched, nothing hand-rolled.
- Dependencies: `go.mod`/`go.sum` are unchanged (absent from `git status` and from the diff). The new imports are stdlib only (`errors`, `os`, `strconv`). I did not re-run `govulncheck`: round 1 got 0 called vulnerabilities on the same module graph. `npm audit` does not apply.
- GCP surface: none touched.
- Tests: `go test -count=1 -run 'TestSpecRule|TestSpecCommit' ./internal/check/` passed, with git 2.47.3. I reasoned that the guard tests fail without each fix (above); I did not mutate the code to confirm it.

## Not examined

- No probe repository and no timing run: the quadratic index (finding 1), the replace-ref false clean (finding 2) and the commit-graph rewiring (finding 3) are reasoned from the code and from git's documented behaviour, not reproduced (no exploits).
- The full `go test -race ./...` is the verifier's lane, not run here.
- The PLAN.md and record hunks of the round-2 diff were not reviewed (docs).
- The rest of `internal/check` and `trailhistory_test.go`, apart from the helpers the guard test uses, were not re-read.

## Outcome

1. Quadratic `index`: fixed in round 3 (see the code review round 2 Outcome, item 1).
2. The `rev-list --count` honours replace refs: fixed. The count runs through the same git options as the history reads (`h.git`). `TestSpecRuleCountIgnoresReplaceRefs` replaces HEAD with the spec's own commit and fails when the count goes back to plain `k.git`.
3. Commit-graph rewiring: fixed for `fyr check` with `-c core.commitGraph=false` on every history read and on the count. It is not tested: no fixture crafts a commit-graph, and `SPEC-fyr-check` names this gap. `leadGit`'s same gap is PLAN.md item 42, fixed in P4.
4. The `ls-tree`/`cat-file` race (low): fixed with the `LimitReader` on the read.

Round 3 is not re-reviewed: the review rule allows at most two rounds.

title: Review — Antigravity (agy) integration audit against the four-strategy reference (2026-10-31)
body:
# Review — Antigravity (`agy`) integration audit against the operator's four-strategy reference   (2026-10-31)

Scope:
- How `fyr` starts, streams from, permissions and cancels `agy` 1.4.12 on dave, checked against the reference the operator pasted on 2026-10-31.
- That reference covers four strategies: the headless CLI in one-shot or persistent stream-json form, ACP, remote control, and the Python SDK.
- Method: read-only. `agy --help` was run and the code read; the recon brief is `.agents/scratch/agents/explorer-2026-10-31-1058.md`. No model turn was started.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: STAY on one-shot `agy -p`, one fresh process per run

Every `agy` run fyr makes is one unattended turn lasting minutes:
- the sandbox `Session` for `fyr eval` and `fyr work`: `agy -p … --mode accept-edits --print-timeout`, with `cmd.Dir` set to the clone (`internal/sandbox/session.go:68`);
- the dream: `--input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --mode plan -p ""`, with the prompt on stdin (`internal/dream/dream.go:231`);
- the oracle: `-p /<cmd> --output-format json` (`internal/dream/agy_visible.go:144`).

No run is multi-turn: `--conversation` and `--continue` are unused, and eval's second prompt is a fresh process. `fyr serve` never starts `agy`. Nothing in fyr asks a human to approve a tool call mid-turn.

The reference's Option A (a persistent stream-json process) saves start-up time that does not matter here, and adds lifecycle and cancellation risk. Option C (`agy_acp_server`) pays off only with a human approval UI, which fyr does not have and R0 does not call for. The SDK cannot use the subscription.

## Findings and proposals

| # | Problem | Proposal |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The reference's Option A, a persistent bidirectional stream-json process | strike: no multi-turn run, start-up time immaterial |
| 2 | The reference's Option C, `agy_acp_server` | strike: no mid-turn human approval anywhere in fyr; a 320–560 MB binary that lags `agy` |
| 3 | The Python SDK, remote control and community ACP wrappers | strike: the SDK needs pay-as-you-go keys and Python (R4); remote control has no API; wrappers carry the reference's own terms-of-service warning |
| 4 | Reference gotcha 1, "omit `-p` with `--input-format stream-json`": `agy --help` on 1.4.12 says `--input-format` is "for print mode", and the dream passes `-p ""`. Only a fake agy pins this (`internal/dream/fakeagy_test.go`). No real 1.4.12 stream-json capture exists, and the oracle's fixtures are from 1.4.9 | fix: one real dream turn on 1.4.12, its stream-json kept as a fixture; the dream's argv changes only if that run fails |
| 5 | Reference gotcha 2, `--add-dir`: never passed. The host runner confines nothing before the run. Work and eval grant `write_file(*)` and `command(*)` (`internal/work/worker.go:16`, `internal/eval/row.go:27`). The after-run fingerprint covers `~/.config/fyr`, `~/.gemini/config` and the real `settings.json`, not `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/scratch` or other paths | fix: an eval probe row that lists what a host run writes outside the clone, including the sandbox HOME's `antigravity-cli/scratch`; pass `--add-dir <clone>` only if the probe shows writes there. The docker runner stays the confinement |
| 6 | The real OAuth token is symlinked into the host sandbox and bind-mounted read-write into docker, so a session can corrupt the login (`internal/dream/agy_home.go:43,81`, and the sandbox) | defer: a design question. A read-only copy loses a refreshed token, and a read-write link lets the session write it. Options to the operator |
| 7 | Reference gotcha 3, the D-Bus keyring: on dave the login is the file `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/antigravity-oauth-token` (0600), and runs work with no D-Bus variable passed (`internal/sandbox/env.go`). Unknown on a Linux with a secret-service keyring | defer: check on borken when the operator is there (Who: user). If agy there needs D-Bus, the allowlist gains `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` |
| 8 | Reference gotcha 4, `modelProvider`: not set in dave's `settings.json`, and fyr never reads or guards it | strike: the operator's own setting; no evidence it is ever set |
| 9 | `--json-schema` (on 1.4.12) could replace the dream's hand-parsed answer (`parse()` in `internal/dream/response.go`) | defer: a design question, after #4's real capture shows how the schema-checked result arrives in stream-json |
| 10 | Parsing depends on undocumented wording and shapes (`auto-denied`, the oracle's 36 settings keys, a conversation `.db` needle), so an agy upgrade can break a check silently | fix, with #4: real 1.4.12 captures as fixtures, and a test that fails loudly when a needed shape is missing |

## Not examined

- No model turn was run: #4, #5 and #9 need one each, which spends the operator's quota and needs their approval.
- borken, the Mac and any keyring-backed Linux.
- The reference's documentation URLs were not fetched, and its claims were checked only against `agy --help` and fyr's code.

title: Review — P3 code and docs, round 1 (2026-10-31)
body:
# Review — p3 zip place fix (BUG-203, ADR-082)   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: .agents/scratch/p3-borken/p3.diff (working tree vs 73efcfb), code + docs lens

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The fix does what ADR-082 says: I read every changed hunk against the code and found no correctness or security defect in it. `gofmt -l`, `go vet`, `go test ./cmd/fyr ./internal/harness` and `TestHarnessMap` pass. The 24 cells of `TestPlaceMatrix` match GUIDE-fyr-matrix row for row. BUG-203's line numbers for `zip_place.go` match the file. One living doc was made false and the diff does not touch it: the harness-audit baseline command (finding 1). The rest is low severity.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md:36` — the IN area's baseline says "when a release zip is at hand, `fyr update --from-zip <zip> --home <the baseline's scratch home> --dry-run`". `SKILL.md:36` (Step 0.3) makes that home with `go run ./cmd/fyr install --home …`, a development build, so its manifest records the checkout path. `refuseDevelZipOverPath` (`cmd/fyr/zip_place.go:322`, called at `run_dispatch.go:155` before the dry-run return) now refuses a development build's `--from-zip`, `--dry-run` too: the matrix cell `devel/checkout/update --from-zip ZIP --dry-run` exits 1. Failure: the next harness audit runs the stated baseline, gets exit 1 and "which no zip replaces", and either records a false "zip path broken" first finding or silently skips the measure.
