Fix: say the command needs a release binary (or a binary-only scratch home made by a release build), or drop the clause; the restatement grep over `from-zip` found no other living file with this shape (README, context/, agents/, rules/, other skills).
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/help_text.go:83` — the help says a development build "refuses it at a checkout's place". The code, ADR-082 and PLAN D12 refuse it at every place whose manifest records a tree, a plain copy included (`st.Origin().Kind == OriginPath && st.Repo != ""`). An operator with a plain-copy place reads the page as "not refused for me". Fix: "at a place installed from a tree" (TDD.md's row already says that).
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/repo.go:246-251` — the new fetch error prints the URL from `git ls-remote --get-url` unredacted, and appends the GitHub port-443 hint to every fetch failure. A remote with credentials in the URL (`https://user:token@host/…`) now prints them in `fyr update` output, which an operator pastes into chats and records. Git's own text may already do so in some versions, so this is not new by much. Fix: strip userinfo from the URL before printing. The hint is a smaller matter: an auth failure on a non-GitHub remote still gets it.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `cmd/fyr/run_dispatch.go:155` — `refuseDevelZipOverPath(c.home)` runs before `c.migrateStateDir()`. A home that still has its state in the pre-rename `~/.config/sh-agent` reads as "not found", so a development build's `--from-zip` passes the new refusal and then converts the tree place into a zip place after the migration. I did not run this; it applies only to a place that never ran a post-rename fyr, so I rank it low.

## Docs check
- ADR-082, BUG-203, SPEC-fyr-delivery § The model, GUIDE-fyr-matrix § Binary × place × command: every claim I checked matches the code (status from manifest with `source none`, exit 0 or 1 on a missing file; `update` refused with exit 1, `--check` and `--dry-run` too; `--from-zip` plus the "did not move" line; refusal at tree-recorded places; unreadable manifest refuses; release cells unchanged; 24 cells).
- Rule 3: the map change is one label on the zip-place node; ADR-082 exists and `TestHarnessMap` passes. No edge was added, so the dashed/solid rule (4) is not touched.
- Rule 6: the development-build sentence sits in SPEC § The model; README adds a one-line pointer; TDD.md's row and the help page describe command behaviour, not the delivery claim. No restatement of the claim was changed away from its home. SPEC § How a machine gets the harness item 3 ("moved forward by repeating … `--from-zip`") stays true for a release binary.
- README.md:46 and :112 and AGENTS.md rule 1 still read true: they describe the release-binary path.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass: `zipAdvice`, `develZipNote`, `statusWithoutSource`, `refuseDevelZipOverPath`, `zipPlaceWithoutSource` all have callers; `gitCleanEnvStrip` is used by the rig.
2. Flow tracing — pass: `run` → `resolveSource` → `zipPlaceWithoutSource` for `status` and `update` only; `--repo` and `FYR_REPO` keep their own error; `--from-zip` check precedes the dry-run return and all writes; `installZip` reports the note after `installFiles`. Edge in finding 4.
3. Standards conformance — fail on one restatement (finding 1) and one imprecise help line (finding 2); otherwise pass. The mutation claim for `TestDevelZipRefusesUnreadableManifest` was not re-run.
4. Directory layout — pass: `zip_place.go` and `place_matrix_test.go` beside their package (`cmd/fyr`); each under 350 lines.
5. Simplicity — pass: stdlib only, no crypto or auth code added.
6. Decoupling — pass: the zip-place answers sit in one new file; `internal/harness` stays free of `cmd/fyr` text except the not-found note.

## Not examined
Full `go test -race ./...` (only `cmd/fyr`, `internal/harness` and the map pin were run, without `-race`). The "8 cells failed before the fix" claim in BUG-203 and its mutation check (not re-run; the cell list is consistent with it). `PLAN.md` item 40's operator output (not pasted per D12). `.agents/trail.jsonl` beyond the four named records. DEPLOY-* and GUIDE-testing records were searched, not read in full.

## Outcome

1. `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md:36`, whose zip dry run would now be refused: fixed. The step now uses a fresh scratch home and says why (ADR-082). It is a docs edit, so it has no test; round 2 confirmed it closed.
2. The help text said "at a checkout's place": fixed. It now reads "where a tree was installed". `TestHelpPageShape` holds at 10 lines.
3. The fetch error printed the URL with its credentials: fixed. Security finding 1, rounds 1 and 2, has the tests. The port-443 hint is kept: it is one clause, worded for its one case.
4. The guard ran before `migrateStateDir`: fixed. Security finding 2 has the test; round 2's change moved the guard below the migration.

title: Review — P3 code and docs, round 2 (2026-10-31)
body:
# Review — p3 zip place fix, round 2 (fixes only)   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: .agents/scratch/p3-borken/p3-r2.diff (working tree vs 73efcfb), the round-2 fixes against round 1 (reviewer-2026-10-31-1135.md)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The round-2 sh-agent refusal (`cmd/fyr/zip_place.go:446`) breaks three existing tests in `cmd/fyr`: `go test ./cmd/fyr` fails. The tests are `TestUpdateFromZipMigrationRefused` and the sub-tests `writes update --from-zip` and `reads update --from-zip …/absent.zip` of `TestStateDirMigrationByVerb`. All three run `update --from-zip` as the test binary, which is a development build, over a home that holds `~/.config/sh-agent`. The new refusal now fires before the migration they pin (plan fyr D13), and none of the three is in the diff. Every other round-1 finding is closed, and I found no new defect in the fixes. `gofmt` and `go vet` are clean. All other packages pass (`go test` over the root package, `internal/*` and `internal/harness`). `TestHarnessMap`, the `TestHelp*` pins, `TestBehindFetchErrorNamesTheRemote`, `TestRemoteForDisplay` and `TestBehindFetchErrorHidesCredentials` pass.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/run_dispatch.go:155` with `cmd/fyr/zip_place.go:446` — `refuseDevelZipOverPath` runs before `c.migrateStateDir()` and refuses every development build's `--from-zip` over a home that has `~/.config/sh-agent`. Three tests written for the migration now fail, and the cause is the diff, not an earlier break:
  - `TestUpdateFromZipMigrationRefused` (`run_arms_test.go:41`) wants "~/.config/sh-agent is a symlink" and gets "this home still holds ~/.config/sh-agent … run `fyr install --repo <checkout>` first".
  - `TestStateDirMigrationByVerb/writes_update_--from-zip` (`migrate_test.go:88-94`) wants `update --from-zip` to migrate the old directory and print the migration line exactly once, and neither happens.
  - `TestStateDirMigrationByVerb/reads_update_--from-zip_…absent.zip` (`migrate_test.go:112`) wants the read-only notice once on stderr, and it prints 0 times.

  The refusal itself is by design (ADR-082, `TestDevelZipRefusesUnmigratedHome`), so the old tests are what is out of date. They need the release path, since the refusal is for a development build only. Fix: run those three cases as a release build, with `version` set to a release string as `runAs(t, matrixRelease, …)` does, so the migration and the notice stay pinned for the build that reaches them. If the migration for a development build is meant to stay, move the guard below `migrateStateDir()` instead. Either way, run the full `go test ./cmd/fyr` before the claim of done, because the report says the fixes are tested.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/repo.go:234-239` — `ShellArg` falls back to `strconv.Quote` (double quotes) for a path with a control character. A double-quoted string in a shell still expands `$(…)`, backticks and `$x`, so a manifest path holding both a control character and `$(cmd)` prints a command that is unsafe to paste, which is the failure `ShellArg` exists to prevent. Reaching it needs a path that was written by something other than fyr's own install, so I rank it low. Fix: refuse to print the suggestion for such a path (say "the recorded path holds a control character; fix the manifest"), or escape `$`, backtick and `\` too.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/harness/repo.go:216` — `remoteForDisplay` drops userinfo only. A token in a URL's query string or fragment (`https://host/x.git?token=…`) would print. Git remotes do not carry one in practice; noted, not blocking.

## Round-1 findings, closed or not
1. Baseline `--from-zip` in `areas.md:36` — closed. The command now says "a fresh scratch home", with the reason (ADR-082). A fresh home has no manifest, so the matrix cell `devel/binary/update --from-zip` (exit 0) is the path it takes, and `--dry-run` passes the same guard.
2. Help text "at a checkout's place" — closed. `help_text.go:83` now says "where a tree was installed". `TestHelpLinesFit` passes. TDD.md's row matches the code (`st.Origin().Kind == OriginPath && st.Repo != ""`).
3. Credentials in the fetch error — closed for userinfo. `remoteForDisplay` handles `scheme://user:pw@`, scp-like `user@host:path` and `user:pw@host:path`, and is pinned by `TestRemoteForDisplay` and, through `Behind`, by `TestBehindFetchErrorHidesCredentials`. The port-443 hint is kept on purpose; its wording "on GitHub over SSH with port 22 blocked" now scopes it, so I leave it. The local `url` variable in `Behind` shadows the `net/url` import only inside its `if`, which compiles and is harmless.
4. Refusal before migration — closed in effect (a home on `~/.config/sh-agent` is refused, covered by `TestDevelZipRefusesUnmigratedHome` for a real run and a dry run, and nothing moves), but see the finding above for what it cost.

## Docs match
ADR-082, BUG-203 and PLAN D12 describe the code as it is now: the sh-agent refusal, the single-quoted path, the userinfo-free URL, `Behind`'s message and 24 matrix cells (I counted 24 `placeCells` entries). GUIDE-fyr-matrix has the sh-agent row and the quoting note. The README map label and the TDD row are consistent. A grep for the old advice ("from-zip <file> again", "refuses it at a checkout") finds only the release-binary copy in `zip_place.go:474` and the comments about the old bug. No stale restatement.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass: `notPrintable`, `ShellArg` and `remoteForDisplay` all have callers.
2. Flow tracing — fail: the new guard sits ahead of `migrateStateDir`, and three tests that pin the order fail (finding 1).
3. Standards conformance — fail on the same finding (a test suite red at the claim of done); docs otherwise match.
4. Directory layout — pass.
5. Simplicity — pass: stdlib only (`net/url`, `unicode`), no crypto or auth code added.
6. Decoupling — pass: `ShellArg` is exported from `internal/harness` for the one caller in `cmd/fyr`, which is small and fine.

## Not examined
The rest of the diff (not re-reviewed as asked). I did not re-run the mutation claim for `TestDevelZipRefusesUnreadableManifest`, nor `-race`, nor a real fetch failure against GitHub. `.agents/trail.jsonl` beyond ADR-082, GUIDE-fyr-matrix and BUG-203.

## Outcome

Past the two-round cap, as in P2: fixed without a third round. Each fix has a test that fails without it.

1. The guard before `migrateStateDir` broke `TestUpdateFromZipMigrationRefused` and `TestStateDirMigrationByVerb`'s two `--from-zip` cases: fixed. The guard now runs after the migration (`cmd/fyr/run_dispatch.go`). The three tests pass again, and so does the rewritten `TestDevelZipRefusesUnmigratedHome`: the real run migrates, then refuses from the moved manifest; the dry run refuses. Before any fix that test was red on both runs (exit 0, installed). No commit carried the break: it came from round 1's fix, checked then with focused tests only. The full suite now runs before every checkpoint claim.
2. `ShellArg`'s double quotes: fixed. Bash and zsh read the `$'…'` escapes back; `TestShellArgRoundTrips` round-trips through bash, with `$(…)` and backticks in the path, and asserts nothing ran. It was red before the fix: bash ran the `touch`.
3. A query token: fixed. Security round 2, finding 3 has the test case.

title: Security review — P3 zip place and fetch error, round 1 (2026-10-31)
body:
# Security review — p3 zip place / fetch error   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: 73efcfb..working tree, as given in .agents/scratch/p3-borken/p3.diff (13 files; code: cmd/fyr/{run_dispatch,status,update_zip,verb_install,zip_place,help_text}.go, internal/harness/repo.go; tests: cmd/fyr/place_matrix_test.go, internal/harness/{source_git_test,zip_test}.go; docs PLAN.md, README.md, TDD.md not reviewed for security content)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Worst: the new fetch-failure message in `harness.Behind` runs `git ls-remote --get-url` and prints its output verbatim. That command prints the configured remote URL with its userinfo intact, and after `url.<x>.insteadOf` rewriting, so a token kept in the URL (`https://user:TOKEN@host/...`) or put there by a global insteadOf rule (a common GitHub token setup) ends up in the `fyr update` error. Git itself strips credentials from its own fetch error, so this is a new leak. Verified in a scratch probe repo (git 2.47.3): with remote `https://fixtureuser:FAKETOKEN123@127.0.0.1:9/x.git`, `ls-remote --get-url` printed the full URL with the token. `git fetch`'s own error printed `'https://127.0.0.1:9/x.git/'`, with the userinfo removed. The error goes to stderr. That is also an agent session's transcript, which reaches the model provider. Records written from it are redacted (`cmd/fyr/record_redact.go`, url-credentials needle `internal/redact/redact.go:85`), but the terminal and transcript copy is not. Second: the new pre-write guard for a development build's `update --from-zip` fails open at a home that still has the pre-rename state directory, because it runs before the migration that would move the manifest into the place it reads. The other new code fails closed. The zip-place fallback does not change which tree any build installs (D15/ADR-034 hold).

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/repo.go:247-251` (`Behind`, the `ls-remote --get-url` branch) — remote URL credentials echoed into the error. `--get-url` prints userinfo verbatim and applies `insteadOf`, so a password or token in the URL, or in a global insteadOf rewrite, appears in `git fetch from <url> failed…`, printed to stderr by `cmd/fyr/main.go:57`. That reaches the operator's terminal, an agy session transcript and the model provider. Git's own `fetch` error is anonymized (verified above), so this undoes git's protection. No test covers a credentialed URL: `TestBehindFetchErrorNamesTheRemote` uses a bare local path. Remediation: name the remote, not its URL (`git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{upstream}` → `origin/main`, or `branch.<b>.remote`). If the URL must be shown, parse it with `net/url` and drop `u.User` entirely: `URL.Redacted()` masks only the password and keeps a token-as-username. An scp-like `user@host:path` carries no password. Also pass it through `internal/redact` as a second layer. Add a test with `https://user:TOKEN@…` that fails while the token appears in the error. The same rewrite reaches `insteadOf`, so test that path too.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/run_dispatch.go:155-160` with `cmd/fyr/zip_place.go:52-63` (`refuseDevelZipOverPath`) — fail-open by ordering. The guard calls `harness.LoadState(home)`, which reads only `~/.config/fyr/state.json` (`internal/harness/state.go:36`). It runs before `c.migrateStateDir()`. At a checkout place still on `~/.config/sh-agent` (v2.7.0 or earlier, `internal/harness/migrate.go:15`), the guard sees `found == false` and allows. The migration then renames the old directory into place, and `updateFromZip` overwrites the checkout place's `path` origin with a zip origin. That is exactly the BUG-203 stranding the guard exists to stop. The operator still named the zip, so this is no trust-boundary break, only a guard that does not hold. Remediation: run the refusal after `migrateStateDir()`. For a dry run, which does not migrate, also read the old directory's manifest, or refuse while `StateDirNotice(home) != ""`. Add a matrix cell with a legacy-dir checkout place.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `cmd/fyr/zip_place.go:61-62` — `st.Repo` from the manifest is put unquoted into a suggested command, `` `fyr install --repo %s` ``. The manifest is a user-owned file, so whoever can edit it already has the operator's account. The text is still advice an agent or operator may paste into a shell, and a path with spaces or shell metacharacters (or terminal control bytes) is reproduced as is. Remediation: quote it (`%q`, or a shell-quoting helper) or print the path on its own line. This is a pattern, not a vulnerability: it matches how other messages already echo manifest values, e.g. `installedFrom` in `cmd/fyr/status.go:83`.

## Checked
- Secrets: no credentials, keys or tokens in the diff's code or tests. Test fixtures use `fixture@example.invalid`, `t@t` and local bare repos. One leak path found (finding 1).
- Injection: every new `exec` is a `git -C <repo> <fixed args>` argv call (`gitOut`), with no shell, and no new argument comes from user input. Manifest values reach messages only (finding 3). `LoadState` still drops non-local or unmanaged `Files` entries (`state.go:62-68`), so `zipDrift`'s `Lstat` joins stay under home.
- Authz / tree selection (ADR-034, D15): `zipPlaceWithoutSource` steps aside when `--repo` or `$FYR_REPO` is set, so a named path keeps its own error. It only reports (`status`) or refuses (`update`, incl. `--check` and `--dry-run`) and installs nothing. It swallows `ResolveSource`'s error only for the not-found case: a release build errors only on named paths, which are excluded. On a manifest read error it falls back to the original error, so it fails closed. `refuseDevelZipOverPath` refuses on an unreadable manifest, so it fails closed (pinned by `TestDevelZipRefusesUnreadableManifest`), except for the ordering gap in finding 2. Release-binary paths are unchanged: `IsReleaseVersion` short-circuits both new guards.
- Crypto: none touched; sha256 values are only shortened for display (`ShortSum`). No hand-rolled primitive.
- Dependencies: `go.mod` and `go.sum` unchanged, no new import beyond stdlib and internal. `govulncheck ./...`: "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities"; 1 vulnerability in a required module, not called (the known set per DEPLOY-local). npm is not applicable: there is no JS in the range.
- GCP surface: none in the range.
- Past bugs: `fyr search --refs` (scratch home) for each changed code file returned BUG-203 (this fix) and BUG-049 (repo.go, dirty-guard). Neither is reopened by this diff.

## Not examined
- PLAN.md, README.md and TDD.md hunks: read only as far as the code diff names them, not reviewed as docs.
- Neither binary was built or run. Finding 2 comes from reading the code; it was not run. The `go test` matrix was not run by this review.
- Whether git's own fetch stderr can carry credentials over ssh or other transports. Only https anonymization was verified (git 2.47.3).
- The cwd-walk behaviour of a development build at a zip place: when the shell sits inside some harness-shaped tree, `update` still installs that tree. That predates this diff and is D15's allowed walk, so it is not re-reviewed.

## Outcome

1. The remote URL's credentials in the fetch error: fixed. `remoteForDisplay` drops the userinfo (round 2 then hardened it). `TestRemoteForDisplay` has a token as the username and as user:password, over https, ssh and scp forms. `TestBehindFetchErrorHidesCredentials` and `TestBehindFetchErrorHidesInsteadOfToken` cover an insteadOf rewrite; both are red with `remoteForDisplay` mutated to the identity.
2. The guard's fail-open by ordering: fixed. Round 2 then moved the guard after the migration. `TestDevelZipRefusesUnmigratedHome` covers the real run and the dry run, both red before.
3. The unquoted manifest path: fixed. `harness.ShellArg` quotes it; `TestDevelZipRefusalQuotesThePath` (a space and `$`) was red before. Round 2 made control characters safe.

title: Security review — P3 zip place and fetch error, round 2 (2026-10-31)
body:
# Security review round 2 — p3 fixes only   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: the round-1 fixes in .agents/scratch/p3-borken/p3-r2.diff, working tree on 73efcfb: `internal/harness/repo.go` (`Behind`'s fetch error, `remoteForDisplay`, `ShellArg`, `notPrintable`), `cmd/fyr/zip_place.go` (`refuseDevelZipOverPath`), plus the tests `TestRemoteForDisplay`, `TestBehindFetchErrorHidesCredentials` (internal/harness/source_git_test.go), `TestDevelZipRefusesUnmigratedHome` and `TestDevelZipRefusalQuotesThePath` (cmd/fyr/place_matrix_test.go). Round 1: .agents/scratch/agents/security-2026-10-31-1129.md.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Finding 1 (credentials in the fetch error) is only partly closed. `remoteForDisplay` (`internal/harness/repo.go:266-278`) removes userinfo only when `net/url.Parse` accepts the URL. When the parse fails, the `else if` fallback strips nothing from a `scheme://` URL, because `remote[:at]` contains "/". The string then goes into the error verbatim, credentials included. `url.Parse` rejects userinfo that carries a character outside RFC 3986's set, such as space, `^`, `|`, `#`, a bad `%` escape or a control byte. It also rejects a non-numeric port. `ls-remote --get-url` validates none of these and prints them. I confirmed this in a scratch probe repo: `git config url.https://tok3n:pw^x@127.0.0.1:1/.insteadOf https://127.0.0.1:1/` makes `--get-url` print `https://tok3n:pw^x@127.0.0.1:1/x.git`. The copied `remoteForDisplay` returns that unchanged, and returns `https://user:pa ss@host/x.git` unchanged too. Real vendor tokens (`ghp_…`, `glpat-…`) use only `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, so the common case is closed and pinned. A human password in the URL is not. Finding 2 is closed on both triggers. Finding 3 is closed for spaces, `$` and quotes, but the control-character branch prints a double-quoted string that bash still expands.

## Round-1 findings, trigger by trigger
- **Finding 1, credentials in the `Behind` fetch error: PARTLY CLOSED.**
  - Token as the username: closed. `u.User = nil` drops the whole userinfo, not only the password. Pinned by `TestRemoteForDisplay` (`https://ghp_tok3n@…`) and end-to-end by `TestBehindFetchErrorHidesCredentials`.
  - user:password: closed when the URL parses. Pinned the same way.
  - insteadOf rewrite: the code handles it, because `--get-url`'s rewritten output goes through `remoteForDisplay` like any other URL. No test sets `url.<x>.insteadOf`, though. A rewrite is just a URL to the parser, so this is a coverage gap, not a leak. It still does not meet the rule that every trigger has a failing-without-fix test.
  - Unparseable URLs: still leak (finding A below).
  - scp-like `user@host:path`: closed, unless the path itself contains "@" (finding A).
- **Finding 2, fail-open before the `~/.config/sh-agent` migration: CLOSED.**
  - The guard (`cmd/fyr/zip_place.go:61-63`) refuses when `~/.config/fyr` is absent and `StateDirNotice` reports the old directory or a symlink to it.
  - It runs before the dry-run branch, so the real run and `--dry-run` refuse alike. `TestDevelZipRefusesUnmigratedHome` pins both, and checks that nothing migrated.
  - When both directories exist, the guard falls through to `LoadState` of `~/.config/fyr`, the one the migration keeps, which is consistent.
  - An `Lstat` error other than not-exist skips the legacy check. `LoadState` then errors and the update refuses, so it fails closed.
  - Side effect: the guard also refuses a legacy home that was a zip or release place. That over-refusal is in the safe direction.
- **Finding 3, unquoted path in the suggested command: CLOSED for space, `$` and `'`; NOT CLOSED for control characters (finding B).**
  - `ShellArg` single-quotes the path and escapes `'` as `'\''`, which is correct.
  - `TestDevelZipRefusalQuotesThePath` pins space and `$`. No test covers `'` or a control character in `ShellArg`.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/repo.go:268-272` (`remoteForDisplay`): fails open when the parse fails.
  - **Weakness:** if `url.Parse` errors on a `scheme://user:pass@host/...` remote, the fallback leaves the string unchanged. The causes include a password with space, `^`, `|`, `#` or a bad `%xx`, and a non-numeric port. Credentials from the remote config or from an insteadOf rule then reach stderr, the terminal and the agent transcript. The scp-like branch has a smaller version of the same problem: it cuts at the LAST "@", so `tok@host:org/a@b.git` comes back verbatim.
  - **Why it matters:** I verified it with the copied function and with git 2.47.3's `--get-url` on an insteadOf rule.
  - **Remediation:** fail closed. When the parse fails or no host is found, do not print the URL. Fall back to the remote's name (`git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{upstream}` gives `origin/main`) or the existing generic text. Alternatively, for a `scheme://` string, cut everything from `://` up to the last "@" before the next "/". For scp-like strings, take the "@" before the first ":".
  - **Tests to add:** cases for `https://u:pa ss@h/x`, `https://u:p^w@h/x` and `tok@host:org/a@b.git`, each failing while the secret appears. Also a `Behind` case driven through `url.<x>.insteadOf`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/repo.go:284-288` (`ShellArg`): the control-character branch is still pasteable and expands.
  - **Weakness:** when `s` holds a non-printable rune, `strconv.Quote` returns a double-quoted string, which is then embedded in a backticked command (`zip_place.go:73`, `repo.go:253`). Bash and zsh expand `$(...)`, `` `...` `` and `$var` inside double quotes. Probe: `ShellArg("/a\x01$(id)`id`b")` gives `"/a\x01$(id)`id`b"`. Pasted, that runs `id` twice.
  - **Why it matters:** the doc comment says no shell quoting makes such a string safe to print, but the output is still laid out as a command to paste. The trust caveat from round 1 still applies: the manifest is user-owned, and a repo path is the operator's own, so this is hardening, not a boundary break.
  - **Remediation:** when `s` is not printable, do not put it inside the suggested command. Print `--repo <checkout>` and give the escaped path on its own line, marked not for pasting. Alternatively, single-quote the escaped form, `'` + escaped `'\''` + `'`, which no shell expands.
  - **Test to add:** a `ShellArg` unit test with `'`, a control byte and `$(…)` together.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/harness/repo.go:270`: a query string survives. `u.String()` keeps `RawQuery`, so `https://host/x.git?private_token=SECRET` is shown with its token. Git remotes rarely carry query credentials, and round 1 named only userinfo, so this is informational. Remediation: also set `u.RawQuery = ""` and `u.Fragment = ""`.

## Checked
- Secrets: the tests use fixture credentials only (`tok3nuser`, `s3cr3tpw`, `ghp_tok3n`, all fake) and a refused local port (127.0.0.1:1). No real secret.
- Injection: no new exec. `gitOut` argv is unchanged. Quoting is covered by finding B.
- Authz / tree selection: the new guard only refuses and never widens what installs. It precedes the dry-run branch and the migration (`cmd/fyr/run_dispatch.go:155-158`).
- Crypto: none touched.
- Dependencies: new imports are `net/url`, `unicode` and `strconv`, all stdlib. `go.mod` is unchanged. I did not re-run `govulncheck` this round, since no module changed (round 1: 0 affecting).
- GCP surface: none.
- Tests run: `go test -count=1 -run 'TestRemoteForDisplay|TestBehindFetchErrorHidesCredentials|TestBehindFetchErrorNamesTheRemote' ./internal/harness` passed. `go test -count=1 -run TestDevelZip ./cmd/fyr` passed.
- Probes: `.agents/scratch/sec-probe-r2/main.go` (a copy of `remoteForDisplay` and `ShellArg`) and `.agents/scratch/sec-probe-r2/repo` (a scratch git repo for the insteadOf rewrite; `rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` checked).

## Not examined
- I did not mutation-test the four new tests against the pre-fix code, because the source cannot be edited. That they fail without the fix is reasoned from the old code, not run.
- The end-to-end leak for a URL that fails to parse was not run through `Behind`. It is shown by the copied function plus `--get-url`'s output, separately.
- Whether git's own `fetch` stderr (the wrapped `%w`) anonymizes an unparseable credentialed URL, or an ssh transport's error. This is outside the fixes.
- Everything outside the listed fixes, by dispatch.

## Outcome

Past the two-round cap, as in P2: fixed without a third round. Each fix has a test that fails without it.

1. A URL `url.Parse` refuses was printed as is: fixed. A `scheme://` value that does not parse is not shown, and the message falls back to "the branch's upstream remote". An scp path's user part ends at the last `@` before the first `/`. `TestRemoteForDisplay`'s cases cover a space and a bad `%` in the password, a non-numeric port, and `user:tok@host:path/a@b.git`; all were red before.
2. A control character fell back to double quotes: fixed. It now gets `$'…'` with the character escaped, and `'` and `\` are escaped too. `TestShellArgRoundTrips` was red before: bash ran the `$(touch …)`.
3. A query token: fixed. The query and the fragment are dropped (`private_token` case, red before).

title: Review — PLAN.md P4, code and docs, round 1 (2026-10-31)
body:
# Review — p4 work-tree diff (lead reflog guard, docker limits and run network, commit-graph)   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: working tree vs HEAD 6f3109c, via .agents/scratch/p4/review-diff.patch (14 files, 385 insertions, 59 deletions), plus the record diffs for SPEC-fyr-work, GUIDE-testing, GUIDE-fyr-matrix and BUG-198, and the ADR-083 body. Docs lens ran over README.md, SDD.md, PRD.md, TDD.md, skills/work/SKILL.md, cmd/fyr/help_text.go, and every current record in .agents/trail.jsonl (grep of the subject nouns over all non-superseded bodies).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing is broken that I could find. The reflog guard fails closed on every error path (an unreadable reflog, an empty one and a missing checkout all read as "moved"). I confirmed on git 2.47.3 that `--date=iso-strict --format='%H %gd %gs'` yields `HEAD@{<date>}` entries as the code assumes. The run network is made before `openRun` and swept on every exit after it. `dockerArgs` refuses any network that is not `fyr-work-<stamp>`, so a missing network cannot become the default bridge. `go test -race` over the changed packages' targeted tests, `cmd/fyr -run WorkVerb`, `gofmt -l` and `go vet` are all clean. The findings below are doc and coverage-claim gaps, all low.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/work.go:133` — The new `o.sweepRun(stamp)` on the `openRun` failure path has no test, yet SPEC-fyr-work states it ("A run whose pid file cannot be opened sweeps its network before it is refused"). Trigger: delete the line and every test stays green. Fix: add a docker-mode row whose pid file cannot be opened, asserting `network rm` is called, or name the gap in the spec's "Not covered" paragraph.
- **[low / confidence: high]** SPEC-fyr-work (the paragraph beginning "Each Phase 2 test…", after-SPEC line 397) and GUIDE-testing § 3k "Not covered by any test here" — Both were left unchanged by P4. Per review-standards § 7, a coverage claim names its gaps. Unnamed P4 gaps: (a) the `openRun` sweep above; (b) `enable_icc=false` is checked only as the option passed and inspected, never as traffic actually blocked between two containers, though the spec says "one worker cannot reach another"; (c) reflog expiry of the start entry by a real `git gc`. The same paragraph still says a real daemon is "not covered … Phase 7c's smoke", while the GUIDE-fyr-matrix row now records a real-daemon run on dave on 2026-10-31. The two statements are not reconciled. Fix: one sentence in each naming (a) to (c), and date the real-daemon evidence.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/work/reflog.go:559-562` and SPEC step 6 — "Expiry drops only old entries, so it never reads as a move" is not strictly true. If the start entry is itself older than `gc.reflogExpire` (a checkout idle for more than 90 days) and a `git gc` or `reflog expire` runs during the run, the entry disappears. `reflogMoved` then reports "lost every entry" (or "over N new entries" if the lead also committed) and fails every worker. It fails closed, so no data is at risk, and `gc --auto` during a run is unlikely. Fix: soften the claim to "an entry the run did not add ages out only if it is old", or accept and say so.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. `sweepContainers` was replaced by `sweepStamp` and `removeLabelled` and has no remaining caller (grep). No commented-out code or leftover debug output.
2. Flow tracing — pass. `Options.Runner` → `makeNetwork` → `dockerConfig` (`sandbox.RunNetwork`) → `dockerArgs` → `sweepRun` and `Kill` → `sweepStamp` are consistent. Network create precedes the stamp line, `openRun` and the session. Removal follows container removal, and an error still tries every id. `p.reflog` flows from `session()` into `leadUnchanged`. Refusal 23 is raised before any docker call and before anything is made (`TestRunLeadNoReflog`). `TestRunLeadReflogMoved` can fail: HEAD and the tree are clean in that scenario, so only the reflog check catches it. `TestRunDockerPass` pins create-before-session and network-rm-after-container-rm. The host path asks docker nothing (`TestRunSweepQuiet`). One tiny uncovered window: a SIGKILL between `makeNetwork` and `openRun` leaves a network with no pid file for `--kill` to find. I judged it too narrow to be a finding.
3. Standards conformance — pass, with the doc nits above. § 8 code-shape rules: the guard keeps data on a check error; there is no read-only mode involved. Comments in `fetch.go`, `docker.go` and the sandbox's `dockerArgs` were updated with the behaviour. Restatement grep for pids-limit, 4096, default bridge, isolated network, container sweep, reflog, commit-graph and replace refs found no stale living copy. `help_text.go`, `skills/work/SKILL.md` step 6, README, SDD and PRD need no change. The skill's "a commit fails every worker" stays true. TDD.md § T18 says "every git call in the lead from then on is `leadGit`", while `trail.Dirty` and `head()` use plain git. The SPEC states that exception for `trail.Dirty`, and the TDD wording is scoped "from then on" (the fetch onward), so I did not count it.
4. Directory layout — pass. `reflog.go` and `reflog_test.go` sit beside `fetch.go` in `internal/work`. Every file stays under the modularity ceilings (largest: `internal/sandbox/docker_test.go`, 431 lines, a test file under 600).
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only (one `regexp` import), no new dependency, and no auth or crypto involved.
6. Decoupling — pass. `sandbox` owns `RunNetwork` and the argv; `work` owns creation and the sweep; the network name is shared through one exported function. The reflog guard is a separate file with a small interface (`reflogStart`, `reflogMoved`).

## Not examined
- A real docker daemon: the GUIDE-fyr-matrix claims (238s PASS on dave, the cgroup readings) were not re-run. I only checked `.agents/scratch/p4/container-inspect.json` (Memory and MemorySwap 8589934592, NanoCpus 2e9, PidsLimit 1024, one network `fyr-work-<stamp>`) and `net-inspect.json` (`enable_icc=false`) for consistency with the claim.
- The full test suite, `GOOS=darwin go vet`, mutation runs of the new tests (I reasoned about whether each can fail, but did not mutate).
- `cmd/fyr` beyond `-run WorkVerb`, and the `agents/`, `context/` and eval rows (the diff touches none).
- Records not in the diff set (PLAN.md and DEPLOY-*): searched by grep only for the subject nouns; no hit needed a change.

## Outcome

- Finding 1 (the `openRun` failure sweep untested): fixed. `TestRunPidFileFailSweepsNetwork` makes the work root unwritable, so the stamp directory's `Mkdir` fails, and asserts the refusal, `network rm net1` and no session; it is red with the sweep removed (mutation).
- Finding 2 (Not-covered paragraphs): fixed. SPEC-fyr-work's Verification paragraph gains P4's sentence (21 mutations, what no test covers, what dave ran), and GUIDE-testing § 3k names the real-daemon gaps and the dave runs. A two-container check on dave now shows `enable_icc=false` blocking and `true` passing (`.agents/scratch/p4/icc-smoke.txt`), recorded in the spec, ADR-083 and GUIDE-fyr-matrix.
- Finding 3 ("expiry never reads as a move"): fixed in the wording. The spec, the `reflogMoved` comment and PLAN.md D13 now say expiry reads as a move only when a gc during the run drops the recorded entry itself, which fails closed.

title: Security review — PLAN.md P4, docker limits, run network and the lead's reflog guard, round 1 (2026-10-31)
body:
# Security review — p4 docker network, limits, lead reflog guard   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: 6f3109c..working tree (`git diff HEAD -- TDD.md internal`, byte-identical to .agents/scratch/p4/review-diff.patch): internal/sandbox/docker.go, internal/work/{docker,fetch,preflight,reflog,slots,work,worker}.go and their tests. Context read: after-SPEC-fyr-work.md § One worker, § Docker mode, § Open questions; record-ADR-083.md; trail.Command; Kill; docker(); localDaemon.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Nothing high or medium. The questions the dispatch asked come out clean. A run cannot reach docker's default bridge or any other network: `dockerArgs` refuses every network that does not match `^fyr-work-[0-9A-Za-z][0-9A-Za-z_.-]*$`, the run is refused when `network create` fails, and a network removed mid-run makes `docker run` fail (exit 125, so the session counts as not started) instead of falling back. No argv injection was found. The sweep removes only what carries the exact `fyr.work=<stamp>` label. The reflog guard fails closed on every error and expiry path. The worst problem is that the new protections are requested but never confirmed to be in force. Docker silently drops `--memory`, `--memory-swap` and `--pids-limit` when a cgroup controller is missing. `enable_icc=false` works only when the daemon manages iptables and bridge netfilter. Neither is checked, and the only tests use a fake `docker`. So ADR-083's Consequences ("one worker cannot take the machine's memory … nor reach another worker's container") are stated as fact without evidence. Second: the HEAD-reflog guard misses a move of the checked-out branch made from a linked worktree (verified with a probe).

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/sandbox/docker.go:99` — the limits `--memory 8g --memory-swap 8g --pids-limit 1024` are passed but never verified. On a host without the memory, swap or pids cgroup controller, dockerd discards them with a warning, not an error. Two common cases: cgroup v1 without the memory controller, and rootless docker under cgroup v2 when systemd does not delegate the memory or pids controller. The container then runs with no limit. The warning goes to the client's stderr, which is `err.txt`, and the host reads `err.txt` only to count `auto-denied`. `--cpus` alone fails closed (dockerd returns an error when CFS is missing). Trigger: `fyr work --runner docker` on such a host gives an unlimited container, and nothing says so. Remediation: in `prepared.dockerRefusals`, refuse unless `docker info --format '{{.MemoryLimit}} {{.SwapLimit}} {{.PidsLimit}} {{.CPUCfsQuota}}'` prints `true true true true`. Alternatively, have check e read `docker inspect -f '{{.HostConfig.Memory}} {{.HostConfig.PidsLimit}}'` and fail when either is 0.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/docker.go:208-209` — `com.docker.network.bridge.enable_icc=false` is enforced by iptables rules that dockerd installs, plus bridge netfilter for traffic inside one bridge. Isolation from other runs' networks relies on the same `DOCKER-ISOLATION` rules. With `"iptables": false` in daemon.json, or where br_netfilter cannot be loaded (some rootless or VM setups), `network create` still succeeds and the option is not enforced. No test touches a real daemon (`TestRunDockerPass` uses a fake `docker`; TDD says "a real daemon is Phase 7c's smoke"), yet ADR-083 § Consequences and SPEC § Open questions state "cannot reach another worker's container" as fact. Trigger: a daemon configured without iptables lets one worker's container connect to another's on the run network. Remediation: a Phase 7c smoke that proves two containers on `fyr-work-<stamp>` cannot connect to each other, and that one cannot reach a container on another bridge. Until it exists, the ADR and SPEC should say the claim is untested. Optionally, refuse when `docker info` reports iptables or bridge-nf-call warnings.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/reflog.go:16`, `internal/work/fetch.go:62` — the guard reads only `HEAD`'s reflog. If the checked-out branch is moved and moved back from a linked worktree (`git -C <wt> update-ref refs/heads/<branch> <Y>`, then back to `<base>`), git writes the branch's reflog, never the lead worktree's `logs/HEAD`. HEAD is `<base>` again, the tree is clean, and the guard passes: the BUG-198 shape, reached through another worktree. Verified on git 2.47.3 with a scratch probe repository (since removed). For contrast, the same `update-ref` run in the lead's own worktree does write HEAD's reflog and is caught. Remediation: at the start, also record the newest entry of the reflog of the ref HEAD points to (`git symbolic-ref -q HEAD`, then `reflog show <ref>`), refuse when there is none, and compare it in `leadUnchanged`. A test runs `update-ref` from a linked worktree.
- **[low / confidence: high, likelihood very low]** `internal/work/work.go:126-133` with `internal/work/slots.go:277-281` — the network is created before the pid file. A process killed (SIGKILL, OOM) between `makeNetwork` and `openRun` leaves a labelled `fyr-work-<stamp>` bridge with no pid file. `--kill <stamp>` then answers "no run" and never sweeps it. Each leaked bridge takes a subnet from the address pool. Once the pool is used up, `network create` fails and every docker-mode run is refused. This fails closed and costs only availability. Remediation: let `--kill <stamp>` sweep a valid `stampRe` stamp even when it has no pid file (local daemon only), or name `docker network ls --filter label=fyr.work` as the hand cleanup in the refusal text.

## Checked

- **Default bridge or another network:** `runNetworkRe` refuses `""`, `bridge`, `host`, `none`, `default`, `container:x` and anything with `=` or `,`, so docker's `--network name=…,alias=…` syntax cannot be reached. The network is a separate argv element and starts with `fyr-`, so no flag injection. It is the only `--network` in the session argv (`TestDockerArgs` counts it). The version-check container stays `--network none`. A network deleted mid-run (e.g. `docker network prune` while no container is attached) makes `docker run` exit 125, which counts as not started; no fallback. A name collision fails `network create` (CLI CheckDuplicate, and always-on since API 1.44) and refuses the run. Re-creating the name with weaker options needs docker access, which is root-equivalent and outside the model.
- **Injection:** the stamp in `Run` is `%F-%H%M%S-<pid>`, made internally. `Kill`'s user-given stamp passes `stampRe` (slots.go:274) before reaching the `label=fyr.work=<stamp>` filter, which is one argv element. Docker's label filter is an exact key=value match, not a prefix. IDs from `ps`/`network ls` output come from the daemon. Reflog notes: the subject goes through `%.128q` (precision limits runes before quoting). The sha and selector are git-formatted. `Box.Note` passes everything through `sandbox.Printable`. The reflog argv is constants plus an int.
- **Sweep scope:** removes only the exact label `fyr.work=<stamp>`. The stamp is unique per (second, pid). `network rm` refuses a network still in use and does not disconnect foreign containers. Every path after `makeNetwork` sweeps: the `openRun` failure, the normal end before the deferred `r.close`, and the create failure itself.
- **Reflog guard fail-open:** an error at the start refuses (refusal 23). An error after the session is a note plus `lead checkout changed`. Expiry (gc `--auto` after a lead commit) drops the start entry, which reads as "over N new" or "lost every entry", i.e. closed. A missing or emptied `logs/HEAD` is closed. Turning `core.logAllRefUpdates` off mid-run does not stop git appending to an existing `logs/HEAD`. `log.showSignature` could have prepended gpg lines and made `es[0]` a signature line, but `trail.Command` already forces `-c log.showSignature=false` and `core.fsmonitor=false`, so the line shape holds. Accepted and documented: an exact (sha, second, subject) repeat; deliberate `reflog delete` or a forged entry (`GIT_COMMITTER_DATE`); a `--runner host` worker writing the lead's `.git/logs/HEAD` (same uid, SPEC § One worker step 6). In docker mode the lead's `.git` is not mounted.
- **leadGit after the session:** `--no-replace-objects`, `GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null`, `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` and now `core.commitGraph=false`. `-c` reaches child git (upload-pack) through `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`. `.git/shallow` can still cut parents, but cutting only removes ancestry: `base` stops being an ancestor ("rewrote history"), or the cut commit is diffed `--root` against the empty tree and shows its whole tree as out of scope. So it fails closed, though the comment's list is not exhaustive. The rest of the lead's `.git/config` (e.g. `url.*.insteadOf`) is the accepted same-uid model, and docker mode cannot write it.
- **Secrets:** none in the diff. Notes and errors print stamps, network names and reflog subjects only.
- **Authz/authn:** no new auth surface. Docker calls keep `FyrEnv()` and the local-daemon refusal.
- **Crypto:** none touched. No hand-rolled primitive.
- **Dependencies:** no go.mod/go.sum change (`git diff HEAD --stat -- go.mod go.sum` is empty). `govulncheck ./...` (/home/kesokaj/.go/bin): "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities"; 1 in a required module, not called (the known one). No npm in scope.
- **GCP surface:** none in the diff. Note: on a GCE host, a container on the bridge reaches 169.254.169.254 the same way the host runner does. This is not new, and it falls under ADR-083's accepted "reaches the host's services and the network".
- **Tests:** `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/work ./internal/sandbox -run 'Reflog|DockerArgs|Network|Sweep|LeadGit|KillStale|RunDocker|LeadNoReflog'` passed (both ok).

## Not examined

- No real docker daemon: limits, `enable_icc` and the network lifecycle were judged from the code and docker's documented behaviour, not run (finding 2).
- Host-side git calls in the session-written clone (fetch's local `upload-pack` reading the clone's `.git/config`, `objects/info/alternates`, or a `.git` file holding `gitdir:`; and sandbox `After`/`ExitChecks`). These predate this diff and were not traced. A docker-mode session can write the clone's `.git`, so this is the blast radius to review next.
- macOS/Colima (deferred in SPEC, Phase 7d).
- `PLAN.md` and `.agents/trail.jsonl` are modified in the tree but are not part of the reviewed patch.
- The full test suite (it runs in parallel elsewhere, per the dispatch).

## Outcome

- Finding 1 (limits unverified): fixed. Refusal 24 (`daemonLimits`, `internal/work/docker.go`) refuses a daemon whose `docker info` does not print `true` for MemoryLimit, SwapLimit, PidsLimit and CPUCfsQuota, naming the missing ones. Pinned by the `no-swap-limit` and `no-limits` rows of `TestRunDockerRefusals`, both red with the check removed and with the `"true"` comparison dropped. On dave `docker info` prints `true true true true`, and the real worker's cgroup read the limits back.
- Finding 2 (`enable_icc` unproven): fixed by evidence and an honest claim. On dave (docker 29.7.2) a listener container was reached from a second container on an `enable_icc=true` bridge and timed out on an `enable_icc=false` one (`.agents/scratch/p4/icc-smoke.txt`). The spec and ADR-083 say the isolation rests on dockerd's iptables rules and that a daemon with `"iptables": false` is not checked.
- Finding 3 (the branch moved from another worktree): fixed. The guard records and compares the newest reflog entry of HEAD and of the branch `git symbolic-ref -q HEAD` names; refusal 23 covers both. `TestReflogBranchMovedFromWorktree` replays the two `update-ref` calls from a linked worktree and is red with only HEAD guarded.
- Finding 4 (a network leaked when killed before the pid file): fixed. `Kill` of a valid stamp with no pid file runs the same local-daemon sweep as a stale one (`goneSweep`); `TestKillStaleSweeps` pins it and is red without it.
- "Not examined" (host-side git in a session-written clone): predates P4. Added as `PLAN.md` item 45, a `security` review in P12b.

title: Review — PLAN.md P4, round 2 over the fixes (2026-10-31)
body:
# Review — p4 round 2, the fixes only   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: .agents/scratch/p4/fixes-r2.patch (round-1 tree to current tree: internal/work, TDD.md, cmd/fyr/verb_work_test.go; it holds no internal/sandbox change), .agents/scratch/p4/record-SPEC-r2.diff, and the current bodies of SPEC-fyr-work, ADR-083, GUIDE-testing, GUIDE-fyr-matrix and BUG-198 (.agents/scratch/p4/). Round 1's two reports were read first.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Every round-1 finding of both reports is fixed or honestly stated, and I found no defect in the fixes. The four security fixes (limits, branch reflog, no-pid-file kill, pid-file sweep) match the code, and each has a test that fails without it. `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/work ./internal/sandbox` and `cmd/fyr -run WorkVerb` pass. `gofmt -l`, `go vet` and `GOOS=darwin go vet` are clean, and no `.orig` file or stray path is left in the tree. What remains is two describing-text restatements the branch-reflog fix left behind, one spec ordering slip, and a test gap the spec does not name. All are low.

## Round-1 findings, one by one

| Report | Finding | State |
|---|---|---|
| reviewer 1 | `sweepRun` on the `openRun` failure path untested | FIXED. `TestRunPidFileFailSweepsNetwork` (work root 0o500) fails without the line; mutation 6 of `.agents/scratch/p4/mutate2.py` covers it. |
| reviewer 2 | coverage claims name no gaps | PARTLY. The spec's P4 paragraph now names `sweptNote`, `"iptables": false` and a large `go test -race` under the limits, and dates the real-daemon run on dave. The test-gap nit below (finding 3) remains. |
| reviewer 3 | "expiry never reads as a move" overstated | FIXED. Spec step 6 and the `reflogMoved` comment now say expiry reads as a move only when a `gc` drops the recorded entry itself, which fails closed. |
| security 1 | limits requested, never confirmed | FIXED as a refusal. `daemonLimits` (refusal 24) refuses unless `docker info` prints four `true`; it uses `cmd.Output()`, so stderr warnings cannot join the fields, and extra or missing fields fail closed. `docker info --format '{{.MemoryLimit}} {{.SwapLimit}} {{.PidsLimit}} {{.CPUCfsQuota}}'` printed `true true true true` on this machine. The spec says plainly that nothing reads the limits back from the running container. |
| security 2 | `enable_icc` claimed, not enforced or tested | HONESTLY STATED. The spec and ADR-083 now say it relies on dockerd's iptables, that `"iptables": false` is not checked, and that the evidence is a manual two-container check on dave. |
| security 3 | branch moved from a linked worktree passes the HEAD-only guard | FIXED. `guardedRefs` adds the branch (`symbolic-ref -q HEAD`, exit 1 is detached, any other error refuses); `TestReflogBranchMovedFromWorktree` fails without it (mutation 1). |
| security 4 | kill between network and pid file leaves a network `--kill` cannot find | FIXED. `Kill` sweeps on `fs.ErrNotExist` through the new `goneSweep`, which the stale branch shares. A live run killed this way only fails closed (a removed network makes `docker run` exit 125). |

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/fetch.go:51-53` and SPEC-fyr-work's failure table (spec-work.body.md:297) — Two restatements still say the guard reads HEAD's reflog alone. The comment says "its HEAD reflog has no entry the run added". The table row says "its HEAD reflog gained an entry". The fix made the guard compare HEAD's and the branch's. Per review-standards § 3 and the project's describing-text rule, change both: "the reflog of HEAD or of its branch". The step 6 text, TDD § T18, ADR-083 and BUG-198 are already updated.
- **[low / confidence: high]** spec-work.body.md:123-128 against `internal/work/docker.go:64-70` — The numbered list puts refusal 24 between 14 and 15. The code makes it after 15 (`localDaemon`, then `daemonLimits`), and the paragraph above the list says "right after 15"; it also says 13 to 20 are "checked in this order". A reader following the list gets the order wrong. Move item 24 below item 15, or say in its own line that it follows 15.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** spec-work.body.md:379 and the P4 "Not covered" sentence — `TestRunLeadNoReflog` refuses on an empty HEAD reflog only, so the new branch half of refusal 23 (HEAD has entries and the branch's reflog is empty) has no test. Trigger: change `reflogStart` to skip the `len(es) == 0` refusal for the second ref and every test stays green. The "Not covered" list also does not name a real `git gc` expiring the recorded entry (round 1, finding 2(c)). The table row correctly says "no HEAD reflog", so nothing is overstated, but the gaps are unnamed. Fix: add one row (`git reflog expire` on the branch only, then expect refusal 23), or add both gaps to the "Not covered" sentence.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. `reflogStart`'s old string form and `goneSweep`'s inlined copy are replaced, and `refEntry`, `guardedRefs` and `refMoved` each have callers. No leftover mutation files or debug output.
2. Flow tracing — pass. `preflight` → `reflogStart` → `p.reflog []refEntry` → `leadUnchanged` → `reflogMoved` compiles and agrees across hops. `dockerRefusals` → `daemonLimits` runs before any image call. `Kill` → `goneSweep` → `sweepStamp` keeps the local-daemon guard on both paths. Errors propagate (docker info failure, symbolic-ref non-1 exit). Tests: the new rows fail under the six round-2 mutations in `mutate2.py` (read, not re-run). The pid-file test depends on `chmod 0o500` and would not fail as intended as root, so it fails loudly, not falsely green; the tree has no root guard anywhere in these tests.
3. Standards conformance — pass with nits. Findings 1 and 2 are describing-text slips. The restatement grep for "HEAD reflog" over README, SDD, PRD, TDD, skills/work, cmd, internal, context and agents found only the fetch.go comment and the tests that pin the HEAD wording.
4. Directory layout — pass. No new files beyond round 1; the new tests sit in the existing `_test.go` files.
5. Simplicity — pass. Stdlib only (`errors`, `os/exec`); no dependency; nothing hand-rolled in auth or crypto.
6. Decoupling — pass. `guardedRefs` and `refMoved` stay inside `reflog.go`; `goneSweep` is the one shared sweep for both gone-run shapes in `slots.go`.

## Not examined
- A real docker daemon beyond `docker info --format` (the dave runs behind the matrix and spec claims: 238s PASS, the cgroup readings, the two-container `enable_icc` check, were not re-run).
- The mutation runs: I read `mutate.py` and `mutate2.py` (15 plus 6, matching the "21 mutations" claim) but did not re-run them.
- The full `go test ./...` and `cmd/fyr` beyond `-run WorkVerb`; the `agents/`, `context/` and eval rows (untouched by the fixes).
- Anything round 1 already passed that these fixes did not touch.

## Outcome

Fixed past the two-round cap without a third round, as in P2 and P3 (PLAN.md D12); each fix has a test or is a text fix checked against the code.
- Finding 1 (stale "HEAD reflog only"): fixed in `internal/work/fetch.go`'s `leadUnchanged` comment and SPEC-fyr-work's failure-table row, which now name HEAD and its branch.
- Finding 2 (refusal 24's place in the list): fixed; the SPEC lists 24 after 15, as the code makes it.
- Finding 3 (the branch half of refusal 23 untested; gc expiry unnamed): fixed. `TestReflogBranchMovedFromWorktree` removes the branch's reflog beside HEAD's and expects refusal 23, red with the check limited to HEAD (mutation); the SPEC's Not-covered list names a real `git gc` expiring the recorded entry.

title: Security review — PLAN.md P4, round 2 over the fixes (2026-10-31)
body:
# Security review round 2 — p4 fixes (limits refusal, branch reflog guard, no-pid sweep)   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: .agents/scratch/p4/fixes-r2.patch (round-1 tree..working tree: internal/work/{docker,preflight,reflog,slots}.go, docker_test.go, reflog_test.go, TDD.md, cmd/fyr/verb_work_test.go), with .agents/scratch/p4/icc-smoke.txt, spec-work.body.md, adr-083.md. Context read in the working tree: localDaemon, docker(), makeNetwork, sweepStamp/removeLabelled, Kill/goneSweep, Run's start sequence (work.go:122-145), sandbox Session exit classification (sandbox/docker.go:160-180).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The round-1 findings are fixed or stated honestly. The fixes add no fail-open path in the limits refusal or the reflog guard, and no argv injection. The one new weakness is in the finding-4 fix. `--kill <stamp>` with no pid file now force-removes (`docker rm -f`) every container on the daemon that carries `fyr.work=<stamp>`, and it never checks that the run is gone. The docker label is global to the daemon, while the pid file belongs to one home. So `fyr work --kill S` against the wrong home (for example without `--home` while a development run lives in `~/sandbox/fyr-work/home`) kills a LIVE run's worker containers in another home. In round 1 this case answered a harmless "no run S". The damage is availability only: the run is operator-initiated and fails closed. But the sweep can remove what is not a dead run's, and ADR-083 states "once the run is gone, its pid file stale or never made", which is not true for "never made".

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/slots.go:295-300` with `slots.go:273-283` and `docker.go:270-273`. The no-pid-file branch calls `goneSweep`, which runs `sweepStamp(stamp)`: `docker ps -a --filter label=fyr.work=<stamp>` then `rm -f` on each container, then `network rm`. A missing pid file in THIS home does not prove the run is dead. The label spans the daemon, and the pid file is per home. Trigger: run A runs in home H1 with stamp S. The operator runs `fyr work --kill S` with home H2 (a different `--home`, or none, so the real home). `OpenRegular` returns ErrNotExist, and A's running containers are force-removed. A then sees exit 137 sessions, with no SIGTERM and no graceful result contract. The same thing happens inside one home during the window between `makeNetwork` and `openRun` (`work.go:127-131`). Round 1's stale-file path did not have this problem, because a stale pid file in this home proves the stamp's process is gone. Remediation: (a) In the no-pid-file branch, sweep networks only. A run with no pid file has never started a worker container (containers start after `openRun`; the version check uses a different label, `fyr.work.check=<pid>`). `docker network rm` also refuses a network that is still in use. (b) Skip the sweep when the pid in the stamp (`stampRe` group 1) is still alive (`syscall.Kill(pid, 0)` is not ESRCH), and say so in the refusal. (c) Correct ADR-083's sentence "once the run is gone, its pid file stale or never made" and the matching TDD § T17 phrase. Add a test that has a live process holding the stamp's pid and asserts that no `rm -f` happens.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `.agents/scratch/p4/spec-work.body.md:328` (and ADR-083 § Consequences, first clause). The text says "another run's containers are on another network" as a reason a worker cannot reach them. Line 226 carries the iptables caveat for `enable_icc` inside one bridge, but line 328 does not. Isolation between two bridges rests on the same dockerd iptables (`DOCKER-ISOLATION`) chains, and the smoke (`icc-smoke.txt`) only tested traffic inside each bridge, not between bridges. Trigger: a daemon with `"iptables": false` makes both claims false, and nothing checks for it. Remediation: add the caveat at line 328 too ("enforced by dockerd's iptables, not checked"). Optionally add a cross-bridge probe to the Phase 7c smoke.
- **[info / confidence: high]** `internal/work/work.go:126-138`. The finding-4 fix works only if the operator knows the stamp. A run killed between `makeNetwork` and `openRun` never printed its stamp line (it is printed after `openRun`). The stamp can be recovered only from the network name, `fyr-work-<stamp>`, via `docker network ls --filter label=fyr.work`, and no user-facing text names that command. Remediation: name it in SPEC § The run's network, or in `--kill`'s "no run" text.

## Round-1 findings, status

1. Limits not verified: **fixed** as a capability check. `daemonLimits` (`docker.go:118-135`) fails closed. A non-zero exit refuses. Fewer or more than 4 fields refuses. Anything other than the literal `true` refuses (`<no value>`, `false`, empty). It reads stdout only (`cmd.Output()`), so stderr warnings cannot shift the fields. It runs after `localDaemon`, so a remote daemon is never asked. Residual risk, stated honestly in SPEC:224: nothing reads the limits back from the running container. The dave cgroup readback is the evidence.
2. `enable_icc` unproven: **stated honestly**. The dave smoke shows `true` passes traffic and `false` times out. ADR-083 and SPEC:226 now say `"iptables": false` is not checked. The cross-bridge claim has a gap (finding 2 above).
3. Reflog guard missed a branch moved from another worktree: **fixed**. `guardedRefs` adds the ref HEAD points to. `reflogStart` refuses when either reflog is empty. `reflogMoved` compares both, and every error or expiry path stays closed. `TestReflogBranchMovedFromWorktree` reproduces the round-1 probe. Its expected message is `refs/heads/main …`, so the test also proves HEAD's own reflog did not catch the move (the must-fail state of the old guard).
4. Network leaked before the pid file: **fixed**, but the fix opened finding 1 above.

## Checked

- **Argv injection, symbolic-ref to reflog:** probed on git (scratch repo, removed). `git symbolic-ref -q HEAD` always prints a name that starts with `refs/`. `HEAD` set to `refs/heads/-x` prints `refs/heads/-x`. A `.git/HEAD` holding `ref: --output=pwn` or `ref: heads/main` is not a valid repository, and git discovery moved on to the enclosing repo, so the dash-led value was never printed. Setting a bare `-x` is rejected as a switch. The ref is one argv element, now followed by `--`. No shell. Exit code 1 is the only "detached" case; any other error refuses (`reflog.go` guardedRefs).
- **Argv injection, user stamp to sweep:** `Kill` checks `stampRe` (`^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-\d{6}-(\d{1,7})$`) before any use (`slots.go:290`). The stamp reaches docker only as `label=fyr.work=<stamp>`, one argv element and an exact match. IDs come from the daemon's output.
- **Fail-open:** `daemonLimits` is closed on every path (above). `reflogStart` and `refMoved` are closed on read error, a missing entry, an empty reflog, or entries over the window. `goneSweep` with a non-local daemon sweeps nothing and says so.
- **Secrets:** none in the fixes. Errors print stamps, ref names, reflog subjects (`%.128q`), and docker info output through `sandbox.Printable`.
- **Authz/authn, crypto:** nothing touched. No hand-rolled primitive.
- **Dependencies:** none added; the patch touches no go.mod or go.sum. govulncheck was not re-run in round 2 (round 1 showed 0 affecting, and nothing new was imported).
- **GCP surface:** none.
- **Tests:** `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/work -run 'Reflog|KillStale|RunDockerRefusals|PidFileFail|LeadNoReflog|LeadReflogMoved'` passed (ok, 3.8 s). They run against a fake `docker`. No real daemon was run by this review.

## Not examined

- A real docker daemon: the cross-home `rm -f` behaviour was judged from the code (the label filter is global to the daemon), not reproduced.
- Whether a live run whose containers were `rm -f`'d mid-session can still land partial commits. This is the same path as an agy crash with exit 137, which predates the fixes. Not traced past `sandbox/docker.go:176`.
- The full test suite, `cmd/fyr` tests, and govulncheck (not re-run).
- Anything outside the fixes (out of scope for round 2), including round 1's unexamined surface: host-side git in the session-written clone.

## Outcome

Fixed past the two-round cap without a third round, as in P2 and P3 (PLAN.md D12).
- Finding 1 (`--kill` with no pid file removing containers by a daemon-wide label): fixed. `noPidSweep` (`internal/work/slots.go`) removes only the stamp's networks, never lists or removes a container, and sweeps nothing while the stamp's pid is alive. `TestKillStaleSweeps` pins all three (no `ps -a` or `rm -f` call; the live case makes no docker call); red with the old `goneSweep` and with the liveness check dropped (mutations). ADR-083's wording is corrected.
- Finding 2 (between-network isolation claimed without its caveat): fixed by evidence and the caveat. On dave a connection from one `enable_icc=false` bridge to a listener on another timed out (`.agents/scratch/p4/icc-smoke.txt`); the SPEC's open question and ADR-083 say both isolations rest on dockerd's iptables rules, unchecked under `"iptables": false`.
- Finding 3 (info: a stamp never printed): the SPEC names `docker network ls --filter label=fyr.work` and `fyr work --kill <stamp>` for a run killed before its stamp line.

title: Review — PLAN.md P5, the PRD reshape (ADR-084), code and docs lens (2026-10-31)
