# Review — P5 PRD reshape (ADR-084), code + docs lens   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: uncommitted change over c03898d: `git diff -- PRD.md`, `.agents/scratch/p5/review-SPEC-fyr-{check,eval,serve}.diff`, ADR-084 (stored records read from `.agents/scratch/workers`), `.agents/trail.jsonl` (7 changed lines: ADR-084 added, three spec lines replaced).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE

Nothing is broken. All eleven requirement bodies are word-for-word unchanged (checked by script: old `### R<n>` title and body against new item title and dedented body, 11 of 11 equal). `fyr check` from the tree binary gives 0 findings and neither PRD note. The must-fail states hold. In a scratch clone with the PRD and trail copied in, a renamed test in R10's `enforced by:` gives one `requirement` finding (exit 1), and a deleted `| R7 |` row in SDD.md gives one `trace` finding (exit 1). One low-severity doc nit on the provenance method, and one commit-time caveat.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `PRD.md:34` — The comment says the provenance date is "the day its title first appears in git (`git log -S`)". Run on `PRD.md` as written, `git log -S` gives 2026-10-29 (commit 43f6f1d) for every title and number, while the comments carry 2026-09-03, 10-23, 10-24 and so on. The stored dates match history only when `git log -S` runs on the predecessor path `REQUIREMENTS.md`. I confirmed this for R0, R1, R2, R9 and R10. ADR-084 explains the rename only for R1, R9 and R10. Fix: have the comment say "found with `git log -S` over `REQUIREMENTS.md`, the file's name before 2026-10-29". This needs the operator's approval, since it is a PRD edit. It affects no check.
- **[low / confidence: high]** Commit-time caveat, not a diff defect. The 0-findings claim in ADR-084 holds only with the three re-stored spec lines in `.agents/trail.jsonl` committed together with `PRD.md`. A clone of HEAD with only the committed files reports 3 `spec-stale` findings (SPEC-fyr-check, -eval, -serve, each "1 commit … since 16449936b04a") plus both PRD notes. The commit must stage `.agents/trail.jsonl`.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. Nothing is added or left behind. The `## Requirements` index table is replaced by the items, and no link or anchor to it remains (`git grep` for `PRD.md#`, `§ Requirements`, `### R<n>` finds only `internal/check/traces_test.go:131`, a fixture for the other-shape note, and PLAN.md).
2. Flow tracing — pass. Rule (c) (`internal/check/requirements.go`, `itemRe`) and rule (d) now parse all eleven items. Nested `- **Install:**` bullets in R9 are indented, so `itemRe` does not take them as items. Every `enforced by:` site resolves (check exits 0), and both must-fail mutations were observed. The spec re-read claims hold: 253ca2c touched only `cmd/fyr/verb_work_test.go` among the code those specs name. `Config.Docker` is not set by `cmd/fyr/eval*.go` or `internal/eval`.
3. Standards conformance — pass. The restatements are consistent. SPEC-fyr-check's two "this repository's `### R0` sections" examples are generalised, and the stored record has no other such citation. SDD.md, TDD.md and README.md cite R0–R10 by number, which is unchanged. The Goals table G3 is a dated baseline (2026-10-29) and is not made false. The approval chain for editing the immutable PRD is stated in ADR-084 (proposal, approval, ADR, same commit). `Last updated` is 2026-10-31.
4. Directory layout — pass. No new files; `PRD.md` stays at the root.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. No code, no dependency, no auth or crypto.
6. Decoupling — pass. The ADR rejected teaching rule (d) a second PRD parser. The parser stays single-shape, and the repository conforms to the template.

## Not examined
- Provenance dates for R3–R8: only R0, R1, R2, R9 and R10 were re-derived.
- The semantic fit of each `enforced by:` site to its requirement. I checked only that the sites resolve and that the ADR states the selection rule.
- `PLAN.md` and `TDD.md` prose beyond the greps above.
- The scratch-clone mutations ran in a mktemp copy outside the checkout (`/tmp/tmp.E7KTTEoZZ5`). I left it in place and did not delete it.

## Outcome

- **Low 1 (provenance dates), upheld in part, deferred to the operator as `PLAN.md` item 47.** The stated method was not `git log -S` on `PRD.md`; it was `git log --all -S"<title>"` over every path. Rerun that way (main thread, 2026-10-31), it reproduces 9 of 11 dates. Two differ. R8 is stored as 2026-09-17, the day its earlier wording "One delivery channel" appeared (`9222762`); its full title gives 2026-10-24. R0 is stored as 2026-10-23, but every search gives 2026-10-24 (`ebfc1cb`). The draft, dates included, was approved as drafted, and any further `PRD.md` edit needs the operator's word. So the reshape lands as approved, and item 47 carries the exact fix to the operator.
- **Low 2 (commit scope), no change needed.** `.agents/trail.jsonl`, which holds ADR-084 and the three re-stamped specs, is committed in the same commit as `PRD.md`. The P5 checkpoint's `fyr check` from a tree binary runs on the committed tree.
- The reviewer's scratch clone `/tmp/tmp.E7KTTEoZZ5` is outside this repository and is left for the operator to delete. This session's standing approvals reach nothing outside the repository.

title: Review — PLAN.md P6 round 1: eval's trial record and replaced graded (code and docs)
body:
# Review — p6 eval trial record (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: working tree vs HEAD 42abc6e (uncommitted): .agents/scratch/p6/review-code.diff and .agents/scratch/p6/review-records.diff (lenses: code and docs)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing blocking and no REQUIREMENTS-level violation found; the code matches what the record diffs claim (line shape, summary, title suffix, three header lines, both tables, WilsonRate, RunModels), and the verification I ran is green. The worst problem is a premise gap in item 1: `replaced` is now a graded FAIL on the claim that only the agent can cause it, but `ReasonReplaced` is also raised for host errors (any open error on out.txt/err.txt, any non-ENOENT removal error), so a full disk or fd exhaustion now lowers a row's pass rate instead of being an un-graded ERROR. The rest is stale or missing docs text (low).

Verification run by me (read-only): `go test -race ./cmd/fyr -run Eval` ok; `go test -race ./internal/eval ./internal/metrics` ok; root package incl. `TestFunctionLength` ok; `gofmt -l cmd internal` empty; `go vet` on the three packages clean; `fyr check --home .agents/scratch/workers`: 0 findings. Not a mutation protocol run (I did not mutate source).

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `internal/sandbox/session.go:48` (also `internal/sandbox/docker.go:158`, `internal/sandbox/box.go:199`, `internal/eval/cause.go:27-37`) — with `replaced` moved into `safetyCauses`, every `b.replaced(...)` call becomes a graded FAIL, and the new justification (SPEC-fyr-eval step 15, cause.go:30-33: "only a process inside the sandbox can make one, and the only such process is the agent's") does not hold for all callers. `agyOutputs` returns any `OpenRegular` error (ENOSPC, EMFILE, EACCES, EIO) and `agy()` reports it as `b.replaced("%v", err)`; `removeInSandbox` does the same for any `root.Remove` error other than ENOENT. Failure scenario: disk fills during a `--runs 25` invocation, agy never starts, the trial is `FAIL (replaced; sandbox replaced)`, is counted in n, is stored as status fail, and drags the row's c/n and Wilson interval down; before the change it was an ERROR counted apart (the eval-metrics plan's own Harbor rule: "a sandbox failure is not graded"). Fix: raise `ReasonReplaced` only for the agent-attributable cases (non-regular file / link / path no longer resolving) and give an open or remove failure that is not one of those the ERROR reason `setup`-like path (or a new ERROR cause), or narrow the SPEC claim and accept the bias explicitly; add a test where the open fails for a non-link reason and expect ERROR.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `GUIDE-testing` § 4 (record, the "`fyr eval` makes the setup proofs itself" bullet; unchanged line) — still says "A failed check is a reason in the row's verdict line, `PASS` or `FAIL (<reason>; <reason>)`". The line is now `FAIL (<cause>; <reason>; …)` (cause first, SPEC-fyr-eval § The verb). Update the shape in the same bullet that the diff already edited two bullets below.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` § eval (record) — PLAN.md P6 item 2 and the eval-metrics plan Phase 2b box name `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` § eval as a doc to update, and it is not in the record diffs. If it is left for the E2E step, that is fine, but the box cannot be ticked until the matrix rows carry the new line/record shape (its rows still quote `FAIL (check failed)` as a historical 2026-10-26 run, which is correct as history).
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `cmd/fyr/eval_record.go:117-127` (`trialModels`) and `eval_record_test.go:63` — the only verb-level assertion is `model: unknown` (the fake agy writes no session with a model). `RunModels` and `modelName` are unit-tested, but the wiring (run keys passed from `r.Run`, store opened from `c.home`) is never exercised to a non-`unknown` value, so a change making `trialModels` always return nil passes every test. SPEC-fyr-eval claims the model comes from the trials' sessions. Add a verb test that seeds a session with `run` = a trial's key and a model in the eval home's store, or state the gap in the plan's verification (the real-agy E2E is the only coverage).

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. `recordEval` moved (not duplicated), `evalBody` has no remaining reference in code or living records; `ReasonReplaced` removed from `errorCauses` with no orphan.
2. Flow tracing — pass with finding 1. Callers of `Result.Status/Cause` (`trialOf`, `ingestRow`, `tallyOf`, serve `/evals` title prefix) agree; `ingestRow` still skips a replaced sandbox; ERROR trials still make exit 1; errors on the trial/ingest/record paths keep their exit semantics. Summary now counts graded trials, matching title and SPEC. Tests can fail: `TestClassify` swap cases fail if `replaced` returns to `errorCauses`; `TestEvalTally` pins the 1/2 suite interval that distinguishes row-mean from pooled.
3. Standards conformance — pass for code (gofmt, vet, 50-line function ceiling: `body()` is 42, `recordEval` 45); docs: finding 2 and 3. The record diffs' claims (SPEC-fyr-eval line shape, table, failure-mode rows; SPEC-fyr-metrics WilsonRate/RunModels; GUIDE-testing title/tables) match the code. SDD.md, PRD.md, README.md and `cmd/fyr/help_text.go` do not restate the old shape (help says "PASS, FAIL or ERROR (the sandbox failed: not graded)", still true as worded). Historical `testing`/`change`/`review`/`handoff` records quote the old shape and are never rewritten.
4. Directory layout — pass. `eval_record.go` and its test sit beside `eval.go`; `RunModels` is in `internal/metrics/trials.go`.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only, no new dependency, no auth/crypto; parameterised SQL with one placeholder per run (modernc/SQLite variable limit is far above rows x 25).
6. Decoupling — pass. `cmd/fyr` owns the record and the tally; `internal/eval` does not import SQLite; `internal/metrics` exposes two small functions.

## Not examined
- The real-agy E2E (golden path and edge in the eval-metrics plan § Verification): needs a login and was out of scope.
- Full `go test ./...` and `govulncheck` (ran the three changed packages, the root package and `./cmd/fyr -run Eval` only).
- No mutation of source (read-only role): "tests can fail" is by reading, except that the suites pass as written.
- `internal/serve`, `internal/work` behaviour beyond reading their use of the title prefix and `ReasonReplaced`.

## Outcome

- **Finding 1 (Medium): fixed** as `PLAN.md` item 48. A file the box cannot open or remove is `sandbox write failed`, an ERROR with cause `write`, when the error is the machine's (ENOSPC, EDQUOT, EIO, EROFS, EMFILE, ENFILE, ENOMEM; `internal/sandbox/box.go` `fileFailed`, `machineErr`). Every other refusal stays `sandbox replaced`, the graded direction. The three call sites (`session.go` and `docker.go`'s `agyOutputs` error, `box.go` `removeInSandbox`) use it. `fyr work`'s `safetyReasons` and eval's `ingestRow` skip list hold the new reason, so a worker is still kept and not fetched, and nothing is ingested, as before. Tests that fail without the fix: `TestFileFailed` (the mutation "always replaced" fails 8 cases), `TestUnsafeReasons`, `TestEvalIngestSkipsWriteFailed` (it failed with `eval=w:1` before the skip), and `TestClassifyEveryReason`'s `write` entry. Not tested: the call sites under a real full disk or descriptor limit; the sandbox tests take no hook (their D12), and neither failure can be made here without root or a process-wide limit (`PLAN.md` D14). `SPEC-fyr-eval` step 15, its cause table and § Data, and `SPEC-fyr-work`'s stamp and failure-modes row say so.
- **Finding 2 (Low): fixed.** `GUIDE-testing` § 4's setup-proofs bullet now gives the line as `PASS`, or `FAIL` or `ERROR` with its cause first.
- **Finding 3 (Low): fixed / answered.** The model wiring now has a verb-level test: `TestEvalVerbRecord`'s fake sessions name `gemini-x` and `gemini-y`, and the header must read `mixed (gemini-x, gemini-y)`. The mutation `trialModels` returning nil fails it. `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` § eval gets its rows from the E2E, which runs after the commit (P6's box 2, D14).

title: Review — PLAN.md P6 round 2: the fixes (sandbox write failed, the model test)
body:
# Review — p6 eval trial record, round 2 (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: .agents/scratch/p6/review2-code.diff and review2-records.diff (the fixes since round 1, reviewer-2026-10-31-1400.md), read against PLAN.md item 48 and D14 and the code in the working tree

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Round 1's finding 1 (host errors graded as `replaced`) is fixed at the three call sites it named, and the fix is correct: `fileFailed` classifies with `errors.Is` over errno-wrapped errors, `ReasonWrite` is an ERROR cause `write`, and `fyr work` (`safetyReasons`) and eval's ingest skip both hold the new reason. Round 1's finding 2 (GUIDE-testing verdict shape) is fixed in the record, and finding 4 (the model wiring) is now covered by `TestEvalVerbRecord`, which seeds three sessions and expects `mixed (gemini-x, gemini-y)`. Finding 3 (`GUIDE-fyr-matrix` § eval) is not in the record diffs; it belongs to the unticked E2E box, so it is open, not wrong. The worst remaining problem is a restatement the fix missed: `skills/work/SKILL.md:57` lists the reasons that end the `fyr work` loop and lacks `sandbox write failed`. Nothing blocking.

Verification I ran (read-only): `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/sandbox ./internal/eval ./internal/work` ok; `go test -race -count=1 ./cmd/fyr -run 'Eval|Metrics'` ok; `go vet` on the four packages clean; `gofmt -l cmd internal` empty. No mutation was run (read-only role).

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/work/SKILL.md:57` — "A safety FAIL ends the loop at once ... a result whose reasons include `credentials left in the sandbox`, `real config changed`, `processes left`, `sandbox replaced` or `lead checkout changed`." The fix moves the machine-error case, which used to read `sandbox replaced` and ended the loop, to `sandbox write failed`. `safetyReasons` (`internal/work/worker.go:22`) and the SPEC-fyr-work table (record, failure modes row) list it, but the skill the lead follows does not. Scenario: a worker's sandbox hits ENOSPC or EIO, the verb reports FAIL `sandbox write failed`, and the lead, reading the skill's list, does not treat it as a safety FAIL and keeps dispatching and merging other phases on a failing disk, where before the change it stopped. Fix: add `sandbox write failed` to that list, in the same edit. Because it is under `skills/`, AGENTS.md's release rule asks for a behavioural run of the changed skill at the gate.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/sandbox/box.go:157-163` (`Intact`) — `err != nil || rerr != nil` from `os.Lstat` / `filepath.EvalSymlinks` raises `b.replaced(...)` for any error, including EIO, ENOMEM or EMFILE. Eval now grades `replaced` as a FAIL, so it is the same class as round 1's finding 1 at a fourth site that item 48 does not name (item 48 lists `session.go`, `docker.go`, `removeInSandbox`). The odds are small (Lstat needs no descriptor) but the SPEC claim "only a process inside the sandbox can replace it" is not true of this site. Fix: route through `fileFailed` for the Lstat/EvalSymlinks error when it is not ErrNotExist, or narrow the claim and say so in item 48.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/sandbox/session.go:153-157` (`Bash`) — a log that cannot be opened (a full disk, ENOSPC) returns false with only a Note; the caller then fails the row `check` (graded FAIL, `afterSession` in `internal/eval/row.go`) or `setup` (ERROR). This predates the diff, but it is the same machine-error-graded-against-the-agent class that item 48 closes for the other opens. Fix: use `fileFailed` for the open error (Bash would need to report the reason, not only false), or record the gap in item 48.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/sandbox/box_write_test.go` — `TestFileFailed` pins the classifier only. The wiring at the three call sites (`session.go:48`, `docker.go:158`, `box.go:229`) has no test: reverting any one to `b.replaced` passes every test. D14 states this and why (no hook; no root or process-wide limit), so it is answered, not hidden. Not a finding that needs action unless the operator wants a seam.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/sandbox/box.go:197` (`machineErrs`) — ENOSPC and EDQUOT can be made by the agent (it fills the disk or its quota) before step 11's unlink; such a failure to remove the token link then reads as an ungraded `write` ERROR, not a graded `replaced`. The box is still kept and not ingested, and a later `Intact` swap would still raise `replaced`, so the exposure is a missed grade, not a leak. Speculative; noted for the D14 trade-off.

## Round 1 findings, status
1. `replaced` graded on host errors: fixed at the named sites (see findings above for two unnamed ones). `TestClassify`/`TestClassifyEveryReason` cover the cause table, `TestEvalIngestSkipsWriteFailed` can fail (the `c` control proves the same home is ingested under another reason), `TestUnsafeReasons` pins `fyr work`.
2. GUIDE-testing verdict shape: fixed (`FAIL (<cause>; <reason>; <reason>)` now in the bullet, checked in the stored record).
3. `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` § eval: still unchanged; the plan's E2E box (P6 item 2) is unticked, so it is open, not wrong.
4. `trialModels` wiring: answered by `TestEvalVerbRecord` (`templateModel` seeds; asserts `mixed (gemini-x, gemini-y)`).

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. `ReasonWrite` has callers in `eval`, `cmd/fyr`, `work` and tests; nothing orphaned.
2. Flow tracing — pass with the Intact/Bash notes above. `fileFailed` once-each behaviour is tested; `agy()` returns -1 on both reasons, so the second session does not start; ingest, classify, `unsafe()` and the record line agree.
3. Standards conformance — fail on one restatement (`skills/work/SKILL.md:57`). Comments in `cause.go`, `session.go`, `eval.go` and the SPEC/GUIDE text match the code. `cause.go:59-63` doc comment wraps awkwardly but is accurate. TDD.md, SDD.md, README.md, `help_text.go` do not restate the reason list.
4. Directory layout — pass. `box_write_test.go` and `unsafe_test.go` sit beside their packages.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib `errors.Is` over a short errno list; no dependency, no auth or crypto.
6. Decoupling — pass. The sandbox owns the reasons; eval and work import the constants.

## Not examined
- The real-agy E2E and a full `go test ./...` / `govulncheck`.
- `internal/serve` and `internal/metrics` beyond what the diff touches.
- No mutation of source (read-only role); "tests can fail" is by reading, except that the suites pass as written.
- `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` content beyond confirming it is not in the record diffs.

## Outcome

Fixed after round 2 without a third round, at the cap (as in P2 and P3), each with a test that fails without it:
- **Medium (the `work` skill's stop list): fixed.** `skills/work/SKILL.md` names `sandbox write failed` among the safety FAILs that end the loop. The skill is in P13's behavioural runs.
- **Low (`Intact`, `Bash`'s log): fixed / answered.** `Bash` sends a log it cannot open through `fileFailed`, so a planted log is `sandbox replaced` and the script does not run (`TestBashLogPlanted`; `TestRunFIFOs` now expects `sandbox replaced` for its FIFO at `check.log`). `Intact` stays `replaced` on any error: with the security review's finding 1, a machine error after a session is `replaced` anyway, and every `Intact` call is after a session.
- **Low (the call-site wiring untested; an agent-induced ENOSPC): answered / fixed.** The wiring gap stands as `PLAN.md` D14 states. The induced error is fixed by the security review's finding 1: `write` only before the first session.
- Round 1's finding 3 (`GUIDE-fyr-matrix`): done with the E2E, after the commit.

title: Security review — PLAN.md P6: sandbox write failed against an agent in the sandbox
body:
# Security review — p6 sandbox write-failed reason   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: 42abc6e..working tree (uncommitted; .agents/scratch/p6/review2-code.diff)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The worst problem: the diff makes a run-caused failure gradeable (`sandbox replaced` is now a FAIL), but leaves an ungraded way out. The new `sandbox write failed` reason is an ERROR, and an ERROR reason beats every non-safety FAIL cause in `classify`. The comments and SPEC-fyr-eval step 15 say a machine error is something "no run could have caused". That is not true for the post-session sites. The agent runs as the operator's uid with `command(*)` on the host. From there it can push the box's own process or the machine into one of the listed error classes: resource exhaustion that is per-process, per-user or system-wide, or a filesystem it controls under the sandbox. When the box's first post-session open or remove then fails, the trial reads ERROR. ERROR trials are left out of c/n and pass^k, so a trial that would have been FAIL drops out of the measured rate. This is narrower than at HEAD, where a planted directory alone produced an ungraded ERROR. Work is not affected: `ReasonWrite` sits in `safetyReasons`, so nothing is fetched and the sandbox is kept. Ingest skips the new reason. No path that a replaced sandbox protected can be reached through the new reason.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `internal/sandbox/box.go:177-201` with `internal/eval/cause.go:24,70-74` — the machine-error classifier runs at sites that come after the agent ran: `After` → `unlink` → `removeInSandbox` (after.go:43-44), the retry in `ExitChecks` (after.go:58), and the second session's `agyOutputs` (session.go:46-48, docker.go:157-158). Before this diff, nothing the agent did after its session could be attributed to it with certainty. Now the agent has a choice of outcome: a refused open or remove reads FAIL `replaced`, while the same refusal under machine-error conditions reads ERROR `write`. Some of those conditions can be caused from inside the run. Which ones depend on the kernel: a system-wide file table, the box process's own descriptor limit when it belongs to the same uid, memory pressure, or a user-mounted filesystem under the sandbox (see the third finding). On ext4/xfs, a disk or quota fill does NOT turn an already-planted link, FIFO, directory or hard link into ENOSPC/EDQUOT, because opening or unlinking an existing name allocates nothing. The errors that are raised before the path lookup (file-table and memory allocation) do not depend on what is at the path. What this buys in eval: a FAIL (check, grant, denied, timeout, agent, replaced) turns into an ungraded ERROR and its sessions are not ingested. Safety checks c/d/e still win over the ERROR unless they fail open (next finding). What it buys in work: nothing. Remediation: count `ReasonWrite` as an ERROR only when it fires before the first session started (`!b.started` at the call). After a session it should read `replaced`, or at least never outrank a FAIL cause in `classify`. Also fix the "no run could have caused" claim in box.go:179-180, cause.go and SPEC-fyr-eval step 15 / the paragraph after the cause table.
- **[medium / confidence: high on code, medium on reachability]** `internal/sandbox/procs_linux.go:30` — `entries, _ := os.ReadDir("/proc")` discards the error, so safety check e passes silently when the read fails. That happens under exactly the error classes this diff now treats as innocent (descriptor or memory exhaustion). A run that has caused one of them can blind check e at the moment it runs. This predates the diff, but it weakens the diff's implicit assumption that a live process behind a machine error would be caught by check e. Remediation: fail closed. A failed `/proc` read fails the box `ReasonProcs`, with a note saying the check could not run. `fingerprint` (guard.go:202-204) and `scanCreds` (creds.go:76-77) already fail closed this way. `scanCreds`' `Lstat` error at creds.go:63-66 returns no findings and should get the same treatment.
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `internal/sandbox/box.go:156-166` (`Intact`), `cmd/fyr/eval.go:274-289` (`realDirs`), `internal/sandbox/box.go:206-230` (`os.Root`) — none of these detect a filesystem mounted inside the sandbox. On this host an unprivileged user can mount FUSE (`/dev/fuse` is 0666, `fusermount3` is setuid). A mount point is a directory and not a link, so `Intact` and `realDirs` accept it. `os.Root` documents that it "do[es] not prohibit traversal of filesystem boundaries", so `removeInSandbox` and the ingest cross into it. A filesystem the run controls chooses the errno for every box operation, so it can choose between `replaced` and `write` (first finding). It can also present any content to the credential scan and the ingest, and it can block box I/O. This predates the diff. Remediation: in `Intact`, compare each approved path's `st_dev` with the one recorded at guard a. Also refuse a sandbox whose subtree holds a mount, by reading `/proc/self/mountinfo` for mount points under `b.dir`. Treat either case as `replaced`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/sandbox/after.go:98-103` (`countLines`) — any `OpenRegular` refusal of `err.txt` returns 0, so a planted object or an unreadable file hides `auto-denied` lines. It neither reads `replaced` nor goes through the classifier. On `--runner host` the agent can rewrite `err.txt` anyway, so this mostly shows that check 12 is advisory on the host. Still, the read sites should fail in the graded direction: a refused read of the box's own `err.txt` should read `replaced`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/eval.go:244-245` — the ingest decides with a deny list of reasons. Each new integrity reason has to be added by hand, and this diff had to do exactly that. An allow list (ingest only when no integrity reason is present), or a shared list in `internal/sandbox` that both eval and work's `safetyReasons` read, would fail closed for the next reason.

Sites checked and found right: `Intact`'s `replaced` (box.go:161) stays unclassified. Its calls do not allocate descriptors, and a misread there goes to the graded direction. `Bash`'s log-open failure (session.go:153-156) fails setup or check, not write. `OpenRegular`'s fstat error, its hard-link refusal and its not-regular refusal are `fmt.Errorf` without `%w`, so they correctly read `replaced`. Work: `fetch.go:23` (`unsafe() || !Intact()`), `worker.go:159` (kept when unsafe) and the Verdict (FAIL for any reason) all treat `ReasonWrite` like `replaced`.

## Checked

- Secrets: none in the diff; the tests use synthetic errnos only.
- Injection: no new external input flows; notes pass through `Printable`.
- Authz/authn: trust boundary is the agent vs the box; covered above (grading, ingest, fetch).
- Crypto: none touched.
- Dependencies: go.mod/go.sum unchanged; `govulncheck ./...` (Go 1.27.3): 0 vulnerabilities affecting code, 1 in a required module not called (not inspected further).
- GCP surface: none touched.
- Tools: `go vet` on sandbox, work, eval, cmd/fyr clean; `go test -run 'TestFileFailed|TestUnsafeReasons|TestClassify|TestClassifyEveryReason'` and `TestEvalIngestSkips*` pass.

## Not examined

- `fyr search --refs <path> --kind bug` for each changed file (not run).
- The full SPEC-fyr-work failure-modes table; `internal/sandbox/docker.go` beyond lines 140-160 and the limits line; `creds.go` past line 90; `internal/eval/invoked.go`, `internal/work/slots.go`, `kickoff.go` read sites (their OpenRegular error handling not read).
- No experiment was run to confirm the kernel-level claims (allocation before lookup, mount crossing on this kernel); they rest on the os.Root documentation and kernel behaviour as known, hence medium confidence.
- The non-sandbox parts of the diff (eval_record.go, metrics estimators, trial record) were not reviewed for security.

## Outcome

- **Finding 1 (medium): fixed.** `fileFailed` gives `sandbox write failed` only when no session has started (`!b.started`): after one, the agent could have caused the machine error, so it is `sandbox replaced`, graded. `TestFileFailed` pins ENOSPC, EMFILE, ENOMEM and EROFS after a session as `replaced` (it failed before the fix). The comments, `SPEC-fyr-eval` step 15 and `PLAN.md` item 48 now say "before the first session".
- **Finding 2 (medium, pre-existing): deferred to `PLAN.md` item 49, P12b** (fix: check e fails closed as `procs`).
- **Finding 3 (medium, pre-existing): deferred to `PLAN.md` item 50, P12b** (fix: a mount under the sandbox is `sandbox replaced`).
- **Low 1 (`countLines` of `err.txt` fails open, pre-existing): deferred to `PLAN.md` item 49, P12b**, with `scanCreds`' `Lstat` (creds.go:63-66): every read site of the box's own files fails in the graded direction.
- **Low 2 (the ingest's deny list): deferred to `PLAN.md` item 51, P12b**: one integrity-reason list in `internal/sandbox`, read by eval's ingest and work's `safetyReasons`.

# Review — p7-per-row-evals-view   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: working tree against HEAD (dff3203), via .agents/scratch/p7/review/code.diff (code, tests, README.md, TDD.md) and records.diff (SPEC-fyr-eval, SPEC-fyr-metrics, SPEC-fyr-serve drafts); live files read for context. Lenses: code and docs.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing is broken in the new view's arithmetic, window handling, flag rules or the dirty-key narrowing, and the three drafted records match the code (checked row by row: flags, columns, `--harness`, `--project` refusal, missing-store exit 1, `/evals` and `/metrics/report` behaviour). `go vet`, `gofmt -l` and `go test -race` over `cmd/fyr`, `internal/{metrics,serve,trail,harness}` pass, as do `.`, `internal/check` and `internal/eval`. The defects are stale restatements of the metrics subcommand list, which a docs lens must catch, and one limit of the narrowed harness key that no document states. The first finding is a cheap edit and should land before the commit.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/help_text.go:42` and `cmd/fyr/main.go:19` — both still list the metrics subcommands as `ingest, show, report, export`. `fyr help` (the top-level page) and the package doc never name `evals`, while `metricsSubverbs` (`verb_metrics.go:38`) and `fyr help metrics` do. No test pins the top-level line (the suite passes without the word), so the next reader finds the new verb only by reading `fyr help metrics`. Fix: add `evals` to both lines. `DEPLOY-remote` (current record, line 84 of its body) also lists the read-only metrics subverbs as `metrics show|report|export`; `evals` is read-only the same way (`writesState`, `run_dispatch.go:187`, answers true for `ingest` only), so name it there too.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/verb_metrics.go:65` — `ingest` refuses a stray flag with "--%s belongs to show or report", but `--since`, `--until` and `--json` now belong to `evals` as well. `fyr metrics ingest --json` is pointed at the wrong subcommands. Fix: "show, report or evals".
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/metrics/verb.go:59` — `shAgentSub` lacks `evals`, so a session's `fyr metrics evals --json` is classified as the verb `fyr metrics --json`; `verb_test.go:45` shows an unknown third word is dropped. Only the recorded verb string is affected.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `SPEC-fyr-eval` draft (§ Known limits, body line 180) and `cmd/fyr/eval_trial.go:24-26` — both state only that two dirty trees at one HEAD share a key. After this change an edit outside `context/ agents/ commands/ rules/ workflows/ skills/` no longer marks the key at all. That includes `cmd/` and `internal/`, which build the `fyr` each sandbox runs (`evalSelf = os.Executable`, `cmd/fyr/eval.go:28`); two different binaries at one HEAD now share a clean key, so `saturated` and `unstable` can mix them. D16 chose this on purpose, so it is a documentation gap, not a bug. Fix: add the sentence to both places.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `.agents/scratch/p7/rec/GUIDE-fyr-matrix.body.md:58-60` — the matrix has rows for `metrics ingest`, `show` and `report`/`export` but none for `metrics evals`, and the draft carries no edit for it. If the P7 checkpoint's E2E adds the row, ignore this.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. No unreferenced export found; `metricsSummary` now serves `show` only and its comment says so. The template move is byte-identical to the old one except the new `{{with .Evals}}` section (diffed).
2. Flow tracing — pass. All `RenderReport` and `WriteReport` callers are updated. `--harness` is refused on every other subcommand (`metricsShowOptions`, `metricsFlagsOutside`). The evals window matches `show`'s ([since, until), 30-day default). `DirtyUnder` filters all four reads (HEAD listing, work tree, index, untracked) with one `keep`, and `indexed != len(inHead)` stays consistent because both count only kept paths. The unclaimed-session rule (`run` NULL or unclaimed, outcome set) matches `show`'s A6. Report and `/evals` call the same `Store.Evals`.
3. Standards conformance — findings 1 to 3 above (vocabulary enumerations not all changed). `rowAcc.addSession` (`evals_acc.go:1376` of the diff) is one function with cyclomatic complexity well above the 10 of `rules/code-modularity.md`; it mirrors `show_add.go`'s step counting. Noted, not a correctness defect. File sizes are within the 350/600 line rules (largest new file 262 lines).
4. Directory layout — pass. New files sit beside their package; no `utils`/`helpers` file.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only, no new dependency, no security primitive involved.
6. Decoupling — pass with a note: `evals_acc.go` re-implements `show_add.go`'s per-step counting, and its replay dedupe key differs (per row version, where `show` keys on vendor, label and step). The two can drift unless changed together; the spec says "as `show` counts them", so a shared step walker would hold that claim by construction.

## Not examined
- The P7 change record and the must-fail mutations that `SPEC-fyr-metrics`'s new test row cites ("each with a must-fail mutation in the P7 change record"): not drafted in the dispatch, so that claim is unchecked. I did not run my own mutations.
- `fyr check` against the drafted records (it reads the brain store, and no real home may be used).
- `GUIDE-testing` and `GUIDE-eval` prose beyond a grep for `metrics show --label eval` (no stale restatement found there); the interactive harness-map page; real-browser rendering of the report and `/evals`.
- `PLAN.md` was excluded from the diff and only grepped for D16 and item 53.

## Outcome

Written by the main thread, 2026-10-31. Every finding fixed; no second round: the fixes are one-word list edits, a message and two comments, each pinned below.

1. **Fixed.** `cmd/fyr/help_text.go` (the short page's metrics line) and `cmd/fyr/main.go`'s doc comment name `evals`; `DEPLOY-remote` § the state dir lists `metrics show|report|evals|export` among the read-only verbs (only `ingest` migrates, `run_dispatch.go` `writesState`). Pinned: `TestHelpShortPageListsEveryVerb` now compares both lines with `metricsSubverbs`; reverting either line fails it.
2. **Fixed.** The ingest refusal reads `belongs to show, report or evals` (`TestMetricsIngestRefusalNamesEvals`, fails on the old text); `shAgentSub` holds `evals` (`TestVerb` case `fyr metrics evals --json --harness`, fails without it).
3. **Fixed (docs).** `SPEC-fyr-eval` § Known limits and `cmd/fyr/eval_trial.go`'s comment state that a tree whose only edits are under `cmd/`, `internal/` or the trail keeps the clean key, so two binaries from one HEAD share it and mix in the per-key flags (PLAN.md D16 chose the installed directories). `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` gains the `metrics evals` rows at the checkpoint, with the E2E.

title: Review — PLAN.md P8, the suite grammar's four columns (code and docs), round 1: REQUEST CHANGES, 3 findings fixed
body:
# Review — p8-suite-grammar   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: uncommitted working tree vs HEAD 53cad0a (`.agents/scratch/p8/code.diff`, `.agents/scratch/p8/records.diff`; lenses code + docs)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The suite grammar change is sound, but `go test ./cmd/fyr` is red. `TestEvalListNeedsNoHome` still asserts the old `--list` line format, which this diff changed. The Definition of Done command (`go test ./...`) therefore fails. One spec line (`SPEC-fyr-metrics` schema comment) also still says the per-row trial fields are NULL until Phase 5b writes them, which P8 now does. `go vet` and `gofmt -l` are clean, and `internal/eval`, `internal/metrics` and the root package pass.

## Findings
- **[high / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/eval_home_test.go:182` — `strings.HasPrefix(out.String(), "ok  -  named\n")` is the pre-ADR-085 format. `--list` now prints `ok  -  named  v1  capability`. Run: `go test -count=1 ./cmd/fyr` gives `--- FAIL: TestEvalListNeedsNoHome` (the only failure there). The diff updated `TestEvalVerbList` but missed this second restatement. Fix: expect the prefix `ok  -  named  v1  capability\n`.
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `SPEC-fyr-metrics` record, schema block, the `row_version INTEGER, kind TEXT, cluster TEXT, expect TEXT` line (line 279 of the current body, `.agents/scratch/p8/SPEC-fyr-metrics.md`) — its comment reads "NULL until the eval-metrics plan's Phase 5b writes them". Since P8 (Phase 5a) `fyr eval` writes all four, so the comment misstates the code. The diff edited the § Data trial paragraph (line 295) and added an "Updated" line (line 11), but not this restatement. Fix: change it to "NULL for a trial stored before ADR-085 (a reader takes the defaults)".
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/metrics/evals.go:156` with `cmd/fyr/eval_trial.go:107` — the per-row view keys on `COALESCE(row_version, 0)`, and `SPEC-fyr-metrics` line 203 says "`-` before the suite has a version column". After P8 a new trial of an unchanged row stores version 1, while every earlier trial has NULL, which reads as 0. In `fyr metrics evals` one row's history therefore splits into a `-` line and a `v1` line, and its flags and harness-key counts split with it. ADR-085 defers "NULL reads as v1" to P9 and says so, so this is an acknowledged transition. Still, `SPEC-fyr-eval` § The suite (and `GUIDE-eval` § Columns) say in the present tense that "trials key on the row and its version, so a row's history restarts". Soften that to say what holds now, or land the P9 read-side before a release. This is not blocking.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `GUIDE-eval` § Columns (the new `expect` bullet) and `SPEC-fyr-eval` § The suite (the `expect` bullet) — "matched in any order at read time" and "compared as strings at read time" describe a reader that does not exist yet (P9). The parser and store only record the list. Not wrong as a specification, but an unmarked present tense; add "from P9".

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. The new `Kind*` constants, `kinds`, `optionalHeader`, `expectMax` and the helpers all have callers. No commented-out code.
2. Flow tracing — pass apart from the finding above. `ParseSuite`, `suiteStart`, `parseRow`, `optionalCells`, `Row`, `trialOf` (via `byID`), `RecordTrial` and the `--list` output are consistent end to end. Error messages carry the GUIDE-eval line. `expect` is capped at 120 bytes, the same bound `internal/metrics` enforces (`trials.go:63`), so a parsed row is not refused at the store. Seven-column and eleven-column tables both parse. The new tests can fail: the mutation log `.agents/scratch/p8/mutations.txt` shows a dropped `Expect` failing `TestEvalTrialSuiteFields/long` and the 120-byte boundary failing `TestSuiteGrammarLong`. I did not re-run the mutations.
3. Standards conformance — FAIL for the stale test assertion (finding 1) and the stale schema comment (finding 2). Restatement grep (`README.md`, `SDD.md`, `TDD.md`, `context/`, `agents/`, `skills/` non-vendored, the trail's specs, guides and adrs) found no other copy of the old `--list` format or the seven-column header outside historical closed records. `GUIDE-testing` § 3j ("`eval --list | diff - <list saved before the change>`") compares against a baseline saved beforehand, so it stays valid. `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.
4. Directory layout — pass. `internal/eval/suite_columns.go` sits beside `suite.go`, and the new tests sit beside the code they cover.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only, no new dependency. The identifier regexp is copied from `internal/metrics/writer.go`, which ADR-085 justifies because `internal/eval` links no SQLite driver (D10). Nothing in the diff touches auth or crypto.
6. Decoupling — pass. The copied regexp creates a drift risk between `internal/eval` and `internal/metrics`. It is stated in a comment but not pinned by a test (low; `RecordTrial` still validates cluster and expect only for printable and length, so a drift would not corrupt the store).

## Not examined
- I did not run the full `go test ./...` (race, 30m); I ran `go vet` and `go test -count=1` on `./internal/eval ./internal/metrics ./cmd/fyr .`.
- I did not run `fyr eval` with a real Antigravity session or `fyr eval --list` against the real `GUIDE-eval` (the 63-row claim in `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` is unverified).
- I did not review `TestSuiteHarness`'s `want`, because GUIDE-eval rows are unchanged in this diff.
- I did not re-run the mutations in `mutations.txt`.
- I did not review PLAN.md or the `.agents/trail.jsonl` diff beyond the records named in the dispatch.
- I ran no git probe, so BUG-204 is not engaged.

## Outcome

1. Fixed: `TestEvalListNeedsNoHome` expects `ok  -  named  v1  capability`. It was the one failing test, and `go test ./cmd/fyr` passes again.
2. Fixed: `SPEC-fyr-metrics`' schema comment says the four columns are written since ADR-085, and that NULL on an older trial reads as the defaults.
3. Fixed in P8 rather than deferred. P7's view already keyed on `COALESCE(row_version, 0)`, so the split would have been live from this commit. A NULL version, and a session no trial claims, now read as 1, and the `v` column prints `1` where it printed `-`. `TestEvalRowsVersionDefault` failed first, and each of its two triggers fails it when mutated back (the NULL trial, the unclaimed session). The goldens of `TestEvalRows`, `TestEvalsTable` and `TestMetricsEvals` print `1`. The eval home still shows 63 rows and the same suite line, so nothing split. `SPEC-fyr-eval` and `GUIDE-eval` now say that the per-kind rates and the `expect` match are P9's. ADR-085 says the same: it was stored this session and not yet committed. Round 2 reviews the fixes.

title: Security — PLAN.md P8, the suite parser's four columns: CLEAR, 2 low findings fixed
body:
# Security review — p8-suite-columns   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: 53cad0a (HEAD)..working tree, uncommitted (`.agents/scratch/p8/code.diff`, 543 lines: `internal/eval/suite.go`, new `internal/eval/suite_columns.go`, `cmd/fyr/eval.go`, `eval_record.go`, `eval_trial.go`, `internal/metrics/trials.go`, their tests, TDD.md), plus where the values go: `cmd/fyr/eval.go` (`readSuite`, `listEval`, `evalRefuse`), `cmd/fyr/eval_trial.go` (`trialOf`, `trialText`), `internal/metrics/trials.go` (`validate`, `RecordTrial`), `internal/metrics/evals.go:156` (the one reader of `row_version`), and ADR-085 as stored in `.agents/trail.jsonl`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: CLEAR (no exploitable weakness; two low hardening/correctness findings)

None of the four new cells can reach a shell, the filesystem or an interpolated query. Here is where each one goes. `version` is parsed to an int from `^[1-9][0-9]{0,8}$`. `kind` must be one of four fixed words. `cluster` and each word of `expect` must match an ASCII identifier pattern (`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.:@/-]{0,63}$`) with no control bytes, no `|` and no spaces except the single space between `expect` words. All four go only to (a) `fyr eval --list`, where the line passes through `search.Printable` anyway, and (b) `metrics.RecordTrial`. RecordTrial checks them again (printable, at most 120 bytes) and binds them as `?` parameters in a fixed `INSERT OR IGNORE`, so SQL injection is not possible. Error messages quote the cell values with `%q`, and `evalRefuse` passes them through `Printable`, so the terminal cannot be injected through a refusal. Bad input is refused, not passed through: every refusal makes `ParseSuite` return `nil, err`, and both callers turn that into exit 2 before anything runs. The suite's trust is unchanged (SPEC-fyr-eval D30; ADR-085: "no new cell runs as code"). The `setup` and `check` cells already run as bash, and the new cells are strictly less powerful than those. The worst issue is a correctness hazard that depends on evaluation order (finding 1). It has no security impact: if it went wrong, values would be lost, not unchecked values let through.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/eval/suite.go:135` — `return r, optionalCells(&r, cells, n)`. This reads `r` and calls a function that changes `r` through a pointer, both in one operand list. The Go spec does not fix the order between evaluating a plain variable and a function call there (spec § Order of evaluation, the `[]int{a, f()}` example). gc happens to evaluate `r` after the call, and the tests pass on gc. But a different compiler or a future gc could return the row from before the call: `Version 0`, `Kind ""`, `Cluster ""`. Those would be stored as NULL, and `--list` would print `v0`. That quietly undoes ADR-085's own rule against storing NULL for an empty cell. The validation error still comes back, so nothing unvalidated gets through. Trigger: any toolchain that evaluates the operands left to right. Fix: `err := optionalCells(&r, cells, n); return r, err`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/eval/suite_columns.go:46` — when the cluster cell is empty, the default cluster is `r.ID`. But `validID` (`suite.go:37`) has no length limit, while an explicit cluster is held to the 64-character identifier rule (`identWord`, line 26). ADR-085 says the cluster is "the row's id or one word under the identifier rule". An id of 65 to about 100 bytes therefore stores a cluster that the explicit-cell path would refuse. The store only checks printable and ≤120 bytes (`internal/metrics/trials.go:63-66`), so this is an integrity gap, not injection: the id's characters are a subset of `identWord`'s. Ids longer than about 100 bytes are already refused at the store through `run`/`label` (the trial write fails, is reported, and the exit is non-zero). That part was there before this change. Trigger: a suite row with a long id and an empty cluster cell. Fix: give `validID` a length limit at parse time (64, matching `identWord`), or run the default through `identWord` too, with a refusal test.

## Checked
- Secrets: none in the diff or its tests. Error messages echo only suite cells, quoted with `%q`.
- Injection: SQL is parameterised (`internal/metrics/trials.go:89-93`). Terminal: `--list` uses `search.Printable`, and refusals use `%q` plus `Printable`. Shell: `grep` of `.Cluster/.Expect/.Kind/.Version` across `cmd/` and `internal/` finds only `eval.go:134`, `eval_trial.go:67` and `trials.go`. No exec, no path join, no template. Per ADR-085, `expect` is compared as strings at read time and never executed. Its entries can look like paths (`a/../b` matches `identWord`), which is harmless today but is worth keeping in mind if a later phase ever uses an entry as a path or a command.
- Bounds/DoS: Go's regexp engine (RE2) runs in linear time with fixed limits; `expectList` is linear, with its 120-byte limit checked after the join (exactly 120 accepted, more refused, both tested). `version` can have at most 9 digits, so `Atoi` cannot overflow, and its ignored error cannot occur after the regex match. The input is a committed trail record body.
- Fail-closed: every `optionalCells` or `expectList` error makes `ParseSuite` return nil, and both callers of `readSuite` refuse with exit 2. A partial 8-column header is refused as "no table". A short table and a long table together are refused as "a second suite table". Seven cells under the long header are refused. `byID[r.Row]` in `eval_record.go` cannot miss, because results come from `rows`, and duplicate ids are refused at parse.
- Header parsing: `suiteLongHeader` is built with copy-then-append, so it does not share `suiteHeader`'s backing array. `append(cells[7:], "", "", "", "")` only writes past the indices already copied into `r`, so it is safe.
- Authz/authn: not touched. The run path still requires the suite to match HEAD's (`readSuite` with `atHead`), and `--list` reads the working export, as before (D19).
- Crypto: none touched; nothing hand-rolled.
- Dependencies: `go.mod` unchanged; the new imports are standard library only (`slices`, `strconv`). `govulncheck ./...`: "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities" (1 in required modules, not called; the known set per DEPLOY-local). npm: there is no JS ecosystem in this diff.
- GCP surface: none touched.
- Tests run bare: `go test ./internal/eval -run TestSuite` ok; `go test ./cmd/fyr -run 'TestEvalVerbList|TestEvalTrialSuiteFields|TestTrialText'` ok; `go vet` on the three packages clean. The verifier's full run was not attempted here.
- Past failures: `fyr search --refs <path> --kind bug` (with `--home .agents/scratch/security-home`) on all six changed Go files found only BUG-194 and BUG-188 against `cmd/fyr/eval.go`. Neither concerns the suite parser.

## Not examined
- The full test suite (`go test -race ./...`) — that is the verifier's job.
- `internal/metrics/evals.go` and `evals_write.go` beyond the `row_version` select and print. Phase P9, which will key on `kind`, `cluster` and `expect`, does not exist yet, so its consumers could not be reviewed.
- The committed `GUIDE-eval` record's current rows: whether any id is already over 64 bytes (this matters for finding 2) was not checked.
- The `PLAN.md`, `TDD.md` and `.agents/trail.jsonl` hunks of the working tree, beyond ADR-085's text: these are docs and records, not code.

## Outcome

1. Fixed: `parseRow` assigns `err := optionalCells(&r, …)` and then returns `r, err`. There is no test, because gc already evaluates `r` after the call, so no test on this toolchain can fail without the fix. The parse tests pin the result either way. `PLAN.md` D17 says so.
2. Fixed: an id is at most 64 bytes (`validID`), the identifier rule's bound, so the default cluster obeys the rule an explicit one does. Test first: `TestSuiteRefusals`' "an id past 64 bytes" failed before the change, and a 64-byte id parses with itself as its cluster (`TestSuiteGrammarLong`). No row in this repository's suite comes near 64 bytes, and `TestSuiteHarness` passes. `SPEC-fyr-eval` § The suite and ADR-085 say so.

title: Review — PLAN.md P8, round 2 over the fixes: APPROVE WITH NITS, 1 doc nit fixed
body:
# Review — p8-suite-grammar round 2   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: round-1 fixes only (`.agents/scratch/p8/fixes-code.diff`, `fixes-records.diff`) against the working tree on HEAD 53cad0a; lenses code + docs

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

All five round-1 findings (reviewer 1-4, security 1-2) are fixed, and I found no new defect in the fixes. `go test -count=1 ./internal/eval ./internal/metrics ./internal/serve` and `go test -count=1 ./cmd/fyr -run 'Eval|Metrics'` pass, and `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l cmd internal` are clean. The version default is consistent across the trial reader, the session reader, the text table and `--json`. One restatement is left stale (`SPEC-fyr-metrics` § Per-row view, `--json`: "`version` when known"), which is cosmetic.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `SPEC-fyr-metrics` record, § Per-row view, the `--json` sentence (line 212 of `.agents/scratch/p8/SPEC-fyr-metrics.md`): "each with `row`, `version` when known". After this fix `Version` is never 0 (NULL reads as 1), so the key is always present, and the `omitempty` tag in `internal/metrics/evals.go:32` can no longer trigger. The doc describes a case that does not exist. Fix: say "`version`" without the qualifier. The `omitempty` tag is harmless and needs no change.

## Round-1 findings, one by one
- Reviewer 1 (stale `--list` prefix, `cmd/fyr/eval_home_test.go`): fixed. It now expects `ok  -  named  v1  capability\n`, and `TestEvalListNeedsNoHome` passes.
- Reviewer 2 (stale schema comment): fixed. The line now reads "written by fyr eval since ADR-085; NULL on a trial stored before, read as the defaults".
- Reviewer 3 (the `-` line splitting from the `v1` line): fixed in code and not just reworded. `COALESCE(row_version, 1)` handles trials, and `t.key.version = 1` handles sessions that no trial claims, so both land on the same `rowKey`. `TestEvalRowsVersionDefault` stores versions 0 (NULL), 1 and 2 plus an old session, and expects `r v1 n3; r v2 n1`. I traced the 0 case: `RecordTrial` binds `NULLIF(?, 0)`, so a zero stores NULL. The flags, harness-key counts (`knownCounts`, `historyFlags`) and `suiteOf` all key on `rowKey`, so they merge with it.
- Reviewer 4 (present-tense claims about P9's read side): fixed. `GUIDE-eval` § Columns and `SPEC-fyr-eval` § The suite now say what each trial stores, and they say that the per-kind rates and the `expect` match are `PLAN.md` P9's.
- Security 1 (operand evaluation order in `return r, optionalCells(&r, ...)`): fixed as suggested, `err := optionalCells(&r, cells, n); return r, err`.
- Security 2 (id longer than 64 bytes as default cluster): fixed. `validID` is `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`, and the error message names the cap. The tests are a 64-byte id kept as the cluster, and a 65-byte id refused. The longest id in the current GUIDE-eval rows is 23 bytes, so no existing row is affected, and ids are only checked at parse time. The run key `<stamp>/<row>/<i>` and the `eval=<id>` label stay far below the store's 120-byte bound.

## Consumers of the version default
Only `internal/metrics/evals.go` (the two readers) and `evals_write.go` `Table()` read `Version`. `Table()` is the one source for the text table, the report block and `fyr serve` /evals, so all three print `1` and the tests were updated together: `metrics_evals_test.go`, `evals_test.go`, `serve/evals_test.go`. `--json` now always carries `version`, at least 1. I found no other reader, and no JSON consumer inside the repository. The only behaviour change is that older stores show `v1` instead of `-`. The transition cost is that old trials of a row whose content changed before P8 now read as v1. That is inherent in the default and is stated in ADR-085.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. The `Version > 0` branch in `Table()` was removed together with the case it served.
2. Flow tracing — pass. NULL to 1 in both readers, then `rowKey`, flags, suite line, `Table()`, `--json`. The new test fails if either reader is reverted: its own record says each trigger was mutated, and I did not re-run those mutations.
3. Standards conformance — pass, with the one stale restatement above. The docs for the id cap, the `--list` format, the schema comment and the P9 deferral agree with the code. The ADR-085 consequences paragraph names `TestEvalRowsVersionDefault` and `TestSuiteGrammar`, and the other tests it names exist.
4. Directory layout — pass. No new files in the fixes.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. A `COALESCE` default and one assignment. No dependency.
6. Decoupling — pass. The default is applied where the store is read (`internal/metrics`), so no other package learns about it.

## Not examined
- I did not re-run the mutation checks, or the full `go test -race ./...`.
- I did not review the P8 code that round 1 already covered and the fixes did not touch.
- I did not check the 63-row real-home claim in the new `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` row (the 0.137 s run on the eval home).
- I ran no git probe, so BUG-204 did not come up.

## Outcome

1. Fixed: `SPEC-fyr-metrics` § Per-row view's `--json` sentence now reads `version` (1 or more) where it said "when known". This is a docs edit and needs no test. `omitempty` stays: it never applies now, and the tag is harmless. This is the second and last round (`review` Steps 4–5).

title: Review — cold read of the fyr auto-mode plan: design needs revision, 21 gaps answered by D2–D16, Open 1 to the operator
body:
# Review — plan fyr auto-mode, cold-reader check   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: `.agents/scratch/automode/plan.md` (record PLAN-2026-10-31-1636-plan-fyr-auto-mode-idle-time-self-improvement-of), no diff. Read also: the research record, `internal/work` (work.go, preflight.go, reflog.go), `internal/sandbox` (after.go, box.go, guard.go), `internal/dream` (timer.go, agy_process.go, response.go, dream.go `activityIn`), `cmd/fyr/status.go`, `cmd/fyr/harnessmap_test.go`, `cmd/fyr/eval_register.go`, SPEC-fyr-work, GUIDE-eval, PRD.md R0/R8, SDD.md:152.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES — design needs revision; implementation not ready

Worst first: Phase 0 cannot pass its own verify clause (`TestHarnessMap` reads every `fyr <word>` in the map, so a `fyr auto` label fails until the verb exists, and `AGENTS.md` rule 3 forbids the map line landing apart from the code). The plan's `work.Run` contract is misread in four places (branch name, sandbox root, record kinds a worker may add, denial handling), which makes Phases 4 and 6 unbuildable as written. The kill switch can be undone by a running `run`. The apply step runs model-authored test code on the host. Several verify clauses name fixtures that cannot produce their condition.

## Findings (gaps), each with where it comes from

G1. **[high / high] Phase 0 contradicts `TestHarnessMap` and AGENTS.md rule 3.** `cmd/fyr/harnessmap_test.go:28-33` runs `fyr ([a-z]+)` over the whole mermaid block and fails any name absent from `shortPage`; nothing "reads the label only once Phase 1 adds the verb" (D3's premise is false, so D3's fallback is the case that holds). Phase 0's verify (`go test ./...` exit 0) fails if the map line is drawn there. `AGENTS.md` rule 3 says a path change lands in ONE commit with the code, docs and map, so the map line, rule 1's sentence and the test's verb list belong to Phase 1's commit; Phase 0 carries PRD.md and the ADR. Also `files:` of Phase 0 lists the test, which Phase 1 must then own.

G2. **[high / high] "Word for word from the approved wording" has no wording.** The research § Requirement edits (research record lines 206-214) are descriptions ("The edit would add ..."), not sentences; D2 and § PRD.md edits say Phase 0 writes the text, and the sentence-level approval does not exist. Phase 0 will invent PRD text under a claim of approval. Name who approves the sentences before the commit as a `who: user` box.

G3. **[medium / high] Restatements not listed.** `SDD.md:152` (§ Security: "three things leave the machine ... the operator's `fyr work` workers"), `PRD.md:81` R8 ("which only the operator's own session starts" is false once a timer starts workers), R0's `enforced by:` list (`PRD.md:38-40`, includes `TestHarnessMap`), `README.md`, `DEPLOY-local`. The plan lists only SDD M19. Run `scripts/restatement-grep.sh` over "three things", "only the operator's own session", "never edits a project".

G4. **[high / high] `work.Run` branch naming.** `Kickoff.Branch()` is `work/<file base name>` (`internal/work/kickoff.go`), the name must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$` (no slash), and `branchesFree` (`preflight.go`) refuses a run when `work/<name>` already exists in the checkout. The plan says the kept branch is `auto/<stamp>/<task>` and the apply step merges `work/<name>`. Undecided: the Kickoff file name (must be unique per run or the second failure of a task class on a project is refused for ever), where the Kickoff file lives (not in the project tree, `leadClean` demands a clean tree), the rename from `work/<name>` to `auto/<stamp>/<task>`, and who deletes `work/<name>` after a PASS.

G5. **[high / high] Sandbox root and `Options.Home`.** `Run` computes `sandbox.Root(o.Home, "work")` = `<Home>/.config/fyr/work` (`work.go`, `sandbox/box.go` `Root`). The plan's `~/.config/fyr/auto/work/` is not reachable with "additive options only" unless an option names the verb directory; a fake Home would break the token path (`RealHome`) and check c. Separately, check c fingerprints the real state directory except the verb directories and the exact writer names in `SkipStores` (SPEC-fyr-work line 172). `auto/` is a new top-level entry written (state, lock, log) while a worker runs, so every auto worker fails `real config changed` unless `auto`'s exact names join the skip list. The plan does not say so. The skip list then leaves `state.json` unwatched (SPEC-fyr-work line 330: a worker may write a listed entry unseen), so a host-runner worker running as the operator's uid could raise `level` or set `enabled`. E2E (d) does not test this (see G15). Also the machine-wide worker limit counts per root, so auto's root is not counted against the operator's own `fyr work` run.

G6. **[high / high] A worker may add only `handoff` and `change` records** (SPEC-fyr-work step 7, D138; refusal otherwise `changed outside its Files`), and "no sandbox brain store is opened" (ADR-063). Phase 6's retro-lite, memory consolidation (retire), memory candidates and `feedback` outputs are memory/feedback records in the global brain store; there is no channel from the worker to the store. The plan must decide: worker drafts under `DraftsDir` and Go writes the records (with provenance `derived`), or something else. As written Phase 6 is unbuildable.

G7. **[high / medium] The denial rule contradicts existing code.** `internal/sandbox/after.go:21-24` already fails a box on ANY `auto-denied` line in `err.txt` (`ReasonDenied`), so "3 consecutive or 20 in total" can never be reached by the post-hoc check; a mid-run stop (the word "stops") needs a monitor/kill option in `work.Run` that the plan does not list. The dream's `denied_actions` parse (`internal/dream/response.go:42-62`) reads one `-p` result event and treats any denial as "no answer"; it counts nothing consecutive and reads no worker conversation. Decide: keep the any-denial FAIL, or add a mid-run monitor (and say which file/option).

G8. **[high / high] The kill switch can be undone.** `state.json` holds operator config (`enabled`, `level`) and run counters (`today`, `projects`). A `run` that read `enabled:true` and works for up to 30 minutes plus apply writes the file back at its end (or at a gate re-read between projects) and overwrites a concurrent `fyr auto off`. G1 is read once; only G3/G4 are re-read between projects. Decide: split config from counters, `off` takes no lock and `run` re-reads `enabled` before each project and before the apply, with a must-fail test. Also unspecified: `off` and `status` with a corrupt state file (the failure table says only that `run` fails closed, exit 1); the kill switch must still remove the timer.

G9. **[high / medium] The apply step runs model-authored code on the host.** Step 3 executes the project's test command outside the sandbox/docker, with the operator's HOME, network and token, over the worker's diff. Trust-boundaries lists "the project's own tests" as a gate but not as an execution risk. Also: (a) the rubric denies only `*_test.go` named by `enforced by:` and does not deny `AGENTS.md` (the very `## Setup commands` block step 3 reads), CI files or other tests, so a worker can weaken the check that judges it; which tree's `AGENTS.md` is read (main or candidate) is not stated; (b) this repo's block is not a test command: it holds `go mod download` (network), `go run ./cmd/fyr install --home ...`, `govulncheck` (known findings) and an `&&` chain whose `gofmt -l` exits 0 when it lists files; "line by line, each bare" does not say which lines count. Decide where the tests run (container, same runner, or a stated acceptance with the operator), which lines of the block are the test command (an explicit fenced marker?), and protect the gate files.

G10. **[medium / high] Apply-step git mechanics.** `git worktree add` of `main` fails while `main` is checked out; G9 does not require the checkout's branch to be `main` (nor name the default branch of a project that uses `master`); "fast-forward the checkout's main" on a checked-out branch is `merge --ff-only` in the checkout (an `update-ref` leaves the tree dirty); the HEAD/reflog/tree compare is a check-then-act with the operator able to return in between (no lock on the checkout); the lead git calls must use `leadGit`'s options (`--no-replace-objects`, hooks off, commit-graph off, ADR-083) and a project's `commit.gpgsign` or hooks can fail the squash commit. The plan names none.

G11. **[high / high] Task classes are not specified.** (a) "The task class's allowed paths" (§ The runner) are never listed; `Files:` is the scope check's whole input. (b) Twelve classes in the priority list map to catalog numbers only by the levels table (research record § catalog, 22 tasks): the list mixes triggers and levels (eval re-runs 10th and harness-only; mini-audit is catalog 22, harness-only; retro-lite, consolidation, mini-audit have no "health finding" to choose from). (c) "Fixed priority" and "rotation key `last_task` so one class never starves" conflict; fixed priority starves by construction. (d) The outcome per class is not stated: applied to `main`, kept on a branch (research: distill drafts on a branch; retro-lite proposals), or a proposal. (e) A "spec" or record edit (spec-drift) is an edit of `.agents/trail.jsonl` text in a clone with no brain store; how the worker edits it and how the project's store loads it after the fast-forward (the next `fyr record` call loads a changed export) is not said. (f) Unmigrated projects (`migrated(p.Root)` in `dream.go`) have no trail; skip or ask.

G12. **[medium / high] Rubric drift.** § Risk rubric says "the research record § The risk rubric, as data" but drops items: anything outside the sandbox clone (the operator's checkout, `~/.config/fyr/` beyond own state, the network beyond the model and skills.sh), "deleting anything a record names", "a change whose gates did not all pass", "text asking for any of the above". Yet catalog task 6 runs `govulncheck` and `go list -m -u` (network) in the free checks, and the apply step writes the operator's checkout. Decide the source of truth and reconcile (the network claim also belongs in § Trust boundaries and R8's edit).

G13. **[medium / high] Phase ordering within Phase 1/2.** Phase 1 builds "gates G1-G9, one test per gate with a must-fail mutation", but G6 needs the `/usage` parser (Phase 2) and the `today.runs` counter (Phase 4). Gate order also puts G6 (an `agy -p "/usage"` call, every hour, every machine) before the cheap per-project gates G7-G9. Which side of the direction "under floor" means remaining or used is ambiguous (`floor_5h` 0.5 and the table text "below the floor" vs failure-mode text `<n>% of 5h`). A1 (output shape) is assumed in Phase 1 and checked in Phase 2.

G14. **[medium / medium] Gate semantics.** "Holds" means "stops the run" in G1-G3 and G5-G9 but G4's row is worded as the condition "user present", with an `or` chain with no precedence (`Active=yes, IdleHint=no, LockedHint=no, or idle under user_idle, or a /dev/pts atime ...`); "a graphical logind session" is not defined (Type x11/wayland?); G1-G6 are machine-wide while the text says "ends the run for that project"; the source that enumerates registered projects is not named (the dream's `search.Global` list), and G7 is then always satisfied unless the marker vanished. G5 (an interactive `agy` the operator left open overnight) blocks auto all night; say so or accept it. Dry-run: whether `--dry-run` writes `auto.log`, `projects[].gates`, takes the lock, calls `/usage`, or runs free checks that write (`fyr metrics ingest` writes `metrics.db`; `observe` "writes only its report records and `auto/`" is false for task 3, and `fyr index` writes `search.db`). `review-standards` § 8 requires the read-only mode to resolve every guard and a test that it performs no write.

G15. **[high / high] Verify fixtures that do not produce their condition.**
 - E2E (d): a fixture project holds no `GUIDE-eval` record, and no class's `Files:` names it, so "no change to either" holds without any model resistance (it tests the scope check, not the injection). The "level" lives in `~/.config/fyr/auto/state.json`, outside the clone; the test that matters is a host-runner worker writing the real state file (G5), not covered.
 - E2E (a): "names gate G5 for every project" needs G1-G4 to pass first; on dave G3/G4 depend on the machine (A5 says G4 passes as unknown). Name the fake `Env` so it is repeatable; as written it depends on a live session.
 - E2E (b)/(c): "an idle registered fixture project" needs G8 to see 6 h idle: `.git/logs/HEAD`'s entry time (backdate with `GIT_COMMITTER_DATE`), file mtimes (`os.Chtimes`), `trail.jsonl` mtime and no conversation within 6 h; a fixture made now is not idle. The plan does not say how it is made, nor that the eval fixture's marker (`registerClone`, `eval_register.go`) is tied to the eval home's key, which `--home .agents/scratch/auto` does not share. "A stale spec" needs the `spec-stale` rule's condition (`internal/check/specs.go`: commits to the spec's code paths since its stamp); name the fixture.
 - E2E (e): "a skill edit that lowers its row's pass count" is stochastic at `--runs 3`; the edit must be a planted deterministic breaker (and the held-out set is hidden only if it is not in the clone: see G17).
 - Phase 5's "a fixture remote whose URL fails" proves no push only if the test also asserts no git network subcommand ran; a refused URL passes a build that never pushes AND one that pushes after failing; say what is asserted.
 - Phase 2's fixture "from a real `agy -p /usage`" holds account data; the redaction step is not stated.

G16. **[high / medium] Phase 7 held-out set.** The sandbox clone carries the whole `.agents/trail.jsonl`, so `GUIDE-eval-holdout` or hidden `indicator` rows sit in the worker's clone and the worker can read them; the "no Kickoff names or carries it, pinned by a test over the templates" claim is about the prompt only. The Goodhart protection in the plan's own rationale needs the rows kept out of the clone (a record the clone's export lacks, or removed from the clone before the session) or the claim dropped. Also unresolved: D5 says "decide in Phase 7", but Verification and Phase 7 rely on it. The cost of the gate is not budgeted: every row naming the skill + all `regression` rows + held-out, at `--runs 3`, on parent and candidate, is dozens of agy sessions against `runs_per_day` 4, `run_timeout` 30 m and the quota floors (does the gate count as one run?). `TimeoutStartSec` for the auto service is not set (the dream's is 2 h): one run = worker + tests (+ the gate) can exceed it.

G17. **[medium / medium] Runner choice.** "Docker when it reaches a local daemon, otherwise host": refusal 24 (daemon cannot apply limits), a missing image (`Options.Image`, `AgyLinux`, `Version`; docker mode is refused from a development build) would silently demote to the host runner, which is a fallback that masks the error. State when docker is refused vs. falls back, and how the image gets built.

G18. **[medium / high] Docs clauses missing.** Phase 5 (apply) has no `docs:` at all; Phase 4 changes `internal/work` Options (SPEC-fyr-work is listed in Surfaces but no phase has the clause) and `internal/sandbox` (named in Surfaces, absent from every `files:`); Phase 6 adds `fyr memory add --provenance` (docs SPEC records are named, `fyr help memory`, `skills/project-memory`, README are not); Phase 7's possible `--suite` flag has no docs clause; `GUIDE-testing` § 3 entry for `internal/auto` and `SDD.md` M19 / `TDD.md` T19 (stubs in Phase 0) are never filled by a later phase; `fyr help uninstall` for the timer removal (Phase 1) is not named.

G19. **[medium / high] `files:` omit real surfaces.** Phase 1: `internal/dream/timer_install.go` (`InstallTimer`, `CheckTimer`, the install side, not only `timer.go`), the dream tests, `README.md`, `cmd/fyr/harnessmap_test.go` (per G1). `renderSystemd`/`renderLaunchd` hard-code `dream --all` and the Description (`timer.go:91,120`), `UnitFor` returns fixed names; "shared by name and command line, never copied" needs a parameterised signature the plan does not give. Phase 4: `internal/sandbox/` (SkipStores). Phase 6: the `cmd/fyr` memory verb, `skills/retro/SKILL.md` (the sentence about `derived`), `internal/brain` schema migration (brain.db column; "memory records are never exported", so provenance is not in the trail and the migration is a SQLite change under ADR-063, unmentioned). Phase 7: `internal/eval/`, `cmd/fyr/eval.go` if a flag.

G20. **[medium / medium] Provenance default.** "An absent value reads as `operator`" and `--provenance` is a self-asserted flag: a memory written by any agent session without the flag (the common case, including after tool output was read) is `operator`, so "derived is never promoted" only guards what auto writes. State the default for a new record written by an agent session, or accept and say what is not covered.

G21. **[low / high] Undefined terms and uncited names (naive-reader check).** `dave` (the operator's machine, undefined; used in E2E, A4, A5); "row 4/5/6" (rows of the research record's § Decisions for the operator, not cited at first use in Scope); "catalog tasks N" (research § The task catalog); `PLAN.md` P9/P13/D15/D18 (cite the file); `ADR-068`, `ADR-083`, `ADR-047a`, `ADR-073` (IDs only, fine as records); "DGM, MINJA, ClawHub" (Rejected line; in the research); "pool", "5-hour window" (of `/usage`); `Env` seam (no signature); "Kickoff", "handoff" (the `handoff` skill); `skills.sh` and "the pinned CLI"; `.agents/scratch/agents/explorer-2026-10-31-1625.md` is gitignored scratch, not durable. PRD items touched but not cited: R4 (uninstall is "easy on and off"; no new dependency), R6 (real-home rule, used in text), R7 (records, memory, provenance).

## Scope (question 2): built but not named in `## Why`, with no D-row saying who asked
- `fyr auto status --json` (shape undefined) and `run --project ROOT`.
- State keys `budget.*` with no flag to set them (D1 fixes the values; a value that never varies is configuration for nothing).

# Review — p9-docs-lens   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: working tree (uncommitted) against HEAD 9d7d081, docs lens only: `.agents/scratch/p9/review.diff` (source and tests), `.agents/scratch/p9/docs.diff` (spec and guide record changes), PLAN.md D19 and item 54, read against SPEC-fyr-eval, SPEC-fyr-metrics, GUIDE-eval, GUIDE-testing, GUIDE-fyr-matrix (copies in `.agents/scratch/p9docs/`), TDD.md, README.md, `cmd/fyr/help_text.go`.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

No claim in the changed docs is contradicted by the code. The changed text was checked line by line and the code backs it: column order, `kind` read from the newest counted trial with NULL as `capability`, the `indicator` row out of every number of the first suite line, the trajectory similarity and the record's interval, and `expect` pooled over graded trials with a main session (`ExpectMatches` filters `status IN ('pass','fail')` and sessions with `parent_id IS NULL`). The JSON keys, the `fyr` allowlist and `fyr eval --list` (run by hand: 17 rows non-capability) also match. What is wrong is one restatement left stale (the `--list` row of GUIDE-fyr-matrix), a `cluster` description that now states a purpose D19 says is gone, and two coverage claims that name no test or the wrong one.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` § `eval`, the `--list` row (record line 149) — it says "every row `v1  capability` since `GUIDE-eval` still has the seven-column header". P9 gives `GUIDE-eval` the eleven-column header and appends cells to every row. Trigger: `go run ./cmd/fyr eval --home .agents/scratch/evalm --list` prints `smoke ... regression`, `catalog-route-1..6`, `catalog-no-leak`, `catalog-precedence` as regression, and `agents-security`, `agent-reviewer`, `inject-*`, `lane-*` as adversarial (17 rows). The row is dated "exercised 2026-10-31 (P8)" but its stated reason is false now. Fix: re-run `--list` and rewrite the row (or date it as P8's state and add the P9 reading), and add the P9 run of `metrics evals` (kind, expect, kind lines) and the record's `expect` column to that guide, since P9's checkpoint expects this very `--list` output.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `GUIDE-eval` line 21 (`cluster`) and `SPEC-fyr-eval` line 74 — both call `cluster` "the family a clustered interval groups by", and the spec adds "no view reads it yet (`PLAN.md` D19)". D19 says the one reader, the cluster-bootstrap line, was removed by the eval-metrics plan's D26, so no clustered interval exists or is planned; "yet" promises a reader. GUIDE-eval line 21 was not touched by P9 and keeps the old purpose. The spec also points a live claim at `PLAN.md` D19, which is removed at the plan's end. Fix: in both, say the stored `cluster` has no reader (the cluster-bootstrap line was removed, eval-metrics plan D26) and cite the ADR or the change record rather than `PLAN.md`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `SPEC-fyr-metrics` (the allowlist bullet and its Verification row `Verb` → `verb_test.go (-run Verb)`) and `SPEC-fyr-eval` § Verification (`go test -race ./cmd/fyr/ -run Eval`) — the new pin `TestEveryVerbSurvivesTheVerbList` lives in `cmd/fyr/eval_record_test.go`. `-run Verb` in `internal/metrics` does not run it, and `-run Eval` in `cmd/fyr` does not match its name (no "Eval").
