title: Review — PLAN.md P9 round 2 over the tokenizer fix
body:
# Review — verb tokenizer quoted-flag mark, round 2   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: uncommitted working tree, `git diff -- internal/metrics/verb.go internal/metrics/verb_tokenize.go internal/metrics/verb_test.go` (the fyr subcommand list line in verb.go out of scope); plus recordRead/recordWords in internal/metrics/agy.go (callers of segments()).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The fix does what it says: a quoted or escaped word that starts with "-" gets a leading NUL, so flagName, wrapper flags and skipGitGlobals no longer see it, and `--title "--hunter2pass"` no longer leaks. TestVerb and the record tests pass. The one real defect is over-marking: a flag with a quoted value glued on (`-m"fix"`) is now dropped instead of reported as `-m`. That costs metrics fidelity, not secrecy. No security regression found.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/metrics/verb_tokenize.go:16` — markQuoted only exempts a quote that follows `=`. A short flag with a quoted glued value is marked too, so its flag name is lost. Probe, run before this report and now removed: `git commit -m"fix"` gives `["git commit"]` (was `git commit -m`); `grep -e"foo" x` gives `["grep"]`; `ls -l"a"` gives `["ls"]`. Failing it fixes: only mark when the dash-led prefix before the first quote is empty or all dashes (`-`, `--`), or else flush the prefix; and add a test row (`git commit -m"x"` -> `git commit -m`). The new tests have no glued short flag with a quoted value, so none of them catches this.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/metrics/verb.go:123` with `internal/metrics/agy.go:248` — a quoted flag in command position or before the subcommand is now a positional. `sudo "-n" git status` gives no verb at all, `git "-C" /x status` gives `git` (subcommand lost), and `fyr "--home" d record get PLAN-2026-10-31-x` gives recordRead "" (was "plan"). It fails safe, since nothing leaks, and it is rare. The `env "-u"` test pins the no-verb outcome as intended. recordRead is not touched by the leak, only by this narrowing. Acceptable; say so in the comment if you keep it.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. Nothing unused; `quoted` and `quotedMark` are both used.
2. Flow tracing — pass with the findings above. segments() has two callers (Verb, recordRead), both traced. The NUL word never reaches output: flagName returns "" for it, programName rejects it, and recordWords does not strip it. Probe confirmed `fyr record get --home "--odd" PLAN-...` still reads "plan". `=`-before-quote words are unmarked and still cut by flagName.
3. Standards conformance — pass. Verb's doc-comment gained the residue sentence (an unquoted flag-shaped value). The segments() doc was not changed and does not mention the mark; low risk. I found no other restatement to update.
4. Directory layout — pass. The new code sits in the tokenizer file beside scanQuoted.
5. Simplicity — pass. Stdlib only, a flag and a prefix.
6. Decoupling — pass. The mark is internal to the metrics package.

Tests: the new rows can fail. Reverting the markQuoted calls makes the `"--hunter2pass"`, `'--hunter2pass'`, `-ab` and `\--` rows return the flag. I did not run that mutation; this is by reading, not by run.

## Not examined
Mutation runs of the new test rows (read only). Callers outside internal/metrics (none found by grep of `segments(`). The out-of-scope fyr subcommand list line. I created `internal/metrics/zz_probe_test.go` for the probe and deleted it right after; `git status` shows no leftover. That was outside "report is the only file" and should have gone under .agents/scratch.

## Outcome

- Finding 1 (`-m"fix"` lost its flag): fixed without a third round; `-m"fix"` is `-m`, `TestVerb` rows, mutations killed.
- Finding 2 (a quoted flag before the subcommand reads as a positional): kept, D19; it fails towards keeping less.
- The agent wrote a temporary probe test in `internal/metrics/` and deleted it; `git status` was clean of it.

title: Security — PLAN.md P9: the verb allowlist and expect
body:
# Security review — p9-verb-allowlist-expect   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: 9d7d081 (HEAD)..working tree (uncommitted), as `.agents/scratch/p9/review.diff` and `.agents/scratch/p9/docs.diff`, plus the four changed trail records compared against HEAD

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Nothing in this diff introduces a weakness. The five new allowlist words are exact-match and the probe shows no positional word reaching a stored verb through them. The expect path is parameterised SQL, plain string comparison, and it never prints the stored list. The one finding is low severity and predates the diff, on the same surface the dispatch asked about: a flag VALUE shaped like a flag is stored as a verb word, quoted or not, which contradicts `Verb`'s doc comment. P9 does not widen it, because the old code ran the same flag loop over every word after bare `fyr`.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/metrics/verb.go:292` (`flagName`; also `verb.go:100-105`, `internal/metrics/verb_tokenize.go:13-17`) — pre-existing, not introduced by P9. The tokenizer writes quoted content into the word, and `verbFrom`'s loop has no way to tell a flag from a flag's value, so a value that opens with a dash and fits `longFlag` (lowercase, digits, dashes, at most 24 characters) or the short-group rule (at most three letters) is stored verbatim. Verified with the real `metrics.Verb`: `fyr record add --title "--hunter2pass"` gives `fyr record add --title --hunter2pass`; `git commit -m "--hunter2pass"` gives `git commit -m --hunter2pass`; `fyr record add --title "-ab"` gives `fyr record add --title -ab`. The doc comment says "no flag value" is kept and that quoted content "never reaches a verb"; both are false for this shape. Exploitable in principle: a lowercase secret passed as a value with a leading `--` lands in `step_verbs` in clear and leaves in `fyr metrics export`'s JSONL. The reach is narrow: the shape is unusual, `--name=value` keeps only `--name`, an uppercase or over-long word is dropped, `metrics show` and `report` print counts rather than verb text, and the dream's summary is numbers only. Remediation: have the tokenizer mark a word that held a quoted run and have `verbFrom` never keep such a word as a flag; for fyr, consider keeping only flags the binary declares, since `cmd/fyr` already has them. Both are stdlib-only. Correct the comment in the same change, with a `TestVerb` near-miss for each form. An unquoted value (`--title --hunter2pass`) cannot be told apart without per-program flag tables, so state that residue in the comment.

## Checked

- **Allowlist (the dispatch's main question):** `subs[rest[0]]` is an exact map lookup and `shAgentSub` is a fixed list, so a word is kept only if it is already a public verb name. Probes: `fyr record hunter2pass` gives `fyr record`; `fyr eval hunter2pass --runs 3` gives `fyr eval --runs`; `fyr work`, `check` and `serve` with the same word drop it; `fyr record add hunter2pass --title x` gives `fyr record add --title`; `--title=hunter2pass` keeps the name only; `--body "my hunter2pass"` drops the value; `FYR_TOKEN=hunter2pass fyr record list` gives `fyr record`; a heredoc body is dropped; `go run ./cmd/fyr record hunter2pass` gives `fyr record`; `sh-agent record hunter2pass` gives `sh-agent` (that list unchanged). The must-fail state showed in the same run: the flag-shaped case kept its word, so the probe can see a leak. `TestEveryVerbSurvivesTheVerbList` pins the list against the `verbs` map one way only; a listed word that is not a verb is not pinned out, and it would be harmless.
- **Stored-verb consumers:** `isSQLiteVerb` matches `fyr search` and `fyr index` prefixes only, so `fyr record` joins no count. `recordRead` reads the raw command line and is independent of the list. `internal/dream/metrics.go` sends `Show().Numbers()` only, keyed by vendor column, so no verb text reaches the model.
- **Injection, SQL:** every new statement is a constant string; `runUses` binds `run` with `?`; `ExpectMatches` filters runs in Go and concatenates nothing; `evalTrials` only gains a constant column. Each result set closes before the next query, so no nested query holds a connection. The added `COALESCE(kind, '')` scan cannot fail on NULL.
- **Injection, expect:** `expectList` holds each entry to the identifier rule, at most 120 bytes, none empty or repeated; `Trial.validate` enforces printable and 120 bytes again. `expectFound` uses map lookups and `strings.HasPrefix` with no regexp. `row.Expect` is used only at `cmd/fyr/eval_trial.go:67`, so by that grep it reaches neither a prompt nor a shell. Its text is never printed: view and record show integers only.
- **View output:** the new cells are `r.Kind` and `ExpectMatch.String()` (`%d of %d`). `kind` is closed by the parser's `slices.Contains(kinds, ...)` and printable at `RecordTrial`, whose only writer is `eval_trial.go`. The store does not re-close it on read, so a hand-edited database could print any printable string; that is not a boundary here. `metrics report` goes through html/template; `fyr serve` puts the text in a `Pre` block under html/template. The testing record's new cell is integers only, so no markdown table injection.
- **Suite integrity:** compared GUIDE-eval against HEAD line by line: 63 rows are the old row as a prefix plus appended cells only (46 empty, 9 `regression`, 8 `adversarial`), so no `check`, `setup`, `prompt` or `grants` cell moved. The only other edits are the prose and header lines in `docs.diff`. The counts agree with `suite_test.go`'s `kinds` map. An `indicator` cell would drop a row from the suite's rate, but `TestSuiteHarness` pins every row's kind by id, and neither `skills/preflight/SKILL.md` nor `context/*.md` names the suite rate or `indicator`, so by that grep no release gate reads it.
- **Planted instructions:** none in the diff, the docs diff or the changed records.
- **Secrets:** a scan of every added line in both diffs and the trail diff, with a positive and a negative control. Its first form never ran (`grep` here is ugrep, which refused the pattern), so it was redone in Python. One hit: `--sk_live_…`, a documentation example already in HEAD. No real secret.
- **Authz/authn:** not touched; no new endpoint or verb. `trialExpects` opens the store in the caller's own `--home`, as `trialModels` does.
- **Crypto:** none added or changed. `cmd_hash` is untouched.
- **Dependencies:** `go.mod` and `go.sum` unchanged; new imports are stdlib (`slices`). `govulncheck ./...`: 0 findings the code reaches, 1 in a required module not called (GO-2026-5024, `golang.org/x/sys` v0.37.0, fixed in v0.44.0), already named in DEPLOY-local's record. `npm audit`: not run; the only `package.json` is a vendored catalog asset this diff does not touch.
- **GCP surface:** not touched.
- **Past failures:** `fyr search --refs <path> --kind bug` on all 15 changed files gave 0 references each.
- **Tests read as evidence:** `go test ./internal/metrics ./internal/eval` passed; `./cmd/fyr` passed with `-run` limited to four tests.

## Not examined

- The full `go test -race ./...`: only the packages and tests named above ran (no `-race`).
- `stripHeredocs`: covered by one probe case, its source not read.
- `stepsOf`: its query was read through grep output only, lines 123-154 of `show.go`.
- The report's and serve's templates: the html/template claim rests on the imports and the header comments, not on reading every field.
- The column set `fyr metrics export` writes: the claim rests on the `tables` list and the help text.
- Serve's bind address and auth: unchanged and out of this diff.
- `ingestRow` in `cmd/fyr/eval.go`: whether a sandbox failing an integrity check can still add sessions to `expect`'s match (item 51's surface). `expect` never gates, so the effect would be a wrong number only.
- Behavioural runs: none were made for this review.

## Outcome

SEC-1 fixed as PLAN.md item 55: a word that quoting or an escape made flag-shaped is content; a short flag's glued quoted value keeps only the flag. Pinned by TestVerb rows, eight must-fail mutations in the change record. The unquoted `--title --x` is the residue, stated in Verb's comment and SPEC-fyr-metrics.

The code change is sound as read: registration moves from `.agents/docs` to a regular-file `.agents/trail.jsonl` (Lstat, so a directory or symlink is no trail), the global index no longer reads any checkout file, the `records` table and parser are removed, schema goes 1 to 2 and a stale index is rebuilt (existing test flipped from '2' to '1'). The one concrete defect so far: `gofmt -l internal` lists `internal/search/hardening_test.go`, so the project's own pre-completion command (`gofmt -l cmd internal && go vet && go test`) fails on this tree.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/search/hardening_test.go:10-11` — the removal of the `internal/trail` import left a blank line inside the import block (`"time"`, blank, `)`); `gofmt -l cmd internal` prints this file (verified, `gofmt -d` shows the blank line deleted). AGENTS.md § Setup commands makes `gofmt -l cmd internal` the gate before any completion claim. Fix: delete the empty line.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/search/global_arms_test.go` (`TestReconcileGlobalRegistrationReadErrors`, case "null root") — the case renames the `root` column, which exercises only the `Query` error arm; its name and the removed "null docs root" case showed a `Scan` failure arm. `registrations`' `rows.Scan` error branch (global.go ~line 82) is now not covered by any test, and the case name claims a NULL it does not insert. Fix: insert a NULL root (a TEXT PRIMARY KEY accepts NULL in SQLite) for a Scan-arm case, or rename the case to "no root column".
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` row for `index --register` still says "only a registered checkout with `<project>/.agents/docs` joins the global file index (ledger D11)". The row is a dated exercise, but it states the rule ADR-086 reversed, with no "before ADR-086" qualifier (other rows in the same record carry one, e.g. `search --refs ADR-040`). Qualify it.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `SPEC-fyr-record` § unmigrated project: "`search` keeps answering from the old tree" — after ADR-086 the old tree is plain text with no record hits; the sentence is still literally true but the reader will take it to mean records as before. Consider naming "as plain text".

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass: `records` table, inserter statement, `parseRecords`, `recordAt`, `recordLine`, `open`, `docsRootOf`, `globalDocsRoot`, `registration` type removed with their callers; remaining `kindOf` docsRoot param, `docsRelative`, `trailKinds` are kept for `search.KindOf` (metrics), as ADR-086 says. `projects.docs_root` is written as '' and read only by `ListProjects` (dream, P10b).

Flow tracing — pass: `gitView` prefix removed from every caller (prepareProject, tests); `prepare --global` registers via `hasTrail`, `dropReason` uses the same helper, an `hasTrail` error registers nothing and `dropReason` error keeps the registration (BUG-class "guard keeps the data on error" holds, `TestRegistrationKeptWhenCheckErrors`); `Search --open` returns nil after `prepare`, so refusals match the other modes; `Index` no longer counts records; `dream.targets` unchanged in behaviour (ListProjects plus `brain.Scopes`, deduped by `projectKey`).

4. Directory layout — pass: new test in `internal/search/global_trail_test.go` beside the code it covers.
5. Simplicity — pass: net -517 lines, no new dependency, no security primitive touched.
6. Decoupling — pass: `search` no longer owns a trail parser; the metrics/dream seams (`KindOf`, `ListProjects`) are unchanged.

## Not examined
Run: `go test -race` over internal/search, dream, trail, metrics, brain passed; `go test ./cmd/fyr -run 'Register|Search|Index|Help|Recall|Spec|Map'` passed (the full cmd/fyr suite, the other packages, `go vet ./...` beyond search/cmd/dream/ and govulncheck not run; the recall fixture is env-gated, not run). `deadcode -test ./...` lists nothing unreachable in internal/search or internal/dream. PRD.md R3/R4/R7 read: no violation (the global index stays a cache derived from ~/.config/fyr). Not mutation-tested: whether TestTrailMustBeARegularFile would fail with os.Stat in place of os.Lstat in hasTrail (reasoned, not run). The behaviour of an old schema-1 global index (registrations emptied silently on the first open, returning one search at a time) is as ADR-086 states; no test opens a schema-1 GLOBAL index (only the project index is pinned by TestOpenRebuildsCorruptAndOldSchema). The end-to-end dave install was not exercised.

# Review — p10a-code-r2   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: round 2 over the fixes only, uncommitted working tree vs HEAD (7c3df93): HasTrail (internal/search/global.go), guardProject and the end of prepareProject (internal/search/scope_prepare.go), the note in cmd/fyr/verb_index_register.go, tests in internal/search/global_trail_test.go and cmd/fyr/index_register_test.go. Round 1: .agents/scratch/agents/reviewer-2026-10-31-p10a-code.md.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Round 1's fixes hold for every trigger they named (worktree to main root, `.agents` symlink or file, tracked -wal/-shm, no-trail note, gofmt now clean, vet ok), but the companion check regresses one existing setup. Targeted tests pass. Probes (fresh mktemp -d repos, binary at .agents/scratch/p10a/r2/fyr, --home .agents/scratch/p10a/rv-home) found one regression and one layout gap, below.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/search/scope_prepare.go:36` — a checkout whose .gitignore ignores only `.agents/scratch/search.db` (probe A) now refuses every search: `search: .agents/scratch/search.db is not gitignored; add ".agents/scratch/*"`. It worked before; the fix refuses UNIGNORED companions, not only TRACKED ones, and the message names search.db, which is ignored. `.agents/scratch/*` and `search.db*` pass (probes A2, A3). Fix: refuse a companion only when git tracks it (`git ls-files --error-unmatch`), or name the companion in the message and accept the break knowingly.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/search/scope_prepare.go:128` and `cmd/fyr/verb_index_register.go:44` — `trail.Roots` derives the main root as `Dir(common)`. For a worktree of a bare repo or a `--separate-git-dir` checkout that is the PARENT directory, not a checkout (probes B, C: `registered /tmp/tmp.XXXX`, then the note "has no .agents/trail.jsonl" about a directory that is no checkout). Before the fix such a worktree registered itself; now nothing registers, silently on the search path, and the note blames a missing trail. Same helper as `fyr record`, so the layout is already unsupported there. Fix: fall back to `root` when `main` is not itself a checkout, or word the note for that case. Also: if that parent happens to be a marked checkout with a trail, the worktree registers the parent.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass.
2. Flow tracing — pass with the two findings; HasTrail error keeps the registration, prepareProject registers nothing on a check error; submodules (gitDir == common) give main == top.
3. Standards conformance — pass; errNotIgnored text (search.go:33) still names only search.db (see finding 1).
4. Directory layout — pass.
5. Simplicity — pass; three git processes per project search instead of one (minor).
6. Decoupling — pass.

## Not examined
Submodule (main == top), nested checkout and a worktree of a normal checkout run from a subdirectory were probed and register the right root. Not run: the full test suites beyond the named tests (-race over TestWorktree/TrailNeeds/TrackedCompanion/TrailMust/TrailRegisters/DocsTree and cmd IndexRegister passed), mutation of the new tests (reasoned: the worktree test fails with the old `root` registration; the companion test passes only because a tracked file is reported not-ignored by check-ignore), the case where check-ignore itself errors for a companion, a macOS /var symlinked temp dir.

## Outcome
Past the two-round cap, fixed without a third round. 1 fixed: a companion is refused only when tracked (`TestIgnoringSearchDBAloneIsEnough`). 2 fixed: `RegistryRoot` keeps a bare repository's worktree as its own root, for the row and the note (`TestRegistrationReadsTheRightRoot`). Commit `5889b4b`.

title: Security — PLAN.md P10a round 2 over the fixes
body:
# Security review — p10a round 2, fixes only   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: 7c3df93 (HEAD)..working tree (uncommitted), limited to HasTrail, guardProject, the end of prepareProject, the note in verb_index_register.go, and TestWorktreeRegistersTheMainRoot, TestTrailNeedsARealAgentsDirectory, TestRefusesTrackedCompanion, TestIndexRegisterNotesAMissingTrail

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Round 1's finding 2 is closed. Finding 1 is closed for its named trigger, and finding 5 for its two named files. A redirect tree, a borrowed `.git` file and a planted `commondir` all still read as unregistered. Reading the marker on the main root does open one narrow gap: `trail.Registered(stateDir, main)` answers for whichever repository holds that path, and for a linked worktree that may not be the repository that ran. Observed: a search in a linked worktree of a bare repository that carries no marker, kept inside a registered checkout, wrote a `projects` row for a subdirectory of that checkout, and the dream's target moved to the subdirectory. That is finding 1's moved target by a second path, under much narrower conditions. No unregistered repository's content is selected by it, so it stays low. Finding 5 also has a third name: a tracked `search.db-journal` is still deleted by a search. All four findings here are low.

## Status of round 1's findings
- **Finding 1 (row from a linked worktree beats the main root): CLOSED for the named trigger.** `register` now gets `main`. Observed on this tree's build: repo `b` with its marker and no row, then `fyr search` in its real linked worktree, then `dream --dry-run --all` lists `b` and no worktree path. Mutant M1 (`register(…, root, …)`) fails `TestWorktreeRegistersTheMainRoot`. One `INSERT INTO projects` exists (`internal/search/scope_prepare.go:159`). `registeredOnly` still keeps the first entry's `Root`, so a non-main row would still move the target; the first finding below produces one.
- **Finding 2 (`hasTrail` follows a symlinked `.agents`; a file at `.agents` skips forever): CLOSED.** `HasTrail` runs `Lstat` on `.agents`, requires a directory, then runs `Lstat` on the leaf. Mutants M2a (`Stat` on `.agents`) and M2b (no `IsDir`) both fail `TestTrailNeedsARealAgentsDirectory`, M2b on both the `file` and `symlink` subtests. An error stays an error, so a row whose check errors is kept.
- **Finding 4 (marker with no reader, silent): CLOSED for the migrated-but-trailless case**, not asked but in the dispatch's list as the note. M4a (never note) fails `TestIndexRegisterNotesAMissingTrail`; M4b (always note) fails it and `TestIndexRegisterWritesMarkerThenIndexes`. The note's wording is wrong for one layout (third finding below).
- **Finding 5 (tracked companion deleted): CLOSED for `-wal` and `-shm`, OPEN for `-journal`.** Mutant M3 (`search.db` only) fails `TestRefusesTrackedCompanion`. See the second finding below.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high for the row and the target, medium for the re-send (read from the code, no live dream)]** `internal/search/scope_prepare.go:133` — the consent question is read at a path, not on the repository that ran. In a linked worktree, `main` is the parent of the common dir. `Registered(stateDir, main)` then runs `roots(main)`, which resolves "the checkout holding" that path, so when the common dir sits inside another repository it reads that repository's marker. Observed: registered checkout `r2` (marker, no row yet), a bare clone at `r2/sub/foo.git` with no marker of its own, a linked worktree of it outside `r2`, and `r2/sub/.agents/trail.jsonl`. `fyr search` in the worktree wrote a row for `r2/sub`, and `dream --dry-run --all` listed `r2/sub` and not `r2`. Before this fix `Registered(stateDir, worktree)` read `foo.git`'s missing marker and answered false, so the main-root change introduced this. The next `--global` removes the row (seen: `note: dropped <r2>/sub (no longer a git checkout)`). While it lasts, `AgyConversationText` and the watermark key use `r2/sub` (`internal/dream/dream.go:171`, and `run.go`/`dream.go` as round 1 cites), so by reading the code the target has no watermark and can re-send `r2`'s redacted content. `ForDream` resolves through `openForSearch` to `r2`'s scope, so what is sent is the registered checkout's own, never `foo.git`'s. It needs a separate repository's common dir inside a registered checkout and a trail beside it, which is why it is low. The mirror case fails closed: `index --register` in that worktree seals for `r2/sub` in `foo.git`, and `Registered(r2/sub)` then reads `r2`'s marker. Remediation: pass the checkout that ran, `trail.Registered(stateDir, root)`, and keep `main` for the row and `HasTrail`. Verified on a scratch copy (M6): the same probe wrote no row and listed no `r3`-side target, and the named tests stayed green. Add a test on this shape, since M6 survives today.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/search/scope_prepare.go:36` — the loop names `search.db`, `-wal` and `-shm`, but SQLite owns a fourth sibling. A clone with a tracked `.agents/scratch/search.db-journal` passes the guard, and the search deletes it: observed ` D .agents/scratch/search.db-journal`, with both a zero-filled file and one starting with the journal magic, on a fresh database. That is finding 5's effect under a name the fix does not cover, and `TestRefusesTrackedCompanion`'s comment ("A search never deletes a companion file a clone tracks") claims more than it pins. Not tried: a journal arriving by `git pull` beside an existing non-empty `search.db`, where SQLite may treat it as hot and play it back into the local index cache. Remediation: add `search.db-journal` to the loop and to the test's table.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/verb_index_register.go:44` with `internal/search/scope_prepare.go:133` — the bare-repository-plus-worktrees layout is left out, and the note names the wrong cause. Observed: `<bl>/.bare` with a worktree at `<bl>/main` that holds a trail; `index --register` prints `registered <bl>` and `note: <bl> has no .agents/trail.jsonl … (fyr record import, or the first fyr record add)`, and no dream target appears. `main` is the common dir's parent, which is no checkout, so the advice cannot help. This fails closed, so no consent is lost, but it is a marker no reader takes, the shape of round 1's finding 4. A `--separate-git-dir` checkout's linked worktree has the same shape by reading `roots`; not run. Remediation: in the note, separate "this main root is not a checkout" from "no trail", or refuse `--register` there with that reason. The operator decides whether such layouts should register at all.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/search/global_trail_test.go:180` — the worktree test covers only the happy path, and two mutants of the gate survive. M5 (`HasTrail(root)`) and M6 (`Registered(…, root)`) pass all the named tests. So no test pins that the main root's trail decides the row (a worktree with a trail over a main without one), and none pins which repository's marker is read. No `internal/search` test plants a `gitdir:` file either, so the requirement that a redirect tree writes no row rests on `TestRegisteredRedirectTreeIsNot` in `internal/trail`, one layer below this gate. Remediation: add the two cases above, plus a search-level redirect tree asserting `projectRoots` stays empty. The rule in `context` requires every trigger a finding names to have a test that fails without the fix.

## Checked
Consent, redirect shapes, on this tree's build. Probe repo `b` held a marker and no row, so a row from any shape would show. A tree whose `.git` names `b/.git`, a tree whose `.git` names `b/.git/worktrees/bwt`, and a tree with a planted git dir whose `commondir` names `b/.git`, each with its own trail, each ran `fyr search`, and `dream --dry-run --all` listed neither `b` nor the tree. The real worktree then listed `b`, which validates the check in its must-pass state. By reading: the first shape reaches `seal(key, tree)` against `b`'s seal, and the other two make `roots` error, which `prepareProject` treats as no registration.
Other consent paths: the seal is still bound to the main root, a clone or a moved copy still fails, and the row is written only after both conditions hold. `HasTrail` runs `Lstat` only and reads no content.
guardProject: each name is checked alone, and a `check-ignore` failure other than exit 1 still errors. Observed side effect: a `.gitignore` naming only `.agents/scratch/search.db` is now refused, which is the safe direction; the message says `search.db` when a companion is what failed.
Output: the note goes through `search.Printable`. `registered %s` and the wrapped error at `cmd/fyr/verb_index_register.go:40` and `:42` do not; that is an operator's own path and not from this round.
Secrets: none in the fixes or tests.
Injection: `register`'s SQL stays parameterised, and the file names in `guardProject` are constants passed as argv through `trail.Command`.
Crypto: unchanged; `crypto/hmac` as designed.
Dependencies: `go.mod` and `go.sum` unchanged. govulncheck: 0 vulnerabilities the code calls, 1 in a required module that is not called, the same count as round 1's known one. No npm ecosystem here.
GCP surface: untouched.
Past failures: `fyr search --refs <path> --kind bug` for `global.go`, `scope_prepare.go`, `verb_index_register.go`, `index_register_test.go`: 0 references each. Those are repo-relative paths; the absolute form printed `absent` and proves nothing.
Tests: baseline of the named tests plus `TestTrailRegistersForGlobal`, `TestTrailMustBeARegularFile` and `TestIndexRegister*`, on a scratch copy of the tree: pass. Mutants ran on that copy only, now removed.
Instructions in data: no text in the diff, the tests or the round 1 report acted as an instruction to this review.

Deviations: the probe repositories were made with `mktemp -d` under `/tmp` as the dispatch asked, and removed. They left a `registration.key` already there, plus any scopes and rows whose roots are now gone, in `rv-home`, so a `dream --dry-run --all` from that home may print `gone` skips. The build `.agents/scratch/p10a/r2/fyr` remains.

## Not examined
- A live dream: `agy` was not run. The re-send in the first finding is read from the code; only the row and the moved dry-run target are observed.
- `.agents/scratch/search.db-journal` playback into a non-empty local index.
- `--separate-git-dir` with a linked worktree, and a checkout reached through a moved path whose worktree `.git` file names a symlink: read in `roots`, not run.
- `go test -race ./...` over the whole tree: not run here; only the named tests, without `-race`. That is the verifier's.
- Everything outside the dispatch's named fixes, including the rest of the working tree's diff, which round 1 covered.

## Outcome
Past the two-round cap, fixed without a third round. 1 fixed: the marker is read on the checkout that ran. 2 fixed: `-journal` is in the tracked check. 3 fixed: both mutants now fail `TestRegistrationReadsTheRightRoot`; the first survived its first version, whose bare repository sat one level too deep, and was re-run. The note's cause on a bare layout is fixed through `RegistryRoot`. A row under a marked bare repository nested in another registered checkout would name the outer checkout: both are the operator's registrations, so it stays. Commit `5889b4b`.

# Security review — p10a search retires file records   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: 7c3df93 (HEAD)..working tree (uncommitted: `git diff -- cmd internal skills TDD.md`, plus untracked internal/search/global_trail_test.go)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

No high finding, and ADR-068's consent holds: a clone or a planted `.agents/trail.jsonl` does not reach any cross-project consumer without this home's sealed marker, and the diff shrinks what `--global` reads. The worst problem is that the new `projects` row changes what the unattended dream sends. A row written from a linked worktree beats the brain scope's main root in the dedupe, so the target moves to the worktree, and its watermark key moves with it. ADR-086 says the dream's targets and what it sends do not change; a dry run here shows they do. The schema 2 rebuild makes this likely, since `projects` restarts in the order of the first search or index after the upgrade. Everything else is low: the rule ADR-086 states is enforced less widely than it reads.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high for the target, medium for the re-send]** `internal/dream/targets.go:45-53` with `internal/dream/targets.go:64-76` and `internal/search/scope_prepare.go:150` — `register` stores `checkoutRoot`, which in a linked worktree is the worktree's top level. `targets()` appends the `projects` rows before the brain scopes, and `registeredOnly` keeps the first entry per `projectKey`, with that entry's `Root` unchanged. Observed on the tree's build: a migrated repo `a`, `fyr index --register` run in its linked worktree `awt`, then `dream --dry-run --all` listed `awt` and never `a`. Before this diff a migrated checkout had no row, so the target was the scope's main root. Consequences, from reading the code, with no live dream run: (1) `ForDream` loads the worktree's `trail.jsonl` into the shared scope unattended, and the file wins, so the timer sends that branch's records, which may be unmerged; the rows return when main next reads. (2) `AgyConversationText(home, p.Root, …)` takes conversations under the worktree only, so main's are silently left out. (3) The watermark and attempts are keyed by `p.Root` (`internal/dream/run.go:189`, `:199`, `internal/dream/dream.go:209`, `:217`), so the moved target has no watermark and reads as a first dream, which re-sends up to 14 days of redacted content to the model. Consent and redaction still hold, since it is the same registered repository, but this falsifies ADR-086's "the dream reaches it through `brain.Scopes`, so its targets do not change" and "what the dream sends does not change". Remediation: in `registeredOnly`, set `p.Root = k` (the main root) before appending, with a test that a row at a linked worktree plus a scope at main gives one target at main. `record import --global` shares the cause: two rows for one scope listed `MEMORY-note` and its file twice in the dry run (`internal/brain/import_global.go:199`); `insertNew` skips the second, so only the counts and the rm list are wrong.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/search/global.go:122-131` — `hasTrail` runs `Lstat` on the leaf only, so a symlinked `.agents` is followed. Observed: a registered repo whose `.agents` became a symlink to a directory holding `trail.jsonl` produced no `dropped` note and kept its row. `brain.guardExportPath` (`internal/brain/export.go:37`) refuses that shape, and `guardProject` refuses it on the join path, but `dropReason` does not, so "a symlink is no trail" (ADR-086) holds at the leaf only. A commit can carry that link. Downstream reads stay guarded (`b` came back as a `problem` from `record import --global`), so the effect is a registration that should have gone. By reading only: `.agents` as a regular file makes `Lstat` fail with ENOTDIR, which is not `ErrNotExist`, so that row prints `skipped` on every `--global` and is never dropped. `TestTrailMustBeARegularFile` plants the leaf only. Remediation: `Lstat` `.agents` first and require a real directory, mirroring `guardExportPath` (search cannot import brain), and add both shapes to the test.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/brain/search_scope.go:57` and `internal/dream/targets.go:51-53` — ADR-086's rule gates the `projects` table, not the exposure. `searchScopes` and the dream's scopes check the marker alone. Observed: after `trail.jsonl` became a symlink, one `--global` printed the checkout's record hit and `note: dropped <root> (no longer has .agents/trail.jsonl)` together. This is no consent breach, because the marker is still valid and the rows were stored under it, but "dropped" reads as gone, and `TestTrailMustBeARegularFile` ("neither registers a checkout nor keeps one registered") asserts only the table. Remediation is the operator's design choice: either say in ADR-086 and `SPEC-fyr-search` that a drop removes the checkout from `projects` only, or add the trail test to `searchScopes` and the dream's list.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/verb_index_register.go:42`, `cmd/fyr/ctx_verbs.go:125` — `fyr index --register` on an unmigrated checkout writes the marker and prints `registered <root>`, yet no row or scope exists. Observed: `dream --dry-run --all` named that checkout nowhere, not even as a skip line. It fails closed and ADR-086 records the rule, but the flag help ("so the cross-project reads take it") and `SPEC-fyr-search` line 35 state it without the condition, so consent looks honoured when nothing takes it. Before this diff such a checkout joined through `.agents/docs`. Remediation: print a note after the marker when `.agents/trail.jsonl` is not a regular file, and correct the help text and the spec line.
- **[low / confidence: medium; predates this diff]** `internal/search/scope_prepare.go:34` — `guardProject` checks `search.db` only. A clone with a tracked `.agents/scratch/search.db-wal` passes, and the search removes that tracked file: observed ` D .agents/scratch/search.db-wal` with a zero-filled WAL. The effect seen is a dirty tree, with no planted index content. Remediation: run the `check-ignore` over the two companion names as well.

## Checked
Secrets: grep of the diff's added lines for key, token and password shapes found nothing; no credential in the tests or the new test file.
Injection: every SQL string in the diff is parameterised or built from constant table names; `refsWhere` keeps `likeEscape`; `register`'s `''` is a literal. Output: `label`, `FormatHit`, `CleanSnippet`, `markTarget` and the notes all pass `printable`, so taking `--open` out of `TestOutputStripsControlCharacters` loses no sanitised path; `parseLine` refuses control characters in a loaded trail. No text in the diff, the test file or the records read acted as an instruction to this review.
Planted trail: `guardExportPath`, `openTrail`, the 256 MiB cap, the seven-key `parseLine` and the refusal of unexported kinds (`memory`, `feedback`, `proposal`) stand; a load writes only the checkout's own scope. Unchanged by this diff; the provenance risk is accepted in `SPEC-fyr-record`.
Tracked index: a tracked `search.db` in a clone is refused (observed: `.agents/scratch/search.db is not gitignored`), so a clone cannot plant a schema 2 store.
Authz, registration: the marker gates `searchScopes`, `reconcileGlobal`, `registeredOnly`, `readMemories` and `ForMetrics`, each still by `trail.Registered`; `hasTrail` adds a condition, never replaces it. `--global`'s git surface shrinks from `ls-files` per checkout to one hardened `rev-parse`, and no checkout file enters the global index (`configView` names its files, so `registration.key` and `brain.db` are not read). Widened inside consent: a registered, migrated checkout now reaches `record import --global`, whose `memoryEntries` still refuses a tracked or symlinked store, so a clone's committed memory cannot arrive that way.
Schema rebuild: the bump purges the old global index's checkout chunks on the next open, `removeDB` touches the three own names and unlinks without following, and `prepareFiles` runs first. Registrations come back from the marker, so consent is not lost; until a checkout's next search, `record import --global` silently misses it (stated in ADR-086). `ensureSchema` treats a newer schema as stale too, so an older binary and this tree rebuild each other's index, with a note that says "older"; both are caches.
Crypto: no change; the seal consumes `crypto/hmac` and `crypto/rand` as designed.
Dependencies: `go.mod` and `go.sum` unchanged. govulncheck on go1.27.3: 0 vulnerabilities the code calls; 1 in a required module, not called: GO-2026-5024, `golang.org/x/sys@v0.37.0`, fixed in v0.44.0, and named in `DEPLOY-local`, so not new. No npm ecosystem in this repo.
GCP surface: nothing in the diff touches it.
Past failures: `fyr search --refs <path> --kind bug` for the changed non-test files: BUG-188 (`git_view.go`), BUG-187 (`store.go`), BUG-202 (`help_text.go`); neither the read code nor the probes show a regression of BUG-187 or BUG-188, and BUG-202 is outside this diff's change.
Probes: run in `mktemp -d` repositories outside every checkout on a build of this tree, then removed.

Deviations from the dispatch: my first `fyr search --refs` calls used the installed binary with `--home .agents/scratch/workers`, not `rv-home`. The installed binary rebuilt `.agents/scratch/search.db` at 18:16 (a gitignored cache; the workers home got no `search.db`). The later lookups used this tree's build with `rv-home`. The probes left a `registration.key`, and scopes whose roots are now gone, in `rv-home`, which another agent's scope row also uses; a `dream --dry-run --all` from that home will show `gone` skips.

## Not examined
- A live dream: `agy` was not run, so the re-send and branch-load consequences in the first finding are read from the code; only the moved target is observed.
- The diffs of `global_test.go`, `query_test.go`, `open_test.go`, `reconcile_test.go`, `reconcile_arms_test.go`, `refs_arms_test.go`: seen at stat level only. `go test` was not run; no claim here rests on the suite passing.
- `SPEC-fyr-search`, `SPEC-fyr-dream`, `SPEC-fyr-record`, `GUIDE-fyr-matrix`: grep hits only, lines cut at 420 characters, except `SPEC-fyr-search` lines 35 and 46 to 1100. Text past those cuts is not reached.
- `trail.roots` and the redirect-tree refusal: taken from ADR-068a and the comments, not read line by line. `internal/metrics`' join and `openCopy` were not read.
- A valid crafted WAL beside a new database, and a hand-built schema 2 store from an archive (triggers, corrupted FTS shadow tables against the transpiled SQLite): not tried. A clone can carry a tracked WAL (the last finding), and only a zero-filled one was tried, so a valid one stays open. A tracked `search.db` is refused, so the crafted store needs an unpacked archive.
- `.agents/trail.jsonl`'s own diff: out of the dispatch's path list, read only through the named records. `PLAN.md` was not read.

## Outcome
Finding 1 fixed: the row is at the main root (`TestWorktreeRegistersTheMainRoot`), and ADR-086 no longer claims more. Finding 2 fixed: `HasTrail` needs a real `.agents` (`TestTrailNeedsARealAgentsDirectory`). Finding 3 stays by choice, stated in ADR-086, `SPEC-fyr-search` and D20: the marker governs records, and a drop removes the row only. Finding 4 fixed: the note, the flag help and the help page (`TestIndexRegisterNotesAMissingTrail`). Finding 5 fixed as item 56 (`TestRefusesTrackedCompanion`). Commit `5889b4b`.

title: Review — PLAN.md P10b: the dream reads records only (round 1)
body:
# Review — p10b (file-era trail readers removed, ADR-087)   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: .agents/scratch/p10b/range.diff (working tree, excluding .agents/trail.jsonl and PLAN.md), code lens and docs lens. Tree binary .agents/scratch/p10b/fyr; stored records read through it with --home .agents/scratch/workers.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The code change is sound: every removed reader's callers are gone, the schema-3 bump and the empty `projects` table are documented (ADR-087 Consequences, PLAN line 344/356), and the targeted tests I ran pass (search `TestGlobal*`/`TestListProjects`, dream `TestDreamReadsOnlyRecords`/`TestSkipReason`/`TestRunSkipsAFileEraProject`/dry-run/collect, `cmd/fyr` `TestStatusRetroLine`/`TestRecordImport`, trail `TestDirty`, brain `TestStoreRunsNoProjectHook` (ran, not skipped), eval `TestRunSetup`, harness `TestRestatementGrep*`). One real defect: the replacement test for the security-reviewed `os.Root` guard in `trail.headEntries` cannot fail, so the guard lost its pin while PLAN.md claims it kept its cover. The rest is stale text in stored specs and one flag help string.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/trail/dirty_test.go:62` — the new `TestDirty` row "tracked directory replaced by a link out, same bytes" cannot fail on the guard it names. Mutation (on a COPY of `internal/trail` under `.agents/scratch/agents/`, since removed): `internal/trail/dirty.go:106` `fsRoot.Lstat(filepath.FromSlash(p))` replaced by `os.Lstat(filepath.Join(root, filepath.FromSlash(p)))` (1 occurrence before the edit, diff read afterwards, it compiled): `TestDirty` still passes, and the whole package fails only `TestRegisteredOutsideACheckout`, an unrelated TMPDIR-inside-a-worktree artifact. The row goes dirty anyway because `dir` is now an untracked symlink (`git ls-files -o` at `dirty.go:76-83`). So the security-review-of-v2.6.0 finding 3 pin (nothing outside the checkout is hashed) went away with the deleted `TestChangedStaysInsideTheCheckout`, and `PLAN.md:355` ("keep their cover in `TestDirty`") is false. Fix: make the row keep the link-out dir out of the untracked list (an entry in `.git/info/exclude`, or tracked path behind an ignored link) so only the `os.Root` read can flag it, then re-run the mutation above red-first.
- **[low / confidence: high]** SPEC-fyr-search (stored record) line 84 — "Unreadable database, or a schema other than 2" is now wrong: `internal/search/store.go:29` is `"3"`. Also line 18, "Git and the files in `~/.config/fyr/` stay the source of truth", restates the removed global-index source. Change both in the same record.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `cmd/fyr/ctx_verbs.go:120` — `search --global` help still says "and the global search index, ~/.config/fyr/search.db" as if it were searched; the index now holds no file (ADR-087), `--global` answers from records. Reword with the next cmd change; `index --global` (line 123) is still accurate.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** SPEC-fyr-dream (stored) — step 2 still says "a trail file's name can hold a secret's shape", but the label is now a record ID (`collect.go` comment changed to say so); and no row of the failure table, nor any line, names the new skip `no .agents/trail.jsonl: fyr record import` (`internal/dream/dream.go:177`, `TestSkipReasonNamesTheImport`), nor ADR-087.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** SPEC-fyr-memory-loop line 14, SPEC-fyr-work line 20, SPEC-fyr-eval line 14 (stored) — the P10a re-read stamps restate ADR-086's "the global index holds `~/.config/fyr`'s files only", which ADR-087 reverses. They are dated notes, so a one-clause "(amended by ADR-087)" is enough.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/dream/collect_fit_test.go:84` — a fixture `Dropped` note "feedback.jsonl: …" names a reader that no longer exists; harmless test data, but it is the only remaining `feedback.jsonl:` dropped-note shape in the tree (restatement grep).

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. No remaining caller or definition of `trail.Dates`/`changed`, `memory.Store`/`trusted`, `harness.LastRetro`, `configView`, `docsOf`, `trailDirs`, `mdFiles`, `linked`, `feedback`/`entry` (grep over `*.go`; `hashesDiffer`, `openRegular`, `readFile`, `Readable`, `DocsRoot` all still have a live caller). Nit, not a finding: `scope.kind/label/rawLabel/kindMatches` still take a `project` argument that nothing reads.
2. Flow tracing — pass with the finding above. `reconcileGlobal` returns `(st, err)` and its one caller was updated; `sc.projects = nil` yields `IN ()`, which SQLite accepts (`TestGlobalReadsNoConfigFile` passes and goes red if the config view returns, since the output would hold "config"). `collect` now returns the brain store's refusal instead of a `Dropped` note: dry run prints `would fail (...)`, a real run logs `fail`; both paths existed. The schema bump removes the old global DB (`openStore` stale-schema path) and so empties `projects`; documented. Lost-then-moved coverage checked: `memory.trusted`'s four refusals live in brain (`import_security_test.go:201`, `import_arms_test.go:155`, the corrupt-index test), the fsmonitor pin moved and runs, the git-args pin stays in `trail_test.go:126`. The dry-run "refused store is left out and named" subtest was removed with no replacement at the dry-run level (the collect level has `TestCollectDoesNotFollowALinkedAgentsDir`); acceptable, the behaviour changed from a note to a failure.
3. Standards conformance — fail on the doc restatements above (specs 84/18, dream, three re-read stamps, one help string); code conforms. `restatement-grep.sh` over `docs_root`, `configView`, `config_view`, `trail.Dates`, `memory.Store`, `~config` returns no living-file hit; over `feedback.jsonl`/`retros.jsonl` only tests and `internal/brain/import_global.go` (the one kept reader). The script's own change is pinned both ways by `TestRestatementGrepRunsOutsideHarness`. The `setupEnv` `FYR=` addition is documented in SPEC-fyr-eval:79 and GUIDE-eval:11 and pinned by `TestRunSetup`.
4. Directory layout — pass. `read_file.go` is a verbatim move of `readAll`/`readIndexable` out of the deleted `config_view.go`, beside the code that uses it.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. No dependency, no crypto, no auth code in the range.
6. Decoupling — pass. `search.Project` loses `DocsRoot`, `scope` loses `proj`/`byKey`/`global`; metrics keeps `trail.DocsRoot` and `search.KindOf` with a comment saying so; no new cross-package reach-in.

## Not examined
- The full test suite (the dispatch forbade it): only the targeted tests named above ran, with TMPDIR set to the session scratchpad because two tests refuse a TMPDIR inside a worktree.
- No mutation run on `TestStoreRunsNoProjectHook` in brain (it ran and was not skipped, so its control fired); no mutation on the other new tests (`TestDreamReadsOnlyRecords`, `TestGlobalReadsNoConfigFile` only reasoned, not mutated).
- ADR-087 body and the DEPLOY-local, SPEC-fyr-record, SPEC-fyr-work and SPEC-fyr-eval records were grepped for the changed nouns, not read end to end. `GUIDE-testing` and the PRD/SDD/TDD files were checked only through `git grep` for the removed symbols and test names (no hit).
- PLAN.md and `.agents/trail.jsonl` were outside the range by instruction.

## Outcome

Fixed: the `TestDirty` row (git excludes `dir`; the mutant fails, the real code passes), `SPEC-fyr-search`, `ctx_verbs.go`'s help, `SPEC-fyr-dream`. The three P10a re-read stamps are historical; the P10b stamp beside each names ADR-087.

title: Security — PLAN.md P10b: the dream input paths
body:
# Security review — p10b dream records only, global index holds no file   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: HEAD f53948c..working tree (uncommitted; `.agents/scratch/p10b/range.diff`, 45 files, excluding `.agents/trail.jsonl` and `PLAN.md`), plus ADR-087, SPEC-fyr-dream, SPEC-fyr-search, SPEC-fyr-memory-loop, SPEC-fyr-work, SPEC-fyr-eval, SPEC-fyr-record, DEPLOY-local, GUIDE-eval.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

No exploitable weakness in the production code. Everything the removed readers guarded is either gone with the reader or still enforced on the one surviving path: the dream's input is now records, a committed `trail.jsonl` cannot carry `memory` or `feedback` (the load refuses those kinds), and `fyr record import` keeps the symlink and tracked-store refusals. Two low findings, both about what vouches for that. The worst: the test moved in to replace `TestChangedStaysInsideTheCheckout` does not pin containment. With the `os.Root` read removed from `headEntries`, it still passes (run on a mutated copy), so nothing now fails if `trail.Dirty` hashes through a link out of the checkout. The other: SPEC-fyr-dream keeps a failure-table row describing a memory-store refusal that no longer exists.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/trail/dirty_test.go:62-71` (with `internal/trail/dirty.go:106`) — The case "tracked directory replaced by a link out, same bytes" carries the comment "Hashed through the root, never outside it", but its only assertion is `dirty == true`, which `git ls-files -o` satisfies by itself: it lists the replacing symlink `dir` as untracked. Measured on a throwaway copy of `internal/trail`: `fsRoot.Lstat` changed to `os.Lstat` in `headEntries`, and `TestDirty` still passes. A probe repo showed `hash-object --no-filters --stdin-paths` reads through the link and returns HEAD's blob for the same bytes, so the mutant really does hash outside the checkout, and it reports clean when that link is ignored. The deleted `TestChangedStaysInsideTheCheckout` was the only pin on this property (`changed` is gone, the property lives on in `headEntries`), and `fyr record import` relies on `trail.Dirty` to refuse a tree whose tracked directory became a link. The production code is correct today; the regression would be silent, and the failure mode is a false clean plus a read outside the checkout. Remediation: in that case, also write `dir` to `.git/info/exclude` so the untracked listing cannot answer. Verified on the same copy: with that line the mutant fails (`Dirty = false, want true`) and the real `dirty.go` passes. Use `.git/info/exclude`, not `.gitignore`: editing a tracked `.gitignore` would itself read dirty.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `SPEC-fyr-dream`, failure table, row "The store is a symlink, or git tracks it" (`.agents/scratch/p10b/SPEC-fyr-dream.md:103`; present in the stored record too) — Says "memory is left out and named in the prompt and the proposal frontmatter; the rest is sent". This range deleted that behaviour: `memory.Store`, `trusted`, `addFiles` and the `memory:` Dropped note are gone, and `.agents/memory` is never read by a dream. SPEC-fyr-memory-loop line 42 already states the new truth, so the two specs now disagree on a trust check. A reader auditing the dream's guards is told of a refusal that no longer runs, and of a partial-send mode that no longer exists. Remediation: delete the row. If the table should stay complete, also say that a symlinked `.agents` with no `trail.jsonl` behind it is skipped as `no .agents/trail.jsonl: fyr record import`, not failed as the neighbouring row says.

## Checked

- **Dream input paths:** `collectIn` calls `addRecords` for every project with no `migrated` gate of its own; both callers (`run.go:152`, `run_dry.go:83`) run `skipReason` first, so a project with no `trail.jsonl` never reaches it. The prompt's stored inputs are memory, trail and feedback from `brain.ForDream`. Old `.agents/memory`, `.agents/docs` and `feedback.jsonl` are unread (`TestDreamReadsOnlyRecords`).
- **Tracked memory cannot return through the trail:** `parseLine` refuses `memory`, `feedback`, `proposal` (`unexported`), and `loadLocked` inserts into the project scope with `project=''`, so a committed line cannot forge a memory or a global feedback record. Global feedback is read by exact `project = scope`.
- **Symlink handling:** `migrated` is an `Lstat` through `.agents`, so a symlinked `.agents` holding a `trail.jsonl` passes the skip, then `openForSearch` runs `guardExportPath` before anything is read and the project fails loudly with its watermark kept; `TestCollectDoesNotFollowALinkedAgentsDir` pins it at dream level. `openTrail` adds `O_NOFOLLOW`, a non-blocking open and a post-open regular-file check, which replaces the deleted FIFO test's concern. `activityIn` ignores a `forDream` error, but the following `collect` reports it.
- **Redaction and labels:** every input's text and label, and every Dropped string, pass `scrub` before `fit`; `redactFeedback` runs `RedactJSONL` on the compacted line. A non-JSON or multi-line feedback body takes the same per-line path, raw needle first, so nothing is less covered than the old reader. Labels are now record IDs, grammar-checked on load, then folded by `oneLine`; `block` escapes fence runs in text. The prompt's `c.Name` is folded but not scrubbed: unchanged by this range and sourced from the checkout's directory name.
- **Removed trust checks:** `memoryEntries` keeps `trusted`'s three refusals (symlinked `.agents`, non-directory or symlinked store, anything git tracks), through `trail.Command`. `readDocs` uses `git ls-files` plus `Lstat`: a committed symlink at a record directory lists as one non-regular path and is refused, covering `linked`'s case. A local link at a tracked directory is refused by `trail.Dirty` on a real run; a dry run reads through it but prints only IDs and paths, and sends nothing. `Dates` and `changed` are gone, so the timer runs fewer git calls in project roots.
- **Hook pin:** `TestStoreRunsNoProjectHook` is a valid must-fail. In a probe repo, plain `git ls-files` fired the `core.fsmonitor` hook and the hardened form did not. PRD R3 still names it, though it now exercises the import, not the timer; the timer's own `trail.Log` keeps `TestLogRunsNoSignatureProgram` and the fsmonitor pin in `internal/trail/trail_test.go`.
- **Global index:** `registerConsented` still requires the marker plus `HasTrail`, which refuses a symlink at either name. `checkRegistered` keeps a registration whose check errors. `dropProject` is one autocommit `DELETE`, atomic without the old transaction, with busy still mapped. `reconcileGlobal` writes no file, and `sc.projects` nil gives `IN ()` at every use (`search.go`, `search_query.go`, `search_refs.go`); no code indexes `sc.projects`. `sc.close` is nil-safe under `--global`. `dream --all` still filters both lists by `trail.Registered`, so the schema-3 emptying of `projects` widens nothing. A schema-2 `search.db` keeps old `~config` text at 0600 until its next open rebuilds it; no reader reaches it.
- **`read_file.go`:** moved verbatim from `config_view.go`; `readAll` and `readIndexable` are unchanged, and the `sha256` that left with `configView` was a content key, no crypto.
- **Eval's `FYR`:** set only by `setupEnv` (`row.go:63`), never by `checkEnv` or the CLI session, and it is `os.Executable()`, passed as an environment value and not interpolated into shell text. Setup already ran as the operator with eval's `PATH`, so it gains no capability. Both rows using it (`retro`, `distill`) pass `--home "$SB"`, and `HOME=$SB` holds even if a row omits it. SPEC-fyr-eval and GUIDE-eval state it.
- **`restatement-grep.sh`, `record.go`, `status.go`:** no input-handling change; `printImport` stays behind `search.Printable`.
- **Secrets:** none in the diff. **Injection:** no SQL built from input (the changed statements are parameterized); shell text only in the review script, with a fixed `grep -F` pattern. **Authz/authn:** consent gates unchanged, see above. **Crypto:** none added or hand-rolled. **GCP surface:** none touched.
- **Dependencies:** `go.mod` and `go.sum` are not in the diff. `govulncheck ./...` (go1.27.3): 0 vulnerabilities affect the code; 1 vulnerability in a required module is reported as not called, not itemized here because `-show verbose` was not run. `npm audit`: not applicable, no `package.json`, `web/` or `ui/`.
- **`fyr search --refs`:** run for 9 changed non-test files (collect, collect_sources, dream, global, scope_prepare, memory, trail, row, redact): only BUG-188 on `trail.go`, whose fix (`errUnhashable`) is untouched.

## Not examined

- `fyr search --refs ... --kind bug` for the remaining changed files, test files included.
- The Antigravity transcript reader (`internal/search/dream*.go`, `agy_*`), metrics and `internal/dream/proposals_write.go` beyond their call sites: unchanged here.
- `import_classify.go`: not read, though the import is now the file era's one path.
- The stored docs were checked by targeted grep for trust, symlink and old-store claims, not read end to end. Each stored record differs from its scratch copy by one line; that line was not inspected beyond `cmp` reporting the first difference at byte 1 of `SPEC-fyr-dream`, and the row in the first finding was confirmed in the stored output.
- The full test suite was not run, by dispatch. Only `TestDirty` ran, on a throwaway copy of `internal/trail`.
- The `govulncheck` module-level item's identity (see Dependencies).
- No live model call was made: what reaches the prompt is established from code and tests.

## Outcome

Fixed: both findings (the same `TestDirty` row; the stale failure row replaced by the no-trail skip).
