# Review — P11 UI skills: frontend replaced by frontend-ui-economist and frontend-ui-modern   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: 503bdf8..3070008 (`git diff 503bdf8 3070008 -- . ':!*.png'`); lenses: code + docs

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing is broken. `skills/frontend` is gone and no live pointer to it remains in context/, rules/, agents/, skills/, README.md, TDD.md, SDD.md, PRD.md or the two GUIDE records. `GUIDE-eval` carries the `frontend-ui-economist` and `frontend-ui-modern` rows (lines 83-84 of the record), and `TestSuiteHarness` in `internal/eval/suite_test.go` was updated to match. `go vet ./...` is clean and `go test` passes for `./cmd/...`, `./internal/eval`, `./internal/harness` and the root package. The README skill count of 38 matches `ls -d skills/*/` (38 directories). The worst items are two leftover assumptions from the removed skill, both low severity (below).

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/docker/SKILL.md:73,98-102` and `skills/typescript/SKILL.md:49` — they still state the SPA layout that the removed `frontend` skill defined: `web/embed.go` embedding `dist/client` with `go:embed`, and e2e against the Go binary serving it. The diff drops the words "the frontend skill" from the docker lines but no remaining skill states that layout or the app wiring (SPA mode, Go catch-all, loaders). The operator chose to drop those rules (PLAN D22), so this is not a defect of the diff. The consequence is that the `build-fullstack` eval row (GUIDE-eval line 105) now has less guidance behind it. Fix: either accept it, or keep a short "embedded SPA" paragraph in `docker` or `typescript`.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `cmd/fyr/install_verbs_test.go:104` — the guard `strings.Contains(s, "settings")` was narrowed to `"settings.json"` so that a skill PNG named `*-settings-*.png` no longer trips it. The `.claude` check on the same line still catches a line about `~/.claude`, so the test can still fail for the behaviour it names. The only loss is a stray `settings.local.json`-style mention without `.claude`. Low risk. If kept, say in the comment that the `.claude` clause is what carries the check.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `skills/typescript/references/testing.md:90-122,165` — the ThemeToggle example (`data-theme`, `localStorage.theme`, the "once per theme" axe run) comes from the removed `theme-system.md`. The new one-line note redirects `frontend-ui-modern` users to the `.dark` class, but `frontend-ui-modern/references/theming.md:75` also sets `data-theme` for switchable themes, so the note is slightly over-narrow. The example is also now an orphan with no skill that defines its theme contract. Not blocking.

## Docs lens: remaining pointers to `frontend`
- Live pointers: none. Every hit for `frontend` in context/, rules/, agents/, skills/*/ (non-vendored), README.md, PRD.md, SDD.md, TDD.md and TODO.md is either generic ("the web frontend") or already renamed.
- Renamed in the diff: `agents/reviewer/agent.md:34`, `context/dev-setup.md:6`, `README.md:219` (the Code row) and `:85` (38 skills), `skills/bash` and `skills/golang` descriptions, `skills/typescript/SKILL.md` description and intro, `skills/review-standards/SKILL.md:47` and `references/typescript-review.md:3`, `skills/harness-audit/references/areas.md:21`.
- Unchanged and harmless: `skills/VENDORED.md:88` is historical (the 2026-10-01 strike). `skills/init-project/assets/README.md:22` names TanStack Start generically.
- Records: `GUIDE-eval` has the two new rows. `GUIDE-skill-matrix` line 4 lists both new row names in its ported-rows sentence, and there is no stale `frontend` row. Both records were updated in `.agents/trail.jsonl` at 18:45-18:46.
- Descriptions of the added skills (frontmatter only, as scoped): both are valid, name-matched, and each has a `Do NOT use for … (other skill)` cross-reference. The listing-budget and lint tests pass.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. The six `frontend` files are deleted, with no orphan references. The `skills/frontend-ui-*` trees carry sample themes and PNGs by design (D22 "keep screenshots", 44.6 MB binary accepted by the operator).
2. Flow tracing — pass. The eval suite row ids, the `GUIDE-eval` rows and `TestSuiteHarness` agree, and the tests ran green. See the docker/typescript residue in the first finding.
3. Standards conformance — pass with nits. Restatements of the renamed skill were grepped across the living files. The two lows above are the residue.
4. Directory layout — pass. The skills sit under `skills/<name>/` with `SKILL.md`, `references/`, `assets/` and `scripts/`.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. No auth or crypto. The scripts only read local files, and `sim.mjs` runs `execFileSync(process.execPath, [theme.mjs …])` with fixed arguments (no shell). No new Go dependency.
6. Decoupling — pass. The two UI skills have a stated boundary ("Do NOT use for … other skill"), and the old overlap with `typescript` is cut.

## Not examined
- The skill bodies, the CSS and JSON assets, the PNGs and `theme-simulator.html` were not read (operator's, out of scope). Scripts were only grepped for exec, network and install patterns. The `security` agent's own read of the scripts is P11's Checkpoint box and was not duplicated here.
- `fyr check`, `govulncheck` and the Antigravity behavioural runs of the new skills (P13) were not run. `go test ./...` was run for the four affected package sets only, not the full tree.

## Outcome

1. Accepted: the operator dropped the TanStack Start rules (D22); the residue in `docker` and `typescript` stays true for a project on that layout.
2. Rebutted: the narrowed guard was run both ways (a `settings.json` under a skill fails it), and the `.claude` clause stands.
3. Rebutted: the note says the dark switch is the `.dark` class, which holds; `theming.md:75` sets `data-theme` to a theme id beside it, a different axis.

title: Security — PLAN.md P11: the scripts and instructions of the two UI skills
body:
# Security review — frontend-ui skills executable content   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: 3070008^..3070008, limited to skills/frontend-ui-economist and skills/frontend-ui-modern: scripts, assets/charts.js, the HTML files' script tags and external URLs, and the markdown's run and fetch instructions. Nothing was run except read-only scans and govulncheck.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

No high-severity finding: no script reaches the network on its own, none opens a shell, none carries a secret, and installing the skills runs none of them (no exec bit, no symlink, no `exec.Command` in `internal/harness` that touches a skill file). The worst problem is an instruction, not code: `frontend-ui-modern` tells the agent to publish a simulation built from the project's real screens and real numbers to claude.ai, with no public-or-OSS scope. That is the step BUG-022's rule in `skills/VENDORED.md` refuses, and `sim.mjs` repeats it in its output on every run. Next come the floating `npx shadcn@latest` runs that every UI task needs, the unpinned third-party agent skill the agent is told to defer to, and an HTML injection sink in `charts.js`, an asset meant to be copied into real pages.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/frontend-ui-modern/SKILL.md:73` (also `references/workflow.md:53`, `references/workflow.md:146`, `scripts/sim.mjs:11`, `scripts/sim.mjs:98`) — BUG-022 breach. "publish it as an HTML artifact (claude.ai)" is offered as a way to show the simulation, with no scope to public or OSS work. The content is project data by the skill's own rules: `SKILL.md:45` collects "the real data shapes (field names, realistic values, row counts)", `SKILL.md:59` rewrites views into "the project's real screens with real content", and `SKILL.md:70` demands "real labels and numbers". `sim.mjs:98` prints the same advice into the agent's tool output on every run, and without even the "(claude.ai)" qualifier. So private screens, labels and figures go to a third party on the agent's own choice of display route. The rule names a "publish" step explicitly and says such a step is scoped to public or OSS work only, or the skill is not kept. Its wording targets vendored and imported skills, and D22 classes these two as the operator's own; they still arrived as imported zips, and this dispatch applies the rule. Remediation: drop the publish route from all five sites, or scope each to "public or OSS projects only, and only on the operator's explicit word". Opening the file and capturing PNGs already cover the need. This changes bodies D22 pins as byte-identical to the zips, so it is the operator's decision.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/frontend-ui-modern/SKILL.md:42` (also `SKILL.md:91`, `SKILL.md:93`, `SKILL.md:97`, `SKILL.md:137`; `references/workflow.md:11`, `:78`, `:82`, `:89`; `references/shadcn-2026.md:33`, `:42-55`; `references/blocks.md:3`, `:54`; `references/components.md:6`, `:105`, `:140`; `references/charts.md:6`, `:113`, `:121`; `references/theming.md:40`, `:76`) — every shadcn step runs `npx shadcn@latest`, so an agent executes whatever that package's `latest` tag points at, with the operator's full environment, on every UI task, starting at discovery (step 0). The agent runs it unprompted because the skill's gates require it. A compromised release of this one package reaches every project the skill touches. `mcp init --client claude` (`SKILL.md:137`, listed as a CLI capability, not a step) would additionally write a floating server into the client's config. The harness's own convention is a pinned version: `npx skills@<version>` in `skills/VENDORED.md`, while `README.md:27` says the skill was verified against CLI 4.23. Remediation: name the verified version once, for example `npx shadcn@4.23.0`, or prefer the project-local `shadcn` devDependency the skill already describes (`references/shadcn-2026.md:34`). Stdlib alternative: none applies; this is a project-side tool the operator's stack chose.

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `skills/frontend-ui-modern/SKILL.md:35` (also `README.md:11`, `references/shadcn-2026.md:273-276`) — `npx skills add shadcn/ui` pulls an unpinned, unreviewed third-party agent skill into the project, and the text then tells the agent to "defer to it" for CLI mechanics and component rules. That gives agent instructions fetched at an unknown revision authority over reviewed text. It sidesteps the repo's rule that third-party skills are pinned, read for BUG-022 steps and listed in `skills/VENDORED.md`. Confidence is medium because `SKILL.md:35` is conditional ("If the project has…"); only `README.md:11` recommends the install. Remediation: remove the install recommendation, or pin it to a commit, and treat a present companion skill as data the agent reads, never as an authority it defers to.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/frontend-ui-economist/assets/charts.js:61` (also `:122`, `:153`) — series names, `slot`, label text, `valueName` and the output of `format` are interpolated into `innerHTML` unescaped: the legend at line 61, the hover tooltips at lines 122 and 153. `SKILL.md:264` scopes the kit to "any server-rendered template", and nothing in `references/charts.md` or `SKILL.md` warns about it. A page that feeds user-controlled or database text into a chart gets stored script injection, fired by rendering the legend or by hover. The rest of the file writes the same strings safely through `textContent` (line 28), so the sink is inconsistent, not a design need. In-tree callers (`starter.html`, the simulator's own copy) pass constants and are not exploitable. Remediation: build legend and tooltip with `createElement` and `textContent`, and validate `slot` against `/^--[a-z0-9-]+$/` before it reaches an attribute. Stdlib only: no dependency is needed.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/frontend-ui-modern/references/components.md:142` (also `references/blocks.md:54`, `SKILL.md:97`, `references/shadcn-2026.md:47`, `references/shadcn-2026.md:44`) — third-party registry items are reviewed after install ("read every added file"), although `--dry-run`, `--diff` and `--view` exist and `add` accepts a bare URL or `owner/repo/item`. `-y` defaults to true at `init`, and `init --preset` accepts a URL. Package dependencies a registry item declares are installed before that read, so install lifecycle scripts would run first. That npm behaviour is general knowledge, not verified against this CLI version. Remediation: require `--view` or `--dry-run` before any non-`@shadcn` item is added.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/frontend-ui-modern/scripts/mockup.mjs:103` (also `:113`, `:116`, `:127`; `references/workflow.md:100`; `SKILL.md:105`) — the proof trail can put sensitive runtime data in the repo. `captures.json` stores page console errors verbatim, the contact sheet writes the target URL as given (including a query token or `user:pass@`), and the PNGs show whatever the running app renders. `workflow.md:100` says "The rounds stay in the repo", and `SKILL.md:105` says "Keep every round". The harness's secret-shaped path list does not cover these files and no reviewer reads a PNG. `SKILL.md:125` softens this with "gitignored or committed on purpose", but no default is set. Remediation: gitignore `ui-mockups/` by default, and strip the URL's credentials and query from the sheet.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `skills/frontend-ui-modern/scripts/sim.mjs:67` (also `sim.mjs:68`; `scripts/theme.mjs:160`, `:173-174`, `:180-181`) — a `--custom` palette's `id`, `title`, `source` and colour names reach the generated file unescaped: into a `<style>` block through `theme.mjs` (a `*/` or `</style>` breaks out) and into an inline script through `JSON.stringify` (a `</script>` breaks out). A palette from an untrusted source therefore runs script when `ui-sim/index.html` is opened. The same names reach CSS the skill tells the agent to paste into the app's stylesheet. Hex values are safe: they are reparsed numerically. Both `.replace` calls also interpret `$` patterns in the replacement string. Remediation: validate `id` against `^[a-z0-9-]+$`, reject `*/` and `<` in the free-text fields, escape `<` as `<` in the JSON, and use a replacer function.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `skills/frontend-ui-modern/scripts/mockup.mjs:112` (also `:101-102`, `:117`) — `esc` does not escape quotes, yet its result goes into `alt="…"`, and `s.file` goes into `src="…"` raw. The file name comes from `--name`, `--themes`, `--views`, `--states` and `--overlays`, so `--name ../../x` also writes outside `--out`. Only command-line input reaches this, so an attacker needs influence over the agent's arguments. Remediation: escape `"`, and reject path separators in the name parts.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `skills/frontend-ui-economist/scripts/measure_whitespace.js:6` (also `:13`, `:35`; `skills/frontend-ui-modern/scripts/mockup.mjs:5`, `:50-51`; `skills/frontend-ui-modern/README.md:10`) — Playwright and its Chromium download are unpinned, and the economist form (`npm i playwright`) adds a runtime dependency to whatever project is the working directory. `mockup.mjs:50` loads `playwright` from the working directory's `node_modules`, so running it inside an untrusted checkout executes that checkout's code. `measure_whitespace.js:13` shows a predictable `/tmp/ink.png` output path, which also breaks the scratch rule. Remediation: pin the version, use `-D`, and show a scratch path in the example. Stdlib alternative: none; Node has no headless browser, so the dependency itself is justified.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `skills/frontend-ui-economist/assets/starter.html:7-9` (also `assets/theme-simulator.html:7-9`, `assets/theme-kit.css:5`, `SKILL.md:255`) — pages built from the starter load fonts from Google at runtime, so each open discloses the visitor's IP and user agent to Google and the page gains a third-party stylesheet that cannot carry an integrity hash. The request holds a fixed family list and no project data, so this does not trip BUG-022. Remediation: note self-hosting `@font-face` files as the option for private or CSP-restricted pages.

## Checked

- **Secrets:** none. A pattern scan of both skill trees for vendor token shapes and private keys found no match. `hooks.slack.com/services/T0…` at `assets/simulation-template.html:672` is truncated sample copy. All 292 PNGs parse cleanly, with no text chunks and no trailing data.
- **Injection:**
  - No `child_process` in `check_theme.js`, `measure_whitespace.js`, `mockup.mjs` or `theme.mjs`. `sim.mjs:45` and `:54` use `execFileSync` with fixed `process.execPath` and no shell.
  - Playwright `page.evaluate` calls pass arguments as parameters.
  - `simulation-template.html` URL and `localStorage` state reach `innerHTML` at line 814 only after the allow-list checks at lines 918-922; `style`, `radius` and `vp` reach only `dataset`, `style.width` and `textContent`.
  - `theme-simulator.html` validates its hash at line 949 and its skin at line 930; its `innerHTML` values are constants or computed CSS from its own stylesheet.
  - `__PROJECT__` lands only in text context (lines 6 and 374) with `<>&` stripped.
- **Network and data egress:** no `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `sendBeacon`, `WebSocket` or `eval` in the HTML files. `gallery.html` has no script tag or external URL: 131 local images only. External URLs in the HTML are Google Fonts and two sample-copy strings; those in the CSS and JSON are source comments. Scripts contact only the URL they are given. `navigator.clipboard` writes only on a button press.
- **Prompt injection:** no directive-shaped text, no HTML comments in the markdown, no zero-width or bidi characters.
- **Authz/authn:** no auth code in scope. `simulation-template.html` holds login mock-ups only. `chromium.launch()` keeps the browser sandbox.
- **Crypto:** none; nothing hand-rolled. `Math.random` at `simulation-template.html:875` makes an SVG id only.
- **Dependencies:** no package manifest added, and no Go dependency in this commit. `govulncheck ./...`: 0 vulnerabilities affecting the code, 1 in a required module that is not called (not new to this commit; the module list was not read). `npm audit` not run: neither skill has a `package.json`, so there is nothing to audit.
- **GCP surface:** none in scope.
- **Install path:** no exec bit and no symlink in either skill. `exec.Command` in `internal/harness` covers `git`, `go`, `gh`, `diff` and the `fyr` binary only.
- **Past failures:** `fyr search --refs` on both `SKILL.md` files returned 0, but it ran against an empty scratch home, so that zero is no evidence. A read of the committed `.agents/trail.jsonl` found no `bug` record naming these skills or scripts, and confirmed BUG-022's text. That run left `.agents/scratch/security-home/.config/fyr/brain.db`, gitignored, a file this review created beyond the findings file.

## Not examined

- `simulation-template.html` lines 1-773 and `theme-simulator.html` lines 1-652: scanned by pattern for tags, handlers, URLs and sinks, not read line by line.
- Markdown other than `SKILL.md` (modern, lines 10-139) and `workflow.md` (lines 40-161): pattern scan only for commands and fetches, plus spot reads. The rest of modern's `SKILL.md`, and economist's `SKILL.md`, were not read end to end.
- `palettes.json`, `shadcn-themes.json` and the CSS files: pattern scan only.
- PNG pixel content: chunk structure was checked; the images were not viewed.
- Upstream behaviour of the `shadcn` CLI, `skills`, `create-next-app` and Playwright, including whether any sends telemetry or project data. The skill text names no such step, but that says nothing about the tools.
- The `fyr search --refs` run was on the two `SKILL.md` files only, not every changed file; the `.agents/trail.jsonl` read covers the rest by name.
- The installer was checked by pattern, not traced. D22 was read to the end of its first paragraph only.
- The behaviour claims above come from reading the code, as dispatched: no script was run.

## Outcome

The four medium findings: fixed on the operator's word (D23); `TestModernOverrides` and `TestChartsEscapeInnerHTML` each failed before the fix. The six low findings: accepted by the operator (D23).

body:
# Security review — p11-round-2-charts-esc-and-harness-overrides   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: 41c4714^..41c4714 (`skills/`, `ui_skills_test.go`; round 2 over the fixes only)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The charts fix holds; the overrides fix is partial. `esc` plus `slotOf` closes all three `innerHTML` sinks in `charts.js`, the attribute context and a `format()` return value included. The worst problem is the scope of `## Harness overrides`: it works for an agent reading `SKILL.md`, but its `npx` rule says "below", and 27 of the `npx shadcn@latest` lines are in `references/`, which `SKILL.md` sends the agent to at each phase. `references/workflow.md:53` and `:78` still give the old instructions at the moment of action. `npx shadcn@4.23` is also a range, so the next 4.23.x publish runs unreviewed; D23 accepts that on the record, and it does not close round 1's threat.

Answers to the two dispatch questions:
- **charts.js: yes, closed.** Verified with a fake-DOM stub on the real file, in both states (see Checked).
- **Overrides: yes for `SKILL.md` read whole, no for the skill read as shipped.** Placement at line 12, before the gates, and "win over every line below" do cover lines 45, 52, 83, 101, 103 and 107. They do not reach `references/`, `README.md` or `assets/simulation-template.html`.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/frontend-ui-modern/SKILL.md:17` (with `:14`, `:230`) — the pin's scope excludes the lines an agent runs. "Every `npx shadcn@latest` below" and "win over every line below and over what `scripts/sim.mjs` prints" literally cover `SKILL.md` only, which has 4 such lines (`:52`, `:101`, `:103`, `:107`). `references/` holds 27: `workflow.md:11,78,82,89`; `shadcn-2026.md:33,42,47-55,250`; `components.md:6,7,105,140`; `blocks.md:3,54`; `charts.md:6,113,121`; `theming.md:40,76`. `assets/simulation-template.html:13` holds one more, and it is copied into `ui-sim/index.html`. `SKILL.md:230` says to read these files at each phase, and `workflow.md` is "the six phases in detail", so at the Build step the agent has an unqualified `npx shadcn@latest init … -y` in front of it. That is round 1's second medium, whose site list named these files, surviving for those sites. D23 says "the 20-odd lines below it … the section says it wins over them": that is false for the 20-odd, most of which are not below it. Remediation: change line 14 and line 17 to name the whole skill: "These win over every line of this skill: this file, `references/`, `README.md`, `assets/` and what `scripts/*.mjs` print", and "Every `npx shadcn@latest` in this skill". Extend `TestModernOverrides` to require that wording.

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `skills/frontend-ui-modern/references/workflow.md:53` (also `:146`; `references/shadcn-2026.md:274-275`; `README.md:11`; `SKILL.md:14`) — the publishing rule and the companion-skill rule are not named as winning over the references. Both bullets are worded absolutely with no "below", so they apply on a careful reading, which is why confidence is medium. But the precedence sentence lists exactly what it beats, and references are not on the list. `workflow.md:53` still offers "publish it as an HTML artifact (claude.ai)", `:146` has an `<artifact link>` template, and `shadcn-2026.md:274-275` still says "defer to it". The content is the project's real screens and numbers, so this is the BUG-022 path. Remediation: the same line-14 change as above covers these; `TestModernOverrides` should pin it.

- **[medium / confidence: high — accepted in D23, recorded and not reopened here]** `skills/frontend-ui-modern/SKILL.md:17` — `shadcn@4.23` is a semver range, not a pin. `npm view` on 2026-10-31 gives `4.23.0` as both the only match and the `latest` dist-tag, so today the range and `@latest` resolve to the same version and the first 4.23.x publish is taken automatically. It blocks 4.24 and 5.x. It does not block a compromised patch release, which is the threat round 1 named. `4.23.0` exists, and round 1's remediation proposed it. D23's reason ("the skill's text names no exact patch") does not stand in the way: it is a one-string edit plus the matching `want` in `TestModernOverrides`. Remediation: write `npx shadcn@4.23.0`.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `skills/frontend-ui-economist/assets/charts.js:89` (also `:93`, `:151`) — `slotOf` is not applied to the other three uses of a slot. `s.slot` and `o.slot` reach `stroke` and `fill` as `var(${…})`. The stub recorded `var(--s1);background:red)` in a path's `stroke`. This is `setAttribute`, so there is no HTML context and no script path; a malformed value is ignored by the browser. What remains is a CSS-value injection: a `var(--x, url(…))` fallback might trigger an outbound paint-server fetch in some browsers (not tested; low confidence on that part). The legend also falls back to `--s1` while the line keeps the raw slot, so legend and line can disagree. Remediation: route all three through `slotOf`, and widen the test to any `var(${` in the file.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `ui_skills_test.go:17` — `TestChartsEscapeInnerHTML` is a grep on the call sites and passes under mutations that reopen the hole, so the fix is not fully pinned. By reading the test, these stay green: a weakened `esc` (`charts.js:26`, for example dropping `"` or `<`) or `slotOf` (`:27`), because their definition lines hold no `innerHTML = ` and are never read; `${esc(a) + b}`, because only the prefix is checked; a fourth sink written `innerHTML=`, `innerHTML +=`, `outerHTML` or `insertAdjacentHTML`; a value concatenated as `'<b>' + name` with no `${}`. The global Definition of Done counts a finding fixed only when every trigger has a test that fails without the fix. Remediation: pin both definitions as exact strings, and match sinks with `(inner|outer)HTML\s*\+?=|insertAdjacentHTML`. Stdlib `regexp` is enough; no dependency is needed.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/frontend-ui-modern/SKILL.md:16` — "public or OSS work only" leaves the classification to the agent. Round 1's remediation read "and only on the operator's explicit word", and that clause was dropped, so an agent can decide a project is public and publish it. Remediation: add "and only on the operator's explicit word".

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/frontend-ui-modern/SKILL.md:147` (also `references/shadcn-2026.md:58`) — the pin names `npx` only, while both lines say "Use the project's runner (`npx` / `pnpm dlx` / `bunx --bun`)". On a pnpm or bun project, `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest` is outside the override's literal words. An agent may translate the version over or may not. Remediation: "with any runner".

## Checked

- **Injection, charts.js sinks:** closed. `esc` handles `& < > " '` in a single pass and `slotOf` accepts only `^--[\w-]+$`; JS `$` without the `m` flag rejects a trailing newline. All values at `:63`, `:124`, `:155` are wrapped, `format()` output included, and the other `innerHTML` writes are `''`.
  - Stub: `.agents/scratch/sec-p11-stub/stub.js` loads the real file under a fake DOM, fires `pointermove` and `pointerenter`, and uses an inert `<x-probe>` marker in name, label, `label.text`, `valueName` and `format()`, with six slot shapes (attribute breakout, CSS escape, trailing newline, array, object with `toString`, valid).
  - Must-pass state (41c4714): 0 bad across 7 scenarios. Must-fail state (41c4714^): 174 bad tags and styles. The detector fires, and the tooltip paths D23 said were covered "by the pin only" now have a stub run. A fake DOM is not a browser parser.
  - `format()` returning `undefined` or a non-string does not throw. Output now shows as text: a `format()` returning markup or a pre-encoded `&` displays literally, which matches the `textContent` paths at `:113` and `:152`, and the doc examples return plain strings. No finding.
- **Injection, in-tree siblings:** `assets/theme-simulator.html:744,799,828` keep the unescaped pattern, but its series are constants (`:702-704`), as D23 says. No finding. `simulation-template.html:814` is allow-listed at `:918-922`, matching round 1.
- **Past failures:** `fyr search --refs --kind bug` returned 0 references for all three paths, run against a fresh scratch home (`.agents/scratch/sec-p11`) as the project rule requires, so that zero is not evidence. A grep of `.agents/trail.jsonl` found no `bug` record naming these paths; BUG-022 reaches them through `skills/VENDORED.md`, per round 1.
- **Secrets:** none in the commit's `skills/` and test diff.
- **Authz/authn:** not touched by this commit.
- **Crypto:** none; `esc` is output encoding, not a primitive.
- **Dependencies:** the commit changes no `go.mod`, `go.sum` or `package*.json`. `govulncheck ./...`: 0 vulnerabilities affecting the code, 1 in a required module not called; exit 0. It was not compared against the known list in `DEPLOY-local`, and the commit does not move it. `npm audit`: not run, no manifest in the range.
- **GCP surface:** not touched by this commit.

## Not examined

- Behaviour of a real agent: "would follow it" is judged from the text. No Antigravity run was made, and D23 leaves that to P13.
- A real browser: the stub proves the strings, not rendering, and the CSS `url()` fallback in the fourth finding is untested.
- `references/` beyond the grep hits and the lines quoted; `README.md` beyond line 11. Grep output was cut at about 200 columns per line.
- Round 1's record past character 11500 (the rest of its Checked section). Its six low findings are accepted in D23 and were not reopened.
- `.agents/trail.jsonl` and `PLAN.md` in the commit, except the D23 row.

## Outcome

Fixed in the next commit, with no third round (D23): the overrides now cover the whole skill, the pin is the exact `@4.23.0` with any runner, publishing needs the operator's explicit word, and `TestChartsEscapeInnerHTML` pins the definitions of `esc` and `slotOf` and refuses the other sinks (an identity `esc` fails it, run). `TestModernOverrides` pins the precedence sentence. Accepted as lows in D23: `slotOf` at the `setAttribute` calls, and a split multi-line sink or raw concatenation the test does not catch.

# Review — p12-t5-thin-agy-dispatch-skill-matrix   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: HEAD~1..HEAD (62020f5), code and docs lens in one report (`/review --code --docs`), plus the six stored records it changed (read from `.agents/trail.jsonl` at HEAD and HEAD~1, diffed body by body).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The worst problem is that the new global rule contradicts a skill the same commit edits: `rules/agy-dispatch.md` tells every dispatcher to "choose each worker's model by tier and pass `--model`", while `skills/work/SKILL.md:76` still says the `/work` lead "never chooses, changes or adds a model, and runs `fyr work` with no `--model`", and step 5 now sends the lead to the rule. Second, `GUIDE-skill-matrix` was declared fully re-pathed to records (D24) but four places still check files that no longer exist, so those checks cannot pass. T5's thinning itself is sound: of the 278 mapped claims, 275 quotes were re-found in their current homes by script (the other 3 are the intended rewordings), and the 14 gaps are accounted for as D24 says. Nothing was run on the matrix (D24 says so too); I read each changed check against the skills and the `fyr record list` output format.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `rules/agy-dispatch.md:8` vs `skills/work/SKILL.md:76` (and :78, step 5) — the rule says to pass `--model` per worker; the `/work` skill, which is the thing that schedules `fyr work`, forbids the lead any model choice and any `--model` (the model comes from the phase's `model:` line). An always-on global rule and a skill now give opposite orders to the same actor, and P13's behavioural run of `/work` will hit it. The commit edited step 5 to cite the rule but left step 3. Fix: scope the rule ("unless the Kickoff's `Model:` line names one; the `/work` lead passes none") or change step 3 under a D-row; say which in the rule. D15 does not settle it (it is silent on `/work`).
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `GUIDE-skill-matrix` rows `agents-data-not-instructions`, `verifier-log-shape`, `verifier-blocked-redispatch` and Procedure step 2 — still name `reviews/*review*`, `reviews/*security*`, `testing/*verify*`, `plans/*recon*`, "the one new `testing/*.md` beside `guide.md`", "exactly one log beside `guide.md`" and "`guide.md` § 4 § Behavioural runs". None of those paths exist (records in the brain store; agents write drafts under `.agents/scratch/agents/`; the guide is `GUIDE-testing`). D24 says "Every row is re-pathed to records ... none struck", which is false for these. As written the three rows' artifact checks cannot be evaluated. Fix: re-path them (the draft in `.agents/scratch/agents/<agent>-*.md` or `rec testing verif` and friends) and `GUIDE-testing § 4`; grep `reviews/\|testing/\|plans/\|guide.md` over the record to confirm none is left.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `GUIDE-skill-matrix` Procedure step 1 and row `distill-from-log` — the seed `fyr record add feedback --global --project <clone> ...` carries no `--home` and step 1 does not set `HOME=<home>` (only step 3's check does). Run from the operator's shell it writes the real `~/.config/fyr` brain (the BUG-006 class `AGENTS.md` names; `GUIDE-eval`'s `distill` row passes `--home "$SB"`). Fix: say `HOME=<home>` (or `--home <home>`) in step 1 for every seed.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `TDD.md:15` — the M-row enumerates the rules as `critical-thinking.md`, `session-sizing.md`, `code-modularity.md`; the commit adds a fourth, `agy-dispatch.md`, and does not join it to the list (a vocabulary join, `review-standards` § 7). Fix: add it with D15 as its source.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `SPEC-fyr-dream` line 63 (stored record) — the inserted sentence "A unit installed by an older fyr keeps its nightly schedule, at which, with the session check, it almost never dreams. It lacks the line and is kept as it is" leaves "the line" (TimeoutStartSec) without its antecedent, and the nightly-schedule claim is then stated again later in the same bullet. Fix: merge the two sentences.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `PLAN.md` P12 boxes for items 25 and 32 are ticked, but their Verify clauses name a change record (the 14-claim table; `du` before/after) that is not in the commit's trail diff, and `fyr check` (tree binary `.agents/scratch/p12/fyr`, 1877273+dirty) reports 7 findings, all `spec-stale` (SPEC-fyr-check, -memory-loop, -metrics, -record, -search, -serve, -work: code under `cmd/fyr` committed after each spec's last update). The final Checkpoint ("0 findings and 0 notes") is still open, so this is not wrong yet, but item 25's own Verify (`fyr check`) does not hold at HEAD. Fix at the checkpoint: re-read those specs and touch them, then store the change record.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `rules/agy-dispatch.md:10` — tier names (`argon`, `flash`, `opus`, `sonnet`, `gpt-oss`) are not `--model` IDs (the verb validates against `agy models`), and D15 calls the flash tier "3.8 flash"; a global rule cannot point at this repo's `DEPLOY-local`, but it could name `agy models` as the source of IDs. `agy -p "/usage"` was not run by me (it would write agy state); I rely on D15's statement that it spends no quota.

- ADR-088: R0's first appearance is 2026-10-24 (`git log -S`), `9222762` is 2026-09-17 with the R8 earlier wording; PRD comment, R0 provenance and the ADR agree; no other copy of R0's old date found.

1. Dead code — pass: nothing orphaned; the thinned T5 prose was moved, not left commented.

title: Security review: PLAN.md P12b item 45, host-side git in a session-written clone
body:
# Security review — host-side git calls on a session-written clone (PLAN.md item 45)   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: HEAD 366c759 (tree at HEAD, no diff; blast-radius review of item 45)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Worst problem: under `--runner docker` the host's `git fetch` starts `upload-pack` on the host, outside the container, and that process interprets the `.git` the session wrote. A session can therefore aim it at another repository on the host, one the container cannot see, and those objects land in the lead under `refs/heads/work/<name>`. They stay there after the scope check fails, and the next run's clone carries them into a session. `Intact` checks only the three sandbox paths, nothing inside `.git`. leadGit's options do not help: git's local transport drops `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` and `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS` before it starts `upload-pack` (seen in the probe's trace).

The dispatch's three questions:

| Question | `--runner docker` | `--runner host` |
|---|---|---|
| Code execution on the host | None on git 2.47.3 (probed). Possible on a git whose `upload-pack` still lazy-fetches, and `fetch()` has no guard for that (finding 2). | No new access: the session already runs as the operator. It would only run after the exit checks (finding 2). |
| A file it could not reach, into the lead | Yes, for anything in a git repository on the host: objects, not arbitrary files (finding 1). | No gain: the same uid reads those repositories directly. |
| Corrupting the lead's objects or refs | No. Only the one fixed, non-forced refspec is written; `index-pack --strict` and the connectivity check ran; a shallow clone is rejected. The lead's `.git` is not mounted. | Accepted threat model: the session can write the lead's `.git` directly (`fetch.go:42-44`, SPEC-fyr-work lines 343-344). |

## Findings

- **[high / confidence: high]** `internal/work/fetch.go:78` (with `internal/sandbox/box.go:156`, `internal/sandbox/creds.go:147`) — docker runner only. `git fetch <clone>` runs `upload-pack` on the host against a `.git` the container wrote, and nothing validates that `.git` first.
  - **Why it crosses the boundary:** the container mounts only the clone, the sandbox home, the token and agy (`internal/sandbox/docker.go:102-105`). `upload-pack` runs in the host's filesystem, so paths the session writes into `.git` resolve there. The session can see its own absolute paths, so it can learn the home directory.
  - **Probed on git 2.47.3 with leadGit's exact options; each brought a third repository's content into the lead:** a `.git` file holding `gitdir:` (the repository needs a branch of the worker's name), and an ordinary `.git` with `objects/info/alternates` plus a ref that is a link to the other repository's ref file (no branch of that name needed).
  - **Checks that do not stop it:** both are a regular file or a link to a regular file. `Intact` looks at `app` only. Check d (`scanCreds`) reads the link's target and finds nothing. From the code, not run: a `.git` or `objects` link to a directory outside, and a dangling link, are caught by check d (`dirLink`/`outside`, `creds.go:94,153-156`), so only those variants are blocked, and by the credential check rather than by design.
  - **The way back to a session:** `fetch()` writes the ref, then `scope()` fails with `does not descend`; nothing in `internal/work` deletes the ref (grep for `branch`, `update-ref`, `-D`: none). `git clone --no-hardlinks` at the next run (`internal/sandbox/prepare.go:56`) copies the object directory, and after `remote remove origin` the object was still readable in the probe. A later session with network access can then send it out. No single session both reads and sends: it takes two runs on the same lead.
  - **Limit:** a git object store only. A plain file cannot be read this way, and content tracked in a repository can.
  - **Not run:** an end-to-end `fyr work --runner docker`. The git behaviour is probed; the walk through `collect` and check d is from reading the code.
  - **Remediation, smallest to strongest (a design choice for the operator):**
    - (a) A pre-fetch check through `os.Root`, after `ExitChecks`, stdlib only: `.git` is a directory, not a link or file; nothing under it is a link, FIFO or device; `objects/info/alternates`, `commondir` and `gitdir` are absent; `config` is regular. The container is gone by then, so the check has no race under docker. A failure takes a safety reason and keeps the sandbox.
    - (b) Stronger: never fetch from the clone's `.git`. Copy only regular files from `objects/` (links refused) and the one validated hex ref into a fresh bare repository the host made, then fetch from that. No clone config, alternates, gitdir or ref link is ever read, which also closes findings 2 and 3's config and ref routes.
    - (c) Alternative: build a bundle inside a second locked-down container, and let the host fetch only the bundle. This needs another docker step.
    - In every case, delete the fetched ref when the scope check fails on history that does not descend from the base. Alone that does not remove the objects: a local clone copies unreachable objects until gc.

- **[high / confidence: low]** `internal/work/fetch.go:76-87` (with `internal/trail/trail.go:116`, `internal/work/preflight.go`) — docker runner: possible code execution on the host on an older git. The repository already refuses to read a partial clone on a git below 2.44, because a missing object is fetched through the repository's own config (`trail.go:123-128`). `fetch()` has no such guard, and neither does `fyr work`'s preflight: the callers of `Readable`/`LazyFetchSafe` are `internal/check` and `internal/search`, and no git version floor exists in `internal/work`.
  - **Probed on 2.47.3, trace only, with a dead remote path and no program run:** `upload-pack` does not lazy-fetch by default or with `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, and it did start the lazy fetch with `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=0`. So the sink is live in this code path, and only git's default closes it.
  - **Uncertain:** no older git was tested, and which older releases carry that default by backport is unverified, which is why confidence is low. macOS is a stated operator platform, and `trail.go:249` itself names `2.39.5 (Apple Git-154)`.
  - **Under the host runner:** no new access, but the program would run after check c, d and e have looked.
  - **Remediation:** refuse `fyr work` when `trail.LazyFetchSafe()` is false (a new SPEC-fyr-work refusal, a D-row, a test taking both sides through the existing variable). Finding 1's option (b) removes the sink.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/work/fetch.go:45,78` (with `internal/work/worker.go:87-89`) — the fetch has no deadline and no memory bound, and it runs while the run-wide `collect` mutex is held.
  - **Probed on 2.47.3:** a FIFO at the clone's `.git/config` hung the fetch until `timeout` killed it (exit 124). A ref that is a link to `/dev/zero` made git read until it hit the probe's 600 MiB address-space cap ("Out of memory, realloc failed").
  - **Effect:** that memory is the host's, outside the container's 8g limit. A hang also stalls every other worker's collection for that run, because `exec.Command` takes no context and `ctx` never reaches `collect`. The clone's `pack.*` settings also apply to the host's `pack-objects` (from git's documentation, not probed).
  - **Checks that do not stop it:** check d skips a FIFO or device (`internal/sandbox/creds.go:165`), so both survive to the fetch.
  - **Both runners**, though the same uid on the host can exhaust the machine anyway; the container's limits are what this bypasses.
  - **Remediation:** run the fetch under a deadline with `Setpgid` and a group kill (a plain context kill leaves the `upload-pack` grandchild), with `cmd.WaitDelay` set, and make the lock wait respect `ctx`. Finding 1's check (a) or copy (b) removes the FIFO and device routes.

- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/eval/row.go:126` (with `internal/sandbox/session.go:150`, GUIDE-eval rows) — eval, host runner only. Step 13 runs each row's check as plain `bash` in the clone, and 10 GUIDE-eval rows run unhardened `git status` there (among them `scaffold`, `agent-dreamer`, `lane-reviewer`, `lane-bugs`, `requirements-check`). `git status` honours the clone's `core.fsmonitor`, so a row's agent that can write `.git/config` gets a program started outside its grants, before `ExitChecks`.
  - **Weight:** low. The `build-*` rows run what the agent wrote by design, and eval accepts the same uid. It matters only for a row whose grants are narrower than `command(*)`; 5 of the 10 lines name `wide`, and the per-row grant was not established.
  - **Remediation:** in those rows use `git -c core.fsmonitor=false status --porcelain`, or strike this with a D-row under eval's threat model.

## Checked

- **Secrets:** no secret in the reviewed code. Git's error text reaches notes through `Printable` (`fetch.go:81`) and holds paths, not content. `include.path` in the clone's config is read by the host's git but nothing surfaces its content (from git's behaviour, not probed).
- **Injection:** the clone path goes to git as an argument. The kickoff name reaches a refspec after `check-ref-format`. `upload-pack`'s shell line is git's own quoted form. Fixed refspec, no `+`. Drafts go through `os.Root` on both sides, refuse hard links and do not block on a FIFO. The trail blob is read through a capped reader.
- **Authz/authn, repository config in the clone:** on 2.47.3, with a nonexistent program name and trace only, `uploadpack.packObjectsHook`, `core.fsmonitor`, `core.sshCommand` and `core.alternateRefsCommand` set in the clone's config were not run, and a planted `.git/hooks` script did not run. Control: the same `packObjectsHook` key in protected (global) config was honoured, so the probe can detect it. Protocol options (`protocol.ext`, `core.sshCommand`) are reachable only through the lazy fetch of finding 2. `bundle-uri` and `packfile-uris` need the client's opt-in, which fetch does not give (from git's documentation, not probed).
- **Other host-side git calls on the clone:**
  - `branch()` (`worker.go:136`), `Clone`'s calls and `outsideCheckout` all run before the session.
  - `registerClone` (`cmd/fyr/eval_register.go:48`) runs after it: only `rev-parse`, hardened, and it refuses a repository outside the clone.
  - `After`, `ExitChecks` and `Intact` run no git. `countLines` uses `OpenRegular`; `Remove` makes only real directories writable.
  - Every other leadGit call reads the lead, whose `.git` is not mounted under docker. `trail.Dirty`'s reads of the lead run with the lead's config, an existing accepted gap under the host runner only (`fetch.go:56-57`).
- **Docker timing:** a dead container is checked before collection (`containersLeft`, a failure is a safety reason), so a pre-fetch validation of `.git` has no race under docker. Under the host runner a survivor could race it, which the threat model accepts.
- **Crypto:** nothing hand-rolled in this surface.
- **Dependencies:** none added. `govulncheck ./...`: exit 0, no vulnerabilities affecting the code; 1 in a required module, not reached (known-findings list: DEPLOY-local). `npm audit`: not applicable, no JS ecosystem in this surface.
- **GCP surface:** none in this surface.
- **Past failures:** `fyr search --refs` on fetch.go gives BUG-200 only (symlink or gitlink at scope check), a different path; 0 for after.go and box.go.
- **Probe hygiene:** probes ran on repositories made with `git init` under a fresh `mktemp -d` outside every checkout, with `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` set, each repository's git dir verified, and caller `GIT_*` variables unset; the directory is removed. A cleanup `pkill -f gitprobe` killed my own shell. The only other `upload-pack` processes listed were an unrelated ssh to github.com, which that pattern does not match.

## Not examined

- `internal/sandbox/mounts_linux.go` and `mounts_other.go`: untracked files that appeared in the tree during this review. I did not create them, they are not at HEAD, and they are unreviewed.
- An end-to-end `fyr work --runner docker` run: no container was started, and finding 1's path through `collect` is from the code.
- Any git older than 2.47.3, and git newer than it; every probed behaviour is for this version only.
- Colima/virtiofs ownership mapping on macOS, and whether `safe.directory` then changes anything.
- The metrics ingest's reads of a registered eval clone beyond `trail.Command`'s options and the `Readable` guard: `internal/metrics` and `internal/search/git_view.go` were listed, not read.
- Which grant each of the 10 `git status` rows has.
- `internal/work/work.go`, `preflight.go`, `reflog.go` beyond their git calls, and ctrl-C behaviour during a hung fetch.

## Outcome

Each finding verified by two refuters. S1 fixed (`Box.GitIntact`, item 61; `TestGitDirClean`, `TestRunSafetyKeepsSandbox`). S2 fixed narrowly, one verifier refuting (refusal 25, item 62; `TestRunRefusals`, `TestDockerNeedsLazyFetchSafe`). S3 fixed (`runBounded`, item 63; `TestRunBoundedKillsTheGroup`). S4 struck, both verifiers refuting (item 64, D25). Each fix's test fails without it (the phase's mutation table).

# Review — p12b-sandbox-failclosed   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: 22d8ecd..HEAD (2 commits, 34 files; code + docs lens)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

The code is sound: `go test -race -count=1` over sandbox, work, eval, dream and cmd/fyr passes, as do `go vet`, `gofmt -l` (empty) and the root and harness packages (agent lint, size pins). Nothing is broken at runtime. The worst problem is a stale restatement. `fyr work` now keeps and does not fetch a sandbox failed `sandbox exists` (`IntegrityReasons` feeds `safetyReasons`, `internal/work/worker.go:23`; PLAN D25 item 51 says so). `skills/work/SKILL.md:57` still lists the six older reasons, so the `work` skill's "a safety FAIL ends the loop" rule does not fire on it. The `SPEC-fyr-work` failure-modes row names the same five or six reasons. Two smaller docs gaps and two small coverage/consistency notes follow.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `skills/work/SKILL.md:57` and the `SPEC-fyr-work` failure-modes row beginning "credentials left, real config changed, processes left, sandbox replaced, sandbox write failed" (record line 312) — both enumerate the safety reasons. `sandbox exists` joined work's `safetyReasons` in this range (`internal/sandbox/box.go:67`, `internal/work/worker.go:23`). The skill's list is the loop's stop condition, so a worker failed `sandbox exists` is kept and unfetched by the verb but does not end the loop. The spec row also lacks `lead checkout changed` (older gap). Fix: add `sandbox exists` to the skill sentence and to the spec row (and `lead checkout changed` to the row). Ideally derive both from one grep of `safetyReasons`. The restatement grep for "safety reason" over `skills/ context/ agents/ README.md` found only these two.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `SPEC-fyr-work` refusal-order paragraph (record line 130) and its failure-modes row "a docker-mode refusal (12–20, and 22's no name)" (line 308); `TDD.md:192` — refusal 25 (`gitFloor`, `internal/work/preflight.go:120`) is stated only in its own entry (line 141). The ordering paragraph places 22, 23 and 24 but not 25, so the refusal count and order the spec gives is now short by one. The failure-modes row and `TDD.md:192` also leave out 24 and 25, which are docker-only and are made before or among the "13 to 20". Fix: add 25 to the order paragraph, the failure-modes row and TDD T18's refusal list.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `TDD.md` T17/T18 (lines 168, 188-194) — no mention of `Box.GitIntact`, the mount check in `Intact` (`internal/sandbox/mounts_linux.go`, `MountsChecked`), the fetch deadline (`runBounded`, `fetchLimit`), or `IntegrityReasons`/`Compromised`. `SPEC-fyr-work` line 195 and `SPEC-fyr-eval` § Safety checks do state them, so only the TDD copy is stale. A grep of `TDD.md SDD.md README.md` for `GitIntact|mountinfo|mountsUnder|fetchLimit|gitFloor|runBounded` returns nothing.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `agents/reviewer/agent.md:78` vs `agents/security/agent.md:65` — the same probe rule is stated twice with different strength. The reviewer's copy gives `mktemp -d` plus `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` plus `git -C`, but omits the `rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` check and the "unset the caller's `GIT_*`" step that the security copy carries (and says caused a past escape: with `GIT_DIR` exported an init exits 0 and creates nothing, and discovery, hence the ceiling, is bypassed). BUG-204's failure can therefore still occur through the reviewer's wording. Separately, both agents now permit `mktemp -d` outside `.agents/scratch/`, while `context/AGENTS.md:57` (the global Hard rule) and `agents/verifier/agent.md:72` ("the global scratch rule applies to you too") say "never `/tmp`" with no exception (the BUG-019 class: a definition instructing against the global rule). Fix: make the reviewer's text the same as the security text, and name the exception in the global scratch rule, or state in D-row that the agent-level carve-out is intended.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/sandbox/failclosed_test.go:14-41` — coverage gap named by none of D25 item 49. The stated residue ("a permission refusal stays tolerated, `ssh-agent` is non-dumpable") has no test, so removing `fs.ErrPermission` from `procGone` (`procs_linux.go`) would fail every real run without any test failing; and step 12's CLI-log arm of `Box.count`, and its machine-error arm (`sandbox write failed` before a session), are untested (only the `err.txt` arm is). `TestIntegrityReasons`'s second loop re-asserts the constant against itself (a pin, not a behaviour test).
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/sandbox/gitdir.go:340-376` — `GitIntact` bounds only `HEAD` and loose refs (4096 bytes). A regular `config`, `packed-refs` or `shallow` of arbitrary size passes, and `fetchLimit` bounds the fetch's time, not the host's upload-pack memory. Speculative (depends on git's parsing of a huge file); it matters only under `--runner docker` with a hostile worker. The spec already lists the rest of `config` as "not checked" for command sinks only. Fix if real: add a size cap on `config`, `packed-refs` and `shallow`, or accept and name it in the spec's residue.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. `slices` import removed from `cmd/fyr/eval.go` (compiles); `ReasonX` eval aliases are still used by `cause.go`. No orphan helpers: `Compromised`, `IntegrityReasons`, `GitIntact`, `mountsUnder`, `gitFloor`, `runBounded` all have callers.
2. Flow tracing — pass. Traced `leftoverProcs` error -> `ExitChecks` -> `ReasonProcs`; `countLines` error -> `Box.count` -> `fileFailed` -> `replaced`/`write`; `Intact` mount error -> `replaced` (guard keeps data on error); `collect` -> `Intact && GitIntact` -> `unsafe()` -> `remove()` keeps the sandbox; `gitFloor` before `dockerRefusals`, matching "after refusal 23, before 13". The old and new ingest skip sets are identical (four reasons). One residual noted in D25 and accepted: `After` still returns true on a failed step 12 read.
3. Standards conformance — fail on restatements (findings 1-3, 4); Go idiom is fine (errors wrapped or noted, no discarded errors, fail-closed guards).
4. Directory layout — pass. New files sit in `internal/sandbox` and `internal/work` beside their tests; fixtures under `internal/dream/testdata/agy-1.4.12/` and scrubbed (no home path, mail address or token found by grep).
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only; no new dependency; no auth/crypto/session code touched.
6. Decoupling — pass. One shared reason list replaces two hand-kept lists; the `mounts_*`/`procs_*` build-tag split keeps the platform seam; `gitFloor`'s `lazyFetchSafe` variable is a test seam consumed in its package.

## Not examined
- Runtime behaviour on a real mount (D25 itself says no real FUSE mount was made) and `fyr work --runner docker` over a planted `.git` (not run by the author either): not reproduced.
- The `writes-outside-clone` `GUIDE-eval` row text and the testing record it cites; I read only `TestSuiteHarness`'s `want`. Behavioural agent runs for the two changed agent definitions (P13's).
- `internal/sandbox/session.go`, `docker.go`, `prepare.go` and the unchanged parts of `After`/`Remove` beyond the call sites above; the full test run of the root package (only `.` and `./internal/harness` were run).
- Scratch note: before reading the instructions to keep dumps elsewhere I wrote `.agents/scratch/agents/spec-eval.txt` and `spec-work.txt` (gitignored copies of the two SPEC records) and may have overwritten earlier copies of the same names; no tracked file was touched.

## Outcome

Each finding verified by a refuter. F1, F2, F3 fixed (the skill's and the spec's reason lists, refusal 25 in the order paragraph and TDD, the security copy's probe wording; the carve-out recorded in D25). F4 refuted (the tolerance is pinned by the real /proc runs). F5 fixed as the config bound, widened in round 2.

# Review — p12b-round-2-fixes   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: 98f090f..HEAD (fixes only)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

No code defect found. The fixes do what they claim, and `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/sandbox ./internal/work` passes. Both new fetch pins fail when their fix is reverted (mutation on a scratch copy; each mutant compiled and the named test failed). The worst problem is documentation. The stored `SPEC-fyr-work` step 6 contradicts itself and the code: its fetch command line still shows `<clone>` and omits `--upload-pack "git upload-pack --strict"`, and its intact clause still reads "no file system mounted at or under it".

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high]** `SPEC-fyr-work` record, step 6 (paragraph beginning "The fetch runs only when…", `.agents/trail.jsonl`) — two stale restatements of claims this diff changed. (a) It ends "The fetch is `git -c fetch.fsckObjects=true fetch -q --no-tags --no-recurse-submodules --no-write-fetch-head <clone> refs/heads/work/<name>:…`". `internal/work/fetch.go` now runs `--upload-pack "git upload-pack --strict" <clone>/.git`, and the very next paragraph says so. (b) "the sandbox is intact (no file system mounted at or under it, PLAN.md item 50)" omits the new mounted-above check. `SPEC-fyr-eval` was updated for (b). Fix: edit the record: put the real command line in (a) and add "or whose mount changed" to (b).
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/work/fetch.go:107-121` — the group kill after `Wait` is removed because "the id may be another's". On Linux a pid cannot be recycled while it is still a process-group id, and a surviving group member (a grandchild left by `upload-pack`/`index-pack`) is the only case the kill ever served. The kill was therefore safe whenever it mattered, and it now leaves such a child running if `git fetch` exits early or `Wait` returns on `WaitDelay`. The residual risk (a recycled pid that is itself a group leader) is also real but much narrower, and the timeout-timer path has it already. No test covers either side. Decide deliberately; I do not insist.

## Evidence
- `TestRunNoFallbackToTheTopLevel`: with both the `.git` path and `--strict` reverted, `toplevel-repo` fails. `nested-repo` passes in that mutant, so it is pinned only by `--strict` alone: with only `--strict` reverted it fails (`Head` was fetched). Both fixes are therefore pinned, each by its own subtest.
- `TestCappedOutput` fails without the cap (1,000,000 bytes returned against 65,536 kept). `cappedWriter` has a named buffer, so `io.Copy` cannot bypass `Write`. Stdout and stderr share one writer value, so exec serialises the writes.
- `TestMountID` separates `>=` from `>` (ids 2 and 3 both on `/s`) and component-wise prefixes (`/s/a` against `/s/ab`). The NBSP rows in `TestMountsUnder` fail under `strings.Fields`. `TestIntactParentMount` records the id at `openSandbox` and then changes it, and it asserts the "above" note.
- Roots in `openSandbox`, `Intact` and `mountIDs` are all the resolved paths, so the map keys agree. A non-Linux build records a nil map and never fails. An unreadable table now fails setup closed.
- `MountsChecked`: no reference remains. `IntegrityReasons` holds `sandbox exists`, which `SKILL.md` now names, and work's `safetyReasons` is built from it. `agents/reviewer/agent.md`: I ran its claim that `git init` with `GIT_DIR` exported exits 0 and creates nothing in the target. It does, in an `mktemp` repo, under `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass: `MountsChecked` removed with no readers left; the new helpers all have callers.
2. Flow tracing — pass: mount ids are recorded and compared on matching keys, failures close, tests can fail (shown by mutation). The post-`Wait` kill removal is the one open item (low finding).
3. Standards conformance — fail on one restatement: the `SPEC-fyr-work` step 6 fetch command line and the "at or under" clause. `TDD.md`, `SPEC-fyr-eval`, `PLAN.md` and `skills/work/SKILL.md` agree with the code.
4. Directory layout — pass: no new files outside the existing packages.
5. Simplicity — pass: stdlib only, no crypto.
6. Decoupling — pass: the mount parsing stays inside `internal/sandbox`, the fetch change inside `internal/work`.
