title: Security review: PLAN.md P12b, round 1
body:
# Security review — p12b-sandbox-integrity   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: 22d8ecd..98f090f

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

`GitIntact` can be walked around, and that re-opens item 61 (S1) under `--runner docker`. It inspects `<clone>/.git`, but `git fetch <clone>` lets upload-pack choose the repository. When `.git` is a directory that is not a valid repository, upload-pack falls back to the clone's top level as a bare repository, and `gitDirProblem` never looks there. A session can create that shape with ordinary writes inside its own mount. Probed on git 2.47.3 with leadGit's exact options: `gitDirProblem` returned "", the fetch exited 0, and a third repository's commit and blob landed in the lead through an alternates file at the top of the clone. Separately, `mountsUnder` misses a mount above the watched roots (host runner only). The fetch deadline, refusal 25, the fail-closed `/proc` reads, the fixtures and eval's ingest are sound.

## Findings

- **[high / confidence: high]** `internal/sandbox/gitdir.go:27`, `internal/work/fetch.go:127` — **`GitIntact` checks a path git does not have to use.** upload-pack's repository lookup (non-strict `enter_repo`) tries `<path>/.git`, then `<path>` itself, and uses `.git` only if it passes `is_git_directory`. A `.git` with its `HEAD` removed is still a directory holding only regular files with none of the foreign names, so `gitDirProblem` returns "". upload-pack then serves `<clone>/HEAD`, `<clone>/refs` and `<clone>/objects`, which are ordinary worktree paths the walk never visits. Everything the fix refuses in `.git` is unchecked there: `objects/info/alternates`, `commondir`, linked refs, FIFOs.
  - Why it is exploitable in principle: under docker the session writes those files freely, and the host's upload-pack reads them as the operator. Foreign objects reach the lead at `fetch`, before `scope` runs. A branch that fails the descent check stays in the lead, and D25 accepts that only because "with `GitIntact` it can no longer hold a foreign object", which is now false. A later run clones the lead into a container that has network access.
  - Evidence: scratch probe. Must-fail side: a valid `.git` with the same top-level files gave `couldn't find remote ref`, nothing fetched. Failing side: `HEAD` removed from `.git`, `gitDirProblem=""`, `fetch rc=0`, `cat-file -t` changed from not found to `commit`, and the foreign blob read back. The probe used an alternates file and a plain ref holding a known id. The linked-ref form of S1 was not re-run; it is the same read path.
  - Remediation: make git take the path literally. `fetch --upload-pack 'git upload-pack --strict' … <clone>/.git`, with `<clone>/.git` as the source, disables the lookup. Probed both ways: strict on the invalid `.git` gave rc=128 and no objects; strict on a valid `.git` gave rc=0 and the ref. Do not rely on a `HEAD`-exists check in `gitDirProblem` alone: `is_git_directory` also rejects a malformed `HEAD` and unsearchable `objects` or `refs` directories, so a partial mirror leaves the fallback open. Keep a test that fails without the fix: `.git` without `HEAD`, bare shape at the clone's top. Correct D25's sentence and the `SPEC-fyr-work` step 6 wording in the same change.

- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `internal/sandbox/mounts_linux.go:40-44`, `internal/sandbox/box.go:190` — **`mountsUnder` lists mounts at or below the roots, never above them.** `within(mp, r)` is false for a mount point that is a parent of `dir`, such as the stamp directory or `~/sandbox/fyr-work`. A file system mounted there hides the whole tree, and `Intact` sees nothing wrong: `Lstat` and `EvalSymlinks` go through the mount and resolve to the same strings when it serves the same layout. This is exactly what item 50 set out to catch ("their EvalSymlinks and os.Root see nothing of a mount"). Those parents are owned by the operator, so `fusermount3` should accept them.
  - Scope: the host runner only, since a container reaches no host path above its mounts. The FUSE server is a surviving process and must also evade check e, which is easy (see the check e finding below). Confidence is medium because the code path is certain (probe: `mountsUnder /proc/self/fd` returns nothing although `/proc` is a mount above it), but no real FUSE mount was made here, and D25 says none was made either.
  - Remediation: at `Make`, record for each root the mount it lives on, meaning the longest-prefix mountinfo line's mount ID. In `Intact`, require that ID to be unchanged as well as nothing at or below the root. Use a stack-aware read: the last matching line wins. Stdlib only. Add a fixture test for a new line at a parent path.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/sandbox/mounts_linux.go:35` — **`strings.Fields` splits on Unicode spaces the kernel does not escape.** The kernel escapes only space, tab, newline and backslash, so U+00A0 or U+0085 reaches the parser raw and shifts or cuts `f[4]`.
  - Two false passes in fixture probes: a `root` field holding U+00A0 makes `f[4]` the tail of that field, so a mount under the sandbox gave `found=[]`; a watched root whose own path holds U+00A0 also gave `found=[]`. The must-pass fixture without U+00A0 found the mount.
  - Reach: the agent does not obviously control either form, since a FUSE mount's root field is `/` and `--home` is the operator's.
  - Remediation: `strings.Split(l, " ")`, with a `TestMountsUnder` row for each form.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/sandbox/gitdir.go:25`, PLAN.md D25 item 49 — **"nothing of the session is left to race it" holds only under docker.**
  - Under docker it holds: `containersLeft` fails closed and removes the container before `After`, and neither `dir` nor the lead is mounted.
  - Under the host runner, check e sees only a process with cwd or exe under the roots or exactly `HOME=<sb>`. A child that changes directory, drops `HOME` and runs a system binary is invisible with no privilege, so D25's "an agent that makes itself non-dumpable" understates the residue. A process whose leader thread exited also reads as a zombie (by kernel behaviour, not probed).
  - Such a survivor, or an agent of another concurrent run under the same uid (`SPEC-fyr-work` names this for host runs only), can change the clone after `GitIntact` even in a docker run. It holds operator rights anyway, so no privilege is gained and the accepted threat model stands. The claims are what is too strong.
  - Remediation: reword the comment and D25 to say this is true for the container's own processes only, and that a process on the host is outside the check. Optionally extend the SPEC limit to docker runs.

- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/work/fetch.go:84-90`, `internal/sandbox/gitdir.go:59-68` — **S3's "fills host memory" is bounded in time, not in size.** `runBounded`'s `bytes.Buffer` has no cap. `maxRefFile` covers only `HEAD` and `refs/`, not `packed-refs` or `config`. A pack in `.git/objects` can declare a very large tree or commit that `index-pack` with `fetch.fsckObjects` holds in memory, and 10 minutes of transfer can also fill the lead's disk. `.git/config` can `include` a FIFO in the worktree, which the walk does not see; the deadline stops that hang, but it holds the collect lock for up to 10 minutes. None of this was probed; the impact is denial of service only.
  - Remediation: have the walk sum regular-file sizes against a cap and refuse above it; cap the captured output with a limited writer; extend the size check to `packed-refs` and `config`.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/sandbox/mounts_other.go:9`, `internal/sandbox/mounts_linux.go:12` — **The mount check is silently absent off Linux.** `MountsChecked` has no caller outside its two definitions (grep of `internal` and `cmd`), while `ProcsChecked` prints a line and reaches `registerClone`. On macOS, a supported machine, `Intact` claims a check that never runs, and nothing says so.
  - Remediation: print one line as `procs_other.go` does, or remove the constant and state the gap in the SPEC.

- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/work/fetch.go:101` — **The group kill after `Wait` reaches for a reaped id.** `docker.go:168` and `docker.go:231` deliberately avoid this ("its id may be another's by now"). In practice it needs a pid wrap inside microseconds, and it can only hit this uid's group.
  - Remediation: accept this with a comment, or kill only while a group member remains.

## Checked

- **Dispatch questions**
  - TOCTOU with a survivor: see the fourth finding. Docker is sound, host is accepted but overclaimed.
  - Nested `.git`, `worktrees/`: `worktrees/*/commondir` and `gitdir` and `modules/*/` are not refused, and are inert for a fetch from the fixed path; they matter only through the fallback in the first finding (`<clone>/commondir` is unchecked there). Read, not probed.
  - `packed-refs`: holds ids only, needs objects already reachable, and links in `.git` are refused; the only gap is size.
  - Any symlink, FIFO, socket or device anywhere in `.git` is refused, because `WalkDir` reports links as links.
  - `mountsUnder`: optional fields follow `f[4]`, so they cannot shift it. The escape handling is right (`i+3 < len(s)` bounds the slice). `EvalSymlinks` output matches the kernel's path form, and a private-namespace mount is correctly out of scope.
  - False fails: `leftoverProcs` run unchanged over this machine's real `/proc` with 346 zombies, kernel threads and a live `unshare -Urm` process gave `found=[] err=<nil>`. Docker's bind mounts sit in the container's namespace, so not in fyr's table (by reading; no docker run here). `countLines`' 16 MiB line limit and `count`'s `ErrNotExist` rule have no normal-run trigger that I found.
  - `gitDirProblem` on a real clone: `--no-hardlinks` clone, no alternates, returned "" in the probe.
- **Secrets**: `internal/dream/testdata/agy-1.4.12/*` has no token, key, email or real username. `config.json`'s values are all defaults; `gcp` and `customModelsConfig` are empty. The home is rewritten to `/sandbox/...` and to a split `file:///home/op/...` in `tool.jsonl`'s deltas; `op` is not an account on dave (`getent` empty, real user differs), so no private path. Conversation UUIDs are harmless. The `.agents/trail.jsonl` diff has no token shape; its only hits are `/home/kesokaj/...` paths in the `TEST-2026-10-31-2059` record, and that login is already public as the module path's owner (`github.com/kesokaj/fyr`).
- **Injection**: `session.go` is unchanged in the range. It uses `exec` with no shell, the prompt is one argv element, and the `--model` value is checked by `modelRe` in `kickoff.go`. `runBounded` and `leadGit` argv are constants plus a validated branch. `Printable` covers `.git` notes. No `--add-dir` was added, as D25 says.
- **Authz-authn**: `IntegrityReasons` is cloned before work's append, and eval's reason constants alias sandbox's, so `Compromised` keeps eval's four. Work now also counts `sandbox exists`. Refusal 25 is docker-only, fails closed on an unreadable version, and runs before `dockerRefusals`.
- **Crypto**: none touched; nothing hand-rolled.
- **Dependencies**: `go.mod` and `go.sum` unchanged. `govulncheck ./...` ran: 0 vulnerabilities in called code, 1 in a required module that is not called. `npm audit`: no `package.json` at the root, `web/` or `ui/`, so not run.
- **GCP surface**: none touched.
- `fyr search --refs` per changed file: BUG-200 (fetch.go), BUG-188 and BUG-194 (eval.go), none repeated here.

## Not examined

- `internal/work/drafts.go`, `internal/eval/run.go`, `internal/metrics` ingest: read only where they cross the diff.
- The `--upload-pack` remediation through `leadGit` itself: probed with a plain `git fetch`, not with leadGit's full option set.
- A crafted `multi-pack-index` naming a pack outside the clone: a possible second route to foreign objects, not probed, and it would need the foreign pack's contents in advance.
- A case-insensitive file system: on APFS `Head` or `REFS/` would escape `rel == "HEAD"`'s size bound; links and FIFOs are still refused. Not run; no macOS here.
- A real FUSE mount, a real docker run, and an end-to-end `fyr work` over a planted clone: the probes copied `gitDirProblem`, `leftoverProcs` and `mountsUnder` unchanged into a scratch program.
- Probe directory, left in place: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-kesokaj-workspace-styrman-harness/e493ac22-47c1-45fd-800b-97170615035d/scratchpad/tmp.2VAHCFUhDJ

## Outcome

Each finding verified by a refuter; none refuted. S1 fixed (the fetch names `<clone>/.git` with `upload-pack --strict`; `TestRunNoFallbackToTheTopLevel`). S2 fixed (the mounts above each root recorded; `TestIntactParentMount`). S3 fixed (`strings.Split`; `TestMountsUnder`). S4 fixed (the comment, D25, both specs). S5 partly fixed (output cap, `config` bound; index-pack memory stated). S6 fixed (constant removed). S7 accepted in round 2 (D25).

title: Security review: PLAN.md P12b, round 2 over the fixes
body:
# Security review — p12b-round-2-fixes   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: 98f090f..38ef79a

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Worst problem: the new `maxConfigFile` bound does not bound what git reads from `config` on the host. Under the docker runner a worker's `.git/config` of about 1.5 KB, with 40 `include.path` lines naming one 16 MiB file in the clone, made `git upload-pack --strict` hit out-of-memory under a 300 MB address-space cap, and it completed under a 1.5 GB cap. Each include stores its own copy of the value, so memory scales with the number of include lines, and 1 MiB of config holds tens of thousands. The SPEC names the FIFO hang as the include's residue and says "Time is bounded and memory is not" of `index-pack` only, at "each file being at most check d's 64 MiB". Neither covers this: the deadline bounds time, not this memory, and the include count multiplies past 64 MiB. Check d also misses files under a lockfile-backed `node_modules`.

The four questions of the dispatch:

1. **`<clone>/.git` with `git upload-pack --strict` through `--upload-pack`: holds on git 2.47.3.** The trace shows `/bin/sh -c "git upload-pack --strict '<path>'"`, the path quoted by git. A fetch succeeded on protocols 0, 1 and 2 and with a space and a single quote in the path. The two fallbacks are closed: `.git/HEAD` removed with a repository at the top level gave rc 128, and a nested `.git/.git` gave rc 128 with `--strict` and rc 0 without it. The string is a constant; nothing external reaches the shell except the path, which git quotes. One limit: `--strict` still follows a `.git` FILE (rc 0). Only `GitIntact`'s Lstat stops that, before the fetch (F3).
2. **False fail on a normal worker from this diff: none found.** All rc 0: a lead that is a linked worktree, a clone holding its own linked worktree (`.git/worktrees/x/{gitdir,commondir}` are nested, so `foreignNames` misses them correctly), a `.git/modules/s/gitdir`. The clone is `git clone --no-hardlinks`, so it has neither alternates nor a `.git` file. A different owner fails the same way in the old form and the new one (both rc 128), and docker runs `--user` as the same uid. One false fail outside the diff: F5.
3. **`Intact`'s id compare: no false fail found; one miss.** In a private user namespace on kernel 6.12: a bind remount to read-only and a propagation change kept the id, a mount elsewhere and a mount under the covering mount left the covering point's line unchanged, and a stacked mount listed last, matching "last of equals". A bind at a root's path already fails `mountsUnder`. A mount over an ANCESTOR of the covering mount goes unseen (F2).
4. **Capped writer: safe.** `Stdout` and `Stderr` are the same pointer, so `childStderr` reuses the fd and one goroutine writes. `cappedWriter` has no `ReadFrom`, so `io.Copy` goes through `Write`. `Wait` receives from `goroutineErr` after closing the pipes on the WaitDelay path, so reading `kept` afterwards does not race. A scratch copy under `go run -race` with stdout and stderr interleaved kept exactly 65536 bytes with no race report; a child outliving the leader, deadline and setsid cases all returned on time. See F4 for the removed kill.

## Findings

- **F1 [medium / confidence: high]** `internal/sandbox/gitdir.go:70` (with `internal/sandbox/gitdir.go:16`, `internal/work/fetch.go:146`) — the 1 MiB `config` bound is bypassed by `include.path`, and `config.worktree` has no bound at all. Upload-pack on the host follows includes from the agent's `.git/config` to any path, the unwalked clone top level included. Measured in a throwaway repo, each under an address-space cap: a sparse 1 GiB target (4 KB allocated) gave out-of-memory at 300 MB; 40 includes of a real 16 MiB file from a 1.5 KB config gave out-of-memory at 300 MB and passed at 1.5 GB, so copies accumulate per include; a 1 GiB `config.worktree` with `extensions.worktreeConfig` gave out-of-memory at 300 MB. Check d (`internal/sandbox/creds.go:177`) would flag a target over 64 MiB, but the include count multiplies below that, and files under a lockfile-backed `node_modules` skip its size check (`internal/sandbox/creds.go:93`, `:169`). `fetchLimit` bounds the time, and the host's memory can go first. This is the docker runner's boundary: the container's limits do not apply to the host's upload-pack, and a host session is the operator's uid already. The docs do not state it: `SPEC-fyr-work` names the FIFO hang for an include and bounds memory at "each file ... 64 MiB"; PLAN.md's "What stays bounded only in time" names the same two. Remediation: after the size check, run `git config --file <config> --no-includes --name-only --list` (probed: it lists `include.path` without following it; stdlib `os/exec`, no dependency) with `WithoutGit`'s env, and refuse `include.*`, `includeif.*` and `extensions.worktreeconfig`, failing closed on an error. A plain clone has none of them, so a normal worker is untouched. A test with a config of many includes must fail without the fix, and the SPEC's residue line changes with it.

- **F2 [low / confidence: high]** `internal/sandbox/mounts_linux.go:50` (`internal/sandbox/box.go:209`) — `mountIDs` takes the longest mount point above a root, so a mount over an ancestor of that point changes nothing it reads. Observed: with `a` (id 570) and `a/b` (id 572), a new mount at `a` (id 573) hid `a/b`, while the table still listed `a/b` at 572, which remains the longest prefix for `a/b/s`. The paths then resolve through the new file system and `Intact` passes, which is finding S2's outcome on a narrower layout: the sandbox must lie under a separate mount, and the agent must be able to mount on a directory above it, as `fusermount` allows on a host session. `TestIntactParentMount`'s table has only `/`, so it does not reach this layout. Remediation: record every mount above each root, as ordered (id, point) pairs, and compare the whole list; or hold each root open and compare with `os.SameFile` against `os.Stat(path)`, which asks the file system instead of the table and needs no mount semantics.

- **F3 [low / confidence: high]** `internal/sandbox/gitdir.go:31` (`internal/work/fetch.go:141`) — the comment claims more than the arguments do: "The fetch's own arguments are what keep upload-pack to this .git". They remove the lookup fallbacks and nothing else. `--strict` followed a `.git` file to another directory (rc 0), and anything written after `GitIntact` (an alternates file, a swapped `.git`) is honoured. The window the same comment names, a process that passed check e or a concurrent run of this uid, stays open whatever the arguments are. Remediation: reword both comments to say the arguments close the fallback lookup only, and keep the race as a stated residue in `SPEC-fyr-work`; this is a comment change, and no code here closes the race.

- **F4 [low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/fetch.go:101` — removing the kill after `Wait` closes the pid-reuse risk but leaves a group member running when the leader exits and `Wait` returns `ErrWaitDelay` before the deadline, since `t.Stop()` then cancels the only kill. The scratch copy confirmed the return path (`ErrWaitDelay` at the delay; a child that keeps writing dies on the closed pipe). A child that does not write is left alive by construction; I did not observe one directly. Reachable only when upload-pack or its child stalls after the client exits, and the fetch fails closed, so the cost is a stray process, not a wrong result. Remediation: on `errors.Is(err, exec.ErrWaitDelay)` send `syscall.Kill(-pgid, SIGKILL)`: a holder of the pipe in the group keeps that pgid allocated, so the reuse the comment guards against does not apply on this path.

- **F5 [low / confidence: medium]** `internal/sandbox/gitdir.go:62` (not changed in this range) — a false fail on a normal worker: `gitDirProblem` refuses any non-regular file, and `git clone` copies symlinks from a template directory. Probed: a symlinked hook in `init.templateDir` landed as a symlink in the clone's `.git/hooks`. The clone at `internal/sandbox/prepare.go:56` runs with the operator's environment, so an operator with such a template would see every worker fail `sandbox replaced`, a safety FAIL that stops the `work` loop. Remediation: add `--template=` to that clone (empty, so no hooks are copied), or take a listing of `.git` at clone time and refuse only what is new.

## Checked

- Secrets: the range's diff has none; the one grep hit is `?token=<T>` placeholder text in `SPEC-fyr-serve`.
- Injection: the `--upload-pack` string is a constant, the path reaches `sh` quoted by git (space and single-quote path probed), and the fetch's output reaches `Note` through `Printable`. `strings.Split(l, " ")` in `readMounts` keeps the mount point at field 4, as the kernel escapes an ASCII space; `TestMountsUnder` pins the NBSP case.
- Authz-authn: nothing in this range touches them.
- Crypto: nothing in this range touches it.
- Dependencies: no `go.mod` or `go.sum` change. `govulncheck ./...`: "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities", with 1 in a required module, not called; not compared against the known list in `DEPLOY-local`. `npm audit`: not run, no `package.json` in this range.
- GCP surface: nothing in this range touches it.
- Tests run from a clean tree, with `-race`: `go test ./internal/sandbox -run 'TestMountID|TestMountsUnder|TestIntact|TestGitDir'` and `./internal/work -run 'TestRunNoFallback|TestCappedOutput|TestSafetyReasons'`, both ok. `git status --short --untracked-files=all` was empty afterwards.
- Non-Linux: `mountIDs` returns nil, so `b.mounts` is nil and the compare loop does not run: no false fail there, and no mount check, which the specs state.
- Probes ran under `mktemp -d` in the session scratchpad with `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` set to that directory and `GIT_*` unset; the mount probes ran in `unshare -Urm`.
- Disclosure of my own run: `fyr search --refs` ran without `--home`, as this agent's definition writes it, while this repo's `AGENTS.md` asks for `--home` on `search`, so it may have touched the real `~/.config/fyr`. One `fyr record get` carried `--home .agents/scratch/secreview`, which may have left that directory under the gitignored scratch.

## Not examined

- A real docker runner session and a real FUSE mount on the host namespace: the mount cases ran with tmpfs and binds in a private namespace, and F2's `fusermount` route is from reading, not a run.
- Any git other than 2.47.3, and any kernel other than 6.12.113; the "last of equals" order was seen on this kernel only.
- `/proc/self/mountinfo` read while mounts change concurrently.
- Whether a check d finding on a large file always reaches `w.unsafe()`: I read the scan, not its path to the fail reason.
- Memory or time through a real `git fetch`: F1's figures come from `git upload-pack --strict --advertise-refs` under `ulimit -v`.
- Other unbounded files under `.git` (`packed-refs`, `shallow`, `info/*`): not probed.
- `.agents/trail.jsonl` and `PLAN.md`: only the changed lines' first 420 characters, plus text searches of `SPEC-fyr-work`; the specs were not read whole.
- `TDD.md`, `agents/reviewer/agent.md`, `skills/work/SKILL.md`: read as diff lines cut at 900 characters; `TDD.md`'s long reordered line was not read to its end.
- The full test suite: only the targeted tests above ran.

## Outcome

F1 fixed (`configProblem` refuses include.*, includeif.*, extensions.worktreeConfig). F2 fixed (the whole chain above each root; `TestMountChains`, `TestIntactParentMount`). F3 fixed (both comments, the spec's residue). F4 fixed with the reviewer's F2. F5 fixed (`git clone --template=`; `TestCloneTakesNoTemplate`). No third round (D25).

title: Review — v5.5.0 gate, code
body:
# Review — release v5.0.0..9298b9b   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: v5.0.0..9298b9b

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE

Nothing broken was found. The fixes of 38ef79a..37756a3, which no review had read, are sound: config includes refused, the chain of mounts above each root, the group kill after Wait, the 64 KiB output cap, the fetch naming `<clone>/.git` with `upload-pack --strict`, and `git clone --template=`. I mutated each one in a `git archive` copy under `.agents/scratch/workers-review-mut`. Every mutant compiled and a named test failed, so each fix is pinned by a test that can fail. The rest of the Go diff read (sandbox, work, eval, cmd/fyr, metrics core, search, check/trailhistory, trail dirty, harness repo) has no concrete correctness, security or rule failure. The reviewed range is large, and the unread parts are named under "Not examined".

## Findings
None at the bar (a bug, a missing error path, a race, an injection, a broken invariant, a missing test, a rule violation).

Not findings, recorded so a later reader does not rediscover them:
- `internal/sandbox/procs_linux.go` `procGone` treats EACCES on `/proc/<pid>/{cwd,exe,environ}` as "not readable by design". A same-uid process that sets `PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0` is therefore not seen by check e. This is stated residue in PLAN.md item 49 and `SPEC-fyr-eval` § Safety checks, and the old code ignored every read error, so it is not a regression.
- `internal/work/fetch.go` `runBounded`: `syscall.Kill(-pgid, SIGKILL)` after `Wait` could in theory hit a recycled group id once the leader is reaped and no member is left. This needs a new process to take that pid and make itself a group leader inside microseconds; `models.go` does the same, and PLAN.md "What stays bounded only in time" accepts the shape.
- `Intact`'s above-chain comparison fails closed if an unrelated mount appears on an ancestor of the sandbox during a run (autofs, for example). That costs availability only, and the failure goes in the safe direction.

## Evidence (what I ran, in a copy, never in the checkout)
- Copy: `git archive 9298b9b` into `.agents/scratch/workers-review-mut`, HOME pointed into it. No fyr verb wrote `~/.config/fyr`. `fyr search`/`record` reads carried `--home .agents/scratch/workers`.
- Baseline: `TestCloneTakesNoTemplate|TestGitDirClean|TestMountChains|TestIntactParentMount|TestRunNoFallback*|TestCappedOutput|TestRunBounded*` pass.
- Mutations, each unique in its file before the edit, restored from a saved copy afterwards:
  - M1 `--template=` removed: `TestCloneTakesNoTemplate` FAILS, as expected (reasons `sandbox replaced`, hooks/pre-commit not a regular file).
  - M2 `--strict` removed: `TestRunNoFallbackToTheTopLevel/nested-repo` FAILS (the nested repository was fetched).
  - M2b first attempt (path to the clone) did not compile (unused import); it is no evidence. M2c (path `filepath.Clean(App())`, `--strict` kept) compiled and `toplevel-repo` FAILS. Each half of the fix is pinned by its own case.
  - M3 post-Wait group kill removed: `TestRunBoundedLeavesNoGroup` FAILS ("the child outlived the fetch").
  - M4 mount-chain comparison disabled: `TestIntactParentMount` FAILS in all three assertions.
  - M5 `configProblem` call removed: `TestGitDirClean` cases include, conditional include, worktreeConfig and "a config git cannot read" FAIL.
  - After the restores the same set passes again.
- `gofmt -l cmd internal` empty and `go vet ./...` clean on the copy.
- `go test` on the copy: internal/metrics, check, trail, harness, search, dream pass. internal/eval fails only `TestRunRealFyrBaseline`, because the copy has no `.git` (the install log then does not name a checkout). The test passes in the real checkout (HOME in scratch). That is a copy artifact, not a defect.
- Restatements: `--pids-limit 1024`, the limits and the network agree between `internal/sandbox/docker.go`, `docker_test.go`, `TDD.md:175` and ADR-083. `skills/work/SKILL.md` names `sandbox exists` as PLAN item 51 says. `MountsChecked` has no remaining reader (only PLAN.md:396 mentions it). TDD.md's Integrity and fetch bullets match the code.
- Untracked `.claude/` in the checkout predates this review (mtime 17:07 and earlier) and is not part of the range.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. `MountsChecked` was removed with its last reader; `specCommit`, `LastRetro`, `evalBody` and the records table are gone with their callers. No orphan found.
2. Flow tracing — pass. `collect` runs `Intact`, then `GitIntact`, then `leadUnchanged` (reflog), then `fetch` via `runBounded`. `openSandbox` records the mount chains and `Intact` compares them (a non-Linux nil map is vacuous). `ReasonWrite` flows through `IntegrityReasons`, `Compromised`, `safetyReasons` and `classify` (an ERROR for eval, a safety stop for work). `makeNetwork` precedes `openRun`, and `sweepRun`, `goneSweep` and `noPidSweep` cover the leaks. Errors are wrapped or noted; `leftoverProcs` now returns its read errors.
3. Standards conformance — pass. gofmt and vet are clean. `knownTools`/lint were not touched. The new comments describe the code (checked for `Intact`, `GitIntact`, `runBounded`, `fetch`). The restatement grep for the changed limits, mounts and safety reasons found no stale copy.
4. Directory layout — pass. `mounts_linux.go`/`mounts_other.go`, `gitdir.go`, `reflog.go`, `trailhistory.go`, `evals*.go` and `suite_columns.go` sit in the package that owns them; tests sit beside the code.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only; no new dependency (SQLite stays inside `internal/metrics`). No hand-rolled auth or crypto. The new SQLite use is confined to the existing packages.
6. Decoupling — pass. `sandbox.IntegrityReasons`/`Compromised` is the one shared list for eval and work. `eval` copies the metrics identifier rule rather than importing a SQLite driver, and the copy is commented.

## Not examined
- `skills/frontend-ui-*` (excluded by the dispatch, read not at all).
- The sizeable remainder of the Go diff was skimmed or unread: `internal/metrics` report.go, report_template.go, report_evals.go, show*.go, verb_tokenize.go, agy*.go beyond the diff hunks shown, `evals_kinds`/test files; `internal/dream` beyond `addRecords`/`finish` and the target selection; `internal/memory`; `internal/trail/trail.go` (88 lines removed); `internal/search` parse.go, config_view.go and the deleted records code (only the replacing hunks read); `cmd/fyr` help_text.go, status.go, record.go, ctx_verbs.go, update_zip.go, verb_index_register.go, main.go; `internal/serve` beyond pages.go.
- Test files outside 38ef79a..37756a3 were not read line by line; their results came from running them, not from reading them.
- Not run: `go test ./...` whole, `cmd/fyr` tests, the `internal/work` docker-mode tests against a real daemon (no docker run was made), `govulncheck`, and any behavioural `fyr eval` row.
- Non-Go content: `context/`, `agents/` other than the reviewer diff, `skills/` other than `work`, README, and the spec/guide records in `.agents/trail.jsonl` (only searched for restatements, not read in full). The `SPEC-fyr-work` and `SPEC-fyr-eval` text was not re-read against the code.
- Scratch left behind: `.agents/scratch/workers-review-mut/` (gitignored copy) and whatever `fyr search` wrote under `.agents/scratch/`.

Verdict: APPROVE

## Outcome

APPROVE, nothing to fix.

body:
# Review — docs lens v5.0.0..HEAD   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: v5.0.0..HEAD (HEAD 67bf395), docs lens only: do the living docs say what the code does

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

The docs track the code closely. Every verb and flag the range added (`fyr metrics evals`, `--harness`, `--outcome error`, `eval --runs`, `--from-zip` refusal at a development build, the `index --register` note, `uninstall --dry-run`) is in `cmd/fyr/help_text.go`, the README rows and the `SPEC-fyr-*` records; the TDD verb table moved to one line plus a spec link each and every link resolves. `fyr check` (built from HEAD, `--home .agents/scratch/workers`) reports docs 0, requirements 0, traces 0. The worst problem: ADR-089 changed the dreamer's claim from "no tools" to "no tool granted" and the HEAD commit changed only some restatements; four copies of the old claim stand, one of them text the code writes into every dream proposal. Nothing blocks the release; these are advisory.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high / owner: P13 gate closer]** `internal/dream/proposals_write.go:86` — every dream proposal's body is generated with "by %s with no tools"; ADR-089 says the dream is granted no tool but plan mode still runs `write_file` for its plan. Same stale claim at `skills/retro/SKILL.md:48` ("had no tools") and `:59` ("a model with no tools"), `SPEC-fyr-delivery` (first leaving-the-machine sentence: "with no tools, headless in plan mode") and the comment `internal/dream/dream.go:5`. README:35,58, SDD:124, PRD:56, SPEC-fyr-dream and the prompt were changed. Fix: "with no tool granted" in all five (a one-line code string, so a test pinning it, if any, changes with it; `grep 'with no tools' *_test.go` found none).
- **[low / confidence: medium / owner: P13 gate closer]** `fyr check` exits 1 with 7 `spec-stale` findings: SPEC-fyr-check, -eval, -memory-loop, -metrics, -record, -search, -serve. Cause: three code commits after their last re-read stamp (64715f3, 37756a3): `internal/dream/{dream,prompt,response}.go`, `internal/sandbox/creds.go`, `internal/metrics/evals_write.go`, `internal/harness/repo.go`, `internal/work/fetch.go`. Reading the diff, only SPEC-fyr-eval (credential scan now reads at most 64 MiB + 1 byte through `readBounded`, which the "over 64 MiB, not read" text already implies) and SPEC-fyr-metrics (eval row names go through `printable`) have anything to add; the other five look like path-granularity false positives. - **[low / confidence: medium / owner: P13 docs pass]** `internal/harness/repo.go` (HEAD commit): the `fyr update` failure message now strips a URL's query from git's text, and `ShellArg` writes a quote as `\x27` in its `$'…'` form. Neither behaviour is named in `SPEC-fyr-delivery`, `DEPLOY-local` or `DEPLOY-remote` (the comments in code say it). A line in SPEC-fyr-delivery's update section would close it. Not a claim reversed; a gap.

## Criteria (docs lens)
1. Dead code — n/a for this lens; the removed docs-root and config-view readers left no dangling doc reference (grep of README, SDD, TDD, AGENTS, help text, context found none).
2. Flow tracing — help_text.go vs the flags registered in `cmd/fyr/ctx_verbs.go`: metrics (`--harness`, `evals`, `--outcome error`), eval (`--runs`), uninstall (`--dry-run`), index (`--register` note) agree. `fyr check` verb/flag/path rule: 0 doc findings.

5. Simplicity — TDD § T5 thinning to one line and a link is the simpler shape; no claim lost: the removed rows' text sits in the specs (spot-checked eval, metrics, search, work, record, dream).
6. Decoupling — each spec carries dated "Updated/Re-read" lines naming the plan and phase; no spec restates another's behaviour except the finding above.

## Not examined
- `fyr work` help page against every new refusal (23, 25) and the run network: help is brief by design and names none of them; the detail is in `SPEC-fyr-work` and TDD § T17/T18, which I read only by grep, not whole.
- `GUIDE-testing` § 1-5 and `DEPLOY-local` beyond grep hits; the `skills/` and `agents/` text beyond the "no tools" grep and the frontend renames (not read in full); `PRD.md` diff body; `GUIDE-fyr-matrix` rows against `place_matrix_test.go`.

# Review — v5.5.0 gate round 1 fixes, code lens   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: 9298b9b..HEAD (67bf395)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing broken on Linux. The five code fixes (bounded credential read, upload-pack address-space cap, query stripping in Behind, dash-safe ShellArg, control-byte filter in the evals table) are correct and each has a test. `go vet` and `go test -race -short` pass on harness, sandbox, metrics, dream and work; the 1 GiB `TestUploadPackCapsMemory` ran un-short and passed (hostile fetch died with "Out of memory, malloc failed", plain fetch passed, so the limit is proved both ways). The R3 amendment left three restatements of "no tools" standing, and `ulimit -v` is untested on the macOS host, where the docker runner's fetch also runs.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/proposals_write.go:86` — ADR-089 says "the restatements say the same", but this line still stamps "by %s with no tools" into every proposal record body. Also stale: `internal/dream/dream.go:5` ("a CLI with no tools"), `skills/retro/SKILL.md:48` and `:59` ("had no tools", "a model with no tools"). The restatement rule (review-standards § 3 and 7) wants them changed with R3; wording to "with no tool granted" is enough. Check that no test pins the proposals_write string first.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/work/fetch.go:151` — `ulimit -v` runs in the host's `sh` for the docker runner, and macOS (a stated platform, Colima) is where the lead's fetch runs on the host. I did not test macOS. If its `sh` refuses `ulimit -v` or `setrlimit(RLIMIT_AS)`, the fail-closed design makes every `fyr work --runner docker` fetch fail there, and `TestUploadPackCapsMemory` fails too. Verify on the Apple Silicon box, or state the Linux-only limit in the code comment and refusal text.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/fetch.go:144` — the 8 GiB cap is an address-space limit (`-v`), not RSS. A legitimate large repo whose packs mmap past 8 GiB could fail the fetch. Git degrades by unmapping windows, so this is unlikely. Not blocking.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. `readBounded`, `uploadPack` and `urlQuery` each have a caller; nothing orphaned.
2. Flow tracing — pass. `Behind`'s `%w` became `%s`, but the only caller (`cmd/fyr/update_checkout.go:53`) does not unwrap, and `gitRun` wraps with `%s` already. `scanEntry` checks the read length after `readBounded`. `maxScan` is an `int64` var, so the test override works. `uploadPack` is used at the single fetch site. New tests can fail: the memory test proved both states, and the dash test depends on the `\x27` form.
3. Standards conformance — one low finding (stale "no tools" restatements). Comments for `command`, `answer`, `ShellArg` and `instructions` were updated. PRD R3, README, SDD and SPEC-fyr-dream § Known limits agree with ADR-089.
4. Directory layout — pass; new tests sit beside their code.
5. Simplicity — pass; stdlib only, no new dependency, no hand-rolled security primitive.
6. Decoupling — pass; each fix is local to its package.

## Not examined
Behaviour on macOS (`ulimit -v`). The full `go test ./...` and the `-short`-skipped tests outside `internal/work`. The `.agents/trail.jsonl` record bodies beyond ADR-089 and SPEC-fyr-dream's Known limits. Whether an old git without `--upload-pack` shell semantics matters. The eval rows added in 9298b9b (outside the range's HEAD^..HEAD).

## Outcome

F1 fixed. F2 left: macOS not run. F3 left: stated in the spec.
