# Review — gate3 (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: 67bf395..2a96952 (PLAN.md excluded; trail.jsonl record churn read only for the new plan/testing rows)

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH NITS

Nothing is broken. I found no correctness, security or requirement defect in the five code changes: `capMemory` in `internal/work/fetch.go` (the memory cap now covers the whole fetch and `cat-file`), `readBounded` in the sandbox, the `markTarget` panic fix in search, the dream "no tool granted" wording, and the doc and README edits. The two nits are test-coverage gaps; the macOS note is unverified.

Verified by running, on this Linux box: `gofmt -l cmd internal` printed nothing, `go vet ./internal/...` was clean, and `TestFetchMemoryLimit` (not skipped; it wrote the 1 GiB blob, 11 s), `TestCapMemoryForm`, `TestTrailAtFailsClosed`, `TestMarkTargetLongerThanTheSnippet`, `TestReadBoundedStopsAtTheBound` and `TestScanBoundsAFileStatSizeHides` all pass. The root `HarnessMap`, `Size` and `Lint` pins and `internal/harness` pass. I did not mutation-run the new tests. By reading: `TestMarkTargetLongerThanTheSnippet` panics on the old `end` at n = snippetMax+1 (`end` = snippetMax+4 < `at+n`), and `TestReadBoundedStopsAtTheBound` fails on either a plain `ReadAll` or a bound without the `+1`.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/records_test.go:66-85`, `internal/work/fetch_mem_test.go:97-104` — the docker branch of `trailAt` is never run. Every `trailAt` call in the tests passes `RunnerHost`, and `TestCapMemoryForm` only checks the command's form. If `capMemory(leadGit(cat-file))` broke the `StdoutPipe` or `Wait` handling under the `sh` wrapper, only a real docker run would show it. Fix: one `trailAt(..., RunnerDocker)` case in `TestTrailAtFailsClosed` that expects the same records.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/fetch_mem_test.go:93-104` — the comment says "the wrapper's `&&` means a limit that cannot be set runs nothing", but the test only greps the command text for `ulimit -v "$0" && exec "$@"`. That is the source-text pin the review standards exclude (§ 2), with no ordering that cannot be observed. A behavioural test would run `capMemory` with a limit the shell refuses and assert the command did not run. The text pin does state its own limit in the comment ("no test isolates index-pack"), so this is a nit.
- **[low / confidence: low, unverified]** `internal/work/fetch.go:151-160` — under `--runner docker` on macOS, `ulimit -v` may be rejected by the host `sh`. The wrapper fails closed, so every fetch and every `trailAt` would fail. The `--upload-pack` form already did this at 67bf395, so the range adds only the `cat-file` site. I did not check this on macOS; confirm once on the Apple Silicon box.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `TODO.md:10` — "the first session after v5.5.0" while the latest tag is v5.0.0. This is correct only once `/preflight v5.5.0` has cut the tag. If the gate is still open, the line is ahead of the tag. TDD.md:189 ("The fetch") does not mention the new memory cap, though it contradicts nothing.

## Criteria
1. Dead code — pass. `uploadPack`, `uploadPackMemKiB` and `TestUploadPackCapsMemory` are fully replaced, with no remaining callers (grep). No commented-out code.
2. Flow tracing — pass. `capMemory` keeps `Dir` and `Env` (so `leadGit`'s `GIT_GRAFT_FILE` survives) and `Args[0]` is `git`. The pipes and `SysProcAttr` are set after wrapping, in `runBounded` and `trailAt`. `exec` keeps the pid for the group kill. Both `trailAt` callers pass the runner. Other lead git calls on worker objects (`rev-list`, `diff-tree --no-renames --name-only`, `ls-tree`) read no blobs. `markTarget`: `start` is clamped to `at`, and `end` is at least `at+n`, so the slices are in range. `readBounded` reads `maxScan+1` bytes.
3. Standards conformance — pass. "no tools" became "no tool granted" in `dream.go`, `proposals_write.go` and `skills/retro/SKILL.md` (both places). A grep finds no remaining "with no tools" restatement apart from the vendored prompt-audit text. The README rules row now lists four rules, matching `rules/*.md`. The AGENTS.md layout line for PLAN.md is removed. Other `PLAN.md` mentions are code comments citing the closed plan, which is acceptable.
4. Directory layout — pass. `search_query_mark_test.go` sits beside its code.
5. Simplicity (DIY-except-security) — pass. Stdlib only, no new dependency, and nothing auth- or crypto-related.
6. Decoupling — pass. `capMemory` is the single seam for the cap and takes the runner as a string. Its two callers are in the same package.

## Not examined
Mutation runs of the new tests (reasoned, not executed). The full `go test -race ./...` (only the focused packages above). The behavioural eval rows. The remaining `.agents/trail.jsonl` record bodies beyond the headline rows (record text, not code). The macOS behaviour of `ulimit -v`. The file `internal/work/fetch_mem_test.go` was read as a diff only; its first-line imports (`slices`) compile, as the run shows.

## Outcome

1 and 2's pin fixed in 05ba26d (TestDockerReadsAreCapped); the fail-closed form is run by the real test's 1 KiB limit. macOS left.

title: Security review — v5.5.0 gate, check, dream, harness, root docs
body:
# Security review — release gate v5.5.0, part: check, dream, harness, cmd/fyr, root docs   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: v5.0.0..9298b9b

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The worst problem is a false security claim. The dream's "no tools" boundary is contradicted by this range's own fixture: `tool.jsonl` shows a `write_file` tool running to DONE under the dream's exact argv and request-review mode, and `answer` only drops the text after the side effect. There is no high finding, no secret and no new dependency. Two lows, on remote URLs and shell quoting, are gaps between what a doc comment or test claims and what the code does. Every path of this part was read end to end. The one thing left open is whether plan mode can write outside agy's own directory.

One process failure of this review, not of the code: this artifact first lived at `security-2026-10-31-2224.md`, the same stamp a parallel security agent (the sandbox, work, eval and docker part) took for its own artifact. My read-modify-write replaced that agent's `## Findings`, `## Checked` and `## Not examined` sections with mine, so that file holds its title and verdict over my findings. This file is the correct copy of this part. The other agent's findings have to come from its own structured output.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: medium]** `internal/dream/testdata/agy-1.4.12/tool.jsonl:4` — the capture of the dream's exact argv shows `write_file` going ACTIVE then DONE (`tool.jsonl:5`, 0.65 s, no approval step) under `permission_mode: request-review`, plan mode and no allow rule. `internal/dream/dream.go:226` says "any tool call is refused", `internal/dream/prompt.go:9` says the model has no tools, and `PRD.md:56` (R3), `README.md:35`, `README.md:58` and `SDD.md:124` restate it. `answer` (`internal/dream/response.go:50`) drops the text after the step; it undoes no side effect. The dream's prompt carries project text and transcripts, so a prompt injected through them reaches a file write in that HOME, which is the operator's own on the visible branch. `PLAN.md:390` read this capture as "wrote a plan and ran nothing" and kept the claim. The capture shows only agy's own `brain/<conversation>/` directory as the target; whether plan mode writes further is unproven, hence medium confidence. Remediation: in a sandbox home, capture a plan-mode turn told to write outside that directory. If it stays confined, state that write as the boundary at every restatement (`PRD.md` needs the operator's approval). If it does not, run the dream only in the private HOME. Pin the result with a `testdata` capture.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/repo.go:255` — `remoteForDisplay` strips a URL's query, and `PLAN.md:281` records that, but `Behind` then wraps git's raw stderr with `%w`, and git prints the query. Probe in a throwaway repo: remote `https://u:PW@127.0.0.1:1/x.git?token=Q` gave `fatal: unable to access 'https://127.0.0.1:1/x.git?token=Q/'`; git dropped the password, not the query. A query token therefore still reaches the terminal and any log of it. `TestBehindFetchErrorHidesCredentials` covers userinfo only, and the query case is tested on `remoteForDisplay` alone. Remediation: replace git's text for the remote's URL before wrapping it, and add a query-token case through `Behind`.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/repo.go:297` — `ShellArg`'s comment says a POSIX sh reads the `$'…'` form as a literal string. That is false when the value holds a control character and a single quote: the form writes `\'`, and in dash the quote closes the string there (probe: `dash -c` on `$'a\'b'` gives "Unterminated quoted string"), so what follows runs as shell text if pasted. The value is `st.Repo` from the manifest or the checkout path, and the output is a command the operator is told to paste (`cmd/fyr/zip_place.go:74`, `internal/harness/repo.go:255`). It needs an odd path and a paste into sh, so the reach is small. `TestShellArgRoundTrips` runs bash only. Remediation: write `'` as `\x27` and `\` as `\x5c` inside `$'…'`, so no quote appears in the form, and run the round trip under `sh` too.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `PLAN.md:415` — instruction-shaped text in a committed file: the `## Kickoff` block grants standing approvals (commit, push, real-home install, `/preflight v5.5.0`), and `PLAN.md:34` states that every verdict was approved by the operator. Both match the operator's relayed request for this run, so neither is planted, and neither changed this review. The risk is the shape: a later edit of the file changes what a session handed the Kickoff runs under. Rule 5 removes the file at P13, which closes it; keep authority in the operator's own turn.

## Checked
- Secrets: regexps for AWS, GitHub, Google, Slack, GitLab, JWT and PEM shapes over every file of this part, testdata included: no hit. Test tokens are fakes (`tok3nuser`, `s3cr3tpw`, a built `ghp_` value). `PLAN.md:415` holds the operator's home path, `/home/kesokaj`, and `PLAN.md` names the hosts dave and borken: not secrets, and the file leaves the root at P13.
- Testdata: `testdata/agy-1.4.12` holds no token, and `config.json` holds no setting of the operator's. `tool.jsonl` keeps the fragments `/home/` and `op/sandbox/fyr-eval/p12b-captur` across chunks where the `README.md` there says the home path was rewritten. No account `op` exists on dave, so no private name leaks, but the rewrite did not reach split text.
- Injection: every git argument in `internal/check/trailhistory.go` is an object ID from git's own output. The blob and merge-depth bounds, `--no-replace-objects`, `core.commitGraph=false` and `GIT_GRAFT_FILE` hold, and `git cat-file blob` runs no textconv. `ShellArg` is a finding; `zip_place.go` prints the manifest path through it. Removing the dream's file collector drops the symlink and FIFO readers along with their tests: no reader is left that needed them, and `TestCollectDoesNotFollowALinkedAgentsDir` now pins the brain store's refusal.
- Authz/authn: `refuseDevelZipOverPath` refuses on an unreadable manifest and on an unmigrated home's dry run; `zipPlaceWithoutSource` keeps a named path's own error; `--project` and marker consent in `internal/dream/targets.go` are unchanged in effect. Instruction-shaped text: only `PLAN.md:34` and `PLAN.md:415`, reported above; nothing in this part addresses a reviewer.
- Crypto: no primitive added; the zip's SHA-256 check is the standard library's, unchanged here.
- Dependencies: `go.mod` and `go.sum` unchanged in the range. govulncheck on go1.27.3: 0 affecting this code; GO-2026-5024 (golang.org/x/sys, windows only) sits in a required module and is not called. npm audit: not run; no package.json in this part, and the only tracked ones are vendored catalog data.
- GCP surface: none in this part.
- Not security, for the docs lens: `README.md:257` says two known govulncheck advisories where one printed; `README.md:87` omits the agy-dispatch rule; `TDD.md:153` still names `Dates`, which `internal/trail` no longer has.

## Not examined
- Paths: none. Every path of this part in `git diff --name-only v5.0.0..9298b9b` was read end to end at 9298b9b: the new and the modified files, tests, testdata and the six root docs, and the deleted `internal/dream/traildate_test.go` at v5.0.0.
- Surface: whether agy's plan mode can write outside its own `brain/` directory. No agy run was made, because a behavioural eval holds the machine; finding 1 names the capture that answers it.
- `internal/metrics`, `internal/search`, `internal/brain`, `internal/trail`, `internal/redact`: read only where this part calls them; other parts of this gate cover them.

## Outcome

S1 fixed by R3's amendment on the operator's word (ADR-089); enforcement outside brain/ stays unproved, named in SPEC-fyr-dream. S2 fixed for the query; a fragment or quoted query is left. S3 fixed. S4 left: the Kickoff is the operator's.

title: Security review — v5.5.0 gate round 2
body:
# Security review — p13-gate-fixes   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: 9298b9b..HEAD

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Worst problem: the new memory limit covers only the sending half of the docker fetch. `ulimit -v` wraps `--upload-pack`, so it reaches `upload-pack` and `pack-objects`, but the receiving `index-pack` or `unpack-objects` is a child of the lead's `git fetch` and runs with no limit on the host. Stock git commands measured it: a clone with 5.4 MiB of loose objects, under the same `core.bigFileThreshold` knob, produced a 631,905-byte pack, and `git index-pack --stdin --strict --fsck-objects` peaked at 1,204 MiB RSS resolving it. `SPEC-fyr-work` names `index-pack` as time-bounded only, so the gap is disclosed, but its "each file being at most check d's 64 MiB" reads as a memory bound and is not one. `fetch_mem_test.go`'s "the fetch fails instead of filling the host" holds only for the sending side. The other fixes in the range do what they say, with the smaller gaps below. No secret, no injection and no new dependency entered the range.

## Findings
- **[medium / confidence: high for the measurement, medium for the unmeasured claim]** `internal/work/fetch.go:164` — The docker fetch's memory limit misses the host's receiving side. `uploadPack` wraps only the command `git fetch` spawns for the remote end; the lead's `index-pack` (or `unpack-objects` under `transfer.unpackLimit`) inherits nothing from it. Why it is reachable in principle: the pack is agent-controlled, and resolving a delta holds base and result whole whatever `core.bigFileThreshold` says on the lead. Measured on git 2.47.3 with 600 MiB blob pairs built by `hash-object`: 631,905-byte pack, 1,204 MiB peak in the receiver. Not measured, inferred from how git reuses deltas: a delta already stored in a clone's pack is copied by `pack-objects` without being inflated, so the 8 GiB limit on the sender does not bound what the receiver is then asked to hold. `leadGit ... cat-file blob` in `internal/work/records.go:50` has the same shape after the fetch: the read is capped, but git's own process is not, and it has no deadline. Remediation: run the whole lead fetch under the limit, `sh -c 'ulimit -v N && exec "$@"' sh git ...` (no dependency; Go's `SysProcAttr` has no rlimit field), so the receiver and `--upload-pack` both inherit it, do the same for the post-fetch `cat-file`, add a test whose hostile run measures the receiving side, and correct the SPEC sentence so 64 MiB is not read as a bound on memory.
- **[medium / confidence: low]** `PRD.md:56` — After ADR-089, R3 still says the dream "writes only under `~/.config/fyr/`", while the ADR and `SPEC-fyr-dream` § Known limits say confinement to `brain/` is not shown and "Nothing stops a plan-mode write outside `brain/` if the CLI allows one". The operator accepted the "no tool granted" wording; this finding is the sentence left beside it, which claims more than the evidence. The input is attacker-influenced (project records, transcripts), and the visible branch runs in the operator's own Antigravity home, so an unconfined plan-mode write would land as the operator. That write is neither proved possible nor proved impossible; the one probe depended on the model's choice. No mechanism backs the claim: the private settings at `internal/dream/agy_home.go:102` hold an empty `allow` and no `deny` rule, and whether a `deny` rule stops plan mode's `write_file` is untested. Remediation: test an explicit `deny` on `write_file` against agy 1.4.12 and adopt it in the private branch and as a condition of the visible one if it holds; otherwise reword R3 to what ADR-089 shows.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/harness/repo.go:297` — `urlQuery` leaves token text in git's output in three cases, each run against real git output. A fragment is not touched: `x.git#fr4gtok` passes through whole, although `remoteForDisplay` treats fragments as sensitive. A quote in the query keeps the rest: `x.git?a=1'qu0tetok` prints `x.git'qu0tetok`. A space does the same: `x.git?a=1 sp4cetok` prints `x.git sp4cetok`. `TestBehindFetchErrorHidesCredentials` tries only a plain query. Separately, `Pull` at `repo.go:351-353` streams git's stderr straight to `out` with no filter (read, not run), so the same URL prints if a network failure lands between `Behind` and the pull. Exposure is the operator's terminal or a captured log. Remediation: replace the exact configured URL from `ls-remote --get-url` with `remoteForDisplay`'s form in git's text, keep a regex that also takes `#` as a fallback, send `Pull`'s stderr through the same filter, and add the three triggers to the test.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/sandbox/creds_bound_test.go:12` — `TestScanBoundsAFileStatSizeHides` does not pin the read bound it claims ("the read itself must stop at maxScan"). In a scratch copy, `readBounded` was changed to an unlimited `io.ReadAll(f)` and the test still passed: `/proc/self/status` ends on its own and the later `len(b)` check gives the same refusal. The `io.LimitReader` that closes the finding therefore has no failing test, which the project's rule for a fixed finding requires. Remediation: test `readBounded` directly on a file longer than `maxScan` and assert it returns exactly `maxScan+1` bytes.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/dream/proposals_write.go:86` — A reversed security claim survives despite ADR-089's "The restatements say the same". This line stamps "with no tools" into every proposal draft the dream writes. The same claim stands in `internal/dream/dream.go:5`, `skills/retro/SKILL.md:48`, `skills/retro/SKILL.md:59` and `SPEC-fyr-dream` ("every tool call is refused and ends the run with no answer"), which also misquotes the prompt sentence this range changed. The retro skill's conclusion (treat the text as data) still holds, but its reason does not. Remediation: use "no tool granted" in all five, and run `scripts/restatement-grep.sh` over the claim.
- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/work/fetch.go:151` — `ulimit -v` may be refused by `/bin/sh` on macOS, which `SPEC-fyr-work` records as untested, and `internal/work/docker.go:38` shows the Mac is a docker host. The failure is closed, so this is availability only: every docker worker there would finish its session and then fail at the fetch, reported as `no commits`. My recollection of macOS behaviour is unverified on this Linux box. Remediation: probe `ulimit -v` at the runner's preflight (beside refusal 25), so it refuses before a session is spent.

## Checked
- **Secrets:** added lines, the `.agents/trail.jsonl` diff included, matched none of the scanner's token shapes. The only tokens are test fixtures (`s3cr3tpw`, `qu3rytok`). Trail records changed: ADR-089 added, `SPEC-fyr-dream` and `SPEC-fyr-work` changed; no instruction-shaped text aimed at a reviewer was found in them.
- **Injection:** `uploadPack` formats one integer into a constant; git shell-quotes the path it appends (per the P12b review's trace). `ShellArg`'s `\x27` form leaves no quote for dash to close on, `\x%02x` is padded so a following hex digit cannot join it, `$'…'` stays literal in dash, and its only callers print text. `printable` covers C0, DEL, C1, separators and format characters. `Table`'s other cells are safe: `Kind` is enumerated by the suite parser at the row's source, `Last` is a formatted date, `Flags` are computed, and `Harness` is the operator's own flag.
- **Authz/authn:** nothing in the range touches auth. The `Runner` gate is exact: `""` and `host` stay unwrapped, and preflight validates the value.
- **Crypto:** none added; `fileSum`'s `crypto/sha256` is stdlib as designed.
- **Dependencies:** none added (`regexp`, `io` are stdlib; `go.mod` not in the diff). `govulncheck ./...`: no vulnerabilities affect the code; it reports 1 in a required module that the code does not call (detail not expanded). `npm audit`: not applicable, no `package.json`, `web` or `ui` at the repo root.
- **GCP surface:** nothing in the range.
- **readBounded:** the bound is correct and the refusal fails closed through `newCreds`. The scan runs after the container is gone (`containersLeft`, then `ExitChecks`, `internal/work/worker.go:81`), so no link can be swapped by a docker session mid-read. Residuals, both older than this range: it bounds bytes, not time, so a regular-mode file on the host whose read blocks would still stall the scan, and a tree of many links costs one 64 MiB read each with no deadline.
- **S1's other readers:** `countLines` (`OpenRegular`), `drafts`, `records` and `kickoff` are bounded. `fileSum` is not, but `fingerprint` walks only the real home's watched paths, which a docker session cannot write.
- **`%w` to `%s` in `Behind`:** `update`'s only `errors.As` target is `exitCode`, which `gitOut` never produces, so nothing breaks.
- **Past failures:** `fyr search --refs` per changed file named BUG-049, 203 (`repo.go`), BUG-200 (`fetch.go`), BUG-198, 204 (`PLAN.md`), BUG-007, 048, 202 (`README.md`), BUG-202 (`SDD.md`). None recurs here.

## Not examined
- A crafted pack: deliberately not built. The reused-delta route in the first finding is reasoning, and `unpack-objects`' peak and the ratio's scaling to 64 MiB were not measured.
- `ulimit -v` on macOS; the macOS finding is unverified.
- The tests were read and one was mutated; the suite was not run (the verifier's job), and `TestUploadPackCapsMemory`, `TestShellArgHoldsInDash` and `TestEvalTableFiltersTheRowName` were not run or mutated.
- agy's real behaviour under a `deny` rule, or any plan-mode write outside `brain/`: no `agy` run was made.
- `fyr serve`'s and `fyr metrics report`'s HTML rendering of the eval table.
- `search.printable` past line 146; its remaining branch was not read.
- The `SPEC-fyr-work` step 6 hunks were read by the sentences they change, not the whole of each long line.
- The govulncheck verbose detail of the one uncalled module finding.

## Outcome

S1 fixed in 33c33b7. S2 left: operator, a further PRD edit. S3 left for the fragment and Pull. S4 fixed. S5 fixed. S6 left: macOS not run.

title: Security review — v5.5.0 gate round 3
body:
# Security review — v5.5.0 gate round 3   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: 67bf395..33c33b7

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The memory limit stops one step short. `capMemory` covers the fetch and `cat-file`, but a docker session can still fill the host through the next step, with a smaller trigger than the one this gate fixed. The scope check runs `diff-tree -r` over the session's history, on the host, with no memory limit, no deadline and no bound on what `fyr` buffers. Trees shared by many parents expand to far more paths than the objects' size suggests. Measured here: 36 KiB of objects passed the capped strict fetch, then produced 1,000,000 paths. `capMemory` itself is sound: no injection, same pid and process group, fails closed. However, neither production call site is pinned, and removing both left every test in `internal/work` green.

## Findings

- **[high / confidence: high]** `internal/work/fetch.go:257-277` (`changedPaths`), `:238-253` (`links`), called from `scope` at `:187` — session-written history is expanded on the host with no bound. `diff-tree -r` walks every path, and `.Output()` buffers all of stdout in `fyr`'s heap. Neither git process has `capMemory`, and neither has a deadline. Evidence, on git 2.47.3, in a throwaway repository: a six-level tree of shared subtrees took 36 KiB on disk and passed `fetch.fsckObjects=true` under the 8 GiB wrapper, because fsck and the connectivity walk visit each object once. The same `diff-tree --stdin -r -m --root --name-only -z` then gave 1,000,000 paths, 20 MB of stdout, 0.62 s, 294 MiB peak RSS in git. Two more tree levels, a few KiB, mean 100 times that: about 2 GB in `fyr` and 29 GB in git. That is a linear extrapolation, not a measured run. Each level multiplies it again. `GitIntact` has no size check that sees this, since the objects are small. Consequences: the host runs out of memory, with `collect.Lock()` (`worker.go:88`) held the whole time, although the `fetchLimit` comment says no step should hold it that long. The docker session is the untrusted party here, and this is the same consequence the gate's first finding fixed. The doc on `hostMemKiB` (`fetch.go:141`) claims the limit covers "the git commands that read what a docker session wrote"; that is false for `rev-parse` (`:176`), `rev-list` (`:189`, `:258`), `merge-base` (`:192`), `diff-tree` (`:239`, `:262`) and `ls-tree` (`records.go:37`). Remediation: run every post-fetch `leadGit` read of session objects through `capMemory` and a deadline. At the measured 294 bytes of git heap per path, the 8 GiB limit stops `diff-tree` near 29 million paths, about 580 MB of stdout. Bound stdout as well, and treat going over the bound as an error that fails `ReasonOutside`. Do not reuse `runBounded`'s `cappedWriter` here as it stands: it truncates silently, and a truncated path list would pass the scope check. No dependency is needed. Add a test with a shared-subtree history that fails without the fix, for both `changedPaths` and `links`.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/work/fetch.go:169`, `internal/work/records.go:49` — the fix's two production call sites are unpinned. `memFetch` (`fetch_mem_test.go`) builds its own command and calls `capMemory` itself, `TestCapMemoryForm` tests the wrapper alone, and `TestTrailAtFailsClosed` passes only `RunnerHost`. Mutation run in a scratch copy of 33c33b7: both `capMemory` calls removed, `go test -count=1 ./internal/work` without `-short` still `ok` (48 s). A later edit can drop the limit silently, and the rule that a finding counts as fixed only when a test fails without the fix is not met for either trigger. Remediation: have the test drive `w.fetch()` and `trailAt(..., RunnerDocker)`, or have them share a named builder that the test also calls.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/fetch.go:141-143` — the limit is per process, not per fetch. `RLIMIT_AS` applies to each process, so in the hostile case pack-objects and index-pack can each reach 8 GiB, which is about 16 GiB of host memory. The comment equates it to the container's `--memory`, which is one cgroup-wide total. Peak was not measured. Remediation: state the real bound in the comment, or lower `hostMemKiB` to the host budget divided by the number of holding processes.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/fetch.go:155-157` — `capMemory` discards `cmd.Err` and `cmd.Path`. `exec.Command("git")` refuses a `git` resolved through `.` or an empty `PATH` entry (`ErrDot`). The wrapper drops that error and lets `sh` look `git` up again, and an empty `PATH` entry in `sh` means the working directory. That is the lead checkout, so a `git` file there could run. Needs an operator `PATH` containing `.` or an empty entry, and a `git` file in the working directory; docker runner only. Remediation: return `cmd` unchanged when `cmd.Err != nil` so `Start` fails, and pass `cmd.Path` as the program to exec.

- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/work/fetch.go:155` — `ulimit -v` on macOS is unverified. The `&&` covers a limit that cannot be set, but not one the kernel accepts and does not enforce. The context names macOS as an operator machine and `records.go:133` a docker runner on the Mac. Darwin's behaviour was not tested here, either way. This already held for upload-pack; the range extends it to the whole fetch and `cat-file`. A large virtual mapping could instead make every fetch fail. Remediation: run `TestFetchMemoryLimit` on a Mac before claiming the limit there, and refuse `--runner docker` at preflight if it is not enforced.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/fetch.go:147-149` — the comment overstates its case. It says fsck in index-pack holds a blob whole "with no config at all". Measured on 2.47.3 with plain config and a 600 MiB blob under a 256 MiB limit: the fetch passes with `fetch.fsckObjects=true`, so above the default 512 MiB `core.bigFileThreshold` the blob is streamed. A 300 MiB blob under a 128 MiB limit fails, but it fails on the serving side, in `remote:` output. The limit is still justified; the sentence needs the threshold. The test comment in `TestFetchMemoryLimit`'s header holds at both sizes tried.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `cmd/fyr/help_text.go:208` — "to agy with no tool" survives the round that replaced the no-tools claim in `dream.go:5` and `proposals_write.go:86`. A security claim printed to the operator should match ADR-089's "no tool granted". Same class, smaller: `search_query.go:205` still says the line is cut to `snippetMax` runes, and a target longer than that now exceeds it.

## Checked

- **Secrets:** none in the diff. The dream header strings carry no values; `o.line` still handles root and dropped paths.
- **Injection:** none. `capMemory` passes the limit as `$0` from `strconv.Itoa` and every argument as a quoted `"$@"`, so a branch name or path never reaches shell parsing. The `--upload-pack` value is now a constant. The `sh -c` string is constant.
- **Process group (`runBounded` with the wrapper):** measured, the wrapper's pid and pgid stay the child's across `exec`, so `pgid := cmd.Process.Pid` and both group kills still reach git. Soft and hard limits are both set (8388608), so a child cannot raise them.
- **Failure shape:** a limit that cannot be set (hard limit lower) prints `ulimit: error setting limit`, exits 2 and runs nothing, verified by probe; the test only pins the string. `fetch` then notes the error and fails `ReasonNoCommits`, with no ref written, verified by probe at `ref=none`. The reason is misleading for a limit hit, though the note carries the truth. In `trailAt`, stderr is not captured, so a limit failure reads `git cat-file: exit status 2`; it fails closed as `ReasonNoHandoff` plus outside. A partial read cannot pass: `Wait`'s error is checked before parsing.
- **Env and dir:** `leadGit`'s `Env` and `GIT_GRAFT_FILE`, `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` and the removal of repository variables are all copied. `Dir` is empty, since `-C` carries the root. `Stdin` and `Stdout` are set after wrapping by each caller. `sh` reads no startup file for a non-interactive `-c`.
- **`trailAt` deadline:** `cat-file` has none, but the capped fetch has already limited what a blob can be, and it streams, so it is not reported separately.
- **`markTarget`:** the arithmetic holds when `at+n <= len(r)`. A target comes from the ASCII-only `pathToken` or `idToken`, so it cannot start inside a multi-byte rune, and `printable` still cleans the output. The 200-rune case panics no more. A raw-byte target that split a rune is not reachable from `parseRefs`.
- **`readBounded` test:** an unbounded read gives 10 bytes and fails the test, by reading; no `t.Parallel` in the sandbox tests, so the `maxScan` swap is safe. `creds.go:167` keeps FIFOs and devices from being opened.
- **Dream strings:** text only; no test or consumer parses them.
- **Authz/authn, crypto:** not touched by the range; no primitive added.
- **Dependencies:** `go.mod` unchanged. `govulncheck ./...`: 0 vulnerabilities affecting the code, 1 in a required module that is not called (not expanded with `-show verbose`). `npm audit` not run: nothing in the range is an npm ecosystem change.
- **GCP surface:** not touched.
- **Tests run:** `TestCapMemoryForm`, `TestFetchMemoryLimit`, `TestTrailAtFailsClosed`, `TestMarkTarget*`, `TestReadBoundedStopsAtTheBound`, `TestScanBounds*` all pass. The working tree was unchanged afterwards.

## Not examined

- `fyr search --refs` returned `absent` for all seven files under `--home .agents/scratch/workers`. That home holds no index for these paths, so this says nothing about past bugs. A body scan of `.agents/trail.jsonl` for bomb, fan-out and `changedPaths` terms found no earlier report of finding 1.
- macOS: nothing ran on Darwin.
- A full-scale run of finding 1 was deliberately not done; the figures above 1,000,000 paths are extrapolated. Peak memory of a whole hostile fetch across its processes was not measured.
- `internal/work/docker_test.go` was not read; only the mutation result speaks for it.
- The rest of `internal/sandbox` (`GitIntact` in full, `gitdir.go`) was searched for size checks, not read end to end. `README.md`, `skills/retro/SKILL.md` and `.agents/trail.jsonl` in the range were looked at as diff lines only, or not at all for the trail.
- The lead's later uncapped reads of the fetched branch (`git merge --squash`, `git log`, `git gc`) and the detached `git maintenance --auto` after a fetch, which leaves the process group.

## Outcome

1 (high) fixed in 05ba26d: every branch read but the tip's rev-parse is capped, with a deadline and an output bound that fails. 2 fixed. 3, 5 left; stated in hostlimit.go and the spec. 4 left. 6's help line fixed.

title: Security review — v5.5.0 gate round 4
body:
# Security review — v5.5.0 gate round 4: host reads of session history   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: 33c33b7..HEAD (05ba26d); source and tests. The trail, PLAN.md, TODO.md and AGENTS.md changes of the range were not read, per the dispatch.

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

The worst gap is `trailAt`'s `git cat-file` (`internal/work/records.go:49-59`): under docker it is memory-capped and its output is bounded, but it alone of the branch reads has no deadline and no process group, and it runs under the collect lock, so commit 05ba26d's "every read of the branch after the fetch under the memory limit, a deadline and an output bound" is not true of it. `fetch.go:160`'s `rev-parse` has neither the limit nor a deadline. No fail-open was found: every bound that trips ends in a failed scope, a claim tested at six caps for the two reads that trip first. A candidate fail-open, `diff-tree --stdin` skipping an unreadable commit with exit 0, is real git behaviour but did not fire under the cap (finding 4). No finding here blocks on its own terms beyond the operator's call on finding 1.

Answer to the dispatch, read by read after the fetch, docker runner:

| Read | Line | Memory | Time | Output | On a trip |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fetch | hostlimit.go:32, fetch.go:155 | capped | 10 min | 64 KiB kept | closed, ReasonNoCommits |
| `rev-parse ref^{commit}` | fetch.go:160 | **uncapped** | **none** | 41 bytes in practice | closed on error |
| `rev-list --count` | fetch.go:173 | capped | 10 min | fails over 64 MiB | closed, as ReasonNoCommits (error dropped) |
| `merge-base --is-ancestor` | fetch.go:176 | capped | 10 min | fails over 64 MiB | closed, as ReasonRewrote (error dropped) |
| `rev-list`, `diff-tree --stdin` | fetch.go:242, 246 | capped | 10 min each | fails over 64 MiB | closed, ReasonOutside; see finding 4 |
| `ls-tree` | records.go:37 | capped | 10 min | fails over 64 MiB | closed, ReasonNoHandoff and outside |
| `cat-file blob` | records.go:49 | capped | **none** | 256 MiB kept, rest drained, over it fails | closed |
| `diff-tree` (links) | fetch.go:223 | capped | 10 min | fails over 64 MiB | closed, ReasonOutside |

## Findings
1. **[medium / confidence: high on the gap, low on a practical hang]** `internal/work/records.go:49-59` — `blobCmd` is run by hand with `StdoutPipe`, `Start`, `io.ReadAll`, `io.Copy(io.Discard, out)` and `Wait`: no deadline, no `runGroup`, no ctx. A blob's cost is not a function of its bytes alone: a delta chain costs depth times size, and the drain continues to the end of the blob. The worker holds `dispatch`'s `collect` mutex (`work.go:157`), so a stall here stops every other worker's collect, and nothing can kill it. The fetch's own 10-minute limit bounds the same chain's cost loosely, since index-pack resolves it under that deadline, so I found no way to make it hang; the bound is inferred, not enforced. Remediation: read through `runGroup` with `branchLimit` and a writer that keeps `maxTrail` and flags overflow (make `overflow`'s limit a field); drop the `StdoutPipe` path; add a test that a stalled read is killed at the deadline.
2. **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/fetch.go:160` — the `rev-parse --verify -q ref^{commit}` that runs right after the fetch uses plain `.Output()`: no memory cap, no deadline. It reads the tip commit whole on the host, uncapped. The tip's size is limited only transitively, by fsck having held it under the fetch's cap, so up to about 8 GiB of real memory outside any limit. It also makes the commit's "every read" false. Remediation: `branchOutput(leadGit(...), w.o.Runner)`.
3. **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/fetch.go:173-248`, `hostlimit.go:45` — `branchLimit` is per read, not per scope. Seven reads at 10 minutes each, plus the fetch and the unlimited cat-file, can hold the collect lock well over an hour for one worker, and `runGroup` takes no ctx, so a stopped run waits too. The comment "holds the collect lock as the fetch does" reads as one bound. Remediation: one deadline across `collect` and cancellation from `ctx`. Not measured how long a crafted history can make each read take.
4. **[low / confidence: high on the git behaviour, medium on non-reachability]** `internal/work/fetch.go:246-251` — `git diff-tree --stdin` exits 0 and drops a commit it cannot read: probed on git 2.47.3 with a missing oid between two good ones, exit 0, no stderr, the two good commits' paths printed. `changedPaths` is the only per-commit scope check, so a skipped commit would hide its paths, including a change kept to the tip. It did not fire in a scale model of the real commands: 14 commits with 40 MiB messages stored as deltas, the oldest touching `outside.txt`, the same `ulimit -v` wrapper at 150, 200, 250, 300, 350 and 400 MiB. The capped fetch and `rev-list` passed; `diff-tree --stdin` exited 128 with `fatal: unable to parse commit` at every cap and `merge-base` exited 128 too; the uncapped control listed `outside.txt`. Why it held: each non-tip commit is a parent of an earlier line, so `parse_commit_or_die` meets it first, and the tip fits by the same cap. That is an ordering accident in git, not a guarantee of it. Remediation: count the commits diff-tree reports (run without `--no-commit-id` and compare with `revs`), so a skipped commit fails the scope.
5. **[low / confidence: low, untested here]** `internal/work/hostlimit.go:25` — `ulimit -v` on macOS, the operator's other platform. As I recall, Darwin either refuses it, which fails every docker fetch closed and breaks the runner, or accepts it without enforcing it, which would make the bound a silent no-op. Nothing in `internal/work` or `internal/sandbox` mentions either. `TestDockerReadsAreCapped` run on the Mac tells the second from the first only partly: a refusal passes it too. Remediation: one real `fyr work --runner docker` run on the Mac before the tag, and a probe at preflight that the limit is enforced.
6. **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/hostlimit.go:33` — the fetch has no `--no-auto-maintenance`, so it can start `git maintenance run --auto`. A detached gc calls `setsid`, which leaves the process group, so `runGroup`'s kill and deadline do not reach it. It inherits the cap, and it needs the lead's own gc thresholds, so one session cannot trigger it at will. Not probed; from git's documented behaviour. Remediation: pass `--no-auto-maintenance`.
7. **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/fetch_mem_test.go:108-133` — `TestDockerReadsAreCapped` does not pin everything its comment says ("each read after the session"). `rev-list --count` and `merge-base` in `scope()` are not in its map, so passing `RunnerHost` there survives. `trailAt` fails at `ls-tree` under `hostMemKiB = 1`, so the blob read's cap is pinned by form only. No test runs `branchOutput` into its deadline. A claim of coverage has to name these.
8. **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/fetch.go:173-179` — a bound that trips on `rev-list --count` or `merge-base` drops the error: a timeout, an out-of-memory or an overflow reports "no commits" or "does not descend from". This fails closed but misstates the cause to the lead. Remediation: note the error, as `changedPaths`' caller does.
9. **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/work/hostlimit.go:25-26` — `capMemory` rebuilds the command from `cmd.Args`, so the `sh` resolves a bare `git` itself and `cmd.Path` and `cmd.Err` are dropped. With `.` or an empty entry on PATH, Go's `exec.ErrDot` refusal no longer applies under docker, and `sh` would run a `git` from the working directory. Under docker the session cannot write the lead, so this takes an operator PATH of that shape. Remediation: pass `cmd.Path` to `exec` and carry `cmd.Err` over.
10. **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/work/hostlimit.go:11-13` — "a fetch's two sides together can hold twice that" undercounts: the limit is per process, and the tree also holds `upload-pack`, `rev-list`, and threads. The bound is address space per process, not host memory, so a host with less RAM than the cap is not protected. Comment fix, or accept it in writing.

## Checked
- Secrets: none in the range; no credential reaches a note on these paths.
- Injection: `ref` passes `check-ref-format` at preflight; `f[2]` comes from git's `ls-tree`; `ulimit`'s argument is `strconv.Itoa` passed as `$0`, the command as `"$@"`, so `sh` interpolates nothing.
- Authz/authn: no new surface. The scope order is unchanged; `branchOutput` returns nil on every error, so partial output never reaches the scope check; `overflow` returns `len(p)`, so git does not die on a pipe and over-limit output is an error. `ErrWaitDelay` and a timeout both surface as `err`.
- Crypto: none touched; no hand-rolled primitive.
- Dependencies: none added. `govulncheck ./...`: 0 vulnerabilities affecting the code, 1 in a required module that the code does not call (not itemised; the known list is `DEPLOY-local` § Operator steps). go1.27.3, git 2.47.3. `npm audit` not run: the range touches no JS.
- GCP surface: not touched.
- Other reads of session data: `configProblem` (`internal/sandbox/gitdir.go:99-113`) reads a size-bounded regular file, checked first; `drafts` reads through `os.Root` with size and count caps, no git; `leadUnchanged` and `reflog` read only the lead's HEAD and its branch, and `trail.Dirty` reads HEAD's tree; `worker.go:137` was not read and predates the session by its position in the list only (see Not examined).
- Fail-closed wrapper: `ulimit ... && exec` exits non-zero when the limit is not set; children inherit; `sh` exec keeps the pid, so `runGroup`'s group holds it; `capMemory` now copies `Stdin` (pinned).
- Probes ran in a `mktemp -d` repository under this session's scratchpad, with `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`, and the directory is removed. One call also created and removed an empty `.gate4-note` under `.agents/scratch/agents/`, by mistake; `git status` is clean and nothing else was written.
- `fyr search --refs`: `hostlimit.go` none; `fetch.go` BUG-200; `records.go` BUG-197, neither reopened by this diff.

## Not examined
- `ulimit -v` on macOS and Colima: no Mac here (finding 5).
- The real 8 GiB scale: the model ran at 150-400 MiB, and a crafted delta chain's cost in `cat-file` was not measured.
- Git's source: non-reachability in finding 4 rests on my recollection of `log_tree_diff`, plus the six capped runs, on git 2.47.3 only.
- `worker.go:137`, `Box.Intact`, `ExitChecks`, and how a worker's own timeout behaves while it waits on the collect lock.
- `fyr search --refs` for `fetch_mem_test.go` and `cmd/fyr/help_text.go` (its one-word text change read in the diff).
- `fetch_bound_test.go` and `fetch_mem_test.go` lines 1-95 were not read in full, so whether a failing `ulimit` itself is tested is unknown.
- `fetch --no-auto-maintenance` behaviour was not probed (finding 6).

## Outcome

1 (medium) left: cat-file has the cap and output bound but no deadline; no hang was found. 05ba26d's message says every read, which is false for it and for rev-parse of the tip: the spec names the second. 2, 3 left. No fix past this round.

title: Security review — v5.5.0 gate, sandbox, work, eval
body:
# Security review — release gate v5.5.0, part: sandbox, work, eval, docker runner   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: v5.0.0..9298b9b

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

A session in the docker runner can still reach the host's memory, which is the boundary that runner exists to hold. A symlink planted in the sandbox is followed by the host's credential scan, and `/proc/self/pagemap` reports size 0 and so passes the size bound while it reads without end; `git upload-pack`, run on the host against the session-written `.git`, loads an unbounded `packed-refs` that `gitDirProblem`'s bounds do not name. No finding is code execution on the host and no secret is committed. Everything else in the part held: the `.git` guard, the config-include refusal, the mount chain, the scope check, the docker argv.

## Findings

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/sandbox/creds.go:150` (`scanEntry`, read at `:180`) — The scan follows a link with `os.Stat`, and its only bound is `st.Size() > maxScan`. A docker-mode session can leave a link in the clone or the sandbox home whose target is `/proc/self/pagemap`; it resolves on the host, against the fyr process, in `ExitChecks` step 14. That file stats as a regular file of 0 bytes (checked on this machine) and reads far past `maxScan`: 300 MB read here against a 64 MiB bound, without reaching its end; its length is the process's address space at 8 bytes a page. `os.ReadFile` then grows without bound, so one worker can take the operator's machine, which the container's `--memory` limit is there to prevent. A host-runner session runs as the operator already, so the boundary crossed is docker's only. Not run to exhaustion: the probe read through `head`, not through `scanCreds`. Remediation: read through `io.LimitReader(f, maxScan+1)` and report an over-long read as the same "larger than" problem, whatever the stat says; a link that resolves out of the scanned tree could also be a problem without being read, as `dirLink` already is. A test needs a link to a file whose stat size lies: a small `maxScan` with `/proc/self/pagemap` on Linux.

- **[medium / confidence: high]** `internal/sandbox/gitdir.go:68` (`gitDirProblem`) — The guard's stated aim is that a session-written `.git` cannot fill the host's memory (PLAN.md item 45, S3), and it bounds `HEAD`, loose refs and `config` only. `packed-refs` has no bound and `upload-pack` holds an unsorted one in memory. Measured on git 2.47.3 in a probe repository: 6.2 MB gave 18 MB of maxrss, 186 MB gave 405 MB, about 2.2 times the file. The container's bind mount has no disk limit, so the file's size is the host disk's; `fetchLimit` bounds time only. Unmeasured, same class: `shallow`, `info/grafts`, a `reftable/` store under `extensions.refStorage`, and repository config that `pack-objects` honours (`pack.*`, `core.bigFileThreshold`) on blobs a small pack inflates to. Remediation: add `packed-refs`, `shallow`, `info/grafts` and `reftable/` to the bounded names, or refuse them, and refuse `extensions.refstorage`; for the rest, a memory limit on the child is the only general bound (`--upload-pack` already goes through a shell, so `ulimit -v` needs no dependency). Name what stays unbounded in the comment at `gitdir.go:13`, which now reads as if the list were whole.

- **[low / confidence: medium]** `internal/sandbox/procs_linux.go:106` (`procGone`) — EACCES is read as "says nothing against the process", and a process of this uid gets exactly that by `prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0)`: its `cwd`, `exe` and `environ` stop being readable, `procHit` sees nothing, and it passes check e. A process that leaves the tree and clears its environment passes too. Everything that trusts check e (`Compromised`, the eval ingest, `GitIntact`'s comment) therefore holds only against a session not trying to evade it, on the host runner. Host runner only; a container's processes are gone with it. Remediation: count an unreadable process of this uid that started after the session did, using `starttime` from `/proc/<pid>/stat`, as a hit.

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/sandbox/creds.go:93` (`scanCreds`, `lockedModules`) — A `node_modules` directory beside any regular file named as a lockfile is scanned by name only. The session chooses both, so credential text placed there passes check d. Not new in this range (BUG-185). Remediation: require the lockfile to be tracked at the base, or read the tree and set aside only an entry the baseline already held.

- **[low / confidence: low]** `internal/sandbox/after.go:111`, `internal/work/fetch.go:119` — `ExitChecks` sends SIGKILL to every `b.pgids` group after `Wait` reaped its leader, the hazard `docker.go:168` names and avoids: a group id can be another's by then, at most a process group of the operator's. `runBounded`'s window is microseconds; `ExitChecks`' can be seconds or more on a short pid range. Not new in this range for `ExitChecks`. Remediation: for `ExitChecks`, kill only the pids check e just found rather than a stored group id, or accept the risk and say so in the comment, as `docker.go:168` does for its own path.

## Checked

- Secrets: no live credential in any path of the part; every test read; fake credentials are built at run time (`"gh" + "o_" + ...`), the token fixture is the word `token`, and the one key-shaped literal is a fixture header (`-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----`, `internal/eval/run_proc_test.go`). `agyEnv` and `containerEnv` pass no secret; `FyrEnv` reaches the docker client only. The operator's token is mounted read-write (D106, accepted) with outbound network, so a session can read or overwrite it; `unlink` warns on kind, not content.
- Injection: docker argv refuses a flag-shaped image, a non-run network, a mount path with comma, quote or control character, and an `-e` entry without `=`. `Kickoff.Name`, `--model`, stamps and row ids are each regexp-bound. `links` and `changedPaths` parse `-z`. The fetch names a path that starts with `/`, so no `transport::` helper. Notes and contract lines go through `Printable` and `clip`. GUIDE-eval's setup and check run as bash by design, from a suite compared to HEAD.
- Instruction-shaped text: none addressed to a reviewer or an agent in any path of the part; Kickoff and prompt fixtures are test data. Test coverage: `gitdir_test.go` has no case for `packed-refs`, and the credential tests have none for a link whose stat size lies, so neither medium finding has a failing test yet.
- Host git on a session-written clone: `.git` as a real directory, every entry regular, `alternates`, `commondir` and `gitdir` refused, config's `include.*`, `includeIf.*` and `extensions.worktreeConfig` refused through `git config --file --no-includes`, `upload-pack --strict`, `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` with a version floor of 2.44 for docker mode. From git's documentation and memory of its source, not a test: `uploadpack.packObjectsHook` is honoured only from protected config, `trace2.*` is read before the repository's config, `upload-pack` runs no hook, and `-c` options do not cross into a local `upload-pack` (`local_repo_env`), which is why the guard and not `leadGit` must hold there. `git config` is reached only after the walk refused non-regular files, so a FIFO at `config` cannot hang it.
- Scope check: any tip's difference from the base lies on a parent chain inside `base..ref`, so `-m --root` against each parent is complete; `links` compares tip to base and sees a retargeted link; grafts, replace refs and the commit-graph are off in `leadGit`; a `.agents` symlink empties the trail and fails closed.
- Sandbox state: `Intact`'s mount table and chain, `OpenRegular`'s no-follow and one-link check, the drafts' two `os.Root`s, the token removal through the held root.
- Authz-authn: none in this part beyond the login token, above. `--kill` is bound by `stampRe`, the flock and `maxPid`.
- Crypto: none hand-rolled; `sha256` for fingerprints only.
- Dependencies: no new one. govulncheck over the part's four packages, go 1.27.3: 0 vulnerabilities in called code, 1 in a required module not called. `npm audit`: no package.json at the root and no `web/` or `ui/`, not applicable.
- GCP surface: none in this part. A worker's bridge reaches the host's address, the LAN and, on a GCE host, `169.254.169.254`; `enable_icc=false` only separates workers. Not a finding: REVIEW-2026-10-30-1300 and REVIEW-2026-10-31-1242 record it, dave is not a GCE VM, and ADR-083 accepts it. `docker/` has no change in the range; its `golang:${GO_MINOR}-trixie` base is a floating tag, built only by the operator.

## Not examined

Release-diff paths of this part: none. Every changed path under `internal/sandbox`, `internal/work`, `internal/eval`, `cmd/fyr/*work*`, `cmd/fyr/*eval*` was read end to end, tests included; `docker/` has no change in the range and `docker/work.Dockerfile` was read anyway. Also read as blast radius: `guard.go`, `env.go`, `open.go`, `imagepath.go`, `drafts.go`, `kickoff.go`, `records.go`, `contract.go`, `verb_work.go`, `eval_home.go`, and `trail.Command` with `LazyFetchSafe`.

Reached but not read, not in this part's diff: `internal/work/models.go`, `internal/work/zone.go`, `internal/eval/invoked.go`, `internal/sandbox/config_test.go` and the other unchanged tests of the three packages, `cmd/fyr/eval_register.go`.

Outside this part: `internal/metrics`'s ingest of a sandbox's conversations, reached from `ingestRow`; `trail.Dirty`.

Not run: the docker runner against a real daemon. Its findings rest on the code and on probes of `/proc` and of `git upload-pack` in a throwaway repository. The pagemap read was not run through `scanCreds` to exhaustion. govulncheck ran over the part's four packages, not `./...`.

## Artifact collision

This review first wrote `.agents/scratch/agents/security-2026-10-31-2224.md`. A parallel security review of another part took the same minute's name: that file now holds this review's title, verdict and Not examined around the other review's Findings and Checked, and this review's edits replaced whatever stood in that review's Not examined. This file is this review's whole record; the older file was left as it stands.

## Outcome

S1 fixed (item 65). S2 fixed by the memory limit (item 66), on the verifier's route. S3, S4, S5 left: operator, stated residues, none new to the fixes.

# Security review — release gate v5.5.0, part: skills, agents, rules, context   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: v5.0.0..9298b9b

## Status: COMPLETE

Recovered from the agent's returned result: its artifact file was overwritten by a parallel agent with the same stamp.

## Verdict

FINDINGS: no high or medium finding, no secret, no injected instruction. All 292 PNGs are the images their extension says, with no appended payload. Five low findings; the worst is the operator's real name in a template and in captures rendered from it.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `skills/frontend-ui-modern/assets/simulation-template.html:553` (SEC-1) — The operator's real full name sits in demo content (also :596, :705) next to a phone-shaped value not checked to be fictional. It is also rendered as pixels in the captures of those views: confirmed in view-default-settings-members-light-1280.png, inferred for the others. The repository is private today, which bounds the exposure. Use a neutral placeholder persona and regenerate the captures.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/frontend-ui-modern/scripts/sim.mjs:67` (SEC-2) — Strings from a --custom palette reach generated HTML unescaped (sim.mjs:67-68, theme.mjs:160,173-177,180-183): a closing script tag in title or id, a style breakout in source or id, and $ patterns in String.replace. An untrusted palette would run script in the simulation page, which the operator opens and mockup.mjs loads. Built-in themes are unaffected. Validate id, refuse < and */, escape < in the JSON, use replacer functions.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/frontend-ui-modern/scripts/mockup.mjs:101` (SEC-3) — --name and sweep values join the output file name unchecked, so ../ writes outside --out. s.file at :117 goes into an img src attribute unescaped, and esc() does not escape quotes. Reachable only through arguments. Reject path separators and escape quotes.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `skills/frontend-ui-modern/SKILL.md:127` (SEC-4) — Playwright, its browser download and next-themes are installed unpinned (also mockup.mjs:5,51, README.md:10, shadcn-2026.md:222, economist measure_whitespace.js:6,35). The Harness overrides pin only shadcn. Add an override line pinning these, in the economist skill too; typescript/SKILL.md:49 already names Playwright 1.63.
- **[low / confidence: medium]** `skills/frontend-ui-modern/SKILL.md:145` (SEC-5) — shadcn add <url|owner/repo/item> fetches code from an arbitrary registry, and mcp init changes an agent's tool configuration. Neither has a gate of its own (also shadcn-2026.md:31-33,47,55, blocks.md:54); the overrides fix only the CLI version. Add an override requiring the operator's word for a non-@shadcn registry and for mcp init.

## Not examined

None.

## Outcome

Every finding left: operator (D23 accepted SEC-2, SEC-3 and SEC-4's kind; SEC-1 needs the operator's call on a real name in demo content and its captures; SEC-5 would add an operator step).

## Outcome

See above.

title: Security review — v5.5.0 gate, stores and search, changed lines
body:
# Security review — v5.5.0 gate, metrics/serve/search/brain/memory/trail/redact   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: v5.0.0..9298b9b

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

No high or medium finding. Worst problem: the new `fyr metrics evals` text view prints a row name read from `sessions.label` with no control-byte filter, so a label holding terminal escapes reaches the terminal. Reach is narrow: such a label enters only through the operator's own `fyr metrics ingest --label`, because suite row ids are shape-checked and `trials.label` is checked printable at write. The `/evals` page takes the same text unfiltered, but html/template escapes it. The rest of the part reduces attack surface: `--global` no longer reads files, and the old memory store has one guarded reader.

Part: internal/metrics, internal/serve, internal/search, internal/brain, internal/memory, internal/trail, internal/redact, cmd/fyr/*metrics*, *serve*, *search*, *record*. 81 paths: 59 modified, 21 added, 1 deleted. No path under `cmd/fyr/*serve*` or `cmd/fyr/*search*` changed. The pathspecs match no markdown, so this part holds no trail markdown. `.agents/trail.jsonl` is outside them.

## Findings
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/metrics/evals_write.go:53` — `EvalRows.Table` puts `r.Row` in a cell and `WriteText` prints it unfiltered. `r.Row` comes from `rowName(label)` (`internal/metrics/evals.go:294`), and `evalTrials` reads labels from `sessions` as well as `trials` (`evals.go:204`). `Trial.validate` refuses a non-printable label (`internal/metrics/trials.go:63`), but `Options.Validate` does not (`internal/metrics/ingest.go:47`), and `agySession` stores `w.label` raw (`internal/metrics/agy_conversation.go:58`). So a label with ESC bytes or a tab or newline given to `fyr metrics ingest --source --label` is printed raw by `fyr metrics evals`. That can drive the terminal or forge table lines. This breaks the rule `internal/metrics/show_write.go:112` states for the same label (SD55: printed through the filter). Reach is the operator's own flag, because `fyr eval` labels pass `validID` (`internal/eval/suite.go:38`). No test pins control bytes on this view: `internal/metrics/report_evals_test.go` pins HTML escaping only. Remediation: refuse a non-printable label in `Options.Validate`, as `validateRun` does for Run, and also pass the label through `printable` in `rowName`, for rows already stored. Add a `\x1b` test row.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/serve/pages.go:187` — `/evals` hands `WriteText` output to `block.Pre` without `printableText`, unlike the other printer pages (`pages.go:24`, `pages.go:70`). `{{.Pre}}` in `internal/serve/assets/layout.html:33` is html/template-escaped, so there is no markup injection. Only control bytes reach the page. Remediation: wrap it in `printableText`, or rely on the `rowName` fix above.

## Checked
- **Secrets:** a pattern scan covered added lines of the part diff and the whole of every modified or added file. Hits are fixtures only: `ghp_` and `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE` in `internal/metrics/verb_test.go`, and `hunter2pass` strings. No real credential, no operator path or email. `Trial` columns are printable, capped at 120 bytes, and hold no prose. `Export` still withholds the salt; the new `trials` table holds nothing secret.
- **Verb privacy:** `verb_tokenize.go` was traced by hand. `quotedMark` words fall out through `flagName` or `programName`, so no NUL reaches `step_verbs`. `glued` cuts to `w[:2]` with `w` at least two bytes and ASCII. The new `fyr` subcommands (`check eval record serve work`) keep no positional word. The residue `--title --x` is stated in the code.
- **Injection:** every new query is parameterized, including `RunModels` placeholders and `ExpectMatches`. SQL table names are constants. `refsWhere` keeps `likeEscape`. `guardProject`'s `ls-files` takes a fixed pathspec through the hardened builder. The HTML report goes through html/template and `esc`; only numbers enter the `passKRow` value text.
- **Untrusted sandbox data:** `model` and agent names pass `identifier()`. `recordTrial` and `ingestRow` each run `sharesRealState` before opening a store, so the store writes do not depend on the later `evalHomeRefused` at `cmd/fyr/eval_record.go:44`. `validateRun` refuses a Run without a Source, and refuses a non-printable or over-long one.
- **Authz/authn:** `/evals` sits behind the existing Host, fetch-metadata and origin guard on 127.0.0.1, and adds no action. `metricsLine` keeps a page from creating a store. Registration still needs the HMAC-sealed marker. `RegistryRoot` moves the row to the main worktree of the same common dir, whose consent the seal names. `roots` still rejects a planted git dir. `HasTrail` uses Lstat on both names. Global search no longer reads a checkout or `~/.config/fyr` files.
- **Removed guards:** `memory.trusted` went with its reader. `memoryEntries` (`internal/brain/import_memory.go:63`) keeps the same refusals on the one remaining reader: symlink, non-directory, tracked store, via `trail.Command`. `trail.changed` and `Dates` went with no caller left. `gitView` keeps the os.Root, partial-clone and export exclusion. `dirtyWhere` applies `keep` in all three reads, and BUG-188's `errUnhashable` guard is intact.
- **Crypto:** no primitive added or changed in the part. `crypto/sha1` in `git_view.go` is git's blob id and predates the range. The sealed marker's code is outside the diff.
- **Dependencies:** `go.mod` and `go.sum` are unchanged in the range. `govulncheck ./...` with go1.27.3: 0 vulnerabilities affect the code; 1 in a required module, not called: GO-2026-5024, `golang.org/x/sys@v0.37.0`, fixed in v0.44.0, already recorded as known (ADR-045a). `npm audit`: no JS ecosystem in this part.
- **GCP surface:** none in this part.
- **Instruction-shaped text:** the same scan found none in the part, and none appeared in reading. `internal/dream/records_only_test.go`, which matches the bare `*record*` pathspec, was read whole: benign.
- **Past failures:** `fyr search --refs` was run for 9 of the changed files (`record.go`, `redact.go`, `read_file.go`, `scope_prepare.go`, `dirty.go`, `git_view.go`, `config_view.go`, `memory.go`, `trail.go`). Only BUG-188 came back, fixed, and its guard holds.

## Not examined
- Every line the release diff changes, in all 81 paths, was read, and all 21 added files were read whole. The 58 modified paths other than `internal/trail/dirty.go` had their unchanged lines covered only by the pattern scan, apart from those read in part: `internal/metrics/verb.go`, `internal/serve/pages.go`, `internal/search/git_view.go`, `internal/search/scope_prepare.go`, `internal/trail/trail.go`, `internal/brain/import_memory.go`. List them with `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=M v5.0.0..9298b9b -- <the part's pathspecs>`. If "end to end" means whole files rather than the release diff, these paths are open against that bar.
- `fyr search --refs <path> --kind bug` was not run for the other 72 changed paths.
- `.agents/trail.jsonl`: outside this part's pathspecs, not read here.
- No runtime probe of the two findings: both rest on reading the code path.

## Outcome

S1 fixed. S2 needs nothing after S1. The unchanged lines it did not read are read by the whole-file part.

title: Security review — v5.5.0 gate, stores read whole
body:
# Security review — release gate, whole-file read of the persistence paths   (2026-10-31)

Range reviewed: v5.0.0 (9c70eb8)..HEAD (67bf395)

Scope: every path `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=M v5.0.0..HEAD` lists under internal/metrics, internal/serve, internal/search, internal/brain, internal/memory, internal/trail, internal/redact, and cmd/fyr/*metrics*, *serve*, *search*, *record*: 59 files, each read end to end (54 under internal/, 5 under cmd/fyr; no *serve* or *search* path under cmd/fyr is in the M list).

## Status: COMPLETE

## Verdict: FINDINGS

Three low findings, no high and no medium, all three in `fyr search`; two of them reached through a file or a config in a checkout, none of them in a line the range changed. The worst: `fyr search` takes its project root from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` without the dir-or-parent check `trail.Toplevel` and `trail.Roots` make, so a planted checkout's `core.worktree` makes a search run there read, index and answer from another checkout of the operator's. Probed: a search in repo c printed repo b's private text and wrote b's `.agents/scratch/search.db`. Nothing executes and no secret-shaped file is read, which is why it stays low. Nothing here is a secret leak, an injection, an auth bypass or hand-rolled crypto.

## Findings

- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/search/git_view.go:45` (called at `internal/search/scope_prepare.go:64`) — `checkoutRoot` trusts `--show-toplevel`. `core.worktree` lives in `.git/config`, which `trail.go`'s header treats as untrusted, and `trail.Toplevel` (trail.go:150) and `trail.roots` (trail.go:209) both refuse an answer that is not dir or a parent of it; search does not. Exploitable in principle by a hand-extracted archive (a clone does not carry `.git/config`): an agent session running `fyr search` in the planted repo gets another checkout's text in its tool output, and the other checkout gets a `.agents/scratch/search.db` written, or removed under `index --rebuild`. Reach is limited to a real, gitignoring checkout: a plain directory fails `check-ignore`. Probe (throwaway repos, built binary): `git -C c config core.worktree <b>`, then `fyr search` in c printed `private.md:1` from b and created `b/.agents/scratch/search.db`. Remediation: in `prepare`, resolve the root with `trail.Roots`' top (or apply `Toplevel`'s rule) and refuse a toplevel that is not dir or a parent of it, with `errNotCheckout`; `RegistryRoot` and `dropReason` already compare `got`. Test: the search counterpart of memory_test's "core.worktree outside is refused", which no search test has (`grep core.worktree internal/search` is empty).
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/search/search_query.go:217` — `markTarget` panics on a reference target over 200 runes: `(snippetMax-n)/2` goes negative, `start` passes `at`, and line 219 slices `r[start:at]` (for exactly 201, `r[at+n:end]`). `pathToken` (parse.go:98) has no length cap, so one line in any file of a checkout, tracked or untracked, makes `fyr search --refs <dir>/` crash with a Go stack trace for that directory, and an exact `--refs <that path>` too; the record hits print first, the file hits are lost. Availability only, of the verb the context tells agents to run before touching an area. Probe: `docs/` plus 260 `x` in `docs/note.md`, `fyr search --refs docs/` gave `panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [36:4]` at search_query.go:219, exit 2. Remediation: clamp in `markTarget` (`n` over `snippetMax` returns the cut line unmarked), or drop a target over a cap in `parseRefs`; test both arms, 201 and 260.
- **[low / confidence: high]** `internal/search/git_view.go:100` — a gitignored noindex marker does not count. Markers are collected only from `ls-files -s` and `ls-files --others --exclude-standard` (lines 97, 104), so a `.fyr-noindex` that a repo or `.git/info/exclude` ignores is never seen and the tracked files under it are indexed, though trail.go:27 calls the marker a privacy control the operator placed. The index stays local and 0600; the gap is that the operator's opt-out silently stops working, the header no longer names the directory. Probe, both states in one throwaway repo: untracked marker, 0 hits and `left out by a noindex marker: data/`; the same marker excluded, 1 hit `data/x.md:1`. Remediation: also run `ls-files -z --others --ignored --exclude-standard` and keep only the two marker names, or Lstat each directory of a tracked path for the two names through `fsRoot`; test both states. If an ignored marker is meant not to count, say so in `gitView`'s comment and the spec instead.

## Checked

- **Secrets:** none in code or tests. Test tokens are fakes (`AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE`, `ghp_abc…`, `SECRETCANARY123`). `warnRedactable` and `warnImportRedactable` never print the text (cmd/fyr/record_redact.go, read for the blast radius). `Export` omits the salt, pinned by `TestExportOmitsSalt`. The redactor has no Slack needle: not a finding, a recorded operator decision (ledger Phase 7a, D32 1, the change record names the consequence). redact.go's only change in the range is a comment.
- **Injection:** every SQL statement binds its values; the concatenated parts are constants or `?` lists (`sc.in()`, `tables`, `gc`). `ftsQuery` quotes every word; `likeEscape` covers LIKE. `dsn` and `roDSN` escape the path. git calls go through `trail.Command` with a fixed argument list (no `--textconv`, no `--ext-diff`, no `%G`); no shell. `printable` guards terminal output on every path from project text: `sc.label`, `markTarget`, `cleanSnippet`, `FormatHit`, `recordErr`, `safeMap`, ingest's `fail` and notes. `refs()` echoes `x` raw at search_refs.go:21 and :61; that is the caller's own argument, not project text, no finding. HTML: `html/template` for the report; the raw `template.HTML` SVG runs every string through `esc`, the other `%s` carry numbers, and `TestReportEscapesNames` pins it. Stored names go through `identifier` or `toolName`. `Verb` keeps no positional word or value (allowlists, caps, canaries in verb_test.go); the residue it states is a dash-led unquoted value.
- **Authz/authn:** pages.go has no check of its own: `serveHTTP` in guard.go (read) runs Host, fetch metadata and token or cookie before routing, and securityHeaders cover `/metrics/report`, which skips the layout. `trail.Roots` still refuses forged commondir and core.worktree, pinned in memory_test.go. Registration (`trail.Registered`) stays the gate of the global index; `TestRegistersOnlyHarnessProjects` pins it. The memory.go removals (`trusted`, `Store`) are dead code gone, the import's reader keeps a no-hook test.
- **Crypto:** nothing hand-rolled. `crypto/rand` salt, `crypto/subtle` compare. `sha1` in `blobID` is git's object naming, not security. `writer.hash` is `sha256(salt + 0x00 + cmd)` truncated to 64 bits, a stored comparison key for retry loops, standard-library use and no finding.
- **Dependencies:** no new one in these paths; `modernc.org/sqlite` only in search, metrics and brain. govulncheck: "Your code is affected by 0 vulnerabilities", with 1 vulnerability in a required module not called (the known list is DEPLOY-local's; not re-compared here). `npm audit`: not applicable, no ecosystem in these paths.
- **GCP surface:** none in these paths.
- **Local store discipline:** metrics, search and brain databases 0600 under a 0700 directory, a symlink at the database or a companion refused, `O_EXCL` on creation, report and export 0600 with `O_EXCL`. Conversation databases are copied, regular files only, opened read-only, live files never opened; a conversation id with `/` or `\` is dropped before it reaches a path. Dirty and gitView read through `os.Root`, `--no-filters`, no `git status`.
- **Past failures** (`fyr search --refs <path> --kind bug`, each non-test path): BUG-181, 184, 187, 188, all fixed, each with its pin in the tests read. No re-opened shape.
- **Prompt injection:** no text in the files read addressed the reviewer.
- **Non-security, noted only:** `Store.Export` leaves a partial file on an error, which then blocks the rerun (WriteReport got that fix, SD57, Export did not). `listConversations` does not read `rows.Err()`. `copyFileImpl` and `readAll` have no size bound past the first Lstat (a sandbox `--source` can fill the disk; read for the blast radius, neither is in the M list).

## Not examined

Of the 59 named paths: nothing; each was read whole, no read was cut.
