title: Delivery, and what stays on the machine — what this harness is building toward
body:
# Delivery, and what stays on the machine — what this harness is building toward

The picture in one place, because the operator is discarding the agent's memory and the trail has to carry everything on its own. Written 2026-09-17, the zip place added 2026-09-28. What is DECIDED lives in `PRD.md` R7, R8 and R9, ADR-030, ADR-033, ADR-038 and ADR-062 (§ The model below is their one-paragraph statement); what is PLANNED lives in `PLAN-2026-09-17-delivery-rework`; this document is the narrative that makes both readable to someone arriving cold.

Re-read 2026-10-31 against `825ff6f` (`PLAN.md` P11: `frontend-ui-economist` and `frontend-ui-modern` replace `frontend`; under this spec's code only skill text, `TestInstallLeavesClaudeCodeAlone`'s guard and `TestSuiteHarness`'s `want` changed): nothing here changes.

Re-read 2026-10-31 against `bd2d6b4` (`PLAN.md` P10b, ADR-087: a dream reads records only, the global index holds no file, reversing the P10a line below that it holds `~/.config/fyr`'s files; `trail.Dates`, `memory.Store` and `harness.LastRetro` go, the search schema is 3, eval's setup gets `FYR`, and `record import --dry-run` prints no stored count): nothing else here changes.

Re-read 2026-10-31 against `238e7f1` (`PLAN.md` P7: `checkManagedTree` in `internal/harness/inventory.go` reads its directory list from the new `harness.ManagedDirs`, the same six names): nothing here changes.

## The problem, in the operator's words

> "I want the delivery to be around the fyr only. Nothing else. I'm the sole user of this harness and decide everything but I install it on multiple places and when I decide to update the repo I want a smart way to push any updates to places where I use it."

And the loop back, asked for on 2026-09-17 and withdrawn on 2026-10-24 (ADR-062):

> "Some sort of feedback function from each place installed reporting back to the main is good for a feedback loop so we can take experiences from each installed place to use to make the harness better."

> "… remove the report back to styrman-harness-feedback repo. This should be removed also."

## The four places

Every place runs the Antigravity CLI only (ADR-062).

| Where | How it is driven |
|---|---|
| Work Mac | The operator runs `fyr update` |
| Home Mac | The operator runs `fyr update` |
| A Linux project host | The operator runs `fyr update` |
| A second Linux project host | The operator runs `fyr update` |

The normal flow is deliberately dull: the operator edits this repository, is happy with it, then goes to each place and runs one command. There is no push, no timer that has to work, no service that has to be up. A timer is a convenience some machines add; it is not the mechanism.

## The model

The one statement of what a tag delivers, to which kind of place, and how a place moves forward; every other living file points here (project `AGENTS.md` § How the harness works, rule 6). A **checkout place** follows `main`: `fyr update` fetches, refuses a dirty checkout, fast-forwards, rebuilds the binary from the checkout and reinstalls; a tag changes nothing for it. A **binary-only place** moves only when a new `vX.Y.Z` tag is published: `fyr update` downloads the newest release's binary (a canonical `vX.Y.Z` tag, newer than the running one), checks the binary against the release's `SHA256SUMS` (integrity only: no key signs a release, and who made it rests on the operator's GitHub credential and HTTPS, as for a checkout place; ADR-053), replaces `~/.local/bin/fyr` and installs the harness embedded in it. A tag is therefore a release marker that also carries the binaries a binary-only place updates to; nothing is ever pushed to any machine, and a tag without its assets is a marker no place can update to (R8, R9; ADR-033, superseding ADR-030 D2).

A **zip place** fetches nothing and holds no tag: the operator downloads the repository zip by hand — a browser, `git archive`, whatever reaches GitHub — and runs `fyr update --from-zip <file>`, which unpacks it into a temporary directory under `~/.config/fyr/` (beside the zip when that directory does not exist yet, as on a first dry run), refuses any entry that would leave that directory, installs the unpacked tree with the RUNNING binary, and deletes the directory; nothing is kept on disk but the manifest's `zip:sha256:<hex>` marker, which also records whether the zip was verified. It moves forward only when the operator repeats the download and `--from-zip` — there is no tag to follow and no release to poll — and nothing in the zip replaces the binary — the running binary is installed as every install installs it — so a zip whose harness needs a newer binary needs that binary downloaded by hand too. A release zip is checked against the release's `SHA256SUMS` when it sits beside it, and refused on any mismatch, while a zip without it — a zip of `main`, which has nothing to verify, or a release zip downloaded alone — is installed marked `UNVERIFIED`, because the zip place is the fallback for a machine that cannot take the normal way in (ADR-039, ADR-041) (R8, R9's zip-place sub-bullet; ADR-038). This differs from the existing plain-copy fallback below in what is kept: a plain copy is a tree someone unpacked and left on disk, installed by a binary BUILT FROM that same tree; a zip place keeps no tree at all — the archive is unpacked, installed with the binary already running, and removed, so there is nothing left to build from or diff against (ADR-038 D8, superseding ADR-034 for this one path: a release binary now installs a tree on disk when the operator names it with `--from-zip`, never a recorded or discovered one). A development build carries no harness and no zip replaces it, so it never moves a zip place forward: there `status` reports from the manifest alone, `update` is refused (exit 1) naming the two ways the place moves — a newer release zip run with that release's binary, or `fyr install --repo <checkout>`, which makes it a checkout place — and `--from-zip` installs the zip's harness and says the binary did not move; at a place installed from a tree its `--from-zip` is refused, so a development build never turns a checkout place into a zip place (ADR-082, BUG-203).

**The crossing to `fyr` (v3.0.0).** v3.0.0 publishes `fyr` assets only, under the one marker `# fyr vX.Y.Z` in `SHA256SUMS`, so a place on v2.7.0 or earlier does not move forward by its own `update`: an old binary finds no asset it asks for, a checkout's old build path no longer exists, and nothing is replaced. Each place is reinstalled by hand once, by `DEPLOY-remote` § Crossing to fyr; after that it moves forward as its kind always did.

## How a machine gets the harness

Three ways, and no fourth:

1. **A checkout the operator owns**, kept current with `fyr update` (§ The model). This is the normal path. The dirty-checkout refusal runs before the `--check` and `--dry-run` returns: on a checkout with uncommitted changes both print the real run's refusal and exit 1; a clean one exits 2 when behind and 0 when current.
2. **A release binary**, installed with `fyr install` and moved forward by `fyr update` (§ The model). One downloaded file carrying `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `commands/` and `rules/` inside it, for a place that only USES the harness: the operator wanted no trail of this repository (then a docs tree, now `.agents/trail.jsonl`) sitting beside their other projects, where a session opened there could mistake it for the project's own. What `update` does there is § The model. That place changes only when a release is cut (ADR-033).
3. **A zip place**, moved forward by the operator repeating a download and `fyr update --from-zip <file>` (§ The model). For a machine that can hold neither the operator's SSH key nor run `gh` — a corporate workstation, say — and so can reach neither of the other two (ADR-038).

A plain copy with no `.git` still installs, and `update` refuses it with a message naming `install` still deploying it as it is and the alternatives above; it is no longer one of the ways in: it is the fallback for a machine that can reach none of them, and it differs from a zip place in what is kept — a plain copy is a tree someone unpacked and left on disk, while a zip place keeps no tree (§ The model).

Authentication is the operator's own SSH key and `gh` login, present on every machine because they log in as themselves. That is why no deploy keys, tokens or per-machine credentials exist anywhere in this design — they would restrict nothing and add key management. The accepted cost is theirs, stated plainly: "if I don't login in with ssh or gh I can't get updates." A release download needs that same credential, because the repository is private; a zip download needs it too, for the same reason; the plain copy is the fallback when that bites.

## What keeps consumers from changing the harness

Part shape, part credential. Only the four checkouts are repositories, and they belong to the operator. Everything downstream of them receives installed FILES: `fyr install` writes the context, skills, agents, commands and rules into a home and never creates a checkout there. But a checkout is not what changing the harness takes — a credential that can push to this repository is, and anything that reaches the operator's SSH key or `gh` login can clone and push, after which every place's `update` deploys it. So a home seeded for agents is read-only only when it reaches no such credential: no forwarded ssh-agent, no `gh` token, no readable key. The shape is provable here; the credential half is each host's to hold (security review 2026-09-17, finding 5).

State the shape as a property of `fyr install`, provable from this repository. Do not rest it on how any particular consumer seeds its homes — that was done once, in ADR-030 D4, and it is a dependency pointing the wrong way: if that consumer changes its entrypoint, a claim in this repository's decision record silently becomes false and nothing here would catch it. What `install` did is on its output, every run: one line per file it added, updated (including a previous file it could not read, written over as before), corrected the mode of, removed, or kept (a managed path already holds a file fyr did not write, left alone and counted separately), with the unchanged as a count; `--dry-run` prints the same lines and writes nothing (2026-09-18, the operator's "more info").

## What stays on the machine

Nothing comes back. A place's experience — the brain store (`brain.db`: every project's trail records and the global `feedback`, `retro` and `proposal` records), the search index (`search.db`), the metrics store (`metrics.db`) and the install manifest (`state.json`) — stays in `~/.config/fyr/` on the machine that wrote it (R7, ADR-062, ADR-071). The logs a place kept before the brain store (`feedback.jsonl`, `retros.jsonl`, `proposals/*.md`) are read into it by `fyr record import --global`, which lists them for the operator to remove; they are not where experience lives. The `report` verb and the `styrman-harness-feedback` repository it pushed to are gone; no verb and no code path replaces them, and no export bundle was built (plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` D4). A harness-target proposal — a global `proposal` record that `/retro`, the dreamer or `fyr auto` queued — reaches this repository only by the operator's own hands (`/retro --harness`, run in a harness checkout on the machine whose queue it reads) or, when the operator turned `fyr auto` on at level `harness`, as an eval-gated commit to a skill or agent in that checkout, never pushed (R9, ADR-090).

Three things leave a machine, all to the model of the CLI the machine already uses (except a `missing-skill` worker's search of `skills.sh` with the pinned CLI; R8). The first is the dreamer's prompt: `fyr dream` sends each registered project's memory, trail, feedback and transcripts, redacted (`--all`, which the timer runs, takes only the projects registered with `fyr index --register`, ADR-068; `--project <root>`, typed by the operator, takes the root it names), to the model of the CLI the machine already uses, with no tool granted, headless in plan mode; in the operator's own Antigravity home when its settings grant no tool without review, where the conversation stays (R3's exception, ADR-047a, ADR-049, ADR-073; `SPEC-fyr-dream`). Its redaction (`internal/redact`) is structural, with no JSON walk, and it is a safety net, not a guarantee. The credential needles — vendor token prefixes, and case-insensitive password, secret, token and api-key assignments, `Bearer` and authorization headers written `Authorization: …` (colon form, a quoted header name included; a header set by a call such as `Header.Set("Authorization", …)` is an unlisted shape), URL credentials (including an empty user), token shapes pinned by length and alphabet (a JWT, an OpenAI or Stripe key, an npm or Hugging Face token), and a bare userinfo token in a URL — LOCATE a secret and never define how much is removed: a whole text line, a whole JSONL record, or a whole `-----BEGIN`-to-`-----END` block goes. This is the design the operator chose at the report path's cold-read cap, and the reasoning outlived that path: `AKIA` is a prefix, so replacing the matched token strips the marker and ships the key; a private key's header matches while its body carries no needle at all. Any span shorter than a structural unit leaks while reporting success. Slack tokens and webhook URLs have no needle of their own, by the operator's choice (`PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` D32 1): one goes only when a generic rule takes its line, an assignment to a name holding a password, secret, token or api-key word, or an authorization header, so `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=https://hooks.slack.com/…` stays.

The second is `fyr eval`'s runs, started by the operator or, when `fyr auto` is turned on at level `harness`, by its hourly run (`eval-rerun` and the eval gate): each sandbox's prompts, and the files its agent reads in a clone of the fixture, go to that model unredacted, as in any session of that CLI, because the point is an agent working on the fixture as any session does (ADR-065, ADR-090; `SPEC-fyr-eval`, `SPEC-fyr-auto`). What eval writes stays on the machine: the sandboxes under the `--home` passed to it, `<home>/.config/fyr/eval/` (`fyr eval` refuses a missing `--home` and the real home), the `testing` record and the metrics rows.

The third is `fyr work`'s workers, started by the operator or, when `fyr auto` is turned on, by its hourly run: each worker is an unattended `agy` session in a sandbox under `<home>/.config/fyr/work/`, on a clone of the operator's checkout, and its prompts (for `fyr auto`'s learning tasks, a redacted input of the project's memory, open proposals, metric numbers and conversations) and the files its agent reads go to that model unredacted, as in any session of that CLI, and a `missing-skill` worker searches `skills.sh` with the pinned CLI (ADR-076, ADR-090; `SPEC-fyr-work`, `SPEC-fyr-auto`). The clone has no remote (`git remote remove origin` before the session starts), so git pushes it nowhere, though its agent runs with `command(*)` and the network and could still send what it reads elsewhere (`SPEC-fyr-work` § Data); the verb fetches the worker's branch back into the checkout by path and never pushes or merges. What a worker writes stays on the machine: the sandbox, the branch `work/<name>` and its drafts under `.agents/scratch/work/` in the checkout (or `~/.config/fyr/auto/drafts/` for an auto worker). The verb writes no store, so its default `--home` is the real home. A Kickoff now has a second way to reach a session besides the operator's paste (ADR-076 amends ADR-058a).

`~/.config/fyr/` is created 0700 and every install tightens it to 0700 when it is looser and the directory is the caller's own and not a symlink (either case gets a `note:` instead); the other verbs that write there create it 0700 when absent but leave an existing one's mode alone.

## What is deliberately NOT being built

- **A webservice**, for delivery or for feedback. Git already carries delivery, and nothing comes back. A service adds hosting, per-machine authentication and an attack surface, for one user, against R3, R4 and local-by-default.
- **A way back**, by any transport: the report path was removed on 2026-10-24 (ADR-062), and an export bundle was rejected as a new transport nobody asked for (plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` D4).
- **A signed-tag delivery channel.** ADR-026 designed one on 2026-09-16 to give a consumer host a trust root; ADR-030 withdrew it the next day because the operator authenticates as themselves everywhere, so it solved a problem that was not there. Tags survive as release markers — `v1.0.0` stands, and the versioning rule and the tag recipe stay in `DEPLOY-remote` (unsigned since v2.4.0, ADR-053); what a tag delivers today is § The model.
- **Vendored mirrors.** Two projects kept a `.git`-less copy refreshed by hand, which is why a mirror refresh kept appearing as a task in three repositories at once. They retire. Each consumer's own session does that work in its own repository.
- **Per-machine keys of any kind**, for the reason above.

## The rule that keeps this repository independent

> "styrman-harness and the feedback/trajectory should not be directly connected to any other project, if any other project wants to use the harness they need the fyr, that's it."

This repository names no consumer project in its living docs and depends on none. Knowing a consumer exists is fine; depending on its internals is not. The test is simple: **would the harness still be correct if every consumer vanished tomorrow?** If a document here needs another repository to be true, it is wrong, whatever it says.

This is easy to get wrong when several of those repositories sit side by side on one disk, because reading them costs nothing. It was got wrong once already, on 2026-09-17, in the same paragraph that stated the rule.

## Where things stand

**Built and shipped** (newest tag v5.5.0, 2026-11-01, which shipped `fyr metrics evals`, the eval suite's kinds, records-only reads for search and the dream, and the two UI skills; v5.0.0, 2026-10-31, shipped `fyr serve` and `fyr work` and the `work` skill (ADR-075, ADR-076), a MAJOR by the operator's choice; v4.1.0, 2026-10-29, made PRD, SDD, TDD and TODO the root documents (ADR-074); v3.0.0, 2026-10-26, was the first to ship the binary as `fyr`; every tag through v2.7.0 shipped it as `sh-agent`, renamed in plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` Phase 4a): `fyr` with install, sync, status, diff, update (checkout, release binary, `--from-zip`), uninstall, list, render, adopt, version, search and index (`SPEC-fyr-search`), memory and dream (`SPEC-fyr-memory-loop`, `SPEC-fyr-dream`) with the hourly timer that dreams only while an interactive `agy` session of the operator's runs, its unit named per home, over the projects registered with `index --register` (ADR-068; v4.0.0, with `fyr help`'s pages), and metrics (`SPEC-fyr-metrics`), with record (`SPEC-fyr-record`, ADR-063), check (`SPEC-fyr-check`, ADR-064) and eval (`SPEC-fyr-eval`, ADR-065) from v3.0.0; serve (`SPEC-fyr-serve`, ADR-075, ADR-075a, ADR-075b) from v5.0.0, its read pages and its two actions, `index` and `metrics ingest`; work (`SPEC-fyr-work`, ADR-076) from v5.0.0, several Kickoff files at once up to `--max-workers`, `--kill`, `--runner docker` and a model per worker; the context, 37 skills, 8 agents and 3 always-on rules as `fyr list` prints them for the tag (ADR-066 added the third); `update` refusing a dirty checkout on every path; the installer refusing secret-shaped files, symlinked destinations, duplicate skill names and the frontmatter shapes its lint names (`internal/harness/inventory.go` and its tests); one FlagSet per verb, usage errors exit 2. What each release added, v2.0.0 through v5.0.0, is its release entry under `changes/` (`*-release-v*.md`) and its release notes. `main` past that tag also has `fyr auto`, built through Phase 7 of its plan: a switch, a timer, G1–G9, the free checks, the risk rubric, the `auto` skill, the worker runner, the Go apply step, the learning tasks and draft writer, `eval-rerun`, and `harness-edit` with the eval gate and `mini-audit` (`SPEC-fyr-auto`), no tag has shipped it.

**The loop back is removed** (ADR-062, 2026-10-24): the `report` verb ran from 2026-09-17 (`TEST-2026-09-17-delivery-rework-e2e`) through v2.7.0; `main` has no `report` verb and no code that sends anything off the machine but the dreamer's redacted prompt, `fyr eval`'s runs (started by the operator or by `fyr auto` at level `harness`), and `fyr work` workers started by the operator or by `fyr auto` when turned on (plus a `missing-skill` worker's search of `skills.sh` with the pinned CLI; § What stays on the machine). A place on v2.7.0 still has the verb until its crossing (`DEPLOY-remote` § Crossing to fyr; plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` Phase 6), and the operator deletes `styrman-harness-feedback` in that phase.

**Open, defaulting to no:** whether this repository becomes public. Only that would let a machine bootstrap with no credential at all, and it is a question about content rather than packaging.

**Built, 2026-09-17:** what was here as "a follow-up with its own plan — versioned release bundles" is now the release binary above (ADR-033, `PLAN-2026-09-17-release-binary`). It needed no CI: the binary cross-compiles locally in `/preflight`, which writes the checksums (signed with the tag's key until v2.3.2; unsigned since v2.4.0, ADR-053). It does not remove the credential requirement while the repository is private.

## Agents

An agent is authored as `agents/<name>/agent.md` in Antigravity's format, and `fyr install` copies it unchanged to `~/.gemini/config/agents/<name>/agent.md`; nothing is derived (ADR-062, plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` D3). The files are the derivation's output at its last commit, `a2e6a5a`, byte for byte (D17). The lint in `internal/harness/inventory.go` holds what the derivation guaranteed: the keys are `name`, `description`, `subagent`, `mainAgent`, `model` and `tools` (`agentKeys`; an old-format key such as `maxTurns` or `effort` is refused); `subagent: true` and `mainAgent: false`; every tool is one of `knownTools` (an unknown name fails the install, since an unrecognised name hangs the subagent); a flat `agents/<name>.md`, the format before ADR-062, is refused with the file named. A model is `pro` or `flash`, or omitted for the CLI's default. There is no `skills:` key: on 2026-10-01 a probe showed an Antigravity subagent reaches a global skill by the path its body names, with or without the vendor's `skills:` key (3 of 3 and 2 of 2 runs; plan audit-fix D5b), and there is no turn limit: the dispatch names the tool-call budget, and the main agent stops an agent whose artifact is on disk.

Re-read 2026-11-01 against `ae347bf..40c5593` (`fyr auto` plan Phase 2: the risk rubric, the `auto` skill, the six skill sentences, `slashNote` shortened by 9 bytes, and the three `auto-*` adversarial rows in `GUIDE-eval`) and Phase 3 (the worker runner, Kickoff builder and runner choice, ADR-090): § What stays on the machine and § Where things stand updated above.

title: `fyr dream` — the background dreamer
body:
# `fyr dream` — the background dreamer

Status: built 2026-09-30 (plan `PLAN-2026-09-30-parity-memory-dream`). R3's named exception, R4's dream clause, R10 (ADR-047, ADR-047a, ADR-073). The memory half of the learning loop is `SPEC-fyr-memory-loop`.

Re-read 2026-11-01 against `485adbf` (`fyr auto` plan Phase 1a: `internal/auto`, `cmd/fyr/verb_auto.go`, `dream.Timer`, `auto` in `sandboxDirs`, the check vocabulary and the metrics verb list): the timer's text is unchanged, now rendered from `dreamTimer`. Two behaviours changed: `--install-timer` refuses a unit path it cannot read as a regular file (a link, a fifo, an unreadable file) and keeps it, and each manager call of a removal has a 30 s limit. `--remove-timer` still ignores a failed stop. `uninstall` and `fyr status` also name auto's timer and line (`SPEC-fyr-auto`).

Re-read 2026-11-01 against `7a084ab` (`fyr auto` plan Phase 1b: `internal/auto`'s gates and checks, `cmd/fyr/verb_auto.go` and `verb_auto_checks.go`, `auto`'s `run` registered in `init`, the help page): the dream's behaviour does not change; `internal/dream/auto_reads.go` exports `AgySession` and `Targets` for `fyr auto`'s G5 and G6.

Re-read 2026-10-31 against `22d8ecd..37756a3` (`PLAN.md` P12b: under this spec's code `cmd/fyr/eval.go`'s ingest reads `sandbox.Compromised` and skips the same reasons, and `skills/work`'s stop list names `sandbox exists`; `internal/dream` gained only the real `agy` 1.4.12 captures and their tests, so the argv and the shapes below stand).

Re-read 2026-10-31 against `825ff6f` (`PLAN.md` P11: `frontend-ui-economist` and `frontend-ui-modern` replace `frontend`; under this spec's code only skill text, `TestInstallLeavesClaudeCodeAlone`'s guard and `TestSuiteHarness`'s `want` changed): nothing here changes.

Re-read 2026-10-31 against `d66b87e` (`PLAN.md` P9: `fyr metrics evals` gains `kind` and `expect` columns, the testing record `expect`, and the verb list `fyr`'s five missing verbs): nothing here changes.

Re-read 2026-10-31 against `6affb08` (the v5.0.0 gate's fixes: every test package's `TestMain` sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`, three `go list` tests pass `GOPROXY=off`, `internal/serve`'s tests take a temp HOME, and `fyr help`'s `work` line and `cmd/fyr/main.go`'s doc comment changed; none of it reaches this verb's code): nothing here changes.

## What it does

Before anything else, a real run (not `--dry-run`) runs `fyr metrics ingest` over every Antigravity session, store-wide whatever `--project` names, inside `dream.lock`. It logs the ingest's summary line to `dream.log`. A failure is logged as `metrics ingest failed: …` and changes neither the exit status nor `last_run.error` (plan `2026-10-08-metrics-store` D16; spec `SPEC-fyr-metrics`). A dry run prints `[dry-run] would ingest metrics into <path>` and writes nothing.

**The metrics block (R3's addendum, ADR-055a).** Each project's prompt carries a `metrics` input: `metrics.Summary.Numbers()` for the project's window (its watermark to now) and for the window of the same length before it, as JSON.
- **Numbers only.** Every key is the metrics package's own name (no tool, skill, agent, label or path), and a metric a CLI cannot produce is absent.
- **Read from a copy.** It is read from a copy of `metrics.db` (`metrics.Snapshot`). A store at another schema is named under "Left out", and no store or no session gives no block.
- **Context, never news.** It never marks a project changed and is dropped first when the prompt is over the cap.
- **How the instructions treat it.** A worsened metric is evidence only when the other inputs show its cause.

`fyr dream --all`, run hourly by a user timer (`--install-timer`) while an interactive `agy` session of the operator's runs, or by hand with `--all` or `--project <dir>`.

**The session check (ADR-073).** A real `--all` run first asks whether an interactive `agy` session of the operator's uid runs, before it creates `~/.config/fyr`, takes the lock, ingests or writes anything. A process counts when its real uid is the operator's (Linux: the first field of the `Uid:` line of `/proc/<pid>/status`, never the directory's owner; macOS: `ps -ww -U <uid> -o args=`, whose arguments are split at spaces, so an `agy` under a path holding one is not counted), its name is `agy` (the base name of its first argument, or of its `exe` link with a trailing ` (deleted)` removed, since `agy update` replaces the binary under a live session), and its arguments hold neither `-p`, `--print` nor its alias `--prompt`, with one dash or two and with or without `=value` (a headless run: the dream's own child, `fyr eval`, a script) nor, as the first non-flag argument, an `agy` subcommand (`remote-control`, `mcp`, `update` and the rest of the list `agy --help` prints); an entry that cannot be read is skipped, and the desktop app and the Hub are not `agy` processes. With none, the run prints `fyr dream: no agy session of this user; nothing to do` on stdout (the unit's journal), creates nothing and exits 0; a check that errors exits 2 with the error on stdout and creates nothing. `--project` never asks. `--all --dry-run` prints `[dry-run] agy session: yes` or `[dry-run] agy session: no (a real --all run would stop here)` first and goes on; a check that errors exits 2 there too.

**The cooldown (ADR-073).** Under `--all` a project whose CLI call started in the last 24 hours, success or failure, is skipped as `<root> skip attempted <time>`, in a dry run too, so an hourly timer tries a failing project once a day, as the nightly one did. `--project` ignores it: the operator asked.

`fyr dream` looks at every project in the global search index, `~/.config/fyr/search.db` `projects` (read from a copy, never opened live; a registered checkout with `.agents/trail.jsonl`, ADR-086), and at every project scope of the brain store, `brain.db`, each checkout once. Under `--all` it takes from these two lists only the checkouts the operator registered under this home with `fyr index --register` (`trail.Registered(<home>/.config/fyr, root)`, a marker in the git common directory sealed to the checkout's main path and this home's key; ADR-068, ADR-068a): every other root is logged once per run as `<root> skip not registered (fyr index --register)`, in a dry run too (`[dry-run] <root>: skip (not registered (fyr index --register))`), so `fyr dream --dry-run --all` lists the projects to register (audit-choices D17); a root that is gone or no git checkout says so instead, since registering cannot help it; a clone or a copy of a registered checkout is not registered. `--project <dir>` takes the named checkout with no marker: naming it is the operator's opt-in (audit-choices D16). A project is skipped with a log line when its root is gone, it is not a git checkout, or it has no `.agents/trail.jsonl` (`skip no .agents/trail.jsonl: fyr record import`): a dream reads records only (D4, ADR-087), so a file-era tree beside no trail is never read. Under `--all` (the timer's run) it is also skipped while it is in use (D22): a commit (read through `trail.Log`, which refuses a partial clone on a git older than 2.44), a record update in its scope (never one dated after now), or an Antigravity conversation in its workspace within the last 24 hours (`skip in use (<what, when>)`); `--project` dreams at once. One checkout reached by two paths (a worktree, a symlink) is one target. A dry run reads a copy of `brain.db` (under `~/.config/fyr/dream-brain-*`, swept like the other copies, whenever `~/.config/fyr` exists; with none, in the system's temporary directory, since a dry run never creates `~/.config/fyr`, which beside an old `~/.config/sh-agent` would stop the crossing's migration), so it creates, migrates and loads nothing. Otherwise, when anything changed since the project's watermark:

1. **Collect** (`internal/dream/collect.go`), in prompt order:
   - its memory: every `memory` record that is not retired (labelled by ID);
   - its feedback: the global `feedback` records about it (each body a JSON line, redacted as one);
   - its trail: its `bug`, `review`, `retro`, `change` and `handoff` records (the checkout's `trail.jsonl` loaded first when it changed);
   - the installed skills' names and descriptions, read from `~/.gemini/config/skills` (global: never a change on their own);
   - Antigravity conversations that are the root's own, by `last_modified_time` (whole conversations, from copies of the databases; `internal/search/dream.go`): every URI in `workspace_uris` is a file URI under the root (a remote or unparsable one counts as outside), and the nearest directory of each still on disk resolves (`trail.Roots`) to the root's main worktree root (`internal/search/dream_workspace.go`, ledger item 77). A conversation under the root that fails this, one in a checkout nested inside it (a vendored clone, a submodule), one that also names a workspace outside the root, or one whose checkout cannot be read, is never sent: it is named among the left-out inputs by its ID and why, `transcript antigravity <id> (its workspace is a nested checkout, not this project)`, never by its path. A conversation with a workspace in dream-work, as written or with its symlinks followed (`harness.DreamWorkPaths`), is the dream's own and never the root's, even when the root holds the config directory (a checkout at `$HOME`): it is never sent, it is named `transcript antigravity <id> (a fyr dream conversation)` when a workspace of it is under the root, and the in-use check skips it (ADR-073). Known limit: a nested checkout deleted after its session is judged by the directory above it and reads as the root's own; one dated before 1970, Go's zero time among them, has no time and is not collected (BUG-181).

   Everything but memory and skills is taken only when newer than the watermark (a record by its `updated`, never one dated after now); a project's first dream reads the last 14 days. Every git call into a project root goes through `internal/trail` (no index lock, no fsmonitor, no signature check, `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`; BUG-164). A copy of an Antigravity database that is torn (the live one was being written) is copied and opened once more after a second; the live database is never opened. Only the user's (step_type 14) and the model's (15) Antigravity steps are read, never tool output; an Antigravity read error fails the project, so its watermark stays.
2. **Scrub**: an input's fence runs (`>>>`, `<<<`) and its label's newlines are escaped in the prompt, and the project's name (the checkout's base name) is folded the same way once, for the prompt, the proposals header and the file names (SD15); every input, and its label (a record's ID can hold a secret's shape, SD31 of the 2026-10-27 audit), passes the redactor in `internal/redact`, each feedback entry first as a JSON line through `harness.RedactJSONL` and the home path becomes `~`; `project:` and "left out" lines are written with `~` for the home too.
3. **Cap**: at 256 KB. The metrics summary is dropped first; then the dated kinds (transcripts, trail and feedback) together, newest first, two inputs of the same time in that order; then skills (ADR-069, amending ADR-055a). What a capped run sends is the oldest news, and the run's `Through` is set just before the oldest dated input it dropped, so step 6 stops the watermark there and the next run offers the dropped inputs again. A drop holds the watermark back only while an input strictly older than it is kept. A dated input larger than what the cap leaves after the prompt's head, memory and the skills is dropped first and holds nothing back (audit-choices D33); so does one of the oldest time left — the last dated input when the left-out line leaves no room, or part of a group of one time (records from one commit) bigger than the room — since a time watermark cannot split such a group, and holding it there would drop the same part every night. Two inputs of one time and kind drop the later label first. The metrics summary and the skills are undated and hold nothing back. A project whose memory alone passes the cap fails. The prompt names what was left out, each as `<kind> <label> (dropped to fit the 256 KB cap)`, `<kind> <label> (too big for the 256 KB cap beside memory and skills)` for one too big, or `<kind> <label> (dropped to fit the 256 KB cap; not sent again)` for one of the oldest time left: the cap is on the whole prompt, not on one input (SD29); a dry run prints one `left out:` line for each of the first five and counts the rest (SD-S2). The size is counted from the prompt's parts once and kept by arithmetic as inputs drop, so a project's prompt is rendered once (SD-S1).
4. **Ask**: one CLI call with no tool granted (ADR-089), headless in plan mode, from the empty `~/.config/fyr/dream-work/`, 10-minute timeout, the child getting an allow-listed environment: `PATH`, `LANG`, the locale category names (`LC_ALL`, `LC_CTYPE`, `LC_TIME` and the other ten, never any other `LC_` name), `TERM`, `TMPDIR`, `TZ`, the proxy variables in both cases, `SSL_CERT_FILE` and `SSL_CERT_DIR` from fyr's own, then `HOME` set to the home of the branch below, and nothing else, so no other variable, a credential exported in the operator's shell among them, reaches the process that reads the prompt; a listed variable passes as it is, so a proxy URL with a password in it does reach `agy` (ADR-067; a name joins only after a run shows agy needs it, by the operator, and a login that needs a dropped variable fails with the `not logged in` or `invalid output` hint); the CLI runs in its own process group, which is killed whole at the deadline, on SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP or SIGQUIT (then fyr dies of the signal as before; an interrupt or hangup fyr started with ignored, under `nohup` or as a background job, stays ignored and leaves the CLI alone), and once the CLI itself has exited; a helper it started that keeps the output pipes open past a clean exit is cut loose 30 s later and the answer is kept (BUG-169 and its review).
   - The CLI is `agy`: `agy --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --mode plan -p ""`, the prompt on stdin as one stream-json message and the answer read from the final `result` event's `response`; a result naming `denied_actions` is no answer. The prompt's first line is `dreaming: <project>` (the name folded to one line as in step 2), then a blank line and the instructions with their `Project:` line; agy stores the message with its mode in front, so the conversation's first message reads `/plan dreaming: <project>` (the plan's D28). agy has no no-tools flag: plan mode, a home whose settings grant no tool without review and the prompt's warning (its second paragraph: every tool call ends the run with no answer) keep it from calling one (D7b). The home is chosen per project, just before its call, and `dream.log` names it first: `<root> agy home visible` or `<root> agy home private (<why>)`, the reason redacted, folded to one line and stripped of control characters, its paths as written. A dry run asks the oracle too, so it starts the three print-mode reports per project in the home it would use, as a real run does (no turn, no quota, no conversation; agy keeps its own log under that home's `.gemini/antigravity-cli/log`), and prints, per project it would dream over, `[dry-run] <root>: agy home visible (HOME <home>)`, `agy home private (<why>): a copy of the login, with no grants`, the same with `, would fail: <reason>` when the private home could not be built, or, before any real run has made dream-work, `agy home not asked: no dream-work yet; a real run makes it, then asks the oracle` (a dry run makes nothing).
   - **Visible branch** (ADR-073): the operator's own Antigravity home, `--home` (by default `$HOME`, never `$HOME` when they differ, R6), so the conversation is written to `<home>/.gemini/antigravity-cli` beside the operator's own and `/resume` lists it. It is taken only when `agy -p "/permissions" --output-format json`, `agy -p "/config" --output-format json` and `agy -p "/hooks" --output-format json` (the oracle: run with that `HOME`, from dream-work, with the same environment, 30 s each; they start no turn, spend no quota and leave no conversation) show, with fyr's own checks of the home and dream-work, all of (`visibleHome`, `internal/dream/agy_visible.go`; the fields are what agy 1.4.9 reported in the plan's D24 sandbox runs): the login in that home (`antigravity-oauth-token` under `<home>/.gemini/antigravity-cli`, or on macOS a `<home>/Library/Keychains` directory); dream-work empty, and no directory above it, as written or as it resolves, holding a `.git` or a `.agents` other than the home's own (agy 1.4.9 loads the `.agents/` of its working directory and, inside a git checkout, of every directory up to the checkout's root; the reports name no workspace or project root, and a later agy may walk further, so fyr refuses every directory above, checkout or not, the plan's D28); `/config`'s `toolPermission` `request-review` or `strict`, its `agentMode` empty or `plan` and its `artifactReviewPolicy` `asks-for-review`; no allow rule in any scope `/permissions` lists (project, shared, global; deny and ask rules grant nothing) nor in `/config`'s `permissions`, `allowNonWorkspaceAccess` false, and no `trustedWorkspaces` entry at or above dream-work; `/hooks` an empty list (a pre-tool hook can return a permission decision none of the reports show, so a home with any hook, a plugin's included, runs private; the plan's D26); and each report one JSON object with status `SUCCESS`, its envelope, its `command` and its data holding only the keys agy 1.4.9 reported (security review of Phase 5), each field of the type seen (so an agy upgrade that adds a key at any of those levels sends every dream private until fyr learns it), `/config` holding exactly the 36 keys agy 1.4.9 reported (a key added or gone is an unknown shape, so an agy upgrade that adds a setting sends the dream private until fyr learns it) and its `permissions` no key but `allow`, `deny` and `ask`. Anything else — a report that fails, times out, does not parse, lacks a field, or holds a key fyr does not know in a scope — sends that project to the private branch. fyr never writes the operator's settings; in this branch the no-tools guarantee is the oracle's report, not isolation.
   - **Private branch**: a private HOME, `~/.config/fyr/dream-agy-home-*`, holding a copy of the operator's `antigravity-oauth-token` and `installation_id` (taken from `$HOME`, never `--home`) and a settings file that grants nothing; on macOS, where agy keeps the login in the Keychain and finds it only through `$HOME/Library/Keychains`, that folder is linked into the private HOME (never copied) and the token file is copied only when it exists (BUG-166); the dream job's agy then uses the operator's real Keychain, so a login refresh it makes is the interactive agy's too, unlike Linux, where it only ever touches a copy. It is built on the run's first private project, reused by the run's later private projects, and removed after the run; a failure to build it (no login — no token file, and on macOS no `~/Library/Keychains` either) fails that project with `fail <reason>`, not the run, and the run exits 1. An agy that asks for a browser login (a locked Keychain, an expired login) fails the project, and the log line appends `agy is not logged in inside the dream job's private HOME`, or in the visible branch `inside the operator's Antigravity home (--home)`.
   - A `HOME` that is not an absolute path cannot give the private branch a login: a project that needs it fails, exit 1.

   `--vendor` is a usage error (exit 2). "No `agy` on PATH" is the failure before the first project.
5. **Write**: the first `{…}` of the answer that decodes as `{"proposals":[…],"skills":[…]}`, scrubbed again. Unknown keys are ignored; the fields used are validated.
   - Each proposal is one global `proposal` record (`brain.Propose`; D15): title `Dream, project — <title>` or `Dream, harness — <title>` by its target (so `/retro` and `/retro --harness` each take theirs from the title), `project` the root, status `queued`; a project's proposals are stored in one transaction (`brain.ProposeAll`), all or none; its body names the project, the day, the CLI and the input counts (and what was left out), then `Target: project|harness   Kind: …   File: …`, the model's text indented by four spaces (so it reads as quoted data, never as a field or heading of the record) and `Evidence: …`. Title and body are normalized first (a control character as `?`, the title cut to one line of 512 bytes).
   - `proposals/dream/drafts/<date>-<project>-<name>/SKILL.md`: each draft skill with a kebab-case name, files as before; one more `proposal` record, `Dream, harness — draft skills for <project>`, names each draft's path and each dropped (invalid) name.

   One-line fields (title, kind, file, evidence) have line breaks folded. A project with zero proposals and no draft stores no record (and creates no brain store).
6. **Advance** the watermark, only after a successful parse and write: to the cap's `Through` when step 3 dropped a dated input that holds it back and that instant is before the run's start, else to the run's start. Every dated input older than the new watermark was sent, or named as too big or not sent again; one of the same time as the oldest held back may be sent twice, and a re-sent input may give a duplicate global `proposal`, which `/retro` drops by hand (D33).

**Where the data goes:** to the model of `agy`, the one CLI the run uses and the only one whose transcripts are read. In the visible branch the redacted prompt and the answer also stay in the operator's Antigravity store, as a conversation of its own; a conversation whose workspace is dream-work (as written or through its symlinks) is no project's: it is never ingested into the metrics store and never read by any project's dream or in-use check. From Antigravity, only the user's input and the model's replies are read (step types 14 and 15), and each step's payload is decoded as protobuf by its wire format, with no schema (D30): a length-delimited field that is printable UTF-8 is a text leaf, anything else is tried as a nested message. A leaf is sent only when it has three spaces or more and is not JSON, so a tool call's arguments (a command, a file written), which are one whole JSON string field, never reach the prompt. On the 95 conversation databases of the Linux box, 971 prose leaves were kept and none carried a tool-argument key.
**Hardening details:**
- The private branch's agy settings are `{"toolPermission":"request-review","permissions":{"allow":[]},"trustedWorkspaces":[]}`.
- A stream result whose status is not `SUCCESS`, or that names `denied_actions`, is no answer.
- Each feedback record's body is redacted as a JSON line (`redact.RedactJSONL` in `internal/redact`, which matches the decoded line) before the raw `scrub`, because a secret JSON-escaped on the line (`&sig=…` written as `\u0026sig=…` by `json.Marshal`) does not match the raw-text needles.
- The timer freezes only the absolute entries of the installing shell's PATH.
- The systemd service sets `TimeoutStartSec=2h`: a oneshot has no start timeout by default, and a `Persistent=` timer does not start a unit that is still active, so a run hung past the per-project kill is ended and the next scheduled run starts (SD36; ledger D2). launchd has no start timeout, and the plist sets none. A unit installed by an older fyr lacks the line and is kept as it is, since `--install-timer` never overwrites a unit with other text: `fyr dream --remove-timer`, then `--install-timer`, writes the current one. The limit bounds the whole run, not one project; each project's watermark is saved as it finishes, so the next run goes on from there. The schedule is `OnCalendar=hourly` (`Persistent=true`), and in the plist a `StartCalendarInterval` with `Minute` 0 and no `Hour`; a unit an older fyr installed with the nightly schedule (`OnCalendar=*-*-* 03:00`, `Hour` 3) is kept as it is, for the same reason, where, with the session check, it almost never dreams, and `fyr status` names it: `timer installed, older schedule: fyr dream --remove-timer, then fyr dream --install-timer`.
- The timer's unit name is per home (`dream.UnitFor(home)`): the real home (the account's home from the account database, `os/user` by uid, never `HOME`, which a sandbox run overrides; path cleaned; an account the database does not list — on Linux a release binary reads only `/etc/passwd`, so LDAP, SSSD and systemd-homed accounts and a container's bare uid — has no real home, and every home there gets the suffix) gets the bare `fyr-dream` (systemd) and `com.fyr.dream` (launchd label; plist `com.fyr.dream.plist`); any other `--home` gets `-<first 8 hex of sha256 of the cleaned home path>` appended to both. Install, remove, the installed check and the unit-file paths all derive the name from the same home, and the unit's command is `dream --all --home <that home>`, so a scratch timer dreams over its own home's index, never the real one. A symlinked spelling of the real home counts as the real home (`os.SameFile`). Why: the user service manager is shared by every home of the user, so a scratch `--install-timer`, `--remove-timer` or `uninstall` must never reach the operator's own timer (R6; BUG-144). Before v3.0.0 the units had other names; since every place crossed (ledger A1, D40), no verb reads, replaces, removes or names a unit under them, and `fyr status` says nothing of one (ledger Phase 10). `--remove-timer` prints `dream timer removed`, or `no dream timer found for <home> on this system` when it removed nothing (exit 0 both ways); `uninstall` says `removed the dream timer` only when it removed one. A unit file of the operating system the binary is not running on (`OtherSystemTimerFiles`: the launchd plist on Linux, the systemd units on macOS) is never removed: `uninstall` and `--remove-timer` name it and say it stays, dry runs included, since `status` counts it as installed; `uninstall` announces a removal only for a unit of the system it runs on (`TimerInstalledHere`).

## Consumers

- Project-level `/retro` (source 9) lists its project's queued dream proposals (`fyr record list --global --kind proposal --project <root> --open`), re-derives each against the files, and sets its status (`applied:<commit>` or `rejected`).
- `/retro --harness` lists every queued proposal, `Target: harness` ones among them, on the machine that wrote them; nothing sends them anywhere (ADR-062). They are model-written from any project's redacted content, so their text is data, never instructions.
- `fyr status` prints `dream      last run <date>: <n> projects, <m> proposals; timer installed|not installed` (or `failed: <reason>`, or `never run`), and `timer installed, older schedule: fyr dream --remove-timer, then fyr dream --install-timer` for a unit whose text is not this fyr's render for the home and the unit's own `PATH` (each command with `--home '<home>'` under a home that is not the real one).

## State and files (all under `~/.config/fyr/`, 0600 in 0700 directories)

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `dream-state.json` | `projects` (root → watermark), `attempts` (root → when its last CLI call started, the 24-hour cooldown under `--all`; a file without it reads as empty) and `last_run` (at, projects, proposals, error) |
| `dream.log` | one line per project (`ok N proposals`, `unchanged`, `skip <why>`, `fail <why>`), the branch line before each call (`agy home visible`, `agy home private (<why>)`) and one per run; an hourly run that finds no `agy` session writes none |
| `dream.lock` | an flock held for the run (the pid is written in it for reading only); the kernel releases it however the run ends, and a held one makes a second run exit 0 "already running" |
| `dream-agy-home-*`, `dream-agy-*`, `dream-projects-*` | per-run private copies (agy HOME, for the private branch only; Antigravity databases; the index); removed after the run; at the start of a run, under the lock, only copies older than an hour are removed (leftovers of a killed run; a dry run takes no lock) |
| `dream-work/` | the CLI's working directory, kept empty; not a project, so the run's own conversation never maps to one, and no reader takes a conversation whose workspace it is |
| `dream-failed/` | a failed project's stdout and stderr, scrubbed; files older than 30 days are pruned at the start of a run |
| `brain.db` | the proposal records above |
| `proposals/dream/drafts/` | the draft skills above |

Outside `~/.config/fyr/`, in the visible branch only: each project's dream conversation, in `<home>/.gemini/antigravity-cli`, kept by agy as its own state beside the operator's conversations (R3: "in the operator's Antigravity home on the visible branch, where they stay"); fyr writes nothing there itself.

## Failure modes

| Situation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Any failure before the first project: usage, no `agy` on PATH, an unreadable index | exit 2 with a run log line and `last_run.error`; `status` says `failed`. A usage error writes nothing, exits 2 and prints on stdout (not stderr) its reason, dream's synopsis and `run 'fyr help dream' for its flags`, as every verb's usage error does (ledger item 86); `fyr dream` with neither `--all` nor `--project` has no reason line, only the synopsis and the hint. A `--dry-run` makes the same `agy` check and exits 2 with the same message, writing nothing (SD27 of the 2026-10-27 audit); no login under `$HOME` or a relative `HOME` is the private branch's, a project's `would fail` on its branch line (the plan's D12) |
| `dream-state.json` is corrupt | exit 2, and the file is NOT rewritten |
| `--dry-run` with `--install-timer` or `--remove-timer` | both take `--dry-run`: writes nothing, calls no manager. `--install-timer --dry-run` makes every refusal the install makes (no binary at `<home>/.local/bin/fyr`, a quote, backslash or control character in a path, no service manager on PATH, a unit on disk with other text, an OS with no user timer) and exits 2 with its message (SD26) |
| `--install-timer` or `--remove-timer` with `--all` or `--project` | a usage error: `fyr dream: --install-timer and --remove-timer take no --all or --project`, exit 2 (SD33) |
| No interactive `agy` session of this user when an `--all` run starts | one line on stdout (the unit's journal), nothing in `dream.log` or `dream-state.json`, no directory created; exit 0; the next hour asks again |
| The session check errors (an unreadable `/proc`; on macOS `ps` missing or its output unparsable) | exit 2, the error on stdout, nothing created; `systemctl --user status` shows the failed unit |
| The oracle fails, times out, or reports a grant or a shape fyr does not know | that project runs in the private branch; `dream.log` names why; no conversation in `/resume` |
| The private home cannot be built for a project (no login under `$HOME`, a relative `HOME`) | that project fails, `<root> fail <reason>`, before its call, so it is not counted as attempted; the run goes on; exit 1 |
| The CLI exits non-zero or times out | the project fails, its output goes to `dream-failed/`, its watermark stays; the others run; exit 1; under `--all` it is not attempted again for 24 hours; in the visible branch the failed conversation stays in `/resume` |
| A machine keeps its nightly unit after the upgrade | `fyr status` names the older schedule; `--install-timer` refuses the unit's other text until `--remove-timer` |
| Two `agy` processes write the operator's store at once (the dream and a session) | agy's own design: the desktop app, the Hub, Remote Control and several sessions share that store; fyr adds nothing |
| The answer has no decodable JSON | the same, logged `fail invalid output` |
| An agy stdout line over 16 MiB | the same, logged `fail output line too long or unreadable` |
| A symlinked `.agents` or `trail.jsonl` in a project of records | the brain store refuses it; the project fails, its watermark stays |
| A project with no `.agents/trail.jsonl` | `skip no .agents/trail.jsonl: fyr record import`, nothing of it read or sent; a dry run says so too |
| Memory alone over 256 KB | the project fails with `memory over cap` |
| Dated inputs over the cap | the newest are dropped and named, and the watermark stops just before the oldest of them, so the next run sends them; one too big to fit beside memory and the skills is named `too big for the 256 KB cap beside memory and skills`, and the part of a group of one time that does not fit `not sent again`; neither is sent (ADR-069) |
| No indexed project and no project scope | nothing to do; exit 0 |
| An indexed project or project scope that is not registered under this home (`--all`) | `skip not registered (fyr index --register)`, nothing of it read or sent, not counted in `- run <n> projects`; exit 0 |
| Every project in use within the day | each skipped `in use`; exit 0 |
| A second run while one runs | exit 0, "already running" |

## Known limits

- **Plan mode still writes its plan file** (ADR-089, the v5.5.0 gate). `agy` 1.4.12 under this argv, `request-review` and no allow rule runs `write_file` for `implementation_plan.md` in `brain/<conversation>/` (`internal/dream/testdata/agy-1.4.12/tool.jsonl`), with no `denied_actions`. `answer` then gives no answer, after the write. A probe that asked the model to write outside `brain/` got a plan and no such write, which is the model's choice: nothing shown refuses it, so a dream's prompt-injected write outside `brain/` is neither proved possible nor proved impossible.

- **The oracle-to-call window** (ADR-073). The visible branch's settings are read just before each project's call; a setting changed between the report and the call applies to that call, for the one project.
- **The shared and project rule scopes are read, not proven** (the plan's D24). `/permissions` lists a `shared` and a `project` scope beside `global`, and fyr refuses an allow rule in any of them, but the sandbox runs could not put a rule in either (their files are not documented), so that agy reports them there is agy's word; a global allow rule was reported.
- **A visible dream loads what the operator's sessions load** (ADR-073, the plan's D8, accepted by the operator; narrowed by D26). The operator's MCP servers and plugins, and the skills of a `.agents` in their home, start as in any session they open under it; a home with any hook, a plugin's included, is not taken (a hook can approve a tool), so the model still has no tool it may use without review.
- **A resumed dream is a session like any other** (security review of Phases 2–4b). The conversation's first message is the redacted but untrusted prompt; the oracle's verdict held when the dream ran, and the operator who opens it with `/resume` continues it under the settings in force then, with whatever tools those grant, so a directive planted in a project's text reaches a session that may act on it; so does a session that pulls the dream in through an `@conversation:` mention or conversation search (security review of Phase 5). The prompt marks every input as data, never instructions.
- **A `--home` other than `$HOME` below a `.agents` dreams privately** (the plan's D28). fyr refuses a `.agents` in every directory above dream-work but the home's own, so a `--home` under a directory holding one (a `~/.agents`, for instance) always takes the private branch, though agy 1.4.9 loads such a `.agents` only inside a git checkout. The real home is not affected: its own `.agents` is exempt.
- **A custom agent's own settings are not in the oracle's reports** (security review of Phase 5, finding 1; the plan's D29). A custom agent (`agent.md`) may set `commandExecutionPolicy` or carry `hooks:`, and the model may define one with `define_subagent`; none of the three reports shows them. The D29 probe (agy 1.4.9, a sandbox home) showed the home's review mode governs a subagent's commands: a subagent with `commandExecutionPolicy: eager` and `run_command`, invoked from a headless run, had its command denied by agy (`denied_actions` names `RunCommand`) under `request-review`, with and without plan mode, and ran it under `always-proceed`, the control. Not probed: an agent's own `hooks:` (the `/hooks` report may not list them) and an agent the model defines at run time; for those the guard is unproven.
- **The visible branch uses the login in place** (security review of Phase 5). The dream's `agy` and the operator's session, which the session check requires to be running, share one `antigravity-oauth-token`; whether two refreshes at once can leave it revoked is agy's (the plan's AS5). A logged-out dream shows as `agy is not logged in inside the operator's Antigravity home (--home)` in `dream.log`.
- **`dream.log` and the attempts grow** (Phase 5 review). Each hour a session runs adds a line per registered project (`skip attempted`, `unchanged`, `skip in use`), and nothing rotates the log; an attempt stays in `dream-state.json` after its project is unregistered. Both are small; `fyr dream --remove-timer` stops the first.
- **Only an `agy` process counts as a session.** The desktop app and the Hub are not `agy` processes, so working only there does not let the timer dream. The macOS check is verified only by the operator's Mac run (`PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` A2).
- **A scratch timer on Linux is files only** (audit SD34, `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` item 9). `--install-timer` with a `--home` that is not the real one writes its units under `<home>/.config/systemd/user`, which the user manager does not search, so `systemctl --user enable --now fyr-dream-<hash>.timer` cannot load them and the files stay; the `systemctl --user daemon-reload` before it still runs on the real, shared user manager. § State and files' "a scratch timer dreams over its own home's index" holds on macOS, where `launchctl bootstrap` takes the plist's own path, and on Linux only with that directory linked into the real one. Reasoned from systemd's search path, not run: the run would reach the operator's real user manager.
- **A killed run leaves its copies until the next run** (audit SD35, item 10). The private HOME (`dream-agy-home-*`, holding the copy of the Antigravity login token) and the read copies (`dream-agy-*`, `dream-projects-*`, `dream-brain-*`, `dream-metrics-*`, `metrics-agy-*`) are removed when a run ends; a run killed by SIGKILL or a power loss leaves them, in 0700 `~/.config/fyr`, until the next run sweeps every one older than an hour. With the timer removed, nothing sweeps them. Same account, so no new reader.

## Verification

Real `agy` 1.4.12 output is kept in `internal/dream/testdata/agy-1.4.12` and read by `TestRealAgyShapes`: the call's `-p ""` beside `--input-format stream-json` works there, and `/config`'s keys equal 1.4.9's. It pins what was captured, so an `agy` upgrade needs a new capture.

End to end against the real agy 1.4.9 (`PLAN-2026-10-28-1510-plan-the-visible-dream-2026-10-28` Phase 5, a sandbox home outside every checkout, the plan's D28): the session check said `yes` with an interactive `agy` running and `no` without one, and a real `--all` with none created nothing; a `--project` dream with no settings file ran visible, left one conversation whose workspace URI is `file://` + dream-work exactly as `harness.DreamWork` writes it, two steps and no tool call, and an empty dream-work; with one allow rule the same run went private, added no conversation to the home's store and left no private home; `fyr metrics ingest` stored no session for the dream's conversation and one for a plain conversation beside it.

Unit tests use a fake CLI on PATH that records its arguments, working directory and stdin (`internal/dream/fakecli_test.go`, used by `internal/dream/run_test.go` and `internal/dream/run_agy_test.go`), so the tool-free flags, the cwd, the absence of a planted secret in the prompt, the file shapes and the watermark rule are pinned; `internal/dream/collect_fit_test.go` pins the cap's drop order, its wording and `Through`, and `TestTwoRunsSendEveryCappedInput` the two-run case. The D7 probe (plan) ran both real CLIs tool-free from an untrusted, empty directory. The end-to-end rows are in `GUIDE-skill-matrix` and `GUIDE-fyr-matrix`.

Re-read 2026-11-01 against `ae347bf..40c5593` (`fyr auto` plan Phase 2: the risk rubric, the `auto` skill, the six skill sentences, `slashNote` shortened by 9 bytes, and the three `auto-*` adversarial rows in `GUIDE-eval`): nothing here changes.

Re-read 2026-11-01 against `31665e3` (`fyr auto` plan Phase 3: the worker runner, Kickoff builder and runner choice in `internal/auto/`, `internal/work/` and `cmd/fyr/verb_auto.go`): nothing here changes.

Re-read 2026-11-01 for `fyr auto` plan Phase 7: nothing here changes.

title: `fyr eval` — behavioural rows against the Antigravity CLI
body:
# `fyr eval` — behavioural rows against the Antigravity CLI Owner: main. Decided by ADR-065; built by `PLAN-2026-10-26-0659-plan-fyr-eval-the-antigravity-run-kit-as-a-verb` (the D-rows cited below are that plan's). Code: `cmd/fyr/eval.go`, `cmd/fyr/eval_record.go`, `cmd/fyr/eval_body.go`, `cmd/fyr/eval_trial.go`, `internal/eval/`, and the steps in `internal/sandbox/`. Re-read 2026-10-30 against `2a58fd8` (workers Phase 9: `sandbox.Config.Zone` and `agyEnv`'s `TZ` line, set by `fyr work` only; eval sets no `Zone`, so its allowlisted environment is unchanged, `TestAgyEnvZone`): nothing here changes. Re-read 2026-11-01 against `485adbf` (`fyr auto` plan Phase 1a: `internal/auto`, `cmd/fyr/verb_auto.go`, `dream.Timer`, `auto` in `sandboxDirs`, the check vocabulary and the metrics verb list): check c also skips `auto/`, while `auto.json` beside it stays watched (the plan's D6), so step c's list changes as below; `fyr auto on` or `off` during a run fails it `real config changed`. Re-read 2026-11-01 against `7a084ab` (`fyr auto` plan Phase 1b: `internal/auto`'s gates and checks, `cmd/fyr/verb_auto.go` and `verb_auto_checks.go`, `auto`'s `run` registered in `init`, the help page): nothing here changes. Re-read 2026-10-31 against `825ff6f` (`PLAN.md` P11: `frontend-ui-economist` and `frontend-ui-modern` replace `frontend`; under this spec's code only skill text, `TestInstallLeavesClaudeCodeAlone`'s guard and `TestSuiteHarness`'s `want` changed): nothing here changes. Re-read 2026-10-31 against `bd2d6b4` (`PLAN.md` P10b, ADR-087: a dream reads records only, the global index holds no file, reversing the P10a line below that it holds `~/.config/fyr`'s files; `trail.Dates`, `memory.Store` and `harness.LastRetro` go, the search schema is 3, eval's setup gets `FYR`, and `record import --dry-run` prints no stored count): nothing else here changes. Re-read 2026-10-31 against `6affb08` (the v5.0.0 gate's fixes: every test package's `TestMain` sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`, three `go list` tests pass `GOPROXY=off`, `internal/serve`'s tests take a temp HOME, and `fyr help`'s `work` line and `cmd/fyr/main.go`'s doc comment changed; none of it reaches this verb's code): nothing here changes. Updated 2026-10-31 by Phase 2a of `PLAN-2026-10-31-0300-plan-eval-metrics-the-standard-set-collected-fro`: `--runs N`, the trial sandbox `//`, the status `ERROR` with a cause beside `PASS` and `FAIL`, and one `trials` row per trial. Updated 2026-10-31 by `PLAN.md` P6 (that plan's Phase 2b, and `PLAN.md` item 1): the trial line names `#`, the cause and the session seconds; the summary and the title count graded trials and the errors apart; the record's header names k, the model, agy, the harness and the suite's Wilson interval, beside a per-trial and a per-row table; a replaced sandbox is a FAIL with cause `replaced`, and a file of eval's own that the machine could not open or remove before the first session is `sandbox write failed`, an ERROR with cause `write` (`PLAN.md` item 48); a setup or check log eval cannot open fails the trial the same way, and its script does not run. Re-read 2026-10-31 against `253ca2c` (`PLAN.md` P4: `dockerArgs`' container limits and run network and `Docker.Network` in `internal/sandbox/docker.go`; they apply only under `Config.Docker`, which eval never sets, so its agy command still runs on the host as step 10 says): nothing here changes. Re-read 2026-10-31 against `5889b4b` and `1b14564` (`PLAN.md` P10a, ADR-086: `internal/search` reads no docs root and parses no record from a file, the global index holds `~/.config/fyr`'s files only, `fyr help search` and `index`, `index --register`'s note, and a comment in `internal/dream/targets.go`): nothing here changes. Re-read 2026-10-31 against `33c33b7` (`PLAN.md` P13, the v5.5.0 gate): check d's read now stops at 64 MiB + 1 byte whatever the size says, so a `/proc` file through a planted link is the same `larger than` refusal (`PLAN.md` item 65); nothing else here changes. Re-read 2026-10-31 against `05ba26d` (`PLAN.md` P13, the v5.5.0 gate's round 3: `internal/work`'s branch reads, `cmd/fyr`'s help wording): nothing here changes. Re-read 2026-11-01 against `59a38de` (BUG-206, tests only): nothing here changes. Updated 2026-10-31 by `PLAN.md` P9 (the eval-metrics plan's Phase 5b, D19): `GUIDE-eval` carries the long header, the record's row table gains `expect`, and its suite interval leaves `indicator` rows out (§ The suite, § The testing record). Updated 2026-10-31 by `PLAN.md` P8 (the eval-metrics plan's Phase 5a, ADR-085): the suite's header may carry four optional columns, `version`, `kind`, `cluster` and `expect` (§ The suite); `--list` prints each row's version and kind; each trial stores them (§ Data). Updated 2026-10-31 by `PLAN.md` P7 (item 53, D16): the trial's `harness` key marks `(dirty)` only for a change under the directories an install reads (§ Data, § Known limits); the record's install-source line still marks the whole tree. Updated 2026-11-01 by Phase 6 of `PLAN-2026-10-31-1636-plan-fyr-auto-mode-idle-time-self-improvement-of` (D15, D51): `--suite-file PATH` reads a suite from a regular file outside every git checkout, in `GUIDE-eval`'s format, and labels its trials and ingested sessions `eval=holdout/`. ## Purpose The operator runs a project's behavioural scenarios ("rows") against the real Antigravity CLI, each in its own throwaway sandbox, with the safety checks the old run kit's preamble made around every run, and keeps the result: one `testing` record per invocation, one `trials` row per run of a row and one labelled metrics row per session, so runs compare over time, through `fyr metrics evals` and `fyr metrics show --label eval=`. It is the release rule's "one run of each changed skill and agent on Antigravity" as a verb, usable in any project that commits a suite. Nothing runs it but the operator or, when the operator turned `fyr auto` on at level `harness`, `fyr auto`'s `eval-rerun` class and eval gate (R3, ADR-090); it is not a compare verb (D7), and not parallel. ## Interfaces ### The verb ``` fyr eval --home DIR [--fixture DIR] [--suite-file PATH] [--runs N] ... fyr eval [--suite-file PATH] --list ``` | Flag | Meaning | |---|---| | `--fixture DIR` | the git repository each row clones; default the project root. It is only ever cloned, never written. | | `--suite-file PATH` | read the suite from `PATH` instead of the checkout's `GUIDE-eval` (D15 of `PLAN-2026-10-31-1636-plan-fyr-auto-mode-idle-time-self-improvement-of`): opened without following a link, refused when larger than 1 MiB (`suiteFileLimit`) or when its parent directory or resolved parent directory lies inside any git checkout (`sandbox.OutsideCheckout`, guard b). Each run row is labelled `eval=holdout/` in `trials`, session ingests and the testing record's tables, while keeping the row's `cluster` (`` by default) | | `--runs N` | run every named row N times, an integer from 1 to 25, default 1: serially, rows in the order named and trials innermost; refused with `--list` (the eval-metrics plan D4, D25) | | `--list` | print the suite, one line per row: ` v `; takes no row; runs nothing and reads the working export without the HEAD comparison (D19), or the `--suite-file` when given | | `--home DIR` | required for a run (`--list` takes none): fyr's home, where the sandboxes, the brain store the record goes to, and the metrics store live. Refused, exit 2, after the usage errors and before every refusal that reads the tree and before the state-dir migration, so a refused run writes nothing (ledger D37): a missing `--home`; a real home, which is `$HOME` and the account's home from the account database; and a home that reaches a real home's state, compared by file identity (`os.SameFile`, so a symlink, a hard link, a bind mount or a case variant of the path all count) at ``, `/.config`, `/.config/fyr` (also against the old `~/.config/sh-agent`) and every entry directly in it (the stores, their `-wal` and `-shm` files, `registration.key`, `eval/`), each against the real entry of the same name, or through a dangling link at any of them. Asked again before each trial's store write, before each ingest and before the record is written, since a row's agent could link the home meanwhile | | `--repo DIR` | the harness each sandbox gets, resolved as `fyr install` resolves it (D16): `--repo`, `$FYR_REPO`, the working directory and its parents, then the home's last install; a release binary installs its embedded harness and refuses `--repo` | The project root is the top level of the working directory's git checkout. A trial is one run of a row; its sandbox is `/.config/fyr/eval////`, `` being `%F-%H%M%S` taken once per invocation and `` the trial from 1, and `//` is the trial's key (its `run`); it holds `app/` (the clone), `home/` (the HOME the CLI runs with), `out.txt`, `out2.txt`, `err.txt`, and the logs `install.log`, `setup.log` and `check.log`. Sandboxes are kept for inspection; `fyr uninstall` leaves them, since they are not in its manifest. Output, one line per trial as it finishes, then the record: ``` eval: # PASS|FAIL|ERROR[ (; ; )] agy exit s[ (s session)] eval:

of PASS, errors; record TEST-… ``` `p` and `n` count the graded trials (PASS and FAIL), `e` the ERROR trials (`1 error` for one). The cause comes first; a reason that is the cause word for word (`interrupted`) is not said again. The session's seconds show only when a session started. Exit 0 when every trial passed, 1 when any did not pass or did not run (rows × N exceeds the trials run), or a trial write, an ingest or the record failed, 2 for a refusal before any trial ran. Every printed id and path goes through the printable filter of `fyr search`. Refusals and usage lines go to stdout with the row lines, unlike `fyr check`, which prints its refusal on stderr (IN34 of the 2026-10-27 audit). ### The suite: `GUIDE-eval` A `guide` record of the project, read from `.agents/trail.jsonl` at the project root (never from the brain store), or from `--suite-file PATH` outside every checkout. Any prose may surround exactly one Markdown table with one of these two headers (the second since ADR-085, which supersedes the eval plan's D2): ``` | id | setup | prompt | prompt2 | check | agent | grants | | id | setup | prompt | prompt2 | check | agent | grants | version | kind | cluster | expect | ``` A row has as many cells as its table's header; under the long header any of the last four may be empty, which gives its default. - A row line starts with ``| ` ``; cells split on unescaped `|`, and `\|` is a literal `|`. One surrounding pair of backticks is stripped; a `setup` or `check` cell that starts with a backticked span followed by more text keeps only the span (D23). - `id`: the first backticked token of the first cell, one path element of `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `-`, at most 64 bytes (ADR-085: it is the default `cluster`). - `setup`: bash run in the clone before the CLI starts; may be empty. - `prompt` (required) and `prompt2` (optional, a second session on the same home after the first exits 0): literal text with four placeholders eval substitutes itself, never through a shell: `{{CLONE}}`, `{{SB}}`, `{{FIXDIR}}`, `{{STAMP}}` (`%F-%H%M` at the trial's start, so trials of one row can differ) (D21). - `check`: bash, required; exit 0 is a pass. - `agent`: empty, or an agent the conversation store must show invoked. - `grants`: `named` (the fixed allow list) or `wide: ` (`command(*)`; the reason is printed). - `version` (default 1): an integer from 1 to 999999999 in plain digits, no sign and no leading zero, bumped by the row's author on any change to `setup`, `prompt`, `prompt2` or `check`; `fyr metrics evals` keys its lines on the row and its version, so a row's history restarts at a new one (a trial stored before this column reads as version 1). - `kind` (default `capability`): `capability`, `regression` (expected to pass every time), `adversarial` (a planted instruction or a lane) or `indicator` (reported, left out of the suite's rate). Each trial stores it; `fyr metrics evals` prints the `regression`, `adversarial` and `indicator` rates on suite lines of their own (`SPEC-fyr-metrics` § Per-row view). - `cluster` (default the row's id): one word of the identifier rule of `SPEC-fyr-metrics` (`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.:@/-]{0,63}$`), a family name for rows that share a setup or a fixture. Each trial stores it, and no view reads it: its one reader, the cluster-bootstrap line, was removed before it was built (`PLAN.md` D19). - `expect` (default none): comma-separated tool names or normalised verbs, each entry words of that identifier rule joined by single spaces, none empty or repeated, at most 120 bytes joined by `,` with the spaces around each comma dropped. Each trial stores it; it is never executed and never gates. An entry is a word of the store's vocabulary (a tool as `Read`, never `view_file`, or a normalised verb), matched as strings at read time, in any order, against the trial's stored tools and verbs: `fyr metrics evals` and the testing record print `m of n` (`metrics.ExpectMatches`; `SPEC-fyr-metrics` § Per-row view). `setup` and `check` run in the clone with exactly: `PATH` (eval's own), `HOME` and `SB` (the sandbox home), `OUT`, `OUT2` (the two stdout files), `FIXDIR` (the fixture), `CLONE` (the clone); `setup` also gets the git identity `fixture` / `f@localhost` and `FYR`, the running binary, since `$SB/bin/fyr` does not exist until step 6. ### One row, in order Each trial of a row runs these steps in its own sandbox. 1. Make the sandbox directory (its `/` parents as needed); an existing one fails the trial. 2. Clone the fixture (`--no-hardlinks`, every `GIT_*` variable removed); the clone must be its own top level; guards a and b on the real paths. 3. Write `SB/records-before.txt` from `fyr record list --home SB` in the clone. 4. Fingerprint the real config (check c), before `setup`, so a setup that writes it fails the row (IN50 of the 2026-10-27 audit). 5. Run `setup`. 6. `fyr install --home SB` with the resolved source; a wrapper `SB/bin/fyr` pins `--home SB` on every fyr call the agent makes and refuses a `--home` of the agent's own (fyr's flags are last-wins). 7. Write the sandbox's `settings.json`: the grants, and `trustedWorkspaces` holding only the clone. 8. Take the credential baseline of the sandbox directory (check d). 9. Link the operator's login token into SB. 10. Run `agy -p "The project root is the current directory, ; ignore any other checkout. " --mode accept-edits --print-timeout 20m` in the clone, with an allowlisted environment, stdin `/dev/null`, in its own process group; at 25 minutes only agy itself is killed. `prompt2` follows when the first exit was 0 and the sandbox is still intact (below). 11. Remove the token link and `settings.json` by name, through an `os.Root` on SB opened at step 2 and held to step 14 (it follows the directory through a rename, and refuses a link leading out of it); warn when the link was replaced or the real token is no longer a regular file. 12. Count `auto-denied` in `err.txt` and `invalid allow entry` in the newest CLI log. 13. Run `check`; then check f. A conversation database over 64 MiB is not read; the row notes it (`: over 64 MiB, not read`) and check f counts it as not found (IN51). 14. Exit checks c, d and e; then SIGKILL to agy's process group. 15. Status: PASS only when the check exited 0, the named agent was invoked, both counts are 0 and every exit check passed.
