Otherwise a failed exit check c, d or e, or a replaced sandbox, is a FAIL whatever else happened: only a process inside the sandbox can replace it, and the only such process is the agent's (`PLAN.md` item 1). A file of eval's own that the machine could not open or remove (a full disk or quota, an I/O error, a read-only file system, no descriptors or memory left) before the first session started is no replacement: it is `sandbox write failed`, an ERROR (`PLAN.md` item 48). After a session the agent, as the operator's uid, could have caused the same errors, so they are `sandbox replaced`, as is any other refused open or removal: the graded direction. Then a reason of the sandbox (a step in 1–9 failed, the run was interrupted) is an ERROR, never graded; anything else is a FAIL. The agy exit status is printed and is not a status condition. The cause is one identifier, in this order of choice (`internal/eval/cause.go`, the eval-metrics plan D6, D28): | Status | Cause | Reason | |---|---|---| | FAIL | `creds`, `config`, `procs`, `replaced` | checks d, c, e, then `sandbox replaced`, in that order when several failed | | ERROR | `exists`, `clone`, `records`, `setup`, `install`, `settings`, `token`, `write`, `interrupted` | the first such reason given | | FAIL | `grant`, `denied` | an invalid allow entry, an auto-denied call | | FAIL | `timeout` | agy was killed at 25 minutes and a reason none of the rows above names remains (the check or check f failed): graded, not an ERROR | | FAIL | `agent`, `check` | check f, the check; a reason no row names is `check` too, the graded direction | `TestClassifyEveryReason` pins that every reason eval and `internal/sandbox` give is named in this table. Steps 1, 2, 4, 6–12 and 14 live in `internal/sandbox` (`TDD.md` § T17), which eval calls in this order; eval keeps 3, 5, 13 and 15, and its behaviour and output are unchanged by the move (`PLAN-2026-10-29-workers` Phase 1). That plan's Phases 2, 3 and 7b-1 gave the sandbox four things only `fyr work` uses (`SPEC-fyr-work`): a model passed to agy as `--model`, check c leaving out the stores the operator's own sessions and the dream write (D45, D64, D70 there), the removal of an intact sandbox, and a session in a container (`Config.Docker`, `fyr work --runner docker`). eval passes no model and no container, so its agy command is step 10's, run on the host; its check c watches the stores; and it removes no sandbox. A failure in steps 1–8 fails the trial with its reason and skips 9–13; step 14 still runs. The agent can write in the sandbox directory, so before `prompt2`, after step 11 and again before check d the sandbox directory, the clone and SB must still resolve to the paths guard a approved: otherwise the trial gets the reason `sandbox replaced` (a FAIL with cause `replaced`, or the safety check's cause when one also failed: step 15), and nothing is removed, run, scanned or ingested through them; check e matches the approved paths, never a fresh resolution, whether or not the clone still exists. A file eval reads or writes in the sandbox (`err.txt`, `out.txt`, the logs, a conversation database) is opened without following a link and without blocking, and anything but a regular file is refused; a file eval writes that is refused fails the trial `sandbox replaced`, unless the machine refused it (`sandbox write failed`, step 15). Then `cmd/fyr`, after the verdicts and in trial order (D6, D22), stores each started trial (§ Data) and ingests its sandbox home into the metrics store with label `eval=` (or `eval=holdout/` under `--suite-file`), outcome `pass`, `fail` or `error`, and the trial's key as every session's `run`, and writes the record. ### Safety checks - a. Refused roots: after resolving links, the clone and the sandbox home are absolute, and neither is `/`, the real home or a parent of it, or the install source's tree or a parent of it. - b. Outside every checkout: `git rev-parse --git-dir` fails with git's own discovery failure, `not a git repository (or any of the parent directories)`, in the nearest existing ancestor of the sandbox root (before anything is created) and in the clone's parent. It fails closed: git runs in the C locale with discovery across mounts, and any other error, a `.git` file whose gitdir is gone included, counts as inside. A `--home` inside a checkout is refused, exit 2, before anything is written (BUG-106). - c. Real config unchanged: the real home's `~/.config/fyr` (minus `eval/` and `work/`, the two sandbox roots: eval's, and the workers' of `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers`, D10 there, and `auto/`, a run's data), `~/.config/sh-agent`, `~/.gemini/config` and `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json`, fingerprinted by relative path, type, mode, size, content hash and link target, before install and at step 14; the differing paths are printed, never content. - d. No new credentials in the sandbox directory (the clone, the CLI's output, the logs and SB): the kit's name, path and content patterns, scanned at step 8 as a baseline and at step 14; a path absent from the baseline, or whose matched patterns or match count grew, fails the row. A dangling link or a link to a directory fails unless the baseline held it with the same target (a directory link the fixture tracks is the fixture's), and a directory link that resolves outside the scanned directory always fails, since nothing walks what it leads to; an unreadable file, or one over 64 MiB (not read), always fails (D17, D32, D37). A `node_modules` directory beside a regular lockfile (`package-lock.json`, `npm-shrinkwrap.json`, `yarn.lock`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `bun.lock`, `bun.lockb`) is a package manager's install: its files are checked by name, path, link and readability, never read, because third-party code carries credential-shaped strings of its own; a link inside it that resolves outside the scanned directory is read as anywhere else, and a file over 64 MiB inside it does not fail, since it is not read (BUG-185). The scan root itself is never such an install. The scan never follows the sandbox directory itself when it is a link. Only paths are printed. - e. No processes left (Linux, `/proc`): a process of the same uid whose cwd or exe lies under the clone or SB as guard a approved them, or whose environment holds exactly `HOME=`, is named, sent SIGTERM, and fails the row. The check fails closed as `procs`: `/proc` that cannot be listed, or a process that cannot be read for any reason but its exit or a permission refusal (a non-dumpable process of the uid, as `ssh-agent`), fails the row, since an agent can exhaust descriptors or memory to hide (`PLAN.md` item 49). A process that leaves the sandbox's paths, drops `HOME` and runs a system binary is not matched, with no privilege needed: the check narrows what a run leaves, and never proves it left nothing. - Step 12's two reads and check d's root fail closed too (`PLAN.md` item 49): after a session, an `err.txt` or CLI log that cannot be read fails the row `sandbox replaced` (`sandbox write failed` for a machine error before any session), and a sandbox directory check d cannot open is a finding. - The sandbox stays what guard a approved: `Box.Intact`, at every step that follows those paths, also fails the row `sandbox replaced` when a file system is mounted at or under the sandbox directory, when the mounts above any of its three paths are no longer those recorded at step 2 (a file system mounted on a parent), or when the mount table cannot be read (Linux, `/proc/self/mountinfo`; `PLAN.md` item 50). A mount inside a namespace of the agent's own is not listed, and is not on the host's paths either. Without `/proc` the check does not run, as check e. - The ingest skips a trial by `sandbox.IntegrityReasons` (`sandbox exists`, `processes left`, `sandbox replaced`, `sandbox write failed`), the one list `fyr work`'s safety reasons start from (`PLAN.md` item 51). - f. Agent invoked: some `SB/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/*.db` holds the bytes `"TypeName":""` (D11, D24). ### The testing record Kind `testing`, status `closed`, in the evaluated project's scope of ``'s brain store (so it is exported to the project's `.agents/trail.jsonl`). Title `Eval —

of PASS at `, `p` and `n` counting the graded trials, followed by ` (k=, errors)` when N is above 1 or a trial was an ERROR. Body: the fyr version, the project and fixture HEADs, the install source (a tree, marked `(dirty)` when anything in it differs from HEAD (`trail.Dirty`, which runs no clean filter) or `(dirty: unknown, )` when that cannot be read, or `embedded `; the header's `harness:` key reads only the installed directories, § Data), then three lines: ``` - runs per row: ; estimator: c/n over graded trials; pass^k = C(c,k)/C(n,k) - model: ; agy: ; harness: - interval: Wilson 95%, per row below and over rows for the suite: [, ] ``` The model is the one model the trials' sessions name in `--home`'s metrics store (`metrics.RunModels`), `mixed (, )` for several, or `unknown` for none (a store that cannot be read names none). The suite's interval is `metrics.WilsonRate` over the rows with a graded trial, each scored by its c/n, an `indicator` row left out, and `n/a` when no row has one; the title and the summary still count every graded trial. Then a line naming the skipped process check off Linux; a table `row | trial | status | cause | reasons | agy exit | seconds | session s | sandbox`, one line per trial, `-` for no cause, no reason or no session; and a table `row | n | c | errors | wilson95 | expect`, one line per row in the order run, its interval `n/a` for a row with no graded trial, its `expect` the `m of n` pooled over the row's trials in this run, `-` when none has an expect list and a main session, or the store cannot be read. Intervals print two decimals. No output of the CLI or a check goes in it. ### Code shape ```go package eval type Row struct{ ID, Setup, Prompt, Prompt2, Check, Agent, Grants string } func ParseSuite(body string) ([]Row, error) func ReadSuiteFile(path string) ([]Row, error) func SelectRows(suite []Row, names []string) ([]Row, error) func Expand(prompt string, vars map[string]string) string func Preflight(o Options) error // checkout, then guards a and b on the sandbox root func Run(ctx context.Context, o Options, rows []Row) ([]Result, error) ``` `Options.Runs` is the trials per row (0 is 1; outside 1–`MaxRuns`, 25, `Run` refuses). A `Result` is one trial: `Row`, `Trial`, `Run` (its key), `Status` (`PASS`, `FAIL` or `ERROR`), `Cause` (empty for a PASS), `Reasons`, `AgyExit`, `Started`, `Seconds`, `SessionSeconds` (the agy sessions, −1 when none started) and `Dir`. On a cancelled context the current trial is an ERROR (`interrupted`) and `Run` returns the trials started with a nil error (D22; the eval-metrics plan D18). `brain.ParseTrail(io.Reader)` parses an export that is not a file in the checkout (HEAD's, from `git show`) under the same cap and line rules as `brain.ReadTrail`. ## Data - Sandboxes: written only by eval, under the sandbox root, never pruned. - `GUIDE-eval`: written by the operator with `fyr record`; eval only reads it. - The `testing` record: written once per invocation by `cmd/fyr` after every trial. - Trials: one `trials` row per trial in `--home`'s metrics store (`SPEC-fyr-metrics` § Data), written by `cmd/fyr` (`cmd/fyr/eval_trial.go`) with `metrics.RecordTrial` after the verdict and before that trial's ingest, whether or not a session ran, after the same `--home` re-check as the ingest: `run`, `label` `eval=` (or `eval=holdout/` under `--suite-file`), `harness` (the install source's short HEAD, with ` (dirty)` when a path under a directory an install reads (`harness.ManagedDirs`: `context/`, `agents/`, `commands/`, `rules/`, `workflows/`, `skills/`) differs from HEAD, tracked or not, or ` (dirty: unknown)` when that cannot be read, so the trail a run's own testing record writes leaves the next run's key alone (`PLAN.md` item 53); `unknown` for a source outside git; `embedded ` for a release binary; taken once before the first trial), `cli` (the first line of `agy --version`), `status` (`pass`, `fail` or `error`, lower case), `cause`, the start, the seconds and the session seconds (NULL when no session started), and the row's `row_version`, `kind` and `cluster` with their defaults applied and its `expect` list, NULL when it has none (ADR-085). `harness` and `cli` are printable and cut to 120 bytes on a rune boundary. A trial whose sandbox existed, was replaced, could not be written by the machine (`sandbox write failed`) or left processes has its row and no session. - Metrics rows: before the ingest, eval registers the row's clone under the eval home (`trail.Register(/.config/fyr, )`, ledger item 76), so the metrics join reads the clone's trail and the row's `eval=` sessions get their handoff, testing, review and bug events; the operator's run of `fyr eval` is the consent, the marker lives in the clone's own git directory and dies with the sandbox, and its seal names the eval home's key. A clone that is a link, or whose git directory or top level resolves outside it (a `.git` file the agent pointed at another repository), is not registered, since the marker would be written there; nor is one when `--home` resolves to the real home or shares its state directory through a link (the seal would take the real key and the join would load the agent's trail into the real brain store). Then its sessions are still ingested, without record events, and the ingest fails with `the clone was not registered, so its sessions have no record events: `. On a system where check e does not run (`ProcsChecked` false, every one but Linux) no clone is registered, since a process left running could swap the git directory between the check and the write: its sessions are ingested without record events, a known limit there and not a failed ingest. A trial that stopped before its clone registers nothing. Then `metrics.Ingest` with `Source` the sandbox home and `Run` the trial's key; the store stamps a label's outcome first-write-wins, so eval ingests only after the verdict. - Invariant: nothing a row's agent does writes the real home's watched config (check c's paths); check c fails the row when something did. The real state directory's `eval/` and `work/` are not watched (D10 of `PLAN-2026-10-29-workers`): a write there is not seen. eval itself, after the rows, writes `--home`'s metrics store and, through the join, its brain store: `--home` is required and never the real home (ledger D37), so neither store is the operator's. ## Failure modes | When | The operator sees | Exit | |---|---|---| | no row and no `--list`; `--list` with a row or with `--runs`; `--runs` outside 1–25 or not an integer; `--suite-file` empty; an unknown flag | the usage or the flag error, naming the flag | 2 | | `--suite-file` inside a checkout, not a regular file, over 1 MiB, or its table does not parse | `eval: --suite-file is inside a git checkout; use a file outside every checkout` / `eval: --suite-file : ` | 2 | | no `--home`; `--home` the real home, or reaching its state directory through a link | `eval: --home is required: …` / `eval: --home is the real home , or shares its state directory; pass a separate home` | 2 | | not a checkout; `--fixture` not a git repository; no install source | `eval: ` | 2 | | the sandbox root inside a checkout | `eval: the sandbox root is inside a git checkout (BUG-106); use a --home outside every checkout` | 2 | | no `GUIDE-eval` in the export; the table does not parse, including a `version`, `kind`, `cluster` or `expect` cell outside its rule (§ The suite) | `eval: `, naming the line | 2 | | `GUIDE-eval` absent from HEAD's export | `eval: GUIDE-eval is not committed; commit it first` | 2 | | `GUIDE-eval` differs from HEAD's | `eval: GUIDE-eval has uncommitted changes; commit them first` | 2 | | a row name unknown or repeated | `eval: no row "" in GUIDE-eval` / `eval: row is named twice` | 2 | | no login token, or it is a link | `eval: no Antigravity login at ` | 2 | | `agy` not on PATH | `eval: agy not found on PATH` | 2 | | a sandbox directory exists, or clone, records list, setup, install or settings fail | that trial is an ERROR with the step's reason; the next trial runs | 1 | | the check fails; the agent not invoked; a denial or an invalid grant | that trial FAILs with the reason | 1 | | a process left, the real config changed, a new credential | that trial FAILs with the reason, even when its check passed or a sandbox step failed | 1 | | agy times out | agy is killed; the check and the exit checks still run; `agy exit -1`; a failing check is cause `timeout` | per the check | | SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP | relayed to agy's group; the trial is an ERROR (`interrupted`); the row's other trials and later rows do not run; the started trials are stored, ingested and recorded | 1 | | SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP before the first row starts | `eval: interrupted before the first row; no record written`; nothing ran, so no sandbox, ingest or record | 1 | | a trial cannot be stored | `eval: # trial: `; the verdict stands and the ingest still runs | 1 | | an ingest fails | `eval: # ingest: `; the verdict stands | 1 | | `--home` came to share the real state during the run | `eval: # trial: not recorded: …` and `eval: # ingest: not ingested: …` for each trial, then `eval: record: not written: …`; no store under the real home is opened | 1 | | the record cannot be written | every row line, then `eval: record: ` | 1 | ## Non-goals - Redacting what a sandbox sends: an agent works on the fixture as any session does (R8, ADR-065). - Running rows in parallel, pruning old sandboxes, a compare or history verb. - Running unasked: no gate, no timer, except `fyr auto` at level `harness` when the operator turned `auto` on (R3, ADR-090). - Isolation from the operator's machine: the token is linked, the CLI's credential broker and `~/.ssh` stay reachable; the checks detect what a run leaves behind, they do not prevent it. ## Known limits - pass^k counted sessions before migration 4: a `prompt2` row added two sessions per run under one label (D12). Since Phase 2a of `PLAN-2026-10-31-0300-plan-eval-metrics-the-standard-set-collected-fro`, `fyr eval` records every trial with `metrics.RecordTrial` and ingests its sessions with the trial's `run`, so a trial counts once, whatever the number of sessions; every session stored before keeps a NULL `run` and still counts per session (`SPEC-fyr-metrics` § Data). - Two trials whose install source was dirty at the same HEAD share one `harness` key: the key does not tell those trees apart (the eval-metrics plan D15; the release rule demands a clean tree). Since `PLAN.md` P7 (item 53, D16) the dirty mark reads only the installed directories, so a tree whose only edits are under `cmd/`, `internal/` or the trail keeps the clean key: two `fyr` binaries built from one HEAD with different code edits share it, and their trials are mixed in `fyr metrics evals`' per-key flags. The key names the installed harness, not the binary. - When the harness itself is the fixture, a row whose agent writes records can make SQLite copy a page holding a quoted key header (this harness's trail quotes some) into the sandbox's `brain.db` or its WAL; check d then sees a count grow with no new credential, a false FAIL in the safe direction (D33). - Check d does not read the files of a `node_modules` beside a lockfile: a credential's content written there, under a name the name patterns do not match, is not seen (BUG-185; the operator's choice, 2026-10-27, so an app build that installs packages can pass). - A write to a path check c watches by any other process during a row, the operator's own concurrent session included, fails the row `real config changed`, as with the old kit (D33). The real token and the CLI's conversations are not watched: a sandboxed session refreshes the token through its link, and the operator's own sessions write the conversations. - `named` grants are not a containment boundary: `bash`, `python3`, `go`, `git` and `ln` each run anything as the operator's uid, and `HOME=SB` is only a variable, so the agent can reach the real home by absolute path. The checks detect what a run leaves in the paths they watch; they prevent nothing. Containment (a user namespace) would be a requirements change (security review of 2026-10-26). - A check reads what the agent could write (the sandbox's `fyr` and its stores, the clone): a PASS is evidence of a cooperative agent's behaviour, not proof against one that forges its evidence (security review of 2026-10-26). - fyr killed by SIGKILL or the OOM killer leaves the token link in that sandbox and agy running; nothing sweeps old sandboxes. - A process that escapes check e (another cwd, another `HOME`, its own session) can still replace the sandbox after step 14. The ingest refuses a link at the sandbox home or on its way down to `conversations`, and skips a row that left processes (`processes left`), so a replacement it can see is not read (IN35 and the security review of its fix). - Check e sends SIGTERM to every process of the operator's uid whose cwd lies under the clone or the sandbox: an operator shell, editor or `tail -f` sitting there while a row runs is killed, and the row FAILs `processes left`. Keep them out of the sandbox during a run (IN45 of the 2026-10-27 audit). - Eval's own writes (`out.txt`, `out2.txt`, `err.txt`, `setup.log`, `check.log`) refuse a name whose file has another hard link, or that changed between the open and the check, before anything is truncated; a directory swapped in above those names is not guarded (IN49; a Follow-up of the 2026-10-27 audit fix). - Check b's discovery across mounts has no test: it needs a mount. - A process that escapes check e and replaces an ancestor of the sandbox directory between check e and check d's intact test is not tested: it is a timing window; the directory itself replaced by a link is caught by the scan, which never follows it. - Trust: `setup` and `check` are bash from the project's committed suite and run as the operator's uid with the real home reachable; the suite is always the project root's, never the fixture's, so running `fyr eval` trusts the project as much as running its tests (D30). - Check d skips every file that starts with an executable's magic (ELF, either Mach-O byte order, or `CAFEBABE`, which a Java class and a universal Mach-O share): a credential written into such a file, or into any file given that four-byte prefix, is not seen (audit IN47). - Sandboxes are never pruned: every trial of every run leaves its directory under `/.config/fyr/eval////` (the clone, the HOME the CLI ran with, `out.txt`, `err.txt` and the logs, none redacted), so the eval home grows with each run, by N directories per row under `--runs N`, until the operator removes old stamps by hand. - The `--home` re-checks before each trial's store write, each ingest and the record narrow, never close, the window: a link made between a re-check and the store's open still sends that store's write through it. Nothing re-checks between trials, so a link a trial's agent makes under `/.config/fyr` puts the next trial's sandbox where it leads; that trial's write, its ingest and the record are then refused, but the sandbox is written (security review of D37, round 2). - The account's home comes from the account database; without cgo on Linux that is `/etc/passwd` alone, so for an LDAP, SSSD or systemd-homed account only `$HOME` is compared. - Off Linux there is no `/proc`: check e prints that it did not run and the record says so; the final process-group kill still runs (plan O1). ## Open questions - None open. A `ps`-based check e for macOS is a follow-up, built after it is tried on the Mac (plan O1). ## Verification - `go test -race ./internal/eval/ ./internal/sandbox/`: in `internal/eval`, the suite grammar and refusals (`TestSuite*`, `TestEvalSuiteFile`), check f (`TestInvoked*`), the records step (`TestPrepareRecordsBaselineRefused`) and `Run` against a fake agy (`TestRun*`, `--runs` in `TestRunTrials` and `TestRunRunsRefused`), the status and cause (`TestClassify`, `TestClassifyEveryReason`), the trial line (`TestResultLine`); in `internal/sandbox`, each other safety check with its kit cases (`TestGuard*`, `TestCreds*`, `TestProcs*`), the other step arms (`TestPrepare*`, `TestAgy*`) and a `Box` against a recording fake agy (`TestBox*`, the trial path in `TestBoxMakeTrialPath`); each check mutation-checked. eval's side of the work-only options: without the store skip, check c still sees a write to each store (`TestGuardFingerprintSkipStores`, `TestBoxSkipStoresExitChecks`), and with no model agy gets no `--model` (`TestBoxSessionModel`). - `go test -race ./cmd/fyr/ -run Eval`: the verb's refusals, golden path, failing row, two-session row (one `run` on both sessions), `--runs 3` (`TestEvalVerbRuns`), `--suite-file` refusal inside a checkout and `eval=holdout/` labelling outside (`TestEvalSuiteFile`), an ERROR trial with no session (`TestEvalVerbErrorTrial`), an unrun trial (`TestEvalVerbUnrunTrials`), the record's title, header and two tables under `--runs 2` with one ERROR (`TestEvalVerbRecord`, `TestEvalTally`), trial-write, ingest and record failures, interrupt, and `--list` (`TestEvalVerb*`), each checking the `trials` rows through `fyr metrics export`; the `--home` refusals, nothing written under the real home, no migration (`TestEvalRefusesItsHome`). - `go test -race ./internal/brain/ -run ParseTrail`: `ParseTrail` equals `ReadTrail` on the same bytes, with the same refusals. - End to end, on a box with the CLI and a login: `fyr eval --fixture project-memory feature lane-reviewer --home `, then `fyr record get ` and `fyr metrics show --label eval=project-memory --json` (`GUIDE-fyr-matrix` § eval). Re-read 2026-11-01 against `ae347bf..40c5593` (`fyr auto` plan Phase 2: the risk rubric, the `auto` skill, the six skill sentences, `slashNote` shortened by 9 bytes, and the three `auto-*` adversarial rows in `GUIDE-eval`): nothing here changes. Re-read 2026-11-01 against `31665e3` (`fyr auto` plan Phase 3: the worker runner, Kickoff builder and runner choice in `internal/auto/`, `internal/work/` and `cmd/fyr/verb_auto.go`): nothing here changes. Re-read 2026-11-01 for `fyr auto` plan Phase 7: nothing here changes.

# The memory loop — one store, and the `dreamer` agent

Status: built 2026-09-29 (plan `PLAN-2026-09-29-dreamer-memory-loop`); writing and loading moved to `fyr memory` on 2026-09-30 (R10, plan `PLAN-2026-09-30-parity-memory-dream`). The hourly background job is `SPEC-fyr-dream`. Code: `internal/brain/memory.go` (the store behind `fyr memory`) and `internal/memory` (the project root, and the old `.agents/memory/` store `fyr dream` still reads); the agent is `agents/dreamer/agent.md`.

Re-read 2026-11-01 against `485adbf` (`fyr auto` plan Phase 1a: `internal/auto`, `cmd/fyr/verb_auto.go`, `dream.Timer`, `auto` in `sandboxDirs`, the check vocabulary and the metrics verb list): under this spec's code only the shared timer rendering changed; nothing here changes.

Re-read 2026-11-01 against `7a084ab` (`fyr auto` plan Phase 1b: `internal/auto`'s gates and checks, `cmd/fyr/verb_auto.go` and `verb_auto_checks.go`, `auto`'s `run` registered in `init`, the help page): nothing here changes.

Re-read 2026-10-31 against `22d8ecd..37756a3` (`PLAN.md` P12b: under this spec's code `cmd/fyr/eval.go`'s ingest reads `sandbox.Compromised` and skips the same reasons, and `skills/work`'s stop list names `sandbox exists`; nothing here describes either).

Re-read 2026-10-31 against `62020f5` (`PLAN.md` P12: under this spec's code only `fyr help`'s install, uninstall and memory text, `rules/agy-dispatch.md` and one `skills/work` line changed): nothing here changes.

Re-read 2026-10-31 against `825ff6f` (`PLAN.md` P11: `frontend-ui-economist` and `frontend-ui-modern` replace `frontend`; under this spec's code only skill text, `TestInstallLeavesClaudeCodeAlone`'s guard and `TestSuiteHarness`'s `want` changed): nothing here changes.

Re-read 2026-10-31 against `bd2d6b4` (`PLAN.md` P10b, ADR-087: a dream reads records only, the global index holds no file, reversing the P10a line below that it holds `~/.config/fyr`'s files; `trail.Dates`, `memory.Store` and `harness.LastRetro` go, the search schema is 3, eval's setup gets `FYR`, and `record import --dry-run` prints no stored count): nothing else here changes.

Re-read 2026-10-31 against `d66b87e` (`PLAN.md` P9: `fyr metrics evals` gains `kind` and `expect` columns, the testing record `expect`, and the verb list `fyr`'s five missing verbs): nothing here changes.

Re-read 2026-10-31 against `6affb08` (the v5.0.0 gate's fixes: every test package's `TestMain` sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`, three `go list` tests pass `GOPROXY=off`, `internal/serve`'s tests take a temp HOME, and `fyr help`'s `work` line and `cmd/fyr/main.go`'s doc comment changed; none of it reaches this verb's code): nothing here changes.

## The store

- **Where:** `memory` records in the brain store, `~/.config/fyr/brain.db`, in the project's scope (the main worktree's root, so every worktree shares one; `SPEC-fyr-record` § Memory). Never exported to `.agents/trail.jsonl`, never committed, local to the machine (brain plan D14, ADR-063). Since brain plan Phase 2 (2026-10-25) it replaces the old per-checkout `.agents/memory/` directory, which `fyr record import` (project) and `import --global` (every registered project, ADR-068: an indexed project without `fyr index --register` is not read) migrate.
- **Shape:** one record per memory, ID `MEMORY-<name>`, the description as its title, `provenance` (`operator`, `derived` or `unknown`), the body `type: <user|feedback|project|reference>`, a blank line, then the text. Every record stored before migration 2 or imported by `fyr record import` reads as `unknown`, never `operator` (D12).
- **Who writes:** `fyr memory add --type T --name SLUG --description TEXT [--provenance operator|derived]` (body on stdin; default `operator`; `--provenance derived` when an agent session saves from a file or tool output; the same name replaces), called by the `project-memory` skill and by `feedback-log` rule 7, and `brain.MemoryDraft` (`add`, `retire`, `merge`, `provenance: derived`), called by `fyr auto`'s draft writer (`SPEC-fyr-auto`). `/retro` promotes neither `derived` nor `unknown` to a rule or a skill without the operator's word. Serialised by the store's write transaction.
- **Who reads:** every session runs `fyr memory show` at the end of the resume order; it prints one line per memory, capped at 200 lines and 25 KB. `fyr record get MEMORY-<name>` prints one in full. `/dream` consolidates them; the `dreamer` agent reads them.
- **Lost:** with `brain.db`. Memory has no second copy, as before (R4, R7).

## The `dreamer` agent

- **What it is:** the consolidation judgement of the learning loop, run by an author-independent reader: given the store and the trail, what should become a rule, a skill or a procedure, and what should be left alone. It proposes; it never applies.
- **Definition:** `agents/dreamer/agent.md` — tools `view_file, grep_search, find_by_name, run_command, write_to_file`; no `model` key (the CLI's default); installed as written like every agent (`delivery.md` § Agents).
- **Dispatch text (the contract):** `Project: <root>. Since: <date of the newest retro record titled "Retro —", or "all">. Promoted: <the memories /dream flagged promote, or none>.` plus the standard draft and budget sentences. Never the conversation. The dreamer does not re-derive `/dream`'s verdicts: the promoted memories are its rule-candidate inputs, one candidate row per memory.
- **Reads:** the memory (`fyr memory show`, each with `fyr record get MEMORY-<name>`); the trail since the date — the three newest `handoff` records, the `bug` records and their prevention rules, the `change` records; what already exists — the global context, the global rule files (`~/.gemini/config/rules/*.md`), the project `AGENTS.md` and `<project>/.agents/rules/`, the installed skills' descriptions (`fyr list` or the skill directories), so a candidate is never something a rule already says.
- **Candidate tests:** a **rule** for each file on the dispatch's `Promoted:` line (given, never re-judged: `/dream` owns the two-memory test), for a bug whose prevention rule is recorded nowhere loaded and that recurs (two bugs, or a bug and a memory on the same fact), and for a memory of any type that a trail record restates (a handoff or `change` record on the same fact) when no loaded rule holds it; a **skill** when a memory or the trail shows a procedure of three or more steps done more than once (`/distill`'s bar); a **procedure** (a `references/` page for an existing skill) when the steps belong to a skill that exists; **none** otherwise, listed under "Left alone" with the reason.
- **Writes:** one draft, `.agents/scratch/agents/dreamer-<stamp>.md`, written early with `Status: IN PROGRESS` and finished with `COMPLETE`: Scope, Summary, a Candidates table (`#`, kind, target file, the exact rule text or the draft's path, evidence as `file:line` and record IDs), "Left alone", "Not examined"; the caller stores it as a `retro` record (brain plan D12). Drafts for skills go under `.agents/scratch/dreamer/<date>/<name>/SKILL.md`. No other file, ever; no edit to source, config, rules, skills or memory.
- **Consumers:** `/retro` dispatches it (Step 1 source 8) and turns rule candidates into proposals through its own Step 2 (target, scope, promotion check) — the one place that decides where a rule lives; `/distill` dispatches it first and takes its skill and procedure candidates as candidates. No global index record of its own; the retro or distill record cites its record's ID.

## Error handling

| Situation | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| No store, or an empty one | `/dream` and the `dreamer` say so in one line; the resume clause reads nothing |
| `~/.config/fyr/` denied to the session | the reader says so; the `dreamer` artifact still writes into the project trail |
| Agent cut at its turn limit | a partial artifact with `Status: IN PROGRESS` (its early-write rule); the caller says so |
| `git clean -fdx`, a fresh clone, a deleted checkout | the memory stays: it is in `~/.config/fyr/brain.db`, keyed by the checkout's root, not in the checkout |
| `brain.db` lost | the memory is lost with it; there is no second copy (R4) |
| an old `.agents/memory` that is a symlink, or one git tracks anything under | `fyr record import` refuses it, its one reader; `fyr dream` reads memory records only (ADR-087) |

## Known differences (R10)

Retired (plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` Phase 2): the harness targets one CLI, so there is no difference between CLIs to list. PRD.md R10 does not cite this section; the limits of the one CLI (compaction window, cost, denials) are in PRD.md § Known limits.

Re-read 2026-11-01 against `31665e3` (`fyr auto` plan Phase 3: the worker runner, Kickoff builder and runner choice in `internal/auto/`, `internal/work/` and `cmd/fyr/verb_auto.go`): nothing here changes.

## Purpose

`fyr metrics` keeps the **shape** of every Antigravity session in `~/.config/fyr/metrics.db`. Shape means:
- the tools each session called;
- the normalised command verbs;
- tokens, timings and errors;
- events joined from git and the trail.

The operator queries the store for agent evaluations (`show`, `report`). The hourly dreamer and `/retro` read it as evidence for proposals; every checkpoint feeds it (§ When ingest runs).

It is not:
- a transcript archive: it holds no arguments and no prose;
- a cache: it is the only copy once a transcript expires (R4);
- sent anywhere: it stays on the machine (ADR-062).

Decisions: ADR-055. Plan: `PLAN-2026-10-08-metrics-store`.

## Interfaces

### Verbs

The verbs reuse the global `--home` flag. `--vendor` does not exist (a usage error, exit 2): `ingest` reads Antigravity only (ADR-062, plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` D7).

```
fyr metrics ingest [--home H] [--source DIR --label KEY=VALUE [--outcome pass|fail|error]]
fyr metrics show   [--home H] [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--until YYYY-MM-DD] [--project DIR] [--label KEY=VALUE | --all-labels] [--context-target N] [--json]
fyr metrics report [--home H] [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--until YYYY-MM-DD] [--project DIR] [--label KEY=VALUE | --all-labels] [--context-target N] [--out FILE]
fyr metrics evals  [--home H] [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--until YYYY-MM-DD] [--harness KEY] [--json]
fyr metrics export [--home H] FILE
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--source` | directory | none | A sandbox home: `DIR/.gemini/antigravity-cli`. Requires `--label`. |
| `--label` | `KEY=VALUE` | none | On `ingest`: stamped on every session added from `--source`. On `show`/`report`: shows only that label. |
| `--outcome` | `pass`, `fail`, `error` | none | The run's acceptance result, supplied by the kit or by `fyr eval`, which calls the same ingest in-process for each sandbox after its verdict, with `--label eval=<row>` (`SPEC-fyr-eval`), used for pass^k; `error` is a trial whose sandbox, clone or setup failed before the agent could be graded (`SPEC-fyr-eval`'s `ERROR` status), counted apart in A6 and never as a failure. Given after the run (a second ingest of the same `--source` and `--label`), it stamps every session of the label that has no outcome yet, even when no transcript changed; an earlier run keeps the outcome it was stamped with. In Go, `Options.Run` names the trial the source's sessions belong to (`trials.run`, § Data), written on each session at insert and kept first-write-wins; it has no flag, and `Validate` and `Ingest` both refuse one given without `Source` (it would stamp the real home's sessions), not printable or over 120 bytes. |
| `--all-labels` | bool | false | Include labelled (sandbox) sessions. Without it, and without `--label`, they are excluded. |
| `--since` | date | 30 days ago | Start of the window. |
| `--until` | date | now | End of the window, exclusive (`show`, `report`, `evals`). `--since A --until B` and `--since B` never overlap; `/retro` reads the window before its own this way. A session belongs to the window it starts in, `[since, until)`, and is counted whole there, so adjacent windows never share one. |
| `--project` | directory | all | Only sessions whose `project_root` is this directory or under it (a session started in a subdirectory is the project's; a sibling that only shares the name's prefix is not). |
| `--context-target` | token count above 0 | 300000 | The peak context a main session should stay under (`show`, `report`). B3 counts the main sessions whose peak passed it; the value is a flag, not a pin, so `/retro` can tune phase sizing against it without a rebuild (plan `2026-10-23-session-sized-work.md` D4, D15). |
| `--json` | bool | false | Print the `## Output` object (`show`) or the per-row view (`evals`) instead of tables. |
| `--harness` | harness key | all | `evals` only: the trials whose `harness` equals this key exactly (§ Data); `unknown` keeps the sessions no trial claims. On any other subcommand, a usage error. |
| `--out` | file | `~/.config/fyr/reports/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>-metrics.html` | Where the report is written. An existing file is refused. |

### Where transcripts are read from

The first rule that applies wins:
1. `--source DIR`
2. `--home H` → `H/.gemini/antigravity-cli`
3. the real home

Ingest reads only the Antigravity CLI's directory; there is no other source. A conversation whose first workspace is the dream's working directory, `<home>/.config/fyr/dream-work` as written or with its symlinks followed (`harness.DreamWorkPaths`), for `--home` and for `--source` alike, is the dream's own (ADR-073): it is not a session and gets no `ingest_state` row (`internal/metrics/agy.go`).

### `ingest` output and exit status

On success it prints this line and exits 0:

```
metrics: N sessions, M steps, K events added; F sources failed
```

- Exit 1 when F > 0. Each failed source is named on its own line, and every other source is still ingested.
- Exit 2 on a usage error.

### When ingest runs

At the moments the context names (R0), run by the agent; nothing inside `fyr` triggers it (no ingest from `fyr record add`, R3):
- the `handoff` skill's last call, after the handoff is stored, committed and pushed; its summary line, or its error and exit status, goes in the chat report;
- `/retro` step 11, before its two `show` calls; skipped under `--dry-run`, which writes nothing and says the numbers are from the last ingest;
- the phase-end checkpoint in the global context (Checkpoint box, `change` record, commit, push, `fyr metrics ingest`);
- every real `fyr dream` run, hourly while an `agy` session runs (`SPEC-fyr-dream`);
- the operator, by hand.

Each run is incremental (per-source offsets in `ingest_state`) and joins every session's events again, so a missed or failed run is made up by the next one. Measured on copies of one box's store (24 MB `metrics.db`, 17 MB Antigravity directory, 2026-10-25): 0.2 s.

### Normalised verb

`Verb(cmd string) []string` reduces a command line to its shape: one string per command in it, `program [subcommand] [flag names…]`.

**What is removed before splitting:**
- here-document bodies (`<<EOF`, `<<-EOF`, `<<'EOF'`);
- comments;
- the insides of quotes, `${…}` and `$((…))`, which stay part of their word and are never split.

**Where it splits:** at `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, `&`, newlines, `(`, `$(`, backticks, `{` and `}`. A redirection such as `2>&1` or `&>f` is part of a word, not a separator.

**What is skipped in front of the program:**
- shell keywords that lead a command (`if then else elif do while until !`);
- the wrappers `sudo env command time nohup exec`, with their own flags and those flags' values (`env -u NAME`);
- `VAR=value` words;
- leading redirections and their targets.

**Segments that yield no verb:**
- a segment opened by `for`, `case`, `select` or `function`, or closed by `done`, `fi`, `esac` or `in`;
- a case pattern, i.e. the words before its `)`.

**The program:**
- It is the basename of the first remaining word. For `go run <target>`, see the `go run` rule below.
- It must match `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.+-]*$`; any other word in command position (a glob, an expansion, a quoted path) yields no verb.
- A subcommand is kept only from a fixed allowlist per tool (`subcommands` in `internal/metrics/verb.go`): git, go, gh, docker, gcloud, kubectl, npm, terraform and fyr. An unlisted word is dropped and the verb is the program alone, because that position can hold a short secret (`gh hunter2pass`). npx's package is never kept. git's global options (`-C dir`, `-c k=v`) are skipped before the subcommand. After fyr's subcommand, one more word is kept when it is one of `ingest show report evals export add` (operator, 2026-10-09: allowlists). Every verb of the binary is on fyr's list (`TestEveryVerbSurvivesTheVerbList`, in `cmd/fyr`), since a suite row's `expect` names verbs.
- A word that quoting or an escape made flag-shaped is content, never a flag (`"--x"`, `'-ab'`, `\--x`; `PLAN.md` item 55). A quote after `=` stays in the value, which is dropped anyway. An unquoted value shaped like a flag (`--title --x`) still reads as a flag.

**Flag names:**
- A long flag `--name[=v]` is kept as `--name` only when the name is lowercase letters, digits and dashes, at most 24 characters (`--sk_live_…`, `--Authorization` are dropped).
- For `go gofmt govulncheck find`, `-name[=v]` is kept as `-name` only when the name is lowercase letters and digits, at most 24 characters.
- A short group of at most three letters is kept whole (`-la`, `-rnw`).
- Any other short flag keeps its first letter only (`-c1-200`, `-psecret`, `-xzvf` become `-c`, `-p`, `-x`), because a short option can carry its value glued on.
- A dash followed by a digit (`-20`) is a value and is dropped.

**Never kept:** positional words, except a bare `.` after `git add`.

**Here-documents:**
- A delimiter is read literally, as bash does. A quoted one runs to its closing quote (`<<'END!'`, `<<"$D"`). An unquoted one is the whole word up to a shell metacharacter (`<<END!`, `<<$END`). The body ends only at a line equal to it.
- A here-doc with no delimiter word cannot be matched, so nothing after its line is read.

**`go run`:** the target counts as the program only when it is a tool the subcommand allowlist knows (`go run ./cmd/fyr search` is `fyr search`). Any other target is content, and the verb is `go run` plus its flag names.

A program name longer than 32 characters is content and is dropped.

**Transcript lines:** a line is read in bounded chunks. A line over 16 MB is consumed and skipped, never held in memory whole. An unterminated tail over that size is passed over rather than re-read on every ingest.

**Tool names** follow the identifier rule below; one that fails it is stored as `unnamed`. Everything `metrics ingest` prints (paths, project roots, errors) goes through search's BUG-152 filter: control, format (bidi overrides, zero-width marks), line-separator and paragraph-separator characters become `?`, by Unicode class, because a `--source` sandbox writes those values. `show`'s text output prints a key holding any of them as `?`. Ingest opens no file of its own: an Antigravity database is copied through `search.OpenCopy`, which opens each source without blocking and checks on the opened file that it is a regular file, and the trail is read through the brain store (`brain.ForMetrics`), so a FIFO swapped in after an earlier check neither hangs the ingest nor is read.

**Identifiers:** a skill name, a model or an agent type is stored only when it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.:@/-]{0,63}$`; otherwise it is left empty. So no escape bytes or prose reach the store or the terminal. A subagent's `.meta.json` is read only as a regular file of 64 KB or less.

**Known limit:** a shell construct the tokenizer does not model can still put one identifier-shaped word in command position. That is never more than a single name-shaped word, never a path, a value or prose. Verbs reflect the normaliser of the binary that ingested them; the command itself is never stored, so older rows are not re-normalised.

### Shared tool vocabulary

Antigravity tool names map to a common name. Unknown names are kept as `agy:<name>`. The Claude Code column maps nothing new: it names the tools of the historical rows an older ingest stored, which are kept and read, never written.

| Common | Claude Code (historical) | Antigravity |
|---|---|---|
| Bash | `Bash` | `run_command` |
| Read | `Read` | `view_file`, `read_file` |
| Write | `Write` | `write_to_file`, `write_file` |
| Edit | `Edit` | `replace_file_content`, `multi_replace_file_content`, `edit_file` |
| Grep | `Grep` | `grep_search` |
| Glob | `Glob` | `find_by_name` |
| LS | (none) | `list_dir` |
| Agent | `Agent` | `invoke_subagent` |
| SendMessage | `SendMessage` | `send_message` |

The Antigravity names come from the spike over the local conversation databases (plan D35); `read_file`, `write_file` and `edit_file` are agy 1.4.7's, found in the eval conversations of 2026-10-26 (BUG-184). `manage_subagents` and any other name not in this table are kept as `agy:<name>`.

**Where the shape is read:** Antigravity: the tool name is at `steps.metadata` 4→2 and the arguments JSON at 4→3, which gives `CommandLine` and the path, under the key its tool sends: `AbsolutePath` (`view_file`), `Path` (`read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`) or `TargetFile` (`write_to_file`, `replace_file_content`, `multi_replace_file_content`). The step time is at `metadata` 1→1, in seconds. An error is status 7. A subagent is its own conversation; `conversation_summaries.agent_name` and `parent_conversation_id` give its type and parent. Usage, the model and the context are in `gen_metadata`: 1→4→2/3/5, 1→19 and 1→9→10→1.

A **skill load** is a read of `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (only `<name>` is stored). A historical Claude Code row's `Skill` call stays as stored.

### Output (`show --json`)

Keys are snake_case. Every metric is keyed by vendor, and `columns` lists the vendors present: `["agy"]`, or `["agy","claude"]` when the window holds sessions with vendor `claude` that an older ingest stored (historical rows: kept, never written again, plan D7). The `claude` keys appear only then; the example below shows that case. A metric the CLI cannot produce is `null` and is named in `notes`, never shown as 0. The shape is the Go type `metrics.Summary`:

```json
{
  "window": {"since": "2026-09-08", "until": "2026-10-08"},
  "columns": ["agy", "claude"],

The values above illustrate the shape. They are not fixtures. In text, `show` prints one `agy` column, plus `claude (historical)` as a second one only when the window holds such rows. Each `pass_k` entry is A6 (§ Metric definitions) for one label: `k`, `passed` and `pass_k` keep their first meaning (all k passed) for the consumers that read them; `n` counts the graded trials, `c` the passed ones, `errors` the `error` trials; `pass_at` and `pass_pow` are given for k in 1, 3, 5 up to n and omitted above n, never written as a non-number; `wilson95` is the interval of c of n, `[0, 0]` when n is 0; `flip` is 1 when 0 < c < n. Rates are rounded to four decimals. The text line reads `pass^k <label>: <c> of <n> passed, pass^<n> = <0|1>; n <n>, c <c>, errors <e>, wilson95 [<lo>, <hi>], flip <0|1>`. `daily` holds one entry per UTC day with activity, keyed by the step's own time, so an idle day has none and a session that ran past the window's end can add a later day (SD52 of the 2026-10-27 audit); the report's trend charts read it. `session_peaks` lists main sessions only, largest peak first, one list per vendor that has a session with a context value in the window; `sessions_over_context_target` counts the entries of that list past `context_target` and is `null`, named in `notes`, for a vendor with no such session (never 0). A session's id and start day are the only identifiers carried: no project path, no content (plan D6, D16).

### Per-row view (`metrics evals`)

`metrics evals` is the suite's view over the trials in `--home`'s store (the eval-metrics plan § Interfaces; `PLAN.md` P7). It reads `trials`, which only `fyr eval` writes, so it needs no `--all-labels`; it also counts each main session of an `eval=` label with an outcome that no trial claims (stored before migration 4) as one graded trial under harness `unknown`, as A6 does. A trial belongs to no project, so `--project` is refused with every flag `evals` does not read (exit 2; `PLAN.md` D16). It never gates (R3).

One line per row and row version (`label`, `row_version`; a trial with no `row_version` and a session no trial claims, both stored before the suite's version column, read as version 1, the suite's default, so a row's history does not split when `fyr eval` starts writing it; ADR-085) with a trial that started in the window, sorted by row then version:

`row | v | kind | n | c | errors | pass@1 | pass^3 | wilson95 | flip | turns | tool calls | tokens in/out/cache | session s | active s | tool err % | retries | peak ctx | expect | last | flags`

- `n`, `c`, `errors`, `pass@1`, `pass^3` (= C(c,3)/C(n,3)), `wilson95` and `flip` are A6's over the line's trials; `pass^3` is `n/a` below n = 3, and `pass@1` and `wilson95` are `n/a` at n = 0.
- The efficiency columns are means over the line's main sessions (a `prompt2` trial has two), counted as `show` counts them: a user step is a turn, a tool step a call, a Bash call repeating the last one's command hash a retry, a gap under five minutes active time; `tokens cache` is cache read plus cache write; `peak ctx` is the mean of each session's peak; `session s` is over the sessions with both ends; `tool err %` is pooled over the calls. A step replayed from another session of the line is counted once. A line with no session prints `-` for each.
- `kind` is the stored kind of the line's newest counted trial; a trial with none, or a line of sessions no trial claims, reads as `capability` (a row's kind can change with no new version).
- `expect` is `m of n`, pooled over the line's graded trials that stored an expect list and have a main session (`ExpectMatches`, `evals_expect.go`): each trial's own list against the tools and verbs of its main sessions together, a subagent's left out, so three trials of a two-entry list give `5 of 6`. An entry is found when it equals a tool name or a verb, or leads a verb word by word (`fyr record` in `fyr record add --title`, never a word cut short). `-` when no trial counts. It never gates.
- `last` is the UTC day of the line's newest trial in the window.
- `flags` read the line's whole history in the store, not the window, over graded trials whose harness is not `unknown` (`PLAN.md` D16): `unstable` when one key both passed and failed; `broken` when no trial passed; `saturated` when none failed and at least two keys have three or more trials; `history` when the line has no graded trial under a known key. At most one flag; `-` for none.

Then the suite lines over the lines with a graded trial, an `indicator` line left out of all of them: their count, the graded trials, the errors, the pass rate (the mean of each line's c/n) with its Wilson 95 % interval over lines (`WilsonRate`) and C_out; one line each for `regression`, `adversarial` and `indicator` with a graded line of that kind, naming its lines, graded trials and rate with its interval (a `regression` or `adversarial` line also counts in the rate above; the `indicator` line says it does not); and the trajectory similarity, the mean over lines with two or more main sessions of their pairwise `SeqSimilarity` over the tool names in step order. `--json` prints `metrics.EvalRows` with the same numbers: `window`, `harness` when given, `rows` (an empty list, never null), each with `row`, `version` (1 or more), `kind`, `n`, `c`, `errors`, `pass_at_1`, `pass_pow_3`, `wilson95`, `flip`, `means` (`sessions`, `turns`, `tool_calls`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `tokens_cache`, `session_seconds`, `active_seconds`, `tool_error_rate`, `retries`, `peak_context`), `expect` (`m`, `n`), `last`, `flags`; and `suite` (`rows`, `trials`, `errors`, `pass_rate`, `wilson95`, `c_out`, `trajectory_similarity`, `trajectory_rows`, and `regression`, `adversarial`, `indicator`, each `rows`, `trials`, `pass_rate`, `wilson95`). A value a line cannot have is an absent key, never a non-number; rates are rounded to four decimals. With no line in the window, the text is the window line and `no eval trial in the window: fyr eval writes them`. The trials live in the home `fyr eval` wrote to, so the way to see them is that home's `--home` (`fyr metrics evals --home ~/sandbox/fyr-eval/home`).

### Report (`metrics report`)

`metrics report` writes one HTML file, mode 0600. An existing file is refused. The default path is `~/.config/fyr/reports/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>-metrics.html`.

**How it is built:**
- `html/template` with SVG drawn in Go;
- no `<script>`, no URL to any host, no `@import` or `url(`;
- light and dark through `prefers-color-scheme`.

**Colours.** Colour follows the CLI and never its rank: Antigravity keeps categorical slot 2, orange (`#eb6834` / `#d95926`); the historical column, "Claude Code (historical)" in the report, is slot 1, blue (`#2a78d6` light / `#3987e5` dark), drawn only when the window holds historical rows. That pair is the dataviz reference palette's first two slots, validated in both modes. Colours are set by CSS classes, because html/template sanitises a CSS variable in a `style` attribute.

**Hover and identity.** Hover values are SVG `<title>` elements, which browsers show without script. Identity never rests on colour alone: the legend names each CLI drawn, each line is labelled where it ends, and every chart has its numbers as a table.

**Charts:**
- tool calls, tokens, cost, the search:grep ratio and tool errors per day, one line per CLI;
- tool calls by tool (the ten most used);
- subagent tool calls by type;
- graded trials passed of n per sandbox label, the Wilson 95 % interval of c of n drawn as a whisker over the bar, the error trials and `flip` written in the value text, and the table carrying `passed`, `k`, `pass^k`, `n`, `c`, `errors`, `wilson95` and `flip` (`pass_at` and `pass_pow` are in `show --json` only);
- the eval rows, under the pass^k chart: the table of `metrics evals` over the report's window and its suite lines; left out under `--project` and when the window holds no suite trial;
- the summary table, where the row `sessions over context target (<N>)` reads `k of n`: k the main sessions whose peak passed the target, n the main sessions in the window with a peak at all; `n/a` for a vendor with none.

**Missing values.** A value a CLI cannot produce is not drawn:
- no Antigravity cost line;
- no search:grep point on a day with no grep call.

Tables show those values as `n/a`.

**Consistency.** Every number in the report comes from the same `Summary` as `show --json` over the same window and filters; the eval rows come from the same `Store.Evals` as `metrics evals` over that window.

**Known limit:** at 400 px the SVG scales down, and tick labels get small (about 6 px) but stay legible. The tables give the same numbers at full size.

### Metric definitions

| Id | Metric | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | DoD closure | A main session's window is `[started_at, ended_at + 30 min]`. The session is closed when the window holds at least one commit in its project AND a handoff: in a migrated project, a `handoff` record whose record time falls in it (§ Invariants, Trail from records only). |
| A2 | Verifier status | The `## Status:` heading of `testing` records in the window whose title matches `^Verif(ication\|y)\b` (the verifier's own title), so a behavioural-run record does not count. Main sessions only. |
| A3 | Review findings | `**[high\|medium\|low / confidence: …]**` lines in `review` records in the window. Main sessions only. |
| A4 | Escaped bugs | A `bug` record whose text contains a hex prefix of 7 or more characters of one of the session's commits. An imported closed bug holds only its title and prevention rule, so it gives none; events stored before the migration stay. |
| A5 | Corrections | Feedback entries in the window whose project is the session's root: global `feedback` records about the root's main worktree, for every root (migrated, unmigrated or gone). An entry is keyed by its `ts` in UTC, so one an older ingest stored from the `feedback.jsonl` log in another offset counts once with its record; the log itself is no longer read (ledger Phase 10, item 66); a body that is not JSON or has no RFC 3339 `ts` is skipped. |
| A6 | pass^k | Per label, over its trials in the window: a `trials` row with status `pass` or `fail` is one graded trial, an `error` row is counted apart and never graded, and a main session with an outcome that no trial in the store claims (`sessions.run` NULL — stored before migration 4, or by a kit's ingest — or naming a run no `trials` row has, because the trial's write failed) is one trial of its own, graded when its outcome is `pass` or `fail` and counted under `errors` when it is `error`; under this a `prompt2` row still counts two (`SPEC-fyr-eval` § Known limits). A session a trial claims is counted by that trial alone, in the window the trial started in, so adjacent windows never count it twice; under `--project` neither the trial nor the session it claims is counted, since a trial belongs to no project root. `k`, `passed` and `pass_k` (1 when every one of the n graded trials passed) keep their first meaning; `pass_at` is Chen et al. 2021's unbiased pass@k, 1 − C(n−c, k)/C(n, k); `pass_pow` is τ-bench's pass^k, C(c, k)/C(n, k), the chance that k trials drawn without replacement all passed (the plug-in (c/n)^k overstates it at small n); both for k in 1, 3, 5 up to n; `wilson95` is the Wilson score interval of c of n at z = 1.96, clamped to [0, 1]; `flip` marks a label that both passed and failed. The estimators are `internal/metrics/estimators.go`, each pinned to a known answer. A trial belongs to the window it starts in, as a session does; a trial carries a label, so the default view shows none. |
| — | Replayed history | A resumed or forked Claude session copies earlier messages into a new transcript. `show` counts a tool step, an assistant message or a generation once per CLI and label by its id, under the first session in the query's window that holds it, so replayed tool calls, tokens, verbs and errors are not counted twice. User turns, interrupts and compactions are not deduplicated, and a replay whose original session lies outside the window still counts once inside it. The label is part of the key, so a sandbox run that reuses real ids never hides a real session's steps under `--all-labels`. |
| B1 | Tokens and cost | Antigravity: `gen_metadata` usage; cost is not exposed. Historical Claude rows keep what an older ingest stored (usage per message id, cost from the session's last `cost-state` line). |
| B2 | Time and volume | Wall time = `ended_at - started_at` of main sessions. Active time = the sum of gaps under 5 min between a main session's steps. A subagent runs inside its parent's time and is counted in neither. Also turns (typed user turns) and tool calls (main and subagent). |
| B3 | Context | Peak context = max(input + cache read + cache write) of one message (Claude); the `gen_metadata` context of one generation (Antigravity). Also the number of compactions. Also the sessions whose peak passed the context target, default 300K, and each main session's peak: the peak follows the replayed-history rule above, so a fork's copy of an earlier session's messages counts under the session that first had them, and a subagent's peak belongs to no session (it runs inside its parent's time). |
| B4 | Subagents | Count by type, the tool calls of each, and SendMessage resumes. |
| C1 | Search vs grep | `fyr search\|index` verb segments divided by `grep`/`rg` segments plus Grep tool calls. |
| C2 | Forbidden shapes | `git add -A`, `git add .`, `git push --force\|-f`, `--no-verify`, and `git commit` in the same Bash call as `go test`. |
| C3 | First reads | The trail kind of a main session's first three steps that carry one: a Read target's kind, or a Bash step that is a record verb — `fyr record get <ID>` as the ID's kind (`record` when the prefix is unknown or no ID follows), `fyr record list` as `list`. Only the first segment whose program is `fyr` (any directory) or `go run ./cmd/fyr` is read, past `--home`/`--repo` and their values and other flags; `fyr search` and `fyr memory show` are not trail reads. Bash steps ingested before this rule carry no kind. |
| C4 | Skills | Skill loads per session. |
| D1 | Errors | Tool error rate, denials and interrupts. |
| D2 | Retry loops | The same `cmd_hash` in two consecutive tool steps. |
| D3 | Subagent volume | Tool calls per subagent session. |

## Data

`~/.config/fyr/metrics.db` has mode 0600 in a 0700 directory. A database or companion file that is a symlink, or any other non-regular file, is refused, as in the search index. The directory itself may be a symlink. It uses WAL with a 10 s busy timeout, and every transaction takes the write lock when it begins (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`), so an ingest that meets another waits for it instead of failing at its first write. A new store opened by two processes at once is retried for the same 10 s, because SQLite answers that race with an immediate `SQLITE_BUSY` (BUG-187). Every time is stored as unix milliseconds, UTC. Writer: `internal/metrics` only.

```sql
meta(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT)            -- 'schema', 'salt' (32 random hex)
sessions(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, vendor TEXT, project_root TEXT, parent_id TEXT, agent_type TEXT,
         model TEXT, label TEXT, outcome TEXT, started_at INTEGER, ended_at INTEGER,
         cost_usd REAL, duration_ms INTEGER, run TEXT)   -- run: migration 4, the trial a sandbox session belongs to; NULL for a real session or one stored before
trials(run TEXT PRIMARY KEY,        -- '<stamp>/<row>/<i>', the trial's sandbox under the eval root   (migration 4)
       label TEXT NOT NULL,         -- 'eval=<row>'
       row_version INTEGER, kind TEXT, cluster TEXT, expect TEXT,   -- the suite's per-row fields, written by fyr eval since ADR-085; NULL on a trial stored before, read as the defaults
       harness TEXT NOT NULL,       -- gitShort(install source) plus ' (dirty)' when an installed directory is dirty (SPEC-fyr-eval § Data), or 'embedded <version>'
       cli TEXT,                    -- the first line of `agy --version`
       status TEXT NOT NULL,        -- 'pass' | 'fail' | 'error'
       cause TEXT NOT NULL,         -- one identifier from SPEC-fyr-eval's closed set; '' for pass
       started_at INTEGER NOT NULL, seconds INTEGER NOT NULL,   -- the whole trial
       session_seconds INTEGER)     -- the agy session(s); NULL when none ran
steps(session_id TEXT, ext_id TEXT, ts INTEGER, kind TEXT, tool TEXT, skill TEXT, target_kind TEXT,
      is_error INTEGER, denied INTEGER, tok_in INTEGER, tok_out INTEGER, cache_read INTEGER,
      cache_write INTEGER, cmd_hash TEXT, context INTEGER,   -- context: migration 2
      PRIMARY KEY(session_id, ext_id))
step_verbs(session_id TEXT, ext_id TEXT, n INTEGER, verb TEXT, PRIMARY KEY(session_id, ext_id, n))
events(session_id TEXT, ts INTEGER, kind TEXT, ref TEXT, value TEXT, PRIMARY KEY(session_id, kind, ref))
ingest_state(source TEXT PRIMARY KEY, size INTEGER, mtime INTEGER, offset INTEGER)
```

**The trial** (migration 4; the eval-metrics plan D13, D17) is one run of a suite row, the unit every rate reads. `Store.RecordTrial` stores it once, after the trial's verdict, whether or not a session ran, with `INSERT OR IGNORE`, so recording a run again adds no row and changes none; a trial whose status is not one of the three, whose cause is missing on a fail or an error or present on a pass or not an identifier, with no run or harness, whose label is not `KEY=VALUE`, whose run, label, harness, cli, kind, cluster or expect is not printable or is over 120 bytes, or that carries a negative count, is refused before anything is written. Its sessions, when any ran, are ingested with `Options.Run` set to the same key, which the writer puts on each session at insert and keeps first-write-wins — never by a label-wide `UPDATE`, which could stamp another trial's session. `fyr eval` writes a trial for every run of a row and ingests its sessions with that run (since Phase 2a of the eval-metrics plan, `SPEC-fyr-eval` § Data), and since ADR-085 sets `row_version`, `kind` and `cluster` from the suite with its defaults applied (1, `capability`, the row's id) and `expect` to the row's list or NULL; a trial stored before then has NULL in all four, which a reader takes as those defaults; for a session `fyr eval` stored before that phase, or a kit's ingest, and for every session stored before this migration, `run` is NULL and A6 counts the session as one graded trial of its own (known limit: old `prompt2` data stays doubled, and old history never earns a per-trial flag). `Store.RunModels(runs)` reads back the distinct non-empty `model` of the sessions whose `run` is among `runs`, sorted, for the eval record's header (`SPEC-fyr-eval` § The testing record).

### Invariants

- **Identity.**
  - Antigravity: `ext_id` = `<conversation id>:<step idx>`.
  - A trial: `trials.run`, written once; `sessions.run` names it.
  - Rows with vendor `claude` (`ext_id` = message id, `tool_use.id` or a line `uuid`) come from an older ingest. They are kept and read, never written: no code path inserts one, and nothing deletes them (plan D7).
  - Re-ingesting anything adds no rows.
- **Time columns.** `sessions.started_at` and `ended_at` hold unix milliseconds of a real time or are NULL; `ingest_state.mtime` is 0 when the source gave none. A time read from another program's store that is before 1970, Go's zero time among them, is no time: `ended_at` stays NULL (migration 3 repaired the rows stored before, BUG-181).
- **Path columns.** Only `sessions.project_root` and `ingest_state.source` may hold a path. No column holds an argument or prose.
- **Identifiers.** `steps.skill`, `sessions.agent_type` and the `git add .` verb are the only identifiers taken from a tool's input. A Bash step's `target_kind` is a kind from a closed set (the record kinds, `list`, `record`), never the ID or any other word of the command. A trial's `cause` is one identifier from `SPEC-fyr-eval`'s closed set; its `harness`, `cli` and `run` are a short hash, a version line and a sandbox key, and with `label`, `kind`, `cluster` and `expect` are printable and at most 120 bytes, never prose.
- **`events` payloads.**

  | kind | ref | value |
  |---|---|---|
  | `commit` | full SHA | `''` or `ambiguous` |
  | `handoff` | the item's ID | `''` |
  | `verifier` | the item's ID | the status word |
  | `review` | the item's ID | `high=N,medium=N,low=N` |
  | `bug` | `BUG-NNN` | the linked SHA |
  | `correction` | the entry's `ts` in UTC, RFC 3339 (`2026-10-21T12:39:54Z`) | `''` |

- **One reference per trail item.** A `handoff`, `verifier` or `review` event's ref is the trail item's record ID; an event an older ingest joined from a trail file carries the ID `fyr record import` gives that file (`brain.ImportedID`: the kind's prefix, a dash, the file's stem slugged), so the project's migration added no second event for the same item. Each ingest first rewrites, inside the join's transaction, every such ref an older ingest stored as a file name (`*.md`) to that ID form; a row whose ID form the session already holds is a duplicate and is deleted. A ref already in ID form is left alone, even one ending in `.md` (a file `notes.md.md` imports as `HANDOFF-notes.md`), so a second ingest changes nothing. No schema change. Known limits: a `-N` suffix a collision added to an ID is not reproduced, so such a file and its record stay two events; an old file whose name is itself ID-shaped (`HANDOFF-x.md`) keeps its file-name ref. A `correction` ref an older ingest stored with another offset (`+02:00`) is rewritten to its UTC form the same way.
- **Trail from records only.** A migrated project (its checkout holds `.agents/trail.jsonl`) is joined from its `handoff`, `testing`, `review` and `bug` records, of every status, in the scope of its main worktree root, read through the file-wins load (`brain.ForMetrics`, which may write `brain.db` as the dream's read does), but only when the operator registered the checkout under this home with `fyr index --register` (`trail.Registered`; ADR-068, audit-choices SD49): an unregistered checkout holding `.agents/trail.jsonl` reads as unmigrated, so its `trail.jsonl` never becomes a brain scope that `fyr dream --all` and `search --global` would then read, and its sessions, commits and corrections are still joined. An `fyr eval` sandbox's clone is registered under the eval home by `fyr eval` itself before the row's ingest (ledger item 76, `SPEC-fyr-eval` § State), so its `eval=<row>` sessions get their record events and its trail becomes a scope of the eval home's brain store, never the real home's; a clone eval refuses to register (its git directory outside it) is joined as unmigrated. An unmigrated one gives no trail events, only its commits and corrections: the join from its docs root's files went with the crossing (ledger Phase 10, item 66), and the events an older ingest stored from them stay. Corrections are read for every root (A5). A record's **time** is the minute stamped in its ID (`^[A-Z]+-(YYYY-MM-DD)-(HHMM)(-|$)`, read in the machine's zone; an impossible minute such as `2459` is none), never `updated`, which an edit or the import moves. A `handoff`, `verifier` or `review` record belongs to every main session whose window overlaps that minute `[stamp, stamp + 60 s)`; a record with no time gives none of these. A `bug` record belongs to the session owning the commit it cites, with `ts` its `date` at 00:00 local. Only these patterns are taken from a body, never its text. Known limit: a record added on a machine in another time zone is placed off by the zones' difference.

- **`cmd_hash`** = `hex(sha256(salt || command))[:16]`. It supports equality checks only.
- **Fixed markers.**
  - `denied`: an Antigravity step status the spike names (none observed; the CLI does not record denials). Historical Claude rows keep the marker an older ingest set.
  - `interrupt`: a user line starting `[Request interrupted by user`.
  - `compaction`: not recorded by Antigravity; historical Claude rows keep the compact-boundary count an older ingest stored.
- **Antigravity sources.** Antigravity databases are read only from copies. `step_payload` is never read; tool names and command lines come from `steps.metadata`.
- **Export.** `export` writes every row but the `salt`: with it, an export would let anyone confirm a guessed command against `cmd_hash`.
- **git in project roots.** Every git call into a session's project root goes through `internal/trail`: `--no-optional-locks -c core.fsmonitor=false -c log.showSignature=false`, `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, and `--no-show-signature --no-textconv` on `log` (`trail.Log`; `--no-textconv` since the security review of 2026-10-25, so a content diff starts no textconv driver the checkout picks). Only commands that read objects and files run there (`log`, `ls-tree`, `ls-files`, `hash-object --no-filters`, `rev-parse`, `check-ignore`, `config --get`), never `status`, which runs the repository's clean filters (BUG-164). This closes the program-starting config keys those commands honour (signature programs, clean filters, fsmonitor, a lazy fetch's ssh command); it does not make the repository's config trusted. A partial clone (`extensions.partialClone` set, or any remote marked `promisor`) is read only when this machine's git is 2.44 or later, which honours `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` (`trail.Readable`, the policy search applies; SD17). With an older git it is not read at all: its sessions get no commit or trail events, and its trail files keep their mtimes in the dreamer. A toplevel is accepted only when it is the session's directory or a parent of it, so a repository's `core.worktree` cannot file a session under another project. Sessions are grouped by their git toplevel (`trail.Toplevel`), so a session started in a subdirectory joins its project's events.
- **Temporary copies.** `metrics-agy-*` (Antigravity conversation copies) and `dream-metrics-*` (a store snapshot) are removed after use. An `ingest` and every `dream` run also sweep any older than an hour, which a killed run left behind.
- **Migrations.** They run forward only, in one transaction. A store with a newer schema is refused untouched. The binary never deletes the store, and `uninstall` keeps it.

## Failure modes

| Trigger | Observable |
|---|---|
| `metrics.db`, `-wal` or `-shm` is a symlink or another non-regular file | `metrics: <name> is not a regular file; refusing to open or write through it`, exit 1 |
| The store's schema is newer than the binary's | `metrics.db schema N is newer than this binary (M); update fyr`, exit 1, store unchanged (`ingest`, `show`, `report`, `export`) |
| A file shrank or was replaced | Re-read from offset 0, with no duplicate rows |
| An Antigravity copy or read fails | That conversation is named and counted in F; the others are ingested; exit 1 |
| An Antigravity token field is absent | Tokens are stored NULL and counted as 0 in `show` and `report` (SD51 of the 2026-10-27 audit: no note names them) |
| `report` cannot render | nothing is written, so a rerun is not refused as an overwrite (SD57) |
| A project root is gone or not git | Session rows are still written; no commit events; `ingest` prints `metrics: note: project root gone: <root>` or `no git history: <root>` |
| A migrated project's records cannot be read (`trail.jsonl` does not parse, `brain.db` busy or newer) | `metrics: note: records not read: <root>: <reason>`; that root gets no record events this run, its stored events stay, its corrections still count; exit 0 |
| Two main sessions overlap in one root | Commits in the overlap are `ambiguous`; A1/A4 are shown as `n (ambiguous m)` and excluded from rates |
| Still locked after the 10 s busy timeout | The source counts as failed (`database is locked`), exit 1; the next run picks it up |
| `show`, `report`, `evals` or `export` on a home with no store (never ingested) | `fyr metrics: no metrics store at <path>; run \`fyr metrics ingest\` first`, exit 1; nothing is created |
| `export FILE` or `report --out FILE` exists | `refusing to overwrite FILE`, exit 1 |
| `--source` without `--label`, `--outcome` with a value other than `pass`, `fail` or `error`, or any metrics flag the subcommand does not read (`ingest --json`, `export --label`, `show --out`, `ingest --context-target`, `show --harness`, `evals --project`) | Usage error naming the flag, exit 2 |
| A store at schema 3 opened by this binary | Migration 4 runs forward in one transaction (`trials`, `sessions.run`); nothing else changes; exit 0 |
| `RecordTrial` with a status outside the three, a cause missing or misplaced, no run or harness, a label not `KEY=VALUE`, text that is not printable or over 120 bytes, a negative count, or a zero start time (Go's zero time is before 1970 and would sit outside every window) | `metrics: trial: <what>`, nothing written; `fyr eval` reports it as a failed trial write (`SPEC-fyr-eval`) |
| `--context-target 0` or a negative value | `--context-target takes a token count above 0`, exit 2 |
| No main session of a vendor in the window carries a context value | That vendor's `sessions_over_context_target` is `null` (`n/a` in the tables), `notes` says so; never 0 |
| Ingest fails inside `dream` | A line in `dream.log`; the dream's exit status and `last_run.error` are unchanged |
| Ingest fails at a handoff or in `/retro` | The skill reports the error and exit status in chat (`/retro` also under `## Metrics`) and goes on; the handoff is never edited; the next ingest joins every session again |

## Non-goals

- Storing or sending arguments, prose, file contents or tool output.
- Sending metrics off the machine. Feedback reaches the harness only as dream or retro proposals, applied by hand (ADR-055, ADR-062).
- A server, a live dashboard or a JavaScript chart library.
- Rebuilding the store from transcripts that no longer exist.

## Open questions

- The Antigravity field numbers for tool name, command line, subagent link, compaction and denial. Default: unknown items stay null and are named in `notes`; PRD.md § Known limits holds the compaction row (Phase 3 spike).
