## What it is

One SQLite store, `~/.config/fyr/brain.db` (under `--home` when given), holds every record of every project's trail with its metadata, the global records, and each project's memory. A project's records other than memory are also written to one committed file in that project, `.agents/trail.jsonl`, which is the backup and how records travel between machines through git. Nothing but `fyr` reads that file.

The store is a store of record like `metrics.db`: it migrates forward (`PRAGMA user_version`), a store a newer binary wrote is refused untouched, and `uninstall` leaves it. The directory is created 0700 and the database and its `-wal` and `-shm` 0600; a database or companion file that is a symlink or not a regular file is refused (the search index's rule, `search.PrepareDBFiles`).

## Commands

```
fyr record add <kind> --title T [--status S] [--id ID] [--global [--project ROOT]]   < body
fyr record get <id>... [--global]
fyr record edit <id> [--status S] [--title T] [--body] [--global]                     [< body]
fyr record list [--kind K] [--open] [--global [--project ROOT]] [--all]
fyr record import [--dry-run] [<docs-root>]
fyr record import --global [--dry-run]
fyr memory add --type T --name SLUG --description TEXT [--provenance operator|derived] < body
fyr memory show
```

- **Scope.** Without `--global` a verb works in the project scope of the git checkout holding the working directory. The scope key is the main worktree's top level, resolved by `trail.Roots` exactly as `memory.Root` resolves it (git's `--show-toplevel` in the main worktree, which must be the working directory or a parent of it; from a linked worktree the common dir's parent, and only when the common dir registers that worktree; a bare repository refused). Every worktree of a repository therefore shares one scope. `--global` selects the global scope, which needs no checkout.
- **`add`** reads the body on stdin and prints the new ID. The body must be UTF-8 text with no control character other than tab and newline (a NUL, an ESC and the `\x01`/`\x02` a search snippet marks matches with are refused), at most 1 MiB; CRLF is folded to LF, leading blank lines and trailing whitespace are dropped, and an empty body is refused. The title is one non-empty line of at most 512 bytes with no control character. `--id` stores the record under that ID instead of the next one (it must fit the kind's grammar and be free in the scope). `--project ROOT` (with `--global` only) names the project a global record is about; it is stored absolute, as the main worktree's root when ROOT is a checkout.
- **The redactor warning (SD42 of the 2026-10-27 audit).** When `add`, or `edit` with `--body` or `--title`, stores a body or title that `fyr dream`'s redactor (`internal/redact`) would change, it prints on stderr, after the store, `fyr record: warning: the body holds text the redactor would change (first at line <n>); stored as written` (`<n>` the first line of the body as read from stdin where the redacted body differs) or `fyr record: warning: the title holds text the redactor would change; stored as written`. `add --id` judges the ID it was given too, first: `fyr record: warning: the ID holds text the redactor would change; stored as written`, never repeating the ID, which stdout still prints as the command's output (ledger D31 3b); a generated ID is never judged. The record is stored, the exit status is unchanged and the matched text is never printed: a project's records reach the committed `trail.jsonl`, and the operator chose a warning over a refusal. Every kind and scope warns alike, a `--global` record and a `memory` record added through `record add` too; a clean field, a refused write and a field `edit` keeps print nothing. `fyr memory add` does not warn. `record import` warns the same way for each record it stores, naming the record by its ID, or by its place in the list as below, never by its text (ledger item 47): `fyr record import: warning: <ID>: the body holds text the redactor would change (first at line <n>); stored as written` (`<n>` a line of the body as stored, which can differ from the source file's line where the import dropped frontmatter or split a file), or `… record <n> in the list above: the title holds …; stored as written`, after the import's own output. An ID is made from the source file's name or, for a line of a global log, from its title, and slugging (lowercased, every other run of characters turned to `-`) can hide a secret from the redactor, so the source path is judged with the ID: `fyr record import: warning: record <n> in the list above: the ID or the source path holds text the redactor would change; stored as written`. A record whose ID, source path or title the redactor would change is named in each of its lines by its place in the list the import printed, never by its ID; any other is named by its ID. Project and `--global` records are judged alike. The import's own list on stdout prints every ID and path as before (the phase's security review, rounds 1 and 2). A run names only the records it stored, never one the scope already held; a dry run, which stores nothing, names every record it read, one already held included, and leaves off `; stored as written`. The exit status is the import's own.
- **`get`** prints, for each ID in the order given, a header line in the list format (plus `  (project ROOT)` for a global record about a project, and `  (provenance P)` when `provenance` is set) and then the body. Records are separated by a blank line. Every line goes through the printable filter of `fyr search` (`search.Printable`, BUG-152): control characters, format characters and line or paragraph separators print as `?`; tabs and newlines are kept. An ID the scope does not hold is a refusal naming it, after the found records are printed.
- **`edit`** changes the status, the title or, with `--body`, the body read from stdin. Without `--body` the body is kept (D9). At least one of the three is required. A plan's status follows its new body.
- **`list`** prints `ID  kind  status  date  title`, newest first (by date, then by last update, then by ID), with `-` for a handoff's empty status. `--kind` filters by kind and `--open` keeps the open records (table below). `--project ROOT` (with `--global` only) keeps the global records about that project: `fyr record list --global --kind proposal --project <root>` is how `/retro` lists a project's proposals. `--all` lists every scope, each line ending in `  [<scope root>]` or `  [global]`; it cannot be combined with `--global`.
- A flag the subverb does not take is a usage error (for example `record add --open`), never parsed and ignored.

## Import (D8, D13, D16)

`fyr record import [--dry-run] [<docs-root>]` migrates a project whose trail is still files. The docs root is the argument (relative to the working directory, inside the checkout, not a symlink), else `<project>/.agents/docs/`, else `<project>/docs/`. It reads the files git tracks there and refuses a file that is not markdown (D17: a script is not a record; move it first) — an empty or whitespace-only `.gitkeep` placeholder is not refused but removed with the tree — a symlink or other non-regular file and a file over 1 MiB; every file is opened without following a link or blocking on a FIFO. The whole import reads at most 256 MiB and 50,000 files (the docs tree, the files that reference it and the old memory store together), and refuses past either. A real run refuses a tree with uncommitted changes, so the import's removals are the only change, and refuses a tree whose state git cannot read by path (a tracked name holding a newline or opening with `"`, which `hash-object --stdin-paths` would split or unquote into another path; BUG-188); a dry run reads and decides the same and writes nothing.

- **Kinds and IDs.** `plans/` plan, `reviews/` review, `testing/` testing (`TEST-`), `changes/` change, `handoffs/` handoff, `retros/` retro, `deploy/` deploy, each `<PREFIX>-<file stem>` lowercased; `specs/<app>/<topic>.md` is `SPEC-<app>-<topic>`; `GUIDE-testing` is `GUIDE-testing` and a `testing/*-matrix.md` with no date `GUIDE-<stem>`; `bugs/BUG-NNN-*.md` keeps `BUG-NNN`; `architecture/DECISIONS.md` gives one `adr` record per `## ADR-NNN: Title (date) — Status` section (status `superseded:ADR-NNN` when the heading ends `Superseded by ADR-NNN`, else `accepted`); `bugs/INDEX.md` is folded into the bugs (a row's status when the file has none, its prevention when the file has no `## Prevention`, and the Graduated table as status `graduated` plus a `Graduated to:` line). A file elsewhere is reported as a problem and left as a file.
- **Title, date, body.** The title is the first `# ` heading (a bug's without its `BUG-NNN:` prefix), else the stem; the date the frontmatter `date:`, else the stem's leading date, else the day of the import (a date that is not a real day, `2026-02-30`, is skipped the same way; so is an ADR heading's); the body the text after the frontmatter. Every imported record is normalized (a control character but tab and newline becomes `?`, the title one line of at most 512 bytes) and then checked by the load's own parser, in a dry run too: a record the load would refuse fails the import, naming its file, before anything is written.
- **What is kept (D8).** The roots: open plans (status derived from the body), the newest handoff (by file name), every ADR, every bug, specs, deploy docs and guides. Then, transitively, every trail file a kept record, or a file git tracks among `PRD.md`, `SDD.md`, `TDD.md`, `REQUIREMENTS.md` (a project not yet migrated), `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `context/`, `skills/`, `agents/` and `rules/`, names, by path relative to the docs root (`TEST-2026-09-03-verify-real-home`, `.agents/docs/…` included) or by the ID it imports as (`TEST-2026-09-03-verify-real-home`). A closed bug is trimmed to its heading and its `## Prevention` section. Everything else is dropped; git history keeps it.
- **The old memory store.** `<main worktree root>/.agents/memory/*.md` (not `MEMORY.md`) become `memory` records `MEMORY-<name>`, the description as the title and `type: <type>` heading the body. The store's trust checks stand (ADR-043): a symlinked `.agents` or store is refused, and so is a store git tracks anything under (a committed memory is the repository's text, never the operator's). A memory file it cannot take is a `problem` and stays; only the files it took, with `MEMORY.md` and `.lock`, are listed for removal.
- **Writes and output.** One transaction stores every record the scope does not hold yet (a record already stored is skipped and counted, so a second run adds nothing; `--dry-run` opens no store, so it counts the sources' records and prints no stored count) and exports. Nothing is removed (D13): the command prints a summary (`plan 3, …; N records, M dropped, K already stored`), one `record  ID  kind  status  path` line per record, a `problem` line per file or line left out, then every tracked trail file under the docs root (to `git --literal-pathspecs rm --` by name after committing `.agents/trail.jsonl`; a file outside the trail's directories is a `problem`, left as a file and never on that list) and the old memory store's files (untracked; `rm` by name). Every path is printed as one shell word, single-quoted when it holds anything but letters, digits and `._/@%+=:,-` (or starts with `-`).

`fyr record import --global [--dry-run]` migrates `~/.config/fyr`: each `feedback.jsonl` line as a `feedback` record (title the `corrected` text, else the `user_quote`; body the line as written; `project` the line's project), each `retros.jsonl` line as a global `retro` record, each `proposals/**/*.md` as a `queued` `proposal` record (`project` from its frontmatter), and the old memory store of every project in the global search index that is registered under this home (`fyr index --register`, ADR-068) into that project's memory records; an unregistered one is reported as `<root>: not registered (fyr index --register); its memory store is not imported`, and its store stays. A line that is not JSON, has no RFC 3339 `ts`, is over 6 MiB, or builds a record the store would not take is reported by number and skipped; so is a proposal file or a project's memory store it cannot take; nothing stops the import. Two entries whose IDs would be equal get `-2`, `-3` … until the ID is free (a slug is cut at 120 characters to leave room). Records already stored are skipped (per scope: two projects may each hold `MEMORY-x`), so it can run again after the logs grew. It prints the files it read, to remove by name once the records are checked; a source with a problem is not on that list.

## Memory (D14)

`fyr memory add --type T --name SLUG --description TEXT [--provenance P]` stores the body on stdin as the `memory` record `MEMORY-<SLUG>` in the project's scope, replacing one of the same name; `T` is `user`, `feedback`, `project` or `reference`, `P` is `operator` (the default) or `derived` (when an agent session saves from a file or tool output; any other value exits 2), the slug `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}`, the description one line of at most 512 bytes with no control character (the record's title; a longer one is refused); the body is `type: T`, a blank line, then the text. `brain.MemoryDraft` writes `fyr auto`'s validated memory drafts (`add`, `retire`, `merge`) in the project's scope with `provenance = 'derived'`, archiving the prior body under `Prior (<provenance>):` on `merge`, refusing `add` over an `operator` memory, and refusing `retire` or `merge` of an ID not in that project's scope. It prints `saved MEMORY-<SLUG>`. `fyr memory show` prints one line per memory record, `- <name> (<type>) — <description>`, sorted by name, each line cut at 640 bytes, capped at 200 lines and 25 KB with a last line naming how many more. Memory is never exported, so neither verb loads or writes `trail.jsonl`, and both work in an unmigrated project. A refusal exits 2, as `fyr memory` always did.

## Kinds

| Kind | Scope | ID | Exported |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bug` | project or global | `BUG-NNN` | yes |
| `adr` | project or global | `ADR-NNN`, `ADR-NNNa` | yes |
| `plan` `review` `testing` `change` `handoff` `retro` `learning` `spec` `deploy` `guide` | project or global | `<PREFIX>-<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>-<slug>` | yes |
| `memory` | project only | `MEMORY-<slug>` (`fyr memory add --name`; `record add memory` without `--id` gets the dated form) | never (D14) |
| `feedback` `proposal` | global only | `FEEDBACK-…`, `PROPOSAL-…` | never |

The prefix is the kind in capitals, except `testing`, whose prefix is `TEST`. `add` refuses `feedback` and `proposal` in a project (R8, D10) and `memory` with `--global` (D14). The other kinds are accepted in the global scope too: a `learning`'s scope is the agent's choice (D4), and `import --global` (Phase 2) brings `retros.jsonl` there.

## IDs (D7)

- `BUG-NNN` and `ADR-NNN` are numbered per scope: the scope's highest number of that kind plus one, read inside the write's transaction, compared as numbers (`BUG-1000` follows `BUG-999`), at least three digits and at most nine. `ADR-047a` counts as 47.
- Every other kind gets `<PREFIX>-<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>-<slug>`, the stamp from the local clock and the slug from the title (lowercase letters and digits, every other run as `-`, at most 48 characters, `record` when nothing is left). When that ID is taken in the scope, `-2`, `-3` … is appended.
- A given `--id` must match the kind: `BUG-NNN`, `ADR-NNN[a-z]`, or the kind's prefix, a dash and a lowercase slug (`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*`, at most 128 characters). The short form (`SPEC-fyr-record`) is what Phase 2's import gives a spec.
- A duplicate ID after a merge is refused by the load, never renamed, unless the two lines are byte-identical: then it is one record (§ Export).

## Status (D6)

| Kind | Values | Open when | Starts as |
|---|---|---|---|
| plan | derived from the body: `open` while it holds a line starting `- [ ]` outside a backtick fence (`search.Unticked`), else `closed` | `open` | derived |
| bug | `open` `fixed` `accepted` `obsolete` `graduated` | `open` | `open` |
| adr | `accepted`, `superseded:ADR-NNN[a-z]` | never | `accepted` |
| spec, deploy, guide | `current` `retired` | `current` | `current` |
| proposal | `queued`, `applied:<commit>` (7–40 lowercase hex), `rejected` | `queued` | `queued` |
| memory | `closed`, `retired` (D28: how `/dream` drops one; `memory show` lists only `closed`, and `memory add` under a retired name makes it `closed` again) | never | `closed` |
| handoff | none (the newest is the live one) | never | none |
| everything else | `closed` | never | `closed` |

`--status` on a plan or a handoff is a usage error, as is a value the kind does not take.

## Export: `.agents/trail.jsonl`

- One record per line, `{"date","id","kind","status","title","updated","body"}` with the keys in that order, JSON without HTML escaping, lines sorted by ID (prefix, then the number numerically, then the letter, else as text), and a final newline. The same rows always give the same bytes.
- `memory`, `feedback` and `proposal` records are never exported.
- Every write in a project rewrites the file inside the write's transaction: the rows are read, the file is written to a temporary file in `.agents/` and renamed over the old one (unchanged bytes are not rewritten), and its SHA-256 is stored in `meta.export_sha`, all before the commit. A write refused before the rename (a bad body, a refused load, a symlink) leaves both the store and the file as they were. When the rename lands and the commit then fails, the file holds the record and the store does not; the next call's load takes the file.
- A symlinked or non-directory `.agents`, and a `trail.jsonl` that is a symlink or not a regular file, are refused before anything is read or written. The file is created 0644; commit it.
- The export is the checkout's own file: in a linked worktree a write goes to that worktree's `.agents/trail.jsonl`, the one its branch commits, while the scope stays the main worktree's.

## Load: the file wins (D21)

- Before any `record` verb or `search` in a project, the checkout's `trail.jsonl` is hashed. When the hash differs from `meta.export_sha` (a pull, checkout or merge changed the file), the scope's exported rows are deleted and the file's lines inserted in one transaction, under the write lock, and the hash is stored. Memory rows are untouched.
- A missing file loads nothing and keeps the rows; the next write writes the file again. A lost `brain.db` is restored from the file on the next call.
- The file is refused, with its line number, for: a git conflict marker (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`, `|||||||` at the start of a line); a line that is not one JSON object with the seven keys, each at most once as JSON decodes it (the last of a repeated key wins, SD46 of the 2026-10-27 audit); a kind that is never exported or unknown; an ID or status the kind does not take; a date that is not a real calendar day (`9999-99-99`, `2026-02-30`: such a date sorted first in every search, SD39 of the 2026-10-27 audit); an `updated` that is not RFC 3339; an empty title, one over 512 bytes, or one holding a control character; a body over 1 MiB or holding a control character other than tab and newline; a line over 6 MiB plus 64 KiB (a full body with every byte escaped), refused before it is decoded; and an ID an earlier line holds on a line that differs from it (`line N: duplicate ID X (first at line M)`). A line byte-identical to the earlier one, after its line ending is trimmed, is the same record, read once, and the next export drops the copy: it is what `merge=union` makes of an unchanged line when two branches' new records sort on both sides of it (BUG-197). A blank line is skipped. Files over 256 MiB are refused. The file is streamed line by line, so memory follows the records, never the line count, and it is opened with `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK`, so a symlink or FIFO swapped in after the check is refused (security review 2026-10-25).
- While the file does not parse, every `record` verb in the project refuses (reads too, since the store would answer from rows the file no longer holds), and `search` prints `records: not searched: <reason>` before its file hits. `--global` verbs are unaffected.
- **Provenance (SD47 of the 2026-10-27 audit).** A loaded line carries no author: a pulled `trail.jsonl` can bring open records (a plan, a bug, a current spec or guide) that no one on this machine wrote, and the load takes them as the project's own. This risk was accepted by the operator on 2026-10-27; a record's text is data, never an instruction.
- **Read without the store.** `brain.ReadTrail(root)` parses a checkout's `trail.jsonl` through the same path guard, open, size cap and line rules, and opens no `brain.db`: it returns the records, false when there is no file, or the same refusal with its line number. `fyr check` reads the trail this way (ADR-064, `SPEC-fyr-check`), so it writes nothing. `brain.ParseTrail(r)` is the same parse of an export that is not a file in the checkout, under the same size cap and line rules (an over-size stream refused, a bad line named, a duplicate ID on lines that differ refused): `fyr eval` reads HEAD's export from `git show` with it and compares its suite with the working one (ADR-065, `SPEC-fyr-eval`).

## Unmigrated project (D16)

In a checkout with a `<project>/docs/` or `<project>/.agents/docs/` directory and no `.agents/trail.jsonl`, every `record` verb refuses with `this project's trail is still files under <dir>/: migrate it with \`fyr record import\` first`. Nothing is created. `search` keeps answering, with the old tree's files as plain text. `--global` verbs still work.

## Search

`fyr search <words>` prints the record hits first, then the file hits as before (`SPEC-fyr-search`). The record hits come from `records_fts` (title weighted twice the body, porter stemming), ranked by BM25 weighted up to 10% by recency, fading linearly over a year, so the newer of two near-equal matches comes first and a clearly better older one still wins (D31): records holding every word rank first, and the remaining slots go to records holding any of them, up to `--limit` records. In a project the search covers the project's scope and the global scope; with `--global`, also every other project scope whose checkout the operator registered under this home with `fyr index --register` (`trail.Registered`; ADR-068, audit-choices D15): an unregistered project's records answer no `--global` query, and the project's own scope stays in either way (ledger D13). Each hit prints `ID  kind status  date  title` and a snippet line. The ID is prefixed `global:` for a global record and, with `--global`, `<root>:` (the full scope path) for another project's record, so two clones of one base name never print alike. A `--kind` that is a record kind filters the records. `trail` takes every record, and a file-only kind (`code`, `doc`) takes none. When there is no `brain.db` and no `trail.jsonl`, nothing is created and no records section is printed. `--refs <ID|path>` prints, before the file results, `records: N naming <ref>` and the records that name the ref as written — the ID's own record first, then every record whose title or body holds the path or ID as a whole name (no path character before it, nor after it unless the ref is a directory ending in `/`), each with the line that names it; `--open` prints `records: N open` and the open records (the status table's "Open when"). Both cover the project's and the global scope, with `--global` also every registered project's scope, and take `--kind` and `--limit` (D30).

## Concurrency (D20)

Every write and every load runs inside `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on one connection, so two processes never allocate the same number or export over each other's rows. The wait is the driver's busy timeout (10 s), after which the verb refuses with `the brain store is busy`. A new store opened by two processes at once is retried for the same 10 s, because SQLite answers that race with an immediate `SQLITE_BUSY`. There is no lock file.

## Known limits

- **A linked worktree of a separate-git-dir checkout gets its own scope** (audit SD44, `PLAN-2026-10-27-ledger` items 37 and 70). A linked worktree's scope is the directory above git's common dir. For a checkout made with `--separate-git-dir`, or a submodule, that common dir lies outside the work tree, so the linked worktree's scope is not the main worktree's top level: one repository gets two scopes, two sets of records and two export rows. The main worktree is not affected. Reasoned, not run; the code is not changed, the layout being rare.

## Exit status

0 with or without output. 1 for a refusal: an empty or oversize body, a global-only kind in a project, `memory --global`, a duplicate `--id`, an ID not found, an unmigrated project, a symlinked export path, a `trail.jsonl` that does not parse, not a git checkout without `--global`, a newer schema or a busy store. 2 for a usage error: no or unknown subverb, a missing kind or ID, an unknown kind, a missing or multi-line `--title`, an `--id` or `--status` the kind does not take, `edit` with nothing to change, a flag the subverb does not take, `--project` without `--global`, `--all` with `--global`. The reason is printed on stdout as `fyr record: <reason>`, through the printable filter. A missing or unknown subverb, a missing kind or ID, and a flag the subverb does not take print, after their reason when they have one (`fyr record: unknown subcommand "<x>"`, or the subverb and the flags it does not take), record's synopsis and `run 'fyr help record' for its flags`; a bare `fyr record`, `record add`, `get` or `edit` has no reason line. The redactor warning (§ Commands) goes to stderr and leaves the status as it is.

## Schema

```sql
records(rid INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, scope TEXT NOT NULL, id TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL,
        status TEXT NOT NULL, date TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, body TEXT NOT NULL,
        project TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', provenance TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', updated TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE(scope, id));
records_fts USING fts5(title, body, content='records', content_rowid='rid', tokenize='porter unicode61');
meta(scope TEXT PRIMARY KEY, export_sha TEXT, last_dream TEXT);
```

`scope` is the main worktree's absolute root, or `''` for global. `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`, the day the record was added. `updated` is RFC 3339 in UTC, set by every write. `rid` is the integer rowid the FTS table keys on: the plan's composite key alone would leave an implicit rowid that `VACUUM` may renumber. Triggers keep `records_fts` in step on insert, update and delete. `last_dream` is for Phase 4. Migration 2 adds `provenance` (`operator`, `derived` or `unknown` on `memory` and `feedback` records, `''` on every other kind; records stored before migration 2 or imported by `fyr record import` read as `unknown`, never `operator`, D12).

## What it is

A derived SQLite index the agent queries instead of reading whole files. Git and the brain store stay the source of truth: the index is a cache, never committed, never sent by `report`, and deleting it loses nothing but the next query's rebuild time (about two seconds for this repository: 2.1 s for 1,351 files on 2026-10-01).

## Commands

```
fyr search [--limit N] [--kind K] [--global] <words...>
fyr search --refs <BUG-NNN|ADR-NNN|path> [--kind K] [--global]
fyr search --open [--kind K] [--global]
fyr index [--global] [--rebuild]
fyr index --register [--rebuild]
```

- **Records first.** A words search first prints the brain store's hits (`~/.config/fyr/brain.db`, `SPEC-fyr-record`): a `records: N hits for "…"` header, then per record `ID  kind status  date  title` and a snippet line, from the project's scope and the global scope (`global:ID`), or with `--global` also from every other project scope whose checkout is registered under this home (`<root>:ID`, the full scope path, for another project's): an unregistered project's records, a clone's or a copy's included, answer no `--global` query, and the project's own scope stays in whether registered or not (ADR-068, audit-choices D15, ledger D13). They are ranked by BM25 over title (weighted twice) and body, weighted up to 10% by recency (linear over a year; D31), every word first and then any word, up to `--limit` records; the file hits that follow keep their own `--limit`. A changed `.agents/trail.jsonl` is loaded first. With no records found nothing is printed, and with no `brain.db` and no `trail.jsonl` nothing is created. A `trail.jsonl` that does not parse prints `records: not searched: <reason>` and the file hits still follow. The usage check runs before the records, so a usage error prints only its reason. `--refs <ID|path>` prints, before the file results, `records: N naming <ref>` and the records that name the ref as written — the ID's own record first, then every record whose title or body holds the path or ID as a whole name (no path character before it, nor after it unless the ref is a directory ending in `/`), each with the line that names it; `--open` prints `records: N open` and the open records (the status table's "Open when"). Both cover the project's and the global scope, with `--global` also every registered project's scope, and take `--kind` and `--limit` (D30).
- **Words** are each quoted for FTS5, so `BUG-049`, `a.go` or `NOT` are searched as text, never as query syntax. Chunks holding every word rank first; the remaining slots are filled with chunks holding any of them (a chunk matching both rounds is printed once and counted once against `--limit` and the per-file cap), and the header line says how many had every word (`search: 10 hits for "…", 2 with every word (…)`). Porter stemming: `verify` finds `verifies`. Hits are ranked by BM25 with a heading weighted twice the body, at most 2 per file, `--limit` (1–50, default 10) in all.
- **Each hit** prints `path:line  kind` and a one-line snippet (at most 200 characters, matched terms in `»«`). Control characters in indexed text, and Unicode's format characters, line separators and paragraph separators (classes Cf, Zl, Zp, and the default-ignorable characters outside them: zero-width and tag characters, direction marks, the byte-order mark, variation selectors, fillers), print as `?`, so a file cannot drive the terminal, forge a line or carry text nobody sees; the cost is that a zero-width joiner or a variation selector in an emoji sequence shows as `?` too. The line is the first line of the chunk holding a matched term.
- **`--refs X`** prints, for a path, its state (`tracked`, `modified`, `untracked`, `absent`, or `directory` for a trailing `/`), then `referenced by N:` and one entry per file that names X, sorted by path, with `×N` when it names X more than once; an ID's own record is the record hit above. A path matches as written; no basename matching, but a bare file name that matches no path prints `hint: did you mean --refs <path>` for up to five tracked paths ending in it.
- **`--open`** is answered by the record hits alone: a file holds no record (ADR-086), so nothing follows them. It refuses what the other modes refuse.
- **`--kind`** is one of `bug adr plan change handoff review testing retro spec deploy trail code doc feedback proposal learning guide memory` and filters every mode by the kind of the printed path, and the record hits by the record's kind. `trail` is every record and no file; `code` and `doc` take no record and are the only kinds of a checkout's file (ADR-086); `bug` through `deploy` are answered by records alone; `feedback` and `proposal` exist only in the global search index and as global records; `learning`, `guide` and `memory` exist only as records.
- **`index`** prints `files`, `chunks`, `refs`, `changed` (by this reconcile), `bytes` (database and WAL) and `ms`. `--rebuild` deletes the database and builds it again.
- **`index --register`** is the operator's consent that this checkout is read across projects (ADR-068, ADR-086): it joins the `projects` table of the global search index (below), its records answer `--global`, and `fyr dream --all` (`SPEC-fyr-dream`), `record import --global` (`SPEC-fyr-record`) and the metrics join (`SPEC-fyr-metrics`) take it. It writes the marker first — the regular file `fyr-registered`, mode 0600, in the checkout's git common directory (`.git/` in a plain checkout; every linked worktree shares it, and no clone carries it, because git never copies `.git/` files), holding `registered <YYYY-MM-DD>` and `seal <hex>`: the HMAC-SHA256 of the checkout's main top level under the home's registration key, `~/.config/fyr/registration.key` (0600, random, created on first use; ADR-068a) — then indexes as a plain `index` does, whose reconcile now registers the checkout, and prints `registered <root>` (the main worktree's top level) after the counts, then, when the checkout has no trail, `note: <root> has no .agents/trail.jsonl, so no cross-project read takes it until it has records (fyr record import, or the first fyr record add)`. A rerun rewrites the date; `--rebuild` combines. The marker is written to a temporary file in the same directory and renamed into place, so a symlink planted at its name is replaced, never followed; an existing symlink or non-regular file there is refused. A marker counts only when its seal matches this checkout's path under this home's key, so a tree whose `.git` file borrows a registered repository's git dir, a copy carrying `.git/` (`cp -a`, rsync, an archive of the directory), a moved checkout, a planted marker and another `--home` all read as unregistered, and a moved checkout registers again. There is no `--unregister`: deleting the marker is the opt-out (audit-choices D5); deleting `registration.key` unregisters every checkout of the home.

Exit status: 0 with hits or without; 1 on a refusal or an error; 2 on a usage error (a flag the verb does not define, a stray argument, a `--limit` outside 1..50, an unknown `--kind`, no mode or two modes at once, `--rebuild` given to `search`; the reason on stdout, BUG-168), as every verb since 2026-10-01.

## Where the indexes live

| Index | Path | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| Project | `<checkout>/.agents/scratch/search.db` (+ `-wal`, `-shm`) | every tracked, modified and untracked-not-ignored file (except what lies under a directory holding a `.fyr-noindex` file, or one under its name before the rename, `.sh-agent-noindex`, honoured the same way (plan `2026-10-24-fyr-agy-only.md` D12; `TestOldNoIndexMarkerStillCounts`): data the project carries, such as the harness's `skills/google-catalog/catalog/`, is not the project's own text; the header of a words search then ends `; left out by a noindex marker: <dir>/, <dir>/` (sorted, the checkout's root as `./`; here `skills/google-catalog/catalog/`; `--refs`, `index` and `--global` print no list; `TestHeaderNamesLeftOutDirectories`), the marker counts committed, staged or not yet added, one at the checkout's root leaves the whole checkout out of the project index, and a reconcile drops what was indexed before it appeared) under 1 MiB with no NUL byte in its first 8 KiB; symlinks, submodules and secret-shaped names (the installer's list, matched in any case: `.env`, `.env.*`, `*.env`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, token and credential files, …) skipped; a secret inside an ordinarily named file is indexed |
| Global search index | `~/.config/fyr/search.db` (+ `-wal`, `-shm`), under `--home` when given; the directory is created 0700. Both indexes' files are mode 0600 (an older 0644 file is tightened on open): they hold the text of every file read, whatever that file's own mode | no file (ADR-087); its `projects` table lists every checkout registered with `index --register` that has `<project>/.agents/trail.jsonl` and has run `search` or `index` since |

The global file is named "the global search index", never "cross-project index": the global `retro` records hold that name (R7). A checkout registers itself in the global search index on any `search` or `index` run inside it, `--global` included, at most once a day, only when it carries the operator's marker (`index --register`, above) and `<project>/.agents/trail.jsonl` is a regular file in a real `.agents` directory (ADR-086; a directory or a symlink at the name, or a symlink or file at `.agents`, is no trail: `TestTrailMustBeARegularFile`, `TestTrailNeedsARealAgentsDirectory`; one without it would be dropped by the next `--global`, ledger D11). The marker is read on the checkout that ran; the row and the trail it needs are the main root's, whichever linked worktree ran, and a worktree of a bare repository is its own root (`TestWorktreeRegistersTheMainRoot`, `TestRegistrationReadsTheRightRoot`). A drop removes the row only: while the marker holds, the checkout's records still answer `--global`. A committed `trail.jsonl` alone is not consent: a clone of a third party's harness-scaffolded repository never carries the marker, so it cannot answer `--global` queries or feed `/retro` (ADR-068, audit finding SD19; `TestRegistersOnlyHarnessProjects`). `--global` reads no file, neither a checkout's nor `~/.config/fyr`'s (its records come from the brain store; `fyr record import --global` is the old stores' one reader, ADR-087), and drops a registration whose root is no longer a git checkout, no longer has `<project>/.agents/trail.jsonl`, or no longer carries this home's valid marker: the marker deleted (the opt-out), `registration.key` deleted, a moved checkout, or a row registered before ADR-068, which is not carried over (audit-choices D4). A row is a cache entry the checkout's own next search writes again once it is registered. Run outside a checkout, `--global` still answers. The registry lives in the database, so `index --global --rebuild` drops it, with a note; each registered checkout returns on its next search.

## Freshness: reconcile before every answer

Every git call runs through `internal/trail.Command`: no index lock, no fsmonitor, no signature check, `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`. None of them starts a program the checkout's config or `.gitattributes` names; `git status` is never run, because it runs clean filters (BUG-165). A partial clone (`extensions.partialClone` set, or any remote marked `promisor`) is searched only when this machine's git is 2.44 or later, which honours `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH`. With an older git, the project search refuses it with a message naming the fix (update git), because a missing object would be fetched through the clone's own `core.sshCommand`. `--global` reads no checkout's objects.

1. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the working directory.
2. `git ls-files -s -z`: path and blob ID of every index entry.
3. Modified tracked files.
   - `git ls-files -s --debug` (read line by line, without `-z`, so a name holding a newline cannot forge another entry's lines) gives the size and mtime the index holds for each entry. A name git quotes (non-ASCII under the default `core.quotePath`, or one holding a tab, quote or backslash) is skipped, so its file is hashed on every reconcile: correct, but slower. A file whose size and mtime (to the nanosecond) still match, and which is not racily clean (written in the second the index was), keeps the index's blob ID.
   - Every other tracked file is read, and its ID is computed from its own bytes as a git blob ID. When that ID differs from the index's, the file is modified. (`git hash-object --stdin-paths` misreads names with a trailing CR or a leading quote, so it is not used.)
   - A file the checkout runs through a clean filter therefore reads as modified and is indexed from its bytes.
   - Deleted paths leave.
4. `git ls-files -z --others --exclude-standard`: untracked files, each ID computed from its bytes. A rename is a deletion and an addition.
5. Everything derived from content (chunks, records, references) is stored once per blob ID, so a branch switch re-reads only content the index has never seen. Every query joins through the current path-to-blob view, which is what keeps another branch's content out of an answer.
6. When nothing changed, no write lock is taken (a per-query insert into the project database's unread `projects` table took one until SD20 of the 2026-10-27 audit; `TestUnchangedSearchTakesNoWriteLock` pins it); the reconcile costs about 15 ms here for the project index. `--global` checks every registered checkout before answering (a `git rev-parse` and two file checks per checkout), so its cost grows with the number of registered checkouts and is not the 15 ms figure. A blob no view references is deleted after 14 days unseen.

No watcher, no service, no hook (R3, R8).

## References

A file is text: search reads no docs root and parses no record from it (ADR-086), so a project's `docs/` is indexed like any other directory, as `code` or `doc`. Records are the brain store's.

References are record IDs (`BUG-NNN`, `ADR-NNN`) and path-shaped tokens on every line of every indexed file, with a trailing `:NN`, trailing punctuation and a leading `./`, `a/` or `b/` removed.

## Failure modes

| Case | Output | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| Not inside a git checkout, or no `git` | `search: not inside a git checkout; use grep` | 1 |
| `.agents/scratch/search.db` not gitignored | `search: .agents/scratch/search.db is not gitignored; add ".agents/scratch/*" to .gitignore (/init-project does)`; nothing created | 1 |
| `.agents/scratch/search.db-wal`, `-shm` or `-journal` is tracked | `search: <path> is tracked; \`git rm --cached\` it, since a rebuild would delete it`; nothing removed (`TestRefusesTrackedCompanion`) | 1 |
| `.agents` or `.agents/scratch` is a symlink | `search: .agents/scratch is a symlink; refusing to write through it` | 1 |
| `search.db`, `search.db-wal` or `search.db-shm` is a symlink or any other non-regular file (either index) | `search: <path>: <file> is not a regular file; refusing to open or write through it`; nothing is written through it | 1 |
| Another process holds the write lock past 10 s | `search: index busy (another fyr is indexing); retry, or use grep`; no answer printed | 1 |
| Two runs open a new index at once | the open is retried for the same 10 s, because SQLite answers that race with an immediate `SQLITE_BUSY` (BUG-187); past it, the line above | 1 |
| Unreadable database, or a schema other than 3 | `note: index at <path> was unreadable (or an older schema); rebuilt`, then the answer | 0 |
| Argument errors (`--limit` out of range, unknown `--kind`, two modes at once, no mode) | `search: <what is wrong>; see fyr help search` | 2 |
| Global: a registered checkout is gone, or lost its `<project>/.agents/trail.jsonl` | `note: dropped <root> (no longer a git checkout)`, or `(no longer has .agents/trail.jsonl)` | 0 |
| Global: a row's checkout no longer carries this home's valid marker | `note: dropped <root> (not registered: fyr index --register)`; nothing of it served | 0 |
| Global rebuild | `note: N project registrations dropped; each registered one returns on its next search` | 0 |
| `index --register --global` | `fyr index: --register and --global do not go together`; no marker written | 2 |
| `index --register` outside a git checkout | `fyr index: --register needs a git checkout` | 2 |
| `index --register`: the marker's name holds a symlink or a non-regular file, the common directory is not writable, the home's `registration.key` is a link or not a regular file, or git places the work tree elsewhere | `fyr: index --register: <path> is not a regular file; refusing to replace it`, or the error naming the path; nothing indexed (`TestIndexRegisterRefusedMarker`, `TestIndexRegisterOtherFailures`) | 1 |
| `index --register`: the marker was written, then the index failed | `fyr: registered <root>, but the index failed: <error>`; the marker stays valid | 1 |
| Global: a registered checkout's check cannot run (for example `.agents` unreadable) | `note: skipped <root> this time (<error>)`; the registration stays | 0 |
| A file edited and then restored while `search` waits for the write lock | the edit stays indexed for that blob until `index --rebuild` (known limit, plan D35) | 0 |
| A copied project directory that brings its own `search.db` | trusted as it is: an index is only as trusted as the folder it sits in, and whoever can plant one can plant `AGENTS.md` and trail files there too; after copying a project in, run `fyr index --rebuild` (known limit, the operator's choice at the v1.13.0 gate) | 0 |
| Network filesystem | not supported: SQLite's WAL needs one host's shared memory; the SQLite error is printed | 1 |

`search.db` never leaves the machine (ADR-062). `fyr uninstall` leaves `~/.config/fyr/search.db`, which is not in the install manifest; delete it by hand if wanted.

## Measured (this repository, 2026-09-29, Linux amd64)

| Measurement | Result |
|---|---|
| Full build, 1,351 files (2026-10-01; 1,080 on 2026-09-29) | 2.1 s on 2026-10-01; 1.7 s (2.2 s before the inserts were prepared once and reference parsing skipped lines that cannot match) |
| Warm `search`, nothing changed, end to end | 23–67 ms |
| Recall@10 on 41 questions from this repository's history (`TEST-2026-09-29-search-recall`; re-measured 2026-10-25 on go1.24.4 in `TEST-2026-10-25-search-recall`, after the "open plan" gold was re-pinned and "open bug", with no bug open, became a refs question) | 0.505 (2026-10-25; 0.633 on 2026-10-01 and 0.653 on 2026-09-29 on the old fixture), against 0.237 for one grep pass; words 0.538 against 0.115, drift 0.170 against 0.172 |
| Warm `--refs` / `--open`, end to end | 47–60 ms / 20 ms |
| Database size | 21.7 MB (10,560 chunks, 40,850 references); 24.1 MB before the unused `refs(oid)` index was dropped |
| Binary size, linux/amd64 | 13.7 MB |

It also runs two maintenance verbs, `fyr index` and `fyr metrics ingest`, as buttons. It is not a service: it runs in the foreground until interrupted, listens on `127.0.0.1` only, serves one operator, and edits no record, memory or file by hand. ## Interfaces ### The verb ``` fyr serve [--port N] [--home DIR] [--repo DIR] ``` | Flag | Type | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---|---| | `--port` | int | `3000` | The port on `127.0.0.1`; `1`–`65535`, anything else is a usage error, exit 2, checked before anything is bound | | `--home` | path | the user's home | The home whose `.config/fyr` holds the stores, made absolute as every verb does | | `--repo` | path | as `fyr status` | The harness tree the status and context pages resolve; the verb resolves a source, as `fyr status` and `fyr render` do | - No positional argument: one is a usage error, exit 2. - The **project** is the git checkout holding the working directory at start, `Options.Dir`, fixed for the run. Every call takes `Options.Dir` exactly as the verbs take their working directory (`brain.Options.Dir`, `search.Options.Dir`, `check.Run`), so a linked worktree is served as the CLI would see it from there. The main worktree root from `trail.Roots` is used only for the start line and to decide that there is no project. - `writesState` answers true for `serve` (its pages load a changed `trail.jsonl`, as `fyr record list` does), so an old state directory is moved first, and that move's own line may print before the start lines. - `serve` is registered in `cmd/fyr`'s `init()`, like `check`, never in the `verbs` literal: its `Check` closure reaches `vocabulary()`, which reads `verbs` (`cmd/fyr/check.go`'s comment on the initialization cycle). After the listener is bound, the server prints on stdout exactly these two lines, then nothing until it stops: ``` fyr serve: http://127.0.0.1:/s/

/?token= fyr serve: serving is not a git checkout> and /.config/fyr; Ctrl-C stops it ``` It opens no browser. **Stopping.** The first SIGINT or SIGTERM stops accepting connections and waits for the handlers in flight to return (`http.Server.Shutdown` with no deadline), then exits 0; `http.ErrServerClosed` is not an error. A second signal while it waits exits 1 at once. The signals are read from one `signal.Notify` channel, not `signal.NotifyContext`, so the second one is seen. A Ctrl-C at the terminal reaches the whole foreground process group, including the `git` children of a running index action, so that action may end `failed:`; the search index is a cache and reconciles on its next run. An interrupted metrics ingest behaves as `fyr metrics ingest` interrupted. ### Listener and server - `Options.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:")`, `net.Listen` by default; never `localhost`, `0.0.0.0` or `::`. No flag widens it. - `http.Server{ReadHeaderTimeout: 10s, ReadTimeout: 30s, IdleTimeout: 60s, MaxHeaderBytes: 64 KiB, ErrorLog: a logger to io.Discard}`; no `WriteTimeout` (an action may run long). A POST body is read through `http.MaxBytesReader` at 4 KiB. ### Tokens Two tokens and a path prefix per run, each 32 bytes from `crypto/rand`, encoded base64url without padding (43 characters); never written to disk, never logged. | Token | Where it travels | Compared | |---|---|---| | session `T` | the printed URL's `token` query parameter, then the cookie `fyr_serve_` | `crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare` | | prefix `P` | the printed URL's path, `/s/

/`; every page and every link the pages render lives under `/s/

` (plan D48, ADR-075a) | a string prefix of `r.URL.Path` | | CSRF `C` | a hidden `csrf` field in every action form (a POST, row 9); the `/search` form is a GET and carries none, since a token in a URL lands in the browser's history (plan D46) | `crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare` | The cookie: `fyr_serve_=; Path=/s/

; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict`, no `Expires` (it dies with the browser session), no `Secure` (plain HTTP on loopback). A browser scopes cookies by host, not port: with `Path=/` the cookie would reach every other port of `127.0.0.1`, and any server there the browser visits would read `T` from its `Cookie` header and then every page with a plain client (security review of row 8, 2026-10-29). The path keeps it home: the browser sends the cookie only for paths under `/s/

`, which a server on another port never learns (no `Referer`, CORP, no CORS). A page served on another local port is still same-site, so `SameSite` is no defence against its requests. The port in the name keeps two runs' cookies apart; the cross-port defences are the `Sec-Fetch-Site` refusal, the CSRF field and the `Origin` check below. `T` is valid for the whole run and is not single-use, by design: a second browser tab or a browser restart reuses the printed URL. Its residue is the 303'd entry in the browser's history, gone with the run. ### Every request, in this order 1. **Host.** `r.Host` must equal `127.0.0.1:` exactly, else `403` (DNS rebinding). `localhost` is not accepted: the printed URL never uses it, and a browser may resolve it to `::1`. 2. **Fetch metadata.** A `Sec-Fetch-Site` header, when sent, must be `same-origin` or `none` (a URL typed or pasted), else `403`: a page on another site or another local port gets nothing, GET included. 3. **Token.** On `GET` or `HEAD`, a query holding the `token` parameter: exactly one value equal to `T` sets the cookie and answers `303 See Other` with `Location` built as a `url.URL` (never by string concatenation) from the request's path (`r.URL.Path`, a leading run of slashes collapsed to one) and the other query parameters, re-encoded; any other `token` (wrong, empty, repeated) is `403`, never a fallback to the cookie. Without the parameter, some cookie named `fyr_serve_` among `r.Cookies()` must equal `T` (every one is compared: a same-site page can plant a second cookie of that name), else `403`. 4. **Route.** A path outside `/s/

/` (`/s/

` itself included), or an unknown one under it, is `404` whatever the method; the routes below are named relative to the prefix. A known path with a method it does not take is `405` with `Allow` (`GET, HEAD` for a page, `POST` for an action). 5. **CSRF (POST only).** The cookie authenticated the request (a POST carrying a `token` query parameter is `403`); `mime.ParseMediaType(Content-Type)` gives `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (a charset parameter is allowed); the body's `csrf` field (`r.PostForm`, never the query) occurs exactly once and equals `C` (plan D53); `Origin`, when sent, equals `http://127.0.0.1:` (`null` or any other value is `403`). A POST without `Origin` passes on the token and `C` alone: every current browser sends it on a form POST, and a client that does not already holds both tokens. Any miss is `403` and runs nothing. A refusal is `text/plain; charset=utf-8` with one line and nothing else (no token, no path): `forbidden` for a 403 of steps 1, 3 and 5; `forbidden: open the printed URL by pasting it into the address bar` for a 403 of step 2 (it holds no secret, and a URL clicked inside a web page or a browser-based terminal arrives `cross-site`); `not found` for a 404 of step 4 and for an `{id}` outside the grammar; `method not allowed` for a 405. The layout's `404` page is for a well-formed request whose object is missing: `no record `, and `/metrics/report` with no store. Accepted residual: a browser that sends no `Sec-Fetch-Site` lets a page on another local port cause the idempotent writes of read pages (a search reconcile, a metrics migration) with the cookie, since `SameSite` does not separate ports; it reads nothing back (CORP, no CORS) and cannot reach an action (CSRF). Accepted residual (availability only, security review of row 9, 2026-10-30): a page on another local port can set enough `Path=/` cookies on `127.0.0.1` that the browser's `Cookie` header passes `MaxHeaderBytes` (64 KiB); every request of that browser to the run, the actions included, is then `431` until the operator clears the host's cookies or uses another browser profile. Nothing is read or run; raising the limit would only move the line. ### Headers on every response ``` Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none' X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff Referrer-Policy: no-referrer Cache-Control: no-store Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin ``` On every status, the 303, the refusals and `/static/style.css` included. No page carries a script. `'unsafe-inline'` is there for one reason, the `

## Purpose

The lead session hands each Kickoff to a worker. A worker is an unattended `agy -p` session in its own sandbox, on a clone of the lead's checkout, committing on its own branch. Several workers run at once, up to a limit counted across the machine. The package fetches each branch back into the lead's checkout by path, checks that the worker stayed inside the files its Kickoff names, and returns a result contract of at most 39 lines per worker. The lead reads that contract instead of a transcript. The package does not merge, tick the plan, store records, or read a sandbox's brain store (ADR-063).

What the worker's agent reads goes to the CLI's model, unredacted, as in any session of that CLI (R8). That is the third thing that leaves the machine, beside the dreamer's redacted prompt and `fyr eval`'s runs. The clone has no remote, so git pushes it nowhere; but the agent runs with `command(*)` and the network, so a misled agent can still send what it reads elsewhere, and on `--runner host` it reads and writes as the operator, outside the clone too. `--runner docker` keeps it off the operator's files but the login token (§ Docker mode), not off the network (the v5.0.0 gate's security review; ADR-076, `SPEC-fyr-delivery` § What stays on the machine). A run that names a model also makes one `agy models` call before anything is made (refusal 21); it is a list request to the same provider and is not a fourth thing that leaves the machine (§ Data).

The session runs on the host by default. With `--runner docker` it runs in a hardened container instead, and every other step stays on the host (§ Docker mode).

## Interfaces

### The verb

```
fyr work [--timeout D] [--model M] [--max-workers N] [--keep]
         [--runner host|docker] [--image REF] [--agy-linux PATH]
         <kickoff-file>...
fyr work --kill <stamp>
```

Beside the global `--home` and `--repo`. `fyr help work` prints the page (`cmd/fyr/help_text.go`).

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--timeout D` | kill the worker's agy after `D`. Default 120m (D45). Whole minutes, at least 10m. |
| `--model M` | the agy model for every worker whose Kickoff has no `Model:` line (§ The Kickoff file); default is agy's own. `M` must match the model-ID pattern (refusal 11) and be listed by the host's `agy models` (refusal 21). |
| `--max-workers N` | the machine-wide limit on workers running at once. Default 4, 1 to 8 (D30). The verb refuses 0 or less; `internal/work` refuses over 8 (`--max-workers N: give 1 to 8`), before its other refusals. |
| `--keep` | keep the sandbox of a fetched worker too. |
| `--runner R` | where each worker's agy session runs: `host` (the default, the path of every other section of this record) or `docker` (§ Docker mode). Any other value is refused (refusal 12). |
| `--image REF` | `--runner docker`'s image. Default `fyr-work:local`, the tag the build line (§ The worker image) gives. Ignored with `--runner host`. |
| `--agy-linux PATH` | `--runner docker`'s linux agy, mounted read-only into the container. Default: the host's own `agy`, on a linux host only; required elsewhere. Ignored with `--runner host`. |
| `--kill STAMP` | end the run whose stamp line printed `STAMP` (below). Takes no Kickoff file. With docker installed it also removes that stamp's containers and network when the run is gone (§ The container sweep). |
| `--home` | fyr's home; the sandboxes are made under `<home>/.config/fyr/work/`. The default is the real home: the verb writes no store (D35). |
| `--repo` | the install source each sandbox gets, resolved as `fyr eval` resolves it (`harness.ResolveSource`, D40). |

Several Kickoff files run at once, up to the limit counted across the machine (D30). A file past the limit waits inside the invocation and starts, in file order, as a slot frees. The stamp line says `<n> workers`. Each worker's result block prints whole, in file order, as soon as it and every file before it ended (D19).

Exit statuses (D34): 0 when every worker PASS, 1 when any FAIL, 2 a refusal or a usage error. A refusal prints one line, `work: <reason>`, before anything is made, so nothing is printed after it and no sandbox exists. A FAIL still prints the result contract.

The verb's refusals, in this order:

1. Usage errors: no file prints the verb's usage; a `--max-workers` or a `--timeout` of 0 or less is refused (`internal/work` would read 0 as its default); `--image` or `--agy-linux` without `--runner docker` is refused (`--image and --agy-linux need --runner docker`): either alone would run every session on the host unasked.
2. The working directory is not a git checkout (`work: <dir> is not a git checkout`). The checkout's top level is the lead's `Root`.
3. The install source: `harness.ResolveSource(--repo, --home, the build version)` fails.
4. There is no home directory (`$HOME`) to name as the real home.
5. The running fyr cannot be located (`os.Executable`). It is the fyr each sandbox installs.
6. `internal/work`'s own refusals, below.

`--kill <stamp>`: it looks under its own `--home`, so it takes the run's (`--kill <stamp> --home DIR` for a run started with one). The stamp must match `%F-%H%M%S-<pid>`, the pid at most seven digits, and the pid in the file must be over 1 and at most 4194304 (1<<22, Linux's highest `pid_max`): a larger one would wrap in `kill(2)`, at worst to -1, every process of the operator's (the Phase 4 security review, finding 1). The run's pid file (below) is opened with `O_NOFOLLOW` and must be a regular file. A missing file is refused (`no run <stamp>`). A shared non-blocking lock that succeeds on it means no run holds it, so it is refused (`<path> is stale: no run holds it`); when `docker` is on PATH and its daemon is local (refusal 15's check), that refusal first sweeps the stamp's containers and says what it did (§ The container sweep). The pid in the file must be the stamp's. Then the verb sends SIGTERM to that pid, which ends that run's context (below; the run prints its own result contract), prints `work: SIGTERM sent to <pid>, the run <stamp>; it prints its result contract`, and exits 0. Every refusal exits 2. A Kickoff file with `--kill` is refused (`--kill takes a stamp and no Kickoff file`). `--kill` writes no state, so it does not migrate an old state directory. Accepted residual: if the run ends between the lock check and the signal and its pid is reused at once, the signal reaches that process; the window is the few instructions between the two calls.

Signals: SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGQUIT end the run's context. Each running worker's agy gets SIGTERM then SIGKILL (in docker mode the container is stopped first, § Docker mode), the worker fails `killed`, the token link is removed, and the result contract still prints (exit 1). A file still waiting for a slot never starts: it fails `killed` with the note `the run ended while it waited for a slot; never started`, and has no sandbox (D26). SIGHUP is handled as eval handles it, and SIGQUIT too, which eval does not: either default would kill fyr before the token link is removed, and agy, in its own process group, would run on with the wide grant. Once the context has ended, a further signal is swallowed until the run returns, as in eval, so a hung cleanup stops only with SIGKILL, which leaves the token link.

### The Go surface

```go
type Options struct {
	Root, Home, RealHome, Self, Repo string // checkout top level; fyr's home; $HOME; installing fyr; install source ("" embedded)
	Timeout   time.Duration // 0 is DefaultTimeout, 120m (D45); whole minutes, at least 10m (D37)
	Model     string        // agy --model for a worker whose Kickoff has no Model: line; "" passes none
	Keep      bool          // keep a fetched worker's sandbox too
	MaxWorkers int          // machine-wide limit, 1 to MaxMaxWorkers (8); 0 is DefaultMaxWorkers (4) (D30)
	Out       io.Writer
	Now       func() time.Time
	StopGrace time.Duration // SIGTERM to SIGKILL on ctx's end; 0 is 5s
	Runner    string        // RunnerHost ("host"; "" too) or RunnerDocker ("docker")
	Image     string        // --runner docker's image ref; "" is DefaultImage ("fyr-work:local")
	AgyLinux  string        // --runner docker's linux agy; "" is the host's own, on linux
	Version   string        // this fyr's build version, which the image must hold; the verb passes buildVersion()
}
func Run(ctx context.Context, o Options, files ...string) ([]Result, error) // results in file order; error: a refusal, nothing made
func Kill(home, stamp string) (int, error)                                   // SIGTERM to the run; the pid signalled
func ParseKickoff(path string) (Kickoff, error)                              // Kickoff.Model: the Model: line's ID, "" when none
func (r Result) Block() []string                                             // the result contract
```

`Run` makes `Root`, `Home` and `RealHome` absolute once, so the fetch and the drafts copy read the same clone. It returns an error for a refusal, and nothing is made. Otherwise it prints the stamp line, runs the workers, prints each result contract in file order, in docker mode prints the container sweep line (§ The result contract), and returns the `Result`s in that order (Verdict `PASS` or `FAIL`, Reasons, AgyExit, Seconds, Model, Base, Head, Commits, Dir, Handoff, Changes, Drafts, DraftsDir, Notes). `Result.Model` is the model the worker's session ran on, `""` for agy's default. The verb maps the outcomes to the exit statuses above.

### The Kickoff file

- The text is passed to agy verbatim, after the sandbox's prefix ("The project root is the current directory, <clone>; ignore any other checkout."). The `Model:` line stays in it.
- The file is opened with `O_NOFOLLOW`, so a link is refused. It is at most 64 KiB.
- The name is the base name without `.md`. It matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$` and `git check-ref-format --branch work/<name>`. The branch is `work/<name>`.
- Exactly one line starts with `Files:`. Its entries are comma-separated and trimmed. Each entry is one of:
  - a record ID, `^[A-Z]+-[0-9A-Za-z-]+$`
  - a repo-relative path to a file, or to a directory ending in `/`. Refused: absolute, a `..`, `.` or empty segment, a glob character (`*?[\`), a control character, and `.agents/trail.jsonl` itself (its records are named by ID).
- An entry covers a path when the two are equal, or when the entry ends in `/` and is a prefix of the path.
- At most one line starts with `Model:`, at column 0 (an indented line is not one). Its trimmed value is the worker's model and must match the model-ID pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$` (`modelRe`). It overrides `--model` for that worker alone. No line is fine: the worker takes `--model`, else agy's default. Whether agy lists the ID is refusal 21's check, not the parse's.

1. Root is not a git checkout (`sandbox.OutsideCheckout`).
2. The tree differs from HEAD: `trail.Dirty`, which answers without `git status` and its filters (BUG-164). An untracked file or a rewritten `trail.jsonl` counts (D13, D32).
3. Each Kickoff file: missing, unreadable, a link, over 64 KiB, no single `Files:` line, a bad entry, more than one `Model:` line (`<n> Model: lines; give one`), or a `Model:` value that is not a model ID (`the Model: line "<value>" is not a model ID`). Each message is prefixed `the Kickoff <path>: `.
4. A bad name, a name given twice (`the Kickoffs A and B share the name N; each worker needs its own branch`), or a branch `work/<name>` that already exists in the checkout.
5. The checkout has no `user.name` and `user.email`. The worker commits as them (D25, D47).
6. Two files whose `Files:` entries intersect: equal, or one a directory entry (ending in `/`) that is a prefix of the other. Record IDs count (D17). The refusal names both files and both entries.
7. `sandbox.CheckRoot` refuses `<home>/.config/fyr/work` (guards a and b, BUG-106).

The machine already runs the limit: the live runs' workers, counted from their pid files, are `--max-workers` or more (`the machine already runs N workers, at --max-workers M: <stamps>; wait, or fyr work --kill <stamp>`, then `; counted as full, unreadable: <path> (<error>)` for each pid file counted as full because it could not be read, which `--kill` cannot clear). It is counted after 7, so nothing under an unapproved root is read, and without `slots.lock`, since nothing is made yet.
9. No Antigravity login at `$HOME/.gemini/antigravity-cli/antigravity-oauth-token`.
10. `agy` is not on PATH. **Not made with `--runner docker`:** the container's agy is a linux one, checked by refusal 19.
11. `--model` does not match the model-ID pattern (`--model <M>: not a model ID`; a value starting with `-`, which agy would read as a flag, is one case); or `--timeout` is under 10m, or not whole minutes.
